steps.text: Toast the sesame seeds in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat, stirring constantly, until fragrant and lightly golden, about 5 minutes. Tip onto a plate.

Pour the honey into the same pan over medium heat. Warm, swirling gently, until it turns a deep amber, about 8 minutes. Don't stir it, just let it happen. You'll know it's ready when it smells toasted and a drop in cold water snaps cleanly.
Remove from heat. Working fast, add the vanilla and salt, then tip in the toasted sesame seeds. Stir hard until everything is coated.
Pour onto a baking tray lined with baking paper, spreading it thin and even with an oiled spatula. Work quickly, it sets fast.
Cool completely at room temperature, about 2 hours. Break into pieces with your hands. That's it, mate.

notes: Keep in an airtight container for up to a week.
If the honey doesn't snap when cold, it needs another minute or two on the heat.

title: Bún Chả Cá Huế
summary: Spicy fish cake noodle soup from Huế, pungent and salty with fermented shrimp and chilli.

items.raw: 300 g fresh fish cakes, sliced 1 cm thick (or canned, drained)
400 g fresh rice vermicelli (or dried, cooked and drained)
Salt and black pepper, to taste

steps.text: In a small bowl, mash the shrimp paste with a fork until it breaks down. Add 2 tbsp of hot water and stir well until it dissolves into a pungent liquid; set aside.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and sliced chillies, stirring constantly until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the shrimp paste liquid to the pot and stir for another minute, until fragrant, letting the flavour bloom. Pour in the stock and bring to a simmer until bubbling gently.
Add the fish sauce and caster sugar, stirring to dissolve. Taste and adjust, it should be salty, pungent, and slightly sweet. This is Huế food; don't be timid.
Gently slide the fish cake slices into the simmering broth and cook for 5 to 8 minutes until they're heated through and tender.
While the broth cooks, divide the cooked rice vermicelli between four bowls.
Ladle the hot broth and fish cakes over the noodles. Top with fresh Vietnamese mint, coriander, and spring onion. Serve with lime wedges and extra chillies on the side for those who want more heat.

notes: Fresh fish cakes are best if you can find them at an Asian grocer. Canned work fine too, just drain them well.
The shrimp paste makes this dish. It's pungent and funky on its own, but dissolves into the broth and gives it depth.
If you can't find fresh Vietnamese mint, use extra Thai basil or regular mint, it won't be the same, but it still works.

title: Moqueca Baiana
summary: Creamy, spiced fish stew from Bahia, made with coconut milk and dendê oil.

items.raw: 800 g white fish fillets (barramundi, snapper, ling), cut into chunks

steps.text: Heat the dendê oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Add the onion and capsicum, stirring occasionally, until softened and the onion is starting to caramelize, about 8 minutes.
Add the garlic and chilli, stirring constantly for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute to deepen the flavour.
Pour in the coconut milk and fish stock, stirring to combine. Bring to a gentle simmer until small bubbles break the surface, then reduce the heat to medium-low.

Carefully add the fish chunks to the pot, season with salt and pepper, and simmer gently for 12 to 15 minutes, until the fish is just cooked through and flakes easily. Do not stir vigorously; gently turn the fish once halfway through.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Serve hot, scattered with fresh coriander and lime wedges on the side.

notes: Serve with white rice and farofa (toasted cassava flour) on the side to soak up the sauce.
Any firm white fish works, barramundi, snapper, ling or flathead are all good choices. Avoid delicate fish like flake.
Make ahead: prep the vegetables and fish the day before; cook just before serving so the fish stays tender.
Food safety: Cook fish until it turns opaque and flakes easily, about 63°C in the thickest part.

title: Honey Soy Chicken Stir-Fry
summary: Chicken strips and frozen veg tossed in a sweet soy sauce, ready in 15 minutes.

items.raw: 600 g chicken breast, sliced into thin strips

steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large wok or frying pan over high heat. Add the chicken strips and cook, stirring often, until cooked through (no pink inside), about 5 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil to the pan. Add the frozen mixed vegetables and stir-fry for 2 minutes until starting to soften.
Pour in the stir-fry sauce and honey, stirring to combine. Return the chicken to the pan and toss everything together until well coated and hot, about 1 minute.
Divide rice or noodles between bowls, top with the stir-fry while the chicken is glossy and cooked through, and garnish with spring onion and sesame seeds if using.

notes: This freezes brilliantly, make a double batch and freeze the cooled stir-fry in containers for a quick weeknight reheat. Thaw overnight in the fridge and warm in a pan over medium heat.
Use any frozen mixed veg (broccoli, carrot, capsicum, snap peas all work), or what's on special.
Food safety: Cook chicken and other poultry until the juices run clear and the thickest part reaches 75°C.

title: Orecchiette con Cime di Rapa
summary: Ear-shaped pasta with bitter greens, garlic and chilli.

items.raw: 500 g cime di rapa (turnip tops), roughly chopped
1 red chilli, deseeded and finely chopped
Salt and black pepper, to taste

steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil. Add the orecchiette and cook until al dente, about 12 minutes.

While the pasta cooks, heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Add the garlic and chilli, and cook gently for 2–3 minutes, stirring often, until the garlic just turns golden, don't let it burn.

Add the cime di rapa to the pan with a splash of water (about 100 ml) and a pinch of salt. Increase the heat to medium-high and cook, stirring occasionally, until the greens are tender, about 8 minutes.
Reserve 200 ml of the pasta cooking water, then drain the pasta. Add it to the pan with the cime di rapa.
Toss well, adding pasta water a little at a time, until everything is coated in a loose, silky sauce. The starch in the water helps emulsify the oil. Taste and adjust the salt and pepper.
Serve hot, with a scatter of flaky salt if you like, and more chilli on the side for anyone who wants it.

notes: Cime di rapa can be hard to find outside Italian delis, but gai lan (Chinese broccoli) works just as well, it's the same plant, just called by a different name.
Serve with a generous pour of your best olive oil and crusty bread to wipe the bowl.

title: Bistek na Isda
summary: Fish steaks braised in soy and vinegar with onions, cooked the Visayan way.

items.raw: 800 g firm white fish steak (or fillet), cut into 4 pieces (barramundi, snapper or ling)
items.note: or fillet; barramundi, snapper or ling

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large shallow pan over medium-high heat. Season the fish pieces with salt and pepper on both sides.
Fry the fish for 2 minutes each side until lightly golden, then remove to a plate.
In the same pan, sauté the garlic until fragrant, about 1 minute. Add the sliced onion and cook, stirring, until soft and translucent, about 4 minutes.
Pour in the soy sauce and vinegar, stirring to combine. Bring to a gentle simmer until small bubbles appear and the sharp vinegar smell has softened.

Return the fish to the pan, nestling the pieces among the onions. Simmer gently for 5–7 minutes, spooning the sauce over the fish occasionally, until the fish is cooked through and flakes easily when tested with a fork.
Taste and adjust the salt if needed. Serve hot with the braising liquid and onions spooned over the fish, alongside steamed white rice.

notes: Food safety: Cook fish until it turns opaque and flakes easily, about 63°C in the thickest part.

title: Pad Pak Ruam Mit
summary: Stir-fried mixed vegetables with garlic, ginger and fish sauce, quick Thai comfort.

items.raw: 150 g green beans, trimmed and halved
Salt and black pepper, to taste

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wok or large frying pan over high heat. When shimmering, add the minced garlic and ginger, and stir-fry for about 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the broccoli florets, carrot slices and green beans. Toss continuously for about 4 minutes until the vegetables start to soften but still have some bite.
Add the sliced mushrooms and stir-fry for another 2 minutes until they release their moisture.
Pour in the fish sauce and sprinkle over the caster sugar. Toss everything to combine, then taste and season with salt and black pepper as needed.
Transfer to a serving plate and scatter Thai basil over the top if you have it. Serve immediately with jasmine rice.

title: Wattleseed and Macadamia Biscuits
summary: Buttery biscuits with wattleseed and native Australian macadamias.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 180°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
In a bowl, beat the butter and caster sugar together until pale and creamy, about 3 minutes.
Add the egg yolk and mix until combined.
In a separate bowl, combine the plain flour, wattleseed, and a pinch of salt.
Fold the dry ingredients into the wet ingredients until just combined, then fold in the macadamias.
Place heaped teaspoons of dough onto the prepared tray, leaving about 3 cm between each biscuit.
Bake for 10–12 minutes until the edges are golden and the centres still have a little give.
Cool on the tray for 2 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.

notes: Store in an airtight container for up to 5 days.
You can make the dough ahead and refrigerate for up to 2 days before baking.

title: Siraegi Bokkeum
summary: Stir-fried dried radish greens, tender and fragrant with sesame and ginger.

steps.text: Rinse the dried radish greens under cold water to remove any dust, then soak in 200 ml water for 10 minutes until they soften and become pliable.
Drain the greens, reserving 100 ml of the soaking water. Gently squeeze out excess moisture from the greens and cut them into 5 cm lengths.
Heat sesame oil in a wide pan or wok over medium heat. Add the minced ginger and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the drained radish greens and stir to coat with oil, cooking for about 3 minutes.

Pour in the reserved soaking water, soy sauce and rice vinegar. Stir well, then simmer gently for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the greens are very tender and the liquid has mostly absorbed.
Taste and adjust salt if needed. Transfer to a serving dish and scatter toasted sesame seeds over the top just before serving.

notes: Siraegi keeps well in the fridge for 3 days and can be served hot, warm or at room temperature.
If you can't find dried radish greens, look for them in Asian markets labelled as 'siraegi' or 'siraegi', they're worth seeking out.

title: Holubtsi
summary: Tender cabbage leaves rolled with beef mince and buckwheat, braised until tender and glossy.

items.raw: 150 g buckwheat groats, cooked and cooled
Salt and black pepper, to taste

steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil. Carefully remove the core from the cabbage with a sharp knife, then place the whole cabbage in the boiling water. After 8–10 minutes, gently peel away the softened outer leaves and set aside on a clean kitchen towel. Repeat until you have about 12 large leaves; reserve any remaining cabbage, finely shredded.

While the cabbage cools, heat 1 tbsp oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes, then add the garlic and cook for 1 minute more. Remove from heat and let cool slightly. In a large bowl, combine the cooled onion and garlic with the beef mince, buckwheat, egg, salt and pepper. Mix gently until just combined, don't overwork it.

Lay a cabbage leaf on a clean surface. Place about 2 tbsp of the filling near the base of the leaf, fold the sides in, then roll away from you into a tight parcel. Repeat with the remaining leaves and filling.

Heat the remaining 1 tbsp oil in a large heavy-based pan over medium-high heat. Arrange the cabbage rolls seam-side down in a single layer (work in batches if needed). Cook for 2–3 minutes until golden on the base, then turn carefully and cook for another 2 minutes. Remove and set aside on a plate.

In the same pan, stir together the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute. Add the crushed tomatoes and beef stock, scraping up any brown bits from the base of the pan. Add the caraway seeds if using, and season with salt and pepper. Scatter the reserved shredded cabbage over the base of the pan.

Return the cabbage rolls to the pan, nestling them into the sauce, seam-side down. Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce heat to low. Cover and braise for 60–70 minutes, until the rolls are tender and the sauce is rich and glossy. Serve warm with a generous dollop of sour cream.

notes: Holubtsi freeze beautifully. Cool them in their sauce, then freeze in an airtight container for up to three months. Reheat gently in a 160°C oven, covered, for about 30 minutes.
If you can't find buckwheat groats, use cooked white rice or pearl barley instead.
The dish tastes even better the next day, once the flavours have settled together.
Cook mince and sausages until they reach 75°C in the centre, with no pink left.
Food safety: Raw and lightly cooked foods aren't recommended for pregnant women, young children, older people or anyone with a weakened immune system.

title: Pad Phed Gai
summary: Fiery stir-fried chicken with red curry paste, charred at the edges.

steps.text: Heat your wok or heavy frying pan over high heat until it's smoking hot, about 2 minutes.
Pour in the oil and swirl it around. It should shimmer immediately.
Add the garlic and chillies. Stir for 15 seconds until fragrant.
Add the chicken pieces, breaking them up with your spatula. Let them sit for 30 seconds without moving, you want them to catch colour.
Stir and cook for 2 minutes until the chicken is mostly cooked through and the edges are starting to char.
Add the curry paste, fish sauce and palm sugar. Toss everything together for another 2 minutes. You're looking for the paste to caramelise into the chicken and the whole thing to smell fierce.
Taste and adjust the salt and heat if you need to. The chicken should be cooked through (75°C inside), with charred, sticky edges.
Serve straight onto a plate with jasmine rice and fresh Thai basil if you have it.

notes: This works best on a gas burner where you can crank the heat. The wok needs to be hot enough that the curry paste caramelises rather than steams.
If you don't have Thai basil, regular basil works, or just serve it plain with rice.
Scale up easily: use 400g chicken for two plates, but keep cooking time about the same, high heat, 8–10 minutes total.
Food safety: Cook chicken until the thickest part reaches 75°C and the juices run clear, with no pink meat near the bone.

title: Kaeng Ho
summary: Layered clay pot curry with mushrooms, noodles and vegetables in creamy coconut sauce.

items.raw: 2 tbsp fish sauce (or soy sauce for fully vegan)
items.note: or soy sauce for fully vegan

items.raw: 200 g fresh egg noodles (or rice noodles)
300 g mixed mushrooms (oyster, shiitake, button), thickly sliced
2 cups bok choy (or spinach), roughly chopped

steps.text: Heat the oil in a clay pot (or heavy-bottomed pot) over medium heat. Add the curry paste and sliced garlic, stirring gently until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk, vegetable stock, fish sauce and palm sugar. Stir well and let it come to a gentle simmer until bubbling lightly and the palm sugar has melted.
Layer the noodles evenly over the curry sauce. Don't stir, just press them down gently so they're submerged.
Layer the potato slices over the noodles, then add the mushrooms, capsicum and bok choy in separate layers on top. Pour any remaining sauce over everything.
Cover the pot and simmer gently for 20 to 25 minutes, until the potatoes are tender and the noodles have absorbed the sauce. Peek at it after 15 minutes, it should smell deeply fragrant.
Gently stir everything together just before serving. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Serve hot, topped with fresh Thai basil and coriander if you have them.

notes: For a fully vegan dish, use soy sauce instead of fish sauce and check that your curry paste and coconut milk are vegan-certified.
You can prep all the vegetables ahead of time. Layer them in the pot just before cooking.
Leftovers keep well for 2 days in the fridge. Reheat gently on the stove with a splash of water.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Stewed Saltfish
summary: Salt cod stewed with onions, peppers and tomatoes, served with provisions and roti.

items.raw: 500 g saltfish, soaked overnight and bones removed
Salt and black pepper, to taste
4 green fig (plantain), peeled and cut into chunks
400 g dasheen (taro), peeled and cut into chunks

steps.text: Soak the saltfish overnight in plenty of cold water, changing the water twice. Drain, rinse and pick through to remove any bones. Break into large flakes.
Boil the green fig and dasheen separately in salted water until tender, about 20 minutes. Drain and keep warm.
Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Fry the onion and red capsicum, stirring, until soft and golden, about 8 minutes.
Add the garlic and green chilli, cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and cook, stirring, for 3 minutes until they start to break down.

Add the saltfish flakes and 300 ml water. Bring to a simmer and cook gently for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the saltfish is very soft and the sauce has thickened. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve the saltfish stew hot with the boiled green fig and dasheen, and warm roti on the side.

notes: Saltfish needs to be soaked overnight to remove excess salt. If you're short on time, use 400 g fresh white fish fillet instead, add it to the stew in the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Green fig is unripe plantain, boiled until tender. Look for it in Caribbean or Latin markets, or swap for potato or sweet potato.
The stew tastes better the next day. Keep it in the fridge for up to 3 days and reheat gently on the stove.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Crêpes aux pommes et cidre
summary: Buckwheat crêpes with spiced apple compote and cider cream.

items.raw: 15 ml melted butter, plus extra for cooking

steps.text: Make the crêpe batter. Whisk together the buckwheat flour, plain flour and salt in a large bowl. In another bowl, whisk the eggs and milk. Pour into the dry ingredients and whisk until smooth. Stir in the melted butter. Let the batter rest for 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, make the apple compote. Melt the butter in a heavy-bottomed saucepan over medium heat. Add the apple slices, sugar, cinnamon stick and cloves. Cover and cook, stirring occasionally, until the apples break down into a soft compote, about 15 minutes. Stir in the cider and cook uncovered for 2 more minutes. Remove the cinnamon stick and cloves.
For the cider cream, whip the thickened cream with the cider and caster sugar until soft peaks form. Set aside.

Heat a 25 cm non-stick crêpe pan or frying pan over medium-high heat. Lightly butter it. Pour in 60 ml of batter and tilt the pan to spread it into a thin, even circle. Cook until the underside is lightly golden, about 1 minute. Flip and cook the other side for 30 seconds. Transfer to a plate. Repeat with the remaining batter, buttering the pan lightly between crêpes.
Warm the compote gently if it has cooled. Spoon compote onto each crêpe, fold into quarters, and serve with a dollop of cider cream.

notes: The batter can be made several hours ahead and chilled.
The apple compote keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days and can be gently reheated.

Food safety: Raw and lightly cooked foods aren't recommended for pregnant women, young children, older people or anyone with a weakened immune system. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Canh Chua Chay
summary: Vietnamese sour broth with mushrooms and vegetables, aromatic and herbaceous.

items.raw: 200 g firm tofu, pressed and cut into cubes
250 g mixed mushrooms (shiitake and button), halved
100 g pumpkin (or kabocha), cut into thin slices

steps.text: Bring the vegetable stock to a gentle simmer in a large pot. Stir in the tamarind paste and palm sugar until dissolved, about 2 minutes. Taste and adjust the balance of sour and sweet, it should brighten your tongue but not overwhelm it.
Add the pumpkin slices and simmer for 5 minutes until they are just tender but still hold their shape.
Add the mushrooms and tofu cubes. Simmer gently for 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the mushrooms are soft and the tofu has absorbed some of the broth's flavour.
Add the tomato wedges and season with salt and black pepper. Simmer for 2 more minutes until the tomatoes are softened, the tomatoes should be warm but still hold their shape.
Remove from heat and stir through most of the fresh dill and coriander, reserving some for serving. Taste once more and adjust the seasoning if needed.
Ladle into bowls and garnish with the remaining herbs and red chilli slices if using. Serve at once, while the broth is still steaming.

notes: The balance of tamarind to palm sugar is personal. Start with equal parts and adjust to taste, some prefer it more sour, others more rounded.
Make the vegetable stock a day ahead if you can; let it chill overnight so any sediment sinks to the bottom, and the broth will be clearer.

title: Tepsi Galay
summary: Baghdad baked vegetables and lamb casserole with potatoes and okra

items.raw: 750 g lamb shoulder, cut into 3 cm cubes
600 g potatoes, peeled and cut into 3 cm cubes
items.prep: peeled and cut into 3 cm cubes

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large heavy-based ovenproof dish (about 30 cm × 20 cm) over medium-high heat. Brown the lamb in two batches, about 6 minutes each, until golden on all sides. Set aside.
Add the onion to the same dish and cook, stirring, until soft and lightly golden, about 5 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, then add the crushed tomatoes, cumin, black pepper, cayenne and salt. Bring to a simmer, stirring.
Return the lamb to the dish and add the water. Stir well. Arrange the potato cubes on top of the lamb and sauce (don't stir them in). Cover tightly with foil.

Bake at 180°C for 45 minutes. Remove the foil, scatter the okra over the top without stirring, and bake uncovered for another 15 minutes, until the lamb is very tender and the okra is just cooked through. Serve straight from the dish.

notes: Tepsi galay is best served warm from the dish. If you don't have an ovenproof dish, brown the meat in a frying pan and transfer to a large baking dish before adding the other ingredients.
The okra really does need to go in at the end, if you add it earlier it will break down and make the sauce slimy. Don't stir once the okra is in.
Food safety: Cook whole cuts of beef, lamb and veal to at least 63°C in the thickest part, then rest for 3 minutes; cook rolled or stuffed cuts to 75°C.

title: Sambal Matah
summary: Raw Balinese shallot and chilli relish, essential with rice and grilled fish.

steps.text: Combine the sliced shallots, chopped bird's eye chillies and sliced garlic in a mortar or bowl.

Using a pestle or the back of a spoon, gently pound to release the oils and aromas, about 1 to 2 minutes, until the ingredients are bruised, glistening and beginning to break down. You want them bruised, not completely crushed.
Stir in the lime juice, neutral oil and salt. Taste and adjust salt or lime to your liking, it should be sharp, hot and bright.
Leave to sit for a few minutes before serving so the flavours marry, then stir through fresh coriander if you like. Serve at room temperature with rice, grilled fish or sate.

notes: Make it fresh each time, sambal matah is best eaten within an hour of pounding, while the shallots still have bite.
Adjust the heat by using fewer chillies, or add a splash more lime juice if you prefer it sharper than hot.

title: Labaneh with Za'atar
summary: Strained yoghurt cheese rolled in za'atar and olive oil, served with warm bread.

steps.text: Line a fine sieve with cheesecloth or a clean tea towel. Pour the yoghurt into it, add the salt, and stir gently to combine. Tie the corners of the cloth together and hang it over a bowl (or suspend it in the fridge) to drain overnight, or for at least 12 hours, until the whey has stopped dripping. You want all the whey to drip away; the longer it strains, the thicker and more cheese-like the labaneh becomes.

Once drained, the labaneh will be thick and creamy. Scrape it into a bowl and stir it smooth. You can serve it at this point, or for a richer texture and more authentic presentation, roll it into balls about the size of walnuts. Chill them for at least 1 hour so they hold their shape.

Just before serving, arrange the balls on a plate or in a shallow dish. Sprinkle the za'atar evenly over the top, then drizzle generously with olive oil. The za'atar will stick to the oil and stay bright. Serve immediately with warm flatbread or pita for dipping, the bread is how you eat labaneh, never with a spoon alone.

notes: Labaneh keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 1 week before rolling. Once rolled and dressed, serve the same day for the best texture and flavour.

title: Mukimo
summary: Creamy mashed potatoes, peas and maize with buttery onions.

items.raw: 800 g potato, peeled and cut into chunks
Salt and black pepper, to taste

steps.text: Put the potato chunks in a large pot of salted boiling water and cook for 15 minutes until very tender.
Add the corn and peas to the pot and cook for 3 more minutes, until heated through.
While the vegetables cook, melt the butter in a separate pan over medium heat. Add the onions and cook, stirring, until soft and golden, about 5 minutes.
Drain the potato, corn and peas well, reserving 60 ml of the cooking water.
Return the drained vegetables to the pot and mash together, adding the cooked onions and butter. Add enough of the reserved cooking water to make a creamy consistency (you might not need it all).
Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve hot.

notes: Mukimo is best eaten fresh and hot. Leftovers can be reheated gently in a pan with a splash of water or milk.
You can use fresh potatoes, corn and peas if they're in season, but frozen work just as well.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Kyoto-Style Tofu Pockets
summary: Inari sushi: sweetened tofu pouches filled with seasoned rice and market vegetables.

items.raw: 300 g sushi rice (or short-grain white rice)

steps.text: Rinse the sushi rice under cold water until the water runs almost clear. Cook in 360 ml water in a rice cooker or pot, about 15 minutes for a cooker or 20 minutes on the stove with the lid on.

While the rice cooks, bring the dashi, soy sauce, caster sugar, mirin and sake to a gentle simmer. Carefully open each tofu pouch along the folded edge with your fingernail or a small knife, then slide them into the liquid. Poach for 8 to 10 minutes until they absorb the broth and soften, turning halfway. Set aside to cool until you can handle them, about 5 minutes.

As the rice finishes, whisk the rice vinegar, salt and caster sugar together. Turn the hot rice into a shallow bowl and gently fold in the vinegar mixture, using a wooden spatula to cool it as you fold. This takes about 5 minutes. Let it rest while you prepare the filling.
Dice the carrot, daikon and mushroom very finely, about the size of a sesame seed. If you like, blanch them in boiling water for 1 minute, then drain well. This keeps them crisp.
Fold the diced vegetables, pickled ginger if using, sesame seeds, salt and white pepper gently through the cooled rice.

Gently squeeze the tofu pockets to remove any excess broth. Hold one open and, using a small spoon, carefully fill each pocket with a modest amount of rice mixture, it should be gentle and not packed tight. The pocket should be full enough to hold its shape but not bursting.
Arrange the filled pockets, seam-side up, on a plate. Serve at room temperature.

notes: Make ahead: prepare the tofu pouches up to a day in advance. Store them in their braising liquid in the fridge, and fill them an hour before serving so the rice softens gently into the pockets.
The rice must be warm when you season it with vinegar, but cool enough to handle before filling the pockets.
Use what the market brings: spring onion greens, tiny diced turnip or lotus root work just as well as daikon.

title: Cassava Fries with Sea Salt
summary: Crispy fried cassava sticks, golden and salty, a beloved Fijian after-school snack.

items.raw: 800 g cassava, peeled and cut into thin fries (about 5 mm thick)
items.prep: peeled and cut into thin fries

steps.text: Cut the peeled cassava into thin sticks, about 5 mm thick and 8 cm long. Place them in a bowl of cold water and let them soak for 10 minutes to remove excess starch.
Drain the cassava fries well and pat them dry thoroughly with a clean kitchen towel.
Heat about 2 litres of neutral oil in a large, deep pan or wok to 170°C. To test, drop a small piece of cassava in; it should sizzle immediately and rise to the surface after a few seconds.
Working in batches to avoid crowding, carefully lower the cassava fries into the hot oil. Fry for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they are golden and crispy.
Remove the cassava fries with a slotted spoon and drain them on paper towels. Sprinkle immediately with sea salt while they are still hot.
Serve hot and crispy with a cup of tea or a cool drink.

notes: Cassava fries are best eaten fresh and hot. If making ahead, reheat them in a 180°C oven for 5 minutes to restore crispness.
Don't skip soaking the cassava, it removes starch and makes the fries crispier.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Slow Cooker Lamb Neck with Tomato
summary: Tender lamb neck braised low and slow with tomato and aromatics until it falls apart.

items.raw: 1.2 kg lamb neck, cut into chunks
Salt and black pepper, to taste

steps.text: Heat a frying pan over high heat. Working in batches, brown the lamb neck on all sides, about 2 minutes per batch. Transfer to a slow cooker.
Add the onions, garlic, crushed tomatoes, beef stock, tomato paste, bay leaves and oregano to the slow cooker. Stir to combine. Season with salt and pepper.
Cover and cook on low for 8 hours, or until the lamb is tender and falling apart. If you're in a hurry, cook on high for 5 hours.
Skim any fat from the surface if needed. Taste and adjust the seasoning.

notes: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the sauce, or over rice or mash.
Makes great leftovers. Cool and store in the fridge for up to 3 days.
Works just as well in a camp oven at low heat, about 3 hours if the coals are right.

title: Slow-Cooked Beef Cheeks with Native Pepper
summary: Tender beef cheeks braised low and slow with root vegetables and Tasmanian native pepper.

items.raw: Salt and black pepper, to taste
1 tsp native pepper (Tasmanian pepper berry), ground, plus extra to serve

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 160°C. Pat the beef cheeks dry with paper towel, then season with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or casserole dish over medium-high heat. Brown the beef cheeks in batches, 3 to 4 minutes each side, until golden. Transfer to a plate.
Add the onions to the pot and cook until just coloured, about 4 minutes. Add the carrots and parsnips and stir for 2 minutes.

Return the beef cheeks to the pot. Pour in the tinned tomatoes and beef stock, and add the bay leaves and thyme. The liquid should mostly cover the beef. Bring to a simmer until gentle bubbles break the surface.
Cover and transfer to the oven. Cook for 3 hours, turning the beef cheeks halfway through, until they are very tender and the meat shreds easily with a fork.

Remove from the oven. Stir through the ground native pepper. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Divide among bowls, spoon the gravy and vegetables over, and finish with a light grind of native pepper.
Serve with mashed potato or crusty bread.

notes: Make this a day ahead if you like, the flavour deepens overnight. Reheat gently on the stove or in a 160°C oven until warmed through.
Native pepper is available from good delis and spice shops, but if you can't find it, use a grind of black pepper instead.
Food safety: Slow-cooked meat is safe once it is tender and the centre has reached at least 75°C. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Flaki
summary: Beef tripe stew with paprika, marjoram and a tangy broth, cooked low and slow.

items.raw: 800 g beef tripe, cleaned and cut into strips
Salt and black pepper, to taste

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large, heavy pot over medium heat. Working in batches, brown the tripe on both sides, about 8 minutes total. Set aside.
In the same pot, cook the onions, stirring often, until soft and golden, about 8 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the paprika and tomato paste, cooking gently for 2 minutes. Pour in the stock, scraping up any brown bits from the bottom of the pot.

Return the tripe to the pot with the bay leaves and marjoram. Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 2.5 to 3 hours, stirring occasionally. The tripe should be very tender, almost silky.
Stir in the vinegar. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Serve hot, scattered with fresh parsley if you like.

notes: Flaki tastes even better the next day. Make it ahead and reheat gently before serving.
Tripe should be cleaned already when you buy it, but if you have any doubt, rinse it well under cold water and rub gently with salt.
Some Kraków cooks add a little strong mustard or horseradish at the end. It's optional.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Cullen Skink
summary: Smoked haddock, potato and onion soup with cream, a North-East classic.

items.raw: 500 g floury potatoes, peeled and cut into 1 cm cubes
items.prep: peeled and cut into 1 cm cubes

items.raw: Salt and black pepper, to taste

steps.text: Put the smoked haddock in a large saucepan with the milk and bay leaves. Bring gently to a simmer and cook for 8 minutes until the fish is just cooked through. Lift the fish out onto a plate, discard the skin and any bones, and break the flesh into flakes. Keep the milk in the pan.
In a separate pan, melt the butter and cook the chopped onion gently, stirring occasionally, until soft and pale, about 5 minutes.
Add the diced potatoes to the buttered onion and stir to coat. Pour in the reserved milk with the bay leaves, bring to a simmer and cook for about 12 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Return the flaked haddock to the pan, add the cream and stir gently. Heat through for 2–3 minutes without boiling.
Season with salt and pepper to taste, go easy on the salt as the smoked fish is already quite salty. Serve hot, scattered with fresh parsley if you like.

notes: This keeps well in the fridge for 2 days and reheats gently, add a splash of milk if it's thickened too much.
Traditionally you'd use the poaching liquid, as this recipe does.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Bacalao al Pil-Pil
summary: Salt cod emulsified with garlic and olive oil into a creamy, silky sauce.

items.raw: 600 g salt cod loin (skinless and boneless), soaked overnight
1 small red chilli, deseeded and chopped (optional)

steps.text: Drain and pat the salt cod dry. Cut into 4 thick pieces, about 150 g each.

Heat 100 ml olive oil in a wide, shallow earthenware dish (cazuela) or heavy-based pan over very low heat. Add the sliced garlic and red chilli (if using). Cook gently, stirring, until the garlic is fragrant and just beginning to soften, about 2 minutes. Don't let it brown.

Lay the salt cod pieces skin-side up in the warm oil. The oil should just barely cover them, add a little more if needed. Keep the heat very low and poach gently, uncovered, for 5–7 minutes. The cod will begin to flake at the edges and turn opaque.

Now the critical part: remove the pan from the heat and let it cool for 1 minute. Using a wooden spoon or your wrist in a smooth, circular motion, begin tilting and rotating the pan while gently stirring the cod in the oil. The gelatine from the fish will start to emulsify the oil into a creamy sauce.

Return the pan to very low heat and continue this tilting and stirring motion. Gradually add the remaining 100 ml olive oil in a thin stream while rotating and tilting, as if you were making a sauce. The emulsion builds slowly, this is the pil-pil. Keep going for 8–10 minutes until the sauce is pale, silky and creamy.
Taste and season with salt if needed. Serve in the pan, spooning the creamy pil-pil sauce over the cod. Scatter with fresh parsley if you like.

notes: The salt cod needs overnight soaking in plenty of cold water (change it a couple of times if you remember). If you're short on time, use 2 changes of water and soak for at least 8 hours.
The whole secret is low heat and patience. Rush it or turn the heat up and the emulsion breaks. If it does, start the oil again in a fresh pan and gently fold in the broken sauce.
An earthenware cazuela looks better and conducts heat more evenly, but a heavy stainless steel or cast-iron pan works just as well.

title: Kåldolmere
summary: Cabbage rolls stuffed with pork and rice in a warm tomato broth.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Carefully peel away the outer leaves of the cabbage and place them in the boiling water. Blanch for 3–4 minutes until soft, then lift out with tongs and set aside on a clean tea towel to cool. Repeat until you have 8–10 good leaves (reserve the rest of the cabbage for another use).

While the leaves cool, cook the rice in a small pot of salted water for 12 minutes, then drain and set aside. In a large bowl, mix the pork mince, cooked rice, chopped onion, egg, salt and pepper until just combined.

Lay a cabbage leaf flat on a board. Trim the thick centre stem if it's very bulky. Place about 60 ml of the pork filling in the middle of each leaf, fold the sides in, then roll tightly from bottom to top. Place seam-side down in a baking dish.
Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute. Add the crushed tomatoes, beef stock and bay leaves, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Pour the warm tomato broth over and around the cabbage rolls. Cover the dish with foil and bake at 180°C for 45 minutes, or until the rolls are heated through and tender.
Serve the rolls warm in shallow bowls with the broth spooned over them. A dollop of sour cream on the side is traditional.

notes: Sour cream or Greek yoghurt to serve is traditional.
The rolls can be assembled up to a day ahead, wrapped in plastic, and refrigerated. Bring to room temperature before adding the broth and baking.
Leftovers keep well for 3 days in the fridge and reheat gently in a low oven.
Cook mince and sausages until they reach 75°C in the centre, with no pink left.
Food safety: Raw and lightly cooked foods aren't recommended for pregnant women, young children, older people or anyone with a weakened immune system.

title: Pasta e Lenticchie
summary: Rustic southern Italian pasta and lentil stew, thick and warming comfort food.

items.raw: Salt and black pepper, to taste

steps.text: Heat the olive oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium heat. Add the onion, garlic, carrot and celery, and cook, stirring often, until the vegetables are soft and golden, about 8 minutes.

Add the brown lentils and stir through the vegetables for 1 minute, then pour in the crushed tomatoes and vegetable stock. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer gently until the lentils are almost tender, about 20 minutes.

Add the pasta and stir well. Simmer, stirring occasionally, until the pasta is cooked through and the broth has thickened slightly, about 8 minutes. If it's getting too thick, add a splash of hot water.
Taste and season with salt and black pepper. Divide among bowls and serve with fresh parsley and grated parmesan if you like.

notes: Make ahead: This actually tastes better the next day. Cool quickly, store in the fridge for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 2 months. Add a splash of water when you reheat.
Brown lentils hold their shape better than red; French lentils work too. Skip the fancy stuff, everyday brown lentils from the market are perfect.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Ärtsoppa med fläsk
summary: Traditional Swedish split pea soup with pork, Thursday's best-loved family dinner.

items.raw: 2 tsp salt, plus more to taste

steps.text: Rinse the split peas in cold water and drain. Place the pork, water, and bay leaf in a large pot and bring to a boil until a grey foam rises to the surface. Skim off any foam from the surface.
Add the split peas, onions, carrots, and celery. Stir in the peppercorns and salt.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer, partially covered, for about 2 hours, stirring occasionally. The peas should break down into the broth and the pork should be very tender.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt as needed. Serve hot in bowls with rye bread and Swedish mustard on the side.

notes: Best made the day before and reheated, the flavours deepen overnight.
Serve with Swedish mustard, rye bread, and a shot of aquavit if you're so inclined.
Food safety: Cook fresh pork to at least 70°C in the thickest part. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Rotkohl mit Äpfeln
summary: Red cabbage braised with apples and vinegar, bright and substantial enough to anchor a meal

items.raw: 1 medium red cabbage, about 800 g, quartered, cored and sliced into 1 cm ribbons
items.prep: about 800 g, quartered, cored and sliced into 1 cm ribbons

items.raw: 2 medium apples, peeled, cored and cut into thin wedges
items.prep: peeled, cored and cut into thin wedges

items.raw: Salt and black pepper, to taste

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large heavy-based pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the onion and cook, stirring, until softened and just starting to colour, about 4 minutes.
Add the sliced red cabbage and stir through to coat in the oil. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 minutes. The cabbage will reduce in volume.
Pour in the vinegar and water, add the bay leaves and caraway seeds, and stir through. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to medium-low. Cover and braise for 15 minutes, stirring once or twice.

Add the apples and golden syrup, stir gently, and return the lid. Cook for another 10–15 minutes until the cabbage is tender and the apples have softened into the mix. The liquid should have reduced by half.
Season to taste with salt and pepper. Serve warm, as a side to roasted meat or alongside a good piece of fish.

notes: Keep this in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days, it reheats gently and actually improves as the flavours settle. Make it in bulk and freeze portions.
If you prefer less sweetness, use just 1 tbsp golden syrup, or substitute a splash of apple juice instead.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Halwa
summary: Sweet semolina halwa with butter, cardamom, and nuts, a Somali dessert for sharing.

steps.text: Heat the ghee in a large, heavy-based saucepan over medium heat. Add the semolina and stir constantly, breaking up any lumps. Toast for 8–10 minutes, stirring often, until the semolina is golden and smells nutty.
Add the crushed cardamom pods and salt, stirring for 30 seconds to release the flavour.
Carefully pour in the water, it will bubble, and stir constantly to combine. The mixture will be thick and pasty.
Add the caster sugar and stir until it dissolves completely into the semolina mixture, about 2 minutes.
Remove from the heat and fold through most of the almonds and raisins, reserving some for the top.
Spoon the halwa into a serving dish and smooth the surface. Scatter the remaining almonds and raisins over the top.
Let it cool to warm, then serve. It sets as it cools but stays soft inside.

notes: Halwa keeps in an airtight container for 3–4 days. You can reheat it gently in a pan with a splash of water if it dries out.
The toasting of the semolina is important, it takes time but the flavour change is worth it. Don't rush it.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Filé Gumbo
summary: Dark roux gumbo with chicken, sausage and the holy trinity, thickened with filé powder.

items.raw: 400 g chicken thigh fillet, cut into 2 cm pieces
Salt and black pepper, to taste

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat. Add the flour slowly, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon. Keep stirring, don't walk away, until the roux is deep chocolate brown, about 30 to 40 minutes. It'll go from light tan to darker shades; when it smells nutty and toasted, you're close.
Add the onion, celery and capsicum to the roux. Stir well and cook, stirring often, until the vegetables are soft and golden, about 8 minutes.
Add the chicken and sausage. Stir to coat with roux, and cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in the stock slowly, stirring constantly until smooth to break up any lumps. Add the bay leaf, thyme and cayenne. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low.
Simmer gently, uncovered, for about 40 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the flavours have melded. Skim any fat from the surface if you like.
Taste and season with salt and pepper. Remove from heat and stir in the filé powder until smooth. Don't boil after adding filé, or it gets stringy.
Serve in bowls over white rice, scattered with spring onion if you like.

notes: Make this ahead: gumbo tastes even better the next day. Reheat gently on the stove, and stir in the filé powder just before serving.
Food safety: Cook chicken and other poultry until the juices run clear and the thickest part reaches 75°C.

title: Fasolada
summary: White bean stew with tomatoes, onion and olive oil, soul of Greek Lenten cooking.

items.raw: 400 g tin white beans, drained and rinsed
Salt and black pepper, to taste

steps.text: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook gently, stirring often, until softened and pale gold, about 8 minutes.
Add the garlic and tomato paste, stir well and cook for another minute until fragrant.
Add the drained beans, crushed tomatoes, oregano and 250 ml water. Stir to combine.

Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce heat to low. Simmer uncovered for about 1 hour, stirring occasionally. The stew should be rich and thick, with the beans beginning to break down slightly and thicken the broth. Add more water if it looks too dry.
Taste and adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper. The fasolada should be flavourful and creamy from the beans and oil, not watery.
Serve warm, with crusty bread on the side.

notes: Fasolada is even better the next day. Store in the fridge for up to three days and reheat gently, adding a splash of water if needed.
If starting with dried beans: soak 250 g overnight, then boil for about 45 minutes until tender before starting the recipe. Add the cooked beans at step 3.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Sancocho de Pollo
summary: Rustic one-pot Colombian chicken stew with yuca, plantain and potatoes.

items.raw: 400 g yuca (cassava), cut into large chunks
400 g plantain, peeled and cut into thick slices
items.prep: peeled and cut into thick slices

items.raw: 3 medium waxy potatoes, peeled and quartered
Salt and black pepper, to taste

steps.text: Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Season the chicken with salt and pepper, then brown it in batches, about 8 minutes total. Set aside.
In the same pot, add the onion and garlic, cook until softened and fragrant, about 3 minutes.
Pour in the chicken stock and bring to a boil, then add the browned chicken back in. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the yuca and potatoes, return to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the plantain slices and simmer for a further 15 minutes, until the yuca is tender and the chicken is cooked through (75°C inside).
Taste and season with salt and pepper. Stir through the fresh coriander and serve hot, ladled into bowls with plenty of broth.

notes: Tastes even better the next day. Reheat gently on the stove.
Traditional Colombian comfort food: serve with white rice and avocado on the side.
Food safety: Cook chicken until the thickest part reaches 75°C and the juices run clear, with no pink meat near the bone.

title: Ful with Egg and Tomato
summary: Creamy fava bean puree topped with fried egg, tomato and onion.

items.raw: Salt and black pepper, to taste

steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a small saucepan over medium heat. Add the drained fava beans and mash with a fork or potato masher until creamy but still a little textured, about 5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Transfer to a shallow bowl or plate.

Meanwhile, in another small pan, heat the remaining 1 tbsp oil over medium heat. Add the diced onion and cook, stirring, until soft and lightly golden, about 5 minutes. Add the diced tomato and cook for another 2 minutes. Set aside.
In a frying pan, heat a little more oil over medium heat. Crack both eggs into the pan and fry until the whites are set but the yolks are still runny, about 3–4 minutes.
Top the warm ful with the onion and tomato mixture, then place the fried eggs on top. Serve with flatbread on the side.

notes: Make a bigger batch of ful and store it in the fridge for 3 days; reheat gently with a splash of water.
Use tinned or cooked dried fava beans, the tinned kind saves time and money if you're cooking on a weeknight.

Food safety: Raw and lightly cooked foods aren't recommended for pregnant women, young children, older people or anyone with a weakened immune system. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Songseun Jjim
summary: Steamed pine nuts with vegetables, earthy and delicate temple food.

items.raw: 80 g waxy potato, cut into matchsticks
2 spring onions, finely sliced (white and green parts separated)

steps.text: Soak the pine nuts in warm water for 15 minutes, then drain well.

In a bowl, combine the drained pine nuts, shiitake, carrot, potato, and spring onion whites. Stir in the minced ginger, sesame oil, soy sauce, rice vinegar and a pinch of salt until everything is evenly coated.
Prepare a steamer by bringing water to a simmer in a pot until steam is rising steadily. Transfer the pine nut mixture to a heatproof bowl or steaming plate that fits in your steamer.
Steam over simmering water for 20 to 25 minutes, until the potato is tender and the pine nuts have softened but still hold their shape.
Remove from the steamer and let cool to room temperature. Scatter the spring onion greens and toasted sesame seeds over the top.
Serve at room temperature in small bowls.

notes: Songseun jjim is traditionally served at room temperature, which is when the flavours are clearest.
You can prepare this a few hours ahead and let it sit; the flavours develop as it cools.
If you can't find pine nuts, blanched almonds work, though the flavour will be less delicate.

title: Tofu Katsu
summary: Crispy panko-crusted tofu cutlet with tonkatsu sauce, a lighter take on the classic.

items.raw: 400 g extra-firm tofu, pressed and cut into 2 cutlets
Salt and black pepper, to taste

steps.text: Press the tofu between kitchen towels or in a tofu press for at least 15 minutes to remove excess moisture.
Slice the pressed tofu block in half lengthways, then slice each half in half again to create two thick, flat cutlets. Pat dry with paper towels.
Set up three shallow bowls: one with plain flour, one with beaten egg, and one with panko breadcrumbs.
Season the tofu cutlets lightly with salt and pepper on both sides.
Coat each cutlet in flour, shaking off excess, then dip in egg, then press firmly into panko until completely coated on both sides.
Heat about 1 cm of neutral oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat until shimmering.

Once the oil is hot, carefully place the tofu cutlets in the pan and fry for 3–4 minutes per side, until the panko is golden brown and crispy. Don't move them around too much, let them sit so they get a good crust.
Transfer to a plate lined with paper towels to drain any excess oil.
Drizzle tonkatsu sauce generously over the top of each cutlet and serve immediately with pickled cabbage and steamed white rice on the side.

notes: Make sure to press the tofu well, this is key to getting it crispy. Soft tofu won't work; stick with extra-firm.
You can prep the tofu cutlets and coat them hours ahead, then fry just before serving.
Food safety: Raw and lightly cooked foods aren't recommended for pregnant women, young children, older people or anyone with a weakened immune system.

title: Fattet Tammam
summary: Chickpea and herb salad layered with crispy pita chips and tahini dressing.

items.raw: 400 g tin chickpeas, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Preheat oven to 200°C. Tear pita into bite-sized pieces, toss with 1 tbsp olive oil and a pinch of salt, spread on a baking tray, and bake for 8–10 minutes until golden and crisp. Set aside.
Meanwhile, soak bulgur in 60 ml hot water for 10 minutes until tender. Drain if needed.
In a large bowl, combine parsley, mint, spring onion, tomato, cucumber, soaked bulgur, and chickpeas. Dress with 2 tbsp olive oil and lemon juice, season with salt.
In a small bowl, whisk tahini with garlic, water and a pinch of salt until smooth and pourable. Add more water if too thick.

To serve, spread half the chickpea salad on a platter, drizzle with half the tahini dressing, scatter half the pita chips, then layer the remaining salad, tahini, and chips. Garnish with paprika and serve immediately.

notes: Make the tahini dressing and baked pita chips up to 1 day ahead. Assemble just before serving so the chips stay crisp.
If you can't find fresh mint, use another 100 g parsley. The salad won't be quite as bright, but it'll still be delicious.

title: Bánh Cuốn Nóng
summary: Steamed rice paper rolls with minced pork and mushrooms, served hot with fish sauce dip.

items.raw: 200 g mixed mushrooms (shiitake and button), finely diced
2 spring onions, white and light green parts, finely sliced
items.prep: white and light green parts, finely sliced

steps.text: Make the fish sauce dip first: stir together fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, garlic, chilli and water until the sugar dissolves. Set aside.

For the filling, heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add garlic and spring onion whites, cook 30 seconds until fragrant. Add pork mince and break it up with a spatula, cooking until no pink remains, about 5 minutes. Add mushrooms and cook, stirring, until they release their moisture and the pan is nearly dry, about 5 minutes. Stir in fish sauce, sugar and black pepper to taste. Transfer to a bowl and set aside to cool slightly.
Make the rice batter: whisk rice flour, water, salt and oil until smooth with no lumps. Let it rest 5 minutes.

Set up your rolling station: place a non-stick crêpe pan or 20 cm non-stick frying pan over medium heat. Have a damp kitchen towel nearby, a plate lined with banana leaf or baking paper, and a small bowl of water for your fingers.

Once the pan is hot, lightly brush it with oil. Pour about 75 ml batter in the centre and immediately tilt and rotate the pan to spread it into a thin, even circle. Cook for about 1 minute until the bottom is set and dry but still pale (it should not brown).

Spoon about 2 tbsp filling along the lower third of the crêpe. Fold the bottom edge up and over the filling, then roll tightly away from you into a log, tucking in the sides as you go. Slide onto the prepared plate.
Repeat with remaining batter and filling. You should make 12 to 16 rolls.

Bring water to a simmer in a large pot or steamer. Arrange the rolls seam-side down on a steamer tray lined with banana leaf or baking paper (steam will cook them gently). Cover and steam for 5 minutes until heated through and slightly firmer (they will still be tender).
Serve hot, sprinkled with coriander, spring onion greens and fresh chilli from the dip, with lettuce leaves and the fish sauce dip on the side for dipping.

notes: Make the rolls up to 3 hours ahead and keep them covered with a damp cloth at room temperature. Steam just before serving.
If you don't have a non-stick crêpe pan, use a small non-stick frying pan and work quickly, the batter sets fast.

Bánh cuốn freezes well before steaming: place rolls on a tray lined with baking paper, freeze until firm, then pack in an airtight container for up to 1 month. Steam straight from frozen, adding 2 to 3 minutes to the cooking time.
Food safety: Cook mince and sausages until no pink remains and the centre reaches 75°C.

title: Escabeche
summary: Sweet and sour fried fish with pickled vegetables, vinegar-forward and meant for sharing.

items.raw: 800 g firm white fish fillets (barramundi, flathead or snapper), skin on
Salt and black pepper, to taste
1 medium red capsicum, cut into strips

steps.text: Pat the fish dry with paper towel. Season both sides with salt and pepper. Dust lightly with flour, shaking off excess.

Heat oil in a large frying pan over high heat until just smoking. Working in batches if needed, fry the fish skin-side down for 4 minutes until the skin is crispy and golden. Flip and cook for 3 minutes more until just cooked through. Transfer to a shallow dish.
In the same pan, reduce heat to medium. Add the sliced onions and cook, stirring, until soft and golden, about 8 minutes. Add the garlic and ginger, cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the carrot and red capsicum. Cook, stirring, for 3 minutes until just starting to soften.
Pour in the cane vinegar, water, brown sugar, salt and bay leaves. Stir to combine and bring to a gentle simmer. Simmer for 2 minutes, then remove from heat.
Pour the hot vinegar mixture and vegetables over the fish. Let it cool to room temperature, then cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or overnight. The flavours develop as it sits.
To serve, bring to room temperature or serve cold. Spoon the fish onto a plate with the vegetables and vinegar sauce. Garnish with fresh coriander if you like.

notes: Escabeche is even better the day after you make it, the fish stays moist and the flavours marry beautifully. Cover and keep in the fridge for up to 3 days.
If you can't find barramundi or flathead, any firm white fish works well. Avoid delicate fish like basa.
This is a dish built for sharing. Take it out of the fridge 20 minutes before serving to let the oil loosen up a bit.
Food safety: Cook fish until it is opaque and flakes easily (63°C in the thickest part), and prawns until pink and opaque all the way through.

title: Shakshuka with Feta and Harissa
summary: Eggs baked in a spiced tomato and capsicum sauce, scattered with feta and herbs.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large deep frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion and capsicum for 8 minutes, until soft and starting to colour.
Add the garlic, cumin, paprika and harissa and stir for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Pour in the tomatoes with a good pinch of salt and simmer for 10 minutes, until thick enough that a spoon leaves a trail.
Make six wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook for 5 to 7 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are still soft.
Scatter over the feta and parsley and serve straight from the pan with bread.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set. If serving anyone vulnerable, cook the yolks through as well.
Use 1 tsp harissa for a mild version.

title: Masala Omelette with Green Chilli and Coriander
summary: A fluffy Indian-style omelette packed with onion, tomato, green chilli and fresh coriander.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs in a bowl with the onion, tomato, chilli, coriander, turmeric and salt until well combined.
Heat half the ghee in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat. Pour in half the mixture and tilt the pan so it spreads in an even layer.
Cook for 2 minutes, until the edges are set, then flip and cook 1 minute more, until golden and no longer wet in the middle.
Repeat with the remaining ghee and mixture until it is all used, then serve with roti.

notes: Food safety: cook until the eggs are fully set with no runny egg in the middle.

title: Vegan Tofu Scramble with Spinach and Turmeric
summary: A savoury, golden tofu scramble with spinach, cherry tomatoes and nutritional yeast.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium heat. Crumble in the tofu with your hands and cook for 3 minutes, stirring now and then.
Add the turmeric, cumin, nutritional yeast and salt and stir for 2 minutes, until the tofu is evenly golden.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes, then fold through the spinach until just wilted.
Stir in the spring onions until the spinach is soft, then spoon onto toast.

notes: Black salt (kala namak) adds an eggy flavour if you have it. Add a pinch at the end.

title: Overnight Oats with Roasted Pears
summary: Creamy oats soaked overnight in milk and yoghurt, topped with spiced roasted pears.

items.raw: 4 pears, cored and cut into wedges

steps.text: Stir the oats, milk, yoghurt and maple syrup together in a bowl. Cover and chill overnight.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Put the pear wedges on a lined tray, drizzle with the honey, dust with cinnamon and roast for 15 minutes, until soft and syrupy.
Spoon the oats into two bowls, top with the warm pears and their juices and finish with the walnuts.

notes: Plus 8 hours soaking overnight.

title: Tamagoyaki Japanese Rolled Omelette
summary: A layered, lightly sweet rolled omelette, cut into neat slices and served with rice.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs gently with the dashi, mirin, sugar and soy sauce, trying not to add air.
Heat a small non-stick frying pan over medium-low heat and wipe it with oiled paper towel. Pour in a quarter of the mixture and tilt to coat.
When the egg is mostly set but still glossy on top, roll it up towards you with chopsticks. Push the roll to the far side and oil the pan again.
Pour in another quarter and lift the roll so egg runs underneath. Cook until set, then roll again. Repeat until all the mixture is used.
Rest the omelette for 2 minutes, slice into 2cm pieces and serve with rice and grated daikon.

notes: Food safety: the egg should be fully set through the middle.

title: Masala Dosa with Spiced Potato
summary: Crisp rice-and-lentil crepes folded around a turmeric and mustard seed potato filling.

items.raw: 4 potatoes, peeled and cut into 2cm chunks

steps.text: Soak the rice, dal and fenugreek in water for 6 hours. Drain, blend with 3/4 cup water and the salt to a pourable batter, then leave covered in a warm spot for 8 hours to ferment.
For the filling, boil the potatoes in salted water for 12 minutes, until tender, then drain.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds until they pop, then the curry leaves, onion and chilli. Cook for 6 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the turmeric and potatoes, mashing roughly. Add the lemon juice and a splash of water and cook for 3 minutes. Keep warm.
Heat a flat non-stick pan over medium-high heat and brush lightly with oil. Pour in a ladle of batter and spread it quickly in a thin circle.
Drizzle a little oil around the edge and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until deep golden and crisp. Spoon filling down the middle, fold over and serve with chutney. Repeat with the rest.

notes: Plus 14 hours soaking and fermenting. The batter keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Chickpea Ful with Tahini and Lemon
summary: Warm, garlicky Egyptian-style beans with lemon, cumin and a tahini drizzle.

steps.text: Warm the chickpeas in a saucepan with 1/2 cup water, the garlic and cumin over medium heat for 6 minutes, until hot through. Mash about a third with a fork for a creamy texture.
Stir in 2 tbsp lemon juice, 2 tbsp oil and a pinch of salt.
Whisk the tahini with the remaining lemon juice and 2 tbsp water until pourable.
Spoon the beans into bowls and top with tomato, onion, parsley, tahini, chilli flakes and the remaining oil. Serve with pita.

notes: Use gluten-free flatbread to keep it no-gluten.

title: Coconut Rice Pudding with Mango
summary: Creamy coconut rice pudding layered with fresh mango and toasted coconut.

steps.text: Simmer the rice, coconut milk, water, maple syrup and vanilla in a saucepan over low heat for 25 minutes, stirring often, until the rice is very soft and creamy. Cool, then chill for at least 2 hours.
Toss the mango with the lime juice.
Layer the pudding and mango into glasses and finish with the coconut.

notes: Dessert or breakfast. Plus 2 hours chilling. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Scrambled Eggs with Berbere-Style Spice and Tomato
summary: Soft eggs with onion, tomato and berbere spice, inspired by Ethiopian egg dishes.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion and chilli for 4 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the spices (a quick berbere-style blend) and tomato and cook 2 minutes, until the tomato breaks down.
Pour in the eggs with the salt. Stir gently for 2 to 3 minutes, until just set but still soft and creamy.
Top with coriander and serve with flatbread.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until set with no raw liquid left. Use fresh, uncracked eggs; for pregnant women, older people, young children and anyone with low immunity, cook the eggs until the yolks are firm.

title: Caribbean Saltfish Fritters
summary: Crisp, spicy fritters of flaked salted white fish with thyme, spring onion and scotch bonnet.

items.raw: 200g white fish fillet, salted and soaked overnight

steps.text: Simmer the soaked fish in fresh water for 10 minutes, until it flakes easily, then drain, cool and flake it, removing any bones.
Mix the flour and baking powder, then stir in the water to a thick batter. Fold in the cod, spring onion, thyme, chilli and garlic.
Heat 1cm of oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Drop in tablespoons of batter and fry for 2 to 3 minutes each side, until golden and cooked through.
Drain on paper towel and serve hot with lime.

notes: Food safety: fry until the fritters are golden and the fish is opaque and the centre is steaming hot.
Plus 12 hours salting and soaking the fish.

title: Swedish Pancakes with Lingonberry Jam
summary: Thin, buttery pancakes rolled around tart lingonberry jam, with a spoon of cream on top.

items.raw: 40g butter, melted, plus extra for the pan
items.prep: melted, plus extra for the pan

steps.text: Whisk the flour, salt and sugar in a bowl. Whisk in the eggs and half the milk until smooth, then the rest of the milk and the melted butter. Rest 10 minutes.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat and brush with butter. Pour in a thin layer of batter and swirl to coat.
Cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until the edges lift and the underside is pale gold, then flip and cook 30 seconds until just set. Stack on a warm plate and repeat.
Spread each pancake with jam, roll up and serve with the cream.

notes: Food safety: cook the pancakes until the batter is fully set with no wet patches.

title: Open Rye Sandwich with Smoked Salmon, Egg and Dill
summary: Buttered dark rye topped with smoked salmon, soft egg, cucumber and dill, in the Scandinavian style.

steps.text: Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook for 7 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are jammy. Cool in cold water, then peel and halve.
Spread the rye with cream cheese and layer on the cucumber and salmon.
Top with the egg halves, dill and capers and serve with lemon.

notes: Food safety: smoked salmon is ready to eat but keep it chilled until serving. Cook the eggs a further 2 minutes if serving anyone vulnerable.

title: Creamy Nordic Porridge with Grated Apple
summary: Creamy oats with grated apple, cinnamon and a knob of butter, in the Nordic style.

steps.text: Combine the oats, milk, water, apple, cinnamon and salt in a saucepan over medium heat.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Spoon into bowls and top with the butter and maple syrup.

notes: Make it no-dairy with oat milk and coconut oil in place of butter.

title: Pap with Tomato and Onion Relish
summary: Soft maize porridge served with a spiced tomato and onion relish, a South African staple.

steps.text: Bring the water and salt to the boil. Whisk in the polenta in a thin stream, then reduce to low and cook for 20 minutes, stirring often, until thick and pulling away from the pan.
Meanwhile heat the oil in a frying pan and cook the onion for 6 minutes, until soft.
Add the garlic, curry powder and chilli for 1 minute, then the tomatoes and sugar. Simmer 10 minutes, until jammy.
Spoon the pap into bowls and top with the relish.

notes: Pap is vegan and gluten-free. Serve it with grilled meat for a braai-style meal.

title: Baked Curried Mince with Egg Custard
summary: A baked, mildly curried beef mince dish with apricot jam, raisins and a savoury egg custard topping.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Soak the bread in half the milk.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan and cook the onion for 6 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, curry powder and turmeric for 1 minute.
Add the mince and cook for 8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned. Squeeze the bread and stir it in with the jam, raisins, lemon juice and 1 tsp salt.
Press into a baking dish. Whisk the eggs with the remaining milk and pour over, then lay the bay leaves on top.
Bake for 30 minutes, until the custard is set and golden. Serve with rice.

notes: Food safety: the mince must reach 75°C throughout. The custard should be firm, not wobbly.

title: Black-Eyed Bean Akara Fritters
summary: Crisp West African bean fritters spiced with chilli and onion, with a fresh tomato dip.

steps.text: Blitz the beans, onion, chilli, flour and salt in a food processor until a thick, slightly coarse batter forms.
Heat 1cm of oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat until a drop of batter sizzles at once.
Spoon in tablespoons of batter and fry for 2 to 3 minutes each side, until deep golden and crisp. Drain on paper towel.
Mix the dip ingredients with a pinch of salt and serve alongside.

notes: Vegan and dairy-free. The chilli is hot, so use less if you prefer.

title: Vegan Jollof Rice with Fried Plantain
summary: Smoky, spicy tomato rice in the West African style, served with golden fried plantain.

items.raw: 2 ripe plantains, sliced on an angle

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion and capsicum for 6 minutes, until soft. Add the tomato paste and fry 3 minutes, until it darkens.
Add the tinned tomatoes, curry powder, thyme and paprika and simmer 8 minutes, until thick and the oil separates at the edges.
Stir in the rice, stock, chilli and 1 tsp salt. Bring to a simmer, cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 20 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid is gone.
Shallow-fry the plantain in oil over medium heat for 2 minutes each side, until deep golden. Remove the chilli and fluff the rice.
Serve the jollof topped with plantain.

notes: Leave the chilli whole for flavour without much heat.

title: Groundnut Stew with Sweet Potato and Greens
summary: A rich, gently spiced peanut stew with sweet potato, chickpeas and spinach.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion for 6 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, ginger and spices for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Stir in the tomatoes, peanut butter and stock until the peanut butter dissolves.
Add the sweet potato and chickpeas, cover and simmer for 20 minutes, until the sweet potato is tender.
Stir in the spinach until wilted. Season to taste and serve with rice.

notes: Check the peanut butter label for added ingredients if you need it vegan or gluten-free.

title: Allspice and Scotch Bonnet Grilled Chicken Thighs
summary: Fiery, allspice-heavy chicken thighs grilled until charred and sticky, Jamaican style.

steps.text: Blitz everything except the chicken and rice into a rough paste. Rub it over the chicken, working it under the skin, then cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Place the chicken skin side up on a rack over a tray.
Roast for 30 to 35 minutes, until the skin is deeply browned and charred in places and the juices run clear.
Rest 5 minutes and serve with rice and peas.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C at the thickest part, with no pink near the bone.
Plus 4 hours marinating. Use gloves when handling scotch bonnet.

title: Callaloo-Style Greens with Coconut
summary: Silky greens simmered with coconut milk, okra, thyme and a little scotch bonnet.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and garlic for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the thyme, coconut milk, water, okra and chilli and simmer for 8 minutes, until the okra is tender.
Stir in the spinach and salt and cook for 5 minutes, until the greens collapse and the sauce is thick. Remove the chilli.

notes: Vegan and gluten-free.

title: Coconut Rice with Kidney Beans and Thyme
summary: Coconut rice cooked with kidney beans, thyme, allspice and spring onion.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a pot and cook the spring onion and garlic for 2 minutes, until fragrant. Add the thyme and allspice.
Stir in the rice, coconut milk, beans and their liquid, water, salt and the whole chilli.
Bring to the boil, cover and cook on the lowest heat for 20 minutes, until the rice is tender and all the liquid is absorbed.
Rest 5 minutes, remove the chilli and thyme stalks and fluff with a fork.

notes: Vegan and gluten-free. A classic side for jerk chicken.

title: Fijian Kokoda (Fish Cured in Lime and Coconut)
summary: Raw fish cured in lime juice, tossed with coconut cream, tomato, cucumber and chilli.

items.raw: 500g white fish fillet, very fresh, cut into 2cm cubes

steps.text: Toss the fish with the lime juice and salt in a glass bowl. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes, until the fish turns opaque and white throughout.
Drain off most of the lime juice. Stir in the onion, tomato, cucumber and chilli.
Fold through the coconut cream and coriander, check the seasoning and serve cold in bowls.

notes: Food safety: use very fresh fish from a trusted fishmonger, keep it cold, and eat it the same day. Lime cures the surface but does not make raw fish safe for pregnant women, older people or anyone immunocompromised.
Plus 30 minutes curing.

title: Coconut-Baked Sweet Potato with Spinach
summary: Tender sweet potato wedges baked in coconut cream with wilted spinach, a Pacific-style side or main.

items.raw: 3 sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into 3cm chunks

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Spread the sweet potato and onion in a baking dish.
Pour over the coconut cream, add the salt and cover with foil. Bake for 30 minutes, until the sweet potato is just tender.
Fold in the spinach, return uncovered for 10 minutes, until the spinach has wilted and the top is lightly golden.
Finish with lime juice and chilli.

notes: Vegan and gluten-free.

title: Hawaiian-Style Tuna Poke Bowl
summary: Cubes of raw tuna dressed in soy and sesame over rice with avocado and cucumber.

items.raw: 2 tbsp soy sauce (use tamari for no-gluten)

steps.text: Mix the tuna with the soy, sesame oil, vinegar and spring onion. Cover and chill until cold, about 10 minutes.
Divide the warm rice between two bowls.
Top with the tuna, avocado, cucumber and nori and scatter with sesame seeds.

notes: Food safety: only use sashimi-grade fish, keep it below 4°C and look for flesh that is firm and glossy, not opaque or dull; and eat it the same day. If you prefer, sear the tuna until opaque on the outside. Not suitable for pregnant women or anyone immunocompromised.

title: Sukuma Wiki (Kenyan Braised Kale)
summary: Kale braised with onion and tomato, a humble everyday Kenyan side.

items.raw: 1 bunch kale, stems removed, leaves shredded

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pot and cook the onion for 6 minutes, until golden.
Add the garlic and cumin for 1 minute, then the tomatoes. Cook 4 minutes, until they break down into a sauce.
Add the kale, water and salt. Cover and cook 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until the kale is silky and tender.
Serve hot, with the lemon wedges squeezed over, until the kale is nicely glossy.

notes: Traditionally eaten with ugali or rice. Vegan and gluten-free.

title: Swahili Coconut Fish Curry
summary: Chunks of white fish simmered in a tangy, spiced tomato and coconut sauce.

items.raw: 600g white fish fillet, cut into 4cm pieces

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pan and cook the onion for 6 minutes, until golden. Add the garlic, ginger, curry powder and turmeric for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, tamarind and coconut milk. Simmer for 8 minutes, until slightly thickened.
Slide in the fish and simmer gently for 5 minutes, until opaque and flaking easily.
Scatter with coriander and serve over rice.

notes: Food safety: the fish is cooked when opaque all the way through and it flakes easily (63°C).

title: East African Chicken Pilau
summary: Fragrant rice cooked with chicken thighs, cumin, cardamom, cinnamon and caramelised onion.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large heavy pot and cook the onion over medium heat for 15 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden brown.
Add the chicken and brown for 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic, ginger and whole spices for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook 3 minutes, then stir in the rice, stock and salt.
Bring to a simmer, cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 20 minutes, until the rice is tender and the chicken is cooked through.
Rest 5 minutes, then fluff and serve.

notes: Food safety: the chicken must reach 75°C and have no pink inside.

title: Mandazi (East African Doughnuts)
summary: Lightly sweet, cardamom-scented fried dough triangles made with coconut milk.

steps.text: Mix the flour, sugar, baking powder, cardamom and salt. Beat the egg with the coconut milk and stir into the flour to a soft dough.
Knead briefly on a floured surface until smooth. Rest 15 minutes, then roll to 1cm thick and cut into triangles.
Heat 5cm of oil to 170°C in a deep pot. Fry a few at a time for 2 to 3 minutes, turning once, until puffed and deep golden.
Drain on paper towel and serve warm.

notes: Plus 15 minutes resting. Best eaten the day they are made.

title: Corn and Zucchini Fritters with Smashed Avocado
summary: Crisp golden fritters of corn, zucchini and herbs, served with lime smashed avocado.

steps.text: Toss the zucchini with the salt, rest 10 minutes, then squeeze out as much liquid as you can.
Mix the zucchini, corn, spring onion, flour, baking powder, eggs and coriander with pepper.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Spoon in quarter-cup mounds and flatten slightly. Cook 3 minutes each side, until golden and cooked through in the middle.
Mash the avocado with the lime juice and a pinch of salt, spoon over the fritters and finish with chilli.

notes: Food safety: cook the fritters until the centre is set, not wet.

title: Smashed Avocado with Feta, Lemon and Sesame
summary: Chunky smashed avocado on toasted sourdough with feta, lemon, chilli and sesame.
