steps.text: Toast the sourdough until golden and crisp.
Smash the avocado with the lemon juice and a pinch of salt, leaving it chunky.
Pile onto the toast until it is generously covered, then top with feta, lemon zest, sesame, chilli and mint.
Finish with a drizzle of olive oil.

notes: Vegetarian, and use gluten-free bread to make it no-gluten.

title: Silky Rice Porridge with Chicken, Ginger and Spring Onion
summary: Silky rice porridge simmered with chicken and ginger, topped with spring onion and sesame oil.

steps.text: Put the rice, stock and ginger in a large pot and bring to the boil. Add the chicken, reduce the heat to low and cook partly covered for 50 minutes, stirring now and then, until the rice breaks down into a thick porridge.
Lift out the chicken, shred it with two forks and return it to the pot, discarding the ginger.
Stir in the soy sauce and pepper until the congee is hot again, adding water if it is too thick.
Ladle into bowls and top with spring onion, sesame oil and fried shallots.

notes: Food safety: the chicken must reach 75°C. Thighs simmered for 50 minutes are well past this.

title: Chinese Steamed Egg Custard with Soy and Spring Onion
summary: A silky, savoury egg custard steamed until just set, dressed with soy and sesame oil.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs, warm stock and salt gently, then strain through a sieve into a shallow heatproof dish. Skim off any bubbles.
Cover the dish with foil and steam over simmering water on medium-low heat for 12 minutes, until the custard is just set and wobbles as one piece.
Drizzle with the soy and sesame oil and scatter with spring onion. Serve with rice.

notes: Food safety: the custard should be set through with no liquid egg in the middle.

title: Pho Ga with Charred Onion and Rice Noodles
summary: A light, fragrant Vietnamese chicken noodle soup with ginger, star anise and fresh herbs.

steps.text: Put the chicken, onion, ginger, star anise and cinnamon in a large pot, cover with 3 litres of water and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 40 minutes, skimming the surface, until the chicken is cooked through.
Lift out the chicken, then strain the broth. Season with the fish sauce, sugar and 1 tsp salt. Shred the meat off the bones.
Soak the noodles in boiling water until tender, about 5 minutes, then drain and divide between bowls.
Top with chicken and ladle over the piping hot broth. Serve with bean sprouts, herbs, spring onion, lime and chilli.

notes: Food safety: the thickest part of the thigh must reach 75°C and the juices must run clear.

title: Banh Mi Op La (Vietnamese Eggs in a Pan)
summary: Fried eggs with pate, tomato and pickled carrot, served with crusty bread for dipping.

steps.text: Toss the carrot with the vinegar, sugar and a pinch of salt and set aside for 10 minutes.
Heat the oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat. Crack in the eggs and add the tomato slices around them.
Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are still soft. Splash the soy sauce over.
Serve in the pan with the pâté, carrot, spring onion, sriracha and the warm baguette.

notes: Food safety: cook the whites until fully set.

title: Gochujang Kimchi Rice Bowl with Runny Egg
summary: Punchy fried rice with kimchi, gochujang and sesame oil, topped with a runny egg.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large frying pan or wok over high heat. Fry the kimchi for 2 minutes, until it softens and smells sharp and savoury.
Stir in the gochujang, then the rice, breaking up any lumps. Stir-fry for 4 minutes, until steaming and slightly crisp in places.
Remove from the heat and stir through the spring onion and sesame oil.
Fry the eggs in a little oil until the whites are set and the yolks are runny. Serve the rice topped with the egg, nori and sesame seeds.

notes: Food safety: cook the egg whites until set. Check the gochujang label if you need it gluten-free. Cool any leftover rice quickly and refrigerate it within 1 hour. Use fresh, uncracked eggs; for pregnant women, older people, young children and anyone with low immunity, cook the eggs until the yolks are firm.

title: Gyeran Jjim (Korean Steamed Egg)
summary: A fluffy, bubbling steamed egg pot with a savoury, mild flavour, ready in under 15 minutes.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs with the dashi and salt, then strain into a small heavy pot or earthenware bowl.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring gently, for 3 minutes until the egg starts to set at the edges.
Cover with a lid, reduce the heat to the lowest setting and cook for 5 minutes, until the top is puffed and no longer wet.
Finish with sesame oil, spring onion and sesame seeds and serve at once.

notes: Food safety: the egg should be completely set when you press the middle.

title: Chilaquiles with Salsa and Fried Eggs
summary: Crisp corn chips simmered briefly in salsa, topped with eggs, sour cream and coriander.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large frying pan and cook the onion and jalapeño for 4 minutes, until soft.
Add the salsa and stock and simmer for 5 minutes, until slightly thickened.
Fold in the corn chips and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until they soften slightly but still have some bite.
Make four wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 3 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are runny.
Top with sour cream, feta and coriander and serve with lime.

notes: Food safety: cook the egg whites until completely set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs; for pregnant women, older people, young children and anyone with low immunity, cook the eggs until the yolks are firm.

title: Breakfast Tacos with Black Beans and Avocado
summary: Soft corn tortillas filled with scrambled eggs, spiced black beans, avocado and salsa.

steps.text: Warm the beans in a small pan with the cumin, paprika and 1/4 cup water for 5 minutes, until hot and slightly thick. Mash a few for texture.
Heat the oil in a non-stick pan over medium-low heat. Add the eggs and stir gently for 2 to 3 minutes, until just set.
Char the tortillas directly over a gas flame or in a dry pan for 30 seconds each side, until lightly blistered.
Fill with beans and eggs, then top with avocado, salsa, coriander and a squeeze of lime.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until set with no liquid egg.

title: Greek Yoghurt with Honey, Walnuts and Orange
summary: Thick yoghurt topped with honey, toasted walnuts, orange segments and cinnamon.

steps.text: Toast the walnuts in a dry frying pan for 3 minutes, until golden and fragrant.
Divide the yoghurt between two bowls and top with orange segments and walnuts.
Drizzle with honey and dust with cinnamon.

notes: Vegetarian and no-gluten.

title: Spinach and Feta Breakfast Pie
summary: A crisp filo pie packed with spinach, feta, herbs and egg, good hot or cold.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Wilt the spinach in a large pan for 3 minutes, cool, then squeeze out all the liquid and chop.
Cook the onion in the oil for 6 minutes, until soft. Combine with the spinach, spring onion, feta, ricotta, eggs, dill, nutmeg and pepper.
Brush a baking dish with butter and layer in half the filo, brushing every sheet with butter. Spread in the filling, then layer on the rest of the filo, buttering each sheet.
Score the top into squares and bake for 35 minutes, until deep golden and puffed. Rest 10 minutes before cutting.

notes: Food safety: the filling should be set and hot in the middle (steaming, no liquid egg).

title: Pain Perdu with Berries and Maple
summary: Thick slices of brioche soaked in vanilla custard and pan-fried until golden, served with berries.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs, milk, vanilla and cinnamon in a shallow dish. Soak each brioche slice for 20 seconds per side.
Warm the berries and maple syrup in a small pan for 4 minutes, until juicy and softened.
Melt the butter in a large frying pan over medium heat. Fry the toast in batches for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through in the middle.
Dust with icing sugar and serve with the berries.

notes: Food safety: cook until the custard is set and no wet egg remains.

title: Full Veggie Breakfast with Mushrooms and Beans
summary: Roasted tomatoes and mushrooms with baked beans, fried eggs and toast, a meat-free English fry-up.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Put the tomatoes and mushrooms on a tray with the oil, thyme and salt and roast for 20 minutes, until the tomatoes collapse and the mushrooms are golden.
Warm the beans in a small pan until bubbling, about 5 minutes.
Fry the eggs in the butter until the whites are set and the yolks are soft. Toast the bread.
Plate everything together and eat while hot.

notes: Food safety: the egg whites should be set.

title: Kedgeree with Smoked Salmon and Eggs
summary: Gently curried rice folded with flaked fish, boiled egg, peas and parsley.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes, until soft. Stir in the curry powder and rice for 1 minute.
Add the stock, cover and cook on low for 15 minutes, until the rice is tender and the stock is absorbed. Stir in the peas for the last 3 minutes.
Meanwhile boil the eggs for 8 minutes, until just firm, then cool, peel and quarter.
Fold the salmon, lemon juice and parsley through the rice, top with the eggs and serve.

notes: Food safety: smoked salmon is ready to eat but should stay chilled until it goes in.

title: Spanish Potato Omelette (Tortilla de Patatas)
summary: A thick, golden omelette of slowly cooked potato and onion, eaten warm or cold.

items.raw: 600g waxy potato, peeled and thinly sliced

steps.text: Heat the oil in a 24cm non-stick frying pan over medium-low heat. Cook the potato and onion for 20 minutes, turning often, until completely tender but not coloured.
Drain the oil into a bowl (keep it). Beat the eggs with the salt, fold in the warm potatoes and rest 5 minutes.
Heat 1 tbsp of the reserved oil in the pan over medium heat, pour in the mixture and cook for 5 minutes, until the edges are set and the base is golden.
Slide the tortilla onto a plate, invert it back into the pan and cook another 4 minutes, until firm. Rest before slicing.

notes: Food safety: the middle should be just set, with no raw egg. Cook another 2 minutes if in doubt.

title: Menemen (Turkish Scrambled Eggs with Peppers)
summary: Soft eggs cooked with sweet peppers, tomato and chilli flakes, eaten with bread.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a frying pan and cook the capsicum and chilli for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the tomatoes and chilli flakes and simmer for 6 minutes, until reduced and jammy.
Crack in the eggs, season and stir gently for 2 to 3 minutes, until softly set but not dry.
Serve straight from the pan with bread.

notes: Food safety: cook until the eggs are fully set.

title: Cilbir (Turkish Eggs with Garlic Yoghurt)
summary: Poached eggs on garlicky yoghurt, drizzled with chilli butter and dill.

steps.text: Stir the yoghurt, garlic and a pinch of salt and let it come to room temperature.
Bring a deep pan of water to a gentle simmer with the vinegar. Swirl, slip in the eggs and poach for 3 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are runny. Lift out with a slotted spoon.
Melt the butter in a small pan until foaming, then stir in the Aleppo pepper.
Spread the yoghurt onto plates, top with eggs, drizzle with the chilli butter and scatter with dill. Serve with bread.

notes: Food safety: the whites must be set. Cook longer if serving anyone vulnerable.

title: Baghrir (Moroccan Thousand-Hole Pancakes)
summary: Spongy, one-sided semolina pancakes covered in tiny holes, drenched in honey butter.

steps.text: Blend the semolina, flour, yeast, baking powder, sugar, salt and water for 2 minutes, until smooth. Rest 20 minutes, until bubbly.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat, with no oil. Pour in a small ladle of batter and cook for 2 minutes, until the top is covered in holes and completely dry. Do not flip.
Stack the cooked pancakes on a plate as you go.
Mix the butter and honey and spoon it over the warm pancakes.

notes: Plus 20 minutes resting.

title: Hummus Toast with Roasted Tomatoes and Za'atar
summary: Warm sourdough piled with hummus, blistered tomatoes, cucumber and za'atar.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the tomatoes in the oil with salt and roast for 12 minutes, until blistered and bursting.
Toast the sourdough until golden.
Spread with hummus and top with cucumber and the roasted tomatoes.
Dress with lemon juice and finish with za'atar and mint.

notes: Vegan. Use gluten-free bread for no-gluten.

title: Sweet Potato and Black Bean Breakfast Hash
summary: Crisp sweet potato cubes with black beans, capsicum and eggs baked in the pan.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large ovenproof frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the sweet potato for 12 minutes, stirring now and then, until tender and browned.
Add the onion, capsicum, paprika and cumin and cook for 5 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the beans, make four wells and crack in the eggs. Cover and cook for 5 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are soft.
Top with spring onion and avocado.

notes: Food safety: the egg whites should be set.

title: Apple and Peanut Butter Oat Pancakes
summary: Wholesome blender pancakes made with oats, grated apple and peanut butter.

steps.text: Blend the apple, oats, eggs, milk, peanut butter, baking powder and cinnamon until smooth. Rest 5 minutes.
Heat a little oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Pour in 1/4 cup batter per pancake.
Cook for 2 minutes, until bubbles form and the edges look set, then flip and cook 1 to 2 minutes, until golden and cooked through.
Stack the pancakes on warm plates and serve with maple syrup.

notes: Food safety: make sure the batter in the middle is cooked, not gluey.

title: Mushroom Ragu with Pappardelle
summary: A deep, wine-rich mushroom ragu with porcini and thyme over wide ribbons of pasta.

steps.text: Soak the porcini in 1 cup of boiling water for 15 minutes, then lift out, chop and keep the liquid.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over high heat and cook the mushrooms in two batches for 8 minutes, until deeply browned. Set aside.
Cook the onion for 6 minutes, until soft, then add the garlic and tomato paste for 2 minutes. Pour in the wine and bubble until nearly gone.
Return the mushrooms with the porcini, their strained liquid, tomatoes and thyme. Simmer 25 minutes, until rich and thick.
Cook the pasta until al dente, toss through the ragu with a splash of pasta water and finish with parsley.

notes: Pappardelle is usually made with egg; use an egg-free pasta to make it vegan. Wine is fine for most vegans but check the label if strict.

title: Soft Polenta with Slow-Braised Lamb Shoulder
summary: Lamb shoulder braised with red wine and rosemary until it falls apart, served on creamy polenta.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Season the lamb well. Brown it in the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat for 10 minutes, turning until deep golden. Remove.
Cook the onion, carrot and garlic in the same pot for 6 minutes, until soft. Stir in the paste for 2 minutes, then add the wine and boil until reduced by half.
Add the tomatoes, rosemary and stock and return the lamb. Cover and braise for 3 hours, until the meat falls from the bone.
Near the end, bring the water and 1 tsp salt to the boil, whisk in the polenta and cook on low for 20 minutes, stirring often, until thick. Beat in the butter.
Shred the lamb into the sauce, spoon over the polenta and scatter with parsley.

notes: Food safety: braise lamb until very tender, well above 75°C.
Naturally gluten-free.

title: Rosemary Oil Bean and Pasta Soup
summary: A thick, comforting Italian bean and pasta soup finished with garlicky rosemary oil.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion, carrot and celery for 8 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic and tomato paste for 2 minutes.
Add the beans and stock and simmer for 10 minutes. Mash about a third of the beans against the side of the pot to thicken.
Add the pasta and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, until tender, adding water if too thick.
Warm the second batch of oil with the rosemary and sliced garlic in a small pan for 2 minutes, until fragrant, and spoon it over each bowl.

notes: Vegan.

title: Spaghetti Cacio e Pepe with Vegetarian Hard Cheese
summary: Black pepper and vegetarian hard cheese melted into a glossy sauce with starchy pasta water.

steps.text: Cook the spaghetti in salted water until al dente, saving 1 cup of the cooking water.
Toast the pepper in the butter in a wide pan for 1 minute, until fragrant, then add 1/2 cup of the pasta water.
Add the spaghetti and toss over low heat. Take off the heat and add the cheese in handfuls, tossing and adding splashes of water until the sauce is creamy and clings.
Serve immediately in warm bowls, while the sauce is still glossy and loose.

notes: Use a cheese labelled vegetarian, made without animal rennet.

title: Eggplant Involtini with Ricotta and Basil
summary: Grilled eggplant slices rolled around lemony ricotta and baked in tomato sauce.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Brush the eggplant with oil, season and roast on trays for 15 minutes, until soft and golden.
Mix the ricotta, lemon zest, half the basil and the breadcrumbs with salt and pepper.
Spread sauce over a baking dish. Place a spoon of filling on each slice, roll up and set seam side down.
Top with the remaining sauce and mozzarella and bake for 20 minutes, until bubbling and golden. Scatter with basil.

notes: Vegetarian.

title: Harissa-Roasted Cauliflower with Herbed Quinoa
summary: Spicy roasted cauliflower on lemony quinoa with pomegranate and mint, vegan and gluten-free.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the cauliflower with 2 tbsp oil and the harissa on a tray and roast for 25 minutes, until charred and tender.
Simmer the quinoa in the water with a pinch of salt for 15 minutes, until the germ spirals out, then drain and fluff.
Toss the quinoa with the herbs, lemon juice and remaining oil.
Top with the cauliflower, pomegranate and almonds.

notes: Vegan and gluten-free.

title: Pumpkin and Sage Gnocchi Bake
summary: Roasted pumpkin and gnocchi baked with sage butter, cream and vegetarian hard cheese.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Roast the pumpkin in the oil on a tray for 20 minutes, until tender and caramelised.
Mix the pumpkin and gnocchi in a baking dish. Melt the butter with the sage and garlic for 2 minutes, until the sage crisps, and pour over.
Add the cream, scatter with the cheese and bake for 20 minutes, until bubbling and golden.

notes: Vegetarian, using hard cheese labelled vegetarian.

title: One-Tray Lemon Garlic Barramundi with Potatoes
summary: Crisp-skinned barramundi fillets roasted with lemony potatoes, olives and cherry tomatoes.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the potatoes, tomatoes, olives, oil, garlic and half the lemon on a large tray with salt. Roast for 20 minutes, until the potato is golden at the edges.
Nestle in the fish, scatter with oregano and top with the remaining lemon.
Roast for 10 to 12 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when opaque throughout and flaking easily (63°C).

title: Pumpkin and Red Lentil Dal with Coconut
summary: A creamy, gently spiced dal with pumpkin, coconut milk and a sizzling cumin tadka.

steps.text: Simmer the lentils, pumpkin, turmeric and water for 20 minutes, stirring often, until the lentils collapse and the pumpkin is soft.
Mash roughly, stir in the coconut milk and salt and warm through.
Heat the ghee in a small pan and fry the cumin seeds, garlic and chilli for 1 to 2 minutes, until the garlic is golden.
Pour the tadka over the dal and serve with rice.

notes: Use oil in place of ghee for vegan.

title: Achari Paneer Tikka Skewers
summary: Tangy pickle-spiced paneer and capsicum skewers, grilled until charred at the edges.

steps.text: Mix the yoghurt, ginger garlic paste, spices, lemon juice, oil and 1 tsp salt. Toss the paneer, capsicum and onion through, cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Thread onto skewers, alternating the paneer and vegetables.
Grill, barbecue or roast at 230°C for 12 to 15 minutes, turning often, until charred in spots and the paneer is golden.
Rest the skewers for 2 minutes, until the juices settle, then serve with mint chutney and lemon.

notes: Plus 1 hour marinating.

title: Hyderabadi-Style Lamb Biryani
summary: Spiced lamb layered with saffron rice and fried onions, sealed and steamed in the pot.

steps.text: Marinate the lamb with the yoghurt, ginger garlic paste, spices and 2 tsp salt for at least 2 hours.
Fry the onions in the oil for 20 minutes, until deep golden and crisp. Lift out, leaving the oil.
Cook the lamb with its marinade and half the onions in a heavy pot with 1/2 cup water on low heat for 40 minutes, until tender.
Boil the rice with the cardamom, cinnamon and bay in salted water for 6 minutes, until 70 percent cooked, and drain.
Layer the rice over the lamb with the herbs, remaining onions and saffron milk. Cover with foil and a tight lid and cook on the lowest heat for 25 minutes, until the rice is tender and fluffy.

notes: Food safety: the lamb must be fork-tender and well above 70°C before layering.
Plus 2 hours marinating.

title: Gobi Aloo (Cauliflower and Potato Dry Curry)
summary: Tender cauliflower and potato tossed in cumin, turmeric and ginger, vegan and gluten-free.

steps.text: Heat the oil and fry the cumin seeds for 30 seconds, until sizzling. Add the onion and ginger and cook 5 minutes, until golden.
Add the potato, turmeric and coriander and cook for 5 minutes. Add the cauliflower, tomato, 1/4 cup water and 1 tsp salt.
Cover and cook for 12 minutes, until both vegetables are tender, then uncover and cook until the water has gone.
Stir through the garam masala and coriander.

notes: Vegan and gluten-free.

title: Tamarind Chickpea Chaat Bowls
summary: Crunchy, tangy street-food chickpea salad with cucumber, tomato, tamarind chutney and yoghurt.

steps.text: Fry the chickpeas in the oil with the cumin for 5 minutes, until lightly crisp and golden.
Toss with the cucumber, tomato, onion and lime juice.
Spoon into bowls, drizzle with yoghurt and chutney and finish with coriander and chilli.

notes: Use a plant-based yoghurt for vegan.

title: Mapo Tofu with Pork and Sichuan Pepper
summary: Silky tofu in a fiery, numbing chilli-bean sauce with minced pork and spring onion.

items.raw: 1 tsp Sichuan peppercorn, toasted and ground

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Stir-fry the pork for 4 minutes, until browned and crisp, then add the doubanjiang, garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Add the stock and soy and bring to a simmer. Slide in the tofu and simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Mix the cornflour with water and stir in until the sauce thickens and turns glossy.
Finish with the ground Sichuan pepper and spring onion and serve with rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork mince to 75°C or above, with no pink, before the tofu goes in.

title: Xinjiang-Style Cumin Lamb Stir-Fry
summary: Sliced lamb seared with cumin seed, chilli and onion over very high heat.

items.raw: 2 tbsp cumin seed, lightly toasted and crushed

steps.text: Toss the lamb with the soy sauce and cornflour and leave 10 minutes.
Heat the oil in a wok over very high heat until smoking. Sear the lamb for 2 minutes without moving, then stir-fry for 2 minutes more, until browned.
Add the cumin, chilli flakes, onion and garlic and stir-fry for 2 minutes, until the onion is charred in places.
Splash in the wine, toss in the spring onions and serve over rice once the lamb is cooked through with no pink.

notes: Food safety: lamb slices are cooked when no pink remains (about 63°C or higher).

title: Garlic Bok Choy and Shiitake Stir-Fry
summary: Fast, glossy greens and mushrooms in a garlic and oyster-style sauce, vegan with mushroom sauce.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and fry the garlic for 15 seconds, until fragrant but not brown.
Add the shiitake and stir-fry for 2 minutes, until golden.
Add the bok choy, soy sauce, wine and sugar and toss for 2 minutes, until the stems are tender-crisp and the leaves have wilted.
Drizzle with sesame oil and serve with rice.

notes: Vegan. Use tamari for no-gluten and a gluten-free rice wine in place of Shaoxing wine.

title: Sweet and Sour Cauliflower with Pineapple
summary: Crisp-roasted cauliflower tossed in a bright, glossy sweet and sour sauce with pineapple.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the cauliflower with the oil, first tbsp of cornflour and a pinch of salt and roast for 25 minutes, until golden and crisp at the edges.
Combine the tomato sauce, vinegar, sugar and soy in a pan and bring to a simmer, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Mix the second cornflour with the water and stir in until the sauce is glossy and thick, about 1 minute.
Add the capsicum and pineapple for 2 minutes, then toss with the cauliflower and scatter with spring onions.

notes: Vegan. Use tamari for no-gluten.

title: Wonton Noodle Soup with Pork and Prawn
summary: Delicate pork and prawn wontons in a clear, ginger-scented broth with egg noodles and greens.

steps.text: Mix the pork, prawn, spring onion, soy, sesame oil, ginger and a pinch of pepper. Place a teaspoon of filling in each wrapper, wet the edges and fold into a sealed parcel.
Simmer the stock with the ginger slices for 10 minutes, until fragrant. Season with salt.
Cook the wontons in the simmering stock for 4 minutes, until they float and the filling is cooked through, then lift out.
Boil the noodles and bok choy until tender, about 3 minutes, and divide between bowls. Add the wontons, ladle over broth and finish with pepper.

notes: Food safety: the pork filling must reach 75°C; wontons should float, with opaque prawn.

title: Tofu and Eggplant Curry in Green Paste
summary: Creamy green curry with crisp tofu, Asian eggplant and Thai basil; use a vegan curry paste to keep it vegan.

steps.text: Fry the tofu in the oil over medium-high heat for 6 minutes, until golden on all sides. Remove.
In the same pan fry the curry paste for 1 minute, until fragrant, then stir in the coconut milk and stock.
Add the eggplant and simmer for 8 minutes. Add the beans, soy, sugar and lime leaves and cook for 4 minutes, until tender.
Return the tofu, stir in the basil and serve with rice.

notes: Many curry pastes contain shrimp paste, so check the label for vegan.

title: Pad Krapow Gai (Holy Basil Chicken)
summary: Fiery minced chicken stir-fried with holy basil, garlic and chilli, topped with a crisp fried egg.

steps.text: Crush or chop the garlic and chilli together. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat and fry the paste for 20 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir-fry for 4 to 5 minutes, breaking it up, until cooked through with no pink.
Add the oyster sauce, soy, sugar and fish sauce and toss for 1 minute, then fold in the basil until wilted.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil until the whites are crisp at the edges and the yolks are runny. Serve over rice.

notes: Food safety: the mince must reach 75°C throughout and the egg whites must be set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs; for pregnant women, older people, young children and anyone with low immunity, cook the eggs until the yolks are firm.

title: Thai Pumpkin and Coconut Soup
summary: A velvety, gently spicy pumpkin soup with red curry paste, coconut and lime.

steps.text: Heat the oil and cook the onion for 5 minutes, until soft. Add the curry paste for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the pumpkin and stock and simmer for 15 minutes, until the pumpkin is very soft.
Blend until smooth, then stir in the coconut milk, lime juice and soy sauce and warm through.
Top with coriander and chilli.

notes: Check the curry paste for shrimp paste if you need it vegan.

title: Thai Chilli Jam Prawn Stir-Fry
summary: Juicy prawns, snake beans and capsicum in a sweet, smoky Thai chilli jam sauce.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Stir-fry the prawns for 2 minutes, until just pink and curled, then remove.
Add the garlic, capsicum and beans and stir-fry for 3 minutes, until tender-crisp.
Return the prawns with the chilli jam, fish sauce and lime juice and toss for 1 minute, until coated and glossy.
Fold in the basil and serve with rice.

notes: Food safety: prawns are cooked when pink and opaque (63°C), so don't overcook them.

title: Sweet Miso Roasted Eggplant over Rice
summary: Silky roasted eggplant brushed with sweet miso glaze over rice, with pickled ginger and sesame.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Score the cut sides of the eggplant in a crisscross, brush with oil and roast cut side down for 15 minutes.
Whisk the miso, mirin, sugar and vinegar into a glaze.
Flip the eggplant, brush on the glaze and roast for 10 minutes more, until the flesh is meltingly soft and the glaze is bubbling and lightly charred.
Serve over rice with spring onion, sesame seeds and pickled ginger.

notes: Vegan. Check the miso for gluten-containing grains if you need it no-gluten.

title: Chicken Katsu with Japanese Curry Sauce
summary: Crumbed chicken breast cutlets served with a mild, glossy Japanese-style curry sauce and rice.

steps.text: Slice each chicken breast in half horizontally to make thin cutlets. Season, dredge in flour, dip in the egg, then press into the panko.
For the sauce, cook the onion and carrot in 1 tbsp oil for 8 minutes, until soft. Stir in the second flour and curry powder for 1 minute, then whisk in the stock.
Simmer for 12 minutes, until the carrots are tender and the sauce is thick. Stir in the soy sauce and honey, blend if you like it smooth.
Shallow-fry the cutlets in the 1/2 cup oil in a wide pan over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until deep golden and cooked through.
Rest, slice and serve over rice with the sauce.

notes: Food safety: the chicken must reach 75°C, with no pink in the middle of the thickest cutlet.

title: Cold Soba with Sesame, Cucumber and Edamame
summary: Chilled buckwheat noodles in a nutty soy-sesame dressing with crisp vegetables.

steps.text: Cook the soba in boiling water for 4 minutes, until tender, adding the edamame in the last minute. Drain and rinse under cold water until cold.
Whisk the soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, sugar and tahini into a dressing.
Toss the noodles with the cucumber, spring onions and dressing.
Top with nori and sesame seeds.

notes: Vegan. Many soba noodles contain wheat; choose 100 percent buckwheat for no-gluten.

title: Salmon Teriyaki with Sesame Greens
summary: Pan-seared salmon glazed in a homemade teriyaki sauce, served over rice with sesame bok choy.

steps.text: Mix the soy sauce, mirin, sugar and ginger. Heat the oil in a frying pan and sear the salmon skin side down over medium-high heat for 4 minutes, until the skin is crisp.
Turn the fillets, pour in the sauce and cook for 3 minutes, spooning the sauce over until it has thickened to a glaze and the salmon is just cooked.
Meanwhile steam the bok choy for 3 minutes, until tender, and toss with sesame oil and seeds.
Serve the salmon over rice with the greens.

notes: Food safety: salmon is cooked at 63°C; it should flake easily with a slightly translucent centre.

title: Slow-Cooked Beef Barbacoa Tacos
summary: Chipotle-spiced beef cheeks braised until shreddable and piled into warm tortillas with onion and lime.

items.raw: 1.2kg beef chuck, cut into large chunks

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C (130°C fan). Blend the chipotle, garlic, lime juice, vinegar, cumin, oregano and 1 tsp salt with the stock.
Put the beef and bay leaves in a Dutch oven, pour over the sauce, cover and braise for 4 hours, until the beef shreds easily.
Shred the meat in the sauce and reduce on the stove for 5 minutes, until glossy.
Warm the tortillas and fill with beef, onion, coriander and a squeeze of lime.

notes: Food safety: beef braised until fork-tender is well past 75°C.

title: Smoky Kumara and Bean Enchilada Bake
summary: Soft tortillas filled with spiced sweet potato and black beans, baked under enchilada sauce and cheese.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the sweet potato in the oil and cumin and roast for 20 minutes, until tender and starting to brown.
Mix with the beans, corn and a pinch of salt.
Spread half the sauce in a baking dish. Fill each tortilla with the mixture, roll up and place seam side down. Pour over the rest of the sauce and sprinkle with cheese.
Bake for 20 minutes, until bubbling and golden. Serve with coriander and sour cream.

notes: Vegetarian. Use corn tortillas for no-gluten.

title: Prawn Ceviche with Mango and Avocado
summary: Cooked prawns marinated briefly in lime with mango, avocado, red onion and chilli.

steps.text: Toss the prawns with the lime juice, onion and chilli and marinate in the fridge for 15 minutes, until the onion softens.
Fold in the mango, avocado, cucumber and coriander.
Season with salt and serve with corn chips.

notes: Food safety: use prawns that have been cooked until pink and opaque and kept chilled. Plus 15 minutes marinating.

title: Chimichurri Steak with Crispy Roasted Potatoes
summary: Seared sirloin sliced over crisp potatoes and drizzled with a punchy parsley and garlic chimichurri.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the potatoes with the 3 tbsp oil and salt and roast for 35 minutes, until golden and crisp.
Stir the parsley, oregano, garlic, 1/2 cup oil, vinegar and chilli flakes with 1 tsp salt into a chimichurri. Rest 15 minutes.
Season the steaks and sear in a hot pan for 3 minutes per side for medium-rare, until well browned. Rest for 5 minutes.
Slice the steak and serve with the potatoes and plenty of chimichurri.

notes: Food safety: steak is cooked at 63°C for medium-rare; use a thermometer if unsure. Rest the meat before slicing.

title: Spiced Chicken Thigh Wraps with Toum and Pickles
summary: Spice-rubbed chicken thighs roasted until charred, with salad, pickles and toum.

steps.text: Mix the spices, lemon juice, oil and 1 tsp salt and coat the chicken. Cover and marinate for at least 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 230°C (210°C fan). Roast the chicken on a tray for 25 minutes, until charred in places and cooked through.
Rest 5 minutes, then slice thinly.
Warm the flatbreads and serve with chicken, salad, toum and pickles.

notes: Food safety: the chicken must reach 75°C and the juices must run clear.
Plus 1 hour marinating.

title: Spiced Lamb Kofta with Tzatziki
summary: Juicy lamb skewers with cumin, coriander and mint, served with cool tzatziki and flatbread.

steps.text: Mix the lamb with the onion, garlic, spices, parsley and salt until sticky. Shape around 8 skewers into long ovals.
Cook on a hot grill or griddle for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until browned all over and cooked through.
Warm the flatbread and serve the kofta with tzatziki and cucumber.

notes: Food safety: lamb mince must reach 75°C with no pink inside.

title: Classic Smash Burgers with Pickles and Special Sauce
summary: Thin, crisp-edged beef patties smashed on a hot pan with melty cheese and tangy sauce.

steps.text: Mix the mayonnaise, tomato sauce, chopped pickle and mustard powder into a sauce.
Divide the mince into 8 loose balls. Heat the oil in a very hot cast-iron pan and smash 2 balls at a time flat with a spatula. Season and cook for 2 minutes, until the edges are crisp and brown.
Flip, top with cheese and cook 1 minute more, until the cheese melts and the beef is cooked through with no pink.
Toast the buns until golden, spread with sauce and stack with onion, lettuce, pickles and two patties.

notes: Food safety: beef mince patties must reach 75°C with no pink inside.

title: Loaded Potato Skins with Cheddar and Chives
summary: Crisp-skinned baked potato shells filled with cheddar and bacon, topped with sour cream and chives.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Prick the potatoes, rub with oil and salt and bake for 55 minutes, until the skin is crisp and a skewer slides in easily.
Halve the potatoes, scoop out most of the flesh and keep it for another use. Brush the shells with oil and bake cut side up for 8 minutes, until crisp.
Fill with cheddar and bacon and bake for 6 minutes, until the cheese is melted and bubbling.
Top with sour cream and chives.

notes: Food safety: make sure the bacon is cooked through (crisp) before using.

title: Vegetable Bibimbap with Gochujang
summary: Rice bowl topped with seasoned vegetables, a fried egg and spicy gochujang sauce.

steps.text: Mix the gochujang with 1 tbsp sesame oil, the sugar and 1 tbsp water.
Cook each vegetable separately in a little sesame oil for 2 to 3 minutes until just tender: carrot, zucchini, mushrooms with garlic and soy, and spinach wilted with a pinch of salt.
Fry the eggs in oil until the whites are set and the yolks are runny.
Divide the rice into bowls, arrange the vegetables on top with an egg and gochujang, and mix everything together before eating.

notes: Food safety: cook the egg whites until set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs; for pregnant women, older people, young children and anyone with low immunity, cook the eggs until the yolks are firm.

title: Korean Fried Chicken with Sweet and Spicy Glaze
summary: Twice-fried, extra-crisp chicken wings tossed in a sticky gochujang glaze.

steps.text: Pat the wings dry. Toss in the cornflour, flour and salt to coat well.
Heat 5cm of oil to 160°C in a deep pot. Fry the wings in batches for 10 minutes, until pale golden and cooked through. Drain.
Raise the oil to 190°C and fry the wings again for 3 minutes, until deep golden and very crisp.
Simmer the gochujang, honey, soy, vinegar and garlic for 3 minutes, until syrupy, and toss the wings through. Scatter with sesame.

notes: Food safety: wings must reach 75°C at the thickest part.

title: Oregano Chicken Drumsticks with Lemon Potatoes
summary: Chicken pieces and potatoes roasted in lemon, oregano and garlic until crisp and juicy.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the chicken and potato in a large roasting tin with the oil, garlic, lemon juice and zest, oregano and 1 tsp salt.
Pour the stock around the edge and roast for 50 to 60 minutes, turning once, until the chicken is golden and the potatoes are tender.
Rest 5 minutes and scatter with parsley.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C at the thickest point, with the juices running clear.

title: Gigantes Plaki (Baked Greek Butter Beans)
summary: Butter beans baked in tomato, dill and olive oil until creamy and caramelised.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Cook the onion in half the oil for 6 minutes, until soft, then add the garlic and tomato paste for 2 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes, oregano, sugar and 1 tsp salt, then the beans. Pour into a baking dish and drizzle with the remaining oil.
Bake for 45 minutes, until the sauce is thick and the top is caramelised at the edges.
Scatter with dill and feta and serve with bread.

notes: Skip the feta for vegan.

title: Chicken Fricassee with Mushrooms and Tarragon
summary: Tender chicken thighs in a creamy white wine and mushroom sauce with tarragon.

steps.text: Season the chicken and brown in the butter in a large pan for 4 minutes per side, until golden. Remove.
Cook the onion and mushrooms for 8 minutes, until golden. Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then add the wine and boil until reduced by half.
Add the stock and return the chicken. Cover and simmer for 25 minutes, until cooked through.
Stir in the cream, tarragon and lemon juice and simmer 3 minutes, until the sauce coats a spoon.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C and show no pink.

title: Ratatouille Tian
summary: Thin slices of zucchini, eggplant and tomato baked in overlapping spirals over a pepper sauce.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Cook the onion, capsicum and garlic in the oil for 8 minutes, until soft. Add the tinned tomatoes and simmer 10 minutes, until thick.
Spread the sauce in a round baking dish.
Arrange the sliced vegetables in tight overlapping spirals on top, alternating them. Drizzle with oil, scatter with thyme and season.
Cover with foil and bake for 40 minutes, then uncover and bake 15 minutes more, until the vegetables are tender and the edges are browned.

notes: Vegan and gluten-free.

title: Wok-Fried Yellow Noodles with Tofu, Egg and Sambal
summary: Wok-fried yellow noodles with tofu, egg, bean sprouts and a sweet-spicy sauce.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and fry the garlic and tofu for 3 minutes, until golden.
Push to the side, crack in the eggs and scramble for 1 minute, until set.
Add the noodles, kecap manis, tomato sauce, sambal and soy and toss for 3 minutes, until the noodles are coated and hot.
Add the bean sprouts and spring onion and toss for 1 minute, until just wilted. Serve with lime.

notes: Food safety: scramble the egg until fully set.

title: Nasi Lemak with Sambal and Egg
summary: Coconut rice served with spicy sambal, cucumber, peanuts, boiled egg and crisp anchovies.

items.raw: 1/2 cup anchovy fillets, fried until crisp

steps.text: Cook the rice with the coconut milk, water, bay leaves and salt in a covered pot over low heat for 18 minutes, until tender and fluffy.
For the sambal, fry the onion in the oil for 6 minutes, until soft. Stir in the sambal oelek, tamarind and palm sugar and cook for 5 minutes, until dark and glossy.
Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, until firm, then peel and halve.
Serve the rice with sambal, egg, cucumber, peanuts and anchovies.

notes: Food safety: eggs boiled until the yolk is firm.

title: Gado-Gado with Peanut Sauce
summary: Steamed vegetables, tofu and egg under a rich, tangy peanut sauce, with prawn crackers on the side.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes for 12 minutes, until tender. Blanch the beans, sprouts and cabbage in boiling water for 1 to 2 minutes, until bright and crisp-tender.
Whisk the peanut butter, kecap manis, lime juice, garlic, chilli and hot water until smooth and pourable.
Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, until firm, peel and halve.
Arrange all the vegetables, tofu and egg on plates, spoon over the sauce and top with prawn crackers.

notes: Food safety: boil eggs until the yolk is firm.

title: Turkish Red Lentil Soup with Chilli Butter
summary: Smooth red lentil soup with carrot and cumin, finished with sizzling paprika butter.

steps.text: Heat the oil and cook the onion and carrot for 6 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, tomato paste and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the lentils and stock and simmer for 20 minutes, until the lentils are completely soft.
Blend until smooth and stir in the lemon juice and salt to taste.
Melt the butter until foaming, stir in the paprika and chilli flakes and spoon it over each bowl.

notes: Use olive oil in place of butter for vegan.

title: Lemon Ricotta Pancakes with Blueberries
summary: Light, tender pancakes made with ricotta and lemon, served with warm blueberries and honey.

steps.text: Whisk the ricotta, egg yolks, sugar, lemon zest and juice, flour, baking powder and milk until combined.
Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks and fold them gently through the batter.
Melt a little butter in a non-stick pan over medium heat and cook 1/4 cup batter per pancake for 2 to 3 minutes each side, until golden and puffed.
Warm the berries with the honey for 3 minutes, until juicy, and spoon over the pancakes.

notes: Food safety: cook the pancakes until the centres are set.

title: Roasted Pumpkin and Lentil Salad with Tahini
summary: Warm pumpkin, lentils, rocket and toasted seeds with a lemony tahini dressing, vegan and gluten-free.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the pumpkin with the oil, paprika and salt and roast for 30 minutes, until tender and caramelised.
Simmer the lentils in plenty of water for 20 minutes, until tender but holding their shape, and drain.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice, water and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Toss the lentils, onion and rocket, top with the pumpkin and seeds and drizzle with the tahini.

notes: Vegan and gluten-free.

title: Crispy-Skin Salmon with Celery and Orange Salad
summary: Pan-seared salmon with a crisp skin, served over a fresh orange, celery and mint salad.

steps.text: Pat the salmon skin dry and season with salt. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and cook skin side down for 5 minutes, until the skin is crisp.
Turn and cook 2 minutes more, until the salmon is just cooked and flakes easily.
Toss the celery, orange, onion, 2 tbsp oil, lemon juice, mint and capers with a pinch of salt.
Serve the salmon over the salad.

notes: Food safety: salmon is cooked at 63°C, flaking easily with a slightly translucent centre.

title: Vegan Chickpea and Spinach Curry
summary: A quick pantry curry of chickpeas, tomato and spinach in a creamy coconut sauce.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 6 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, ginger and spices for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomatoes, chickpeas and coconut milk and simmer for 12 minutes, until thickened.
Add the spinach until wilted, then the lemon juice. Serve with rice.

notes: Vegan and gluten-free.

title: Sicilian Caponata on Toasted Sourdough
summary: Sweet and sour eggplant stew with capers and olives, piled onto garlicky toast.

steps.text: Fry the eggplant in 1/4 cup oil in batches over medium-high heat for 8 minutes, until golden and soft. Set aside.
Cook the onion and celery in the remaining oil for 6 minutes. Add the tomatoes, vinegar and sugar and simmer for 10 minutes.
Return the eggplant with the capers and olives and cook 5 minutes, until glossy and thick. Stir in the basil.
Toast the sourdough until golden, rub with garlic and top with caponata.

notes: Vegan. Use gluten-free bread for no-gluten.

title: Farinata (Ligurian Chickpea Flatbread) with Rosemary
summary: A crisp-edged, custardy chickpea flour flatbread baked in a hot pan with rosemary and olive oil.

steps.text: Whisk the chickpea flour, water and salt until smooth. Rest 30 minutes, then skim off any foam.
Heat the oven to 250°C (230°C fan) and put a cast-iron pan in to heat for 10 minutes. Add the oil to the pan, swirl, and pour in the batter. Scatter with rosemary.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until the edges are deep golden and crisp and the middle is set.
Cut into wedges and finish with pepper.

notes: Plus 30 minutes resting. Vegan and gluten-free.

title: Almond Amaretti Biscuits
summary: Chewy, crackled almond biscuits with no flour at all.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan) and line two trays with baking paper.
Whisk the egg whites in a bowl until they hold soft peaks, then fold in the almond meal, caster sugar and vanilla until a sticky dough forms.
Roll tablespoons of the dough into balls, toss in the icing sugar and set them 3cm apart on the trays.
Bake for 18 minutes, until pale golden and cracked on top. Cool on the tray, where they firm up.

notes: Dessert.
Gluten-free: check your icing sugar label for added starch.

title: Pears Poached in Marsala
summary: Tender pears simmered in sweet Marsala and cinnamon until glossy.

steps.text: Put the marsala, water, sugar, cinnamon stick and orange peel in a saucepan and stir over medium heat until the sugar dissolves.
Add the pears, cover with a circle of baking paper and simmer gently for 25 minutes, until a knife slides in easily.
Lift out the pears, then boil the syrup for 5 minutes, until reduced by half. Spoon over the pears and serve warm or cold.

notes: Dessert.
Vegan and gluten-free.

title: French Apple Tarte Fine
summary: Paper-thin apple slices fanned over crisp puff pastry and glazed with apricot jam.

items.raw: 4 apple, cored and very thinly sliced

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Cut the pastry in half, lay on two lined trays and prick the centres with a fork, leaving a 2cm border.
Fan the apple slices over the pastry, overlapping them. Brush with melted butter and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake for 30 minutes, until the pastry is puffed and the apple edges are golden.
Warm the jam with the water until runny, then brush over the hot tarts.

notes: Dessert.

title: Dark Chocolate Pots
summary: Silky, rich chocolate custards set in little cups.

steps.text: Heat the cream and milk in a saucepan until just steaming, then pour over the chocolate in a bowl and stir until smooth.
Whisk the egg yolks, sugar and salt together, then slowly whisk in the warm chocolate mixture.
Return to the pan and stir over low heat for 5 minutes, until it coats the back of a spoon and reaches 75°C. Do not let it boil.
Pour into six small cups and chill until set.

notes: Dessert.
Plus 4 hours chilling.
Food safety: the egg yolks are cooked to 75°C, so the pots are safe to serve, but keep them chilled and eat within 2 days.
Gluten-free.

title: Honey Lemon Madeleines
summary: Buttery little shell cakes with a honey and lemon scent, best eaten warm.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs, sugar, honey and lemon zest in a bowl for 3 minutes, until pale and thick.
Fold in the flour and baking powder, then the melted butter. Cover and rest the batter in the fridge.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and grease a madeleine tray.
Spoon the batter into the moulds and bake for 10 minutes, until puffed and golden at the edges. Dust with icing sugar.

notes: Dessert.
Plus 1 hour resting the batter.

title: Whole Orange and Almond Cake
summary: A dense, fragrant cake made with boiled whole oranges.

steps.text: Cover the whole oranges with water in a saucepan and simmer for 1 hour, until very soft. Drain, cool, halve and discard any pips, then blitz the oranges, skin and all, to a purée.
Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and line a 22cm tin.
Whisk the eggs and sugar until pale, then stir in the orange purée, almond meal and baking powder.
Pour into the tin and bake for 60 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Cool and dust with icing sugar.

notes: Dessert.
Gluten-free if you use gluten-free baking powder. Plus 1 hour simmering the oranges, which can be done a day ahead.

title: Churros with Chocolate Sauce
summary: Crisp ridged fried dough rolled in cinnamon sugar and dunked in warm chocolate.

steps.text: Bring the water and butter to the boil in a saucepan, tip in the flour and beat with a wooden spoon until it forms a smooth ball.
Cool for 5 minutes, then beat in the egg until glossy. Spoon into a piping bag with a star nozzle.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 180°C. Pipe 10cm lengths into the oil, snip with scissors and fry for 3 minutes, until deep golden. Drain on paper towel.
Toss the churros in the sugar and cinnamon. Warm the cream until steaming, pour over the chocolate and stir until smooth, then serve for dipping.

notes: Dessert.
Keep the oil at 180°C and never leave hot oil unattended.

title: Smoked Paprika Crispy Chickpeas
summary: A crunchy, salty, smoky bar snack made in a tray.

items.raw: 800g tinned chickpeas, drained and patted dry

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan).
Toss the chickpeas with the olive oil, paprika, garlic powder and salt on a lined tray.
Roast for 30 minutes, shaking the tray halfway, until crisp and deep golden. Squeeze over the lemon juice and eat the same day.

notes: Vegan and gluten-free.

title: Thick Yoghurt Parfait with Walnut Crumb
summary: Thick yoghurt, toasted walnuts, orange segments and a thread of honey.

items.raw: 1 orange, peeled and cut into segments

steps.text: Toast the walnuts in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 4 minutes, until fragrant, then crush roughly.
Cut the orange into segments, catching any juice.
Layer the yoghurt, orange and walnuts in two glasses, then drizzle with the honey and dust with cinnamon.

notes: Dessert.
Vegetarian and gluten-free.

title: Rosewater Pistachio Shortbread
summary: Crumbly buttery shortbread scented with rose and topped with green pistachios.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan) and line two trays.
Beat the butter and icing sugar for 3 minutes, until pale. Stir in the flour, cornflour and rose water to form a soft dough.
Roll into walnut-sized balls, flatten gently and press a few pistachios into each.
Bake for 18 minutes, until just pale gold at the edges. Cool on the trays.

notes: Dessert.

title: Za'atar Labneh Dip with Flatbread Crisps
summary: Thick labneh swirled with za'atar and olive oil, scooped up with crisp flatbread.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the flatbread with 1 tbsp of the olive oil and the salt, spread on a tray and bake for 8 minutes, until crisp.
Spread the labneh in a shallow bowl, swirl in the lemon juice, then top with the remaining oil and the za'atar.
Serve with the warm crisps.

notes: Vegetarian.

title: Honey Almond Crescents
summary: Gluten-free Moroccan-style almond moons, soft and fragrant with a honey glaze.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan) and line a tray.
Mix the almond meal, icing sugar, cinnamon, egg white and orange juice into a firm paste.
Shape tablespoons of the paste into small crescents and set them on the tray. Brush with honey and scatter with sesame seeds.
Bake for 15 minutes, until lightly golden. Cool on the tray.

notes: Dessert.
Gluten-free.

title: Buttermilk Scones with Jam and Cream
summary: Tall, light scones for a proper afternoon tea.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and flour a tray.
Rub the butter into the flour and sugar with your fingertips until it looks like breadcrumbs, then stir in the buttermilk with a knife to a soft dough.
Pat out to 3cm thick on a floured bench and cut rounds with a 6cm cutter.
Bake for 15 minutes, until risen and golden. Serve warm with the whipped cream and jam.

notes: Do not twist the cutter, so the scones rise straight.

title: Sticky Ginger Cake
summary: A dark, treacly, spicy loaf that gets stickier on day two.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan) and line a 20cm tin.
Warm the butter, golden syrup, molasses and brown sugar in a saucepan over low heat until melted, then stir in the milk.
Whisk the flour, ginger, cinnamon and bicarbonate of soda in a bowl, pour in the warm syrup mixture and beat in the egg until smooth.
Pour into the tin and bake for 45 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.

notes: Dessert.
Better after a day in an airtight tin.

title: Oat Soda Bread
summary: A no-yeast Irish loaf you can have on the table within the hour.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and flour a tray.
Mix the flour, oats, bicarbonate of soda and salt in a bowl, make a well and pour in the buttermilk. Stir with a wooden spoon to a shaggy dough.
Shape into a round on the tray, cut a deep cross in the top and bake for 40 minutes, until the base sounds hollow when tapped.
Cool on a rack for 20 minutes before slicing.

notes: Vegetarian.
Best eaten the day it's made.

title: Apple Strudel Rolls
summary: Crisp filo rolls packed with cinnamon apples and sultanas.

steps.text: Cook the apple, sultanas, brown sugar, cinnamon and lemon juice in a frying pan over medium heat for 8 minutes, until the apple is just tender. Cool.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Layer two filo sheets, brushing each with butter, and scatter with a tablespoon of breadcrumbs.
Spoon a quarter of the filling along one long edge, roll up and place seam-side down on a lined tray. Repeat for four rolls and cut each in half.
Brush with the remaining butter and bake for 25 minutes, until deep golden. Dust with icing sugar.

notes: Dessert.

title: Palatschinken with Apricot Jam
summary: Thin Austrian pancakes rolled around tangy apricot jam.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, milk, water, eggs and salt until smooth and let the batter stand while the pan heats.
Melt a little butter in a 24cm non-stick frying pan over medium heat. Pour in a thin layer of batter, swirling to coat.
Cook for 1 minute each side, until golden and set, and stack the pancakes on a plate. Repeat with the remaining batter.
Spread each pancake with jam, roll up and dust with icing sugar.

notes: Dessert.
Plus 15 minutes resting the batter.

title: Lamington Squares
summary: Butter cake squares dipped in chocolate icing and rolled in coconut.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and line a 20cm square tin.
Beat the butter and caster sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs one at a time. Fold in the flour and milk.
Bake for 30 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely, then cut into 16 squares.
Sift the icing sugar and cocoa into a bowl and stir in the boiling water until smooth. Dip each square in the icing, then roll in the coconut and set on a rack.

notes: Dessert.
Day-old cake cuts cleanest, so bake it the day before.

title: Chewy Coconut Anzac Cookies
summary: Chewy oat and coconut biscuits with a golden syrup caramel edge.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan) and line two trays.
Mix the oats, flour, coconut and sugar in a bowl.
Melt the butter, golden syrup and water in a small saucepan, stir in the bicarbonate of soda and pour into the dry mix.
Roll tablespoons into balls, flatten on the trays and bake for 15 minutes, until golden. They firm up as they cool.

notes: Dessert.

title: Chocolate Zucchini Loaf
summary: A moist chocolate loaf with grated zucchini that keeps it tender.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan) and line a loaf tin.
Whisk the eggs, sugar and oil in a bowl, then stir in the zucchini.
Fold in the flour, cocoa and milk until just combined, then the chopped chocolate.
Pour into the tin and bake for 50 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tin.

notes: Dessert.

title: Fudgy Walnut Brownies
summary: Dense chocolate brownies with a shiny crust and crunchy walnuts.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan) and line a 20cm square tin.
Melt the chocolate and butter in a bowl over a pan of simmering water, stirring until smooth, then cool for 5 minutes.
Whisk in the sugar and eggs, then fold in the flour, cocoa, salt and walnuts.
Pour into the tin and bake for 28 minutes, until the top is set but the centre still has a slight wobble. Cool before cutting.

notes: Dessert.

title: Maple Roasted Pecans
summary: Crunchy pecans glazed with maple, salt and a little cayenne.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan) and line a tray.
Toss the pecans with the maple syrup, salt, cayenne and cinnamon until well coated.
Spread on the tray and roast for 15 minutes, stirring once, until glossy and fragrant. Cool completely so they crisp.

notes: Vegan and gluten-free.

title: Cinnamon Tortilla Crisps with Chocolate Dip
summary: Crunchy cinnamon sugar tortilla triangles with a warm chocolate sauce.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Brush the tortilla wedges with butter, toss in the sugar and cinnamon and spread on two trays.
Bake for 8 minutes, until crisp and golden.
Warm the cream until steaming, pour over the chocolate and stir until smooth. Serve with the crisps.

notes: Dessert.

title: Arroz con Leche
summary: Creamy cinnamon rice pudding, served warm or chilled.

steps.text: Simmer the rice with the water and cinnamon stick in a saucepan for 10 minutes, until the water is mostly absorbed.
Add the milk, sugar and raisins and cook over low heat for 25 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Remove the cinnamon stick, stir in the vanilla and dust with ground cinnamon.

notes: Dessert.
Gluten-free and vegetarian.
Food safety: cool leftovers quickly and refrigerate within an hour; reheat until steaming hot.

title: Coconut Rum Raisin Rice Pudding
summary: Rice simmered in coconut milk with warm spices and rum-soaked raisins.

steps.text: Warm the raisins and rum in a small pan for 2 minutes, then set aside to soak.
Simmer the rice, coconut milk, water, sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt in a saucepan over low heat for 30 minutes, stirring often, until thick.
Stir through the raisins and rum and serve warm.

notes: Dessert.
Vegan and gluten-free.
Food safety: cool leftovers quickly and refrigerate within an hour; reheat until steaming hot.

title: Cornflour Sandwich Biscuits
summary: Melt-in-the-mouth shortbread sandwiched with jam, inspired by South American alfajores.

steps.text: Beat the butter and icing sugar until pale, then beat in the yolks.
Stir in the cornflour, plain flour and baking powder to a soft dough. Wrap and chill.
Heat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan). Roll the dough 5mm thick, cut 5cm rounds and bake on lined trays for 12 minutes, until pale. Cool.
Sandwich pairs with jam and roll the edges in the coconut.

notes: Dessert.
Plus 30 minutes chilling.

title: Crisp Plantain Tostones
summary: Twice-fried green plantain discs with lime salt, great with any dip.

items.raw: 3 plantain, peeled and cut into thick rounds
items.prep: peeled and cut into thick rounds

steps.text: Heat the oil in a deep frying pan to 160°C and fry the plantain rounds for 3 minutes each side, until pale gold. Drain.
Press each round flat with the bottom of a glass.
Raise the oil to 180°C and fry again for 2 minutes each side, until crisp and golden. Drain on paper towel.
Toss with the salt, lime juice and garlic and serve hot.

notes: Vegan and gluten-free.

title: Coconut Bake
summary: A soft, slightly sweet Caribbean bread made with coconut milk.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a bowl, then stir in the warm coconut milk and butter to form a dough.
Knead on a floured bench for 8 minutes, until smooth and elastic. Cover and prove in a warm spot.
Divide into 8, flatten into rounds and set on a lined tray. Rest for 15 minutes.
Bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 25 minutes, until golden and hollow-sounding underneath.

notes: Plus 1 hour proving and 15 minutes resting.
Vegetarian.

title: White Bean Panzanella
summary: Crusty bread, ripe tomatoes and creamy beans soaked in a sharp red wine dressing.

steps.text: Toss the bread with 1 tbsp of the oil and toast in a hot frying pan for 5 minutes, until golden and crisp.
Combine the tomatoes, beans, cucumber and onion in a large bowl.
Whisk the remaining oil, vinegar and salt, pour over the salad, add the bread and basil, and toss. Rest for 10 minutes so the bread soaks up the juices.

notes: Vegan.

title: Pesto Mozzarella Pressed Sandwiches
summary: Crisp, golden panini filled with melting mozzarella, pesto and tomato.

steps.text: Spread the pesto on two slices of bread and top with mozzarella and tomato, then the other slices.
Brush the outsides with olive oil.
Cook in a hot frying pan, pressing down with a plate, for 4 minutes each side until golden and the cheese has melted.

notes: Vegetarian: check the pesto label for a vegetarian hard cheese.

title: Tuna Niçoise Platter
summary: Classic French salad of tuna, soft-boiled eggs, beans, potatoes and olives.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes, until tender, adding the beans for the last 3 minutes. Drain and cool.
Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are just firm, then cool in cold water, peel and halve.
Whisk the oil, mustard and vinegar. Arrange the potatoes, beans, tuna, olives, tomatoes and eggs on a platter and drizzle with the dressing.

notes: Gluten-free and pescatarian.
Food safety: boiled eggs should have fully set whites and yolks; tuna from a tin is cooked and flakes easily.

title: Leek and Goat Cheese Tart
summary: Sweet slow-cooked leeks and tangy goat cheese in a crisp pastry case.

steps.text: Cook the leeks in the butter in a frying pan over low heat for 12 minutes, until soft and sweet.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Line a 24cm tart tin with the pastry and prick the base.
Whisk the eggs and cream. Spread the leeks over the pastry, scatter with the goat cheese and thyme and pour over the egg mixture.
Bake for 35 minutes, until puffed and golden with a firm centre.

notes: Vegetarian.
Food safety: the egg filling is cooked through when the centre is firm, not wobbly.

title: Croque Monsieur
summary: Grilled ham and gruyère sandwich under a bubbling cheesy béchamel.

steps.text: Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk until the sauce thickens. Season with nutmeg and a third of the gruyère.
Spread two slices of bread with mustard, top with the ham, half the remaining gruyère and the other slices.
Place on a tray, spoon over the sauce and scatter with the rest of the gruyère.
Grill at 220°C for 10 minutes, until bubbling and golden.

notes: Food safety: ham is cooked and ready to eat; heat the sandwich until it is steaming hot in the middle.

title: Tortilla Española Wedges
summary: A thick Spanish potato and onion omelette, cooked until just set.

steps.text: Cook the potato and onion in the oil in a 24cm non-stick frying pan over medium-low heat for 15 minutes, turning, until very tender but not browned. Drain, saving 1 tbsp of the oil.
Beat the eggs and salt in a large bowl, stir in the potato mixture and rest for 5 minutes.
Heat the saved oil in the pan, add the mixture and cook over low heat for 8 minutes, until the base is golden and most of the egg is set.
Flip with a plate and cook for 4 minutes more, until the centre is cooked through. Serve warm or at room temperature.

notes: Vegetarian and gluten-free.
Food safety: egg must be fully cooked through, with no runny centre.

title: Chilled Gazpacho
summary: A cold Andalusian tomato and capsicum soup that needs no cooking.

steps.text: Blend the tomato, cucumber, capsicum, garlic, bread, vinegar and salt in batches until very smooth.
With the blender running, stream in the oil until emulsified.
Strain if you like, then chill until very cold. Taste and add more salt or vinegar.

notes: Plus 2 hours chilling.
Vegan.

title: Horiatiki Salad with Grilled Halloumi
summary: Chunky tomato and cucumber salad topped with golden halloumi.

steps.text: Combine the tomatoes, cucumber, onion and olives in a bowl.
Whisk the oil, vinegar and oregano, pour over and toss.
Fry the halloumi in a dry non-stick pan over medium-high heat for 3 minutes each side, until golden. Serve on top.

notes: Vegetarian and gluten-free.

title: Avgolemono Orzo Soup
summary: A bright, silky lemon soup with shredded chicken and orzo.

steps.text: Simmer the chicken, stock, carrot and onion in a large pot for 15 minutes, until the chicken reaches 75°C in the centre. Lift out the chicken and shred it.
Add the orzo to the stock and cook for 8 minutes, until tender.

Whisk the eggs and lemon juice, then slowly ladle in a cup of hot stock, whisking. Stir back into the pot off the heat with the chicken and dill, and warm gently until the soup thickens slightly, without boiling.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the centre and have no pink meat. Eat within 3 days.

title: Fattoush with Sumac Chickpeas
summary: Crisp pita and garden vegetables with a lemony sumac dressing and spiced chickpeas.

steps.text: Toss the pita with 1 tbsp oil and bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 10 minutes, until crisp.
Fry the chickpeas in 1 tbsp oil with 1 tsp sumac for 5 minutes, until crisp at the edges.
Toss the tomato, cucumber, lettuce and mint with the lemon juice, remaining oil and remaining sumac. Top with the pita and chickpeas just before serving.

notes: Vegan.

title: Cumin Carrot Salad with Parsley
summary: Tender carrots in a garlicky cumin and lemon dressing, served cold.

steps.text: Boil the carrots in salted water for 10 minutes, until just tender. Drain.
Toss with the garlic, cumin, paprika, oil, lemon juice and salt while still warm.
Chill, then stir through the parsley before serving.

notes: Plus 1 hour chilling.
Vegan and gluten-free.

title: Ploughman's Toastie
summary: Sharp cheddar, pickle and apple in a crisp toastie.

steps.text: Butter the bread on the outside.
Spread pickle inside two slices and top with cheddar and apple, then the other slices.
Cook in a frying pan over medium heat for 4 minutes each side, until golden and the cheese has melted.

notes: Vegetarian.

title: Coronation Chicken Sandwiches
summary: Cold poached chicken in a mild curry mayo with sultanas and almonds.

steps.text: Poach the chicken in simmering water for 15 minutes, until it reaches 75°C in the centre and the juices run clear. Cool completely, then shred.
Mix the mayonnaise, yoghurt, curry powder and chutney, then fold in the chicken, sultanas and almonds.
Fill the bread with salad leaves and the chicken mixture.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken until 75°C inside, cool quickly and keep refrigerated; eat within 2 days.

title: Buttery Leek Soup with Chives
summary: A velvety Irish-style soup with sweet leeks and buttery potato.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat and cook the leeks for 8 minutes, until soft.
Add the potato and stock and simmer for 20 minutes, until the potato falls apart.
Blend until smooth, stir in the milk and pepper and heat until steaming. Top with chives.

notes: Vegetarian and gluten-free.

title: Kartoffelpuffer with Apple Sauce
summary: Crisp, lacy potato pancakes with warm apple sauce on the side.

steps.text: Squeeze as much liquid as you can out of the grated potato in a clean tea towel, then mix with the onion, eggs, flour and salt.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Drop in heaped tablespoons and flatten.
Fry for 4 minutes each side, until deep golden and crisp, and drain on paper towel. Serve with the apple sauce and sour cream.

notes: Vegetarian.

title: Bratwurst and Sauerkraut Rolls
summary: Browned bratwurst in a soft roll with sauerkraut and sweet mustard.

steps.text: Fry the bratwurst in a pan with a little oil over medium heat for 15 minutes, turning, until browned and the centre reaches 75°C.
Add the onion for the last 8 minutes and cook until soft and golden.
Warm the sauerkraut in the pan for 2 minutes, until steaming. Fill the rolls with a sausage, onions, sauerkraut and mustard.

notes: Food safety: pork sausages must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside.

title: Corn and Zucchini Fritters with Feta
summary: Golden fritters packed with sweet corn, zucchini and salty feta.

steps.text: Mix the zucchini, corn, flour, eggs, milk, feta and spring onion in a bowl.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and fry heaped spoonfuls for 3 minutes each side, until golden and cooked through.
Serve warm with the yoghurt.

notes: Vegetarian.

title: Lemon Pepper Chicken Burgers
summary: Crispy-coated chicken on a toasted bun with lettuce and tangy mayo.

items.raw: 500g chicken breast, sliced into 4 thin steaks

steps.text: Mix the panko, pepper and lemon zest on a plate and beat the egg in a shallow bowl. Dip each chicken piece in egg, then crumbs.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the chicken for 6 minutes each side, until golden and the centre reaches 75°C.
Toast the buns until golden, spread with mayonnaise and fill with lettuce, tomato and chicken.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part and have no pink meat.

title: Olive Oil and Orange Cake
summary: A fragrant, tender dairy-free cake made with good olive oil and fresh orange.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan) and line a 22cm tin.
Whisk the eggs and sugar for 3 minutes, until pale, then whisk in the oil, orange juice and zest.
Fold in the flour and baking powder until just combined and pour into the tin.
Bake for 40 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool and dust with icing sugar.

notes: Dessert.
Dairy-free and vegetarian.

title: Honey Pears with Vanilla Mascarpone Cream
summary: Pears simmered in honey and vanilla, served with softly whipped mascarpone cream.

steps.text: Simmer the pears with the honey, half the vanilla and the water in a covered saucepan for 20 minutes, until a knife slides in easily.
Lift out the pears and boil the syrup for 5 minutes, until reduced and glossy.
Whisk the mascarpone, cream, icing sugar and remaining vanilla until soft peaks form.
Serve the pears warm with the cream, a spoonful of syrup and the pistachios.

notes: Dessert.
Vegetarian and gluten-free.

title: Rosemary Sea Salt Focaccia
summary: A deep-dimpled, olive oil-rich loaf with a crisp base and chewy middle.

steps.text: Stir the flour, yeast, 2 tsp salt, water and 2 tbsp oil in a large bowl to a sticky dough. Cover and rest until doubled.
Pour 2 tbsp oil into a 25 x 35cm tray, tip in the dough and stretch it to the corners. Rest for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Dimple the dough with oiled fingers, drizzle with the remaining oil and scatter with the rosemary and 1 tsp salt.
Bake for 25 minutes, until deep golden. Cool on a rack.

notes: Plus about 2 hours resting and rising.
Vegan.

title: Pear and Almond Clafoutis
summary: A custardy baked batter around soft pears, finished with a dusting of sugar.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and butter a 24cm baking dish. Arrange the pears in the dish.
Whisk the eggs and sugar, then whisk in the flour, almond meal, milk, cream and vanilla until smooth.
Pour the batter over the pears and bake for 35 minutes, until puffed, golden and set in the centre. Dust with icing sugar and serve warm.

notes: Dessert.
Vegetarian.

title: Crème Caramel
summary: A classic baked custard with a bittersweet caramel that pools around it.

steps.text: Heat the white sugar and water in a saucepan over medium heat, without stirring, for 8 minutes, until a deep amber caramel forms. Pour quickly into six ramekins.
Heat the oven to 150°C (130°C fan). Warm the milk and cream until steaming.
Whisk the whole eggs, yolks, caster sugar and vanilla, then slowly whisk in the warm milk. Strain into the ramekins.
Set the ramekins in a deep roasting dish and pour in boiling water to halfway up their sides. Bake for 40 minutes, until set with a slight wobble and the custard reaches 75°C.
Cool, chill, then run a knife around the edge and turn out onto plates.

notes: Dessert.
Plus 4 hours chilling.
Food safety: bake the custard until it reaches 75°C so the egg is fully cooked.
Gluten-free.

title: Crema Catalana
summary: Cinnamon and lemon-scented custard under a crackling burnt sugar crust.

steps.text: Heat the milk with the lemon zest and cinnamon stick until steaming, then take off the heat and infuse for 15 minutes.
Whisk the yolks, caster sugar and cornflour until pale, then strain in the hot milk.
Return to the pan and stir over low heat for 6 minutes, until thick and reaching 75°C. Pour into six shallow dishes and chill.
Sprinkle with the white sugar and caramelise with a blowtorch or under a very hot grill until bubbling and amber.

notes: Dessert.
Plus 3 hours chilling.
Food safety: heat the custard to 75°C so the yolks are fully cooked.
Vegetarian; gluten-free if you use cornflour labelled gluten-free.

title: Lemon Olive Oil Polvorones
summary: Crumbly Spanish shortbreads made with olive oil and almond.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan) and line a tray.
Toast the flour in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 5 minutes, until pale gold, then cool.
Stir the flour, almond meal, oil, 1/3 cup icing sugar and the lemon zest into a soft dough.
Roll into 24 balls, flatten slightly and bake for 20 minutes, until just coloured. Cool on the tray, then dust with the remaining icing sugar.

notes: Dessert.
Vegan.

title: Honey Loukoumades
summary: Crisp-shelled, fluffy Greek doughnut puffs drenched in warm honey and cinnamon.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, yeast, sugar, salt and warm water to a thick, sticky batter. Cover and rest until doubled and bubbling.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 180°C. Drop in tablespoons of batter, using a wet spoon, and fry for 3 minutes, turning, until deep golden.
Drain on paper towel, then toss with the warm honey and finish with cinnamon and walnuts.

notes: Dessert.
Plus 1 hour rising.
Vegan if you swap the honey for maple syrup.

title: Walnut Baklava Bites
summary: Crisp layers of buttery filo with a cinnamon walnut filling and a lemon honey syrup.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan). Mix the walnuts, caster sugar, cinnamon and cloves.
Brush a 20cm square tin with butter and layer in 4 sheets of filo, brushing each with butter and trimming to fit. Scatter over half the filling.
Add 4 more buttered sheets and the rest of the filling, then finish with the last 4 sheets, buttering the top.
Cut into 12 squares and bake for 40 minutes, until deep golden.
Simmer the white sugar, honey, water and lemon juice for 8 minutes, until syrupy. Pour the cooled syrup over the hot baklava.

notes: Dessert.
Keep the filo covered with a damp cloth while you work.
Plus 3 hours standing so the syrup soaks in.

title: Spinach and Feta Triangles
summary: Crisp filo parcels of spinach, feta and dill.

items.raw: 300g frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry

steps.text: Mix the spinach, feta, egg, spring onion and dill.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cut the filo into long strips, brush with butter and place a spoonful of filling at one end.
Fold each strip over the filling like a flag, working down the strip into a triangle. Place seam-side down on a lined tray and brush with butter.
Bake for 25 minutes, until crisp and deep golden.

notes: Vegetarian.

title: Roasted Capsicum and Walnut Muhammara
summary: A smoky, tangy Syrian dip with roasted capsicum, walnuts and pomegranate molasses.

steps.text: Blitz the capsicum, walnuts, breadcrumbs, molasses, garlic, cumin, chilli and salt in a food processor until almost smooth.
With the motor running, stream in the oil until thick and spoonable.
Taste and season, then serve with flatbread or raw vegetables.

notes: Vegan. Use gluten-free breadcrumbs or a spoonful of ground almonds to keep it gluten-free.

title: Coconut Semolina Cake with Lemon Syrup
summary: A moist, golden semolina and coconut cake cut into diamonds and soaked in syrup.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and grease a 20cm square tin.
Mix the semolina, coconut, flour, caster sugar and baking powder, then stir in the yoghurt and butter to a thick batter.
Spread into the tin, cut into 12 diamonds and press an almond into each. Bake for 35 minutes, until golden.
Meanwhile simmer the white sugar, water and lemon juice for 8 minutes, until syrupy, then stir in the rose water. Pour the cooled syrup over the hot cake.

notes: Dessert.

title: Cinnamon Orange Salad with Honey
summary: Chilled orange slices with cinnamon, honey and a little mint, a light Moroccan finish to a meal.

items.raw: 4 orange, peeled and sliced into rounds

steps.text: Arrange the orange slices on a platter.
Drizzle with the honey, sprinkle with cinnamon, then chill until cold.
Scatter with the mint and pistachios to serve.

notes: Dessert.
Plus 30 minutes chilling.
Vegetarian and gluten-free.

title: Beghrir with Honey Butter
summary: Moroccan thousand-hole semolina pancakes, cooked on one side only.

steps.text: Blend the semolina, flour, yeast, baking powder, sugar, salt and water until very smooth. Rest for 20 minutes, until bubbly.
Heat a non-stick frying pan over medium heat and pour in a small ladle of batter, cooking one side only for 2 minutes, until the top is covered in tiny holes and set.
Slide out onto a clean tea towel and repeat with the remaining batter.
Melt the butter with the honey until smooth and serve poured over the pancakes.

notes: Plus 20 minutes resting.
Vegetarian.

title: Classic Victoria Sponge
summary: Two light butter cake layers sandwiched with jam and whipped cream.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and line two 20cm tins.
Beat the butter and sugar for 4 minutes, until pale and fluffy, then beat in the eggs one at a time. Fold in the flour, milk and vanilla.
