Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Put the pork skin-side up on a rack over a tray with the bay leaves and 1 cup water, and roast for 30 minutes, until the skin starts to blister.
Reduce to 150°C (130°C fan) and roast for 4 hours, until the meat is very tender and reads 90°C in the centre.
Raise the oven to 230°C (210°C fan) for 15 minutes, until the crackling is crisp. Rest for 20 minutes, then pull the meat apart.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C inside; for pulled pork 90°C gives the best texture. Rest it before carving.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Venezuelan-Style Shredded Beef and Black Bean Bowls
summary: Slow-cooked shredded beef with black beans, rice and fried plantain.

steps.text: Brown the beef in 1 tablespoon of oil in a heavy pot for 8 minutes, until deep golden, then add the onion, capsicum, garlic and cumin for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and stock, cover and simmer very gently for 2 hours, until the beef shreds easily. Shred it in the sauce.
Warm the beans in a small pan for 5 minutes, until hot. Cook the rice in boiling water for 12 minutes, until tender, and drain.
Fry the plantain in the remaining oil for 3 minutes each side, until golden and soft. Serve the beef over rice with beans, plantain and cheese.

notes: Food safety: beef chuck is safe at 75°C and tender once it shreds; the sauce should be steaming hot.
Gluten-free.

title: Colombian-Style Scrambled Eggs on Corn Tortillas
summary: Tomato and spring onion scrambled eggs on warm, lightly toasted corn tortillas.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the spring onion and tomato for 3 minutes, until soft and juicy.
Whisk the eggs with a pinch of salt, pour in and stir gently for 3 minutes, until just set.
Toast the tortillas in a dry pan for 30 seconds each side, until warm and flecked.
Pile the eggs on the tortillas and top with avocado and coriander.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until set with no raw egg left if serving to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Vegetarian. Gluten-free.

title: Argentine Skirt Steak with Chimichurri and Potatoes
summary: Charred skirt steak with a parsley, garlic and vinegar chimichurri and crisp roast potatoes.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the potato with 3 tablespoons of oil and salt and roast for 35 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
Mix the parsley, oregano, garlic, vinegar, 1/2 cup oil and chilli flakes for the chimichurri and leave it to sit for 15 minutes.
Season the steak and cook in a very hot pan for 3 minutes each side for medium-rare, until charred and a thermometer reads 55°C, then rest for 5 minutes.
Slice the steak across the grain and serve with the potatoes and plenty of chimichurri.

notes: Food safety: a whole steak is safe once seared on the outside; 55°C is medium-rare, 63°C medium, 71°C well done. Serve minced or pierced cuts well done.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Peruvian-Style Roast Chicken with Lime and Cumin
summary: Chicken pieces rubbed with cumin, paprika and lime, roasted until crisp-skinned.

steps.text: Mix the garlic, lime juice, cumin, paprika, oregano, soy sauce and oil. Rub it over the chicken and marinate for 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Spread the potato and onion on a large tray and set the chicken on top.
Roast for 45 minutes, turning the potato once, until the chicken is golden and the potato is crisp.
Check the thickest piece reaches 75°C, rest for 5 minutes and serve with the pan juices.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part, with clear juices.

title: Tapioca Cheese Rolls
summary: Chewy, airy tapioca bread rolls with melted cheese in the middle.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line a tray with baking paper.
Bring the milk, oil, water and salt to the boil in a pot, then pour over the tapioca starch in a bowl and stir until a sticky dough forms. Cool for 10 minutes.
Beat in the egg until smooth, then fold through the cheese.
Roll tablespoons of dough into balls, set them 3cm apart on the tray and bake for 25 minutes, until puffed and pale golden.

notes: Food safety: the egg cooks through in the oven; the puffs are done when golden and no longer wet inside.
Vegetarian. Gluten-free.

title: Plantain and Egg Breakfast Plate
summary: Sweet fried plantain, soft eggs, black beans and avocado.

items.raw: 2 plantain, ripe and sliced on the diagonal
items.prep: ripe and sliced on the diagonal

steps.text: Warm the black beans in a small pan for 4 minutes, until hot.
Fry the plantain in the oil in a frying pan for 3 minutes each side, until deep golden and soft. Lift out onto a plate.
Fry the eggs in the same pan for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Serve the plantain, eggs, beans and avocado with coriander and lime.

notes: Food safety: cook until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Vegetarian. Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Chermoula Chicken Braise with Green Olives
summary: Chicken braised in a fresh herb and spice chermoula with green olives and preserved lemon.

steps.text: Blend the coriander, parsley, garlic, cumin, paprika, oil and lemon juice into a loose paste. Coat the chicken and marinate for 1 hour.
Cook the onion in a wide pot for 5 minutes, until soft. Add the chicken and chermoula and brown for 6 minutes.
Add the stock, preserved lemon and olives, cover and simmer for 35 minutes, until the chicken reaches 75°C.
Soak the couscous in 1 1/2 cups of boiling water for 5 minutes, then fluff and serve under the chicken.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part, with juices running clear.

title: Moroccan Slow-Roast Lamb Shoulder
summary: Lamb shoulder rubbed with ras el hanout and honey, slow-roasted until it pulls apart.

steps.text: Mix the ras el hanout, garlic, oil, honey and lemon juice into a paste and rub it all over the lamb. Rest for at least 2 hours.
Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Sit the lamb on the onion in a deep roasting dish, pour in the stock and cover tightly with foil.
Roast for 4 hours, until very tender and 90°C in the centre. Add the apricots for the last 30 minutes.
Uncover, raise the heat to 220°C (200°C fan) and roast for 15 minutes, until the top is dark and sticky. Rest for 15 minutes and scatter with almonds.

notes: Food safety: lamb shoulder is safe at 63°C, and slow-roasted until 90°C it pulls apart. Rest before carving.

title: Tunisian Egg Brik with Tuna and Capers
summary: Crisp filo parcels with a runny egg, tuna, capers and parsley.

steps.text: Mix the tuna, capers, parsley, spring onion and cheese in a bowl.
Lay two filo sheets on the bench, brush the top with oil and spoon the tuna mix into the centre, pressing a small well in it. Crack an egg into the well.
Fold the filo over into a triangle and seal the edges quickly with a little oil.
Shallow-fry each brik in the remaining oil for 2 minutes per side, until deep golden and crisp. Serve hot with lemon.

notes: Food safety: the yolk is meant to stay soft; cook it until firm, or skip this dish, for young children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Pescatarian.

title: Harissa Roast Chicken with Chickpeas
summary: A whole chicken rubbed with harissa and roasted over sweet onions and chickpeas.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Mix the harissa, oil and lemon juice and rub it over and under the skin of the chicken.
Toss the chickpeas, onion, garlic and cumin in a roasting dish and sit the chicken on top.
Roast for 1 hour 20 minutes, until the skin is dark and crisp and the thigh juices run clear, with the thickest part at 75°C.
Rest for 15 minutes, scatter with coriander and serve with yoghurt.

notes: Food safety: whole chicken must reach 75°C at the thickest part of the thigh; rest it before carving.
Gluten-free.

title: Chermoula Baked Fish with Tomatoes and Potatoes
summary: White fish fillets baked on potato and tomato under a fresh chermoula.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Layer the potato in an oiled baking dish, season and roast for 15 minutes, until starting to soften.
Mix the coriander, parsley, garlic, cumin, paprika, oil and lemon juice into a chermoula.
Layer the tomato over the potato, set the fish on top and spoon over the chermoula.
Bake for 18 minutes, until the fish turns opaque and flakes easily and the potato is tender. Serve with lemon.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when opaque and it flakes with a fork.

title: Spiced Chickpea Breakfast Plate with Poached Eggs
summary: Warm cumin-spiced chickpeas topped with poached eggs, yoghurt and herbs.

steps.text: Warm the oil in a pan and cook the garlic, cumin and paprika for 1 minute, until fragrant. Add the chickpeas and tomato and simmer for 6 minutes, mashing a few chickpeas, until thick.
Poach the eggs in barely simmering water for 3 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks soft.
Spoon the chickpeas into bowls, top with yoghurt and the eggs.
Finish with parsley and a swirl of harissa.

notes: Food safety: cook until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Vegetarian. Gluten-free.

title: Lamb, Apricot and Almond Tagine
summary: Tender lamb braised with apricots, honey and warm spices, finished with toasted almonds.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil in a heavy pot for 8 minutes, until golden, then lift out. Cook the onion in the same pot for 6 minutes, until soft.
Add the garlic, cumin, ginger, cinnamon and saffron for 1 minute, then return the lamb with the tomatoes and stock.
Cover and simmer gently for 1 hour 15 minutes, until the lamb is tender. Add the apricots and honey and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, until the sauce thickens.
Soak the couscous in 2 cups of boiling water for 5 minutes, fluff and serve with the tagine, scattered with almonds.

notes: Food safety: lamb is safe at 63°C; this braise is cooked long past that, and the stew should be steaming hot.

title: Seven-Vegetable Couscous
summary: A large dish of fluffy couscous with a fragrant vegetable and chickpea stew.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil in a wide pot for 6 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, ras el hanout and turmeric for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and stock, then the carrot, turnip and pumpkin. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes, until nearly tender.
Add the zucchini, chickpeas and raisins and simmer for 12 minutes, until all the vegetables are tender.
Soak the couscous in 2 cups of boiling water for 5 minutes, fluff with a fork and serve under the vegetables, scattered with parsley.

notes: Vegan.

title: Prawns in Spicy Chermoula Tomato with Couscous
summary: Prawns cooked in a spiced tomato and herb sauce over fluffy couscous.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, until soft, then add the garlic, cumin, paprika and chilli for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes, until thick.
Stir in the prawns and cook for 4 minutes, until pink, curled and opaque.
Soak the couscous in 1 1/2 cups of boiling water for 5 minutes, fluff and serve under the prawns with coriander and lemon juice.

notes: Food safety: prawns are cooked when pink, curled and opaque all the way through.

title: Maqluba Upside-Down Chicken and Rice
summary: A fragrant pot of spiced chicken, fried eggplant and rice turned out like a cake.

steps.text: Boil the chicken with the onion and half the spices in water for 25 minutes, until cooked through, then drain, saving 3 cups of the stock. Rinse the rice and soak for 20 minutes.
Fry the eggplant in the oil for 3 minutes each side, until golden, and drain on paper.
Line the base of a large pot with the tomato, then the eggplant, then the chicken. Toss the rice with the remaining spices and layer over the top.
Pour over the stock, bring to the boil, cover and cook on low for 35 minutes, until the rice is tender and the stock absorbed. Rest for 10 minutes.
Turn the pot out onto a platter, scatter with pine nuts and serve with yoghurt.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C right through before layering; rest the rice covered and refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Gluten-free.

title: Lamb and Pistachio Kofta with Sumac Onions
summary: Herby spiced lamb skewers with pistachios, served with sumac onions and warm flatbread.

steps.text: Mix the lamb, pistachios, grated onion, garlic, cumin, coriander, allspice, parsley and a good pinch of salt. Shape into 12 long ovals and chill for 20 minutes.
Toss the red onion with the sumac and a pinch of salt and leave to soften.
Cook the kofta in the oil in a hot pan for 10 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through at 75°C.
Warm the flatbread and serve the kofta with the sumac onions and yoghurt.

notes: Food safety: lamb mince must reach 75°C all the way through; no pink should remain.

title: Fatteh with Chickpeas and Garlic Yoghurt
summary: Crisp pita layered with warm chickpeas and garlicky yoghurt, topped with toasted pine nuts.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the pita with the oil and bake for 8 minutes, until crisp and golden.
Warm the chickpeas with the cumin and a splash of water for 6 minutes, until hot and soft.
Stir the yoghurt, garlic and tahini together. Brown the pine nuts in the butter in a small pan for 3 minutes, until golden.
Layer the pita, chickpeas and yoghurt in a dish and pour over the pine nut butter. Finish with parsley.

notes: Vegetarian.

title: Sabich Eggplant and Egg Pita
summary: Fried eggplant and boiled egg in a pita with tahini, tomato and pickles.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, until hard, then cool, peel and slice.
Fry the eggplant in the oil in batches for 3 minutes each side, until golden and soft. Drain on paper.
Whisk the tahini with the lemon juice and 3 tablespoons of water until smooth.
Open the pita and fill with eggplant, egg, tomato, cucumber, pickles and parsley, then spoon in the tahini and amchur.

notes: Food safety: hard-boil the eggs until firm; refrigerate leftovers.
Vegetarian.

title: Chicken Musakhan with Sumac Onions
summary: Roast chicken piled on flatbread with sumac-sweet onions and toasted pine nuts.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Rub the chicken with half the oil, 1 tablespoon of sumac, allspice and cinnamon and roast for 40 minutes, until golden.
Cook the onion in the remaining oil for 15 minutes, until very soft and sweet. Stir in the remaining sumac.
Check the chicken reaches 75°C, then warm the flatbread in the oven for 3 minutes.
Top the flatbread with the onions and chicken, scatter with pine nuts and parsley and serve with yoghurt.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part, with clear juices.

title: Layered Lamb and Bulgur Kibbeh Tray
summary: Layers of spiced bulgur and lamb with a sweet lamb and pine nut filling, baked until golden.

steps.text: Soak the bulgur in cold water for 20 minutes, then drain and squeeze dry. Blend with the 500g mince, grated onion, allspice, cinnamon and salt into a smooth paste.
Cook the diced onion in 1 tablespoon of oil for 5 minutes, then add the 300g mince, pine nuts and cumin and cook for 8 minutes, until browned and cooked through. Cool.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Press half the kibbeh paste into an oiled baking dish, spread the filling over, then top with the remaining paste and smooth it.
Score into diamonds, drizzle with the remaining oil and bake for 40 minutes, until deep golden and cooked through. Serve with yoghurt.

notes: Food safety: lamb mince must reach 75°C right through; the middle of the kibbeh should be steaming hot.
Contains gluten (bulgur).

title: Eggs with Za'atar and Labneh on Flatbread
summary: Soft eggs with olive oil, za'atar and tangy labneh on warm flatbread.

steps.text: Warm the flatbread in a dry pan or oven for 2 minutes, until soft.
Fry the eggs in half the oil for 3 minutes, until the whites are set and edges crisp.
Spread the labneh over the flatbread and top with the eggs.
Drizzle with the remaining oil, scatter with za'atar and serve with cucumber, tomato, mint and olives.

notes: Food safety: cook until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Vegetarian.

title: Spiced Beef and Rice Stuffed Zucchini
summary: Hollowed zucchini filled with spiced beef and rice and simmered in tomato sauce.

steps.text: Cut the top off each zucchini and scoop out the flesh with an apple corer, keeping the walls about 5mm thick.
Mix the mince, rice, allspice, cinnamon, parsley, oil and a good pinch of salt. Fill each zucchini only two-thirds full as the rice swells.
Pack the zucchini into a wide pot. Mix the tomatoes, stock, paste and lemon juice and pour over.
Cover and simmer for 45 minutes, until the zucchini and rice are tender. Serve with yoghurt.

notes: Food safety: the mince filling must reach 75°C right through; the rice should be soft and the sauce steaming hot.
Gluten-free.

title: Saffron Chicken with Pomegranate and Walnuts
summary: Chicken in a tangy, nutty pomegranate molasses sauce lifted with saffron.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil in a heavy pot for 8 minutes, until golden, then lift out. Cook the onion for 6 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the walnuts and toast for 3 minutes, until fragrant. Add the molasses, saffron, cinnamon, stock and honey and bring to a simmer.
Return the chicken, cover and simmer very gently for 40 minutes, until the chicken reaches 75°C and the sauce is thick and dark.
Cook the rice in boiling water for 12 minutes, until tender, drain and serve with the chicken, scattered with pomegranate.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part, with clear juices.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Roast Eggplant with Spiced Lamb and Pine Nuts
summary: Soft roasted eggplant halves topped with spiced lamb, tahini yoghurt and pine nuts.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Score the eggplant flesh, brush with half the oil and roast cut-side up for 35 minutes, until soft and golden.
Cook the onion in the remaining oil for 5 minutes, then add the lamb, garlic and spices and cook for 8 minutes, until browned and cooked through. Stir in the paste.
Mix the yoghurt and tahini with a splash of water.
Pile the lamb onto the eggplant, then top with the yoghurt, pine nuts and parsley.

notes: Food safety: lamb mince must reach 75°C right through before serving.
Gluten-free.

title: Jamaican-Style Curry Lamb
summary: Lamb shoulder braised with curry powder, allspice, thyme and scotch bonnet until meltingly tender.

steps.text: Toss the lamb with half the curry powder, the allspice, garlic and ginger and marinate for 2 hours.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot, add the remaining curry powder and the onion and cook for 6 minutes, until soft. Add the lamb and brown for 8 minutes.
Add the water, scotch bonnet and thyme, cover and simmer for 1 hour 15 minutes, until the lamb is tender. Add the potato and carrot and cook for 20 minutes, until soft. Remove the scotch bonnet.
Cook the rice in boiling water for 12 minutes, until tender, then drain and serve with the curry.

notes: Food safety: lamb is safe at 63°C; this braise is cooked far beyond that. Handle scotch bonnet with gloves and keep it whole for gentle heat.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Callaloo-Style Egg Scramble with Fried Plantain
summary: Greens, tomato and thyme scrambled with eggs and served with golden fried plantain.

steps.text: Fry the plantain in the coconut oil for 3 minutes each side, until golden and caramelised. Lift out.
Cook the spring onion, garlic, thyme and tomato in the oil for 3 minutes, until soft.
Add the spinach and cook for 2 minutes, until wilted, then pour in the whisked eggs.
Stir gently for 3 minutes, until just set. Serve with the plantain.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until set with no raw egg left if serving to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Vegetarian. Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Garlicky Black Bean and Plantain Rice Bowls
summary: Garlicky black beans over rice with fried plantain, avocado and lime.

steps.text: Cook the onion and capsicum in the olive oil for 6 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, cumin and oregano for 1 minute.
Add the beans, bay leaf and 1/2 cup water and simmer for 15 minutes, until thick. Stir in the vinegar.
Cook the rice in boiling water for 12 minutes, until tender, and drain. Fry the plantain in the neutral oil for 3 minutes each side, until golden.
Serve the beans over rice with plantain, avocado and lime.

notes: Vegan. Gluten-free.

title: Puerto Rican-Style Chicken with Sofrito and Olives
summary: Chicken thighs simmered in a garlicky pepper sofrito with green olives and potato.

steps.text: Blend the capsicum, onion, garlic, coriander, cumin and oregano into a rough sofrito.
Brown the chicken in the oil in a wide pot for 8 minutes, until golden. Add the sofrito and tomato paste and cook for 5 minutes, until thick.
Add the stock, olives and potato, cover and simmer for 30 minutes, until the potato is tender and the chicken reaches 75°C.
Uncover and simmer for 5 minutes, until the sauce thickens.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part, with clear juices.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Coconut Prawn Skewers with Pineapple
summary: Prawns and pineapple threaded onto skewers, glazed with a coconut, lime and chilli marinade.

steps.text: Mix the coconut cream, lime juice, garlic, ginger and chilli, then toss the prawns through.
Thread the prawns and pineapple onto skewers.
Cook on a hot, oiled grill pan for 4 minutes, turning once, until the prawns are pink and opaque and the pineapple is charred.
Cook the rice in boiling water for 12 minutes, until tender, and serve with the skewers and coriander.

notes: Food safety: prawns are cooked when pink, curled and opaque all the way through; don't re-use the raw prawn marinade as a sauce unless boiled.

title: Jamaican Cornmeal Porridge
summary: Creamy cornmeal porridge cooked in coconut milk with nutmeg, cinnamon and vanilla.

steps.text: Whisk the polenta with 1 cup of the water to make a smooth slurry.
Bring the remaining water, coconut milk, cinnamon stick, nutmeg and salt to a gentle simmer, until steaming.
Stir in the polenta slurry and cook for 15 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Remove the cinnamon, stir through the sugar and vanilla and serve hot.

notes: Vegan. Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Haitian-Style Griot Pork with Citrus
summary: Pork shoulder simmered in citrus and spices, then browned until crisp at the edges.

steps.text: Combine the pork, orange juice, lime juice, garlic, onion, scotch bonnet, thyme and salt and marinate for 2 hours.
Simmer the pork and marinade in a pot with 1 cup water for 45 minutes, until tender. Drain and keep the liquid.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and fry the pork for 12 minutes, turning, until browned and crisp at the edges and 70°C in the middle.
Fry the plantain in the pan for 3 minutes each side, until golden. Serve with the pork and pickled cabbage.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach 70°C inside; keep the scotch bonnet whole and remove before serving.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Caribbean Pumpkin and Coconut Curry
summary: A mild, sweet pumpkin and chickpea curry in coconut milk with thyme and allspice.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, ginger, curry powder and allspice for 1 minute.
Add the pumpkin, thyme, chickpeas and coconut milk with 1/2 cup water. Simmer for 20 minutes, until the pumpkin is tender.
Stir through the spinach for 2 minutes, until wilted.
Cook the rice in boiling water for 12 minutes, until tender, and serve with the curry.

notes: Vegan. Gluten-free.

title: Hungarian Lecso with Smoked Sausage
summary: Capsicum and tomato stewed with onion and paprika, with smoked sausage and a poached egg.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 6 minutes, until soft, then stir in the paprika for 30 seconds.
Add the capsicum and cook for 8 minutes, then add the tomato and simmer for 10 minutes, until thick and sweet.
Add the sausage and cook for 5 minutes, until hot all the way through.
Make four wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 4 minutes, until the whites are set. Serve with bread and parsley.

notes: Food safety: cook the whites until set; the sausage must be steaming hot (75°C) inside.

title: Polish Cabbage Rolls in Tomato Sauce
summary: Cabbage leaves wrapped around pork, beef and rice and baked in a tomato sauce.

steps.text: Boil the whole cabbage for 10 minutes, until the leaves peel away easily. Cut out the core and separate 12 leaves, shaving the thick ribs.
Cook the onion in the oil for 5 minutes. Mix with the mince, rice, egg, paprika and 1 teaspoon of salt.
Place a spoonful of filling on each leaf, fold in the sides and roll tightly.

Pack the rolls seam-side down in a baking dish, pour over the tomatoes, stock and tomato paste, cover and bake at 180°C (160°C fan) for 1 hour 30 minutes, until the rice is tender and the filling reaches 75°C.
Rest for 10 minutes and scatter with parsley.

notes: Food safety: mince filling must reach 75°C right through.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Swiss Rosti with Fried Eggs and Smoked Salmon
summary: Crisp grated-potato cake topped with fried egg and silky smoked salmon.

steps.text: Squeeze the grated potato and onion in a clean tea towel to remove the liquid, then season with salt.
Heat the butter and oil in a non-stick pan and press the potato into a flat round about 2cm thick.
Cook over medium heat for 10 minutes per side, until deep golden and crisp, flipping with a plate.
Fry the eggs for 3 minutes, until the whites are set. Top the rosti with the eggs, salmon, creme fraiche and chives.

notes: Food safety: cook until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to children, older people or anyone pregnant. Smoked salmon is not recommended during pregnancy.
Gluten-free. Pescatarian.

title: Czech-Style Roast Pork with Caraway and Sauerkraut
summary: Caraway-crusted pork shoulder roasted until tender, served with sauerkraut and potatoes.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Rub the pork with the caraway, garlic, oil and salt and sit it on the onion in a roasting dish.
Pour the beer around the pork, cover and roast for 30 minutes.
Reduce to 160°C (140°C fan), add the potato to the dish and roast for 1 hour 30 minutes, uncovering for the last 30, until the pork reaches 85°C and is tender.
Warm the sauerkraut for 5 minutes, until hot. Rest the pork for 15 minutes, slice and serve with the potatoes, pan juices and sauerkraut.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C inside; at 85°C the shoulder slices cleanly.
Dairy-free.

title: Kasespatzle with Caramelised Onion
summary: Swabian egg noodles layered with melted cheese and sweet, sticky onions.

steps.text: Cook the onion with 2 tablespoons of the butter and the oil over low heat for 25 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden and sweet.
Beat the flour, eggs, milk, nutmeg and salt into a thick, elastic batter and rest it for 10 minutes.
Press the batter through a spatzle maker or colander into a pot of salted boiling water in batches. Cook for 2 minutes, until they float, and lift out.
Layer the spatzle with the cheeses in a warm dish, tossing with the remaining butter until melted and stringy. Top with the onions and chives.

notes: Food safety: the noodle batter contains raw egg: cook it until the noodles float and are firm.
Vegetarian.

title: Porchetta-Style Pork Belly with Fennel and Rosemary
summary: Rolled pork belly packed with garlic, fennel and herbs, roasted until the crackling shatters.

items.raw: 2 tbsp fennel seeds, toasted and crushed

steps.text: Score the pork skin and pat it very dry. Mix the garlic, fennel, rosemary, parsley, lemon zest, oil, chilli and 1 tablespoon of salt and spread it over the meat side.
Roll the belly up tightly and tie with string at 3cm intervals. Rub the remaining salt over the skin and leave uncovered in the fridge overnight.
Heat the oven to 240°C (220°C fan) and roast for 30 minutes, until the skin starts to blister.
Reduce to 160°C (140°C fan) and roast for 2 hours 30 minutes, until the centre reaches 80°C. Rest for 20 minutes, then slice with a serrated knife.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre; 80°C gives a tender, sliceable roll. Rest it before carving.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Lasagne al Forno with Slow Beef Ragu and Bechamel
summary: Layers of rich beef ragu, silky bechamel and fresh pasta baked until bubbling.

steps.text: Cook the onion, carrot and celery in the oil for 8 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, brown the minces for 10 minutes, then stir in the paste and wine.
Add the tomatoes, partly cover and simmer for 1 hour 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and rich and the mince is fully cooked.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk and cook for 8 minutes, until it thickens. Add the nutmeg and salt.
Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Layer ragu, pasta and bechamel in a dish, finishing with bechamel and the cheeses.
Bake for 40 minutes, until golden and bubbling. Rest for 15 minutes before cutting.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C right through; the lasagne should be steaming hot in the middle.
Contains gluten, dairy and egg (pasta).

title: Chicken Cacciatore with Olives and Capers
summary: Chicken braised with tomatoes, capsicum, olives and capers, hunter-style.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil in a wide pot for 8 minutes, until golden, and lift out.
Cook the onion and capsicum for 6 minutes, until soft, then add the garlic and wine and boil for 2 minutes.
Return the chicken with the tomatoes, olives, capers and rosemary, cover and simmer for 35 minutes, until the chicken reaches 75°C.
Uncover and simmer for 5 minutes, until the sauce thickens. Scatter with parsley.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part, with clear juices.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Eggs in Purgatory
summary: Eggs poached in a spicy tomato sauce with chilli and garlic, served with crusty bread.

steps.text: Warm the oil in a deep frying pan and cook the garlic and chilli for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and oregano and simmer for 12 minutes, until thick.
Make four wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 5 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks soft.
Scatter with basil and parmesan and serve with the bread.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.

title: Polenta with Mushroom Ragu
summary: Creamy polenta under a deep, garlicky mushroom and herb ragu.

steps.text: Cook the mushrooms in the oil in a wide pan in two batches for 8 minutes each, until deeply browned. Add the garlic and thyme for 1 minute.
Add the wine and paste and simmer for 5 minutes, until glossy.
Bring the stock to the boil, whisk in the polenta and cook over low heat for 25 minutes, stirring often, until thick and tender.
Stir the butter and cheese through the polenta and serve topped with the mushrooms and parsley.

notes: Vegetarian. Gluten-free.

title: Baked Fish Livornese-Style
summary: White fish baked in a tomato, olive and caper sauce with potatoes.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the potato with half the oil and roast in a baking dish for 20 minutes, until half tender.
Cook the garlic and chilli in the remaining oil for 1 minute, add the tomatoes, olives and capers and simmer for 8 minutes.
Nestle the fish into the dish, spoon over the sauce and bake for 15 minutes, until the fish turns opaque and flakes easily.
Scatter the parsley over the finished dish just before serving it, while hot.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when opaque and it flakes easily with a fork.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Fennel Sausages Baked with Cannellini and Rosemary
summary: Fennel sausages baked with cannellini beans, tomato and rosemary.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cook the onion in the oil in an ovenproof pan for 5 minutes, until soft, then add the garlic.
Add the beans, tomatoes, stock and rosemary and bring to a simmer, until bubbling.
Nestle in the sausages and bake for 35 minutes, turning once, until browned and cooked through at 75°C.
Scatter the parsley over the finished dish just before serving it, while hot.

notes: Food safety: sausages must reach 75°C right through, with no pink left.
Gluten-free: check the sausage label.

title: Spinach and Ricotta Cannelloni
summary: Pasta tubes filled with ricotta and spinach, baked under tomato sauce and melted cheese.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Mix the spinach, ricotta, egg, nutmeg and salt.
Cook the garlic in the oil for 1 minute, add the passata and simmer for 8 minutes, until slightly thick.
Spread 3/4 cup of sauce over a baking dish, spoon filling along each pasta sheet, roll up and lay seam-side down.
Pour over the rest of the sauce, top with mozzarella and bake for 35 minutes, until bubbling and golden. Scatter with basil.

notes: Food safety: the filling contains raw egg and cooks to set in the oven; the dish should be steaming hot in the centre.
Vegetarian.

title: Lemon Ricotta Griddle Cakes with Warm Honey
summary: Fluffy ricotta pancakes served with warm honey and lemon.

steps.text: Whisk the ricotta, egg yolks, milk and lemon zest in a bowl, then fold through the flour and baking powder.
Whisk the egg whites until they hold soft peaks and fold them in gently.
Cook spoonfuls in the buttered pan over medium heat for 2 minutes per side, until golden and puffed.
Warm the honey and drizzle over the hotcakes.

notes: Food safety: the pancakes are cooked when puffed and set through.
Vegetarian.

title: Duck Leg Confit with Puy-Style Lentils
summary: Slow-cooked duck legs with crisp skin on garlicky brown lentils.

steps.text: Rub the duck with the salt, thyme and half the garlic and cure in the fridge for 12 hours. Rinse and pat dry.
Heat the oven to 140°C (120°C fan). Submerge the legs in melted duck fat in a snug dish and cook for 2 hours 30 minutes, until the meat is tender and pulls from the bone.
Simmer the lentils with the vegetables, remaining garlic and stock for 25 minutes, until tender. Stir in the mustard and vinegar.
Lift out the duck, drain and crisp it, skin-side down, in a hot pan for 5 minutes, until the skin is crisp and the meat reaches 74°C.

notes: Food safety: duck legs should reach at least 74°C; confit goes well beyond that and falls from the bone.
Duck legs should reach at least 75°C; confit goes well beyond that and falls from the bone.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Provencal Fish Stew with Rouille Toast
summary: White fish and prawns in a saffron, fennel and tomato broth with garlicky rouille on toast.

steps.text: Cook the leek in the oil in a wide pot for 8 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, fennel seeds, saffron and orange peel for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and stock and simmer for 20 minutes, until rich.
Mix the mayonnaise, harissa and one crushed garlic clove for the rouille, then toast the baguette until golden.

Add the fish and cook for 4 minutes, then add the prawns and mussels, cover and cook for 4 minutes, until the fish is opaque and the mussel shells have opened. Discard any mussels that stay closed and serve with rouille toast.

notes: Food safety: fish should flake and turn opaque, prawns pink and the mussel shells open; discard any that stay shut.
Contains gluten (baguette), egg and shellfish.

title: Beef Bourguignon with Mashed Potato
summary: Beef braised in red wine with bacon, mushrooms and baby onions until silky.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Brown the beef in the oil in batches for 10 minutes in total, until deeply coloured, and lift out. Fry the bacon until crisp.
Cook the carrot and onion in the same pot for 6 minutes, add the garlic and paste, then the wine. Boil for 5 minutes, scraping the pot.
Return the beef with the stock, thyme and bay leaves, cover and braise for 2 hours 30 minutes, until very tender.
Add the mushrooms and pearl onions, uncover and cook for 25 minutes, until glossy.
Boil the potato for 18 minutes, until tender, drain and mash with the butter and milk. Serve with the beef.

notes: Food safety: beef chuck is safe at 75°C and tender once it shreds; the stew should be steaming hot.
Gluten-free.

title: Hunter-Style Chicken with Tomato and Wine
summary: Chicken braised with mushrooms, tomato, white wine and fresh tarragon.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil in a wide pan for 8 minutes, until golden, and lift out.
Cook the mushrooms for 6 minutes, until browned, then add the shallot and garlic for 2 minutes.
Add the wine and boil for 2 minutes, then add the tomatoes and stock and return the chicken.
Cover and simmer for 30 minutes, until the chicken reaches 75°C. Stir through the butter and tarragon.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part, with clear juices.
Gluten-free.

title: Baked Eggs with Spinach and Cream
summary: Eggs baked in ramekins on creamy garlic spinach, French cafe-style.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Melt the butter and cook the garlic and spinach for 2 minutes, until wilted.
Divide the spinach and cream between two ramekins, crack in two eggs each and top with gruyere.
Bake for 12 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks still soft.
Scatter with chives and serve with toasted baguette.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.

title: Ham and Gruyere Crepes with Fried Egg
summary: Thin savoury crepes folded around ham, melted gruyere and a fried egg.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, 2 eggs, milk, melted butter and a pinch of salt into a smooth batter and rest for 15 minutes.
Cook four thin crepes in a buttered non-stick pan for 1 minute each side, until golden and lacy.
Return each crepe to the pan, add ham and gruyere and cook for 1 minute, until the cheese melts. Fold into squares.
Fry the remaining eggs in the butter for 3 minutes, until the whites are set, and top each crepe.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.

title: Paper-Baked Salmon with Fennel, Beans and Dill
summary: Salmon steamed in baking paper parcels with fennel, lemon and dill.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Tear four large sheets of baking paper.
Divide the green beans and lemon among the sheets, set a salmon fillet on each and top with dill, oil, butter and wine.
Fold and crimp the paper into sealed parcels and bake on a tray for 15 minutes, until the salmon turns opaque and flakes easily.
Open the parcels at the table, taking care with the hot steam, until the salmon is flaked and ready to eat.

notes: Food safety: salmon is cooked when opaque and flakes easily, or at 63°C.
Gluten-free.

title: Mushroom, Leek and Gruyere Tart
summary: A crisp puff pastry tart with sweet leeks, mushrooms and melted cheese.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cook the leeks in the butter for 8 minutes, until soft, then add the mushrooms and thyme for 8 minutes, until browned and dry.
Lay the pastry on a lined tray, score a 2cm border and spread the creme fraiche inside it.
Top with the mushrooms and cheese and brush the border with beaten egg.
Bake for 25 minutes, until puffed and deep golden.

notes: Vegetarian.

title: Fabada-Style Chorizo and White Bean Bake
summary: White beans slowly cooked with chorizo, smoked paprika and saffron.

steps.text: Fry the chorizo and pork belly in a heavy pot for 8 minutes, until browned, and lift out. Cook the onion in the fat for 6 minutes, then add the garlic, paprika and saffron.
Add the tomatoes, stock, beans, bay leaves and the meats.
Cover and simmer for 55 minutes, until the beans are creamy and the pork is tender and reads 70°C.
Uncover and cook for 5 minutes, until thick. Scatter with parsley.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach 70°C inside; the stew should be steaming hot.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Pisto with Baked Eggs
summary: A Spanish vegetable stew of zucchini, capsicum and tomato with eggs baked into it.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, until soft. Add the capsicum, eggplant and zucchini and cook for 10 minutes, until golden.
Add the garlic, paprika and tomatoes and simmer for 12 minutes, until thick and soft.
Make four wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 5 minutes, until the whites are set.
Scatter the parsley over the finished dish just before serving it, while hot.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.

title: Galician-Style Octopus with Paprika Potatoes
summary: Tender octopus on soft potatoes, drizzled with olive oil and smoked paprika.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of water with the bay leaf to a rolling boil. Dip the octopus in and out three times until the tentacles curl, then submerge it.
Simmer gently for 1 hour 15 minutes, until a knife slips easily into the thickest part. Cool in the liquid for 15 minutes.
Boil the potato in salted water for 12 minutes, until tender, and drain.
Cut the octopus into thick slices, pile onto the potato, drizzle with oil and scatter with paprika and salt. Serve with lemon.

notes: Food safety: octopus is cooked when tender and opaque; eat it hot and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Chicken with Chorizo and Sherry
summary: Chicken thighs braised with chorizo, sherry and smoked paprika until sticky.

steps.text: Fry the chicken in a wide pan for 8 minutes, until golden, and lift out. Fry the chorizo for 3 minutes, until the oil runs.
Cook the onion in the chorizo oil for 5 minutes, then add the garlic and paprika.
Add the sherry and boil for 2 minutes, then the stock, potato and chicken. Cover and simmer for 30 minutes, until the chicken reaches 75°C and the potato is tender.
Uncover for 5 minutes, until the sauce is sticky, and scatter with parsley.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part, with clear juices.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Roast Cod with Romesco Potatoes
summary: White fish roasted over potatoes crusted with a smoky almond and capsicum romesco.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the potato in 1 tablespoon of oil and roast for 25 minutes, until golden.
Blend the capsicum, almonds, garlic, paprika, vinegar and the remaining oil into a coarse romesco.
Set the fish on the potatoes and spread romesco over each piece.
Bake for 14 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flakes. Scatter with parsley.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when opaque and flakes with a fork.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Lamb Youvetsi with Orzo
summary: Lamb shoulder baked with tomatoes, cinnamon and orzo until the pasta is silky.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan). Brown the lamb in the oil in an ovenproof pot for 8 minutes, until golden, and lift out. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, then the garlic.
Add the wine, tomatoes, stock, cinnamon, bay leaves and lamb, cover and bake for 1 hour 45 minutes, until the lamb is tender.
Stir in the orzo, add 1 cup of water if dry and bake uncovered for 25 minutes, until the orzo is tender and creamy.
Top with feta and parsley.

notes: Food safety: lamb is safe at 63°C; this braise cooks well beyond that. The dish should be steaming hot.
Contains gluten (orzo).

title: Spanakopita Pie
summary: Crisp filo pie with spinach, feta, dill and spring onion.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Mix the spinach, feta, ricotta, spring onion, herbs, eggs and nutmeg.
Brush a baking dish with oil and layer in six sheets of filo, brushing each with oil.
Spread the filling over the filo and cover with the remaining filo, brushing each sheet with oil. Score the top into squares.
Bake for 45 minutes, until deep golden and crisp, and rest for 10 minutes.

notes: Food safety: the filling has raw egg: bake until the pie is golden and set through.
Vegetarian.

title: Baked Fish with Tomato, Capers and Feta
summary: White fish baked in a Greek-style tomato sauce with capers, olives and feta.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the tomatoes, onion, garlic, oil, capers, olives and oregano in a baking dish and roast for 10 minutes.
Nestle the fish into the tomatoes, squeeze over the lemon juice and crumble over the feta.
Bake for 14 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Serve straight from the dish.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when opaque and flakes with a fork.
Gluten-free.

title: Greek Omelette with Feta, Tomato and Olives
summary: A fluffy omelette filled with tomato, olives, feta and oregano.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs with a pinch of salt.
Warm the oil in a non-stick pan, add the tomato and olives and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the eggs and cook for 3 minutes, lifting the edges, until nearly set.
Scatter over the feta, oregano and parsley, fold and cook for 1 minute, until just set.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Vegetarian. Gluten-free.

title: Pork Souvlaki Plate with Lemon Rice
summary: Lemon and oregano pork skewers served on lemon rice with tomato and cucumber.

steps.text: Toss the pork with 2 tablespoons of oil, the juice of 1 lemon, garlic and oregano and marinate for 1 hour.
Cook the rice in boiling water for 12 minutes, until tender, drain and toss with the remaining lemon juice and oil.
Thread the pork onto skewers and grill for 10 minutes, turning, until browned and the centre reaches 70°C.
Serve on the rice with tomato, cucumber, onion and yoghurt.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach 70°C in the middle with no pink; rice should be refrigerated within 1 hour if there are leftovers.
Gluten-free.

title: Irish Beef and Stout Casserole
summary: Slow-braised beef with carrot and parsnip in a dark, malty stout gravy.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Toss the beef in the flour and brown in the oil in batches for 10 minutes in total, until deeply coloured.
Cook the onion for 6 minutes in the same pot, add the garlic and paste, then pour in the beer and boil for 3 minutes.
Return the beef with the stock, carrot, thyme and bay leaves, cover and braise for 2 hours, until tender.
Add the potato for the final 40 minutes, until soft and the sauce is thick.

notes: Food safety: beef chuck is safe at 75°C and tender once it shreds; the casserole should be steaming hot.
Contains gluten (stout, flour).

title: Beef and Swede Hand Pasties
summary: Handmade pasties of beef, potato, swede and onion in short, golden pastry.

steps.text: Rub the butter into the flour and salt until like breadcrumbs, then mix in the water until a dough forms. Chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Mix the beef, potato, swede, onion and pepper.
Roll out six 20cm rounds, pile the filling on one half, fold over and crimp the edge firmly. Brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 20 minutes, then reduce to 160°C (140°C fan) and bake for 35 minutes, until deep golden and the beef is tender at 75°C.

notes: Food safety: the beef filling must reach 75°C throughout; check one pasty in the centre of the filling.

title: Full English Breakfast Tray
summary: Bacon, sausages, mushrooms, tomato, beans and eggs roasted and cooked together.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Roast the sausages on a tray with the oil for 15 minutes, then add the bacon, tomatoes and mushrooms.
Roast for a further 12 minutes, until the sausages are browned and cooked through at 75°C and the bacon is crisp.
Warm the beans in a small pot for 5 minutes, until hot. Fry the eggs in the butter for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Toast the bread until golden and serve everything together while hot.

notes: Food safety: sausages must reach 75°C with no pink; bacon should be crisp and eggs set.

title: Colcannon Cakes with Poached Eggs
summary: Crisp potato and cabbage cakes topped with poached eggs.

steps.text: Boil the potato for 15 minutes, until tender, drain well and mash with the butter and milk.
Cook the cabbage and spring onion in a little butter for 5 minutes, until soft, then fold into the mash with the starch and season. Shape into eight patties.
Fry the cakes in the oil for 4 minutes each side, until deep golden and crisp.
Poach the eggs in barely simmering water with the vinegar for 3 minutes, until the whites are set. Serve on the cakes.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Vegetarian. Gluten-free.

title: Crumbed Sausage-Wrapped Eggs
summary: Soft-boiled eggs wrapped in seasoned sausage meat, crumbed and baked until golden.

items.raw: 500g pork sausage, meat squeezed from skins

steps.text: Boil six eggs for 6 minutes, then cool in iced water and peel carefully.
Mix the sausage meat with the thyme and pepper and press around each egg to cover it fully.
Roll in the flour, dip in the beaten egg and coat in panko. Brush with oil.
Bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 30 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and the sausage reaches 75°C.

notes: Food safety: the sausage meat must reach 75°C throughout; the centre yolk will be soft, so keep these away from children, older people and anyone pregnant unless boiled hard.

title: Lamb Hotpot with Sliced Potato Crust
summary: Lamb neck and onion braised under overlapping slices of crisp potato.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Brown the lamb in the oil in batches for 8 minutes, until golden, and place in a deep casserole.
Add the onion, carrot, stock, worcestershire sauce and thyme.
Overlap the potato slices over the top, dot with butter and season. Cover and bake for 1 hour 30 minutes, until the lamb is tender.
Uncover and bake for 30 minutes, until the potato is golden and crisp.

notes: Food safety: lamb is safe at 63°C; this braise cooks well past that and should be steaming hot.

title: Prawns and Cheesy Grits
summary: Creamy cheese grits topped with garlicky, paprika-spiced prawns and bacon.

steps.text: Bring the water to the boil with a pinch of salt, whisk in the polenta and cook over low heat for 20 minutes, stirring often, until thick. Stir in the butter and cheese.
Fry the bacon for 5 minutes, until crisp, and lift out.
Cook the garlic and paprika in the bacon fat for 30 seconds, add the prawns and cook for 4 minutes, until pink and opaque.
Add the lemon juice, spoon the grits into bowls and top with the prawns, bacon and spring onion.

notes: Food safety: prawns are cooked when pink, curled and opaque all the way through.

title: Sausage Gravy Biscuits
summary: Fluffy buttermilk biscuits with creamy black pepper sausage gravy.

items.raw: 400g pork sausage, meat squeezed from skins

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Rub the butter into the self-raising flour, mix in the buttermilk and pat out to 3cm thick.
Cut into six rounds and bake for 15 minutes, until risen and golden.
Brown the sausage meat in the oil for 8 minutes, until cooked through. Stir in the plain flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk.
Simmer for 6 minutes, until thick, season with the pepper and spoon over the split biscuits.

notes: Food safety: sausage meat must reach 75°C throughout, with no pink.

title: Sausage, Egg and Potato Breakfast Bake
summary: A make-ahead bake of sausage, potato, eggs and cheese.

items.raw: 300g pork sausage, meat squeezed from skins

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Cook the potato in boiling water for 6 minutes, until just tender, and drain.
Brown the sausage meat, onion and capsicum in the oil for 8 minutes, until the sausage is cooked through.
Spread the potato and sausage mix in a greased baking dish and top with cheese.
Whisk the eggs and milk, pour over and bake for 30 minutes, until set in the centre and golden.

notes: Food safety: sausage meat must reach 75°C; the bake is done when the egg is firmly set in the centre.
Gluten-free: check the sausage label.

title: Oven-Barbecued Beef Brisket
summary: Brisket rubbed with smoky spices and cooked low and slow until it pulls apart.

steps.text: Mix the paprika, sugar, garlic powder, onion powder, pepper and salt and rub it all over the brisket. Rest for 2 hours.
Heat the oven to 150°C (130°C fan). Sit the brisket in a deep tray with the stock and vinegar, cover tightly with foil and cook for 4 hours 30 minutes.
Brush with bbq sauce, uncover and cook for 30 minutes, until the surface is sticky and the centre reaches 93°C.
Rest for 30 minutes, then slice across the grain.

notes: Food safety: brisket needs to reach 93°C to be tender (it is safe at 63°C); rest before slicing.
Gluten-free: check the sauce label. Dairy-free.

title: Cajun Blackened Fish with Corn Rice
summary: Spice-crusted fish seared until blackened, on rice with sweet corn.

steps.text: Cook the rice in boiling water for 12 minutes, until tender, adding the corn for the last 3 minutes. Drain and stir through the spring onion.
Press the cajun seasoning over the fish.
Sear the fish in the butter in a hot pan for 3 minutes per side, until blackened and opaque all the way through.
Serve on the corn rice with lime.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when opaque and it flakes with a fork.
Gluten-free: check the seasoning label.

title: Southwest Stuffed Sweet Potatoes
summary: Baked sweet potatoes stuffed with black beans, corn, cheese and lime crema.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Prick the sweet potatoes and bake for 50 minutes, until very soft.
Warm the beans, corn, cumin and paprika in a pan for 5 minutes, until hot.
Stir the sour cream with the lime juice.
Split the potatoes, fill with the beans, top with cheese and return to the oven for 5 minutes, until melted. Finish with crema, avocado and coriander.

notes: Vegetarian. Gluten-free.

title: Macadamia and Herb-Crusted Fish
summary: Fish fillets under a golden macadamia, parsley and lemon crust.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the potato in 1 tablespoon of oil and roast for 20 minutes.
Mix the macadamias, parsley, lemon zest, remaining oil and a pinch of salt.
Brush the fish with the mustard and lemon juice and press the crust on top.
Add the fish to the tray with the green beans and bake for 15 minutes, until the fish is opaque, flakes and the crust is golden.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when opaque and flakes with a fork.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Lamb Cutlets with Mint and Pea Smash
summary: Seared lamb cutlets with a buttery mint and pea smash and lemon.

steps.text: Season the cutlets and sear in the oil in a hot pan for 3 minutes each side for medium, until browned, then rest for 5 minutes.
Simmer the peas and garlic in water for 3 minutes, drain and smash roughly with the butter, mint, lemon zest and juice.
Warm the potato in the pan juices for 3 minutes, until golden.
Serve the cutlets on the pea smash.

notes: Food safety: cutlets are safe seared on all sides; 63°C is medium, 71°C well done.
Gluten-free.

title: Avocado, Feta and Poached Egg on Sourdough
summary: Smashed avocado and feta on sourdough with poached eggs, lemon and chilli.

steps.text: Mash the avocado with the feta and lemon juice and season.
Poach the eggs in barely simmering water with the vinegar for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Toast the sourdough until golden and spread with the avocado.
Top with the eggs, chilli, mint and oil.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Vegetarian.

title: Roast Pumpkin and Ricotta Breakfast Bake
summary: Roasted pumpkin and spring onion folded into a baked ricotta and egg custard.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Roast the pumpkin with the oil for 25 minutes, until tender and browned.
Whisk the ricotta, eggs, milk and half the spring onion until smooth and season.
Scatter the pumpkin in a greased baking dish, pour over the egg mix and scatter with feta.
Bake for 25 minutes, until set in the centre and golden. Top with the remaining spring onion and chives.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Vegetarian. Gluten-free.

title: Braised Beef Shin Tacos with Chipotle
summary: Beef shin braised in chipotle and tomato until it falls apart, piled into warm corn tortillas.

steps.text: Brown the beef in the oil in a heavy pot for 10 minutes, until deeply coloured, and lift out. Cook the onion for 6 minutes, then add the garlic, chipotle, cumin and oregano.
Add the tomatoes and stock, return the beef, cover and cook at 150°C (130°C fan) for 3 hours, until the beef shreds easily.
Shred the meat into the sauce and simmer for 10 minutes, until thick.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan and fill with beef, pickled onion and coriander. Serve with lime.

notes: Food safety: beef shin is safe at 75°C and tender when it shreds; the filling should be steaming hot.
Gluten-free: check the tortilla and chipotle labels. Dairy-free.

title: One-Pan Mexican Chicken and Rice
summary: Chicken thighs cooked with rice, tomato, corn and beans in a single pan.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil in a wide pan for 6 minutes, until golden, and lift out. Cook the onion for 4 minutes, then add the garlic, taco seasoning and rice.
Add the tomatoes and stock, bring to a simmer and nestle the chicken on top. Cover and cook for 25 minutes, until the rice is tender and the chicken reaches 75°C.
Stir in the corn and beans, scatter with cheese, cover and cook for 5 minutes, until melted.
Scatter the coriander over the finished dish and serve straight from the pan while hot.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part; refrigerate leftover rice within 1 hour.
Gluten-free: check the taco seasoning label.

title: Refried Bean and Egg Tostadas
summary: Crisp corn tortillas spread with refried beans, topped with fried eggs, avocado and lime.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and bake the tortillas on a tray for 6 minutes, until crisp.
Warm the beans, garlic and cumin with a splash of water in a pan for 5 minutes, mashing until thick and spreadable.
Fry the eggs for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Spread the beans on the tostadas, top with eggs, avocado, salsa and coriander and serve with lime.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Vegetarian. Gluten-free.

title: Spiced Pork and Charred Pineapple Tacos
summary: Spiced pork fillet and charred pineapple in warm tortillas with coriander and onion.

steps.text: Mix the chipotle, garlic, cumin, oregano, 1 tablespoon of oil and lime juice, coat the pork and marinate for 1 hour.
Cook the pork in a very hot pan in batches for 5 minutes each, until browned and cooked through at 70°C.
Char the pineapple in the remaining oil for 3 minutes, until caramelised.
Warm the tortillas and fill with pork, pineapple, onion and coriander.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach 70°C in the middle with no pink.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Huevos con Chorizo
summary: Soft scrambled eggs with crumbly spiced chorizo, served with warm tortillas.

steps.text: Fry the chorizo in the oil for 5 minutes, until crisp and the oil runs red. Add the spring onion for 1 minute.
Pour in the whisked eggs and stir gently for 3 minutes, until just set.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 30 seconds each side, until soft.
Serve the eggs in the tortillas with salsa and coriander.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Gluten-free.

title: Carne Asada Steak Bowls with Lime Rice
summary: Grilled marinated skirt steak over lime rice with beans, corn and avocado.

steps.text: Mix the juice of 2 limes, garlic, cumin, paprika and 1 tablespoon of oil, coat the steak and marinate for 1 hour.
Cook the rice in boiling water for 12 minutes, until tender, drain and stir through the remaining lime juice and coriander.
Cook the steak in the remaining oil in a very hot pan for 3 minutes per side for medium-rare, until charred and 55°C in the centre. Rest for 5 minutes and slice across the grain.
Warm the beans and corn and serve over the rice with the steak and avocado.

notes: Food safety: whole steaks are safe seared; 55°C is medium-rare, 63°C medium, 71°C well done.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Chicken Tortilla Pie Pastel Azteca
summary: Layers of corn tortilla, shredded chicken, enchilada sauce and cheese baked until bubbling.

steps.text: Poach the chicken in simmering water for 18 minutes, until it reaches 75°C, then shred.
Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Mix the chicken with 1 cup of enchilada sauce, the corn and the beans.
Spread a little sauce in a baking dish and layer tortillas, filling and cheese three times, finishing with sauce and cheese.
Bake for 30 minutes, until bubbling and golden. Rest for 10 minutes and serve with sour cream and coriander.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C right through before shredding; the pie should be steaming hot in the middle.
Gluten-free: check the tortilla and sauce labels.

title: Churrasco-Style Picanha with Garlic Rice
summary: Salted picanha roasted and sliced thinly over garlic rice with lime.

steps.text: Score the fat cap, slice the picanha into thick steaks and press the salt into them. Rest at room temperature for 20 minutes.
Cook the garlic in the oil for 1 minute, add the rice and stir for 1 minute, then add 3 cups boiling water and cook covered for 15 minutes, until the rice is tender.
Sear the steaks fat-side down first in a very hot pan for 4 minutes, then 3 minutes per side for medium-rare, until the centre reaches 55°C. Rest for 5 minutes.
Toss the tomato, onion, vinegar and parsley. Slice the steak and serve with the rice and vinaigrette.

notes: Food safety: whole steaks are safe seared; 55°C is medium-rare, 63°C medium, 71°C well done.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Colombian Pork, Chorizo and Bean Feast Plate
summary: A hearty plate of pork, chorizo, beans, rice, fried egg, plantain and avocado.

items.raw: 1 x 400g tinned red kidney beans, drained

steps.text: Cook the rice in boiling water for 12 minutes, until tender, and drain.
Fry the pork belly slices in a pan for 15 minutes, turning, until crisp, browned and 70°C inside. Fry the chorizo for 8 minutes, until browned.
Simmer the beans with the garlic, tomato and spring onion for 10 minutes, until thick.
Fry the plantain in oil for 3 minutes each side, until golden, then the eggs for 3 minutes, until the whites are set. Plate everything with the avocado.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach 70°C with no pink; chorizo and sausages should be steaming hot. Cook eggs until set.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Brazilian Garlic Prawns with Coconut Rice
summary: Garlicky prawns in a lime and coconut sauce over fragrant coconut rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice with 1 cup of coconut milk and 1 cup of water, covered, for 15 minutes, until tender and creamy.
Cook the garlic, capsicum and tomato in the oil for 4 minutes, until soft.
Add the prawns and 1/2 cup coconut milk and simmer for 4 minutes, until pink and opaque.
Add the lime and coriander and serve over the rice.

notes: Food safety: prawns are cooked when pink, curled and opaque all the way through.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Corn and Cheese Cakes Arepas de Choclo-Style
summary: Sweet corn griddle cakes with melted mozzarella, served warm with butter.

steps.text: Blend the corn, milk, egg, sugar and salt into a coarse batter. Stir in the polenta and rest for 10 minutes.
Heat a buttered frying pan over medium heat and pour in 1/4 cup batter per cake.
Cook for 3 minutes, scatter with mozzarella, then flip and cook for 3 minutes, until golden and the cheese melts.
Serve warm with extra butter.

notes: Food safety: the egg cooks through in the pan: cook until the cakes are set.
Vegetarian. Gluten-free.

title: Feijoada-Style Black Bean and Pork Stew
summary: Black beans slowly cooked with pork, smoked sausage and bay, served with rice and orange.

steps.text: Brown the pork, sausage and bacon in a heavy pot for 10 minutes, until deep golden.
Add the onion and garlic for 5 minutes, then the beans, bay leaves and stock.
Cover and simmer for 1 hour 45 minutes, until the pork is tender and 70°C inside and the stew has thickened.
Cook the rice in boiling water for 12 minutes, until tender, and serve with the stew, orange and coriander.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach 70°C inside; the stew should be steaming hot.
Gluten-free if you use a sausage labelled gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Peruvian-Style Green Rice with Chicken
summary: Chicken and rice cooked in a vivid coriander and spinach sauce.

steps.text: Blend the coriander, spinach, garlic and chilli with 1/2 cup of the stock until smooth.
Brown the chicken in the oil in a wide pan for 8 minutes, until golden, and lift out. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, add the rice and the green purée for 2 minutes.
Add the remaining stock, nestle in the chicken, cover and cook for 25 minutes, until the rice is tender and the chicken reaches 75°C.
Stir in the peas for 3 minutes and serve with lime.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part; refrigerate leftover rice within 1 hour.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Beef Tagine with Sweet Potato and Chickpeas
summary: Beef braised with sweet potato, chickpeas, cinnamon and ginger.

steps.text: Brown the beef in the oil in a heavy pot for 10 minutes, until deep golden, and lift out. Cook the onion for 6 minutes, then the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Return the beef with the tomatoes and stock, cover and simmer for 1 hour 15 minutes, until nearly tender.
Add the sweet potato and chickpeas and simmer for 30 minutes, until soft and the sauce thickens.
Scatter the coriander over the finished dish and serve straight from the pan while hot.

notes: Food safety: beef chuck is safe at 75°C and tender once soft; the tagine should be steaming hot.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Spiced Lamb Patties with Harissa Eggs
summary: Cumin-spiced lamb patties served with harissa-spiked fried eggs and flatbread.

steps.text: Mix the lamb, cumin, paprika, cinnamon, garlic, parsley and salt and shape into eight small patties.
Cook the patties in the oil for 8 minutes, turning, until browned and 75°C in the centre.
Fry the eggs in the same pan for 3 minutes, until the whites are set, and dot with harissa.
Warm the flatbread and serve with the patties and eggs.

notes: Food safety: lamb mince must reach 75°C right through, with no pink. Cook the eggs until the whites are set.

title: Harissa Honey Salmon with Couscous
summary: Salmon glazed with harissa and honey, served on herby couscous.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Mix the harissa, honey and half the lemon juice and spread over the salmon on a lined tray.
Bake for 12 minutes, until the salmon turns opaque and flakes easily.
Soak the couscous in 1 1/2 cups boiling water for 5 minutes, fluff and stir through the herbs, oil and remaining lemon juice.
Serve the salmon on the couscous with yoghurt.

notes: Food safety: salmon is cooked when opaque and flakes easily, or at 63°C.

title: Ras el Hanout Sweet Potato and Lentil Bake
summary: A hearty vegan bake of sweet potato and lentils in a fragrant spiced tomato sauce.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cook the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, then add the garlic and ras el hanout for 1 minute.
Tip into a baking dish with the sweet potato, lentils, tomatoes and stock and stir.
Cover and bake for 40 minutes, then uncover and bake for 10 minutes, until the lentils and sweet potato are tender.
Scatter with coriander and almonds.

notes: Vegan. Gluten-free.

title: Chicken, Chickpea and Almond Traybake
summary: Spiced chicken roasted with chickpeas, carrot and almonds with a squeeze of lemon.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the chickpeas, carrot and onion with half the oil and spices in a large tray.
Rub the chicken with the remaining oil and spices, set it on top and roast for 40 minutes.
Scatter with almonds and roast for 5 minutes, until the chicken is golden and reaches 75°C.
Squeeze over the lemon juice and scatter with coriander.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part, with clear juices.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Shish Tawook-Style Chicken Skewers with Toum
summary: Yoghurt-marinated chicken skewers served with garlic toum and rice.

steps.text: Mix the yoghurt, garlic, lemon juice, paste, paprika, cumin and oil, coat the chicken and marinate for 2 hours.
Cook the rice in boiling water for 12 minutes, until tender, and drain.
Thread the chicken onto skewers and grill for 12 minutes, turning, until charred at the edges and the centre reaches 75°C.
Serve on the rice with toum and parsley.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part; discard the raw marinade.
Gluten-free.

title: Shawarma-Spiced Pulled Lamb with Tahini Yoghurt
summary: Lamb shoulder rubbed with shawarma spices and roasted until it can be pulled apart.

steps.text: Mix the oil, spices, garlic, lemon juice and 2 teaspoons of salt into a paste. Rub it over the lamb and marinate overnight in the fridge.
Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Sit the lamb in a deep tray with the stock and cover tightly with foil.
Roast for 4 hours, until the meat pulls apart and reaches 90°C, then uncover and roast at 220°C (200°C fan) for 15 minutes, until crisp.
Shred and serve with yoghurt mixed with tahini.

notes: Food safety: lamb shoulder is safe at 63°C; for pulled lamb 90°C gives the best texture.
Gluten-free.

title: Musaqa'a-Style Eggplant, Tomato and Chickpea Bake
summary: Silky roast eggplant baked in a spiced tomato and chickpea sauce.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Brush the eggplant with half the oil and roast on trays for 25 minutes, until golden.
Cook the onion in the remaining oil for 6 minutes, add the garlic and spices, then the tomatoes and chickpeas and simmer for 12 minutes, until thick.
Layer the eggplant and sauce in a baking dish and bake for 20 minutes, until bubbling.
Drizzle with pomegranate molasses and scatter with parsley.

notes: Vegan. Gluten-free.

title: Green Shakshuka with Spinach and Labneh
summary: Eggs baked in a bright green sauce of spinach, zucchini and herbs, with labneh.

steps.text: Cook the zucchini in the oil for 5 minutes, until soft, then add the garlic and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the spinach and cook for 3 minutes, until wilted, then stir in the coriander and parsley.
Make four wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 5 minutes, until the whites are set.
Dollop with labneh and scatter with chilli.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Vegetarian. Gluten-free.

title: Saffron Crispy Rice Tahdig with Chicken
summary: Saffron chicken under a crown of golden, crunchy rice.

steps.text: Mix half the yoghurt with the lemon juice, turmeric and saffron, coat the chicken and marinate for 4 hours.
Brown the chicken and onion in the butter in a heavy pot for 8 minutes, then add 1/2 cup water, cover and cook for 30 minutes, until the chicken reaches 75°C.
Boil the rice in salted water for 6 minutes, drain and mix a third with the remaining yoghurt, egg yolks and saffron.

Heat the oil in a non-stick pot, spread the yoghurt rice over the base, top with the chicken and remaining rice, and steam covered on low for 45 minutes, until the base is crisp and golden. Turn out onto a platter.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part; the rice mixture contains raw egg yolk and cooks through, so steam until piping hot. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Gluten-free.

title: Baked Falafel Plates with Tahini
summary: Herby baked chickpea falafel with cucumber, tomato and a lemon tahini drizzle.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Pulse the chickpeas, onion, garlic, herbs, spices, chickpea flour and baking powder into a coarse mixture.
Shape into 16 patties, set them on a lined tray and brush with oil.
Bake for 25 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp outside.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice and 3 tablespoons of water. Serve the falafel with cucumber, tomato and the tahini drizzle.

notes: Vegan. Gluten-free if you use gluten-free baking powder.

title: Cinnamon Chicken and Bulgur One-Pot
summary: A one-pot spiced chicken and bulgur pilaf with toasted almonds.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil in a wide pot for 8 minutes, until golden, and lift out. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, then add the garlic and spices.
Add the bulgur and stock, return the chicken, cover and simmer for 25 minutes, until the bulgur is tender and the chicken reaches 75°C.
Rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Scatter with almonds and parsley and serve with yoghurt.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part, with clear juices.
Contains gluten (bulgur).

title: Jerk Salmon with Coconut Rice
summary: Jerk-spiced salmon over coconut rice with lime and mango.

steps.text: Mix the oil, allspice, cinnamon, thyme, chilli, sugar and garlic and rub over the salmon.
Cook the rice with the coconut milk and 1 cup of water, covered, for 15 minutes, until tender.
Sear the salmon in a hot pan for 4 minutes per side, until the fish turns opaque and flakes easily.
Serve over the rice with mango and lime.

notes: Food safety: salmon is cooked when opaque and flakes easily, or at 63°C.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Dark-Sugar Braised Chicken with Thyme and Carrot
summary: Chicken thighs browned and simmered in a dark, thyme-scented sauce with carrot and capsicum.

steps.text: Season the chicken with the soy sauce and marinate for 1 hour.
Melt the sugar in the oil in a heavy pot for 2 minutes, until dark amber, add the chicken and brown for 8 minutes.
Add the onion, garlic, carrot, capsicum, tomato, thyme, scotch bonnet and stock, cover and simmer for 35 minutes, until the chicken reaches 75°C and the sauce is thick.
Cook the rice in boiling water for 12 minutes, until tender, and serve with the stew. Remove the scotch bonnet first.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part, with clear juices. Keep the scotch bonnet whole and remove it before serving.

title: Jamaican-Style Beef Patties
summary: Flaky turmeric pastry filled with spiced beef and baked until golden.

steps.text: Rub the butter into the flour, turmeric and a pinch of salt, add the water to form a dough and chill for 30 minutes.
Cook the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add the mince, garlic, curry powder and thyme and cook for 10 minutes, until browned and cooked through. Stir in the stock and breadcrumbs and cool.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Roll the pastry, cut 12cm rounds, fill, fold and crimp the edges. Brush with egg yolk.
Bake for 30 minutes, until deep golden and the filling is steaming.

notes: Food safety: the mince filling must reach 75°C right through; the baked patties should be steaming hot.

title: Trini Chicken Pelau
summary: Caramelised chicken cooked with rice, black-eyed beans and coconut milk in one pot.

steps.text: Melt the sugar in the oil in a heavy pot for 2 minutes, until dark amber. Add the chicken and brown for 8 minutes.
Add the onion, garlic and curry powder for 3 minutes, then the carrot, thyme, rice and beans.
Pour in the coconut milk and stock, bring to a simmer, cover and cook on low for 35 minutes, until the rice is tender and the chicken reaches 75°C.
Rest for 10 minutes, fluff and scatter with coriander.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part; cool and refrigerate leftover rice within 1 hour.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Coconut Sweet Potato Pancakes
summary: Soft sweet potato and coconut pancakes with a pinch of nutmeg and warm syrup.

steps.text: Whisk the sweet potato, coconut milk and egg until smooth.
Fold in the flour, baking powder, nutmeg and coconut until just combined.
Cook 1/4 cup spoonfuls in the oil over medium heat for 3 minutes per side, until golden and puffed.
Serve warm with maple syrup.

notes: Food safety: the pancakes are cooked when set through; refrigerate leftovers.
Vegetarian.

title: Braised Oxtail with Butter Beans
summary: Oxtail slowly braised with allspice, thyme and butter beans until the meat falls from the bone.

steps.text: Season the oxtail with the soy sauce, allspice, garlic and ginger and marinate overnight.
Brown the oxtail in the oil in a heavy pot in batches for 12 minutes, until deeply coloured. Cook the onion in the same pot for 5 minutes, then stir in the paste.
Return the oxtail with the stock, thyme and scotch bonnet, cover and simmer for 3 hours 30 minutes, until the meat falls from the bone. Add the beans for the last 20 minutes.
Cook the rice in boiling water for 12 minutes, until tender, and serve with the oxtail. Remove the scotch bonnet first.

notes: Food safety: oxtail needs long cooking; it is safe and tender when the meat falls from the bone and the stew is steaming hot (above 75°C).
Dairy-free.

title: Cuban Mojo Chicken
summary: Chicken marinated in garlic, orange and lime mojo and roasted until the skin is crisp.

steps.text: Mix the garlic, orange juice, lime juice, cumin, oregano, oil and 1 teaspoon of salt. Coat the chicken and marinate for 4 hours.
Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Spread the potato and onion on a tray and set the chicken on top.
Roast for 45 minutes, until golden and the thickest piece reaches 75°C.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve with the pan juices.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part, with clear juices.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Szekely Pork and Sauerkraut Stew
summary: Hungarian pork stewed with sauerkraut, paprika and sour cream.

steps.text: Brown the pork in the oil in a heavy pot for 10 minutes, until golden, and lift out. Cook the onion for 6 minutes, then the garlic, paprika and caraway.
Return the pork with the sauerkraut and stock, cover and simmer for 1 hour 30 minutes, until the pork is tender and 70°C inside.
Stir through the sour cream until just heated.
Scatter the dill over the stew and serve it hot with crusty bread or boiled potatoes.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach 70°C inside; the stew should be steaming hot.
Gluten-free.

title: Rinderrouladen with Mustard and Pickles
summary: German beef rolls filled with bacon, mustard, onion and pickle, braised in gravy.

steps.text: Spread each beef slice with mustard and top with bacon, onion and pickle. Roll up and tie with string.
Brown the rolls in the oil in a heavy pot for 8 minutes, until deeply coloured, and lift out. Stir the paste in the pot, add the wine and boil for 3 minutes.
Return the rolls with the stock, cover and simmer for 1 hour 30 minutes, until very tender. Lift out and keep warm.
Mix the cornflour with water, whisk into the sauce and simmer for 3 minutes, until thick. Serve the rolls with the sauce and potato.

notes: Food safety: beef rolls are safe at 75°C and tender after the long braise; the bacon must be cooked through.
Gluten-free if you use cornflour labelled gluten-free.

title: Vinegar-Marinated Beef Roast with Red Cabbage
summary: Beef marinated in vinegar and wine, then slow-cooked and served with red cabbage.
