steps.text: Combine the wine, vinegar, onion, carrot, cloves, bay leaves and pepper with 1 cup of water, add the beef and marinate in the fridge for 3 days, turning daily.
Dry the beef and brown in the oil for 10 minutes, until deeply coloured. Add the strained marinade, stock and honey.
Cover and cook at 150°C (130°C fan) for 3 hours, until very tender and 85°C inside.
Slice, spoon over the reduced gravy and serve with the red cabbage.

notes: Food safety: beef must reach at least 63°C inside; for a tender pot roast it cooks to 85°C. Keep the marinating beef in the fridge, covered.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Bratwurst with Onion Gravy and Mash
summary: Pan-browned bratwurst with buttery mash and slow-cooked onion gravy.

steps.text: Cook the onion in 2 tablespoons of butter for 20 minutes, until deeply golden and sweet. Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the stock and mustard and simmer for 5 minutes, until thick.
Boil the potato for 18 minutes, until tender, drain and mash with the butter and milk.
Brown the bratwurst in a pan over medium heat for 15 minutes, turning, until golden and 75°C in the centre.
Serve the sausages on the mash with the onion gravy.

notes: Food safety: bratwurst must reach 75°C with no pink.

title: Poached Beef with Horseradish Cream
summary: Austrian-style beef gently poached with root vegetables and served with apple and horseradish cream.

steps.text: Place the beef, carrot, celery, onion, leek, bay leaves, pepper and salt in a large pot and cover with water.
Bring to a bare simmer, never a boil, and cook gently for 2 hours 30 minutes, until the beef is tender and reaches 70°C inside.
Rest the beef in the broth for 15 minutes, then slice across the grain.
Serve with the vegetables, potato, horseradish cream and apple sauce.

notes: Food safety: beef should reach at least 63°C inside; it is cooked to 70°C or more for tenderness. Keep leftovers refrigerated.
Gluten-free.

title: Turos Csusza Cheese Noodles with Bacon
summary: Hungarian pasta tossed with crisp bacon, ricotta and sour cream.

steps.text: Cook the pasta in salted boiling water for 10 minutes, until tender, and drain.
Fry the bacon in the butter for 8 minutes, until crisp.
Stir the ricotta and sour cream through the hot pasta until creamy.
Top with the bacon and chives.

notes: Food safety: bacon should be cooked through and crisp.

title: German Apple Oven Pancake
summary: A puffed oven pancake with cinnamon apples, served straight from the dish.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) with a 24cm ovenproof frying pan inside.
Blend the eggs, flour, milk and a pinch of salt until smooth. Cook the apples in 1 tablespoon of the butter with the sugar and cinnamon for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the remaining butter to the hot pan until melted, add the apples and pour the batter over.
Bake for 18 minutes, until puffed and golden. Dust with icing sugar.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Vegetarian.

title: Swiss Alpine Macaroni with Potato and Apple Sauce
summary: Macaroni, potato and melted cheese topped with crisp onions, served with apple sauce.

steps.text: Cook the potato in boiling salted water for 6 minutes, add the macaroni and cook for 8 minutes, until both are tender, and drain.
Fry the onions in the butter for 20 minutes, until deep golden and crisp.
Return the pasta and potato to the pot with the cream and cheese and stir over low heat for 3 minutes, until melted and creamy.
Serve topped with onions and a side of apple sauce.

notes: Vegetarian.

title: Chicken, Leek and Ham Pie
summary: A golden pie of tender chicken, leek and ham in a creamy mustard sauce.

steps.text: Cook the leeks in the butter for 8 minutes, until soft. Add the chicken and cook for 8 minutes, until cooked through.
Stir in the flour for 1 minute, whisk in the milk and simmer for 5 minutes, until thick. Add the ham and mustard and cool.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Fill a pie dish, cover with pastry and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 35 minutes, until golden and the filling reaches 75°C.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C throughout; the pie should be steaming hot in the middle.

title: Sunday Lamb Leg on Crisp Potatoes
summary: A classic roast leg of lamb with garlic and rosemary over crisp roast potatoes.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Stab the lamb all over and push in the garlic and rosemary. Rub with oil, lemon juice and salt.
Roast for 20 minutes, then reduce to 180°C (160°C fan). Add the potatoes around it.
Roast for 1 hour 30 minutes, until the lamb reaches 60°C for medium or 70°C for well done and the potatoes are crisp.
Rest for 20 minutes, then carve.

notes: Food safety: lamb is safe at 63°C; 60°C then rest takes it to about 63°C for medium. Use 70°C for well done.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Bubble and Squeak Breakfast Cakes
summary: Crisp patties of leftover potato and cabbage topped with fried eggs.

steps.text: Cook the onion and cabbage in half the butter for 8 minutes, until soft and golden.
Mix with the mashed potato, season and shape into four patties.
Fry the patties in the remaining butter for 5 minutes per side, until deeply crisp.
Fry the eggs in the oil for 3 minutes, until the whites are set, and serve on the cakes.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Vegetarian. Gluten-free.

title: Glamorgan Sausages
summary: Crisp breadcrumbed leek and cheese patties, served with a mustard dip.

steps.text: Cook the leek in the butter for 6 minutes, until soft. Mix with the breadcrumbs, cheese, 1 egg, mustard and parsley.
Shape into eight sausages and chill for 20 minutes.
Roll in the flour, dip in the beaten second egg and coat in panko.
Fry in the oil for 8 minutes, turning, until golden and hot all the way through.

notes: Vegetarian.

title: Denver Omelette
summary: A fluffy omelette with ham, capsicum, onion and cheese.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs with a pinch of salt.
Melt the butter in a non-stick pan and cook the ham, capsicum and onion for 4 minutes, until soft.
Pour in the eggs and cook for 3 minutes, lifting the edges, until nearly set.
Scatter over the cheese, fold and cook for 1 minute, until just set. Top with chives.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Gluten-free.

title: Maple Salmon with Roast Broccoli
summary: Salmon glazed with maple and mustard over roasted broccoli and potatoes.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the potato and broccoli in the oil and roast on a tray for 12 minutes.
Mix the maple, mustard and soy sauce and spread over the salmon.
Add the salmon to the tray and roast for 12 minutes, until the salmon turns opaque and flakes and the potato is golden.
Serve the salmon and vegetables straight from the tray with the lemon wedges alongside.

notes: Food safety: salmon is cooked when opaque and flakes easily, or at 63°C.
Dairy-free.

title: Oven Pulled Pork Shoulder
summary: Pork shoulder rubbed with smoky spices and cooked low and slow until it pulls apart.

steps.text: Mix the paprika, sugar, garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne and salt and rub it over the pork. Rest overnight in the fridge.
Heat the oven to 150°C (130°C fan). Sit the pork in a deep tray with the vinegar and 1/2 cup water and cover tightly with foil.
Cook for 5 hours, until the pork reaches 93°C and shreds easily.
Shred the meat in the juices, stir through the bbq sauce and serve.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C inside; for pulled pork it is cooked to 93°C so it shreds.
Gluten-free: check the sauce label. Dairy-free.

title: Red Beans and Rice with Smoked Sausage
summary: Creamy red kidney beans slowly cooked with smoked sausage, served over rice.

items.raw: 3 x 400g tinned red kidney beans, drained

steps.text: Brown the sausage in a heavy pot for 6 minutes, until golden, then add the onion, capsicum and celery for 6 minutes, until soft.
Add the garlic, cajun seasoning, bay leaves, beans and stock and simmer for 30 minutes, mashing some beans, until thick and creamy.
Cook the rice in boiling water for 12 minutes, until tender, and drain.
Serve the beans over the rice, scattered with spring onion.

notes: Food safety: sausages should be steaming hot (75°C) all the way through; refrigerate leftover rice within 1 hour.
Gluten-free: check the seasoning label. Dairy-free.

title: Chipotle Honey Pork Ribs
summary: Slow-baked pork ribs lacquered with chipotle, honey and lime until sticky.

steps.text: Rub the ribs with the cumin, paprika, garlic powder and salt. Wrap tightly in foil and rest in the fridge for 2 hours.
Heat the oven to 150°C (130°C fan) and bake the foil parcels on a tray for 2 hours 15 minutes, until the meat is very tender.
Mix the chipotle, honey, lime juice and vinegar. Unwrap the ribs, brush with the glaze and roast at 220°C (200°C fan) for 15 minutes, brushing twice, until sticky and 75°C inside.
Rest for 10 minutes, cut between the bones and scatter with coriander before serving.

notes: Food safety: pork ribs must reach at least 70°C; slow-cooked ribs go well beyond that and are tender when the meat pulls from the bone.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Capsicum Egg Rings with Salsa
summary: Rings of red capsicum with eggs cooked inside, served with salsa and avocado.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat and add four capsicum rings.
Crack an egg into each ring and sprinkle with cumin and salt.
Cover and cook for 5 minutes, until the whites are set and the capsicum has softened.
Lift onto plates and serve with the salsa, avocado and coriander on the side.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Vegetarian. Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Prawn and Black Bean Burrito Bowls
summary: Chilli-lime prawns over rice with black beans, corn, avocado and crunchy lettuce.

steps.text: Cook the rice in boiling water for 12 minutes, until tender, then drain and stir through half the lime juice and half the coriander.
Toss the prawns in the taco seasoning and cook in the oil for 4 minutes, until pink, curled and opaque.
Warm the beans and corn for 4 minutes, until hot.
Build bowls of rice, lettuce, beans, corn, prawns and avocado and top with salsa, the remaining lime juice and coriander.

notes: Food safety: prawns are cooked when pink, curled and opaque all the way through.
Gluten-free: check the seasoning label. Dairy-free.

title: Baked Chicken Flautas
summary: Rolled corn tortillas filled with shredded chicken and cheese, baked until crisp.

steps.text: Poach the chicken in simmering water for 18 minutes, until it reaches 75°C, then shred and mix with the chipotle, cheese and 1/4 cup salsa.
Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 20 seconds each side, until pliable.
Fill each tortilla with chicken, roll tightly and set seam-side down on a lined tray. Brush with oil.
Bake for 20 minutes, until golden and crisp. Serve with sour cream, avocado, coriander and the remaining salsa.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C right through before shredding; the flautas should be steaming hot.
Gluten-free: check the tortilla label.

title: Loaded Chilli Beef Corn Chip Bake
summary: Corn chips layered with beany chilli beef, melted cheese and fresh toppings.

steps.text: Cook the onion in a pan for 5 minutes, until soft, then add the garlic and mince and cook for 8 minutes, until browned and cooked through.
Stir in the seasoning, tomatoes and beans and simmer for 10 minutes, until thick.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Layer the chips, chilli and cheese in a large dish and bake for 10 minutes, until the cheese is melted and bubbling.
Top with sour cream, avocado and coriander and serve straight away.

notes: Food safety: the beef mince must reach 75°C right through before baking.
Gluten-free: check the chips and seasoning labels.

title: Sweet Potato, Chorizo and Egg Breakfast Bowls
summary: Roasted sweet potato and chorizo with soft eggs, lime and avocado.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the sweet potato, chorizo, onion, oil and paprika on a large tray.
Roast for 25 minutes, turning once, until the potato is tender and the chorizo is crisp.
Fry or poach the eggs for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Divide the sweet potato and chorizo between bowls and top with the eggs, avocado, coriander and lime wedges.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Citrus Pollo Asado with Charred Corn
summary: Spatchcock chicken marinated in orange, lime and garlic and roasted with corn on the cob.

steps.text: Mix the juices, garlic, cumin, oregano, paprika, oil and 2 teaspoons of salt. Coat the chicken and marinate for at least 4 hours.
Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Sit the chicken skin-side up on a tray and roast for 30 minutes.
Add the corn to the tray and roast for 25 minutes, until the thigh reaches 75°C and the corn is tender and charred.
Rest for 10 minutes, carve and scatter with coriander.

notes: Food safety: whole chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part of the thigh; discard any raw marinade.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Spatchcock Chicken with Parsley and Garlic
summary: Butterflied chicken roasted over potatoes with a punchy parsley and garlic dressing.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Rub the chicken with 2 tablespoons of oil, paprika and salt. Toss the potato in the remaining oil on a large tray.
Set the chicken over the potato and roast for 50 minutes, until the skin is golden and the thigh reaches 75°C.
Mix the parsley, garlic, vinegar, the 1/3 cup oil and chilli flakes for the dressing.
Rest the chicken for 10 minutes, carve and serve with the potato and plenty of dressing.

notes: Food safety: whole chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part of the thigh, with clear juices.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Ecuadorian-Style Coconut Prawn Stew
summary: Prawns simmered in a coconut, tomato and peanut broth with coriander and lime.

steps.text: Cook the onion and capsicum in the oil for 6 minutes, until soft, then add the garlic and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, coconut milk and peanut butter and simmer for 10 minutes, until thick and creamy.
Cook the rice in boiling water for 12 minutes, until tender, and drain.
Add the prawns to the stew and cook for 4 minutes, until pink and opaque. Stir through the lime and coriander and serve over the rice.

notes: Food safety: prawns are cooked when pink, curled and opaque all the way through. Contains peanuts.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Humita-Style Corn Bake
summary: A creamy, sweet corn and basil bake with melted mozzarella.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Cook the onion in the butter for 5 minutes, until soft.
Blend three-quarters of the corn with the milk, eggs, polenta and basil until coarse, then stir in the remaining corn and the onion.
Pour into a greased baking dish, scatter with mozzarella and paprika.
Bake for 35 minutes, until set in the centre and golden on top. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

notes: Food safety: the bake contains raw egg and must be set in the centre.
Vegetarian. Gluten-free.

title: Olive and Capsicum Chicken Pot Rice, Dominican-Style
summary: Seasoned chicken and rice cooked with olives, capsicum and tomato in one pot.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil in a wide pot for 8 minutes, until golden, and lift out. Cook the onion and capsicum for 5 minutes, then add the garlic, oregano and paste.
Stir in the rice, stock and olives, bring to a simmer until bubbling and nestle the chicken on top.
Cover and cook on low for 25 minutes, until the rice is tender and the chicken reaches 75°C. Stir through the peas for 3 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes, then scatter with coriander and serve.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part; cool and refrigerate leftover rice within 1 hour.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Estrogonofe de Carne with Rice
summary: Tender beef and mushrooms in a creamy tomato sauce, served over rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice in boiling water for 12 minutes, until tender, and drain.
Sear the beef in the oil in two batches for 2 minutes each, until browned, and lift out. Cook the onion and mushrooms for 8 minutes, until golden.
Add the garlic, paste and wine and boil for 2 minutes. Stir in the cream and mustard and simmer for 4 minutes, until slightly thick.
Return the beef for 2 minutes until hot, with the centre at least 63°C, and serve over the rice with parsley.

notes: Food safety: beef strips are safe once browned and hot through; the centre should reach at least 63°C.
Gluten-free.

title: Moroccan Chicken Bastilla Pie
summary: Layers of crisp filo around spiced shredded chicken, almonds and egg, dusted with cinnamon sugar.

steps.text: Simmer the chicken, onion, garlic, ginger, 1/2 teaspoon of cinnamon, saffron and 1 cup water for 35 minutes, until the chicken reaches 75°C. Shred it, boil the liquid down to 1/2 cup and stir in the beaten eggs over low heat for 4 minutes, until scrambled and set.
Mix the chicken with the herbs, egg mixture and half the almonds.
Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Layer six brushed filo sheets in a round tin, overhanging the edge, pile in the filling, fold over and cover with six more brushed sheets.
Bake for 35 minutes, until deep golden. Dust with icing sugar, the remaining almonds and cinnamon.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C right through and the egg mixture be fully set before baking.
Contains nuts.

title: Lamb and Chickpea Couscous with Harissa
summary: Tender spiced lamb and chickpeas ladled over fluffy couscous, with harissa on the side.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil in a heavy pot for 8 minutes, until golden. Add the onion, garlic and spices for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, stock and carrot, cover and simmer for 1 hour, until the lamb is tender.
Add the chickpeas and simmer for 15 minutes, until the sauce thickens.
Soak the couscous in 2 cups boiling water for 5 minutes, fluff and serve with the lamb, harissa and coriander.

notes: Food safety: lamb is safe at 63°C; this braise cooks well beyond that and should be steaming hot.
Contains gluten (couscous).

title: Maakouda-Style Potato Omelette
summary: A thick, spiced potato and herb omelette, cooked until golden on both sides.

steps.text: Mix the potato with the garlic, cumin, paprika and herbs and season.
Beat in the eggs until the mixture is just combined.
Heat the oil in a 24cm non-stick pan and pour in the mix. Cook over low heat for 10 minutes, until set around the edges, then flip with a plate and cook for 8 minutes, until golden and set through.
Cut into wedges and serve warm with yoghurt.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Vegetarian. Gluten-free.

title: Roast Cauliflower Tagine with Green Olives
summary: Roast cauliflower and carrots simmered in a ginger and saffron tagine sauce with olives.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the cauliflower and carrot with 2 tablespoons of oil and roast for 25 minutes, until golden.
Cook the onion in the remaining oil for 5 minutes, then the garlic and spices for 1 minute. Add the tomatoes and stock and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the roast vegetables, olives and preserved lemon and simmer for 10 minutes, until tender and the sauce is thick.
Scatter with coriander and serve with couscous or bread.

notes: Vegan. Gluten-free.

title: Charred Fish Kebabs with Lemon and Cumin
summary: White fish chunks marinated in cumin, paprika and lemon, grilled on skewers.

steps.text: Mix the oil, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, paprika and coriander, add the fish and marinate for 30 minutes.
Thread the fish onto skewers with the onion and capsicum.
Grill for 8 minutes, turning, until the fish is opaque and flakes and the vegetables are charred.
Soak the couscous in 2 cups boiling water for 5 minutes, fluff and serve with the kebabs.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when opaque and it flakes with a fork.

title: Moroccan Orange and Honey Chicken
summary: Chicken roasted in an orange, honey and cinnamon glaze over fragrant rice.

steps.text: Mix the orange juice, honey, cinnamon, ginger, garlic and oil, coat the chicken and marinate for 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Arrange the chicken and onion in a roasting dish and pour over the marinade.
Roast for 45 minutes, basting twice, until the chicken reaches 75°C and the glaze is sticky. Scatter with almonds for the last 5 minutes.
Cook the rice in boiling water for 12 minutes, until tender, and serve with the chicken, juices and coriander.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part; the glaze should be boiled in the oven, not served raw.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Lebanese Beef Kafta Tray Bake
summary: Spiced beef kafta baked on potato and tomato until the juices run into the vegetables.

steps.text: Mix the mince, onion, parsley, allspice, cinnamon, cumin and salt and press into a thin layer in a baking dish.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cut the kafta into squares, then layer over the potato and tomato slices, tucked between the pieces.
Whisk the stock and tomato paste and pour over. Drizzle with oil, scatter with pine nuts and cover with foil.
Bake for 30 minutes, uncover and bake for 20 minutes, until golden, the potatoes are tender and the beef reaches 75°C.

notes: Food safety: beef mince must reach 75°C right through, with no pink.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Lebanese Spiced Rice with Chicken and Almonds
summary: Cinnamon-scented rice with shredded chicken, toasted almonds and parsley.

steps.text: Simmer the chicken in the stock for 25 minutes, until it reaches 75°C. Lift out, shred it and keep the stock.
Cook the onion in the butter for 5 minutes, add the spices and rice and stir for 1 minute, then pour in 3 cups of the hot stock.
Cover and cook on low for 15 minutes, until the rice is tender. Rest for 5 minutes.
Fluff the rice, top with chicken, almonds, pine nuts and parsley and serve with yoghurt.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C right through before shredding; refrigerate leftover rice within 1 hour.
Gluten-free.

title: Cilbir Poached Eggs with Chilli Butter
summary: Poached eggs on garlicky yoghurt with sizzling paprika butter and dill.

steps.text: Stir the yoghurt and garlic with a pinch of salt and spread on two plates.
Poach the eggs in barely simmering water with the vinegar for 3 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks soft.
Melt the butter until foaming, then stir in the paprika and chilli for 30 seconds.
Set the eggs on the yoghurt, spoon over the butter and scatter with dill. Serve with toasted sourdough.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Vegetarian.

title: Whole Roast Cauliflower with Tahini and Pomegranate
summary: A whole cauliflower roasted until golden, dressed in lemon tahini with pomegranate and herbs.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Rub the cauliflower with 2 tablespoons of oil, the cumin, paprika and salt and roast with the chickpeas alongside for 55 minutes, until deeply golden and tender when pierced.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice, garlic and 1/4 cup water until smooth.
Set the cauliflower on a platter and spoon over the tahini.
Scatter with chickpeas, pomegranate, parsley and pistachios, and cut into wedges to serve.

notes: Vegan. Gluten-free.

title: Lebanese Fish and Rice Sayadieh
summary: Spiced rice with caramelised onion and golden fish, topped with toasted pine nuts.

steps.text: Season the fish with the cumin, turmeric and salt and fry in 2 tablespoons of oil for 3 minutes per side, until golden and flaking. Lift out.
Cook the onions in the remaining oil for 25 minutes, until very dark and sweet. Lift out half and keep for the top.
Stir the rice and cinnamon into the pot, add the stock, cover and cook on low for 15 minutes, until the rice is tender.
Fold in the fish gently and top with the reserved onions, pine nuts and lemon.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when opaque and flakes with a fork; refrigerate leftover rice within 1 hour.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Za'atar Chicken Traybake with Chickpeas
summary: Za'atar-coated chicken roasted over chickpeas, red onion and lemon.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the chickpeas, onion, lemon and garlic with half the oil in a large tray.
Rub the chicken with the za'atar, remaining oil and salt and set on top.
Roast for 45 minutes, until the chicken is golden and reaches 75°C and the chickpeas are crisp at the edges.
Serve with yoghurt and parsley.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part, with clear juices.
Gluten-free.

title: Halloumi and Egg Breakfast Wraps
summary: Flatbread wraps with golden halloumi, scrambled eggs, tomato and mint.

steps.text: Fry the halloumi in a dry pan for 2 minutes each side, until golden. Lift out.
Scramble the eggs in the oil for 3 minutes, until just set.
Warm the flatbread and spread with hummus.
Fill with halloumi, eggs, tomato, cucumber and mint, then roll up and serve.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Vegetarian.

title: Caribbean Spiced Pork Chops with Mango Salsa
summary: Allspice and thyme pork loin steaks served with a fresh mango and lime salsa.

steps.text: Rub the pork with the allspice, thyme, sugar and salt.
Cook the rice in boiling water for 12 minutes, until tender, and drain.
Sear the pork in the oil for 5 minutes each side, until browned and the centre reaches 70°C. Rest for 5 minutes.
Mix the mango, onion, lime juice, coriander and chilli and serve over the pork with the rice.

notes: Food safety: pork steaks must reach 70°C in the centre, then rest.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Escovitch Fish with Pickled Vegetables
summary: Crisp fried fish topped with a tangy pickled onion, carrot and chilli dressing.

steps.text: Simmer the vinegar, allspice, sugar, 1/4 cup water and a pinch of salt for 3 minutes, then pour over the onion, carrot, capsicum and scotch bonnet and leave to pickle.
Cook the rice in boiling water for 12 minutes, until tender, and drain.
Dust the fish in cornflour and shallow-fry in the oil for 4 minutes each side, until golden, crisp and flaking.
Spoon the pickled vegetables and some of their liquid over the hot fish and serve with rice.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when opaque and flakes with a fork.
Gluten-free if you use cornflour labelled gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Trinidad-Style Potato and Chickpea Roti Wraps
summary: Warm roti wrapped around curried potato and chickpeas with a squeeze of lime.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, then add the garlic, curry powder and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the potato and water and simmer for 12 minutes, until the potato is tender.
Add the chickpeas and mash roughly, cooking for 5 minutes, until thick.
Warm the roti, fill with the curry and coriander, roll up and serve with lime.

notes: Vegan.

title: Jerk Lamb Cutlets with Pineapple Rice
summary: Jerk-spiced lamb cutlets over rice with sweet charred pineapple.

steps.text: Mix 1 tablespoon of oil, the allspice, thyme, cinnamon, chilli, garlic and soy sauce and coat the lamb. Marinate for 1 hour.
Cook the rice in boiling water for 12 minutes, until tender, and drain.
Sear the cutlets in a hot pan for 3 minutes each side for medium, until browned. Rest for 5 minutes.
Char the pineapple in the remaining oil for 3 minutes, until caramelised, and toss through the rice with the spring onion. Serve with the cutlets.

notes: Food safety: lamb cutlets are safe seared; the centre reaches 63°C for medium and 71°C for well done.
Dairy-free.

title: Potato and Ricotta Pierogi with Buttered Onions
summary: Pillowy dumplings of potato and ricotta, boiled, then pan-fried with butter and onion.

steps.text: Knead the flour, egg, water, 1 tablespoon sour cream and a pinch of salt for 5 minutes, until smooth. Rest for 30 minutes.
Cook half the onion in 1 tablespoon of butter for 8 minutes, until golden, and mix with the potato, ricotta and seasoning.
Roll the dough thin, cut 8cm rounds, fill, fold into half-moons and pinch to seal.
Boil in batches for 4 minutes, until they float. Fry in the remaining butter and onion for 4 minutes, until golden. Serve with sour cream and chives.

notes: Food safety: the dumpling dough contains raw egg: boil until the dumplings float and are cooked through.
Vegetarian.

title: Polish Meatballs in Dill Cream Sauce
summary: Tender pork and beef meatballs in a creamy dill sauce, served over mashed potato.

steps.text: Mix the minces, onion, egg, breadcrumbs and salt and roll into 20 balls.
Brown the meatballs in the oil for 8 minutes, until golden, and lift out.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, whisk in the stock and simmer for 5 minutes. Return the meatballs and cook for 10 minutes, until cooked through and 75°C in the middle.
Stir in the sour cream and dill and serve over the mash.

notes: Food safety: meatballs must reach 75°C right through, with no pink.

title: Czech Garlic Potato Pancakes with Bacon
summary: Crisp grated potato pancakes with garlic and marjoram, served with crisp bacon.

steps.text: Squeeze the grated potato in a tea towel to remove the liquid. Mix with the garlic, marjoram, eggs, starch and salt.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan and fry spoonfuls, flattened, for 4 minutes per side, until deeply golden and crisp.
Fry the bacon in a separate pan for 6 minutes, until crisp.
Serve the pancakes with bacon and sour cream.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Gluten-free.

title: Rakott Krumpli Layered Potato Bake
summary: Hungarian layers of potato, boiled egg and smoked sausage under sour cream.

steps.text: Hard-boil the eggs for 10 minutes, until firm, then cool, peel and slice.
Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Butter a baking dish and layer potato, egg, sausage and seasoning, repeating twice.
Mix the sour cream and milk, pour over and sprinkle with paprika.
Bake for 35 minutes, until bubbling and golden. Scatter with parsley.

notes: Food safety: hard-boil the eggs until firm; the sausage should be steaming hot (75°C) all the way through.
Gluten-free if you use a sausage labelled gluten-free.

title: Caraway Roast Chicken with Braised Cabbage
summary: Roast chicken scented with caraway and paprika over sweet braised cabbage.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Rub the chicken with the caraway, paprika, 1 tablespoon of butter and salt.
Cook the onion, cabbage and apple in the remaining butter in a roasting dish for 8 minutes, until starting to wilt, then add the stock and vinegar.
Sit the chicken on the cabbage and roast for 1 hour 15 minutes, until the thigh reaches 75°C and the cabbage is tender.
Rest for 15 minutes, then carve and serve with the cabbage and juices.

notes: Food safety: whole chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part of the thigh, with clear juices.
Gluten-free.

title: Bacon and Caraway Onion Tart, German-Style
summary: A crisp pastry tart with soft onions, bacon, caraway and a creamy egg custard.

steps.text: Cook the onion and bacon in the butter for 20 minutes, until very soft and golden. Cool.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Line a tart tin with the pastry and prick the base.
Whisk the eggs, sour cream, caraway, nutmeg and salt, stir in the onions and pour into the tin.
Bake for 35 minutes, until the custard is set and the pastry is deep golden.

notes: Food safety: the custard has raw egg and must be fully set in the centre.

title: Krautfleckerl Cabbage and Noodle Pan
summary: Caramelised cabbage tossed with egg pasta and caraway.

steps.text: Cook the sugar in the butter for 2 minutes, until golden, add the onion and cabbage and cook for 20 minutes, stirring, until deeply golden and soft.
Add the caraway and vinegar and season.
Cook the pasta in salted boiling water for 10 minutes, until tender, and drain.
Toss the pasta through the cabbage with the sour cream and parsley.

notes: Vegetarian.

title: Parsley and Lemon Salmon Fishcakes
summary: Crisp pan-fried salmon and potato cakes with parsley and lemon, served with peas.

steps.text: Mix the salmon, potato, parsley, lemon zest and mustard and shape into eight patties. Chill for 20 minutes.
Dip in beaten egg and coat in breadcrumbs.
Fry the cakes in the oil for 4 minutes per side, until golden and hot all the way through.
Boil the peas for 3 minutes, until tender, and serve with the fishcakes.

notes: Food safety: salmon is cooked when opaque and flakes; the cakes should be steaming hot in the middle.

title: Sausage and Egg English Muffin Stacks
summary: English muffins layered with a herby sausage patty, fried egg and melted cheese.

items.raw: 400g pork sausage, meat squeezed from skins

steps.text: Mix the sausage meat with the sage and shape into four patties.
Fry the patties for 10 minutes, turning, until browned and 75°C in the centre.
Toast the muffins and fry the eggs in the butter for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Stack each muffin with a patty, cheese and egg.

notes: Food safety: sausage patties must reach 75°C with no pink; cook the eggs until the whites are set.

title: Chicken and Waffles with Maple Butter
summary: Crisp oven-fried chicken thighs on fluffy waffles with maple butter.

steps.text: Marinate the chicken in half the buttermilk and salt for 2 hours. Mix the plain flour, paprika and garlic powder and coat the chicken.
Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the chicken in the oil on a tray and bake for 35 minutes, turning once, until crisp and 75°C inside.
Whisk the self-raising flour, eggs, milk and the remaining buttermilk and cook in a waffle iron until golden and crisp.
Melt the butter and maple syrup together and serve the chicken on the waffles with the maple butter.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part; discard the raw chicken marinade.

title: Pan-Fried Salmon Cakes with Lemon Mayo
summary: Pan-fried salmon cakes with a lemon mayonnaise and a crisp cabbage slaw.

steps.text: Mix the salmon, half the breadcrumbs, the egg, 2 tablespoons of mayonnaise, mustard and spring onion and shape into eight cakes.
Coat in the remaining breadcrumbs.
Fry the cakes in the oil for 4 minutes per side, until golden and hot all the way through.
Stir the lemon zest and juice into the remaining mayonnaise and serve with the cakes and slaw.

notes: Food safety: salmon is cooked when opaque and flakes; the cakes should be steaming hot in the middle.

title: Prawn, Corn and Potato Boil
summary: A one-pot boil of prawns, corn, potatoes and sausage with a spicy seasoning.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of water to the boil with the cajun seasoning, lemon and half the garlic. Add the potatoes and cook for 12 minutes, until almost tender.
Add the sausage and corn and cook for 6 minutes.
Add the prawns and cook for 3 minutes, until pink and opaque. Drain.
Melt the butter with the remaining garlic until foaming, toss it through the boil and scatter with parsley.

notes: Food safety: prawns are cooked when pink, curled and opaque; the sausage must be steaming hot.
Gluten-free: check the seasoning and sausage labels.

title: Cannellini and Sweet Corn Turkey Chilli
summary: A mild, hearty chilli of turkey mince, white beans and sweet corn.

steps.text: Cook the onion and capsicum in the oil for 6 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Add the turkey mince and cook for 8 minutes, until browned and cooked through.
Add the beans, tomatoes, stock and corn and simmer for 25 minutes, until thick.
Scatter with coriander and serve with the toppings of your choice.

notes: Food safety: turkey mince must reach 75°C right through, with no pink.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Chicken Parmigiana with Crisp Potato Wedges
summary: A crumbed chicken schnitzel under tomato sauce and melted cheese, with golden wedges.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the potato in the olive oil and roast for 35 minutes, until golden.
Flatten the chicken to 1.5cm, coat in flour, egg and panko, then fry in the oil for 3 minutes per side, until golden.
Simmer the passata, garlic and oregano for 5 minutes. Set the chicken on a tray, top with sauce, mozzarella and parmesan.
Bake for 15 minutes, until the cheese is golden and the chicken reaches 75°C. Serve with the wedges.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part.

title: Snag Breakfast Rolls with Onion and Tomato Sauce
summary: Soft rolls filled with grilled sausage, caramelised onion, fried egg and tomato sauce.

steps.text: Cook the sausages in the oil in a pan for 15 minutes, turning, until browned and 75°C inside.
Cook the onion in the same pan for 10 minutes, until soft and golden.
Fry the eggs in the butter for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Split the rolls and fill with sausages, onion, egg and tomato sauce.

notes: Food safety: sausages must reach 75°C with no pink; cook eggs until the whites are set.

title: Sticky Lemon-Garlic Chicken Bake, Greek-Style
summary: Chicken thighs roasted with potatoes in lemon, garlic and oregano until sticky and golden.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Mix the oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano and salt in a roasting dish and toss the chicken and potato through.
Pour the stock around, and roast for 55 minutes, turning once, until the chicken reaches 75°C and the potatoes are golden.
Rest for 5 minutes, spooning the pan juices over the potatoes.
Scatter with parsley and serve.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part, with clear juices.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Huevos Rotos-Style Eggs on Crisp Potatoes
summary: Fried eggs broken over crisp potatoes and cured ham, Spanish tavern-style.

steps.text: Fry the potato in the oil in a large pan for 15 minutes, turning, until golden, crisp and tender. Season with salt.
Move the potato to the side and fry the eggs for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Break the yolks over the potato and add the torn ham.
Dust with paprika and scatter with parsley.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Provencal Lamb Shoulder with White Beans
summary: Lamb shoulder roasted slowly with herbes de Provence, garlic and white beans.

steps.text: Make slits in the lamb and push in the garlic. Rub with the oil, herbs, lemon juice and salt and rest for 2 hours.
Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Sit the lamb on the onion in a deep tray with the tomatoes and stock, cover with foil and roast for 3 hours 15 minutes, until very tender.
Add the beans around the lamb, uncover and roast for 30 minutes, until the lamb is browned and reaches 90°C.
Rest for 15 minutes, scatter with parsley and serve with the beans and juices.

notes: Food safety: lamb shoulder is safe at 63°C; this slow roast reaches 90°C and pulls apart.
Gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Sicilian-Style Eggplant and Ricotta Bake
summary: Pasta baked with fried eggplant, tomato, basil and ricotta salata-style feta.

steps.text: Fry the eggplant in the oil in batches for 8 minutes, until deeply golden, and drain.
Cook the onion for 5 minutes, add the garlic and tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes, until thick.
Cook the penne in salted boiling water for 8 minutes, until just short of tender, drain and mix with the sauce, eggplant and basil.
Spoon into a dish, dot with ricotta, top with mozzarella and bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 20 minutes, until golden and bubbling.

notes: Vegetarian.

title: Pork Belly Gyro Plates with Lemon Potatoes
summary: Crisp roast pork belly slices with lemon potatoes, tomato, red onion and garlic yoghurt.

steps.text: Rub the pork with half the oregano, half the garlic, 2 tablespoons of oil and salt. Dry the skin well and leave uncovered in the fridge for 4 hours.
Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and roast the pork for 30 minutes, until the skin blisters, then reduce to 160°C (140°C fan) for 1 hour 30 minutes, until tender and 85°C inside.
Toss the potato with the lemon juice, remaining oil and oregano and roast alongside for the last 50 minutes, until golden.
Stir the remaining garlic into the yoghurt, slice the pork and serve with the potatoes, tomato and onion.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C; belly is tender at 85°C. Rest for 15 minutes before slicing.
Gluten-free.

title: Baked Prawns with Tomato, Chilli and Feta
summary: Prawns baked in a tomato and herb sauce under melted feta.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, until soft, then add the garlic and chilli for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and oregano and simmer for 10 minutes, until thick.
Stir in the prawns, top with feta and bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 8 minutes, until the prawns are pink and opaque and the feta softens.
Scatter with parsley and serve with the bread.

notes: Food safety: prawns are cooked when pink, curled and opaque all the way through.

title: Greek Baked Giant Beans with Spinach and Eggs
summary: Giant beans baked in tomato with spinach and eggs, with feta on top.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, then add the garlic and oregano.
Add the tomatoes and beans and simmer for 10 minutes, until thick, then stir through the spinach until wilted.
Make four wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 5 minutes, until the whites are set.
Scatter with feta and serve from the pan.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Vegetarian. Gluten-free.

title: Chicken Souvlaki Pita Wraps with Tzatziki
summary: Lemon-oregano chicken skewers in warm pita with tzatziki, tomato and onion.

steps.text: Mix the oil, lemon juice, garlic and oregano, add the chicken and marinate for 1 hour.
Thread onto skewers and grill for 12 minutes, turning, until charred and the centre reaches 75°C.
Warm the pita for 1 minute each side, until soft.
Fill with chicken, tzatziki, tomato and onion.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the centre; discard the raw marinade.

title: Spiced Beef Keftedes with Rice and Tomato
summary: Herby Greek beef meatballs baked and served on rice with a fresh tomato salad.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Mix the mince, onion, herbs, garlic, oregano, breadcrumbs, egg and salt and roll into 20 balls.
Bake on an oiled tray for 20 minutes, until browned and 75°C in the centre.
Cook the rice in boiling water for 12 minutes, until tender, and drain.
Serve the keftedes over the rice with the diced tomato and pan juices.

notes: Food safety: meatballs must reach 75°C right through.

title: Greek Yoghurt Omelette Wraps with Herbs
summary: Thin herby omelettes rolled around yoghurt, cucumber and olives.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs with the dill, mint and a pinch of salt.
Cook half the egg in half the oil in a non-stick pan for 2 minutes, until just set, and repeat.
Spread each omelette with yoghurt and top with cucumber and olives.
Roll up the omelettes, cut each in half and serve warm straight away.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Vegetarian. Gluten-free.

title: Vegetable Moussaka-Style Stacks
summary: Layered eggplant, potato and zucchini stacks baked in tomato sauce with a cheesy topping.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the eggplant, potato and zucchini with the oil and roast for 25 minutes, until golden.
Cook the onion and garlic for 5 minutes, add the tomatoes and cinnamon and simmer for 15 minutes, until thick.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, whisk in the milk and simmer for 6 minutes, until thick. Stir in half the cheese.
Layer the vegetables and sauce in a dish, top with the white sauce and remaining cheese and bake for 30 minutes, until golden and bubbling.

notes: Vegetarian.

title: Spanish Chicken and Chorizo Rice Bake
summary: Rice baked with chicken, chorizo, smoked paprika and peas.

steps.text: Brown the chicken and chorizo in the oil in an ovenproof pan for 8 minutes, until golden, and lift out. Cook the onion, capsicum and garlic for 5 minutes.
Add the paprika and rice, stir for 1 minute, then pour in the hot stock and return the meat.
Bake at 190°C (170°C fan) for 25 minutes, until the rice is tender and the chicken reaches 75°C.
Scatter the peas over, rest for 5 minutes until hot and serve with lemon.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part; refrigerate leftover rice within 1 hour.
Gluten-free.

title: Pork and Beef Meatballs in Smoky Almond Sauce
summary: Soft meatballs simmered in a smoky tomato and almond sauce.

steps.text: Mix the minces, egg, breadcrumbs, 1 garlic clove, parsley and salt and roll into 20 balls.
Brown the meatballs in half the oil for 8 minutes, until golden, and lift out.
Cook the onion in the remaining oil for 5 minutes, add the garlic, paprika, tomatoes, almond meal and stock and simmer for 10 minutes.
Return the meatballs and simmer for 10 minutes, until cooked through at 75°C and the sauce is thick.

notes: Food safety: meatballs must reach 75°C right through.

title: Garlic Prawn and Chorizo Eggs
summary: Eggs baked in a sizzling pan of garlic prawns and chorizo.

steps.text: Fry the chorizo in the oil for 3 minutes, until crisp. Add the garlic and chilli for 30 seconds.
Add the prawns and cook for 3 minutes, until pink and opaque.
Make four gaps, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 4 minutes, until the whites are set.
Scatter with parsley and serve with the bread.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Prawns are cooked when pink and opaque.

title: Roast Pork Loin with Sherry and Smoked Paprika
summary: Pork loin rubbed with paprika, roasted over potatoes and sherry.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Rub the pork with the paprika, garlic, half the oil and salt.
Toss the potato and onion with the remaining oil in a roasting dish, set the pork on top and pour in the sherry and stock.
Roast for 20 minutes, reduce to 180°C (160°C fan) and roast for 45 minutes, until the pork reaches 70°C and the potato is golden.
Rest the pork for 10 minutes, slice and scatter with parsley.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach 70°C in the centre, then rest.
Gluten-free.
Dairy-free.

title: Baked Hake with Pimenton Potatoes and Peppers
summary: Fish baked over smoky potatoes and roasted peppers with garlic and parsley.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the potato, capsicum, oil, paprika and garlic in a roasting dish and roast for 22 minutes, until nearly tender.
Nestle the fish into the vegetables and spoon over the lemon juice.
Roast for 12 minutes, until the fish turns opaque and flakes easily.
Scatter the parsley over the fish and potatoes and serve straight from the dish.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when opaque and flakes with a fork.
Gluten-free.
Dairy-free.

title: Spanish Mushroom and Egg Breakfast Toast
summary: Garlicky mushrooms and fried eggs on toasted bread with smoked paprika.

steps.text: Cook the mushrooms in half the oil for 8 minutes, until golden and dry. Add the garlic and paprika for 1 minute.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Toast the bread until golden.
Spoon the mushrooms onto the bread and top with the eggs and parsley.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Vegetarian. Dairy-free.

title: Seafood Fideua
summary: Short noodles cooked in saffron stock with prawns, mussels and squid, Valencian-style.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil in a wide pan for 5 minutes, then add the garlic and tomato and cook for 8 minutes, until thick and jammy.
Stir in the pasta and saffron for 2 minutes, then add the hot stock and simmer for 8 minutes, until nearly tender.
Nestle in the calamari, prawns and mussels, cover and cook for 6 minutes, until the prawns are pink, the calamari opaque and the mussel shells open. Discard any that stay closed.
Rest for 3 minutes and serve with aioli.

notes: Food safety: seafood is cooked when prawns are pink and opaque and mussel shells have opened; discard any that stay shut.

title: Lamb and Rosemary Pies
summary: Individual golden pies of tender lamb, rosemary and red wine.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil for 8 minutes, until golden. Add the onion, carrot and garlic for 6 minutes, stir through the flour, then add the wine, stock and rosemary.
Cover and simmer for 1 hour 30 minutes, until the lamb is tender and the sauce is thick. Cool.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Line six pie tins with pastry, fill, top with pastry and seal. Brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 30 minutes, until golden and the filling reaches 75°C.

notes: Food safety: the filling must be steaming hot (75°C) in the centre.

title: Pepper Steak with Mushroom Sauce and Chips
summary: A pan-seared sirloin with creamy mushroom pepper sauce and oven chips.

steps.text: Bake the chips on a tray at 220°C (200°C fan) for 30 minutes, until golden and crisp.
Press the pepper into the steaks and sear in the oil for 3 minutes each side for medium-rare, until the centre reaches 55°C. Rest for 5 minutes.
Cook the mushrooms and garlic in the butter in the same pan for 6 minutes, until golden. Add the brandy, cream and stock and simmer for 5 minutes, until thickened.
Serve the steaks with the sauce and chips.

notes: Food safety: whole steaks are safe seared; 55°C is medium-rare, 63°C medium, 71°C well done.

title: Chilli Prawn and Zucchini Pasta
summary: Garlicky chilli prawns tossed through linguine with zucchini, lemon and parsley.

steps.text: Cook the linguine in salted boiling water for 10 minutes, until al dente, and drain, keeping 1/2 cup of the water.
Cook the zucchini in the oil for 4 minutes, until golden, then add the garlic and chilli for 1 minute.
Add the prawns and cook for 3 minutes, until pink and opaque.
Toss the pasta through with the lemon, butter, parsley and a splash of pasta water.

notes: Food safety: prawns are cooked when pink, curled and opaque all the way through.

title: Smashed Pea and Haloumi Breakfast Stack
summary: Golden halloumi on smashed minty peas with a poached egg and lemon.

steps.text: Simmer the peas for 3 minutes, until bright and tender, drain and smash with the mint, oil, lemon zest and juice.
Fry the halloumi in a dry pan for 2 minutes each side, until golden.
Poach the eggs in barely simmering water with the vinegar for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Toast the sourdough until golden, then stack with the peas, halloumi and eggs.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Vegetarian.

title: Honey Soy Barramundi with Ginger Rice
summary: Barramundi fillets glazed with honey and soy over ginger-scented rice with greens.

steps.text: Mix the honey, soy sauce, ginger and garlic.
Cook the rice in boiling water for 12 minutes, until tender, and drain.
Sear the fish in the oil for 3 minutes per side, add the glaze and cook for 2 minutes, until sticky and the fish is opaque and flakes.
Steam the bok choy for 3 minutes, until tender, and serve with the rice, fish and spring onion.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when opaque and flakes with a fork.
Dairy-free.

title: Sweetcorn Fritter Stacks with Crisp Bacon
summary: Sweet corn fritters with crisp bacon, smashed avocado and lime.

steps.text: Mix the corn, flour, eggs, milk, spring onion and coriander with a pinch of salt into a thick batter.
Fry spoonfuls in the oil over medium heat for 3 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through.
Cook the bacon in a pan for 6 minutes, until crisp.
Mash the avocado with the lime juice and serve over the fritters with the bacon.

notes: Food safety: fritters are done when golden and set through; bacon should be cooked and crisp.

title: Pan-Fried Chicken in Marsala Mushroom Sauce
summary: Pan-fried chicken in a rich Marsala and mushroom sauce.

steps.text: Slice the chicken breasts in half horizontally and coat in flour. Fry in the oil for 4 minutes per side, until golden, and lift out.
Cook the mushrooms in the same pan for 6 minutes, until golden, then add the garlic.
Add the marsala and stock and simmer for 5 minutes, until reduced by half. Stir in the butter.
Return the chicken for 3 minutes until it reaches 75°C and serve with the sauce, parsley and potato.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part.

title: Slow-Roasted Tomato and Basil Risotto
summary: Creamy risotto with slow-roasted tomatoes, basil and mascarpone.

steps.text: Roast the tomatoes with 2 tablespoons of oil at 180°C (160°C fan) for 30 minutes, until collapsed and sticky.
Cook the onion in the remaining oil for 5 minutes, add the garlic and rice and stir for 2 minutes, then the wine until absorbed.
Add the hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring for 20 minutes, until the rice is creamy and tender.
Stir in the mascarpone, cheese and basil until creamy and top with the roast tomatoes.

notes: Vegetarian. Gluten-free.

title: Baked Gnocchi alla Sorrentina
summary: Potato gnocchi baked in tomato sauce under melting mozzarella and basil.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cook the garlic in the oil for 1 minute, add the passata and simmer for 8 minutes, until thick.
Stir in the gnocchi and half the basil and tip into a baking dish.
Top with mozzarella and cheese and bake for 20 minutes, until bubbling and golden.
Scatter with the remaining basil.

notes: Vegetarian.

title: Pork Fillet Saltimbocca with Sage Potatoes
summary: Pork fillet wrapped in prosciutto and sage, pan-fried and served with crisp potatoes.

steps.text: Roast the potato in 1 tablespoon of oil at 220°C (200°C fan) for 30 minutes, until crisp.
Cut the pork into eight pieces, flatten, top each with sage and wrap in prosciutto.
Fry in the remaining oil for 4 minutes per side, until golden and the centre reaches 70°C. Lift out and rest.
Add the wine to the pan and simmer for 3 minutes, whisk in the butter and spoon over the pork.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach 70°C in the centre with no pink.
Gluten-free.

title: Italian Breakfast Frittata with Spinach and Ricotta
summary: A thick baked frittata with spinach, ricotta and sundried tomatoes.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Wilt the spinach and spring onion in the oil in an ovenproof pan for 3 minutes, until soft.
Whisk the eggs with the cheese and seasoning and pour over, dotting with ricotta and tomato.
Cook on the stove for 3 minutes, until the edges set.
Bake for 15 minutes, until puffed and set in the centre.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Vegetarian. Gluten-free.

title: Tuscan Beef Stew with Rosemary and Red Wine
summary: Beef braised in red wine, tomato and rosemary until tender, served over polenta.

steps.text: Brown the beef in the oil in batches for 10 minutes, until deep golden, and lift out. Cook the onion and carrot for 6 minutes, add the garlic and wine and boil for 3 minutes.
Return the beef with the tomatoes, rosemary and stock, cover and simmer for 2 hours 30 minutes, until very tender.
Bring the water to the boil, whisk in the polenta and cook for 25 minutes, until thick, then stir in the butter.
Serve the beef over the polenta.

notes: Food safety: beef chuck is safe at 75°C and tender once it falls apart; the stew should be steaming hot.
Gluten-free.

title: Coq au Riesling-Style Chicken with Bacon and Onions
summary: Chicken braised in white wine with bacon, mushrooms and baby onions.

steps.text: Fry the bacon in a heavy pot until crisp for 5 minutes and lift out. Brown the chicken in the fat for 8 minutes, until golden, and lift out.
Cook the onions and mushrooms in the butter for 8 minutes, until golden, then add the garlic and wine and boil for 3 minutes.
Return the chicken and bacon with the stock and thyme, cover and simmer for 35 minutes, until the chicken reaches 75°C.
Stir in the cream, simmer for 5 minutes until slightly thick and serve with the potato.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part.
Gluten-free.

title: Mussels in White Wine and Garlic with Frites
summary: Mussels steamed in white wine, garlic and herbs, with crisp frites.

steps.text: Bake the chips at 220°C (200°C fan) for 30 minutes, until golden and crisp.
Cook the shallot in the butter in a large pot for 4 minutes, then add the garlic and wine and bring to the boil.
Add the mussels, cover and cook for 5 minutes, shaking the pot, until the shells have opened. Discard any that stay closed.
Stir in the cream and parsley and serve with the frites.

notes: Food safety: mussel shells must open when cooked; discard any that stay closed.

title: Pork Normande with Apples and Mustard
summary: Pork steaks with caramelised apple and a cream mustard sauce.

steps.text: Season the pork and sear in the oil for 5 minutes each side, until golden and the centre reaches 70°C. Lift out and rest.
Cook the apple in the butter for 4 minutes, until golden. Add the shallot and thyme for 2 minutes.
Add the apple juice and boil for 3 minutes, then the cream and mustard and simmer for 3 minutes, until slightly thick.
Return the pork for 1 minute and serve with the potato.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach 70°C in the centre, then rest.
Gluten-free.

title: French Omelette with Herbs and Goat Cheese
summary: A soft rolled omelette with chives, tarragon and creamy goat cheese.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs with the herbs and a pinch of salt.
Melt the butter in a non-stick pan until foaming and pour in the eggs.
Stir gently for 1 minute, then leave to set for 1 minute, until the base is just cooked and the top is still soft.
Add the goat cheese, roll onto a plate and serve.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Vegetarian. Gluten-free.

title: Lamb Navarin with Spring Vegetables
summary: A light French lamb stew with young carrots, peas and baby potatoes.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil in a heavy pot for 8 minutes, until golden. Add the onion and garlic for 5 minutes, stir through the paste and flour, then the wine and stock.
Add the thyme, cover and simmer for 1 hour, until the lamb is nearly tender.
Add the potatoes and carrots and cook for 30 minutes, until tender.
Stir through the peas for 3 minutes until hot.

notes: Food safety: lamb is safe at 63°C; this braise cooks well beyond that and should be steaming hot.

title: Smoked Salmon Egg Cocotte with Chives
summary: Eggs baked in cream with smoked salmon and chives in small ramekins.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Butter two ramekins and divide the salmon and cream between them.
Crack in the eggs and season.
Bake in a tray of hot water for 12 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks soft.
Scatter with chives and serve with toasted baguette.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Smoked salmon is not recommended during pregnancy.

title: Chicken and Leek Mash-Topped Pie
summary: A crusty mashed-potato topped pie of chicken and leek in a creamy sauce.

steps.text: Cook the leek in the butter for 6 minutes, add the chicken and cook for 8 minutes, until cooked through.
Stir in the flour for 1 minute, add the stock, cream and mustard and simmer for 6 minutes, until thick.
Tip into a dish and cover with mash mixed with the egg yolk, ruffling the top.
Bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 25 minutes, until golden and the filling is steaming and reaches 75°C.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C throughout and the pie be steaming hot.

title: Smoky Black Bean Tostada Stack
summary: Crisp corn tortillas layered with smoky beans, cheese, slaw and avocado.

steps.text: Brush the tortillas with oil and bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 8 minutes, until crisp.
Warm the beans with the chipotle and garlic and mash roughly for 5 minutes, until thick.
Spread the beans on the tostadas, top with cheese and grill for 2 minutes, until melted.
Top with slaw, avocado and coriander.

notes: Vegetarian. Gluten-free.

title: Moroccan Chicken Meatballs in Tomato with Eggs
summary: Spiced chicken meatballs poached in tomato sauce with eggs.

steps.text: Mix the mince, cumin, paprika, 1 garlic clove, parsley and salt and roll into 16 balls.
Brown the meatballs in half the oil for 6 minutes, until golden, and lift out. Cook the onion in the remaining oil for 5 minutes, add the garlic, tomatoes and harissa and simmer for 8 minutes.
Return the meatballs and simmer for 8 minutes, until cooked through at 75°C.
Crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 4 minutes, until the whites are set.

notes: Food safety: chicken mince must reach 75°C right through; cook the eggs until the whites are set.
Gluten-free.
Dairy-free.

title: Jerk Chicken Rice Bowls with Pineapple Slaw
summary: Jerk-spiced chicken over rice and beans with a crunchy pineapple slaw.

steps.text: Mix the oil, allspice, thyme, chilli, garlic and soy sauce and coat the chicken. Marinate for 1 hour.
Cook the rice in boiling water for 12 minutes, until tender, adding the beans for the last 2 minutes. Drain.
Cook the chicken in a hot pan for 12 minutes, turning, until charred and 75°C inside. Rest and slice.
Toss the pineapple, slaw and lime juice and serve over the rice with the chicken.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part.
Dairy-free.

title: Hungarian Paprika Potatoes with Fried Eggs
summary: Paprika potatoes with onion and sausage under fried eggs.

steps.text: Fry the sausage and onion in the oil for 8 minutes, until golden. Add the paprika, capsicum and potato with 1/2 cup water.
Cover and cook for 20 minutes, until the potato is tender and the water has gone.
Fry the eggs for 3 minutes in a separate pan, until the whites are set.
Serve the potatoes topped with the eggs and parsley.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set; serve firm yolks to young children, older people or anyone pregnant.
Gluten-free if you use a sausage labelled gluten-free. Dairy-free.

title: Pulled Beef Brisket Sliders
summary: Slow-cooked shredded brisket with tangy slaw in soft rolls.

steps.text: Mix the paprika, sugar, garlic powder and salt and rub over the brisket. Rest for 1 hour.
Place in a deep tray with the stock, cover tightly and cook at 150°C (130°C fan) for 4 hours 30 minutes, until the centre reaches 93°C and shreds easily.
Shred the beef in the juices and stir through the bbq sauce.
Pile into the buns with the slaw.

notes: Food safety: brisket needs to reach 93°C to shred (it is safe at 63°C); the filling should be steaming hot.

title: Strapatsada (Greek Scrambled Eggs with Tomato and Feta)
summary: Soft eggs folded through jammy fresh tomato and salty feta, served on toasted bread.

steps.text: Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat, add the grated tomato and oregano and simmer for 8 minutes, until thick and jammy.
Beat the eggs lightly with a pinch of salt and pour into the pan. Stir gently with a spatula for 3 minutes, until the eggs are just set but still soft.
Fold through half the feta, then serve over the bread and finish with the remaining feta and parsley.

notes: Grate the tomato on the large holes of a box grater and discard the skin.

Food safety: cook the eggs until firm enough to hold their shape, and keep leftovers in the fridge for no more than a day. Use fresh, uncracked eggs; for pregnant women, older people, young children and anyone with low immunity, cook the eggs until the yolks are firm.

title: Tiganites (Greek Pancakes with Honey and Walnuts)
summary: Thin, fluffy pan-fried pancakes drizzled with honey and scattered with cinnamon walnuts.

steps.text: Whisk the flour and baking powder in a bowl, then whisk in the egg, milk and 1 tablespoon of honey until a smooth, pourable batter forms.

Melt a little of the butter in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat and pour in 1/4 cup of batter. Cook for 2 minutes, until bubbles appear, then flip and cook for 1 minute, until golden. Repeat with the remaining batter and butter.
Stack the pancakes on plates, drizzle with the 1/4 cup of honey and top with the walnuts and cinnamon.

notes: Makes about 8 pancakes.
Vegetarian.

title: Beef Stifado with Whole Onions and Cinnamon
summary: A slow Greek beef stew with sweet whole onions, red wine, vinegar and warm cinnamon.

items.raw: 600g small brown onion, peeled and left whole

steps.text: Pat the beef dry and season. Heat half the oil in a large heavy pot over high heat and brown the beef in two batches for 5 minutes each, until deep brown. Set aside.

Add the remaining oil, onions and garlic and cook for 6 minutes, until the onions colour. Stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute, then pour in the wine and vinegar and bubble for 3 minutes, until reduced by half.
Return the beef, add the stock, cinnamon, bay leaves and allspice, cover and simmer gently over low heat for 2 hours, until the beef is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Take out the cinnamon and bay leaves, season to taste and scatter with parsley. Serve with crusty bread or boiled potatoes.

notes: Food safety: braised beef is safe once piping hot; it is tender when it reaches around 90°C inside. Cool leftovers within an hour and refrigerate for up to 3 days.
Gluten-free if you serve it with potatoes instead of bread.

title: Lamb Kleftiko-Style with Lemon, Oregano and Potatoes
summary: Lamb shoulder sealed in foil with garlic, lemon and feta, baked until it falls off the bone.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Cut a large sheet of foil and a matching sheet of baking paper and lay them in a deep roasting tin, with plenty overhanging.

Toss the potato, tomato, garlic, bay, half the lemon juice, half the oil and half the oregano in the tin. Rub the lamb with the remaining oil, lemon juice, oregano and plenty of salt and lay it on top.
Scatter the feta around the lamb, pour in the water and fold the foil over to seal the parcel tightly.
Bake for 3 hours 30 minutes, until the meat pulls away from the bone. Open the foil, raise the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and roast for 15 minutes, until the potatoes and lamb are browned.

notes: Food safety: lamb shoulder is safe at 70°C but becomes tender only around 90°C, so cook it until it shreds. Rest for 15 minutes before serving.
Gluten-free.

title: Gemista (Rice-Stuffed Tomatoes and Capsicums)
summary: Summer tomatoes and capsicums baked with a herby rice and pine nut filling beside crisp potatoes.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Slice the tops off the tomatoes and capsicums and keep them as lids. Scoop the tomato flesh into a bowl, break it up and discard the capsicum seeds.

Heat half the oil in a pan over medium heat and cook the onion and garlic for 5 minutes, until soft. Stir in the rice, tomato flesh, tomato paste, parsley, mint and pine nuts with a good pinch of salt and cook for 3 minutes.
Stand the vegetables in a deep tin, fill each two-thirds full (the rice swells), pop the lids on and tuck the potatoes around them.
Pour the water around the vegetables, drizzle with the remaining oil and bake for 1 hour 15 minutes, until the rice is tender and the potatoes are golden.

notes: Vegan and gluten-free.
Fill the vegetables only two-thirds so the rice has room to swell.

title: Spetsofai (Greek Sausage and Capsicum Stew)
summary: Browned sausages simmered with capsicum and tomato until rich and sticky, mopped up with bread.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large deep frying pan over medium heat and brown the sausages for 8 minutes, until golden. Lift out and slice thickly.
Cook the onion, capsicum and garlic in the same pan for 8 minutes, until softened and lightly coloured.
Add the tomatoes, oregano, chilli and sausage slices with a splash of water, cover and simmer for 20 minutes, until the sausage is cooked through and the sauce is thick.
Serve in bowls with the sourdough for mopping.

notes: Food safety: sausages must reach 75°C in the centre and have no pink inside before serving.
Check the sausage label if you need it gluten-free.

title: Pollo a la Vasca (Basque Chicken with Capsicum and Ham)
summary: Bone-in chicken braised with sweet capsicum, tomato, prosciutto and smoked paprika.

steps.text: Season the chicken. Heat the oil in a wide heavy pan over medium-high heat and brown the chicken, skin side down first, for 10 minutes, until deep golden. Set aside.
Cook the onion, capsicum, garlic and prosciutto in the same pan for 8 minutes, until soft. Stir in the paprika and chilli for 30 seconds.
Pour in the wine and bubble for 2 minutes, then add the tomatoes and return the chicken.
Cover and simmer for 30 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce is thick. Serve with rice or crusty bread.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C at the thickest part, with clear juices.
Gluten-free.

title: Revuelto de Setas (Spanish Mushroom Scramble on Toast)
summary: Garlicky sherried mushrooms folded into silky scrambled eggs.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over high heat and cook the mushrooms for 6 minutes, until golden and the liquid has gone. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Pour in the sherry and cook for 1 minute, until it has evaporated, then stir in the paprika.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt, pour over the mushrooms and stir gently over low heat for 3 minutes, until just set and creamy.
Serve over the bread, scattered with parsley.

notes: Vegetarian.

Food safety: cook the eggs until set, and refrigerate any leftovers promptly. Use fresh, uncracked eggs; for pregnant women, older people, young children and anyone with low immunity, cook the eggs until the yolks are firm.

title: Pollo al Ajillo (Spanish Garlic Chicken)
summary: Golden chicken thighs simmered in olive oil, plenty of garlic, sherry and smoked paprika.

steps.text: Season the chicken. Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium heat, add the chicken and brown for 6 minutes each side, until golden. Lift out.
Add the garlic and bay leaves to the oil and cook for 1 minute, until pale gold. Stir in the paprika, then pour in the sherry and stock.
Return the chicken, cover and simmer over low heat for 12 minutes, until cooked through and the sauce is syrupy.
Finish with the lemon juice and parsley and serve with bread or potatoes.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part, with no pink inside.
Keep the garlic pale gold, as dark garlic turns bitter.

title: Migas with Chorizo and Fried Eggs
summary: Crisp fried breadcrumbs with chorizo and garlic, topped with a runny egg for a hearty Spanish breakfast.

items.raw: 4 thick slice stale sourdough bread, torn into small pieces

steps.text: Sprinkle the bread with the water and toss, then leave for a few minutes to soften slightly.
Cook the chorizo in a large frying pan over medium heat for 4 minutes, until the fat runs. Add 2 tablespoons of the oil, the garlic, capsicum and paprika and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the bread and fry, tossing often, for 8 minutes, until crisp and golden. Spoon onto plates.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil for 3 minutes, until the whites are set, and slide one onto each plate.

notes: Food safety: fry the eggs until the whites are fully set; skip runny yolks for children, older adults and anyone pregnant.
Stale bread crisps best; fresh bread can be dried in a low oven.

title: Croque Madame
summary: Toasted ham and gruyere sandwiches under a creamy cheese sauce, topped with a fried egg.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and line a tray with baking paper. Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk a little at a time and simmer for 5 minutes, until thick. Season with nutmeg and salt.
Top 4 slices of bread with the ham and half the gruyere, then close the sandwiches with the other slices. Place on the tray and spread each with the white sauce.
Scatter the remaining gruyere on top and bake for 12 minutes, until the cheese is bubbling and golden.
Fry the eggs in a non-stick pan over medium heat for 3 minutes, until the whites are set, and place one on each sandwich.

notes: Food safety: fry the eggs until the whites are fully set; skip runny yolks for children, older adults and anyone pregnant.
Use sliced bread that is a day old if you can, as it holds the sauce better.

title: Galette Complète (Buckwheat Crepes with Ham, Egg and Gruyere)
summary: Lacy buckwheat crepes folded around ham, melted gruyere and a soft egg.

steps.text: Whisk the buckwheat flour, 1 egg, water and salt in a bowl until smooth, then melt 20g of the butter and whisk it in.

Heat a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat and brush with a little butter. Pour in a quarter of the batter and swirl to coat. Cook for 2 minutes, until the edges lift and the base is crisp, then flip.
Scatter a quarter of the ham and gruyere in the centre, crack an egg on top and cook for 4 minutes, until the white is set and the cheese has melted.
Fold in the four sides to make a square, slide onto a plate and repeat with the remaining batter and filling.

notes: Food safety: cook the egg until the white is fully set; skip runny yolks for children, older adults and anyone pregnant.
Gluten-free: buckwheat flour is gluten-free but check the packet for cross-contamination.

title: Boeuf en Daube Provençale
summary: Beef braised for hours with red wine, orange peel, tomato and olives, in the style of Provence.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C (130°C fan). Brown the beef in the oil in a heavy casserole over high heat in batches for 4 minutes each, until deep brown. Set aside.
Cook the pancetta, onion and carrot in the same pot for 8 minutes, until golden. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and boil for 5 minutes, until reduced by a third. Return the beef, add the tomatoes, orange peel, thyme and bay leaves and bring to a simmer.
Cover and bake for 2 hours 30 minutes, until the beef is very tender, adding the olives for the last 15 minutes. Season to taste.

notes: Food safety: braised beef is tender at around 90°C inside. Cool leftovers within an hour and refrigerate for up to 3 days; it improves on day two.
Gluten-free. Serve with creamy mash or buttered pasta.

title: Poulet Rôti à l'Ail (Roast Chicken with Whole Garlic)
summary: Roast chicken scented with thyme and lemon, surrounded by soft, sweet cloves of garlic and crisp potatoes.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Rub the chicken all over with the butter and salt, then put the lemon and half the thyme in the cavity.
Scatter the potatoes, onion, garlic and remaining thyme in a roasting tin and sit the chicken on top. Pour the wine into the tin.
Roast for 1 hour 15 minutes, until the skin is golden and the juices run clear, turning the potatoes once.
Rest the chicken for 15 minutes, then carve and serve with the potatoes, squeezing the soft garlic from its skins.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part of the thigh, with clear juices. Rest it for 15 minutes.
Gluten-free.

title: Tartiflette-Style Potato Bake
summary: Sliced potatoes baked with bacon, onion, white wine and melting soft cheese.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Boil the potato slices in salted water for 8 minutes, until just tender, then drain.
Cook the bacon and onion in the oil in a frying pan over medium heat for 8 minutes, until golden. Add the wine and boil for 2 minutes, until reduced.
Layer half the potato in a baking dish, scatter with half the bacon mixture and half the cheese. Repeat, then pour the cream over the top.
Bake for 25 minutes, until the cheese is bubbling and golden. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

notes: Food safety: cook the bacon until browned and serve the dish piping hot; refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Traditionally made with reblochon; gruyere melts just as well.

title: Fish Meunière with Lemon Butter and Baby Potatoes
summary: Flour-dusted white fish fillets pan-fried in butter and finished with lemon, parsley and capers.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes, until tender, then drain and keep warm.

Season the fish and dust lightly with the flour. Melt half the butter in a large frying pan over medium-high heat and cook the fish for 3 minutes each side, until golden and opaque all the way through. Lift onto plates.
Add the remaining butter to the pan and cook for 2 minutes, until it smells nutty and is golden brown. Take off the heat and stir in the lemon juice, capers and parsley.
Spoon the butter over the fish and serve with the potatoes.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily with a fork.
Use any firm white fish such as snapper, flathead or whiting.

title: Quiche Lorraine
summary: A buttery homemade pastry case filled with bacon, gruyere and a silky egg and cream custard.

steps.text: Rub the butter into the flour with your fingertips until it looks like breadcrumbs, then mix in the egg and iced water until a dough forms. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan), roll the dough out to fit a 23cm tart tin, prick the base with a fork and bake with baking paper and weights for 15 minutes, until pale golden. Remove the paper and weights and bake for 5 minutes more.
Fry the bacon in a pan over medium heat for 5 minutes, until golden, and scatter over the pastry with the gruyere.
Whisk the eggs, cream, milk, nutmeg and a pinch of salt and pour over the filling. Reduce the oven to 170°C (150°C fan).
Bake for 30 minutes, until the filling is set with a slight wobble in the centre. Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

notes: Food safety: the custard must be set and the centre hot (at least 72°C). Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Good served warm or cold.

title: Frittata di Pasta (Italian Pasta Frittata)
summary: A thick, golden omelette studded with spaghetti, peas and herbs, sliced like a cake.

steps.text: Cook the spaghetti in salted boiling water for 8 minutes, adding the peas for the last minute, then drain and cut roughly with scissors.
Beat the eggs with the cheese, parsley, salt and pepper and stir in the pasta and peas.
Heat the oil in a 24cm non-stick frying pan over medium heat, pour in the mixture and cook for 8 minutes, until the base is golden and the edge is set.
Slide onto a plate, flip back into the pan and cook for 5 minutes, until the centre is firm. Cut into wedges.

notes: Food safety: cook until the egg is fully firm; refrigerate leftovers within an hour and eat within 2 days.
Vegetarian; good warm or at room temperature.

title: Ricotta and Honey Toast with Pear and Walnuts
