summary: Thick sourdough toast spread with creamy ricotta, sliced pear, toasted walnuts and honey.

steps.text: Toast the walnuts in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 3 minutes, until fragrant.
Stir the lemon zest into the ricotta and spread thickly over the toast.
Top with the pear slices and walnuts and drizzle with the honey.

notes: Vegetarian.
Ripe, juicy pears work best; swap in figs when in season.

title: Sweet Polenta Porridge with Cinnamon Apples and Almonds
summary: Creamy polenta cooked in milk and served with buttery spiced apple and crunchy almonds.

steps.text: Bring the milk, water and honey to a gentle simmer in a saucepan, then whisk in the polenta in a thin stream. Cook, stirring often, for 10 minutes, until thick and creamy.
Melt the butter in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the apple with the cinnamon for 5 minutes, until soft and golden.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 2 minutes, until golden.
Spoon the porridge into bowls and top with the apple and almonds.

notes: Vegetarian and gluten-free.
Loosen with a splash of hot milk if it thickens as it stands.

title: Egg Bruschetta with Roasted Tomatoes and Ricotta
summary: Garlic-rubbed sourdough topped with blistered cherry tomatoes, ricotta and a fried egg.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the tomatoes with half the oil and a pinch of salt in a tin and roast for 12 minutes, until blistered and bursting.
Rub the toasted bread with the cut garlic and spread with the ricotta, until evenly covered.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Pile the tomatoes on the bread, top with the eggs and basil, then serve right away.

notes: Food safety: fry the eggs until the whites are fully set; skip runny yolks for children, older adults and anyone pregnant.
Vegetarian.

title: Aussie Burger with the Lot
summary: A beef patty piled with bacon, egg, beetroot, pineapple, cheese and tomato sauce on a toasted bun.

steps.text: Mix the mince with the salt and shape into four patties about 2cm thick. Press a dent into the middle of each.
Heat half the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 10 minutes, until soft and golden. Push to the side, add the bacon and cook for 4 minutes, until crisp.
Cook the patties on a hot barbecue plate or in the pan for 5 minutes each side, until browned and cooked through. Top each with cheese for the last minute, until melted.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil for 3 minutes, until the whites are set, and grill the pineapple for 1 minute each side, until lightly charred.
Build the burgers on the buns with lettuce, tomato, beetroot, pineapple, patty, bacon, egg, onion and tomato sauce.

notes: Food safety: burger patties must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Fry the eggs until the whites are fully set.
Swap the beef for a vegetarian patty if you like, but check the label.

title: Sweet Potato and Chickpea Hash with Poached Eggs
summary: Crisp spiced sweet potato and chickpeas topped with poached eggs, avocado and lime.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the sweet potato with the oil, cumin, paprika and salt on a large tray and roast for 20 minutes, until browned.
Add the chickpeas and onion, toss and roast for 10 minutes, until the onion softens and the chickpeas are crisp at the edges.
Bring a wide pan of water to a gentle simmer. Crack in the eggs one at a time and poach for 3 minutes, until the whites are set. Lift out with a slotted spoon.
Divide the hash among plates and top with the eggs, avocado, coriander and a lime wedge.

notes: Food safety: poach the eggs until the whites are fully set; skip runny yolks for children, older adults and anyone pregnant.
Vegetarian and gluten-free.

title: Macadamia-Crusted Chicken Schnitzel with Lemon
summary: Thin chicken fillets in a crunchy macadamia and panko crumb, shallow-fried and served with lemon.

items.raw: 600g chicken breast, sliced in half horizontally

steps.text: Place the chicken between two sheets of baking paper and flatten to 1cm with a rolling pin. Season with salt.
Put the flour on one plate, the beaten eggs in a shallow bowl and the panko mixed with the macadamias on a third plate. Dust the chicken in flour, dip in egg, then press into the crumbs to coat.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat and fry the schnitzels for 4 minutes each side, until deep golden and cooked through. Drain on paper towel.
Scatter with parsley and serve with the lemon wedges.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part, with no pink inside. Keep the pan at medium so the crumb does not burn before the centre is cooked.
Serve with steamed greens or a pile of chips.

title: Chicken and Sweetcorn Pie with Mustard Cream
summary: A creamy chicken, leek and corn filling under a crisp puff pastry lid.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a large pan over medium heat and cook the chicken and leek for 8 minutes, until the chicken is no longer pink on the outside and the leek is soft.
Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then add the stock and milk gradually, stirring, and simmer for 8 minutes, until thick. Stir in the corn and mustard, season and cool for 15 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Spoon the filling into a 1.5L pie dish, cover with the pastry, trim and crimp the edges and brush with the egg.
Cut a small steam hole and bake for 30 minutes, until the pastry is puffed and golden and the filling is bubbling.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the centre and the filling must be piping hot. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Egg wash is raw egg on the pastry only; it is fully cooked in the oven.

title: Trofie al Pesto with Potato and Green Beans
summary: The Ligurian way: twisted pasta cooked with potato and beans, tossed through fresh basil pesto.

items.raw: 150g green beans, cut into short lengths

steps.text: Blitz the basil, pine nuts, garlic, oil and cheese in a food processor with a pinch of salt until a coarse paste forms, adding a splash of cold water if it is thick.
Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil and cook the potato for 5 minutes. Add the pasta and cook for 8 minutes, adding the beans for the last 3 minutes, until the pasta is al dente.
Scoop out a mug of the cooking water, then drain. Return to the pot off the heat and toss with the pesto and enough cooking water to make it creamy.

notes: Vegetarian.
Add the pesto off the heat so the basil keeps its colour.

title: Provençal Chicken with Olives, Tomato and Thyme
summary: Bone-in chicken braised with ripe tomatoes, black olives, white wine and orange peel.

steps.text: Season the chicken. Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat and brown the chicken for 10 minutes, until golden all over. Set aside.
Cook the onion and garlic in the same pan for 6 minutes, until soft. Pour in the wine and boil for 2 minutes, until reduced by half.
Add the tomatoes, olives, orange peel and thyme, return the chicken and simmer covered for 25 minutes.
Add the zucchini and cook uncovered for 10 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce is thick.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C at the thickest part, with clear juices.
Gluten-free and dairy-free.

title: Piperade with Fried Eggs and Jamón
summary: A Basque pan of slowly stewed capsicum, onion and tomato topped with ham and fried eggs.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and cook the onion, capsicum and garlic for 12 minutes, until very soft. Stir in the paprika for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and a pinch of salt and simmer for 15 minutes, until thick and glossy.
Make four wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook for 5 minutes, until the whites are set.
Lay the prosciutto over the top and serve from the pan with bread.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set; skip runny yolks for children, older adults and anyone pregnant.
Gluten-free if served without bread.

title: Lomo Saltado (Peruvian Beef Stir-Fry with Chips)
summary: Beef, red onion and tomato wok-tossed with soy and vinegar, served over rice with oven chips.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the chips with 1 tablespoon of oil and salt on a tray and bake for 30 minutes, until golden and crisp.
Cook the rice in a covered pot with 1 1/2 cups of water for 12 minutes, until the water is absorbed, then rest covered for 5 minutes.
Heat a wok over very high heat with the remaining oil and sear the beef in two batches for 2 minutes each, until browned. Set aside.
Stir-fry the garlic, onion and chilli for 2 minutes, until charred at the edges. Add the tomato, soy and vinegar and toss for 1 minute, then return the beef and cook for 1 minute.
Fold in the chips and coriander and serve over the rice.

notes: Food safety: beef strips are cooked once browned and hot through (at least 63°C). Keep cooked rice hot, or cool and refrigerate it within an hour.
Dairy-free.

title: Aji de Gallina (Peruvian Creamy Chicken)
summary: Shredded chicken in a mild, golden walnut and chilli sauce, served over potatoes with egg.

steps.text: Poach the chicken in the water with a pinch of salt over low heat for 18 minutes, until cooked through. Lift out, shred and keep 1 cup of the stock.
Soak the bread in the milk, then blitz with the walnuts and reserved stock until a smooth sauce forms.
Heat the oil in a deep pan over medium heat and cook the onion and garlic for 8 minutes, until soft. Stir in the chilli paste, turmeric and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the sauce and cheese, stir for 8 minutes until thick, then fold in the chicken and warm through for 3 minutes.
Serve over the potatoes with the egg and olives.

notes: Food safety: poached chicken must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside; the finished dish must be piping hot.
Cook the eggs for 10 minutes so the yolks are firm.

title: Oaxacan-Style Black Bean Tlayudas
summary: Big crisp tortillas spread with garlicky black beans, melting cheese, cabbage, avocado and lime.

steps.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a small pan, cook the garlic and cumin for 1 minute, then add the beans with a splash of water and mash roughly for 4 minutes, until thick and spreadable.
Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Lay the tortillas on two trays and bake for 5 minutes, until stiff and lightly browned.
Spread the beans over the tortillas, scatter with the mozzarella and bake for 6 minutes, until the cheese has melted and the edges are crisp.
Toss the cabbage with the lime juice and the remaining oil, then pile onto the tortillas with the avocado, tomato, coriander and chilli.

notes: Vegetarian.
Use the biggest tortillas you can find; two per person makes a generous dinner.

title: Kotopita (Greek Chicken and Feta Filo Pie)
summary: Crisp, buttery filo layers around a creamy filling of chicken, feta, ricotta and dill.

steps.text: Poach the chicken in the water at a gentle simmer for 15 minutes, until cooked through. Lift out and shred finely.
Cook the onion in the oil over medium heat for 6 minutes, until soft. Mix in a bowl with the chicken, feta, ricotta, eggs, dill and pepper.

Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Brush a 20cm x 30cm dish with butter and layer in half the filo, brushing each sheet with butter. Spread over the filling and cover with the rest of the filo, brushing between sheets.
Score the top into squares and bake for 40 minutes, until deep golden and puffed. Rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the centre and the pie must be hot all the way through. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Keep unused filo covered with a damp cloth so it does not dry out.

title: Yiouvarlakia (Greek Meatballs in Egg and Lemon Sauce)
summary: Soft rice-and-herb meatballs poached in broth, finished with a silky egg and lemon sauce.

steps.text: Mix the mince, rice, onion, parsley, 1 egg, oil, salt and pepper and roll into 16 walnut-sized balls.
Bring the stock to a gentle simmer in a wide pot, add the meatballs and cook covered over low heat for 40 minutes, until the rice is tender and the meatballs are cooked through.
Whisk the 2 eggs and lemon juice in a bowl, then slowly whisk in 1 cup of hot stock. Take the pot off the heat and stir the egg mixture in gently.
Return to very low heat for 2 minutes, until the sauce thickens slightly. Do not let it boil or it will curdle.

notes: Food safety: meatballs must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. The sauce is thickened by the heat of the stock, so keep it just below a boil until the eggs are set.
Gluten-free and dairy-free.

title: Arroz al Horno (Spanish Baked Rice with Pork Ribs and Chorizo)
summary: A Valencian tray of rice baked in stock with pork ribs, chorizo, chickpeas and tomato.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Brown the ribs and chorizo in the oil in a large ovenproof pan over medium-high heat for 8 minutes, until golden.
Add the tomato and paprika and cook for 3 minutes, until thick. Stir in the rice and chickpeas for 1 minute.
Pour in the stock mixed with the saffron, nestle the garlic on top and bring to a simmer, until bubbling across the pan. Do not stir again.
Bake uncovered for 40 minutes, until the stock is absorbed and the surface is crusty. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C; the ribs should be tender at the end. Cool leftover rice within an hour and refrigerate.
Dairy-free.

title: Hachis Parmentier (French Beef and Potato Pie)
summary: Savoury beef mince under buttery mashed potato with a golden gruyere crust.

steps.text: Boil the potato in salted water for 18 minutes, until tender, then drain, mash with the butter and milk and season.

Heat the oil in a large pan and cook the onion and carrot for 6 minutes, until soft. Add the mince and cook for 8 minutes, until browned and broken up. Stir in the tomato paste and flour for 1 minute.
Pour in the stock and simmer for 8 minutes, until thick. Tip into a baking dish and heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Cover with the mash, rake the top with a fork and scatter with the gruyere. Bake for 20 minutes, until golden and bubbling.

notes: Food safety: the mince filling must reach 75°C and be piping hot before it is topped. Cool leftovers within an hour.
Good for the freezer for up to 3 months.

title: Orecchiette with Sausage and Broccolini
summary: Pugliese-style ear-shaped pasta with browned Italian sausage, garlic, chilli and tender broccolini.

items.raw: 2 bunch broccolini, cut into short lengths

steps.text: Cook the pasta in plenty of salted boiling water for 10 minutes, adding the broccolini for the last 3 minutes, until the pasta is al dente. Reserve a mug of cooking water, then drain.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat and cook the sausage, breaking it into chunks, for 8 minutes, until browned and cooked through.
Add the garlic and chilli for 1 minute, then toss through the pasta, broccolini, lemon zest and enough cooking water to make a glossy sauce.

notes: Food safety: sausage must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside.
Dairy-free.

title: Swiss Brown Mushroom Risotto with Thyme
summary: Creamy arborio rice stirred with browned mushrooms, white wine, thyme and a little butter.

steps.text: Heat half the oil in a large pan over high heat and cook the mushrooms for 6 minutes, until golden. Set aside.
Add the remaining oil, onion and garlic and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes, until soft. Stir in the rice for 1 minute, then add the wine and stir until absorbed.
Add the hot stock a ladleful at a time, stirring often, for 20 minutes, until the rice is creamy and tender with a slight bite. Add the thyme and mushrooms halfway.
Take off the heat and beat in the butter and cheese. Rest, covered, for 2 minutes.

notes: Vegetarian.
Keep the stock at a simmer in a second pot so the rice cooks evenly.

title: Enfrijoladas (Oaxacan Bean-Sauced Tortillas with Eggs)
summary: Corn tortillas dipped in smooth black bean sauce and topped with eggs, crumbled cheese and avocado.

steps.text: Blend the beans with the water, garlic, cumin and a pinch of salt until smooth. Pour into a wide pan and simmer for 8 minutes, until thickened to a thin gravy.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 30 seconds each side, until soft and pliable. Dip each in the bean sauce, fold into quarters and arrange on plates.
Fry the eggs in the oil over medium heat for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Top each plate with an egg, extra sauce, feta, avocado and coriander.

notes: Food safety: fry the eggs until the whites are fully set; skip runny yolks for children, older adults and anyone pregnant.
Vegetarian.

title: Pollo a la Brasa-Style Roast Chicken with Potatoes
summary: Peruvian-spiced chicken with cumin, paprika, garlic and soy, roasted with crisp potatoes.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Mix the soy, oil, vinegar, garlic, cumin, paprika and oregano into a paste and rub it over the chicken, working it under the skin.
Toss the potato with a spoonful of the paste and a pinch of salt in a large roasting tin and sit the chicken on top, skin side up.
Roast for 50 minutes, until the skin is crisp and the potatoes golden.
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes and serve with the lime wedges.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part, with clear juices.
Dairy-free.

title: Jamaican Oven Jerk Chicken
summary: Chicken thighs rubbed with a fiery allspice, thyme and scotch bonnet paste, then roasted until sticky and charred.

steps.text: Blitz the spring onion, allspice, thyme, chilli, garlic, soy sauce, lime juice, sugar, oil and nutmeg to a coarse paste.
Slash the thighs to the bone, rub the paste in well, then cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Lay the chicken skin side up on a rack over a lined tray.
Roast for 40 to 45 minutes, until the skin is dark and crisp and the juices run clear.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve with rice and peas or fried plantain.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Jamaican Curried Chicken
summary: A turmeric-heavy Jamaican curry of chicken and potato in a mellow, golden sauce with a little scotch bonnet heat.

items.raw: 800g chicken thigh fillet, cut in chunks

steps.text: Rub the chicken with half the curry powder and the turmeric and leave for 30 minutes.
Fry the remaining curry powder in the oil for 1 minute, then add the onion, garlic and ginger and cook until soft.
Add the chicken and brown for 5 minutes.
Add the potato, thyme, chilli and stock, cover and simmer for 35 minutes, until the potato is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Scatter with spring onion and serve with rice.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Trinidadian Chicken Pelau
summary: Chicken browned in burnt sugar, then cooked with rice, pigeon peas and coconut milk in one pot.

items.raw: 800g chicken thigh fillet, cut in chunks

steps.text: Season the chicken with the garlic, thyme and a pinch of salt.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot, add the sugar and cook until dark amber and foaming, then add the chicken and brown for 8 minutes.
Add the onion and carrot and cook for 3 minutes, then stir in the rice, peas and tomato sauce.
Pour in the coconut milk and stock, bring to a boil, cover and cook on low for 25 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid has absorbed.
Rest for 10 minutes, fold through the spring onion and serve hot.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Cool leftover rice quickly and refrigerate within an hour.

title: Trinidadian Doubles
summary: Soft fried bara flatbreads filled with spiced curried chickpeas and a sharp tamarind and chilli sauce.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, turmeric, sugar and a pinch of salt with the warm water into a soft dough. Knead for 5 minutes and rest, covered, for 1 hour.
Fry the onion and garlic until soft, add the cumin and curry powder for 1 minute, then add the chickpeas and water.
Simmer for 20 minutes, mashing some chickpeas, until thick and saucy.
Stir the tamarind, chilli and lime juice together for the sauce.
Shape the dough into 12 thin discs and deep fry for 30 seconds a side, until puffed and pale gold.
Fill two bara with chickpeas, top with sauce and serve warm.

notes: Vegan and dairy-free.

title: Trinidadian Aloo Pie
summary: Fried turmeric dough pockets filled with spiced mashed potato, served with tamarind chutney.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, turmeric, sugar, salt and water to a soft dough, knead for 5 minutes and rest for 1 hour.
Boil the potato until tender, drain, mash with the cumin, curry powder, garlic and spring onion, and cool.
Divide the dough into 6, flatten each, fill with potato, fold over and seal the edges firmly.
Deep fry for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until golden and puffed.
Serve hot with the tamarind paste thinned with a little water.

notes: Vegan and dairy-free.

title: Cuban Pan con Lechon
summary: Garlic and citrus roast pork piled into crusty bread with caramelised onions.

steps.text: Blend the garlic, juices, cumin, oregano and 2 tsp salt, pour over the pork and marinate overnight.
Heat the oven to 160°C. Roast the pork covered for 3 hours, until it pulls apart and reaches 90°C in the centre.
Cook the onion in the oil for 25 minutes, until soft and golden.
Shred the pork, moisten with the pan juices and pile into split rolls with the onions.
Toast the filled rolls in a hot pan or press for 2 minutes until the bread is crisp.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Puerto Rican Pollo Guisado
summary: Chicken and potatoes braised in a sofrito-style tomato sauce with olives and capers.

items.raw: 800g chicken thigh fillet, cut in chunks

steps.text: Season the chicken with the cumin, oregano and salt.
Brown it in the oil in a large pot, then add the onion, capsicum and garlic and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, tomatoes, stock and potato.
Cover and simmer for 30 minutes, until the potato is tender and the chicken is cooked through.
Add the olives, capers and coriander and serve with rice.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Puerto Rican Pernil
summary: Garlic and oregano pork shoulder roasted low and slow until the crackling shatters.

steps.text: Crush the garlic, oregano, oil, vinegar, salt and pepper to a paste.
Score the skin, cut deep slits in the meat and rub the paste in everywhere. Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Heat the oven to 160°C. Roast for 4 hours, until the meat reaches 90°C in the centre and shreds easily.
Increase to 230°C for the last 20 minutes, until the skin is blistered and crisp.
Rest for 20 minutes, then shred or carve.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Cottage Pie with Cheddar Mash
summary: Rich beef and vegetable mince under a golden, cheesy mash.

steps.text: Boil the potato until tender, drain and mash with the butter and milk, then stir in half the cheddar.
Brown the mince in the oil for 8 minutes, then add the onion, carrot and celery and cook until soft.
Stir in the paste and flour, then add the stock, worcestershire and thyme and simmer for 15 minutes, until thick.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Spoon the mince into a baking dish, top with mash and the rest of the cheddar.
Bake for 25 minutes, until bubbling and golden.

notes: Food safety: beef mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.

title: Steak and Ale Pie
summary: Slow-cooked beef and ale filling under a golden puff pastry lid.

steps.text: Toss the beef in the flour and brown in batches in the oil until deeply coloured.
Add the onion, carrot and mushroom and cook for 5 minutes, then stir in the paste, ale, stock, bay leaves and thyme.
Cover and simmer gently for 2 hours, until the beef is tender and the sauce has thickened. Cool slightly.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Spoon the filling into a pie dish, lay the pastry over, trim and brush with egg.
Bake for 30 minutes, until the pastry is puffed and golden.

notes: Food safety: mince and beef must be cooked through to 75°C with no pink in the middle. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.

title: Irish Beef and Guinness Stew
summary: Beef braised with root vegetables in a malty stout gravy.

steps.text: Toss the beef in the flour and brown in batches in the oil in a heavy pot until deeply coloured.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes, then stir in the paste.
Pour in the stout and stock, add the thyme and bay leaves, cover and simmer for 1 1/2 hours.
Add the carrot, parsnip and potato and cook for 40 minutes more, until the beef and vegetables are tender and the gravy has thickened.
Serve in wide bowls with soda bread to mop up the gravy.

notes: Food safety: mince and beef must be cooked through to 75°C with no pink in the middle. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.

title: Fish Pie with Prawns and Parsley
summary: Cod, salmon and prawns in a creamy parsley sauce under a golden mash crust.

steps.text: Poach the fish in the milk for 5 minutes, then strain, keeping the milk, and flake into a baking dish with the prawns and peas.
Make a sauce by melting 30g butter, stirring in the flour, then whisking in the hot milk until thick and smooth. Add the parsley and mustard and pour over the fish.
Boil the potato until tender, mash with the remaining butter and the egg, and spread over the top.
Bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 30 minutes, until golden and the filling is bubbling and prawns are pink.

notes: Food safety: fish should be opaque and flake easily, at least 63°C. Eat within a day of cooking and keep refrigerated.
Prawns must be pink and firm. Eat within a day of cooking.

title: Coronation Chicken Jacket Potato
summary: Curried chicken in a creamy mango mayo over a fluffy baked potato.

steps.text: Bake the potatoes at 200°C (180°C fan) for 1 hour, until the skins are crisp and the centres soft.
Poach the chicken in simmering water for 15 minutes, until cooked through at 75°C, then cool and shred.
Mix the mayonnaise, yoghurt, chutney, curry powder and lemon juice, then fold through the chicken, sultanas and spring onion.
Split the potatoes, fill with the chicken and top with almonds.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Keep the chicken mixture refrigerated until serving.

title: Wiener Schnitzel
summary: Thin veal cutlets crumbed and shallow-fried in butter until golden and puffed, with lemon.

steps.text: Crush the veal to 5mm thick and season well.
Dredge each piece in flour, then beaten egg, then breadcrumbs, pressing lightly.
Heat the butter and oil in a wide pan and fry the schnitzels for 2 to 3 minutes a side, shaking the pan, until golden and crisp.
Drain on paper and serve with lemon wedges, parsley and potato salad.

notes: Food safety: mince and beef must be cooked through to 75°C with no pink in the middle. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Veal must be cooked until no pink remains.

title: Hungarian Beef Goulash
summary: Beef and paprika slowly stewed with onions and capsicum until the sauce is rich and brick red.

steps.text: Brown the beef in the oil in batches and set aside.
Cook the onion until deep gold, add the garlic, then take off the heat and stir in the paprika, caraway and paste.
Return the beef with the stock and bay leaves, cover and simmer for 1 1/2 hours.
Add the capsicum and potato and cook for 40 minutes more, until the beef is tender and the sauce is thick.
Serve with bread or egg noodles.

notes: Food safety: mince and beef must be cooked through to 75°C with no pink in the middle. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.

title: Polish Bigos Hunter's Stew
summary: Sauerkraut, cabbage, pork and kielbasa simmered slowly into a smoky, tangy stew.

steps.text: Brown the pork and kielbasa in the oil in a large pot, then add the onion and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the sauerkraut, cabbage, chopped soaked mushrooms, prunes, paste, bay leaves and juniper.
Pour in the stock and simmer, covered, for 2 hours, stirring occasionally, until the pork is very tender.
Rest overnight if you can, then reheat and serve with rye bread.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Sausage must reach 75°C in the centre.

title: Czech Bramboraky Potato Pancakes
summary: Crisp garlicky potato pancakes fried until lacy and golden.

steps.text: Grate the potato, squeeze out the liquid and mix with the eggs, flour, crushed garlic, marjoram and salt.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat.
Drop in spoonfuls, flatten and fry for 3 to 4 minutes a side, until deep golden and crisp at the edges.
Drain on paper and serve hot.

notes: Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Dairy-free. Fry until the eggs are set through.

title: German Rouladen
summary: Beef slices rolled around bacon, mustard, onion and pickle, then braised in rich gravy.

steps.text: Spread each slice with mustard and top with bacon, onion and a pickle quarter, then roll up and tie with string.
Brown the rolls in the oil, set aside, then fry the carrot, celery and paste for 5 minutes.
Add the wine, stock and rolls, cover and simmer for 1 1/2 hours, until the beef is very tender.
Whisk a little flour with water, stir into the pan juices and simmer until the gravy is thick.
Remove the string and serve with potato dumplings and red cabbage.

notes: Food safety: mince and beef must be cooked through to 75°C with no pink in the middle. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.

title: Moroccan Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemon
summary: Chicken braised with saffron, ginger, olives and preserved lemon until the sauce turns fragrant and golden.

steps.text: Rub the chicken with the ginger, turmeric, cumin, salt and pepper and brown it in the oil in a heavy pot until golden on all sides.
Add the onion, garlic and saffron and cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in the stock, cover and simmer for 40 minutes, until the chicken is tender and the sauce has reduced.
Add the lemon rind and olives for the last 5 minutes.
Scatter with coriander and serve with couscous.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Egyptian Koshari
summary: Rice, lentils and pasta layered with spiced tomato sauce and crisp fried onions.

steps.text: Simmer the lentils for 20 minutes until tender, drain, then cook the rice and pasta until tender.
Toss the onion in the flour and fry in the oil in batches for 15 minutes, until crisp and dark golden.
Fry the garlic and cumin in 2 tbsp oil for 1 minute, add the tomatoes and chilli and simmer for 15 minutes until thick, then add the vinegar.
Layer the rice, lentils, pasta and chickpeas in bowls, spoon over the sauce and top with onions.

notes: Vegan and dairy-free.

title: Egyptian Hawawshi
summary: Pita stuffed with spiced beef and onion, baked until the bread is crisp and the filling juicy.

steps.text: Mix the mince with the onion, capsicum, garlic, cumin, paprika, parsley, tomato and salt.
Cut the top off each pita to make a pocket and stuff with the filling, pressing it flat.
Brush with the oil and bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 25 minutes, until the bread is crisp and the beef reaches 75°C.
Rest for 3 minutes, slice and serve.

notes: Food safety: beef mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.

title: Tunisian Chicken Couscous
summary: Spiced chicken and vegetables over fluffy couscous with a harissa broth.

items.raw: 600g chicken thigh fillet, cut in chunks

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil, add the onion and garlic and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the harissa and cumin, then add the carrot, stock and chickpeas and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the zucchini and cook for 10 minutes more, until the chicken is cooked through and the vegetables are tender.
Pour the boiling water over the couscous, cover for 5 minutes and fluff.
Serve the stew over the couscous.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Algerian Chicken Chakchouka
summary: Peppers, tomatoes and chicken braised with cumin, finished with softly set eggs.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil for 5 minutes until no longer pink, then set aside.
Soften the onion, capsicum and garlic for 8 minutes, add the spices and tomatoes and simmer for 12 minutes.
Return the chicken, make 4 wells and crack in the eggs.
Cover and cook for 5 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are just soft.
Top with parsley and serve with bread.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set.

title: Sheikh al Mahshi (Lebanese Lamb-Stuffed Zucchini in Yoghurt)
summary: Small zucchini filled with spiced lamb and pine nuts, simmered in a tangy warm yoghurt sauce.

steps.text: Hollow out the zucchini with a corer, leaving the walls about 5mm thick.
Cook the onion in the oil over medium heat for 5 minutes, until soft. Add the lamb, allspice, salt and pepper and cook for 8 minutes, until browned. Stir in the rice and pine nuts.
Fill each zucchini about three quarters full and arrange in a wide pot.

Whisk the yoghurt, egg white and cornflour in a saucepan over low heat, stirring in one direction, until it just starts to bubble. Pour over the zucchini, add the garlic and 1/2 cup water and simmer gently for 25 minutes, until the zucchini are tender.
Scatter the mint over and serve with the sauce spooned around.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Always stir the yoghurt in one direction over low heat so it does not split.

title: Fatteh bil Djej (Levantine Chicken Fatteh)
summary: Layers of crisp pita, chickpeas and shredded chicken under garlicky yoghurt and toasted pine nuts.

steps.text: Put the chicken, onion and cinnamon in a pot, cover with water and simmer for 25 minutes, until cooked through. Lift out the chicken and shred it. Keep 1/2 cup of the stock.
Tear the pita into pieces, toss with the oil and bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 8 minutes, until crisp.
Warm the chickpeas in the reserved stock for 3 minutes. Whisk the yoghurt, garlic, tahini and lemon juice with salt.
Toast the pine nuts in the butter for 2 minutes, until golden.
Layer the pita in a deep dish, add the chickpeas with a little stock, then the chicken and yoghurt. Top with the pine nuts and parsley and serve straight away.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Assemble at the last minute so the pita keeps some crunch.

title: Chicken Mandi (Yemeni Spiced Rice with Chicken)
summary: Fragrant long grain rice with tender spiced chicken, a Yemeni feast dish cooked until the meat falls off the bone.

steps.text: Rub the chicken with the oil, half the spices, the garlic and 1 tsp salt. Rest at room temperature while you start the rice, up to 30 minutes.
Brown the chicken in a large heavy pot over medium-high heat for 8 minutes. Add the onion and tomato and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the stock and bring to a simmer. Cover and cook for 30 minutes, until the chicken is very tender. Lift out the chicken.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear. Add the rice and remaining spices to the stock, cover and cook on low for 15 minutes, until the stock is absorbed.
Meanwhile, grill the chicken for 6 minutes, until the skin is crisp. Fry the almonds and sultanas in the butter for 2 minutes. Pile the rice on a platter, top with the chicken, almonds and sultanas.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Cool leftover rice quickly and eat within a day.

title: Saltah (Yemeni Lamb and Vegetable Stew)
summary: A bubbling Yemeni stew of lamb, tomato and lentils, served in a hot dish with rice.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil in a heavy pot over high heat for 8 minutes, until deeply coloured. Add the onion and garlic and cook for 4 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, tomato and spices and cook for 3 minutes, until thick.
Add the water, lentils and 1 tsp salt. Cover and simmer for 45 minutes, until the lamb is tender.
Add the potato and capsicum and cook for 15 minutes, until the potato is soft and the stew is thick.
Serve in bowls over the rice, with extra black pepper and a squeeze of lemon if you like.

notes: Food safety: lamb pieces should reach at least 70°C and be tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour; reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Ghormeh Sabzi (Persian Herb and Lamb Stew)
summary: The classic Persian herb stew with lamb, kidney beans and dried lime, deep green and sour.

steps.text: Brown the lamb with the onion and turmeric in half the oil in a heavy pot for 10 minutes.
Fry the herbs in the remaining oil in a pan over medium heat for 10 minutes, until dark and fragrant.
Add the herbs, pierced dried limes and water to the lamb. Cover and simmer on low for 1 1/2 hours, until the lamb is very tender.
Add the beans and simmer for 20 minutes. Season, then add lemon juice to taste.
Spoon the stew over the rice in shallow bowls and serve hot.

notes: Food safety: lamb pieces should reach at least 70°C and be tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour; reheat until steaming hot.
Canned beans are already cooked. If you use dried kidney beans, soak them overnight and boil hard for 10 minutes before they go in.
Dairy-free and gluten-free. Better the next day.

title: Fesenjan (Persian Chicken in Walnut and Pomegranate Sauce)
summary: Chicken braised in a rich, sweet-sour sauce of ground walnuts and pomegranate molasses.

steps.text: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 5 minutes, then grind finely in a food processor.
Cook the onion in the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat for 10 minutes, until golden. Add the turmeric and the chicken and brown for 5 minutes.
Add the walnuts and water and bring to a simmer. Cover and cook on low for 40 minutes, stirring now and then.
Stir in the molasses, honey and cinnamon and cook uncovered for 20 minutes, until the sauce is thick and dark. Taste and balance the sweet and sour.
Spoon the chicken and sauce over the rice on warm plates and serve at once.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains walnuts. Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Zereshk Polo ba Morgh (Persian Rice with Saffron Chicken)
summary: Buttery saffron rice jewelled with sweet sultanas, served with tender saffron chicken.

steps.text: Grind the saffron with a pinch of salt and steep in 3 tbsp hot water.
Brown the onion in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the chicken, half the saffron, tomatoes and 1 cup water. Cover and simmer for 35 minutes, until tender.
Boil the rice in plenty of salted water for 6 minutes, until just soft outside and firm inside. Drain.
Fry the sultanas (or barberries, if you can find them) in 1 tbsp butter with the sugar for 1 minute, until plump.

Layer the rice in the pot with the remaining butter, the rest of the saffron water and a tea towel under the lid. Steam on low for 25 minutes. Pile onto a platter, scatter the sultanas and almonds over and serve with the chicken.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Gluten-free.

title: Joojeh Kabab (Persian Saffron Chicken Skewers)
summary: Juicy saffron and yoghurt marinated chicken pieces grilled over high heat.

items.raw: 800g chicken thigh fillets, cut into chunks

steps.text: Steep the saffron in 2 tbsp hot water. Mix with the onion (and its juice), yoghurt, lemon juice, oil, garlic, salt and pepper. Add the chicken and marinate in the fridge for at least 4 hours.
Thread onto flat skewers with the tomatoes at the ends.
Grill over a hot barbecue or griddle for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until browned at the edges and cooked through.
Slide the chicken off the skewers onto a bed of rice with the grilled tomatoes and spoon over any juices from the platter.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Marinate in the fridge, never on the bench. Discard leftover marinade.

title: Kubideh (Persian Minced Lamb Kebabs)
summary: Soft, onion-rich minced lamb kebabs pressed on to flat skewers and grilled.

steps.text: Squeeze the onion dry. Knead it with the mince, turmeric, salt and pepper for 5 minutes, until sticky and well combined.
With wet hands, mould the mince around flat skewers in a long sausage shape, pressing flat with finger dents.
Grill the kebabs and tomatoes on a hot barbecue or griddle for 8 to 10 minutes, turning once, until cooked through.
Brush with butter, dust with sumac and serve in the flatbread.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Chill the shaped skewers for 30 minutes so they hold together.

title: Adana Kebab (Turkish Spicy Lamb Kebabs)
summary: Hand-chopped style lamb kebabs with tail-fat richness and chilli, grilled on wide skewers.

steps.text: Squeeze out the capsicum and onion well, then knead into the lamb with the pepper, cumin and salt for 5 minutes.
Press around wide skewers in a long flat shape. Chill for 30 minutes.
Toss the sliced onion, parsley and sumac with the oil.
Grill over high heat for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through. Serve in flatbread with the onion.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Use less Aleppo pepper if you like it mild.

title: Iskender Kebab (Turkish Sliced Lamb on Pide with Tomato and Yoghurt)
summary: Thin lamb strips over torn pide, with hot tomato sauce, melted butter and cool yoghurt.

steps.text: Season the lamb with the cumin, oregano, salt and pepper. Sear in batches in the oil over high heat for 2 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through.
Cook the onion and garlic in the same pan for 4 minutes. Add the paste and tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes, until thick.
Toast the pide until crisp at the edges, then tear into pieces. Divide among plates.
Top with the lamb and tomato sauce. Melt the butter until it sizzles and pour it over, then spoon on the yoghurt.

notes: Food safety: lamb slices should reach at least 70°C with no pink. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Serve straight away so the bread stays soft rather than soggy.

title: Manti (Turkish Lamb Dumplings with Garlic Yoghurt)
summary: Tiny lamb dumplings baked until crisp, served with garlic yoghurt and chilli butter.

steps.text: Knead the flour, egg, water and 1/2 tsp salt into a firm dough. Rest for 30 minutes.
Mix the lamb with the onion, parsley, salt and pepper.
Roll the dough very thin, cut into 3cm squares and place a pinch of filling in each. Pinch the corners together to seal.
Bake the manti in a 220°C (200°C fan) tray for 15 minutes, until golden. Pour over the hot stock and bake for 10 minutes more.
Mix the yoghurt and garlic. Melt the butter with the paprika and mint. Serve the manti with the yoghurt and the spiced butter.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Freeze uncooked manti on a tray, then bag them. Cook from frozen, adding 5 minutes.

title: Karniyarik (Turkish Eggplant Stuffed with Spiced Lamb)
summary: Split eggplants fried until soft and filled with a tomato and lamb mixture, baked until sticky.

steps.text: Peel the eggplants in stripes and slit lengthways, leaving the ends joined. Salt lightly and rest for 15 minutes, then pat dry.
Fry the eggplants in the oil over medium heat for 10 minutes, turning, until soft and golden. Place in a baking dish.
Cook the onion and garlic in a little oil, add the lamb and cook for 8 minutes. Add the tomato, capsicum, half the paste and the parsley and cook for 6 minutes.
Open the eggplants and pack in the filling. Mix the rest of the paste with the water and pour around.
Cover and bake at 190°C (170°C fan) for 30 minutes, until tender.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Hunkar Begendi (Turkish Lamb Stew on Smoky Eggplant Puree)
summary: The Sultan's Delight: tender lamb stew over a creamy, smoky eggplant and cheese puree.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the onion and cook for 4 minutes, then the tomato, capsicum, paste, water, salt and pepper. Cover and simmer for 1 hour, until tender.
Char the eggplants over a gas flame or under a hot grill for 15 minutes, turning, until blackened and collapsed. Peel and mash the flesh.
Melt the butter, whisk in the flour for 1 minute, then add the milk and cook until thick. Stir in the eggplant and cheese for 4 minutes, until smooth.
Spoon the puree on plates and top with the lamb.

notes: Food safety: lamb pieces should reach at least 70°C and be tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Uses mild cheddar, which is not suitable for vegetarians.

title: Nashville Hot Chicken
summary: Crisp fried chicken brushed with a fiery cayenne oil and served on white bread with pickles.

steps.text: Soak the chicken in the buttermilk, hot sauce and 1 tsp salt in the fridge for at least 4 hours.
Mix the flour, smoked paprika, garlic powder and 1 tsp salt. Dredge the chicken, pressing the flour on.
Heat the oil to 170°C in a deep heavy pot. Fry in two batches for 14 minutes, until deep golden and 75°C inside. Drain on a rack.
Whisk 1/3 cup of the hot frying oil with the cayenne, sugar and paprika. Brush it over the chicken.
Serve on the bread with pickles.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Hot oil can spit and ignite: never fill a pot more than a third full and keep a lid nearby. Wear gloves when handling the cayenne oil.

title: Southern Smothered Pork Chops
summary: Pan-fried chops simmered in a dark onion gravy until fork-tender.

steps.text: Season the chops with salt, pepper, paprika and garlic powder, then dust in 1/4 cup of the flour.
Brown in the oil in a large lidded pan over medium-high heat for 4 minutes per side. Lift out.
Cook the onion in the pan for 8 minutes, until golden. Stir in the garlic and the remaining flour for 1 minute. Add the stock, thyme and Worcestershire and stir until smooth.
Return the chops, cover and simmer gently for 25 minutes, until tender and the gravy has thickened.
Spoon the chops and onion gravy over the rice on warm plates and serve hot.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Dairy-free.

title: Shrimp Etouffee
summary: Prawns smothered in a roux-based Creole sauce with the holy trinity of onion, capsicum and celery.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a heavy pot and stir in the flour. Cook, stirring, for 8 minutes, until the roux is the colour of peanut butter.
Add the onion, capsicum and celery and cook for 8 minutes, until soft. Stir in the garlic, paste and seasoning for 1 minute.
Whisk in the stock, add the bay leaves and simmer for 15 minutes, until thick.
Add the prawns and cook for 4 minutes, until pink and opaque. Remove the bay leaves, add the spring onion and serve over rice.

notes: Food safety: prawns are cooked when pink and opaque all through; do not overcook or they turn rubbery. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Contains shellfish. Cajun seasoning is salty, so taste before adding extra salt.

title: Chicken and Andouille Gumbo
summary: A deep brown roux gumbo with chicken thigh, smoked sausage and okra, served over rice.

steps.text: Whisk the oil and flour in a heavy pot over medium-low heat for 30 to 40 minutes, stirring constantly, until the roux is the colour of dark chocolate. Do not stop stirring or it will burn.
Add the onion, capsicum and celery and cook for 6 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the stock. Add the chicken, sausage, seasoning and bay leaves and simmer for 40 minutes.
Add the okra and cook for 10 minutes. Skim off excess oil, season and serve over rice.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Roux is extremely hot and sticks to skin. Take care when adding the vegetables, as they will spit.

title: Shrimp Creole
summary: Prawns in a spicy tomato and capsicum sauce, served over steamed rice.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a large pan and cook the onion, capsicum and celery for 8 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, stock, seasoning, paprika and bay leaves. Simmer for 15 minutes, until thick.
Add the prawns and cook for 4 minutes, until pink. Remove the bay leaves, stir in the hot sauce and serve over rice.

notes: Food safety: prawns are cooked when pink and opaque all through; do not overcook or they turn rubbery. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Contains shellfish. Gluten-free.

title: King Ranch Chicken Casserole
summary: A Texas classic of shredded chicken, corn tortillas, cheese and a creamy chilli sauce baked until bubbling.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Cook the onion and capsicum in the butter for 6 minutes. Stir in the flour, chilli and cumin for 1 minute, then whisk in the stock and cook until thick. Stir in the sour cream and tomatoes.
Tear the tortillas. Layer half in a baking dish, then half the chicken, half the sauce and a third of the cheese. Repeat, finishing with the remaining cheese.
Bake for 25 minutes, until golden and bubbling.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C before shredding and make sure the casserole is steaming hot in the middle. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Uses cheddar, which is not suitable for vegetarians.

title: Loco Moco
summary: The Hawaiian comfort plate: a beef patty on rice, topped with a fried egg and rich brown gravy.

steps.text: Mix the mince, egg, breadcrumbs, garlic powder, salt and pepper and shape into 4 patties. Fry in the oil for 5 minutes per side, until cooked through. Rest.
Cook the onion in the butter for 8 minutes, until golden. Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the stock and soy. Simmer for 6 minutes until thick.
Fry the 4 eggs sunny side up, or until the whites are fully set and the yolks as firm as you like.
Pile rice on plates, add a patty, an egg and the gravy.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot. Cook the eggs until the whites are set; avoid runny yolks for the very young, elderly, pregnant or unwell.

title: Huli Huli Chicken
summary: Sweet, sticky grilled chicken with pineapple, soy and ginger, a Hawaiian roadside favourite.

steps.text: Mix the juice, soy, sugar, tomato sauce, ginger, garlic and vinegar. Reserve 1/2 cup and marinate the chicken in the rest in the fridge for at least 4 hours.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Bake the chicken for 30 minutes.
Simmer the reserved marinade for 5 minutes, until syrupy, and brush on the chicken. Grill for 8 minutes, turning, until charred in spots. Grill the pineapple for 2 minutes per side.
Serve with rice and the grilled pineapple, spooning any pan juices over.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot. Use only the reserved, unused marinade as a glaze.

title: Moqueca Baiana (Brazilian Fish and Coconut Stew)
summary: Fish simmered in coconut milk with tomato, capsicum and coriander, a Bahian favourite.

items.raw: 600g firm white fish fillets, cut into chunks

steps.text: Toss the fish with the lime juice, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Marinate in the fridge for 20 minutes.
Cook the onion, capsicum and garlic in the oil in a wide pot for 8 minutes. Add the tomato and paprika for 4 minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk and simmer for 8 minutes. Add the fish and cook gently for 5 minutes, until opaque and flaking.
Stir in the coriander and serve with rice.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when opaque and reaches 63°C. Eat on the day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Escondidinho de Carne (Brazilian Beef and Potato Mash Bake)
summary: Seasoned beef hidden under a golden layer of creamy mash and cheese.

steps.text: Boil the potato in salted water for 20 minutes, until very soft. Mash with the butter and milk until smooth.
Cook the onion in a pan for 5 minutes. Add the mince and cook for 8 minutes, until browned. Stir in the garlic, tomato, cumin and paste and cook for 8 minutes, until thick. Add the parsley.
Spread the beef in a baking dish and cover with the mash and mozzarella.
Bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 20 minutes, until golden and bubbling.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Estrogonofe de Frango (Brazilian Chicken Stroganoff)
summary: Creamy chicken in a mild tomato and mushroom sauce, served with rice and crunchy potato sticks.

steps.text: Season the chicken and brown in the oil in a large pan for 6 minutes. Lift out.
Cook the onion and garlic for 4 minutes, add the mushroom and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the paste, tomato sauce and mustard, return the chicken and simmer for 8 minutes, until cooked through.
Stir in the cream and lime juice and warm through. Serve with rice and potato sticks.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Do not boil after the cream goes in.

title: Milanesa Napolitana (Argentinian Crumbed Beef with Ham, Tomato and Cheese)
summary: A thin crumbed beef cutlet topped with napoli sauce, ham and melted cheese.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs with the garlic, parsley, salt and pepper. Dip the beef in the egg, then press into the breadcrumbs.
Shallow-fry in the oil for 3 minutes per side, until golden. Drain on paper.
Place on a tray, top with the passata, ham and cheese. Grill for 5 minutes, until melted and bubbling.
Serve the milanesas hot with a pile of chips and a wedge of lemon on the side.

notes: Food safety: beef must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink. Use separate hands and a clean plate for raw and cooked beef. Contains egg.
Flatten the beef thin between baking paper with a rolling pin if the butcher has not done it.

title: Pastel de Choclo (Chilean Corn and Beef Pie)
summary: A savoury pie of beef, olives and egg under a thick, golden crust of sweet corn.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the beef and cook for 8 minutes, until browned. Stir in the cumin, paprika, salt and pepper. Spoon into a baking dish and top with the sultanas, olives and egg.
Blend the corn, basil, milk and butter into a thick puree. Cook in a pan, stirring, for 8 minutes, until it thickens.
Spread the corn over the filling and sprinkle with the sugar.
Bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 25 minutes, until golden and browned in spots.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot. Boil the eggs for 10 minutes and use within a day of cooking.
Contains egg.

title: Bandeja Paisa (Colombian Mixed Plate)
summary: The big Antioquian platter of beans, rice, pork, fried egg, plantain and avocado.

items.raw: 1 cup dried red kidney beans, soaked

steps.text: Simmer the soaked beans with half the onion, 1 clove of garlic and water to cover for 50 minutes, until soft. Season with salt.
Cook the remaining onion, garlic and tomato in a little oil for 8 minutes for a hogao and stir half into the beans.
Pan-fry the pork belly slices in the oil for 12 minutes, until crisp and cooked through. Cook the chorizo in the same pan for 8 minutes.
Fry the plantain for 3 minutes per side, until golden, and the eggs until the whites are set.
Serve everything on a large plate with the rice and avocado.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour. Cook the eggs until the whites are set. Kidney beans must be boiled hard for 10 minutes then simmered until fully soft.
Contains egg.

title: Pabellon Criollo (Venezuelan Shredded Beef, Black Beans and Plantain)
summary: Venezuela's national plate: slow-cooked shredded beef, black beans, rice and sweet fried plantain.

steps.text: Cover the beef with water, add the onion, garlic and 1 tsp salt and simmer for 2 hours, until it shreds easily. Cool slightly and shred.
Cook the capsicum and tomato in the olive oil for 8 minutes. Add the beef, cumin and 1/2 cup stock and simmer for 15 minutes, until saucy.
Warm the beans with the sugar and a splash of water for 8 minutes.
Fry the plantain in the vegetable oil for 3 minutes per side, until golden.
Serve the beef, beans and plantain in separate piles on a plate beside the rice.

notes: Food safety: beef is simmered well past 75°C in the centre until it shreds, and must be steaming hot when served. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Seco de Cordero (Peruvian Lamb and Coriander Stew)
summary: Lamb braised in a vivid green coriander and beer sauce, served with rice and beans.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil in a heavy pot for 8 minutes. Add the onion, garlic, cumin and aji paste and cook for 6 minutes.
Blend the coriander, spinach and beer into a smooth green paste. Pour into the pot with the stock.
Cover and simmer for 1 hour 15 minutes, until the lamb is tender. Add the potato for the last 25 minutes and the peas for the final 5.
Serve the stew in wide bowls beside the rice and spoon plenty of the green sauce over the top.

notes: Food safety: lamb pieces should reach at least 70°C and be tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Dairy-free.

title: Uova in Purgatorio (Eggs in Tomato Purgatory)
summary: Eggs poached in a fiery tomato sauce with chilli and garlic, mopped up with crusty bread.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a deep frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic and chilli for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomatoes and oregano with salt and pepper. Simmer for 10 minutes until thickened.
Make four wells in the sauce and crack in the eggs. Cover and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are still soft.
Scatter with basil and serve with toasted sourdough.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set. Serve hot and refrigerate leftovers within an hour.

title: Flammekueche (Alsatian Onion and Mushroom Tarte Flambée)
summary: A paper-thin Alsatian flatbread spread with tangy cream and topped with sweet onion and mushrooms.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 250°C (230°C fan) with two trays inside. Mix the flour, baking powder, salt, oil and water into a firm dough and knead for 2 minutes.
Stir the sour cream, ricotta, nutmeg, salt and pepper together.
Divide the dough in two and roll each piece very thin on baking paper, about 3mm.
Spread with the cream mixture, then top with the onion, mushrooms and thyme.
Slide onto the hot trays and bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until the edges are charred and crisp. Cut into squares.

notes: The dough needs no rising, so it is quick enough for a weeknight.
Swap the mushrooms for extra onion if you prefer the classic look.

title: Huevos a la Flamenca (Baked Eggs with Chorizo and Peas)
summary: Eggs baked in a smoky tomato and pepper base with chorizo, peas and asparagus.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Heat the oil in an ovenproof frying pan and fry the chorizo for 3 minutes until it releases its oil.
Add the onion and capsicum and cook for 6 minutes, then stir in the garlic and paprika for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and 1/2 cup water, simmer for 8 minutes, then stir through the peas.
Make eight wells and crack in the eggs. Bake for 8 to 10 minutes, until the whites are set.
Scatter with parsley and serve from the pan.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set and the sauce is steaming hot. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Serve with crusty bread.

title: Poulet Basquaise (Basque Chicken with Peppers)
summary: Chicken thighs braised with sweet peppers, tomatoes and smoked paprika in the style of the Basque country.

steps.text: Season the chicken and brown it skin side down in the oil in a large pan for 6 minutes. Turn, brown for 3 minutes more, then lift out.
Cook the onion and capsicums in the same pan for 8 minutes, then add the garlic and paprika for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes. Add the tomatoes, stock and thyme.
Return the chicken, cover and simmer for 25 minutes, until cooked through and tender. Uncover for the last 5 minutes to thicken the sauce.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Good with rice or boiled potatoes.

title: Frango Piri-Piri (Portuguese Piri-Piri Chicken Traybake)
summary: Chicken marinated in a chilli, lemon and garlic paste and roasted with potatoes until sticky and charred.

steps.text: Mix the lemon juice, garlic, oil, vinegar, paprika, chilli, oregano and salt. Coat the chicken and marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the potatoes and onion in a little oil on a large tray and push to the sides.
Add the chicken to the middle with the marinade. Roast for 40 to 45 minutes, turning once, until cooked through and charred at the edges.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Do not reuse raw marinade as a sauce. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Prep time excludes marinating.

title: Kolokithokeftedes (Greek Zucchini Fritters with Yoghurt)
summary: Crisp fritters of grated zucchini, feta and mint, served with garlicky yoghurt.

steps.text: Toss the zucchini with the salt and leave for 10 minutes, then squeeze out as much water as you can in a clean tea towel.
Mix the zucchini with the crumbled feta, eggs, flour, spring onion, mint and dill. Season with pepper.
Heat half the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Drop in heaped spoonfuls, flatten slightly and fry for 3 to 4 minutes each side until golden, working in batches.
Stir the garlic into the yoghurt. Serve the fritters hot with the yoghurt and lemon.

notes: Food safety: cook the fritters until the centre is set and hot. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Serve with a handful of leaves and some bread to make it a meal.

title: Soutzoukakia (Greek Cumin Meatballs in Tomato Sauce)
summary: Oval cumin-scented beef meatballs simmered in a cinnamon tomato sauce.

steps.text: Mix the mince, breadcrumbs, egg, half the garlic, the cumin, parsley, vinegar, salt and pepper. Shape into 16 short ovals.
Brown the meatballs in half the oil in a wide pan for 5 minutes, turning, then lift out.
Cook the onion in the remaining oil for 5 minutes, add the rest of the garlic, then the tomatoes, cinnamon and sugar.
Return the meatballs, cover and simmer for 20 minutes, until cooked through and the sauce is thick.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with rice or mashed potato.

title: Mücver (Turkish Zucchini and Herb Fritters)
summary: Golden zucchini fritters with dill, spring onion and white cheese, served with a garlic yoghurt.

steps.text: Salt the zucchini and leave for 10 minutes, then squeeze very dry in a tea towel.
Mix with the crumbled feta, eggs, flour, spring onion, dill, parsley and pepper.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Fry spoonfuls for 3 minutes each side until golden and set.
Stir the garlic into the yoghurt and serve alongside.

notes: Food safety: cook the fritters until the centre is set and hot. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Add a spoon of flour if the mix seems wet.

title: Mujaddara (Lebanese Lentils and Rice with Crispy Onions)
summary: Brown lentils and rice spiced with cumin and topped with deeply browned onions.

steps.text: Simmer the lentils in plenty of water for 15 minutes, until nearly tender, then drain.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat and cook the onion for 20 minutes, stirring often, until deep brown and crisp at the edges. Lift out half for topping.
Add the cumin and cinnamon to the pan, then the lentils, rice, water and 1 tsp salt. Bring to the boil, cover and cook on low for 15 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes, fluff with a fork and top with the reserved onion. Serve with yoghurt and lemon.

notes: Vegan if you swap the yoghurt for a dairy-free one.
Stir often once the onions start to colour so they do not burn.

title: Kuku Sabzi (Persian Herb Frittata)
summary: A dense green frittata packed with parsley, coriander, dill and walnuts, with a hint of turmeric.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs with the flour, baking powder, turmeric, salt and pepper. Fold in the herbs, spring onion and walnuts.
Heat the oil in a 24cm non-stick frying pan over medium heat and pour in the mixture.
Cover and cook on low for 12 minutes, until the base is golden and the top is nearly set.
Slide onto a plate, flip back into the pan and cook 4 minutes more. Cut into wedges and serve with yoghurt.

notes: Food safety: cook until the egg is fully set in the centre. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Eaten warm or cold, with flatbread.

title: Adas Polo (Persian Lentil Rice with Sultanas and Saffron)
summary: Fragrant basmati rice layered with lentils, caramelised onion, cinnamon and sweet sultanas.

steps.text: Boil the lentils for 12 minutes until just tender, drain. Boil the rice in salted water for 6 minutes, then drain.
Cook the onion in the oil for 15 minutes until golden, stir in the cinnamon, turmeric and sultanas for 2 minutes.
Melt the butter in a pot, stir in saffron soaked in 2 tbsp hot water, then layer in the rice, lentils and onion mixture.
Wrap the lid in a tea towel, cover and steam on low for 25 minutes. Top with toasted almonds.

notes: Use half a teaspoon of ground saffron if you do not have threads.
Swap the butter for olive oil to make it vegan.

title: Boxty (Irish Potato Pancakes with Creamy Mushrooms)
summary: Pan-fried potato pancakes from the Irish midlands, topped with garlic mushrooms in a thyme cream.

steps.text: Squeeze the grated potato dry in a tea towel. Mash the boiled potato and mix both with the flour, milk, baking powder and 1 tsp salt to a thick batter.
Melt half the butter in a large frying pan and fry spoonfuls, flattened to 1cm, for 4 minutes each side until golden. Keep warm in a low oven.
Melt the remaining butter in a second pan, cook the mushrooms for 6 minutes, then add the garlic and thyme for 1 minute.
Pour in the cream and simmer for 2 minutes. Spoon over the boxty and top with chives.

notes: Squeeze the potato well, or the pancakes will be gluey.

title: Irish Stew (Lamb and Potato)
summary: Tender lamb with potatoes, carrots and onions simmered in a light broth until the potatoes start to thicken it.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil in a heavy pot in two batches, 5 minutes each, then lift out.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes. Layer the lamb, carrot and potato in the pot, seasoning each layer with salt and pepper.
Pour over the stock, add the thyme and bay leaf, bring to the boil, then cover and simmer gently for 1 hour 15 minutes, until the lamb is tender and the potatoes are soft.
Skim off any fat, scatter with parsley and serve in bowls.

notes: Food safety: lamb pieces must reach 71°C in the centre and be steaming hot throughout. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
A splash of Worcestershire sauce is common but not traditional.

title: Placki Ziemniaczane (Polish Potato Pancakes with Sour Cream)
summary: Crisp grated potato and onion pancakes, served with sour cream and a fried egg.

steps.text: Grate the potatoes and onion, then squeeze out as much liquid as you can in a clean tea towel.
Stir in the two eggs, flour, salt and pepper straight away, until the mix is thick and evenly coated.
Heat half the oil in a large frying pan and fry spoonfuls, pressed flat, for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp. Drain on paper towel.
Fry the remaining four eggs in the same pan until the whites are set. Serve the pancakes with an egg, sour cream and chives.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Fry in batches and keep warm in a low oven.

title: Vareniki (Ukrainian Potato and Onion Dumplings)
summary: Soft little dumplings filled with mashed potato and golden onion, tossed in browned butter.

steps.text: Mix the flour, egg, water and 1/2 tsp salt into a soft dough, knead for 3 minutes, then cover.
Boil the potatoes until tender, 12 minutes, drain and mash. Cook the onion in half the butter for 10 minutes until golden and mix into the potato with salt and pepper.
Roll the dough thin, cut 8cm rounds, fill each with a spoonful of potato and pinch tightly shut.
Boil in batches for 4 to 5 minutes, until they float. Toss in the remaining butter, browned, and serve with sour cream and dill.

notes: Prep time excludes resting the dough for 20 minutes.
Cooked dumplings freeze well.

title: Raggmunk (Swedish Potato Pancakes with Lingonberry and Fried Egg)
summary: Thin, crisp Swedish potato pancakes served with tart berry jam and a fried egg.

steps.text: Whisk the milk, flour, two eggs and salt into a thin batter, then stir in the grated potato.
Melt a little butter in a large non-stick pan. Spoon in the batter to make thin pancakes about 10cm wide and fry for 3 minutes each side until golden and crisp at the edges.
Fry the remaining eggs in butter until the whites are set.
Serve the pancakes with the eggs and a spoonful of lingonberry jam.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Cranberry sauce works if you cannot find lingonberry.

title: Biff à la Lindström (Swedish Beef and Beetroot Patties)
summary: Beef patties studded with beetroot, capers and onion, fried until crusty and served with potatoes.

items.raw: 200g canned beetroot, drained and finely diced

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes until tender, then drain.
Mix the mince, egg, breadcrumbs, milk, beetroot, onion, capers, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Shape into 8 patties.
Melt the butter in a large frying pan over medium heat and fry the patties for 5 minutes each side, until browned and cooked through.
Serve with the potatoes and parsley.

notes: Food safety: patties must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Pickled cucumber is a good side.

title: Chile con Carne (Texan Beef and Bean Chilli)
summary: A thick, smoky beef and kidney bean chilli with cumin, paprika and a little dark chocolate.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the mince and cook for 8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned.
Stir in the cumin, paprika, chilli, oregano and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, stock and beans. Simmer for 30 minutes, uncovered, until thick. Stir in the chocolate and season.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C throughout with no pink. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with rice, sour cream and coriander. It freezes well.

title: Bean and Cheese Chimichangas (Baked)
summary: Crisp baked tortilla parcels filled with spiced black beans, rice and melting cheese.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Cook the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, then add the garlic, cumin and paprika for 1 minute.
Add the beans, rice and salsa, mash lightly and cook for 3 minutes. Stir in the cheese.
Spoon a quarter of the filling into each tortilla, fold in the sides and roll up into tight parcels.
Brush with oil, place seam side down on a lined tray and bake for 15 to 18 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp. Serve with sour cream and avocado.

notes: Freezes well before baking.

title: Calabacitas con Elote (Mexican Zucchini and Corn Sauté)
summary: Zucchini, sweet corn and green chilli cooked in a pan with tomato and finished with crumbled cheese and black beans.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large frying pan and cook the onion for 4 minutes. Add the garlic and chilli for 1 minute.
Add the zucchini, corn and cumin and cook for 6 minutes, until just tender.
Stir in the tomato and beans and cook for 5 minutes. Season well.
Top with crumbled feta and coriander and serve with warm tortillas.

notes: Easily made vegan by leaving out the feta.

title: Enchiladas Suizas (Swiss-Style Green Chicken Enchiladas)
summary: Chicken-filled tortillas baked under a creamy tomatillo sauce and melted cheese.

steps.text: Poach the chicken in simmering salted water for 15 minutes until cooked through. Shred it.
Blend the salsa, chilli, garlic, coriander and cream until smooth. Heat the oil in a pan, pour in the sauce and simmer for 8 minutes. Season with salt.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Warm the tortillas, dip each in the sauce, fill with chicken and a pinch of cheese and roll into a baking dish.
Pour the remaining sauce on top, scatter with the cheese and bake for 15 minutes, until bubbling. Serve with sour cream.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Use a good-quality jar of green salsa verde.

title: Sopes de Frijol (Mexican Bean Sopes)
summary: Thick little masa cakes pinched into cups and piled with refried beans, crumbled cheese and crunchy lettuce.

items.raw: 400g canned black beans, drained and mashed

steps.text: Mix the masa, water and salt into a soft dough and leave to rest for 10 minutes. Divide into 8 balls and press each into a 9cm disc, 1cm thick.
Cook the discs in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 minutes each side. While still warm, pinch up a rim around each edge.
Fry the sopes in the oil for 2 minutes each side until golden, then drain.
Warm the beans and spread over each sope. Top with lettuce, salsa, feta, sour cream and avocado.

notes: Prep time excludes resting the dough.
Use vegan toppings and skip the feta and cream to make this vegan.

title: Tacu Tacu (Peruvian Rice and Bean Cake with Fried Egg)
summary: Leftover rice and beans mashed with aji amarillo and fried into a crisp golden cake, topped with a runny egg.

steps.text: Cook the onion in 1 tbsp of the oil for 5 minutes, add the garlic and aji paste for 1 minute.
Add the beans and mash roughly, then stir through the rice and season. Shape into 4 thick oval cakes.
Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large frying pan and fry the cakes for 4 minutes each side, until crisp and golden.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil until the whites are set. Toss the red onion with lime juice, coriander and salt and serve on top.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set. Cool and refrigerate leftover rice within an hour.
Use day-old rice for the best crust.

title: Baião de Dois (Brazilian Rice and Beans with Grilled Cheese)
summary: North-eastern Brazilian rice and beans cooked together with spring onion and topped with golden halloumi.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Stir in the rice, beans and stock, bring to the boil, cover and simmer on low for 15 minutes.
Fold in the tomato, spring onion and coriander, cover and rest for 5 minutes.
Fry the halloumi in a dry pan for 2 minutes each side until golden. Serve over the rice with lime.

notes: Halloumi is a good vegetarian choice as it is made without animal rennet in most brands. Check the label.

title: Feijão Tropeiro (Brazilian Bean, Bacon and Egg Stir-Fry)
summary: Cowboy-style beans stir-fried with bacon, kale, scrambled egg and spring onion, a classic from Minas Gerais.

steps.text: Fry the bacon in a large pan for 6 minutes until crisp, then lift out, leaving the fat.
Add the oil and onion and cook for 5 minutes until soft, then the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the beans and kale and stir-fry for 4 minutes, until the kale has wilted and the beans are hot.
Push everything aside, pour the eggs into the gap and scramble for 2 minutes until fully set, then fold through. Return the bacon, add the spring onion and parsley and serve with lime.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until fully set and the bacon until crisp. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with rice.

title: Chorrillana (Chilean Beef and Egg Chips Platter)
summary: A mountain of crisp chips topped with sizzling steak strips, caramelised onion and fried eggs.

items.raw: 500g beef rump steak, sliced into thin strips

steps.text: Heat the oven to 230°C (210°C fan). Toss the chips with 2 tbsp of the oil and spread over two trays. Roast for 30 minutes, turning once, until crisp.
Cook the onion in the remaining oil for 12 minutes until golden, then add the garlic and paprika.
Turn up the heat, add the beef and fry for 3 minutes until browned. Add the vinegar and season.
Fry the eggs for 3 minutes, until the whites are set. Pile the chips on a platter with the beef and onion, top with eggs and parsley.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef strips through and fry the eggs until the whites are set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Bifanas (Portuguese Garlic Pork Rolls)
summary: Thin pork slices simmered in garlic, white wine and paprika, piled into soft rolls.

steps.text: Toss the pork with the garlic, paprika, wine, bay and salt and marinate for at least 1 hour in the fridge.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over high heat and fry the pork in batches for 2 minutes each side, until browned.
