Return all the pork and its marinade to the pan with the water and simmer for 10 minutes, until the pork is cooked through and the sauce is syrupy.
Split the rolls, spread with mustard and fill with pork and sauce.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach 70°C with no pink inside. Do not reuse raw marinade unless boiled. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Prep time excludes marinating.

title: Spanakorizo (Greek Spinach and Lemon Rice with Feta)
summary: Rice simmered with spinach, dill and lemon, with white beans and feta to make it a full meal.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pot and cook the onion and spring onion for 5 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Stir in the rice, then pour in the stock. Bring to the boil, cover and cook on low for 12 minutes.
Fold in the spinach and beans, cover and cook for 6 minutes more, until the rice is tender and the spinach has wilted.
Stir through the dill and lemon juice, season, then crumble over the feta.

notes: Swap the feta for extra olive oil and lemon to make it vegan.

title: Fasolakia Ladera (Greek Braised Green Beans and Potatoes)
summary: Green beans and potatoes slowly braised in olive oil and tomato until silky, served with feta and bread.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pot and cook the onion for 6 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the beans, potatoes, tomatoes, tomato paste, oregano, water, salt and pepper.
Cover and simmer for 40 minutes, stirring now and then, until the beans and potatoes are very tender and the sauce is thick and oily.
Scatter with parsley and serve with feta and bread.

notes: Greek cooks braise these beans until they are soft, not crisp.
Leave out the feta to make it vegan.

title: Revithada (Greek Oven-Baked Chickpeas with Lemon)
summary: Chickpeas baked with onion, rosemary and plenty of olive oil until creamy and golden on top.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Cook the onion in the oil in an ovenproof pot for 8 minutes, then add the garlic, paprika, rosemary and bay.
Add the chickpeas and stock with salt and pepper and simmer for 3 minutes, until hot.
Bake uncovered for 35 minutes, until the stock has reduced and the top is golden.
Stir in the lemon juice and parsley and serve with bread.

notes: The traditional version uses dried chickpeas baked for hours; canned makes this a weeknight dish.

title: Bryndzové Halušky (Slovak Potato Dumplings with Feta and Bacon)
summary: Soft grated-potato dumplings tossed with tangy sheep's cheese and crisp bacon, Slovakia's national dish.

steps.text: Mix the potato, flour, egg and salt into a thick, sticky dough.
Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil. Press or scrape small pieces of dough into the water and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until they float. Lift out with a slotted spoon.
Fry the bacon in a dry pan for 6 minutes until crisp.
Mash the feta with the sour cream and toss through the hot dumplings. Top with bacon and chives.

notes: Food safety: cook the bacon until crisp and the dumplings until they float and are firm. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Feta stands in for the traditional bryndza; leave out the bacon for a vegetarian version.

title: Mămăligă cu Brânză și Ouă (Romanian Polenta with Cheese and Eggs)
summary: Soft polenta swirled with butter and feta, topped with sour cream and a fried egg.

steps.text: Bring the water and salt to the boil. Whisk in the polenta in a thin stream and cook on low for 20 minutes, stirring often, until thick and pulling away from the pot.
Stir in half the butter and half the crumbled feta.
Fry the eggs in the remaining butter for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Spoon the polenta into bowls and top with the egg, remaining feta, sour cream and dill.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Leftover polenta can be sliced and fried the next day.

title: Patatas a lo Pobre (Spanish Slow-Fried Potatoes with Peppers and Eggs)
summary: Potatoes, green pepper and onion slow-cooked in olive oil until soft and golden, topped with runny eggs.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large deep pan over medium heat. Add the potatoes with 1 tsp salt and cook for 10 minutes, turning often.
Add the onion, capsicum and garlic and cook for 20 minutes, covered, stirring every few minutes, until the potatoes are tender and golden.
Stir through the paprika. Push the potato aside and fry the eggs in the pan for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Scatter with parsley and serve.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Add a few slices of jamón if you like.

title: Loubia (Moroccan White Bean Stew with Paprika and Cumin)
summary: Tender white beans in a garlicky tomato sauce spiced with paprika and cumin, finished with coriander.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pot and cook the onion for 6 minutes, then add the garlic, paprika, cumin and chilli for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until thick.
Add the beans and stock and simmer for 15 minutes, until the sauce is rich and clinging to the beans.
Stir in the herbs and lemon juice. Serve with bread or rice.

notes: A vegan one-pot dinner that keeps well and tastes better the next day.

title: Fatayer bi Sabanekh (Lebanese Spinach Pies)
summary: Little triangular pies filled with spinach, onion, sumac and lemon, baked until golden.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, 1 tsp salt, first measure of oil and water into a soft dough, knead for 5 minutes, then cover.
Squeeze the spinach very dry, then mix with the onion, sumac, lemon juice, second measure of oil, pine nuts, salt and pepper.
Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Roll the dough out thin, cut 10cm rounds, fill each with a spoonful and pinch into triangles.
Bake on lined trays for 18 to 20 minutes, until golden. Serve with yoghurt.

notes: Prep time excludes resting the dough for 40 minutes.
Vegan if you use a plant-based yoghurt.

title: Sfiha (Lebanese Open Lamb Flatbreads)
summary: Spiced lamb and tomato spread on flatbreads and baked until crisp at the edges, an easy shortcut on the classic.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 230°C (210°C fan). Mix the mince, onion, tomato, tomato paste, allspice, cinnamon, pomegranate molasses and salt.
Spread the mixture thinly over the flatbreads right to the edges and scatter with pine nuts.
Bake on trays for 12 to 15 minutes, until the lamb is cooked and the edges are crisp.
Top with parsley and serve with yoghurt.

notes: Food safety: lamb mince must reach 75°C throughout with no pink. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with lemon wedges.

title: Stamppot Boerenkool (Dutch Kale Mash with Sausage)
summary: Buttery mashed potato mixed with kale and served with a browned smoked sausage and mustard.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 12 minutes. Add the kale for the last 5 minutes, then drain well.
Fry the sausages in the oil over medium heat for 12 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through. Cook the onion in the same pan for 6 minutes.
Mash the potato and kale with the milk, butter, salt and pepper until it is mostly smooth but still green flecked.
Serve the mash with sausages, onion and mustard.

notes: Food safety: sausages must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Köttbullar (Swedish Meatballs with Cream Sauce)
summary: Small, tender meatballs with allspice in a gravy of cream and stock, served with potatoes and lingonberry jam.

steps.text: Mix both minces with the breadcrumbs, milk, egg, onion, allspice, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Roll into 24 small balls.
Brown the meatballs in half the butter for 8 minutes, turning, then lift out.
Melt the remaining butter in the pan, whisk in the flour for 1 minute, then slowly whisk in the stock until smooth. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the cream and meatballs and simmer for 6 minutes, until cooked through. Serve with potatoes and jam.

notes: Food safety: meatballs must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Cranberry sauce works in place of lingonberry.

title: Smoky Black Bean Burgers
summary: Hearty burgers of black beans, oats and smoked paprika, crisp outside and soft inside.

steps.text: Mash the beans roughly in a bowl, leaving some whole. Mix in the oats, onion, garlic, paprika, cumin, tomato paste and 1 tsp salt.
Shape into 4 firm patties and chill for 10 minutes if you have time.
Fry in the oil over medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes each side, until crisp and hot all the way through.
Toast the buns for 2 minutes until golden, then build with the patties, avocado, tomato and lettuce.

notes: Vegan if the buns are dairy-free.
Patties freeze well, uncooked, between sheets of baking paper.

title: Prawn Po' Boy (Louisiana Fried Prawn Sandwich)
summary: Crunchy cornmeal-coated prawns piled into soft rolls with lettuce, tomato and a spicy mayonnaise.

steps.text: Mix the polenta with the cajun seasoning and a pinch of salt. Dust the prawns in flour, dip in egg, then press into the polenta mix.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the prawns in batches for 2 to 3 minutes each side, until golden and opaque all the way through.
Stir the mayonnaise, hot sauce and lemon juice together.
Split the rolls, spread with the sauce and fill with lettuce, tomato and prawns.

notes: Food safety: prawns must be opaque and firm all the way through. Keep raw prawns cold and refrigerate leftovers within an hour; eat within a day.
Fry in small batches so the crumb stays crisp.

title: Chivito (Uruguayan Steak Sandwich)
summary: Thin grilled beef steak in a soft roll with ham, mozzarella, a fried egg, tomato and lettuce.

steps.text: Season the steak. Heat the oil in a frying pan over high heat and cook the steak in two batches for 2 minutes each, until browned and cooked through.
Lay the ham and mozzarella over the steak in the pan for 1 minute so the cheese melts.
Fry the eggs in the butter in another pan for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Split the rolls, spread with mayonnaise and fill with lettuce, tomato, the steak stack and an egg.

notes: Food safety: cook the thin steak to at least 63°C and rest it for 3 minutes, and cook the eggs until the whites are set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.

title: Anticuchos de Res (Peruvian Beef Skewers)
summary: Beef marinated in aji panca, cumin and vinegar, grilled on skewers and served with potatoes and corn.

items.raw: 700g beef sirloin steak, cut in 3cm cubes

steps.text: Mix the aji panca, vinegar, garlic, cumin, oregano, oil and salt. Coat the beef and marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour. Soak 8 skewers in water.
Boil the potatoes and corn for 12 minutes until tender, then drain.
Thread the beef onto the skewers and grill or fry on high for 3 minutes each side, until browned and cooked to your liking.
Scatter with coriander and serve with the potatoes, corn and lime.

notes: Food safety: beef cubes may be served medium (63°C) but must be seared on every side. Do not reuse raw marinade. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Prep time excludes marinating.

title: Mofongo with Garlic Prawns (Puerto Rican Plantain Mash)
summary: Fried green plantain mashed with garlic and olive oil, topped with garlicky prawns in a light tomato sauce.

items.raw: 4 green plantain, peeled and cut into chunks

steps.text: Fry the plantain chunks in the vegetable oil over medium heat for 10 minutes, turning, until golden and tender. Drain.
Crush 4 garlic cloves with the salt and olive oil in a large mortar or bowl, add the hot plantain and mash into a coarse mound. Shape into 4 domes.
Melt the butter in a pan, cook the onion for 5 minutes, then the remaining crushed garlic. Add the passata and simmer for 4 minutes.
Add the prawns and cook for 3 minutes, until opaque and firm. Add the lime juice, spoon over the mofongo and top with coriander.

notes: Food safety: prawns must be opaque and firm all the way through. Keep raw prawns cold and refrigerate leftovers within an hour; eat within a day.
Use plantain that is firm and green.

title: Pollo en Pepitoria (Spanish Chicken in Almond and Saffron Sauce)
summary: Chicken braised in white wine and saffron, thickened with ground almonds and a hard-boiled egg yolk.

steps.text: Season the chicken and brown it in the oil in a wide pot for 8 minutes. Lift out.
Cook the onion in the same pot for 6 minutes, add the garlic for 1 minute, then the wine, and bubble for 2 minutes.
Return the chicken, add the stock, saffron and bay, cover and simmer for 30 minutes.

Mash the egg yolks with the ground almonds and a ladle of sauce, stir into the pot and simmer for 5 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce thickens. Top with chopped egg white and parsley.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with rice or boiled potatoes.

title: Polpette di Melanzane (Calabrian Aubergine Meatballs in Tomato Sauce)
summary: Soft aubergine and breadcrumb balls with mint, simmered in a light tomato sauce.

steps.text: Prick the aubergines and roast whole at 220°C (200°C fan) for 35 minutes, until collapsed. Scoop out the flesh, drain well and chop.
Mix the flesh with the eggs, breadcrumbs, cheese, garlic, mint, salt and pepper, then shape into 16 balls.
Cook the onion in the first measure of oil for 5 minutes, add the tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes.
Brown the balls in the second measure of oil for 6 minutes, then lower them into the sauce and simmer gently for 10 minutes. Top with basil.

notes: Serve with crusty bread.

title: Gnudi (Tuscan Spinach and Ricotta Dumplings in Sage Butter)
summary: Light spinach and ricotta dumplings poached and tossed in brown butter and sage.

steps.text: Squeeze the spinach very dry and chop finely. Mix with the ricotta, egg yolks, flour, grated cheese, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Shape into 20 small balls and roll in semolina. Chill for 20 minutes if you can.
Poach in barely simmering salted water in batches for 3 to 4 minutes, until they float and feel firm.
Melt the butter with the sage over medium heat for 3 minutes until foaming and nutty. Spoon over the gnudi.

notes: Food safety: cook until the dumplings float and are hot in the centre. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Prep time excludes chilling.

title: Cataplana de Peixe (Portuguese Fish and Tomato Stew)
summary: White fish, peppers and tomato steamed in a covered pan with paprika, wine and coriander.

items.raw: 600g firm white fish fillet, cut into chunks

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pot with a lid and cook the onion and capsicum for 8 minutes. Add the garlic and paprika for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, wine and bay and simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the potatoes and fish, spoon the sauce over, cover and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Scatter with coriander and serve with lemon.

notes: Food safety: cook fish until opaque and it flakes easily (63°C). Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and eat within a day.
A closed pot works if you do not own a cataplana.

title: Bacalhau com Natas (Portuguese Cod and Potato Bake with Cream)
summary: Flaked salt-free white fish, soft onion and potato layered in a creamy sauce and baked until golden.

steps.text: Poach the fish in simmering water for 5 minutes, until it flakes. Drain, then flake into large pieces, removing any bones.
Cook the potato in boiling salted water for 8 minutes, until just tender. Drain well.

Soften the onion and garlic in the oil for 6 minutes. Melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk and cream. Simmer for 4 minutes, until thick, then add nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Layer potato, onion and fish in a baking dish, pour over the sauce and top with the mozzarella.
Bake for 20 minutes, until bubbling and golden. Scatter with parsley and serve.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until shells open or flesh is opaque and discard any that stay shut. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Fresh fish is used here instead of salt cod, so no soaking is needed.

title: Bacalhau à Brás (Portuguese Shredded Cod with Egg and Potato)
summary: Flaked fish, soft onion and crisp potato strands bound with softly scrambled egg.

steps.text: Poach the fish in simmering water for 5 minutes, until it flakes. Drain and flake, removing any bones.
Dry the potato well. Fry in the oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat for 10 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp. Lift out and drain.
In the same pan, soften the onion and garlic for 8 minutes with a pinch of salt.
Add the fish and potato and toss for 2 minutes. Beat the eggs with pepper, pour in and stir over low heat for 3 minutes, until just set and creamy.
Scatter with parsley and serve with lemon wedges.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until shells open or flesh is opaque and discard any that stay shut. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.

Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set; avoid runny eggs for pregnant, elderly, very young or immune-compromised eaters. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Arroz de Pato (Portuguese Duck Rice)
summary: Shredded braised duck baked through rice with smoky chorizo until the top turns crisp.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Put the duck, onion, garlic, bay leaves, wine and 2 cups water in a lidded casserole, cover and braise for 1 1/2 hours, until the meat falls from the bone.
Lift out the duck, strain the juices and shred the meat, discarding skin and bones. Skim the fat from the juices.
Fry the chorizo in the oil for 3 minutes. Add the rice and stir for 1 minute, then add the stock and 1 cup of the duck juices.
Cover and bake for 20 minutes, until the rice is tender. Fold in most of the duck.
Top with the rest of the duck and the chorizo. Bake uncovered for 10 minutes, until crisp on top, then scatter with parsley.

notes: Food safety: duck must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Cool leftover rice quickly and eat within a day.
Dairy-free.

title: Porco à Alentejana (Portuguese Pork and Clams)
summary: Marinated pork pieces fried then tossed with clams, paprika and fried potato cubes.

steps.text: Toss the pork with the paprika, garlic, wine, bay leaves and salt. Marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour.
Fry the potato in half the oil for 12 minutes, until golden. Drain and set aside.
Drain the pork, saving the marinade. Fry in the remaining oil over high heat for 10 minutes, until browned. Add the onion and cook for 4 minutes.
Add the marinade and bring to a boil. Add the clams, cover and cook for 5 minutes, until the shells open. Discard any that stay shut.
Fold in the potato and coriander and serve with lemon.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until shells open or flesh is opaque and discard any that stay shut. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Boil the marinade for the full time or discard it; never serve it raw.

title: Bitoque (Portuguese Steak with Fried Egg and Chips)
summary: A thin pan-fried steak in garlicky wine sauce, topped with a fried egg and served with chips and rice.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the chips with the oil and salt on a tray and roast for 30 minutes, turning once, until crisp.
Season the steaks. Fry in half the butter over high heat for 2 minutes each side. Rest on a plate.
Add the garlic, wine and bay leaves to the pan, simmer for 3 minutes, then whisk in the remaining butter with any resting juices.
Fry the eggs in a little oil for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Plate each steak with rice and chips, pour over the sauce and top with an egg. Serve with lemon.

notes: Food safety: whole steaks are safe seared medium-rare, but cook any minced or rolled beef to 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set; avoid runny eggs for pregnant, elderly, very young or immune-compromised eaters. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Feijoada à Transmontana (Portuguese Pork and Bean Stew)
summary: Slow-cooked beans with pork, smoked sausage and cabbage in a thick, comforting stew.

steps.text: Brown the pork and chorizo in the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat for 8 minutes. Add the onion, garlic and carrot and cook for 6 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, paprika and bay leaves for 1 minute, then add the stock. Cover and simmer for 45 minutes, until the pork is tender.
Add the beans and cabbage and cook uncovered for 15 minutes, until the stew has thickened.
Season to taste and finish with parsley. Serve with crusty bread.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free. Better the next day.

title: Khachapuri Adjaruli (Georgian Cheese Boat with Egg)
summary: A boat of soft dough filled with melted cheese, finished with an egg and a knob of butter.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and 1 tsp salt. Stir in the milk and oil to form a dough, knead for 8 minutes, then cover and leave until doubled, about 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 240°C (220°C fan) with a tray inside. Mix the mozzarella, feta and 1 egg.
Divide the dough into 4. Roll each into an oval, roll the long edges inward and pinch the ends to form a boat. Fill with the cheese mix.

Bake on the hot tray for 12 minutes, until the crust is golden. Make a well in each filling, drop in an egg yolk (save the whites for another dish) and bake for 2 minutes more, so the yolk stays soft.
Top each with butter, stir the yolk into the cheese at the table and tear off pieces of crust to dip.

notes: Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set; avoid runny eggs for pregnant, elderly, very young or immune-compromised eaters. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten. The yolk is left soft, so leave it out if eaters are pregnant or vulnerable.

title: Chakhokhbili (Georgian Chicken and Tomato Stew)
summary: Chicken braised in its own juices with tomato, onion and a big handful of fresh herbs.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil in a heavy pot for 8 minutes, skin side down first. Lift out.
Cook the onion in the pot for 8 minutes. Add the tomato, garlic and spices and cook for 5 minutes, until it breaks down.
Return the chicken, cover and simmer on low for 30 minutes, until cooked through and tender.
Stir in half the herbs and season. Scatter the rest over and serve with bread or rice.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Lobio (Georgian Kidney Bean Stew with Walnuts)
summary: Spiced kidney beans mashed to a thick stew with walnuts, coriander and fenugreek, eaten with cornbread.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 10 minutes, until deep golden.
Add the garlic, spices and walnuts and stir for 1 minute.
Add the beans and water, simmer for 20 minutes, mashing about a third with a spoon, until thick.
Stir in the vinegar and half the coriander, season, and scatter the rest over. Serve with bread.

notes: Canned beans are already cooked; if using dried kidney beans, soak overnight and boil hard for 10 minutes first.
Vegan and dairy-free. Contains walnuts.

title: Chashushuli (Georgian Beef and Tomato Stew)
summary: Beef simmered with tomato, onion, garlic and fresh herbs until rich and spoonable.

steps.text: Brown the beef in batches in the oil for 8 minutes, until deeply coloured. Lift out.
Cook the onion for 8 minutes, then add garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Return the beef with the tomatoes and water. Cover and simmer on low for 1 hour, until very tender.
Stir through the herbs, season and serve with bread or rice.

notes: Food safety: beef pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender; braise until the meat pulls apart. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Kibinai (Lithuanian Lamb Pasties)
summary: Half-moon pastries filled with lamb, onion and herbs, a Karaite Lithuanian speciality.

steps.text: Rub the cold butter into the flour with 1/2 tsp salt. Mix in the sour cream and egg to a dough, wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Soften the onion in the butter for 6 minutes. Mix with the lamb, marjoram, dill, salt and pepper.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Roll the dough 3mm thick and cut 12cm rounds. Put filling on each, fold over and pinch the edge to seal.
Brush with the egg yolk and bake for 25 minutes, until golden and the filling is cooked through.
Rest for 5 minutes, then serve warm.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten, egg and dairy.

title: Cepelinai (Lithuanian Potato Dumplings with Pork)
summary: Large grated-potato dumplings around a seasoned pork centre, served with bacon and sour cream.

steps.text: Grate 2/3 of the potato and squeeze it in a cloth, saving the starchy liquid. Boil the remaining potato for 15 minutes, mash, and mix with the raw grated potato, the settled starch from the liquid and 1 tsp salt.
Mix the pork, half the onion, garlic, marjoram, salt and pepper.
Wet your hands, flatten some potato mix in your palm, put a spoon of pork in the middle and shape into an oval, sealing completely. Make 8.
Simmer gently in salted water for 30 minutes, until firm. Don't let the water boil hard or they'll break up.
Fry the bacon and remaining onion in the butter until golden. Serve the dumplings with the bacon, sour cream and dill.

notes: Food safety: pork mince must reach 75°C in the centre; cut one open to check. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Kugelis (Lithuanian Baked Potato Pudding with Bacon)
summary: A grated-potato bake studded with bacon and onion, crusty on top and soft inside.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan) and butter a 22cm baking dish.
Fry the bacon and onion in a pan for 8 minutes, until golden. Cool slightly.
Grate the potato and drain off the liquid. Mix with the eggs, milk, bacon and onion, salt and pepper.
Pour into the dish and bake for 1 hour, until deep golden and set through.
Rest for 5 minutes. Serve in squares with sour cream and dill.

notes: Food safety: bacon and eggs should be fully cooked; the centre should be firm and hot. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Gluten-free.

title: Karjalanpiirakka with Egg Butter (Karelian Rice Pasties)
summary: Thin rye shells filled with creamy rice porridge, served with egg butter, a Finnish classic.

steps.text: Simmer the rice with the milk and water for 30 minutes, stirring often, until a thick porridge. Season well.
Mix both flours, 1/2 tsp salt, the water and oil into a firm dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Heat the oven to 250°C (230°C fan). Roll the dough into 12 thin rounds about 12cm wide, put porridge in the middle and fold the edges in to make an oval.
Bake for 15 minutes, until the edges are browned. Brush with melted butter.
Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, until the yolks are firm. Peel, mash with the soft butter and salt and serve on warm pasties.

notes: Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set; avoid runny eggs for pregnant, elderly, very young or immune-compromised eaters. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten, egg and dairy.

title: Janssons Frestelse (Swedish Potato and Anchovy Gratin)
summary: Thin potato matchsticks baked with sweet onion, anchovies and cream until golden.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Soften the onion in half the butter for 8 minutes.
Layer potato, onion and anchovies in a buttered dish, finishing with potato.
Mix the cream, milk and 1 tbsp of the anchovy oil; pour over, scatter with breadcrumbs and dot with the remaining butter.
Bake for 50 minutes, until the potato is tender and the top is deep golden.
Rest 5 minutes and scatter with dill.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until shells open or flesh is opaque and discard any that stay shut. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Main course in Sweden, often with a green salad on the side.

title: Frikadeller (Danish Pork Meatballs with Potatoes and Gravy)
summary: Pan-fried pork meatballs seasoned with onion and allspice, served with boiled potatoes and brown gravy.

steps.text: Mix the pork, onion, egg, 1/2 cup flour, milk, allspice, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Chill for 15 minutes if time allows.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 20 minutes, until tender.
Shape the pork mix into 12 oval balls. Fry in half the butter over medium heat for 12 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through. Lift out.
Whisk the 2 tbsp flour into the pan juices, then the stock, and simmer for 5 minutes into a gravy.
Serve with potatoes and gravy, sprinkled with parsley.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten and egg.

title: Flæskesteg (Danish Roast Pork with Crackling)
summary: A Danish Sunday roast of pork loin with crisp crackling, bay and cloves, served with red cabbage and potatoes.

items.raw: 1.5 kg pork loin, skin on, scored

steps.text: Dry the pork skin, rub with the salt and leave uncovered in the fridge for 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 230°C (210°C fan). Push the cloves into the meat and tuck bay leaves into the scoring. Sit on the onion in a tin.
Roast for 25 minutes, then turn down to 180°C (160°C fan) and cook for 1 1/2 hours, until the meat reaches 70°C and the skin is crisp.
Rest for 15 minutes. Meanwhile boil the potatoes for 20 minutes.
Whisk the flour into the pan juices, add the stock and simmer for 5 minutes. Carve and serve with gravy and potatoes.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free. Add pickled red cabbage on the side if you like.

title: Fårikål (Norwegian Lamb and Cabbage Stew)
summary: Norway's national dish: lamb and cabbage layered in a pot with whole pepper and simmered gently.

items.raw: 1.2 kg lamb shoulder, bone in, cut in pieces

steps.text: Layer the lamb and cabbage in a heavy pot, sprinkling flour, peppercorns and salt between the layers.
Pour in the water, cover and bring to a simmer. Cook gently for 2 hours, until the lamb is tender and falling off the bone.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 20 minutes.
Serve in deep bowls with the lamb, cabbage, broth and potatoes.

notes: Food safety: lamb pieces should reach at least 70°C and be tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free. Even better the next day.

title: Kjøttkaker (Norwegian Meatball Patties in Brown Gravy)
summary: Spiced beef and pork patties in a creamy brown gravy with potatoes, peas and lingonberry jam.

steps.text: Mix the beef, pork, onion, egg, milk, 1/4 cup flour, spices, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Shape into 8 flat patties.
Fry in half the butter for 12 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through. Lift out.
Whisk the 2 tbsp flour into the pan with the remaining butter, add the stock and simmer for 8 minutes into a gravy.
Boil the potatoes for 20 minutes, adding the peas for the last 3.
Serve the patties with gravy, potatoes, peas and jam.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten and egg.

title: Pasta alla Gricia (Roman Guanciale and Pecorino Pasta)
summary: The cacio e pepe and amatriciana's older cousin: crisp cured pork, pecorino and black pepper.

steps.text: Boil the pasta in well-salted water until al dente, saving 1 cup of the cooking water.
Fry the pancetta in a large pan over medium heat for 8 minutes, until crisp, with the pepper for the last minute.
Add the pasta and 1/2 cup of the water to the pan and toss over low heat for 1 minute.
Take off the heat, add the pecorino and toss, adding more water as needed until the sauce is glossy and clings to the pasta. Serve at once.

notes: Food safety: cured pork like pancetta should be cooked until crisp and eaten the same day, or refrigerated within an hour. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains pecorino, a hard cheese that usually isn't vegetarian.

title: Risotto alla Milanese (Saffron Risotto)
summary: The golden risotto of Milan, scented with saffron and finished with butter and vegetarian hard cheese.

steps.text: Steep the saffron in 1/4 cup of the hot stock.
Melt half the butter in a wide pan and cook the onion for 6 minutes, until soft. Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble away. Add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for 18 to 20 minutes, adding the saffron liquid halfway.
When the rice is creamy and just tender, take off the heat. Stir in the remaining butter and the vegetarian hard cheese, cover and rest for 2 minutes.
Serve straight away on warm plates.

notes: Vegetarian. Serves four as a main or six as a side with osso buco.
Gluten-free.

title: Risotto ai Funghi Misti (Mixed Mushroom Risotto)
summary: Earthy mushrooms folded through creamy rice with thyme and vegetarian hard cheese.

steps.text: Fry the mushrooms in the oil over high heat in two batches for 6 minutes each, until golden. Season and set aside.
Melt half the butter, cook the onion and garlic for 5 minutes, then stir in the rice and thyme for 2 minutes.
Add the wine, then the stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for 18 to 20 minutes.
Fold in the mushrooms, remaining butter and vegetarian hard cheese. Rest for 2 minutes.
Serve topped with parsley.

notes: Vegetarian. Gluten-free.

title: Risotto alla Pescatora (Seafood Risotto)
summary: Creamy rice with prawns, mussels and white fish in a light tomato and white wine base.

steps.text: Soften the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes. Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes, then the wine.
Add the tomatoes, then the stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for about 15 minutes.
Add the fish and cook 3 minutes, then the prawns and mussels, cover and cook for 4 minutes, until the prawns are pink and the mussels open. Discard any that stay shut.
Rest for 2 minutes, then stir in the lemon juice and parsley.
Serve straight away; no cheese is added.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until shells open or flesh is opaque and discard any that stay shut. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Contains shellfish. Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Risi e Bisi (Venetian Rice and Pea Stew)
summary: A thick Venetian rice and pea dish with pancetta, somewhere between a soup and a risotto.

steps.text: Fry the pancetta in the oil for 5 minutes. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the rice and stir for 1 minute, then add the stock a ladle at a time for 12 minutes.
Add the peas and cook for 5 minutes more, until the rice is tender but the dish is still wet.
Stir in the butter, pecorino and parsley and serve in shallow bowls.

notes: Food safety: cured pork should be cooked until crisp and eaten the same day, or refrigerated within an hour. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains pecorino, a hard cheese that usually isn't vegetarian.

title: Cotoletta alla Milanese (Milanese Crumbed Veal Cutlet)
summary: A thin veal cutlet crumbed and fried in butter until golden, served with lemon and rocket.

steps.text: Flatten the veal with a rolling pin to 6mm thick and season.
Dredge in the flour, dip in the beaten eggs, then press into the breadcrumbs.
Heat half the butter and oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Fry two cutlets at a time for 3 minutes each side, until deep golden and cooked through. Repeat with the rest.
Drain on paper and serve at once with rocket and lemon.

notes: Food safety: veal must reach 70°C in the centre with no pink. Cook the crumbed meat fully. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Pork or chicken cutlets can be used instead.

title: Fisherman's Pie
summary: Chunks of white fish, salmon and prawns in a parsley cream sauce under golden cheesy mash.

steps.text: Boil the potato for 18 minutes, until soft. Drain, mash with half the butter, a splash of milk and salt.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Soften the onion in the remaining butter for 5 minutes. Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk and simmer for 5 minutes, until thick.
Off the heat, fold in the fish, salmon, prawns, peas, parsley and lemon juice. Pour into a baking dish.
Spoon the mash on top, rough it up with a fork and scatter with the cheese.
Bake for 25 minutes, until the fish is cooked through and the top is golden.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until shells open or flesh is opaque and discard any that stay shut. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Contains fish, shellfish, milk and gluten.

title: Cumberland Pie (Mince and Potato Pie with Cheesy Crumb Top)
summary: Savoury beef mince in rich gravy under mashed potato and a crisp cheese and breadcrumb topping.

steps.text: Boil the potato for 18 minutes, until soft. Drain and mash with the butter, milk and salt.
Brown the mince in a pan for 8 minutes, then add the onion and carrot and cook for 6 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and flour for 1 minute, add the stock and worcestershire, and simmer for 15 minutes, until thick.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Spoon the mince into a dish, top with the mash, then the cheese mixed with the breadcrumbs.
Bake for 25 minutes, until bubbling and golden on top.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Scottish Bridies (Beef Pasties from Forfar)
summary: Half-moon shortcrust pasties filled with beef, onion and a little butter, a Scottish bakery classic.

steps.text: Rub the cold butter into the flour with 1/2 tsp salt, then mix in about 1/2 cup ice water until it forms a dough. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Mix the beef, onion, suet, stock, pepper and 1 tsp salt.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Roll out the dough and cut four 18cm rounds. Put the filling on one half, fold over and crimp the edge firmly.
Brush with egg, cut a small steam hole, and bake for 35 minutes, until golden and the filling is hot and cooked through.
Rest for 5 minutes before eating.

notes: Food safety: beef pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender; braise until the meat pulls apart. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten and egg. Cut one open to check the beef is hot all the way through.

title: Dublin Coddle
summary: Pork sausages and bacon gently simmered with potatoes and onions in a mild, savoury broth.

steps.text: Lightly brown the sausages and bacon in a heavy pot for 8 minutes. Remove and cut the sausages in thirds.
Layer the onion, potato, sausages and bacon in the pot with the thyme, salt and pepper.
Pour in the stock, cover and simmer gently for 45 minutes, until the potato is tender and the sausages cooked through.
Scatter with parsley and serve in bowls with the broth and soda bread.

notes: Food safety: pork sausages must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free.

title: Stovies (Scottish Potato and Corned Beef Hash)
summary: A frugal Scottish one-pot of soft potatoes, onion and beef dripping or butter, with corned beef.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a heavy pot and cook the onion for 8 minutes, until soft.
Add the potato, stock, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Cover and cook gently for 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the potato is soft and slightly broken.
Fold in the corned beef and cook for 5 minutes, until hot all the way through.
Serve with oatcakes or beetroot.

notes: Corned beef from a tin is already cooked; just heat it through. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Gluten-free.

title: Mince and Tatties (Scottish Beef Mince with Mashed Potato)
summary: The Scottish weeknight plate: savoury mince with carrot and onion over buttery mash.

steps.text: Brown the mince in a pan for 8 minutes. Add the onion and carrot and cook for 6 minutes.
Stir in the flour and tomato paste for 1 minute, then add the stock and worcestershire. Simmer for 25 minutes, until thick.
Boil the potato for 18 minutes, until soft. Drain and mash with the butter, milk and salt.
Serve the mince beside the mash.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Roast Beef with Yorkshire Puddings
summary: Roast sirloin with golden Yorkshire puddings and gravy, the centrepiece of a British Sunday lunch.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 230°C (210°C fan). Rub the beef with oil, salt and pepper and sit on the onion in a tin. Roast 20 minutes, then reduce to 180°C (160°C fan) and roast 40 to 60 minutes, until 60°C for medium.
Whisk the cup of flour, eggs, milk and a pinch of salt into a smooth batter and rest for 30 minutes.
Parboil the potatoes for 10 minutes, then roast them in a second tin with a little oil for 45 minutes, until golden.

Rest the beef for 20 minutes. Raise the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Put 1 tsp vegetable oil in each hole of a 12-hole muffin tin and heat for 5 minutes until smoking. Pour in the batter and bake for 18 minutes, until risen and golden. Don't open the oven early.
Whisk 2 tbsp flour into the beef juices, add the stock and simmer 5 minutes. Carve and serve with everything.

notes: Food safety: roast beef is safe at 60°C for medium or 70°C for well done in the centre; rest it before carving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten, egg and milk.

title: Roast Chicken with Sage and Onion Stuffing
summary: A whole roast chicken with a crisp skin and a savoury sage and onion stuffing baked alongside.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Rub the chicken with the softened butter, thyme, salt and pepper and put the lemon inside. Roast for 20 minutes.
Reduce to 190°C (170°C fan) and cook for 1 hour more, until the juices run clear and a thermometer reads 75°C in the thickest part of the thigh.
Cook the onion in the butter for 5 minutes. Mix with the breadcrumbs, sage and 1/2 cup stock, press into a small dish and bake for the last 25 minutes.
Parboil the potatoes for 10 minutes and roast around the chicken for the last 40 minutes.
Rest the chicken for 15 minutes. Make gravy by whisking the flour and 1 cup stock into the pan juices over heat for 5 minutes.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten and milk. Cook stuffing in a separate dish, not inside the bird.

title: Linguine allo Scoglio (Rock Pool Seafood Linguine)
summary: Linguine with mussels, clams, prawns and squid in a garlicky white wine and tomato sauce.

steps.text: Cook the linguine in salted water for 2 minutes less than the packet says. Keep 1 cup of the water.
Soften the garlic and chilli in the oil for 1 minute. Add the wine and tomatoes and simmer for 8 minutes, until slightly thick.
Add the mussels and clams, cover and cook for 4 minutes, until they open. Discard any that stay shut.
Add the prawns and squid and cook for 3 minutes, until opaque.
Toss the drained pasta in the pan with a splash of the water for 2 minutes. Scatter with parsley and serve.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until shells open or flesh is opaque and discard any that stay shut. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Contains shellfish. Dairy-free.

title: Spaghetti alle Vongole (Spaghetti with Clams)
summary: A Neapolitan beachside classic of spaghetti, clams, garlic, white wine and parsley.

steps.text: Cook the spaghetti in salted water for 2 minutes less than the packet says. Keep 1/2 cup of the water.
Warm the oil, garlic and chilli for 2 minutes. Add the clams and wine, cover and cook for 5 minutes, until the shells open. Discard any that stay shut.
Add the drained spaghetti and a splash of water. Toss over medium heat for 2 minutes, until the sauce clings.
Stir in the parsley and serve.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until shells open or flesh is opaque and discard any that stay shut. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Dairy-free.

title: Bucatini all'Amatriciana (Bucatini with Pork Cheek and Tomato)
summary: Hollow pasta in a sharp tomato sauce with crisp cured pork and pecorino from Amatrice.

steps.text: Fry the pancetta in the oil for 8 minutes, until crisp, with the chilli. Add the wine and boil for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes, until thick.
Cook the bucatini in salted water until al dente. Drain, saving a splash of water.
Toss the pasta through the sauce for 1 minute with half the pecorino and a splash of water. Serve with the rest of the cheese.

notes: Food safety: cured pork should be cooked until crisp and eaten the same day, or refrigerated within an hour. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains pecorino, a hard cheese that usually isn't vegetarian.

title: Penne all'Arrabbiata (Angry Penne)
summary: Penne in a fiery garlic and chilli tomato sauce, a Roman plate that takes ten minutes to make.

steps.text: Warm the oil, garlic and chilli over low heat for 2 minutes, until the garlic is just golden.
Add the tomatoes, sugar and 1 tsp salt. Simmer for 15 minutes, until thick.
Cook the penne in salted water until al dente and drain, saving a splash of water.
Toss the penne through the sauce, add the parsley and a splash of water and serve.

notes: Vegan and dairy-free. Add a little more chilli if you like it hotter.

title: Boeuf Bourguignon
summary: Beef braised slowly in red wine with bacon, mushrooms and pearl onions, served with mash.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Fry the bacon in the oil in a casserole for 5 minutes. Lift out. Brown the beef in batches for 10 minutes in total. Lift out.
Cook the carrot and onion for 8 minutes. Stir in the flour and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the wine, stock, garlic, herbs, bacon and beef. Bring to a simmer, cover and braise in the oven for 2 1/2 hours, until the beef is very tender.
Fry the mushrooms and pearl onions in a pan for 8 minutes, until golden. Stir through for the last 15 minutes.
Skim off fat and serve with mashed potato.

notes: Food safety: beef pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender; braise until the meat pulls apart. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten. Better made a day ahead.

title: Blanquette de Poulet (French Chicken in Creamy Lemon Sauce)
summary: Gently simmered veal in a creamy lemon sauce with mushrooms and pearl onions, finished with a yolk liaison.

steps.text: Put the veal, studded onion, carrot, bay and stock in a pot. Bring to a simmer, skimming, and cook gently for 30 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and tender. Strain, keeping the stock and veal.
Simmer the mushrooms and pearl onions in the stock for 10 minutes, then lift out.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 2 minutes, then whisk in 3 cups of the stock. Simmer for 10 minutes, until thick.
Whisk the yolks, cream and lemon juice, stir in a little hot sauce, then return all to the pot off the boil, stirring until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Add the veal, mushrooms and onions, heat gently without boiling, and serve over rice.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink. The egg liaison needs to reach about 75°C but must not boil or it will curdle. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains egg, gluten and milk.

title: Sole Meunière
summary: Pan-fried fish fillets in browned butter, lemon and parsley, a French bistro classic.

steps.text: Dry the fish, season and dust lightly with flour.
Heat half the butter in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the fish for 2 to 3 minutes a side, until golden and it flakes. Plate.
Wipe the pan, add the remaining butter and cook for 2 minutes until nutty brown.
Add the lemon juice, parsley and capers, swirl and pour over the fish. Serve with potatoes.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until shells open or flesh is opaque and discard any that stay shut. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Contains fish, gluten and milk.

title: Choucroute Garnie (Alsatian Sauerkraut with Sausages and Pork)
summary: Sauerkraut simmered with white wine, pork belly and sausages, served with potatoes and mustard.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the oil in a heavy pot for 5 minutes. Add the sauerkraut, wine, stock and bay.
Add the pork belly, cover and simmer on low for 1 hour.
Add the sausages and simmer for 25 minutes, until cooked through. Boil the potatoes in salted water for 20 minutes.
Serve the sauerkraut with the pork, sausages, potatoes and mustard.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Sausages must reach 75°C in the centre. Dairy-free.

title: Arroz Negro (Spanish Black Squid Ink Rice)
summary: Short grain rice cooked in squid ink and fish stock with squid and prawns, served with garlic mayo.

steps.text: Soften the onion, garlic and capsicum in the oil in a wide pan for 8 minutes. Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the squid and cook for 3 minutes. Stir in the rice for 1 minute.
Dissolve the ink in the hot stock, pour in and simmer without stirring for 15 minutes, until the rice is nearly tender.
Add the prawns on top, cover and cook for 5 minutes, until pink. Rest for 5 minutes, then serve with aioli.

notes: Food safety: squid and octopus turn tough if cooked briefly then overcooked; cook until opaque and firm. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Contains shellfish, egg (in aioli). Cool any leftover rice quickly and eat within a day.

title: Zarzuela de Mariscos (Catalan Seafood Stew)
summary: A Catalan stew of mixed fish and shellfish in a rich tomato, almond and brandy sauce.

steps.text: Soften the onion and garlic in the oil for 8 minutes. Stir in the paprika for 30 seconds, then add the brandy and boil for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, stock and almonds and simmer for 15 minutes, until thick.
Add the fish and squid and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the mussels and prawns, cover and cook for 5 minutes, until the shells open and the prawns turn pink. Discard any shells that stay shut.
Scatter with parsley and serve with bread.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until shells open or flesh is opaque and discard any that stay shut. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Contains shellfish, fish and almonds. Dairy-free.

title: Rabo de Toro (Andalusian Braised Oxtail)
summary: Oxtail slowly braised in red wine, vegetables and spices until the meat falls from the bone, a Cordoba classic.

steps.text: Season the oxtail and brown it in the oil in a heavy casserole in batches for 12 minutes in total. Lift out.
Cook the onion, carrot and garlic for 8 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste, paprika and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the wine, boil for 3 minutes, then add the stock, bay and oxtail. Cover and cook at 160°C (140°C fan) for 3 hours, until the meat falls from the bone.
Add the potato for the last 40 minutes.
Skim the fat and serve the oxtail with the sauce and potatoes.

notes: Food safety: beef pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender; braise until the meat pulls apart. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free. Better made a day ahead; skim the set fat before reheating.

title: Bacalao al Pil Pil (Basque Salt Cod in Garlic Oil Emulsion)
summary: Fish gently cooked in garlic-infused olive oil that thickens into a glossy emulsion.

items.raw: 4 firm white fish fillets, skin on

steps.text: Warm the oil and garlic over low heat for 6 minutes, until the garlic is pale gold. Lift out the garlic and chilli and set aside.
Dry the fish and season. Add skin side down to the warm oil and cook gently for 6 minutes, turning once, until just cooked through. Lift out.
Off the heat, swirl the pan in a circular motion for 5 minutes as the oil cools; the gelatin from the skin makes it thicken into a sauce.
Return the fish, spoon the sauce over and top with garlic and chilli. Serve with potatoes.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until shells open or flesh is opaque and discard any that stay shut. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Salt cod needs 48 hours soaking; this version uses fresh fish. Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Cocido Madrileño (Madrid Chickpea and Meat Stew)
summary: The classic Madrid cocido of chickpeas, pork, chorizo and vegetables, traditionally served in three courses.

steps.text: Put the pork, chicken, chorizo, onion and water in a large pot. Bring to a simmer, skim, and cook gently for 1 hour.
Add the chickpeas and carrot and simmer for 30 minutes, then add the potato and cabbage and simmer for 25 minutes more, until all are tender.
Lift out the meats and vegetables and slice. Strain 6 cups of broth into a pan and cook the noodles for 4 minutes.
Serve the broth with noodles first, then the meat, chickpeas and vegetables.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Chicken and sausages must reach 75°C. Canned chickpeas are already cooked.

title: Mansaf (Jordanian Lamb in Yoghurt Sauce with Rice)
summary: Tender lamb in a tangy cooked yoghurt sauce over rice and flatbread, topped with toasted almonds.

steps.text: Put the lamb, onion, bay and allspice in a pot, cover with water and simmer gently for 1 1/2 hours, until the lamb is very tender. Keep 3 cups of the broth.
Whisk the yoghurt and egg white in a pan, then stir in 2 cups of broth over low heat, always one direction, until it just simmers. Add the lamb and keep warm.
Cook the rice in salted water for 12 minutes, until tender. Toast the almonds in the butter for 2 minutes.
Tear the pita onto a platter, top with rice, lamb and sauce, then scatter with the almonds and parsley.

notes: Food safety: lamb pieces should reach at least 70°C and be tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Stir the yoghurt in one direction over low heat so it does not split.

title: Chicken Kabsa (Saudi Spiced Rice with Chicken)
summary: Fragrant long grain rice cooked with tomato, warm spices and tender chicken, a Gulf family dish.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil in a large pot for 8 minutes. Lift out. Cook the onion for 8 minutes, then add garlic, tomato, paste and spices for 3 minutes.
Return the chicken with the stock. Cover and simmer for 25 minutes, until cooked through. Lift out and keep warm.
Rinse the rice, add to the pot with the sultanas, cover and cook on low for 15 minutes, until the stock is absorbed and the rice is tender.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 2 minutes, until golden. Pile rice on a platter with the chicken and almonds.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Cool leftover rice quickly and eat within a day. Dairy-free.

title: Tahchin (Persian Saffron Yoghurt and Chicken Rice Cake)
summary: A crisp-bottomed baked rice cake layered with saffron chicken, yoghurt and barberries.

steps.text: Steep the saffron in 3 tbsp hot water. Simmer the chicken and onion in water for 20 minutes, until cooked through. Shred.
Parboil the rice in salted water for 6 minutes. Drain. Mix half with the yoghurt, eggs, half the saffron water and 1 tsp salt.
Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Oil a 24cm dish and press the yoghurt rice into the base and sides.
Layer the chicken and sultanas, then the plain rice, mounded in the middle. Drizzle with the oil, melted butter and remaining saffron water. Cover with foil.
Bake for 1 hour, until the base is golden. Rest for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a plate.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Shevid Polo ba Gusht (Persian Dill Rice with Braised Lamb)
summary: Herby dill rice served with lamb braised until falling off the bone.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil for 10 minutes, then add the onion and turmeric and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the water, cover and simmer gently for 2 hours, until the meat falls from the bone.
Parboil the rice for 6 minutes, until just tender outside. Drain and mix with the dill.
Melt the butter in a pot, layer in the rice, poke steam holes and cook covered on low with a tea towel under the lid for 25 minutes.
Serve the rice with the lamb and its juices.

notes: Food safety: lamb pieces should reach at least 70°C and be tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Gluten-free.

title: Khoresh Gheimeh (Persian Split Pea and Lamb Stew)
summary: Lamb braised with split peas, tomato and dried lime, topped with crisp fried chips.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 10 minutes, then brown the lamb with the turmeric for 8 minutes.
Stir in the paste, split peas, cinnamon, pierced limes and water. Cover and simmer for 1 1/2 hours, until the lamb is tender and the peas soft.
Shallow fry the chips in oil for 8 minutes, until crisp.
Serve the stew over rice with chips on top.

notes: Food safety: lamb pieces should reach at least 70°C and be tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Tas Kebabi (Turkish Lamb and Vegetable Casserole)
summary: Cubed lamb braised with onion, tomato and capsicum, served with rice or bread.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the onion and cook for 6 minutes.
Add the garlic, paste, capsicum, tomato, oregano and water.
Cover and simmer for 1 hour, until the lamb is tender and the sauce is thick. Serve over rice.

notes: Food safety: lamb pieces should reach at least 70°C and be tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Kuzu Tandir (Turkish Slow-Roasted Lamb Shoulder)
summary: Lamb shoulder roasted in a covered tin until it pulls apart, with garlic, tomato and oregano.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Stab the lamb all over and push in the garlic. Rub with oil, paste, oregano and 1 tsp salt.
Put the onion and water in a deep tin, rest the lamb on top and cover tightly with foil.
Roast for 3 hours, adding the potato for the last hour, until the lamb is falling apart.
Rest for 15 minutes, then shred and serve with the pan juices and potatoes.

notes: Food safety: lamb pieces should reach at least 70°C and be tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Karides Güveç (Turkish Prawn Casserole)
summary: Prawns baked in a clay-pot style tomato and capsicum sauce topped with melted cheese.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Soften the onion and capsicum in the oil for 8 minutes. Add garlic, tomatoes and chilli and simmer for 8 minutes.
Stir in the prawns and tip into four small dishes.
Top with mozzarella and bake for 10 minutes, until the prawns are pink and the cheese is bubbling.
Scatter with parsley and serve with bread.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until opaque. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Contains shellfish and milk.

title: Kokkinisto (Greek Beef in Red Tomato Sauce)
summary: Beef braised in a cinnamon-scented tomato and wine sauce, served with pasta or potatoes.

steps.text: Brown the beef in the oil in batches for 10 minutes. Lift out. Cook the onion and garlic for 6 minutes.
Add the wine and boil for 2 minutes, then the tomatoes, paste, cinnamon, bay, water and beef.
Cover and simmer for 1 1/2 hours, until the beef is very tender and the sauce thick.
Boil the pasta until tender and serve with the beef.

notes: Food safety: beef pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender; braise until the meat pulls apart. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free.

title: Lahanodolmades (Greek Cabbage Rolls with Mince and Rice)
summary: Cabbage leaves wrapped around spiced beef and rice, cooked in lemon and tomato sauce.

steps.text: Core the cabbage and simmer in salted water for 8 minutes. Peel off 12 soft leaves and trim the thick ribs.
Mix the mince, rice, onion, dill, paste, salt and pepper. Put 2 tbsp on each leaf, fold in the sides and roll up.
Pack seam-down in a pot lined with spare leaves. Add the oil, stock and lemon juice and weigh down with a plate.
Cover and simmer for 45 minutes, until the rice and meat are cooked through.
Serve with the pan juices.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free.

title: Pescado a la Veracruzana (Veracruz-Style Fish)
summary: Fish simmered in a tomato, olive, caper and green chilli sauce, a Gulf coast Mexican classic.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the oil for 6 minutes, then add the garlic, tomatoes, olives, capers, chilli and bay. Simmer for 12 minutes, until thick.
Season the fish and nestle into the sauce.
Cover and cook for 8 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flakes.
Add the lime juice and serve over rice.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until opaque. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Pollo Pibil (Yucatan Achiote Chicken in Banana Leaf Style)
summary: Chicken marinated in citrus and achiote, wrapped and slowly baked until tender.

steps.text: Blend the achiote, juices, garlic, cumin, oregano and 1 tsp salt. Coat the chicken well.
Heat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan). Wrap the chicken and marinade in baking paper and foil parcels.
Bake for 75 minutes, until tender and cooked through.
Pickle the onion in lime juice for 15 minutes. Shred the chicken, serve in warm tortillas with onion and wedges.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
For best flavour, marinate the chicken in the fridge for a few hours or overnight, never on the bench. Dairy-free.

title: Tinga de Pollo (Shredded Chipotle Chicken)
summary: Shredded chicken in a smoky chipotle and tomato sauce, piled on crisp tostadas.

steps.text: Simmer the chicken in water for 18 minutes, until cooked through. Shred.
Blend the tomato, garlic and chipotle until smooth.
Cook the onion in the oil for 6 minutes, add the sauce and stock and simmer for 8 minutes. Stir in the chicken for 5 minutes.
Crisp the tortillas under the grill and top with tinga, sour cream and coriander.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk. Gluten-free.

title: Jamaican-Style Curried Lamb
summary: Lamb shoulder marinated in curry powder and thyme, simmered until meltingly tender, in the style of Jamaican curry goat.

steps.text: Rub the meat with half the curry powder, garlic, ginger and 1 tsp salt and marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour.
Fry the remaining powder in the oil for 1 minute. Brown the meat for 10 minutes with the onion.
Add the thyme, whole chilli and water. Cover and simmer for 1 1/2 hours.
Add the potato and cook for 20 minutes, until the meat is tender and the sauce thick. Remove the chilli and serve with rice.

notes: Food safety: lamb pieces should reach at least 70°C and be tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
The whole chilli adds heat without bursting; take care when removing it. Dairy-free and gluten-free.
Goat is traditional in Jamaica; lamb shoulder is used here because it is easier to buy. Diced goat works the same way with about 30 minutes more simmering.

title: Stew Peas (Jamaican Red Bean and Pork Stew)
summary: Red kidney beans simmered in coconut milk with pork, thyme and spinners.

steps.text: Brown the pork for 8 minutes. Add the onion and garlic and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the beans, coconut milk, thyme, whole chilli and 3 cups water. Cover and simmer for 40 minutes.
Mix the flour, 1/2 cup water and a pinch of salt into a dough and roll into small spinners.
Drop them in and cook for 15 minutes, until the stew is thick. Serve with rice.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free. Canned beans are already cooked.

title: Pastelón (Puerto Rican Plantain and Beef Lasagne)
summary: Layers of sweet plantain around spiced beef picadillo and cheese, baked until golden.

steps.text: Fry the plantain in oil for 4 minutes a side until golden. Drain.
Brown the mince for 8 minutes, add the onion, garlic and cumin for 5 minutes, then paste and olives for 3 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Layer half the plantain in a dish, top with half the cheese, all the beef, then the rest of the plantain.
Pour over the beaten eggs and top with the remaining cheese. Bake for 30 minutes, until set and golden.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Moros y Cristianos (Cuban Black Beans and Rice with Pork)
summary: Black beans cooked with rice, pork and sofrito into one comforting pot.

steps.text: Brown the pork in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the onion, capsicum and garlic and cook for 8 minutes with the cumin.
Add the beans, rice, stock, vinegar and bay. Bring to a boil, then cover and cook on low for 20 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid absorbed.
Rest for 5 minutes and fluff with a fork.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Cool leftover rice quickly and eat within a day. Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Vaca Frita (Cuban Crispy Shredded Beef)
summary: Slow-simmered beef shredded then fried with garlic and lime until crisp at the edges.

steps.text: Simmer the steak with the halved onion and bay in water for 2 hours, until tender. Cool, then shred.
Toss the beef with the lime juice, garlic and 1 tsp salt and leave 15 minutes.
Fry the sliced onion in half the oil for 8 minutes. Add the beef and remaining oil in a hot pan and cook for 10 minutes without stirring much, until crisp and browned. Serve over rice.

notes: Food safety: beef pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender; braise until the meat pulls apart. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Locro (Argentine Pumpkin, Corn and Pork Stew)
summary: A thick Andean stew of pumpkin, corn, beans and pork, traditionally served on national holidays.

steps.text: Brown the pork and chorizo in a heavy pot for 8 minutes. Add the onion, garlic and paprika for 5 minutes.
Add the pumpkin and water, cover and simmer for 1 hour, until the pork is tender.
Mash some of the pumpkin into the stew to thicken, then add the corn and beans for 15 minutes.
Season and serve in bowls topped with spring onion.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Sausages must reach 75°C. Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Tangia Marrakchia (Marrakech Slow-Cooked Beef Pot)
summary: Beef cooked for hours in a clay pot with preserved lemon, saffron and cumin, a street food classic.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C (130°C fan). Put the beef, garlic, cumin, ginger, saffron, lemon, oil, butter, 1 tsp salt and water into a heavy lidded pot.
Cover tightly with foil and the lid.
Cook for 3 1/2 hours, until the beef falls apart. Stir once in the middle, then serve with bread.

notes: Food safety: beef pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender; braise until the meat pulls apart. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk. Gluten-free.

title: Barbunya Pilaki (Turkish Borlotti Beans in Tomato)
summary: Soft borlotti beans stewed with carrot, onion and tomato, served warm or cold with bread.

steps.text: Cook the onion and carrot in the oil for 10 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic and paste for 2 minutes.
Add the beans, sugar, water and salt and simmer for 15 minutes, until thick.
Scatter with parsley and serve with lemon and bread.

notes: Vegan and dairy-free. Canned beans are already cooked.

title: Brunswick Stew (Slow Cooker Chicken and Pork)
summary: Smoky shredded chicken and pork with sweet corn and beans in a tangy tomato base, left to bubble all day.

steps.text: Put the chicken, pork, onion, garlic, tomatoes, stock, barbecue sauce, Worcestershire sauce, paprika and salt in the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on low for 6 hours, until the pork is very tender and the chicken falls apart.
Lift out the chicken, shred it with two forks and return it to the pot with the corn and beans.
Cook on high for 30 minutes, until the stew is thick and the corn is hot.
Stir through the vinegar, taste and serve in bowls with cornbread.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken until the thickest part reaches 75°C and the juices run clear. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: cook pork until it reaches at least 70°C in the thickest part. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with cornbread or crusty bread.
Freezes well for up to 3 months in portions.

title: Dirty Rice (Cajun Chicken Liver and Pork)
summary: Cajun rice with browned pork mince, chicken liver, onion, capsicum and celery.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large deep pan and brown the pork mince for 8 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains.
Add the liver and cook for 3 minutes, until browned all over, then add the onion, capsicum, celery and garlic and cook until soft.
Stir in the Cajun seasoning and rice for 1 minute, until coated, then pour in the stock and bring to the boil.
Cover and cook on low for 18 minutes, until the rice is tender and the stock is absorbed.
Rest for 5 minutes, then fold through the spring onion, parsley and hot sauce.

notes: Food safety: cook pork mince until it reaches 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: cook chicken until the thickest part reaches 75°C and the juices run clear. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Chicken liver can be swapped for more mince if you prefer.

title: New England Boiled Dinner (Corned Beef and Cabbage)
summary: Tender corned beef simmered with cabbage, potato, carrot and swede, served with sharp mustard.

steps.text: Put the corned beef, bay, pepper and onion in a large pot, cover with water and bring to the boil, then skim and simmer for 2 1/2 hours, until the beef is tender.
Add the potato, carrot and swede and simmer for 15 minutes, until nearly tender.
Add the cabbage and cook for 10 minutes, until soft and bright.
Lift the beef onto a board, rest for 10 minutes, then slice across the grain.
Serve the beef and vegetables with a spoonful of the broth, the butter and mustard.

notes: Food safety: cook beef until tender and at least 70°C throughout for slow-cooked cuts. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Keep the cooking broth for soup the next day.

title: Chicken Sauce Piquante
summary: A Louisiana chicken stew in a spicy, dark tomato gravy, served over rice.

steps.text: Season the chicken and dust with the flour. Brown it in the oil in a heavy pot for 8 minutes, until deep golden, then set aside.
Cook the onion, capsicum, celery and garlic in the same pot for 6 minutes, until soft, then stir in the tomato paste and Cajun seasoning.
Add the tomatoes, stock, hot sauce and bay, return the chicken and simmer covered for 50 minutes, until the sauce is thick and the chicken is tender.
Uncover for 10 minutes if the sauce needs to reduce, then scatter with the spring onion and serve over the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken until the thickest part reaches 75°C and the juices run clear. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Add more hot sauce at the table if you like heat.

title: Bifteki (Greek Beef Patties with Feta and Lemon Potatoes)
summary: Juicy oregano beef patties stuffed with feta, roasted alongside lemon potatoes.

items.raw: 800 g waxy potato, cut into wedges

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200C. Toss the potato with the olive oil, garlic, lemon juice and a pinch of salt on a tray and roast for 15 minutes.
Mix the mince, onion, egg, breadcrumbs, oregano, parsley and salt, then shape into 8 patties, pressing a feta cube into the middle of each.
Nestle the patties among the potatoes and roast for 20 minutes, turning once, until browned and cooked through.
Check the potatoes are golden and tender, then serve with lemon wedges.

notes: Food safety: cook mince and sausages until they reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with tzatziki and sliced tomato.

title: Kibbeh bil Sanieh (Baked Lamb and Bulgur Tray)
summary: A layered Levantine tray bake of spiced lamb and bulgur shell around a pine nut and lamb filling.

steps.text: Soak the bulgur in cold water for 15 minutes, then drain and squeeze dry. Heat the oven to 190C.
Knead the bulgur with 500 g lamb mince, grated onion, half the spices, salt and ice water into a smooth paste.
For the filling, fry the diced onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add 250 g mince, the pine nuts, cumin and remaining spices and cook for 8 minutes, until browned.
Press half the paste into an oiled 23 cm square dish, spread the filling over it, then cover with the rest of the paste, smoothing the top.
Score into diamonds, drizzle with the butter and bake for 35 minutes, until golden and the middle reaches 75C.

notes: Food safety: cook mince and sausages until they reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with yoghurt and a simple cucumber salad.

title: Tortilla Espanola (Spanish Potato and Onion Omelette)
summary: A thick, tender omelette of slow-cooked potato and onion, set in a pan and flipped.

steps.text: Cook the potato and onion in the oil over medium-low heat for 20 minutes, turning often, until completely soft but not browned.
Drain off most of the oil, then tip the potato into the beaten eggs with the salt and stand for 5 minutes.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a 24 cm non-stick pan, pour in the mixture and cook on low for 6 minutes, until the edges are set.
Slide onto a plate, flip back into the pan and cook for 5 minutes, until the centre is just set.
Rest for 5 minutes, then slice into wedges.

notes: Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Pollo alla Cacciatora (Hunter-Style Chicken)
summary: Tender braised chicken in a rustic tomato, wine, olive and capsicum sauce.

steps.text: Brown the seasoned chicken in the oil in a large pan for 8 minutes, until golden, then set aside.
Cook the onion, capsicum and garlic for 6 minutes, until soft, then add the wine and boil for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, olives, capers, oregano, rosemary and chicken, cover and simmer for 40 minutes, until the chicken is tender.
Uncover and simmer for 5 minutes, until the sauce is thick, and serve with polenta or crusty bread.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken until the thickest part reaches 75°C and the juices run clear. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Delicious with soft polenta.

title: Saltimbocca di Pollo (Chicken with Prosciutto and Sage)
summary: Thin chicken breast wrapped in prosciutto and sage, pan-fried and finished in a white wine butter sauce.

steps.text: Slice each breast through the middle to make 8 thin cutlets and flatten them to 1 cm.
Lay a sage leaf on each and wrap with prosciutto, securing with a toothpick. Dust lightly with flour.
Fry in the oil for 3 minutes each side, until golden and cooked through, then set aside.
Add the wine to the pan and simmer for 3 minutes, until reduced by half, then swirl in the butter and lemon juice.
Return the chicken to the sauce for 1 minute and serve with greens or mash.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken until the thickest part reaches 75°C and the juices run clear. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Remove toothpicks before serving.
