title: Melanzane alla Parmigiana (Baked Eggplant with Tomato and Mozzarella)
summary: Layers of roasted eggplant, basil tomato sauce and melting mozzarella, baked until bubbling.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220C. Brush the eggplant with 3 tbsp oil, salt it, and roast on trays for 25 minutes, turning once, until golden and soft.
Fry the onion and garlic in the remaining oil until soft, add the passata and simmer for 12 minutes, until thick, then stir in half the basil.
Layer sauce, eggplant and mozzarella in a baking dish, finishing with sauce, mozzarella and breadcrumbs.
Bake at 190C for 25 minutes, until golden and bubbling, then rest for 10 minutes and top with the remaining basil.

notes: Tastes even better the next day.
Freezes well.

title: Bacalhau a Bras-Style Fish, Egg and Potato Scramble
summary: A Portuguese favourite of flaked fish, crisp potato and soft egg, made here with fresh white fish.

items.raw: 500 g potato, cut into thin matchsticks

steps.text: Shallow-fry the potato in half the oil for 10 minutes, until crisp and golden, then drain.
Cook the onion and garlic in the remaining oil until soft, add the fish and cook for 4 minutes, until opaque, breaking it into flakes.
Stir in the potato, then pour in the beaten eggs and stir gently over low heat for 2 minutes, until just set but still creamy.
Fold through the olives and parsley and serve with lemon wedges.

notes: Soak and cook salt cod if you want the traditional version.

Food safety: cook fish until it turns opaque and flakes easily with a fork. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot. cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot. Use fresh, uncracked eggs; for pregnant women, older people, young children and anyone with low immunity, cook the eggs until the yolks are firm.

title: Kotlet Schabowy (Polish Crumbed Pork Cutlets)
summary: Pounded pork loin in crisp breadcrumbs, served with buttery mash and pickled cucumber.

steps.text: Flatten the pork to 1 cm thick and season with salt and pepper.
Dust with flour, dip in beaten egg, then coat in breadcrumbs.
Boil the potato for 15 minutes, until tender, then mash with the butter and milk.
Fry the cutlets in the oil for 4 minutes each side, until golden and the pork reaches 70C inside.
Drain on paper and serve with the mash, pickle and lemon.

notes: Food safety: cook pork until it reaches at least 70°C in the thickest part. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Fry in batches to keep the crumb crisp.

title: Zrazy (Polish Beef Rolls with Bacon and Pickle)
summary: Thin slices of beef rolled around bacon, mustard and pickle, braised until fork tender.

items.raw: 700 g beef topside, cut into 8 thin slices

steps.text: Flatten the beef thin, spread with mustard, then lay bacon, pickle and onion on each slice. Roll up and tie with string.
Roll the beef in flour and brown in the oil in a heavy pot for 8 minutes, until deep golden.
Add the stock and bay, cover and simmer on low for 1 1/2 hours, until very tender.
Lift out the rolls, whisk the sour cream into the sauce and simmer for 3 minutes, until glossy.
Remove the string and serve with buckwheat or mash.

notes: Food safety: cook beef until tender and at least 70°C throughout for slow-cooked cuts. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Braise gently, never boil hard.

title: Tfaya (Moroccan Chicken with Caramelised Onion and Raisins)
summary: Chicken braised in saffron and cinnamon, finished with a sweet onion and raisin topping.

steps.text: Rub the chicken with half the spices and salt. Brown it in the oil in a wide pot for 8 minutes, until golden, and set aside.
Cook one onion with the stock and remaining spices, add the chicken and simmer covered for 40 minutes, until tender.
In a pan, cook the remaining onion with the raisins and honey over low heat for 20 minutes, until jammy.
Pile the topping over the chicken, scatter with almonds and serve with couscous.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken until the thickest part reaches 75°C and the juices run clear. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with couscous.

title: Tourtiere (Quebecois Spiced Pork Pie)
summary: A festive French-Canadian pie of spiced pork and potato in flaky pastry.

steps.text: Simmer the pork, onion, potato, water, spices and salt in a pan for 25 minutes, until the pork is cooked and the liquid has gone. Cool.
Heat the oven to 200C. Line a 23 cm pie dish with one pastry sheet.
Fill with the pork mixture until level and cover with the second sheet, sealing the edges until firmly closed. Cut a steam vent and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 40 minutes, until deep golden and the filling reaches 75C.
Rest 10 minutes before cutting.

notes: Food safety: cook pork mince until it reaches 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with chutney or relish.
Freezes well baked or unbaked.

title: Pate Chinois (Quebec Beef, Corn and Potato Pie)
summary: A comforting Canadian layered pie of beef mince, sweet corn and golden mashed potato.

steps.text: Boil the potato for 20 minutes, until tender, then mash with the butter, milk and salt.
Brown the onion and mince in the oil for 10 minutes, until no pink remains, then add the Worcestershire and stock and simmer for 5 minutes.
Spread the beef in a baking dish, scatter the corn over, then top with the mash.
Bake at 200C for 20 minutes, until golden and bubbling.

notes: Food safety: cook mince and sausages until they reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Freezer friendly before baking.

title: Chicken Parma (Aussie Pub-Style)
summary: Crumbed chicken breast topped with ham, napoli sauce and melted cheese, baked crisp.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220C. Butterfly the chicken to 1.5 cm thick and coat in flour, egg and panko.
Fry in the oil for 3 minutes each side, until golden, and place on a tray.
Simmer the passata, garlic and oregano for 5 minutes, until thick.
Top each breast with ham, sauce and mozzarella.
Bake for 12 minutes, until the cheese is melted and the chicken reaches 75C.
Serve with chips and salad.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken until the thickest part reaches 75°C and the juices run clear. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with chips and salad.

title: Mince and Cheese Pie (New Zealand Style)
summary: A hearty NZ bakery favourite of beef mince and melty tasty cheese in puff pastry.

steps.text: Brown the onion and mince in the oil for 10 minutes, until no pink remains, then stir in the flour.
Add the stock and Worcestershire and simmer for 10 minutes, until thick. Cool and stir through the cheese.
Heat the oven to 200C. Line 6 pie tins with pastry, fill, and top with pastry lids, sealing the edges.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 25 minutes, until puffed and golden and the filling is steaming hot.

notes: Food safety: cook mince and sausages until they reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with tomato sauce.
Freezes well.

title: Chiles Rellenos (Cheese-Stuffed Capsicum in Egg Batter)
summary: Roasted capsicum stuffed with melting cheese, fried in fluffy egg batter and served in tomato sauce.

items.raw: 200 g Monterey Jack, cut into strips

steps.text: Blister the capsicums under a hot grill for 10 minutes, turning, until charred. Steam in a covered bowl, peel, then slit and remove the seeds.
Stuff each with cheese and close with a toothpick. Dust with flour.
Simmer the passata, garlic, onion, cumin and salt for 10 minutes, until thickened.
Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks, fold in the yolks, dip the capsicums and fry in the oil for 3 minutes per side, until golden and puffed.
Spoon the sauce over the capsicums and serve hot.

notes: Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Vegetarian.

title: Lapskaus (Norwegian Beef and Root Vegetable Stew)
summary: A thick, comforting Norwegian stew of beef, potato, swede and carrot.

steps.text: Brown the beef in the butter in a heavy pot for 8 minutes, until golden, then add the onion and cook until soft.
Add the stock, bay, allspice and salt, cover and simmer for 1 1/2 hours, until the beef is nearly tender.
Add the potato, swede, carrot and leek and simmer for 30 minutes, until the vegetables are soft and the stew is thick.
Mash a few of the vegetables against the pot to thicken it, then stir through the parsley and serve.

notes: Food safety: cook beef until tender and at least 70°C throughout for slow-cooked cuts. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with crispbread.
Freezes well.

title: Pyttipanna (Swedish Beef and Potato Hash)
summary: Crisp diced potato and beef fried with onion, topped with an egg and pickled beetroot-style pickles.

steps.text: Boil the potato for 5 minutes, until just tender, and drain well.
Fry the potato in half the butter in a large pan for 10 minutes, until crisp and golden, turning rarely.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes, until soft, then add the beef and Worcestershire and cook until hot.
Fry the eggs in the remaining butter until the whites are set.
Top the hash with the eggs, pickle and parsley.

notes: Food safety: cook beef until tender and at least 70°C throughout for slow-cooked cuts. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Use leftover roast beef for best results.

title: Pot-au-Feu (French Boiled Beef and Vegetables)
summary: Beef shin simmered with leeks, carrots and potatoes, served with strong mustard.

steps.text: Put the beef, bone, onion, bay, thyme and pepper in a large pot, cover with cold water and bring slowly to the boil. Skim the froth until the surface is clear.
Simmer very gently for 2 1/2 hours, until the beef is tender.
Add the carrot, leek, potato, celery and salt and simmer for 30 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Slice the beef, arrange with the vegetables in bowls with some broth and serve with mustard and pickles.

notes: Food safety: cook beef until tender and at least 70°C throughout for slow-cooked cuts. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Keep the broth for soup.

title: Carbonada Criolla (Argentine Beef and Pumpkin Stew)
summary: Sweet and savoury beef stew with corn, pumpkin and sweet potato, baked in a hollowed pumpkin.

steps.text: Brown the beef in the oil in a heavy pot for 8 minutes, until golden. Add the onion, capsicum and garlic and cook until soft.
Add the tomatoes, stock, paprika and oregano, cover and simmer for 1 hour, until the beef is nearly tender.
Add the pumpkin, sweet potato, potato, corn and apricots and simmer for 40 minutes, until the vegetables are soft and the stew is thick.
Serve in bowls with crusty bread.

notes: Food safety: cook beef until tender and at least 70°C throughout for slow-cooked cuts. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Traditionally served inside a roasted pumpkin.

title: Kapama (Greek Cinnamon Chicken in Tomato)
summary: Chicken braised in a sweet-spiced tomato sauce, served over rice or orzo.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil in a wide pan for 8 minutes, until golden, then set aside.
Cook the onion and garlic for 5 minutes, until soft, add the cinnamon, cloves, wine, tomatoes, stock, oregano and salt and return the chicken.
Cover and simmer for 40 minutes, until the chicken is tender.
Stir in the orzo and cook uncovered for 10 minutes, until the orzo is tender and the sauce is thick.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken until the thickest part reaches 75°C and the juices run clear. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Remove the cinnamon stick and cloves before serving.

title: Bistecca alla Pizzaiola (Steak in Tomato and Oregano Sauce)
summary: Seared steak finished in a garlicky tomato, caper and oregano sauce.

steps.text: Season the steak and sear in the oil in a hot pan for 3 minutes each side, until browned. Set aside.
Fry the garlic for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes, capers, oregano, salt and pepper and simmer for 10 minutes, until thick.
Return the steak to the sauce and cook 3 minutes more, until the internal temperature reaches at least 60C for medium.
Slice and serve with the sauce, parsley and potatoes or bread.

notes: Food safety: cook beef until tender and at least 70°C throughout for slow-cooked cuts. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Rest the meat for 5 minutes before slicing.

title: Choripan (Argentine Grilled Sausage with Chimichurri)
summary: Smoky grilled sausages in crusty bread with a bright parsley and garlic chimichurri.

steps.text: Stir the parsley, garlic, oregano, oil, vinegar and chilli flakes together for the chimichurri and stand for 10 minutes.
Grill the sausages over medium heat for 15 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through at 75C.
Split the rolls, toast them on the grill for 1 minute, until warm.
Fill each roll with 2 sausages, sliced tomato and a spoonful of chimichurri.

notes: Food safety: cook mince and sausages until they reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Butterfly the sausages if you prefer.

title: Faggots in Onion Gravy (British Pork Meatballs)
summary: Old-fashioned British pork and liver meatballs baked in a rich onion gravy.

steps.text: Mix the mince, liver, grated onion, breadcrumbs, sage, nutmeg and egg and shape into 8 balls. Heat the oven to 190C.
Brown the faggots in a pan for 6 minutes, until golden, and set in a baking dish.
Cook the sliced onion in the butter for 10 minutes, until deeply golden, stir in the flour and add the stock and Worcestershire, simmering until thickened.
Pour the gravy over, cover and bake for 30 minutes, until the faggots reach 75C, then serve with mash.

notes: Food safety: cook pork mince until it reaches 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Liver can be swapped for more mince.

title: Pisto Manchego Style Capsicum Stew with Poached Eggs
summary: Slow-cooked Spanish capsicum, zucchini and tomato stew with eggs baked on top.

steps.text: Cook the onion and capsicums in the oil for 10 minutes, until soft.
Add the zucchini and garlic and cook for 5 minutes, then stir in the paprika, tomatoes and salt and simmer for 20 minutes, until thick and jammy.
Make 4 wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 5 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are still soft, then serve with bread.

notes: Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Vegetarian.

title: Fabada Asturiana (White Bean, Pork and Chorizo Stew)
summary: A rich Spanish stew of white beans, smoked chorizo and pork belly.

steps.text: Put the pork belly, chorizo, onion, garlic, paprika, saffron, bay and water in a pot and simmer gently for 1 hour, until the pork is tender.
Add the beans and salt and cook for 30 minutes, until the liquid is thick and creamy.
Skim off excess fat, taste and rest 10 minutes.
Ladle into bowls with crusty bread.

notes: Food safety: cook pork mince until it reaches 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Better the next day.

title: Albondigas en Salsa (Spanish Meatballs in Tomato Sauce)
summary: Tender pork and beef meatballs simmered in a sherry tomato sauce thickened with almond.

steps.text: Mix the mince, egg, breadcrumbs, 1 garlic, parsley and salt, shape into 24 balls and brown in the oil for 6 minutes, until golden. Set aside.
Cook the onion and remaining garlic until soft, add the sherry and boil for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, stock, almond meal and paprika, simmer for 10 minutes, then return the meatballs.
Cook for 15 minutes, until the meatballs reach 75C and the sauce is thick.

notes: Food safety: cook mince and sausages until they reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with rice or crusty bread.

title: Pinchos Morunos (Spanish Spiced Pork Skewers)
summary: Pork fillet skewers coated in smoky cumin and paprika, grilled until charred.

steps.text: Mix the oil, spices, garlic, oregano, vinegar and salt, toss the pork through and thread onto skewers.
Heat the grill or barbecue to high, then grill for 10 minutes, turning, until charred and the pork reaches 70C inside.
Rest for 3 minutes and serve with lemon wedges and flatbread.

notes: Food safety: cook pork until it reaches at least 70°C in the thickest part. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Marinate for 1 hour if time allows.

title: Empanada Gallega (Galician Tuna and Capsicum Pie)
summary: A golden Galician pie of tuna, sweet capsicum and onion in a flaky pastry crust.

steps.text: Cook the onion and capsicum in the oil for 15 minutes, until very soft, then add the garlic, paprika and tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes, until thick. Cool, then stir in the tuna.
Heat the oven to 200C. Line a baking tray with one pastry sheet, spread the filling over leaving a border, cover with the second sheet and seal the edges.
Brush with beaten egg, cut a vent and bake for 30 minutes, until deep golden.

notes: Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Good cold.

title: Lahana Dolmades (Greek Cabbage Rolls with Avgolemono)
summary: Cabbage leaves stuffed with beef, rice and herbs, finished in silky egg-lemon sauce.

steps.text: Boil the cabbage for 8 minutes, until the leaves soften, and separate 14 leaves.
Mix the mince, rice, onion, dill, oil and salt. Roll a spoonful in each leaf.
Pack the rolls into a pot, pour in the stock, weigh them down with a plate and simmer for 45 minutes, until the rice and beef are cooked at 75C.
Whisk the eggs and lemon juice, slowly whisk in a ladle of hot broth, then pour back and swirl gently over low heat for 3 minutes, until slightly thick, then serve at once.

notes: Food safety: cook mince and sausages until they reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Do not boil after adding the egg or it will curdle.

title: Arni Fricassee (Greek Lamb with Cos Lettuce and Dill)
summary: Spring lamb braised with cos lettuce and dill, brightened with lemon.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil for 8 minutes, until golden, then add the onion and spring onion and cook until soft.
Add the water and salt, cover and simmer for 1 hour, until the lamb is tender.
Add the lettuce and dill and cook 15 minutes, until wilted and soft.
Whisk the eggs with lemon juice and a ladle of broth, stir into the pot off the heat until the sauce thickens slightly.

notes: Food safety: cook lamb until tender and at least 70°C throughout. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with crusty bread.

title: Tavuk Sote (Turkish Chicken Saute)
summary: Quick pan-cooked chicken with capsicum, tomato and gentle chilli.

steps.text: Sear the chicken in the oil in a wide pan over high heat for 6 minutes, until browned.
Add the onion, capsicum and garlic and cook for 5 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the paste, tomato, oregano, chilli, stock and salt and simmer for 10 minutes, until the chicken reaches 75C and the sauce is thick.
Serve with rice or bread.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken until the thickest part reaches 75°C and the juices run clear. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with rice.

title: Biber Dolmasi (Turkish Lamb and Rice Stuffed Capsicums)
summary: Capsicums filled with spiced lamb and rice, baked in a tomato bath.

steps.text: Cut the tops off the capsicums and remove the seeds.
Mix the mince, rice, onion, 1 tbsp paste, cumin, mint, parsley, oil and salt, then fill the capsicums two-thirds full.
Stand them in a pot, whisk the stock with the remaining paste and pour around, then cover.
Simmer for 45 minutes, until the capsicums are tender and the filling reaches 75C. Rest for 10 minutes.

notes: Food safety: cook mince and sausages until they reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with yoghurt.

title: Kafta bil Tahini (Lebanese Lamb and Potato Bake)
summary: Spiced lamb kofta baked with potatoes and a creamy tahini sauce.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200C. Mix the mince, onion, parsley, allspice and salt, shape into 16 finger-shaped patties.
Toss the potato with the oil and roast for 15 minutes in a baking dish, then arrange the kofta on top.
Whisk the tahini, water, lemon juice and garlic into a smooth sauce, pour over and bake for 25 minutes, until golden and the lamb reaches 75C.
Scatter with parsley and serve.

notes: Food safety: cook mince and sausages until they reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with rice or flatbread.

title: Sfeeha (Lebanese Open Lamb Pies)
summary: Soft little pies topped with spiced lamb, tomato and pine nuts.

steps.text: Knead the flour, yeast, salt, water and oil for 8 minutes, until smooth, and rise for 1 hour, until doubled.
Mix the mince, onion, tomato, molasses and allspice.
Heat the oven to 230C. Divide the dough into 12 balls, roll thin and top with the mince and pine nuts.
Bake for 12 minutes, until the edges are golden and the lamb reaches 75C, then serve warm.

notes: Food safety: cook mince and sausages until they reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Freeze baked pies.

title: Lubia Polo (Persian Green Bean and Beef Rice)
summary: Fragrant saffron rice layered with cinnamon beef and green beans in tomato.

items.raw: 500 g green bean, cut into pieces

steps.text: Brown the beef and onion in 2 tbsp oil for 10 minutes, until golden. Add the turmeric, cinnamon, paste and water, cover and simmer for 40 minutes, until tender.
Add the beans and simmer 10 minutes, until tender.
Boil the rice for 6 minutes, until half-cooked, and drain.
Layer rice over the stew in the pot, sprinkle with saffron, wrap the lid in a towel and steam on low for 25 minutes, until the rice is fluffy.

notes: Food safety: cook beef until tender and at least 70°C throughout for slow-cooked cuts. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with yoghurt.

title: Chicken Pastilla (Moroccan Spiced Chicken and Almond Pie)
summary: Crisp layered filo pie of cinnamon-spiced chicken and almond, dusted with icing sugar.

steps.text: Simmer the chicken, onion, oil, spices and stock for 25 minutes, until the chicken reaches 75C. Shred the chicken and boil the liquid until reduced to 1/2 cup.
Stir in the beaten eggs and cook over low heat for 3 minutes, until scrambled and set. Fold in the chicken, almonds and parsley.
Heat the oven to 190C. Layer half the filo in a round tin, brushing with butter, spoon in the filling and cover with the rest.
Bake for 30 minutes, until golden and crisp, then dust with icing sugar.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken until the thickest part reaches 75°C and the juices run clear. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Cool slightly before slicing.

title: Mrouzia (Moroccan Honey Lamb with Raisins)
summary: Sweet-savoury lamb braised with ras el hanout, honey, raisins and almonds.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil for 8 minutes, until golden, then add the onion, spices and salt and cook for 3 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the water and cinnamon, cover and simmer for 1 1/2 hours, until the lamb is very tender.
Stir in the raisins and honey, uncover, and simmer for 15 minutes, until the sauce is glossy and thick.
Serve with couscous and almonds scattered over.

notes: Food safety: cook lamb until tender and at least 70°C throughout. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Remove the cinnamon stick before serving.

title: Kefta Mkaouara (Moroccan Meatballs with Tomato and Eggs)
summary: Cumin-spiced meatballs simmered in tomato sauce with eggs baked on top.

steps.text: Mix the mince, onion, parsley, half the cumin and paprika and salt, then shape into 20 small balls.
Heat the oil, cook the garlic for 30 seconds, add the tomatoes, remaining spices and chilli and simmer for 10 minutes, until thick.
Add the meatballs, cover and cook for 12 minutes, until they reach 75C.
Make 4 gaps, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 5 minutes, until the whites are set, then top with coriander.

notes: Food safety: cook mince and sausages until they reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with bread.

title: Ojja (Tunisian Spicy Sausage and Egg Pan)
summary: Fiery tomato and harissa sauce with chorizo and eggs baked in the pan.

steps.text: Fry the onion, garlic, chorizo and capsicum in the oil for 8 minutes, until the chorizo is crisp and the onion soft.
Stir in the harissa and spices, add the tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes, until thick.
Make 6 wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 5 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks still soft.
Scatter with parsley and serve with bread.

notes: Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: cook mince and sausages until they reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Use less harissa for milder heat.

title: Mole Poblano-Style Chicken
summary: Chicken in a deep, smoky chilli, almond, sesame and dark chocolate sauce.

steps.text: Simmer the chicken in water for 25 minutes, until the thickest part reaches 75C. Set aside and keep 2 cups of the broth.
Fry the onion, garlic, almonds, sesame and raisins in the oil for 6 minutes, until golden, then add the chilli, spices and paste.
Blend with the stock until smooth, then return to the pot with the chocolate and salt and simmer for 20 minutes, until thick and glossy.
Add the chicken and simmer for 10 minutes, until heated through.
Serve with rice and sesame seeds.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken until the thickest part reaches 75°C and the juices run clear. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Leftover sauce freezes well.

title: Chicken and Mushroom Pie with Puff Pastry Lid
summary: Creamy thyme chicken and mushrooms under a golden puff pastry lid.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the butter for 6 minutes, until golden, then add the onion and mushrooms and cook for 8 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the flour, then add the stock, cream, thyme and salt and simmer for 10 minutes, until thick. Cool slightly.
Heat the oven to 200C. Pour the filling into a pie dish and cover with the pastry, pressing the edges and cutting a vent.
Brush with beaten egg and bake for 30 minutes, until puffed and golden and the filling reaches 75C.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken until the thickest part reaches 75°C and the juices run clear. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with peas.

title: Sausage and Bean Casserole (Slow Cooker)
summary: Pork sausages and beans slowly cooked in a smoky tomato gravy.

steps.text: Brown the sausages in a pan for 5 minutes, until coloured all over.
Put everything in the slow cooker with the sausages.
Cook on low for 5 hours, until the sausages are cooked through at 75C and the sauce is thick.
Remove the bay and serve with mash or crusty bread.

notes: Food safety: cook mince and sausages until they reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Freezes well.

title: Prawns and Cheesy Polenta (Southern Shrimp and Grits)
summary: Spicy bacon prawns over creamy polenta.

steps.text: Whisk the polenta into the boiling salted water and cook on low for 20 minutes, stirring, until thick and creamy. Stir in the cheddar and butter.
Fry the bacon in a pan for 5 minutes, until crisp.
Add the garlic, Cajun seasoning and prawns and cook for 3 minutes, until the prawns turn pink and opaque.
Add the stock and lemon juice and simmer until glossy.
Spoon over the polenta and scatter with spring onion.

notes: Food safety: cook fish until it turns opaque and flakes easily with a fork. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Seafood must be cooked until opaque.

title: Baked Crab Cakes with Lemon and Herb Mayonnaise
summary: Sweet crab and herbs, baked until golden rather than fried.

steps.text: Mix the crab, egg, 1/4 cup mayonnaise, mustard, 1/2 cup panko, spring onion, parsley and Cajun seasoning.
Shape into 8 cakes and chill for 15 minutes, until firm.
Toss the remaining panko with the butter, press onto the cakes, and bake at 220C for 18 minutes, until golden and hot through.
Stir the lemon juice and dill into the remaining mayonnaise and serve alongside.

notes: Food safety: cook fish until it turns opaque and flakes easily with a fork. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Use fresh or pasteurised crab and keep chilled.

title: Tamale Pie (Beef and Polenta Bake)
summary: Spiced beef and corn filling under a golden polenta crust.

steps.text: Brown the mince and onion for 8 minutes, until no pink remains, add the garlic, seasoning, tomatoes, corn and beans and simmer for 10 minutes, until thick.
Whisk the polenta into the boiling salted water and cook for 10 minutes, until thick, stirring in half the cheese.
Spread the filling in a baking dish, spoon the polenta over and top with the remaining cheese.
Bake at 200C for 25 minutes, until golden and bubbling.

notes: Food safety: cook mince and sausages until they reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Freezes well before baking.

title: Al Pastor-Style Pork and Pineapple Tray Bake
summary: Chilli-spiced pork shoulder with caramelised pineapple, for tacos or rice bowls.

steps.text: Toss the pork with chilli, cumin, oregano, garlic, juice, vinegar and salt.
Spread the pork, onion and pineapple on a lined tray, heat the oven to 230C and roast for 30 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges.
Check the pork reaches 70C inside, then chop roughly.
Warm the tortillas and fill with pork, pineapple, coriander and lime.

notes: Food safety: cook pork until it reaches at least 70°C in the thickest part. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Marinate overnight for more flavour.

title: Pescado Zarandeado-Style Grilled Fish
summary: Whole-style fish fillets brushed with a chilli-citrus paste and grilled until flaky.

steps.text: Mix the chilli, garlic, soy sauce, juice of the orange and lime, mayonnaise and oil into a paste.
Brush the fish all over, then grill on medium-high for 4 minutes each side, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Serve with warm tortillas, coriander and onion.

notes: Food safety: cook fish until it turns opaque and flakes easily with a fork. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Marinate 30 minutes in the fridge if you have time.

title: Brazilian Chicken Strogonoff
summary: Creamy tomato chicken with mushrooms, served with rice and corn.

steps.text: Cook the chicken in the butter for 6 minutes, until golden, and set aside.
Cook the onion, garlic and mushrooms for 8 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the paste, sauce and mustard, then add the chicken and 1/2 cup water and simmer for 10 minutes, until the chicken reaches 75C.
Add the cream and corn and warm gently until hot, then serve over the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken until the thickest part reaches 75°C and the juices run clear. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Do not boil after adding the cream.

title: Xinxim de Galinha (Bahian Chicken with Peanuts and Coconut)
summary: Chicken in a creamy peanut and coconut sauce with chilli and herbs.

steps.text: Blend the peanuts with the stock until smooth.
Brown the chicken in the oil for 6 minutes, then cook the onion, garlic, ginger, chilli and paste for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the peanut mixture and coconut milk, then simmer for 30 minutes, until the chicken reaches 75C and the sauce is thick.
Finish with coriander and lime.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken until the thickest part reaches 75°C and the juices run clear. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with rice.

title: Hangi-Style Slow Roast Lamb with Kumara and Pumpkin
summary: New Zealand-inspired oven-steamed lamb and root vegetables with a savoury stuffing.

steps.text: Rub the lamb with oil and salt. Heat the oven to 150C.
Wrap the lamb tightly in foil with the stock, set on a tray and cook for 3 hours, until falling apart at 85C.
Add the vegetables to a dish and cook beside the lamb for the last hour, until soft.
Mix the stuffing with the water and bake for 30 minutes, until set. Rest the lamb 15 minutes and pull apart.

notes: Food safety: cook lamb until tender and at least 70°C throughout. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
A tray version of the earth-oven classic.

title: Lentil Shepherd's Pie with Sweet Potato Mash
summary: A vegan pie of lentils, mushrooms and carrots under creamy sweet potato.

steps.text: Cook the onion, carrot, celery, mushrooms and garlic in the oil for 10 minutes, until soft.
Add the lentils, stock, paste, soy sauce and thyme and simmer for 30 minutes, until the lentils are tender and the sauce is thick. Stir in the peas.
Boil the sweet potato for 15 minutes, until soft, then mash with the olive oil.
Spoon the lentils into a dish, top with mash and bake at 200C for 20 minutes, until golden.

notes: Vegan and freezer friendly.

title: Mushroom Bourguignon
summary: Red wine braised mushrooms and carrots, rich and glossy, over creamy polenta.

steps.text: Sear the mushrooms in the oil in batches for 6 minutes, until browned, and set aside.
Cook the onion, carrot and garlic for 6 minutes, stir in the paste, then add the wine, stock, thyme and bay and simmer for 20 minutes, until reduced.
Return the mushrooms, stir in the cornflour mixed with a little water and simmer for 10 minutes, until glossy.
Whisk the polenta into the boiling salted water and cook for 10 minutes, until thick, then serve with the mushrooms.

notes: Vegan.

title: Vegan Cassoulet with Herbed Breadcrumbs
summary: A slow-baked white bean stew with a crisp garlicky crumb crust.

steps.text: Cook the onion, carrot, celery and garlic in the oil for 8 minutes, until soft.
Add the beans, tomatoes, stock, herbs and bay and simmer for 15 minutes, until thick.
Tip into a baking dish, toss the breadcrumbs with the parsley and oil, and scatter over.
Bake at 200C for 30 minutes, until the crumb is golden and the beans bubble.

notes: Vegan.

title: Eggplant Rollatini with Ricotta and Tomato
summary: Roasted eggplant rolled around herbed ricotta and baked in tomato sauce.

steps.text: Brush the eggplant slices with oil and roast at 220C for 20 minutes, until soft and golden.
Mix the ricotta, egg, basil and garlic.
Spread the passata in a baking dish, spoon ricotta onto each slice, roll up and set seam down.
Sprinkle with mozzarella and breadcrumbs and bake at 190C for 25 minutes, until bubbling and golden.

notes: Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Vegetarian.

title: Frittata di Spaghetti
summary: A crisp-edged Italian omelette made with leftover spaghetti, peas and mozzarella.

steps.text: Cook the spaghetti until al dente, drain and cool a little.
Beat the eggs with the mozzarella, peas, parsley and salt, then fold in the pasta.
Heat the oil and garlic in a 26 cm non-stick pan, pour in the mixture and cook on low for 8 minutes, until the base is golden and the edges set.
Flip with a plate, cook for 5 minutes, until firm, and slice into wedges.

notes: Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Uses up leftover spaghetti.

title: Cheese Boreks (Turkish Feta and Parsley Filo Rolls)
summary: Crisp filo cigars filled with salty feta and parsley.

steps.text: Mix the feta, parsley, egg and yoghurt.
Cut each filo sheet in half, brush with oil, add a line of filling and roll into cigars, tucking in the ends.
Place on a tray, brush with oil and scatter with sesame seeds.
Bake at 190C for 20 minutes, until deep golden and crisp.

notes: Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Vegetarian.

title: Leek and Potato Pie with Cheddar
summary: A creamy leek, potato and cheddar pie under puff pastry.

steps.text: Boil the potato for 8 minutes, until nearly tender, and drain.
Cook the leeks in the butter for 8 minutes, until soft, stir in the flour, then the milk, crème fraîche and mustard and simmer 5 minutes, until thick.
Fold in the potato and cheddar and cool slightly.
Fill a pie dish, cover with pastry, brush with beaten egg and bake at 200C for 30 minutes, until golden.

notes: Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Vegetarian.

title: Kale and Potato Frittata with Feta
summary: Golden baked frittata with soft potato, kale and salty feta.

steps.text: Cook the potato in the oil for 12 minutes, until tender and golden. Add the onion and kale and cook until wilted.
Beat the eggs with the salt and pour over, scattering with feta.
Cook on low for 5 minutes until the base is set, then bake at 190C for 12 minutes, until puffed and set.
Rest for 5 minutes and slice.

notes: Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Vegetarian.

title: Potato Rosti with Fried Egg and Chive Sour Cream
summary: Crisp golden grated potato cakes topped with a fried egg.

steps.text: Squeeze the potato and onion dry in a clean cloth and mix with the salt.
Heat half the butter in a pan, press in the mixture in 4 patties and cook on medium for 6 minutes each side, until crisp and golden.
Fry the eggs in the remaining butter until the whites are set.
Top each rosti with an egg and a spoonful of sour cream mixed with chives.

notes: Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Vegetarian.

title: Roasted Cauliflower Shawarma Wraps
summary: Spice-roasted cauliflower with garlic tahini, pickles and parsley in flatbread.

steps.text: Toss the cauliflower with the oil, spices and salt and roast at 220C for 30 minutes, until charred and tender.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice, garlic and 1/4 cup water until smooth.
Warm the flatbread, then fill with cauliflower, tahini, parsley and pickled turnip.

notes: Vegan.

title: Red Lentil Kofte (Turkish Lentil Patties)
summary: Spiced red lentil and bulgur patties wrapped in lettuce with lemon.

steps.text: Simmer the lentils in the water for 12 minutes, until soft. Stir in the bulgur, cover and stand for 15 minutes, until fluffy.
Cook the onion in the oil for 6 minutes, stir in the paste, cumin and chilli, then mix into the lentils with spring onion, parsley and salt.
Knead until it holds together, then shape into small ovals.
Serve wrapped in lettuce leaves with lemon.

notes: Vegan.

title: Gnocchi alla Romana (Baked Semolina Gnocchi)
summary: Discs of set semolina and milk baked with butter and parmesan until golden and crisp at the edges.

steps.text: Heat the milk with 1 tsp salt and the nutmeg until steaming. Rain in the semolina, whisking, and stir over low heat for 8 minutes, until very thick.
Off the heat, beat in the yolks and half the cheese. Spread 1.5cm thick on a tray and chill for 30 minutes, until firm.
Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Cut into 5cm rounds and overlap in a buttered dish.
Dot with the butter, scatter with the remaining cheese and bake for 25 minutes, until golden and crisp.

notes: Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk, egg and gluten.

title: Strangolapreti (Trentino Spinach and Bread Dumplings)
summary: Soft spinach and bread dumplings from Trentino, served with sage butter and parmesan.

steps.text: Squeeze the spinach very dry and chop finely. Soak the bread in the milk for 10 minutes, then squeeze lightly.
Mix the bread, spinach, eggs, flour, half the cheese, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Rest for 10 minutes, then shape into 16 oval dumplings.
Simmer in salted water for 8 minutes, until they float and are firm.
Melt the butter with the sage for 2 minutes. Spoon over the dumplings and top with the remaining cheese.

notes: Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk, egg and gluten.

title: Canederli (Tyrolean Speck and Bread Dumplings)
summary: Big bread dumplings with ham and parsley from the South Tyrol, tossed in sage butter.

steps.text: Soften the onion in half the butter for 5 minutes. Soak the bread in the warm milk for 10 minutes.
Mix with the eggs, ham, parsley, flour, salt and pepper. Rest for 10 minutes, then roll into 8 balls with wet hands.
Simmer in salted water for 15 minutes, until firm and cooked through.
Melt the remaining butter with the sage and spoon over the dumplings.

notes: Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk, egg and gluten.

title: Pesce all'Acqua Pazza (Neapolitan Fish in Crazy Water)
summary: White fish poached in a light broth of cherry tomatoes, garlic and parsley, served with crusty bread.

steps.text: Cook the garlic and chilli in the oil for 1 minute. Add the tomatoes and wine and simmer for 6 minutes, until the tomatoes collapse.
Add the water and salt, then lay in the fish.
Cover and poach gently for 8 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flakes.
Scatter with parsley and serve with the broth and toasted bread.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until opaque. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Dairy-free.

title: Branzino al Forno (Roast Fish Traybake with Potato and Olives)
summary: Fish fillets roasted over lemony potatoes, cherry tomatoes and olives on one tray.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the potato with 2 tbsp oil, salt and rosemary on a tray and roast for 25 minutes, until golden.
Add the tomatoes, olives and lemon slices.
Rub the fish with the last of the oil, season and set on top. Roast for 10 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flakes.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until opaque. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Mozzarella in Carrozza (Fried Mozzarella Sandwich)
summary: Crisp egg-dipped sandwiches with a molten mozzarella centre, a Neapolitan lunch.

steps.text: Make 4 sandwiches with the bread and mozzarella. Trim the crusts and press the edges firmly.
Whisk the eggs, milk and a pinch of salt. Dust the sandwiches in flour, then soak briefly in the egg.
Fry in the oil over medium heat for 3 minutes each side, until golden and the cheese has melted.

notes: Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk, egg and gluten.

title: Cordero Asado (Castilian Roast Lamb with Potatoes)
summary: Lamb shoulder roasted slowly with garlic and white wine over potatoes until it pulls apart.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan). Rub the lamb with 1 tbsp oil, paprika, salt and pepper.
Spread the potato, garlic and rosemary in a deep tin with the wine, and rest the lamb on top. Cover with foil.
Roast for 2 1/2 hours, then uncover, drizzle the potato with the remaining oil and roast for 30 minutes, until golden.
Rest the lamb for 15 minutes, then pull apart and serve with the potato and pan juices.

notes: Food safety: lamb pieces should reach at least 70°C and be tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Arroz de Marisco (Portuguese Seafood Rice)
summary: A wet, tomato-rich rice with prawns and white fish, sloppy rather than dry.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the oil for 6 minutes. Add the garlic, tomatoes and wine and simmer for 8 minutes.
Stir in the rice and stock, cover and simmer for 14 minutes.
Fold in the fish and prawns, cover and cook for 6 minutes, until opaque and the rice is soft but still soupy.
Stir in the coriander and rest for 3 minutes.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until opaque. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Contains shellfish. Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Espetada (Madeiran Beef Skewers with Garlic and Bay)
summary: Garlicky beef cubes threaded on bay branches or skewers, grilled and served with bread.

steps.text: Toss the beef with the garlic, oil, vinegar and salt. Thread onto 4 skewers with the bay leaves.
Grill or barbecue on high for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked to your liking.
Slide the beef off the skewers into the rolls, or serve alongside, with the juices spooned over.

notes: Food safety: beef pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Whole beef cubes are safe once browned outside; cook to at least 70°C if serving well done.

title: Scouse (Liverpool Lamb and Potato Stew)
summary: A thick, peppery lamb and root vegetable stew from Liverpool, traditionally served with beetroot or pickles.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the onion and carrot and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the stock, Worcestershire and bay. Cover and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the potato and simmer for 40 minutes, until the lamb is tender and the potatoes are breaking down.
Season with plenty of pepper.

notes: Food safety: lamb pieces should reach at least 70°C and be tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free.

title: Schweinebraten (Bavarian Roast Pork with Beer Gravy)
summary: Crackling-topped pork shoulder roasted over beer and vegetables, with potatoes and a dark gravy.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Rub the pork with 2 tsp salt and the caraway. Set on the onion, carrot and garlic in a tin with the beer.
Roast for 30 minutes, then drop to 160°C (140°C fan) and roast for 1 1/2 hours, adding the potatoes in the last hour.
Rest the pork for 15 minutes. Strain the pan juices, whisk in the flour over heat and simmer for 5 minutes into a gravy.
Slice and serve with the potatoes and gravy.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten from the beer.

title: Paprikas Krumpli (Hungarian Paprika Potatoes with Sausage)
summary: A one-pot stew of potatoes, smoked sausage and sweet paprika, a classic comfort dinner.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the oil for 8 minutes. Off the heat, stir in the paprika so it does not burn.
Add the sausage, tomato and capsicum and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the potato and water, cover and simmer for 25 minutes, until the potato is tender and the liquid is thick and red.

notes: Food safety: smoked sausage should be steaming hot throughout, reaching at least 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free.

title: Segedinsky Gulas (Slovak Pork and Sauerkraut Goulash)
summary: Pork braised with sauerkraut, paprika and caraway, finished with a swirl of sour cream.

steps.text: Brown the pork in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the onion and cook for 6 minutes, then stir in the paprika.
Add the sauerkraut, caraway and water. Cover and simmer for 1 hour 15 minutes, until the pork is tender.
Whisk the flour into the sour cream and stir into the pot. Simmer for 5 minutes, until thickened.
Serve with the boiled potatoes.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk.

title: Svickova na Smetane (Czech Beef in Creamy Vegetable Sauce)
summary: Pot-roasted beef sliced and served in a smooth root vegetable and cream sauce.

steps.text: Brown the beef in the oil for 10 minutes. Add the carrot, onion, bay and stock, cover and simmer for 1 1/2 hours, turning once, until tender.
Lift out the beef and keep warm. Remove the bay and blend the vegetables and liquid until smooth.
Whisk the flour into the cream and stir into the sauce. Simmer for 5 minutes, then add the lemon juice and season.
Slice the beef and serve with the sauce and bread.

notes: Food safety: beef pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk and gluten.

title: Smazeny Syr (Czech Fried Cheese Sandwich)
summary: A crumbed slab of cheese fried until molten, tucked into a bun with pickles.

steps.text: Dust the cheese in flour, dip in the beaten egg, then press in breadcrumbs. Repeat the egg and crumbs for a thicker crust and chill for 10 minutes.
Fry in the hot oil for 2 minutes each side, until deep golden. Drain.
Split the rolls and fill with the cheese and pickles.

notes: Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk, egg and gluten.

title: Cevapi (Bosnian Grilled Beef and Lamb Fingers)
summary: Small skinless sausages of beef and lamb, grilled and tucked into warm flatbread with raw onion.

steps.text: Mix the mince, garlic, soda, paprika and 1 1/2 tsp salt well for 3 minutes. Shape into 20 short fingers.
Grill or pan fry for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.
Warm the pita, fill with the cevapi and top with the onion.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten.

title: Pljeskavica (Serbian Spiced Beef and Pork Patty)
summary: A large, juicy grilled patty served in a bun with onion and tomato.

steps.text: Mix the mince, grated onion, garlic, soda, 1 1/2 tsp salt and pepper. Shape into 4 flat patties 1.5cm thick.
Grill or pan fry for 6 minutes each side, until browned and cooked through.
Fill the buns with the patties, tomato and red onion.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten.

title: Sarma (Balkan Cabbage Rolls with Mince and Rice)
summary: Cabbage leaves wrapped around paprika-spiced beef, pork and rice, simmered in tomato.

steps.text: Core the cabbage and simmer for 8 minutes. Peel off 12 soft leaves and trim the ribs.
Cook the onion in the oil for 6 minutes. Mix with the mince, rice, paprika, salt and pepper.
Put 3 tbsp on each leaf, fold in the sides and roll up. Pack seam-down in a pot.
Pour over the passata and water, cover and simmer gently for 1 hour, until the rice and meat are cooked through.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains pork. Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Burek (Bosnian Meat Pie with Filo)
summary: Coiled filo pie filled with spiced beef and onion, baked until crisp and golden.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cook the onion and mince in 1 tbsp oil for 10 minutes, with salt and pepper, until cooked through. Cool.
Lay 2 filo sheets, brush with oil, spoon the mince along one long edge and roll up. Coil into a greased 26cm tin. Repeat to fill.
Whisk the egg, water and remaining oil and pour over. Bake for 35 minutes, until golden and crisp.
Rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Mici (Romanian Garlic Beef and Pork Rolls)
summary: Garlic and thyme scented skinless sausages, grilled until charred and served with mustard and bread.

steps.text: Mix the mince, garlic, soda, paprika, thyme, 1 1/2 tsp salt and pepper, adding the stock slowly. Knead for 3 minutes.
Shape into 12 short rolls and chill for 10 minutes.
Grill or pan fry for 10 minutes, turning, until charred and cooked through.
Serve with the rolls and mustard.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains pork and gluten.

title: Chiftele (Romanian Herb Meatballs with Mash)
summary: Fried pork and beef meatballs flavoured with dill and parsley, served over creamy mash.

steps.text: Mix the mince, onion, egg, crumbs, herbs, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Roll into 16 balls and roll in the flour.
Boil the potato for 20 minutes, until tender. Drain and mash with the milk.
Shallow fry the meatballs in the oil for 10 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.
Serve over the mash with the pan juices spooned on top and extra dill.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Kotlet Mielony (Polish Pork Patties)
summary: Soft pork patties bound with soaked bread and marjoram, fried until golden and served with potatoes.

steps.text: Squeeze the roll and mash into the pork with the onion, egg, marjoram, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Shape into 8 patties and coat in crumbs.
Boil the potato for 20 minutes, until tender. Drain and toss with the butter.
Fry the patties in the oil for 5 minutes each side, until golden and cooked through.
Serve the patties with the potatoes and spoon any pan juices over.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot. Pork mince is safe at 75°C.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Kaldomar (Swedish Cabbage Rolls with Lingonberry)
summary: Cabbage rolls of pork and beef mince glazed with syrup and butter, served with lingonberry jam.

steps.text: Blanch the cabbage leaves in boiling water for 3 minutes and trim the ribs. Mix the mince, rice, milk, 1 tsp salt and pepper.
Put 1/8 of the filling on each leaf and roll up. Set seam-down in a buttered dish.
Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Brush the rolls with syrup, dot with butter and pour in the stock.
Bake for 50 minutes, basting twice, until glazed and cooked through. Serve with the jam.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains pork and milk.

title: Kjottkaker (Norwegian Meat Cakes with Brown Gravy)
summary: Tender beef patties in a brown gravy with boiled potatoes, a Norwegian Sunday staple.

steps.text: Mix the mince, onion, egg, 1/4 cup flour, milk, nutmeg, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Shape into 8 oval cakes.
Boil the potato for 20 minutes, until tender.
Brown the cakes in the butter for 4 minutes each side. Lift out.
Whisk the 2 tbsp flour into the pan, then the stock, and simmer for 5 minutes. Return the cakes and simmer for 8 minutes, until cooked through. Serve with the potato.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Fiskeboller (Norwegian Fish Balls in White Sauce)
summary: Light, springy white fish balls poached and served in a creamy white sauce with potatoes.

steps.text: Blend the fish with the egg, cornflour, nutmeg and 1 tsp salt. Add 1 cup milk slowly until smooth. Chill for 15 minutes.
Boil the potato for 20 minutes. Shape the fish mix into 16 balls with wet spoons and poach in simmering salted water for 8 minutes, until firm and white.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute and whisk in 1 cup milk. Simmer for 4 minutes until thick.
Serve the balls with the sauce and potatoes.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until opaque. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Bragioli (Maltese Beef Olives)
summary: Thin beef slices rolled around bacon, egg and herbs, then braised in a wine and tomato sauce.

steps.text: Chop 1 egg and quarter the other. Mix the bacon, crumbs, parsley and chopped egg, and spread on the beef slices with a quarter of egg on each pair.
Roll up and tie with string or secure with toothpicks. Brown in the oil for 8 minutes, then lift out.
Cook the onion in the pan for 5 minutes, add the wine, paste and stock and bring to a simmer.
Return the rolls, cover and simmer for 1 hour, until the beef is tender. Boil the potatoes for 20 minutes, until tender, and serve alongside.

notes: Food safety: beef pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Timpana (Maltese Baked Macaroni Pie)
summary: Pastry-wrapped pasta baked with beef ragu, egg and cheese, a Maltese celebration dish.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 6 minutes, then brown the mince for 8 minutes. Add the tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes, until thick.
Boil the pasta for 2 minutes short of the pack time. Drain and mix with the sauce, cheese and sliced eggs.
Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Line a 24cm tin with 1 pastry sheet and pile in the pasta.
Cover with the second sheet, seal the edges and brush with the beaten egg. Bake for 40 minutes, until golden and the centre is steaming hot. Rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Sheftalia (Cypriot Pork Patties in Pita)
summary: Herby pork patties grilled until charred, stuffed into warm pita with tomato and onion.

steps.text: Mix the pork, grated onion, parsley, cumin, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Shape into 8 short sausages.
Grill or pan fry for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.
Warm the pita, fill with sheftalia, tomato and red onion.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten.

title: Afelia (Cypriot Pork in Red Wine and Coriander)
summary: Pork cubes braised in red wine with crushed coriander seed, served with rice.

steps.text: Brown the pork in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the coriander and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and water, cover and simmer gently for 1 hour 15 minutes, until the pork is tender and the sauce reduced.
Meanwhile cook the rice in salted water for 12 minutes, until tender. Serve the pork over the rice.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Psari Plaki (Greek Baked Fish with Tomato and Potato)
summary: Fish baked over sliced potato in a garlicky tomato and wine sauce.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Layer the potato and onion in a dish with the garlic, tomatoes, wine, 3 tbsp oil, salt and pepper.
Bake for 25 minutes, until the potato is nearly tender.
Set the fish on top, drizzle with the remaining oil and bake for 12 minutes, until opaque and flaking.
Scatter with parsley and serve straight from the dish with the pan juices.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until opaque. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Garides Saganaki (Greek Prawns with Tomato and Feta)
summary: Prawns simmered in a tomato sauce, topped with feta and baked until bubbling.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Soften the onion in the oil for 6 minutes, add the garlic, tomatoes and wine and simmer for 8 minutes.
Stir in the prawns, scatter with the feta and bake in a dish for 8 minutes, until the prawns are pink and the feta is soft.
Serve hot from the dish with the bread to mop up the sauce.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until opaque. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Contains shellfish and milk.

title: Khinkali (Georgian Spiced Meat Dumplings)
summary: Pleated dumplings filled with a peppery meat broth, eaten by hand and held by the topknot.

steps.text: Mix the flour, salt and 1/2 cup water into a firm dough. Knead for 8 minutes and rest for 20 minutes.
Mix the mince, onion, cumin, coriander, 1 tsp salt, pepper and 3/4 cup water well.
Roll the dough thin, cut into 10cm rounds and put 1 tbsp filling in each. Pleat the edges and pinch into a knot at the top.
Boil in salted water for 12 minutes, until they float and the meat is cooked through. Serve with black pepper.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten and pork.

title: Ojakhuri (Georgian Pan-Fried Pork and Potatoes)
summary: Browned pork with crisp potatoes and onion, a hearty Georgian family supper.

steps.text: Brown the pork in half the oil for 10 minutes. Lift out.
Fry the potato in the remaining oil for 15 minutes, until golden. Add the onion and cook for 6 minutes.
Return the pork with the dried coriander, salt and pepper, cover and cook for 12 minutes, until the pork is cooked through.
Scatter with fresh coriander.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Chkmeruli (Georgian Garlic Chicken in Milk)
summary: Pan-seared chicken simmered in a garlicky cream and milk sauce.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the butter for 5 minutes each side. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Pour in the milk and cream, season, cover and simmer for 15 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce is thick.
Scatter with coriander and serve with the bread.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk and gluten.

title: Khorovats (Armenian Pork Skewers)
summary: Chunky pork skewers with capsicum, grilled over high heat and served with lavash.

steps.text: Toss the pork with the oil, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Thread onto skewers, alternating with the onion and capsicum.
Grill or barbecue on high for 12 to 15 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.
Serve with the tomato and lavash.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten.

title: Shish Taouk (Lebanese Garlic Chicken Skewers in Pita)
summary: Lemony yoghurt-marinated chicken skewers, grilled and tucked into warm pita.

steps.text: Mix the chicken with the yoghurt, lemon, garlic, paprika, oil and 1 tsp salt. Thread onto skewers.
Grill or pan fry on high for 12 to 15 minutes, turning, until charred and cooked through.
Warm the pita and fill with the chicken and tomato.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk and gluten.

title: Lamb Kofta Flatbreads with Yoghurt and Cucumber
summary: Spiced lamb patties in warm flatbread with a cool yoghurt, cucumber and mint filling.

steps.text: Mix the lamb, onion, parsley, cumin, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Shape into 8 oval patties.
Pan fry or grill for 8 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.
Warm the flatbreads, spread with the yoghurt and fill with the kofta, cucumber and mint.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk and gluten.

title: Jerk Chicken Wraps with Mango and Slaw
summary: Spicy jerk chicken in a warm tortilla with sweet mango and crunchy cabbage.

steps.text: Toss the chicken with the allspice, thyme, chilli, garlic and a pinch of salt.
Cook in the oil over high heat for 8 to 10 minutes, until charred and cooked through.
Mix the cabbage, yoghurt and lime juice. Warm the tortillas and fill with the chicken, mango and slaw.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk and gluten.

title: Fricase de Pollo (Cuban Chicken Stew with Potatoes and Olives)
summary: Chicken simmered with potatoes, olives and capers in a tomato sauce, served with rice.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil for 6 minutes. Add the onion and garlic and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the potato, passata, olives, capers, wine and 1/2 cup water. Cover and simmer for 30 minutes, until the potato is tender and the chicken is cooked through.
Cook the rice in salted water for 12 minutes and serve with the stew.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free.

title: Lechon Asado (Cuban Mojo Roast Pork)
summary: Pork shoulder slow-roasted in a garlic, orange and lime mojo until it pulls apart, with rice.

steps.text: Mix the garlic, juices, oil, oregano, cumin and 2 tsp salt. Pour over the pork in a tin and turn to coat.
Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Cover the tin tightly with foil and roast for 2 1/2 hours.
Uncover and roast for 30 minutes, until browned and pulling apart.
Cook the rice in salted water for 12 minutes. Shred the pork and serve with the rice and pan juices.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Arroz Chaufa (Peruvian Chicken Fried Rice)
summary: A Chinese-Peruvian fried rice with chicken, egg and spring onion, tossed over high heat.

steps.text: Cook the rice in salted water for 12 minutes, until tender, then spread on a tray to cool. Stir fry the chicken in half the oil for 6 minutes, until cooked through. Push aside.
Scramble the eggs in the same pan for 1 minute, until set, then break up.
Add the remaining oil, capsicum, peas and ginger, then the rice and soy. Fry for 4 minutes, until piping hot.
Toss through the spring onion.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Papa Rellena (Peruvian Stuffed Potato Balls)
summary: Mashed potato wrapped around spiced beef, egg and olive, then fried until crisp.

steps.text: Boil the potato for 20 minutes, until tender. Mash smooth with the raw egg, 1 tsp salt and pepper.
Cook the onion, mince and cumin for 10 minutes, until cooked through. Cool and stir in the boiled egg and olives.
Wrap 3 tbsp potato around 1 tbsp filling to make 8 balls. Dust with the flour.
Shallow fry in the oil for 8 minutes, turning, until golden.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Bife a Cavalo (Brazilian Steak with Fried Egg and Rice)
summary: Seared steak topped with a runny fried egg, served over rice with tomato.

steps.text: Cook the rice in salted water for 12 minutes, until tender.
Season the steaks and sear in half the oil over high heat for 3 minutes each side for medium. Rest for 5 minutes.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Serve each steak on rice, topped with an egg, tomato and parsley.

notes: Food safety: steaks are safe at 63°C in the centre for medium (60°C for medium rare), once the outside is well seared. Keep raw and cooked meat apart. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Coxinha (Brazilian Chicken Croquettes)
summary: Teardrop croquettes of soft shredded chicken in a golden crumb, fried until crisp.

steps.text: Simmer the chicken in the stock for 15 minutes, until cooked through. Shred and keep the stock. Cook the onion with the chicken for 4 minutes.
Bring 2 cups of the stock to a boil with the butter. Stir in the flour for 3 minutes, until it forms a smooth dough. Cool.
Wrap 2 tbsp dough around 1 tbsp chicken and shape into 12 teardrops. Dip in egg, then crumbs.
Fry in batches in the oil for 4 minutes each, until deep golden.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Tacos al Pastor (Mexican Spiced Pork and Pineapple Tacos)
summary: Chilli and pineapple pork seared on a griddle and piled in corn tortillas with onion and coriander.

steps.text: Toss the pork with the paprika, cumin and 1 tsp salt.
Sear in the oil over high heat in batches for 6 minutes, until browned and cooked through. Add the pineapple for the last minute.
Warm the tortillas and fill with the pork, onion and coriander. Serve with lime.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Chile Relleno (Cheese-Stuffed Capsicum in Tomato Sauce)
summary: Roasted capsicum filled with melting cheese, coated in a light egg batter and simmered in tomato sauce.

steps.text: Roast the capsicums under a hot grill for 15 minutes, turning, until blistered. Rest covered, then peel and slit and remove the seeds.
Fill with the mozzarella and close with toothpicks. Dust with flour.
Whisk the whites to stiff peaks, fold in the yolks and a pinch of salt. Simmer the onion, garlic and tomatoes for 12 minutes, until thickened.
Dip each capsicum in the batter and fry in the oil for 3 minutes each side, until golden. Serve in the sauce.

notes: Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk and gluten. Fully cook the eggs; the batter should be set and golden.

title: Camarones al Mojo de Ajo (Mexican Garlic Prawns)
summary: Prawns sizzled in garlic butter and lime, served over rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice in salted water for 12 minutes, until tender.
Heat the butter and oil, cook the garlic and chilli for 1 minute, until golden.
Add the prawns and cook for 4 minutes, until pink and opaque. Add the lime juice and parsley.
Serve over the rice with the pan juices.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until opaque. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Contains shellfish and milk.

title: Torta Ahogada (Guadalajara Drowned Pork Sandwich)
summary: Pulled pork in a crusty roll, drowned in a spicy tomato sauce, a Jalisco street classic.

steps.text: Season the pork with salt, put in a pot with water to cover and simmer for 1 1/2 hours, until it shreds.
Soften the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes. Add the tomatoes, chilli, oregano and 1/2 cup water and simmer for 12 minutes, until saucy.
Shred the pork, fill the rolls and spoon the sauce over them.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten. Dairy-free.

title: Carne Guisada (Tex-Mex Beef Stew with Potatoes)
summary: Slow-simmered beef in a cumin tomato gravy, scooped up with warm flour tortillas.

steps.text: Brown the beef in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the onion, capsicum and garlic and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the cumin, tomatoes, 1 cup water and salt. Cover and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the potato and simmer for 25 minutes, until the beef and potato are tender and the gravy is thick.
Warm the tortillas and serve with the stew.

notes: Food safety: beef pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free.

title: Country Captain (Georgia Curried Chicken with Currants)
summary: A mild curry-spiced chicken and tomato dish from the American South, with currants and toasted almonds over rice.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil for 6 minutes. Lift out. Cook the onion and capsicum for 6 minutes, then add the garlic and curry powder for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and currants, return the chicken, cover and simmer for 25 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce is thick.
Cook the rice in salted water for 12 minutes, until tender. Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 2 minutes, until golden.
Serve the chicken over the rice, scattered with the almonds.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free.

title: Hoppin' John (Southern Black-Eyed Pea and Sausage Rice)
summary: A Southern one-pot of black-eyed peas, smoked sausage and rice, traditionally eaten for luck.

steps.text: Brown the sausage in the oil for 5 minutes. Add the onion, capsicum and celery and cook for 6 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the rice, thyme and cayenne, then the peas and stock. Cover and simmer on low for 18 minutes, until the rice is tender and the stock absorbed.
Rest covered for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.

notes: Food safety: sausage and cured meats must be steaming hot, reaching at least 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free.

title: Kentucky Hot Brown-Style Open Chicken Sandwich with Cheese Sauce
summary: Toast topped with chicken, bacon and tomato under a bubbling cheese sauce.

steps.text: Pan fry the chicken in a little of the butter for 8 minutes, until cooked through. Cook the bacon until crisp and toast the bread.
Melt the remaining butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, whisk in the milk and simmer for 5 minutes, until thick. Stir in 3/4 of the cheese.
Heat the grill. Put the toast in a dish, top with chicken, tomato, bacon and the sauce, then the remaining cheese. Grill for 4 minutes, until browned and bubbling.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk and gluten. Classically made with turkey; chicken keeps it simple.

title: Monte Cristo (Fried Ham and Cheese Sandwich)
