summary: A ham and Swiss-style cheese sandwich dipped in egg and pan fried, served with apricot jam.

steps.text: Build 4 sandwiches with the ham and cheese.
Whisk the eggs and milk in a shallow dish. Dip each sandwich for a few seconds each side.
Fry in the butter over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes each side, until golden and the cheese has melted. Serve with the jam.

notes: Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk and gluten.

title: Patty Melt (Beef Patty and Caramelised Onion on Rye)
summary: A griddled beef patty with melted cheese and sweet onion between toasted rye.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the butter for 15 minutes, until soft and golden.
Shape the mince into 4 thin patties, season and fry in the oil for 3 minutes each side, until cooked through.
Layer patty, cheese and onion between slices of bread. Toast in the pan for 2 minutes each side, until golden and the cheese melts.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk and gluten.

title: Cheeseburger Pie
summary: A cheese and onion beef filling baked in a puff pastry case.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cook the onion and mince for 10 minutes, until browned and cooked through. Stir in the paste and Worcestershire and cool.
Line a 22cm pie dish with 1 pastry sheet and spoon in the mince. Top with the cheese.
Cover with the second sheet, seal the edges and brush with the egg. Bake for 30 minutes, until puffed and golden.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Crumbed Fish Burgers with Yoghurt Tartare
summary: Crisp panko-crumbed fish in a soft bun with lettuce and a quick tartare, an Australian beach-town favourite.

steps.text: Mix the yoghurt and pickle for the tartare. Dust the fish in flour, dip in egg and press into the crumbs.
Fry in the oil for 3 to 4 minutes each side, until golden and the fish flakes. Drain.
Toast the buns for 1 minute, until golden, and fill with lettuce, fish and tartare.

notes: Contains egg, milk and gluten.

Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until opaque. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours. Use very fresh, well-chilled seafood for anything served raw or lightly cured, and serve it straight away; pregnant women, older people, young children and anyone with low immunity should avoid raw fish.

title: Chicken Kyiv (Garlic Butter Crumbed Chicken)
summary: Crumbed chicken breast filled with garlic and parsley butter that runs out when cut.

steps.text: Mix the butter, garlic and parsley, shape into a log and freeze for 20 minutes. Cut a deep pocket in each breast.
Stuff with the butter and seal with toothpicks. Dust with flour, dip in egg and coat in crumbs.

Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Brown the chicken in the oil for 2 minutes each side, then bake for 20 minutes, until cooked through. Boil the potatoes for 20 minutes, until tender, and serve alongside.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Pariserbof (Danish Beef Patty with Fried Egg and Capers)
summary: A seared beef patty on rye with a fried egg, capers, onion and beetroot, a Danish lunch classic.

steps.text: Mix the mince with 1 tsp salt and pepper and shape into 4 patties. Fry in half the oil for 4 minutes each side, until cooked through.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Set each patty on a slice of rye, top with an egg, capers, onion and beetroot.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Hakkebof (Danish Onion Beef Patties with Gravy)
summary: Soft beef patties smothered in browned onions and a simple gravy, served with potatoes.

steps.text: Mix the mince, milk, 2 tbsp flour, 1 tsp salt and pepper and shape into 4 patties. Boil the potato for 20 minutes, until tender.
Brown the onion in the butter for 12 minutes. Lift out. Fry the patties in the same pan for 5 minutes each side, until cooked through.
Stir the remaining flour into the pan, whisk in the stock and simmer for 5 minutes. Return the onion.
Serve the patties with the gravy and potatoes.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk and gluten.

title: Biksemad (Danish Beef and Potato Hash with Fried Egg)
summary: Crisp fried potato and beef with onion, topped with a fried egg and a splash of Worcestershire.

steps.text: Boil the potato for 8 minutes, until just tender, and drain well.
Fry the beef in 1 tbsp oil for 8 minutes, until browned and cooked through. Lift out. Fry the potato and onion in the remaining oil for 12 minutes, until crisp and golden.
Return the beef with the Worcestershire and heat through for 2 minutes. Fry the eggs separately for 3 minutes, until the whites are set, then top the hash.

notes: Food safety: beef pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Flaeskesteg (Danish Crackling Pork Roast with Potatoes)
summary: Pork loin with a crackling rind, roasted with bay and served with browned potatoes.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 240°C (220°C fan). Dry the rind well and rub in the salt. Set on a rack over a tin with the bay and water.
Roast for 30 minutes, then lower to 180°C (160°C fan) and roast for 1 hour, adding the potatoes for the last 40 minutes.
Rest the pork for 15 minutes. If the rind is not crisp, grill it for 3 to 5 minutes, watching closely.
Carve and serve with the potatoes and pan juices.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Karjalanpaisti (Karelian Beef and Pork Hot Pot)
summary: A slow-baked Finnish stew of beef and pork with allspice and onion, served with potatoes.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Layer the beef, pork, onion and carrot in a casserole with the allspice and bay, seasoning each layer with salt.
Pour in the water, cover tightly and bake for 2 1/2 hours, until the meat is falling apart.
Serve with the boiled potatoes and the cooking juices.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Lihapullat (Finnish Meatballs with Cream Gravy)
summary: Soft allspice meatballs in a light cream gravy, served with potatoes and lingonberry jam.

steps.text: Soak the crumbs in the milk for 5 minutes. Mix with the mince, onion, egg, allspice, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Roll into 20 balls and boil the potato for 20 minutes, until tender.
Brown the meatballs in the butter for 8 minutes. Lift out.
Stir the flour into the pan, whisk in the stock and simmer for 4 minutes. Add the cream and meatballs and simmer for 6 minutes, until cooked through.
Serve with the potato and jam.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Makaronilaatikko (Finnish Macaroni and Mince Bake)
summary: A comforting baked macaroni and beef custard, eaten with ketchup in Finland.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Boil the macaroni for 2 minutes short of the pack time and drain. Cook the onion in the butter for 5 minutes, then the mince for 8 minutes, until cooked through.
Mix the macaroni and mince in a greased dish. Whisk the eggs, milk, 1 tsp salt and pepper and pour over. Scatter with the cheese.
Bake for 35 minutes, until the custard is set and golden.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Kroppkakor (Swedish Potato Dumplings with Bacon)
summary: Soft potato dumplings with a smoky bacon and onion centre, served with melted butter and lingonberry jam.

steps.text: Cook the bacon and onion for 8 minutes, until crisp and golden. Cool.
Mix the potato, flour, egg and 1 tsp salt into a soft dough. Shape 12 balls, press a hollow into each and fill with 1 tbsp of the bacon.
Close and re-roll. Simmer in salted water for 15 minutes, until they float and are firm.
Serve with melted butter and the jam.

notes: Food safety: sausage and cured meats must be steaming hot, reaching at least 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Laxpudding (Swedish Salmon and Potato Gratin)
summary: Layers of potato and onion baked with salmon and dill in a creamy egg custard.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Layer the potato, onion and salmon in a buttered dish, seasoning each layer and scattering with dill.
Whisk the eggs, milk, cream and 1 tsp salt and pour over.
Bake for 45 minutes, until the custard is set and the potato is tender.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until opaque. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Pulled Pork Sandwiches with Barbecue Sauce and Slaw
summary: Slow-cooked pork shredded in smoky barbecue sauce, piled in a soft bun with crunchy cabbage.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C (130°C fan). Rub the pork with the paprika, cumin and 2 tsp salt. Put in a covered tin with 1/2 cup water.
Roast for 4 hours, until it shreds easily. Shred and mix with the barbecue sauce.
Mix the cabbage, yoghurt and vinegar. Pile the pork and slaw into toasted buns.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk and gluten.

title: Baked Cod with Chorizo, Potatoes and Peppers
summary: A one-tray Iberian bake of white fish over chorizo-flavoured potatoes and capsicum.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the potato, capsicum, onion, chorizo, oil and paprika in a tray with the tomatoes and 1/2 cup water.
Roast for 30 minutes, until the potato is nearly tender.
Season the fish, set on top and roast for 12 minutes, until opaque and flaking.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until opaque. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Contains pork. Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Pollo Encebollado (Ecuadorian Onion Chicken)
summary: Chicken braised under a heap of lime-soaked onions until soft and sweet, served with rice.

steps.text: Toss the chicken with the cumin, garlic and half the lime juice. Brown in the oil for 6 minutes.
Add the onion and 1/2 cup water, cover and cook for 25 minutes, until the onion is soft and the chicken is cooked through.
Cook the rice in salted water for 12 minutes, until tender. Stir the remaining lime into the chicken and serve over the rice.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free.

title: Machaca con Huevo (Northern Mexican Shredded Beef with Eggs)
summary: Shredded beef fried with onion, capsicum and tomato, set with eggs and served in warm tortillas.

steps.text: Simmer the beef in salted water to cover for 1 1/2 hours, until it shreds. Shred finely.
Fry the onion and capsicum in the oil for 6 minutes. Add the beef and tomato and cook for 5 minutes, until the liquid has gone.
Pour in the beaten eggs and stir for 2 minutes, until set. Warm the tortillas and fill.

notes: Food safety: beef pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Pambazos (Mexican Chilli-Dipped Potato and Chorizo Rolls)
summary: Soft rolls dipped in red chilli sauce and fried, filled with potato and chorizo.

steps.text: Boil the potato for 10 minutes, until tender. Fry the chorizo for 6 minutes, until cooked through, and mix with the potato.
Warm the passata with the paprika and 1/4 tsp salt for 4 minutes, until thick.
Split the rolls and fill with the chorizo mix and lettuce. Dip the outside in the sauce.
Fry in the oil for 2 minutes each side, until crisp.

notes: Food safety: sausage and cured meats must be steaming hot, reaching at least 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains pork and gluten. Dairy-free.

title: Peposo (Tuscan Slow-Cooked Black Pepper Beef)
summary: A Tuscan beef braise driven by a lot of black pepper, red wine and tomato, cooked until spoon tender.

items.raw: 800g beef chuck, cut into large chunks

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Brown the beef in the oil in a heavy pot for 8 minutes, in batches.
Return all the beef, add the garlic, pepper, tomato paste, wine, stock, rosemary and 1 tsp salt. Bring to a simmer, until bubbling gently.
Cover and braise for 2 hours, until the beef is very tender. Add the potato for the last 40 minutes.
Rest for 10 minutes and serve with the pan juices.

notes: Food safety: braised beef is safe once it reaches at least 70°C and is tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Polpettone (Italian Baked Meatloaf with Peas and Tomato)
summary: A baked Italian meatloaf of beef and pork with parsley and cheese, finished in tomato sauce with peas.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Mix the minces, egg, breadcrumbs, cheese, parsley, garlic, oregano and 1 tsp salt and shape into a loaf in a baking dish.
Pour the tomatoes around the loaf. Bake for 45 minutes.
Scatter in the peas, bake 10 minutes more, until the loaf reaches 75°C in the centre.
Rest 10 minutes, slice and spoon over the sauce.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains egg, milk and gluten.

title: Maiale al Latte (Pork Slow-Cooked in Milk and Sage)
summary: A Bolognese braise where pork shoulder cooks gently in milk until the sauce turns nutty and thick.

steps.text: Brown the pork all over in the oil and butter in a heavy pot for 10 minutes. Add the garlic, sage, lemon zest, 1 tsp salt and the milk.

Simmer, partly covered, on low for 1 hour 45 minutes, turning the pork now and then, until the milk has reduced to a thick golden sauce and the pork is very tender. Add the potato for the last 30 minutes.
Slice the pork and serve with the sauce spooned over.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk. The sauce looks curdled; it is meant to.

title: Spezzatino di Manzo con Piselli (Italian Beef and Pea Stew)
summary: A gentle Italian beef stew with tomato, carrot and sweet peas, good with soft polenta.

steps.text: Brown the beef in the oil for 8 minutes. Lift out, then cook the onion, carrot and celery for 8 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, then the wine and stock. Return the beef, cover and simmer for 1 hour 45 minutes, until tender. Stir in the peas for the last 5 minutes.
Cook the polenta in 4 cups of salted water for 10 minutes, stirring, until thick. Serve the stew over the polenta.

notes: Food safety: braised beef is safe once it reaches at least 70°C and is tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Poule au Pot (French Poached Chicken with Winter Vegetables)
summary: Henri IV's Sunday chicken, gently poached with leek, carrot and swede in its own broth.

steps.text: Put the chicken, onion, bay leaves, peppercorns and 2 tsp salt in a large pot and cover with cold water. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 40 minutes, skimming.
Add the carrot, swede and leek and simmer for 30 minutes, until the chicken reaches 75°C at the thigh and the vegetables are tender.
Carve the chicken, serve with vegetables and a ladle of broth, with the mustard and parsley.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free. Keep the broth for soup.

title: Tian Provencal (Baked Provencal Vegetable Gratin)
summary: Slices of zucchini, eggplant, tomato and potato layered upright and baked with thyme and olive oil.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Soften the onion and garlic in 1 tbsp oil for 6 minutes and spread over a baking dish with the lentils.
Stand the sliced vegetables in rows over the top, drizzle with the remaining oil, thyme, 1 tsp salt and pepper.
Cover and bake for 35 minutes. Uncover, add the cheese and bake 15 minutes more, until golden and the potato is tender.

notes: Vegetarian. Contains milk.

title: Soupe au Pistou (Provencal Vegetable and White Bean Soup)
summary: A summer vegetable and bean soup finished with a basil, garlic and cheese pistou stirred through.

steps.text: Soften the onion in 1 tbsp oil for 5 minutes, then add the carrot, zucchini, potato, beans and stock. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the pasta and cook for 8 minutes, until tender.
Crush or blitz the basil, garlic, cheese and remaining oil with a pinch of salt into a paste. Stir through the soup off the heat.

notes: Vegetarian. Contains milk and gluten.

title: Gigot d'Agneau aux Anchois (French Roast Leg of Lamb with Anchovy and Garlic)
summary: A leg of lamb studded with garlic, rosemary and anchovy, roasted until pink and rested well.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cut small slits in the lamb and push in the garlic, anchovy and rosemary. Rub with the oil and 1 tsp salt.
Roast on a bed of potato for 20 minutes, then reduce to 170°C (150°C fan) and roast for 1 hour 10 minutes, until a thermometer reads 60°C for medium.
Rest the lamb for 20 minutes. Simmer the wine and stock in the tin for 8 minutes to a sauce. Carve and serve.

notes: Food safety: lamb pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender; whole cuts are safe at 63°C with a 3 minute rest. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot. Contains fish (anchovy).
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Cuisses de Canard aux Lentilles (Roast Duck Legs with Lentils)
summary: Crisp roasted duck legs on a bed of lentils cooked with carrot, thyme and white wine.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Salt the duck legs, set on a rack and roast for 70 minutes, until the skin is crisp and the meat tender.
Meanwhile, cook the onion, carrot and garlic in 1 tbsp duck fat from the tray for 6 minutes. Add the lentils, wine, stock and thyme and simmer for 30 minutes, until tender. Stir in the mustard.
Serve the duck on the lentils.

notes: Food safety: duck must reach 75°C in the thickest part with clear juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Baeckeoffe (Alsatian Baker's Oven Casserole)
summary: Three meats layered with potato, leek and onion and baked slowly in white wine, the classic Alsatian Sunday pot.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Season all the meat with 2 tsp salt, pepper and the garlic.
Layer half the potato, then the vegetables, then the meat, then the rest of the vegetables and potato in a lidded casserole, adding the bay and thyme.
Pour in the wine and 1 cup water. Cover and bake for 2 hours 30 minutes, until the meat is tender.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot. Beef and lamb must be tender and above 70°C.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Steak Frites (Bistro Pan-Seared Steak with Oven Chips and Pepper Butter)
summary: The bistro classic: a well-rested seared steak with crisp oven chips and a quick pepper butter.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the chips with the oil and 1 tsp salt and bake for 35 minutes, turning once, until golden.
Mash the butter with the pepper, parsley and garlic.
Pat the steaks dry and sear in a very hot pan for 3 to 4 minutes a side for medium. Rest 5 minutes.
Top the steaks with the butter and serve with the chips and rocket.

notes: Food safety: sear steak on the outside; whole steaks are safe at 63°C with a rest, and any pieces must be cooked through if cut or minced. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk.

title: Gratin de Courgettes (French Zucchini and Egg Gratin)
summary: A custardy zucchini gratin baked with onion, thyme and cheese, a light bistro main with a salad.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Cook the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add the zucchini and cook for 8 minutes, until just soft.
Whisk the eggs, cream, half the cheese, thyme and 1/2 tsp salt. Fold in the zucchini and pour into a baking dish.
Top with the breadcrumbs and remaining cheese. Bake for 25 minutes, until set and golden.

notes: Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Vegetarian. Contains egg, milk and gluten.

title: Lancashire Hotpot (Lamb and Potato Pot)
summary: Lamb and onion in a rich stock beneath overlapping golden potato slices, a northern English classic.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Toss the lamb with the flour and layer in a casserole with the onion and carrot.
Pour over the stock and worcestershire sauce, add the thyme and 1 tsp salt. Lay the potato in overlapping rows on top and brush with the butter.
Cover and bake for 2 hours. Uncover and bake 25 minutes, until the potato is golden and the lamb tender.

notes: Food safety: lamb pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender; whole cuts are safe at 63°C with a 3 minute rest. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk and gluten.

title: Cornish Pasty (Beef, Potato and Swede in Short Pastry)
summary: A hand-sized pasty of beef, potato, swede and onion baked in a sturdy pastry crust.

steps.text: Rub the butter into the flour with 1 tsp salt, add about 1/3 cup cold water to make a firm dough and rest it while you prep the filling.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Mix the beef, potato, swede, onion, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Roll the dough and cut four 20cm rounds.
Pile filling onto each, fold over and crimp the edge. Brush with the egg.
Bake for 15 minutes, then at 170°C (150°C fan) for 40 minutes, until golden and the beef is cooked through.

notes: Food safety: braised beef is safe once it reaches at least 70°C and is tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot. Pasties must be steaming hot throughout.
Contains egg, milk and gluten.

title: Cawl (Welsh Lamb and Root Vegetable Broth)
summary: A Welsh lamb and root vegetable broth, thick with leek and potato, traditionally eaten from a bowl with bread.

steps.text: Put the lamb, onion, stock, thyme and 1 tsp salt in a pot, bring to a simmer and cook gently for 1 hour, skimming.
Add the carrot, swede and potato and simmer for 25 minutes. Add the leek and cook 10 minutes more, until the lamb is tender.
Stir in the parsley and serve with bread.

notes: Food safety: lamb pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender; whole cuts are safe at 63°C with a 3 minute rest. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free.

title: Beef and Ale Casserole with Herb Dumplings
summary: A deep brown beef and dark beer casserole with fluffy herb dumplings steamed on top.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Brown the beef in the oil in batches. Add the onion and carrot and cook for 6 minutes, stir in the plain flour and tomato paste, then the beer and stock.
Cover and cook in the oven for 2 hours, until tender.
Rub the butter into the self-raising flour with the thyme and 1/2 tsp salt, add 1/3 cup cold water and form 6 dumplings.
Set on top of the casserole, cover and cook for 20 minutes, until puffed.

notes: Food safety: braised beef is safe once it reaches at least 70°C and is tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten and milk. Beer is cooked off but not fully removed.

title: Leek and Potato Gratin with Wholegrain Mustard
summary: A creamy baked leek and potato gratin with mustard and a golden cheese crust, good as a vegetarian main with greens.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Warm the cream, milk, mustard, garlic and 1 tsp salt together.
Layer the potato, leek and spinach in a baking dish, pouring over the creamy mix as you go. Top with the cheese.
Cover and bake for 40 minutes, uncover and bake 20 minutes more, until the potato is tender and golden.

notes: Vegetarian. Contains milk.

title: Lentejas con Chorizo (Spanish Lentil and Chorizo Stew)
summary: A homely Spanish lentil pot with chorizo, potato, carrot and smoked paprika.

steps.text: Cook the chorizo in a pot for 4 minutes, until it releases its oil. Add the onion, carrot, capsicum and garlic and cook for 6 minutes.
Add the paprika, lentils, bay leaf, potato and stock. Simmer for 30 minutes, until the lentils are tender and the stew thickened.
Season with salt and serve with bread.

notes: Food safety: sausage and cured meats must be steaming hot, reaching at least 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free.

title: Caldereta de Cordero (Spanish Lamb Stew with Peppers and Wine)
summary: A Spanish shepherd's lamb stew with capsicum, garlic, paprika and white wine.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil in batches, 8 minutes. Cook the onion, capsicum and garlic in the same pot for 6 minutes. Stir in the paprika.
Add the wine, tomatoes, bay and 1 tsp salt and return the lamb. Cover and simmer gently for 1 hour.
Add the potato and simmer 30 minutes more, until the lamb and potato are tender.

notes: Food safety: lamb pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender; whole cuts are safe at 63°C with a 3 minute rest. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Kavurma (Turkish Slow-Fried Lamb with Tomato and Peppers)
summary: Lamb cooked down in its own juices with onion, tomato and peppers until tender and glossy, eaten with rice or bread.

steps.text: Heat the oil and brown the lamb in a heavy pot over medium-high heat for 10 minutes. Add the onion, capsicum, garlic, cumin and chilli and cook for 8 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and 1 tsp salt, cover and cook on low for 1 hour 10 minutes, until the lamb is very tender and the juices thick.
Cook the rice in salted water for 12 minutes, drain and serve with the lamb.

notes: Food safety: lamb pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender; whole cuts are safe at 63°C with a 3 minute rest. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Moroccan Lamb Kefta Tagine with Baked Eggs
summary: Spiced lamb meatballs simmered in a cumin and paprika tomato sauce, with eggs set on top and bread to mop up.

steps.text: Mix the lamb, onion, half the garlic, half the cumin, the paprika, coriander and 1 tsp salt and roll into 20 small balls.

Brown the balls in the oil for 6 minutes. Add the remaining garlic and cumin, the cinnamon, tomatoes and 1/2 cup water and simmer for 15 minutes, until the sauce is thick and the meatballs cooked through.
Make 4 wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 6 minutes, until the whites are set. Serve with bread.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot. Cook the eggs until the whites are fully set.
Contains egg. Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Kapusta z Kielbasa (Polish Braised Cabbage with Smoked Sausage and Potato)
summary: A Polish one-pot of soft braised cabbage, smoked sausage and potato, seasoned with caraway and a splash of vinegar.

steps.text: Brown the sausage in the oil for 5 minutes. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the cabbage, potato, caraway, paprika, stock and 1/2 tsp salt. Cover and simmer for 30 minutes, until the cabbage and potato are tender.
Stir in the vinegar and serve.

notes: Food safety: sausage and cured meats must be steaming hot, reaching at least 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free; gluten-free if you use a sausage labelled gluten-free.

title: Pierogi Ruskie (Polish Potato and Cheese Dumplings with Fried Onion)
summary: Tender dumplings filled with potato and ricotta, boiled and finished in butter with caramelised onion.

steps.text: Mix the flour, egg, 1/2 tsp salt and about 3/4 cup warm water into a soft dough. Cover and set aside.
Cook half the onion in 20g butter for 8 minutes. Mix into the mash with the ricotta and 1/2 tsp salt.
Roll the dough thin, cut 8cm rounds, fill with the potato mix and pinch to seal.
Boil in batches for 4 minutes, until they float. Fry the remaining onion in the remaining butter until golden and toss the dumplings through. Serve with sour cream.

notes: Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Vegetarian. Contains egg, gluten and milk.

title: Karelian Stew (Finnish Slow-Baked Beef and Pork with Allspice)
summary: A Finnish stew of beef and pork baked low for hours with onion and allspice, served with mash.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C (130°C fan). Toss the meat with the flour and 2 tsp salt and layer in a casserole with the onion, allspice and bay.
Pour over the stock. Cover tightly and bake for 3 hours, until the meat is tender and the juices rich.
Mash the potato with the butter and a splash of the cooking juices, then serve the stew over the mash.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot. Beef must be tender and above 70°C.
Contains milk and gluten.

title: Stegt Flaesk med Persillesovs (Danish Crisp Pork Belly with Parsley Sauce)
summary: The Danish national dish: crisp fried pork belly slices with potatoes and a creamy parsley sauce.

steps.text: Fry the pork belly slices in a dry pan over medium heat for 8 minutes a side, until golden and crisp. Drain on paper.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute and whisk in the milk. Simmer for 5 minutes, add the parsley, 1/2 tsp salt and pepper.
Serve the pork with the potatoes and sauce.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk and gluten.

title: Chicken and Dumplings (American Southern Comfort Stew)
summary: A creamy chicken and vegetable stew topped with tender drop dumplings, an American family favourite.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the butter for 6 minutes. Add the onion, carrot and celery and cook for 6 minutes. Stir in the plain flour, then the stock and cream. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Rub the cold butter into the self-raising flour with 1/2 tsp salt, stir in the milk and spoon in 8 dumplings.
Cover and cook for 15 minutes without lifting the lid, until the dumplings are cooked through and the chicken reaches 75°C.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk and gluten.

title: Sancocho (Colombian-Style Beef, Yuca and Plantain Stew)
summary: A big pot of beef broth with corn, plantain and potato, eaten as a hearty Latin American family dinner.

steps.text: Put the beef, onion, garlic, cumin, stock, 1 tsp salt and 2 cups water in a pot. Simmer for 1 hour, until nearly tender.
Add the potato, carrot, plantain and corn and simmer for 30 minutes more.
Serve with coriander and lime.

notes: Food safety: braised beef is safe once it reaches at least 70°C and is tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Lamb Cutlets with Salsa Verde and Crisp Roast Potatoes
summary: Grilled lamb cutlets with a sharp parsley, caper and anchovy salsa verde and golden roast potatoes.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the potato with 1 tbsp oil and 1 tsp salt and roast for 40 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
Chop the parsley, capers, anchovy and garlic finely, then mix with the mustard, lemon juice and 2 tbsp oil.
Season the cutlets and grill or pan fry for 3 minutes a side for medium, until browned. Rest for 5 minutes and serve with the salsa and potatoes.

notes: Food safety: lamb pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender; whole cuts are safe at 63°C with a 3 minute rest. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot. Contains fish (anchovy).
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Pollo in Potacchio (Marche Chicken with Rosemary, Wine and Tomato)
summary: A Marche braise of chicken pieces with rosemary, garlic, white wine and tomato, simple and fragrant.

steps.text: Brown the drumsticks in the oil in a wide pan for 10 minutes. Add the garlic and rosemary for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble for 3 minutes, then add the tomatoes, potato and 1 tsp salt.
Cover and simmer for 30 minutes, until the chicken reaches 75°C and the sauce is thick.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Pasta alla Norma (Sicilian Eggplant and Ricotta Pasta)
summary: Fried eggplant in tomato and basil sauce over pasta, finished with baked ricotta salata-style cheese.

steps.text: Fry the eggplant in the oil in two batches for 8 minutes each, until golden and soft. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and 1/2 tsp salt and simmer for 12 minutes, until thick.
Cook the pasta in salted water for 10 minutes, until al dente, drain and toss with the sauce and basil. Dollop with ricotta.

notes: Vegetarian. Contains gluten and milk.

title: Parmigiana di Zucchine (Baked Zucchini with Tomato and Cheese)
summary: Layers of roasted zucchini, tomato sauce and cheese baked until bubbling, a lighter take on parmigiana.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the zucchini with the oil and 1/2 tsp salt and roast on trays for 20 minutes, until soft and golden.
Warm the passata with the garlic and 1/4 tsp salt for 5 minutes.
Layer sauce, zucchini, basil and hard cheese in a baking dish, finishing with mozzarella. Bake for 25 minutes, until golden and bubbling.

notes: Vegetarian. Contains milk. Fresh mozzarella is made with microbial rennet in many brands; check the label.

title: Torta Pasqualina (Ligurian Spinach and Ricotta Pie with Baked Eggs)
summary: A Ligurian pie of spinach and ricotta in crisp filo with whole eggs baked inside.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Wilt the spinach in a pan for 4 minutes, squeeze dry and chop. Mix with the ricotta, hard cheese, marjoram and 1/2 tsp salt.
Layer half the filo, brushing each sheet with butter, in a 24cm tin. Spread in the filling, make 5 wells and crack an egg into each.
Top with the remaining filo, brushing with butter. Bake for 40 minutes, until golden and the eggs are set.

notes: Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Vegetarian. Contains egg, milk and gluten.

title: Polenta e Funghi (Soft Polenta with Garlic Mushrooms)
summary: Creamy polenta with garlic and thyme mushrooms and shaved cheese, a vegetarian northern Italian dinner.

steps.text: Whisk the polenta into 6 cups of simmering salted water. Cook on low for 25 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Cook the mushrooms in the oil in a hot pan for 8 minutes, until browned. Add the garlic and thyme for 1 minute.
Stir the butter and cheese into the polenta, top with mushrooms and parsley.

notes: Vegetarian. Contains milk. Gluten-free.

title: Lentil Bolognese with Spaghetti (Vegan)
summary: A rich lentil and tomato ragu with carrot, celery and red wine, spooned over spaghetti.

steps.text: Cook the onion, carrot, celery and garlic in the oil for 8 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute, then the wine.
Add the lentils, tomatoes and 2 cups water. Simmer for 30 minutes, until the lentils are tender and the sauce thick.
Cook the spaghetti in salted water for 10 minutes, drain and serve with the ragu.

notes: Vegan.

title: Chicken Marengo (Napoleonic Chicken with Tomato, Mushrooms and Wine)
summary: A French and Italian classic of chicken braised with tomato, mushrooms and white wine.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil for 8 minutes a side, skin down first. Lift out.
Cook the onion and mushrooms in the same pan for 6 minutes. Add the garlic, wine and tomatoes and simmer for 5 minutes.
Return the chicken, cover and simmer for 25 minutes, until it reaches 75°C. Scatter with parsley.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Flamiche (Picardy Leek and Cream Tart)
summary: A savoury Picardy tart of soft leek, cream and egg in a buttery crust, served with a green salad.

steps.text: Rub 100g butter into the flour with 1/2 tsp salt and add about 1/3 cup cold water to form a dough. Roll to fit a 24cm tart tin and press in.
Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Cook the leek in the remaining butter for 12 minutes, until soft. Blind bake the case 15 minutes.
Whisk the eggs, cream, cheese, nutmeg and 1/2 tsp salt. Fill the case with leek, pour over the custard and bake 30 minutes, until just set and golden.

notes: Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Vegetarian. Contains egg, milk and gluten.

title: Pimientos Rellenos (Spanish Stuffed Capsicums in Tomato Sauce)
summary: Capsicums stuffed with beef, rice and onion and baked in a smoky tomato sauce.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Cut the tops off the capsicums and remove the seeds.
Cook the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes, then mix with the mince, rice, paprika and 1/2 tsp salt. Fill the capsicums.
Stand in a dish with the passata and 1/2 cup water. Cover and bake for 45 minutes, until the filling reaches 75°C and the capsicums are soft.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Patatas a la Riojana (Spanish Potato and Chorizo Stew)
summary: A Riojan peasant stew of potato and chorizo in a smoky paprika broth.

items.raw: 1kg potato, peeled and torn into chunks

steps.text: Cook the chorizo in a pot for 5 minutes. Add the onion, capsicum and garlic and cook for 6 minutes.
Stir in the paprika and potato, then the stock and bay leaves. Simmer for 25 minutes, until the potato is tender and the broth thickened by its starch.
Season with salt and serve.

notes: Food safety: sausage and cured meats must be steaming hot, reaching at least 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Garbanzos con Espinacas (Andalusian Chickpeas with Spinach and Cumin)
summary: A Seville tapas classic made a full dinner: chickpeas and spinach in a garlicky cumin and paprika sauce.

steps.text: Fry the bread and garlic in the oil for 3 minutes, until golden. Blitz with the cumin, paprika, vinegar and 1/2 cup water to a paste.
Heat the paste in a pan, add the chickpeas and 1/2 cup water and simmer for 8 minutes, until thick.
Stir in the spinach for 3 minutes, until wilted. Season with salt.

notes: Vegan. Contains gluten.

title: Arroz con Costillas (Spanish Rice with Pork Ribs and Paprika)
summary: Pork rib pieces simmered with rice, tomato and smoked paprika, a hearty Spanish one-pan dinner.

steps.text: Brown the ribs in the oil for 10 minutes. Lift out. Cook the onion and capsicum for 6 minutes with the garlic, paprika and tomato.
Return the ribs, add the stock and simmer, covered, for 30 minutes, until nearly tender.
Stir in the rice, season with salt and simmer uncovered for 18 minutes, until the rice is tender and the pork cooked through. Rest for 5 minutes.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Soupa Avgolemono (Greek Chicken, Rice and Lemon Soup)
summary: A silky Greek soup of chicken and rice thickened with egg and lemon.

steps.text: Simmer the chicken, stock and carrot for 15 minutes, until the chicken reaches 75°C. Lift out and shred.
Add the rice and cook for 12 minutes, until tender.
Whisk the eggs with the lemon juice and a ladle of hot broth, then stir back into the pot off the heat with the chicken and dill. Warm gently without boiling.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot. Cook the egg and lemon mixture gently until thickened; do not eat raw egg.
Contains egg. Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Hortopita (Greek Wild Greens and Feta Pie)
summary: A Greek filo pie packed with greens, herbs and feta, crisp outside and lush inside.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Cook the leek and spring onion in 1 tbsp oil for 6 minutes. Wilt the spinach for 4 minutes, squeeze dry and chop.
Mix the greens with the dill, crumbled feta, eggs and pepper.
Layer half the filo in a 24cm tin, brushing each sheet with oil. Add the filling, then top with the remaining filo, brushing again. Bake for 40 minutes, until deep golden.

notes: Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Vegetarian. Contains egg, milk and gluten.

title: Khoresh Bademjan (Persian Lamb and Eggplant Stew)
summary: A tangy Persian lamb stew with fried eggplant, tomato and dried lime flavours.

steps.text: Fry the eggplant in 2 tbsp oil in batches for 10 minutes, until golden. Set aside.
Brown the lamb and onion in the remaining oil for 10 minutes. Stir in the turmeric, tomato paste, tomatoes, lemon juice and 1.5 cups water. Simmer, covered, for 1 hour 15 minutes, until tender.
Lay the eggplant on top and simmer 15 minutes. Cook the rice in salted water for 12 minutes and serve.

notes: Food safety: lamb pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Abgoosht (Persian Lamb and Chickpea Stew)
summary: A Persian lamb, chickpea and potato stew eaten as a broth with bread then a mash of the solids.

steps.text: Put the lamb, onion, chickpeas, tomato paste, turmeric and 1 tsp salt in a pot with 1.2L water. Bring to a boil, until scum rises, and skim.
Simmer, covered, for 1 hour 30 minutes, until the chickpeas and lamb are tender. Add the potato and cook for 30 minutes more.
Stir in the lemon juice. Serve the broth with bread, and mash the solids to eat alongside.

notes: Food safety: lamb pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free. Soaking is not counted in prep.

title: Koobideh (Persian Minced Lamb and Beef Kebabs with Saffron Rice)
summary: Flat skewers of spiced minced lamb and beef, grilled and served over saffron rice with grilled tomato.

items.raw: 1 brown onion, grated and squeezed dry

steps.text: Knead the minces, onion, sumac and salt for 5 minutes until sticky. Mould around flat skewers.
Cook the rice in salted water for 12 minutes, drain and stir through the saffron steeped in 2 tbsp hot water and the butter.
Grill the kebabs and tomato halves on high for 10 minutes, turning, until the kebabs reach 75°C and are browned.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk.

title: Hunter's Chicken (Bacon and Cheese Barbecue Chicken Bake)
summary: Chicken breast wrapped in bacon, brushed with a smoky barbecue glaze and baked under melted cheese.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the potato with the oil and 1/2 tsp salt and roast for 35 minutes.
Wrap each breast in a rasher of bacon and place in a dish. Brush with half the sauce and bake for 20 minutes.
Add the remaining sauce and cheese and bake for 8 minutes, until the chicken reaches 75°C and the cheese is bubbling. Steam the beans for 5 minutes and serve.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot. Bacon must be fully cooked.
Contains milk.

title: Mushroom and Spinach Wellington
summary: A golden puff pastry Wellington packed with roasted mushrooms, spinach and herbs, a vegetarian roast for entertaining.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cook the mushrooms in the oil for 12 minutes, until all the liquid has evaporated. Add the garlic, thyme and spinach for 3 minutes. Stir in the breadcrumbs and 1/2 tsp salt. Cool.
Overlap the pastry sheets, pile the filling in a log, fold the pastry over and seal. Place seam-down on a tray and brush with the egg.
Bake for 35 minutes, until deep golden and puffed.

notes: Vegetarian if puff pastry is. Contains egg and gluten.

title: Semmelknodel with Creamy Mushroom Sauce
summary: Bavarian bread dumplings with a creamy mushroom and parsley sauce, a vegetarian dinner.

steps.text: Cook the onion in half the butter for 5 minutes. Mix with the bread, milk, eggs, parsley and 1 tsp salt and rest for 15 minutes. Shape into 8 balls.
Simmer the dumplings in salted water for 20 minutes, until firm and cooked through.
Cook the mushrooms in the remaining butter for 8 minutes, add the cream and simmer for 5 minutes. Serve over the dumplings.

notes: Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Vegetarian. Contains egg, milk and gluten.

title: Toltott Paprika (Hungarian Stuffed Peppers in Tomato Sauce)
summary: Peppers stuffed with pork and rice and simmered in a sweet tomato sauce with paprika, served with sour cream.

steps.text: Cut the tops from the capsicums and remove the seeds. Mix the pork, rice, onion, half the paprika, egg and 1 tsp salt and fill the capsicums.
Stand them in a pot, pour in the passata, 1 cup water and the remaining paprika. Cover and simmer for 55 minutes, until the filling reaches 75°C and the rice is tender.
Serve with the sauce and a spoon of sour cream.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot. Mince must be cooked through.
Contains egg and milk.

title: Biff Rydberg (Swedish Beef, Potato and Onion Hash with Egg Yolk)
summary: Swedish diced beef and potato fried crisp with onion, topped with a fried egg and pickles.

steps.text: Boil the potato for 5 minutes, drain and dry. Fry in the oil in a wide pan for 10 minutes, until crisp.
Add the butter, onion and beef and cook for 6 minutes, until the beef is browned and reaches 70°C. Add the mustard and 1/2 tsp salt.
Fry the eggs for 3 minutes, until the whites are set. Top each plate with an egg and pickles.

notes: Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot. Beef pieces must be cooked through.
Contains egg and milk.

title: Boller i Karry (Norwegian Meatballs in Mild Curry Sauce)
summary: Pork and beef meatballs in a mild creamy curry sauce, a Norwegian family classic served with rice.

steps.text: Mix the minces, breadcrumbs, milk, egg, 1/2 the onion and 1 tsp salt and roll into 24 balls. Brown in half the butter for 8 minutes.

Melt the remaining butter, cook the remaining onion for 4 minutes, stir in the flour and curry powder, then whisk in the stock. Add the meatballs and simmer for 12 minutes, until the sauce is thick and the meatballs reach 75°C.
Cook the rice in salted water for 12 minutes and serve.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk, egg and gluten.

title: Kalamojakka (Finnish Salmon and Potato Soup with Dill and Cream)
summary: A gentle Finnish salmon and potato soup with leek, allspice and dill.

steps.text: Simmer the potato, leek, onion, allspice and stock for 15 minutes, until the potato is tender.
Add the salmon and simmer for 5 minutes, until opaque and flaking.
Stir in the cream and dill, season with salt and pepper and warm through without boiling.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours. Contains fish and milk.
Gluten-free.

title: Boston Baked Beans with Smoked Sausage
summary: Slow-baked white beans in molasses and tomato with smoked sausage, an American pulses dinner served with bread.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C (130°C fan). Mix the beans, onion, molasses, tomato paste, mustard, vinegar, stock and 1/2 tsp salt in a casserole.
Tuck in the sausage. Cover and bake for 1 hour 30 minutes, uncovering for the last 30 minutes, until thick and glossy.
Rest for 10 minutes and serve with bread.

notes: Food safety: sausage and cured meats must be steaming hot, reaching at least 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free.

title: Baked Stuffed Pumpkin with Rice, Mushrooms and Cheese
summary: A whole small pumpkin baked with a savoury filling of rice, mushrooms, spinach and cheese, a vegetarian showpiece.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Cut the top from the pumpkin, scoop out the seeds and rub the inside with a little oil and salt. Bake for 30 minutes.
Cook the onion, mushrooms and garlic in the oil for 8 minutes, add the spinach to wilt. Mix with the rice, thyme, half the cheese and 1/2 tsp salt.
Fill the pumpkin, top with the remaining cheese and bake for 40 minutes, until the flesh is tender and the top golden. Cut into wedges.

notes: Vegetarian. Contains milk. Gluten-free.

title: Jambon-Beurre (French Ham and Butter Baguette)
summary: The Parisian lunch classic: crisp baguette, soft butter, good ham and a swipe of Dijon.

steps.text: Split the baguette lengthways, leaving one edge attached, and cut it in half crossways.
Spread both cut sides generously with the butter and the mustard.
Layer the ham and the sliced pickles along the base, close firmly and press down until the filling holds together.
Eat straight away, or wrap tightly for the lunchbox.

notes: Food safety: ham is ready to eat but should stay below 5°C. For a packed lunch keep it in an insulated bag with an ice pack and eat within 4 hours, or refrigerate until lunch.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Pan Bagnat (Nicoise Tuna Sandwich)
summary: Tuna, egg, anchovy, tomato and olives pressed into a roll with olive oil, made for the beach.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool under cold water, peel and slice.
Split the rolls and pull out a little crumb from the middle. Mix the oil and vinegar and brush it over the cut sides.
Layer the tuna, tomato, cucumber, onion, olives, anchovy, egg and basil in the rolls, then close and press firmly.
Wrap tightly and press under a weight for 15 minutes, until the bread has soaked up the juices.

notes: Food safety: hard-boiled egg and tuna must stay below 5°C. For a packed lunch use an insulated bag with an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
Contains egg, fish and gluten.

title: Muffuletta (New Orleans Olive Salad Sandwich)
summary: A big sandwich of salami, ham and mozzarella with a punchy chopped olive and artichoke salad that soaks into the bread.

steps.text: Stir the olives, artichoke, roasted capsicum, oil, vinegar, garlic and oregano together in a bowl.
Slice the loaf in half horizontally and pull out a little of the soft middle. Spread the olive salad over both cut sides.
Layer the ham, salami and mozzarella on the base, close, wrap tightly and press under a weight for 20 minutes, until the bread is soaked through, then cut into four wedges.

notes: Food safety: cured meats and cheese should stay below 5°C. Wrapped wedges keep in the fridge for 2 days; for a packed lunch use an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Cubano (Cuban Pressed Pork and Ham Sandwich)
summary: Roast pork, ham, Swiss cheese, pickles and mustard in buttered bread, pressed in a pan until crisp and melted.

steps.text: Split the bread lengths, butter the outsides and spread the mustard inside.
Layer the pork, ham, cheese and pickles, and close.
Cook in a hot frying pan over medium heat, pressing down firmly with a heavy pan or a plate, for 4 minutes each side, until golden and the cheese has melted.
Slice on the diagonal and serve hot.

notes: Food safety: use cooked roast pork that has been chilled promptly. The sandwich should be steaming hot in the middle after pressing; eat within 4 hours if packed, with an ice pack until you can reheat it.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Chicken Shawarma Wrap (with Garlic Yoghurt)
summary: Spiced chicken thigh seared hard and rolled in flatbread with garlic yoghurt, tomato and pickled turnip.

steps.text: Toss the chicken with the spices, 2 of the garlic cloves, the oil, half the lemon juice and 1 tsp salt.
Sear in a very hot pan in two batches for 5 minutes each, until browned and cooked through to 75°C.
Mix the yoghurt with the remaining garlic, lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Warm the flatbreads, spread with the yoghurt and fill with chicken, tomato, cucumber and turnip. Roll tightly.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest piece with no pink. Cool leftovers within an hour; for a packed lunch keep with an ice pack, eat within 4 hours and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Egg Salad Sandwich (with Chives)
summary: Creamy chopped egg with mustard and chives on soft white bread with crisp lettuce, a lunchbox staple.

steps.text: Cover the eggs with cold water, bring to the boil and cook for 10 minutes. Cool in cold water, then peel.
Chop the eggs roughly and mix until creamy but still chunky, with the mayonnaise, mustard, chives, a pinch of salt and pepper.
Pile onto two slices of bread with the lettuce and top with the remaining bread. Cut in half.

notes: Food safety: egg mixtures spoil quickly. Keep below 5°C, pack with an ice pack and eat within 4 hours, or keep in the fridge until lunch.
Contains egg and gluten.

title: Bacon Butty (English Bacon Roll)
summary: Crisp streaky bacon in a buttered soft roll with a squirt of tomato sauce, the 10-minute brunch-or-lunch fix.

steps.text: Cook the bacon in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 8 minutes, turning once, until crisp and well browned with no pink.
Split and butter the rolls.
Fill with the bacon and the sauce and eat hot.

notes: Contains gluten and milk.

Food safety: bacon must be cooked right through until the fat is rendered and the meat is no longer pink. Eat hot; if packed, keep chilled and reheat until steaming. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Chip Butty (English Hot Chips in Buttered Bread)
summary: Oven chips in soft buttered white bread with malt vinegar, the comfort lunch of northern England.

steps.text: Bake the chips on a tray at 220°C (200°C fan) for 25 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
Butter the bread and pile the hot chips onto two slices. Sprinkle with the vinegar and salt, add the sauce and top with the remaining bread.
Press down gently and eat while hot.

notes: Eat straight away, as the chips go soft in the bread.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Torta de Jamon (Mexican Ham Roll with Avocado)
summary: A toasted roll of ham, melted cheese, avocado and pickled jalapeno, a Mexico City street lunch.

steps.text: Split the rolls and toast the cut sides in a dry pan for 2 minutes.
Spread with mayonnaise and layer the ham and cheese on the base. Grill for 2 minutes, until the cheese melts.
Top with the avocado, jalapeno, tomato and lettuce, close and press down.

notes: Food safety: ham should stay below 5°C until cooking. Eat hot; if packed, keep chilled and eat within 4 hours.
Contains egg, milk and gluten.

title: Tacos de Papa (Mexican Crispy Potato Tacos)
summary: Spiced mashed potato folded into corn tortillas and crisped in a pan, topped with lettuce, salsa and a little cheese.

steps.text: Boil the potato in salted water for 15 minutes, until soft. Drain and mash roughly.
Cook the onion in the first oil for 4 minutes, stir in the spices, then mix into the potato and season.
Warm the tortillas to soften them. Put 2 tbsp of potato on one half of each, fold over and press the edges.
Fry the tacos in the second oil for 2 minutes each side, until crisp and golden.
Top with lettuce, salsa, sour cream and crumbled feta.

notes: Eat hot for the best crunch. The potato filling keeps 3 days in the fridge.
Contains milk.

title: Tarte a la Moutarde (French Tomato and Mustard Tart)
summary: A Burgundy-style tart of puff pastry brushed with sharp Dijon, layered with ripe tomato and melted mozzarella.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Lay the pastry on a lined tray and score a border 2cm in.
Spread the mustard inside the border, then layer the cheese and tomatoes.
Scatter the thyme, drizzle with oil and season with pepper.
Bake for 28 minutes, until the pastry is puffed and golden.

notes: Eat warm or at room temperature. Keeps 2 days in the fridge.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Tamago Sando (Japanese Egg Sandwich)
summary: Ultra-soft egg salad with Japanese mayonnaise in fluffy white bread, crusts trimmed.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool in cold water and peel.
Mash the eggs with the mayonnaise, milk, sugar and a pinch of salt until creamy but still a little chunky.
Butter the bread, spread the filling thickly on two slices and top with the rest. Trim off the crusts and cut in half.

notes: Food safety: keep the filling below 5°C. For a packed lunch use an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
Contains egg, milk and gluten.

title: Teriyaki Chicken Bento (with Egg and Edamame)
summary: Glazed chicken thigh, rolled omelette, edamame and carrot packed over rice in a box that eats well cold.

steps.text: Sear the chicken in the first oil for 6 minutes, add the teriyaki sauce and cook for 3 more minutes, until glossy and cooked through to 75°C.
Whisk the eggs with the soy sauce and sugar. Cook in the second oil in a small pan over low heat, rolling it up as it sets, about 5 minutes, then slice.
Boil the edamame and carrot for 3 minutes and drain.
Pack the rice into two boxes and arrange the chicken, egg, edamame and carrot on top. Sprinkle with sesame seeds.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C. Cool the rice and chicken quickly, then keep below 5°C. For a packed lunch use an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
Contains egg, soy and sesame.

title: Oyakodon (Japanese Chicken and Egg Rice Bowl)
summary: Tender chicken and onion simmered in a sweet soy broth, finished with loosely set egg over steaming rice.

steps.text: Simmer the stock, soy sauce, mirin and sugar in a wide pan. Add the onion and chicken and cook for 8 minutes, until the chicken reaches 75°C.
Pour the egg over in a circle, cover and cook for 2 minutes, until just set but still soft.
Slide it over the rice in two bowls and top with spring onion.

notes: Contains egg, soy and gluten.

Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C and the egg should be set, not runny. Best eaten straight away; refrigerate leftovers within an hour and eat within a day. Use fresh, uncracked eggs; for pregnant women, older people, young children and anyone with low immunity, cook the eggs until the yolks are firm.

title: Chicken Yakisoba (Japanese Stir-Fried Noodles)
summary: Chewy wheat noodles tossed with chicken, cabbage and carrot in a tangy Worcestershire and soy sauce.

steps.text: Loosen the noodles in boiling water for 1 minute and drain.
Stir-fry the chicken in half the oil over high heat for 5 minutes, until cooked through to 75°C. Remove.
Stir-fry the cabbage and carrot in the remaining oil for 3 minutes.
Add the noodles, chicken, sauces and sugar and toss for 2 minutes. Scatter with spring onion.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour; for a packed lunch use an ice pack, eat within 4 hours and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten, soy and fish (Worcestershire sauce).

title: Korean Egg Toast (Gilgeori Toast)
summary: A thick vegetable omelette in buttery toast with a sprinkle of sugar, the Seoul street breakfast.

steps.text: Beat the eggs with the cabbage, carrot, spring onion and a pinch of salt.
Melt a little butter in a pan and toast the bread on both sides for about 2 minutes each, until golden. Set aside.
Pour half the egg mixture into the pan, shape into a square the size of the bread and cook for 3 minutes, folding the edges in and flipping once, until fully set. Repeat.
Sprinkle the toast with sugar, put the omelette on, squeeze on the tomato sauce and close, pressing until the toast is warm through.

notes: Food safety: the egg must be cooked through with no wet patches. Eat straight away.
Contains egg, milk and gluten.

title: Pad See Ew (Thai Soy Sauce Rice Noodles with Chicken)
summary: Wide, charred rice noodles with chicken, egg and gai lan in a sweet-savoury dark soy sauce, a 20-minute wok lunch.

steps.text: Separate the noodles gently, microwaving for 30 seconds if they are stiff.
Stir-fry the chicken in the oil in a hot wok for 4 minutes, until cooked through to 75°C. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Push to one side, scramble the eggs in the gap, then add the gai lan stems for 1 minute.
Add the noodles, sauces and sugar and toss for 3 minutes, until some noodles catch and char, adding the leaves for the last minute.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C. Cool and refrigerate leftovers within an hour; reheat until steaming hot.
Contains egg, soy and gluten.

title: Mie Goreng (Indonesian Sweet Soy Prawn Noodles)
summary: Egg noodles wok-tossed with prawns, egg and cabbage in sweet kecap manis with a kick of sambal.

steps.text: Cook the noodles per the packet until tender, drain and toss with a little oil.
Stir-fry the shallot and garlic in the oil for 1 minute, add the prawns for 2 minutes until pink and opaque, then push aside.
Scramble the eggs in the gap, then add the cabbage for 2 minutes.
Add the noodles, kecap manis, soy sauce and sambal and toss for 3 minutes. Top with fried shallots.

notes: Food safety: prawns must be pink and opaque throughout. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and eat within a day; for a packed lunch use an ice pack, eat within 4 hours and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains crustacean, egg, gluten and soy.

title: Singapore Noodles (Curried Vermicelli with Prawn and Egg)
summary: Thin rice vermicelli stir-fried with curry powder, prawns, egg, capsicum and bean sprouts, light and fragrant.

steps.text: Soak the vermicelli in boiling water for 4 minutes, drain and snip into shorter lengths.
Scramble the eggs in half the oil for 1 minute and remove.
Stir-fry the prawns for 2 minutes until pink and opaque, add the capsicum and curry powder for 2 minutes.
Add the noodles, soy sauce, sesame oil, egg, sprouts and spring onion and toss for 2 minutes.

notes: Food safety: prawns must be pink and opaque right through. Cool and refrigerate leftovers within an hour; for a packed lunch use an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
Contains crustacean, egg and soy.

title: Peynirli Ispanakli Pide (Turkish Spinach and Feta Flatbread)
summary: A boat-shaped flatbread baked with spinach, feta and an egg in the middle, a bakery lunch from Turkey.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 230°C (210°C fan). Cut the base in half and roll each piece into an oval, pinching the long edges up to make a rim.
Soften the spinach and onion in the oil in a pan for 3 minutes until the spinach wilts, then cool slightly and mix with the crumbled feta.
Fill the boats and bake for 10 minutes, until the edges are golden.
Crack an egg into the middle of each, sprinkle with chilli and bake for 3 more minutes, until the white is set.

notes: Food safety: the egg white must be set right through. Keeps 2 days in the fridge; reheat until steaming hot.
Contains egg, milk and gluten.

title: Pork Souvlaki Pitas (with Tzatziki)
summary: Lemon and oregano pork skewers pan-seared and wrapped in warm pita with tzatziki, tomato and onion.

steps.text: Toss the pork with the oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano and 1 tsp salt.
Thread onto skewers or leave loose and cook in a hot pan for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through to 70°C with no pink inside.
Warm the pitas, spread with tzatziki and fill with the pork, tomato and onion.

notes: Food safety: pork must be cooked through with no pink. Cool leftovers within an hour; for a packed lunch pack the meat chilled with an ice pack, eat within 4 hours and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk and gluten.

title: Greek Chicken Gyro Pitas (with Red Onion)
summary: Oregano and lemon chicken thigh seared until charred, tucked into warm pita with tzatziki, tomato and red onion.

steps.text: Toss the chicken with the oil, lemon juice, oregano, paprika, garlic and 1 tsp salt.
Cook in a hot frying pan in two batches for 6 minutes each, until charred in places and cooked through to 75°C.
Warm the pitas and fill with tzatziki, chicken, tomato and onion.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour; for a packed lunch use an ice pack, eat within 4 hours and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk and gluten.

title: Spiced Lamb and Hummus Bowl (with Pita)
summary: Cumin-spiced lamb mince over a swirl of hummus with cucumber, tomato and parsley, scooped up with warm pita.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil over high heat for 8 minutes, breaking it up, with the spices and salt, until cooked through to 75°C.
Spread the hummus in four bowls and top with the lamb.
Add the cucumber, tomato and parsley and serve with the warmed pita.

notes: Food safety: lamb mince must reach 75°C with no pink. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot; for a packed lunch keep the lamb and hummus below 5°C with an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
Contains gluten and sesame.

title: Tuna Nicoise Bowl (with Potato and Green Beans)
summary: Tinned tuna, boiled egg, potato, beans and olives with a mustard dressing, a lunch bowl that holds up in a lunchbox.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes for 12 minutes, adding the beans for the last 3 minutes, until the potatoes are tender. Drain.
Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool in cold water, peel and halve.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice and mustard with salt and pepper.
Arrange the potatoes, beans, tuna, tomato, olives and eggs in two boxes and pour over the dressing.

notes: Food safety: tuna, egg and potatoes must stay below 5°C. For a packed lunch use an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
Contains egg and fish.

title: Quinoa and Chickpea Lunch Bowl (with Feta)
summary: Fluffy quinoa, chickpeas, cucumber, tomato and feta in a lemon dressing that keeps well in the fridge.

steps.text: Rinse the quinoa, simmer in the water for 15 minutes, until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender, then cool.
Toss with the chickpeas, cucumber, tomato, feta and parsley.
Dress with the oil, lemon juice and salt and pepper.

notes: Keeps 3 days in a sealed container in the fridge. For a packed lunch use an ice pack.
Contains milk.

title: Caprese Panini (with Pesto)
summary: Pressed crusty bread with melting mozzarella, ripe tomato, basil and a spoon of pesto, crisp outside and gooey inside.

steps.text: Spread the pesto on both cut sides of the bread, then layer the mozzarella, tomato and basil on the base. Season and close.
Brush the outsides with the oil.
Press in a hot pan or sandwich press for 4 minutes each side, until golden and the cheese has melted.

notes: Pesto is traditionally made with a hard cheese; check the label if you need it vegetarian.
Contains milk, gluten and nuts.

title: Piadina Romagnola (with Prosciutto, Mozzarella and Rocket)
summary: A warm Italian flatbread folded around prosciutto, creamy mozzarella and peppery rocket, ready in 10 minutes.

steps.text: Warm each flatbread in a dry pan for 1 minute each side, until soft with a few brown spots.
Cover half of each with the mozzarella and warm for 1 minute until it just softens.
Add the prosciutto and rocket, drizzle with oil and fold over.

notes: Food safety: prosciutto and mozzarella should stay below 5°C until use. For a packed lunch use an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Dal Tadka (with Ghee and Basmati Rice)
summary: Creamy red lentils finished with a sizzling ghee, cumin and garlic tempering, served over basmati rice.

steps.text: Simmer the lentils, water, turmeric, onion, tomato and 1 tsp salt for 20 minutes, until the lentils break down into a thick soup.
Cook the rice per the packet until tender, about 12 minutes.
Heat the ghee in a small pan, fry the cumin seeds and garlic for 1 minute until golden, add the chilli flakes and pour the tempering sizzling over the dal.
Serve the dal over the rice.

notes: Food safety: cool leftover rice within an hour; reheat once until steaming hot. The dal keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes well.
Contains milk (ghee).

title: Paneer Kathi Rolls (with Mint Chutney)
summary: Spiced paneer, capsicum and onion rolled in warm flour tortillas with a smear of mint chutney, a Kolkata street classic.

steps.text: Fry the paneer in the oil over medium-high heat for 4 minutes, until golden on all sides.
Add the capsicum, onion and garam masala and cook for 4 minutes, until the vegetables soften. Squeeze over the lemon and season.
Warm the tortillas, spread with the chutney, fill with the paneer mixture and roll tightly.

notes: Keeps 1 day in the fridge wrapped in foil. For a packed lunch use an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
Contains milk and gluten.

title: Vada Pav (Mumbai Spiced Potato Fritter in a Bread Roll)
summary: A garlicky spiced potato fritter in a soft bread roll with mint chutney, Mumbai's favourite hand-held lunch.

steps.text: Boil the potato for 15 minutes until tender, drain and mash roughly.
Fry the mustard seeds, curry leaves, garlic, chilli and turmeric in the first oil for 1 minute, then mix into the potato with 1 tsp salt. Shape into 8 patties.
Whisk the chickpea flour, water and a pinch of salt into a thick batter. Dip the patties and shallow fry in the second oil for 3 minutes each side, until deep golden.
Split the rolls, spread with chutney and fill with two fritters each.

notes: Best eaten hot. The potato mixture keeps 2 days in the fridge.
Contains gluten.

title: Lemon Rice (South Indian, with Peanuts and Curry Leaves)
summary: Turmeric-gold rice with a zesty lemon kick, crunchy peanuts and mustard seeds, a lunchbox favourite that eats well cold.

steps.text: Cook the rice per the packet until tender, about 12 minutes, then spread out to cool for 10 minutes.
Heat the oil, add the mustard seeds until they pop, then the curry leaves, peanuts and chilli for 2 minutes, until the peanuts are golden.
Stir in the turmeric, then toss through the rice with the lemon juice and 1 tsp salt.

notes: Food safety: rice must be cooled within an hour and kept below 5°C; eat within a day. For a packed lunch use an ice pack.
Contains peanuts.

title: Curd Rice (South Indian Yoghurt Rice with Cucumber)
summary: Cooling rice stirred with yoghurt, tempered with mustard seeds and curry leaves, with cucumber and pomegranate on top.

steps.text: Cook the rice in plenty of water for 15 minutes until very soft, drain and mash lightly. Cool for 10 minutes.
Stir through the yoghurt, milk and 1/2 tsp salt.
Heat the oil, add the mustard seeds until they pop, then the curry leaves and ginger for 30 seconds and pour over the rice.
Top with the cucumber and pomegranate.

notes: Contains milk.
Food safety: cool the rice within an hour and keep below 5°C. For a packed lunch use an ice pack, eat within 4 hours and do not reheat. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Egg Bhurji on Buttered Toast (Indian Spiced Scrambled Eggs)
summary: Soft scrambled eggs cooked with onion, tomato, chilli and turmeric, served on buttery toast in under 15 minutes.

steps.text: Soften the onion, chilli and tomato in half the butter for 4 minutes, until soft. Stir in the turmeric.
Add the beaten eggs and stir gently for 2 minutes, until just set but still creamy.
Toast and butter the bread until golden, then spoon the eggs on top. Sprinkle with coriander.

notes: Contains egg, milk and gluten.

Food safety: the eggs should be cooked until set, with no runny parts. Eat straight away. Use fresh, uncracked eggs; for pregnant women, older people, young children and anyone with low immunity, cook the eggs until the yolks are firm.

title: Jamaican Beef Patties (Flaky Spiced Pastry Pockets)
summary: Flaky pastry pockets of curried, thyme-scented beef with a little scotch bonnet heat, perfect for the lunchbox.

steps.text: Brown the beef with the onion for 8 minutes, add the garlic, curry powder, thyme, allspice and scotch bonnet and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the water and breadcrumbs and simmer for 5 minutes, until thick. Season and cool completely.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cut each pastry sheet into 3 rectangles, fill one half with the beef, fold over and crimp the edges with a fork.
Brush with the egg and bake for 20 minutes, until puffed and deep golden.

notes: Food safety: the beef must reach 75°C before it is cooled and filled, and the baked patties must be steaming hot in the middle. Cool within an hour; they keep 3 days in the fridge, and for a packed lunch use an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
Contains egg and gluten.

title: Cuban Picadillo Bowl (with Rice, Olives and Raisins)
summary: Savoury-sweet beef simmered with tomato, olives and raisins, served over rice, a make-ahead lunch that reheats well.

steps.text: Cook the onion and capsicum in the oil for 5 minutes, add the beef and brown for 8 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains.
Stir in the garlic, spices, tomatoes, olives and raisins and simmer for 15 minutes, until thick and the beef reaches 75°C.
Meanwhile cook the rice per the packet until tender.
Serve the picadillo over the rice.

notes: Food safety: beef mince must reach 75°C. Cool within an hour; keeps 3 days in the fridge and freezes well. Reheat until steaming hot.
For a packed lunch use an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.

title: Meatball Subs (with Marinara and Melted Mozzarella)
summary: Tender beef meatballs in tangy marinara, piled into toasted rolls and grilled under melted mozzarella.

steps.text: Mix the mince, breadcrumbs, egg, garlic, oregano and 1 tsp salt and roll into 16 balls. Bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 12 minutes, until browned.
Simmer the meatballs in the marinara for 10 minutes, until they reach 75°C in the centre.
Split the rolls, fill with meatballs and sauce, top with the cheese and grill for 3 minutes, until bubbling.

notes: Food safety: meatballs must reach 75°C with no pink. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains egg, milk and gluten.

title: Steak Sandwich (with Caramelised Onion and Rocket)
summary: Seared sirloin sliced over sweet onions, mustard mayo and rocket in a toasted crusty roll, a pub-style lunch.

steps.text: Cook the onion in half the oil over medium heat for 15 minutes, until soft and caramelised. Remove.
Season the steak and sear in the remaining oil for 3 minutes each side for medium, until browned with a core of 60°C. Rest for 5 minutes and slice thinly.
Toast the bread until crisp, spread with the mayonnaise and mustard and fill with the onions, steak and rocket.

notes: Food safety: whole steaks may be eaten medium once seared on the outside. For a packed lunch keep chilled with an ice pack and eat within 4 hours; cook the steak through if serving to anyone vulnerable.
Contains egg and gluten.

title: Chicken Club Sandwich (with Bacon and Tomato)
summary: A triple-decker of seared chicken, crisp bacon, tomato and lettuce with mayonnaise, a diner classic.

steps.text: Season the chicken and sear in the oil for 6 minutes each side, until cooked through to 75°C. Rest, then slice.
Cook the bacon in a dry pan for 6 minutes, until crisp.
Toast the bread until golden and spread with mayonnaise. Layer chicken, lettuce and tomato on two slices, add a second slice, then the bacon and the remaining slices.
Secure with picks, halve and serve.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C and bacon must be cooked right through. For a packed lunch keep chilled with an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
Contains egg and gluten.

title: Open Prawn Smorrebrod (on Rye with Dill and Egg)
summary: Buttered rye topped with cooked prawns, egg, cucumber and dill mayonnaise, a Danish open sandwich.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes until hard, cool in cold water, peel and slice.
Mix the mayonnaise with half the dill and a squeeze of lemon.
