Butter the rye, layer on the cucumber, egg and prawns until generously covered, and spoon over the mayonnaise. Finish with the remaining dill and lemon.

notes: Food safety: cooked prawns and egg must stay below 5°C; use within a day of cooking and eat within 4 hours at room temperature. For a packed lunch pack separately with an ice pack.
Contains crustacean, egg, milk and gluten.

title: Sloppy Joes (with Capsicum on Toasted Buns)
summary: Saucy, sweet-tangy beef mince with capsicum piled into toasted burger buns, a quick American lunch.

steps.text: Brown the beef with the onion and capsicum for 10 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains.
Add the garlic, paste, tomato sauce, Worcestershire, sugar, mustard and 1/4 cup water and simmer for 8 minutes, until thick and the beef reaches 75°C.
Toast the buns until golden and pile on the filling.

notes: Food safety: beef mince must reach 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour; for a packed lunch pack the filling in an insulated container, eat within 4 hours, or reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten, fish (Worcestershire) and milk may be in buns.

title: Omurice (Japanese Chicken Fried Rice in a Soft Omelette)
summary: Ketchup-flavoured chicken fried rice wrapped in a soft, silky omelette, a Japanese comfort lunch.

steps.text: Cook the rice per the packet until tender, about 12 minutes.

Fry the chicken and onion in the oil for 6 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through to 75°C. Add the peas, rice and tomato sauce and stir-fry for 3 minutes, until the rice is evenly coloured and hot.
Beat the eggs with salt. Cook half in half the butter in a non-stick pan over medium-low heat for 2 minutes, until just set with a soft top.
Spoon half the rice onto the omelette, fold over and slide onto a plate. Repeat for the second serve.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C and the egg must be set, not raw. Eat straight away; refrigerate leftover rice within an hour.
Contains egg and milk.

title: Chicken Yaki Udon (with Cabbage and Mushroom)
summary: Thick, chewy udon stir-fried with chicken, cabbage and mushrooms in a savoury soy and mirin glaze.

steps.text: Cook the udon per the packet until tender and drain.
Stir-fry the chicken in half the oil for 5 minutes, until cooked through to 75°C. Remove.
Stir-fry the cabbage, mushroom and carrot in the remaining oil for 3 minutes, until just tender.
Add the noodles, chicken, soy sauce and mirin and toss for 2 minutes, until glossy and hot. Finish with the sesame oil.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour; for a packed lunch use an ice pack, eat within 4 hours and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten, soy and sesame.

title: Cold Sesame Chicken Noodles (with Cucumber)
summary: Chilled wheat noodles with poached chicken, cucumber and a creamy tahini and soy dressing, a no-reheat packed lunch.

steps.text: Poach the chicken in simmering water for 12 minutes, until it reaches 75°C and no pink remains. Cool, then shred.
Cook the noodles per the packet until tender, rinse under cold water and drain well.
Whisk the tahini, soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, sugar and warm water until smooth.
Toss the noodles with the dressing, cucumber and chicken and top with spring onion.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C, then be chilled within an hour and kept below 5°C. For a packed lunch use an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
Contains gluten, soy and sesame.

title: Peanut Noodle Bowl (with Crispy Tofu)
summary: Rice noodles in a lime and chilli peanut sauce with golden tofu, carrot and cucumber, good warm or cold.

steps.text: Soak or cook the noodles per the packet until tender, then drain and rinse.
Fry the tofu in the oil for 8 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp on all sides.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice, sriracha and 1/4 cup warm water until smooth and pourable.
Toss the noodles with the sauce, carrot and cucumber, top with the tofu and coriander.

notes: Keeps 2 days in the fridge; add the tofu on the day. Check the soy sauce label if avoiding gluten.
Contains peanuts and soy.

title: Zha Jiang Mian (Beijing Pork and Bean Sauce Noodles)
summary: Chewy noodles under a thick, savoury pork and bean sauce with cool cucumber, a Beijing home lunch.

steps.text: Brown the pork in the oil for 8 minutes, until no pink remains, with the garlic and ginger.
Stir in the doubanjiang, hoisin, soy sauce, sugar and water and simmer for 8 minutes, until thick and glossy and the pork reaches 75°C.
Cook the noodles per the packet until tender and drain.
Serve the noodles topped with the sauce, cucumber and spring onion.

notes: Food safety: pork mince must reach 75°C with no pink. The sauce keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat until steaming hot. For a packed lunch use an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
Contains gluten and soy.

title: Chicken Chow Mein (with Cabbage and Carrot)
summary: Egg noodles stir-fried with chicken, cabbage, carrot and capsicum in a savoury soy and oyster sauce.

steps.text: Cook the noodles per the packet until just tender, drain and toss with a little oil.
Stir-fry the chicken in half the oil over high heat for 5 minutes, until cooked through to 75°C. Remove.
Stir-fry the cabbage, carrot and capsicum in the rest of the oil for 3 minutes.
Return the chicken, add the noodles, soy sauce, oyster sauce and sesame oil and toss for 2 minutes, until hot.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour; for a packed lunch use an ice pack, eat within 4 hours and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains egg, gluten, soy and shellfish (oyster sauce).

title: Chicken Katsu Don (Crumbed Chicken and Egg Rice Bowl)
summary: Crisp panko chicken simmered briefly in sweet soy broth and egg, served over steaming rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice per the packet until tender, about 12 minutes.
Coat the chicken in flour, the single beaten egg, then panko. Shallow fry in the oil for 4 minutes each side, until golden and cooked through to 75°C. Slice.
Simmer the onion with the stock, soy sauce, mirin and sugar for 4 minutes, until soft.
Lay the chicken in the pan, pour over the two beaten eggs, cover and cook for 2 minutes, until just set. Slide over the rice.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C and the egg must be set. Best eaten straight away; refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Contains egg, gluten and soy.

title: Italian Sub (with Salami, Ham and Mozzarella)
summary: Salami, ham and mozzarella with crisp lettuce and an oregano and vinegar dressing in a crusty roll.

steps.text: Whisk the oil, vinegar and oregano and brush over the cut sides of the bread.
Layer the ham, salami and cheese on the base, then the tomato, onion and lettuce, piling until generously full.
Close, press firmly and cut in half.

notes: Food safety: cured meats and cheese should stay below 5°C. For a packed lunch use an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Chicken Parmigiana Rolls (with Marinara)
summary: Crumbed chicken breast under tomato sauce and melted mozzarella in a toasted roll.

steps.text: Coat the cutlets in flour, egg, then panko.
Shallow fry in the oil for 4 minutes each side, until golden and cooked through to 75°C.
Top with the marinara and cheese and grill for 3 minutes, until the cheese bubbles.
Toast the rolls until crisp and fill with the cutlets.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains egg, milk and gluten.

title: Chilli Dogs (with Beef and Bean Sauce)
summary: Frankfurts in soft buns under a quick smoky beef and bean chilli, an American lunch counter favourite.

steps.text: Brown the beef and onion for 8 minutes until no pink remains, then add the spices and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and beans and simmer for 12 minutes, until thick and the beef reaches 75°C.
Heat the frankfurts in simmering water for 5 minutes, until steaming hot in the middle.
Fill the buns with the frankfurts, chilli and mustard.

notes: Food safety: beef mince must reach 75°C and the frankfurts must be steaming hot. Refrigerate leftover chilli within an hour; it keeps 3 days and freezes well.
Contains gluten.

title: Smoked Salmon and Cream Cheese Rye Sandwiches
summary: Dark rye with whipped cream cheese, smoked salmon, cucumber and capers, a quick no-cook lunch.

steps.text: Mix the cream cheese with the dill and a squeeze of lemon.
Spread over the rye until the bread is fully covered.
Lay the salmon, cucumber and capers over two slices, season with pepper and top with the other slices.

notes: Food safety: smoked salmon is ready to eat but should be avoided by anyone pregnant or immunocompromised. Keep below 5°C; for a packed lunch use an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
Contains fish, milk and gluten.

title: Prawn and Corn Quesadillas (with Lime)
summary: Juicy prawns, sweet corn and capsicum under melted cheese in a crisp tortilla, finished with lime and coriander.

steps.text: Cook the prawns, corn, capsicum and cumin in half the oil for 4 minutes, until the prawns are pink and opaque.
Spread over half of each tortilla, add the cheese and coriander and fold over.
Cook in the remaining oil for 3 minutes each side, until golden and the cheese has melted. Serve with lime.

notes: Contains crustacean, gluten and milk.

Food safety: prawns must be pink and opaque right through. Eat hot; for a packed lunch use an ice pack, eat within 4 hours and reheat until steaming. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Tacos de Chorizo y Papa (Chorizo and Potato Tacos)
summary: Crumbled chorizo fried with golden potato and spooned into warm corn tortillas with salsa and coriander.

steps.text: Boil the potato for 8 minutes until almost tender and drain.
Fry the chorizo in a dry pan for 5 minutes until the fat runs and it is crisp, then add the onion and potato and cook for 8 minutes, until golden.
Warm the tortillas and fill with the mixture, salsa and coriander.

notes: Food safety: chorizo should be cooked until sizzling and hot all the way through. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Check the chorizo label for gluten.

title: Roasted Cauliflower Tacos (with Lime Yoghurt)
summary: Spiced roasted cauliflower in corn tortillas with avocado, red cabbage and a cooling lime yoghurt.

steps.text: Toss the cauliflower with the oil, paprika, cumin and salt and roast at 220°C (200°C fan) for 25 minutes, turning once, until charred and tender.
Stir the lime juice into the yoghurt with a pinch of salt.
Warm the tortillas and fill with cauliflower, avocado and cabbage, then drizzle with the yoghurt.

notes: Keeps 2 days in the fridge; assemble just before eating.
Contains milk.

title: Carne Asada Tacos (with Onion and Coriander)
summary: Lime and garlic skirt steak seared fast and chopped into warm corn tortillas with onion, coriander and salsa.

steps.text: Rub the steak with the lime juice, garlic, cumin, oil and 1 tsp salt.
Sear in a very hot pan for 3 minutes each side for medium, until charred with a centre of 60°C. Rest for 5 minutes, then chop finely.
Warm the tortillas and fill with the steak, onion, coriander and salsa.

notes: Food safety: whole steak is safe medium once seared on the outside; cook through for anyone vulnerable. For a packed lunch keep with an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
No dairy or gluten in the ingredients.

title: Sweetcorn Fritters (with Avocado and Lime)
summary: Golden corn and spring onion fritters topped with smashed avocado, a brunch-cafe lunch ready in 20 minutes.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder, eggs, milk and a pinch of salt into a thick batter. Stir through the corn and spring onion.
Fry spoonfuls in the oil in batches for 2 minutes each side, until golden and cooked through in the middle.
Smash the avocado with the lime juice and salt and spoon over the fritters.

notes: Food safety: fritters must be cooked through with no raw batter. Keep 2 days in the fridge and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains egg, gluten and milk.

title: Hoisin Chicken Bao Buns (with Cucumber)
summary: Steamed bao filled with sticky hoisin chicken, cucumber, spring onion and a little coriander.

steps.text: Stir-fry the chicken in the oil over high heat for 6 minutes, until cooked through to 75°C. Add the hoisin and soy sauce and toss for 1 minute, until sticky.
Steam the buns for 8 minutes, until soft and puffed.
Open the buns and fill with the chicken, cucumber, spring onion and coriander.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C. Refrigerate leftover chicken within an hour and reheat until steaming hot; steam leftover buns until hot all the way through.
Contains gluten and soy.

title: Chicken Rice Paper Rolls (with Peanut Dipping Sauce)
summary: Fresh rolls of shredded chicken, vermicelli and herbs in rice paper with a creamy peanut hoisin dip.

steps.text: Soak the vermicelli in boiling water for 4 minutes until soft, then drain and rinse.
Dip a rice paper in warm water for 10 seconds, lay it flat and layer lettuce, noodles, chicken, carrot, cucumber and herbs on the lower third.
Fold in the sides and roll up firmly until the roll is tight. Repeat for 12 rolls.
Whisk the peanut butter, hoisin, lime juice and 3 tbsp warm water until smooth, for dipping.

notes: Food safety: use chicken that was cooked through to 75°C and chilled within an hour. Fresh rolls are best eaten within 4 hours; for a packed lunch keep with an ice pack and cover with a damp cloth.
Contains peanuts and soy; check the hoisin label for gluten.

title: Arepa Reina Pepiada (Venezuelan Chicken and Avocado Arepa)
summary: Griddled cornmeal cakes split and stuffed with a creamy chicken, avocado and lime filling.

steps.text: Stir the cornmeal, water and salt into a soft dough and rest it for 5 minutes, then shape into 4 thick discs.
Cook the discs in the oil in a frying pan over medium heat for 6 minutes each side, until golden with a hollow sound when tapped.
Mix the chicken, avocado, mayonnaise, lime juice, coriander and spring onion, and season.
Split the arepas, fill with the chicken mixture and eat warm.

notes: Food safety: cook or buy the chicken ready-cooked and keep it chilled until steaming hot and no longer pink in the middle (poultry and mince to 75°C, pork to 70°C). For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C or with an ice pack, and eat within 3 days from the fridge (reheat until steaming hot, once only). Keep the filling separate from the arepas and eat within 24 hours.
Contains egg (mayonnaise).

title: Arepas con Caraotas y Queso (Venezuelan Black Bean and Cheese Arepas)
summary: Crisp cornmeal cakes filled with seasoned black beans and melted mozzarella.

steps.text: Mix the cornmeal, water and salt into a dough, rest 5 minutes and shape into 4 discs.
Cook in half the oil in a frying pan over medium heat for 6 minutes each side until golden.
Soften the onion and garlic in the remaining oil for 4 minutes, add the beans and cumin and mash lightly while heating through for 5 minutes.
Split the arepas, fill with the beans and mozzarella and serve warm.

notes: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat the filling until steaming hot.
Contains milk.

title: Pupusas de Queso y Frijoles (Salvadoran Bean and Cheese Pupusas)
summary: Thick griddled corn cakes stuffed with refried beans and melted cheese, served with a quick cabbage slaw.

items.raw: 200g canned black beans, drained and mashed

steps.text: Mix the cornmeal, water and salt to a soft dough and divide into 4 balls.
Press a hollow into each ball, fill with the mashed beans and mozzarella, close and flatten to 1cm thick discs.
Cook in the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat for 4 minutes each side until blistered and golden.
Toss the cabbage, carrot, vinegar and oregano with a pinch of salt and serve with the pupusas.

notes: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat in a dry pan.
Contains milk.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Gozleme with Spinach and Feta (Turkish Filled Flatbread)
summary: Thin hand-rolled flatbread folded around spinach, feta and herbs, griddled until blistered.

steps.text: Knead the flour, water, salt and oil into a smooth dough for 5 minutes, then divide into 4 balls.
Wilt the spinach in a hot pan for 2 minutes, squeeze out the water and mix with the feta and spring onion.
Roll each ball very thin, spoon the filling over half, fold over and seal the edges so none can leak.
Cook in a dry pan over medium heat for 3 minutes each side until blistered and golden, brush with the butter and serve with lemon.

notes: Keeps 2 days in the fridge; reheat in a dry pan.
Contains gluten and milk.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Gozleme with Spiced Lamb (Turkish Mince Flatbread)
summary: Rolled flatbread filled with cumin-spiced lamb mince, onion and parsley.

steps.text: Knead the flour, water, salt and half the oil into a dough and divide into 4 balls.
Brown the lamb with the onion, garlic, cumin and paprika for 8 minutes until cooked through (75°C) and dry, then stir in the parsley and cool slightly.
Roll the dough very thin, fill half of each, fold and seal.
Cook in a dry pan over medium heat for 3 minutes each side until blistered and golden, and serve with lemon.

notes: Food safety: cook lamb mince until steaming hot and no longer pink in the middle (poultry and mince to 75°C, pork to 70°C). For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C or with an ice pack, and eat within 3 days from the fridge (reheat until steaming hot, once only).  Cool the filling quickly if making ahead.
Contains gluten.

title: Gozleme with Potato and Herbs (Turkish Vegan Flatbread)
summary: A vegan filling of mashed potato, onion and chilli flakes in a thin griddled flatbread.

steps.text: Knead the flour, water, salt and 1 tbsp oil into a dough and divide into 4 balls.
Boil the potato for 12 minutes, drain and mash with the onion softened in a little oil, chilli, parsley and salt.
Roll the dough thin, fill half of each, fold and seal.
Cook in a dry pan over medium heat for 3 minutes each side until blistered and golden, and serve with lemon.

notes: Keeps 2 days in the fridge.
Contains gluten.

title: Katsu Sando (Japanese Pork Cutlet Sandwich)
summary: A panko-crumbed pork cutlet with tangy tonkatsu sauce and shredded cabbage in soft white bread.

steps.text: Flatten the pork thin, season, then dust with flour, dip in egg and press into the panko.
Shallow-fry in the oil over medium-high heat for 3 to 4 minutes each side until golden and cooked through, then drain and rest 2 minutes.
Mix the mayonnaise into the cabbage and spread the bread with the tonkatsu sauce.
Fill with the cutlets and cabbage, trim the crusts and halve.

notes: Food safety: cook pork to 70°C until the juices run clear and no pink remains until steaming hot and no longer pink in the middle (poultry and mince to 75°C, pork to 70°C). For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C or with an ice pack, and eat within 3 days from the fridge (reheat until steaming hot, once only).  Best eaten the same day; if packed, keep below 5C for no more than 4 hours.
Contains gluten and egg.

title: Ebi Katsu Sando (Japanese Prawn Cutlet Sandwich)
summary: Crumbed prawn cutlets with lemony mayonnaise and cabbage in soft white bread.

steps.text: Flatten the prawns lightly and form into two patties, dust with flour, dip in egg and coat with panko.
Shallow-fry in the oil over medium-high heat for 3 minutes each side until golden and opaque.
Mix the mayonnaise and lemon juice and toss with the cabbage.
Fill the bread with the cutlets and cabbage and halve.

notes: Food safety: cook prawns until pink and opaque all the way through until steaming hot and no longer pink in the middle (poultry and mince to 75°C, pork to 70°C). For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C or with an ice pack, and eat within 3 days from the fridge (reheat until steaming hot, once only).  Eat within 4 hours if packed, with an ice pack; do not reheat seafood more than once.
Contains gluten, egg and crustacean shellfish.

title: Chicken Tikka Roti Wrap (with Mint Yoghurt)
summary: Spiced chicken pieces rolled in warm roti with onion, cucumber and mint yoghurt.

steps.text: Toss the chicken with the garam masala, 1 tbsp yoghurt and a pinch of salt.
Cook in the oil in a hot pan for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.
Mix the remaining yoghurt with the mint and lemon juice.
Warm the roti, spread with the yoghurt, add chicken, onion and cucumber, and roll.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75C with no pink in the middle until steaming hot and no longer pink in the middle (poultry and mince to 75°C, pork to 70°C). For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C or with an ice pack, and eat within 3 days from the fridge (reheat until steaming hot, once only).
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Egg Roti Wrap (Malaysian-Style Roti Telur)
summary: A soft roti wrapped around a spiced onion omelette with chilli sauce.

steps.text: Beat the eggs with the onion, chilli, turmeric and salt.
Cook half the mixture in the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat, 3 minutes, until set, and repeat.
Warm the roti, lay an omelette on each pair, add chilli sauce and cucumber.
Roll tightly, tucking in the ends, and serve warm or halved.

notes: Food safety: cook the omelettes until fully set with no runny egg until steaming hot and no longer pink in the middle (poultry and mince to 75°C, pork to 70°C). For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C or with an ice pack, and eat within 3 days from the fridge (reheat until steaming hot, once only).  Eat the same day; if packed, keep chilled and eat within 4 hours.
Contains gluten and egg.

title: Tofu Banh Mi (Vietnamese Lemongrass Tofu Baguette)
summary: Crisp lemongrass tofu in a baguette with quick-pickled carrot, cucumber and coriander.

steps.text: Press the tofu dry and marinate in the soy sauce and lemongrass while you pickle.
Toss the carrot with the vinegar, sugar and a pinch of salt.
Fry the tofu in the oil over medium-high heat for 4 minutes each side until golden.
Split the baguettes, fill with tofu, pickled carrot, cucumber, chilli and coriander.

notes: Pickled carrot keeps 5 days in the fridge.
Contains gluten and soy.

title: Tofu and Mango Rice Paper Rolls (Vegan)
summary: Fresh rolls of baked tofu, mango, herbs and crunchy vegetables with a lime and chilli dip.

steps.text: Pat the tofu dry and season with a little of the soy sauce.
Soften one wrapper at a time in warm water for 10 seconds and layer lettuce, tofu, mango, carrot, cucumber and coriander.
Fold in the sides and roll tightly until each roll holds its shape.
Stir the remaining soy sauce with the lime juice, chilli and sugar for dipping.

notes: Eat within 24 hours; keep covered and chilled.
Contains soy.

title: Salmon Avocado Rice Paper Rolls
summary: Hot-smoked style flaked salmon with avocado and cucumber in fresh rice paper rolls.

steps.text: Season the salmon and bake at 200C for 10 minutes until opaque and flaking; cool and flake.
Soften one wrapper at a time in warm water and layer lettuce, salmon, avocado, cucumber and carrot.
Roll tightly, tucking in the sides.
Mix the soy sauce, lime juice and sesame oil with the sesame seeds for dipping.

notes: Food safety: cook salmon until opaque and flaking all the way through until steaming hot and no longer pink in the middle (poultry and mince to 75°C, pork to 70°C). For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C or with an ice pack, and eat within 3 days from the fridge (reheat until steaming hot, once only). Chill within 1 hour and eat within 24 hours; keep below 5C.
Contains fish, soy and sesame.

title: Tofu Poke Bowl (Vegan Soy-Sesame Tofu on Rice)
summary: Marinated tofu cubes over sushi rice with edamame, cucumber, avocado and pickled ginger.

steps.text: Rinse the rice and simmer with 1.5 cups water, covered, for 12 minutes until the water is absorbed, then season with a pinch of salt.
Toss the tofu with the soy sauce, sesame oil and vinegar while the rice cooks.
Boil the edamame for 3 minutes and drain.
Divide the rice into bowls and top with tofu, edamame, cucumber, avocado, ginger, sesame and spring onion.

notes: Keeps 2 days in the fridge.
Contains soy and sesame.

title: Chicken Poke-Style Bowl (Teriyaki, Cucumber and Pineapple)
summary: Teriyaki chicken strips on rice with pineapple, cucumber, edamame and sesame mayo.

steps.text: Simmer the rice with 1.5 cups water, covered, for 12 minutes until tender.
Fry the chicken in the oil over medium-high heat for 7 minutes until cooked through (75°C), add the teriyaki sauce and toss for 1 minute until glazed.
Mix the mayonnaise and sesame oil.
Serve the rice topped with chicken, pineapple, cucumber, edamame, sesame mayo and sesame seeds.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken until cooked through, no pink at the centre until steaming hot and no longer pink in the middle (poultry and mince to 75°C, pork to 70°C). For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C or with an ice pack, and eat within 3 days from the fridge (reheat until steaming hot, once only). Pack rice and chicken chilled within 1 hour; eat within 3 days.
Contains egg, soy and sesame.

title: Vegan Burrito Bowl (Sweet Potato and Black Bean)
summary: Roasted sweet potato, spiced black beans and rice with corn salsa and avocado.

steps.text: Roast the sweet potato with the paprika and oil at 220C for 25 minutes until tender and caramelised.
Cook the rice in 2 cups water for 12 minutes and warm the beans with the cumin.
Mix the corn, tomato, onion, lime juice and coriander into a salsa.
Build bowls with rice, sweet potato, beans, salsa and avocado.

notes: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; add the avocado fresh.
Check labels on canned goods for gluten.

title: Greek Chicken Meal Prep Bowl (with Rice and Tzatziki)
summary: Oregano and lemon chicken with rice, cucumber, tomato and tzatziki, packed for the week.

steps.text: Toss the chicken with the oil, oregano, lemon juice, garlic and salt, then roast at 200C for 22 minutes until cooked through (75°C); rest and slice.
Cook the rice in 3 cups water for 12 minutes.
Grate half the cucumber into the yoghurt with the dill and a pinch of salt.
Pack the rice, chicken, tomato, remaining cucumber, onion and tzatziki into 4 containers.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75C throughout until steaming hot and no longer pink in the middle (poultry and mince to 75°C, pork to 70°C). For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C or with an ice pack, and eat within 3 days from the fridge (reheat until steaming hot, once only).  Cool within 1 hour, refrigerate below 5C and eat within 3 days; cool rice quickly and reheat once until steaming hot.
Contains milk.

title: Beef Taco Meal Prep Bowls (with Rice and Corn)
summary: Spiced beef mince over rice with beans, corn and salsa, divided into containers.

steps.text: Cook the rice in 3 cups water for 12 minutes.
Brown the onion in the oil, add the mince and seasoning and cook for 10 minutes until browned all through (75°C).
Mix the tomato, corn, lime juice and coriander for a salsa.
Divide the rice, beef, beans and salsa into 4 containers.

notes: Food safety: cook mince until browned and no pink remains until steaming hot and no longer pink in the middle (poultry and mince to 75°C, pork to 70°C). For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C or with an ice pack, and eat within 3 days from the fridge (reheat until steaming hot, once only).  Cool within 1 hour and eat within 3 days; reheat until steaming hot.
Check the taco seasoning label for gluten.

title: Chickpea Tikka Masala Meal Prep Boxes
summary: A creamy tomato chickpea curry with rice and spinach, packed for four lunches.

steps.text: Soften the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes, add the garam masala and paprika and fry for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and chickpeas and simmer for 12 minutes, then stir in the cream and spinach.
Cook the rice in 3 cups water for 12 minutes.
Simmer the curry until thick, then divide the rice and curry into 4 containers and top with coriander.

notes: Cool quickly and refrigerate within 1 hour; eat within 3 days and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk.

title: Egg and Veg Muffin Cups (High-Protein Meal Prep)
summary: Baked egg cups with spinach, capsicum and feta, ready for grab-and-go lunches.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180C and grease a 12-hole muffin tin with the oil.
Whisk the eggs, milk and salt, then stir in the spinach, capsicum, spring onion and feta.
Pour into the holes and bake 20 to 22 minutes until set in the middle.
Cool and pack three per lunch.

notes: Food safety: cook the egg cups until set in the centre until steaming hot and no longer pink in the middle (poultry and mince to 75°C, pork to 70°C). For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C or with an ice pack, and eat within 3 days from the fridge (reheat until steaming hot, once only). Cool within 1 hour and refrigerate; eat within 3 days and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains egg and milk.

title: Teriyaki Chicken Meal Prep Boxes (with Broccoli and Rice)
summary: Glazed chicken thigh with steamed broccoli and rice, a simple weekday lunch.

steps.text: Cook the rice in 3 cups water for 12 minutes.
Brown the chicken in the oil for 8 minutes until cooked through (75°C), add the teriyaki sauce and cook 2 minutes until glossy.
Steam the broccoli for 4 minutes.
Divide into 4 containers and finish with sesame seeds and spring onion.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken until no pink remains until steaming hot and no longer pink in the middle (poultry and mince to 75°C, pork to 70°C). For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C or with an ice pack, and eat within 3 days from the fridge (reheat until steaming hot, once only).  Cool within 1 hour, keep below 5C and eat within 3 days; reheat until steaming hot.
Contains soy and sesame.

title: Lentil Bolognese Meal Prep Boxes (Vegan)
summary: Rich brown lentil and mushroom ragu over wholemeal pasta, made to be batch-cooked.

steps.text: Soften the onion, carrot and mushroom in the oil for 8 minutes with the garlic.
Add the lentils, passata, stock and oregano and simmer for 25 minutes until the lentils are tender.
Boil the pasta until al dente and drain.
Divide into 4 containers and top with the lentil sauce.

notes: Cool within 1 hour and eat within 4 days; freezes well.
Contains gluten.

title: Tuna and White Bean Meal Prep Boxes
summary: Canned tuna with white beans, tomato, red onion and a lemon dressing over baby leaves.

items.raw: 425g canned tuna in olive oil, drained

steps.text: Mix the beans, tomato and onion in a bowl until evenly combined.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice, oregano and salt and stir through.
Fold in the tuna in large flakes and the parsley.
Pack into 4 containers over rocket, adding the leaves when ready to eat.

notes: Food safety: cook canned tuna only from a freshly opened can until steaming hot and no longer pink in the middle (poultry and mince to 75°C, pork to 70°C). For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C or with an ice pack, and eat within 3 days from the fridge (reheat until steaming hot, once only).  Keep below 5C and eat within 2 days; do not leave out for more than 2 hours.
Contains fish.

title: Chickpea Smash Sandwich (Vegan)
summary: Mashed chickpeas with lemon, mustard and herbs piled into toasted bread with crisp lettuce and tomato.

steps.text: Mash the chickpeas roughly with the tahini, lemon juice, mustard, parsley, spring onion and salt until chunky but holding together.
Toast the bread until golden.
Pile the chickpea mix onto 2 slices and top with tomato and lettuce.
Top with the other 2 slices and halve.

notes: Filling keeps 3 days in the fridge; assemble just before eating.
Contains gluten, sesame and mustard.

title: Tofu Scramble Wrap (Vegan)
summary: Turmeric and black salt style tofu scramble with capsicum and spinach in a warm tortilla.

steps.text: Fry the capsicum in the oil for 3 minutes, then add the tofu, turmeric, cumin and soy sauce.
Cook for 6 minutes, stirring, until the tofu is dry and golden at the edges.
Stir in the spinach and nutritional yeast until the leaves wilt.
Warm the tortillas, fill with the scramble and avocado and roll.

notes: Eat within 2 days; keep the avocado separate.
Contains gluten and soy.

title: Cottage Cheese Egg Wraps (High-Protein)
summary: A thin egg and cottage cheese wrap with ham, spinach and mustard for a quick high-protein lunch.

steps.text: Blend the eggs and cottage cheese smooth with a pinch of salt.
Cook half the mixture in the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat for 3 minutes until set, flip for 30 seconds, and repeat.
Spread each wrap with mustard and fill with ham, spinach and tomato.
Roll up tightly, tucking in the ends so the filling stays put, and halve to serve.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites and yolks are fully set. For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C and eat within 24 hours.
Contains egg and milk.

title: Spinach and Ricotta Hand Pies
summary: Golden puff pastry parcels filled with spinach, ricotta, lemon and nutmeg.

items.raw: 250g frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200C and cut each pastry sheet into 4 squares.
Mix the spinach, ricotta, half the egg, lemon zest, nutmeg, spring onion and salt.
Spoon onto half of each square, fold over and crimp the edges, then brush with the remaining beaten egg.
Bake for 20 to 22 minutes until deep golden and puffed.

notes: Food safety: bake until the filling is steaming hot in the centre. For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C and eat within 24 hours.
Contains gluten, egg and milk. Check the pastry label for vegetarian suitability.

title: Potato and Pea Samosa Pasties
summary: Baked pasty parcels of curried potato and peas in puff pastry.

steps.text: Boil the potato for 10 minutes until just tender and drain.
Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add the garam masala and cumin, then fold in the potato, peas and lemon juice and mash lightly.
Cut the pastry into 4 large rounds, fill with the mixture, fold, crimp and brush with beaten egg.
Bake at 200C for 25 minutes until golden.

notes: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten and egg. Check the pastry label for vegetarian suitability.

title: Empanadas de Queso (Argentine Cheese Empanadas)
summary: Baked half-moon pastries of melted mozzarella and a little onion, crisp outside and oozy inside.

steps.text: Cut the pastry into 8 rounds about 12cm across.
Mix the mozzarella, onion, spring onion and oregano and spoon onto each round.
Fold over, press and crimp the edges, then brush with the beaten egg.
Bake at 200C for 18 to 20 minutes until golden and the cheese bubbles.

notes: Best warm; reheat until steaming hot. Keeps 2 days in the fridge.
Contains gluten, egg and milk.

title: Manakish Jibneh (Lebanese Cheese Flatbread)
summary: Soft baked flatbreads topped with melted mozzarella and a sprinkle of za'atar.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the water and 1 tbsp oil and knead for 6 minutes into a smooth dough, then cover and leave 40 minutes until doubled.
Divide into 4, roll into 15cm discs and press dimples in with your fingers.
Top with mozzarella and bake at 230C for 10 to 12 minutes until bubbling and golden.
Brush with the remaining oil, scatter with za'atar and serve with tomato.

notes: Eat the same day or reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Shakshuka Pita Pockets
summary: Spiced tomato and capsicum with soft-set eggs tucked into warm pita.

steps.text: Soften the onion and capsicum in the oil for 6 minutes, then add the garlic, cumin and paprika for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and simmer for 8 minutes until thick.
Crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 4 minutes until the whites are fully set and the yolks are firm.
Split the pitas, spoon in the shakshuka and scatter with parsley.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites and yolks are fully set. For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C and eat within 24 hours.
Contains gluten and egg.

title: Egg Foo Young (Chinese Omelette with Prawns)
summary: Fluffy omelettes of egg, beansprouts and prawns with a simple soy gravy, served with rice.

steps.text: Simmer the rice with 1 cup water, covered, for 12 minutes until tender. Beat the eggs with the prawns, beansprouts, spring onion and a pinch of salt.
Cook two ladlefuls in the oil in a hot pan for 2 minutes each side until golden and set through.
Simmer the soy sauce, stock and cornflour mixed with a splash of water for 2 minutes until glossy.
Serve the omelettes over the rice with the gravy.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites and yolks are fully set. For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C and eat within 24 hours. Use pre-cooked prawns only if bought chilled and used by their date.
Contains egg, crustacean shellfish and soy.

title: Rice and Bean Burritos (Budget Lunch)
summary: Rice, black beans, corn and a little cheese rolled in flour tortillas, a filling lunch for a few dollars.

steps.text: Simmer the rice with 2 cups water, covered, for 12 minutes until tender.
Warm the beans, corn, cumin and paprika for 5 minutes, mashing some beans.
Warm the tortillas and fill with rice, beans, cheese, tomato and lime juice.
Fold in the ends and roll tightly.

notes: Wrap in foil to freeze for up to 2 months; reheat until steaming hot. Cheddar here is not suitable for vegetarians unless labelled vegetarian hard cheese.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Lentil Dal Rice Bowl (Budget Lunch)
summary: A thick red lentil dal with turmeric and cumin over rice, topped with yoghurt and coriander.

steps.text: Soften the onion, garlic and ginger in the oil for 5 minutes, then stir in the cumin and turmeric.
Add the lentils and water and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring, until soft and thick.
Simmer the rice with 2 cups water, covered, for 12 minutes until tender.
Serve the dal on the rice with yoghurt and coriander.

notes: Cool within 1 hour; keeps 3 days in the fridge and freezes well. Reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk.

title: Ploughman's Sandwich (with Vegetarian Hard Cheese and Pickle)
summary: Crusty bread with sharp vegetarian hard cheese, chutney, apple and lettuce.

steps.text: Butter the bread and spread two slices with chutney.
Layer the cheese, apple, lettuce and pickled onion on top.
Close with the remaining slices, press down until the filling holds together and halve.

notes: Eat the same day; if packed, keep chilled below 5C.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Porchetta Panino (Italian Roast Pork Roll)
summary: Herb-rubbed roast pork sliced into a crusty roll with salsa verde and rocket.

steps.text: Rub the pork with the garlic, fennel, rosemary, oil and salt and roast at 180C for 1 hour until the middle reaches 70°C and it is tender; rest 10 minutes and slice.
Chop the capers and mix with the parsley, second portion of oil and lemon juice for salsa verde.
Split the rolls and layer the pork, salsa verde and rocket.
Close the rolls and press gently with the heel of your hand until the pork sits snugly, then halve.

notes: Food safety: cook pork to 70°C in the thickest part until steaming hot and no longer pink in the middle (poultry and mince to 75°C, pork to 70°C). For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C or with an ice pack, and eat within 3 days from the fridge (reheat until steaming hot, once only). Slice and chill within 1 hour; eat within 3 days.
Contains gluten.

title: Bauru (Brazilian Roast Beef and Cheese Sandwich)
summary: Warm sliced roast beef with melted mozzarella, tomato and pickles in a split roll.

steps.text: Split the rolls and butter the cut sides.
Layer the beef, mozzarella, tomato and pickles and sprinkle with oregano.
Bake at 200C for 8 minutes until the cheese melts and the beef is steaming hot.
Close the rolls, press down gently and halve for serving while still hot.

notes: Food safety: cook roast beef that was chilled promptly after cooking until steaming hot and no longer pink in the middle (poultry and mince to 75°C, pork to 70°C). For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C or with an ice pack, and eat within 3 days from the fridge (reheat until steaming hot, once only). The filling should be steaming hot before eating.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Bun Cha Gio Bowl (Vietnamese Spring Roll Noodle Bowl)
summary: Crisp baked pork spring rolls over vermicelli with herbs, cucumber and nuoc cham.

steps.text: Mix the pork, carrot, spring onion, garlic and a pinch of salt, roll in the wrappers and brush with oil.
Bake at 200C for 20 minutes, turning once, until golden and cooked through (75°C).
Soak the vermicelli in boiling water for 4 minutes, then drain and rinse.
Stir the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar and chilli with 3 tbsp water and serve over the noodles, cucumber, mint and rolls.

notes: Food safety: cook pork mince rolls to 75°C in the centre until steaming hot and no longer pink in the middle (poultry and mince to 75°C, pork to 70°C). For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C or with an ice pack, and eat within 3 days from the fridge (reheat until steaming hot, once only). Eat the same day; if packed, keep sauce separate.
Contains gluten, fish and sugar.

title: Turkey and Vegetable Rice Bowls
summary: Lean turkey mince stir-fried with carrot, zucchini and ginger over rice, a high-protein prep lunch.

steps.text: Simmer the rice with 3 cups water, covered, for 12 minutes until tender.
Brown the turkey in the oil for 8 minutes until cooked through (75°C), then add the carrot, zucchini, ginger and garlic for 4 minutes.
Stir in the soy sauce and sesame oil until the sauce coats the mince.
Divide into 4 boxes over the rice and top with spring onion.

notes: Food safety: cook turkey mince to 75°C with no pink until steaming hot and no longer pink in the middle (poultry and mince to 75°C, pork to 70°C). For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C or with an ice pack, and eat within 3 days from the fridge (reheat until steaming hot, once only). Cool within 1 hour, keep below 5C and eat within 3 days; reheat until steaming hot.
Contains soy and sesame.

title: Tofu Katsu Sando (Vegan)
summary: Panko-crumbed tofu with tangy sauce and cabbage in soft white bread.

steps.text: Press the tofu dry and season. Mix the flour with the soy milk into a thick batter.
Dip the tofu in the batter, then press into the panko.
Shallow-fry in the oil over medium-high heat for 3 minutes each side until crisp and golden.
Toss the cabbage with the lemon juice and a pinch of salt, spread the bread with the tomato paste mixed with a splash of soy sauce, fill and halve.

notes: Eat the same day for best crunch.
Contains gluten and soy.

title: Pad Kra Pao Chicken Rice Bowl with Fried Egg
summary: Chilli-basil chicken mince stir-fry over rice with a crisp-edged fried egg.

steps.text: Simmer the rice in 1.5 cups water, covered, for 12 minutes until tender. Fry the garlic and chilli in the oil for 30 seconds, then add the chicken and cook for 6 minutes until cooked through (75°C).
Add the soy sauce, oyster sauce and sugar and cook 1 minute, then stir in the basil until wilted.
Fry the eggs in a little oil until the whites are set and edges crisp.
Serve the chicken over the rice with an egg on top.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken mince to 75°C until steaming hot and no longer pink in the middle (poultry and mince to 75°C, pork to 70°C). For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C or with an ice pack, and eat within 3 days from the fridge (reheat until steaming hot, once only). Cook the egg until the white is fully set; eat the same day.
Contains egg, soy, shellfish (oyster sauce) and gluten.

title: Stuffed Baked Sweet Potato with Black Beans (Vegan)
summary: Baked sweet potatoes filled with spiced black beans, corn salsa and avocado.

steps.text: Prick the sweet potatoes and bake at 200C for 45 to 50 minutes until soft when squeezed.
Warm the beans with the cumin and paprika for 5 minutes, mashing some.
Mix the corn, tomato, lime juice and coriander.
Split the potatoes, fill with the beans, salsa and avocado.

notes: Keeps 3 days in the fridge without the avocado.
Check labels on canned goods for gluten.

title: Bean Burger with Avocado (Vegan)
summary: Smoky black bean and oat patties in a bun with avocado, tomato and lettuce.

steps.text: Mash the beans with the oats, paprika, cumin, tomato paste and salt until they hold together, then shape into 2 patties.
Fry in the oil over medium heat for 5 minutes each side until crisp and heated through.
Toast the buns cut side down in a dry pan for 1 to 2 minutes until golden.
Build with the patties, avocado, tomato and lettuce.

notes: Patties keep 3 days in the fridge or freeze for 2 months.
Contains gluten.

title: Egg Bhurji Pav (Indian Spiced Scrambled Egg Bun)
summary: Mumbai-style scrambled eggs with onion, tomato and green chilli, served with buttered rolls.

steps.text: Soften the onion and chilli in the oil for 4 minutes, then add the tomato and turmeric and cook 3 minutes until pulpy.
Pour in the beaten eggs and stir for 2 to 3 minutes until fully set.
Stir through the garam masala and coriander.
Toast the split rolls in the butter until golden and serve with the bhurji.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites and yolks are fully set. For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C and eat within 24 hours.
Contains gluten, egg and milk.

title: Bulgogi Beef Lettuce Wraps (High-Protein)
summary: Sweet soy beef strips with ginger in crisp lettuce cups with rice and kimchi.

steps.text: Toss the beef with the soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, ginger and garlic.
Sear in the oil in a very hot pan for 3 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Simmer the rice in 1 cup water, covered, for 12 minutes until tender, then spoon it and the beef into the lettuce leaves.
Top with kimchi and spring onion.

notes: Food safety: cook beef strips until browned all through with no pink until steaming hot and no longer pink in the middle (poultry and mince to 75°C, pork to 70°C). For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C or with an ice pack, and eat within 3 days from the fridge (reheat until steaming hot, once only). Eat within 3 days if packed, keeping the lettuce separate.
Contains soy and sesame.

title: Beef Kofta Flatbread Wrap
summary: Spiced beef kofta in warm flatbread with tomato, onion and a garlic yoghurt sauce.

steps.text: Mix the beef, onion, half the garlic, cumin, coriander, parsley and salt and shape into 8 finger-shaped koftas.
Fry in the oil over medium-high heat for 8 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through (75°C).
Stir the remaining garlic and the lemon juice into the yoghurt.
Warm the flatbreads, spread with the yoghurt, add koftas and tomato and roll.

notes: Food safety: cook beef kofta to 75°C with no pink until steaming hot and no longer pink in the middle (poultry and mince to 75°C, pork to 70°C). For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C or with an ice pack, and eat within 3 days from the fridge (reheat until steaming hot, once only). Eat within 3 days if chilled promptly; reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Roast Pumpkin and Chickpea Wrap (Vegan)
summary: Cumin-roasted pumpkin and chickpeas with tahini sauce and rocket in a tortilla.

steps.text: Roast the pumpkin and chickpeas with the oil, cumin and paprika at 210C for 25 minutes until the pumpkin is tender and the edges are crisp.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice and water into a pourable sauce.
Warm the tortillas and spread with the tahini sauce.
Fill with the roast mix and rocket and roll tightly until sealed.

notes: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; pack the rocket separately.
Contains gluten and sesame.

title: Egg and Chorizo Torta (Mexican Sandwich)
summary: Scrambled egg with spiced chorizo, refried-style black beans and avocado in a toasted roll.

items.raw: 200g canned black beans, drained and mashed

steps.text: Fry the chorizo in the oil for 4 minutes until crisp and cooked through, then pour in the beaten eggs.
Stir for 2 to 3 minutes until the egg is fully set.
Warm the mashed beans in a small pan for 3 minutes until hot.
Split the rolls and toast them in a dry pan until golden, then fill with the beans, egg mix, avocado, tomato and lime juice.

notes: Food safety: cook chorizo until the fat runs and no pink remains until steaming hot and no longer pink in the middle (poultry and mince to 75°C, pork to 70°C). For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C or with an ice pack, and eat within 3 days from the fridge (reheat until steaming hot, once only).  Cook the egg until fully set; eat the same day or chill within 1 hour and keep below 5C for 24 hours.
Contains gluten and egg.

title: Tuna Salad Wrap with Avocado
summary: Flaked tuna, avocado, cucumber and lemon yoghurt in a wholemeal tortilla.

steps.text: Mix the tuna, avocado, yoghurt, lemon juice, cucumber and spring onion until just combined.
Warm the tortillas briefly so they fold without cracking.
Pile the spinach and tuna mix down the centre.
Fold in the sides and roll up tightly.

notes: Food safety: cook canned tuna only from a freshly opened can until steaming hot and no longer pink in the middle (poultry and mince to 75°C, pork to 70°C). For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C or with an ice pack, and eat within 3 days from the fridge (reheat until steaming hot, once only). Keep below 5C and eat within 24 hours if packed; discard if left out for over 2 hours.
Contains fish, gluten and milk.

title: Fish Finger Sandwich
summary: Crisp baked fish fingers with tartare sauce and lettuce in buttered white bread.

items.raw: 300g firm white fish fillet, cut into 6 fingers

steps.text: Dust the fish in flour, dip in egg and press into the panko, then place on a tray brushed with the oil.
Bake at 220C for 15 to 18 minutes, turning once, until golden and the fish flakes easily (63°C).
Mix the mayonnaise, gherkin and lemon juice.
Butter the bread, fill with lettuce, fish fingers and tartare sauce and cut in half.

notes: Food safety: cook fish to 63°C until opaque and flaking until steaming hot and no longer pink in the middle (poultry and mince to 75°C, pork to 70°C). For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C or with an ice pack, and eat within 3 days from the fridge (reheat until steaming hot, once only). Eat the same day; chill within 1 hour if packing and keep below 5C.
Contains fish, gluten and egg.

title: Veggie Pad Thai Box
summary: Rice noodles stir-fried with egg, tofu and vegetables in a tamarind sauce, topped with peanuts.

steps.text: Soak the noodles in hot water for 8 minutes until pliable and drain.
Fry the tofu in the oil for 5 minutes until golden, push aside and scramble in the eggs until fully set.
Add the carrot, noodles, soy sauce, tamarind and sugar and toss for 3 minutes until the noodles are tender and coated.
Fold in the beansprouts and spring onion and top with peanuts and lime.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites and yolks are fully set. For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C and eat within 24 hours.
Contains egg, peanuts and soy.

title: Hoisin Tofu Rice Paper Rolls
summary: Glazed tofu, crunchy vegetables and herbs in fresh rice paper rolls with a lime dip.

steps.text: Fry the tofu in the oil with the hoisin for 6 minutes until sticky and golden.
Soften one wrapper at a time in warm water and layer lettuce, tofu, carrot, cucumber and mint.
Roll up tightly, tucking in the sides, until each roll is firm.
Stir the soy sauce, lime juice and sugar for dipping.

notes: Eat within 24 hours; keep covered and chilled.
Contains soy and sulphites; check the hoisin label for gluten.

title: Chickpea Frittata Wedges (Vegan, Besan)
summary: An egg-free frittata of chickpea flour, spinach and onion baked until set, great cold.

steps.text: Whisk the besan, water, cumin, turmeric and salt into a smooth batter.
Soften the onion in the oil in an ovenproof pan for 4 minutes, add the spinach and tomato until wilted.
Pour in the batter and scatter the coriander, then bake at 200C for 20 minutes until set and golden.
Cool slightly and cut into wedges.

notes: Keeps 4 days in the fridge and can be eaten cold.
Contains no gluten ingredients; check the besan label.

title: Paneer Bhurji Wrap
summary: Crumbled paneer scrambled with onion, tomato and spices, rolled in a warm roti.

steps.text: Soften the onion and chilli in the oil for 5 minutes, then add the cumin and turmeric.
Add the tomato and cook for 3 minutes until pulpy, then stir in the paneer and garam masala for 3 minutes until heated through.
Stir through the coriander.
Warm the roti, spread with the yoghurt, add the bhurji and roll.

notes: Keeps 2 days in the fridge; reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Aloo Tikki Burger
summary: Spiced potato patties pan-fried until crisp and served in a bun with mint yoghurt and onion.

steps.text: Boil the potato for 12 minutes until tender, drain and mash with the peas, cumin, garam masala, chilli, coriander, flour and salt.
Shape into 2 thick patties.
Fry in the oil over medium heat for 5 minutes each side until golden and crisp.
Mix the yoghurt and mint, then fill the buns with patties, yoghurt and onion.

notes: Patties keep 3 days in the fridge; reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Egg Curry Wrap
summary: Hard-boiled eggs in a spiced tomato masala, rolled in a roti with cucumber.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes until hard-set, cool in cold water and peel.
Soften the onion, garlic and ginger in the oil for 6 minutes, add the spices, then the tomatoes and simmer 8 minutes until thick.
Halve the eggs and warm them in the sauce for 2 minutes.
Fill the roti with the egg curry, cucumber and coriander and roll.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites and yolks are fully set. For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C and eat within 24 hours.
Contains gluten and egg.

title: Kale and Bean Quesadilla
summary: Crisp tortillas of white beans, kale and cheese, cooked in a pan until melted.

steps.text: Wilt the kale and garlic in the oil for 3 minutes until soft, then mash in the beans and cumin.
Spread over 2 tortillas, scatter the mozzarella and top with the remaining tortillas.
Cook in a dry pan over medium heat for 3 minutes each side until golden and the cheese has melted.
Cut into wedges and serve with salsa.

notes: Best eaten warm; keeps 2 days in the fridge.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Chicken Banh Mi Rolls
summary: Pulled chicken with pickled carrot, cucumber, coriander and chilli mayo in a crisp roll.

steps.text: Toss the carrot with the vinegar, sugar and a pinch of salt for the pickle.
Mix the mayonnaise and sriracha.
Split the baguettes and spread with the chilli mayo.
Fill with chicken, pickled carrot, cucumber, coriander and chilli until generously packed, then press the roll closed.

notes: Food safety: cook use chicken cooked to 75°C and chilled promptly until steaming hot and no longer pink in the middle (poultry and mince to 75°C, pork to 70°C). For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C or with an ice pack, and eat within 3 days from the fridge (reheat until steaming hot, once only). Keep below 5C and eat within 4 hours if packed, or within 24 hours with an ice pack.
Contains gluten and egg.

title: Tuna Onigiri Bento (with Cucumber and Egg)
summary: Rice balls with tuna mayo and nori, a rolled egg and cucumber, packed in a lunch box.

steps.text: Simmer the rice with 1.5 cups water, covered, for 12 minutes until tender, then stir through the vinegar and cool.
Mix the tuna with the mayonnaise and shape the rice around spoonfuls of it into 4 balls, wrapping each in nori.
Beat the eggs with the soy sauce and cook in the oil in a small pan for 3 minutes until fully set, then roll and slice.
Pack the onigiri, egg and cucumber into a lunch box.

notes: Food safety: cook canned tuna only from a freshly opened can until steaming hot and no longer pink in the middle (poultry and mince to 75°C, pork to 70°C). For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C or with an ice pack, and eat within 3 days from the fridge (reheat until steaming hot, once only). Cook the egg until fully set; keep the box below 5C and eat within 24 hours. Cool rice within 1 hour.
Contains fish, egg and soy.

title: Smoky Tofu Rice Bowl (Budget Lunch)
summary: Paprika-roasted tofu on rice with sweetcorn and shredded cabbage, for very little money.

steps.text: Toss the tofu with the oil, paprika and soy sauce and roast at 220C for 25 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp at the edges.
Simmer the rice with 1 cup water, covered, for 12 minutes until tender.
Warm the corn in a pan for 3 minutes.
Serve the rice topped with tofu, corn, cabbage, lime juice and spring onion.

notes: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat until steaming hot.
Contains soy.

title: Egg and Potato Curry Roll (Budget Lunch)
summary: Soft roti rolled around a mild potato and egg curry with peas.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes until hard-set, cool and peel.
Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add the curry powder, then the potato, tomatoes and 1/2 cup water and simmer for 15 minutes until the potato is tender.
Add the peas and halved eggs and heat for 3 minutes.
Fill the roti with the curry and coriander and roll.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites and yolks are fully set. For packed lunches chill within 1 hour, keep below 5C and eat within 24 hours.
Contains gluten and egg.

title: Shake Shioyaki Teishoku (Japanese Salted Grilled Salmon Set Lunch)
summary: Salted grilled salmon with rice, grated radish and a quick cucumber pickle, set out like a Japanese lunch counter.

steps.text: Rinse the rice, then cook it with 300ml water in a lidded pot for 12 minutes and rest it covered.
Salt the salmon on both sides and leave for 10 minutes while you pickle the cucumber with the vinegar and a pinch of salt.
Grill the fillets skin side up under a hot grill for 5 to 6 minutes until the skin blisters and the flesh flakes.
Serve the fish on plates with rice, a mound of grated daikon dressed with the soy sauce, the pickle and a lemon wedge.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, and keep raw fish below 5°C until it goes under the grill.
Contains fish and soy.

title: Buta no Shogayaki Teishoku (Ginger Pork Set Lunch)
summary: Thin pork slices in a sweet, sharp ginger and soy glaze, served with rice and shredded cabbage.

steps.text: Stir the soy sauce, mirin, ginger and sugar together.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over high heat and fry the pork for 2 to 3 minutes until just browned.
Pour in the sauce and toss for 1 minute until glossy and the pork is cooked through.
Check the pork is cooked through with no pink and reaches 70°C, then serve over the warm rice with the raw cabbage alongside.

notes: Food safety: pork must be cooked through with no pink, and raw pork should be kept below 5°C until cooking.
Contains soy.

title: Tamagoyaki Teishoku (Rolled Omelette Set Lunch)
summary: A soft, lightly sweet rolled omelette with rice, spinach and pickled cucumber for a quiet vegetarian set lunch.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs with the soy sauce, mirin and sugar.
Wilt the spinach in a pan with a splash of water for 1 minute, squeeze dry and toss with the sesame seeds.
Oil a small non-stick pan over medium heat, pour in a third of the egg and roll it up as it sets, pushing it to one side.
Add more egg in two more rounds, rolling each time, until the omelette is set and golden, then slice into thick pieces.
Serve with the rice, spinach and the cucumber tossed in the vinegar.

notes: Food safety: cook the omelette until set throughout and don't serve it runny to young children or older adults.
Contains egg, soy and sesame.

title: Chicken Nanban (Japanese Fried Chicken with Tartare Sauce)
summary: Crisp chicken thigh dipped in a sweet-sour vinegar glaze, then spooned over with an egg tartare sauce.

items.raw: 350g boneless chicken thigh, cut into pieces

steps.text: Dust the chicken in the flour, then dip it in the beaten egg.
Shallow-fry in the oil over medium heat for 6 to 7 minutes, turning, until golden and cooked through.
Warm the soy sauce, vinegar and sugar in a small pan until the sugar dissolves, then turn the hot chicken in it.
Mix the mayonnaise, boiled egg and pickles into a tartare sauce.
Serve the chicken over the rice with the tartare sauce spooned on top.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C inside with no pink, and don't reuse the raw egg bowl for the sauce.
Contains egg, gluten and soy.

title: Hiyashi Chuka (Japanese Cold Ramen Noodle Plate)
summary: Chilled noodles under neat rows of egg, ham, cucumber and tomato, finished with a sharp soy-vinegar dressing.

steps.text: Cook the noodles until tender as the packet says, rinse under cold water and drain well.
Beat the eggs, fry them in the oil as a thin omelette until set, then slice into ribbons.
Whisk the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar and sesame oil with 2 tbsp water until the sugar dissolves.
Pile the noodles in two bowls and arrange the egg, ham, cucumber and tomato on top.
Pour over the dressing and scatter with the sesame seeds.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until set, and keep the ham and prepared plate below 5°C until you eat.
Contains gluten, egg, soy and sesame.

title: Soboro Don (Japanese Minced Chicken and Egg Rice Bowl)
summary: Sweet-salty minced chicken and fluffy scrambled egg over rice with green beans, a classic bento-style bowl.

steps.text: Simmer the chicken with the soy sauce, mirin, the first spoon of sugar and the ginger, stirring to keep it crumbly, for 6 minutes until the liquid has gone.
Beat the eggs with the second teaspoon of sugar and scramble them in a pan over low heat, stirring constantly, until small and just set.
Blanch the green beans for 3 minutes, drain and slice.
Divide the rice between two bowls and arrange the chicken, egg and beans in neat sections.

notes: Food safety: chicken mince must reach 75°C and be cooked until no pink remains; set the scrambled egg firm.
Contains egg, gluten and soy.

title: Korean Classic Kimbap with Egg and Pickled Radish
summary: Seaweed rolls of sesame rice filled with egg, carrot, spinach and pickled radish, sliced for a picnic lunch.

steps.text: Toss the warm rice with the sesame oil and the salt and let it cool a little.
Beat the eggs, fry them thinly in the vegetable oil until set and cut into long strips.
Stir-fry the carrot for 2 minutes, and wilt the spinach with a splash of water, squeezing it dry.
Spread a third of the rice over each nori sheet, leaving a gap at the top, and lay the egg, carrot, spinach and radish in a line across the middle.
Roll up tightly, brush the end with water to seal, and slice into rounds with a sharp wet knife until you have 8 per roll.

notes: Food safety: cool the rice quickly, refrigerate within 1 hour and eat within 4 hours out of the fridge, as cooked rice left warm can grow Bacillus cereus.
Contains egg and sesame.

title: Tuna Mayo Kimbap
summary: Rice and seaweed rolls filled with creamy tuna mayo, cucumber and carrot, an easy kimbap to start with.

steps.text: Mix the rice with the sesame oil and sesame seeds.
Mash the tuna with the mayonnaise.
Spread rice over each nori sheet, leaving a gap at the top, and line up the tuna, cucumber and carrot across the middle.
Roll tightly until firm, seal the edge with a dab of water and slice into rounds.

notes: Food safety: canned tuna mayo should be kept below 5°C and eaten within 4 hours out of the fridge.
Contains fish, egg and sesame.

title: Bulgogi Kimbap
summary: Sweet soy-marinated beef, cooked fast and rolled in rice and seaweed with crunchy vegetables.

steps.text: Toss the beef with the soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil and garlic and leave for 15 minutes.
Fry the beef in the vegetable oil over high heat for 3 minutes until cooked through and the liquid has reduced.
Wilt the spinach with a splash of water, squeeze dry and season with a pinch of salt.
Spread rice over each nori sheet and line up the beef, carrot, cucumber and spinach.
Roll tightly, seal with water and slice into rounds.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef through until no pink remains, and keep raw meat below 5°C until cooking.
Contains soy and sesame.

title: Korean Jajangmyeon Black Bean Noodles
summary: Thick noodles in a glossy, savoury black bean sauce with pork and vegetables, a favourite Korean lunch.

steps.text: Fry the black bean paste in the oil for 2 minutes to cook out the rawness, then stir in the pork and brown it.
Add the onion, potato and 300ml water, cover and simmer 10 minutes, then add the zucchini and sugar for 4 minutes more.
Stir the cornflour into 2 tbsp cold water, pour it in and simmer until the sauce thickens and shines.
Boil the noodles until tender as the packet says and drain well.
Pile the noodles in bowls, spoon over the sauce and top with cucumber.

notes: Food safety: pork mince must reach 75°C and be cooked until no pink remains.
Contains gluten and soy.

title: Bibim Guksu (Korean Spicy Cold Noodles)
summary: Chilled wheat noodles tossed in a sweet, hot gochujang sauce with crunchy cucumber and a boiled egg.

steps.text: Boil the noodles for 3 to 4 minutes, rinse under cold water until cool and drain very well.
Stir the gochujang, soy sauce, vinegar, sugar and sesame oil into a sauce.
Toss the noodles with the sauce and the cucumber.
Serve topped with the eggs, spring onion and sesame seeds.

notes: Food safety: boil the eggs for at least 8 minutes so they are firm, and keep the dish below 5°C if it sits.
Contains gluten, egg, soy and sesame.

title: Dakgalbi Lettuce Wraps (Korean Spicy Chicken Wraps)
summary: Sticky gochujang chicken with cabbage and sweet potato, spooned into crisp lettuce cups with rice.

steps.text: Mix the gochujang, soy sauce, honey and garlic and coat the chicken.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat, add the sweet potato and 60ml water, cover and cook 5 minutes.
Add the chicken and cabbage and cook, stirring, for 8 to 10 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce is sticky.
Spoon into lettuce leaves with a little rice.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink, and wash hands and board after handling it raw.
Contains soy.

title: Thai Omelette Rice (Khai Jiao Rice Plate)
summary: A puffed, crisp-edged Thai omelette over steamed rice with sweet chilli sauce and cucumber.

steps.text: Beat the eggs with the fish sauce and lime juice until frothy.
Heat the oil in a wok until very hot, then pour in the egg from a height so it puffs and crisps at the edges.
Cook 1 minute, flip, cook 30 seconds and lift out onto paper towel.
Serve over rice with cucumber and sweet chilli sauce.

notes: Food safety: cook the omelette until fully set, and take care with hot oil.
Contains fish (fish sauce).

title: Nasi Lemak with Ayam Goreng Berempah (Fried Chicken)
summary: Coconut rice with spiced fried chicken, sambal, cucumber, peanuts and egg for a Malaysian lunch plate.

steps.text: Rinse the rice, then cook with the coconut milk, 200ml water, bay leaf and salt in a lidded pot for 14 minutes and rest covered.
Rub the chicken with the turmeric, coriander, cumin and salt and leave 15 minutes.
Shallow-fry the chicken in 1 cm of oil over medium heat for 18 to 20 minutes, turning, until golden and cooked through.
Serve with the rice, eggs, cucumber, peanuts and sambal.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C at the bone with clear juices; cook the eggs until firm.
Contains egg and peanuts.

title: Nasi Lemak Vegetarian Plate with Crisp Tofu
summary: Fragrant coconut rice with crisp tofu, sambal, peanuts, cucumber and a fried egg.

steps.text: Cook the rinsed rice with the coconut milk, 150ml water and bay leaf in a lidded pot for 14 minutes, then rest covered.
Fry the tofu in half the oil for 3 minutes each side until crisp.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil until the whites are set.
Plate the rice with tofu, egg, cucumber, peanuts and sambal.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the white is fully set.
Contains egg, soy and peanuts.

title: Nasi Goreng Kampung (Malaysian Village Fried Rice)
summary: Smoky anchovy and chilli fried rice with greens and a fried egg, a Malaysian kampung staple.

steps.text: Fry the anchovies in 1 tbsp oil for 1 minute until crisp, then add the garlic and chilli for 30 seconds.
Add the cold rice and stir-fry over high heat for 3 minutes.
Add the greens and soy sauce and toss for 1 minute.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil until the whites are set and serve on top.

notes: Food safety: use rice cooled quickly and refrigerated within 1 hour of cooking, and cook the eggs until set.
Contains fish (anchovies), egg and soy.

title: Mee Goreng Mamak (Malaysian Spicy Fried Noodles)
summary: Yellow noodles wok-tossed with chilli paste, tofu, egg and tomato, the way the mamak stalls do it.

steps.text: Fry the tofu in the oil over high heat until golden, then push aside.
Add the chilli paste and fry for 30 seconds, then crack in the eggs and scramble until set.
Add the noodles, soy sauce and tomato sauce and toss for 3 minutes.
Add the tomato and choy sum and toss 2 minutes more.
Add the tomato and bok choy and toss 2 minutes more until the greens wilt, then serve with lime wedges.

notes: Food safety: cook the egg until set before adding the noodles.
Contains gluten, egg and soy.

title: Indian Lemon Rice Tiffin Box
summary: Tangy turmeric rice with peanuts, curry leaf and mustard seeds, packed with cucumber and yoghurt for the tiffin.

steps.text: Heat the oil, then add the mustard seeds and let them pop.
Add the peanuts, curry leaf and chilli and fry for 1 minute.
Stir in the turmeric and the rice and toss over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Add the lemon juice and salt to taste and toss until the rice is evenly coloured.
Pack with the yoghurt and cucumber in the tiffin.

notes: Food safety: cool the rice quickly and keep the tiffin in an insulated bag with an ice pack, eating within 4 hours.
Contains peanuts, milk and mustard.

title: Curd Rice Tiffin (Thayir Sadam with Pickle)
summary: Cool, creamy South Indian yoghurt rice tempered with mustard and curry leaf, packed with a spoon of pickle.

steps.text: Mash the warm rice with the yoghurt, milk and salt until soft and creamy.
Heat the oil, pop the mustard seeds, then add the curry leaf and ginger for 20 seconds.
Pour the tempering over the rice and stir in the grated carrot.
Serve at room temperature with the pickle.

notes: Food safety: keep it chilled and eat within 4 hours out of the fridge, as dairy-based rice spoils quickly in warm weather.
Contains milk and mustard.

title: Masala Dosa with Coconut Chutney Lunch Plate (Quick Batter)
summary: Crisp rice and lentil crepes folded around a turmeric potato filling and served with a quick coconut chutney.

steps.text: Fry the mustard seeds in the oil for the filling, add the onion and chilli until soft, then the turmeric and potato with a splash of water; mash lightly and season.
Blend the coconut, chilli, lemon juice and water into a chutney.
Whisk the rice flour, semolina, plain flour, 400ml water and a pinch of salt into a thin batter and rest it while you make the filling. Heat a non-stick pan and pour a ladle in a thin lacy circle.
Cook until crisp and golden underneath, spoon in the filling, fold and serve with the chutney.

notes: Contains mustard.
Ready-made dosa batter is sold chilled in Indian grocers.

title: Rava Upma Tiffin with Vegetables
summary: Soft, savoury semolina cooked with mustard seed, ginger and vegetables, a South Indian tiffin staple.

steps.text: Dry-roast the semolina in a pan for 3 to 4 minutes until it smells nutty, then set aside.
Heat the oil, pop the mustard seeds, then add the onion, ginger, curry leaf and carrot for 3 minutes.
Add the peas and the water with a teaspoon of salt and bring to the boil until bubbling.
Pour in the semolina in a steady stream, stirring, then cover and cook 2 minutes.
Finish with the lemon juice.

notes: Contains gluten and mustard.

title: Poha with Peanuts and Lemon (Maharashtrian Flattened Rice)
summary: Light, turmeric-yellow flattened rice with onion, peanuts and lemon, a quick Indian lunch box favourite.

steps.text: Rinse the poha in a sieve until just soft and drain well.
Heat the oil, pop the mustard seeds and fry the peanuts for 1 minute.
Add the onion, chilli and curry leaf for 3 minutes, then the turmeric.
Stir in the poha and salt, and cook gently 3 minutes.
Finish with lemon juice and coriander.

notes: Contains peanuts and mustard.

title: Vegetable Uttapam (South Indian Savoury Pancake)
summary: Thick, soft rice and lentil pancakes studded with onion, tomato and chilli.

steps.text: Whisk the rice flour, semolina, plain flour, water and a pinch of salt into a thick pourable batter, then rest it while you chop. Mix the onion, tomato, chilli and coriander together.
Heat a non-stick pan with a little oil and pour on a ladle of batter, spreading it only slightly so it stays thick.
Scatter a handful of the vegetables over the top and press them in.
Drizzle oil around the edge, cook 3 minutes, flip and cook 2 minutes more until golden, then serve with the chutney.

notes: Ready-made dosa batter is sold chilled in Indian grocers.

title: Besan Chilla (Chickpea Flour Pancakes)
summary: Savoury gram flour pancakes with onion, tomato and spices, served with a mint yoghurt dip.

steps.text: Whisk the chickpea flour with the water, cumin, turmeric and a pinch of salt into a smooth batter.
Stir in the onion, tomato, chilli and coriander.
Cook ladlefuls in a lightly oiled non-stick pan for 3 minutes each side until golden and set.
Stir the mint into the yoghurt and serve alongside.

notes: Contains milk.

title: Egg Kathi Roll (Calcutta Style)
summary: A beaten egg cooked onto a flaky paratha with onion, lime and chilli, rolled up as a street-style lunch.

steps.text: Toss the onion with the chilli, lime juice and garam masala.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt.
Cook a paratha in a hot pan with a little oil, pour half the egg over the top side, flip once it sets and cook until the egg is set, about 1 minute.
Spread with chutney, add the onion mix and roll up tightly in baking paper.
Repeat for the second roll.

notes: Food safety: cook the egg until set throughout.
Contains egg, gluten and milk.

title: Moroccan Chicken and Preserved Lemon Couscous Plate
summary: Spiced chicken thigh over fluffy couscous with preserved lemon, olives and parsley.

items.raw: 500g boneless chicken thigh, cut into pieces

steps.text: Toss the chicken with the cumin, turmeric, paprika and a pinch of salt.
Brown the chicken in the oil over medium-high heat, then cook, turning, until golden and cooked through, about 12 minutes.
Pour the hot stock over the couscous in a bowl, cover and leave until all the stock is absorbed, about 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Stir the preserved lemon, olives and parsley through the couscous and top with the chicken.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C inside with no pink; wash hands and boards after handling it raw.
Contains gluten.

title: Kefta Meatball Pita (Moroccan Spiced Lamb in Pita)
summary: Cumin and coriander lamb meatballs tucked into warm pita with tomato, yoghurt and mint.

steps.text: Mix the lamb with the onion, spices, parsley and a good pinch of salt, then roll into 18 small meatballs.
Fry the meatballs in the oil over medium heat, turning, until browned all over and cooked through, about 10 minutes.
Stir the mint into the yoghurt and warm the pita.
Fill each pita with meatballs, tomato and minty yoghurt.

notes: Food safety: lamb mince must reach 75°C and be cooked until no pink remains.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Lebanese Chicken Shawarma Plate with Garlic Sauce
summary: Spiced chicken thigh with garlic sauce, pickles, tomato and flatbread, in plate form.

steps.text: Coat the chicken with the spices, half the garlic, half the lemon juice and the oil, and leave for 20 minutes.
Cook in a hot frying pan in two batches until browned and cooked through, about 6 minutes each.
Stir the yoghurt, tahini, the remaining garlic and lemon juice into a sauce.
Serve the chicken with warm flatbread, tomato, pickles and the garlic sauce.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; keep raw chicken below 5°C while marinating.
Contains gluten, milk and sesame.

title: Falafel Plate with Tomato Cucumber Salad and Tahini
summary: Crisp falafel with a chopped tomato and cucumber salad, hummus, pickles and a lemony tahini sauce.

steps.text: Bake the falafel in a 200°C oven for 8 to 10 minutes until hot and crisp.
Toss the tomato, cucumber, parsley, olive oil and half the lemon juice together.
Whisk the tahini with the remaining lemon juice and 2 tbsp water until pourable.
Plate the falafel with the salad, hummus, pickles and warm pita and spoon the tahini over.

notes: Contains gluten and sesame.

title: Mujaddara Lunch Plate with Yoghurt and Cucumber
summary: Lentils and rice topped with deeply browned onions, served with cool yoghurt and cucumber.

steps.text: Simmer the lentils in plenty of water for 15 minutes until almost tender, then drain.
Fry the onions in the oil over medium heat, stirring, until deep brown and crisp at the edges, about 25 minutes.
Stir the rice, cumin, a teaspoon of salt and 350ml water into the lentils, cover and cook gently until all the water is absorbed, about 12 minutes.
Fold half the onions through and top with the rest.
Mix the yoghurt, cucumber and mint and serve alongside.

notes: Contains milk.

title: Kofta Kebab Plate with Tahini Yoghurt
summary: Herby beef and lamb kofta with a tahini yoghurt, tomato and onion salad and warm flatbread.

steps.text: Mix the mince with the grated onion, parsley, cumin, allspice and a teaspoon of salt and shape into 6 fat sausages.
Fry in the oil over medium-high heat, turning, until browned and cooked through, about 10 minutes.
Stir the yoghurt and tahini together.
Serve the kofta on flatbread with the tahini yoghurt, tomato and red onion.

notes: Food safety: minced meat must reach 75°C and be cooked until no pink remains.
Contains gluten, milk and sesame.

title: Mezze Lunch Board with Hummus, Labneh and Warm Pita
summary: A relaxed board of hummus, labneh, olives, cucumber, tomato and warm pita for a no-cook lunch.

steps.text: Warm the pita in a dry pan until soft and lightly blistered, about 30 seconds a side.
Spoon the hummus and labneh onto a board and swirl with the back of a spoon.
Drizzle the oil over both and scatter the sumac.
Arrange the olives, cucumber, tomato, feta and walnuts around the dips and serve with the pita.

notes: Contains gluten, milk, sesame and tree nuts.

title: Greek Meze Plate with Tzatziki, Feta and Roasted Capsicum
summary: Tzatziki, roasted capsicum, feta, olives and tomato with warm pita for a summer Greek lunch.

steps.text: Squeeze the water out of the grated cucumber, then mix it with the yoghurt, garlic and oil to make tzatziki.
Warm the pita in a dry pan until soft, about 30 seconds each side.
Arrange the capsicum, feta, olives and tomato on a platter.
Sprinkle the tomato and feta with oregano and serve with the tzatziki and pita.

notes: Contains gluten and milk.

title: Spanakopita Triangles Lunch Plate with Tomato and Olives
