summary: Crisp filo triangles filled with spinach and feta, served with tomato, olives and lemon.

steps.text: Squeeze the spinach very dry, then mix with the feta, ricotta, egg, spring onions and dill.
Cut each filo sheet into 3 strips, brush with butter and put a spoonful of filling at one end.
Fold the corner over to make a triangle and keep folding to the end of the strip, then brush the top with butter.
Bake in a 190°C oven for 22 to 25 minutes until deep golden and crisp.
Serve with the tomato, olives and lemon wedges.

notes: Food safety: bake the filling until piping hot, as it contains raw egg when assembled.
Contains gluten, egg and milk.

title: Turkish Meze Lunch Plate with Cacik and Sigara Boregi
summary: Cigar-shaped feta and parsley pastries with garlicky cucumber yoghurt, olives and tomato.

steps.text: Mash the feta with the parsley and egg.
Cut the filo into long triangles, put a line of filling along the wide end and roll into cigars, sealing the tip with a little water.
Brush with the oil and bake in a 200°C oven for 12 to 15 minutes until crisp and golden.
Stir the yoghurt, cucumber, garlic and mint into cacik.
Serve the boregi with the cacik, olives and tomato.

notes: Food safety: bake until the filling is hot throughout, as it includes raw egg when rolled.
Contains gluten, egg and milk.

title: Mediterranean Tuna and White Bean Lunch Board
summary: Tuna and cannellini beans with olives, tomato and rocket on a board with toasted bread.

steps.text: Toast the bread under a grill until golden, about 2 minutes a side, then rub with the cut garlic.
Toss the beans with the oil, lemon juice, capers and a pinch of salt.
Arrange the beans, tuna, olives, tomatoes and rocket on a board.
Serve with the garlic toast while it is still warm and crisp.

notes: Food safety: keep opened tinned tuna covered in the fridge and eat within 2 days.
Contains fish and gluten.

title: Smorrebrod with Roast Beef and Pickle Remoulade
summary: Thin roast beef on buttered rye with a quick pickle and caper remoulade and crisp onion.

steps.text: Stir the mayonnaise, pickles, capers, mustard and horseradish together into a remoulade.
Butter the rye slices right to the edges until each is evenly covered.
Fold the beef over the bread in loose ribbons.
Spoon the remoulade over the beef until the slices are well covered and finish with the crisp onions.

notes: Food safety: cooked sliced beef should stay below 5°C and be eaten within 2 days of opening.
Contains gluten, egg, milk and mustard.

title: Smorrebrod with Smoked Salmon and Cucumber
summary: Dark rye with horseradish cream cheese, smoked salmon, cucumber ribbons and dill.

steps.text: Beat the cream cheese with the horseradish and spread over the rye.
Toss the cucumber ribbons with the lemon juice.
Drape the salmon over the bread until each slice is covered and add the cucumber.
Finish with dill and capers.

notes: Food safety: smoked salmon is ready to eat but should be kept below 5°C and eaten within 2 days of opening; pregnant people are often advised to avoid it.
Contains gluten, fish and milk.

title: Smorrebrod with Liver Pate and Pickled Beetroot
summary: Rye topped with smooth liver pate, tangy beetroot and crisp onion, a Danish classic.

steps.text: Butter the rye slices right to the edges until evenly covered.
Spread the pate over the bread in an even layer.
Lay the beetroot slices over the pate until it is just covered, then add the pickles.
Finish with the fried onions and dill.

notes: Food safety: pate is a high-risk food for pregnancy and should be kept below 5°C; eat within 2 days of opening.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Smorrebrod with Potato, Chives and Radish
summary: Rye topped with sliced potato, mayo, radish, chives and a soft herb sprinkle, a simple vegetarian smorrebrod.

steps.text: Boil the potato slices until tender, about 12 minutes, drain and cool.
Butter the rye and spread with the mayonnaise.
Layer the potato over the bread and season with salt.
Top with radish, chives, dill and a squeeze of lemon juice.

notes: Contains gluten, egg and milk.

title: Tartine with Ricotta, Peas and Mint
summary: Crusty toast with whipped lemon ricotta, crushed peas and mint, a fresh spring open sandwich.

steps.text: Cook the peas in boiling water until tender, about 3 minutes, drain and lightly crush with the oil and mint.
Toast the bread until golden and rub with the cut garlic.
Beat the ricotta with the lemon juice and a pinch of salt until light.
Spread the ricotta on the toast and spoon over the peas until generously covered.

notes: Contains gluten and milk.

title: Tartine with Goat Cheese, Honey and Walnuts
summary: Grilled sourdough topped with creamy goat cheese, honey, thyme and walnuts, with peppery rocket.

steps.text: Spread the goat cheese on the bread and grill until the cheese is soft and lightly golden, about 4 minutes.
Toss the rocket with the oil and a pinch of salt.
Drizzle the toasts with the honey and scatter with walnuts and thyme.
Serve with the rocket on top.

notes: Contains gluten, milk and tree nuts.

title: Tartine with Avocado and Soft Egg
summary: Toasted sourdough with smashed avocado, lemon, chilli and a jammy egg.

steps.text: Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook for 6 minutes for a jammy yolk, then cool in cold water and peel.
Toast the bread until golden.
Mash the avocado with the lemon juice, olive oil and salt.
Spread the avocado on the toast, top with halved eggs and sprinkle with chilli flakes.

notes: Food safety: soft-yolk eggs are not recommended for young children, pregnant people or older adults; use eggs boiled for 8 minutes if unsure.
Contains gluten and egg.

title: Tartine with Tuna, Tomato and Olives
summary: Grilled sourdough with olive oil tuna, ripe tomato, olives and parsley.

steps.text: Toast the bread until golden and rub with the cut garlic.
Flake the tuna with the oil and lemon juice.
Layer the tomato on the toast until covered and season with salt.
Top with the tuna, olives and parsley.

notes: Food safety: keep opened tinned tuna covered in the fridge and eat within 2 days.
Contains fish and gluten.

title: Tartine with Roasted Mushrooms and Thyme
summary: Garlicky roast mushrooms and thyme piled on toasted sourdough over soft cheese.

steps.text: Toss the mushrooms with the oil, garlic, thyme and salt on a tray and roast at 220°C until browned and shrunken, about 18 minutes.
Toast the bread until golden.
Spread the toast with cream cheese until covered.
Pile on the mushrooms, drizzle with the balsamic and sprinkle with parsley.

notes: Contains gluten and milk.

title: Halloumi and Roast Vegetable Pita Plate with Hummus
summary: Golden halloumi with roast zucchini, capsicum and red onion, served with hummus and warm pita.

steps.text: Roast the zucchini, capsicum and onion with the oil and salt at 220°C until browned at the edges, about 22 minutes.
Fry the halloumi in a dry pan over medium-high heat until golden on both sides, about 2 minutes a side.
Warm the pita in a dry pan.
Serve the vegetables and halloumi with hummus, pita, lemon juice and parsley.

notes: Contains gluten, milk and sesame.

title: Harissa Chicken Flatbread with Yoghurt and Herbs
summary: Harissa-coated chicken on warm flatbread with cucumber, yoghurt and herbs.

steps.text: Coat the chicken with the harissa and oil.
Cook in a hot frying pan in two batches until browned and cooked through, about 5 minutes each.
Warm the flatbreads and spread with the yoghurt.
Top with chicken, cucumber, coriander and lemon juice.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C inside with no pink.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Baked Potato with Chilli Beef
summary: A crisp-skinned baked potato filled with spicy beef and bean chilli, soured cream and cheese.

steps.text: Prick the potatoes, rub with oil and salt and bake at 200°C until the skins are crisp and the middle is soft, about 60 minutes.
Meanwhile brown the beef and onion in a pan until the beef is no longer pink, about 6 minutes.
Add the garlic and spices for 1 minute, then the beans and tomatoes and simmer until thick, about 20 minutes.
Split the potatoes, spoon in the chilli and top with the cheese and sour cream.

notes: Food safety: beef mince must reach 75°C and be cooked until no pink remains.
Contains milk.

title: Baked Potato with Tuna and Corn
summary: Fluffy baked potato topped with tuna, sweetcorn, spring onion and a spoon of mayonnaise.

steps.text: Prick the potatoes, rub with oil and bake at 200°C until the skins are crisp and the middle is soft, about 60 minutes.
Mix the tuna with the corn, spring onion, mayonnaise and lemon juice.
Split the potatoes, fluff the insides, spoon in the filling and scatter with the cheese.

notes: Food safety: keep the tuna filling below 5°C if you make it ahead and eat within 2 days.
Contains fish, egg and milk.

title: Baked Potato with Cheesy Broccoli
summary: Baked potato stuffed with broccoli and a cheddar-style cheese sauce, an easy vegetarian lunch.

steps.text: Prick the potatoes, rub with oil and bake at 200°C until the skins are crisp and the middle is soft, about 60 minutes.
Steam the broccoli until just tender, about 4 minutes.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk and simmer until thickened, about 4 minutes.
Stir in the cheese and mustard until melted, then fold in the broccoli.
Split the potatoes and spoon the sauce over.

notes: Contains gluten and milk.

title: Twice-Baked Potatoes with Bacon and Chives
summary: Potato shells refilled with a creamy mash of cheese, bacon and chives and baked until golden.

steps.text: Prick the potatoes, rub with oil and bake at 200°C until soft inside, about 60 minutes.
Fry the bacon until crisp, about 6 minutes.
Halve the potatoes, scoop out the flesh into a bowl leaving a thin shell, and mash with the sour cream, butter, two-thirds of the cheese, bacon and chives.
Refill the shells, top with the remaining cheese and bake at 200°C until golden and bubbling, about 15 minutes.

notes: Food safety: cook bacon until well done with no pink, and eat the potatoes piping hot.
Contains milk.

title: Buckwheat Galettes with Ham, Egg and Cheese
summary: Brittany-style buckwheat crepes folded around ham, melted cheese and a runny-edged egg.

steps.text: Whisk the buckwheat flour, plain flour, egg, water, melted butter and a pinch of salt into a smooth batter and rest for 15 minutes.
Cook a thin ladle of batter in a buttered hot pan until the edges lift and the underside is crisp, about 2 minutes.
Flip, scatter with a quarter of the cheese and ham, crack an egg in the middle and cook until the white is set, about 3 minutes.
Fold the edges in to a square and serve at once; repeat for the rest.

notes: Food safety: cook the egg until the white is set and the yolk warm; use firm yolks for young children, pregnant people or older adults.
Contains gluten, egg and milk.

title: Savoury Crepes with Spinach and Ricotta
summary: Thin crepes rolled around a spinach, ricotta and lemon filling and baked in a light tomato sauce.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, eggs, milk, melted butter and a pinch of salt into a thin batter and rest for 10 minutes.
Cook 8 thin crepes in a lightly buttered pan until golden underneath, about 1 minute each side.
Squeeze the spinach dry and mix with the ricotta, lemon zest and salt.
Fill and roll the crepes, then lay them in a dish over the passata.
Top with the cheese and bake at 190°C until bubbling and golden, about 18 minutes.

notes: Contains gluten, egg and milk.

title: Dutch Pannenkoeken with Bacon and Cheese
summary: Big thin Dutch pancakes cooked with crisp bacon and melted cheese, served flat and folded.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, eggs, milk and a pinch of salt into a smooth batter.
Fry the bacon in a large non-stick pan until crisp, about 5 minutes.
Add a little butter, pour in a third of the batter and scatter with a third of the bacon.
Cook until the underside is golden, flip, add a third of the cheese and cook until it melts, about 2 minutes.
Fold and serve; repeat for the rest.

notes: Food safety: cook bacon until well done with no pink.
Contains gluten, egg and milk.

title: Okonomiyaki (Japanese Cabbage Pancakes)
summary: Thick savoury cabbage pancakes with pork belly slices, brushed with sweet sauce and mayonnaise.

steps.text: Whisk the flour and water into a batter, then fold in the cabbage, eggs and spring onions.
Heat the oil in a large non-stick pan and spoon in a third of the mixture to make a thick round.
Lay a third of the bacon over the top and cook for 5 minutes until golden underneath.
Flip and cook until the bacon is crisp and the centre is set, about 5 minutes more.
Brush with tonkatsu sauce and drizzle with mayonnaise; repeat for the rest.

notes: Food safety: cook until the centre is fully set and the bacon is well done.
Contains gluten, egg and soy.

title: Corn Fritter Stack with Avocado and Lime
summary: Golden sweetcorn fritters stacked with smashed avocado, lime and sour cream.

steps.text: Mix the flour, eggs, milk, corn, spring onions, cumin and salt into a thick batter.
Fry spoonfuls in the oil over medium heat for 3 minutes each side until golden and set through.
Mash the avocado with the lime juice and salt.
Stack the fritters with the avocado and sour cream.

notes: Food safety: cook the fritters until the centres are set and no longer wet.
Contains gluten, egg and milk.

title: Orecchiette with Broccoli and Anchovy
summary: Puglian orecchiette with soft broccoli, anchovy, garlic and chilli, a classic southern Italian lunch.

steps.text: Cook the pasta in salted water for 10 minutes, adding the broccoli for the last 5 minutes, until both are very tender.
Melt the anchovies in the oil over low heat with the garlic and chilli until the anchovy dissolves, about 3 minutes.
Toast the breadcrumbs in a dry pan until golden, about 3 minutes.
Drain the pasta and broccoli, toss in the anchovy oil, crushing the broccoli, and top with the crumbs.

notes: Contains gluten and fish.

title: Tuna Pasta with Capers and Cherry Tomatoes
summary: Quick pasta with tuna, blistered cherry tomatoes, capers and olives.

steps.text: Cook the spaghetti in salted water until al dente and drain, keeping a little water.
Fry the garlic in the oil for 30 seconds, add the tomatoes and cook until they burst and turn jammy, about 7 minutes.
Stir in the capers, olives and tuna and warm through.
Toss with the spaghetti, parsley and a splash of cooking water.

notes: Food safety: keep opened tinned tuna covered in the fridge and eat within 2 days.
Contains gluten and fish.

title: Pesto Pasta Bowl with Green Beans and Potato
summary: Trofie-style pasta tossed with basil pesto, green beans and soft potato, the Ligurian way.

items.raw: 100g green beans, cut into short lengths

steps.text: Boil the potato in salted water for 5 minutes, then add the pasta and cook until al dente, adding the beans for the last 3 minutes.
Keep a mug of the water and drain.
Toss everything with the pesto and enough water to make it creamy, then serve with the cheese.

notes: Contains gluten, milk and tree nuts (pesto).

title: Cold Sesame Soba Noodle Plate with Cucumber and Egg
summary: Chilled buckwheat noodles in a nutty sesame-soy dressing with cucumber and egg.

steps.text: Cook the soba until tender, about 5 minutes, then rinse under cold water and drain well.
Whisk the tahini, soy sauce, vinegar, sugar and sesame oil with 2 tbsp water until smooth.
Toss the noodles and cucumber in the dressing.
Top with eggs and spring onions.

notes: Food safety: boil the eggs for at least 8 minutes until firm.
Contains gluten (most soba), egg, soy and sesame.

title: Summer Platter with Poached Chicken, Fruit and Dips
summary: Cold poached chicken, sliced fruit and crunchy vegetables with two easy dips for a hot day.

steps.text: Poach the chicken with the bay leaf in simmering water until cooked through and the juices run clear, about 16 minutes, then chill.
Slice the chicken and stir the mint into the yoghurt.
Arrange the chicken, hummus, minty yoghurt, vegetables, mango and cheese on a platter.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C; chill quickly and keep the platter below 5°C, serving within 2 hours at room temperature.
Contains milk and sesame.

title: Vietnamese Cold Noodle Platter with Herbs and Pork
summary: Rice vermicelli with grilled pork, lettuce, cucumber and herbs with a sweet-sharp nuoc cham dressing.

steps.text: Toss the pork with 1 tbsp fish sauce, half the sugar and the garlic and leave 15 minutes.
Grill or pan-fry the pork over high heat until browned and cooked through, about 4 minutes.
Soak the vermicelli in boiling water until tender, about 4 minutes, rinse cold and drain.
Whisk the remaining fish sauce and sugar with the lime juice, chilli and 3 tbsp water into nuoc cham.
Arrange the noodles with the pork, salad and herbs, then dress and scatter with peanuts.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach 70°C with no pink; keep marinating pork below 5°C.
Contains fish and peanuts.

title: Prawn Cocktail Lunch Platter with Avocado
summary: Sweet prawns in a classic marie rose sauce with avocado, lettuce, egg and brown bread.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 8 minutes until firm, cool in cold water and peel.
Stir the mayonnaise, tomato sauce and lemon juice into a pink sauce.
Toss the prawns in the sauce.
Plate the lettuce, avocado, cucumber and egg with the prawns on top, and serve with the bread.

notes: Food safety: keep cooked prawns below 5°C and eat within 2 days; boil eggs until the yolk is firm.
Contains egg, gluten and shellfish.

title: Hidden Vegetable Mac and Cheese
summary: Creamy cheese sauce with blended butternut and carrot hidden inside, a kid-friendly pasta lunch.

steps.text: Boil the pumpkin and carrot until very soft, about 15 minutes, then blend with a ladle of the water until smooth.
Cook the macaroni in salted water until tender and drain.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute and whisk in the milk, simmering until thickened.
Stir in the blended vegetables, cheese and mustard until melted, then fold through the macaroni.

notes: Contains gluten and milk.

title: Crumbed Chicken Strips Lunchbox with Veggie Sticks
summary: Baked crumbed chicken strips with cucumber, carrot, cheese and a mild yoghurt dip for kids.

steps.text: Dip the chicken strips in the egg, then the breadcrumbs, and lay them on a tray brushed with the oil.
Bake at 200°C until golden and cooked through, about 16 minutes, turning once.
Stir the yoghurt with the lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Pack the strips with the vegetable sticks and dip.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C and have no pink; for a lunchbox use an insulated bag with an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
Contains gluten, egg and milk.

title: Fish Finger Wraps for Kids with Crunchy Slaw
summary: Crumbed baked white fish strips in soft wraps with a mild carrot and cabbage slaw.

items.raw: 400g white fish fillets, cut into strips

steps.text: Dip the fish in the egg, then the breadcrumbs, and lay on a tray brushed with the oil.
Bake at 200°C until golden and the fish flakes easily, about 12 minutes.
Mix the cabbage, carrot and mayonnaise into a slaw.
Fill the tortillas with the slaw and fish and roll up.

notes: Food safety: cook fish until opaque and flaking; check for bones before serving to young children.
Contains fish, gluten and egg.

title: Ham and Cheese Pinwheels for Lunchboxes
summary: Soft wraps spread with cream cheese and rolled with ham, cheese and cucumber, sliced into easy spirals.

steps.text: Spread each tortilla with cream cheese right to the edges until evenly covered.
Layer the ham, cheese, carrot and cucumber across each wrap.
Roll up tightly and chill for 20 minutes until firm.
Slice into spirals with a sharp knife.

notes: Food safety: ham should stay below 5°C; pack with an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Mini Frittata Muffins for Toddlers
summary: Soft little egg muffins with zucchini, corn and cheese, easy for small hands and good cold.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs with the milk and a pinch of salt.
Squeeze the water from the zucchini and stir into the eggs with the corn and cheese.
Pour into a 12-hole muffin tin brushed with the oil.
Bake at 180°C until puffed and set in the middle, about 16 minutes.

notes: Food safety: bake until fully set with no liquid egg; keep below 5°C and eat within 2 days.
Contains egg and milk.

title: Sweet Potato and Chickpea Toddler Patties
summary: Soft, mildly spiced patties of sweet potato and chickpea, baked and served with yoghurt.

steps.text: Boil the sweet potato until very soft, about 12 minutes, then drain.
Mash with the chickpeas and cumin until mostly smooth.
Stir in the egg and breadcrumbs, then shape into 12 patties.
Brush with the oil and bake at 200°C until golden on both sides, about 20 minutes, turning once, and serve with the yoghurt.

notes: Food safety: bake until firm and hot throughout.
Contains gluten, egg and milk.

title: Pasta Lunchbox with Corn, Cheese and Ham
summary: Cold pasta with sweetcorn, cucumber, ham and cheese in a light yoghurt dressing, built for the lunchbox.

steps.text: Cook the pasta in salted water until tender, about 10 minutes, drain and rinse under cold water until cool.
Stir the yoghurt, mayonnaise and lemon juice together.
Fold the pasta, corn, cucumber, ham and cheese through the dressing.
Pack into containers with an ice pack.

notes: Food safety: keep below 5°C, pack with an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
Contains gluten, egg and milk.

title: Apple and Ricotta Pancake Fingers
summary: Soft apple and ricotta pancakes cut into fingers, lightly sweet for a gentle kids lunch.

steps.text: Squeeze the grated apples dry and mix with the ricotta, then whisk in the eggs and milk.
Fold in the flour and baking powder until just combined.
Cook spoonfuls in the butter in a non-stick pan over medium heat until golden underneath and bubbles appear, about 3 minutes, then flip and cook 2 minutes more.
Cut into fingers and serve with the yoghurt.

notes: Food safety: cook until the middle is set with no wet batter.
Contains gluten, egg and milk.

title: Gyeran Mari (Korean Rolled Omelette Lunch Plate)
summary: Fluffy vegetable-flecked rolled omelette with rice, kimchi and spinach, a classic Korean banchan lunch.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs with the carrot, spring onions, soy sauce and a pinch of salt.
Oil a small non-stick pan over low-medium heat and pour in a thin layer of egg.
When just set but still glossy, roll it to one side, add more egg and roll again, repeating until the egg is used up and the omelette is set.
Wilt the spinach in a splash of water until soft, about 1 minute, and squeeze dry.
Slice the omelette and plate with the rice, kimchi and spinach.

notes: Contains egg and soy; kimchi often contains fish sauce.

Food safety: cook the omelette until the egg is completely set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs; for pregnant women, older people, young children and anyone with low immunity, cook the eggs until the yolks are firm.

title: Khao Kha Moo (Thai Braised Pork on Rice)
summary: Tender five-spice braised pork with a boiled egg over rice, with pickled mustard greens.

items.raw: 700g pork shoulder, cut into large chunks

steps.text: Combine the pork, soy sauce, sugar, garlic, pepper, star anise, five-spice and water in a pot.
Bring to the boil, then cover and simmer gently until the pork is very tender, about 90 minutes.
Add the eggs for the last 10 minutes until they take on colour.
Serve the sliced pork and eggs on the rice with the sauce and pickle.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach 70°C and be cooked until tender; cool leftovers quickly and eat within 2 days.
Contains egg and soy.

title: Tomato Rice Tiffin (Thakkali Sadam)
summary: Tangy South Indian tomato rice with onion, ginger and spices, packed with yoghurt for the tiffin.

steps.text: Heat the oil and pop the mustard seeds, then fry the onion until soft and golden, about 5 minutes.
Add the ginger, curry leaf and spices for 1 minute, then the tomatoes and cook until jammy, about 8 minutes.
Fold through the rice and salt until evenly coloured.
Pack with the yoghurt in the tiffin.

notes: Food safety: cool the rice quickly, refrigerate within 1 hour and eat within 4 hours out of the fridge.
Contains milk and mustard.

title: Aloo Paratha with Yoghurt and Pickle
summary: Soft whole wheat flatbreads stuffed with spiced mashed potato, served with yoghurt and mango pickle.

steps.text: Knead the flour, water, oil and a pinch of salt into a soft dough and rest it for 20 minutes.
Mix the potato, chilli, cumin, garam masala, coriander and salt.
Roll the dough into 8 small rounds, put a spoon of filling in the middle of half of them, cover with the rest and seal the edges.
Roll each gently flat, then cook in a dry hot pan until brown spots appear on both sides, about 2 minutes a side, brushing with butter.
Serve hot with yoghurt and pickle.

notes: Contains gluten and milk.

title: Antipasto Lunch Platter with Marinated Vegetables
summary: Cured meats, mozzarella, olives and marinated vegetables with crusty bread, a no-cook summer lunch.

steps.text: Tear the mozzarella and arrange it on a board with the prosciutto and salami.
Toss the capsicum, tomatoes and olives with the oil and vinegar until well coated.
Add the vegetables and rocket to the board.
Slice the baguette and serve alongside.

notes: Food safety: cured meats and cheese should stay below 5°C and be eaten within 2 hours at room temperature; pregnant people are often advised to avoid cured meats.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Cold Poached Chicken Platter with Green Herb Sauce
summary: Sliced poached chicken with potatoes, green beans and a punchy parsley and caper sauce.

steps.text: Poach the chicken in simmering water with the bay leaf until cooked through and the juices run clear, about 16 minutes, then chill.
Boil the potatoes until tender, about 15 minutes, adding the beans for the last 3 minutes, then drain.
Stir the parsley, capers, garlic, oil, lemon juice and mustard into a sauce.
Slice the chicken and arrange with the potatoes and beans and spoon the sauce over.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C; chill quickly and keep below 5°C, serving within 2 hours at room temperature.
Contains mustard.

title: Summer Rice Paper Platter with Prawns and Herbs
summary: Build-your-own rice paper rolls with prawns, vermicelli, herbs and a peanut dipping sauce.

steps.text: Soak the vermicelli in boiling water until tender, about 4 minutes, rinse cold and drain.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice and 3 tbsp warm water into a dipping sauce.
Arrange the prawns, noodles, vegetables, herbs and lettuce on a platter.
Dip each rice paper in warm water until just soft, fill, fold in the sides, roll up tightly and serve with the sauce.

notes: Food safety: keep cooked prawns below 5°C and eat within 2 days.
Contains shellfish, peanuts and soy.

title: Mini Pizza Pitas for Kids
summary: Little pizzas on pita bread with tomato, ham, pineapple and melting cheese, ready in 12 minutes.

steps.text: Spread each pita with passata.
Top with ham, pineapple and mozzarella.
Bake at 220°C until the cheese is melted and bubbling, about 8 minutes.
Cool for a few minutes and slice into wedges.

notes: Food safety: serve hot throughout and let cool before giving to small children.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Egg Fried Rice for Kids with Peas and Corn
summary: Mild fried rice with scrambled egg, peas, corn and a touch of soy, quick and lunchbox friendly.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wok and stir-fry the carrot for 2 minutes until just soft.
Push aside, pour in the beaten eggs and scramble until set.
Add the cold rice, peas and corn and stir-fry for 3 minutes until piping hot.
Stir through the soy sauce.

notes: Food safety: use rice cooled quickly and refrigerated within 1 hour of cooking, and eat the dish the same day.
Contains egg and soy.

title: Chicken and Vegetable Quesadilla Triangles for Kids
summary: Crisp tortillas filled with shredded chicken, grated zucchini and melted cheese, cut into easy triangles.

steps.text: Squeeze the water from the zucchini and mix with the chicken, cheese and cumin.
Spread the filling over 3 tortillas and top with the rest.
Cook each quesadilla in a lightly oiled pan until golden and the cheese melts, about 3 minutes a side.
Rest for 2 minutes and cut into triangles.

notes: Food safety: use chicken cooked to 75°C and chilled promptly; the quesadilla must be piping hot inside.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Tuna and Sweetcorn Rice Balls for Lunchboxes
summary: Soft rice balls with tuna mayo and sweetcorn wrapped in a strip of nori, easy to eat with small hands.

steps.text: Mix the tuna, mayonnaise, corn and soy sauce.
Wet your hands, take a handful of rice and press a hollow in the middle until it is a firm cup shape.
Add a spoon of filling, close the rice around it and shape into a ball or triangle.
Wrap a strip of nori around each ball.

notes: Food safety: use rice cooled quickly after cooking; keep the rice balls below 5°C and eat within 4 hours.
Contains fish, egg and soy.

title: Suya Chicken Wraps (Nigerian Peanut-Spiced Chicken)
summary: Quick-seared chicken rubbed with a peanut and chilli spice mix, rolled with tomato, onion and cabbage.

steps.text: Mix the peanut, chilli powder, paprika, ginger, garlic powder and salt, and toss the chicken through it.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through to 75°C.
Warm the tortillas, fill with the chicken, tomato, onion and cabbage, and roll up.

notes: Food safety: chicken must be cooked through to 75°C with no pink. Pack chilled with an ice pack if taking it to work and eat within 4 hours.
Contains peanut and gluten.

title: Jollof Rice Bowl with Fried Plantain and Egg
summary: Tomato and capsicum jollof rice with golden plantain and a fried egg on top.

steps.text: Soften the onion and capsicum in the first measure of oil for 5 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste, curry powder and thyme for 2 minutes.
Add the tinned tomatoes, stock, salt and rice, cover and simmer on low for 20 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid has been absorbed.
Fry the plantain in the second measure of oil for 3 minutes each side until golden, then set aside and fry the eggs in the same pan.
Serve the rice topped with plantain and an egg.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set. Cool leftover rice within an hour and eat within 1 day, reheated until steaming hot.
Contains egg.

title: Red Red (Ghanaian Black-Eyed Bean Stew with Plantain)
summary: Spiced tomato and black-eyed bean stew with fried sweet plantain, a vegan Ghanaian favourite.

steps.text: Soften the onion, garlic, ginger and chilli in the first measure of oil for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and paste and cook for 5 minutes, then stir in the beans, water and salt and simmer for 12 minutes.
Fry the plantain in the second measure of oil for 3 minutes each side until golden.
Serve the stew with the plantain alongside.

notes: Wash your hands after handling the scotch bonnet and leave the seeds out for less heat.

title: Fataya (Senegalese Tuna Pastries)
summary: Crisp baked filo parcels filled with spiced tuna and onion, a Dakar street lunch.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C. Soften the onion in the first measure of oil for 5 minutes, add the mustard seed, chilli, cumin and salt, then fold in the tuna and parsley and cool for 5 minutes.
Cut each filo sheet in half lengthways, brush with oil and fold into 6 triangle parcels around spoonfuls of the filling.
Brush the tops with the remaining oil and bake for 15 minutes until golden and crisp.

notes: Food safety: keep tinned tuna chilled once opened. Cool the parcels within an hour; eat within 2 days and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains fish and gluten.

title: Misir Wot Flatbread Plate (Ethiopian Spiced Red Lentils)
summary: Slow-simmered red lentils in a deep berbere-style spice blend, scooped up with warm flatbread.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil over medium heat for 8 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger, paste and spices and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the lentils, water and salt, simmer for 15 minutes, stirring often, until thick and soft.
Warm the flatbread and serve with the lentils.

notes: Contains gluten.

title: Atkilt Wat (Ethiopian Cabbage, Potato and Chickpea Plate)
summary: Turmeric-gold cabbage, potato and carrot stew with chickpeas, mild and filling.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 6 minutes, add the garlic, ginger and turmeric for 1 minute.
Add the potato, carrot and water, cover and simmer for 10 minutes, then add the cabbage, chickpeas and salt and cook 8 minutes more until tender.
Serve warm in bowls, with a squeeze of lemon if you like.

notes: Good cold the next day as a packed lunch.

title: Githeri (Kenyan Maize and Bean Bowl with Avocado)
summary: Kenyan maize and kidney beans fried with tomato and onion, topped with creamy avocado.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add the tomatoes and turmeric and cook for 4 minutes.
Stir in the beans, corn, salt and water and simmer for 8 minutes until the liquid has reduced.
Serve topped with avocado and coriander.

notes: Make a double batch; it reheats well.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Sukuma Wiki with Fried Eggs and Polenta
summary: Garlicky Kenyan braised kale with tomato and onion, a fried egg and a wedge of firm polenta in place of ugali.

steps.text: Whisk the polenta into the boiling salted water and stir over low heat for 8 minutes until thick, then spread into a dish to firm.
Cook the onion in the first measure of oil for 5 minutes, add the garlic and tomatoes for 3 minutes, then the kale and 3 tbsp water, covered, for 6 minutes.
Fry the eggs in the second measure of oil until the whites are set, cut the polenta into wedges and serve with the kale and eggs.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set.
Contains egg.

title: Vegetarian Bunny Chow (South African Curry Beans in Bread)
summary: A Durban classic: hollowed bread loaf filled with a spiced bean and potato curry.

items.raw: 1 crusty bread, cut into 2 lengths, hollowed

steps.text: Soften the onion, garlic and ginger in the oil for 5 minutes, stir in the curry powder for 1 minute.
Add the tomato, potato, water and salt, simmer for 12 minutes, then add the beans and cook 4 minutes until thick.
Spoon the curry into the hollowed bread, top with coriander and serve with the bread lids on the side.

notes: Contains gluten.

title: Boerewors-Style Sausage Rolls with Tomato Relish
summary: Grilled spiced pork sausage in a soft roll with a quick tomato and onion relish, South African braai style.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add the tomatoes, sugar, vinegar and salt and simmer for 10 minutes into a thick relish.
Rub the sausages with the coriander and pepper, then grill or pan-fry over medium heat for 12 to 15 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through to 75°C.
Tuck the sausages into the buns and top with the relish.

notes: Food safety: pork sausages must be cooked through to 75°C with no pink. Eat packed lunches within 4 hours, chilled, and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten.

title: Gatsby (Cape Town Steak and Chips Roll)
summary: A long roll stuffed with seared steak strips, hot chips, onion and sauce, a Cape Town sharing classic.

steps.text: Bake the chips as the pack directs, about 20 minutes.
Season the steak with paprika, garlic powder and a pinch of salt. Cook with the onion in the oil over high heat for 4 minutes until browned and cooked through (63°C or more).
Spread mayonnaise and tomato sauce in the rolls, fill with the chips, steak, onion and tomato.

notes: Food safety: beef steak cooked to at least 63°C. Pack chilled and eat within 4 hours.
Contains egg and gluten.

title: Chakalaka Beans on Toast with Fried Egg
summary: Baked beans lifted with carrot, capsicum and curry spice in a quick chakalaka, piled on toast with an egg.

steps.text: Soften the onion, carrot and capsicum in the oil for 6 minutes, stir in the curry powder, then add the tomato and beans and simmer for 6 minutes.
Fry the eggs until the whites are set.
Cook the eggs until the whites are set, then pile the beans on the toast and top with an egg and parsley.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set.
Contains egg and gluten.

title: Bandeja Paisa Lunch Plate (Colombian Rice, Beans, Chorizo and Egg)
summary: A trimmed-down Colombian platter of rice, red beans, chorizo, plantain, avocado and a fried egg.

steps.text: Cook the rice in 280 ml salted water, covered, for 15 minutes. Simmer the beans with the tomato, spring onion, cumin and 100 ml water for 12 minutes until thick.
Fry the chorizo in a dry pan for 4 minutes, remove, and fry the plantain in the oil for 3 minutes each side. Fry the eggs in the same pan until the whites are set.
Plate the rice with beans, chorizo, plantain, egg and avocado.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set and the chorizo until hot through to 75°C.
Contains egg.

title: Casado (Costa Rican Chicken, Rice and Black Bean Plate)
summary: The classic Costa Rican set lunch: seared chicken, rice, black beans, fried plantain and a lime cabbage slaw.

steps.text: Cook the rice in the water with a pinch of salt, covered, for 15 minutes. Warm the beans with 50 ml water.
Season the chicken with cumin and salt and cook in the first measure of oil for 6 minutes each side until cooked through to 75°C. Rest 3 minutes, then slice.
Fry the plantain in the second measure of oil for 3 minutes each side. Toss the cabbage with the lime juice and coriander.
Plate everything together.

notes: Food safety: chicken must be cooked through to 75°C with no pink.

title: Prato Feito (Brazilian Steak, Egg, Rice and Beans Plate)
summary: The everyday Brazilian lunch plate: seared steak, fried egg, rice, stewed beans and tomato.

steps.text: Cook the rice in the water, covered, for 15 minutes. Soften the garlic in 1 tbsp of the oil, add the beans and 100 ml water and simmer for 10 minutes.
Season the steak with salt and sear in a hot pan for 3 to 4 minutes each side, rest for 4 minutes and slice. Fry the eggs in the remaining oil until the whites are set.
Toss the tomato and onion with the lime juice and plate everything together.

notes: Food safety: cook steak to at least 63°C and rest it. Cook the eggs until the whites are set.
Contains egg.

title: Gallo Pinto Bowl with Fried Egg and Avocado (Costa Rican Rice and Beans)
summary: Rice and black beans fried with onion, capsicum and a splash of Worcestershire, topped with egg and avocado.

steps.text: Cook the rice in the water with a pinch of salt, covered, for 15 minutes.
Soften the onion and capsicum in the first measure of oil for 5 minutes, add the beans, cumin and Worcestershire sauce and the rice, and stir-fry for 5 minutes until hot and lightly speckled.
Fry the eggs in the second measure of oil until the whites are set.
Serve the rice topped with egg, avocado and coriander.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set. Cool leftover rice within an hour and eat within 1 day.
Contains egg and fish (Worcestershire sauce).

title: Sanguche de Pollo (Peruvian Chicken Sandwich with Aji Cream)
summary: Warm sliced chicken in a crusty roll with creamy jalapeño and lime sauce and red onion.

steps.text: Season the chicken with cumin and salt, cook in the oil for 5 to 6 minutes each side until cooked through to 75°C, then rest 3 minutes and slice.
Mix the mayonnaise, jalapeño and half the lime juice. Toss the onion in the rest of the juice.
Fill the rolls with lettuce, chicken, onion and the cream.

notes: Food safety: chicken must be cooked through to 75°C with no pink. Pack chilled and eat within 4 hours.
Contains egg and gluten.

title: Patacones with Fried Egg and Avocado (Ecuadorian Twice-Fried Plantain)
summary: Crisp smashed green plantain discs topped with a runny egg, avocado and fresh salsa.

items.raw: 2 plantain, peeled and cut in thick rounds
items.prep: peeled and cut in thick rounds

steps.text: Fry the plantain rounds in 2 tbsp oil for 3 minutes each side, then smash flat between baking paper and fry again for 2 minutes each side until crisp. Sprinkle with salt.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil until the whites are set.
Mix the tomato, onion and lime juice. Top the patacones with eggs, avocado and salsa.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set.
Contains egg.

title: Loco Moco (Hawaiian Beef Patty, Egg and Gravy Rice Bowl)
summary: A Hawaiian diner staple: rice topped with a juicy beef patty, fried egg and rich onion gravy.

steps.text: Cook the rice in 320 ml water, covered, for 15 minutes. Shape the mince with salt and pepper into 2 patties.

Cook the patties in a pan over medium-high heat for 5 minutes each side until cooked through to 75°C, then set aside. Cook the onion in the same pan for 5 minutes, stir in the flour, then add the stock and soy sauce and simmer 4 minutes into a gravy.
Fry the eggs until the whites are set, then stack rice, patty, egg and gravy in bowls and top with spring onion.

notes: Food safety: beef patties must be cooked through to 75°C with no pink. Cook the eggs until the whites are set.
Contains egg and gluten.

title: Hawaiian Garlic Prawn Plate Lunch with Rice and Pineapple
summary: North Shore style garlic butter prawns with steamed rice and sweet pineapple.

steps.text: Cook the rice in 320 ml water, covered, for 15 minutes.
Melt the butter over medium heat and cook the garlic and paprika for 1 minute, then add the prawns and salt and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until pink and curled. Add the lemon juice.
Serve over rice with pineapple and parsley.

notes: Food safety: prawns must be opaque and pink all the way through. Eat leftovers within 1 day, reheated until steaming hot.
Contains crustacean shellfish and milk.

title: Huli Huli Chicken Plate with Rice and Slaw
summary: Pineapple, soy and ginger glazed chicken thighs with rice and a crunchy cabbage slaw.

steps.text: Cook the rice in 320 ml water, covered, for 15 minutes. Mix the soy, sugar, juice, ginger and garlic.
Brown the chicken in the oil for 5 minutes each side, pour in the sauce and cook for 6 minutes, turning, until glossy and cooked through to 75°C.
Toss the cabbage and carrot with the vinegar. Sear the pineapple rings in the pan until caramelised and serve everything together.

notes: Food safety: chicken must be cooked through to 75°C with no pink.
Contains soy.

title: Pacific Corned Beef and Coconut Spinach Rice
summary: Tinned corned beef fried with onion and folded through coconut spinach rice, a Pacific island pantry lunch.

steps.text: Cook the rice with the coconut milk, water and salt, covered, on low for 15 minutes.
Fry the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add the corned beef and cook for 4 minutes until crisp at the edges.
Fold the spinach and corned beef through the hot rice, cover for 2 minutes and finish with lime.

notes: Food safety: keep opened tinned corned beef chilled and use within 2 days.

title: Sapasui (Samoan Glass Noodle Stir-Fry)
summary: Soy and ginger glass noodles tossed with beef, carrot and cabbage, a Samoan potluck favourite.

steps.text: Soak the noodles in hot water for 8 minutes, drain and snip into shorter lengths.
Stir-fry the beef in the oil over high heat for 3 minutes, add the onion, garlic, ginger and carrot for 3 minutes.
Add the cabbage, soy, water and noodles and toss for 3 minutes until the liquid is absorbed.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef until browned and cooked through to at least 63°C.
Contains soy.

title: Dibi Lamb Baguette (Senegalese Grilled Lamb with Onion Mustard)
summary: Grilled lamb strips in a crusty baguette with a hot mustard and caramelised onion sauce, Dakar roadside style.

steps.text: Season the lamb with pepper, garlic powder and salt and cook in half the oil over high heat for 5 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through to 63°C. Set aside.
Cook the onions in the rest of the oil for 12 minutes until soft and golden, then stir in the mustard and vinegar.
Fill the baguette with the lamb and onion mustard.

notes: Food safety: lamb must be cooked to at least 63°C. Pack chilled and eat within 4 hours.
Contains gluten and mustard.

title: Kelewele Plantain and Peanut Wraps (Ghanaian Spiced Fried Plantain)
summary: Ginger and chilli spiced plantain cubes fried until caramelised, wrapped with peanuts, tomato and cabbage.

steps.text: Toss the plantain with the ginger, cayenne and salt.
Fry in the oil over medium-high heat for 8 minutes, turning, until deep golden and caramelised at the edges.
Warm the flatbread, fill with plantain, peanuts, tomato and cabbage, and squeeze over the lime.

notes: Contains peanut and gluten.

title: Pierogi Ruskie Plate (Polish Potato and Ricotta Dumplings)
summary: Tender dumplings filled with potato, ricotta and onion, served with butter-fried onions and sour cream.

steps.text: Boil the potato for 12 minutes until soft, drain and mash with the ricotta, salt and pepper. Soften half the onion in half the butter for 5 minutes and fold in.
Mix the flour, egg, first measure of sour cream and water into a soft dough, knead for 3 minutes, roll thin and cut into 8 cm rounds.
Fill the rounds with the potato mix, fold over and press the edges to seal. Boil in batches for 4 minutes, until they float and the dough is tender.
Fry the remaining onion in the remaining butter for 8 minutes until golden, toss the pierogi through it and serve with sour cream and chives.

notes: Food safety: cook the egg dough dumplings through; eat leftovers within 2 days reheated until steaming hot.
Contains egg, gluten and milk.

title: Blini with Smoked Salmon and Dill Creme Fraiche
summary: Small fluffy pancakes topped with smoked salmon, dill cream and lemon, a Russian lunch classic.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder, milk, egg, half the butter and salt into a smooth batter.
Brush a pan with the remaining butter and cook small spoonfuls over medium heat for 2 minutes each side, until golden and puffed.
Mix the crème fraîche with the dill. Top the blini with salmon, dill cream, capers and a squeeze of lemon.

notes: Food safety: smoked salmon is ready to eat but keep it chilled and eat within 2 days of opening.
Contains egg, fish, gluten and milk.

title: Draniki with Fried Eggs and Sour Cream (Belarusian Potato Pancakes)
summary: Crisp grated potato and onion pancakes topped with a fried egg and cool sour cream.

steps.text: Grate the potato and onion and squeeze out the liquid in a clean tea towel. Mix with the first egg, flour, salt and pepper.
Fry 4 mounds in 2 tbsp oil over medium heat for 4 minutes each side, until deep golden and crisp, and drain on paper.
Fry the remaining eggs in the last of the oil until the whites are set. Serve the pancakes with an egg, sour cream and dill.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set.
Contains egg, gluten and milk.

title: Kotleti Rolls (Russian Chicken Patties with Pickles and Sour Cream)
summary: Tender dill chicken patties in a soft roll with crunchy pickles and sour cream.

steps.text: Mix the mince, onion, breadcrumbs, egg, dill and salt, and shape into 2 flat patties.
Cook in the oil over medium heat for 6 minutes each side, until golden and cooked through to 75°C.
Fill the rolls with sour cream, pickles and the patties.

notes: Food safety: chicken patties must be cooked through to 75°C with no pink. Pack chilled and eat within 4 hours.
Contains egg, gluten and milk.

title: Banosh (Ukrainian Polenta with Bacon, Mushrooms and Sour Cream)
summary: Creamy Carpathian polenta topped with crisp bacon, fried mushrooms and sour cream.

steps.text: Whisk the polenta into the boiling salted water and stir over low heat for 10 minutes, until thick and creamy.
Fry the bacon for 4 minutes until crisp, add the onion and mushrooms and cook for 6 minutes, until golden.
Serve the polenta topped with the bacon mixture, sour cream and parsley.

notes: Food safety: cook the bacon until crisp and no longer pink.
Contains milk.

title: Langos with Sour Cream and Garlic (Hungarian Fried Flatbread)
summary: Golden Hungarian street-food flatbread rubbed with garlic and topped with sour cream.

steps.text: Mix the flour, baking powder and salt with the yoghurt and water into a soft dough, knead for 1 minute and divide into 2 balls.
Press each ball out to 15 cm and fry in 2 tbsp oil per flatbread for 3 minutes each side, until puffed and golden.
Rub the hot langos with garlic, spread with sour cream and scatter with chives.

notes: Contains gluten and milk.

title: Polish Zapiekanka (Baguette with Mushrooms and Melted Mozzarella)
summary: The Krakow street-food toasted baguette: buttery mushrooms, melted cheese and a drizzle of tomato sauce.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C. Fry the onion and mushrooms in the butter for 8 minutes, until golden and the liquid has gone.
Pile onto the baguette halves, top with the mozzarella and bake for 6 minutes, until bubbling and golden.
Drizzle with tomato sauce and scatter with oregano and chives.

notes: Contains gluten and milk.

title: Mamaliga with Feta, Fried Egg and Sour Cream (Romanian Polenta Lunch)
summary: Romanian polenta topped with crumbled feta, a fried egg and sour cream.

steps.text: Whisk the polenta into the boiling salted water and stir over low heat for 10 minutes, until thick.
Fry the eggs in the oil until the whites are set.
Spoon the polenta into bowls and top with feta, sour cream, an egg and dill.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set.
Contains egg and milk.

title: Skagenrora Toasts (Swedish Prawn and Dill on Rye)
summary: Cold prawns in a creamy dill and lemon mix piled on buttered rye, a 10-minute Swedish classic.

steps.text: Mix the prawns, mayonnaise, crème fraîche, dill, lemon zest and juice and pepper until evenly coated.
Butter the rye, layer with cucumber and pile on the prawn mix.
Serve straight away, while the rye is still crisp.

notes: Food safety: keep the prawns chilled until serving and eat within 2 days; if packing for lunch use an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
Contains crustacean shellfish, egg, gluten and milk.

title: Lompe-Style Wraps (Norwegian Smoked Salmon and Cream Cheese Wraps)
summary: Soft flatbread filled with smoked salmon, cream cheese, cucumber and dill, a no-cook Norwegian lunch.

steps.text: Spread the flatbread with cream cheese and lemon juice.
Lay on the salmon, cucumber, dill and pepper, then roll up tightly until sealed.
Halve on the diagonal and serve cold.

notes: Food safety: keep smoked salmon chilled and eat within 2 days of opening. Pregnant people should avoid smoked fish.
Contains fish, gluten and milk.

title: Pylsur (Icelandic Hot Dogs with Crispy Onion and Remoulade)
summary: Hot dogs the Reykjavik way: soft buns, sweet mustard, raw and crispy onion and a tangy remoulade.

steps.text: Simmer the frankfurts in hot water for 6 minutes, until steaming hot through to 75°C.
Mix the mayonnaise, pickle and vinegar into a remoulade.
Warm the buns, fill with the frankfurts and layer with mustard, remoulade, raw onion and fried shallots.

notes: Food safety: frankfurts must be steaming hot through to 75°C.
Contains egg, gluten and mustard.

title: Smashed Chickpea and Tahini Sandwich
summary: Creamy mashed chickpea, tahini and lemon with crunchy cucumber on sourdough, a vegan protein lunch in 10 minutes.

steps.text: Mash the chickpeas with the tahini, lemon juice, mustard, salt and cumin until mostly smooth with a few chunks left.
Pile onto 2 slices of sourdough with cucumber and lettuce and top with the remaining bread.
Cut in half and eat fresh, or wrap and chill for up to 4 hours.

notes: Contains sesame, gluten and mustard. Keeps 2 days chilled.

title: Black Bean Tofu Scramble Wraps
summary: Turmeric-spiced crumbled tofu and black beans rolled in a warm tortilla with salsa, a vegan protein lunch.

steps.text: Fry the tofu in the oil with the spices and salt for 5 minutes, until golden and slightly dry.
Add the beans and cook 3 minutes until hot.
Warm the tortillas, fill with spinach, the tofu mix and salsa, and roll.

notes: Contains soy and gluten.

title: Lentil and Walnut Lettuce Cups
summary: Savoury soy-seasoned lentils and walnuts with ginger, spooned into crisp cos lettuce cups.

steps.text: Fry the garlic and ginger in the oil for 30 seconds, add the lentils and walnuts and cook for 5 minutes, until lightly crisp at the edges.
Add the soy, vinegar and sesame oil and toss for 1 minute.
Spoon into the lettuce leaves and top with carrot and spring onion.

notes: Contains soy, sesame and tree nuts (walnut).

title: Quinoa, Edamame and Tahini Power Bowl
summary: Fluffy quinoa with edamame, avocado and cucumber under a lemony tahini dressing, a complete vegan protein bowl.

steps.text: Rinse the quinoa and simmer in the water for 12 minutes, until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender. Boil the edamame for 3 minutes and drain.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice, water and salt into a pourable dressing.
Divide the quinoa between bowls, top with edamame, avocado, cucumber and seeds and drizzle with dressing.

notes: Contains soy and sesame.

title: Cold Peanut Tofu Soba Bowl
summary: Chilled soba with golden tofu, cucumber and edamame in a creamy peanut and lime dressing.

steps.text: Cook the soba in boiling water for 5 minutes until tender, adding the edamame for the last 2 minutes. Drain and rinse under cold water until cool.
Fry the tofu in the oil for 6 minutes, turning, until golden on all sides.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy, lime juice, sesame oil and water into a dressing.
Toss the noodles with the dressing, vegetables and tofu and top with spring onion.

notes: Contains peanut, soy, sesame and gluten (most soba contains wheat).

title: Chickpea Flour Socca with Spinach and Tomato
summary: Crisp-edged chickpea flour flatbreads topped with wilted spinach, tomato and hummus, naturally vegan and gluten-free.

steps.text: Whisk the chickpea flour, water, salt and cumin into a smooth batter.
Heat half the oil in a pan and pour in half the batter, cook for 3 minutes until set and golden underneath, flip and cook 2 minutes more. Repeat with the rest.
Wilt the spinach in the pan for 1 minute. Top the socca with spinach, tomato, hummus and parsley.

notes: Naturally free of gluten, dairy and egg.

title: Tuna-Stuffed Avocados
summary: Whole avocados filled with creamy lemon tuna and capers, a low-carb lunch with no cooking.

steps.text: Mix the tuna, mayonnaise, mustard, lemon juice, capers and spring onion.
Spoon into the avocado halves until generously mounded.
Scatter with parsley and serve at once.

notes: Food safety: keep opened tuna chilled; eat the same day.
Contains fish, egg and mustard.

title: Chicken Lettuce Wraps with Peanut Sauce
summary: Ginger-spiced chicken mince in crisp cos cups with a quick peanut and lime sauce, low in carbs.

steps.text: Fry the chicken in the oil for 6 minutes, breaking it up, with the garlic and ginger until cooked through to 75°C.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy, lime juice and water into a sauce and stir half through the chicken.
Spoon into the lettuce, top with carrot, spring onion and the rest of the sauce.

notes: Food safety: chicken mince must be cooked through to 75°C with no pink.
Contains peanut and soy.

title: Garlic Chilli Prawns with Zucchini Noodles
summary: Quick garlic and chilli prawns tossed through spiralled zucchini with lemon and parsley, low in carbs.

steps.text: Heat the oil over medium-high heat, cook the garlic and chilli for 30 seconds, then add the prawns and cook for 3 minutes, until pink and curled.
Add the tomatoes and zucchini noodles and toss for 2 minutes, until just tender.
Stir through the lemon zest, juice, salt and parsley.

notes: Food safety: prawns must be opaque and pink all the way through.
Contains crustacean shellfish.

title: Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry (No Rice)
summary: Tender beef and bright broccoli in a glossy oyster and soy sauce, piled high without the rice.

steps.text: Toss the beef with the cornflour. Sear in half the oil over high heat for 2 minutes, until browned, and set aside.
Stir-fry the broccoli in the rest of the oil for 3 minutes, add the garlic, ginger and water and cover for 2 minutes until tender-crisp.
Return the beef with the oyster sauce and soy and toss for 1 minute, until glossy and cooked through to 63°C or more.

notes: Food safety: beef must be cooked through to at least 63°C.
Contains soy and shellfish (oyster sauce).

title: Falafel and Hummus Wraps with Pickled Turnip
summary: Ready-made falafel warmed through and rolled with hummus, tomato, cucumber and pickled turnip in 10 minutes.

steps.text: Warm the falafel in a hot oven or pan for 5 minutes, until hot through.
Spread the flatbread with hummus, add the falafel, tomato, cucumber, turnip and parsley, squeeze over lemon and roll up.
Cut in half and serve warm.

notes: Contains gluten and sesame. Check the falafel label for allergens.

title: White Bean, Tuna and Rocket Toast
summary: Lemony cannellini beans and flaked tuna on thick toasted sourdough with peppery rocket.

steps.text: Toast the sourdough for 3 minutes, until golden.
Crush the beans roughly with the oil, lemon juice and pepper.
Spread over the toast until covered, then top with tuna, capers and rocket.

notes: Food safety: keep opened tuna chilled; eat the same day.
Contains fish and gluten.

title: Smashed Avocado and Chickpea Toast with Lime and Chilli
summary: Lime-smashed avocado on sourdough, topped with crisp-edged chickpeas and chilli flakes, vegan in 10 minutes.

steps.text: Toast the sourdough for 3 minutes until golden. Fry the chickpeas in the oil for 4 minutes, until crisp at the edges.
Mash the avocado with the lime juice and salt until chunky, spread over the toast and top with the chickpeas, chilli and coriander.
Serve straight away while the chickpeas are crisp.

notes: Contains gluten.

title: Sheet-Pan Lemon Herb Chicken Thighs with Potatoes and Broccoli
summary: Crisp-skinned chicken thighs roast over lemony potatoes, with broccoli added near the end, all on one tray.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the potato with half the oil, half the lemon juice, the oregano and half the salt on a large tray.
Rub the chicken with the remaining oil, lemon zest, garlic, remaining salt and pepper and nestle it skin-side up among the potatoes.
Roast for 30 minutes, then add the broccoli and remaining lemon juice and roast for 15 minutes more, until the chicken skin is crisp and the juices run clear.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink and clear juices; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Sheet-Pan Sausages with Capsicum, Onion and Gnocchi
summary: Pork sausages, sweet capsicum and shop-bought gnocchi crisp up together on one tray with a little Italian seasoning.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the gnocchi, capsicum, onion, oil, seasoning and salt together on a large tray.
Nestle the sausages among the vegetables and roast for 30 minutes, turning once, until the sausages are browned and cooked through and the gnocchi is golden.
Scatter with parsley and serve from the tray.

notes: Food safety: pork sausages must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Contains gluten.

title: Sheet-Pan Salmon with Asparagus and Baby Potatoes
summary: Salmon fillets and asparagus finish on a tray of roasted baby potatoes with lemon and dill.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 210°C (190°C fan). Toss the potatoes with half the oil and half the salt on a tray and roast for 20 minutes.
Add the asparagus and salmon, drizzle with the remaining oil, season and top with lemon slices.
Roast for 10 minutes, until the salmon flakes easily and the asparagus is tender, then scatter with dill.

notes: Food safety: cook the salmon until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C; eat leftovers cold within 1 day.

title: Sheet-Pan Harissa Chicken with Chickpeas and Carrots
summary: Harissa-rubbed chicken thighs roast on a bed of chickpeas and carrots that soak up the juices.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Mix the harissa, half the oil, cumin and half the salt and rub it over the chicken.
Toss the chickpeas, carrots and onion with the remaining oil and salt on a large tray and nestle the chicken on top.
Roast for 40 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the carrots are tender. Serve with yoghurt and coriander.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Sheet-Pan Miso Tofu with Broccoli and Sweet Potato
summary: Firm tofu, sweet potato and broccoli roast with a savoury miso glaze for an easy plant-based tray.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Whisk the miso, soy sauce, maple syrup and half the sesame oil until smooth.
Toss the sweet potato with the remaining oil on a tray and roast for 15 minutes, then add the tofu and broccoli and brush with the glaze.
Roast for 20 minutes more, until the tofu is golden and the sweet potato is tender. Serve over rice with sesame seeds and spring onion.

notes: Contains soy, sesame and gluten.

title: Air-Fryer Crumbed Chicken Schnitzel with Crunchy Slaw
summary: Golden schnitzels cooked in the air fryer with barely any oil, served with a lemony cabbage slaw.

steps.text: Flatten the chicken to 1 cm. Dip each piece in flour, then egg, then panko mixed with the oil, salt and pepper.
Air-fry at 190°C for 12 to 15 minutes, turning once, until golden and cooked through.
Toss the cabbage, carrot, mayonnaise and lemon juice together and serve alongside the schnitzel.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; wash hands and board after handling raw chicken and egg, and eat leftovers within 2 days.
Contains gluten and egg.

title: Air-Fryer Salmon with Honey Soy Glaze and Greens
summary: Salmon fillets cook in about 10 minutes in the air fryer, then get a sticky honey soy glaze.

steps.text: Mix the honey, soy sauce, ginger and garlic. Brush half over the salmon.
Air-fry the salmon at 200°C for 8 to 10 minutes, until the fish flakes, adding the bok choy tossed in the sesame oil for the last 4 minutes.
Brush with the remaining glaze and serve over rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the salmon until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C; eat leftovers cold within 1 day.
Contains soy, fish and sesame.

title: Air-Fryer Chicken Drumsticks with Smoky Corn
summary: Smoked paprika drumsticks cook up crisp in the air fryer, with corn cobs and a squeeze of lime.

steps.text: Toss the drumsticks with half the oil, paprika, garlic powder and salt.
Air-fry at 190°C for 25 minutes, turning halfway, until the skin is crisp and the juices run clear. Rest for 3 minutes.
Rub the corn with the remaining oil and air-fry at 200°C for 8 to 10 minutes until charred, then toss with butter and serve with lime.

notes: Food safety: drumsticks must reach 75°C at the bone with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Air-Fryer Crispy Tofu with Peanut Sauce and Rice
summary: Cornflour-dusted tofu crisps in the air fryer and is tossed in a quick peanut sauce.

steps.text: Toss the tofu with the cornflour and oil, then air-fry at 200°C for 15 minutes, shaking twice, until crisp and golden.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice, maple syrup, chilli and 3 tbsp warm water until smooth.
Toss the tofu in half the sauce and serve over rice with cucumber and the rest of the sauce.

notes: Contains peanuts, soy and gluten.

title: Air-Fryer Stuffed Capsicums with Beef and Rice
summary: Capsicums filled with beef mince, rice and tomato bake in the air fryer under melted cheese.

items.raw: 4 red capsicum, tops cut off and deseeded

steps.text: Fry the onion in the oil for 4 minutes, add the mince, cumin, paprika and salt and cook for 6 minutes until browned. Stir in the rice and passata.
Fill the capsicums, stand them upright in the basket and top with cheese.
Air-fry at 180°C for 15 minutes, until the capsicums are tender and the cheese is bubbling.

notes: Food safety: beef mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink; eat leftovers within 2 days.
Contains milk.

title: Slow-Cooker Beef Stew with Dark Ale and Creamy Mash
summary: Chuck steak simmers all day in dark ale with carrots and onion until fork-tender, served over mash.

steps.text: Toss the beef in the flour and brown it in the oil in batches for 6 minutes, until deeply coloured, then tip into the slow cooker.
Add the onion, carrot, garlic, ale, stock, tomato paste, thyme and salt. Cook on low for 8 hours, until the beef is fork-tender.
Boil the potatoes for 15 minutes until soft, drain and mash with the butter and milk. Serve the stew over the mash.

notes: Food safety: braise beef to well above 75°C, until fork-tender; cool leftovers quickly and eat within 3 days.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Slow-Cooker Butter Chicken with Basmati
summary: Chicken thigh simmers gently in a creamy tomato and spice sauce while you get on with your day.

steps.text: Put the chicken, onion, garlic, ginger, spices, tomatoes, butter and salt into the slow cooker and stir. Cook on low for 5 hours, until the chicken is very tender.
Stir in the cream and cook for 10 minutes more.
Cook the rice in 3 cups of boiling water, covered, for 12 minutes until tender, and serve the curry over the top with coriander.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C throughout; cool leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Contains milk.

title: Slow-Cooker Pulled Pork Tacos with Lime Slaw
summary: Pork shoulder slow-cooks with smoky spices until it shreds, then fills warm tortillas with crunchy lime slaw.

steps.text: Rub the pork with the paprika, cumin, oregano and salt, then place in the slow cooker with the onion, garlic and orange juice. Cook on low for 8 hours, until it shreds easily.
Shred the pork with two forks and moisten with some of the cooking juices.
Toss the cabbage with the lime juice and coriander. Serve the pork in warm tortillas with slaw and sour cream.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 75°C and be very tender; cool leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Slow-Cooker Chickpea and Sweet Potato Curry
summary: A mild, creamy vegan curry that cooks itself, with sweet potato, chickpeas and spinach.

steps.text: Put the sweet potato, chickpeas, onion, garlic, curry powder, coconut milk, tomatoes and salt in the slow cooker. Cook on low for 6 hours, until the sweet potato is soft.
Stir through the spinach until wilted.
Cook the rice in boiling water for 12 minutes until tender, drain and serve with the curry.

notes: Naturally vegan.

title: Slow-Cooker Lamb Shoulder with Red Wine and Rosemary
summary: Lamb shoulder braises until the meat falls apart in a rich red wine and rosemary sauce.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil for 8 minutes, until deeply coloured, and place in the slow cooker.

Soften the onion, carrot and garlic in the same pan for 5 minutes, add the wine and bubble for 3 minutes, then add to the cooker with the tomatoes, stock, rosemary and salt. Cook on low for 7 hours, until the meat falls apart.
Boil the potatoes for 15 minutes until tender, mash with the butter and serve under the lamb.

notes: Food safety: cook lamb until very tender and above 75°C; cool leftovers quickly and eat within 3 days.
Contains milk.

title: Slow-Cooker Cannellini Cassoulet-Style Pork Sausage Pot
summary: Pork sausages, cannellini beans and tomato simmer into a thick, hearty casserole.

items.raw: 2 can cannellini beans, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Brown the sausages in a pan for 6 minutes, then slice them into thick pieces.
Put them in the slow cooker with the beans, tomatoes, onion, carrot, garlic, stock, paprika, thyme and salt. Cook on low for 6 hours, until the vegetables are soft.
Scatter with parsley and serve with crusty bread.

notes: Food safety: pork sausages must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink; cool leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.
Contains gluten.

title: Date Night Pan-Seared Steak with Garlic Butter and Asparagus
summary: Two sirloin steaks seared hard and finished with garlic butter, with crisp asparagus on the side.

steps.text: Season the steaks and sear in the oil in a very hot pan for 3 to 4 minutes a side for medium, then add half the butter, garlic and thyme and baste for 1 minute. Rest for 5 minutes.
Cook the asparagus in the remaining butter for 4 minutes, until bright green and just tender.
Slice the steak, spoon over the pan butter and serve with asparagus and lemon.

notes: Food safety: whole cuts of steak can be served medium (63°C) but rest the meat; use a clean plate for cooked steak.
Contains milk.

title: Date Night Creamy Garlic Prawn Linguine
summary: Plump prawns in a lemony garlic cream sauce over linguine, ready in 25 minutes for two.

steps.text: Boil the linguine in salted water for 10 minutes, until al dente, and reserve a cup of the water.
Cook the garlic and chilli in the oil for 1 minute, add the prawns and cook for 2 minutes until pink, then add the wine and simmer for 2 minutes.
Stir in the cream, lemon zest and juice, toss through the pasta with a splash of pasta water and finish with parsley.

notes: Food safety: cook prawns until pink and opaque all the way through; eat leftovers within 1 day.
Contains gluten, crustacean shellfish and milk.

title: Date Night Mushroom and Thyme Risotto for Two
summary: A creamy mushroom risotto finished with parmesan and a little butter, made in one pan.

steps.text: Cook the mushrooms in the oil in a wide pan for 6 minutes until golden, then set aside.
Soften the onion and garlic in the butter for 4 minutes, add the rice and stir for 1 minute, then add the wine until absorbed.
Add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for 20 minutes until the rice is creamy and tender. Fold in the mushrooms, thyme, parmesan and salt.

notes: Contains milk.

title: Date Night Pan-Roasted Chicken Breast with White Wine Sauce
summary: Golden chicken breasts finished in a quick white wine and mustard sauce with green beans.

steps.text: Season the chicken and sear in the oil for 5 minutes a side until golden, then roast in a 200°C oven for 8 minutes until cooked through. Rest for 3 minutes.
Soften the onion in the butter for 3 minutes, add the wine and stock and reduce for 5 minutes, then stir in the mustard and cream.
Steam the beans for 5 minutes until tender, slice the chicken and serve with the sauce.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink; eat leftovers within 2 days.
Contains milk and mustard.

title: Cooking for One: Single-Serve Chicken Fried Rice
summary: A quick fried rice for one, using leftover cooked rice, a small chicken thigh and frozen veg.

steps.text: Stir-fry the chicken in half the oil for 4 minutes until cooked through, then push aside.
Scramble the egg in the remaining oil for 1 minute until set, add the garlic, rice and vegetables and fry for 3 minutes until piping hot.
Season with soy sauce and sesame oil and top with spring onion.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink and the egg must be set; use rice that was cooled and refrigerated within 1 hour of cooking, and eat leftovers within 1 day.
Contains egg, soy and sesame.

title: Cooking for One: Garlic Butter Gnocchi with Spinach
summary: Pan-fried gnocchi tossed with garlic, spinach and parmesan in a single frying pan.

steps.text: Fry the gnocchi in the oil for 5 to 6 minutes, until golden and crisp on the outside.
Add the butter and garlic and cook for 1 minute, then toss through the spinach until wilted.
Season with pepper and finish with parmesan.

notes: Contains gluten and milk.

title: Cooking for One: Teriyaki Salmon Rice Bowl
summary: One salmon fillet glazed in teriyaki, served over rice with cucumber and edamame.

steps.text: Pan-fry the salmon in the oil for 3 minutes a side, until golden and just cooked through.
Pour in the soy sauce, mirin and honey and simmer for 1 minute until sticky.
Serve over the rice with edamame and cucumber, topped with sesame seeds.

notes: Food safety: cook salmon until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C; eat leftovers cold within 1 day.
Contains fish, soy and sesame.

title: Cooking for One: One-Pan Egg and Tomato Shakshuka
summary: Two eggs poached in a spiced tomato and capsicum sauce, scooped up with toasted bread.

steps.text: Soften the onion and capsicum in the oil for 5 minutes, add the garlic and spices for 1 minute, then add the tomatoes and simmer for 6 minutes until thick.
Make two wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 5 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are as firm as you like.
Scatter with parsley and serve with the toast once the eggs are set.

notes: Food safety: cook eggs until the whites are completely set, and eat the dish the same day.
Contains egg and gluten.

title: Cooking for One: Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry
summary: Thin beef strips and broccoli in a glossy garlic soy sauce, ready in 15 minutes.

steps.text: Toss the beef with the cornflour. Stir-fry in half the oil over high heat for 2 minutes until browned, then remove.
Stir-fry the broccoli, garlic and ginger in the remaining oil for 3 minutes, add the soy sauce, oyster sauce and water and simmer for 2 minutes until glossy.
Return the beef to heat through and serve over rice.

notes: Food safety: beef strips must be cooked through to 71°C with no pink; eat leftovers within 2 days.
Contains soy and gluten.

title: Cooking for One: Creamy Tomato and White Bean Pasta
summary: A quick vegetarian pasta with white beans, tomato and a spoonful of cream cheese for richness.

items.raw: 1/2 can cannellini beans, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Boil the penne in salted water for 10 minutes until al dente and drain.
Cook the garlic in the oil for 1 minute, add the tomatoes and beans and simmer for 6 minutes until thickened.
Stir in the cream cheese and salt until melted, toss through the pasta and top with basil.

notes: Contains gluten and milk.

title: Crowd-Pleasing Beef Lasagne for Twelve
summary: A big tray of beef and tomato lasagne with a creamy white sauce, made to feed a party.

steps.text: Soften the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes, add the mince and cook for 10 minutes until browned, then add the tomatoes, paste, oregano and salt and simmer for 20 minutes until thick.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk and stir for 8 minutes until it thickens into a white sauce.

Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Layer meat sauce, lasagne sheets and white sauce in a large deep dish, finishing with sauce and the cheeses. Bake for 40 minutes, until golden and bubbling and the centre reaches 75°C.

notes: Food safety: beef mince must reach 75°C in the centre; cool leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.
Contains gluten and milk. Rest 10 minutes before cutting.

title: Big-Batch Chicken and Vegetable Curry for Ten
summary: A mild, family-friendly chicken curry with potato and peas that scales happily for a crowd.

steps.text: Soften the onion, garlic and ginger in the oil for 8 minutes, add the curry powder for 1 minute, then the chicken and brown for 6 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, coconut milk, potato and salt and simmer for 30 minutes, until the potato is tender and the chicken reaches 75°C. Stir in the peas for the last 5 minutes.
Cook the rice in boiling water for 12 minutes until tender, then serve with the curry and coriander.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C throughout; cool leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Feed-a-Crowd Pulled Beef Sliders
summary: Slow-cooked beef chuck shredded in barbecue sauce and piled into soft slider rolls with slaw.

steps.text: Rub the beef with the paprika, garlic powder and salt and brown in the oil for 8 minutes. Place in a roasting dish with the barbecue sauce and stock, cover tightly and braise at 160°C for 4 hours, until the beef shreds easily.
Shred the beef and stir through the sauce in the dish.
Mix the cabbage, carrot, mayonnaise and vinegar for slaw and pile the beef and slaw into the rolls.

notes: Food safety: braise the beef to well above 75°C until tender; cool leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.
Contains gluten and egg.

title: Slow-Roasted Pork Shoulder for a Crowd with Apple Slaw
summary: A big pork shoulder roasted until it pulls apart, served with crunchy apple and cabbage slaw.

steps.text: Rub the pork with the oil, sugar, paprika, fennel seeds and salt, place in a deep roasting dish with the vinegar and 1 cup of water, cover with foil and roast at 150°C for 5 hours, until the pork shreds and reaches at least 90°C inside.
Shred the pork and toss with the pan juices.
Toss the cabbage, apple and mayonnaise for slaw and pile into the rolls with pork.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 75°C and will be well above that when pull-apart tender; cool leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.
Contains gluten and egg.

title: Budget Brown Lentil Ragu over Spaghetti
summary: Brown lentils and grated carrot make a thick, cheap bolognese that feeds a family for a few dollars.

steps.text: Soften the onion, carrot and garlic in the oil for 6 minutes.
Add the lentils, tomatoes, stock, oregano and salt and simmer for 25 minutes, until the lentils are tender and the sauce is thick.
Boil the spaghetti for 10 minutes until al dente, drain and serve with the sauce.

notes: Naturally vegan. About $2.50 a serve.
Contains gluten.

title: Budget Egg Fried Rice with Frozen Veg
summary: A cheap, speedy fried rice with eggs and frozen vegetables, ready in 15 minutes.

steps.text: Scramble the eggs in half the oil for 1 minute until just set, then remove.
Fry the garlic and vegetables in the remaining oil for 3 minutes, add the rice and stir-fry for 3 minutes until piping hot.
Return the egg, add the soy sauce, sesame oil and spring onion and toss through.

notes: Food safety: cook eggs until set; use rice that was chilled within 1 hour of cooking and eat leftovers within 1 day, reheated until steaming hot.
Contains egg, soy and sesame. About $1.80 a serve.

title: Budget Sausage and Veg Tray Bake with Mustard
summary: Cheap pork sausages roast with potato, carrot and onion, finished with a mustard dressing.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 210°C (190°C fan). Toss the potato, carrot, onion, oil and salt on a large tray and roast for 15 minutes.
Add the sausages and roast for 25 minutes more, turning once, until golden and the sausages reach 75°C in the centre.
Whisk the mustard and vinegar and toss through the tray to serve.

notes: Food safety: pork sausages must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink; cool leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Contains gluten and mustard. About $3 a serve.

title: Budget Chickpea and Spinach Curry with Rice
summary: Pantry chickpeas, tinned tomatoes and frozen spinach make a very cheap, filling vegan curry.

steps.text: Soften the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes, add the curry powder and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the chickpeas, tomatoes, water and salt and simmer for 12 minutes, then stir in the spinach for 3 minutes until hot.
