Cook the rice in boiling water for 12 minutes until tender and serve with the curry. About $1.60 a serve.

notes: Naturally vegan.

title: Budget Bean and Cheese Quesadillas with Salsa
summary: Crisp tortillas filled with refried-style beans, cheese and corn, served with quick tomato salsa.

items.raw: 1 can black beans, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Mash half the beans with the cumin, then mix with the whole beans, corn and cheese.
Spread over four tortillas, top with the rest and cook in the oil in a frying pan for 3 minutes a side, until golden and the cheese has melted.
Mix the tomato, onion, lime juice and salt and serve with the cut quesadillas.

notes: Contains gluten and milk. About $2.20 a serve.

title: Five-Ingredient Baked Chicken Parmigiana
summary: Crumbed chicken schnitzels baked with tomato passata and mozzarella, using just five ingredients.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Dip the chicken in the egg, then the breadcrumbs, and bake on a tray for 20 minutes, turning once, until golden.
Spoon over the passata and top with mozzarella.
Bake for 8 minutes more, until the cheese is bubbling and the chicken reaches 75°C.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; wash hands after handling raw chicken and egg, and eat leftovers within 2 days.
Contains gluten, egg and milk.

title: Five-Ingredient Creamy Tomato Chicken Thighs
summary: Chicken thighs simmered in tomato and cream with garlic, in one pan.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil for 6 minutes a side.
Add the garlic for 1 minute, pour in the tomatoes, cover and simmer for 15 minutes, until the chicken reaches 75°C.
Stir in the cream and simmer for 3 minutes. Serve with rice or bread.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink; cool leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Contains milk.

title: Five-Ingredient Honey Mustard Salmon with Potatoes
summary: Salmon fillets brushed with honey mustard and roasted over crisp baby potatoes.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the potatoes with the oil on a tray and roast for 15 minutes.
Mix the mustard and honey, brush over the salmon and place on the tray.
Roast for 10 minutes, until the salmon flakes and the potatoes are golden.

notes: Food safety: cook the salmon until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C; eat leftovers cold within 1 day.
Contains fish and mustard.

title: Five-Ingredient Peanut Noodles with Chicken
summary: Egg noodles and shredded chicken tossed in a quick peanut and soy sauce.

steps.text: Poach the chicken in simmering water for 12 minutes, until it reaches 75°C and is white throughout, then shred.
Cook the noodles for 4 minutes until tender, drain and keep a little water.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice and 3 tbsp warm noodle water, then toss through the noodles and chicken.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; eat leftovers within 2 days.
Contains peanuts, egg, soy and gluten.

title: Five-Ingredient One-Pot Garlic Prawn Rice
summary: Prawns steamed over garlicky rice in a single pot.

steps.text: Cook the garlic in the oil for 1 minute, stir in the rice, then add the stock and bring to the boil.
Cover and simmer on low for 15 minutes, until the rice is nearly tender.
Lay the prawns on top, cover and cook for 5 minutes, until pink and opaque.

notes: Food safety: cook prawns until pink and opaque; eat leftovers within 1 day and cool leftover rice within 1 hour.
Contains crustacean shellfish.

title: Pantry Staples Tuna Pasta Bake
summary: A tin of tuna, pasta, tinned tomatoes and cheese baked into a cosy dinner.

steps.text: Boil the penne for 8 minutes until just tender and drain.
Stir through the tuna, tomatoes, corn, oregano and salt and tip into a baking dish. Top with cheese.
Bake at 200°C for 20 minutes, until bubbling and golden.

notes: Contains gluten, fish and milk.

Food safety: use tinned tuna within its date and eat leftovers within 2 days. Cooked rice, pasta and legumes spoil quickly: cool leftovers fast, refrigerate within 1 hour, eat within 2 days and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Pantry Staples Rice and Lentil Kitchari
summary: A soothing one-pot of rice and split red lentils with turmeric and cumin.

steps.text: Fry the cumin seeds in the oil for 30 seconds until fragrant, stir in the turmeric and coriander, then add the rice, lentils, salt and water.
Simmer, partly covered, for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until everything is soft and porridge-like.
Top with ghee and serve hot.

notes: Contains milk (ghee). Use oil for vegan.

title: Pantry Staples Baked Bean and Egg Tray
summary: Baked beans, onion and spice with eggs baked on top, served with toast.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add the paprika and baked beans and simmer for 5 minutes.
Make four wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 6 minutes, until the whites are set.
Season with pepper once the eggs are set and serve with toast.

notes: Food safety: cook eggs until the whites are set; eat leftovers the same day.
Contains egg and gluten.

title: Pantry Staples Creamy Chickpea and Tomato Pasta
summary: Tinned chickpeas and tomatoes simmered into a rich sauce, tossed through pasta.

steps.text: Boil the pasta for 11 minutes until al dente, saving a cup of cooking water.
Soften the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes, add the chickpeas, tomatoes, salt and chilli and simmer for 10 minutes, until thick.
Stir in the cream, toss through the pasta and loosen with cooking water.

notes: Contains gluten and milk.

title: Pantry Staples Potato and Egg Frittata
summary: A thick potato, onion and egg frittata that needs nothing from the shops but the staples.

steps.text: Cook the potato and onion in the oil in an ovenproof frying pan for 12 minutes, until tender.
Beat the eggs with salt and pepper, pour over and cook on low heat for 5 minutes until the edges set.
Bake at 190°C for 8 minutes, until the centre is firm and golden.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the centre is firm; eat leftovers within 2 days.
Contains egg.

title: Meal-Prep Chicken Burrito Bowls for the Week
summary: Five lunch-and-dinner containers of spiced chicken, rice, black beans and corn that keep for days.

items.raw: 1 can black beans, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Cook the rice in boiling water for 12 minutes until tender and drain.
Toss the chicken with the spices, salt and oil and cook in a hot pan for 8 minutes, until it reaches 75°C and is golden.
Divide the rice, chicken, beans, corn and tomato among five containers and finish with lime juice and coriander.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; cool the boxes within 1 hour, refrigerate and eat within 3 days; reheat until steaming hot.

title: Meal-Prep Turkey Meatballs with Roast Veg and Quinoa
summary: Baked turkey meatballs, roast vegetables and quinoa packed for four easy meals.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Mix the turkey, egg, breadcrumbs, garlic, oregano and salt and roll into 20 meatballs.
Place on a tray with the vegetables tossed in the oil and bake for 25 minutes, until the meatballs reach 75°C.
Simmer the quinoa in 3 cups water for 15 minutes until tender, then divide among four containers with the meatballs and vegetables.

notes: Food safety: turkey mince must reach 75°C in the centre; refrigerate within 1 hour and eat within 3 days.
Contains egg and gluten.

title: Meal-Prep Teriyaki Tofu and Vegetable Rice Boxes
summary: Crisp baked tofu and broccoli in sweet teriyaki sauce over rice, packed for the work week.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Roast the tofu in the oil with the broccoli and carrot for 20 minutes, until the tofu is golden.
Simmer the soy sauce, mirin, honey and ginger for 3 minutes until syrupy, then toss through the tofu and vegetables.
Divide the rice and tofu among four boxes and top with sesame seeds.

notes: Food safety: use rice cooled within 1 hour; refrigerate and eat within 3 days.
Contains soy, gluten and sesame.

title: Meal-Prep Beef and Sweet Potato Chilli
summary: A hearty chilli with sweet potato and beans that freezes and reheats beautifully.

items.raw: 1 can kidney beans, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Soften the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes, add the mince and brown for 8 minutes.
Add the sweet potato, beans, tomatoes, spices, salt and stock and simmer for 30 minutes, until the sweet potato is tender and the beef reaches 75°C.
Cool and divide into six containers.

notes: Food safety: beef mince must reach 75°C; cool within 1 hour and refrigerate for 3 days or freeze for 3 months; reheat until steaming hot.

title: Meal-Prep Souvlaki-Style Chicken Boxes with Cucumber Yoghurt
summary: Lemon-oregano chicken, rice, cucumber, tomato and tzatziki in four grab-and-go boxes.

steps.text: Toss the chicken with the oil, lemon juice, oregano, garlic and salt. Cook in a hot pan or grill for 14 minutes, until it reaches 75°C and is golden.
Cook the rice in boiling water for 12 minutes until tender.
Slice the chicken and divide among four boxes with the rice, cucumber, tomato and yoghurt.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C; cool within 1 hour, refrigerate and eat within 3 days.
Contains milk.

title: High-Protein Chicken and Quinoa Power Bowl
summary: Grilled chicken breast over quinoa with edamame, avocado and a lemon-tahini dressing.

steps.text: Simmer the quinoa in 2 cups water for 15 minutes until tender and the water is absorbed.
Season the chicken with paprika, salt and oil and cook in a hot pan for 6 minutes a side, until it reaches 75°C and is white throughout.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice and 2 tbsp water, slice the chicken and serve over the quinoa with edamame, avocado and tomatoes.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; eat leftovers within 2 days.
Contains sesame and soy.

title: High-Protein Beef and Egg Rice Bowl
summary: Lean beef mince with ginger and soy over rice, topped with a fried egg and greens.

steps.text: Brown the mince in the oil for 6 minutes until cooked through, add the garlic, ginger and soy sauce and cook for 2 minutes.
Fry the eggs for 3 minutes until the whites are set.
Serve the beef over rice with spinach, eggs, sesame oil and spring onion.

notes: Food safety: beef mince must reach 75°C in the centre and the egg whites must be set; eat leftovers within 2 days.
Contains egg, soy and sesame.

title: High-Protein Turkey Chilli with Black Beans
summary: A lean, smoky turkey and black bean chilli that gives more than 40 g of protein a bowl.

items.raw: 2 can black beans, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Soften the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes, add the mince and spices and brown for 8 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, beans and stock and simmer for 20 minutes, until thick and the turkey reaches 75°C.
Serve with a spoonful of yoghurt.

notes: Food safety: turkey mince must reach 75°C; refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.
Contains milk.

title: High-Protein Salmon and Sweet Potato Tray with Greens
summary: Salmon fillets with roasted sweet potato and green beans, a recovery dinner rich in protein and omega-3.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Roast the sweet potato in half the oil for 15 minutes.
Add the salmon and beans with the remaining oil and salt and roast for 10 minutes, until the salmon flakes easily.
Serve the salmon on the sweet potato and beans with lemon wedges for squeezing.

notes: Food safety: cook salmon until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C; eat leftovers cold within 1 day.
Contains fish.

title: High-Protein Lean Lamb Kofta Bowls with Lentils
summary: Grilled lean lamb koftas over spiced lentils with yoghurt and cucumber.

steps.text: Mix the lamb, cumin, coriander, garlic and half the salt and shape into 12 koftas.
Simmer the lentils in water for 20 minutes until tender, drain and toss with the oil, lemon juice and remaining salt.
Grill the koftas for 10 minutes, turning, until browned and they reach 75°C, and serve over the lentils with yoghurt, cucumber and tomato.

notes: Food safety: lamb mince must reach 75°C in the centre; eat leftovers within 2 days.
Contains milk.

title: High-Protein Tofu and Edamame Stir-Fry with Brown Rice
summary: Firm tofu, edamame and broccoli in a ginger soy sauce, a plant-based high-protein dinner.

steps.text: Fry the tofu in the oil for 6 minutes until golden on all sides, then set aside.
Stir-fry the broccoli, edamame, garlic and ginger for 4 minutes until the broccoli is tender-crisp.
Return the tofu, add the soy sauce and sesame oil and toss for 1 minute, then serve over rice.

notes: Contains soy, gluten and sesame.

title: High-Protein Chicken Mince Lettuce Cups with Rice
summary: Chicken mince with water chestnuts and hoisin in crisp lettuce cups, with rice on the side.

steps.text: Cook the mince in the oil for 6 minutes, breaking it up, until cooked through and no pink remains.
Add the garlic, ginger and carrot for 2 minutes, then the hoisin and soy sauce and cook for 1 minute.
Spoon into the lettuce leaves, scatter with spring onion and serve with rice.

notes: Food safety: chicken mince must reach 75°C throughout with no pink; eat leftovers within 2 days.
Contains soy and gluten.

title: Pregnancy-Friendly Well-Cooked Chicken and Vegetable Bake
summary: Fully cooked chicken thighs with pumpkin, spinach and brown rice, rich in iron, folate and protein.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 210°C (190°C fan). Toss the chicken, pumpkin and onion with the oil, cumin and salt on a tray.
Roast for 40 minutes, until the chicken reaches 75°C, juices run clear and the pumpkin is tender.
Wilt the spinach on the hot tray for 2 minutes, squeeze over lemon and serve with rice.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; reheat leftovers until steaming hot and eat within 2 days. Suitable in pregnancy because all meat is well cooked; wash the spinach well.

title: Pregnancy-Friendly Baked Salmon with Sweet Potato Mash
summary: Well-cooked salmon, a low-mercury fish rich in omega-3, with creamy sweet potato mash and peas.

steps.text: Boil the sweet potato for 15 minutes until soft, drain and mash with the butter and half the salt.
Bake the salmon with the oil at 200°C for 12 minutes, until opaque and flaking all the way through.
Simmer the peas for 3 minutes until hot and serve everything with lemon.

notes: Food safety: cook salmon until opaque all the way through, at least 63°C and ideally flaking; do not eat it raw or lightly cooked while pregnant. Salmon is low in mercury; limit to 2 to 3 serves of low-mercury fish a week.
Contains fish and milk.

title: Pregnancy-Friendly Beef and Spinach Pasta Bake
summary: A well-cooked, iron-rich pasta bake of beef mince, spinach and pasteurised cheese.

steps.text: Boil the penne for 8 minutes until just tender and drain.

Soften the onion and garlic in the oil for 4 minutes, add the mince and cook for 8 minutes until browned, then add the tomatoes, oregano and salt and simmer for 8 minutes. Stir in the spinach until wilted.
Mix with the pasta, top with mozzarella and bake at 200°C for 15 minutes, until the cheese is golden and the centre is steaming hot at 75°C.

notes: Food safety: beef mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink; use pasteurised cheese and eat leftovers within 2 days. Pregnancy-friendly: everything is cooked until steaming hot.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Pregnancy-Friendly Lentil and Vegetable Shepherd's Pie
summary: A folate-rich lentil and vegetable pie under golden mash, fully cooked and suitable for pregnancy.

steps.text: Soften the onion, carrot and garlic in the oil for 6 minutes, add the lentils, paste and stock and simmer for 25 minutes until the lentils are tender. Stir in the peas.
Boil the potatoes for 15 minutes until soft, then mash with the butter, milk and salt.
Spread the mash over the lentils and bake at 200°C for 20 minutes, until golden and bubbling hot.

notes: Contains milk. Use olive oil spread and plant milk for vegan.

title: Pregnancy-Friendly Fully Cooked Egg and Veg Fried Rice
summary: A veg-packed fried rice with firmly cooked eggs and no raw ingredients, served piping hot.

steps.text: Cook the egg in half the oil, stirring, for 2 minutes until completely set and no liquid remains, then remove.
Fry the carrot and garlic in the remaining oil for 3 minutes, add the rice and peas and stir-fry for 4 minutes, until steaming hot.
Return the egg, add the soy sauce and spring onion and toss through.

notes: Food safety: eggs must be fully set with a firm yolk; use rice that was cooled and refrigerated within 1 hour and eat within 1 day, reheated until steaming hot. Pregnancy-friendly.
Contains egg, soy and gluten.

title: Easy Teen Cook: Pan-Fried Chicken Quesadillas
summary: A first-cook recipe: shredded chicken and cheese in a tortilla, crisped in a frying pan.

steps.text: Mix the chicken with the cumin, salsa and cheese.
Spread over four tortillas, top with the other four and fry in the oil for 3 minutes a side, until golden and the cheese has melted.
Cut into wedges and serve with sour cream.

notes: Food safety: use fully cooked chicken, reheat until steaming hot (75°C) and eat leftovers within 2 days.
Contains gluten and milk. A good first recipe for a teen: ask an adult to help with the hot pan.

title: Easy Teen Cook: One-Pot Spaghetti with Meat Sauce
summary: Everything cooks in one pot: mince, tomato and spaghetti, with almost no washing up.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 4 minutes, add the mince and brown for 8 minutes, breaking it up.
Add the tomatoes, stock, oregano and salt, bring to the boil, then add the spaghetti. Simmer for 14 minutes, stirring often, until the pasta is tender and the sauce is thick.
Top with cheese and serve.

notes: Food safety: beef mince must reach 75°C and have no pink; eat leftovers within 2 days.
Contains gluten and milk. A good first recipe for a teen: ask an adult to help with the boiling pot.

title: Easy Teen Cook: Sheet-Pan Beef Nachos
summary: A tray of corn chips, taco beef, beans and melted cheese, cooked mostly in the oven.

items.raw: 1 can black beans, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Brown the mince in the oil for 8 minutes, add the seasoning and water and cook for 3 minutes until thick and no pink remains.
Spread the chips on a tray, scatter over the beef and beans and top with cheese.
Bake at 200°C for 8 minutes, until the cheese is melted and bubbling, then top with tomato, sour cream and avocado.

notes: Food safety: beef mince must reach 75°C with no pink; eat leftovers within 2 days.
Contains milk. A good first recipe for a teen: ask an adult to help with the hot oven.

title: Easy Teen Cook: Cheesy Veggie Omelette with Toast
summary: A simple three-egg omelette with cheese and capsicum, served with buttered toast.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs with the salt. Soften the capsicum in half the butter in a small frying pan for 2 minutes.
Pour in the eggs and cook on medium heat for 3 minutes, until the base is set and the top is nearly set.
Add the cheese, fold the omelette over and cook for 1 minute more, until the egg is firm. Serve with buttered toast.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until firm with no runny egg left, and eat straight away.
Contains egg, milk and gluten. A good first recipe for a teen.

title: Easy Teen Cook: Chicken and Veg Noodle Stir-Fry
summary: A fast stir-fry with chicken, frozen stir-fry vegetables and noodles in a bottled sauce.

steps.text: Soak the noodles in boiling water for 4 minutes until tender and drain.
Stir-fry the chicken in the oil for 5 minutes until white throughout, add the garlic and vegetables and cook for 4 minutes.
Add the noodles, soy sauce and oyster sauce and toss for 2 minutes until hot.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; eat leftovers within 2 days.
Contains gluten, egg and soy. A good first recipe for a teen: ask an adult to help with the hot wok.

title: Easy Teen Cook: Baked Sausage and Potato Tray
summary: Chop, toss and bake: sausages, potato and onion on one tray with nothing tricky.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 210°C (190°C fan). Toss the potato and onion with the oil, herbs and salt on a tray.
Add the sausages and bake for 35 minutes, turning once, until golden and cooked through.
Boil the peas for 3 minutes until tender and serve alongside.

notes: Food safety: pork sausages must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink; eat leftovers within 2 days.
Contains gluten. A good first recipe for a teen: ask an adult to help with the hot oven.

title: Easy Teen Cook: Tuna and Sweetcorn Patties
summary: Pan-fried patties made from tinned tuna, corn and egg, served with a squeeze of lemon.

steps.text: Mix the tuna, corn, eggs, breadcrumbs and spring onion and shape into 8 patties.
Fry in the oil for 4 minutes a side, until golden and firm all the way through.
Serve hot with lemon wedges.

notes: Food safety: cook patties until firm and steaming hot (75°C) in the centre because they contain raw egg when mixed; eat leftovers within 2 days.
Contains fish, egg and gluten. A good first recipe for a teen.

title: Air-Fryer Honey Garlic Chicken Thighs with Broccoli
summary: Sticky honey garlic chicken thighs and broccoli, done in 20 minutes in the air fryer.

steps.text: Marinate the chicken in the soy sauce, honey, garlic and ginger for 10 minutes, then air-fry at 190°C for 15 minutes, turning once, until golden and the juices run clear.
Toss the broccoli with the oil and air-fry for the last 6 minutes, until tender.
Brush the chicken with any remaining marinade and serve with rice.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; do not reuse raw marinade unless boiled, and eat leftovers within 2 days.
Contains soy and gluten.

title: Air-Fryer Barramundi with Lemon Pepper and Sweet Potato Chips
summary: Flaky barramundi and crisp sweet potato chips, both cooked in the air fryer.

steps.text: Toss the sweet potato with half the oil and salt and air-fry at 200°C for 18 minutes, shaking twice, until crisp.
Rub the fish with the remaining oil and lemon pepper and air-fry for the last 8 minutes, until opaque and flaking.
Serve with lemon wedges and mayonnaise.

notes: Food safety: cook fish until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C; eat leftovers within 1 day.
Contains fish and egg.

title: Slow-Cooker Moroccan Chicken and Apricot Tagine
summary: Chicken thighs, apricots and chickpeas in warm spices, simmered until tender and served with couscous.

steps.text: Put the chicken, onion, garlic, spices, chickpeas, tomatoes, apricots, stock and salt into the slow cooker and stir. Cook on low for 5 hours, until the chicken is tender and reaches 75°C.
Cover the couscous with 1.5 cups boiling water for 5 minutes until fluffy.
Serve the tagine over couscous with coriander.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C; cool leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Contains gluten.

title: Slow-Cooker Creamy Tuscan Chicken and White Bean Stew
summary: Chicken thigh, cannellini beans, sun-dried tomato and spinach in a creamy garlic sauce.

items.raw: 2 can cannellini beans, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Put the chicken, beans, onion, garlic, sun-dried tomato, stock, herbs and salt into the slow cooker. Cook on low for 5 hours, until the chicken is tender and reaches 75°C.
Stir in the cream and spinach and cook for 10 minutes more, until the spinach has wilted.
Ladle into bowls and serve with warm crusty bread to mop up the sauce.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C; cool leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Contains milk.

title: Feed-a-Crowd Sheet-Pan Fajitas for Ten
summary: Spiced chicken, capsicum and onion roasted on two trays and served with tortillas and toppings.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 230°C (210°C fan). Toss the chicken, capsicum and onion with the oil, seasoning and salt on two large trays.
Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring once, until the chicken reaches 75°C and the vegetables are charred at the edges.
Warm the tortillas and serve with sour cream, cheese and lime.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; cool leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Date Night Lamb Cutlets with Minted Pea Puree and Roast Potatoes
summary: Pink-centred lamb cutlets over a bright pea and mint puree with crisp roast potatoes.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Roast the potatoes with half the oil and salt for 25 minutes, until golden and crisp.
Simmer the peas for 4 minutes until tender, blend with the butter, mint and a splash of cooking water until smooth.
Rub the cutlets with the garlic and remaining oil and sear for 3 minutes a side, then rest for 3 minutes. Serve on the puree with the potatoes.

notes: Food safety: lamb cutlets are whole cuts: sear all sides and rest, aiming for 63°C for medium or 71°C for well done; eat leftovers within 2 days.
Contains milk.

title: Date Night Chicken Marsala with Mushrooms and Mash
summary: Golden chicken breasts in a glossy mushroom and marsala sauce with creamy mash.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes for 15 minutes until soft, drain and mash with half the butter, the milk and half the salt.
Sear the chicken in the oil for 5 minutes a side until golden and cooked to 75°C, then set aside.
Cook the mushrooms and garlic in the remaining butter for 5 minutes, add the marsala and stock and simmer for 5 minutes until syrupy. Return the chicken for 1 minute and serve on the mash.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; eat leftovers within 2 days.
Contains milk.

title: Date Night Seared Scallops with Lemon Butter Linguine
summary: Golden scallops on lemony linguine with garlic and parsley, a restaurant-style meal for two.

steps.text: Boil the linguine for 10 minutes until al dente and keep half a cup of water.
Sear the scallops in the oil for 90 seconds a side, until golden outside and just opaque in the centre.
Melt the butter with the garlic for 1 minute, add the lemon zest, juice, linguine and a splash of water and toss with the parsley. Top with scallops.

notes: Food safety: cook scallops until opaque and firm; eat the same day.
Contains gluten, shellfish and milk.

title: Date Night Creamy Mushroom Gnocchi with Spinach
summary: Pillowy gnocchi in a garlic and thyme mushroom cream, finished with spinach.

steps.text: Boil the gnocchi for 3 minutes until they float and drain.
Cook the mushrooms in the oil for 6 minutes until golden, add the garlic and thyme for 1 minute, then the cream and salt and simmer for 3 minutes.
Toss through the gnocchi and spinach until wilted and top with the cheese.

notes: Contains gluten and milk.

title: Date Night Miso-Glazed Salmon with Sesame Greens and Rice
summary: Sweet-savoury miso salmon with bok choy and steamed rice.

steps.text: Stir the miso, mirin and honey together and brush over the salmon.
Grill or bake at 220°C for 10 minutes, until caramelised and the fish flakes.
Pan-fry the bok choy in the sesame oil for 3 minutes until tender and serve with the salmon, rice and sesame seeds.

notes: Food safety: cook salmon until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C; eat leftovers cold within 1 day.
Contains fish, soy and sesame.

title: Date Night Steak Diane with Green Beans
summary: Seared eye fillet in a quick Dijon, cream and Worcestershire pan sauce.

steps.text: Season the steaks and sear in the oil for 3 to 4 minutes a side, then rest on a plate for 5 minutes.
Soften the onion in the butter for 3 minutes, add the brandy and simmer for 1 minute, then add the Worcestershire, mustard and cream and cook for 3 minutes until slightly thick.
Steam the beans for 5 minutes until tender and serve with the steak and sauce.

notes: Food safety: whole steaks can be served medium (63°C) after resting; use a clean plate for cooked steak.
Contains milk and mustard.

title: Cooking for One: Sheet-Pan Chicken Thigh with Roast Veg
summary: A single chicken thigh with potato and broccoli roasted on a small tray.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the potato with half the oil and salt and roast for 15 minutes.
Rub the chicken with the paprika and remaining oil, add to the tray with the broccoli and roast for 20 minutes, until the chicken reaches 75°C and the skin is crisp.
Squeeze over the lemon juice and serve.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C at the bone with no pink; eat leftovers within 2 days.

title: Cooking for One: Ten-Minute Prawn and Veg Stir-Fry
summary: A quick prawn stir-fry with capsicum and snow peas in a garlic soy sauce, over noodles.

steps.text: Cook the noodles in boiling water for 4 minutes until tender and drain.
Stir-fry the capsicum and snow peas in the oil for 3 minutes, add the garlic and prawns and cook for 2 minutes until pink and opaque.
Add the soy sauce and honey, toss with the noodles for 1 minute.

notes: Food safety: cook prawns until pink and opaque; eat the same day.
Contains shellfish, egg, gluten and soy.

title: Cooking for One: Lamb Mince Flatbread Pizza
summary: Spiced lamb mince on a flatbread with feta and yoghurt, ready in 20 minutes.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil with the cumin and cinnamon for 5 minutes until cooked through.
Spread the flatbread with tomato paste and top with the lamb, onion and feta.
Bake at 220°C for 8 minutes, until crisp at the edges and the lamb reaches 75°C. Drizzle with yoghurt.

notes: Food safety: lamb mince must reach 75°C in the centre; eat the same day.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Cooking for One: Ten-Minute Chickpea Curry
summary: A small-batch curry of chickpeas, tomato and spinach with curry powder, served on rice.

steps.text: Soften the onion and garlic in the oil for 3 minutes, add the curry powder for 30 seconds.
Add the chickpeas and tomatoes and simmer for 6 minutes, until thick.
Stir in the spinach until wilted and serve over the rice.

notes: Naturally vegan.

title: Cooking for One: Pan-Fried Fish with Lemon Caper Butter
summary: A crisp barramundi fillet with lemon caper butter, served with steamed greens and potato.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes for 12 minutes until tender, adding the beans for the last 3 minutes, then drain.
Pan-fry the fish in the oil for 3 to 4 minutes a side, until golden and opaque all the way through.
Melt the butter with the capers and lemon juice for 1 minute, spoon over the fish and scatter with parsley.

notes: Food safety: cook fish until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C; eat the same day.
Contains fish and milk.

title: Crowd-Pleasing Slow-Cooker Chicken Tinga Tacos for Twelve
summary: Shredded chipotle chicken with tomato and onion, piled into corn tortillas with toppings.

steps.text: Put the chicken, onion, garlic, tomatoes, chipotle, oregano and salt in the slow cooker. Cook on low for 5 hours, until the chicken reaches 75°C and shreds easily.
Shred the chicken and stir it through the sauce.
Warm the tortillas and serve with sour cream, coriander and lime.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C; cool leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Contains milk.

title: Crowd-Pleasing Baked Ziti for Ten
summary: A big dish of pasta, rich tomato sauce, ricotta and melted mozzarella with sausage.

steps.text: Boil the penne for 8 minutes until just tender and drain.
Cook the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes, add the sausage meat and brown for 8 minutes, then add the tomatoes, oregano and salt and simmer for 12 minutes.
Mix the pasta with the sauce and ricotta in a large dish, top with mozzarella and bake at 200°C for 20 minutes, until bubbling and golden.

notes: Food safety: pork sausage meat must reach 75°C in the centre; cool leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Crowd-Pleasing Honey Soy Chicken Wings for a Party
summary: Sticky oven-baked wings with a honey, soy and garlic glaze, sized for ten.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Mix the soy sauce, honey, garlic, ginger and sesame oil and toss the wings through.
Roast on two lined trays for 45 minutes, turning and basting twice, until sticky, golden and cooked to 75°C.
Scatter with sesame seeds and spring onion.

notes: Food safety: wings must reach 75°C with no pink at the bone; wash hands and trays after touching raw chicken, and eat leftovers within 2 days.
Contains soy, gluten and sesame.

title: Crowd-Pleasing Vegetable and Chickpea Biryani for Ten
summary: A fragrant baked rice dish with vegetables, chickpeas and whole spices.

steps.text: Fry the onion in the oil for 12 minutes until golden, add the garlic, ginger and spice mix for 1 minute, then the carrot, cauliflower, chickpeas and yoghurt and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the rice, stock and salt, cover and simmer on low for 15 minutes, until the rice is tender.
Fold in the peas and coriander, cover for 5 minutes and fluff before serving.

notes: Contains milk. Use coconut yoghurt for vegan.
Cool leftover rice within 1 hour and eat within 1 day.

title: Budget Smoky Cannellini and Pasta Pot
summary: Tinned beans, pasta and tomato simmered in one pan with smoked paprika, for about $2 a serve.

items.raw: 1 can cannellini beans, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Soften the onion and garlic in the oil for 4 minutes, add the paprika for 30 seconds, then the tomatoes, beans, water and salt.
Bring to the boil, add the pasta and simmer for 12 minutes, stirring, until the pasta is tender and the sauce is thick.
Scatter with the grated cheese and serve straight from the pan while hot.

notes: Contains gluten and milk.

title: Budget Potato and Egg Curry with Roti
summary: Hard-boiled eggs and potato in a tomato and spice gravy, served with warm roti.

steps.text: Soften the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes, add the curry powder for 1 minute, then the tomatoes, potato, water and salt.
Simmer for 20 minutes, until the potato is tender and the gravy is thick, then add the halved eggs and warm for 2 minutes.
Warm the roti and serve with the curry.

notes: Food safety: boil eggs for 10 minutes until the yolk is firm; eat leftovers within 2 days.
Contains egg and gluten. About $2.40 a serve.

title: Budget Sausage Hotpot with Mash
summary: Pork sausages, baked beans and carrot in a savoury gravy over cheap creamy mash.

steps.text: Brown the sausages in the oil for 6 minutes, slice them and cook the onion and carrot in the pan for 5 minutes.
Add the beans, stock and Worcestershire, return the sausages and simmer for 20 minutes, until thick and the sausages reach 75°C.
Boil the potatoes for 15 minutes until soft, mash with the butter and milk and serve with the hotpot.

notes: Food safety: pork sausages must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink; eat leftovers within 2 days.
Contains gluten and milk. About $3 a serve.

title: High-Protein Greek Yoghurt Chicken Pasta Bake
summary: Chicken, wholemeal pasta, spinach and a creamy Greek yoghurt sauce for a lighter, high-protein bake.

steps.text: Boil the pasta for 9 minutes until just tender and drain.
Cook the chicken in the oil for 6 minutes until white throughout, add the garlic, tomatoes, oregano and salt and simmer for 5 minutes. Stir in the spinach, yoghurt and pasta.
Top with mozzarella and bake at 200°C for 15 minutes, until golden and the chicken reaches 75°C.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; eat leftovers within 2 days.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Pregnancy-Friendly Slow-Cooked Beef and Vegetable Casserole
summary: A slow-cooked, iron-rich beef casserole with vegetables, cooked well beyond medium.

steps.text: Brown the beef in the oil in batches for 6 minutes and place in the slow cooker with the onion, carrot, celery, garlic, paste, stock, potato and salt.
Cook on low for 7 hours, until the beef is fall-apart tender.
Stir in the peas for 10 minutes until hot.

notes: Food safety: beef must be cooked until fall-apart tender and well above 75°C; reheat leftovers until steaming hot and eat within 3 days. Pregnancy-friendly.

title: Pregnancy-Friendly Baked Chicken and Vegetable Risotto
summary: An oven-baked risotto with chicken, pumpkin and spinach, cooked until steaming hot.

steps.text: Cook the chicken and onion in the oil in an ovenproof pot for 6 minutes, add the pumpkin and rice for 1 minute.
Pour in the hot stock and salt, bring to a simmer, cover and bake at 190°C for 30 minutes, until the rice is tender and the chicken reaches 75°C.
Stir in the spinach until wilted and top with cheese.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C; use pasteurised cheese and reheat leftovers until steaming hot, eating within 1 day. Pregnancy-friendly.
Contains milk.

title: Easy Teen Cook: Sheet-Pan Chicken Nuggets and Wedges
summary: Homemade crumbed chicken nuggets and potato wedges baked on one tray.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the potato wedges with half the oil, salt and paprika on a tray and roast for 10 minutes.
Dip the chicken in egg, then breadcrumbs mixed with the remaining oil, and add to the tray.
Bake for 20 minutes, turning once, until the nuggets are golden and reach 75°C and the wedges are crisp. Serve with tomato sauce.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; wash hands after handling raw chicken and egg, and eat leftovers within 2 days.
Contains egg and gluten. A good first recipe for a teen: ask an adult to help with the hot oven.

title: One-Pot Creamy Tomato and Basil Penne
summary: Penne cooks right in a garlicky tomato sauce, finished with cream and fresh basil.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the oil in a wide pot for 4 minutes, add the garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, stock, salt and penne, bring to the boil, then simmer for 12 minutes, stirring often, until the pasta is tender and the sauce is thick.
Stir through the cream and basil and heat for 1 minute until glossy.

notes: Contains gluten and milk. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.

title: One-Pot Chicken Alfredo Pasta
summary: Chicken, fettuccine and a creamy garlic sauce made in a single pot with no draining.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil for 5 minutes until golden, then add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the stock, milk, fettuccine, salt and pepper, bring to a simmer and cook for 12 minutes, stirring often, until the pasta is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Stir in the cream and parmesan for 2 minutes until silky and the chicken is cooked through.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: One-Pot Beef Bolognese Spaghetti
summary: Spaghetti simmers straight in a rich beef and tomato sauce, so there is only one pot to wash.

steps.text: Brown the mince in the oil for 6 minutes until no pink remains, then add the onion, carrot and garlic for 4 minutes until soft.
Stir in the tomatoes, paste, stock, oregano, salt and the spaghetti snapped in half, and bring to the boil until bubbling.
Simmer for 13 minutes, stirring often, until the spaghetti is tender and the sauce clings.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C right through with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Contains gluten.

title: One-Pot Sausage and Kale Orecchiette
summary: Sausage, kale and orecchiette in a garlicky tomato broth, all cooked together.

steps.text: Brown the sausage in the oil for 6 minutes, breaking it into chunks, then add the onion and garlic for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes, stock, chilli and orecchiette and simmer for 12 minutes, stirring often, until the pasta is nearly tender.
Stir in the kale for 3 minutes until wilted and the pasta is cooked.

notes: Food safety: pork sausage must reach 75°C with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Contains gluten.

title: One-Pot Lemon Prawn Linguine
summary: Linguine cooked in garlicky lemon stock, topped with quick-seared prawns and parsley.

steps.text: Sear the prawns in half the oil for 2 minutes until pink, then set aside.
Soften the garlic and chilli in the remaining oil for 30 seconds, add the stock, lemon juice, salt and linguine and simmer for 11 minutes, stirring, until tender and the liquid is mostly absorbed.
Return the prawns with the zest and parsley and toss for 1 minute until hot.

notes: Food safety: cook prawns until pink and opaque; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.
Contains gluten and crustacean shellfish.

title: One-Pot Mushroom and Spinach Pasta
summary: Creamy-tasting vegan pasta with mushrooms, spinach and garlic cooked in one pot.

steps.text: Cook the mushrooms in the oil for 6 minutes until golden, then add the onion and garlic for 3 minutes until soft.
Add the stock, thyme, salt and penne and simmer for 11 minutes, stirring often, until the pasta is tender.
Stir in the coconut milk and spinach for 2 minutes until the spinach has wilted.

notes: Contains gluten. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.

title: Fakeaway Chicken Tikka Masala with Basmati Rice
summary: A mild, creamy tikka masala with yoghurt-marinated chicken, just like the takeaway.

steps.text: Mix the chicken with the yoghurt, half the garam masala, turmeric and paprika and marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Fry the onion in the oil for 6 minutes, add the garlic, ginger and remaining garam masala for 1 minute, then add the tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes until thick.
Add the chicken and simmer for 12 minutes until cooked through, then stir in the cream and salt.
Cook the rice for 12 minutes until tender, drain and serve under the curry.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; refrigerate rice within 1 hour and leftovers within 2 hours, and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk.

title: Fakeaway Sweet and Sour Chicken with Rice
summary: Crispy-coated chicken in a glossy sweet and sour sauce with capsicum and pineapple.

steps.text: Toss the chicken in the egg, then the cornflour. Fry in the oil in batches for 6 minutes until golden and cooked through, then set aside.
Whisk the tomato sauce, vinegar, sugar and soy sauce together. Stir-fry the capsicum and onion for 3 minutes, add the sauce and pineapple and simmer for 3 minutes until glossy.
Return the chicken for 1 minute to coat. Cook the rice for 12 minutes until tender and serve.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; refrigerate rice within 1 hour and leftovers within 2 hours.
Contains egg, soy and gluten.

title: Fakeaway Sichuan Peanut Chicken with Rice
summary: Spicy, tangy chicken stir-fried with peanuts, capsicum and dried chilli, served over rice.

steps.text: Toss the chicken with the cornflour. Cook the rice for 12 minutes until tender.
Stir-fry the chicken in the oil over high heat for 6 minutes until golden, add the capsicum, garlic, ginger and chilli for 2 minutes.
Add the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar and peanuts and toss for 2 minutes until the sauce is sticky and the chicken is cooked through. Scatter with spring onion and serve over the rice.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; refrigerate rice within 1 hour and leftovers within 2 hours.
Contains peanuts, soy and gluten.

title: Fakeaway Lamb Doner Kebab Bowls
summary: Spiced lamb patty slices with salad, pickled onion and garlic yoghurt, no skewer needed.

steps.text: Knead the mince with the cumin, paprika, oregano, half the garlic and the salt until sticky, then press into a flat loaf about 2cm thick.
Fry in the oil for 8 minutes a side until deeply browned and cooked to 75°C, then slice thinly.
Stir the remaining garlic and lemon juice into the yoghurt. Pile the lamb, tomato, cucumber and onion over warm flatbread and spoon on the sauce.

notes: Food safety: lamb mince must reach 75°C right through with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Fakeaway Naan Pizzas Margherita
summary: Crisp naan bases with tomato sauce, mozzarella and basil, ready from the oven in minutes.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 230°C (210°C fan) and mix the passata, garlic and oregano.
Spread the sauce over the naan, top with mozzarella and drizzle with oil. Bake on trays for 8 minutes until bubbling and golden at the edges.
Scatter with basil and serve.

notes: Contains gluten and milk. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Fakeaway Chicken Katsu Curry
summary: Crisp panko chicken with a mild, sweet Japanese-style curry sauce over rice.

steps.text: Soften the onion and carrot in a little oil for 6 minutes, stir in the garlic, curry powder and 1 tablespoon flour for 1 minute, then add the stock, soy sauce and sugar and simmer for 12 minutes until thick. Blend if you like it smooth.
Coat the chicken in flour, egg and panko. Shallow-fry in the oil for 4 minutes a side until golden and cooked to 75°C.
Cook the rice for 12 minutes until tender. Slice the chicken and serve over rice with the sauce.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; refrigerate rice within 1 hour and leftovers within 2 hours.
Contains egg, soy and gluten.

title: Fakeaway Crispy Chilli Beef
summary: Crunchy strips of beef tossed in a sticky sweet chilli sauce with capsicum and spring onion.

steps.text: Toss the beef with the egg white and cornflour. Fry in batches in the oil for 3 minutes until crisp and browned, then drain.
Stir-fry the capsicum and garlic for 2 minutes, add the sweet chilli sauce, soy sauce and vinegar and simmer for 1 minute until sticky.
Toss in the beef and spring onion for 30 seconds. Cook the rice for 12 minutes until tender and serve.

notes: Food safety: beef strips should reach 71°C with no pink; refrigerate rice within 1 hour and leftovers within 2 hours.
Contains egg, soy and gluten.

title: Fakeaway Tamarind Noodles with Prawns and Egg
summary: Rice noodles tossed with prawns, egg, bean sprouts and a tangy tamarind-style sauce.

steps.text: Soak the noodles in hot water for 8 minutes until pliable, then drain. Stir the fish sauce, sugar and lime juice together.
Stir-fry the garlic and prawns in the oil for 2 minutes until pink, push aside and scramble the eggs for 1 minute.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss for 3 minutes until tender, then add the sprouts and spring onion for 1 minute. Top with peanuts.

notes: Food safety: cook prawns until pink and opaque and eggs until set; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.
Contains egg, peanuts, crustacean shellfish and fish.

title: Lightened Cauliflower Mac and Cheese
summary: Creamy baked mac and cheese with cauliflower blended into the sauce for less fat.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Boil the macaroni for 8 minutes until just tender, then drain.
Simmer the cauliflower in the milk for 10 minutes until very soft. Blend with the flour, mustard and salt until smooth, then heat for 2 minutes until thickened and stir in the cheddar until melted.
Fold through the macaroni, tip into a dish, top with the hard cheese and breadcrumbs and bake for 15 minutes until golden.

notes: Contains gluten and milk. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.

title: Lightened Grilled Chicken Parmigiana
summary: Chicken breast under tomato sauce and melted mozzarella, grilled rather than fried.

steps.text: Simmer the tomatoes, garlic, oregano and half the salt for 10 minutes until thick.
Rub the chicken with the oil and remaining salt. Grill or pan-fry for 5 minutes a side until golden.
Top with the sauce and cheeses and grill for 4 minutes until bubbling and the chicken is 75°C. Steam the beans for 5 minutes until tender and serve alongside.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Contains milk.

title: Lightened Beef Stroganoff with Yoghurt
summary: All the creamy mushroom flavour of stroganoff using yoghurt in place of cream.

steps.text: Sear the beef in half the oil in batches for 2 minutes until browned, then set aside.
Cook the onion and mushrooms in the remaining oil for 8 minutes until golden, add the garlic, paprika and flour for 1 minute, then pour in the stock and simmer for 5 minutes until thick.
Boil the noodles for 6 minutes until tender. Off the heat stir the yoghurt and mustard into the sauce, return the beef and serve over the noodles.

notes: Food safety: beef strips should reach 71°C with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Contains gluten, egg and milk.

title: Lightened Shepherd's Pie with Cauliflower Mash
summary: Lamb and vegetable filling under a fluffy potato and cauliflower mash topping.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil for 6 minutes until no pink remains, add the onion, carrot and garlic for 5 minutes, then the paste, stock and Worcestershire sauce and simmer for 12 minutes until thick. Stir in the peas.
Boil the potato and cauliflower for 15 minutes until soft, drain and mash with the milk and salt.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Spoon the filling into a dish, top with the mash and bake for 20 minutes until golden.

notes: Food safety: lamb mince must reach 75°C right through with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Contains milk. Worcestershire sauce contains fish and gluten.

title: Lightened Chicken Pot Pie with Filo Top
summary: Creamy chicken and vegetable filling under a crisp filo lid for far less pastry.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil for 5 minutes, add the onion, carrot and leek for 6 minutes until soft, then stir in the flour for 1 minute.
Add the stock, milk and thyme and simmer for 12 minutes until thick and the chicken is cooked through. Stir in the peas.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Pour into a dish, scrunch the filo over the top, brush with butter and bake for 15 minutes until golden and crisp.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Lightened Zucchini and Beef Lasagne
summary: A pasta-light lasagne layering zucchini ribbons, beef ragu and ricotta.

steps.text: Brown the mince in the oil for 6 minutes until no pink remains, add the onion and garlic for 4 minutes, then the tomatoes, paste, oregano and salt and simmer for 15 minutes until thick.
Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Mix the ricotta and egg. Layer the ragu, zucchini, lasagne sheets and ricotta in a dish, finishing with the mozzarella.
Cover with foil and bake for 25 minutes, then uncover for 10 minutes until golden and bubbling.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C right through with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.
Contains gluten, egg and milk.

title: Lightened Sweet Potato Topped Fish Pie
summary: Salmon and white fish in a light herby sauce under a golden sweet potato mash.

steps.text: Boil the sweet potato for 15 minutes until soft, drain and mash with half the salt.

Poach the fish in the milk with the bay leaf for 4 minutes, lift out and strain the milk. Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, whisk in the milk and simmer for 4 minutes until thick, then fold in the fish, peas, dill and zest.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Spoon into a dish, top with the mash and bake for 20 minutes until golden and bubbling.

notes: Food safety: fish should be opaque and flake easily, reaching 63°C; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.
Contains fish, milk and gluten.

title: Mediterranean Baked Cod with Tomatoes, Olives and Capers
summary: Cod baked on a bed of cherry tomatoes, olives and capers with lemon and oregano.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Roast the potatoes with a third of the oil for 15 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, olives, capers, garlic, oregano and remaining oil, nestle in the cod and top with lemon.
Bake for 15 minutes until the fish flakes easily and the tomatoes have burst.

notes: Food safety: fish should be opaque and flake easily, reaching 63°C; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.
Contains fish.

title: Mediterranean Chickpea Stew with Paprika and Lemon
summary: A fragrant tomato and chickpea stew with spinach, paprika and a squeeze of lemon.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, then stir in the garlic, paprika and cumin for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, chickpeas, stock and salt and simmer for 15 minutes until thick.
Stir in the spinach and lemon juice for 2 minutes until wilted.

notes: Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 4 days.

title: Mediterranean Salmon with Herby Couscous
summary: Roasted salmon with lemon on couscous loaded with parsley, cucumber and tomato.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Rub the salmon with half the oil, lemon zest, garlic and half the salt and roast for 12 minutes until it flakes.
Pour the boiling water over the couscous with the remaining salt, cover for 5 minutes until fluffy, then fork through the remaining oil and lemon juice.
Fold in the cucumber, tomato and parsley and top with the salmon.

notes: Food safety: salmon should reach 63°C and flake easily; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.
Contains fish and gluten.

title: Blended Mushroom and Beef Burgers with Slaw
summary: Finely chopped mushrooms stretch the beef for juicy burgers with extra veg and less meat.

steps.text: Fry the mushrooms in half the oil for 6 minutes until dry and golden, then cool a little. Mix with the mince, garlic, paprika and salt and shape into 4 patties.
Cook the patties in the remaining oil for 5 minutes a side until browned and cooked to 75°C.
Toss the cabbage, carrot, yoghurt and lemon juice together and pile into toasted buns with the patties.

notes: Food safety: burger patties must reach 75°C right through with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Beef and Lentil Chilli with Rice
summary: Half the beef is swapped for lentils in a smoky chilli that feeds a crowd for less.

steps.text: Brown the mince in the oil for 6 minutes until no pink remains, then add the onion and garlic for 4 minutes until soft and stir in the spices for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, beans, lentils and stock and simmer for 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils are soft and the chilli is thick.
Cook the rice for 12 minutes until tender and serve with the chilli.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C with no pink; refrigerate rice within 1 hour and leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Cauliflower and Chickpea Tikka Tray Bake
summary: Tikka-spiced cauliflower and chickpeas roasted on one tray, served with yoghurt and rice.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Mix half the yoghurt with the spices, oil, salt and half the lemon juice and toss through the cauliflower, chickpeas and onion on a large tray.
Roast for 35 minutes, turning once, until the cauliflower is charred at the edges.
Cook the rice for 12 minutes until tender. Stir the remaining lemon juice into the remaining yoghurt and serve over the tray bake and rice.

notes: Contains milk. Refrigerate rice within 1 hour and leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Tofu and Vegetable Coconut Curry
summary: Golden tofu and seasonal vegetables simmered in a mild coconut curry sauce.

steps.text: Fry the tofu in half the oil for 8 minutes until golden on all sides, then set aside.
Soften the onion in the remaining oil for 4 minutes, stir in the garlic, ginger and curry paste for 1 minute, then add the coconut milk and stock.
Add the capsicum, beans and zucchini and simmer for 10 minutes until tender, then return the tofu with the lime juice. Cook the rice for 12 minutes until tender and serve.

notes: Contains soy. Refrigerate rice within 1 hour and leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Black Bean and Sweet Potato Enchilada Bake
summary: Roasted sweet potato and black beans rolled in tortillas under red sauce and melted cheese.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Roast the sweet potato with the oil, cumin and salt for 20 minutes until soft and golden. Mix with the beans and corn.
Simmer the passata, paprika and garlic for 5 minutes. Spread a third in a dish, fill the tortillas with the mix, roll and place seam-down.
Pour over the rest of the sauce, top with the cheddar and bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 15 minutes until bubbling.

notes: Contains gluten and milk. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.

title: Gluten-Free Chicken and Vegetable Rice Bowls
summary: Herby roast chicken and vegetables over fluffy rice, with nothing containing gluten.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the chicken and vegetables with the oil, paprika, oregano and salt on a tray.
Roast for 25 minutes, turning once, until the chicken is cooked to 75°C and the vegetables are charred.
Cook the rice for 12 minutes until tender. Spoon the chicken and vegetables over the rice and squeeze over the lemon.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; refrigerate rice within 1 hour and leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Gluten-Free Pork Meatballs with Creamy Polenta
summary: Tender pork meatballs bound with rice flour, in tomato sauce over soft polenta.

steps.text: Mix the mince, rice flour, egg, half the garlic, oregano and half the salt and roll into 16 balls. Brown in the oil for 6 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and remaining garlic and simmer for 15 minutes until the meatballs reach 75°C and the sauce is thick.
Whisk the polenta into the boiling water with the remaining salt and cook for 8 minutes, stirring, until thick. Stir in the parmesan and serve under the meatballs.

notes: Food safety: pork mince meatballs must reach 75°C right through with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Contains egg and milk.

title: Gluten-Free Beef and Potato Tray Roast
summary: Beef strips roasted with potatoes, carrots and rosemary, with a rice-flour-thickened pan sauce.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the potato, carrot and onion with two-thirds of the oil, rosemary and half the salt and roast for 25 minutes.
Toss the beef with the remaining oil and salt, add to the tray and roast for 12 minutes until browned and 71°C inside.
Whisk the rice flour into the water with the tomato paste, pour into a pan with the tray juices and simmer for 3 minutes until glossy and thick. Serve over the tray.

notes: Food safety: beef chunks should reach 71°C with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Gluten-Free Chicken and Rice Soup
summary: A soothing soup of chicken, rice and vegetables that works for the whole family.

steps.text: Soften the onion, carrot, celery and garlic in the oil for 6 minutes until tender.
Add the chicken, rice, water and salt, bring to the boil and simmer for 18 minutes until the rice is tender and the chicken reaches 75°C.
Stir in the lemon juice and parsley.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; refrigerate rice within 1 hour and leftovers within 2 hours, and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Gluten-Free Fish and Polenta Chips with Peas
summary: Crisp-coated baked fish and golden polenta chips with minty mashed peas.

steps.text: Boil the 1 cup polenta in the water with half the salt for 8 minutes until thick, pour into a tray and chill for 20 minutes, then cut into chips.

Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Coat the fish in rice flour, egg, then the dry polenta mixed with paprika. Bake the fish and chips with the oil on trays for 20 minutes until golden and the fish flakes.
Simmer the peas for 3 minutes until tender, mash with the mint and remaining salt and serve.

notes: Food safety: fish should be opaque and flake easily, reaching 63°C; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.
Contains egg and fish.

title: Dairy-Free Coconut Chicken Curry
summary: A creamy, mild curry made with coconut milk instead of cream or yoghurt.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil for 5 minutes, add the onion, garlic and ginger for 4 minutes until soft, then stir in the curry powder for 1 minute.
Add the coconut milk, tomatoes and salt and simmer for 18 minutes until thick and the chicken reaches 75°C. Stir in the spinach until wilted.
Cook the rice for 12 minutes until tender and serve.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; refrigerate rice within 1 hour and leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Dairy-Free Tuscan Chicken with Coconut Cream
summary: Chicken in a garlicky sun-dried tomato and spinach sauce, creamed with coconut milk.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes for 15 minutes until tender and drain.

Sear the chicken in the oil for 5 minutes a side until golden, then set aside. Add the garlic, tomatoes and oregano for 1 minute, pour in the stock and coconut milk and simmer for 5 minutes until slightly thick.
Return the chicken for 5 minutes until it reaches 75°C, stir in the spinach and salt until wilted and serve with the potatoes.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Dairy-Free Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry with Noodles
summary: Tender beef and broccoli in a garlicky ginger sauce tossed through egg noodles.

steps.text: Toss the beef with the cornflour. Boil the noodles for 4 minutes until tender and drain.
Stir-fry the beef in half the oil for 3 minutes until browned and 71°C inside, then set aside. Stir-fry the broccoli, garlic and ginger in the remaining oil for 3 minutes.
Add the soy sauce, honey and water and simmer for 2 minutes until glossy, then toss with the beef and noodles.

notes: Food safety: beef strips should reach 71°C with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Contains gluten, soy and egg.

title: Dairy-Free Creamy Mushroom Pasta with Coconut
summary: Garlicky mushrooms in a silky coconut sauce, with no dairy and no nuts.

steps.text: Boil the penne for 10 minutes until al dente and keep half a cup of the water.
Cook the mushrooms in the oil for 8 minutes until golden, add the garlic and thyme for 1 minute, then the wine and simmer for 2 minutes.
Add the coconut milk and salt and simmer for 3 minutes until slightly thick, stir in the spinach until wilted, then toss with the pasta and a splash of the water.

notes: Contains gluten. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.

title: Dairy-Free Salmon Fishcakes with Herby Potato
summary: Crisp salmon and potato cakes with dill and lemon, served with a green salad.

steps.text: Boil the potato for 15 minutes until soft, drain and mash with the salt. Poach the salmon in simmering water for 6 minutes until it flakes, then flake into the mash with the egg, dill and zest.
Shape into 8 cakes, press into the breadcrumbs and chill for 10 minutes.
Fry in the oil for 4 minutes a side until golden and hot through. Dress the leaves with the juice and serve.

notes: Food safety: salmon should reach 63°C and the cakes 75°C in the centre; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.
Contains fish, egg and gluten.

title: Egg-Free Chicken Schnitzel with Mustard Crumb
summary: Crunchy schnitzel where mustard and milk replace the egg, served with lemony cabbage slaw.

steps.text: Whisk the mustard into the milk. Coat the chicken in flour, then the mustard milk, then the breadcrumbs.
Shallow-fry in the oil for 4 minutes a side until golden and the chicken reaches 75°C.
Toss the cabbage with the lemon juice and salt and serve with the schnitzel.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Egg-free recipe. Contains gluten and milk.

title: Egg-Free Chickpea Burgers with Yoghurt Sauce
summary: Herby chickpea patties that hold together with oats rather than egg.

steps.text: Mash the chickpeas roughly and mix with the oats, spices, half the garlic, parsley, half the lemon juice and the salt. Rest 5 minutes, then shape into 4 patties.
Fry in the oil for 5 minutes a side until crisp and golden.
Stir the remaining garlic and lemon juice into the yoghurt and serve the patties in buns with tomato and the sauce.

notes: Egg-free recipe. Contains gluten and milk. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.

title: Egg-Free Spaghetti with Lentil Ragu
summary: A rich lentil and carrot ragu over dried spaghetti, a budget meal with no eggs or meat.

steps.text: Soften the onion, carrot, celery and garlic in the oil for 6 minutes until tender.
Add the lentils, tomatoes, stock, oregano and salt and simmer for 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils are soft and the sauce is thick.
Boil the spaghetti for 10 minutes until al dente, drain and toss with the ragu.

notes: Egg-free recipe. Contains gluten. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.

title: Egg-Free Pork and Apple Meatballs with Mash
summary: Juicy meatballs held together with breadcrumbs and milk, with grated apple and creamy mash.

steps.text: Mix the mince, breadcrumbs, first milk, apple, sage and half the salt and roll into 16 balls.
Brown in the oil for 6 minutes, then cover and cook gently for 12 minutes until they reach 75°C right through.
Boil the potato for 15 minutes until soft and mash with the butter, second milk and remaining salt. Simmer the peas for 3 minutes and serve all together.

notes: Food safety: pork mince meatballs must reach 75°C right through with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Egg-free recipe. Contains gluten and milk.

title: Nut-Free Sunflower Seed Satay Chicken with Rice
summary: Satay-style chicken with a sauce blended from sunflower seeds, safe for nut-free homes.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil for 6 minutes. Cook the rice for 12 minutes until tender.
Blend the seeds, coconut milk, soy sauce, lime juice, sugar, garlic and ginger together, add to the chicken and simmer for 10 minutes until thick and the chicken reaches 75°C.
Serve over the rice with cucumber.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; refrigerate rice within 1 hour and leftovers within 2 hours.
Nut-free recipe: check every label for nut traces. Contains soy and gluten.

title: Nut-Free Sunflower Seed Pesto Pasta with Peas
summary: Basil pesto made with sunflower seeds, tossed through pasta and sweet peas.

steps.text: Boil the fusilli for 10 minutes until al dente, adding the peas for the last 2 minutes, then drain and keep half a cup of water.
Blend the seeds, basil, garlic, oil, lemon juice, cheese and salt until a rough paste.
Toss the pesto through the pasta and peas with a splash of the water until glossy.

notes: Nut-free recipe: check every label for nut traces. Contains gluten and milk.

title: Nut-Free Lamb Kofta with Tzatziki and Flatbread
summary: Spiced lamb skewers with cool cucumber yoghurt, tomato and warm flatbread.

steps.text: Squeeze the liquid from the onion and mix it with the mince, half the garlic, spices, parsley and salt until sticky. Shape into 12 sausages around skewers.
Grill or pan-fry for 10 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked to 75°C.
Squeeze the cucumber dry and stir into the yoghurt with the remaining garlic and lemon juice. Serve the kofta with flatbread, tomato and the tzatziki.

notes: Food safety: lamb mince must reach 75°C right through with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Nut-free recipe: check every label for nut traces. Contains gluten and milk.

title: Nut-Free Chicken Pad See Ew-Style Noodles
summary: Wide rice noodles with chicken, greens and egg in a sweet-salty soy sauce, with no nuts.

steps.text: Soak the noodles in hot water for 8 minutes until pliable and drain. Whisk the soy sauce, oyster sauce and sugar together.
Stir-fry the chicken in the oil for 5 minutes until cooked, add the garlic and broccoli for 3 minutes, push aside and scramble the eggs for 1 minute until set.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss for 3 minutes until tender and caramelised at the edges.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink and eggs must be set; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.
Nut-free recipe: check every label for nut traces. Contains egg, soy, gluten and shellfish (oyster sauce).

title: Hidden-Veg Beef and Carrot Pasta Sauce with Spirals
summary: A smooth tomato beef sauce with carrot, zucchini and capsicum blended in, loved by fussy eaters.

steps.text: Brown the mince in the oil for 6 minutes until no pink remains, then add the onion, carrot, zucchini, capsicum and garlic and cook for 8 minutes until very soft.
Add the tomatoes and oregano and simmer for 15 minutes until thick, then blend with a stick blender until smooth.
Boil the fusilli for 10 minutes until al dente, drain and toss with the sauce.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C right through with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Contains gluten.

title: Hidden-Veg Chicken Nuggets with Sweet Potato Wedges
summary: Baked nuggets with grated cauliflower and zucchini mixed in, served with sweet potato wedges.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Squeeze the zucchini dry and mix with the chicken, cauliflower, first breadcrumbs, egg, garlic powder and salt.
Shape into 20 nuggets, roll in the second breadcrumbs and bake on a tray with half the oil for 20 minutes, turning once, until golden and 75°C inside.
Toss the wedges with the remaining oil and roast alongside for 30 minutes until crisp.

notes: Food safety: chicken nuggets must reach 75°C right through with no pink; wash hands after handling raw chicken and egg, and eat leftovers within 2 days.
Contains egg and gluten.

title: Hidden-Veg Mac and Cheese with Pumpkin
summary: Creamy macaroni cheese where pumpkin puree makes the sauce golden, sweet and extra nutritious.

steps.text: Boil the pumpkin in the milk for 12 minutes until soft, then blend until smooth.
Boil the macaroni for 8 minutes until tender, adding the peas for the last 2 minutes, then drain.
Heat the pumpkin sauce with the mustard, garlic powder and salt, stir in the cheese until melted, then fold through the pasta.

notes: Contains gluten and milk. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.

title: Hidden-Veg Meatballs in Tomato Sauce
summary: Soft beef meatballs hiding grated carrot and zucchini, simmered in mild tomato sauce.

steps.text: Squeeze the zucchini dry and mix with the mince, carrot, breadcrumbs, egg, oregano and salt and roll into 20 meatballs.
Brown in the oil for 5 minutes, add the tomatoes and garlic and simmer for 15 minutes until the meatballs reach 75°C and the sauce is thick.
Boil the spaghetti for 10 minutes until al dente and serve with the meatballs.

notes: Food safety: beef mince meatballs must reach 75°C right through with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Contains egg and gluten.

title: Hidden-Veg Fish Fingers with Broccoli Mash
summary: Crumbed fish fingers with a green-tinged potato and broccoli mash kids happily eat.

items.raw: 500g white fish fillet, cut into fingers

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Coat the fish in flour, egg then breadcrumbs, place on an oiled tray and bake for 15 minutes until golden and the fish flakes.
Boil the potato for 12 minutes, add the broccoli for 5 minutes more until both are very soft, then drain.
Mash with the butter, milk and salt until smooth and green-flecked and serve with the fish fingers.

notes: Food safety: fish should be opaque and flake easily, reaching 63°C; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.
Contains fish, egg, gluten and milk.

title: Hidden-Veg Cheesy Chicken Quesadillas
summary: Crisp tortillas filled with melty cheese, shredded chicken and finely grated carrot and spinach.

steps.text: Cook the chicken in the oil for 6 minutes until cooked to 75°C, then add the carrot, spinach, cumin and salt for 2 minutes until wilted.
Fill half of each tortilla with the chicken mix and cheese, fold over and press.
Cook in a dry pan for 2 minutes a side until crisp and the cheese has melted. Slice into wedges.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Roast Chicken Leftover Fried Rice with Peas
summary: Use up cold roast chicken in a quick egg fried rice with peas, spring onion and soy sauce.

steps.text: Heat half the oil in a wok, scramble the eggs for 1 minute until set and tip out.
Stir-fry the garlic, chicken and peas in the remaining oil for 2 minutes, add the cold rice and fry for 4 minutes until hot and lightly crisp.
Return the egg with the soy sauce, sesame oil and spring onion and toss until steaming hot.

notes: Food safety: use roast chicken within 2 days of cooking, keep cooked rice chilled and refrigerate it within 1 hour, and reheat everything until steaming hot (75°C).
Contains egg, soy, gluten and sesame.

title: Roast Beef Leftover Hash with Fried Egg
summary: Crisp potato and onion hash with chopped cold roast beef, topped with a runny fried egg.

steps.text: Boil the potato for 6 minutes until just tender and drain well.
Fry the potato and onion in the oil for 10 minutes until crisp and golden, then add the beef, paprika, Worcestershire sauce and salt for 3 minutes until hot.
Fry the eggs in a little oil for 3 minutes until the whites are set and serve on the hash with parsley.

notes: Food safety: use roast beef within 2 days of cooking and reheat to 75°C; eggs should be cooked until the whites are set. Not for pregnant women or the elderly if the yolk is runny.
Contains egg. Worcestershire sauce contains fish and gluten.

title: Roast Lamb Leftover Pita Pockets with Tzatziki
summary: Shredded cold roast lamb warmed with cumin and stuffed into pita with crisp salad and tzatziki.

steps.text: Warm the lamb in the oil with the cumin and oregano for 5 minutes until steaming hot and edges crisp.
Squeeze the cucumber dry and stir into the yoghurt with the garlic.
Warm the pita, fill with the lamb, tomato and onion and spoon over the tzatziki.

notes: Food safety: use roast lamb within 2 days of cooking and reheat until steaming hot (75°C).
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Roast Pork Leftover Noodle Soup
summary: Slices of cold roast pork warmed in a ginger-soy broth with noodles, greens and a boiled egg.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 7 minutes, cool in cold water, peel and halve.
Simmer the stock, soy sauce, ginger and garlic for 8 minutes until fragrant, add the noodles for 4 minutes until tender and the bok choy for the last 2 minutes.
Add the pork for 1 minute until steaming hot and serve topped with the eggs and spring onion.

notes: Food safety: use roast pork within 2 days of cooking and reheat until steaming hot (75°C); boil eggs until the whites are firm.
Contains egg, soy and gluten.

title: BBQ Lemon Herb Chicken Skewers with Greek Salad
summary: Juicy chicken skewers marinated in lemon and oregano, grilled and served with a crisp Greek salad.

steps.text: Marinate the chicken in half the oil, half the lemon juice, the garlic, oregano and salt for at least 30 minutes, then thread onto skewers.
Grill over medium-high heat for 10 minutes, turning, until charred and the chicken reaches 75°C.
Toss the tomato, cucumber, onion and olives with the remaining oil and lemon juice, crumble over the feta and serve with the skewers.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; keep marinade away from cooked food, wash hands and boards, and eat leftovers within 2 days.
Contains milk.

title: BBQ Honey Mustard Pork Chops with Corn on the Cob
summary: Sticky honey mustard pork chops grilled alongside buttery sweet corn.

steps.text: Mix the honey, mustard, oil, garlic and salt and brush over the chops.
Grill the corn over medium heat for 12 minutes, turning, and the chops for 5 minutes a side, basting until the pork reaches 70°C and is glazed.
Steam the beans for 5 minutes until tender, brush the corn with the butter and serve.

notes: Food safety: pork chops must reach 70°C, then rest 3 minutes; wash hands after handling raw pork and eat leftovers within 2 days.
Contains milk.

title: BBQ Smoky Prawn Skewers with Mango Salsa
summary: Paprika prawns flash-grilled and served with a fresh mango, lime and coriander salsa.

steps.text: Toss the prawns with the oil, paprika and garlic and thread onto skewers.
Mix the mango, onion, capsicum, lime juice and coriander for the salsa. Cook the rice for 12 minutes until tender.
Grill the skewers over high heat for 2 minutes a side until pink and opaque and serve with the salsa and rice.

notes: Food safety: cook prawns until pink and opaque; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day, and refrigerate rice within 1 hour.
Contains crustacean shellfish.

title: BBQ Beef Burgers with Grilled Pineapple and Slaw
summary: Thick beef burgers topped with charred pineapple and a creamy cabbage slaw.

steps.text: Mix the mince with the paprika and salt and shape into 4 patties.
Grill the patties over medium-high heat for 6 minutes a side until 75°C inside and the pineapple for 2 minutes a side until charred.
Toss the cabbage, carrot, yoghurt and lemon juice into a slaw and build the burgers in toasted buns.

notes: Food safety: burger patties must reach 75°C right through with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: BBQ Lamb Cutlets with Minted Yoghurt and Zucchini
summary: Quick-grilled lamb cutlets with charred zucchini ribbons and a cooling mint yoghurt.

steps.text: Rub the cutlets with half the oil, garlic, cumin and salt. Toss the zucchini with the remaining oil.
Grill the cutlets for 3 minutes a side until browned, rest 3 minutes, and grill the zucchini for 3 minutes a side until charred.
Stir the mint and lemon juice into the yoghurt and serve with the lamb, zucchini and warmed flatbread.

notes: Food safety: lamb cutlets are whole cuts: sear all sides and rest, aiming for 63°C for medium or 71°C for well done; eat leftovers within 2 days.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Quick Lemon Garlic Prawn and Zucchini Pasta in 20 Minutes
summary: Spaghetti with garlicky prawns and zucchini ribbons, on the table in 20 minutes.

steps.text: Boil the spaghetti for 10 minutes until al dente and keep half a cup of the water.
Sear the prawns in the oil for 2 minutes until pink, add the garlic, zucchini and chilli for 3 minutes until just tender.
Toss with the pasta, lemon zest and juice, parsley, salt and a splash of water until glossy.

notes: Food safety: cook prawns until pink and opaque; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.
Contains gluten and crustacean shellfish.

title: Quick Chicken and Vegetable Teriyaki Noodles in 25 Minutes
summary: A fast stir-fry of chicken, carrot and cabbage in a sticky homemade teriyaki sauce.

steps.text: Boil the noodles for 4 minutes until tender and drain. Whisk the soy sauce, honey, vinegar, garlic and ginger together.
Stir-fry the chicken in the oil for 6 minutes until golden and cooked to 75°C, add the carrot and cabbage for 3 minutes.
Pour in the sauce and noodles and toss for 2 minutes until glossy and hot.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Contains soy, gluten and egg.

title: Quick Black Bean and Corn Tostadas in 20 Minutes
summary: Crisp tortillas piled with spiced black beans, corn, avocado and lime, with no long cooking.
