steps.text: Brush the tortillas with half the oil and bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 6 minutes until crisp.
Warm the beans with the cumin, garlic and remaining oil for 5 minutes, mashing about half roughly.
Spread the beans over the tostadas and top with corn, avocado, tomato, lime juice, coriander and a spoonful of yoghurt.

notes: Contains milk. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Quick Crisp Fish with Garlic Parsley Butter and Greens
summary: Crisp-skinned fish fillets in a bright caper butter with garlicky green beans and broccolini.

steps.text: Pat the fish dry, season with the salt and pan-fry in the oil for 4 minutes a side until golden and it flakes easily.
Steam the beans and broccolini for 5 minutes until tender-crisp.
Melt the butter with the parsley, lemon juice and garlic for 1 minute until foaming and spoon over the fish and greens.

notes: Food safety: fish should be opaque and flake easily, reaching 63°C; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.
Contains fish and milk.

title: Quick Egg and Vegetable Shakshuka for the Family
summary: Eggs baked in spiced tomato and capsicum sauce, ready in 25 minutes with flatbread.

steps.text: Soften the onion and capsicum in the oil for 5 minutes, add the garlic and spices for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and salt and simmer for 8 minutes until thick. Make 6 wells and crack in the eggs.
Cover and cook for 5 minutes until the whites are set, scatter with parsley and serve with warm flatbread.

notes: Food safety: cook eggs until the whites are set and yolks thickened; keep out of reach if serving to pregnant women, infants or the elderly with runny yolks; eat leftovers within 2 days.
Contains egg and gluten.

title: Freezer-to-Table Chicken and Vegetable Curry
summary: Make a big batch, freeze in portions, and reheat from frozen for an easy weeknight curry.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil for 6 minutes, add the onion, garlic and ginger for 5 minutes, then stir in the curry powder for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, coconut milk, carrot and salt and simmer for 25 minutes until thick and the chicken reaches 75°C. Stir in the peas.
Cool within 1 hour, portion into containers and freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat from frozen in a covered pan over low heat for 20 minutes, stirring, until steaming hot.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; cool and freeze within 2 hours, thaw in the fridge if you prefer, reheat only once until steaming hot (75°C) and serve with freshly cooked rice.

title: Freezer-to-Table Beef and Bean Burritos
summary: Wrap, freeze and bake straight from frozen for a hot burrito dinner with no thawing.

steps.text: Brown the mince in the oil for 6 minutes until no pink remains, add the onion, garlic and spices for 4 minutes, then the beans, passata and salt and simmer for 8 minutes until thick. Cool.
Spoon onto the tortillas with the cheese, fold in the sides and roll tightly. Wrap individually and freeze.
Bake from frozen at 200°C (180°C fan) for 35 minutes, turning once, until golden and hot in the centre.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C with no pink, and the burritos 75°C in the centre after reheating; cool within 1 hour, freeze for up to 3 months and do not refreeze once baked.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Freezer-to-Table Spinach and Ricotta Cannelloni
summary: Rolled pasta sheets filled with spinach and ricotta under tomato sauce, assembled and frozen ready to bake.

steps.text: Wilt the spinach in a pan for 2 minutes until soft, squeeze dry and mix with the ricotta, egg, nutmeg and salt. Simmer the tomatoes, garlic and oregano for 10 minutes until thick.
Spread the ricotta mix over the lasagne sheets, roll them up, lay seam-down in a dish, cover with sauce and mozzarella and wrap well. Freeze for up to 3 months.
Bake from frozen, covered, at 190°C (170°C fan) for 50 minutes, then uncovered for 10 minutes until golden and bubbling hot in the centre.

notes: Food safety: bake until hot through to 75°C in the centre; cool before freezing, do not refreeze after baking and eat leftovers within 2 days.
Contains gluten, egg and milk.

title: Freezer-to-Table Lentil and Vegetable Soup
summary: A thick, hearty vegan lentil soup that freezes brilliantly and reheats in minutes.

steps.text: Soften the onion, carrot, celery and garlic in the oil for 8 minutes until tender, then stir in the cumin and turmeric for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, tomatoes, stock and salt and simmer for 25 minutes until the lentils are soft. Blend half for a thicker texture and stir in the lemon juice.
Cool within 1 hour, freeze in portions for up to 3 months and reheat from frozen over low heat for 15 minutes, stirring, until steaming hot.

notes: Cool and freeze within 2 hours; reheat only once until steaming hot and eat within 2 days of thawing.

title: Mediterranean Tuna, Lemon and Cherry Tomato Spaghetti
summary: Pantry spaghetti with tinned tuna, cherry tomatoes, garlic, lemon and parsley.

steps.text: Boil the spaghetti for 10 minutes until al dente and keep half a cup of the water.
Fry the garlic and chilli in half the oil for 1 minute, add the tomatoes for 6 minutes until they burst, then flake in the tuna and heat for 2 minutes.
Toast the breadcrumbs in the remaining oil for 3 minutes until golden. Toss the pasta with the sauce, lemon and parsley and a splash of water, and top with the crumbs.

notes: Contains fish and gluten. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.

title: Mediterranean Chicken with Olives, Lemon and Potatoes
summary: Tray-roasted chicken legs with potatoes, green olives, lemon and thyme.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the chicken, potato, oil, lemon, garlic, thyme and salt on a large tray.
Roast for 35 minutes, then add the olives and tomatoes and roast for 15 minutes more until the skin is crisp and the chicken reaches 75°C.
Serve straight from the tray with the pan juices.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C at the thickest part with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Mediterranean White Bean and Vegetable Stew with Gremolata
summary: Cannellini beans, zucchini and tomato stewed with garlic and finished with lemony parsley gremolata.

steps.text: Soften the onion and carrot in the oil for 6 minutes, add two-thirds of the garlic and the rosemary for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, beans, stock and salt and simmer for 15 minutes, adding the zucchini for the last 8 minutes, until thick.
Mix the parsley, lemon zest and remaining crushed garlic and scatter over the stew.

notes: Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 4 days.

title: Mediterranean Baked Eggplant with Chickpeas and Feta
summary: Roasted eggplant halves filled with tomatoey chickpeas and crumbled feta.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Score the eggplant, brush with two-thirds of the oil and roast cut-side down for 25 minutes until soft.
Soften the onion in the remaining oil for 5 minutes, add the garlic and cumin for 1 minute, then the tomatoes, chickpeas and salt and simmer for 10 minutes until thick.
Turn the eggplant over, fill with the chickpeas, top with feta and bake for 10 minutes until golden.

notes: Contains milk. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.

title: Mediterranean Grilled Fish with Tomato and White Bean Salad
summary: Lemony grilled fish over a salad of tomato, white beans, red onion and basil.

steps.text: Rub the fish with half the oil, half the lemon juice and the garlic. Grill for 4 minutes a side until it flakes easily.
Toss the beans, tomato, onion and basil with the remaining oil, lemon juice and salt.
Serve the fish over the salad.

notes: Food safety: fish should be opaque and flake easily, reaching 63°C; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.
Contains fish.

title: Mediterranean Lamb and Vegetable Souvlaki Bowls
summary: Oregano lamb with roast vegetables, quick tzatziki and rice in a satisfying bowl.

steps.text: Marinate the lamb in two-thirds of the oil, oregano, half the garlic, lemon juice and salt for at least 30 minutes.

Grill or pan-fry the lamb for 8 minutes, turning, until browned and 71°C inside, and roast or fry the zucchini and capsicum in the remaining oil for 10 minutes. Cook the rice for 12 minutes until tender.
Squeeze the cucumber dry and mix into the yoghurt with the remaining garlic. Serve over the rice.

notes: Food safety: lamb pieces should reach 71°C with no pink; refrigerate rice within 1 hour and leftovers within 2 hours.
Contains milk.

title: Lightened Butter Chicken with Cauliflower Rice
summary: All the creamy tomato flavour of butter chicken with yoghurt and less butter, over cauliflower rice.

steps.text: Marinate the chicken in half the yoghurt, half the garam masala and the paprika for at least 30 minutes.

Cook the onion in the butter for 5 minutes, add the garlic, ginger and remaining garam masala for 1 minute, then the tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes. Blend until smooth and add the chicken, simmering for 10 minutes until it reaches 75°C. Stir in the remaining yoghurt and the cream.
Fry the cauliflower in a dry pan for 5 minutes until tender, season with the salt and serve under the curry.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Contains milk.

title: Lightened Creamy Chicken and Leek Pasta Bake
summary: A comforting bake of chicken, leek and pasta in a light yoghurt-milk sauce.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Boil the penne for 8 minutes until just tender and drain.

Cook the chicken in the oil for 5 minutes, add the leek and garlic for 5 minutes, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk and simmer for 5 minutes until thick. Off the heat, stir in the yoghurt and mustard.
Fold through the pasta, tip into a dish, top with the cheese and breadcrumbs and bake for 15 minutes until golden and the chicken reaches 75°C.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Contains gluten and milk.

title: Fakeaway Chicken Doner Kebab Plates with Chilli Sauce
summary: Spiced chicken thigh grilled until charred, served with salad, chips and garlic chilli sauce.

steps.text: Marinate the chicken in half the yoghurt, the cumin, paprika, two-thirds of the garlic and the oil for at least 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and roast the chips with the 2 tablespoons oil for 30 minutes until golden. Grill or fry the chicken for 10 minutes until charred and 75°C inside.
Mix the remaining yoghurt, garlic and chilli sauce. Serve the chicken with the chips, cabbage, tomato and onion and drizzle with sauce.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Contains milk.

title: BBQ Teriyaki Salmon Skewers with Sesame Rice
summary: Glazed salmon skewers grilled for a few minutes and served over sesame rice with cucumber.

steps.text: Simmer the soy sauce, honey, vinegar and garlic for 3 minutes until syrupy and cool. Toss half with the salmon and thread onto skewers.
Cook the rice for 12 minutes until tender and stir through the sesame seeds. Grill the skewers over medium-high heat for 5 minutes, turning and brushing with the glaze, until the fish flakes.
Serve over the rice with cucumber and spring onion and drizzle with the remaining glaze.

notes: Food safety: salmon should reach 63°C; use fresh glaze for serving, not the portion that touched raw fish; refrigerate rice within 1 hour and leftovers within 2 hours.
Contains fish, soy, gluten and sesame.

title: BBQ Halloumi and Vegetable Skewers with Couscous
summary: Grilled halloumi, zucchini and capsicum skewers with lemony couscous and mint yoghurt.

steps.text: Thread the halloumi and vegetables onto skewers and brush with the oil and oregano.

Pour the boiling water over the couscous, cover for 5 minutes until fluffy and fork through the lemon juice. Grill the skewers over medium-high heat for 10 minutes, turning, until charred and the halloumi is golden.
Stir the mint into the yoghurt and serve with the skewers and couscous.

notes: Contains milk and gluten. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: One-Pot Chicken and Chorizo Paella-Style Rice
summary: Rice, chicken and chorizo simmered with paprika and peas for an easy weeknight paella.

steps.text: Brown the chicken and chorizo in the oil for 8 minutes until golden and the chicken reaches 75°C, then add the onion, capsicum and garlic for 4 minutes and stir in the paprika.
Add the rice and stock, bring to a simmer and cook gently, uncovered and without stirring, for 20 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid absorbed. Scatter on the peas for the last 3 minutes.
Rest covered for 5 minutes and serve with lemon.

notes: Food safety: chicken and chorizo must reach 75°C with no pink; refrigerate rice within 1 hour and leftovers within 2 hours, and reheat until steaming hot.

title: One-Pot Creamy Garlic Prawn and Spinach Orzo
summary: Orzo cooks in garlicky stock and finishes with cream, spinach and quick prawns.

steps.text: Sear the prawns in half the oil for 2 minutes until pink and set aside.
Cook the garlic in the remaining oil for 30 seconds, add the orzo and stock and simmer for 10 minutes, stirring often, until tender and mostly absorbed.
Stir in the cream, spinach, lemon and salt for 2 minutes until wilted, then return the prawns for 1 minute.

notes: Food safety: cook prawns until pink and opaque; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.
Contains gluten, milk and crustacean shellfish.

title: Freezer-to-Table Turkey Meatballs in Tomato Sauce
summary: Batch-cooked turkey meatballs in tomato sauce that go from freezer to table in 30 minutes.

steps.text: Mix the mince, breadcrumbs, egg, half the garlic, oregano and salt and roll into 24 meatballs. Brown in the oil for 6 minutes.
Add the onion, tomatoes and remaining garlic and simmer for 15 minutes until the meatballs reach 75°C and the sauce is thick. Cool within 1 hour, portion and freeze for up to 3 months.
Reheat from frozen, covered, over low heat for 25 minutes, stirring, until steaming hot. Boil the spaghetti for 10 minutes until al dente and serve.

notes: Food safety: turkey mince must reach 75°C right through with no pink; reheat only once until steaming hot (75°C), do not refreeze and eat within 2 days of thawing.
Contains egg and gluten.

title: Freezer-to-Table Vegetable and Bean Chilli Bake
summary: A vegetarian chilli topped with cornbread-style crumbs, baked straight from frozen.

steps.text: Soften the onion, capsicum, zucchini and garlic in the oil for 8 minutes, stir in the spices, then add the tomatoes, beans and corn and simmer for 15 minutes until thick. Cool and spoon into a dish.
Scatter the polenta and cheese over the top and freeze, wrapped, for up to 3 months.
Bake from frozen, covered, at 190°C (170°C fan) for 45 minutes, then uncovered for 15 minutes until golden and hot in the centre.

notes: Contains milk. Cool before freezing and reheat only once until steaming hot (75°C).

title: Barramundi with Lemon Caper Butter and Greens
summary: Pan-seared farmed barramundi fillets with a quick lemon and caper butter, green beans and potatoes.

steps.text: Boil the potato for 15 minutes until tender, adding the beans for the last 4 minutes, then drain.
Pat the fish dry, season with the salt and sear in the oil, skin side down, for 4 minutes. Turn and cook for 2 minutes more.
Melt the butter in the pan, add the capers, lemon zest and juice and parsley, and spoon over the fish with the potato and beans.

notes: Barramundi is widely farmed in Australia, a more sustainable pick.
Food safety: cook fish until opaque and flaking, and shellfish until opaque and firm; keep raw seafood below 5°C, refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.

title: Tinned Salmon and Tomato Spaghetti with Lemon Crumbs
summary: A pantry pasta using tinned salmon, tomato, garlic and lemon crumbs.

steps.text: Boil the spaghetti for 10 minutes until al dente and keep half a cup of the water.
Fry the garlic and chilli in half the oil for 1 minute, add the tomatoes and simmer for 8 minutes. Break in the salmon and warm for 2 minutes.
Toast the breadcrumbs in the remaining oil for 3 minutes. Toss the pasta with the sauce, a splash of pasta water and the lemon zest and parsley, and top with the crumbs.

notes: Contains fish and gluten. Tinned salmon is a convenient pantry fish.
Food safety: cook fish until opaque and flaking, and shellfish until opaque and firm; keep raw seafood below 5°C, refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.

title: Baked Snapper with Herb Crust and Crunchy Slaw
summary: Snapper fillets under a golden herb crumb with a fresh cabbage and apple slaw.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and line a tray. Mix the breadcrumbs, parsley, zest and oil.
Brush the fillets with mustard, press on the crumbs and bake for 12 minutes until golden and the fish flakes.
Toss the cabbage, apple, carrot, mayonnaise and vinegar and serve alongside.

notes: Contains fish, egg and gluten.
Food safety: cook fish until opaque and flaking, and shellfish until opaque and firm; keep raw seafood below 5°C, refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.

title: Lemony Prawn Linguine with Zucchini Ribbons and Parsley
summary: Quick prawn linguine with zucchini, garlic, chilli and lemon.

steps.text: Boil the linguine for 10 minutes until al dente and keep half a cup of the water.
Fry the garlic and chilli in the oil for 1 minute, add the zucchini for 3 minutes, then the prawns for 3 minutes until pink and curled.
Toss the pasta through with the lemon, parsley, salt and a splash of pasta water.

notes: Contains shellfish and gluten.
Food safety: cook fish until opaque and flaking, and shellfish until opaque and firm; keep raw seafood below 5°C, refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.

title: Salmon and Sweet Potato Fishcakes with Yoghurt Dip
summary: Pan-fried fishcakes from tinned salmon and mash, with a lime yoghurt dip and salad.

steps.text: Boil the sweet potato for 12 minutes until soft, drain and mash.
Mix the mash with the salmon, spring onion, zest, half the breadcrumbs and the egg, shape into 8 patties and coat with the remaining crumbs.
Fry in the oil for 4 minutes each side until golden and hot through. Stir the yoghurt and lime and serve with the leaves.

notes: Contains fish, egg, dairy and gluten. Patties freeze well before cooking.
Food safety: cook fish until opaque and flaking, and shellfish until opaque and firm; keep raw seafood below 5°C, refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.

title: Mussels in White Wine and Garlic with Crusty Bread
summary: Farmed mussels steamed open in garlic, wine and parsley, with bread for the broth.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the oil and butter for 4 minutes, add the garlic for 1 minute, then pour in the wine.
Add the mussels, cover and steam for 5 minutes, shaking the pot, until the shells open.
Discard any that stay closed, scatter over the parsley and serve with the bread.

notes: Farmed mussels are among the most sustainable seafood choices.
Food safety: discard mussels that are open before cooking and will not close when tapped, and any that stay shut after steaming; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.

title: Thai-Style Fish Parcels with Lime and Ginger
summary: Firm white fish steamed in baking paper with lime, ginger, lemongrass and chilli, served with rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice according to the packet. Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Place each fillet on a sheet of baking paper with bok choy, ginger, lemongrass, chilli, lime and fish sauce, and fold into sealed parcels.
Bake for 14 minutes until the fish flakes, then open and scatter over coriander. Serve with the rice.

notes: Contains fish. Use any sustainable firm white fish such as flathead or barramundi.
Food safety: cook fish until opaque and flaking, and shellfish until opaque and firm; keep raw seafood below 5°C, refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.

title: Smoked Salmon and Potato Salad with Horseradish Dressing
summary: A warm dinner salad of new potatoes, smoked salmon, beans and a creamy horseradish dressing.

steps.text: Boil the potato for 12 minutes, adding the beans for 3 minutes and the eggs for 8 minutes in a separate pot. Drain, peel and quarter the eggs.
Stir the sour cream, horseradish, dill and lemon juice together.
Toss the warm potato, beans, salmon and onion with the dressing and top with the egg, until everything is evenly coated.

notes: Contains fish, egg and dairy.
Food safety: cook fish until opaque and flaking, and shellfish until opaque and firm; keep raw seafood below 5°C, refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.

title: Pan-Seared Calamari with Chilli, Lemon and Rocket
summary: Quickly seared calamari tossed with chilli and lemon over rocket and white beans.

steps.text: Toss the calamari with the paprika and salt.
Heat the oil in a very hot pan and sear the calamari in two batches for 90 seconds each until just opaque. Add the garlic and chilli for the last 30 seconds.
Toss the beans, rocket, lemon and calamari together and serve at once.

notes: Calamari turns tough if overcooked, so work in batches.
Food safety: cook fish until opaque and flaking, and shellfish until opaque and firm; keep raw seafood below 5°C, refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.

title: Chicken Liver with Caramelised Onions and Mash
summary: A gentle introduction to offal: chicken liver, sweet onions and creamy mash.

steps.text: Boil the potato for 15 minutes, drain and mash with half the butter, the milk and half the salt.
Cook the onions in the remaining butter over low heat for 20 minutes until deep golden, add the vinegar and set aside.
Pat the liver dry and dust with flour. Fry in the oil for 3 minutes each side until browned and no pink remains. Add the stock to the pan for 2 minutes and serve over the mash with the onions.

notes: Liver is rich in vitamin A, so enjoy it occasionally rather than daily, and avoid it in pregnancy.
Food safety: cook liver until no pink remains inside and it reaches 75°C; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.

title: Chicken Liver Ragu with Sage and Mushrooms
summary: A rich, silky ragu with chicken livers blended through mushrooms and tomato, served over pappardelle.

steps.text: Cook the onion and mushroom in the oil for 8 minutes until golden, add the garlic and sage for 1 minute.
Add the livers and cook for 4 minutes, stirring, until browned all over. Pour in the wine, then the tomatoes, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Boil the pappardelle for 9 minutes and toss through the ragu with the parmesan.

notes: Contains gluten and dairy. Chicken liver is rich in vitamin A, so avoid it in pregnancy.
Food safety: cook the liver until no pink remains and it reaches 75°C; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Braised Beef Cheek with Red Wine and Creamy Polenta
summary: Slow-braised beef cheeks that fall apart, over soft polenta. A beginner step into nose-to-tail cooking.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Brown the cheeks in the oil in batches and set aside.
Cook the onion, carrot and celery for 6 minutes, add the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute, then the wine and stock and bay leaf. Return the beef, cover and braise for 3 hours until tender.
Cook the polenta with 6 cups of water for 15 minutes, stirring, then stir in the butter and parmesan. Spoon the beef and sauce on top.

notes: Contains dairy. Cheek is a cheap cut that becomes tender with long, slow cooking.
Food safety: braise beef until very tender and above 75°C; cool leftovers quickly, refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.

title: Oxtail and Butter Bean Stew with Smoked Paprika
summary: A deeply savoury stew of oxtail and butter beans, even better the next day.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Brown the oxtail in the oil in batches and set aside.
Soften the onion and carrot for 6 minutes, add the garlic and paprika for 1 minute, then the tomatoes, stock and bay leaf. Return the oxtail, cover and braise for 3 hours.
Add the beans and cook uncovered for 20 minutes. Skim off excess fat and scatter with parsley.

notes: Chill overnight so the fat sets and lifts off easily.
Food safety: braise until the meat falls from the bone; cool quickly, refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.

title: Braised Beef Cheek Tacos with Green Salsa
summary: Tender braised beef cheek shredded into soft tortillas with green salsa and onion.

steps.text: Simmer the cheeks with the onion, garlic, bay leaf and salt in water for 2.5 hours until completely tender, then shred.
Blend the green tomato, jalapeno, half the coriander and lime into a salsa.
Sear the shredded beef in a hot pan for 3 minutes until crisp at the edges and serve in warm tortillas with salsa, diced onion and remaining coriander.

notes: Beef cheek is a budget cut that needs only time.
Food safety: simmer until completely tender and well above 75°C; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.

title: Crispy Tofu and Greens with Black Bean Sauce
summary: Golden tofu cubes and gai lan in a savoury fermented black bean sauce over rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice according to the packet until tender.
Toss the tofu in cornflour and fry in 2 tablespoons of the oil for 8 minutes until golden on all sides. Set aside.
Fry the garlic, ginger and black bean sauce in the remaining oil for 1 minute, add the greens, soy sauce, sugar and 1/4 cup of water for 3 minutes, then toss in the tofu.

notes: Contains soy. Use tamari and a gluten-free black bean sauce for gluten-free.

title: Crumbed Tofu Cutlets with Japanese Vegetable Curry
summary: Crumbed tofu cutlets with a mild Japanese-style vegetable curry sauce and rice.

items.raw: 600g firm tofu, pressed and sliced into 8 slabs

steps.text: Cook the rice. Soften the onion, carrot and potato in a little oil for 5 minutes, stir in the curry powder and 2 tablespoons of flour for 1 minute, then add the stock, soy and maple syrup and simmer for 20 minutes until thick.
Dip the tofu in the flour, then the milk, then the panko.
Shallow-fry the tofu in the oil for 3 minutes each side until golden and serve with the sauce and rice.

notes: Contains soy and gluten. Use a plant milk of your choice.

title: Smoky Tofu and Peanut Sambal Bowls
summary: Pan-fried tofu with a quick chilli peanut sambal, cucumber, greens and rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice, steaming the beans on top for the last 4 minutes.
Fry the tofu in the oil for 4 minutes each side until golden, adding the soy sauce and paprika for the last minute.
Whisk the peanut butter, sweet chilli, lime and 3 tablespoons of warm water into a sambal. Serve over the rice, tofu, beans and cucumber.

notes: Contains soy and peanuts. Check the soy sauce label if avoiding gluten.

title: Tofu and Capsicum Skewers with Coconut Rice
summary: Marinated tofu and vegetable skewers grilled with Thai red curry paste, served with coconut rice.

steps.text: Mix the curry paste, 2 tablespoons coconut milk and soy sauce and toss the tofu in it. Thread onto skewers with the capsicum and onion.
Cook the rice with the cup of coconut milk and 1 cup of water for 15 minutes.
Brush the skewers with oil and grill for 4 minutes each side until charred. Serve with the rice and lime.

notes: Contains soy. Soak wooden skewers in water for 30 minutes first. Check the curry paste for shrimp paste if you need it vegan.

title: Harissa Chickpea and Eggplant Tagine
summary: A fragrant vegetable tagine of chickpeas, eggplant and apricot, served over couscous.

steps.text: Soften the onion and eggplant in the oil for 8 minutes, add the garlic, harissa and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, chickpeas, apricot and stock, cover and simmer for 25 minutes until the eggplant is soft.
Cover the couscous with 1.5 cups of boiling water for 5 minutes, fluff, and serve under the tagine with the coriander.

notes: Contains gluten (couscous). Serve over rice for gluten-free.

title: Lentil and Spinach Dal with Garlic Tarka
summary: Creamy red lentil dal finished with a sizzling garlic and cumin tarka, served with rice.

steps.text: Simmer the lentils, onion, ginger, turmeric, salt and 5 cups of water for 25 minutes until soft, stirring occasionally. Stir in the spinach to wilt. Cook the rice separately.
Heat the ghee in a small pan and fry the garlic, cumin seeds and chilli for 1 minute until golden.
Pour the tarka over the dal and serve with the rice.

notes: Contains dairy (ghee). Use oil for vegan.

title: Pumpkin and Chickpea Stew with Ras el Hanout and Preserved Lemon
summary: Chickpeas and pumpkin simmered with ras el hanout, tomato and preserved lemon.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the oil for 6 minutes, add the garlic and spice for 1 minute.
Add the pumpkin, tomatoes, chickpeas and stock and simmer for 25 minutes until the pumpkin is soft.
Stir through the preserved lemon and serve with the coriander and yoghurt.

notes: Contains dairy. Skip the yoghurt for vegan. Serve with flatbread or couscous.

title: Feijoada-Style Black Bean Stew with Rice and Orange
summary: A smoky vegetarian black bean stew in the style of feijoada, with rice, greens and orange.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 6 minutes, add the garlic, paprika, cumin and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the beans, stock and bay leaf, simmer for 30 minutes until thick, then mash a quarter of the beans to thicken.
Stir in the silverbeet for 3 minutes. Cook the rice and serve with the stew and orange.

notes: Vegan and gluten free. Traditional feijoada includes pork; this version is plant-based.

title: Roast Vegetable Barley Bowl with Feta and Lemon Tahini
summary: A warm Mediterranean grain bowl of pearl barley, roasted zucchini, capsicum and chickpeas with feta.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Roast the zucchini, capsicum and chickpeas with the oil for 25 minutes until charred at the edges.
Simmer the barley in plenty of water for 25 minutes until tender, then drain.
Whisk the tahini, lemon, garlic and 3 tablespoons of water until smooth. Pile the barley, vegetables and feta into bowls and drizzle with the dressing and parsley.

notes: Contains gluten, dairy and sesame. Use brown rice instead of barley for gluten-free.

title: Beef Bibimbap-Style Bowls with Gochujang Sauce
summary: Rice topped with seasoned beef, sauteed vegetables, a fried egg and gochujang sauce.

steps.text: Cook the rice. Brown the beef with half the soy sauce and the sugar for 6 minutes until cooked through with no pink left.
Stir-fry the carrot and zucchini in the vegetable oil for 3 minutes until just tender, and wilt the spinach with the remaining soy sauce for 1 minute.
Fry the eggs until the whites are set. Mix the gochujang with the sesame oil and 1 tablespoon of water. Build the bowls with rice, beef, vegetables and egg and add the sauce.

notes: Contains soy, sesame and egg.
Food safety: cook the mince to 75°C with no pink, and cook eggs until the whites are set; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Mexican Brown Rice Bowl with Black Beans and Corn Salsa
summary: A vegetarian bowl of brown rice, spiced beans, charred corn salsa and avocado.

steps.text: Simmer the rice in plenty of water for 30 minutes until tender, then drain.

Warm the beans with the cumin, paprika and 1/4 cup of water for 8 minutes. Char the corn in a hot pan for 8 minutes until blackened in spots, cut off the kernels and mix with the onion, tomato, lime and coriander.
Build bowls with the rice, beans, salsa, avocado and a spoon of yoghurt.

notes: Contains dairy. Swap the yoghurt for a dairy-free yoghurt if needed.

title: Spiced Tomato Rice Bowl with Grilled Chicken and Sweet Plantain
summary: West African-style tomato and pepper rice with spiced grilled chicken thigh and sweet plantain.

steps.text: Rub the chicken with half the paprika, thyme and a little oil, then grill for 12 minutes, turning, until cooked through at 75°C.

Cook the onion, garlic and capsicum in 1 tablespoon of oil for 6 minutes, add the tomatoes, paste and remaining paprika for 5 minutes, then stir in the rice and stock. Cover and cook gently for 20 minutes until the rice is tender.
Fry the plantain in the remaining oil for 3 minutes each side until golden and serve with the rice and chicken.

notes: Add a chilli for heat.
Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C at the thickest part with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Persian-Style Barley Bowl with Saffron Chicken and Herbs
summary: Pearl barley tossed with herbs and pomegranate, topped with saffron yoghurt chicken.

steps.text: Soak the saffron in 2 tablespoons of hot water for 5 minutes, then stir into the yoghurt with the lemon juice and toss the chicken in it.
Simmer the barley for 25 minutes until tender, then drain. Fry the chicken in the oil for 8 minutes until cooked through.
Toss the barley with the herbs, pomegranate and almonds and serve topped with the chicken.

notes: Contains gluten, dairy and nuts.
Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Teriyaki Salmon Donburi with Pickled Cucumber
summary: Glazed salmon over rice with quick pickled cucumber, edamame and sesame.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender. Toss the cucumber with the vinegar and a pinch of sugar and leave while you cook the fish.
Sear the salmon in the oil for 4 minutes, skin side down, turn, add the soy sauce, mirin and sugar and cook for 3 minutes until glossy and the fish flakes.
Serve the rice topped with the salmon, glaze, cucumber, edamame and sesame.

notes: Contains fish, soy and sesame.
Food safety: cook salmon until opaque and flaking; keep raw fish below 5°C and eat leftovers within 1 day.

title: Moroccan Couscous Bowl with Spiced Lamb and Roast Carrots
summary: Couscous with cumin lamb, roasted carrots, yoghurt and mint.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and roast the carrot with half the oil for 25 minutes until caramelised.
Fry the lamb with the spices in the remaining oil for 8 minutes until browned with no pink left. Cover the couscous and raisins with 1.5 cups of boiling water for 5 minutes, then fluff.
Serve the couscous topped with lamb, carrot, yoghurt, mint and lemon.

notes: Contains gluten and dairy.
Food safety: cook the mince to 75°C with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Vietnamese Vermicelli Bowl with Lemongrass Pork
summary: Rice noodles with grilled lemongrass pork, herbs, pickled carrot and nuoc cham dressing.

steps.text: Mix the pork with the lemongrass, garlic, 1 tablespoon fish sauce and half the sugar, shape into small patties and grill or pan-fry for 8 minutes until cooked through with no pink.
Soak the noodles in boiling water for 5 minutes, then drain and rinse. Stir the lime, 1/4 cup fish sauce, remaining sugar and 1/4 cup of water for the dressing.
Pile the noodles, carrot, cucumber and mint into bowls, top with the pork and peanuts and pour over the dressing.

notes: Contains fish and peanuts.
Food safety: cook pork mince to 75°C with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Spinach and Feta Stuffed Bread Roll
summary: A rolled and baked pizza dough filled with spinach, feta and mozzarella.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Wilt the spinach with the garlic in the oil for 2 minutes, squeeze out the water and cool.
Roll the dough into a 30cm by 40cm rectangle, top with the spinach, feta, mozzarella and oregano leaving a border, then roll up from the long side and seal the ends.
Brush with egg and bake for 28 minutes until deep golden and cooked through. Rest for 5 minutes before slicing.

notes: Contains gluten, dairy and egg. Serve with a green salad.
Food safety: bake until the dough is cooked through and no longer doughy; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Ham, Cheese and Mushroom Calzone
summary: Folded pizza pockets stuffed with leg ham, mushroom, mozzarella and ricotta.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 230°C (210°C fan). Fry the mushroom in the oil for 6 minutes until golden and dry.
Divide the dough into 4, roll into rounds and fill half of each with passata, ham, mushroom, ricotta and mozzarella. Fold over and crimp the edges.
Bake for 18 minutes until puffed and golden, with the cheese melted inside.

notes: Contains gluten and dairy. Use cooked ham, not raw.
Food safety: bake until piping hot in the centre; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Potato and Cheddar Stuffed Flatbreads
summary: Pan-fried wholemeal flatbreads stuffed with spiced potato and cheddar, served with yoghurt.

steps.text: Knead the flour, salt and 3/4 cup of water into a soft dough and rest while you mix the mash, spices and cheddar.
Divide the dough into 8, flatten each, fill with the potato mix, seal and roll out gently to 15cm rounds.
Cook each flatbread on a hot pan with a little ghee for 3 minutes each side until golden and cooked through. Serve with yoghurt.

notes: Contains gluten and dairy.

title: Lamb and Mint Sfiha-Style Open Pies
summary: Little Lebanese-style open pies with spiced lamb, tomato and pine nuts.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt, oil and 1 cup of warm water, knead for 8 minutes until smooth and rest for 1 hour until doubled.
Mix the lamb, onion, tomato, spices, pine nuts and lemon juice. Heat the oven to 230°C (210°C fan).
Divide the dough into 12 discs, top with the mixture and bake for 15 minutes until the lamb is cooked through with no pink and the base is golden.

notes: Contains gluten and nuts.
Food safety: lamb mince must reach 75°C with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Leek and Chicken Pot Pie with Mustard Cream
summary: A creamy chicken and leek filling topped with golden puff pastry.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Brown the chicken in the butter for 5 minutes, add the leek for 5 minutes until soft, then stir in the flour for 1 minute.
Add the stock, cream and mustard and simmer for 8 minutes until thick, stir in the peas and tip into a pie dish to cool slightly.
Cover with the pastry, trim, cut a slit, brush with egg and bake for 30 minutes until puffed, golden and bubbling.

notes: Contains gluten, dairy and egg.
Food safety: chicken must be cooked to 75°C with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Mushroom and Lentil Pie with Sweet Potato Top
summary: A vegan pie of mushroom and lentil gravy under a golden sweet potato mash.

steps.text: Boil the sweet potato for 15 minutes until soft, drain and mash with the second 2 tbsp of oil.
Soften the onion, carrot and mushroom in the oil for 8 minutes, add the garlic, lentils, paste, stock, soy and thyme and simmer for 30 minutes until the lentils are tender and thick.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Spoon the filling into a dish, top with the mash and bake for 25 minutes until golden at the edges.

notes: Contains soy. Vegan. Use tamari instead of soy sauce for gluten-free.

title: Spiced Pumpkin and Chickpea Hand Pies
summary: Flaky folded pies filled with spiced pumpkin, chickpeas and spinach.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Roast the pumpkin with half the oil for 20 minutes until soft.
Soften the onion in the remaining oil for 5 minutes, stir in the curry powder, then the pumpkin, chickpeas, spinach and chutney until the spinach wilts. Cool slightly.
Cut the pastry into 6 large squares, fill, fold, crimp and brush with egg. Bake for 25 minutes until golden.

notes: Contains gluten and egg.

title: Rosemary Lamb and Vegetable Pie with Sweet Potato Mash
summary: A lighter shepherd's pie with lamb mince, vegetables and a sweet potato and potato mash.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Boil the potato and sweet potato for 18 minutes until tender, drain and mash with the butter.

Cook the onion, carrot and lamb in the oil for 10 minutes until browned, add the garlic, paste and flour for 1 minute, then the stock and rosemary and simmer for 12 minutes until thick. Stir in the peas.
Spoon into a dish, top with the mash and bake for 25 minutes until golden and bubbling.

notes: Contains gluten and dairy.
Food safety: lamb mince must reach 75°C with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.

title: Modern Prawn Cocktail Avocados with Marie Rose Sauce
summary: A 70s dinner-party classic updated with lime, avocado and a lighter yoghurt dressing.

steps.text: Whisk the mayonnaise, yoghurt, tomato sauce, worcestershire and lemon together.
Fold through the prawns and keep chilled until serving.
Toast the bread until crisp. Fill each avocado half with lettuce and prawn mixture, scatter over the chives and serve with the toast.

notes: Contains shellfish, egg, dairy and gluten. Use only cooked prawns from a reliable source.
Food safety: keep cooked prawns below 5°C and serve within 30 minutes of leaving the fridge; eat leftovers within 1 day.

title: Oven-Baked Chicken Kievs with Garlic Herb Butter
summary: A 70s classic baked rather than fried, stuffed with garlic and parsley butter and served with green beans.

steps.text: Mix the butter, garlic, parsley and zest and chill until firm. Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Cut a deep pocket into each chicken breast, add a quarter of the butter, then coat in flour, egg and the breadcrumbs mixed with the oil.
Bake for 28 minutes until golden and the chicken reaches 75°C in the thickest part. Steam the beans for 4 minutes until tender and serve.

notes: Contains gluten, dairy and egg.
Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C at the thickest part with no pink and the butter hot; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Salmon en Croute with Spinach and Lemon Cream Cheese
summary: A show-stopping 80s dinner-party dish: salmon wrapped in puff pastry with spinach and cream cheese.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Wilt the spinach in a dry pan for 2 minutes, squeeze very dry and mix with the cream cheese, zest, dill and salt.
Place the salmon on one sheet of pastry, spread with the filling, cover with the second sheet, seal the edges, trim and brush with egg and sesame seeds.
Bake for 35 minutes until the pastry is deep golden and the fish flakes in the centre.

notes: Contains fish, gluten, dairy, egg and sesame. Cut the fillet into 2 smaller fillets for easier wrapping.
Food safety: cook fish until opaque and flaking, and shellfish until opaque and firm; keep raw seafood below 5°C, refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.

title: Beef Wellington with Mushroom Duxelles
summary: The classic dinner-party centrepiece with a simplified duxelles and puff pastry.

steps.text: Sear the seasoned beef in the oil for 6 minutes all over, brush with mustard and chill. Cook the mushroom, garlic and thyme in a dry pan for 12 minutes until all the moisture has gone.
Lay the ham on cling film, spread the mushroom over, roll the beef in it, chill for 20 minutes, then wrap in the pastry and brush with egg.
Bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 35 minutes until the pastry is golden and the beef reaches 55 to 60°C for medium. Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

notes: Contains gluten and egg. Use a probe thermometer; the centre stays pink for medium.

Food safety: whole cuts of beef can be served medium (55 to 60°C) once the outside is fully seared; for children, pregnant women and the elderly, cook to 70°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Baked Chicken Cordon Bleu with Lemon and Greens
summary: Chicken breast stuffed with ham and Swiss cheese, crumbed and baked with a lemon and green bean side.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Slit each chicken breast open, fill with ham and cheese and close with toothpicks.
Coat in flour, egg and the breadcrumbs mixed with the oil, and bake for 30 minutes until golden and the chicken reaches 75°C.
Steam the beans for 4 minutes until tender and serve with the lemon wedges.

notes: Contains gluten, dairy and egg. Remove toothpicks before serving.
Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C at the thickest part; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Lighter Coq au Vin with Mushrooms and Baby Onions
summary: A modernised French braise with chicken thigh, mushrooms and less fat, served with mash.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil for 6 minutes each side and set aside. Cook the bacon, onions and mushroom in the pot for 8 minutes until golden, then stir in the garlic and flour for 1 minute.
Add the wine, stock and thyme, return the chicken, cover and simmer for 35 minutes until the chicken is falling off the bone and reaches 75°C.
Boil the potato for 15 minutes until tender, mash with the butter and serve with the coq au vin.

notes: Contains gluten and dairy.
Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Prawn and Pea Risotto with Lemon and Mint
summary: Creamy risotto with prawns, peas and a squeeze of lemon, a modern take on a 90s favourite.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add the garlic and rice for 1 minute, then the wine until absorbed.
Add the hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for 20 minutes until the rice is creamy and tender.
Stir in the prawns and peas for 3 minutes until the prawns are pink and cooked, then the butter, parmesan, lemon and mint.

notes: Contains shellfish and dairy.
Food safety: cook fish until opaque and flaking, and shellfish until opaque and firm; keep raw seafood below 5°C, refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.

title: Christmas Glazed Ham with Orange Mustard Glaze
summary: A cooked leg ham scored and baked with an orange, mustard and brown sugar glaze, great hot or cold on Christmas Day.

items.item: cooked leg ham on the bone
items.raw: 4kg cooked leg ham on the bone

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Peel the rind off the ham, leaving a thin layer of fat, and score it in a diamond pattern, pressing a clove into each cross.
Warm the marmalade, sugar, mustard and juice in a pan for 3 minutes until syrupy.
Brush the ham with half the glaze and bake for 1 hour, brushing every 20 minutes until deep, sticky and golden.

notes: Christmas in summer: serve cold with salad and bread if it is hot. Ham is salty.
Food safety: a cooked ham is reheated until steaming hot at the centre (at least 70°C); refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 4 days.

title: Christmas Turkey Breast Roll with Herb Butter and Cranberry
summary: A boneless turkey breast roasted with herb butter, perfect for a smaller Christmas table.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Mix the butter, thyme, garlic and zest and rub all over the turkey.
Sit it on the onion in a tray with the stock and roast for 75 minutes until golden and a thermometer in the centre reads 75°C.
Rest for 15 minutes, slice and serve with the pan juices and cranberry sauce.

notes: Contains dairy.
Food safety: turkey must reach 75°C in the centre; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Christmas Prawn and Mango Platter with Lime Mayo
summary: A cold summer-Christmas platter of cooked prawns, mango, avocado and lime mayonnaise.

steps.text: Arrange the lettuce on a platter and top with the mango and avocado.
Check the prawns are opaque and firm, then pile them on top and scatter over the chilli and coriander.
Stir the mayonnaise with the lime zest and juice, adding a spoonful of water until pourable, and serve alongside.

notes: Contains shellfish and egg. Keep chilled until serving.
Food safety: keep cooked prawns below 5°C and serve within 30 minutes of leaving the fridge; eat leftovers within 1 day.

title: Thanksgiving Turkey Breast with Sage Gravy and Cornbread Stuffing
summary: A smaller-scale Thanksgiving dinner using a turkey breast roll, a sage gravy and cornbread stuffing.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Rub the turkey with the butter and sage and roast on a tray for 70 minutes, until the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Soften the onion and celery in a little butter for 6 minutes, mix with the cornbread, egg and 1 cup of stock and bake in a dish alongside for 30 minutes until golden.
Rest the turkey, stir the flour into the pan juices for 1 minute, add 2 cups of stock and simmer for 5 minutes until thick for the gravy.

notes: Contains gluten, dairy and egg.
Food safety: turkey must reach 75°C at the thickest part, and stuffing baked separately until steaming hot; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Lunar New Year Longevity Noodles with Prawns and Greens
summary: Long egg noodles tossed in garlicky soy sauce with prawns, mushrooms and bok choy.

steps.text: Boil the noodles for 4 minutes until tender and drain. Fry the prawns in half the oil for 3 minutes until pink and set aside.
Fry the garlic and mushroom in the remaining oil for 4 minutes until golden, add the bok choy for 2 minutes until wilted.
Toss in the noodles, prawns, soy sauce, oyster sauce and sesame oil until everything is coated and scatter with spring onion.

notes: Contains shellfish, gluten, soy, egg and sesame.
Food safety: cook fish until opaque and flaking, and shellfish until opaque and firm; keep raw seafood below 5°C, refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.

title: Eid Spiced Lamb and Rice Tray Bake
summary: A halal-friendly, fragrant tray bake of spiced lamb, rice, almonds and sultanas that feeds a crowd.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Mix the lamb, onion and spices and press into the base of a large deep tray with the oil.
Scatter over the rice, sultanas and half the almonds, pour in the hot stock and cover tightly with foil.
Bake for 45 minutes until the rice is tender and the lamb is cooked through. Scatter the parsley and remaining almonds and serve with yoghurt.

notes: Made with halal-certified meat and stock if required. Contains dairy, nuts and gluten (if stock contains it).
Food safety: lamb mince must reach 75°C with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Eid Chicken Mandi-Style Rice with Tomato Sauce
summary: Spiced chicken legs over fragrant rice with raisins and a fiery tomato salsa.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Rub the chicken with the spices and oil and roast for 45 minutes until golden and the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Meanwhile simmer the rice in the stock with raisins, covered, for 15 minutes until tender.
Mix the tomato, chilli and coriander into a salsa and serve the chicken over the rice.

notes: Made with halal chicken if required.
Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C at the thickest part with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Diwali Paneer Pea Masala with Jeera Rice
summary: A festive vegetarian main of paneer and peas in a creamy tomato masala with cumin rice.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the ghee for 8 minutes until golden, add the ginger, garlic and spices for 1 minute, then the tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes. Blend until smooth if you like.
Stir in the cream, paneer and peas and simmer for 6 minutes until the peas are tender.
Cook the rice with the cumin seeds for 12 minutes until tender and serve.

notes: Contains dairy. Paneer is a vegetarian cheese made without animal rennet.

title: Diwali Stuffed Capsicum with Spiced Potato and Cashews
summary: Whole capsicums stuffed with spiced potato, peas and cashews and baked until soft.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Fry the cumin seeds and onion in the oil for 5 minutes until golden, add the spices, potato, peas and cashews for 4 minutes, then the lemon and coriander.
Fill the capsicums with the mix, stand them upright in a dish with 1/4 cup of water and replace the tops.
Bake for 30 minutes until the capsicums are tender and slightly charred. Serve with the yoghurt.

notes: Contains nuts and dairy. Use dairy-free yoghurt for vegan.

title: Passover-Style Slow-Roast Lamb Shoulder with Lemon and Herbs
summary: Lamb shoulder roasted until falling apart with garlic, lemon and rosemary. Contains no flour, grains or leavening.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Stab the lamb all over, push in the garlic, and rub with the rosemary, lemon and oil.
Place on the potato in a deep tray, add the stock, cover tightly with foil and roast for 3.5 hours.
Remove the foil, raise to 220°C (200°C fan) and roast for 20 minutes until browned and the meat shreds easily.

notes: Uses no flour, grains or leavening, but check packaged ingredients such as stock for Passover certification if you observe it.
Food safety: lamb must be cooked until tender and above 75°C; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.

title: Slow-Braised Brisket with Carrots and Onions for Passover
summary: Beef brisket braised for hours with onions, carrots and garlic until it slices easily. Uses no flour or grains.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C (130°C fan). Brown the seasoned brisket in the oil on all sides for 10 minutes and set aside.

Soften the onions for 8 minutes, add the garlic, paprika and paste for 1 minute, then the stock and bay leaf. Return the brisket with the carrots, cover tightly and braise for 3.5 hours until very tender.
Rest for 20 minutes, slice across the grain and serve with the sauce and parsley.

notes: Uses no flour, grains or leavening, but check packaged ingredients such as stock for Passover certification if you observe it.
Food safety: braise until very tender and well above 75°C; cool quickly, refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.

title: Easter Roast Lamb with Garlic, Rosemary and Spring Vegetables
summary: A classic Easter lamb leg roasted pink with asparagus and baby carrots.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Stud the lamb with garlic and rub with rosemary, oil and zest.
Roast with the potato and carrots for 90 minutes until a thermometer reads 60°C for medium or 70°C for well done. Add the asparagus for the last 10 minutes.
Rest the lamb for 20 minutes and slice.

notes: Spring vegetables suit Easter in the northern hemisphere; in Australia, use autumn veg like pumpkin.

Food safety: whole cuts of lamb can be served medium (60°C) when the outside is seared; cook to 70°C for children, the elderly and pregnancy. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.

title: Easter Ham and Egg Pie with Parsley
summary: A puff-topped pie of ham, egg and parsley.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line a pie dish with one sheet of pastry.
Layer the ham and parsley in the base, crack in 6 eggs, and pour over the cream mixed with the remaining 2 beaten eggs, parmesan and pepper.
Cover with the second sheet, seal, cut a slit and bake for 40 minutes until puffed and golden and the egg is set in the centre.

notes: Contains gluten, dairy and egg.
Food safety: cook until the egg is fully set; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Iftar Chicken and Rice with Apricots and Almonds
summary: A gentle, nourishing iftar main of spiced chicken, rice, sweet apricots and toasted almonds.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil for 6 minutes, add the onion and spices for 4 minutes until soft.
Stir in the rice, stock and apricots, cover and cook gently for 20 minutes until the rice is tender and the chicken reaches 75°C.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 2 minutes until golden and scatter over with the parsley.

notes: Made with halal chicken if required. Contains nuts.
Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C at the thickest part with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Iftar Red Lentil Soup with Lemon and Spiced Lamb Fatayer
summary: A comforting lentil soup served with small pastry pockets of spiced lamb.

steps.text: Simmer the lentils, onion, carrot, cumin and stock for 25 minutes until the lentils are soft, blend smooth and add the lemon.
Fry the lamb, onion and allspice in the oil for 8 minutes until browned with no pink left. Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan).
Cut the dough into 12 rounds, fill, pinch into triangles and bake for 15 minutes until golden. Serve with the soup.

notes: Contains gluten. Made with halal lamb if required.
Food safety: lamb mince must reach 75°C with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Iftar Grilled Fish with Chermoula and Saffron Rice
summary: Firm white fish grilled with a fresh coriander and cumin chermoula over saffron rice.

steps.text: Blend the coriander, parsley, garlic, cumin, paprika, lemon and oil into a chermoula and spoon half over the fish.
Cook the rice with the saffron in 3 cups of water for 12 minutes until tender.
Grill the fish for 5 minutes each side until opaque and flaking, and serve with the remaining chermoula over the rice.

notes: Contains fish.
Food safety: cook fish until opaque and flaking, and shellfish until opaque and firm; keep raw seafood below 5°C, refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.

title: Picnic Halloumi and Roast Vegetable Frittata Squares
summary: A portable frittata of roasted vegetables and halloumi, cut into squares for the picnic basket.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan) and line a 20cm by 30cm tin. Roast the zucchini, capsicum and onion with the oil for 15 minutes until soft.
Whisk the eggs, milk, halloumi, basil and salt and stir in the vegetables, then pour into the tin.
Bake for 25 minutes until puffed and set in the centre. Cool and cut into squares.

notes: Contains egg and dairy. Keep cold in a cooler bag.
Food safety: cook until the egg is set; keep chilled below 5°C and eat within 2 hours of leaving the fridge; refrigerate leftovers and eat within 2 days.

title: Layered Chicken, Corn and Black Bean Enchilada Bake for a Crowd
summary: A layered, make-ahead enchilada bake with shredded chicken, corn, beans and cheese that travels well.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Mix the chicken, beans, corn and 1 cup of the sauce.
Layer tortillas, chicken mixture and cheese in a large dish, three times, and pour over the remaining sauce.
Bake for 30 minutes until bubbling and golden. Serve with sour cream and coriander.

notes: Contains dairy.
Food safety: chicken must be cooked to 75°C before shredding; reheat until steaming hot and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Potluck Sesame Noodle Salad with Edamame and Cucumber
summary: A cold noodle salad with a creamy sesame dressing that travels beautifully.

steps.text: Boil the soba for 5 minutes until tender, drain and rinse under cold water. Cook the edamame in boiling water for 3 minutes until bright green.
Whisk the tahini, soy, vinegar, sesame oil, maple syrup and 1/4 cup of water until smooth.
Toss everything together with the dressing and sprinkle with the sesame seeds.

notes: Contains gluten, soy and sesame. Use 100% buckwheat soba and tamari for gluten-free.

title: Potluck Baked Ziti with Italian Sausage and Spinach
summary: A hearty baked pasta for a crowd with sausage, tomato, spinach and melting mozzarella.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Boil the penne for 8 minutes until almost tender and drain.
Brown the sausage and onion for 8 minutes until cooked through with no pink, add the garlic and tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes, then stir in the spinach until wilted.
Toss the pasta with the sauce and ricotta, tip into a dish, top with the cheeses and bake for 25 minutes until golden and bubbling.

notes: Contains gluten and dairy.
Food safety: sausage must reach 75°C with no pink; reheat until steaming hot and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Picnic Chicken and Vegetable Hand Pies
summary: Handheld puff pastry pies with chicken, corn and carrot that are good cold.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil for 5 minutes, add the onion and carrot for 5 minutes, stir in the flour, then the stock and corn and simmer for 5 minutes until thick. Cool completely.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cut the pastry into 8 squares, fill, fold over, crimp and brush with egg.
Bake for 25 minutes until puffed and golden and the filling is steaming.

notes: Contains gluten and egg.
Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C at the thickest part with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Chana Masala with Fresh Ginger and Coriander
summary: A North Indian chickpea curry in a tangy tomato and onion gravy, served with rice.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the oil for 8 minutes until golden, add the ginger, garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and chickpeas with 1/2 cup of water and simmer for 20 minutes until thick. Cook the rice separately until tender.
Finish with the lemon and coriander and serve over the rice.

notes: Vegan and gluten free.

title: Egyptian-Style Stewed Beans with Lemon, Tahini and Soft Egg
summary: Stewed beans in the style of ful medames, with cumin, lemon and tahini, served with a boiled egg and flatbread.

steps.text: Simmer the beans with the garlic, cumin and 1/2 cup of water for 8 minutes until heated through and lightly mashed.
Boil the eggs for 7 minutes until the yolks are just set, then peel. Whisk the tahini with half the lemon and 2 tablespoons of water until smooth.
Stir the remaining lemon and the oil through the beans, top with the egg, tahini, tomato and parsley and serve with the flatbread.

notes: Contains egg, gluten and sesame.
Food safety: boil eggs until the whites and yolks are set; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Rajma Kidney Bean Curry with Cumin Rice
summary: A creamy Punjabi-style red kidney bean curry served with cumin rice.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 8 minutes until golden, add the ginger, garlic and spices for 1 minute, then the tomatoes and simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the beans and 1/2 cup of water and simmer for 20 minutes until thick, mashing a few beans against the pan.
Cook the rice with the cumin seeds until tender and serve with the curry and coriander.

notes: Vegan and gluten free.

title: Brazilian Bean and Egg Pan with Greens
summary: A Brazilian-inspired pan of pinto beans, silverbeet, garlic and fried eggs.

steps.text: Cook the rice. Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add the garlic and paprika for 1 minute.
Add the beans and silverbeet and cook for 6 minutes until the greens are wilted and the beans are hot.
Fry or poach the eggs until the whites are set and serve over the beans with the spring onion, lime and rice.

notes: Contains egg.
Food safety: cook eggs until the whites are set; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: White Bean and Silverbeet Stew with Rustic Bread
summary: A thick Tuscan-style stew of cannellini beans, silverbeet and tomato thickened with bread.

steps.text: Soften the onion, carrot and celery in the oil for 8 minutes, add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, beans and stock and simmer for 20 minutes until thick, then add the silverbeet for 5 minutes until wilted.
Stir through the bread until it breaks down and thickens the stew and serve topped with the cheese.

notes: Contains gluten and dairy. Skip the cheese for vegan.

title: Ethiopian-Style Red Lentil Stew with Collard Greens
summary: A warming, spicy red lentil stew in the style of misir wot, with sauteed greens and injera-style flatbread.

steps.text: Cook the onions in the oil for 10 minutes until very soft, add the garlic, ginger, spices and paste for 2 minutes.
Add the lentils and stock and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring, until thick and soft.
Stir through the silverbeet for 4 minutes until wilted and serve with the flatbread.

notes: Contains gluten (flatbread). Add chilli flakes for heat.

title: Caribbean Red Bean and Sweet Potato Stew with Coconut
summary: Kidney beans and sweet potato simmered in coconut milk with thyme and allspice, served with rice.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add the garlic, ginger, allspice and thyme for 1 minute.
Add the sweet potato, beans, coconut milk and stock and simmer for 25 minutes until the sweet potato is tender. Cook the rice separately until tender.
Serve over the rice and scatter with the spring onion.

notes: Vegan and gluten free. Use tinned kidney beans; if using dried, soak overnight and boil hard for 10 minutes before simmering.

title: Pan-Seared Snapper with Celery, Tomato and White Beans
summary: A Mediterranean fillet of snapper over a warm celery, tomato and cannellini bean base.

steps.text: Soften the celery in half the oil for 6 minutes, add the garlic and tomato for 3 minutes, then the wine, beans and zest and simmer for 6 minutes.
Sear the seasoned fish in the remaining oil, skin side down, for 4 minutes, turn and cook for 2 minutes until opaque and flaking.
Serve the fish on the beans with the parsley.

notes: Contains fish.
Food safety: cook fish until opaque and flaking, and shellfish until opaque and firm; keep raw seafood below 5°C, refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.

title: Seared Tuna with Salsa Verde and Roast Potatoes
summary: Seared tuna fillets with a punchy parsley, caper and lemon salsa verde and roasted potatoes.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Roast the potato with 2 tablespoons of oil for 25 minutes until crisp.
Blitz the parsley, capers, garlic, lemon and 1/4 cup oil into a rough salsa verde. Steam the beans for 4 minutes until tender.
Sear the tuna in the remaining oil for 2 minutes each side until browned outside and slightly pink within, and serve with the salsa verde, potato and beans.

notes: Contains fish. Choose pole-and-line or sustainably certified tuna.

Food safety: tuna may be served rare in the centre only if very fresh and sashimi-grade; cook through to opaque for children, pregnancy or the elderly. Keep below 5°C, refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.

title: Squid and Chorizo Pan with Chickpeas and Lemon
summary: Quick-seared squid with chorizo and chickpeas in a smoky tomato sauce.

steps.text: Fry the chorizo in the oil for 4 minutes until crisp and the oil turns red, add the onion for 5 minutes, then the garlic and paprika for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and chickpeas and simmer for 8 minutes until thick.
Stir in the squid and cook for 2 minutes until just opaque, then finish with the lemon and parsley.

notes: Squid goes tough past 3 minutes of cooking.
Food safety: cook fish until opaque and flaking, and shellfish until opaque and firm; keep raw seafood below 5°C, refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.

title: Crab and Lime Fritters with Smashed Avocado
summary: Pan-fried fritters with crab and sweetcorn, served with a fresh avocado and lime salsa.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder, eggs and milk into a thick batter and fold in the corn, crab and spring onion.
Fry heaped spoonfuls in the oil for 3 minutes each side until golden and cooked through, in batches.
Mix the avocado, tomato, lime and coriander and serve on top.

notes: Contains shellfish, gluten, egg and dairy.
Food safety: cook fish until opaque and flaking, and shellfish until opaque and firm; keep raw seafood below 5°C, refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.

title: Slow-Braised Beef Cheek Ragu with Pappardelle
summary: Tender beef cheeks braised in tomato and red wine, shredded through ribbon pasta.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C (130°C fan). Brown the beef in the oil in batches and set aside.
Soften the onion and carrot for 6 minutes, add the garlic, wine, tomatoes, stock and rosemary, return the beef, cover and braise for 2.5 hours until the cheeks fall apart.
Shred the beef into the sauce. Boil the pappardelle for 9 minutes until al dente and toss with the ragu and parmesan.

notes: Contains gluten and dairy.
Food safety: beef must be cooked until tender and well above 75°C; cool leftovers quickly, refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.

title: Black Pepper Beef Heart and Mushroom Stir-Fry
summary: Thin slices of lean beef heart stir-fried hot and fast with mushrooms and black pepper sauce.

items.raw: 500g beef heart, trimmed and thinly sliced

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender. Toss the beef heart with the cornflour.
Stir-fry the beef in half the oil in a very hot wok for 3 minutes until browned and cooked through, then set aside. Stir-fry the mushroom, capsicum and garlic in the remaining oil for 4 minutes.
Return the beef with the soy, oyster sauce and pepper for 1 minute and serve over the rice with spring onion.

notes: Heart is a lean muscle, not tough if sliced thinly and cooked quickly. Contains soy and gluten.
Food safety: cook offal until no pink remains and it reaches 75°C; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Peri-Peri-Style Chicken Livers with Garlic Bread
summary: A South African-Portuguese favourite: chicken livers in a warm chilli and cream sauce with garlic bread.

steps.text: Fry the onion in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, add the garlic and the livers and cook for 4 minutes until browned.
Add the chilli, cream and lemon and simmer for 3 minutes until the livers are cooked through with no pink.
Toast the baguette with the butter until golden and serve with the livers and parsley.

notes: Contains gluten and dairy. Avoid in pregnancy due to high vitamin A.
Food safety: cook liver until no pink remains and it reaches 75°C; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.

title: Crispy Baked Tofu with Sweet Chilli and Sesame Greens
summary: Oven-baked tofu cubes in a sticky sweet chilli glaze with sesame broccolini and rice.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the tofu in the soy, cornflour and oil and bake on a tray for 25 minutes until golden and crisp, turning once.
Cook the rice. Steam the broccolini for 4 minutes until tender and toss with the sesame oil and seeds.
Toss the hot tofu with the sweet chilli sauce for 1 minute and serve with the greens and rice.

notes: Contains soy and sesame.

title: Braised Tofu and Mushroom Claypot-Style Rice
summary: Rice, tofu, shiitake and greens cooked together in one pot with a caramelised soy base.

steps.text: Brown the tofu in the oil for 6 minutes until golden, add the mushroom, garlic and ginger for 4 minutes.
Stir in the rice, soy, oyster sauce and stock, cover and cook gently for 15 minutes until the rice is nearly tender.
Lay the bok choy on top, cover for 5 minutes until wilted and drizzle with sesame oil.

notes: Contains soy, gluten and sesame. Use vegetarian mushroom sauce for a vegan version.

title: Eggplant and Lentil Moussaka-Style Bake
summary: A plant-based moussaka layered with lentil ragu, grilled eggplant and a creamy yoghurt topping.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Brush the eggplant with oil and roast for 20 minutes until golden.
Soften the onion in a little oil, add the garlic, lentils, tomatoes, stock and cinnamon and simmer for 25 minutes until the lentils are tender and thick.
Layer the eggplant and lentils in a dish. Whisk the eggs, yoghurt and half the cheese, pour over, top with the remaining cheese and bake for 25 minutes until golden and set.

notes: Contains egg and dairy.
Food safety: bake until the egg topping is set; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Slow-Cooker Beef and Barley Stew with Root Vegetables
summary: A hearty stew of diced beef, pearl barley, carrot and potato that cooks all day while you are out.

steps.text: Brown the beef in the oil in batches for 5 minutes and tip into the slow cooker.
Add the onion, garlic, tomato paste, stock, bay leaves, carrot, potato and barley and stir well.
Cook on low for 8 hours until the beef is tender and the barley is soft, then remove the bay leaves and serve.

notes: Contains gluten.
Food safety: cook beef until tender and steaming hot throughout (at least 75°C); refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.

title: Pressure-Cooker Chicken and Chickpea Tagine
summary: Chicken thighs, chickpeas and dried apricots in a warm spiced sauce, ready in about 35 minutes in the pressure cooker.

steps.text: Use the sauté setting to soften the onion in the oil for 4 minutes, add the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Add the chicken, chickpeas, tomatoes, apricots and stock, seal and cook at high pressure for 10 minutes, then release the pressure.
Check the chicken is cooked through at 75°C. Prepare the couscous with boiling water until the grains are tender, then serve the tagine over it with the coriander.

notes: Contains gluten (couscous).
Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C at the thickest part with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Sheet-Pan Garlic and Thyme Chicken with Potatoes and Green Beans
summary: Chicken thighs roasted on one tray with baby potatoes, lemon and thyme, with green beans added at the end.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C. Toss the potatoes, garlic, lemon, thyme, oil and salt on a large tray, then nestle the chicken on top, skin side up.
Roast for 25 minutes, add the beans, and roast for 12 minutes more until the chicken is golden and cooked through.
Rest for 5 minutes and spoon the tray juices over to serve.

notes: Gluten free.
Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C at the thickest part with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Freezer-Batch Turkey and Vegetable Meatballs in Tomato Sauce
summary: Turkey meatballs with grated zucchini and carrot, simmered in tomato sauce and portioned for the freezer.

steps.text: Mix the mince, zucchini, carrot, crumbs, egg, parmesan and oregano and roll into 32 balls.
Soften the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes, add the tomatoes and 1/2 cup of water, and bring to a simmer.
Add the meatballs, cover and simmer for 20 minutes, turning once, until cooked through.
Cool, portion into containers and freeze.

notes: Contains egg, dairy and gluten. Parmesan is not vegetarian.

Food safety: mince must reach 75°C throughout with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days. Freeze in portions for up to 3 months and thaw in the fridge overnight; reheat until steaming hot.

title: Slow-Cooker Pulled Pork Rolls with Apple Slaw
summary: Smoky pulled pork shoulder piled into rolls with a crisp apple and cabbage slaw.

steps.text: Rub the pork with the sugar, paprika, cumin and 1 teaspoon of salt, then set on the sliced onion in the slow cooker with the vinegar and stock.
Cook on low for 8 hours until the pork shreds easily, then shred and toss in the juices.
Toss the cabbage, apple and mayonnaise for the slaw and pile into the rolls with the pork.

notes: Contains egg and gluten.
Food safety: pork must reach 70°C or more with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Pressure-Cooker Lamb and Chickpea Curry
summary: Tender lamb shoulder and chickpeas in a mild tomato curry sauce, pressure cooked in under an hour.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil using the sauté setting for 6 minutes, then add the onion, garlic, ginger and spices for 3 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, chickpeas and stock, seal and cook at high pressure for 25 minutes, then release naturally.
Cook the rice separately until tender. Check the lamb is tender and steaming hot, then stir the yoghurt through the curry off the heat and serve.

notes: Contains dairy.
Food safety: cook lamb until tender and at least 75°C throughout; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: One-Pot Lemon Chicken and Rice with Peas
summary: Chicken thighs and rice cooked together in one pot with lemon, garlic and peas.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil in a lidded pot for 5 minutes, add the onion and garlic and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in the rice, stock and lemon zest, cover and simmer on low for 18 minutes until the rice is tender.
Stir through the peas and lemon juice, rest covered for 5 minutes, then scatter with parsley.

notes: Gluten free.
Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C at the thickest part with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Sheet-Pan Baked Salmon with Broccolini and Sweet Potato
summary: Salmon fillets roasted with sweet potato wedges and broccolini on one tray, finished with lemon.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C. Toss the sweet potato with half the oil, paprika and salt on a tray and roast for 15 minutes.
Add the broccolini and salmon, drizzle with the remaining oil, and roast for 12 minutes until the salmon flakes.
Serve with the lemon wedges.

notes: Gluten free and dairy free.
Food safety: cook fish until opaque and flaking, and shellfish until opaque and firm; keep raw seafood below 5°C, refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day.

title: Freezer-Friendly Beef and Bean Burrito Parcels
summary: Beef mince, black beans and cheese rolled in tortillas, wrapped individually and frozen for quick lunches.

steps.text: Brown the mince and onion in the oil for 8 minutes, add the spices, tomato paste, beans and 1/2 cup of water and simmer for 8 minutes.
Cool the filling, then roll with the cheese into the tortillas and wrap each in baking paper.
Freeze, then reheat from frozen in a 180°C oven for 25 minutes or until steaming hot throughout.

notes: Contains dairy and gluten.

Food safety: mince must reach 75°C throughout with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days. Freeze in portions for up to 3 months and thaw in the fridge overnight; reheat until steaming hot.

title: Slow-Cooker Chicken Cacciatore with Olives
summary: Chicken thighs braised with capsicum, tomato and olives, served over soft polenta.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil for 5 minutes and place in the slow cooker with the onion, capsicum, garlic, tomatoes, olives, stock and oregano.
Cook on low for 6 hours until the chicken falls from the bone.
Cook the polenta in 4 cups of water until thick, and serve under the chicken.

notes: Gluten free.
Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C at the thickest part with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: High-Protein Chicken Burrito Bowl Meal Prep
summary: Four lunch boxes of spiced chicken, rice, black beans and corn with a lime yoghurt dressing.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and cool. Toss the chicken with the cumin, paprika and oil and pan-fry for 8 minutes until cooked through.
Divide the rice, chicken, beans, corn, tomato and lettuce into four containers.
Mix the yoghurt and lime and add a spoonful to each. Keep refrigerated.

notes: Contains dairy.
Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C at the thickest part with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days. Eat within 2 days of cooking when packed.

title: Pressure-Cooker Beef Ragu with Pappardelle
summary: A rich shredded beef and tomato ragu cooked fast in the pressure cooker and tossed through ribbon pasta.

steps.text: Brown the beef in the oil on the sauté setting, then add the onion, carrot, celery, garlic and tomato paste for 4 minutes.
