Bake for 16 minutes until golden at the edges, then cool on the tray.

notes: Snack. Dessert. Vegetarian.

title: Pumpkin Fritters with Cinnamon Sugar
summary: Soft spiced pumpkin fritters fried until golden and rolled in cinnamon sugar.

steps.text: Mash the pumpkin, then stir in the flour, egg, milk and 1/2 tsp cinnamon to a thick batter.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat.
Fry spoonfuls for 3 minutes each side until puffed and golden brown.
Drain, then roll in the sugar mixed with the remaining cinnamon.

notes: Food safety: fry until the centre is cooked through. Snack. Vegetarian.

title: Soy Poached Chicken with Ginger Spring Onion Oil
summary: Silky poached chicken sliced over rice with a hot ginger and spring onion oil.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of water to a gentle simmer until just trembling, with half the ginger, the whole spring onions, wine and salt.
Lower in the chicken, cover, turn off the heat after 10 minutes of simmering and leave for 40 minutes until cooked through.
Check the thickest part of the thigh reads 75°C, then plunge the chicken into iced water for 10 minutes.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender, using a ladle of the poaching broth in place of some water.
Heat the neutral oil until shimmering and pour over the remaining ginger and sliced spring onion with the sesame oil and half the soy sauce.
Carve the chicken, serve over rice with the cucumber and spoon over the ginger oil and remaining soy sauce.

notes: Food safety: the thickest part of the thigh must reach 75°C and the juices run clear. Hot oil spits, so pour carefully.
Dinner. Dairy-free.

title: Dan Dan Noodles with Spiced Pork
summary: Springy noodles in a nutty, tingly chilli sauce topped with crisp spiced pork mince.

steps.text: Fry the pork in the oil over high heat for 6 minutes until crisp and cooked through, adding the garlic and peppercorn for the last minute.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, vinegar, chilli oil and 3 tbsp hot water until smooth.
Boil the noodles for 4 minutes until tender, adding the spinach for the last 30 seconds, then drain.
Toss the noodles with the sauce, top with the pork and spring onion.

notes: Food safety: pork mince must reach 75°C throughout with no pink.
Dinner. Dairy-free.

title: Ginger Soy Steamed White Fish with Hot Oil
summary: Delicate steamed fish fillets topped with sizzling oil, ginger and spring onion.

items.raw: 3 spring onion, cut into thin strips

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Place the fish on a heatproof plate with half the ginger and spring onion and steam over high heat for 8 minutes until the flesh turns opaque and flakes easily.
Pour off the liquid, then mix the soy sauce, wine, sugar and sesame oil and pour over the fish.
Top with the remaining ginger, spring onion and coriander, then heat the oil until smoking and pour it over.
Serve straight away with rice.

notes: Food safety: the fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes with a fork. Hot oil spits, so pour carefully.
Dinner. Dairy-free.

title: Braised Eggplant in Garlic Sauce
summary: Silky eggplant braised in a sweet, sour and spicy garlic sauce until glossy.

steps.text: Fry the eggplant in the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat for 8 minutes until browned and soft, then lift out.
Fry the garlic, ginger and doubanjiang for 1 minute until the oil turns red.
Add the stock, soy sauce, vinegar and sugar and return the eggplant, then simmer for 8 minutes until the sauce is thick and clings.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender, and serve topped with spring onion.

notes: Dinner. Vegan.

title: Gyudon Beef and Onion Rice Bowls
summary: Thinly sliced beef and sweet onion simmered in a soy dashi sauce over rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and sticky.
Simmer the dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar in a pan, add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the beef and cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until no pink remains.
Spoon the beef and sauce over the rice and top with spring onion and pickled ginger.

notes: Food safety: thin beef slices are cooked once no pink remains and they reach 71°C.
Dinner. Dairy-free.

title: Pan-Fried Mushroom and Cabbage Gyoza
summary: Crisp-bottomed dumplings filled with mushroom and cabbage, pleated by hand.

steps.text: Salt the wombok lightly for 10 minutes, squeeze out the liquid, then mix with the mushrooms, garlic, ginger, spring onion, 1 tbsp soy sauce and the sesame oil.
Place a spoonful of filling in each wrapper, wet the edge, then fold and pleat to seal.
Heat the oil in a wide non-stick pan and sit the gyoza flat-side down for 3 minutes until golden underneath.
Pour in the water, cover and steam for 5 minutes until the wrappers turn translucent and the water has gone.
Mix the remaining soy sauce with the vinegar for dipping.

notes: Dinner. Vegan.

title: Spicy Gochujang Chicken and Sweet Potato Pan
summary: Chicken thigh, cabbage and sweet potato stir-fried in a fiery gochujang sauce.

steps.text: Mix the gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, honey and garlic and coat the chicken in it.
Cook the sweet potato in the oil in a wide pan over medium heat for 8 minutes until starting to soften.
Add the chicken, onion and cabbage and stir-fry for 12 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce is sticky.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender, and serve the dakgalbi with spring onion.

notes: Food safety: the thickest piece of chicken must reach 75°C with no pink juices. Plus 30 minutes marinating.
Dinner. Dairy-free.

title: Soy Braised Beef Short Rib Pot
summary: Beef chuck braised with daikon and carrot in a sweet soy sauce until falling apart.

steps.text: Boil the beef in water for 5 minutes, then drain and rinse to remove scum.
Return the beef to the pot with the soy sauce, sugar, mirin, onion, garlic, ginger, sesame oil and 3 cups water.
Cover and simmer gently for 90 minutes until the beef is tender.
Add the daikon and carrot and simmer uncovered for 40 minutes until tender and the sauce is thick and glossy.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender, and serve the braise over the rice.

notes: Food safety: braised beef should reach at least 75°C in the centre and be fork-tender.
Dinner. Dairy-free.

title: Sweet Soy Wide Noodles with Crisp Tofu
summary: Wide rice noodles charred in a sweet soy sauce with tofu and gai lan.

steps.text: Fry the tofu in 1 tbsp oil in a hot wok for 6 minutes until golden, then lift out.
Stir-fry the garlic in the remaining oil for 30 seconds, then add the noodles and press against the wok for 2 minutes until charred.
Add the gai lan and sauces with the sugar and toss for 3 minutes until the stalks are tender-crisp.
Return the tofu, toss and serve immediately.

notes: Dinner. Vegetarian (oyster sauce makes this not vegan; use mushroom-free soy for a vegan version).

title: Curried Pineapple Rice with Prawns and Cashews
summary: Fragrant wok-fried rice with sweet pineapple, prawns and cashews.

steps.text: Use cold, day-old rice that was cooled and refrigerated within 1 hour of cooking.
Fry the garlic in the oil over high heat for 30 seconds, push aside and scramble the eggs for 1 minute until set.
Add the prawns and cook for 3 minutes until pink and opaque, then add the rice, curry powder and soy sauce and toss for 4 minutes until hot.
Toss through the pineapple, cashews and spring onion.

notes: Food safety: cool leftover rice and refrigerate it within 1 hour; prawns are cooked when pink and opaque. Reheat until steaming hot.
Dinner. Dairy-free.

title: Shaking Beef Bo Luc Lac
summary: Cubes of seared beef tossed in a garlicky soy sauce and served on herbs with a lime dip.

steps.text: Marinate the beef with the garlic, soy sauce, oyster sauce and sugar.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Heat the oil in a wok until smoking and sear the beef in two batches for 2 minutes, shaking the pan, until browned outside and pink in the centre.
Arrange the rocket, red onion and tomato on plates and pile the beef on top.
Mix the lime juice, pepper and salt for dipping, and serve with the rice.

notes: Food safety: beef cubes should reach 63°C internal for medium or 71°C for well done. Plus 30 minutes marinating.
Dinner. Dairy-free.

title: Chicken Satay Skewers with Peanut Sauce
summary: Turmeric-marinated chicken skewers with a rich peanut dipping sauce and cucumber.

steps.text: Mix the oil, turmeric, coriander, cumin, garlic and kecap manis and coat the chicken in it. Thread onto skewers.
Grill for 10 minutes, turning, until charred and cooked through.
Warm the peanut butter, coconut milk, soy sauce and lime juice for 4 minutes until smooth and thick.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender, and serve the skewers with the sauce, rice and cucumber.

notes: Food safety: the chicken must reach 75°C throughout with no pink juices. Plus 1 hour marinating.
Dinner. Dairy-free.

title: Smoky Wok Rice Noodles with Prawns and Chives
summary: Wok-charred flat rice noodles with prawns, egg, bean sprouts and chives.

steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok until smoking, fry the garlic for 30 seconds, then add the prawns and cook for 2 minutes until pink and opaque.
Push the prawns aside, add the egg and scramble for 1 minute until set.
Add the noodles, soy sauce, kecap manis and sambal and toss on high heat for 4 minutes until charred in places.
Toss through the bean sprouts and chives for 1 minute and serve hot.

notes: Food safety: prawns are cooked when pink and opaque. Egg must be fully set.
Dinner. Dairy-free.

title: Chicken Inasal-Style Grilled Thighs
summary: Lemongrass, vinegar and garlic marinated chicken thighs grilled and basted with annatto oil.

steps.text: Mix the lemongrass, garlic, ginger, vinegar, lemon juice and salt and marinate the chicken in it.
Warm the oil with the annatto seed for 3 minutes until orange, then strain.
Grill the chicken for 20 minutes, turning and basting with the annatto oil, until charred and cooked through.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender, and serve with the chicken and soy sauce.

notes: Food safety: the thickest part must reach 75°C with no pink juices. Plus 2 hours marinating.
Dinner. Dairy-free. Gluten-free (use tamari).

title: Goan Pork Vindaloo Pots
summary: Tender pork shoulder in a tangy, fiery vinegar and spice paste, served with rice.

steps.text: Grind the dried chilli, cumin, mustard seed, garlic, ginger, vinegar and turmeric to a paste and coat the pork in it.
Soften the onion in the oil in a heavy pot for 8 minutes until golden, then add the pork and brown for 6 minutes.
Add the sugar, water and salt, cover and simmer for 80 minutes until the pork is tender and the sauce is thick.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender, and serve the vindaloo over it.

notes: Food safety: the pork must reach at least 75°C in the centre and be fork-tender. Plus 3 hours marinating.
Dinner. Dairy-free. Gluten-free.

title: Smoky Baingan Bharta Eggplant Mash
summary: Charred eggplant mashed with tomato, onion and spices and scooped with flatbread.

steps.text: Char the whole eggplants over a flame or under a hot grill for 20 minutes, turning, until the skin is blackened and the flesh collapses.
Cool, peel off the skin and mash the flesh.
Soften the onion in the oil for 6 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger, chilli, cumin, garam masala and turmeric for 1 minute.
Add the tomato and cook for 8 minutes until broken down, then stir in the eggplant and cook for 5 minutes until thick.
Fold through the coriander and serve with warm naan.

notes: Dinner. Vegetarian (naan may contain dairy).

title: Paneer Tikka Skewers with Mint Chutney
summary: Marinated paneer, capsicum and onion grilled until charred, with a fresh mint chutney.

steps.text: Mix the yoghurt, ginger garlic paste, garam masala, chilli powder, lemon juice and oil, and coat the paneer and vegetables in it.
Thread onto skewers, alternating the paneer and vegetables.
Grill for 12 minutes, turning, until charred at the edges and the paneer is golden.
Serve with the mint chutney and warm naan.

notes: Plus 1 hour marinating. Dinner. Vegetarian.

title: Ugandan Groundnut Chicken Stew
summary: Chicken thighs simmered with tomato, onion and ground peanut in a thick, savoury stew.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil in a heavy pot for 8 minutes, then lift out.
Soften the onion for 6 minutes, add the garlic, ginger, cumin and coriander for 1 minute, then the tomato for 5 minutes.
Stir in the peanut butter and stock, return the chicken and simmer for 30 minutes until the sauce is thick and the chicken is tender.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender, and serve alongside.

notes: Food safety: the chicken must reach 75°C throughout with no pink juices.
Dinner. Dairy-free. Gluten-free.

title: Cape Lamb and Potato Pot with Cinnamon Tomato
summary: Slow-cooked lamb and tomato stew with potato, warm spices and a touch of sugar.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil in a heavy pot for 10 minutes until deeply coloured, then lift out.
Soften the onion for 6 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger, cinnamon, tomatoes, paste, sugar and salt.
Return the lamb with the water, cover and simmer gently for 80 minutes.
Add the potato and cook for 30 minutes more until the lamb and potato are very tender.
Remove the cinnamon stick and serve in bowls.

notes: Food safety: the lamb should be tender and reach at least 70°C in the centre of the largest piece.
Dinner. Dairy-free. Gluten-free.

title: Chakalaka Beans with Garlic Bread
summary: Spicy South African-style vegetable relish stewed with beans, served with garlic toast.

steps.text: Soften the onion, carrot and capsicum in the oil for 8 minutes, then add 2 of the garlic, curry powder and chilli powder for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes until thick, then stir in both beans and cook for 8 minutes until hot.
Mix the remaining garlic with the olive oil, brush over sliced bread and toast until golden.
Serve the chakalaka with the garlic bread.

notes: Dinner. Vegan. Use canned beans only; if cooking dried kidney beans, boil them hard for 10 minutes first.

title: Seared Tuna Poke-Style Rice Bowls
summary: Seared tuna steaks over rice with avocado, cucumber, edamame and a sesame soy dressing.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and sticky, and cook the edamame in boiling water for 4 minutes until tender.
Sear the tuna in the oil in a very hot pan for 1 to 2 minutes each side until browned outside; for fully cooked, continue until the flesh turns opaque and flakes.
Whisk the soy sauce, sesame oil and vinegar.
Slice the tuna and arrange over the rice with avocado, cucumber and edamame.
Drizzle with the dressing and scatter with sesame seed and spring onion.

notes: Food safety: seared tuna is rare in the centre; cook until opaque and flaking for pregnant, elderly or immune-compromised people.
Dinner. Dairy-free.

title: Prawn Egg Foo Yung Omelettes with Gravy
summary: Fluffy prawn and bean sprout omelettes with a glossy soy gravy.

steps.text: Beat the eggs with the prawns, sprouts, spring onion and sesame oil.
Heat the oil in a pan and cook ladles of the mixture for 2 minutes each side until golden and fully set.
Simmer the stock, soy sauce and cornflour mixed with 2 tbsp water for 2 minutes until thick and glossy.
Serve the omelettes with the gravy poured over.

notes: Food safety: prawns must be pink and opaque and the egg fully set.
Lunch. Dairy-free.

title: Crisp Pork in Pineapple Sweet Sour Glaze
summary: Crunchy battered pork pieces tossed in a tangy pineapple and capsicum sauce.

steps.text: Whisk the cornflour, plain flour and water into a thick batter and coat the pork.
Shallow-fry the pork in the oil over medium-high heat for 8 minutes, turning, until golden, crisp and cooked through.
Simmer the tomato sauce, vinegar, sugar and soy sauce for 3 minutes until syrupy, then add the capsicum and pineapple.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender, toss the pork through the sauce and serve over rice.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach 70°C throughout with no pink.
Dinner. Dairy-free.

title: Black Pepper Beef with Capsicum
summary: Tender beef strips stir-fried with cracked pepper and capsicum in a rich soy sauce.

steps.text: Toss the beef with the cornflour and the soy sauce.
Stir-fry the beef in the oil in a very hot wok for 2 minutes until browned, then lift out.
Stir-fry the onion, capsicum and garlic for 3 minutes until tender-crisp.
Return the beef with the pepper and oyster sauce and toss for 1 minute until glossy.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender, and serve alongside.

notes: Food safety: thin beef strips are cooked when no pink remains and they reach 71°C.
Dinner. Dairy-free.

title: Pan-Fried Chive and Tofu Dumplings
summary: Crisp-based dumplings filled with garlic chives, tofu and mushroom.

steps.text: Mix the tofu, chives, mushroom, 1 tbsp soy sauce and sesame oil.
Fill and seal each wrapper with a spoonful of the mixture.
Fry the dumplings flat-side down in the oil for 3 minutes until golden, add the water, cover and steam for 6 minutes until the wrappers are translucent.
Mix the vinegar with the remaining soy sauce and serve for dipping.

notes: Lunch. Vegan.

title: Savoury Rice Porridge with Pickled Mustard Greens
summary: Silky rice porridge topped with pickled greens, spring onion and a soft egg.

steps.text: Simmer the rice with the water for 40 minutes, stirring now and then, until the grains break down and the porridge is thick.
Soft-boil the eggs for 6 minutes, cool and peel.
Ladle the porridge into bowls and top with the egg, greens, spring onion and fried shallots.
Drizzle with soy sauce and sesame oil.

notes: Food safety: soft-boiled eggs are not recommended for pregnant or vulnerable people; boil for 10 minutes instead. Breakfast. Dairy-free.

title: Hong Kong-Style Peanut French Toast
summary: Thick toast sandwiches with peanut butter, dipped in egg and pan-fried golden.

steps.text: Spread two slices with peanut butter and top with the other two.
Beat the eggs and milk, and dip the sandwiches until soaked through.
Melt the butter and fry the sandwiches for 3 minutes each side until deep golden and the egg is set.
Serve drizzled with golden syrup.

notes: Food safety: cook the egg coating until fully set. Breakfast. Vegetarian.

title: Crumbed Chicken Katsu Sandwiches
summary: Crisp chicken cutlets with shredded cabbage and tangy sauce in soft white bread.

steps.text: Slice each chicken breast in half horizontally and flatten to an even thickness.
Coat in flour, then egg, then panko.
Shallow-fry for 4 minutes each side until golden and the chicken is cooked through.
Mix the tomato sauce and Worcestershire, spread on the bread with the mayonnaise, and fill with the chicken and cabbage.

notes: Food safety: the chicken must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink.
Lunch.

title: Ginger Soy Pork Slices on Rice
summary: Thin pork slices pan-fried in a ginger soy glaze, served with rice and cabbage.

steps.text: Mix the ginger, soy sauce, mirin and sake and marinate the pork.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and sticky.
Fry the pork in the oil in a hot pan for 5 minutes until cooked through and glazed, adding the leftover marinade for the last minute.
Serve over the rice with cabbage.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach 70°C with no pink. Plus 15 minutes marinating. Dairy-free.
Dinner.

title: Cabbage Yakisoba with Egg
summary: Pan-fried noodles with cabbage and carrot in a sweet-savoury sauce, topped with a fried egg.

steps.text: Boil the noodles for 2 minutes until just tender, then drain.
Stir-fry the onion, carrot and cabbage in 2 tbsp oil for 5 minutes until tender-crisp.
Add the noodles, okonomiyaki sauce and soy sauce and toss for 3 minutes until glossy.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil until the whites are set.
Serve the noodles topped with an egg and furikake.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set and yolks as firm as you prefer. Lunch.

title: Inari Rice Pockets
summary: Sweet tofu pockets stuffed with seasoned sushi rice and sesame.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and sticky.
Warm the vinegar, sugar and salt until dissolved and fold through the rice with the sesame seed and ginger.
Open each tofu puff and pack it with rice until plump.
Serve at room temperature.

notes: Snack. Vegan.

title: Miso Mushroom Egg Rice Porridge
summary: Gentle miso rice porridge with mushrooms, ginger and a stirred-in egg.

steps.text: Simmer the dashi with the mushrooms and ginger for 8 minutes until the mushrooms are tender.
Add the rinsed rice and simmer for 20 minutes until the grains have swollen and the porridge is thick.
Whisk the miso into a ladle of the broth and stir it back in off the heat.
Pour in the beaten egg and stir for 1 minute until set, then top with spring onion.

notes: Food safety: cook the egg until fully set. Cool and refrigerate leftover rice within 1 hour. Breakfast.

title: Seaweed Kimchi Rice Pan with Fried Eggs
summary: Sizzling kimchi rice topped with a crisp-edged fried egg and sesame.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method, cool and refrigerate within 1 hour, ready for this dish.
Fry the kimchi in 1 tbsp oil for 3 minutes until softened, then add the rice and gochujang and toss for 4 minutes until hot and crisp in places.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil until the whites are set and the edges crisp.
Divide the rice between bowls and top with the eggs, sesame oil, spring onion and nori.

notes: Food safety: cool leftover rice and refrigerate it within 1 hour; reheat until steaming hot. Lunch.

title: Gochujang Pork Lettuce Wraps
summary: Sticky, spicy pork mince spooned into crisp lettuce leaves with pickled carrot.

steps.text: Toss the carrot with the vinegar and a pinch of salt.
Fry the pork in the oil over high heat for 8 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute, then the gochujang, soy sauce and honey for 2 minutes until sticky.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender. Serve the pork in lettuce leaves with pickled carrot and rice.

notes: Food safety: pork mince must reach 75°C throughout with no pink.
Dinner. Dairy-free.

title: Gamja Jeon Crisp Potato Pancakes
summary: Shredded potato pancakes fried until lacy and crisp, with a soy dipping sauce.

steps.text: Squeeze the liquid from the potato and onion and mix with the chilli, potato starch and salt.
Heat the oil in a pan and press in half the mixture into a thin round.
Fry for 5 minutes each side until deep golden and crisp, and repeat.
Mix the soy sauce and vinegar for dipping.

notes: Snack. Vegan.

title: Gochujang Tofu and Zucchini Rice Bowls
summary: Silky pan-seared tofu and zucchini glazed in a sweet gochujang sauce, served on rice.

steps.text: Pan-fry the tofu in the oil for 8 minutes until golden on each side, then lift out.
Cook the zucchini and garlic in the same pan for 4 minutes until just tender.
Stir the gochujang, soy sauce, maple syrup and 2 tbsp water together, pour in and simmer for 2 minutes until glossy.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender, and serve with the tofu, zucchini and sesame seed.

notes: Dinner. Vegan.

title: Garlic Pepper Chicken Rice Plates
summary: Garlicky peppered chicken strips with fried egg over fragrant rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Stir-fry the chicken with the garlic and pepper in 1 tbsp oil for 8 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Add the oyster sauce and soy sauce and toss for 1 minute.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil until the whites are set, and serve everything over the rice with cucumber.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C with no pink; the egg whites must be set.
Lunch. Dairy-free.

title: Red Curry Prawns with Pineapple
summary: Plump prawns in a sweet-sour coconut red curry with pineapple and basil.

steps.text: Fry the curry paste in the oil for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the coconut milk, fish sauce and sugar and simmer for 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
Add the pineapple and prawns and cook for 3 minutes until the prawns are pink and opaque.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender. Stir the basil through the curry and serve with the rice.

notes: Food safety: prawns are cooked when pink and opaque.
Dinner. Dairy-free. Gluten-free.

title: Thai Sweet Corn Fritters with Cucumber Dip
summary: Crisp golden corn fritters with chilli and coriander, served with a sweet-sour dip.

steps.text: Mix the corn, rice flour, egg, curry paste and coriander into a thick batter.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat.
Fry spoonfuls for 3 minutes each side until golden and crisp and cooked through, then drain.
Stir the sweet chilli sauce with the cucumber and vinegar and serve alongside.

notes: Food safety: fry until the centres are set. Snack. Most red curry pastes contain shrimp paste; check the label, or use a vegan paste, to keep it vegetarian.

title: Steamed Fish Curry Custard Cups
summary: Silky steamed coconut curry custard with fish, set in little cups.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs with the coconut milk, curry paste, fish sauce and sugar until smooth.
Fold in the fish, lime leaf and spinach and spoon into 4 heatproof cups.
Steam over simmering water for 22 minutes until the custard is set and the fish flakes easily.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender, and serve with the custards.

notes: Food safety: the fish must be opaque and flake and the custard fully set.
Dinner. Dairy-free. Gluten-free.

title: Grilled Pork Banh Mi Rolls
summary: Lemongrass pork patties in crusty rolls with pickled carrot, cucumber and chilli.

steps.text: Toss the carrot with the vinegar and a pinch of sugar and rest.
Mix the pork, lemongrass, garlic, fish sauce and sugar and shape into 8 small patties.
Grill or pan-fry for 6 minutes each side until browned and cooked through.
Spread the rolls with mayonnaise and fill with patties, pickled carrot, cucumber, chilli and coriander.

notes: Food safety: pork patties must reach 75°C throughout with no pink.
Lunch.

title: Caramel Clay-Pot Style Fish
summary: Fish fillets simmered in a dark caramel, fish sauce and pepper glaze, served with rice.

steps.text: Cook the sugar and 2 tbsp water in a wide pan over medium heat for 5 minutes until deep amber.
Add the shallot, garlic, fish sauce and 1/4 cup water and simmer for 2 minutes.
Lay in the fish and spoon over the sauce, cooking for 8 minutes until the flesh is opaque and flakes easily.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender, and serve topped with pepper, chilli and spring onion.

notes: Food safety: the fish is cooked when the flesh turns opaque and flakes with a fork.
Dinner. Dairy-free. Gluten-free.

title: Sticky Rice with Peanuts and Coconut
summary: Sweet-salty sticky rice with toasted peanuts, sesame and coconut for a hearty breakfast.

steps.text: Soak the rice for 2 hours, drain, and cook with the water, coconut milk and salt, covered, for 20 minutes until tender and sticky.
Toast the peanuts, sesame and coconut in a dry pan for 4 minutes until golden, then crush with the sugar.
Spoon the rice into bowls and top with the peanut mix.

notes: Plus 2 hours soaking. Breakfast. Vegan and gluten-free.

title: Ginger Tofu and Mushroom Clay Pot Rice
summary: Sticky ginger soy tofu and mushrooms steamed over crisp-bottomed rice in one pot.

steps.text: Rinse the rice and cook with the water in a heavy pot, covered, for 12 minutes until most of the water is absorbed.
Fry the tofu, mushrooms and ginger in the oil for 8 minutes until golden, then add the soy sauce and sugar for 1 minute.
Spread the tofu mixture over the rice, cover and cook on low for 15 minutes until the rice is tender and a crust forms underneath.
Top with spring onion and serve from the pot.

notes: Dinner. Vegan.

title: Spiced Onion Omelette on Buttered Toast
summary: Spiced egg omelette with onion, tomato and green chilli, folded onto buttered toast.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs with the onion, tomato, chilli, turmeric, garam masala, coriander and salt.
Melt half the butter in a non-stick pan over medium heat and pour in half the mixture. Cook 2 minutes each side until set through and golden.
Repeat with the remaining mixture until set, then toast the bread until golden, spread with the remaining butter and serve the omelettes on the toast.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until firm with no runny egg.

title: Vegan Semolina Upma Breakfast Pots
summary: Toasted semolina cooked with mustard seed, curry leaf and peas into a soft, savoury breakfast.

steps.text: Toast the semolina in a dry pan over medium heat for 3 minutes until fragrant, then tip out.
Heat the oil in the same pan and fry the mustard seed and curry leaf until they pop. Add the onion, chilli and ginger and cook 4 minutes.
Pour in the water, add the peas and salt, and bring to the boil until bubbling.
Stir in the semolina in a steady stream, stirring constantly, then cover on low heat for 3 minutes until thick and fluffy.
Finish with lemon juice and serve hot.

title: Besan Chilla Vegan Pancakes
summary: Savoury chickpea flour pancakes with onion, tomato and coriander, naturally gluten free.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, water, turmeric, cumin, chilli powder and salt into a smooth batter, then fold through the onion, tomato and coriander.
Heat a little oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat and pour in a ladle of batter, spreading thin.
Cook 3 minutes until the underside is golden, flip and cook 2 minutes more until cooked through.
Repeat with the remaining batter and serve warm.

title: Rava Uttapam with Tomato and Peas
summary: Thick South Indian semolina pancakes topped with tomato, peas and coriander.

steps.text: Mix the semolina, yoghurt, water and salt into a thick batter and rest 15 minutes, then stir in the bicarbonate of soda.
Heat a little oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat and pour in a thick ladle of batter.
Scatter over the tomato, peas, chilli and coriander and press in lightly.
Cook 4 minutes, flip and cook 3 minutes more until golden and cooked through. Repeat with remaining batter.

notes: Plus 15 minutes resting the batter.

title: Spiced Flatbread Scramble with Yoghurt
summary: Torn flatbread fried in spiced butter with onion and tomato, served with cool yoghurt.

steps.text: Tear the flatbread into bite-sized pieces.
Melt the butter in a pan over medium heat and fry the onion 3 minutes. Add the paprika, cumin, cardamom and chilli flakes and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the tomato and cook 2 minutes, then toss through the flatbread and salt for 3 minutes until crisp at the edges.
Serve topped with yoghurt and parsley.

title: Eggs on Spiced Tomato Flatbread
summary: Eggs baked in a cumin and paprika tomato base, scooped up with flatbread.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a deep frying pan over medium heat and soften the onion and garlic for 4 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, paprika, cumin and salt and simmer 6 minutes until thick.
Make four wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook 4 to 5 minutes until the whites are set.
Scatter with coriander and serve with the flatbread.

notes: Food safety: cook until the whites are fully set; do not serve runny eggs to young children, pregnant women or older people.

title: Mealie Pap Porridge with Cinnamon Apple
summary: Creamy maize porridge topped with butter-braised apple and cinnamon.

steps.text: Bring the milk, water and salt to a simmer in a saucepan until steaming.
Whisk in the polenta and cook over low heat, stirring often, for 15 minutes until thick and creamy.
Meanwhile melt the butter in a small pan and cook the apple with the sugar and cinnamon for 8 minutes until soft.
Spoon the porridge into bowls and top with the apple.

title: Roosterkoek Grilled Bread Rolls with Cheddar
summary: Soft yeasted rolls browned on the grill and filled with melted cheddar and tomato.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, then add the water and oil and knead 8 minutes until smooth.
Cover and prove 45 minutes until doubled, then shape into 8 flat rolls and rest 10 minutes.
Cook in a lightly oiled pan over medium heat for 6 to 7 minutes each side until golden and hollow when tapped.
Split, butter, then fill with cheddar and tomato and grill until melted.

notes: Plus about 55 minutes proving and resting.

title: Tapsilog Beef and Egg Rice Plates
summary: Soy-calamansi style marinated beef strips with garlic rice and a fried egg.

steps.text: Marinate the beef with the soy sauce, lime juice, 1 garlic clove and pepper.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy. Fry the remaining garlic in half the oil until golden and fold through the rice.
Sear the beef in a hot pan 2 minutes each side until browned and cooked through to at least 63°C inside, then rest briefly.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil until the whites are set and serve with the beef, garlic rice and tomato.

notes: Food safety: cook steak strips to at least 63°C (75°C for mince) and keep raw meat away from ready foods. Cook eggs until the whites are set.
Plus 30 minutes marinating.

title: Curry Egg Roti Pockets
summary: Roti folded around a spiced egg and onion filling.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the oil over medium heat for 4 minutes, then stir in the curry powder and chilli for 1 minute.
Beat the eggs with the salt and pour in. Stir gently for 3 minutes until just firm, then add the coriander.
Warm the roti in a dry pan 30 seconds each side.
Spoon the egg onto the roti, fold in the sides and serve.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until firm with no liquid egg left.

title: Martabak Telur Egg and Onion Parcels
summary: Crisp parcels of wrapper filled with spiced egg, spring onion and onion.

steps.text: Beat the eggs with the spring onion, onion, curry powder, salt and pepper.
Lay a wrapper flat, pour a quarter of the mixture into the centre and fold the corners in to make a square parcel.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and fry the parcels seam-side down for 3 minutes each side until golden and the egg is set.
Cut into squares and serve hot.

notes: Food safety: cook until the egg is fully set.

title: Thai Omelette with Jasmine Rice
summary: Puffy deep-fried style omelette with fish sauce and lime over steamed rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Beat the eggs with the fish sauce, lime juice and spring onion.
Heat the oil in a small wok until very hot and pour in the egg, letting it puff and crisp.
Cook 1 minute, flip and cook 1 minute more until golden and set.
Serve over rice with sriracha.

notes: Food safety: cook the egg until fully set.

title: Pâté Baguette with Pan-Fried Eggs and Soy
summary: Eggs fried in a pan with pâté, soy and spring onion, served with a crusty baguette.

steps.text: Warm the baguette and split it, spreading the pâté inside.
Melt the butter in a small frying pan over medium heat. Crack in the eggs and cook 3 minutes until the whites are set.
Splash over the soy sauce and scatter with spring onion and pepper.
Serve straight from the pan with the baguette and coriander.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set.

title: Korean Potato Hash Rounds
summary: Crisp grated potato rounds with spring onion and a gochujang-sesame dip.

steps.text: Grate the potatoes, squeeze out as much liquid as you can and mix with the spring onion, egg, starch and salt.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and fry heaped spoonfuls, pressed flat, for 4 minutes each side until deep golden and cooked through.
Mix the gochujang, vinegar and sesame oil for dipping.

notes: Food safety: cook until the egg is set.

title: Sweet Potato Rice Porridge with Sesame
summary: Soft rice and sweet potato congee finished with toasted sesame and a little soy.

steps.text: Simmer the rice, water and ginger in a pot over medium-low heat for 20 minutes, stirring now and then.
Add the sweet potato and cook 15 minutes more until the porridge is thick and the potato soft.
Toast the sesame seed in a dry pan for 2 minutes.
Ladle into bowls and top with the sesame, spring onion, soy sauce and sesame oil.

title: Okayu Rice Porridge with Furikake Egg
summary: Plain Japanese rice porridge topped with a soft-set egg and furikake.

steps.text: Rinse the rice and simmer in the water over low heat, partly covered, for 25 minutes until thick and creamy.
Meanwhile boil the eggs for 7 minutes, cool in cold water and peel.
Ladle the porridge into bowls, halve the eggs on top and finish with furikake, soy sauce and spring onion.

notes: Food safety: use fresh eggs; the yolk will be soft but the white should be set.

title: Miso Butter Mushroom Toast
summary: Seared mushrooms in miso butter piled on thick toast with spring onion.

steps.text: Sear the mushrooms in a dry pan over high heat for 5 minutes until golden.
Add the butter, miso, soy sauce and garlic and cook 2 minutes more until glossy.
Toast the sourdough until golden and spoon the mushrooms on top.
Finish with spring onion and pepper.

title: Steamed Egg and Pork Rice Plates
summary: Silky steamed eggs with savoury minced pork over rice.

steps.text: Mix the pork with the soy sauce and sesame oil and spread in a shallow heatproof dish.
Beat the eggs with the water and salt, strain, and pour over the pork.
Cover the dish tightly and steam over simmering water for 15 minutes until the egg is just set and the pork reaches 75°C.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy and serve topped with the steamed egg and spring onion.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork mince to 75°C with no pink, and make sure the egg is fully set.

title: Kenyan Spiced Potato Mashed Bread Wraps
summary: Chapati wraps filled with turmeric potato, peas and fresh tomato.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes for 12 minutes until tender, adding the peas for the last 2 minutes. Drain.
Fry the onion in the oil for 4 minutes, add the turmeric and cumin and stir 30 seconds.
Add the potatoes, peas, tomato and salt, mash roughly, and cook 3 minutes. Stir in the coriander and lemon juice.
Warm the roti, fill with the potato mix and roll up.

title: Kachumbari Beef Samosa Pockets
summary: Crisp baked pastry pockets with spiced beef mince and a tomato-onion relish.

steps.text: Fry the onion and garlic in the oil for 4 minutes, add the mince and spices and cook 8 minutes, breaking up, until browned and cooked through at 75°C. Cool.
Fold the wrappers into triangles around the filling and brush the edges with a little water to seal.
Bake at 200°C for 15 minutes until golden and crisp.
Mix the tomato, red onion, lime juice and coriander and serve alongside.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef mince to 75°C with no pink before wrapping, and cool it quickly.

title: Pilau Beef Rice Lunch Pot
summary: Fragrant Swahili-style spiced rice with tender beef and caramelised onion.

steps.text: Brown the onion in the oil over medium heat for 10 minutes until deep golden.
Add the beef, garlic, ginger and spices and sear 5 minutes.
Add the stock and salt, cover and simmer 25 minutes until the beef is tender.
Stir in the rice, cover and cook on low for 12 minutes until the rice is tender and the beef reaches at least 75°C inside, then rest 5 minutes.

notes: Food safety: cook diced beef to at least 75°C inside; refrigerate leftovers within an hour.

title: Chickpea Coconut Curry Wraps
summary: Creamy coconut chickpeas with tomato and coriander wrapped in warm flatbread.

steps.text: Fry the onion, garlic and ginger in the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the curry powder and tomato and cook 3 minutes, then add the chickpeas, coconut milk and salt.
Simmer 8 minutes until thick, then stir in the coriander.
Spoon into warmed flatbread and roll up.

title: Samp and Beans Lunch Bowls
summary: Hearty maize and bean bowls with tomato, onion and a little chilli.

steps.text: Bring the water and salt to the boil, whisk in the polenta and cook on low 15 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Meanwhile fry the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes, add the paprika and curry powder, then the tomatoes.
Simmer 8 minutes, add the beans and heat through.
Spoon the polenta into bowls, ladle over the beans and scatter with parsley.

title: Fried Bread Balls with Curried Beef Mince
summary: Golden fried bread balls split and filled with a mild curried beef mince.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt with the warm water into a soft dough, knead 5 minutes, cover and prove 45 minutes.
Cook the onion in a little oil for 4 minutes, add the mince and curry powder and brown 8 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste and water and simmer 10 minutes until cooked through at 75°C.
Shape the dough into 8 balls and fry in shallow oil over medium heat for 8 minutes, turning, until deep golden and cooked inside.
Split each vetkoek and fill with the mince.

notes: Food safety: cook the mince to 75°C with no pink.
Plus about 45 minutes proving.

title: Chicken Mayo Lunch Rolls
summary: Poached chicken with spring onion and mayonnaise in soft rolls with lettuce.

steps.text: Simmer the chicken in water for 15 minutes until the juices run clear and the thickest part reaches 75°C. Cool and shred.
Mix the chicken with the mayonnaise, spring onion, mustard powder, lemon juice and pepper.
Fill the rolls with lettuce, tomato and the chicken mix.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C before shredding; keep filled rolls refrigerated until serving.

title: Crisp Chopped Chicken Sisig Plates
summary: Chopped crisp-edged chicken thigh with onion, chilli and lime over rice, topped with an egg.

steps.text: Grill or pan-fry the chicken 8 minutes each side over medium-high until browned and 75°C at the thickest point. Rest, then chop finely.
Fry the chopped chicken in the oil in a hot pan for 4 minutes until crisp at the edges.
Toss with the onion, chilli, soy, lime juice and mayonnaise.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, fry the eggs and serve on top.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C throughout and fry the eggs until whites are set.

title: Filipino Egg Rolls with Pork
summary: Crisp lumpia rolls of pork mince, carrot and onion.

steps.text: Mix the pork with the carrot, onion, garlic, spring onion and soy sauce.
Place a spoonful on each wrapper, roll tightly and seal the edge with a dab of water.
Fry in the oil over medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes, turning, until golden and the pork reaches 75°C inside.
Drain and serve with the sweet chilli sauce.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork to 75°C throughout; cut one roll open to check no pink remains.

title: Filipino Chicken Pastel Hand Pies
summary: Flaky pies of creamy chicken, potato, carrot and peas.

steps.text: Melt the butter, cook the onion 4 minutes, add the chicken and brown 6 minutes.
Add the flour, then the milk gradually, with the potato, carrot and salt. Simmer 10 minutes until thick and the chicken is cooked through at 75°C. Add the peas and cool.
Cut the pastry into 8 squares, fill 4, top with the rest and seal. Brush with beaten egg.
Bake at 200°C for 20 to 25 minutes until puffed and golden.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C before filling, and cool the filling quickly.

title: Calamansi-Style Chicken Adobo Rice Plates
summary: Gluten-free adobo of chicken in tamari, coconut vinegar, garlic and bay leaf.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil in a pot over medium-high heat for 6 minutes.
Add the tamari, vinegar, garlic, bay and pepper with 1/2 cup water, cover and simmer 25 minutes until the chicken reaches 75°C.
Uncover and reduce the liquid for 5 minutes until glossy.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy and serve with the chicken.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until 75°C throughout.

title: Pork Bistek Style Tamari Pork and Onions
summary: Tender pork slices with lime and tamari over onion rings, gluten free.

steps.text: Marinate the pork in the tamari, lime juice and garlic.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Sear the onions in half the oil for 5 minutes and set aside.
Cook the pork in the remaining oil for 6 minutes with the marinade until no pink remains and it reaches 70°C, then return the onions.

notes: Food safety: cook fresh pork to 70°C with no pink remaining.
Plus 30 minutes marinating.

title: Rendang Daging Slow Beef
summary: Beef simmered in coconut milk, lemongrass and chilli until dark, dry and intensely rich.

steps.text: Blend the garlic, shallots, galangal, ginger and soaked chillies to a paste.
Toast the desiccated coconut in a dry pan until deep golden.
Add the paste, coconut milk, lemongrass, lime leaves, spices and beef to a heavy pot and simmer, stirring, for 2 hours.
Stir in the coconut, sugar and salt and cook until the sauce is dry and clinging, about 20 minutes.
Check the beef is tender and has passed 75°C inside, then serve.

notes: Food safety: braise diced beef until tender and well past 75°C inside.

title: Ayam Percik Grilled Coconut Chicken
summary: Chicken thighs grilled with a lemongrass and turmeric coconut baste, gluten free.

steps.text: Blend the lemongrass, ginger, garlic, shallots and spices with half the coconut milk and marinate the chicken.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Grill the chicken 12 minutes each side, basting with the remaining coconut milk, until browned and 75°C.
Stir the tamari and sugar into the leftover marinade and simmer 5 minutes, then spoon over the chicken.

notes: Food safety: boil the leftover marinade 5 minutes before using as a glaze, and cook chicken to 75°C.
Plus 1 hour marinating.

title: Malaysian Kapitan Chicken Curry
summary: Mild coconut chicken curry with lemongrass, turmeric and lime leaves.

steps.text: Blend the onion, garlic and ginger to a paste and fry in the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the curry powder and chicken and brown 5 minutes.
Add the coconut milk, lemongrass and lime leaves and simmer 25 minutes until the chicken reaches 75°C.
Finish with lime juice and serve with cooked jasmine rice.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken thigh to 75°C throughout.

title: Apricot Cinnamon Chicken Curry Pot
summary: Gently spiced chicken curry with apricot, tomato and cinnamon.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil for 6 minutes and set aside.
Fry the onion, garlic and ginger 5 minutes, add the curry powder and cinnamon.
Return the chicken, add the tomatoes, apricot and salt, cover and simmer 30 minutes until 75°C at the thickest part.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy and serve alongside.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C throughout.

title: Mozambican Peri-Peri Prawns with Rice
summary: Garlicky chilli-lemon prawns over steamed rice, gluten free.

steps.text: Toss the prawns with the garlic, chilli, lemon juice, paprika and oil.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Sear the prawns in a hot pan 2 to 3 minutes each side until opaque and curled.
Serve over rice with parsley.

notes: Food safety: cook prawns until opaque and pink all the way through.

title: Durban Chickpea Curry with Rice
summary: Spicy tomato chickpea curry, vegan and gluten free.

steps.text: Fry the onion, garlic and ginger in the oil 5 minutes, add the curry powder.
Add tomatoes, potato, chickpeas, salt and 1 cup water and simmer 25 minutes until potato is tender.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Scatter with the coriander and serve over the rice.

title: Kenyan Plantain and Beef Stew
summary: Slow-cooked beef with green plantain, tomato and coriander, gluten free.

steps.text: Brown the beef in the oil 8 minutes.
Add onion, garlic and ginger and cook 4 minutes, then tomato, spices and salt.
Cover with water, simmer 30 minutes, add plantain and cook 15 minutes more until beef is tender and above 75°C.
Scatter with the coriander and serve hot with plenty of the juices.

notes: Food safety: cook beef cubes to at least 75°C inside.

title: Tomato Coconut Fish Pot with Chilli and Lemon
summary: White fish in a coconut-tomato base with lemon and chilli, gluten free.

items.raw: 600g white fish fillet, cut in chunks

steps.text: Fry the onion, garlic and chilli in the oil 5 minutes, then add tomato and coconut milk and simmer 5 minutes.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Add the fish and simmer 5 minutes until opaque and flaking.
Finish with lemon juice and coriander.

notes: Food safety: fish is done when opaque and flakes easily.

title: Tandoori Fish Tikka with Basmati
summary: Yoghurt and spice marinated fish pieces, grilled and served with basmati rice, gluten free.

items.raw: 600g white fish fillet, cut in chunks

steps.text: Mix the yoghurt, spices, ginger garlic paste, lemon juice and oil and coat the fish.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Grill or pan-sear 3 to 4 minutes each side until opaque and flaking.
Serve over rice with coriander.

notes: Food safety: cook until opaque and flaking.
Plus 30 minutes marinating.

title: Cardamom Butter Chicken Pots
summary: Creamy tomato chicken with cardamom, gluten free.

steps.text: Melt the butter, cook the onion 5 minutes, add garlic and ginger, then the spices.
Add tomatoes and simmer 10 minutes, then blend smooth.
Add the chicken and simmer 15 minutes until 75°C, then stir in the cream.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy and serve.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C throughout.

title: Lamb Keema and Peas
summary: Dry-spiced lamb mince with peas and ginger, served with basmati rice, gluten free.

steps.text: Fry the onion, garlic and ginger in the oil 5 minutes, add the spices.
Add the lamb and brown 8 minutes, breaking up.
Add tomato and 1/2 cup water and simmer 10 minutes, add peas.
Cook until lamb reaches 75°C. Cook rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy and serve.

notes: Food safety: cook lamb mince to 75°C with no pink.

title: Egg Curry with Coconut Rice
summary: Boiled eggs in a coconut-tomato curry, gluten free.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes until hard, cool and peel.
Fry onion, garlic, ginger 5 minutes, add curry powder, tomato and coconut milk, simmer 10 minutes.
Add the eggs and heat through.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, serve with coriander.

notes: Food safety: boil eggs until the yolk is firm.

title: Coconut Beef Rice Noodle Stir-Fry
summary: Beef strips stir-fried with basil, chilli and tamari over rice noodles, gluten free.

steps.text: Soak or cook the noodles per the packet until tender, drain.
Stir-fry beef in hot oil 2 minutes until browned and 63°C inside, remove.
Fry garlic and chilli 30 seconds until fragrant, add noodles, tamari, fish sauce, sugar.
Return beef, toss with basil.

notes: Food safety: cook beef strips to at least 63°C inside.

title: Lemongrass Chicken Rice Plates
summary: Charred lemongrass chicken with cucumber and rice, gluten free.

steps.text: Marinate chicken with lemongrass, garlic, fish sauce, sugar, tamari.
Cook rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Grill 8 minutes each side until charred and 75°C.
Slice and serve with rice, cucumber and mint.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C throughout.
Plus 1 hour marinating.

title: Vegan Rice Paper Rolls with Peanut Dipping
summary: Tofu and herb rolls with peanut dip, vegan and gluten free.

steps.text: Cook the vermicelli per the packet until tender and drain.
Soften a wrapper in warm water until pliable, fill with tofu, vegetables, herbs, noodles and roll tightly.
Whisk peanut butter, tamari, lime juice and a splash of water until smooth for dipping.

title: Glazed Shiitake and Edamame over Sushi Rice
summary: Glazed mushrooms and edamame over rice, vegan.

steps.text: Cook rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Sear mushrooms in oil 6 minutes until golden.
Add teriyaki sauce and edamame, cook 2 minutes.
Serve over rice with sesame seed and spring onion.

title: Peanut Noodle Lunch Bowls
summary: Wheat noodles with peanut sesame coating, cabbage and carrot, vegan.

steps.text: Cook noodles per packet until tender, drain and rinse.
Whisk peanut butter, soy, vinegar, sesame oil and a little warm water until smooth.
Toss with noodles, carrot, cabbage.
Top with spring onion and peanuts.

title: Sweet Chilli Tofu Lettuce Cups
summary: Crisp tofu cubes tossed in sweet chilli and wrapped in lettuce, vegan.

steps.text: Fry tofu in the oil for 8 minutes until crisp.
Add sweet chilli and soy sauce, toss.
Spoon into lettuce leaves, top with carrot, mint and peanuts.

title: Lentil Dhal Samosa Rolls
summary: Baked spring roll wrapper rolls of spiced red lentil, vegan.

steps.text: Simmer lentils in water 12 minutes until thick, drain extra.
Fry onion and ginger in oil 4 minutes, add curry powder, mix with lentils and coriander.
Roll in wrappers and brush with oil.
Bake at 200°C for 15 minutes until crisp.

title: Numbing Chilli Bean Tofu with Pork over Rice
summary: Silken tofu in a numbing chilli bean gravy with pork mince, served over rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Fry the pork in the oil over high heat for 4 minutes until browned and cooked through at 75°C, then add the doubanjiang, garlic, ginger and peppercorn and stir until fragrant.
Pour in the stock and soy sauce, add the tofu and simmer gently for 5 minutes until hot.
Stir the cornflour with a little water and add until the gravy thickens and turns glossy. Scatter with spring onion and serve over rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork mince to 75°C with no pink.

title: Cantonese Steamed Chicken with Ginger and Shiitake
summary: Tender chicken pieces steamed with shiitake and ginger.

steps.text: Toss the chicken with the tamari, wine, sesame oil, cornflour, ginger and mushrooms.
Spread on a heatproof plate and steam over simmering water for 20 minutes until the chicken is opaque and reaches 75°C.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then serve the chicken and its juices over rice with spring onion.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C throughout with no pink.

title: Honey Garlic Pork Rice Plates
summary: Sticky glazed pork slices with garlic and sesame over rice.

steps.text: Mix the honey, soy sauce and garlic.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, and steam the broccoli for 4 minutes until bright green.
Sear the pork in the oil for 4 minutes until browned, add the glaze and cook until sticky and the pork reaches 70°C.
Serve over rice with broccoli and sesame seed.

notes: Food safety: cook fresh pork to 70°C with no pink remaining.

title: Tofu and Mushroom Vegan Lunch Pot
summary: Braised tofu and mushrooms with soy and ginger over rice, vegan.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Fry the tofu in the oil for 6 minutes until golden, then set aside.
Cook the mushrooms and ginger for 5 minutes until browned, then return the tofu with the soy sauce and 1/4 cup water and simmer until reduced.
Finish with sesame oil and spring onion and serve over rice.

title: Okinawan Sweet Potato Rice Pot
summary: Rice cooked with purple-fleshed style sweet potato and kombu, savoury and gently sweet.

steps.text: Rinse the rice and place in a pot with the water, kombu, soy sauce, mirin and potato.
Bring to the boil, cover and simmer on low for 15 minutes until the rice is tender and the potato soft.
Rest, covered, for 10 minutes until fluffy, then stir and scatter with sesame seed.

title: Okinawan Pork and Tofu Champuru
summary: Stir-fried pork, firm tofu, cabbage and egg Okinawa style.

steps.text: Fry the pork in the oil 4 minutes until browned and cooked through to 70°C.
Add the cabbage and crumbled tofu and stir-fry for 4 minutes until wilted.
Pour in the beaten eggs and soy sauce and stir until set, then top with the bonito flakes.

notes: Food safety: cook fresh pork to 70°C and cook the egg until set.

title: Hokkaido Butter Corn Rice Bowls
summary: Sweet corn and butter over rice with soy and spring onion.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Melt the butter in a pan and fry the corn 5 minutes until lightly golden.
Stir in the soy sauce and pepper, spoon over the rice and top with spring onion.

title: Salmon Teriyaki Tray Bake with Rice
summary: Glazed salmon with broccoli roasted together, served with rice.

steps.text: Toss the broccoli in the oil on a large tray and bake at 200°C for 8 minutes until beginning to colour.
Add the salmon brushed with the teriyaki sauce and bake 10 minutes until the salmon is opaque and flakes easily.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy and serve with sesame seed.

notes: Food safety: salmon is cooked when opaque and flaking, or 63°C.

title: Jeju Style Braised Pork and Radish Rice Pot
summary: Pork belly and radish simmered in soy and ginger until tender.

steps.text: Simmer the pork in water for 10 minutes and drain.
Return to the pot with the daikon, soy sauce, sugar, ginger, garlic and fresh water.
Cover and simmer 45 minutes until the pork is tender and has passed 70°C inside.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy and serve with spring onion.

notes: Food safety: cook fresh pork to 70°C.

title: Dakgalbi Spicy Chicken Rice Plates
summary: Chicken thigh with gochujang, sweet potato and cabbage stir-fried together.

steps.text: Mix the gochujang, soy, honey and garlic and coat the chicken.
Fry the sweet potato in the oil 6 minutes until starting to soften.
Add the chicken and cabbage and cook 10 minutes until the chicken reaches 75°C and the sweet potato is tender.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy and serve alongside.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C throughout.

title: Gochujang Tofu Lunch Wraps
summary: Crisp tofu with gochujang glaze, kimchi and cucumber in flour tortillas.

steps.text: Fry the tofu in the oil 7 minutes until golden.
Toss with gochujang and maple syrup for 1 minute until sticky.
Warm the tortillas until pliable and fill with tofu, kimchi and cucumber.

title: Isan Grilled Chicken with Sticky Rice
summary: Marinated grilled chicken thighs with lemongrass and garlic over sticky rice, gluten free.

steps.text: Blend the lemongrass, garlic, fish sauce, sugar, tamari and pepper and coat the chicken.
Soak the rice 30 minutes, then steam 25 minutes until tender and chewy.
Grill the chicken 12 minutes each side until charred and 75°C.
Serve with the sticky rice.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C throughout.
Plus 1 hour marinating.

title: Cashew Tofu with Capsicum over Jasmine Rice
summary: Crisp tofu, capsicum and cashews in a sweet-savoury sauce, vegan.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Fry the tofu in the oil 6 minutes until golden, add garlic and capsicum and cook until crisp-tender.
Add the soy, sugar and cashews and toss until glossy.
Spoon the glossy tofu and cashews over the rice and serve straight away.

title: Hue Style Lemongrass Beef Noodle Bowls
summary: Beef strips with lemongrass, chilli and noodles.

steps.text: Cook the vermicelli per the packet until tender and drain.
Marinate the beef in lemongrass, chilli, fish sauce, sugar.
Sear in the oil 2 minutes until browned and 63°C inside.
Serve over noodles with sprouts and mint.

notes: Food safety: cook beef to at least 63°C.
Plus 20 minutes marinating.

title: Ginger Tofu Banh Mi Baguettes
summary: Crisp ginger soy tofu in baguette with pickled carrot, vegan.

steps.text: Marinate the tofu in soy and ginger.
Fry in the oil until golden, 3 minutes a side.
Toss the carrot in the vinegar until softened.
Fill the baguette with tofu, carrot, cucumber and coriander.

title: Javanese Sweet Soy Chicken Rice Plates
summary: Chicken thigh braised in kecap manis and garlic.

steps.text: Fry shallot, garlic and ginger in oil 3 minutes until fragrant.
Add chicken and brown 5 minutes.
Add kecap manis and 1/2 cup water, cover and simmer 15 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C.
Cook rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy and serve with cucumber.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C.

title: Sambal Egg Rice Bowls
summary: Boiled eggs coated in sambal and tomato over rice.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 8 minutes until firm, peel.
Fry garlic and tomato in oil 3 minutes until soft, add sambal.
Add eggs and coat for 2 minutes until sticky.
Cook rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, serve together.

notes: Food safety: boil eggs until firm.

title: Sabah Style Fish Curry with Okra
summary: Tangy chilli fish curry with okra and tomato, gluten free.

steps.text: Fry onion, garlic and ginger in oil 5 minutes.
Add chilli powder, tomato, tamarind paste, and 1 cup water and simmer 8 minutes until thick.
Add okra and fish and simmer 6 minutes until fish is opaque and flakes.
Cook rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy and serve.

notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when opaque and flaking.

title: Malaysian Coconut Egg Breakfast Bowls
summary: Soft-boiled eggs with coconut rice and sambal.

steps.text: Cook the rice with the coconut milk and 1/2 cup water until tender and fluffy.
Boil the eggs for 6 minutes then cool and peel.
Serve rice topped with eggs, sambal, cucumber, peanuts.

notes: Food safety: use fresh eggs.

title: Kerala Style Coconut Prawn Stir-Fry
summary: Prawns with curry leaf, coconut and black pepper, gluten free.

steps.text: Heat the coconut oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat. Add the sliced onion with a pinch of salt and fry for 5 minutes, stirring often, until soft and golden at the edges.
Stir in the curry leaf, turmeric and black pepper and cook for 30 seconds until the leaves crackle and the pan smells fragrant.
Add the prawns and toss over medium-high heat for 4 minutes, until they curl, turn pink and opaque, and the spices cling to the shells or flesh.
Sprinkle over the desiccated coconut and toss for 1 minute until it turns lightly golden and nutty. Taste and add salt if needed.
Meanwhile cook 1 cup of dry basmati rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then fluff with a fork and serve the prawns over the top.

notes: Food safety: cook prawns until opaque and pink throughout, then eat straight away or chill within 1 hour and eat within 24 hours.
Tip: do not overcook the prawns or they turn rubbery; pull the pan off the heat as soon as they curl into a loose C shape.

title: Punjabi Chole Bhature-Style Chickpea Plates
summary: Spiced chickpeas with puffed fried breads, vegan.

steps.text: Mix the flour with 1 tsp salt in a bowl. Add the water and 1 tbsp of the oil and knead for 5 minutes until the dough is smooth and elastic. Cover and rest.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Fry the onions for 6 minutes, stirring, until deep golden brown.
Stir in the ginger garlic paste and garam masala and cook for 1 minute until fragrant, then add the chopped tomato and cook for 6 minutes until jammy and the oil separates at the edges.
Tip in the drained chickpeas with 1/2 cup water, mash a few against the pot and simmer for 10 minutes, until thick and glossy. Season with salt.

Divide the dough into 8 balls and roll each into a 12cm oval. Heat the 1/4 cup oil in a deep pan to about 180°C (a scrap of dough should sizzle and rise at once). Fry each bread for 30 to 40 seconds, pressing gently, until puffed and golden on both sides.
Drain the breads on paper towel and serve hot with the chickpeas.

notes: Plus 20 minutes resting the dough.
Tip: roll the dough evenly so the breads puff; thin patches stay flat. Keep the oil hot between batches.
Food safety: take care with hot oil and never leave the pan unattended.

title: Mushroom Matar Lunch Curry with Roti
summary: Mushrooms and peas in a spiced tomato base, vegan.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Fry the onion with a pinch of salt for 5 minutes until soft and golden.
Stir in the ginger garlic paste and garam masala and cook for 1 minute until fragrant, then add the chopped tomato and cook for 5 minutes, mashing, until jammy.
Add the sliced mushrooms and 1/2 cup water. Cook for 5 minutes until the mushrooms release their liquid and shrink, then add the peas.
Simmer for 8 minutes until the mushrooms are tender and the sauce is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. Season with 1/2 tsp salt.
Warm each roti in a dry pan over medium heat for 30 seconds a side until soft and flecked with brown, and serve with the curry.

notes: Tip: do not wash mushrooms under water; wipe them so the sauce stays rich rather than watery.
Storage: keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat until steaming hot.

title: Sri Lankan Black Pork Curry
summary: Dark roasted spice pork shoulder curry with tamarind, gluten free.

steps.text: Toast the curry powder, ground coriander and black pepper in a dry heavy pot over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until a few shades darker and smoky-fragrant. Tip into a bowl.
Heat the oil in the same pot over medium-high heat. Brown the pork in two batches for 5 minutes each until deeply coloured on all sides, then set aside.
Add the sliced onion to the pot and cook for 6 minutes until soft. Stir in the crushed garlic and grated ginger and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Return the pork with the roasted spices, tamarind paste, cinnamon stick, 1 tsp salt and 2 cups water. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook on low for 80 minutes, stirring now and then, until the pork is very tender (at least 70°C inside) and the sauce is dark, thick and clings to the meat.
Meanwhile cook 1 1/2 cups of dry basmati rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy. Remove the cinnamon stick, taste and adjust the salt, then serve the curry over the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook fresh pork to 70°C or above, refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until steaming hot.
Tip: the dark colour comes from the long roast of the spices; stop before they turn bitter and black.
Storage: tastes better the next day; keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Sri Lankan Egg Roti Lunch Pockets
summary: Spiced egg and onion pockets in roti.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Fry the finely sliced onion and green chilli with a pinch of salt for 4 minutes until soft and translucent.
Stir in the curry powder and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt, pour into the pan and stir gently for 2 to 3 minutes, until just set and no longer runny.
Warm each roti in a dry pan for 30 seconds a side until soft. Spoon the egg onto one half, fold over into a pocket and serve warm.

notes: Food safety: cook the egg until set and eat promptly; do not keep the filling warm for long.
Tip: leave the chilli seeds out for a milder filling.

title: Berbere-Style Spiced Chicken Flatbread Rolls
summary: Spiced chicken stewed with eggs, rolled in flatbread.

steps.text: Cook the finely diced onion in a dry, wide pan over medium heat for 8 minutes, stirring, until soft and lightly browned at the edges.
Add the butter, paprika and cumin with 1/2 tsp salt and stir for 1 minute until the butter melts and the spices smell fragrant.
Add the chicken and 1/2 cup water. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the chicken is cooked through (at least 75°C) and the sauce is thick.
Meanwhile boil the eggs in simmering water for 9 minutes until firm, cool in cold water and peel. Halve them and warm through in the sauce for 2 minutes.
Warm the flatbread in a dry pan for 30 seconds a side until soft and pliable. Spoon the chicken and egg onto each, roll up tightly and serve.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C and boil eggs until firm; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Tip: sweet paprika is used here, so the dish is warm rather than hot; add a pinch of chilli flakes for heat.

title: Kenyan Beef Samosa Plates
summary: Crisp beef mince triangles with tomato and cucumber.

steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan over medium heat. Cook the finely chopped onion for 5 minutes until soft, then add the mince and curry powder with 1/2 tsp salt.
Cook for 8 minutes, breaking up the mince, until browned and cooked through (at least 75°C) and the liquid has evaporated. Cool for 10 minutes.
Cut each wrapper in half. Place a spoonful of filling at one corner and fold over and over into a triangle, sealing the final edge with a dab of water.
Heat the remaining oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Shallow-fry the samosas for 3 minutes a side, until golden brown and crisp.
Drain on paper towel and serve with sliced tomato and cucumber.

notes: Food safety: cook beef mince to 75°C; cool the filling and refrigerate within 2 hours if not using straight away.
Tip: let the filling cool or the wrappers tear and turn soggy.
Make ahead: fold the samosas and chill for up to a day before frying.

title: Tanzanian Coconut Bean Stew
summary: Kidney beans in coconut milk and tomato, vegan, gluten free.

steps.text: Heat a splash of oil in a large pot over medium heat. Fry the chopped onion and crushed garlic with a pinch of salt for 5 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the chopped tomato and curry powder and cook for 6 minutes, stirring, until the tomato breaks down into a thick paste.
Add the drained beans and coconut milk with 1/2 tsp salt. Simmer gently for 10 minutes, mashing a few beans against the pot, until the stew is thick and creamy.
Meanwhile cook 1 cup of dry basmati rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy. Serve the stew over the rice.

notes: Tip: simmer rather than boil the coconut milk so it stays smooth.
Storage: keeps 4 days in the fridge; thin with a splash of water when reheating until steaming hot.

title: Maize Pap Bowls with Curried Tomato Onion
summary: Maize pap with spiced tomato and onion, vegan.

steps.text: Bring the water and 1/2 tsp salt to the boil in a heavy pot. Slowly pour in the polenta in a thin stream, whisking constantly until smooth and lump-free.
Reduce to low and cook for 15 minutes, stirring often with a wooden spoon, until the pap is thick, pulls from the sides and no grittiness remains.
Meanwhile heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and fry the sliced onions with a pinch of salt for 6 minutes until soft and golden.
Stir in the curry powder for 30 seconds, then add the chopped tomato and simmer for 8 minutes, stirring, until thick and jammy.
Spoon the pap into bowls and top with the curried tomato onion while hot.

notes: Tip: pour the polenta in a thin stream; adding it quickly makes lumps.
Pap thickens as it cools, so serve at once.

title: Curried Apricot Chicken Skewers on Basmati
summary: Curried chicken skewers with apricot, gluten free.

steps.text: Soak 8 wooden skewers in water for 20 minutes (or use metal skewers). Toss the cubed chicken with the curry powder, apricot jam, oil and 1/2 tsp salt in a bowl until evenly coated.
Thread the chicken onto the skewers with the onion cut into wedges, leaving a little space between pieces.
Grill or barbecue on medium-high heat for 15 minutes, turning every few minutes, until the chicken is cooked through (at least 75°C) and charred at the edges.
Meanwhile cook 1 cup of dry basmati rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Serve the skewers whole on top of the rice, or slide the chicken off the skewers into the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C, use clean utensils for the cooked chicken and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Plus 30 minutes marinating is optional for a deeper flavour.
Tip: jam burns easily, so keep the heat medium and turn often.

title: Bunny Chow Bean Curry Loaf
summary: Hollowed bread filled with spiced bean curry, vegan.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Fry the chopped onion with a pinch of salt for 6 minutes until golden, then stir in the curry powder for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the chopped tomato, drained beans, cubed potato, 1 tsp salt and 1 cup water. Bring to a simmer and cook for 20 minutes, until the potato is tender and the curry is thick.
Cut the loaf in half, or slice off the top, and pull out the soft crumb to leave a 2cm thick shell.
Fill the bread with the hot curry and serve with the pulled-out bread for dipping.

notes: Tip: use a sturdy crusty loaf so the shell holds the curry without going soggy.
Traditionally eaten with your hands, so serve with plenty of napkins.

title: Purple Sweet Potato Rice Pancakes
summary: Rice flour pancakes with sweet potato mash.

steps.text: Peel the sweet potato, cut into chunks and boil for 12 minutes until very tender when pierced with a knife. Drain well and mash until completely smooth.
Whisk the mash with the rice flour, coconut milk, egg, sugar and a pinch of salt until you have a thick pourable batter. Rest for 5 minutes.
Heat a little coconut oil in a non-stick pan over medium-low heat. Pour in 1/4 cup batter per pancake and cook for 3 minutes until bubbles appear and the underside is golden.
Flip and cook for 2 minutes until golden and cooked through. Repeat with the remaining oil and batter and serve warm.

notes: Food safety: cook until the centre is set and no longer wet; do not eat raw batter.
Tip: keep the heat low or the sugar in the batter will scorch before the middle sets.

title: Filipino Beef Tapa Lunch Wraps
summary: Garlic soy beef strips with tomato in tortillas.

steps.text: Toss the sliced beef with the soy sauce, crushed garlic and brown sugar and set aside for 20 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large pan over high heat. Sear the beef in 2 batches for 2 minutes a side until browned and caramelised at the edges and at least 63°C inside.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 20 seconds a side until soft and pliable.
Slice the tomato and divide with the beef among the tortillas, then fold or roll up and serve warm.

notes: Plus 20 minutes marinating.
Food safety: cook beef to 63°C, keep raw meat away from ready-to-eat food and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Tip: do not crowd the pan or the beef steams rather than sears.

title: Vegan Pancit Lunch Noodles
summary: Egg-free noodles stir-fried with cabbage, carrot and soy, vegan.

steps.text: Cook the noodles in boiling water for 4 minutes, or to packet directions, until tender but still springy. Drain and rinse briefly.
Heat the oil in a large wok over high heat. Stir-fry the crushed garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant, then add the julienned carrot and shredded cabbage.
Stir-fry for 4 minutes until crisp-tender and bright, with the edges just starting to colour.
Add the noodles and soy sauce and toss for 2 minutes until the noodles are glossy, evenly coloured and steaming hot.
Divide into bowls and serve with lime wedges to squeeze over.

notes: Tip: cut the vegetables thin and even so they cook in the same time as the noodles.
Storage: keeps 2 days in the fridge; reheat until steaming hot.

title: Pacific Cassava Coconut Dumpling Plates
summary: Grated cassava flour dumplings in coconut milk, vegan, gluten free.

steps.text: Mix the cassava flour, coconut milk and salt in a bowl, kneading for 3 minutes until a soft, smooth dough forms that holds together. Add a splash of water if it cracks.
Shape into 12 balls the size of a walnut. Drop into a pot of simmering salted water and boil for 10 minutes, until they float and feel firm.
Drain well. Heat the coconut oil in a frying pan over medium heat and fry the dumplings for 3 minutes a side, until golden and lightly crisp.
Serve warm with sliced fresh tomato on the side, and a pinch of salt over the tomato.

notes: Tip: cassava flour absorbs a lot of liquid, so the dough should feel soft like play dough, not dry.
Storage: best eaten the same day.

title: Baked Lime Coconut Fish Rice Plates
summary: Fish baked in coconut milk with lime, gluten free.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C. Slice the onion and tomato and layer them in a baking dish with 1/2 tsp salt.
Lay the fish fillets on top. Pour over the coconut milk and the juice of the lime and season with a little more salt.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until the fish turns opaque, flakes easily with a fork and reaches 63°C, and the sauce is bubbling.
Meanwhile cook 1 cup of dry jasmine rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Spoon the rice onto plates and top with fish and the coconut sauce.

notes: Food safety: cook fish until opaque and flaking (63°C); refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 24 hours.
Tip: pat the fish dry first so the sauce stays creamy.

title: Hawaiian Pineapple Tofu Rice Bowls
summary: Glazed tofu and pineapple over rice, vegan.

steps.text: Cook 1 cup of dry jasmine rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Pat the tofu dry. Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat and fry the cubes for 6 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp on all sides.
Drain the pineapple and add to the pan with the teriyaki sauce. Cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until the sauce bubbles and turns sticky and glossy.
Spoon the tofu and pineapple over the rice and serve hot.

notes: Tip: pressing the tofu for 10 minutes before frying makes it crisper.
Storage: keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat until steaming hot.

title: Samoan Style Coconut Chicken Parcels
summary: Chicken in coconut and spinach in foil, gluten free.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C. Cut the chicken into large pieces and mix in a bowl with the coconut milk, thinly sliced onion, baby spinach and salt.
Cut four 35cm squares of foil. Divide the mixture among them and fold the edges over twice, pressing until sealed into airtight parcels with a little room for steam.
Place on a baking tray and bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through (at least 75°C) and the juices are bubbling and creamy.
Rest the parcels for 5 minutes, then open carefully, away from your face, as the steam is very hot, and serve straight from the foil.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C and check the thickest piece before serving.
Tip: serve with steamed rice or boiled cassava to soak up the coconut sauce.

title: Tongan Style Corned Beef Rice Pans
summary: Corned beef with onion and tomato over rice.

steps.text: Cook 1 cup of dry jasmine rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Fry the sliced onion for 5 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the chopped tomato and cook for 4 minutes until softened and pulpy, then add the corned beef, breaking it up with a spoon.
Cook for 4 minutes, stirring, until the mixture is hot throughout and the tomato juices have reduced.
Spoon over the rice and serve hot.

notes: Food safety: reheat corned beef until steaming hot; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Tip: canned corned beef is salty, so taste before adding any extra salt.

title: Malaysian Jam and Butter Toast Fingers with Soy Eggs
summary: Thick toast layered with sweet jam and butter, served with gently cooked eggs and a splash of soy and pepper.

steps.text: Bring a small pot of water to a gentle boil, lower in the eggs and cook for 6 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks are jammy, then cool in cold water for 1 minute and peel.
Toast the bread in a toaster or dry pan until golden and crisp on both sides, about 3 minutes.
Spread two slices with the jam and the other two with the cold butter, then sandwich together and press lightly until the butter starts to soften.
Crack the eggs into a shallow bowl, add the soy sauce and pepper and break up lightly with a fork until saucy.
Cut the toast into fingers and serve with the eggs for dipping until the plate is clean.

notes: Tip: the jam is sweet, so go easy on the soy sauce.
