Food safety: cook eggs until the whites are fully set; do not serve to anyone at risk with runny yolks. Use fresh, uncracked eggs; for pregnant women, older people, young children and anyone with low immunity, cook the eggs until the yolks are firm.

title: Nasi Lemak Egg Breakfast Wraps
summary: Coconut rice, sambal and a crisp fried egg rolled in a flatbread for a portable take on the classic breakfast.

steps.text: Rinse the rice, then simmer with the coconut milk, water and 1/2 tsp salt in a covered pot over low heat for 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender and fluffy. Rest covered for 5 minutes.
Heat the oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and fry the eggs for 2 to 3 minutes until the whites are crisp at the edges and fully set.
Warm the flatbreads in a dry pan for 20 seconds a side until soft and pliable.
Spread each flatbread with a spoonful of sambal, then add coconut rice, a fried egg, sliced cucumber and peanuts.
Fold in the sides and roll up tightly, then serve warm.

notes: Tip: sambal oelek is hot, so start with 1 tbsp for a milder wrap.

Food safety: cook eggs until the whites are fully set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs; for pregnant women, older people, young children and anyone with low immunity, cook the eggs until the yolks are firm.

title: Roti Jala Lace Pancakes with Curry Dip
summary: Delicate net-like crepes poured from a squeeze bottle and rolled around a mild, spiced potato and pea curry.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, egg, coconut milk, water, turmeric and 1/2 tsp salt until completely smooth and the consistency of thin cream. Rest for 10 minutes, then pour into a squeeze bottle with a few small holes.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat. Fry the chopped onion for 5 minutes until soft, stir in the curry powder for 30 seconds until fragrant, then add the potato and 1 1/2 cups water.
Simmer for 15 minutes, mashing a few pieces of potato, until the potato is tender and the curry is thick. Stir in the peas for the last 2 minutes until bright green.

Heat a non-stick pan over medium-low heat and lightly grease. Squeeze the batter in a circular lacy pattern and cook for 1 minute until set and the underside is pale, with no browning. Do not flip. Slide out and repeat with the remaining batter.
Fold each lace pancake into a quarter and serve with the curry.

notes: Food safety: make sure the batter is cooked through and refrigerate leftover curry within 2 hours.
Tip: the pan must be hot enough to set the batter at once but not so hot that the lace colours.

title: Nasi Kerabu Style Herb Rice Breakfast Bowls
summary: Fragrant rice tossed with herbs, served with a salty coconut topping, soft egg and crisp cucumber.

steps.text: Cook the rice with 1 1/2 cups water in a covered pot over low heat for 15 minutes until tender and fluffy, then rest for 5 minutes.
Toast the desiccated coconut in a dry pan over medium heat for 3 minutes, stirring, until golden. Tip into a bowl and mix with the soy sauce.
Boil the eggs for 8 minutes until the yolks are just set, cool in cold water, then peel and halve.
Finely slice the coriander and mint, then slice the cucumber into thin matchsticks.
Toss the warm rice with the herbs, oil and the juice of half the lime until the grains are speckled green. Spoon into bowls.
Top with the eggs, cucumber and toasted coconut mixture, and serve with the remaining lime in wedges.

notes: Food safety: boil eggs until firm and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Sambal Egg Wraps with Crisp Onion
summary: Soft eggs cooked in a quick sambal base, rolled in warm roti with crisp fried onion.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Slice half the onion thinly and fry for 4 minutes until deep golden and crisp, then lift out onto paper towel.
Chop the remaining onion and cook in the pan for 3 minutes until soft, then add the diced tomato and sambal and cook for 3 minutes until thick and saucy.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt, pour over the sauce and stir gently for 2 minutes until just set and creamy.
Warm the roti in a dry pan for 30 seconds a side until soft and flecked with brown.
Spoon the egg onto the roti, scatter over the crisp onion, roll up and serve warm.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until set throughout. Use fresh, uncracked eggs; for pregnant women, older people, young children and anyone with low immunity, cook the eggs until the yolks are firm.

title: Jakarta Style Turmeric Chicken Rice Porridge with Egg
summary: Silky rice porridge cooked with ginger, topped with shredded turmeric chicken, fried shallot and a soft egg.

steps.text: Combine the rice, water, ginger, garlic and 1 tsp salt in a large pot. Bring to the boil until bubbling, then reduce to a low simmer.
Add the chicken and turmeric and simmer gently for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is cooked through (at least 75°C). Lift out the chicken and shred with two forks.
Keep simmering the rice for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring often, until it breaks down into a thick, creamy porridge. Add hot water if it gets too thick.
Boil the eggs for 7 minutes until jammy, cool and peel.
Ladle the porridge into bowls and top with the shredded chicken, halved egg, soy sauce, spring onion and a drizzle of the oil.

notes: Tip: stir the porridge from the bottom often as it catches easily.

Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C and eat porridge hot; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until steaming. Use fresh, uncracked eggs; for pregnant women, older people, young children and anyone with low immunity, cook the eggs until the yolks are firm.

title: Kolak Pumpkin Coconut Breakfast Pots
summary: Sweet pumpkin and sweet potato simmered in coconut milk with palm sugar and warm spice, served warm.

steps.text: Combine the water, coconut milk, brown sugar, cinnamon and salt in a pot and bring to a gentle simmer, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Add the pumpkin and sweet potato and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, until both are tender when pierced with a fork and the liquid has thickened slightly.
Remove the cinnamon stick and ladle into bowls. Serve warm.

notes: Tip: keep the heat low so the coconut milk does not split.
Vegan.

title: Sweet Potato Pancakes with Coconut Syrup
summary: Soft rice flour pancakes made with sweet potato, drizzled with warm palm sugar coconut syrup.

steps.text: Peel and boil the sweet potato for 12 minutes until very tender, then drain and mash smooth.
Beat the mash with the rice flour, egg and half the coconut milk until a thick batter forms.
Heat the coconut oil in a non-stick pan over medium-low heat. Cook 1/4 cup scoops of batter for 3 minutes a side, until golden and cooked through.
Simmer the brown sugar, water and remaining coconut milk for 5 minutes until syrupy.
Stack the pancakes and spoon over the warm syrup.

notes: Food safety: cook until set in the centre.

title: Mandazi Spiced Coconut Breakfast Fingers
summary: Lightly sweet cardamom doughnut fingers fried until puffed and golden, served with warm tea.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder, sugar, cardamom and 1/2 tsp salt in a bowl, make a well and add the coconut milk and egg.
Mix to a soft dough and knead for 3 minutes on a floured bench until smooth and no longer sticky. Cover and rest for 10 minutes.
Roll out to 1cm thick and cut into fingers.
Heat the oil in a deep frying pan to 175°C (a cube of bread browns in about 30 seconds). Fry in batches for 2 minutes a side until puffed and deep golden.
Drain on paper towel and serve warm.

notes: Food safety: take care with hot oil; cook until golden and cooked through.
Plus 10 minutes resting.

title: Kampala Street Rolex Omelette Wraps
summary: Street-style omelette rolled in a soft chapati with cabbage and tomato.

steps.text: Finely shred the cabbage, dice the tomatoes and slice the onion.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Cook the onion and cabbage for 3 minutes until just soft, then add the tomato and 1/2 tsp salt and cook for 1 minute.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt. Pour a quarter into a clean oiled pan, swirl, and cook for 2 minutes until set. Fold in a quarter of the vegetables. Repeat to make 4 omelettes.
Warm the chapati in a dry pan for 20 seconds a side until soft and flecked with brown.
Lay an omelette on each chapati, roll up tightly and serve hot until steaming.

notes: Food safety: cook the omelettes until fully set and eat promptly.

title: Kenyan Spiced Sweet Potato Mash Breakfast Bowls
summary: Mashed sweet potato and kidney bean with coconut, topped with a fried egg and tomato.

steps.text: Peel and cube the sweet potato and boil for 15 minutes until very tender. Drain and mash with the coconut milk and 1/2 tsp salt until smooth.
Heat half the oil in a pan and stir the beans with the cumin for 3 minutes until hot and fragrant. Fold into the mash.
Heat the remaining oil and fry the sliced tomato for 2 minutes until softened.
Fry the eggs in the same pan for 3 minutes until the whites are firm.
Spoon the mash into bowls and top with tomato and a fried egg.

notes: Food safety: cook eggs until the whites are firm. Use fresh, uncracked eggs; for pregnant women, older people, young children and anyone with low immunity, cook the eggs until the yolks are firm.

title: Ethiopian Spiced Scrambled Eggs with Flatbread
summary: Soft eggs cooked with onion, tomato and warming spice, scooped up with warm flatbread.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a frying pan over medium heat. Cook the diced onion for 4 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the paprika and cumin and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant, then add the chopped tomato and cook for 3 minutes until saucy.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt, pour in and stir gently for 2 minutes until softly set.
Warm the flatbread in a dry pan until soft and serve alongside.

notes: Food safety: cook eggs until set; do not use cracked eggs.

title: Rusk Dipping Porridge with Cinnamon Milk
summary: Warm maize porridge finished with cinnamon milk and crunchy toasted almond topping.

steps.text: Toast the flaked almonds in a dry pan for 3 minutes until golden, then set aside.
Bring the milk and water to a gentle simmer in a heavy pot. Whisk in the polenta in a thin stream until smooth.
Cook on low heat for 12 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Stir in the sugar and cinnamon and divide into bowls. Top with the almonds.

notes: Tip: add extra milk for a looser porridge.

title: Eggs Bobotie Breakfast Cups
summary: Mini curried mince cups topped with an egg custard layer, baked until set.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C and lightly oil a 4-cup muffin tin. Soak the bread in the milk.

Fry the onion in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, add the mince and curry powder and cook for 6 minutes until browned and cooked through. Stir in the jam and squeezed bread, mixing until moist and thick.
Divide among 4 large muffin cups, pressing down firmly.
Bake for 10 minutes. Crack an egg over each and bake for 8 to 10 minutes until the whites are fully set and the mince is at least 75°C.
Rest for 3 minutes, then lift out and serve warm.

notes: Food safety: cook mince to 75°C and eggs until set.

title: Mielie Fritters with Cinnamon and Honey
summary: Sweet corn fritters pan-fried until golden and served with cinnamon honey.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder and a pinch of salt in a bowl. Beat in the eggs and milk until a thick batter forms, then fold in the corn.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Drop in spoonfuls of batter and cook for 3 minutes a side until golden and cooked through.
Warm the honey with the cinnamon for 1 minute until runny.
Stack the fritters and drizzle over the cinnamon honey.

notes: Food safety: cook until set in the middle.

title: Samoan Panikeke Coconut Pancakes
summary: Soft coconut pancakes cooked in a pan and served with warm lime syrup.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder, 1 tbsp of the sugar and a pinch of salt in a bowl. Add the egg, coconut milk and water and whisk until just smooth.
Heat the oil in a non-stick pan over medium-low heat and ladle in 1/4 cup batter per pancake. Cook for 3 minutes until bubbles form, flip and cook for 2 minutes until golden.
Simmer the remaining sugar with the lime juice and 2 tbsp water for 3 minutes until syrupy.
Stack the pancakes and spoon over the syrup.

notes: Food safety: cook until set.

title: Hawaiian Coconut Sweet Bread Toast
summary: Thick slices of bread griddled with coconut egg custard and topped with warm pineapple.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs, coconut milk and cinnamon in a shallow dish.
Melt the butter in a frying pan over medium heat. Soak the bread in the mixture for 20 seconds a side, then fry for 3 minutes a side until golden and set in the middle.
Warm the drained pineapple in the pan for 2 minutes until just caramelised.
Serve the toast topped with the pineapple while hot and golden.

notes: Food safety: cook until the custard is set.

title: Fijian Cassava Coconut Pan Cakes
summary: Cassava flour batter fried into golden coconut cakes with a crisp edge.

steps.text: Stir the cassava flour with the coconut, coconut milk, sugar, egg, 1/4 cup water and a pinch of salt into a thick batter that holds a shape.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Spoon the batter into flat cakes and cook for 5 minutes a side until deeply golden and cooked through.
Drain on paper towel and serve warm.

notes: Food safety: cook cassava thoroughly, never eat it raw; cook until tender throughout.

title: Okinawan Sweet Potato Yoghurt Parfait Bowls
summary: Baked purple-fleshed sweet potato with yoghurt, honey and crunchy sesame oats.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C. Bake the sweet potatoes for 40 minutes until a knife slides in easily. Cool for 10 minutes.
Toast the oats and sesame in a dry pan for 4 minutes until golden and fragrant.
Mash the sweet potato flesh and spoon into bowls. Top with yoghurt, honey and the oat mixture.

notes: Tip: bake the potatoes the night before to save time.

title: Japanese Soy Egg Toasties
summary: Soft egg mixed with soy and mayo, griddled in buttered bread until golden.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes until firm, cool in cold water, peel and chop.
Mix with the mayonnaise and soy sauce until creamy.
Spoon onto two slices of bread and top with the remaining slices.
Butter the outsides and toast in a pan for 3 minutes a side, until golden and crisp.

notes: Food safety: boil eggs until firm; keep the filling cold until cooking and eat promptly.

title: Congee with Soy Egg and Crisp Shallots
summary: Slow-cooked rice congee topped with soy-marinated eggs and crisp fried shallots.

steps.text: Combine the rice, water, ginger and 1 tsp salt in a large pot. Bring to the boil, then simmer on low for 45 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Boil the eggs for 7 minutes until jammy, cool and peel, then steep in 2 tbsp soy sauce for 10 minutes.
Fry the thinly sliced shallots in the oil for 4 minutes until crisp and golden.
Ladle the congee into bowls and top with halved eggs, shallots, spring onion and remaining soy sauce.

notes: Food safety: boil eggs until the whites are firm. Use fresh, uncracked eggs; for pregnant women, older people, young children and anyone with low immunity, cook the eggs until the yolks are firm.

title: Korean Egg and Kimchi Breakfast Rice Cakes
summary: Chewy rice cakes pan-fried with kimchi and topped with a runny egg.

steps.text: Soak the rice cakes in warm water for 10 minutes if firm, then drain.
Heat the sesame oil in a pan over medium heat. Fry the kimchi for 3 minutes until softened, then add the rice cakes and gochujang and toss for 5 minutes until chewy and glossy.
Make two wells and crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 2 minutes until the whites are set.
Scatter with spring onion and serve.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set.

title: Vietnamese Sticky Rice Breakfast Pots
summary: Sticky rice with peanuts and coconut for a filling start to the day.

steps.text: Rinse the rice, then simmer with the water and 1/2 tsp salt in a covered pot on low for 20 minutes until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender and sticky.
Toast the coconut for 3 minutes until golden and crush the peanuts roughly.
Mix the sugar through the rice, then divide into bowls and top with coconut and peanuts.

notes: Vegan.

title: Indian Egg Paratha Rolls with Mint Yoghurt
summary: Flaky flatbreads sealed with a spiced egg layer and served with cool mint yoghurt.

steps.text: Beat the eggs with the finely diced onion, chilli, garam masala and 1/2 tsp salt.
Heat the oil in a pan and cook the egg mixture in 3 batches for 2 minutes each until set.
Warm the parathas in a dry pan for 1 minute a side until crisp and golden.
Stir the mint into the yoghurt.
Roll an omelette in each paratha, drizzle with mint yoghurt and serve.

notes: Food safety: cook eggs until set.

title: Pilau Spiced Beef and Potato Rice Pot
summary: A fragrant one-pot rice, browned beef and potatoes cooked in whole spices and a deep onion base.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Fry the thinly sliced onions with 1 tsp salt for 15 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden brown.
Add the beef and brown for 8 minutes until coloured all over. Stir in the crushed garlic, grated ginger, cumin, pepper and cinnamon and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add 3 cups water, cover and simmer on low for 40 minutes until the beef is tender.

Add the potato chunks and rinsed rice with 2 1/2 cups water. Bring to the boil, stir once, cover and cook on very low heat for 18 minutes until the rice is tender and fluffy and the water is absorbed.
Rest covered for 10 minutes, then fluff and serve. The beef should reach at least 75°C.

notes: Food safety: cook beef pieces to 75°C and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Tip: do not skip the slow browning of the onions, as they give the colour and sweetness.

title: Swahili Fish in Coconut Tamarind Sauce
summary: White fish simmered in a tangy coconut and tamarind sauce, served over rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice in 1 1/2 cups water, covered, on low heat for 15 minutes until tender and fluffy.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and fry the sliced onion for 5 minutes until soft. Add garlic and turmeric for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the chopped tomato and cook for 5 minutes until broken down, then pour in the coconut milk, tamarind and 1/2 tsp salt. Simmer for 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
Lay the fish in the sauce and simmer for 6 to 8 minutes, spooning the sauce over, until opaque and flaking at 63°C.
Serve the fish and sauce over the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook fish to 63°C; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 24 hours.

title: Nairobi Style Beef Curry with Coconut Finish
summary: Tender beef simmered with spices and coconut until the sauce clings to the meat, served with rice.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a heavy pot and fry the onions for 6 minutes until soft and golden.
Add garlic, ginger and curry powder for 1 minute until fragrant, then the beef and brown for 6 minutes.
Add the chopped tomato, 1/2 tsp salt and 1/2 cup water, cover and simmer for 35 minutes until the beef is tender, reaching at least 75°C.
Uncover, stir in the coconut milk and cook for 5 minutes until the sauce is thick and clings to the beef.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy and serve alongside.

notes: Food safety: cook beef to 75°C; refrigerate leftovers promptly.

title: Ugali with Spiced Egg and Tomato Stew
summary: Firm maize porridge with a simple tomato stew cooked with whole eggs.

steps.text: Boil the water with 1/2 tsp salt and whisk in the polenta. Cook on low heat for 15 minutes, stirring hard, until very thick and pulling away from the pot.
Meanwhile fry the sliced onion in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, add the curry powder and chopped tomato and simmer for 8 minutes until thick.
Make three wells in the stew, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 4 minutes until the whites are set.
Shape the ugali into mounds and serve with the stew.

notes: Food safety: cook eggs until set.

title: Mchuzi Mix Coconut Chicken Wraps
summary: Chicken simmered in a mild coconut curry sauce and wrapped in warm chapati with kachumbari.

steps.text: Fry the onion in a little oil for 5 minutes until soft, then add the curry powder for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the chicken, tomato and 1/2 tsp salt. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring, until the chicken is cooked through at 75°C.
Pour in the coconut milk and simmer for 5 minutes until thick.
Finely dice the cucumber and red onion with a pinch of salt for a quick kachumbari.
Warm the chapati until soft and fill with chicken and kachumbari.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Zanzibar Spiced Potato and Pea Patties
summary: Crisp potato cakes with peas and cumin, shallow-fried and served with a lime wedge.

steps.text: Boil the potato for 15 minutes until tender, drain and mash roughly. Cool for 10 minutes.
Mix the mash with the peas, cumin, turmeric, egg, flour and 1 tsp salt until it holds together when pressed into a ball. Chill for 10 minutes so the patties firm up.
Shape into 8 patties and fry in the oil for 4 minutes a side over medium heat until golden brown and crisp.
Serve warm with lime wedges.

notes: Food safety: cook until set in the middle.

title: Cape Malay Style Chicken Biryani Pot
summary: Layered rice and spiced chicken with caramelised onions, cooked slowly so the grains stay separate.

steps.text: Fry the sliced onions in the oil for 15 minutes until deeply golden, then lift half out for the topping.
Add garlic, curry powder, turmeric and cinnamon for 1 minute until fragrant, then add the chicken and yoghurt and simmer for 20 minutes until the chicken reaches at least 75°C and the sauce is thick.
Boil the rice and lentils in salted water for 8 minutes until just tender, then drain.
Layer half the rice over the chicken, add the rest of the chicken mix, then the remaining rice. Scatter over the fried onion.
Cover tightly and cook on very low heat for 25 minutes until the rice is tender and steamed through.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C and cool leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Durban Style Lamb Curry with Roti
summary: Slow-cooked lamb curry with potato and a warming spice base, scooped up with roti.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a heavy pot and fry the onions for 8 minutes until golden. Add garlic, ginger and curry powder for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the lamb and brown for 8 minutes, then add tomato, 1 tsp salt and 1 cup water.
Cover and simmer on low for 70 minutes until the lamb is very tender.
Add the potato chunks and cook for 20 minutes until tender, reaching at least 75°C in the lamb.
Warm the roti in a dry pan and serve with the curry.

notes: Food safety: cook lamb to 75°C and reheat leftovers until steaming hot.

title: Potjie Style Chicken and Butternut Stew
summary: A gentle one-pot chicken stew with butternut, tomatoes and a hint of apricot.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in oil for 8 minutes until golden, then set aside.
Fry the onions for 5 minutes until soft, stir in the curry powder, then add tomato and jam and simmer for 5 minutes.
Return the chicken with the pumpkin and 1/2 cup water. Cover and cook on low for 35 minutes until the chicken reaches 75°C and the pumpkin is tender.
Season with salt and serve with rice or bread.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C.

title: Curried Chicken Mayo Sandwiches with Apricot Chutney
summary: Shredded cooked chicken folded through curry mayo and apricot chutney, layered with cucumber in toasted bread.

steps.text: Toast the bread in a toaster or dry pan for 3 minutes until golden and crisp, then let it cool on a rack so the sandwiches do not turn soggy.
Shred the cooked chicken finely and mix in a bowl with the mayonnaise, curry powder, apricot jam and a pinch of salt until creamy and evenly coated.
Slice the cucumber thinly and pat dry with paper towel.
Spread the chicken mixture over three slices of toast, top with cucumber, then close with the remaining toast and press gently until the filling holds.
Cut into halves or triangles and serve at once, or wrap and chill for up to 4 hours until needed.

notes: Food safety: use chicken that was cooked and chilled promptly; keep refrigerated until eating and discard after 2 days.
Tip: a squeeze of lemon lifts the filling if the jam is very sweet.

title: Prawn Sambal Plates with Crisp Sweet Corn Cakes
summary: Crisp sweet corn fritters served over fluffy rice with fiery sambal prawns.

steps.text: Rinse 1 cup of dry jasmine rice, then cook with 1 1/2 cups water in a covered pot on low heat for 15 minutes until tender and fluffy. Rest covered for 5 minutes.
Stir the corn, flour, egg, 1/2 tsp salt and 1/2 cup water into a thick, spoonable batter.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Drop in heaped spoonfuls of batter and fry for 3 minutes a side until deep golden and crisp at the edges. Drain on paper towel.
Wipe the pan, heat the remaining oil and stir-fry the prawns with the sambal for 4 minutes until pink, opaque and coated in the glossy sauce.
Divide the rice among bowls, arrange the fritters on top and spoon over the prawns and their sauce.

notes: Food safety: cook prawns until opaque and pink throughout; eat promptly and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Tip: sambal oelek is hot, so use 1 tbsp for a milder bowl.

title: Malaysian Chicken Curry Puffs with Cucumber
summary: Flaky pastry half-moons filled with spiced chicken and potato, baked until puffed and deep golden.

steps.text: Boil the finely diced potato for 8 minutes until just tender, then drain and leave to steam dry.

Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Cook the finely chopped onion for 4 minutes until soft, add the mince and curry powder and cook for 8 minutes, breaking it up, until the mince is cooked through at 75°C and no longer pink.
Stir in the potato and 1/2 tsp salt, then spread on a tray and cool for 15 minutes so the pastry stays crisp.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Cut each pastry sheet into 4 squares, add a spoonful of filling to each, fold into triangles and press the edges with a fork until sealed. Brush with beaten egg.
Bake on a lined tray for 20 minutes until deep golden and puffed. Serve warm with sliced cucumber.

notes: Food safety: cook mince to 75°C and cool the filling quickly; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Tip: cold filling and cold pastry give the flakiest puffs.

title: Sambal Tumis Egg and Long Bean Lunch Plates
summary: Green beans stir-fried in a mild sambal with halved boiled eggs, served over steamed rice.

steps.text: Cook 1 cup of dry jasmine rice with 1 1/2 cups water in a covered pot on low heat for 15 minutes until tender and fluffy.
Boil the eggs in simmering water for 8 minutes until the yolks are just set, then cool in cold water, peel and halve.
Heat the oil in a wok or large pan and fry the sliced onion for 4 minutes until soft. Add the sambal and stir for 1 minute until darker and fragrant.
Add the beans cut into 5cm lengths with 1/4 cup water and cook for 6 minutes, tossing, until crisp-tender and coated in sauce.
Divide the rice between plates, top with the beans and the halved eggs, and spoon over any sauce left in the pan.

notes: Food safety: boil eggs until the whites and yolks are firm and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Soto Betawi Style Beef and Coconut Stew
summary: A rich beef stew in a creamy, spiced coconut broth with potato and tomato.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Fry the sliced onion for 5 minutes until soft, then add the crushed garlic and grated ginger and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the beef and ground coriander and stir for 3 minutes to coat. Pour in the water with 1 tsp salt, cover and simmer on low for 70 minutes until the beef is tender when pressed with a fork.
Add the potato chunks and simmer for 15 minutes until tender.
Stir in the coconut milk and wedges of tomato and simmer uncovered for 8 minutes until the broth thickens slightly and the beef reaches at least 75°C.
Taste and add salt, then ladle into bowls with the potato and beef.

notes: Food safety: cook beef to 75°C; reheat leftovers until steaming hot.
Tip: skim the oil that rises to the top for a lighter broth.

title: Tahu Isi Stuffed Tofu with Peanut Sauce
summary: Golden fried tofu pockets stuffed with crunchy vegetables and drizzled with creamy peanut sauce.

steps.text: Press the tofu for 10 minutes, then cut into 8 triangles and pat dry with paper towel.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the tofu for 8 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp on all sides. Drain on paper towel.
Slice a pocket into each piece and stuff with grated carrot and bean sprouts.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice and 1/4 cup warm water until smooth and pourable like cream.
Arrange the tofu on a plate and drizzle with the sauce while the tofu is still warm.

notes: Vegan.
Tip: loosen the sauce with a little more warm water if it thickens.

title: Pacific Coconut Fish Stew with Sweet Potato
summary: A gentle fish stew in coconut milk with tender sweet potato and wilted spinach.

steps.text: Peel and cube the sweet potato and boil for 12 minutes until tender when pierced. Drain and set aside.
Cook the sliced onion with a splash of water in a wide pot for 5 minutes until soft, then add the coconut milk, 1/2 cup water and 1/2 tsp salt. Simmer for 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
Cut the fish into large chunks, add to the pot and simmer gently for 6 minutes until opaque, flaking easily and at least 63°C.
Stir in the spinach and sweet potato for 1 minute until the spinach wilts, then finish with the lime juice.
Ladle into bowls and serve warm.

notes: Food safety: cook fish to 63°C; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 24 hours.

title: Samoan Style Coconut Beef and Potato Hash
summary: Browned beef mince and crisp potato hash finished with coconut milk and spring onion.

steps.text: Dice the potatoes small and fry in the oil in a large pan over medium heat for 10 minutes, turning, until golden and tender.
Add the chopped onion and cook for 3 minutes until soft, then add the mince and cook for 6 minutes until browned and cooked through at 75°C.
Pour in the coconut milk with 1/2 tsp salt and cook for 2 minutes until absorbed and creamy.
Scatter with the spring onion and serve straight from the pan.

notes: Food safety: cook mince to 75°C and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Hawaiian Style Seared Fish Rice Bowls
summary: Seared white fish over fluffy rice with sweet pineapple, cucumber and soy.

steps.text: Cook 1 cup of dry jasmine rice with 1 1/2 cups water in a covered pot on low heat for 15 minutes until tender and fluffy.
Pat the fish dry and season with salt. Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat and sear for 3 minutes a side until golden, opaque and flaking at 63°C.
Slice the cucumber and drain the pineapple.
Break the fish into chunks and arrange over the rice with pineapple and cucumber, then drizzle over the soy sauce.

notes: Food safety: cook fish to 63°C; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Gluten Free Tamari Beef and Broccoli
summary: Tender beef and bright broccoli in a glossy tamari sauce thickened with cornflour, served on rice.

steps.text: Toss the beef with 1 tsp of the cornflour and 1 tbsp tamari and set aside for 10 minutes.
Cook 1 cup of dry jasmine rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Sear the beef for 2 minutes until browned and 63°C inside, then lift out.
Stir-fry the broccoli florets, crushed garlic and grated ginger for 4 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp.
Mix the remaining tamari and cornflour with 1/2 cup water, pour in and cook for 2 minutes until glossy and thick, then return the beef.
Toss for 30 seconds until hot and serve over the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook beef to 63°C; keep raw meat away from ready-to-eat food.
Check the tamari label is gluten-free.

title: Gluten Free Rice Noodle Stir-Fry with Tamarind, Prawn and Egg
summary: Rice noodles with prawns, egg and tamarind in a sweet-sour sauce with peanuts.

steps.text: Soak the noodles in hot water for 8 minutes, or to packet directions, until just tender, then drain.
Mix the tamarind, tamari, sugar and 2 tbsp water for the sauce.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Stir-fry the prawns for 3 minutes until pink and opaque, push aside and scramble the eggs for 1 minute until set.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss for 3 minutes until glossy, hot and the noodles have absorbed the sauce.
Toss through the sprouts, then serve topped with crushed peanuts and lime wedges.

notes: Food safety: cook prawns until opaque and eggs until set.
Check the tamari and tamarind labels are gluten-free.

title: Gluten Free Korean Style Beef Bowls
summary: Sliced beef marinated in tamari, sesame and garlic, seared and served over rice with cucumber.

steps.text: Mix the beef with the tamari, sesame oil, sugar and crushed garlic. Set aside for 20 minutes.
Cook 1 cup of dry jasmine rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Heat a heavy pan over high heat and sear the beef in 2 batches for 3 minutes each until browned, caramelised and at least 63°C.
Slice the cucumber and divide with the rice among bowls.
Top with the beef and any pan juices and serve warm.

notes: Plus 20 minutes marinating.
Food safety: cook beef to 63°C and discard leftover marinade.

title: Gluten Free Japanese Style Ginger Pork with Rice
summary: Thin pork slices glazed in a ginger, honey and tamari sauce, served with crisp cabbage and rice.

steps.text: Cook 1 cup of dry jasmine rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Heat a frying pan over medium-high heat and cook the pork in two batches for 3 minutes each until browned and at least 70°C inside.
Add the tamari, honey and grated ginger and bubble for 2 minutes until sticky and glossy.
Finely shred the cabbage and divide with the rice among plates.
Top with the pork and spoon over the glaze.

notes: Food safety: cook pork to 70°C and keep raw pork away from ready-to-eat food.
Check the tamari label is gluten-free.

title: Chengdu Sliced Pork Belly with Doubanjiang and Leek
summary: Thick slices of simmered pork belly stir-fried until curled and crisp-edged with leek, doubanjiang and fermented.

steps.text: Put the pork belly in a pot with the ginger, spring onion and enough water to cover. Bring to the boil, then simmer gently for 25 minutes until just tender when pierced with a skewer. Lift out and cool for 15 minutes so it slices cleanly.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, and keep it covered.
Slice the cooled pork into 3mm slices. Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and fry the pork for 4 minutes, turning, until the fat renders and the edges curl and brown.
Push the pork aside, add the doubanjiang and black beans and stir for 30 seconds until the oil turns red and fragrant. Add the garlic and toss through.
Add the leek, sugar and wine and stir-fry for 2 minutes until the leek is tender but still bright. Serve straight away over the rice.

notes: Food safety: simmer the pork until cooked through and keep leftovers refrigerated for no more than 2 days; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Sichuan. Dinner.

title: Cantonese Steamed Pork Patty with Mushrooms
summary: A tender hand-chopped style pork patty steamed with shiitake and ginger, with its own savoury juices spooned over rice.

steps.text: Soak the shiitake in hot water for 20 minutes until soft, then squeeze dry, remove the stems and chop finely.
Mix the pork with the shiitake, ginger, half the spring onion, soy sauce, oyster sauce, cornflour, sesame oil and sugar. Stir in one direction for 2 minutes until sticky and cohesive.
Press the mixture into a shallow heatproof dish in an even layer. Steam over boiling water for 15 minutes until the pork is cooked through and the juices run clear.
Meanwhile cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then steam the bok choy for 3 minutes until just tender.
Scatter the patty with the remaining spring onion and serve with the rice, bok choy and the juices from the dish.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork patty until no pink remains and the juices run clear; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Cantonese. Lunch.

title: Hakka Stuffed Tofu Puffs with Pork
summary: Hakka yong tau foo style: tofu puffs stuffed with a ginger pork filling, browned and braised in a light garlic soy.

steps.text: Mix the pork with the spring onion, ginger, soy sauce, sesame oil and cornflour until sticky. Make a slit in each tofu puff and press in a spoonful of filling.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and fry the stuffed puffs, filling side down, for 3 minutes each side until golden.
Add the garlic and stir for 20 seconds until fragrant, then pour in the stock and oyster sauce. Cover and simmer for 10 minutes until the pork is cooked through.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy. Blanch the gai lan for 2 minutes until bright green and tender.
Spoon the puffs and sauce over the rice and serve with the gai lan.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork filling until no pink remains in the centre of a puff; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Hakka. Dinner.

title: Okinawan Taco Rice Bowls
summary: Okinawa's beloved taco rice: spiced beef mince over hot rice, topped with lettuce, tomato and melted cheddar.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, and keep it warm.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat and cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and beef and brown for 6 minutes, breaking up the lumps, until no pink remains.
Stir in the taco seasoning, tomato sauce, Worcestershire sauce and water and simmer for 3 minutes until thick and glossy.
Divide the rice between 4 bowls and spoon over the beef. Top with the cheddar so it melts, then the lettuce and tomato.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef mince until browned right through with no pink remaining; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Okinawa. Lunch.

title: Miyazaki Chicken Nanban with Tartare Sauce
summary: Kyushu's crisp fried chicken dipped in a sweet vinegar glaze and finished with a creamy egg and pickle tartare.

items.raw: 600g chicken thigh, cut in large pieces

steps.text: Hard-boil 1 egg for 9 minutes, cool, peel and mash with the mayonnaise, pickle and chives to make the tartare.
Stir the soy sauce, vinegar and sugar in a small pot over low heat for 2 minutes until the sugar dissolves, then pour into a shallow dish.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy. Dust the chicken in the flour, then dip in the remaining beaten egg.
Heat the oil in a deep frying pan to 170C and fry the chicken in batches for 6 minutes until golden and cooked through. Drain briefly.
Turn each piece in the sweet vinegar glaze, slice and serve over the rice with the cabbage and tartare spooned over.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75C in the thickest part; eggs should be fully cooked; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Kyushu. Dinner.

title: Jeyuk Bokkeum Spicy Pork with Rice
summary: A fiery Korean pork stir-fry with gochujang, gochugaru and onion, served with rice and lettuce leaves for wrapping.

steps.text: Mix the gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, honey, sesame oil, garlic and ginger into a paste, then coat the pork in it.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.

Heat the oil in a wok or large pan over high heat and stir-fry the onion for 2 minutes until just softened. Add the pork in two batches and cook for 5 minutes each until browned with no pink remaining.
Return everything to the pan, toss with the spring onion for 1 minute until glossy, and serve over rice with lettuce leaves for wrapping.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork until browned right through and keep leftovers refrigerated; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Marinating the pork for 30 minutes gives deeper flavour. Dinner.

title: Isaan Crying Tiger Steak with Jaew Dipping Sauce
summary: Isaan-style grilled beef sliced and served with a smoky, tangy jaew sauce and sticky rice.

steps.text: Soak the sticky rice in water for 30 minutes if you have time, then steam it over boiling water for 25 minutes until tender and chewy.
Toast the rice flour in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 minutes until golden and nutty, then tip out.
Brush the steak with the soy sauce and oil and cook in a hot pan or grill for 4 minutes each side for medium until well browned. Rest for 5 minutes, then slice thinly against the grain.
Stir the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, chilli flakes, shallot, coriander, spring onion and toasted rice flour together until the sugar dissolves.
Serve the steak with the jaew sauce, sticky rice and cucumber.

notes: Food safety: cook beef steak to your preference but rest it, and keep the whole-muscle surface well seared; check the thickest part reaches 63°C for a steak.
Gluten-free if tamari is used for the soy sauce. Dinner.

title: Hue Banh Beo Steamed Rice Cakes with Prawn
summary: Hue's delicate steamed rice cakes in small dishes, topped with minced prawn, crisp shallots and a sweet fish sauce.

steps.text: Whisk the rice flour, tapioca starch, 2 cups water, salt and oil until smooth. Lightly oil 16 small heatproof dishes or ramekins.
Set the dishes in a steamer over boiling water for 5 minutes to heat. Fill each halfway with batter and steam for 10 minutes until set translucent and springy.
Stir-fry the minced prawn in a dry pan over medium heat for 3 minutes until pink and cooked through. Add the spring onion for 30 seconds until wilted.
Stir the fish sauce, sugar, lime juice, chilli and 1/2 cup water until the sugar dissolves, to make the dressing.
Loosen each cake with a small spoon. Top with prawn and fried shallots and spoon over the dressing, serving warm.

notes: Food safety: cook the prawn until opaque and pink and eat the same day; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Hue. Dinner. Gluten-free.

title: Telur Balado Padang Eggs in Chilli Sambal
summary: West Sumatran Padang eggs fried until blistered and simmered in a spicy red chilli and tomato sambal, served with rice.

steps.text: Hard-boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool in iced water and peel. Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat and fry the eggs for 4 minutes, turning, until the skins blister and turn golden. Lift out.
Blend the chillies, shallot, garlic and tomato to a coarse paste. Fry in the remaining oil for 8 minutes until darkened and the oil separates.
Stir in the sugar, salt and lime juice, return the eggs and coat for 2 minutes until heated through.
Serve with the rice and spoon over the sambal.

notes: Food safety: boil the eggs until fully set and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Padang. Lunch. Gluten-free.

title: Nyonya Ayam Pongteh Braised Chicken
summary: A Melaka Nyonya braise of chicken and potato with fermented black beans and palm sugar, rich but not spicy.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and fry the shallot and garlic for 4 minutes until golden and fragrant.
Add the black beans, palm sugar and dark soy and stir for 1 minute until bubbling.
Add the chicken and brown for 5 minutes, then pour in the water and add the potato. Cover and simmer for 30 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the potato is tender.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy. Uncover the pot for the last 5 minutes if you want the sauce thicker.
Serve the chicken with the sauce over the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until the juices run clear and it reaches 75C; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Nyonya. Dinner.

title: Visayan Pork Humba
summary: A Visayan braise of pork belly in soy, vinegar and brown sugar with star anise and bay, until sticky and tender.

steps.text: Brown the pork belly in the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat for 8 minutes until golden on all sides.
Add the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, garlic, bay, star anise, pepper and water. Bring to the boil, then cover and simmer gently for 55 minutes until the pork is fork-tender.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Uncover and simmer for 10 minutes until the sauce reduces to a sticky glaze that coats the pork.
Serve the pork and sauce spooned over the rice.

notes: Food safety: simmer the pork until tender and cooked through; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Visayan. Dinner.

title: Kerala Beef Ularthiyathu Dry Roast
summary: Kerala's slow-cooked dry beef roast with coconut slivers, curry leaf and black pepper, fried to a dark, spicy finish.

steps.text: Put the beef in a pot with the ginger garlic paste, coriander, turmeric, chilli powder, 1 tsp salt and the water. Cover and simmer for 45 minutes until the beef is tender and the liquid has reduced to a thick coating.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and fry the coconut for 3 minutes until golden. Lift out with a slotted spoon.
Fry the onion in the same oil for 8 minutes until deep golden, then add the curry leaf and black pepper for 30 seconds until crackling.
Add the beef with its sauce and the garam masala and stir-fry over medium-high heat for 10 minutes until dark, dry and glossy. Fold in the toasted coconut.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, and serve with the beef.

notes: Food safety: simmer the beef until tender and cooked through and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Kerala. Dinner. Gluten-free.

title: Goan Chicken Xacuti
summary: Goa's complex coconut and toasted spice curry, built on a paste of dry-roasted coriander and whole spices.

items.raw: 900g chicken thigh, cut in large pieces

steps.text: Dry-roast the coconut in a pan over medium heat for 4 minutes until deep golden, then tip out. Roast the coriander, cumin, fennel, chilli, cinnamon, cloves and pepper for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Grind the roasted spices, coconut, half the onion and the garlic with 1/2 cup water to a smooth paste.
Fry the remaining onion in the oil for 8 minutes until golden, add the turmeric and the paste and cook for 8 minutes until the oil separates.
Add the chicken, tamarind, 1 tsp salt and the remaining water. Cover and simmer for 25 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce is thick.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then serve with the curry.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until the juices run clear and it reaches 75C; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Goa. Dinner. Gluten-free.

title: Bengali Shorshe Maach Mustard Fish Curry
summary: Bengal's pungent mustard fish: firm white fish in a sharp mustard seed and green chilli gravy cooked in mustard oil.

items.raw: 600g white fish fillet, cut in large pieces

steps.text: Soak the mustard seed in 1/4 cup warm water for 10 minutes, then blend with 1 green chilli and a pinch of salt to a smooth paste.
Rub the fish with turmeric and salt. Heat 1 tbsp mustard oil in a pan until smoking, and sear the fish for 1 minute each side until just coloured, then lift out.
Add the remaining oil, cumin and the mustard paste and fry for 2 minutes until fragrant. Add the water and 2 slit green chillies and simmer for 5 minutes.
Return the fish and simmer gently for 6 minutes until opaque and cooked through.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, and serve with the fish and gravy.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, and eat the same day; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Bengal. Dinner. Gluten-free.

title: Samoan Sapasui Glass Noodles with Beef
summary: Samoan sapasui: slippery glass noodles stir-braised with beef, carrot, garlic and ginger in a soy sauce.

steps.text: Soak the glass noodles in hot water for 10 minutes until pliable, then drain and cut into shorter lengths.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the beef for 3 minutes until browned with no pink. Lift out.
Fry the onion, carrot, garlic and ginger for 3 minutes until fragrant and softened.
Add the stock, soy sauce and oyster sauce and bring to the boil, then add the noodles and toss for 4 minutes until they absorb the sauce and turn translucent.
Return the beef, fold in the spring onion for 1 minute until wilted, and serve hot.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef through and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Samoa. Dinner.

title: Ethiopian Awaze Beef Tibs with Peppers
summary: Quick-seared Ethiopian beef tibs with onion, capsicum and a spiced awaze-style chilli paste, served with rice.

steps.text: Mix the chilli powder, paprika, cardamom, cumin, 1/2 tsp salt and the water into a thin spice paste.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Melt the butter in a large pan over high heat and sear the beef in two batches for 3 minutes each until browned outside. Lift out.
Fry the onion for 5 minutes until golden, then add the garlic, ginger, capsicum and jalapeño for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in the spice paste for 1 minute, return the beef and toss for 2 minutes until coated and hot through. Serve with the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef until browned all over and the centre reaches at least 63°C, resting it briefly.
Ethiopia. Dinner. Gluten-free.

title: Cape Malay Denningvleis Tamarind Lamb
summary: A slow-cooked Cape Malay lamb stew sweet and sour with tamarind, bay and allspice, falling apart over yellow rice.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat for 8 minutes in batches until deeply coloured. Lift out.
Cook the onion in the same pot for 6 minutes until soft and golden, then add the garlic, allspice and cinnamon for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return the lamb with the tamarind, sugar, bay, 1 tsp salt and water. Cover and simmer gently for 90 minutes until the lamb is very tender and the sauce thick.
Cook the rice with the turmeric and sultana by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Serve the lamb and sauce over the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the lamb until tender and at least 75°C in the centre; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Cape Malay. Dinner. Gluten-free.

title: Fijian Coconut Curry Fish with Pumpkin
summary: Fijian-style fish in a gentle turmeric coconut curry with pumpkin and a little heat, served with rice.

items.raw: 600g white fish fillet, cut in chunks

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, ginger, curry powder and turmeric and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the coconut milk, add the pumpkin and chilli, and simmer for 12 minutes until the pumpkin is tender.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Nestle in the fish and simmer for 5 minutes until opaque and flaking. Squeeze over the lime and season with salt.
Serve the curry over the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flakes easily, to at least 63°C, and eat the same day.
Fiji. Dinner. Gluten-free.

title: Samaki wa Kupaka Swahili Grilled Fish in Coconut Tamarind
summary: Coastal Swahili fish grilled and coated in a coconut, tamarind and cumin sauce, with coconut-flavoured rice.

steps.text: Season the fish with turmeric and salt. Cook the rice with the extra 1/2 cup coconut milk and water by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium-high heat and cook the fish for 3 minutes each side until golden and just cooked. Lift onto a tray.
In the same pan, fry the garlic, cumin, coriander and chilli for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the coconut milk and tamarind and simmer for 6 minutes until slightly thick.
Return the fish and spoon over the sauce for 2 minutes until heated through.
Serve with the rice and lime wedges.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until it flakes easily and reaches 63°C; eat the same day.
Swahili coast. Dinner. Gluten-free.

title: Sri Lankan Devilled Chicken
summary: Sri Lankan style devilled chicken: crisp fried pieces tossed in a sweet, sour and chilli sauce with capsicum and onion.

items.raw: 700g chicken thigh, cut in bite-size pieces

steps.text: Toss the chicken with the cornflour, egg and a pinch of salt. Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 170C and fry the chicken in batches for 5 minutes until golden and cooked through. Drain on paper.
Pour off all but 1 tbsp of oil. Stir-fry the onion and capsicum for 3 minutes until just tender but still bright.
Add the garlic, ginger and chilli flakes for 30 seconds until fragrant, then the tomato sauce, sweet chilli sauce, soy and vinegar. Simmer for 2 minutes until glossy.
Toss the chicken through the sauce for 1 minute until coated and serve over the rice.

notes: Food safety: fry the chicken until golden and cooked through to at least 75°C, and keep the eggs fully cooked.
Sri Lanka. Dinner.

title: Sri Lankan Ambul Thiyal Sour Fish Curry
summary: Southern Sri Lankan sour fish curry, dry-cooked with black pepper and goraka-style tamarind until dark and sticky.

items.raw: 600g white fish fillet, cut in 3cm cubes

steps.text: Mix the tamarind, pepper, turmeric, garlic, ginger and salt into a paste and coat the fish in it.
Put the tuna in a wide pan with the curry leaf, cinnamon stick, coconut oil and water.
Cover and simmer over low heat for 12 minutes until the fish is cooked through and the liquid is almost gone.
Uncover and cook for 5 minutes, stirring gently, until the pieces are dark, dry and coated.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, and serve with the fish.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until it reaches 63°C in the thickest part; eat the same day.
Sri Lanka. Dinner. Gluten-free.

title: Dak Bokkeumtang Korean Braised Chicken and Potatoes
summary: Korean spicy braised chicken with potato and carrot in a gochujang and soy sauce that turns sticky and glossy.

steps.text: Mix the gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, honey, garlic and sesame oil in a large pot, then stir in the water.
Add the chicken and bring to the boil, then cover and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the potato, carrot and onion, cover and simmer for 15 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Uncover and cook on medium-high for 8 minutes until the sauce is thick and glossy and the chicken is cooked through.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then serve the chicken and sauce over it.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until the juices run clear and it reaches 75°C.
Korea. Dinner.

title: Khua Kling Southern Thai Dry Pork Curry
summary: Fiery dry-fried southern Thai pork with turmeric, lemongrass and makrut lime leaf, served with rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat and fry the curry paste, turmeric, lemongrass and garlic for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the pork and stir-fry over high heat for 8 minutes, breaking it up, until fully cooked and dry with no liquid left.
Add the fish sauce, palm sugar, chilli and lime leaf and stir for 2 minutes until the pork is dark and aromatic.
Serve with the rice and cucumber slices.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork mince until it reaches 75°C and no pink remains.
Southern Thailand. Dinner. Gluten-free.

title: Bo Kho Vietnamese Beef Stew with Carrot
summary: Vietnamese lemongrass beef stew with star anise, carrot and tomato, thick with annatto-coloured sauce, eaten with.

steps.text: Warm the oil with the annatto seed in a small pan for 1 minute until the oil turns orange, then strain and discard the seed.
Brown the beef in the orange oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat for 8 minutes until coloured. Add the shallot and garlic for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomato paste, lemongrass, star anise, cinnamon, fish sauce and water. Cover and simmer gently for 80 minutes until the beef is tender.
Add the carrot and simmer uncovered for 20 minutes until the carrot is soft and the sauce thick.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy. Serve the stew over the rice with coriander.

notes: Food safety: simmer the beef until tender and at least 75°C in the centre; cool and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Vietnam. Dinner. Gluten-free.

title: Ayam Bakar Taliwang Lombok Grilled Chicken
summary: Lombok chilli-garlic chicken roasted until charred, brushed with a spicy sweet sambal and served with rice.

steps.text: Blend the chillies, shallot, garlic, tomato and shrimp paste to a coarse paste. Fry in the oil in a pan for 10 minutes until darkened and the oil separates.
Stir in the kecap manis, palm sugar, lime juice and 1 tsp salt, then cool slightly.
Toss the chicken in half the sambal and roast on a tray at 200C for 30 minutes, turning once, until deep brown and cooked through.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Brush the chicken with the remaining sambal and grill for 3 minutes until charred at the edges, then serve with the rice.

notes: Food safety: roast the chicken until it reaches 75°C at the thickest part and the juices run clear.
Lombok. Dinner.

title: Ikan Bakar Malaysian Foil-Baked Fish with Sambal
summary: Malaysian banana-leaf-style fish baked in foil with a chilli, lemongrass and shrimp paste sambal, served with rice.

steps.text: Blend the chillies, shallot, garlic, lemongrass, shrimp paste and tamarind to a paste. Fry in the oil for 6 minutes until darkened and fragrant, then add the palm sugar and 1/2 tsp salt.
Spread the sambal over both sides of each fish fillet and wrap each in foil, sealing the edges.
Bake the parcels at 200C for 15 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Open the parcels and finish under the grill for 3 minutes until the sambal caramelises. Serve with the rice, cucumber and lime.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until it reaches 63°C and flakes easily; eat the same day.
Malaysia. Dinner. Gluten-free.

title: Oxtail Kare-Kare Filipino Peanut Stew
summary: Filipino oxtail stew in a rich peanut sauce with green beans and eggplant, traditionally served with a salty.

steps.text: Simmer the oxtail in the water for 2 hours, skimming, until the meat is tender and pulls from the bone. Lift out and keep 3 cups of the broth.
Warm the oil with the annatto seed for 1 minute until the oil turns orange, then strain out the seed. Cook the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes until soft.
Whisk in the peanut butter and the reserved broth and simmer for 15 minutes until thick and glossy, seasoning with the fish sauce.
Add the oxtail, eggplant and green beans and simmer for 10 minutes until tender, adding the bok choy for the final 2 minutes until wilted.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy. Serve with the stew and shrimp paste on the side.

notes: Food safety: simmer the oxtail until tender and at least 75°C throughout; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Visayan and Luzon tradition. Dinner. Gluten-free.

title: Rajasthani Laal Maas Fiery Lamb
summary: A Rajasthani fiery red lamb curry cooked in ghee with Kashmiri chilli, garlic and yoghurt, hot but richly flavoured.

steps.text: Soak the dried chillies in hot water for 15 minutes, then blend with the garlic and Kashmiri chilli powder to a smooth paste.
Heat the ghee in a heavy pot over medium heat and fry the cumin seed, coriander seed, cardamom, bay and cinnamon for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the onion and cook for 10 minutes until deep golden.
Add the lamb and brown for 8 minutes, then stir in the chilli paste for 3 minutes until the oil rises. Whisk in the yoghurt gradually so it does not split.
Add the water and 1 tsp salt, cover and simmer for 75 minutes until the lamb is very tender and the sauce is thick and red.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, and serve with the lamb.

notes: Food safety: cook the lamb until tender and at least 75°C in the centre; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Rajasthan. Dinner. Gluten-free.

title: Hawaiian Loco Moco Rice Bowls
summary: Hawaiian loco moco: rice topped with a beef patty, a runny fried egg and onion gravy.

steps.text: Mix the beef mince with the egg, breadcrumbs and 1/2 tsp salt, shape into 4 patties. Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Fry the patties in a pan over medium heat for 5 minutes each side until browned and cooked through. Rest them on a plate.
Cook the onion in 1 tbsp butter for 6 minutes until golden. Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the stock and soy sauce and simmer for 4 minutes until it thickens into gravy.
Fry the 4 eggs in the remaining butter for 3 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks stay soft.
Pile rice into bowls, add a patty, an egg, spoon over the gravy and scatter with spring onion.

notes: Food safety: cook the patties until they reach 75°C in the centre; cook the egg whites firm. Avoid soft yolks for vulnerable eaters.
Hawaii. Lunch.

title: Meen Pollichathu Kerala Pan-Roasted Fish
summary: Kerala fish smothered in a shallot, tomato and curry leaf masala and roasted in baking paper parcels.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Heat the coconut oil in a pan over medium heat and fry the shallots, ginger, garlic and curry leaf for 6 minutes until golden and soft.
Add the turmeric, chilli, coriander and tomatoes and cook for 8 minutes until the masala is thick and the oil separates, then stir in the tamarind.
Spread half the masala over four sheets of baking paper, lay a fish fillet on each, top with the remaining masala and fold into sealed parcels.
Bake the parcels at 200°C for 14 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily, then open and serve over the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and the thickest part reaches 63°C.
Kerala. Dinner. Naturally gluten-free.

title: Chicken Chettinad Black Pepper Curry
summary: Tamil Nadu chicken curry with freshly ground pepper, fennel and coconut for a deep, dry-spiced heat.

items.raw: 800g chicken thigh fillets, cut in chunks

steps.text: Toast the peppercorns, fennel and desiccated coconut in a dry pan for 2 minutes until fragrant, then grind them to a coarse paste with a splash of water.
Heat the oil in a deep pan and cook the onion and curry leaf for 10 minutes until deeply golden.
Add the ginger, garlic, cumin, coriander and turmeric and stir for 1 minute until fragrant, then add the tomatoes and cook for 6 minutes until jammy.
Stir in the chicken and the pepper paste and cook for 20 minutes with a splash of water until the chicken is tender and the sauce clings.
Cook the rice by your usual method until fluffy and serve the curry over it.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until the centre reaches 75°C with no pink.
Tamil Nadu. Dinner.

title: Kerala Nadan Egg Roast with Rice
summary: Boiled eggs coated in a sweet-onion, tomato and black pepper masala, a classic Kerala home dinner.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes until the yolks are set, then cool them in cold water and peel.
Heat the coconut oil in a wide pan and cook the onion and curry leaf for 12 minutes until soft and golden brown.
Stir in the ginger, garlic, turmeric, chilli and coriander for 1 minute, then add the tomatoes and cook for 8 minutes until thick and oily.
Add a splash of water and the garam masala, then slide in the eggs and roll them for 3 minutes until coated and hot.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy and serve with the eggs.

notes: Food safety: boil the eggs until the yolks are firm and keep leftovers refrigerated for up to 2 days.
Kerala. Dinner. Naturally gluten-free.

title: Jjimdak Andong Braised Chicken with Sweet Potato Noodles
summary: Andong-style soy-braised chicken with potato, carrot and chewy glass noodles in a sweet, savoury glaze.

steps.text: Soak the noodles in warm water for 30 minutes, and blanch the chicken in boiling water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Combine the soy sauce, sugar, ginger, garlic and 2 cups of water in a large pot and bring to a simmer until the sugar dissolves.
Add the chicken, potato, carrot and onion and simmer covered for 25 minutes until the chicken is cooked and the vegetables are tender.
Drain the noodles, stir them in with the sesame oil and chillies and simmer 5 minutes until the noodles are soft and the sauce is glossy.
Top with the spring onion and serve hot.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until the thickest part reaches 75°C and the juices run clear.
Andong, Korea. Dinner.

title: Galbi Jjim Korean Braised Short Ribs
summary: Slow-braised beef short ribs with daikon, carrot and jujube in a sweet soy and pear glaze.

items.raw: 1.2 kg beef short ribs, cut in pieces

steps.text: Soak the ribs in cold water for 1 hour, then blanch them in boiling water for 8 minutes and rinse off the scum.
Mix the pear, soy sauce, sugar, ginger, garlic and half the sesame oil with 2 cups of water in a heavy pot.
Add the ribs and onion and simmer covered on low for 1 hour 30 minutes until the meat is nearly tender.
Add the daikon and carrot and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes until the vegetables are tender and the sauce thickens to a glaze.
Cook the rice by your usual method until fluffy, then serve the ribs over it with the spring onion and remaining sesame oil.

notes: Food safety: braise the beef until it reaches at least 75°C and falls tender from the bone.
Korea. Dinner. Festive dish.

title: Buta no Kakuni Japanese Braised Pork Belly
summary: Pork belly simmered until meltingly tender in soy, mirin and ginger, served with soft eggs and rice.

steps.text: Simmer the whole belly in plenty of water for 1 hour 15 minutes until a skewer slides in easily, then cool and cut in 4 cm cubes.
Combine the soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, ginger and spring onion with 1 cup of water in a pot and add the pork.
Simmer covered on low for 45 minutes until the pork is very tender, then boil the eggs for 7 minutes until just set, peel and add them for the last 10 minutes.
Cook the rice by your usual method until fluffy, and steam the bok choy for 3 minutes until tender.
Reduce the braising liquid for 5 minutes until syrupy, then serve the pork and halved eggs over the rice with the glaze.

notes: Food safety: simmer the pork until it reaches 75°C throughout and keep leftovers refrigerated.
Japan. Dinner.

title: Sake Shioyaki Salt-Grilled Salmon Rice Plates
summary: Crisp salt-grilled salmon with grated daikon, lemon and rice, a Japanese home dinner in 25 minutes.

steps.text: Salt the salmon on both sides and leave for 10 minutes, then pat dry.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Toss the cucumber with the vinegar and sesame seeds for a quick pickle.
Grill the salmon skin side up under a hot grill for 8 minutes until the skin blisters and the flesh flakes.
Serve the fish with the rice, a mound of grated daikon, the cucumber and lemon wedges.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until it flakes and reaches 63°C; use only very fresh fish.
Japan. Dinner. Naturally gluten-free.

title: Tebasaki Nagoya Sticky Pepper Chicken Wings
summary: Twice-cooked Nagoya wings with a sweet soy glaze and plenty of black pepper and sesame, served with rice.

steps.text: Toss the wings with the cornflour and a pinch of salt, brush with the oil and spread on a lined tray.
Bake at 220°C for 35 minutes, turning once, until the skin is crisp and the wings are cooked through.
Simmer the soy sauce, mirin, sugar and garlic for 4 minutes until syrupy.
Toss the hot wings in the glaze with the pepper and sesame seeds until coated.
Cook the rice by your usual method until fluffy and serve the wings with it.

notes: Food safety: cook the wings until the thickest part reaches 75°C and the juices run clear.
Nagoya, Japan. Dinner.

title: Hambagu Japanese Hamburg Steak with Demi Sauce
summary: Juicy Japanese-style hamburg steaks in a ketchup, Worcestershire and mushroom sauce, served with rice.

steps.text: Soften the onion in half the oil for 5 minutes until translucent, then cool.
Mix the beef, onion, panko, egg, milk, nutmeg and a pinch of salt, knead until sticky and shape into four oval patties.
Fry the patties in the remaining oil for 4 minutes per side until browned and cooked through at 75°C, then lift out.
Fry the mushrooms in the same pan for 4 minutes until golden, add the ketchup, Worcestershire, soy sauce and 1/2 cup of water and simmer until thick.
Cook the rice by your usual method until fluffy and serve the patties with the sauce.

notes: Food safety: cook the mince patties until the centre reaches 75°C with no pink remaining.
Japan. Dinner.

title: Moo Ping Bangkok Coconut Pork Street Plates
summary: Coconut and coriander-root marinated pork skewers grilled until caramelised and served with sticky rice.

steps.text: Crush the garlic and coriander root, then mix with the oyster sauce, fish sauce, sugar, coconut milk and pepper and coat the pork. Marinate 2 hours.
Soak the rice for 2 hours, then steam it over simmering water for 25 minutes until tender and sticky.
Thread the pork onto skewers.
Grill over medium-high heat for 12 minutes, turning, until browned at the edges and cooked through.
Serve the skewers with the sticky rice, cucumber and chilli.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork until the centre reaches 75°C with no pink remaining.
Thailand. Dinner.

title: Pad Kra Pao Gai Thai Basil Chicken with Fried Egg
summary: Hot and savoury minced chicken stir-fried with chilli, garlic and basil, topped with a crisp fried egg.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat and fry the garlic and chilli for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the chicken and beans and stir-fry for 5 minutes until cooked through and lightly browned.
Add the oyster sauce, soy, fish sauce and sugar and toss for 1 minute until glossy, then fold through the basil until just wilted.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil until the whites are crisp and the yolks are cooked to your liking, then serve over the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken mince to 75°C and fry the eggs until the whites are fully set.
Thailand. Dinner.

title: Phuket Dry-Fried Beef Mince Curry with Turmeric
summary: Fiery southern Thai dry-fried beef with turmeric, lemongrass and kaffir lime, served with rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until fluffy.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and fry the curry paste, turmeric, lemongrass and ginger for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the beef and stir-fry for 8 minutes, breaking it up, until cooked through and the pan is nearly dry.
Season with the fish sauce and sugar and toss through the lime leaves and chilli for 1 minute until the leaves are bright.
Serve with the rice and cucumber.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef mince until it reaches 75°C with no pink remaining.
Southern Thailand. Dinner.

title: Thai Lime Steamed Fish Plates with Lemongrass
summary: Tender steamed fish in a hot, sour lime, garlic and chilli broth, served over jasmine rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Lay the lemongrass and lime leaves on a heatproof plate, top with the fish and steam over simmering water for 10 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes.
Stir the lime juice, fish sauce, sugar, garlic and chilli together until the sugar dissolves.
Pour the sauce over the hot fish, scatter with the coriander and steam for 1 minute more until the aromatics are fragrant.
Serve the fish and its juices over the rice.

notes: Food safety: steam the fish until it reaches 63°C and flakes easily.
Thailand. Dinner. Naturally gluten-free.

title: Ca Kho To Vietnamese Caramel-Braised Fish
summary: Firm white fish braised in a dark caramel, fish sauce and pepper sauce, a southern Vietnamese staple.

items.raw: 4 firm white fish fillets, cut in thick pieces

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until fluffy.
Melt the sugar in a heavy pot with 2 tbsp of water over medium heat for 5 minutes until it turns deep amber.
Add the shallot, garlic and ginger for 1 minute, then pour in the fish sauce, 1/2 cup of water and the pepper.
Lay in the fish and simmer for 10 minutes, spooning the sauce over, until the fish is cooked and the sauce is thick and glossy.
Scatter with the chilli and spring onion and serve with the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until it reaches 63°C and flakes easily.
Vietnam. Dinner. Naturally gluten-free.

title: Thit Kho Trung Vietnamese Braised Pork and Eggs
summary: Pork belly and eggs braised in caramel and fish sauce, the Tet table favourite, with rice.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 7 minutes until just set, then cool and peel.
Caramelise the sugar in a heavy pot over medium heat for 4 minutes until amber, then add the pork, shallots and garlic and stir for 5 minutes until coated and lightly browned.
Add the fish sauce, pepper and water and simmer covered for 45 minutes until the pork is tender.
Add the eggs and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes until the sauce is thick and the eggs are glazed.
Cook the rice by your usual method until fluffy and serve with the spring onion.

notes: Food safety: braise the pork until it reaches 75°C and is tender; boil the eggs until the yolk is firm.
Vietnam. Dinner. Naturally gluten-free.

title: Lamb Kaldereta Filipino Tomato and Peanut Stew
summary: Filipino festive stew of lamb with tomato, capsicum, olives and peanut butter, simmered until rich.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil in batches for 8 minutes until deep golden, then set aside.
Cook the onion and garlic in the same pot for 5 minutes until soft, then stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, bay leaves, chilli, lamb and 1 cup of water and simmer covered for 1 hour 15 minutes until the lamb is nearly tender.
Add the potato and carrot and cook 25 minutes until tender, then stir in the capsicum, olives and peanut butter and simmer 5 minutes until thick.
Taste, season and serve hot.

notes: Food safety: cook the lamb until it reaches at least 75°C and is tender.
Philippines. Dinner. Contains peanuts. Naturally gluten-free.

title: Bicol Express Pork in Chilli Coconut Cream
summary: Pork simmered in coconut cream with long green chillies and shrimp paste, the fiery dish of the Bicol region.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and cook the onion, garlic and ginger for 5 minutes until soft, then stir in the shrimp paste for 1 minute.
Add the pork and brown for 6 minutes, then pour in the coconut cream and fish sauce.
Simmer gently for 30 minutes until the pork is tender and the cream reduces and turns oily.
Stir in the chillies and cook 3 minutes until tender, then serve over the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork until it reaches 75°C throughout and is tender.
Bicol, Philippines. Dinner. Naturally gluten-free.

title: Beef Salpicao Filipino Garlic Beef with Rice
summary: Seared beef cubes with lots of garlic, mushrooms, soy and Worcestershire, served over garlic rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until fluffy.
Toss the beef with the soy sauce, Worcestershire and pepper.
Sear the beef in the oil over high heat in two batches for 3 minutes until browned and just cooked through, then set aside.
Melt the butter and fry the garlic for 2 minutes until golden, add the mushrooms and cook 4 minutes until tender, then return the beef with its juices.
Toss for 1 minute until glossy and serve over the rice with the spring onion.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef cubes until browned all over and the centre reaches at least 63°C.
Philippines. Dinner.

title: Lechon Kawali Crispy Pork Belly with Vinegar Dip
summary: Pork belly simmered with bay and peppercorns, dried and deep-fried until blistered, with a sharp vinegar dip.

steps.text: Simmer the pork with the bay, peppercorns, salt and onion in water for 1 hour 15 minutes until tender, then lift out, pat very dry and chill uncovered for 2 hours.
Cook the rice by your usual method until fluffy.
Mix the vinegar, red onion, garlic, chilli and a pinch of salt for the dip.
Heat the oil to 180°C in a deep heavy pot and carefully fry the pork skin side down for 10 minutes, covered with a splatter guard, until the skin blisters and turns golden.
Rest 5 minutes, chop into pieces and serve with the rice and dip.

notes: Food safety: simmer the pork until it reaches 75°C; keep water away from hot oil and never leave it unattended.
Philippines. Dinner. Naturally gluten-free.

title: Pininyahang Manok Filipino Chicken in Pineapple and Milk
summary: Chicken braised with pineapple, carrot, capsicum and evaporated milk into a gently sweet, creamy stew.

items.raw: 800g chicken thigh fillets, cut in chunks

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until fluffy.
Brown the chicken in the oil for 6 minutes, then add the onion and garlic and cook 3 minutes until soft.
Add the fish sauce, water, pineapple and carrot and simmer covered for 20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the carrot is tender.
Stir in the capsicum and evaporated milk and simmer gently 5 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Taste the sauce, adjust with a little fish sauce if needed, then spoon the chicken and creamy sauce over the rice and serve.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until the centre reaches 75°C with no pink.
Philippines. Dinner.

title: Adobong Pusit Filipino Squid Adobo
summary: Tender squid simmered quickly in vinegar, soy, garlic and pepper, served with rice to catch the sauce.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until fluffy.
Fry the garlic and onion in the oil for 4 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the vinegar, soy sauce, bay, peppercorns and sugar and simmer 3 minutes without stirring until the sharp smell mellows.
Add the squid and cook for 6 minutes until just tender and curled, then reduce the sauce for 3 minutes until it clings.
Serve the squid and sauce over the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the squid until opaque and firm and use only fresh, well-chilled squid.
Philippines. Dinner.

title: Semur Daging Javanese Sweet Soy Beef Stew
summary: Beef and potato braised in sweet soy with nutmeg, clove and cinnamon, a gentle Javanese-Dutch home dish.

steps.text: Brown the beef in the oil in batches for 6 minutes until golden, then set aside.
Cook the onion and garlic in the same pot for 5 minutes until soft, then add the nutmeg, cloves and cinnamon for 30 seconds.
Return the beef with the kecap manis, soy sauce, tomatoes and water and simmer covered for 1 hour until the beef is nearly tender.
Add the potato and cook 25 minutes until tender and the sauce is thick and glossy.
Cook the rice by your usual method until fluffy and serve the stew over it.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef until tender and at least 75°C throughout.
Java, Indonesia. Dinner.

title: Gulai Kambing Sumatran Lamb Curry
summary: Lamb simmered in a turmeric, lemongrass and coconut milk gravy, rich and aromatic, from Sumatra.

steps.text: Blend the shallots, garlic, ginger, turmeric, coriander and cumin to a paste with a splash of water.
Fry the paste in the oil for 6 minutes until fragrant and the oil separates, then add the lamb and brown for 6 minutes.
