Add the coconut milk, 1 cup of water, lemongrass, lime leaves and chilli and simmer covered for 1 hour 15 minutes until the lamb is tender.
Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes until the gravy thickens slightly.
Cook the rice by your usual method until fluffy and serve the curry over it.

notes: Food safety: cook the lamb until at least 75°C throughout and tender.
Sumatra, Indonesia. Dinner. Naturally gluten-free.

title: Ayam Betutu Balinese Spiced Roast Chicken
summary: Chicken rubbed with the Balinese base genep spice paste and slow roasted in a sealed foil parcel until falling tender.

steps.text: Blend the shallots, garlic, chilli, ginger, galangal, turmeric, lemongrass, pepper, shrimp paste and oil to a thick paste.
Rub the paste all over the chicken and marinate in the fridge for 2 hours.
Wrap the chicken and all the paste in a sealed double layer of foil on a tray and roast at 160°C for 1 hour 30 minutes until the meat is very tender.
Open the parcel and roast at 220°C for 15 minutes until the skin is browned and sticky.
Cook the rice by your usual method until fluffy and serve the chicken with its juices.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until the thickest part reaches 75°C and the juices run clear.
Bali, Indonesia. Dinner. Naturally gluten-free.

title: Pepes Ikan Sundanese Spiced Fish Parcels
summary: Fish in a turmeric, lemongrass and chilli paste steamed in baking paper parcels, the Sundanese way.

steps.text: Blend the shallots, garlic, chilli, turmeric, ginger, half the lemongrass, oil and salt to a coarse paste.
Cook the rice by your usual method until fluffy.
Coat each fillet in the paste and place on a sheet of baking paper with the tomato, basil, remaining lemongrass and lime juice, then fold into sealed parcels.
Bake at 200°C for 18 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Open the parcels and serve over the rice with the juices.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and the thickest part reaches 63°C.
West Java, Indonesia. Dinner. Naturally gluten-free.

title: Ayam Rica-Rica Manado Chilli Chicken
summary: North Sulawesi chicken fried with a big chilli, lemongrass and basil paste until sticky and fiery.

items.raw: 800g chicken thigh fillets, cut in chunks

steps.text: Blend the chillies, shallots, garlic, ginger, lemongrass and tomatoes to a coarse paste.
Fry the paste in the oil for 10 minutes until the raw smell goes and the oil separates.
Add the chicken and 1/2 cup of water and simmer covered for 20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce is thick.
Stir in the sugar, lime juice and basil until the basil wilts.
Cook the rice by your usual method until fluffy and serve with the chicken.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until the centre reaches 75°C with no pink.
Manado, Indonesia. Dinner. Naturally gluten-free.

title: Asam Pedas Melaka Sour and Spicy Fish Stew
summary: White fish and okra simmered in a tamarind, chilli and lemongrass gravy, a Melaka classic.

items.raw: 4 white fish fillets, in thick pieces

steps.text: Blend the shallots, garlic, dried chillies, ginger and turmeric to a smooth paste.
Fry the paste in the oil for 8 minutes until darker and fragrant, then add the lemongrass, tamarind, water and sugar and simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the tomato and okra and simmer for 5 minutes until the okra is tender.
Slide in the fish and cook gently for 8 minutes until opaque and cooked through.
Cook the rice by your usual method until fluffy and serve the stew over it.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until it reaches 63°C and flakes easily.
Melaka, Malaysia. Dinner. Naturally gluten-free.

title: Ayam Masak Merah Malaysian Tomato Chilli Chicken
summary: Fried chicken simmered in a sweet-hot tomato and chilli sauce, the Malay festive favourite.

items.raw: 800g chicken thigh fillets, cut in chunks

steps.text: Blend the dried chillies, shallots, garlic and ginger to a paste.
Brown the chicken with the turmeric in half the oil for 8 minutes until golden, then set aside.
Fry the chilli paste in the remaining oil for 8 minutes until fragrant, add the tomato paste and tinned tomatoes and cook 6 minutes until thick.
Return the chicken with the onion, sugar, tamarind and 1/2 cup of water and simmer 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and glossy.
Cook the rice by your usual method until fluffy and serve with the chicken.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until the centre reaches 75°C with no pink.
Malaysia. Dinner. Naturally gluten-free.

title: Mombasa Grilled Chicken in Coconut and Tamarind Gravy
summary: Mombasa-style grilled chicken simmered in a creamy coconut, tamarind and turmeric gravy.

steps.text: Rub the chicken with half the turmeric, a pinch of salt and half the garlic, then grill for 12 minutes until charred at the edges.
Fry the onion in the oil for 8 minutes until golden, add the ginger, remaining garlic, spices and chilli and cook 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and cook 5 minutes until soft, then pour in the coconut milk and tamarind.
Add the chicken and simmer for 15 minutes until cooked through and the sauce is creamy.
Cook the rice by your usual method until fluffy and serve with the curry and coriander.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until the centre reaches 75°C with no pink.
Kenya. Dinner. Naturally gluten-free.

title: Doro Wat Ethiopian Chicken and Egg Stew
summary: Ethiopia's celebration stew of slowly cooked onions, berbere and spiced butter with tender chicken and boiled eggs.

steps.text: Cook the onions in a dry heavy pot over medium heat for 20 minutes, stirring often, until they reduce and turn sweet and golden.
Add the butter, ginger, garlic, berbere and tomato paste and cook for 15 minutes on low until a deep red paste forms.
Add the wine, stock and chicken and simmer covered for 40 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Boil the eggs for 8 minutes until set, peel, prick lightly and simmer in the stew for the last 10 minutes.
Cook the rice by your usual method until fluffy and serve with the stew.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until the thickest part reaches 75°C and the eggs until the yolks are firm.
Ethiopia. Dinner.

title: Zigni Eritrean Berbere Beef Stew
summary: Eritrean beef stew with onions, tomato and berbere cooked down until thick, dark and deeply spiced.

steps.text: Cook the onions in a dry heavy pot for 15 minutes, stirring often, until reduced and golden.
Add the butter, berbere, tomato paste, ginger and garlic and cook for 10 minutes on low until thick and dark.
Add the beef, stock and cardamom and simmer covered for 1 hour until the beef is nearly tender.
Add the potato and simmer for 25 minutes until tender and the sauce is thick.
Taste, season and serve hot.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef until at least 75°C throughout and tender.
Eritrea. Dinner. Naturally gluten-free.

title: Seared Kitfo-Style Beef with Chilli and Spiced Butter
summary: Fully cooked Ethiopian-style minced beef with spiced butter, mitmita and cardamom, served with rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until fluffy.
Melt the butter with the turmeric, cardamom, garlic and ginger over medium heat for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the onion and cook 4 minutes until soft, then stir in the beef and chilli and cook for 8 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Stir in the lemon juice and season.
Serve the beef with the rice and a spoonful of cottage cheese.

notes: Food safety: this version is fully cooked, so cook the mince until it reaches 75°C with no pink remaining.
Ethiopia. Dinner. Naturally gluten-free.

title: Luwombo Ugandan Chicken and Groundnut Parcels
summary: Chicken and mushrooms in a peanut sauce steamed in baking paper parcels, served with sweet potato.

items.raw: 800g chicken thigh fillets, cut in chunks

steps.text: Fry the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, then add the tomatoes and turmeric and cook 5 minutes until thick.
Whisk in the peanut butter and stock until smooth, then mix with the chicken and mushrooms.
Divide among four double sheets of baking paper, fold and tie into sealed parcels and set in a deep ovenproof dish with 2 cm of water.
Bake covered with foil at 170°C for 1 hour 15 minutes until the chicken is tender, adding the sweet potato in a separate tray for the last 40 minutes to roast until soft.
Open the parcels and serve with the sweet potato.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until the centre reaches 75°C with no pink.
Uganda. Dinner. Contains peanuts. Naturally gluten-free.

title: Frikkadelle South African Meatballs with Yellow Rice
summary: Spiced beef meatballs baked until golden and served with sweet turmeric and raisin yellow rice.

steps.text: Soak the bread in the milk, then mix the beef, onion, squeezed bread, egg, coriander, nutmeg and a pinch of salt and shape into 16 balls.
Bake the meatballs on an oiled tray at 200°C for 20 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Simmer the rice with the turmeric, raisins, cinnamon stick and 3 cups of water covered for 15 minutes until tender and fluffy.
Brush the meatballs with the chutney and bake 5 minutes until glossy.
Serve the meatballs over the yellow rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the meatballs until the centre reaches 75°C with no pink remaining.
South Africa. Dinner.

title: Huli Huli Hawaiian Pineapple-Glazed Chicken
summary: Hawaiian grilled chicken turned in a pineapple, soy and ginger glaze until sticky and caramelised.

steps.text: Whisk the pineapple juice, soy sauce, ketchup, sugar, ginger and garlic together and marinate the chicken for 2 hours, reserving a third of the mixture.
Cook the rice by your usual method until fluffy.
Simmer the reserved marinade for 6 minutes until syrupy.
Grill the chicken and pineapple for 18 minutes, turning and brushing with the glaze, until charred at the edges and cooked through.
Serve with the rice and spring onion.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until the thickest part reaches 75°C; boil any marinade that touched raw chicken before using it as a glaze.
Hawaii. Dinner.

title: Lu Pulu Tongan Beef in Coconut Cream
summary: Tongan beef and onion baked in coconut cream in a sealed parcel until soft and rich, served with kumara.

steps.text: Mix the beef with the onion, garlic, lemon juice and salt and place on a large double layer of baking paper over foil.
Pour over the coconut cream, fold and seal the parcel tightly and set it in a baking dish.
Bake at 160°C for 1 hour 45 minutes until the beef is very tender.
Add the sweet potato to a tray and roast at 200°C for 35 minutes until golden and soft, and wilt the silverbeet in the beef juices for 3 minutes until tender.
Serve the beef with the sweet potato and juices.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef until at least 75°C throughout and tender.
Tonga. Dinner. Naturally gluten-free.

title: Hong Shao Rou Shanghai Red-Braised Pork Belly
summary: Pork belly braised in caramel, soy and Shaoxing wine until glossy and soft, served with rice and greens.

steps.text: Blanch the pork in boiling water for 5 minutes, then drain and rinse.
Melt the sugar in a heavy pot with a splash of water over medium heat for 4 minutes until amber, add the pork and toss for 5 minutes until coated and lightly browned.
Add the wine, soy sauce, ginger, star anise, cinnamon, spring onion and water and simmer covered on low for 1 hour until the pork is tender.
Boil uncovered for 10 minutes until the sauce reduces to a sticky glaze.
Cook the rice by your usual method until fluffy, steam the bok choy for 3 minutes until tender and serve everything together.

notes: Food safety: braise the pork until it reaches 75°C and is tender.
Shanghai, China. Dinner.

title: Lion's Head Meatballs Yangzhou Pork and Cabbage
summary: Large soft pork and ginger meatballs braised on a bed of wombok until tender, a Jiangsu classic.

steps.text: Mix the pork, egg, ginger, spring onion, half the wine, half the soy sauce and the cornflour, stirring one way until sticky, and shape into four large balls.
Brown the meatballs in the oil for 6 minutes until golden, then set aside.
Layer the wombok in a pot, set the meatballs on top and add the stock, remaining wine and soy.
Cover and simmer gently for 35 minutes until the meatballs reach 75°C and the cabbage is silky.
Cook the rice by your usual method until fluffy and serve the meatballs with the cabbage and broth.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork meatballs until the centre reaches 75°C with no pink.
Yangzhou, China. Dinner.

title: Salt and Pepper Squid Cantonese-Style with Rice
summary: Crisp cornflour-coated squid tossed with chilli, garlic and Sichuan pepper salt, served with rice and greens.

items.raw: 600g squid tubes, scored and cut in pieces

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until fluffy.
Pat the squid very dry and toss in the cornflour mixed with the white pepper.
Heat the oil to 190°C in a wok and fry the squid in two batches for 90 seconds until crisp and pale golden, then drain.
Pour off most oil, stir-fry the chilli, garlic, spring onion, Sichuan pepper and salt for 1 minute until fragrant, then toss through the squid.
Blanch the gai lan for 2 minutes until tender and serve with the squid and rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the squid until opaque and firm and take care with hot oil.
Guangdong, China. Dinner. Gluten-free if you use cornflour labelled gluten-free.

title: Yu Xiang Qiezi Sichuan Fish-Fragrant Eggplant
summary: Silky fried eggplant in a garlicky, sour-sweet Sichuan chilli bean sauce, with no fish in sight.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until fluffy.
Fry the eggplant in half the oil in batches for 8 minutes until golden and soft, then set aside.
Stir-fry the chilli bean paste, ginger and garlic in the remaining oil for 1 minute until the oil turns red.
Add the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar and 1/2 cup of water, return the eggplant and simmer 4 minutes until tender.
Stir through the cornflour mixed with water until the sauce thickens and glazes, then top with the spring onion and serve with the rice.

notes: Vegan. Sichuan, China. Dinner.

title: Ojingeo Bokkeum Korean Spicy Stir-Fried Squid
summary: Squid and cabbage stir-fried in a sweet gochujang and gochugaru sauce, served over rice.

items.raw: 600g squid tubes, scored and cut in pieces

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until fluffy.
Mix the gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar and garlic into a sauce.
Stir-fry the onion, cabbage and carrot in the neutral oil over high heat for 4 minutes until just tender.
Add the squid and sauce and toss for 4 minutes until the squid is opaque and curled and the sauce clings.
Finish with the sesame oil and spring onion and serve over the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the squid until opaque and firm; do not overcook or it turns rubbery.
Korea. Dinner.

title: Char Siu Cantonese Roast Pork with Rice and Greens
summary: Sticky honey-hoisin roast pork scroll shoulder, sliced over rice with steamed greens.

items.raw: 700g pork scotch fillet, cut in strips

steps.text: Mix the hoisin, 1 tbsp honey, soy sauce, wine, garlic and five spice, coat the pork and marinate for 4 hours.
Roast the pork on a rack over a tray of water at 200°C for 35 minutes, basting twice, until sticky and browned.
Brush with the remaining honey and grill 3 minutes until charred at the edges.
Cook the rice by your usual method until fluffy and blanch the gai lan for 2 minutes until tender.
Rest the pork for 5 minutes, slice and serve with the rice, greens and pan juices.

notes: Food safety: roast the pork until the centre reaches 75°C with no pink.
Guangdong, China. Dinner.

title: Dau Hu Sot Ca Chua Vietnamese Tofu in Tomato Sauce
summary: Golden fried tofu simmered in a sweet, tangy tomato and spring onion sauce, served over jasmine rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat and fry the tofu for 8 minutes, turning, until golden on most sides, then lift out.
In the same pan fry the garlic and white spring onion for 1 minute until fragrant, add the tomatoes and cook for 6 minutes until they collapse into a sauce.
Stir in the soy sauce, sugar, salt and pepper, return the tofu and simmer for 4 minutes until the sauce clings, then scatter the green spring onion and serve over the rice.

notes: Naturally vegan. Serve with extra black pepper.

title: Com Ga Hoi An Turmeric Chicken Rice Plates
summary: Hoi An style shredded chicken on turmeric rice with a sharp onion and herb relish.

steps.text: Rinse the rice, then cook it with the turmeric, a pinch of salt and the right amount of water until tender and fluffy.
Poach the chicken in simmering water for 18 minutes until cooked through, then lift out, cool for a few minutes and shred.
Toss the sliced onion with the lime juice, 1 tbsp fish sauce and the sugar and leave it to soften while the chicken cooks.
Fry the garlic in the oil for 1 minute until golden, add the shredded chicken and the remaining fish sauce and stir for 2 minutes until hot and lightly coloured.
Pile the chicken over the rice and top with the onion relish, mint and coriander.

notes: Food safety: poach the chicken until the thickest part reaches 75°C, and wash hands and board after handling raw chicken.

title: Tahu Orek Javanese Sweet Soy Tofu
summary: Crisp tofu strips tossed in a sticky kecap manis, chilli and shallot glaze with green beans.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok over medium-high heat and fry the tofu for 9 minutes until deep golden and crisp, then lift out onto paper.
Add the remaining oil, fry the shallots, garlic and chilli for 2 minutes until soft, then add the beans and stir-fry for 3 minutes until bright and just tender.
Return the tofu with the kecap manis, tamarind and salt and toss for 2 minutes until glossy and sticky, then serve on the rice.

notes: Vegan if your kecap manis is. Check the label.

title: Laksa Lemak Tofu Puff Curry Noodles
summary: Rich coconut laksa paste noodles with fried tofu puffs, bean sprouts and lime, finished in one pot.

steps.text: Cover the vermicelli with boiling water for 5 minutes until just tender, drain and divide among four bowls.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and fry the laksa paste and shallots for 3 minutes until fragrant and the oil darkens.
Pour in the stock and coconut milk, add the sugar and simmer gently for 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Add the tofu puffs and simmer for 4 minutes until swollen and hot, then ladle over the noodles and top with sprouts, coriander and lime.

notes: Check the laksa paste for shrimp paste if you need it vegan.

title: Palak Paneer Spinach and Paneer Curry
summary: Silky spinach gravy with golden paneer cubes, spiced with cumin, garam masala and ginger.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 1 minute until bright green, drain, cool a little and blend to a coarse purée.
Heat 1 tbsp ghee in a pan, fry the paneer for 4 minutes until golden on each side, then lift out.
Add the remaining ghee, fry the onion for 6 minutes until golden, add garlic, ginger and spices for 1 minute, then the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the spinach, cream and salt, simmer for 5 minutes until thick, return the paneer and heat through before serving with the rice.

notes: Paneer is a fresh cheese and suits vegetarians.

title: Aloo Bodi Nepali Potato and Black-Eyed Pea Curry
summary: A tangy Nepali one-pot of potatoes, black-eyed peas and spinach with fenugreek and turmeric.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot until it shimmers, add the fenugreek seeds for 20 seconds, then the onion and fry for 6 minutes until golden.
Add the ginger, garlic and spices and stir for 1 minute, then the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until they break down.
Add the potatoes, peas, salt and 1 1/2 cups water, cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the potatoes are tender, then fold in the spinach for 2 minutes until wilted and the sauce is thick.

notes: Naturally vegan and gluten-free.

title: Githeri Kenyan Maize and Bean Stew
summary: A hearty Kenyan one-pot of maize and kidney beans cooked with tomato, onion and a little coriander.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat and fry the onion for 6 minutes until soft and golden.
Stir in the garlic and spices for 1 minute until fragrant, then the tomatoes and carrots and cook for 6 minutes until the tomatoes break down.
Add the beans, corn, stock and salt, cover and simmer for 18 minutes until the carrot is tender and the stew is thick.
Stir in half the coriander and serve scattered with the rest.

notes: Naturally vegan and gluten-free.

title: Hawaiian Chicken Long Rice Noodles
summary: Glass noodles simmered in ginger chicken broth with shiitake and spring onion, a Hawaiian luau favourite.

items.raw: 500g chicken thighs, boneless and skinless, sliced
6 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and sliced

steps.text: Soak the noodles in warm water for 10 minutes until pliable, drain and cut into shorter lengths.
Heat the oil in a wide pot, fry the ginger and garlic for 1 minute until fragrant, then add the chicken and cook for 5 minutes until no longer pink.
Add the stock, soy sauce, mushrooms and carrot and simmer for 8 minutes until the carrot is tender.
Add the noodles and cook for 4 minutes until clear and soft, then stir in the spring onions and serve in bowls.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C in the thickest piece, and wash hands and boards after handling raw chicken.

title: Tofu Steaks with Mushroom Soy Glaze
summary: Seared tofu slabs with a glossy mushroom, mirin and soy glaze over rice, a quick vegan Japanese dinner.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Pat the tofu dry, heat the oil in a wide pan and sear for 4 minutes each side until deep golden, then lift out.
Fry the mushrooms, ginger and garlic in the same pan for 4 minutes until browned and soft.
Mix the soy sauce, mirin, vinegar, cornflour and 1/4 cup water, pour it in and simmer for 2 minutes until glossy and thick.
Return the tofu, spoon the glaze over, and serve on rice with spring onions.

notes: Naturally vegan. Use tamari for gluten-free.

title: Yakisoba Japanese Festival Noodles
summary: Chewy noodles with cabbage, carrot and pork in a tangy sauce, finished with pickled ginger.

steps.text: Loosen the noodles under warm running water until separate and drain well.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the pork for 3 minutes until browned and cooked through, then lift out.
Add the remaining oil, stir-fry the onion, carrot and cabbage for 4 minutes until the cabbage is wilted and lightly charred.
Add the noodles and toss for 2 minutes, add the pork, sauces and sugar, and cook for 2 minutes until the noodles are glossy and hot.
Serve topped with pickled ginger.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork until it reaches 63°C in the thickest slice, then rest briefly. The pork should reach 75°C if you prefer it well done.

title: Rendang Cendawan Mushroom Curry
summary: Meaty mushrooms slow-cooked in a dry coconut and lemongrass rendang until it clings and darkens.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Blend the shallots, garlic, ginger and chillies into a paste, and tear the mushrooms into thick strips.
Fry the paste in the oil for 5 minutes until fragrant, add the spices and lemongrass and stir for 1 minute.
Add the mushrooms, coconut milk, tamarind and salt and simmer on low heat for 35 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce is thick, dark and almost dry.
Remove the lemongrass and serve with the rice.

notes: Naturally vegan and gluten-free.

title: Chongqing La Zi Ji Chilli Chicken Bites
summary: Crisp chicken pieces tossed with dried chillies and Sichuan pepper, with rice and cucumber on the side.

items.raw: 700g chicken thighs, boneless and skinless, cut into bite pieces
items.prep: boneless and skinless, cut into bite pieces

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Toss the chicken with the soy sauce, wine and cornflour until coated.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and fry the chicken in two batches for 5 minutes each until deep golden and cooked through, then lift out.
Pour off most of the oil, add the chillies and peppercorns and stir for 30 seconds until they darken and smell sharp.
Add the garlic, ginger and chicken with the sugar and toss for 2 minutes until coated, then serve with the rice and cucumber.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until the thickest piece reaches 75°C, and wash hands and boards after handling raw chicken.

title: Doubanjiang Braised Tofu Home Style
summary: Soft tofu simmered in chilli bean paste, garlic and spring onion, a quick Sichuan weeknight dish.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Simmer the tofu in salted water for 3 minutes until firm, then drain.
Fry the chilli bean paste, garlic and ginger in the oil for 2 minutes until the oil turns red and fragrant.
Add 1 cup water, the soy sauce and sugar, then the tofu, and simmer for 6 minutes until the sauce reduces.
Stir in the cornflour mixed with water, cook for 1 minute until glossy, scatter over the spring onions and serve with rice.

notes: Naturally vegan.

title: Salted Egg Yolk Prawns with Rice
summary: Crisp prawns coated in a buttery salted egg yolk sauce with curry leaves and chilli.

items.raw: 6 salted egg yolks, cooked and mashed

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Pat the prawns dry and toss in the cornflour until lightly coated.
Heat the oil in a wok and fry the prawns for 3 minutes until pink and crisp, then lift out.
Pour off the oil, melt the butter, add the mashed yolks and cook for 1 minute until foamy.
Add the garlic, chilli and curry leaves for 30 seconds, return the prawns and toss until coated, then serve on rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until opaque and pink, and eggs fully cooked to 75°C. Keep raw prawns chilled.

title: Gochujang Glazed Salmon with Sesame Spinach Rice
summary: Salmon fillets roasted under a sweet-hot gochujang glaze, served on sesame rice with wilted spinach.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Heat the oven to 200°C and line a tray. Mix the gochujang, soy sauce, honey and vinegar.
Brush the glaze over the salmon and roast for 12 minutes until the flesh flakes and the glaze bubbles.
Wilt the spinach in a pan with the sesame oil for 2 minutes until soft, stir through the rice with the sesame seeds and serve with the salmon.

notes: Food safety: cook the salmon until the thickest part reaches 63°C.

title: Dwaeji Bulgogi Spicy Pork Rice Bowls
summary: Gochujang-marinated pork stir-fried with onion and finished over rice with kimchi and sesame.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Mix the gochujang, soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, garlic and ginger and coat the pork.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over high heat and stir-fry the onion for 3 minutes until softened.
Add the pork in batches and cook for 6 minutes until browned, sticky and cooked through.
Serve over rice with the spring onions and kimchi.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork until it reaches 75°C in the thickest piece, and wash hands after handling raw pork.

title: Gamjajorim Soy Braised Potatoes with Egg
summary: Baby potatoes and soft-boiled eggs glazed in a sweet soy braise, a staple of Korean home cooking.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Boil the eggs for 9 minutes until just firm, cool in cold water and peel.
Simmer the potatoes with 1 1/2 cups water, the soy sauce, sugar, garlic and chilli for 15 minutes until tender.
Add the eggs, syrup and sesame oil and simmer for 5 minutes until the sauce is glossy and thick, then serve on rice with sesame seeds.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until fully set and hold the dish above 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers.

title: Khao Pad Sapparot Thai Pineapple Fried Rice
summary: Day-old rice stir-fried with pineapple, prawns, cashews and curry powder for a sweet-savoury dinner.

steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the prawns for 3 minutes until pink, then lift out.
Scramble the eggs in the wok for 1 minute until just set and break them up.
Add the remaining oil and the onion, cook for 2 minutes, then the rice and curry powder and stir for 3 minutes until hot and loose.
Add the pineapple, prawns, cashews, soy sauce and fish sauce and toss for 2 minutes until heated through.
Scatter over the spring onions.

notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until opaque and pink (63°C) and eggs until set, and cool leftover rice quickly and refrigerate within 1 hour.

title: Gai Pad Med Mamuang Thai Cashew Chicken
summary: Chicken stir-fried with roasted cashews, capsicum and dried chilli in a glossy oyster sauce.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and fry the chillies and garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir-fry for 5 minutes until cooked through and lightly golden.
Add the onion and capsicum and cook for 2 minutes until just tender, then the sauces and sugar until glossy.
Toss in the cashews and spring onions and serve with rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C in the thickest piece, and wash hands and boards after handling raw chicken.

title: Pla Tod Khamin Thai Turmeric Fried Fish
summary: Crisp turmeric and garlic fish fillets with sweet chilli sauce and steamed rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Rub the fish with the turmeric, garlic, pepper and salt, then dust with the rice flour.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat and fry the fish for 4 minutes each side until crisp and golden and the flesh flakes.
Serve with sweet chilli sauce, lime and rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until the thickest part reaches 63°C. Naturally gluten-free.

title: Thit Kho Hot Vit Pork and Egg Braise
summary: Pork belly and boiled eggs braised in coconut water and caramel until tender and lacquered.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, cool and peel.
Melt the sugar in a pot with the oil over medium heat for 3 minutes until amber, add the shallots and garlic and the pork and brown for 6 minutes.
Add the fish sauce, pepper, coconut water and eggs, cover and simmer for 55 minutes until the pork is tender and the sauce is syrupy, then serve with the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook pork to 75°C throughout and eggs until fully set. Refrigerate leftovers promptly.

title: Ayam Penyet Smashed Fried Chicken
summary: Spiced fried chicken smashed with a fiery sambal, with cucumber and rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Simmer the drumsticks in 2 cups water with the turmeric, garlic, coriander and salt for 20 minutes until cooked through, then drain and dry.
Fry the chicken in the hot oil for 8 minutes, turning, until crisp and golden.
Blend the chillies, tomatoes and shallots into a sambal with the lime juice and a pinch of salt.
Smash the chicken lightly, cover with sambal and serve with cucumber and rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C at the bone, and wash hands and boards after handling raw chicken.

title: Ikan Assam Pedas Malaysian Sour Fish Curry
summary: Fish simmered in a tamarind, chilli and lemongrass gravy with okra and tomato.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Blend the chillies, shallots, garlic and ginger to a paste and fry in the oil for 5 minutes until fragrant.
Add 3 cups water, the lemongrass, tamarind, sugar and salt and simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the okra and tomatoes for 4 minutes until tender, then lay the fish in and cook for 6 minutes until opaque and flaky.
Serve the fish and its sour gravy with the rice and a little extra tamarind at the table.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until the thickest part reaches 63°C. Naturally gluten-free.

title: Curry Mee Mamak Style Noodles
summary: Egg noodles in a spicy coconut curry with tofu puffs, potato and bean sprouts.

steps.text: Blend the shallots, garlic and ginger and fry in the oil for 4 minutes until fragrant.
Add the curry powder and sambal and stir for 1 minute, then the stock, coconut milk and potatoes and simmer for 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Add the tofu puffs and simmer for 4 minutes until hot.
Cook the noodles in boiling water for 3 minutes until tender and drain.
Divide the noodles among bowls, ladle the curry over and top with bean sprouts.

notes: Contains egg and wheat.

title: Bhindi Masala Dry Okra Curry
summary: Crisp-tender okra with onion, tomato and cumin, served with rice and dal.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wide pan and fry the okra for 8 minutes until browned and no longer sticky, then lift out.
Add the remaining oil, cumin seeds and onions and cook for 6 minutes until golden.
Add the spices, tomatoes and chickpeas and cook for 5 minutes until thick, then return the okra with the salt and amchur and cook for 3 minutes until tender.

notes: Naturally vegan and gluten-free.

title: Kadai Paneer Peppers and Paneer
summary: Paneer and capsicum in a spicy coarse-ground kadai masala gravy.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Heat the ghee in a kadai or wide pan and toast the coriander and chillies for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the onion, ginger and garlic and cook for 6 minutes until golden.
Add the tomatoes and salt and cook for 8 minutes until the oil separates.
Fold in the capsicums, paneer and garam masala and cook for 4 minutes until the capsicum is tender and the paneer is hot.

notes: Paneer is a fresh cheese and suits vegetarians.

title: Matoke Plantain and Peanut Stew
summary: Green plantain simmered with tomato, onion and ground peanut, a Ugandan comfort one-pot.

steps.text: Heat the oil and fry the onion for 6 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic and spices for 1 minute, then the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the plantain, ground peanuts, salt and stock, cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the plantain is tender and the sauce is thick.
Stir in the coriander and taste for salt before serving the stew hot.

notes: Naturally vegan and gluten-free.

title: Wali wa Nazi Coconut Rice with Pigeon Peas
summary: Swahili coconut rice cooked with pigeon peas, cardamom and tomato, served with a lime kachumbari.

steps.text: Fry the onion in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, then add the cardamom.
Add the rinsed rice, coconut milk, 1 1/2 cups water and salt, bring to the boil, cover and cook on low for 15 minutes until the rice is tender and fluffy.
Fold in the pigeon peas, cover and rest for 5 minutes.
Toss the tomatoes with the lime juice and coriander and serve on top.

notes: Naturally vegan and gluten-free.

title: Boerewors and Pap with Tomato Gravy
summary: Browned boerewors with a spiced tomato and onion gravy over soft maize pap.

steps.text: Bring 3 cups salted water to the boil, whisk in the maize meal and cook on low for 20 minutes until thick and soft.
Fry the boerewors in the oil for 12 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through, then lift out.
Fry the onion in the pan for 5 minutes until golden, add garlic, paprika, tomatoes and paste and simmer for 8 minutes until thick.
Slice the sausage, return to the gravy and serve over pap.

notes: Food safety: cook the sausage until it reaches 75°C throughout. Check the label for gluten.

title: Lomi Lomi Hawaiian Poached Salmon and Tomato Plates
summary: Hawaiian style poached salmon with tomato, onion and cucumber over rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Poach the salmon in simmering salted water for 8 minutes until opaque, flake it and cool.
Toss the tomatoes, onion, cucumber and spring onions with the lime juice, soy sauce and sesame oil.
Fold in the salmon and serve over rice.

notes: Food safety: cook salmon until it reaches 63°C. Refrigerate leftovers promptly.

title: Shuizhu Yu Sichuan Poached Fish in Chilli Oil
summary: Tender fish slices poached in a numbing chilli broth over bean sprouts, served with steamed rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Toss the fish with the egg white, cornflour and a pinch of salt and chill while you make the broth.
Blanch the bean sprouts in boiling water for 1 minute until just wilted and spread in a deep bowl.
Fry the chilli bean paste, garlic and ginger in 1 tbsp oil for 2 minutes until the oil reddens, add the stock and bring to a simmer.
Slide in the fish and poach for 3 minutes until opaque, then ladle over the sprouts.
Fry the dried chillies and peppercorns in the remaining oil for 30 seconds until they darken and pour the hot oil over the fish.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and the thickest part reaches 63°C. Contains egg. Keep any leftover garlic, herb or chilli oil in the fridge and use it within 4 days.

title: Xiang La Xia Hunan Chilli Prawns
summary: Fast Hunan stir-fried prawns with fresh and dried chilli, garlic and a splash of black vinegar.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat, add the dried chillies for 20 seconds until they darken, then the garlic, ginger and fresh chilli for 30 seconds.
Add the prawns and stir-fry for 3 minutes until pink and curled.
Splash in the soy sauce, vinegar and sugar and toss for 1 minute until glazed, then scatter the spring onions and serve with rice.

notes: Food safety: cook prawns until opaque and pink (63°C inside), and keep raw prawns chilled.

title: Teochew Steamed Fish with Tomato and Ginger
summary: Silky white fish steamed with tomato, ginger, vinegar and mushrooms in a light savoury broth.

items.raw: 4 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and sliced

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Lay the fish in a heatproof dish and scatter over the tomatoes, mushrooms, vinegar, ginger and soy sauce.
Steam over boiling water for 10 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Heat the vegetable and sesame oils until shimmering and pour over the spring onions on top.
Serve with the juices spooned over the rice.

notes: Food safety: steam the fish until the thickest part reaches 63°C. Naturally dairy-free.

title: Nikujaga Japanese Beef and Potato Simmer
summary: Thin beef, potato and onion simmered in sweet soy dashi, a homestyle Japanese comfort dinner.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Heat the oil in a pot and fry the beef for 3 minutes until just browned, then add the onions and cook for 3 minutes until soft.
Add the potatoes, carrots, dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar and bring to a gentle boil until the pot is bubbling steadily.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the liquid has reduced by half.
Stir in the peas for 2 minutes until hot, then serve in bowls with rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef until it reaches 75°C throughout, and wash hands after handling raw beef.

title: Tonkatsu with Shredded Cabbage and Rice
summary: Crumbed pork cutlets fried until golden, with cabbage, rice and tangy tonkatsu sauce.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Season the pork, dust with flour, dip in the egg and press into the panko.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and fry the cutlets for 4 minutes each side until deep golden and cooked through.
Rest on a rack for 3 minutes, slice and serve with the cabbage, sauce, lemon and rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork until it reaches 75°C in the centre. Contains egg and wheat.

title: Haemul Pajeon Korean Seafood Pancake
summary: Crisp spring onion pancakes studded with prawns and squid, served with a soy and vinegar dip.

steps.text: Whisk the plain flour, rice flour, egg, water and a pinch of salt into a thin batter.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a non-stick pan and lay a quarter of the spring onions in a row.
Pour over a quarter of the batter and scatter with seafood, then cook for 4 minutes until the base is crisp and golden.
Flip and cook for 3 minutes until the seafood is opaque, repeating for the other pancakes.
Mix the soy sauce, vinegar and gochugaru and serve as a dip.

notes: Food safety: cook seafood until opaque and reaching 63°C, and eggs until set. Contains egg and wheat.

title: Pad Prik King Thai Green Bean Stir-Fry
summary: Pork mince and snake beans fried in red curry paste with kaffir lime leaf, served with rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Fry the curry paste in the oil for 2 minutes until fragrant and the oil separates.
Add the pork mince and cook for 6 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and cooked through.
Add the beans, fish sauce, sugar and 1/4 cup water and stir-fry for 4 minutes until the beans are tender-crisp, then fold in the lime leaves.
Serve the pork and beans straight from the wok over the steaming rice, with extra lime leaf if you like.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork until no pink remains and it reaches 75°C.

title: Gaeng Keow Wan Gai Thai Green Chicken Curry
summary: Creamy green curry with chicken thigh, aubergine and basil, simmered in coconut milk.

items.raw: 600g chicken thighs, boneless and skinless, sliced

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Fry the paste in the oil for 2 minutes until fragrant, add half the coconut milk and cook until the oil splits.
Add the chicken and cook for 5 minutes until sealed, then the remaining milk, eggplant, fish sauce and sugar.
Simmer for 12 minutes until the chicken is cooked and the eggplant is soft, add the beans for 3 minutes and stir in the basil.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C in the thickest piece, and wash hands after handling raw chicken.

title: Khao Soi Gai Chiang Mai Chicken Curry Noodles
summary: Northern Thai coconut curry noodles with chicken, crisp noodles, pickled mustard greens and lime.

items.raw: 600g chicken thighs, boneless and skinless, sliced

steps.text: Cook 100g of the noodles in hot oil for 1 minute until puffed and crisp, and boil the rest for 3 minutes until tender, then drain.
Fry the curry paste and turmeric in 1 tbsp oil for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Add the coconut milk and cook for 3 minutes until the oil rises, then add the stock, fish sauce and sugar.
Add the chicken and simmer for 15 minutes until cooked through and tender.
Divide the noodles among bowls, ladle over the curry and top with crisp noodles, greens, shallots and lime.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C. Contains egg and wheat.

title: Bun Rieu Style Tomato Tofu Noodles
summary: Rice vermicelli in a sour tomato broth with fried tofu, herbs and a spoon of shrimp paste.

steps.text: Cook the vermicelli in boiling water for 4 minutes until tender, then drain and rinse.
Fry the tofu in 2 tbsp oil for 8 minutes until golden, then lift out.
Fry the shallots in the remaining oil for 3 minutes until soft, add the tomatoes and cook for 6 minutes until they collapse.
Add the stock, tamarind, fish sauce and shrimp paste and simmer for 10 minutes until fragrant.
Divide the noodles among bowls, add the tofu and ladle over the broth, then top with sprouts, mint and lime.

notes: Contains fish sauce and shrimp paste, so not vegetarian.

title: Thit Heo Quay Vietnamese Crispy Pork Rice Plates
summary: Crackling-topped roast pork belly sliced over rice with pickled cucumber and nuoc cham.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Pat the pork dry, prick the skin, rub the meat with five spice and the skin with salt and vinegar.
Roast at 160°C for 60 minutes until the meat is tender, then raise to 230°C for 15 minutes until the skin is blistered and crisp.
Mix the fish sauce, sugar, lime juice and chilli with 3 tbsp water for the dipping sauce.
Rest the pork for 10 minutes, slice and serve with rice, cucumber and sauce.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork until it reaches 75°C in the centre. Wash hands and boards after handling raw pork.

title: Mi Quang Danang Turmeric Noodles
summary: Wide rice noodles with turmeric prawns and pork in a little rich broth, with peanuts and herbs.

steps.text: Soak the noodles in boiling water for 8 minutes until tender, then drain.
Fry the shallots, turmeric and pork in the oil for 6 minutes until the pork is browned and cooked through.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 4 minutes, pour in the stock and fish sauce and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the prawns and cook for 3 minutes until pink and opaque.
Divide the noodles among bowls and ladle over a little broth, then top with peanuts, mint and sprouts.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork to 75°C and the prawns until opaque and pink.

title: Ca Ri Ga Vietnamese Chicken Curry
summary: Chicken, potato and carrot braised in a mild coconut curry with lemongrass.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Fry the onion, garlic and curry powder in the oil for 5 minutes until fragrant, add the chicken and brown for 5 minutes.
Add the lemongrass, coconut milk, fish sauce, sugar and 1 cup water.
Simmer for 15 minutes, add potatoes and carrots and cook for 15 minutes until tender and the chicken is cooked through.
Spoon the curry over the cooked rice and serve while the sauce is still hot and glossy.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C at the bone, and wash hands after handling raw chicken.

title: Opor Ayam Javanese Coconut Chicken
summary: Chicken simmered in a mild, creamy coconut gravy with galangal, lemongrass and candlenut.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Blend the shallots, garlic, ginger, coriander and turmeric into a paste and fry in the oil for 5 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chicken and brown for 5 minutes, then the lemongrass, bay leaves, coconut milk, salt and 1/2 cup water.
Simmer for 25 minutes until the chicken is tender and the sauce is thick.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C at the bone.

title: Sate Ayam Indonesian Peanut Chicken Skewers
summary: Grilled turmeric chicken skewers with a sweet peanut sauce, served on rice with cucumber.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Mix the turmeric, kecap manis and oil and coat the chicken, then thread onto metal skewers.
Grill or pan-fry for 12 minutes, turning, until charred and cooked through.
Warm the peanut butter, lime juice, garlic, sambal and 1/2 cup water in a pot for 3 minutes until smooth and pourable.
Serve over rice with cucumber.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C, and wash hands after handling raw chicken. Contains peanuts.

title: Kari Kapitan Nyonya Chicken Curry
summary: Nyonya style chicken curry with lemongrass, galangal, tamarind and coconut milk.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Blend the shallots, garlic, chillies, ginger and turmeric into a paste and fry in the oil for 6 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chicken and lemongrass and cook for 5 minutes, then the coconut milk, tamarind, sugar, salt and 1/2 cup water.
Simmer for 25 minutes until the chicken is cooked and the sauce is thick.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C at the bone.

title: Udang Asam Tamarind Prawns
summary: Sticky tamarind prawns with chilli and curry leaves, served over rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and fry the garlic, chillies and curry leaves for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the prawns and stir-fry for 3 minutes until pink.
Add the tamarind, sugar, soy sauce and 1/4 cup water and cook for 2 minutes until sticky and glossy, then serve over rice.

notes: Food safety: cook prawns until opaque and pink (63°C inside), and keep raw prawns chilled.

title: Pinakbet Filipino Mixed Vegetable Stew with Pork
summary: Okra, eggplant, squash and beans stewed with pork and a salty fermented shrimp paste.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Fry the pork in the oil for 8 minutes until browned, then the onion, garlic and tomatoes for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the shrimp paste and 1 cup water, add the pumpkin and eggplant and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the okra and beans and cook for 6 minutes until tender, then serve with rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork to 75°C.

title: Lumpiang Shanghai Filipino Spring Roll Plates
summary: Crisp pork and carrot rolls served with sweet chilli sauce and rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Mix the pork, carrot, onion, garlic, egg and soy sauce until well combined.
Roll a spoonful in each wrapper and seal the edge with water.
Fry in the oil in batches for 5 minutes until deep golden and cooked through.
Serve with chilli sauce and rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the rolls until the centre reaches 75°C. Contains egg and wheat.

title: Goan Xitt Kodi Fish Curry with Rice
summary: Coconut and tamarind fish curry with kokum and red chilli, as made in Goan homes.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Blend the onions, chillies, coriander and turmeric with a little water to a paste and fry in the oil for 6 minutes until fragrant.
Add the coconut milk, tamarind, salt and 1/2 cup water and simmer for 8 minutes.
Lay in the fish and cook for 6 minutes until opaque and flaking, then serve with rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until the thickest part reaches 63°C. Naturally gluten-free.

title: Chettinad Mushroom Pepper Fry
summary: Mushrooms fried with black pepper, fennel and curry leaves, served with rice and yoghurt.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Heat the oil, add fennel, cumin and curry leaves for 30 seconds, then the onions and cook for 8 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic, mushrooms and salt and cook for 8 minutes until browned and the liquid has gone.
Add the tomatoes and pepper and cook for 4 minutes until dry, then serve with rice and yoghurt.

notes: Vegetarian. Naturally gluten-free.

title: Sri Lankan Chickpea and Bean Curry with Roasted Curry Powder
summary: A dark, spicy Sri Lankan curry of chickpeas, beans and coconut, cooked with roasted curry powder.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Fry the onion, garlic and curry leaf in the oil for 6 minutes until golden.
Add the curry powder and turmeric for 1 minute, then the chickpeas, coconut milk, tamarind and 1/2 cup water.
Simmer for 15 minutes, add the beans and cook for 8 minutes until tender and the sauce is thick.

notes: Naturally vegan and gluten-free.

title: Wok-Roasted Tomato and Ginger Chicken Peshawar Style
summary: Chicken cooked in a wok with tomato, ginger and green chilli until the oil rises.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Heat the ghee in a wok, fry the cumin, garlic, ginger and chicken for 8 minutes until browned.
Add the tomatoes, salt and pepper, cover and cook for 20 minutes until the chicken is tender and the oil separates.
Stir in the chillies and garam masala for 3 minutes and finish with coriander.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C at the bone. Naturally gluten-free.

title: Nepali Chicken Choila
summary: Charred chicken tossed with ginger, garlic, cumin and mustard oil in the Newari style.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Grill the chicken for 14 minutes, turning, until charred and cooked through.
Cool for 3 minutes, chop and toss with the oil, ginger, garlic, spices, onion, chillies and lime juice.
Fold in the coriander and serve with the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C. Naturally gluten-free and dairy-free.

title: Chingri Malaikari Bengali Coconut Prawn Curry
summary: Bengali prawns in a creamy coconut gravy with ginger, cardamom and bay leaf.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Heat the oil, fry the bay leaves, cardamom and onions for 8 minutes until golden.
Add the ginger, turmeric, chilli, sugar and salt for 1 minute.
Pour in the coconut milk and simmer for 6 minutes until thick, then add the prawns and cook for 4 minutes until pink and opaque.
Spoon the curry over the cooked rice and serve while the sauce is still hot and glossy.

notes: Food safety: cook prawns until opaque and pink (63°C). Naturally gluten-free.

title: Doi Maach Bengali Yoghurt Fish Curry
summary: Fish fillets simmered in a spiced yoghurt gravy with turmeric and ginger.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Fry the onions in the oil for 8 minutes until golden, add the ginger and spices.
Stir in the yoghurt, sugar, salt and 1/2 cup water on low heat for 3 minutes.
Add the fish and simmer gently for 8 minutes until opaque and flaking, then serve with rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until the thickest part reaches 63°C. Contains dairy.

title: Shiro Wat Ethiopian Chickpea Flour Stew
summary: Silky chickpea flour stew with onion, garlic and paprika, served over rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Fry the onions in a dry pot for 8 minutes, then add the oil, garlic and ginger for 2 minutes.
Add the paprika, cumin and tomato paste for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Whisk in the stock and chickpea flour, simmer for 10 minutes, stirring, until thick and smooth, then serve over rice.

notes: Naturally vegan and gluten-free.

title: Mukimo Kenyan Mashed Potato Peas and Greens
summary: Comforting Kenyan mash of potato, peas, corn and spinach, served with a tomato stew.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes for 15 minutes until tender, adding the peas for the last 3 minutes.
Fry the onion in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, add tomatoes and cook for 6 minutes, then add tofu and salt for 4 minutes.
Wilt the spinach in the hot pot for 2 minutes until soft.
Mash potatoes with butter, corn and spinach until chunky and serve with the stew.

notes: Vegetarian.

title: Potjiekos South African Lamb and Vegetable Stew
summary: A layered lamb stew with potatoes, carrots and cabbage simmered slowly in a heavy pot.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil in a heavy pot for 8 minutes until deep golden, then lift out.
Fry the onions, garlic and curry powder for 4 minutes until soft.
Return the lamb with the stock, salt and carrots and simmer covered for 45 minutes.
Add the potatoes and cabbage and cook for 30 minutes until the lamb is very tender and the sauce has thickened.

notes: Food safety: cook lamb until it reaches 75°C.

title: Peri-Peri Chicken with Rice and Slaw
summary: Roast chicken in a fiery peri-peri marinade, with rice and a quick cabbage slaw.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Blend the chillies, garlic, oil, lemon juice, paprika, salt and oregano and coat the chicken.
Roast at 200°C for 35 minutes until deep golden and cooked through.
Toss cabbage and carrot with a spoon of the marinade and serve with the chicken and rice.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken until it reaches 75°C at the bone. Naturally gluten-free.

title: Rourou Fijian Taro Leaf Coconut Curry
summary: Taro leaves, or spinach, simmered in coconut milk with onion and chilli, served with rice and chickpeas.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Fry the onion, garlic, ginger and chillies in the oil for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the turmeric, chickpeas, coconut milk and salt and simmer for 8 minutes until slightly thick.
Stir in the spinach for 4 minutes until tender and serve with rice.

notes: Naturally vegan and gluten-free.

title: Poisson Cru Tahitian Fish in Coconut and Lime
summary: Raw-style Tahitian fish dish, here lightly poached, with lime, coconut milk and crisp vegetables.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then keep it covered.
Poach the fish in simmering water for 3 minutes until just opaque, then drain and cool.
Toss with lime juice and salt, leave for 10 minutes, then add the diced vegetables.
Fold in the coconut milk and spring onions and serve over the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and 63°C.

title: Kalua Pork Rice Bowls with Pineapple
summary: Slow-cooked Hawaiian pulled pork with pineapple and cabbage over rice.

steps.text: Rub the pork with salt and smoked paprika and place in a covered pot with 1/2 cup water.
Cook at 160°C for 3 hours until fork tender.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Shred the pork, return to the juices and serve over rice with cabbage and pineapple.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork until it reaches 75°C in the thickest part.

title: Mapo Eggplant
summary: Silky Sichuan-style eggplant in a glossy chilli bean sauce, finished with spring onion and served over rice.

items.raw: 1 tbsp cornflour mixed with 2 tbsp water

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender, then keep it covered. Toss the eggplant with a pinch of salt and let it sit while you prep the rest.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and fry the eggplant for 8 minutes, turning often, until golden and softened. Lift out and set aside.
In the same wok fry the chilli bean paste, garlic and ginger for 1 minute until the oil turns red, then add the stock, soy sauce and sugar.
Return the eggplant and simmer for 6 minutes until very tender. Stir in the cornflour slurry and cook for 1 minute until glossy.
Sprinkle with Sichuan pepper and spring onions and serve over the rice.

title: Zha Jiang Mian Beijing Noodles
summary: Beijing-style wheat noodles topped with a dark, savoury pork and fermented bean sauce and crunchy cucumber.

steps.text: Fry the pork in the oil over medium-high heat for 6 minutes, breaking it up, until browned. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the hoisin sauce, soybean paste, wine, soy sauce and sugar, then add the water.
Simmer on low for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and glossy and the oil rises to the top.
Boil the noodles in plenty of water until just tender, drain well and divide between bowls.
Spoon over the sauce and top with cucumber and spring onions. Toss at the table.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork until no pink remains and it reaches 75°C, and wash hands after handling raw mince.

title: Hokkien Prawn Mee Stir-Fry
summary: Yellow noodles and thick rice noodles wok-fried with prawns, squid, egg and bean sprouts in a savoury prawn stock.

items.raw: 4 stalks garlic chives, cut in 4cm lengths

steps.text: Soak the vermicelli in hot water for 5 minutes and drain. Mix the stock, oyster sauce and both soy sauces in a jug.
Heat half the oil in a wok over high heat, fry the garlic for 20 seconds, add the prawns and squid and cook for 2 minutes. Remove.
Add the remaining oil, crack in the eggs and scramble for 30 seconds, then add both noodles and the stock mixture.
Toss for 4 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the noodles are lightly caramelised at the edges.
Return the seafood with the sprouts and chives, toss for 1 minute, and serve with lime.

notes: Food safety: cook the prawns, squid and eggs until the prawns are opaque and the noodles are steaming hot, at least 75°C. Contains egg and shellfish.

title: Mie Goreng Jawa Javanese Fried Noodles
summary: Smoky Javanese noodles wok-fried with sweet soy sauce, greens, egg and chicken, topped with crisp shallots.

steps.text: Cook the noodles in boiling water for 2 minutes, drain and toss with a teaspoon of the oil.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and fry the shallots and garlic for 1 minute. Add the chicken and stir-fry for 4 minutes until cooked through.
Push to one side, scramble the eggs in the gap, then add the noodles, kecap manis, oyster sauce, soy sauce and pepper.
Add the bok choy and tomato and toss for 3 minutes until the greens wilt and the noodles take on colour.
Serve topped with fried shallots.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C in the thickest piece, and wash hands after handling raw chicken. Contains egg.

title: Tahu Orek Sticky Sweet Tofu Stir-Fry
summary: Crisp tofu strips tossed in a sticky sweet-chilli kecap manis glaze with green beans, served with rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender, then keep it covered.
Fry the tofu in the oil over medium-high heat for 8 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp. Lift out onto paper towel.
In the same pan fry the shallots, garlic, chillies and lime leaves for 2 minutes, then add the beans and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the kecap manis, tamarind and sugar with 2 tbsp water and bubble for 1 minute, then return the tofu and toss until coated and sticky.
Serve over the rice while the glaze is still sticky and glossy.

title: Tahu Telur Surabaya Tofu Omelette
summary: Fried tofu folded into an egg omelette, served with rice, bean sprouts and a sweet peanut sauce.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender, then keep it covered. Whisk the peanut butter, kecap manis, lime juice, chilli and hot water into a sauce.
Fry the tofu in half the oil for 6 minutes until golden on all sides.
Beat the eggs with the spring onions, salt and pepper and stir in the tofu.
Heat the remaining oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat, pour in the mix, and cook for 4 minutes each side until set and golden.
Cut into wedges, serve over the rice with sprouts and spoon over the peanut sauce.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until firm all the way through and 75°C. Contains egg and peanuts.

title: Tahu Bacem Braised Tofu
summary: Javanese tofu braised in palm sugar, coriander and bay leaf until dark and sticky, then pan-fried.

items.raw: 500g firm tofu, cut into thick slices

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender, then keep it covered.
Combine the shallots, garlic, coriander, bay leaves, sugar, kecap manis, tamarind and water in a pan and bring to a simmer until the sugar dissolves.
Add the tofu and simmer for 25 minutes, turning once, until the liquid is nearly gone and the tofu is dark and glazed.
Heat the oil in a frying pan and fry the tofu for 2 minutes each side until the edges caramelise.
Serve with the rice, the remaining glaze spooned over and the cucumber on the side.

title: Pad Kra Pao Moo Thai Holy Basil Pork
summary: Fiery minced pork wok-fried with garlic, chillies and basil, served over rice with a crisp-edged fried egg.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender, then keep it covered. Crush the garlic and chillies to a rough paste.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat and fry the paste for 20 seconds. Add the pork and stir-fry for 5 minutes, breaking it up, until cooked and lightly browned.
Add the oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce, sugar and a splash of water, toss for 1 minute, then fold through the basil until just wilted.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil over high heat for 2 minutes until the whites are crisp and the yolks set to your liking.
Serve the pork over rice, each topped with a fried egg.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork until it reaches 75°C and no pink remains, and cook the eggs until the whites are fully set. Contains egg. Use fresh, uncracked eggs; for pregnant women, older people, young children and anyone with low immunity, cook the eggs until the yolks are firm.

title: Khao Man Gai Thai Chicken Rice
summary: Rice cooked in rich chicken broth, topped with poached chicken and a punchy ginger, chilli and soy dipping sauce.

steps.text: Simmer the chicken with the sliced ginger, salt, 2 garlic cloves and the water, covered, for 25 minutes. Lift out the chicken and keep the broth.
Fry the rice with the remaining crushed garlic for 2 minutes, then cook it in 3 cups of the broth in a covered pot for 15 minutes until tender and fluffy.
Mix the miso, soy sauce, vinegar, grated ginger, chillies, sugar and 2 tbsp broth to make the dipping sauce.
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes, slice it off the bone and serve on the rice with cucumber and the sauce.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C in the thickest part near the bone, and wash hands after handling raw chicken.

title: Mi Quang Central Vietnamese Turmeric Noodles
summary: Wide turmeric rice noodles in a small amount of rich pork and prawn broth, topped with herbs, peanuts and sesame.

steps.text: Fry the shallots and garlic with the turmeric in the oil for 1 minute. Add the pork and cook for 5 minutes until browned.
Add the tomatoes, stock and fish sauce and simmer for 10 minutes until the pork is tender and the broth reduced by a quarter.
Add the prawns and cook for 3 minutes until pink and opaque.
Cook the noodles until tender per the packet, drain and divide between bowls, then ladle over the pork and prawns with a little broth.
Top with sprouts, herbs, peanuts and crackers and serve with lime.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork and prawns until the pork reaches 75°C and the prawns are opaque. Contains shellfish and peanuts.

title: Com Tam Suon Nuong Broken Rice with Grilled Pork Chop
summary: Lemongrass-marinated pork chops grilled until charred, served on rice with pickled carrot, cucumber and nuoc cham.

steps.text: Mix the lemongrass, garlic, 1 tbsp fish sauce, honey, soy sauce and oil, coat the chops and marinate.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender. Toss the carrot with the vinegar and a pinch of sugar and let it pickle.
Whisk the lime juice, remaining fish sauce, sugar, chilli and 3 tbsp water for the dipping sauce.
Grill or pan-fry the chops over medium-high heat for 5 minutes each side until charred and cooked through.
Rest for 3 minutes and serve on rice with the pickled carrot, cucumber, spring onions and dipping sauce.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork chops until the thickest part reaches 75°C with no pink and rest for 3 minutes, and wash hands after handling raw pork.
Plus 30 minutes marinating.

title: Bun Bo Xao Lemongrass Beef Noodle Bowl
summary: Stir-fried lemongrass beef over rice vermicelli with fresh herbs, lettuce, peanuts and a tangy dressing.

steps.text: Toss the beef with the lemongrass, half the garlic, 1 tbsp fish sauce and half the sugar and leave to sit while you prep.
Cook the vermicelli until tender per the packet, rinse under cold water and drain well.
Whisk the remaining fish sauce, sugar and garlic with the lime juice, chilli and water for the dressing.
Stir-fry the beef in the oil in two batches over high heat for 2 minutes each until browned and cooked through.
Build bowls with lettuce, vermicelli, cucumber and herbs, top with beef and peanuts and spoon over the dressing.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef until no pink remains and it reaches 75°C if minced, or 63°C for steak slices, and wash hands after handling raw beef. Contains peanuts.

title: Pancit Palabok Filipino Prawn Noodles
summary: Rice noodles under a golden prawn sauce, topped with prawns, egg, crushed chicharron and spring onion.

steps.text: Cook the noodles until tender per the packet, drain and divide between plates.
Fry the onion and garlic in the oil for 3 minutes until soft, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then add the stock and fish sauce.
Simmer for 6 minutes until thick, add the prawns and cook for 3 minutes until pink and opaque.
Spoon the sauce and prawns over the noodles and top with egg, crackling and spring onions.
Serve with lime wedges on the side for squeezing over the top.

notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until opaque, with the sauce hot to 75°C, and chill leftovers promptly. Contains egg and shellfish.

title: Katsudon Pork Cutlet Rice Bowl
summary: Crumbed pork cutlets simmered with onion in sweet dashi, set with egg and served over steamed rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and sticky, then keep it warm. Flatten the cutlets thin, then coat in flour, egg and panko.
Fry the cutlets in the oil over medium heat for 3 minutes each side until golden and cooked through. Drain and slice.
Simmer the onion with the dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar for 5 minutes until soft.
Lay the cutlets in the pan, pour the topping eggs over and cover for 1 minute until just set.
Slide over bowls of rice and sprinkle with spring onions.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork until it reaches 63°C and the eggs are just set; for firm eggs cook until 75°C. Contains egg.

title: Yaki Udon with Pork and Cabbage
summary: Chewy udon stir-fried with pork, cabbage and carrot in a savoury Worcestershire-soy sauce, finished with.

steps.text: Fry the pork in the oil over high heat for 4 minutes until browned and crisp at the edges.
Add the onion, carrot and cabbage and stir-fry for 3 minutes until just tender.
Loosen the udon under warm water, add to the pan and toss for 2 minutes until heated through.
Pour in the soy sauce, Worcestershire and mirin and toss for 1 minute until glossy.
Serve topped with spring onions and pickled ginger.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork until it reaches 75°C and no pink remains, and wash hands after handling raw pork.

title: Omurice Japanese Omelette Rice
summary: Ketchup-flavoured chicken fried rice wrapped in a soft, silky omelette.

steps.text: Melt half the butter in a large pan and cook the chicken, onion and carrot for 6 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Add the rice and peas, break up the rice and stir-fry for 3 minutes, then add the ketchup and soy sauce and toss for 2 minutes.
Whisk the eggs with the milk and salt. Melt a little butter in a non-stick pan over medium heat and pour in a quarter of the eggs.
Stir the eggs for 20 seconds, then set the base for 30 seconds and spoon a quarter of the rice on one half.
Fold over the omelette, slide onto a plate and repeat to make four.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C in the thickest piece and the eggs are set; use cooked rice cooled quickly and eaten within a day. Contains egg.

title: Jjajangmyeon Black Bean Noodles
summary: Korean-Chinese noodles in a glossy black bean sauce with pork, zucchini and onion.

items.raw: 1 tbsp cornflour mixed with 2 tbsp water

steps.text: Fry the black bean paste in the oil for 2 minutes, then remove from the pan. Brown the pork in the same pan for 5 minutes.
Add the onions, potato and zucchini and cook for 5 minutes. Return the paste, add the sugar, soy sauce and water and simmer for 10 minutes until the potato is tender.
Stir in the cornflour slurry and cook for 1 minute until thick and glossy.
Boil the noodles until just tender, drain and divide between bowls.
Spoon over the sauce and top with cucumber.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork until it reaches 75°C and no pink remains, and wash hands after handling raw pork.

title: Besan Chilla Chickpea Flour Crepes
summary: Savoury chickpea flour crepes with ginger, chilli and onion, cooked crisp and served with a coconut chutney.

steps.text: Whisk the chickpea flour with the chillies, ginger, cumin, salt and about 2 cups water into a smooth pouring batter and rest it while you make the chutney.
Blend the coconut, peanuts, extra chilli and water to a coarse chutney with a pinch of salt.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat, ladle on batter and spread thin into a 20cm round.
Scatter on onion, drizzle oil around the edges and cook for 3 minutes until crisp underneath, then flip for 1 minute.
Repeat with the remaining batter and serve hot with the chutney.

notes: Vegan. Breakfast or lunch.
Plus 10 minutes resting the batter.

title: Chole Bhature Spiced Chickpeas with Puffed Bread
summary: Punjabi chickpea curry served with fluffy deep-fried bread.

steps.text: For the bhature, knead the flour, yoghurt, baking powder, 1/2 tsp salt and water into a soft dough, cover and rest.
Fry the onion in the oil for 6 minutes until golden, add the ginger and garlic for 1 minute, then the ground spices for 30 seconds.
Add the tomato puree and cook for 8 minutes until thick and the oil separates, then add the chickpeas, salt and 1 cup water.
Simmer for 15 minutes until thick, lightly mashing some of the chickpeas, and stir in the garam masala.
Roll the dough into ovals and deep-fry in hot oil for 1 minute each side until puffed and golden. Serve at once with the chickpeas.

notes: Vegetarian. Dinner. Take care with the hot oil.
Plus 30 minutes resting the dough.

title: Usal Pav Maharashtrian Bean Curry with Bread
summary: Spicy black-eyed bean curry from Maharashtra, topped with fried shallots and served with soft bread rolls.

steps.text: Fry one onion in the oil for 5 minutes until browned, add the coconut, ginger and garlic for 2 minutes and blend with a splash of water to a paste.
Fry the remaining onion for 4 minutes, add the spices and tomatoes and cook for 6 minutes until thick.
Stir in the paste, beans, tamarind, water and salt and simmer for 15 minutes until the sprouts are tender and the gravy is thick.
Ladle into bowls and top with the fried shallots, onion and lemon.
Serve with the bread rolls for dipping.

notes: Vegan. Breakfast or lunch.

title: Kothu Roti Sri Lankan Chopped Roti
summary: Sri Lankan street food of flatbread chopped on a hot plate with egg, vegetables, chicken and curry spices.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large pan or wok over high heat, add the curry leaves, onion, garlic and ginger and fry for 3 minutes.
Add the chicken and the spices and cook for 6 minutes until cooked through.
Add the carrot and cabbage and stir-fry for 3 minutes, then push aside and scramble in the eggs.
Add the shredded flatbreads and salt and chop everything together with two spatulas for 4 minutes until heated and well mixed.
Serve straight from the pan.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C, and the eggs until set. Contains egg.

title: Bangladeshi Khichuri with Egg
summary: Soft rice and yellow lentils simmered with ginger, turmeric and ghee, served with fried eggs and fried onions.

steps.text: Rinse the rice and lentils together until the water runs clear.
Heat half the ghee in a heavy pot and fry the bay leaves, cumin, ginger and turmeric for 1 minute, then add the rice and lentils and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the water and salt, bring to the boil then simmer covered for 25 minutes, stirring often, until soft and porridge-like.
Fry the onion in the remaining ghee for 8 minutes until deep golden. Fry the eggs in the same pan for 3 minutes.
Serve the khichuri topped with eggs, fried onion and chillies.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set and the yolks at least 63°C. Contains egg and dairy.

title: Nihari Slow-Cooked Beef Shank Curry
summary: Pakistani slow-braised beef shank in a thick, spiced gravy, finished with ginger and green chilli.

items.raw: 1 tbsp fresh ginger, cut in matchsticks

steps.text: Fry the onions in half the ghee for 12 minutes until deep golden. Remove half for garnish.
Add the remaining ghee, beef, ginger and garlic and brown the beef for 8 minutes, then stir in all the ground spices and salt for 1 minute.
Add the water, bring to the boil then cover and simmer on very low heat for 2 1/2 hours until the beef is falling off the bone.
Whisk the flour with 1/2 cup cold water, stir into the pot and simmer for 10 minutes until the gravy is thick and glossy.
Serve with the fried onions, green chilli, ginger, lemon and naan.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef until fork-tender and well above 75°C, and chill leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Egusi Stew with Spinach and Rice
summary: Nigerian ground pumpkin seed stew with spinach, tomato, palm oil and chilli, served with rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender, then keep it covered.
Heat the oil in a pot and fry the onion for 4 minutes, then add the blended tomato and capsicum and cook for 12 minutes until the oil rises.
Stir in the pumpkin seeds, chillies, crayfish and stock, add the chicken and simmer covered for 18 minutes until cooked through.
Fold in the spinach and cook for 4 minutes until wilted, season with salt and serve over the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C near the bone, and wash hands after handling raw chicken.

title: Kik Alicha Yellow Split Pea Stew with Flatbread
summary: Ethiopian-style red lentils slow-cooked with onion, garlic and a warming spice paste, served with flatbread.

steps.text: Cook the onions in a dry pot over medium heat for 8 minutes, stirring, until soft and golden. Add the oil, garlic and ginger and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, chilli powder, paprika, cardamom and cumin and fry for 3 minutes until dark and fragrant.
Add the rinsed lentils, water and salt, bring to a simmer and cook, stirring, for 22 minutes until thick and the lentils have broken down.
Serve with warm flatbreads for scooping.

title: Awaze Tibs Spiced Ethiopian Beef Saute
summary: Quick-seared beef strips with onion, green chilli and rosemary in a spiced butter, served with flatbread.

steps.text: Melt half the butter in a large frying pan over high heat and sear the beef in two batches for 2 minutes each. Set aside.
Add the remaining butter, onions, garlic, ginger and chillies and cook for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the paprika, chilli flakes, cardamom, rosemary and salt and stir for 1 minute.
Return the beef with the tomato and toss for 2 minutes until just cooked.
Serve with the flatbreads.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef strips until browned and no pink remains, 63°C for steak cuts, and wash hands after handling raw beef.

title: Lu Pulu Samoan Taro Leaf Coconut Bake
summary: Silverbeet and corned beef baked in coconut milk, a Samoan comfort dish served with rice.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180C and cook the rice by your usual method until tender.
Fry the onion in the oil for 4 minutes until soft and stir through the corned beef for 2 minutes.
Place the silverbeet in a baking dish, spoon over the beef mix and season with the salt.
Pour in the coconut milk, cover with foil and bake for 40 minutes, until the greens are soft and the sauce thick.
Serve over rice with lime.

notes: Food safety: reheat the corned beef bake until steaming hot and 75°C throughout, and chill leftovers promptly.

title: Sukiyaki Don Beef Rice Bowl
