Cook the noodles in boiling water for 4 minutes until tender, drain and slip them into the broth to finish.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef to at least 71°C and serve piping hot. Do not dip cooked food into raw egg. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Mizutaki Fukuoka Chicken Hot Pot
summary: A clear chicken broth pot with tender thigh pieces, tofu and winter vegetables, served with a ponzu-style dip.

items.raw: 600g chicken thigh fillets, cut into chunks

steps.text: Put the water, kombu and chicken into a pot and bring slowly to a gentle simmer until the foam rises, skimming it off.
Simmer the chicken for 15 minutes, then lift out the kombu.
Add the carrots, cabbage and mushrooms and simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the tofu and leek and cook 4 minutes more until the chicken reaches 75°C in the centre.
Stir the soy sauce, lemon juice and sugar into a dip and serve with the pot and ladled broth.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C in the centre and keep the pot at a gentle simmer. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Chanko Nabe Sumo Wrestler Hot Pot
summary: A hearty chicken and meatball pot loaded with daikon, tofu and vegetables, the sumo training staple.

items.raw: 400g chicken thigh fillets, cut into chunks

steps.text: Mix the minced chicken, egg, ginger and 1 tsp salt into a sticky paste and shape into 18 small balls.
Bring the water, soy sauce and mirin to a simmer in a large pot until steaming, then add the chicken chunks and daikon.
Simmer for 12 minutes, then drop in the meatballs and cook for 8 minutes.
Add the cabbage, mushrooms and tofu and simmer 8 minutes more until the meatballs reach 75°C inside.
Add the leek and noodles and cook 4 minutes until the noodles are tender.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken and meatballs to 75°C in the centre. Contains egg. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Yudofu Kyoto Simmered Tofu Pot
summary: Silken tofu warmed in kombu broth with greens and mushrooms, dipped in soy and spring onion. Calm and light.

items.raw: 400g silken tofu, cut into large cubes

steps.text: Rinse the rice, cook it with 1 1/2 cups water until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Put the water and kombu in a shallow pot and warm gently for 5 minutes, then remove the kombu.
Add the mushrooms and simmer 4 minutes, then slide in the tofu and heat very gently for 5 minutes without boiling.
Add the spinach for the last minute until just wilted.
Mix the soy sauce, ginger, sesame seeds and spring onion as a dip and serve with the pot and rice.

title: Budae Jjigae Korean Army Stew
summary: A bubbling spicy stew of kimchi, sausage, tofu and noodles from the post-war Uijeongbu kitchens.

steps.text: Mix the gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar and garlic into a paste.
Arrange the kimchi, sausage, ham, tofu and onion in a wide pot and place the paste in the centre.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil, then simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the noodles and cook 6 minutes until tender, then scatter with spring onion.

notes: Food safety: cook the sausages and ham until they reach 75°C and serve piping hot. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Dakgalbi Chuncheon Spicy Chicken Stir-Fry
summary: Chicken thigh, sweet potato and cabbage fried in a chilli paste, finished with melted cheese in the pan.

items.raw: 700g chicken thigh fillets, cut into chunks
2 sweet potatoes, cut into thick sticks

steps.text: Mix the gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar and garlic and coat the chicken in it.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and fry the sweet potato for 6 minutes, then push aside.
Add the chicken and onion and fry for 8 minutes, then stir in the cabbage and cook 5 minutes until the chicken reaches 75°C.
Scatter the mozzarella over the top, cover for 2 minutes until melted and serve with the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C in the centre. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Haemul Sundubu Clam and Egg Soft Tofu Pot
summary: A fiery bubbling pot of soft tofu, clams and chilli oil with a raw egg cracked in at the table.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Warm the sesame oil in a small pot, stir in the gochugaru and garlic for 30 seconds without burning.
Add the water, soy sauce and clams, bring to a boil and simmer 5 minutes until the clams are opaque and firm.
Spoon in the tofu in large pieces, simmer 5 minutes, then crack in the eggs and cover for 3 minutes until the whites are firm.
Scatter with spring onion and serve bubbling with the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the clams until they are hot throughout and the eggs until the whites are set. Contains egg and shellfish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Gamjatang Pork Bone and Potato Stew
summary: A peppery pork-neck bone stew with potatoes and perilla-style greens, deeply savoury and warming.

steps.text: Cover the ribs with water in a large pot, boil for 10 minutes, drain and rinse them.
Return to the pot with the 8 cups water, onion, ginger and half the garlic and simmer for 50 minutes.
Stir the gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce and remaining garlic into the pot, add the potatoes and simmer 25 minutes.
Add the spinach and spring onions for the last 3 minutes.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy and serve the stew over or beside it.

notes: Food safety: simmer the pork until it is fully tender and reaches at least 70°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Jeonju Bibimbap Rice Bowl with Beef and Egg
summary: A rice bowl topped with seasoned beef, vegetables and a fried egg, mixed with gochujang at the table.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Toss the beef with 2 tbsp soy sauce, sugar and 1 tbsp sesame oil and fry in a hot pan for 4 minutes until cooked through.
Separately stir-fry the carrot and zucchini 2 minutes each, blanch the spinach and sprouts for 1 minute and dress with the remaining soy and sesame oil.
Fry the eggs in the vegetable oil until the whites are firm.
Pile the rice into bowls, arrange the toppings and eggs on top and serve with the gochujang.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef to at least 71°C and fry the eggs until the whites are set. Contains egg. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Dolsot Bibimbap Stone Pot Crispy Rice Bowl
summary: Rice crisped in a hot oiled pot with vegetables and an egg, with a crackling base you scrape up.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Stir-fry the carrot, zucchini and mushrooms separately in a little vegetable oil for 2 minutes each.
Blanch the spinach and sprouts for 1 minute, drain and dress with soy sauce.
Heat two small heavy pans, brush with sesame oil, press in the rice and let it sizzle for 5 minutes until crisp underneath.
Arrange the vegetables on top, crack an egg on each and cover for 3 minutes until the whites are firm. Serve with gochujang.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set. Contains egg. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Tendon Prawn and Vegetable Tempura Rice Bowl
summary: Crisp tempura over rice, glazed with a sweet soy sauce.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Simmer the soy sauce, mirin and sugar for 3 minutes until slightly syrupy.
Whisk the flour, sparkling water and egg lightly, leaving a few lumps.
Heat the oil to 175°C, dip the vegetables and prawns in batter and fry in batches for 3 minutes until crisp, draining on paper.
Spoon the rice into bowls, top with the tempura and drizzle with the sauce.

notes: Food safety: fry the prawns until pink and opaque, at least 63°C inside. Contains egg, gluten and shellfish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Tekkadon Tuna and Avocado Rice Bowl
summary: Seasoned tuna over warm sushi-style rice with avocado and sesame.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes, then stir through the rice vinegar and sugar.
Mix 2 tbsp soy sauce with the mirin and toss the tuna in it for 2 minutes.
Spoon the rice into bowls and fan out the tuna and avocado.
Scatter with sesame seeds, nori and spring onion and drizzle with the remaining soy sauce.

notes: Food safety: use only very fresh, sashimi-grade tuna kept cold until serving, and eat the same day. Pregnant people and the immunocompromised should choose cooked fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Tamago Don Soft Egg and Onion Rice Bowl
summary: Softly set eggs over onion simmered in dashi-style soy broth on rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Simmer the onion with the water, soy sauce, mirin and sugar for 5 minutes until soft.
Beat the eggs, pour over the onion in two stages, cover and cook 2 minutes until just set with no runny liquid.
Slide over the rice and top with spring onion.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until fully set. Contains egg. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Ji Rou Fan Chiayi Shredded Chicken Rice
summary: Taiwanese shredded chicken over rice with a glossy shallot-garlic oil.

steps.text: Simmer the chicken in the water with the ginger and 1 tsp salt for 25 minutes until it reaches 75°C in the centre, then lift out and shred, discarding the skin and bones.
Cook the rice in 2 cups of the strained chicken broth until tender and fluffy.
Fry the shallots in the oil over medium heat for 6 minutes until golden, then stir in the soy sauce and sugar.
Pile the rice into bowls, top with chicken and spoon over the shallot oil.
Spoon the shallot oil over the rice, add the cucumber slices alongside and serve while the chicken is still warm.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C in the centre. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Sanbeiji Three-Cup Chicken with Basil
summary: Taiwanese claypot chicken braised in sesame oil, soy and rice wine until sticky, finished with basil.

items.raw: 800g chicken thigh fillets, cut into chunks

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Heat the sesame oil in a heavy pot and fry the ginger and garlic for 3 minutes.
Add the chicken and brown for 6 minutes, then add the soy sauce, wine, sugar and chillies.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes, then uncover and boil 4 minutes until the sauce clings and the chicken reaches 75°C.
Stir in the basil and serve with the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C in the centre. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Prawn Omelette Taiwanese Night Market Style
summary: Taiwanese night market omelette: prawns in a starchy omelette with greens and a sweet chilli sauce.

steps.text: Whisk the potato starch with the water until smooth.
Heat the oil in a non-stick pan and fry the prawns and bok choy for 2 minutes until the prawns turn pink.
Pour in the starch mix, let it set for 1 minute, then pour in the beaten eggs.
Cook for 3 minutes until the eggs are set and the edges crisp, then flip and cook 1 minute.
Mix the tomato sauce, chilli sauce and soy sauce and spoon over the omelette.

notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until pink and opaque, at least 63°C inside, and the eggs until set. Contains egg and shellfish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Cai Pu Dan Radish Preserve Omelette
summary: A crisp omelette with salty preserved radish, served with rice.

items.raw: 1/3 cup preserved radish, rinsed and chopped

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Squeeze the radish dry and fry it in 1 tbsp oil for 2 minutes.
Beat the eggs with the soy sauce, radish and spring onions.
Heat the remaining oil in a non-stick pan, pour in the egg and cook 3 minutes over medium heat until golden underneath.
Flip and cook 2 minutes until fully set and serve with the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until fully set. Contains egg. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Fan Qie Chao Dan Tomato and Egg Stir-Fry
summary: Soft egg curds in a sweet-sharp tomato sauce over rice. Homely comfort.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and scramble in 1 tbsp hot oil for 1 minute until just set, then set aside.
Fry the tomatoes in the remaining oil for 4 minutes until they collapse, stirring in the sugar and soy sauce.
Fold the egg back in with the spring onions and cook 1 minute until the egg is fully set.
Spoon the egg and tomato over the rice, scatter with any remaining spring onion and serve straight away.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until fully set. Contains egg. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Bo Zai Fan Claypot Chicken and Mushroom Rice
summary: Hong Kong claypot rice with a crisp base, chicken, mushrooms and a ginger-soy finish.

items.raw: 500g chicken thigh fillets, cut into pieces

steps.text: Toss the chicken with 1 tbsp soy sauce, the oyster sauce, ginger, sugar and sesame oil.
Rinse the rice and bring to a boil in the water in a heavy pot with a lid, then simmer covered for 10 minutes.
Lay the chicken and mushrooms on the rice, cover and cook on low for 15 minutes until the chicken reaches 75°C.
Drizzle the vegetable oil around the edge, raise the heat for 2 minutes to crisp the base.
Mix the remaining soy sauce with 2 tbsp water, pour over, scatter with spring onions and stir at the table.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C in the centre. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Luohan Zhai Buddha's Delight Vegan Braise
summary: A vegetarian monastery braise of tofu, mushrooms and vegetables in a deep, gently sweet sauce, served with rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Fry the tofu in the vegetable oil for 6 minutes until golden, then set aside.
Add the mushrooms and carrots and fry 4 minutes, then pour in the water, soy sauce and sugar and simmer 8 minutes.
Stir in the broccoli, snow peas and tofu and simmer 4 minutes.
Stir the cornflour with 1 tbsp water, add and stir until glossy, then finish with sesame oil and cashews. Serve with the rice.

title: Dongpo Rou Hangzhou Braised Pork Belly
summary: Square pork belly braised until it melts, in soy and rice wine with a gloss of sugar, over greens and rice.

steps.text: Blanch the pork in boiling water for 5 minutes, drain and rinse.
Line a heavy pot with the spring onions and ginger, add the pork skin side down, then the wine, soy sauce, sugar and water.
Cover tightly and simmer on very low heat for 2 hours until a knife slides in with no resistance.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, blanch the bok choy for 2 minutes.
Reduce the sauce uncovered for 5 minutes until syrupy, then spoon it over the pork and serve with rice and greens.

notes: Food safety: braise the pork until it reaches at least 70°C and is fully tender. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Mala Chongqing Beef Hot Pot
summary: A numbing, fiery table pot of beef, tofu and vegetables in a chilli and Sichuan pepper broth.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pot and fry the doubanjiang, peppercorns, chillies, garlic and ginger for 3 minutes.
Add the water and soy sauce, bring to a boil and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the tofu, mushrooms and cabbage and cook for 6 minutes.
Swish the beef slices into the simmering broth for 1 to 2 minutes until cooked through.
Cook the noodles in the broth for the last 3 minutes until tender.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef to at least 71°C and keep the pot at a steady simmer. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Guoqiao Mixian Crossing the Bridge Noodles
summary: A Yunnan chicken broth poured over raw ingredients at the table which cook in the heat.

steps.text: Simmer the whole chicken pieces in the water with the ginger and 1 tsp salt for 45 minutes, skimming, until the meat reaches 75°C.
Strain the broth and keep it at a full boil until you are ready to pour.
Cook the noodles in boiling water 4 minutes until tender, drain into four bowls.
Arrange the sliced chicken breast, spinach and mushrooms on the noodles and crack a quail egg on each.
Pour in the boiling broth, stir, wait 2 minutes until the breast slices turn opaque and the eggs set, then season with soy sauce and spring onion.

notes: Food safety: the broth must be at a full boil when poured so the thin chicken cooks to 75°C and the eggs are set; return to the pot if anything is pink. Contains egg. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Mongolian Lamb Hot Pot with Tofu
summary: A copper-style broth with thin lamb, tofu and cabbage, dipped in sesame and chive sauce.

steps.text: Bring the water, ginger and spring onions to a boil and simmer for 10 minutes.
Whisk the tahini, soy sauce and 2 tbsp warm water into a dipping sauce, stir in the chives.
Add the tofu, cabbage and mushrooms and cook for 6 minutes.
Swish the lamb slices through the broth for 1 to 2 minutes until cooked, then add the noodles for the last 3 minutes.
Serve with the sauce for dipping.

notes: Food safety: cook the lamb to at least 71°C and keep the broth at a steady simmer. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Hong Kong Claypot Lap Cheong Winter Rice
summary: Cured sausage and mushrooms steam through the rice in a heavy pot, finished with sweet soy.

steps.text: Rinse the rice and bring to a boil in the water in a heavy lidded pot, then simmer covered 10 minutes.
Lay the sausage and mushrooms over the rice, cover and cook on low for 15 minutes.
Stir the soy sauce, sugar and sesame oil with 2 tbsp water.
Drizzle the vegetable oil down the side and cook 2 minutes uncovered to crisp the base, adding the bok choy for the last minute.
Pour over the sauce and toss until the rice is evenly coated, then serve.

notes: Food safety: cook the sausage to 75°C until steaming hot throughout. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Chirashi Sushi Scattered Rice Bowl with Egg Ribbons
summary: Vinegared rice scattered with cooked prawns, egg ribbons, cucumber and nori; no raw fish, family friendly.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes, and fold in the vinegar and sugar while warm.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt, cook thin omelettes in the oil until set, cool and cut into ribbons.
Spread the rice in bowls and arrange the prawns, egg ribbons, cucumber and carrot on top.
Scatter with nori and sesame seeds and serve with the soy sauce.

notes: Food safety: use prawns that are cooked and kept chilled until serving, and cook the eggs until set. Contains egg and shellfish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Gaeng Som Southern Thai Sour Fish Curry
summary: A thin, sharp and fiery orange curry of white fish and vegetables with no coconut, tangy with tamarind.

items.raw: 600g firm white fish fillet, cut into chunks

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Stir the curry paste into the water in a pot and bring to a boil until the water turns deep orange.
Add the tamarind, fish sauce, sugar, carrot and cabbage and simmer for 8 minutes until the carrot is tender.
Add the beans and fish and simmer gently for 5 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily at 63°C.
Taste for sour, salty and sweet balance and serve in bowls with the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Gaeng Panang Thai Peanut Beef Curry
summary: A thick, mild, sweet-salty coconut curry of tender beef with peanut and lime leaf.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Simmer half the coconut milk with the curry paste in a wide pan for 5 minutes until the oil separates.
Add the beef, fish sauce and sugar and cook 5 minutes, then stir in the remaining coconut milk, peanut butter and lime leaves.
Simmer for 10 minutes until the beef is tender and reaches 71°C, adding the capsicum for the last 4 minutes.
Spoon the curry over the rice, spoon the thickened coconut cream from the top of the pan and serve while hot.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef to at least 71°C. Contains peanuts and fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Kai Palo Thai Five-Spice Egg and Pork Stew
summary: Hard-boiled eggs and pork belly in a sweet five-spice broth, served over rice with pickled greens.

steps.text: Hard-boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool in cold water and peel.
Simmer the pork in the water with soy sauce, sugar, five-spice, garlic and fish sauce for 30 minutes until the pork is tender and reaches 70°C.
Add the eggs and simmer for 10 minutes until the eggs are tinted brown and the sauce is glossy.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy and serve with the stew spooned over.

notes: Food safety: simmer the pork to at least 70°C and hard-boil the eggs. Contains egg and fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Or Lam Luang Prabang Smoky Eggplant Stew
summary: A Lao stew of pork, eggplant and beans thickened with ground rice and perfumed with dill.

steps.text: Crush the garlic, shallots and chillies to a paste.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Simmer the pork in the water with the paste and fish sauce for 20 minutes.
Add the eggplant and ground rice and simmer for 10 minutes until the eggplant is tender and the stew thickens.
Add the beans for the last 4 minutes, check the pork reaches 70°C and is tender, then stir through the dill.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork to at least 70°C. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Nom Banh Chok Khmer Fish Gravy Noodles
summary: Fresh rice noodles with a lemongrass and turmeric fish gravy and a platter of raw herbs and vegetables.

steps.text: Simmer the fish in the water for 8 minutes until opaque and flaking at 63°C, then flake it apart.
Blend the fish with the lemongrass, turmeric, garlic and ginger to a rough paste.
Return to the pot with the cooking water, fish sauce and coconut milk and simmer 12 minutes until thick.
Cook the noodles until tender, about 4 minutes, and drain.
Pile the noodles into bowls, ladle over the gravy and serve with the cucumber, sprouts and mint.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Shan Khao Swe Burmese Chicken Noodles
summary: Noodles in a mild tomato and turmeric chicken sauce, topped with crisp garlic and pickled greens.

steps.text: Fry the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes until golden.
Add the turmeric, tomatoes and chicken and cook 6 minutes, stirring.
Pour in the water and fish sauce and simmer 15 minutes until the chicken reaches 75°C and the sauce thickens.
Cook the noodles until tender, about 4 minutes, and divide into bowls.
Spoon over the chicken sauce and scatter with peanuts and coriander.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C in the centre. Contains peanuts and fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Ohn No Khao Swe Burmese Coconut Chicken Noodle Soup
summary: The signature Burmese coconut chicken noodle soup, golden and soothing, topped with boiled egg and chilli.

items.raw: 600g chicken thigh fillets, cut into chunks

steps.text: Hard-boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool and peel.
Blend the onion, garlic and ginger, fry in a pot with the turmeric for 5 minutes.
Add the chicken, stock, coconut milk and fish sauce and simmer for 20 minutes until the chicken reaches 75°C.
Stir the chickpea flour with 1/4 cup cold water, add and simmer 5 minutes until the soup thickens.
Boil the noodles until tender, about 4 minutes, divide into bowls, ladle over the soup and top with halved eggs and lime.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C in the centre and hard-boil the eggs. Contains egg, gluten and fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Canh Chua Ca Southern Vietnamese Sour Fish Soup
summary: A sweet-sour tamarind soup of fish, tomato and pineapple with sprouts and herbs.

items.raw: 500g firm white fish fillet, cut into chunks

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Bring the water, tamarind, garlic, fish sauce and sugar to a simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and pineapple and simmer 4 minutes.
Add the fish and cook gently for 5 minutes until opaque and flaking at 63°C.
Stir through the sprouts and coriander and serve with the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Nasi Goreng Kampung Anchovy Fried Rice
summary: Village-style fried rice with chilli, anchovies and greens, topped with a fried egg.

steps.text: Crush the shallots, garlic and chillies to a paste.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok and fry the paste and anchovies for 2 minutes.
Add the beans and rice and fry on high for 5 minutes, stirring until piping hot, then add the kecap manis.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil until the whites are set.
Top each serve with an egg.

notes: Food safety: use rice that was chilled within 1 hour of cooking, reheat until steaming hot, and fry the eggs until the whites are set. Contains egg and fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Bak Kut Teh Klang Herbal Pork Rib Soup
summary: A peppery garlic and herb pork rib soup, simmered long and eaten with rice and dark soy.

steps.text: Blanch the ribs in boiling water for 5 minutes, drain and rinse.
Simmer the ribs in the 8 cups water with the garlic, spice mix, soy sauce and pepper for 75 minutes until the meat is tender and reaches 70°C.
Add the tofu puffs and simmer 8 minutes.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy and blanch the bok choy for 2 minutes.
Serve the soup with the rice, bok choy and the dark soy for dipping.

notes: Food safety: simmer the ribs until tender and at least 70°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Chilli Prawns Singapore Sweet-Tangy Style
summary: Prawns in a sweet-tangy tomato chilli sauce with a ribboned egg, mopped up with rice or buns.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Fry the garlic, ginger and chillies in the oil for 1 minute, then add the prawns and cook 3 minutes until pink and curled.
Stir the tomato sauce, sweet chilli sauce, cornflour and water together and pour in, simmering 2 minutes until glossy.
Stir the beaten egg slowly into the sauce and cook 1 minute until it forms ribbons and sets.
Spoon the prawns and sauce over the rice, scatter with the remaining egg ribbons and serve while hot.

notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until pink and opaque, at least 63°C inside, and the eggs until set. Contains egg and shellfish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Tinolang Manok Filipino Ginger Chicken Soup
summary: A clear ginger and chicken soup with green papaya-style chayote and leafy greens, plain and restorative.

steps.text: Fry the onion, garlic and ginger in the oil for 4 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chicken and fish sauce and cook 4 minutes.
Pour in the water and simmer for 20 minutes until the chicken reaches 75°C.
Add the chayote and simmer 8 minutes until tender, then stir in the spinach for 1 minute.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy and serve alongside.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C at the thickest part. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Egg Kari Mamak Malaysian Egg Curry
summary: Boiled eggs in a spiced tomato and coconut gravy, mopped up with rice.

steps.text: Hard-boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool and peel.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Fry the onion, garlic and ginger in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, then stir in the curry powder for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, coconut milk and water and simmer 12 minutes until thick.
Slide in the eggs, warm 3 minutes and serve with the rice.

notes: Food safety: hard-boil the eggs until the yolk is firm. Contains egg. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Kai Jeow Moo Sap Thai Pork Omelette Rice Bowl
summary: A puffy, crisp-edged omelette with minced pork over rice, drizzled with a salty-sweet sauce.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Beat the eggs with the fish sauce and soy sauce and stir through the pork.
Heat the oil in a wok until shimmering and pour in the egg mix from a height.
Fry for 2 minutes per side until puffed, golden and the pork reaches 75°C, then drain on paper.
Serve over the rice with the sweet chilli sauce and cucumber.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork mince to 75°C and the eggs until set. Contains egg and fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Mee Rebus Mamak Sweet Potato Gravy Noodles
summary: Yellow noodles in a thick sweet-potato and peanut gravy topped with egg, tofu and lime.

steps.text: Hard-boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool and peel.
Boil the sweet potato in the water for 12 minutes until soft, then blend with the peanuts, shallots and garlic.
Fry the curry powder in the oil for 1 minute, add the blended gravy and soy sauce and simmer 12 minutes until thick.
Boil the noodles until tender, about 4 minutes, and divide into bowls.
Pour over the gravy and top with halved egg, tofu and lime.

notes: Food safety: hard-boil the eggs until the yolk is firm. Contains egg, gluten and peanuts. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Bun Rieu Cua Vietnamese Tomato Crab-Style Noodle Soup
summary: A tomato broth with soft prawn-and-egg cakes, tofu and rice noodles.

items.raw: 400g raw prawns, peeled and finely chopped

steps.text: Mix the prawns, eggs and 1 tsp fish sauce into a paste.
Fry the shallots and tomatoes in the oil for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the water, tamarind and remaining fish sauce and bring to a simmer until steaming.
Drop spoonfuls of the prawn mix into the broth and simmer 8 minutes until the cakes float, are firm and pink, then add the tofu.
Cook the noodles until tender, about 4 minutes, and serve with broth, cakes and sprouts.

notes: Food safety: cook the prawn cakes until firm and pink, at least 63°C inside, and the eggs until set. Contains egg, fish and shellfish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Pho Ga Hanoi Chicken Noodle Soup
summary: A clear chicken broth with ginger, onion and star anise over rice noodles and herbs.

steps.text: Char the onion and ginger in a dry pan for 5 minutes.
Simmer the chicken with the onion, ginger, star anise and water for 40 minutes until the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Lift out the chicken, shred the meat and strain the broth, seasoning with fish sauce and 1 tsp salt.
Cook the noodles until tender, about 4 minutes, and divide into bowls.
Top with the chicken, ladle over the hot broth and serve with spring onion, coriander, sprouts and lime.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C at the thickest part. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Cha Ca La Vong Turmeric Fish with Dill
summary: Hanoi turmeric fish seared with dill and spring onion, served over noodles with peanuts and fish dip.

items.raw: 700g firm white fish fillet, cut into chunks

steps.text: Toss the fish with the turmeric, ginger and 1 tsp salt.
Cook the noodles until tender, about 4 minutes, and drain.
Stir the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar and 2 tbsp water into a dip.
Sear the fish in the oil for 6 minutes until golden and opaque, flaking easily at 63°C.
Toss in the dill and spring onions for 1 minute, then serve over the noodles with peanuts and the dip.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C. Contains fish and peanuts. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Gaeng Hung Lay Northern Thai Pork Belly Curry
summary: A dry-spiced Chiang Mai pork curry with ginger and tamarind, sweet-sour and rich, with no coconut milk.

steps.text: Fry the curry paste in a dry heavy pot for 3 minutes, then add the pork and brown for 6 minutes.
Add the water, tamarind, sugar, fish sauce and soy sauce and simmer, covered, for 50 minutes until the pork is tender.
Add the ginger and garlic and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes until the sauce is thick and the pork reaches 70°C.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Scatter the curry with peanuts and serve spooned over the rice with a little of the glossy sauce.

notes: Food safety: simmer the pork until tender and at least 70°C. Contains peanuts and fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Mie Aceh Spicy Curried Prawn Noodles
summary: Thick noodles in a spicy, curry-spiced tomato sauce with prawns, from the Sumatran coast.

steps.text: Blend the shallots, garlic and chillies to a paste.
Boil the noodles until tender, about 4 minutes, and drain.
Fry the paste and curry powder in the oil for 4 minutes, add the tomatoes and cook 4 minutes until soft.
Add the prawns, water and kecap manis and cook 4 minutes until the prawns turn pink and opaque.
Push to the side, scramble the eggs until set, toss in the noodles and sprouts for 2 minutes until hot and coated.

notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until pink and opaque, at least 63°C inside, and the eggs until set. Contains egg, gluten and shellfish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Rajma Chawal Punjabi Kidney Beans with Rice
summary: Soft kidney beans in a thick onion and tomato gravy, pressure-cooked and served over rice.

items.raw: 300g dried kidney beans, soaked overnight and drained

steps.text: Boil the soaked beans hard in fresh water for 10 minutes to destroy the natural toxins, drain, then pressure-cook in the 4 cups water with 1 tsp salt for 25 minutes at high pressure until completely soft, then release the pressure.
Fry the onions in the oil for 8 minutes until golden, then add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Stir in the turmeric, cumin and tomatoes and cook 8 minutes until the oil separates.
Tip in the beans with their liquid, add the garam masala and simmer 10 minutes until the gravy is thick.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes, and serve with the beans.

title: Sambar Rice Plate Tamil Lentil and Vegetable Stew
summary: A tamarind-sour lentil stew with drumstick-style vegetables, pressure-cooked and eaten over rice.

steps.text: Pressure-cook the lentils with the water and turmeric for 12 minutes at high pressure until they are completely soft, then release the pressure and mash lightly.
Add the onion, carrots, eggplant, tomatoes, tamarind and curry powder and simmer for 15 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Heat the oil, pop the mustard seeds until they crackle and stir into the pot.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Serve the sambar over the rice.

title: Bisi Bele Bath Karnataka Spiced Lentil Rice
summary: A one-pot hot lentil rice with vegetables, tamarind and a roasted spice blend, finished with ghee.

steps.text: Pressure-cook the lentils, rice and water with the turmeric for 15 minutes at high pressure until completely soft and mushy.
Release the pressure and stir in the vegetables, tamarind, spice mix and 1 tsp salt.
Simmer for 15 minutes until the vegetables are soft and the mixture is thick like porridge, adding hot water if too stiff.
Heat the ghee, pop the mustard seeds until they crackle and pour over the top.

title: Thukpa Gyathuk Tibetan Chicken Noodle Soup
summary: A comforting Tibetan noodle soup with chicken, vegetables and ginger.

steps.text: Fry the onion, ginger and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the chicken and cook 4 minutes, then pour in the water, soy sauce and pepper.
Simmer for 15 minutes until the chicken reaches 75°C, adding the carrots for the last 8 minutes.
Add the noodles and bok choy and cook 4 minutes until tender.
Ladle into bowls and top with spring onions.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C in the centre. Contains gluten. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Shapta Tibetan Stir-Fried Beef with Capsicum
summary: Quick stir-fried beef with onion, capsicum and chilli, served with rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Sear the beef in 1 tbsp hot oil for 3 minutes in two batches until browned, then set aside.
Fry the onion, capsicums, garlic, ginger and chillies in the remaining oil for 5 minutes.
Return the beef, add the soy sauce and peppercorns and toss for 2 minutes until the beef reaches 71°C.
Spoon the beef and vegetables over the rice and serve straight away while the capsicum is still crisp.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef to at least 71°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Chicken Haleem Pakistani Slow-Cooked Wheat and Lentil Stew
summary: A thick, spiced porridge-like stew of chicken, wheat and lentils, topped with ginger and fried onion.

steps.text: Rinse the wheat and lentils, then pressure-cook with the water, turmeric and 1 tsp salt for 30 minutes at high pressure until completely soft.
Fry one onion in 2 tbsp oil until golden, add the ginger, garlic and chicken and cook 8 minutes until the chicken reaches 75°C.
Stir the chicken mix and spices into the cooked wheat, simmer 20 minutes and beat with a wooden spoon until thick and smooth.
Fry the second onion in the remaining oil for 10 minutes until crisp.
Serve topped with fried onion, ginger and lemon.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C in the centre. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Karahi Gosht Peshawari Lamb
summary: A simple Peshawari lamb karahi with tomato, ginger and black pepper, no onion, eaten with flatbread.

steps.text: Heat the ghee in a karahi or heavy pan and sear the lamb in batches for 8 minutes until browned.
Add the garlic and half the ginger and fry 2 minutes, then the tomatoes, chillies, pepper, cumin and 1 tsp salt.
Cover and cook on low for 35 minutes until the lamb is tender and reaches 71°C and the oil separates.
Stir in the coriander and the remaining ginger and serve with the flatbreads.

notes: Food safety: cook the lamb to at least 71°C. Contains milk and gluten. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Plov Uzbek Carrot and Beef Rice
summary: The festive Uzbek rice pilaf of beef, carrot and chickpeas cooked under a lid.

items.raw: 1 whole garlic bulb, top sliced off

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large heavy pot and brown the beef for 8 minutes, then add the onions and cook 8 minutes until golden.
Add the carrots and cumin and fry 6 minutes, then pour in half the water and 1 tsp salt and simmer, covered, for 30 minutes until the beef is tender and reaches 71°C.
Rinse the rice, spread over the meat, add the chickpeas, remaining water and garlic bulb pressed into the centre.
Cover and cook on low for 20 minutes until the rice is tender and the water is absorbed.
Rest 10 minutes, then mix gently and serve.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef to at least 71°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Lagman Uzbek Beef and Vegetable Noodle Stew
summary: Hand-pulled style noodles under a thick beef, capsicum and tomato stew.

steps.text: Brown the beef in the oil for 8 minutes, then add the onions and cook 5 minutes.
Add the carrots, capsicums, garlic, tomato paste and cumin and cook 4 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and water and simmer for 30 minutes until the beef is tender and reaches 71°C.
Boil the noodles until tender, about 4 minutes, and drain.
Serve the stew over the noodles.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef to at least 71°C. Contains gluten. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Dal Tadka Pressure-Cooker Yellow Lentils with Tempering
summary: Creamy yellow lentils finished with a sizzling garlic, cumin and chilli tempering.

steps.text: Pressure-cook the lentils with the water, turmeric, tomato and 1 tsp salt for 12 minutes at high pressure until completely soft, then release the pressure and whisk smooth.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Heat the ghee, fry the cumin seeds until they crackle, then add the onion and cook 5 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic and chillies for 1 minute and pour the sizzling mix over the dal.
Scatter with coriander and serve with the rice.

notes: Contains milk.

title: Anda Curry Spiced Egg Curry
summary: Boiled eggs in a thick onion and tomato gravy with garam masala.

steps.text: Hard-boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool and peel, then score lightly.
Fry the onions in the oil for 8 minutes until golden, then add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Stir in the spices and tomatoes and cook 8 minutes until the oil separates.
Add the water and simmer 5 minutes, slide in the eggs and warm 3 minutes.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes, and serve with the curry.

notes: Food safety: hard-boil the eggs until the yolk is firm. Contains egg. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Bhuna Khichuri Bengali Roasted Lentil Rice
summary: A rainy-day Bengali rice and lentil dish with vegetables and ghee, pressure-cooked.

steps.text: Dry-roast the lentils in a pot for 4 minutes until fragrant and light golden.
Melt the ghee, fry the cumin and bay leaves until the seeds crackle, then add the ginger and turmeric.
Add the rice, lentils, vegetables, water and 1 tsp salt and pressure-cook for 10 minutes at high pressure until soft.
Release the pressure, stir well and serve thick and porridge-like.

notes: Contains milk.

title: Nihari Pakistani Slow-Braised Beef Shank
summary: A rich, silky beef braise in a gingery spiced gravy, traditional for festive breakfasts and Eid.

steps.text: Fry the onions in the ghee for 15 minutes until deep brown.
Add the beef, grated ginger, garlic and spices and brown for 8 minutes.
Pour in the water, bring to a simmer and cook, covered, for 2 hours until the meat is falling apart and reaches 71°C.
Stir the flour with 1/2 cup water until smooth, add to the pot and simmer 10 minutes until the gravy is glossy.
Serve topped with ginger matchsticks and lemon.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef to at least 71°C. Contains milk and gluten. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Aloo Gosht Pakistani Lamb and Potato Curry
summary: Everyday lamb and potato curry, pressure-cooked until tender.

steps.text: Fry the onions in the oil for 8 minutes until golden, then add the garlic and ginger.
Add the lamb and spices and brown for 6 minutes, then stir in the tomatoes.
Add the water and pressure-cook for 20 minutes at high pressure until the lamb is tender and reaches 71°C.
Release the pressure, add the potatoes and simmer 12 minutes until tender.
Serve with the flatbreads.

notes: Food safety: cook the lamb to at least 71°C. Contains gluten. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Kofta Challow Afghan Meatballs with Rice
summary: Spiced beef meatballs in a tomato sauce over fragrant rice.

steps.text: Mix the beef, grated onion, spices, coriander and egg with 1 tsp salt and roll into 16 balls.
Fry the chopped onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add the tomatoes and paste and cook 6 minutes.
Add the water, bring to a simmer and add the meatballs, cooking gently for 20 minutes until the meatballs reach 75°C inside.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Serve the meatballs and sauce over the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the meatballs to 75°C in the centre. Contains egg. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Borani Banjan Afghan Eggplant with Garlic Yoghurt
summary: Fried eggplant in a tomato sauce, topped with garlic yoghurt and dried mint, served with flatbread.

steps.text: Brush the eggplant slices with 3 tbsp oil and roast at 220°C for 25 minutes until soft and golden.
Fry the onion in the remaining oil for 5 minutes, add the turmeric and tomatoes and cook 12 minutes until jammy.
Layer the eggplant in a dish, spoon the tomato sauce over and simmer 5 minutes.
Mix the yoghurt with the garlic and a pinch of salt, spoon over the top and dust with mint.
Serve warm with the flatbreads.

notes: Contains milk and gluten.

title: Sabzi Challow Afghan Spinach and Lamb
summary: A slow-cooked spinach and lamb stew, deeply green, served with rice.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil for 8 minutes, add the onion and cook 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, coriander, turmeric and water, cover and simmer for 30 minutes until the lamb is tender.
Stir in the spinach in handfuls and cook 10 minutes until the stew is thick and the lamb reaches 71°C.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Finish the stew with lemon juice and serve over the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the lamb to at least 71°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Shurpa Uzbek Lamb and Vegetable Soup
summary: A clear, hearty lamb soup with big chunks of potato, carrot and tomato.

items.raw: 700g lamb shoulder, cut into large pieces

steps.text: Simmer the lamb in the water with the onions and 1 tsp salt for 45 minutes, skimming, until nearly tender.
Add the carrots and potatoes and simmer 15 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, capsicums and cumin and simmer 8 minutes until all the vegetables are tender and the lamb reaches 71°C.
Stir through the dill and serve in large bowls.

notes: Food safety: cook the lamb to at least 71°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Dimlama Uzbek Layered Lamb and Vegetable Pot
summary: A layered pot of lamb, potato, carrot and cabbage steamed in its own juices with no stirring.

steps.text: Layer the onions, then the lamb, cumin and 2 tsp salt, in a heavy lidded pot brushed with oil.
Layer in the potatoes, carrots, cabbage, tomatoes and garlic, drizzle with oil and add the water.
Cover tightly and cook on very low heat for 90 minutes without stirring until the lamb is tender and reaches 71°C.
Rest 10 minutes and serve straight from the pot.

notes: Food safety: cook the lamb to at least 71°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Sekuwa Nepali Grilled Chicken Thigh Skewers
summary: Spice-rubbed chicken grilled until charred, served with rice and sliced onion.

items.raw: 800g chicken thigh fillets, cut into chunks

steps.text: Mix the chicken with the yoghurt, ginger, garlic, spices, oil and 1 tsp salt.
Thread onto metal skewers and grill or barbecue over a high heat for 14 minutes, turning, until charred and the chicken reaches 75°C.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Serve the sekuwa with rice, onion and lemon.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C in the centre. Contains milk. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Thenthuk Tibetan Hand-Torn Noodle Soup with Beef
summary: Torn dough noodles in a spiced beef and vegetable broth.

steps.text: Knead the flour with the 150ml water and 1/2 tsp salt into a firm dough and rest 20 minutes under a damp cloth.
Fry the onion, garlic and ginger in the oil for 5 minutes, add the beef and cook 3 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, soy sauce and 5 cups water and simmer 12 minutes until the beef reaches 71°C.
Flatten and tear the dough into thin pieces, drop them in and cook 5 minutes until tender, adding the spinach for the last minute.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef to at least 71°C. Contains gluten. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Shapaley Tibetan Beef Pasties
summary: Crisp half-moon pastries filled with spiced minced beef and onion.

steps.text: Knead the flour, water and 1/2 tsp salt into a smooth dough and rest 20 minutes under a damp cloth.
Mix the beef, onion, garlic, ginger, pepper and soy sauce into a filling.
Roll the dough thin, cut into 10cm rounds, fill each, fold over and crimp the edges.
Fry in oil heated to 170°C for 3 minutes per side until deep golden and the filling reaches 75°C.
Drain on paper and serve hot.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef filling to 75°C in the centre. Contains gluten. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Egusi Soup Nigerian Melon Seed Stew with Beef
summary: A thick, nutty ground melon seed stew with spinach and beef, traditionally eaten with pounded yam or rice.

steps.text: Simmer the beef in the stock with half the onion and 1 tsp salt for 25 minutes until tender and at least 71°C.
Heat the oil, fry the remaining onion for 5 minutes, then add the tomato and capsicum purée and cook 12 minutes until reduced and the oil separates.
Mix the pumpkin seeds with 1/2 cup water to a paste and drop spoonfuls into the sauce, cooking 8 minutes without stirring until set into curds.
Add the beef with its stock, chilli and dried shrimp and simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in the spinach for 2 minutes until wilted, cook the rice until tender and fluffy and serve alongside.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef to at least 71°C. Contains shellfish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Suya Spiced Beef Skewers with Peanut Rub
summary: Nigerian street skewers dusted with peanut-chilli spice, served with onion, tomato and rice.

steps.text: Mix the peanuts, paprika, chilli, ginger, garlic powder and 1 tsp salt.
Toss the beef with the oil and two-thirds of the spice mix and thread onto metal skewers.
Grill or barbecue over high heat for 8 minutes, turning, until charred and the beef reaches 71°C.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Dust the skewers with the remaining spice and serve with the rice, onion and tomato.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef to at least 71°C. Contains peanuts. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Mafe Senegalese Peanut Stew with Chicken
summary: A rich peanut and tomato stew with chicken and sweet potato, served over rice.

items.raw: 700g chicken thigh fillets, cut into chunks

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil for 6 minutes and set aside.
Fry the onion and garlic in the same pot for 5 minutes, add the tomatoes and tomato paste and cook 6 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter into the stock, add to the pot with the chicken, sweet potatoes and carrots.
Simmer for 25 minutes until the vegetables are tender and the chicken reaches 75°C.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy and serve with the stew.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C in the centre. Contains peanuts. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Yassa Poulet Senegalese Lemon Onion Chicken
summary: Chicken braised under a mountain of caramelised onions with mustard and lemon, over rice.

steps.text: Grill the drumsticks for 12 minutes, turning, until browned and nearly cooked through.
Cook the onions in the oil for 15 minutes over medium heat until very soft and golden.
Stir in the garlic, mustard, lemon juice and stock and add the chicken and chillies.
Cover and simmer 15 minutes until the chicken reaches 75°C and the sauce is thick.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy and serve with the chicken and onions.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C at the thickest part. Contains mustard. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Ndole Cameroonian Peanut and Greens Stew with Prawns
summary: A creamy peanut stew with greens and prawns, a Cameroon celebration dish.

steps.text: Blend the onion, garlic and ginger with a splash of water.
Fry the purée in the oil for 6 minutes until the water cooks away.
Whisk the peanut butter into the water and add with the spinach and chilli, simmering 20 minutes until the greens are soft and the sauce thickens.
Add the prawns and cook 4 minutes until pink and opaque.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy and serve with the stew.

notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until pink and opaque, at least 63°C inside. Contains peanuts and shellfish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Gomen Besiga Ethiopian Collards with Beef
summary: Slow-cooked silverbeet-style greens with beef, ginger and garlic.

steps.text: Brown the beef in the oil for 8 minutes and add the onion for 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger and water, cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the beef is nearly tender.
Stir in the silverbeet and chilli and cook, covered, for 12 minutes until the greens are soft and the beef reaches 71°C.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy and serve alongside.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef to at least 71°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Pilau ya Nyama Kenyan Spiced Beef Rice
summary: Fragrant Swahili-coast pilau with beef, cumin and cardamom, a festive staple.

steps.text: Fry the onions in the oil for 12 minutes until deep brown.
Add the beef, garlic, ginger and spices and brown for 8 minutes.
Add 1 cup stock, cover and simmer 25 minutes until the beef is tender and reaches 71°C.
Add the rinsed rice and remaining stock, bring to a boil, then cover and cook on low for 15 minutes until the rice is tender and fluffy.
Rest 5 minutes and fluff before serving.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef to at least 71°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Lu Sipi Samoan Lamb in Coconut Cream
summary: Lamb slow-cooked in coconut cream with onion until the sauce is rich and sweet, served with rice and sweet potato.

steps.text: Fry the onion, garlic and ginger in a dry heavy pot for 5 minutes.
Add the lamb and water, cover and simmer for 40 minutes until the lamb is nearly tender.
Stir in the coconut cream and sweet potatoes and simmer uncovered for 25 minutes until the sauce thickens, the sweet potato is soft and the lamb reaches 71°C.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy and serve with the lamb.

notes: Food safety: cook the lamb to at least 71°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Sapasui Samoan Beef Chop Suey Noodles
summary: Glass noodles tossed with beef, ginger and soy, a staple of every Samoan gathering.

steps.text: Soak the noodles in hot water for 8 minutes until pliable, then drain.
Fry the onion, garlic and ginger in the oil for 4 minutes, add the beef and stir-fry 4 minutes until browned.
Add the carrots, soy sauce and water and simmer 6 minutes.
Toss in the noodles for 3 minutes until tender and the beef reaches 71°C.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef to at least 71°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Kare Raisu Tofu Katsu Curry Plate
summary: Crumbed pan-fried tofu with a mild Japanese-style curry sauce over rice, fully vegan.

steps.text: Press the tofu on paper towels for 10 minutes to remove water.
Cook the onion, carrots and potatoes in 1 tbsp oil for 5 minutes, stir in the curry powder and 2 tbsp flour for 1 minute, then add the stock and soy sauce.
Simmer the sauce for 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the sauce is thick.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Dip the tofu in flour, soy milk then breadcrumbs and shallow-fry in the remaining oil for 3 minutes per side until crisp and golden. Slice and serve over the rice with the sauce.

title: Agedashi Tofu Donburi with Mushrooms
summary: Crisp-coated tofu in a savoury soy broth over rice with mushrooms and spring onion; fully vegan.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Pat the tofu dry, coat in starch and shallow-fry in the oil for 5 minutes until crisp and pale gold.
Simmer the mushrooms with the water, soy sauce and mirin for 4 minutes until soft.
Spoon the rice into bowls, top with tofu and ladle over the mushroom broth.
Scatter with spring onion and serve at once while the coating is still crisp.

title: Kimchi Dubu Jjigae Vegan-Style Tofu Stew
summary: A bubbling tofu and kimchi stew with mushrooms, finished with sesame oil.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Fry the kimchi in the sesame oil for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the water, gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce and mushrooms and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the tofu and simmer 6 minutes until heated through, then stir in the spring onions.
Serve in the pot with the rice.

title: Gyeran Mari Rolled Omelette and Rice Bowl
summary: A neat layered omelette with carrot and spring onion over rice with soy dressing.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and stir in the carrot and spring onions.
Pour a thin layer into an oiled non-stick pan, cook until almost set, roll it up, then pour more egg and roll again, repeating until used.
Cook each layer for 2 minutes until set and the roll is firm in the centre.
Slice the roll, serve over the rice and drizzle with soy sauce, sesame oil and seeds.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until fully set. Contains egg. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Pad Kra Pao Tofu Holy Basil Rice Bowl
summary: Stir-fried tofu with chilli, garlic and basil over rice with a fried egg; the egg can be left out for vegan.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Crush the garlic and chillies together.
Fry the tofu in 1 tbsp oil for 6 minutes until golden and set aside.
Stir-fry the garlic and chillies for 30 seconds, add the tofu, soy sauce and sugar and toss 2 minutes until glossy.
Fold in the basil, fry the eggs in the remaining oil until the whites are set, and serve everything over the rice.

notes: Food safety: fry the eggs until the whites are fully set. Contains egg. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Doenjang Jjigae Korean Soybean Paste Stew
summary: A savoury fermented soybean stew with zucchini, tofu and potato.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Stir the doenjang into the water in a pot, add the potatoes and onion and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the zucchini, mushrooms, garlic and gochugaru and simmer 6 minutes until the potato is tender.
Add the tofu and spring onions for 3 minutes and serve with the rice.

title: Hayashi Rice Japanese Beef and Red Wine Stew
summary: A rich beef and onion stew in a glossy tomato and demi-glace-style sauce over rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Melt the butter, brown the beef for 6 minutes, then add the onions and mushrooms for 8 minutes.
Stir in the flour and tomato paste for 1 minute, then add the stock, tomato sauce and worcestershire.
Simmer 25 minutes until the sauce is thick and glossy and the beef reaches 71°C.
Spoon the beef and its glossy sauce over the rice and serve straight away.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef to at least 71°C. Contains milk and gluten. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Japchae Korean Glass Noodle Stir-Fry with Beef
summary: Chewy sweet potato noodles stir-fried with beef and colourful vegetables in a sesame-soy glaze.

steps.text: Boil the noodles for 6 minutes until tender and chewy, drain and toss with 1 tbsp sesame oil.
Blanch the spinach for 1 minute, squeeze dry and season with a little soy sauce.
Stir-fry the beef with half the soy, sugar and garlic for 4 minutes until it reaches 71°C.
Stir-fry the carrot, onion and mushrooms in the remaining oil for 5 minutes.
Toss everything with the noodles, remaining soy and sugar for 2 minutes, then sprinkle with sesame seeds.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef to at least 71°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Samgyetang Ginseng Chicken and Rice Soup
summary: A whole small chicken stuffed with rice and garlic, simmered in a delicate broth.

steps.text: Rinse the rice, then stuff each chicken with rice, and garlic and tie the legs together.
Place in a pot with the water and ginger, bring to a boil, then simmer, covered, for 50 minutes until the chicken reaches 75°C at the thickest part.
Season the broth with 1 tsp salt and ladle around each chicken.
Serve scattered with spring onions.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C at the thickest part, including the stuffing. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Yukgaejang Spicy Shredded Beef Soup
summary: A fiery brisket and vegetable soup, with plenty of spring onion and greens.

steps.text: Simmer the brisket in the water for 45 minutes until tender and at least 71°C, then lift out and shred.
Fry the garlic and gochugaru in the sesame oil for 1 minute.
Return the beef to the broth with the garlic mix, soy sauce, sprouts, spinach and spring onions and simmer 8 minutes.
Stream in the beaten egg and stir until it forms strands and sets, about 1 minute.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef to at least 71°C and the egg until set. Contains egg. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Tteokbokki Korean Chilli Rice Cakes with Eggs
summary: Chewy rice cakes in a sweet, spicy gochujang sauce with fish cake and boiled egg.

steps.text: Hard-boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool and peel.
Bring the water, gochujang, gochugaru, sugar and soy sauce to a boil in a wide pan until the sauce is smooth.
Add the rice cakes and fish cake and simmer for 10 minutes, stirring, until the rice cakes are soft and chewy and the sauce is thick.
Add the eggs and spring onions for the last 2 minutes.

notes: Food safety: hard-boil the eggs until the yolk is firm. Contains egg, fish and gluten. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Bobotie Cape Malay Spiced Mince with Egg Custard
summary: South African curried mince baked under an egg custard topping, served with rice and chutney.

steps.text: Fry the onions in the oil for 6 minutes, add the mince and cook 8 minutes until browned.
Squeeze the milk from the bread (keep the milk), mash the bread and stir into the mince with the curry powder, jam, vinegar, sultanas and 1 tsp salt.
Press into a baking dish and bake at 180°C for 20 minutes.
Whisk the saved milk with the eggs, pour over the top, add the bay leaves and bake 20 minutes until the custard is set and the mince reaches 75°C.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy and serve with the bobotie.

notes: Food safety: cook the mince to 75°C in the centre and the custard until set. Contains milk, egg and gluten. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Suan Cai Bai Rou Northeastern Pickled Cabbage and Pork Pot
summary: A tangy Dongbei pot of pickled cabbage, pork belly slices and glass noodles that melt into a sour-savoury broth.

steps.text: Simmer the pork in the water with the ginger for 15 minutes until it turns opaque and firm.
Add the pickled cabbage, soy sauce and sugar and simmer 15 minutes until the cabbage is soft and the pork reaches 70°C.
Add the tofu and noodles and simmer 6 minutes until the noodles are tender and glassy.
Scatter with spring onions and serve from the pot.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork to at least 70°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Hui Guo Rou Sichuan Twice-Cooked Pork with Leek
summary: Pork belly simmered, sliced and fried with leek and chilli bean paste until the edges curl.

steps.text: Simmer the pork in water for 30 minutes until a skewer slides in easily and the centre reaches 71°C, then cool and slice thinly.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Fry the pork slices in a dry wok for 5 minutes until the edges curl and the fat renders.
Push aside, add the oil, doubanjiang and garlic for 1 minute, then add the soy sauce, sugar and leeks and toss 3 minutes until the leeks are just soft.
Spoon the pork and leeks over the rice and serve while the edges are still crisp.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork to at least 70°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Yangzhou Chao Fan Egg and Prawn Fried Rice
summary: Golden egg-coated rice with prawns, ham and peas, the banquet classic.

steps.text: Beat the eggs and scramble in 1 tbsp oil for 1 minute until just set, then set aside.
Heat the remaining oil in a wok and fry the rice for 4 minutes on high until it jumps and is piping hot.
Add the ham, prawns and peas and toss 3 minutes until heated through at 75°C.
Return the egg, add the soy sauce and spring onions and toss 1 minute.

notes: Food safety: use rice that was chilled within 1 hour of cooking, reheat until steaming hot, and cook the eggs until set. Contains egg and shellfish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Jiu Cai He Zi Chive and Egg Pockets
summary: Pan-fried pastry pockets of garlic chives, egg and glass noodles.

steps.text: Mix the flour with the boiling water and 1/4 tsp salt, knead smooth and rest the dough 20 minutes covered.
Scramble the eggs until just set, soak the noodles in hot water until tender and chop, then mix both with the chives, sesame oil and soy sauce.
Roll the dough thin, cut 12cm rounds, fill, fold and crimp the edges closed.
Pan-fry in the oil for 3 minutes per side until deep golden and the filling is hot at 75°C.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until set and heat the filling to 75°C. Contains egg and gluten. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Tie Ban Dou Fu Sizzling Hotplate Tofu
summary: Golden tofu sizzled with mushrooms and capsicum in a soy-ginger sauce; fully vegan.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Fry the tofu in 2 tbsp oil for 6 minutes until golden on both sides.
Add the mushrooms, capsicum and ginger and fry 4 minutes until soft.
Stir the soy sauce, sugar, cornflour and 3 tbsp water and add, simmering 2 minutes until glossy.
Serve sizzling over the rice.

title: Jia Chang Dou Fu Home-Style Braised Tofu
summary: Golden pan-fried tofu simmered with pork, carrot and peas in a savoury sauce.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Fry the tofu in 2 tbsp oil for 6 minutes until golden and set aside.
Fry the pork and garlic in the remaining oil for 5 minutes until no pink remains and it reaches 75°C.
Add the carrot, soy sauce, oyster sauce and water and simmer 6 minutes, return the tofu and add the peas.
Thicken with the cornflour stirred in 1 tbsp water for 1 minute and serve over the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork mince to 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Shao Qie Zi Claypot Braised Eggplant with Mince
summary: Soft eggplant simmered in a garlicky mince sauce in a clay pot.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Fry the eggplant in 3 tbsp oil for 8 minutes until golden and set aside.
Fry the pork, garlic and doubanjiang in the remaining oil for 5 minutes until no pink remains and it reaches 75°C.
Add the soy sauce, sugar, water and eggplant and simmer, covered, for 10 minutes until soft.
Thicken with the cornflour stirred in 1 tbsp water, scatter with spring onions and serve with the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork mince to 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Sha Guo Dou Fu Claypot Tofu with Prawns and Mushrooms
summary: Silky tofu and prawns simmered in a ginger broth in a clay pot.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Bring the stock, ginger, soy sauce and oyster sauce to a simmer in a clay pot until fragrant.
Add the mushrooms and tofu and simmer 6 minutes.
Add the prawns and bok choy and cook 3 minutes until the prawns are pink and opaque.
Finish with the sesame oil and serve with the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until pink and opaque, at least 63°C inside. Contains shellfish and soy. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Ma Yi Shang Shu Ants Climbing a Tree Pork Noodles
summary: Glass noodles with spicy minced pork that clings like ants on a tree.

steps.text: Soak the noodles in hot water for 8 minutes until pliable, then drain.
Fry the garlic, ginger and doubanjiang in the oil for 1 minute, then add the pork and cook 5 minutes until no pink remains and it reaches 75°C.
Add the stock and soy sauce, then the noodles, and simmer 5 minutes until the liquid is absorbed.
Scatter with spring onions and serve hot.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork mince to 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Pidan Shou Rou Zhou Century Egg and Pork Congee
summary: Silky rice porridge with century egg and pork, topped with ginger and spring onion.

steps.text: Rinse the rice and simmer it with the water and ginger for 50 minutes, stirring now and then, until the grains collapse into a thick porridge.
Stir in the pork and cook 5 minutes until no pink remains and it reaches 71°C.
Add the century eggs, soy sauce and sesame oil and warm for 2 minutes.
Serve in bowls topped with spring onions.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork to at least 70°C. Use century eggs from a trusted source and keep them chilled. Contains egg. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Dan Hua Zhou Egg Drop Congee with Mushrooms
summary: Comforting egg ribbon porridge with shiitake and ginger.

steps.text: Rinse the rice and simmer it with the water and ginger for 40 minutes until the grains collapse into porridge.
Add the mushrooms and cook 5 minutes until soft.
Beat the eggs and stream them in while stirring so they form ribbons, cooking 1 minute until set.
Season with soy sauce and sesame oil and top with spring onions.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until fully set. Contains egg. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Hong Kong Prawn and Egg Scramble Rice Plate
summary: Silky eggs with prawns, spring onion and a splash of soy over rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Fry the prawns in 1 tbsp oil for 2 minutes until pink and curled, then set aside.
Beat the eggs with the wine and a pinch of salt and scramble in the remaining oil for 1 minute until barely set.
Fold in the prawns and spring onion and cook 30 seconds until the egg is set with no liquid remaining.
Spoon over the rice and drizzle with soy sauce.

notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until pink and opaque, at least 63°C inside, and the eggs until set. Contains egg and shellfish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Sizzling Black Pepper Beef Hotplate Cantonese Style
summary: Beef strips and onion in a glossy black pepper sauce, served sizzling with rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Sear the beef in 1 tbsp very hot oil for 2 minutes per batch until browned and at least 71°C.
Fry the onions and capsicum in the remaining oil for 4 minutes.
Stir the oyster sauce, soy sauce, pepper, cornflour and water together, add and simmer 2 minutes until glossy.
Return the beef, toss and serve over the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef to at least 71°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Hong Kong Soy Sauce Chicken with Ginger Oil Rice
summary: Whole chicken poached in a soy and spice liquid until glossy, served with ginger-scented rice.

steps.text: Bring the soy sauces, wine, sugar, star anise, ginger slices and water to a boil in a pot just large enough for the chicken until the sugar dissolves.
Lower the chicken in, cover and simmer very gently for 35 minutes, turning once, until the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Rest 15 minutes, then chop. Cook the rice until tender and fluffy in some strained braising liquid and water.
Heat the oil, pour over the grated ginger and a pinch of salt and spoon over the rice.
Serve the chicken with the rice and a little braising liquid.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C at the thickest part of the thigh. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Gu Lao Ji Pineapple Sweet and Sour Chicken
summary: Crisp chicken pieces in a bright sweet and sour sauce with pineapple and capsicum.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Toss the chicken in the egg, then the cornflour, and fry in the oil for 6 minutes in batches until golden and 75°C in the centre.
Simmer the tomato sauce, vinegar, sugar and soy sauce for 3 minutes until syrupy.
Toss in the pineapple and capsicum for 1 minute, add the chicken to coat and serve with the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C in the centre. Contains egg. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Jiang Cong Yu Cantonese Ginger and Spring Onion Fish
summary: Steamed white fish dressed with sizzling oil, ginger, spring onion and soy.

items.raw: 4 spring onions, cut into fine strips

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Steam the fish with the wine on a heatproof plate for 8 minutes until opaque and flaking at 63°C.
Pour off the liquid and top the fish with half the ginger and spring onion.
Heat the oil until smoking, pour it over the topping to sizzle, then add the soy sauce.
Serve with the rice and the remaining spring onion.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Luo Bo Niu Nam Daikon and Beef Brisket Claypot
summary: Brisket and radish slow-braised in an aromatic soy broth.

steps.text: Blanch the brisket in boiling water for 5 minutes, drain and rinse.
Simmer the brisket in a clay pot with the water, ginger, star anise, soy sauce, oyster sauce and sugar for 90 minutes until tender and at least 71°C.
Add the daikon and simmer 25 minutes until translucent and soft.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, scatter the stew with spring onions and serve.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef to at least 71°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Ge Zai Yu Fish and Tofu Claypot with Ginger
summary: White fish and silken tofu in a ginger broth with mushrooms and greens.

items.raw: 500g white fish fillet, cut into chunks

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Bring the water, ginger and mushrooms to a simmer in the pot until fragrant, about 8 minutes.
Add the tofu, fish and soy sauce and simmer gently for 6 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes at 63°C.
Add the bok choy for 1 minute, finish with sesame oil and serve with the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Lazi Ji Chongqing Chilli Chicken
summary: Crisp fried chicken pieces buried in dried chillies and Sichuan pepper, the Chongqing bar-snack classic.

items.raw: 600g boneless chicken thigh, cut into 2cm pieces

steps.text: Toss the chicken with the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine and cornflour until each piece is coated.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Heat the oil in a wok and shallow-fry the chicken in 2 batches for 4 minutes each, until golden and crisp. Lift out.
Wipe the wok, add a little oil if needed, Stir-fry the chillies and peppercorns for 30 seconds until fragrant but not burnt.
Add the garlic and ginger for 15 seconds, return the chicken and toss for 1 minute until well coated. Scatter with sesame and serve with the rice.

notes: Food safety: fry the chicken until the thickest piece reaches at least 75°C. Wash hands and board after raw chicken. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 15 minutes marinating. Chillies are for flavour, not for eating.

title: Gan Bian Si Ji Dou Dry-Fried Green Beans
summary: Blistered green beans with crisp pork mince, preserved vegetable and chilli, a Sichuan favourite with rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and fry the beans for 5 minutes, turning, until the skins wrinkle and blister. Lift out.
Add the pork mince and stir-fry for 3 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and cooked through.
Add the chilli bean paste, chillies and garlic for 30 seconds, then return the beans with the soy sauce and sugar and toss for 1 minute.
Finish with the sesame oil and serve with the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork mince until no pink remains and it reaches at least 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Cong You Ji Cantonese Spring Onion Ginger Chicken
summary: Poached chicken pieces under a hot oil sauce of spring onion and ginger, Cantonese banquet style.

steps.text: Put the chicken in a pot with the sliced ginger and the first tbsp of salt, cover with water and bring to a gentle simmer for 20 minutes until cooked through.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Mix the spring onions, grated ginger, 1 tsp salt and soy sauce in a heatproof bowl.
Heat the oil until just smoking and pour it over the spring onion mixture; it will sizzle for about 10 seconds.
Lift out the chicken, drain well, chop through the bones and spoon the sauce over. Serve with the rice and cucumber.

notes: Food safety: the chicken must reach at least 75°C at the thickest part and the juices run clear. Pour hot oil carefully. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Zheng Yu Cantonese Steamed Fish with Ginger and Soy
summary: Whole-fillet steamed fish with a scalding oil finish, light, clean and ready in minutes.

items.raw: 3 tbsp ginger, cut into fine matchsticks
4 spring onions, cut into fine strips

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Lay the fish on a heatproof plate, sprinkle with the Shaoxing wine and half the ginger, and steam over boiling water for 8 minutes until opaque and flaking.
Steam the bok choy beside it for the last 2 minutes until just tender.
Pour away the liquid from the plate, scatter over the spring onions and remaining ginger, and drizzle with the soy sauce.
Heat the neutral and sesame oils until shimmering and pour over the top. Serve with the rice.

notes: Food safety: steam the fish until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Fen Zheng Rou Rice-Flour Steamed Pork
summary: Pork belly coated in toasted spiced rice flour and steamed until meltingly soft, a Sichuan and Hunan home dish.

steps.text: Toast the rice, peppercorns and star anise in a dry pan for 5 minutes until golden, cool, then grind coarsely.
Mix the pork with the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, chilli bean paste, ginger and sugar. Fold in the ground rice until every slice is coated.
Lay the sweet potato in a heatproof dish and arrange the pork on top.
Steam over simmering water for 80 minutes, topping up the water as needed, until the pork is very tender.
Rest for 5 minutes, then serve straight from the dish.

notes: Food safety: the pork must reach at least 70°C throughout; steaming this long takes it well past that. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 30 minutes marinating.

title: San Bei Ji Taiwanese Three-Cup Chicken
summary: Chicken braised in a cup each of sesame oil, soy and rice wine with ginger, garlic and plenty of basil.

items.raw: 800g chicken thigh, bone in, chopped into pieces

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Heat the sesame oil in a wok over medium heat and fry the ginger, garlic and chillies for 2 minutes until golden at the edges.
Add the chicken and sear for 5 minutes, turning, until browned all over.
Add the soy sauce, rice wine and sugar, cover and cook for 12 minutes until the sauce is thick and clinging.
Toss through the basil until just wilted and serve with the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to at least 75°C at the thickest part. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Yan Su Ji Taiwanese Salt and Pepper Chicken
summary: Night-market fried chicken pieces dusted with white pepper, five-spice and salt, finished with fried basil.

items.raw: 600g boneless chicken thigh, cut into bite-size pieces

steps.text: Toss the chicken with the soy sauce and rice wine until coated.
Coat each piece well in the sweet potato flour, pressing it on, and let sit for 5 minutes so it clings.
Heat the oil in a wok and shallow-fry the chicken in batches for 4 minutes each until deep golden and crisp. Lift out.
Fry the basil and garlic in the same oil for 20 seconds until crisp, then lift out.
Toss the chicken with the pepper, five-spice and salt, and top with the basil and garlic.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches at least 75°C inside. Keep hot oil away from water. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 20 minutes marinating.

title: Tang Cu Pai Gu Sweet and Sour Spare Ribs
summary: Sticky pork ribs in a glossy black vinegar and sugar glaze, a Shanghai and Zhejiang home favourite.

items.raw: 800g pork spare ribs, cut into 4cm pieces

steps.text: Put the ribs in a pot with the ginger, cover with cold water and bring to the boil, then simmer for 5 minutes until the scum rises. Drain and rinse.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Heat the oil in a wok over low heat, add the sugar and stir for 3 minutes until amber, then add the ribs and toss to coat.
Add the vinegar, soy sauces, wine and water, cover and simmer for 35 minutes until the ribs are tender.
Uncover and boil hard for 5 minutes until the sauce is thick and sticky. Serve with the rice.
