notes: Food safety: the pork must reach at least 70°C; simmering until tender takes it well past that. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Zi Ran Yang Rou Xinjiang Cumin Lamb
summary: Fast, fierce wok-fried lamb with toasted cumin, chilli and onion, the signature flavour of Xinjiang.

items.raw: 2 tbsp cumin seeds, toasted and crushed

steps.text: Toss the lamb with the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine and cornflour. Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok over very high heat and sear the lamb in 2 batches for 2 minutes each, until browned. Lift out.
Add the remaining oil, the onion and garlic and stir-fry for 2 minutes until charred at the edges.
Return the lamb with the cumin and chilli flakes and toss for 1 minute.
Scatter with the coriander and serve with the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the lamb until it reaches at least 71°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 15 minutes marinating.

title: Bi Feng Tang Typhoon Shelter Prawns
summary: Hong Kong prawns showered in crisp garlic, chilli and fermented black beans, finished with a hot wok toss.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Pat the prawns dry and dust with the cornflour. Fry in the hot oil for 2 minutes until pink and crisp, then lift out.
Pour off all but 1 tbsp of oil. Fry the garlic for 2 minutes until golden and crisp, then lift out onto paper.
Add the black beans and chillies for 30 seconds, return the prawns, pour in the wine and toss for 1 minute.
Add the garlic, spring onions and salt, toss, and serve with the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until pink and opaque, at least 63°C. Contains shellfish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Hong Kong Baked Pork Chop Rice
summary: Cha chaan teng style: fried pork chops on egg fried rice, smothered in tomato sauce and baked until bubbling.

items.raw: 4 boneless pork loin chops, about 150g each

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes, then spread out to cool. Toss the chops with the soy sauce, pepper and cornflour and pan-fry in 1 tbsp oil for 3 minutes each side until golden. Slice.
Fry the onion in 1 tbsp oil for 4 minutes, add the passata, ketchup and sugar and simmer for 5 minutes until thick.
Scramble the eggs in the remaining oil, add the rice and stir-fry for 3 minutes until hot and loose. Spread in a baking dish.
Lay the pork on the rice, spoon over the sauce and top with the mozzarella.
Bake at 220C for 12 minutes until the cheese is golden and the sauce bubbles.

notes: Food safety: the pork must reach at least 70°C; check after baking. Cool leftover rice quickly and refrigerate within 1 hour.

title: Ebi Furai Panko Fried Prawns
summary: Straight, crisp panko prawns served with shredded cabbage, lemon and tonkatsu sauce.

items.raw: 16 large raw prawns, peeled and tails left on

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Make 3 small cuts along the belly of each prawn and press flat so they stay straight. Season with the salt.
Coat in flour, then egg, then panko, pressing the crumbs on.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat and shallow-fry the prawns in 2 batches for 2 minutes each side until golden. Drain.
Serve on the cabbage with lemon, tonkatsu sauce and the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until pink and opaque, at least 63°C. Contains shellfish, egg and gluten. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Nasu Dengaku Miso-Glazed Aubergine
summary: Seared aubergine halves with a sweet miso glaze grilled until bubbling, with sesame and rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Score the aubergine flesh in a crosshatch, brush with the oil and roast cut-side down at 220C for 15 minutes until soft.
Warm the miso, mirin, sugar and sake in a small pan over low heat for 3 minutes until smooth and glossy.
Turn the aubergines, spread with the miso glaze and grill for 4 minutes until bubbling and lightly charred.
Scatter with the sesame seeds and spring onions and serve with the rice.

title: Shioyaki Salt-Grilled Barramundi
summary: Salted barramundi fillets grilled until the skin crackles, served with grated daikon and lemon.

steps.text: Salt the fish on both sides. Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes, while the salt draws out moisture; pat the fish dry.
Heat the grill to high. Brush the fish with the oil and grill skin-side up for 6 minutes until the skin blisters and the flesh is opaque.
Mix the grated daikon with the soy sauce.
Serve the fish with the daikon, lemon, green beans and rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Buta no Shogayaki Japanese Ginger Pork
summary: Thin pork slices pan-fried in a sweet-salty ginger sauce, the everyday teishoku favourite.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Mix the soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar and ginger. Toss the pork in half of it for 5 minutes.
Heat the oil in a pan over high heat and fry the onion for 2 minutes, then add the pork in a single layer and cook for 3 minutes until browned.
Pour in the rest of the sauce and cook for 1 minute until glossy.
Serve on the cabbage with the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork until no pink remains and it reaches at least 70°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Teriyaki Buri Glazed Yellowtail
summary: Pan-seared yellowtail steaks glazed in a homemade teriyaki until sticky and lacquered.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Mix the soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar.
Sear the fish in the oil over medium-high heat for 3 minutes each side until golden.
Pour in the sauce and cook for 3 minutes, spooning it over, until thick and glossy and the fish is opaque.
Steam the broccolini for 3 minutes until tender. Serve with the fish, rice and sesame seeds.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Domi Gui Korean Grilled Snapper
summary: Salted snapper fillets pan-grilled until crisp, served with rice and a soy-sesame dipping sauce.

steps.text: Salt the fillets and rest for 10 minutes; pat dry.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Fry the fillets in the oil over medium-high heat, skin-side down first, for 4 minutes each side until crisp and opaque.
Mix the soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, gochugaru and spring onions for the dip.
Serve the fish with the dip, rice and cucumber.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 10 minutes salting.

title: Tteokgalbi Grilled Short Rib Patties
summary: Sweet soy beef and pork rib-style patties, pan-grilled, the royal court Korean classic.

steps.text: Mix both minces with the soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, garlic, pear and pine nuts, kneading for 2 minutes until sticky. Rest for 15 minutes.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Shape into 8 oval patties about 2cm thick.
Pan-fry in the oil over medium heat for 5 minutes each side until browned and cooked through.
Serve with the rice and lettuce leaves.

notes: Food safety: mince must be cooked right through; patties reach at least 75°C inside. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 15 minutes resting.

title: Jangjorim Soy-Braised Beef with Eggs
summary: Beef simmered in soy, garlic and green chilli until tender and shredded, a staple of the Korean table.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Put the beef, soy sauce, sugar, garlic, ginger and water in a pot, bring to the boil, then cover and simmer for 45 minutes until the beef is tender.
Add the eggs and chillies and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes until the sauce is reduced and glossy.
Shred the beef a little with two forks, stir in the sesame oil and serve with the rice.

notes: Food safety: beef must reach at least 71°C; simmered until tender it will. Boil the eggs until the yolk is firm. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Saengseon Jeon Korean Pan-Fried Fish Fillets
summary: White fish fillets coated in flour and egg, shallow-fried to a golden coat and served with soy dipping sauce.

items.raw: 600g firm white fish fillets, cut into 5cm pieces

steps.text: Season the fish with the salt. Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Dredge each piece in flour, then dip in egg.
Fry in the oil over medium heat for 3 minutes each side, until golden and the fish flakes.
Mix the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar and gochugaru for the dip.
Serve the fish hot with the dip and rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C; eggs are fully cooked in the coating. Contains fish and egg. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Gai Tod Hat Yai Southern Thai Fried Chicken
summary: Hat Yai fried chicken marinated in coriander root and white pepper, topped with crisp fried shallots.

items.raw: 800g chicken thigh, bone in, cut into pieces

steps.text: Mix the chicken with the coriander roots, garlic, pepper, fish sauce and rice flour. Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Heat the oil to 170C and fry the chicken in 2 batches for 10 minutes each until deep golden.
Check that the thickest piece is cooked right through, then drain on paper.
Scatter with the fried shallots.
Serve with the sweet chilli sauce and rice.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach at least 75°C at the thickest part. Keep hot oil away from water. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 30 minutes marinating.

title: Moo Tod Gratiem Thai Garlic Pepper Pork
summary: Pork slices fried with plenty of garlic and black pepper, served with rice and a fried egg.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Crush the garlic, coriander root and pepper together and mix with the oyster sauce and fish sauce.
Toss the pork in the paste and fry in 2 tbsp oil over high heat for 5 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil until the whites are set and the yolks are firm.
Serve the pork with the rice, eggs and cucumber.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork until it reaches at least 70°C. Fry the eggs until yolks are firm. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 15 minutes marinating.

title: Nam Tok Neua Thai Waterfall Beef
summary: Grilled steak sliced and dressed with lime, fish sauce, chilli, toasted rice and mint, an Isaan classic.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Toast the 2 tbsp of rice in a dry pan for 4 minutes until deep golden, then grind coarsely.
Grill the steak over high heat for 4 minutes each side, rest for 5 minutes, then slice thinly.
Toss the beef with the lime juice, fish sauce, sugar, chilli, shallots and ground rice.
Fold through the herbs and serve with the lettuce and rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the steak to at least 63°C and rest for 3 minutes; slices cooked through reach 71°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Pla Kapong Neung Thai Lime Steamed Barramundi
summary: Whole-fillet fish steamed and drenched in a punchy garlic, chilli, lime and coriander dressing.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Put the fish and lemongrass on a heatproof plate and steam over boiling water for 10 minutes, until opaque and flaking.
Steam the bok choy for the last 2 minutes until just tender.
Whisk the garlic, chillies, lime juice, fish sauce and sugar until the sugar dissolves.
Pour over the hot fish, scatter with the coriander and serve with the rice.

notes: Food safety: steam the fish until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Pla Pao Thai Salt-Crusted Grilled Fish
summary: Whole fish packed in salt and lemongrass, baked until the flesh is moist, served with a spicy seafood dip.

items.raw: 1 whole snapper, about 1.2kg, gutted and scaled

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Stuff the fish with half the lemongrass and the galangal, and bed it on the rest of the lemongrass in a baking tray.
Pack the salt over the fish and bake at 220C for 25 minutes until the flesh is opaque.
Mix the lime juice, fish sauce, chillies, garlic and sugar for the dip.
Crack away the salt, lift the flesh from the bones and serve with the dip and rice.

notes: Food safety: the fish must be opaque and flake easily, at least 63°C at the thickest part. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Chicken 65 Chennai Fried Chicken
summary: Crisp, fiery fried chicken bites from Chennai, tossed with green chilli and lemon.

items.raw: 600g boneless chicken thigh, cut into 3cm pieces

steps.text: Mix the chicken with the yoghurt, cornflour, rice flour, ginger, garlic, chilli powder, garam masala and salt until coated.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan over medium-high heat and fry the chicken in 2 batches for 6 minutes each, turning, until deep red-gold and crisp.
Drop the green chillies into the pan for 30 seconds until blistered.
Toss the chicken with the chillies and serve hot with lemon wedges.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches at least 75°C at the thickest part. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 30 minutes marinating.

title: Malai Tikka Creamy Chicken Skewers
summary: Mild, creamy chicken tikka scented with cardamom and white pepper, roasted until lightly charred.

items.raw: 700g chicken thigh fillets, cut into 4cm pieces

steps.text: Mix the chicken with the cream, yoghurt, ginger, garlic, cardamom, pepper, salt and lemon juice.
Thread onto skewers and brush with the ghee.
Roast at 230C on a rack over a tray for 18 minutes, turning once, until lightly charred at the edges.
Warm the naan and serve with the tikka and sliced onion.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach at least 75°C at the thickest part. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 1 hour marinating.

title: Hariyali Chicken Tikka Green Herb Skewers
summary: Chicken tikka in a bright mint, coriander and spinach marinade, grilled until fragrant and juicy.

items.raw: 700g chicken thigh fillets, cut into 4cm pieces

steps.text: Blend the coriander, mint, spinach, chillies, yoghurt, ginger, garlic, lemon juice, garam masala and salt to a smooth paste.
Coat the chicken in the paste and thread onto skewers.
Brush with the oil and grill or roast at 230C for 18 minutes, turning once, until charred in spots.
Serve hot with extra lemon.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach at least 75°C at the thickest part. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 1 hour marinating.

title: Reshmi Kebab Silky Cashew Chicken
summary: Silky, golden chicken kebabs in a cashew and cream marinade, grilled and served with warm naan.

items.raw: 700g chicken thigh fillets, cut into 4cm pieces

steps.text: Blend the soaked cashews with the cream, yoghurt, ginger, garlic, cumin, cardamom and salt until smooth.
Coat the chicken in the paste and thread onto skewers.
Roast at 230C for 18 minutes, turning once and brushing with the butter, until golden and cooked through.
Warm the naan and serve with the kebabs and lemon.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach at least 75°C at the thickest part. Contains tree nuts. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 1 hour marinating.

title: Galouti Kebab Lucknow Melting Lamb Patties
summary: Lucknowi lamb patties so tender they melt, spiced with fried onion and cardamom and pan-fried in ghee.

steps.text: Fry the onions in 1 tbsp ghee for 12 minutes until deep brown and crisp, then crush them.
Mix the lamb with the onions, ginger, garlic, spices, toasted chickpea flour and salt, kneading for 3 minutes until very smooth.
Shape into 12 small flat patties about 1.5cm thick.
Pan-fry in the remaining ghee over medium heat for 4 minutes each side until browned and cooked through.
Serve on the warm flatbreads with the mint chutney.

notes: Food safety: cook the patties right through to at least 75°C; mince carries bacteria throughout. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 30 minutes chilling.

title: Amritsari Machhi Punjabi Fried Fish
summary: Chickpea-flour-coated fish pieces spiced with ajwain and chilli, shallow-fried until crisp, a Punjabi street classic.

items.raw: 600g firm white fish fillets, cut into 4cm pieces

steps.text: Toss the fish with the ginger, garlic, chilli powder, salt and lemon juice.
Mix the chickpea flour with the ajwain and enough water for a thick batter, then coat the fish.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat and fry the fish in batches for 3 minutes each side until crisp and golden.
Drain on paper and serve with the onion and mint chutney.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 20 minutes marinating.

title: Meen Varuthathu Kerala Fried Fish with Rice
summary: Kingfish steaks rubbed with chilli, turmeric and pepper and shallow-fried in coconut oil, served with rice.

steps.text: Rub the fish with the chilli powder, turmeric, pepper, ginger, garlic, lemon juice and salt.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Heat the coconut oil in a pan over medium heat and fry the steaks for 4 minutes each side until crisp and opaque.
Serve with the rice and lime.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 20 minutes marinating.

title: Kolkata Mutton Biryani with Potato and Egg
summary: Mild, fragrant biryani with tender lamb, golden potato and boiled egg, a Calcutta speciality.

steps.text: Brown the potatoes in 1 tbsp ghee for 8 minutes until golden, then lift out. Fry the onions in the same pot for 10 minutes until golden.
Add the lamb, yoghurt, ginger, garlic, garam masala and salt and cook covered for 40 minutes on low heat until the lamb is tender.
Boil the rice in salted water for 6 minutes until three-quarters cooked, then drain.
Layer the rice over the lamb, tucking the potatoes and eggs in, and drizzle with the saffron milk and remaining ghee.
Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 20 minutes until the rice is tender and fluffy.

notes: Food safety: lamb must reach at least 71°C; simmered until tender it will. Boil the eggs until the yolk is firm. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Thalassery Chicken Biryani Malabar
summary: Malabar biryani of masala chicken under short-grain khaima rice, with fried onion, cashews and raisins.

steps.text: Fry the cashews and sultanas in 1 tbsp ghee for 1 minute until golden, then lift out. Fry two-thirds of the onion in the same pot for 12 minutes until deep gold.
Add the ginger, garlic, tomatoes, chillies, spices and salt and cook for 8 minutes into a thick masala.
Add the chicken, cover and cook for 20 minutes on low heat until tender; lift out.
Stir the rice into the masala with the stock, bring to the boil, cover and cook on low for 15 minutes until the rice is tender and fluffy.
Layer the chicken over the rice, scatter with the cashews, sultanas and remaining onion, and rest covered for 10 minutes.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach at least 75°C at the thickest part. Contains tree nuts. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Kacchi Gosht Biryani Bangladeshi Raw-Marinated Lamb
summary: Lamb marinated in yoghurt and spices, layered raw with part-cooked rice and sealed to steam in its own juices.

items.raw: 2 onions, sliced and fried until golden

steps.text: Mix the lamb with the yoghurt, ginger, garlic, chilli powder, garam masala, half the onions and the salt.
Boil the rice in salted water for 6 minutes until three-quarters cooked, then drain.
In a heavy pot, layer the potatoes, then the lamb and its marinade, then the rice, ghee, remaining onion and milk.
Seal the lid with foil or a tight cloth and cook on high for 5 minutes, then on the lowest heat for 70 minutes, until the lamb is tender.
Rest for 10 minutes before opening and serve.

notes: Food safety: lamb must reach at least 71°C and be fully tender before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 4 hours marinating.

title: Ambur Star Chicken Biryani
summary: Tamil Nadu biryani with a green chilli, mint and tomato masala and plenty of fragrant basmati.

steps.text: Fry the onions in the oil for 10 minutes until golden.
Add the ginger, garlic, chillies, mint and tomatoes and cook for 8 minutes until the oil separates.
Add the chicken, yoghurt, chilli powder, garam masala and salt and cook for 10 minutes.
Stir in the water and rice, bring to the boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 20 minutes until the rice is tender and fluffy.
Rest covered for 10 minutes, then fluff and serve.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach at least 75°C at the thickest part. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Bihari Kebab Smoky Beef Strips
summary: Thin beef strips tenderised in yoghurt and lemon and grilled hot with a smoky, spicy crust.

items.raw: 700g beef sirloin, cut into thin strips

steps.text: Mix the beef with the yoghurt, lemon juice, ginger, garlic, spices and salt.
Thread the strips onto skewers in loose folds and brush with the oil.
Grill over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes each side, until charred at the edges and cooked through.
Warm the naan and serve with the kebabs and onion.

notes: Food safety: beef strips must reach at least 71°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 2 hours marinating.

title: Lahori Fried Fish
summary: Spiced fish pieces in a thin chickpea batter, shallow-fried and served with lemon and a crunchy salad.

items.raw: 600g firm white fish fillets, cut into 4cm pieces

steps.text: Mix the chickpea flour, spices, salt and lemon juice with enough water for a thick batter.
Coat the fish pieces in the batter.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat and fry the fish for 3 minutes each side until golden and crisp.
Drain on paper and serve with the cabbage, tomato and lemon.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Tabaka Uzbek Flattened Chicken with Garlic
summary: Whole spatchcocked chicken pressed flat, seared and roasted until crisp, with garlic and potatoes.

steps.text: Rub the chicken with the butter, garlic, coriander, paprika, salt and pepper.
Sear skin-side down in the oil in a large oven-safe pan for 8 minutes until golden, with a heavy pan pressed on top.
Turn the chicken, add the potatoes around it and roast at 220C for 35 minutes until the skin is crisp and the potatoes are tender.
Rest for 10 minutes, then carve.
Stir the dill into the yoghurt and serve alongside.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach at least 75°C at the thickest part of the thigh. Wash hands and board after raw chicken. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Samarkand Lamb Shashlik with Onion Salad
summary: Cubes of lamb leg marinated in onion and vinegar, grilled hot and served with flatbread and a tomato onion salad.

steps.text: Mix the lamb with the grated onions, vinegar, cumin, salt, pepper and oil.
Thread onto skewers and grill over high heat for 12 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.
Toss the tomatoes, red onion and coriander together.
Serve the lamb on the flatbread with the salad.

notes: Food safety: lamb must reach at least 71°C; cut one cube to check. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 2 hours marinating.

title: Mutton Sukka Dry Pepper Lamb
summary: Tender lamb slow-cooked until dry and coated in a toasted black pepper, fennel and coriander masala.

steps.text: Toast the coriander, peppercorns and fennel in a dry pan for 2 minutes, then grind with the coconut.
Fry the onions in the oil for 10 minutes until golden, then add the ginger, garlic and tomatoes and cook for 8 minutes into a paste.
Add the lamb, turmeric, salt and ground masala with 1 cup of water, cover and cook on low for 50 minutes until the lamb is tender.
Uncover and stir over high heat for 8 minutes until the liquid has gone and the meat is coated and dark.

notes: Food safety: lamb must reach at least 71°C and be tender before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Kozhi Varuval Kerala Pepper Fried Chicken
summary: Chicken fried with plenty of shallot, ginger and black pepper until dry and glossy, served with rice.

steps.text: Rub the chicken with the turmeric, salt and half the pepper.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat, fry the onions for 10 minutes until golden, then add the ginger, garlic and coriander.
Add the chicken, cover and cook for 15 minutes, then uncover and fry for 8 minutes until dry and browned.
Stir through the remaining pepper and garam masala and serve with the rice.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach at least 75°C at the thickest part. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Prawn Balchao Goan Pickled Prawns
summary: Fried prawns folded through a tangy, fiery Goan vinegar masala and served with rice.

steps.text: Blend the soaked chillies, garlic, ginger, cumin and vinegar to a paste.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Fry the onions in 2 tbsp oil for 8 minutes until golden, add the paste, sugar and salt and cook for 5 minutes until the oil rises.
In a separate pan, fry the prawns in the remaining oil for 3 minutes until pink and opaque.
Fold the prawns into the masala for 2 minutes and serve with the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until pink and opaque, at least 63°C. Contains shellfish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Tawa Machhi Mumbai Pan-Fried Spiced Fish
summary: Fish fillets in a green chilli, coriander and lemon rub, seared on a flat pan and served with warm rotis.

steps.text: Blend the coriander, chillies, ginger, garlic, lemon juice, turmeric and salt into a thick paste.
Coat the fish in the paste.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat and sear the fish for 4 minutes each side until opaque and golden.
Warm the rotis and serve with the fish and onion.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 15 minutes marinating.

title: Kala Bhuna Chittagong Black Beef
summary: Chittagong beef slow-cooked until dark, dry and intense with mustard oil, onion and roasted spices.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil in a heavy pot until it just smokes, then lower the heat and fry the onions for 12 minutes until dark brown.
Add the ginger, garlic, chilli, cumin, coriander, bay and salt and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the beef and 1/2 cup water, cover and cook on low for 90 minutes until very tender, stirring now and then.
Uncover and stir over medium heat for 10 minutes until the sauce clings and is very dark.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes, and serve with the beef finished with the garam masala.

notes: Food safety: beef must reach at least 71°C and be tender before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Murgh Kali Mirch Black Pepper Chicken
summary: Creamy yoghurt-marinated chicken with a heavy hand of freshly cracked black pepper, served with rice.

items.raw: 700g boneless chicken thigh, cut into pieces

steps.text: Mix the chicken with the yoghurt, half the pepper, ginger, garlic and salt.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Fry the onion in the ghee for 8 minutes until golden, add the chicken and cook covered for 15 minutes on medium heat.
Stir in the cream and remaining pepper and cook for 3 minutes until glossy, then serve over the rice.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach at least 75°C at the thickest part. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 30 minutes marinating.

title: Tandoori Gobi Roasted Spiced Cauliflower
summary: Whole florets coated in a chickpea flour and yoghurt marinade, roasted until charred, with chapatis and mint yoghurt.

steps.text: Mix the yoghurt, chickpea flour, ginger, garlic, chilli powder, garam masala, salt and oil.
Coat the cauliflower in the mix, turning well.
Roast on a tray at 230C for 25 minutes, turning once, until charred at the tips and tender.
Stir the mint through a little extra yoghurt.
Serve the cauliflower with the chapatis, mint yoghurt and lemon.

notes: Plus 30 minutes marinating.

title: Kathi Roll Kolkata Chicken and Egg Roll
summary: Spiced chicken and egg wrapped in a flaky paratha with onion, lime and chutney, a Kolkata street classic.

steps.text: Toss the chicken with the ginger, garlic, garam masala, chilli powder and salt.
Fry in 2 tbsp oil over high heat for 6 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Fry the parathas in the remaining oil, spreading one side with beaten egg and cooking for 1 minute until the egg sets firm.
Fill with the chicken, onion, chutney and a squeeze of lime, and roll up tightly.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach at least 75°C at the thickest part and the egg be fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 15 minutes marinating.

title: Ping Gai Lao Grilled Lemongrass Chicken
summary: Lao-style grilled chicken thighs marinated in lemongrass, garlic and coriander root, served with sticky rice.

steps.text: Blend the lemongrass, garlic, coriander roots, fish sauce, oyster sauce, sugar and pepper into a paste, and coat the chicken.
Steam the rice, soaked beforehand, for 25 minutes until sticky and tender.
Brush the chicken with the oil and grill or roast at 220C for 25 minutes, turning once, until deeply golden.
Serve with the sticky rice and sweet chilli sauce.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach at least 75°C at the thickest part. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 1 hour marinating and 4 hours soaking the rice.

title: Muc Rang Muoi Vietnamese Salt and Chilli Squid
summary: Tender squid tossed in a hot pan with garlic, chilli and salt, crisp-edged and served with lime and rice.

items.raw: 600g squid tubes, scored and cut into pieces

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Pat the squid dry and toss with the cornflour.
Fry in 3 tbsp oil in a very hot pan for 2 minutes, in 2 batches, until golden and curled. Lift out.
Add the remaining oil, garlic and chillies for 30 seconds, return the squid with the salt, sugar and spring onions and toss for 30 seconds.
Serve with the lime and rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the squid until opaque and firm, at least 63°C; do not overcook or it turns rubbery. Contains shellfish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Sate Lilit Balinese Fish Skewers
summary: Minced fish with coconut, lime leaf and spice paste wrapped around lemongrass sticks and grilled.

items.raw: 600g firm white fish fillets, finely minced

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Mix the fish with the coconut, shallots, garlic, ginger, chillies, lime juice, sugar and salt, kneading for 2 minutes until sticky.
Mould a heaped spoonful around each lemongrass stalk, pressing firmly.
Brush with the oil and grill over medium-high heat for 5 minutes, turning, until golden and opaque, then serve with the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Bebek Goreng Indonesian Crispy Fried Duck
summary: Duck legs simmered in spiced coconut water, then fried until the skin crackles, served with sambal and rice.

steps.text: Put the duck, coconut water, shallots, garlic, coriander, turmeric, salt and bay in a pot, cover and simmer gently for 90 minutes until the duck is very tender.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Lift out the duck and pat dry thoroughly.
Fry in the oil over medium-high heat for 8 minutes, turning, until the skin is deep golden and crisp.
Serve with the sambal and rice.

notes: Food safety: duck must reach at least 75°C; long simmering takes it well past that. Keep hot oil away from water. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Empal Gepuk Javanese Sweet Fried Beef
summary: Beef simmered in palm sugar, coriander and galangal, flattened, then fried until crisp-edged and sweet.

items.raw: 700g beef shin, cut into large pieces

steps.text: Put the beef, water, shallots, garlic, coriander, galangal, sugar, soy sauce and salt in a pot, cover and simmer for 80 minutes until tender.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Lift out the beef, drain, and press flat with the back of a heavy pan.
Fry in the oil over medium heat for 4 minutes each side until browned and crisp at the edges.
Slice and serve with the rice.

notes: Food safety: beef must reach at least 71°C and be tender before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Sambal Sotong Malaysian Squid in Sambal
summary: Squid rings tossed in a fiery sweet-sour chilli sambal and served with rice.

steps.text: Blend the chillies, shallots and garlic into a paste.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Fry the paste in the oil for 6 minutes until the oil rises, then add the tomatoes, tamarind, sugar and salt and cook for 4 minutes.
Add the squid and cook for 2 minutes only, until opaque and curled, then serve with the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the squid until opaque and firm, at least 63°C. Contains shellfish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Daing na Isda Garlic Vinegar Fried Fish
summary: Fish fillets marinated in vinegar, garlic and pepper then fried until crisp, served with garlic rice.

steps.text: Marinate the fish in the cane vinegar, half the garlic, pepper and salt.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Fry the fish in 2 tbsp oil for 4 minutes each side until crisp and opaque.
Fry the remaining garlic in the last tbsp of oil until golden and stir through the rice.
Serve the fish with the garlic rice, tomato and white vinegar for dipping.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 30 minutes marinating.

title: Tokwa't Baboy Filipino Tofu and Pork
summary: Fried tofu and tender pork tossed in a sharp soy, vinegar and onion dressing, served with rice.

steps.text: Simmer the pork in the water until tender, about 25 minutes, then drain and pat dry.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Fry the tofu in 2 tbsp oil for 8 minutes until golden on all sides, then lift out.
Fry the pork in the remaining oil for 5 minutes until browned.
Mix the vinegar, soy sauce, onions, chillies and pepper, toss through the tofu and pork, and serve with the rice.

notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C; simmered until tender it will. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Ayam Goreng Kalasan Javanese Sweet Fried Chicken
summary: Chicken simmered in coconut water and palm sugar, then fried until golden, a Yogyakarta classic.

steps.text: Simmer the chicken with the coconut water, shallots, garlic, coriander, turmeric, sugar, bay and salt for 35 minutes until tender and the liquid has nearly gone.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Drain the chicken, reserving any remaining paste.
Fry in the oil over medium heat for 8 minutes, turning, until deep golden.
Serve with the rice and the reserved paste.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach at least 75°C at the thickest part. Keep hot oil away from water. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Ga Nuong Sa Vietnamese Lemongrass Grilled Chicken
summary: Chicken thighs marinated in lemongrass, garlic and fish sauce, grilled until sticky, served with rice and pickles.

steps.text: Mix the lemongrass, garlic, fish sauce, sugar, honey and oil, and coat the chicken.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Toss the carrot with the vinegar for quick pickles.
Grill the chicken over medium-high heat for 8 minutes each side, until charred in spots and cooked through.
Slice and serve with the rice, cucumber and pickles.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach at least 75°C at the thickest part. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 1 hour marinating.

title: Singapore Black Pepper Prawns
summary: Prawns tossed in a hot buttery sauce with cracked black pepper, garlic and oyster sauce.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Heat the oil and butter in a wok over high heat, add the prawns and cook for 3 minutes until pink.
Add the garlic and pepper for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the oyster sauce, soy sauce and sugar and toss for 1 minute until glossy.
Scatter with the spring onions and serve with the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until pink and opaque, at least 63°C. Contains shellfish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Sai Oua Lao Herb Pork Patties
summary: Lao herb sausage mixture shaped into patties with lemongrass, galangal and chilli, served with sticky rice.

steps.text: Mix the pork with the lemongrass, galangal, garlic, chillies, shallots, fish sauce and dill, kneading for 2 minutes until sticky.
Steam the rice, soaked beforehand, for 25 minutes until tender and sticky.
Shape into 8 flat patties.
Pan-fry in the oil over medium heat for 6 minutes each side until browned and cooked through.
Serve with the sticky rice and cucumber.

notes: Food safety: pork mince must be cooked through to at least 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 4 hours soaking the rice.

title: Mok Pa Lao Steamed Fish Parcels
summary: Fish mixed with dill, lemongrass and coconut cream, steamed in parcels until soft and set.

steps.text: Mix the fish with the coconut cream, dill, lemongrass, spring onions, chillies, fish sauce and rice flour.
Steam the rice, soaked beforehand, for 25 minutes until tender and sticky.
Divide the mixture among 4 squares of baking paper, fold into sealed parcels and steam over boiling water for 18 minutes until set.
Open the parcels and serve with the sticky rice and lettuce.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until set and flaking, at least 63°C. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
Plus 4 hours soaking the rice.

title: Kahuku Style Garlic Prawns with Rice and Mac Salad
summary: Shell-on prawns sautéed in lots of garlic butter with lemon, served with rice and macaroni salad.

steps.text: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Toss the macaroni with the mayonnaise and a pinch of salt.
Toss the prawns with the cornflour, paprika and salt, and fry in the oil over high heat for 3 minutes until pink and crisp.
Add the butter and garlic for 1 minute until fragrant, then finish with the lemon juice.
Serve with the rice and macaroni.

notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until pink and opaque, at least 63°C. Contains shellfish, egg and gluten. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Ghanaian Grilled Snapper with Pepper Sauce
summary: Whole snapper rubbed with ginger and chilli, grilled until crisp, with a fresh tomato and pepper sauce.

items.raw: 2 whole snapper, about 600g each, scaled and gutted

steps.text: Slash the fish on both sides and rub with the ginger, garlic, chilli powder, salt and 1 tbsp oil.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Grill or roast the fish at 220C for 22 minutes, turning once, until the skin is crisp and the flesh opaque.
Blend the tomatoes, chillies and onion, then simmer in the remaining oil for 8 minutes until thick.
Serve the fish with the sauce and rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Baked Vegetable Samosas
summary: Crisp baked pastry triangles filled with spiced potato and peas, easy to make ahead for a snack plate.

steps.text: Rub the flour, salt and 2 tbsp of the oil together, then add the water and knead for 5 minutes until smooth. Cover and rest.

Boil the potato for 10 minutes until tender, drain well and roughly mash. Fry the onion and cumin seeds in the remaining oil for 5 minutes until soft, stir in the curry powder, potato, peas and lemon juice, then cool.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Divide the dough into 4 balls and roll each into a 22cm round, then halve each to make 8 half-moons.
Shape each half into a cone, fill with 2 tbsp of the filling and press the edges closed with a little water.
Bake on a lined tray for 25 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp. Cool for 5 minutes before eating.

notes: Plus 20 minutes resting the dough.
Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 2 samosas.

title: Mushroom Arancini
summary: Golden crumbed risotto balls with a melting mozzarella centre, baked rather than deep-fried.

steps.text: Fry the mushrooms in the olive oil for 6 minutes until dry and golden, add the garlic for 30 seconds, then stir in the rice for 1 minute.
Add the stock a cup at a time, stirring, for 20 minutes until the rice is tender and creamy. Stir through the parmesan and spread on a tray to cool completely.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Wrap about 2 tbsp of rice around each mozzarella cube to make 12 balls.
Roll each ball in the flour, then the beaten egg, then the breadcrumbs.
Bake on a lined tray for 20 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and hot through the middle.

notes: Plus 30 minutes cooling the risotto.
Snack. Vegetarian-style cheese not specified, so it is not tagged vegetarian. Per serving: 3 balls.
Food safety: the egg coating is cooked through in the oven; wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg.

title: Onion Pakoras
summary: Crunchy chickpea-flour fritters packed with onion and spice, shallow-fried and best eaten hot.

steps.text: Toss the onion with the salt and leave for 10 minutes so it softens and releases juice.
Mix in the besan, cumin, turmeric and chilli, adding the water a splash at a time until the batter just coats the onion.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat until a drop of batter sizzles straight away.
Fry heaped tablespoons for 3 to 4 minutes each side until deep golden and crisp, in 3 batches, draining on paper towel.
Squeeze over the lemon juice and serve hot.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 4 pakoras.

title: Salmon Onigiri
summary: Hand-pressed Japanese rice triangles with a flaked salmon centre wrapped in nori, ideal for the lunchbox.

steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then simmer covered with the water for 15 minutes until tender, and rest covered for 10 minutes.
Pan-cook the salmon for 4 minutes each side until opaque and flakes easily, then flake it with the soy sauce.
Wet your hands, rub with a little salt, and press a quarter of the rice into a flat cup in your palm.
Add a spoonful of salmon, cover with more rice and press into a firm triangle. Make 8 onigiri.
Roll in the sesame seeds and wrap each with a strip of nori just before eating.

notes: Plus 10 minutes resting the rice.
Snack. Per serving: 2 onigiri.
Food safety: cook the salmon until opaque all through, and keep onigiri in the fridge and eat within 24 hours.

title: Pork and Cabbage Spring Rolls
summary: Crisp baked rolls filled with juicy pork mince, cabbage and ginger, served with a sharp vinegar dip.

steps.text: Stir-fry the pork in a hot pan for 5 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches at least 75°C.
Add the cabbage, carrot and ginger and cook for 3 minutes until wilted, then stir in half the soy sauce and the sesame oil. Cool for 10 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Spoon 3 tbsp of filling onto each wrapper, fold in the sides and roll up tightly, sealing with a little water.
Brush with the neutral oil and bake for 15 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
Mix the remaining soy sauce with the rice vinegar and serve alongside.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 rolls.
Food safety: cook pork mince to at least 75°C; cool leftovers within 1 hour and refrigerate.

title: Ham and Cheese Croquetas
summary: Creamy bechamel croquetas with ham and cheddar and a crisp crumb, a Spanish bar classic.

steps.text: Melt the butter, stir in 1/4 cup of the flour for 2 minutes, then whisk in the milk and stir for 8 minutes until very thick.
Fold in the ham, cheddar and nutmeg, then chill in a shallow dish for at least 2 hours until firm.
Shape into 18 small logs using wet hands. Roll in the remaining flour, the beaten eggs, then the breadcrumbs.
Shallow-fry in the oil in batches over medium heat for 2 minutes, turning, until deep golden and hot through the middle.
Drain on paper towel and serve warm.

notes: Plus 2 hours chilling.
Snack. Per serving: 3 croquetas.
Food safety: wash hands after handling raw egg and keep the chilled mix refrigerated; eat leftovers within 2 days.

title: Potato Aloo Tikki
summary: Spiced potato patties with a crisp golden crust, served with yoghurt and chutney.

steps.text: Boil the potato whole for 20 minutes until a knife slides in easily, then peel, mash and cool for 10 minutes.
Mix with the peas, spices, cornflour and salt.
Shape into 8 patties about 1.5cm thick.
Fry in the oil over medium heat for 4 minutes each side until a crisp golden crust forms.
Serve hot with the yoghurt and a squeeze of lemon if you like.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 tikki.

title: Lamb and Mint Sausage Rolls
summary: Flaky sausage rolls with spiced lamb mince and fresh mint, cut into party-size pieces.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Mix the lamb, onion, breadcrumbs, mint, cumin and salt.
Cut the pastry sheets in half, run a log of filling down each and roll up, sealing the join underneath.
Brush with the beaten egg, scatter with sesame seeds and cut each log into 4 pieces to make 24.
Bake on lined trays for 30 minutes until the pastry is deep golden and puffed.
Check the middle of one roll reads at least 75°C before serving.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 4 pieces.
Food safety: lamb mince must reach at least 75°C all through; refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour and eat within 2 days.

title: Prawn Toast Fingers
summary: Crisp sesame-topped toast spread with a prawn and ginger paste, pan-fried until golden.

steps.text: Blitz the prawns, egg white, ginger, cornflour and soy sauce into a rough paste.
Cut each slice of bread into 3 fingers and spread the paste thickly over one side. Press the sesame seeds on top.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and fry paste-side down for 2 minutes until golden.
Turn and fry for 2 minutes more until the bread is crisp and the prawn reads at least 63°C.
Drain on paper towel and serve hot.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 3 fingers.
Food safety: cook prawns until opaque and at least 63°C; keep raw seafood refrigerated and cook within a day.

title: Masala Vada
summary: Crunchy South Indian lentil fritters with onion, chilli and fennel.

items.raw: 1 cup split chickpeas (chana dal), soaked for 4 hours

steps.text: Drain the dal and blitz half of it to a coarse paste, leaving the rest whole for crunch.
Mix with the onion, chilli, fennel, coriander and salt.
Shape into 12 flat patties.
Shallow-fry in the oil over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes each side until deep golden and crisp, draining on paper towel.
Serve warm, with chutney or yoghurt on the side, within 20 minutes of frying while the crust is crisp.

notes: Plus 4 hours soaking.
Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 3 vadas.

title: Baked Lamb Kibbeh Bites
summary: Torpedo-shaped bulgur shells with a spiced lamb and pine nut filling, baked until crisp outside.

steps.text: Soak the bulgur in cold water for 15 minutes, drain and squeeze dry. Knead with the first lamb, grated onion, allspice and salt, or blitz in a processor, until a smooth paste forms.
Fry the chopped onion in 1 tbsp of the oil for 4 minutes, add the filling lamb and cook for 6 minutes until no pink remains. Stir in the pine nuts and cinnamon and cool.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). With wet hands, flatten a golf-ball of shell mix, fill, and close into a torpedo. Make 18.
Brush with the remaining oil and bake on a lined tray for 25 minutes, turning once, until browned and at least 75°C in the middle.
Serve warm with the yoghurt.

notes: Plus 15 minutes soaking.
Snack. Per serving: 3 kibbeh.
Food safety: lamb mince must reach at least 75°C; refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Potato Knish
summary: Baked pastry parcels of soft potato and caramelised onion, an Eastern European deli favourite.

steps.text: Mix the flour, baking powder, 1/4 cup of the oil, water and half the salt into a dough, kneading for 3 minutes. Rest for 20 minutes.
Boil the potato for 12 minutes until tender, drain and mash. Cook the onion with the butter and remaining oil for 15 minutes until deep golden, then mix in the potato, pepper and remaining salt.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Roll the dough into a 30 x 40cm rectangle and spoon the filling in a log along the long side.
Roll up, cut into 6 pieces and pinch the cut ends closed, standing them upright. Brush with the egg.
Bake for 40 minutes until golden and crisp at the edges.

notes: Plus 20 minutes resting the dough.
Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 knish.
Food safety: wash hands after handling raw egg.

title: Khaman Dhokla
summary: Light, spongy steamed chickpea-flour squares tempered with mustard seeds and sesame.

steps.text: Whisk the besan, semolina, sugar, turmeric, salt, water and lemon juice into a smooth batter.
Stir in the bicarbonate of soda until it froths, and pour at once into a greased 18cm tin.
Steam over boiling water, covered, for 15 minutes until a skewer comes out clean and the top is springy.
Heat the oil, pop the mustard seeds for 30 seconds, add the sesame seeds and pour over the dhokla.
Cool for 10 minutes and cut into 12 squares.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 2 squares.

title: Baked Cinnamon Churros
summary: Ridged choux sticks baked until crisp, rolled in cinnamon sugar and served with melted chocolate.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Bring the water, butter, 1 tbsp sugar and salt to the boil, tip in the flour and beat for 2 minutes until a smooth ball forms.
Cool for 5 minutes, then beat in the eggs one at a time until glossy.
Pipe 12cm lengths onto a lined tray with a star nozzle and bake for 20 minutes until golden and crisp.
Toss in the cinnamon and the remaining sugar while still warm.
Melt the chocolate with the milk and serve for dipping.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 3 churros with chocolate.
Food safety: wash hands after handling raw egg.

title: Classic Lamingtons
summary: Squares of light sponge dipped in chocolate icing and rolled in coconut.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin. Beat the butter and caster sugar for 4 minutes until pale, then beat in the eggs one at a time with the vanilla.
Fold in the flour and first measure of milk until just combined and spread into the tin.
Bake for 30 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool fully, ideally overnight in an airtight container, then cut into 12 squares.
Sift the icing sugar and cocoa, then stir with the second measure of milk and the 1 tbsp butter over low heat until smooth and runny.
Dip each square in the icing, let the excess drip off and roll in coconut. Set for 30 minutes.

notes: Plus overnight cooling and 30 minutes setting.
Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 lamington.
Food safety: wash hands after handling raw egg; the cake is baked until a skewer is clean.

title: Honey Walnut Baklava
summary: Crisp filo layers filled with spiced walnuts and soaked in lemon honey syrup.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Mix the walnuts with the cinnamon.
Brush a 20cm square tin with butter and layer 6 filo sheets, brushing each with butter and trimming to fit.
Spread over the walnuts, then top with the remaining 6 sheets, brushing each with butter. Cut into 16 diamonds right through.
Bake for 40 minutes until deep golden and crisp.
Simmer the honey, water and lemon juice for 8 minutes until slightly thick, pour over the hot baklava and cool for 3 hours.

notes: Plus 3 hours soaking.
Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 pieces.

title: Caramel Slice
summary: Three layers of shortbread base, soft condensed milk caramel and dark chocolate.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Mix the flour, coconut, sugar and melted butter, press into a lined 20cm square tin and bake for 15 minutes until lightly golden.
Stir the condensed milk, 60g butter and golden syrup over medium heat for 10 minutes until thick and golden, constantly stirring.
Pour over the base and chill for 30 minutes.
Melt the chocolate with the oil and spread over the caramel. Chill for 2 hours.
Cut into 16 small squares with a hot knife and keep refrigerated.

notes: Plus 2 hours 30 minutes chilling.
Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 squares.

title: Peanut Butter Sultana Balls
summary: No-bake bites of sultanas, oats and peanut butter, rolled in coconut.

steps.text: Soak the sultanas in hot water for 10 minutes and drain.
Blitz the sultanas, oats, peanut butter and honey into a sticky crumb that holds when squeezed.
Roll the mixture into 18 balls, squeezing firmly until each holds its shape.
Roll in the coconut until evenly coated.
Chill for 20 minutes until firm, and keep in the fridge for up to 5 days.

notes: Plus 20 minutes chilling.
Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 3 balls.

title: Gobi Pakora
summary: Cauliflower florets in a spiced chickpea-flour batter, shallow-fried until crisp.

steps.text: Whisk the besan, cumin, turmeric, chilli, salt and water into a thick batter that coats a spoon.
Steam the cauliflower for 3 minutes, drain well and toss through the batter.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat until a drop of batter sizzles straight away.
Fry the florets in 3 batches for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until deep golden and crisp, then drain on paper towel.
Squeeze over the lemon juice and serve hot while the crust is crisp.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: about 8 pieces.

title: Chilli Lime Corn Ribs
summary: Roasted corn cobs cut into curled strips, glazed with smoky butter and finished with lime.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C fan (240°C conventional). Cut each cob in half crosswise, then stand upright and slice each half into 4 long wedges.
Toss the wedges with the butter, paprika, chilli and salt.
Spread on a lined tray cut side up and roast for 30 minutes, turning once, until the kernels are golden and the edges curl.
Squeeze over the lime juice and scatter with the coriander.
Eat warm, holding the ribs by the cob.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 cob.

title: Potato Bhajia
summary: Thin potato slices in a turmeric and chilli batter, shallow-fried and served with a tomato chilli dip.

steps.text: Whisk the besan, water, turmeric, cumin, chilli and salt into a batter the thickness of pouring cream.
Dip the potato slices into the batter so they are fully coated.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and fry the slices in batches for 3 minutes each side until golden and the potato is tender.
Drain the bhajia on paper towel and keep them in a single layer so they stay crisp.
Mix the tomato sauce with the lemon juice and serve alongside while the bhajia are hot.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 6 to 8 slices.

title: Baked Tequenos
summary: Cheese-filled pastry sticks, a Venezuelan party snack, baked until crisp and gooey inside.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Cut each pastry sheet into 6 strips.
Wrap one strip around each cheese stick in a spiral, pinching the ends so the cheese cannot leak.
Brush with the egg, scatter with sesame seeds and place on a lined tray.
Bake for 20 minutes until deep golden and puffed.
Warm the tomato sauce with the chilli and serve for dipping.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 tequenos.
Food safety: wash hands after handling raw egg.

title: Hong Kong Egg Tarts
summary: Flaky shortcrust tartlets filled with a smooth, lightly sweet egg custard.

steps.text: Rub the butter into the flour and icing sugar, add the yolk and cold water, and bring together into a dough. Chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Roll the dough thinly, cut 8 rounds and press into a greased 8-hole muffin tin.
Stir the caster sugar into the hot water until dissolved and cool for 10 minutes, then whisk in the eggs and milk and strain.
Pour into the pastry cases and bake for 25 minutes until the custard is set with a slight wobble and the pastry golden.
Cool for 15 minutes before lifting out of the tin.

notes: Plus 30 minutes chilling.
Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 tart.
Food safety: bake the custard until set, wash hands after handling raw egg, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Lokma Honey Doughnut Bites
summary: Crisp-outside, soft-inside Turkish dough balls soaked in a honey and lemon syrup.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, yeast, sugar and salt with the warm water into a loose, sticky batter. Cover and prove for 1 hour until bubbly.
Simmer the honey, the 1/4 cup water and lemon juice for 5 minutes until syrupy and keep warm.
Heat the oil in a deep frying pan over medium heat. Drop in teaspoons of batter and fry for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until golden and puffed.
Drain briefly, then roll in the warm syrup until glossy.
Serve at once so they stay crisp.

notes: Plus 1 hour proving.
Snack. Swap the honey for golden syrup to make them vegan. Per serving: 5 bites.

title: Alfajores with Caramel Filling
summary: Tender cornflour shortbread sandwiches filled with thick caramel and rolled in coconut.

steps.text: Simmer the condensed milk in a saucepan over medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring constantly, until thick and caramel coloured. Cool.
Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Beat the butter and icing sugar until pale, then beat in the yolks.
Fold in the cornflour, flours and baking powder, roll to 5mm and cut 16 rounds with a 5cm cutter.
Bake for 12 minutes until set but still pale. Cool completely.
Sandwich pairs with caramel and roll the edges in the coconut.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 alfajores.
Food safety: wash hands after handling raw egg yolks.

title: Welsh Cakes
summary: Small spiced griddle cakes studded with sultanas, cooked in a dry pan.

steps.text: Rub the butter into the flour until it looks like breadcrumbs, then stir in the sugar, sultanas and spice.
Mix in the egg and milk to make a soft dough, and roll to 1cm thick.
Cut 12 rounds with a 6cm cutter.
Cook in a dry non-stick pan over medium-low heat for 3 minutes each side until golden brown and cooked through.
Dust with a little sugar and serve warm.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 cakes.
Food safety: wash hands after handling raw egg.

title: Cheddar and Mustard Cheese Twists
summary: Crisp puff pastry twists with sharp cheddar, mustard and sesame.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Spread one side of each pastry sheet with the mustard.
Scatter over the cheddar, fold in half and press down, then cut into 12 strips.
Twist each strip and lay on lined trays, pressing the ends down.
Brush with the egg, scatter with sesame seeds and bake for 15 minutes until puffed and golden.
Cool for 5 minutes so the cheese sets before eating.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 4 twists.
Food safety: wash hands after handling raw egg.

title: Golden Oat Flapjacks
summary: Chewy British oat bars with butter and golden syrup, cut into squares.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin.
Melt the butter, sugar and golden syrup together over low heat, stirring until smooth.
Stir in the oats, sultanas and salt until fully coated.
Press firmly into the tin and bake for 25 minutes until golden at the edges but still soft in the middle.
Cool completely in the tin, about 1 hour, then cut into 12 bars.

notes: Plus 1 hour cooling.
Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 bar.

title: Apple Cinnamon Muffins
summary: Tender muffins studded with apple and a cinnamon sugar crust.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a 6-hole muffin tin.
Whisk the oil, egg and milk, then fold in the flour, sugar and 1 tsp cinnamon until just combined.
Fold in the apple and divide between the holes.
Sprinkle with the remaining cinnamon and bake for 22 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 muffin.
Food safety: wash hands after handling raw egg.

title: Honey Sesame Pasteli
summary: Crunchy Greek sesame and honey bars that set hard as they cool.

steps.text: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan for 4 minutes until golden, then tip out.
Simmer the honey and lemon juice in the pan over medium heat for 5 minutes until it reaches a bubbling, thick caramel.
Stir in the sesame seeds and salt for 30 seconds until fully coated.
Press onto baking paper in a rectangle about 1cm thick.
Cool for 20 minutes until set, then break or cut into 10 pieces.

notes: Plus 20 minutes setting.
Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 piece.

title: Whipped Feta Dip with Pita Crisps
summary: Cloud-light feta and yoghurt dip with lemon and olive oil, served with crisp pita.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Cut the pita into 16 triangles and toss with 1 tbsp oil.
Bake the pita for 8 minutes until golden and crisp.
Blend the feta, yoghurt, lemon juice, garlic and remaining oil for 2 minutes until completely smooth.
Spoon into a bowl and make a swirl on top.
Serve with the pita crisps while they are still warm.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: a quarter of the dip with 4 crisps.

title: Beetroot Hummus with Veggie Sticks
summary: Vivid pink hummus with tahini and lemon, served with crunchy carrot and cucumber sticks.

steps.text: Drain the beetroot and chickpeas.
Blend the beetroot, chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, oil, cumin and salt for 3 minutes until completely smooth, scraping down the sides.
Taste and add more lemon or salt if needed.
Spoon into a bowl and drizzle with a little extra oil.
Serve with the carrot and cucumber sticks.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: a sixth of the dip with sticks.

title: White Bean and Rosemary Dip
summary: A creamy cannellini dip with lemon and rosemary, served with raw vegetable dippers.

steps.text: Blend the beans, oil, lemon juice, garlic, rosemary and salt for 2 minutes until completely smooth.
Add a splash of water if too thick.
Spoon into a bowl and drizzle with a little oil.
Taste and add more lemon or salt if needed.
Serve with the carrot sticks and capsicum strips.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: a quarter of the dip with veg.

title: Smoked Salmon and Dill Dip
summary: Creamy smoked salmon and cream cheese dip with dill and lemon, served with cucumber rounds.

steps.text: Chop the smoked salmon finely.
Beat the cream cheese, yoghurt and lemon juice until smooth.
Fold in the salmon, dill and pepper until evenly combined.
Chill for 30 minutes until firm.
Serve with the cucumber rounds.

notes: Plus 30 minutes chilling.
Snack. Per serving: a quarter of the dip with cucumber.
Food safety: keep smoked salmon below 5°C, eat within 2 days of opening, and avoid it if pregnant or immunocompromised.

title: Smoky Paprika Almonds
summary: Roasted almonds tossed with smoked paprika, garlic and sea salt.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional).
Toss the almonds with the oil, paprika, garlic powder and salt.
Spread on a tray and roast for 12 minutes until fragrant and a shade darker.
Cool for 10 minutes so they crisp.
Store in an airtight jar for up to 2 weeks.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: a small handful, about 30g.

title: Egg and Veggie Protein Mini Frittatas
summary: High-protein egg bites with spinach, capsicum and a little cheddar, baked in a muffin tin.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and grease a 6-hole muffin tin.
Whisk the eggs, milk, salt and pepper.
Divide the spinach, capsicum and cheddar between the holes and pour over the egg.
Bake for 18 minutes until puffed, set in the middle and golden.
Cool for 5 minutes in the tin before lifting out.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 frittata (about 9g protein).
Food safety: cook eggs until fully set, refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.

title: Chaat Masala Roasted Chickpeas
summary: Crunchy oven-roasted chickpeas with a tangy spiced finish.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional).
Drain the chickpeas and dry them thoroughly in a tea towel.
Toss with the oil and roast on a tray for 30 minutes, shaking twice, until crisp and golden.
Toss with the cumin, amchur, chilli and salt while hot.
Cool for 10 minutes to crisp up further and eat the same day.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: about 3/4 cup.

title: Chilli Salt Edamame
summary: Steamed edamame pods tossed with flaky salt, chilli and lime.

steps.text: Boil the edamame in salted water for 5 minutes until the pods are bright green and the beans tender.
Drain well in a colander and shake off the excess water.
Toss with the salt and chilli while still steaming so the seasoning sticks.
Squeeze over the juice of the lime and toss again.
Serve warm, squeezing the beans from the pods straight into your mouth.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: a quarter of the pods.

title: Orange Almond Biscotti
summary: Twice-baked Italian biscuits with almonds and orange zest, made for dunking.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a tray. Mix the flour, sugar and baking powder.
Beat the eggs with the zest and vanilla, stir into the flour, then knead in the almonds to form a stiff dough.
Shape into a log 30cm long and 6cm wide and bake for 30 minutes until firm and pale golden. Cool for 15 minutes.
Slice the log on the diagonal into 20 pieces, 1.5cm thick, lay cut side down and bake for 15 minutes more, turning once, until dry and golden.
Cool on a rack for 20 minutes, where they crisp up further.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 biscotti.
Food safety: wash hands after handling raw egg.

title: Soft Ginger Biscuits
summary: Spicy golden-brown ginger biscuits with a chewy centre.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line two trays.
Beat the butter, sugar and golden syrup, then beat in the yolk.
Stir in the flour, ginger and bicarbonate of soda to make a soft dough.
Roll into 20 balls, place 5cm apart and flatten slightly.
Bake for 12 minutes until golden at the edges and cracked on top. Cool for 10 minutes on the tray.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 to 3 biscuits.
Food safety: wash hands after handling raw egg yolk.

title: Fudgy Brownie Bites
summary: Rich, fudgy chocolate squares with a crackly top.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin.
Melt the butter and chocolate together over low heat, stirring until smooth, and cool for 5 minutes.
Whisk in the sugar and eggs, then fold in the flour and cocoa.
Stir through the walnuts, pour into the tin and bake for 22 minutes until the top is crackly and a skewer has a few moist crumbs.
Cool in the tin for 30 minutes, then cut into 18 squares.

notes: Plus 30 minutes cooling.
Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 squares.
Food safety: wash hands after handling raw egg.

title: Mango Yoghurt Ice Blocks
summary: Creamy mango and yoghurt ice blocks with a pinch of ground ginger.

steps.text: Blend the mango, yoghurt, honey, ginger and lemon juice for 2 minutes until completely smooth.
Pour into 6 ice-block moulds.
Freeze for 5 hours until solid.
Run the moulds under warm water for 10 seconds to release.
Eat straight away while the ice block is firm and before it starts to drip.

notes: Plus 5 hours freezing.
Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 ice block.

title: Baked Polenta Chips
summary: Crisp-edged baked polenta fingers with rosemary and sea salt.

steps.text: Bring the water and salt to the boil, whisk in the polenta and cook over low heat for 10 minutes, stirring, until very thick.
Spread into a lined 20cm tin and cool for 1 hour until firm.
Heat the oven to 220°C fan (240°C conventional). Cut into 16 chips and toss with the oil and rosemary.
Bake on a tray for 30 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp at the edges.
Serve with the yoghurt as a dip.

notes: Plus 1 hour setting.
Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 4 chips with dip.

title: Cheese and Tomato Pizza Scrolls
summary: Soft yeast-free scrolls spread with tomato paste and cheese, a classic school lunchbox snack.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray.
Mix the flour, yoghurt and salt into a soft dough and knead for 2 minutes until smooth.
Roll into a 25 x 35cm rectangle, spread with the tomato paste, then scatter with oregano and mozzarella.
Roll up from the long side and cut into 12 slices.
Place cut side up and bake for 20 minutes until puffed and golden. Cool for 5 minutes.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 scrolls.

title: Potato Latkes
summary: Crisp-edged grated potato pancakes with onion, served with apple and sour cream.

steps.text: Squeeze the grated potato and onion hard in a tea towel to remove the liquid.
Mix with the eggs, flour and salt.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat and spoon in heaped tablespoons, flattening each into a disc.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes each side until deep golden and crisp, draining on paper towel.
Serve hot with the grated apple and sour cream.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 4 latkes.
Food safety: wash hands after handling raw egg.

title: Fish Fingers with Tartare Dip
summary: Crumb-coated white fish strips baked until crisp, with a quick pickle and yoghurt dip.

items.raw: 400g firm white fish fillets, such as barramundi

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C fan (240°C conventional). Cut the fish into 12 fingers.
Roll in the flour, then the beaten egg, then the breadcrumbs.
Place on a lined tray, drizzle with the oil and bake for 15 minutes, turning once, until golden and the fish flakes easily and reaches at least 63°C.
Mix the yoghurt, pickles and lemon juice for the dip.
Serve the fish fingers hot straight from the oven with the dip alongside.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 3 fish fingers with dip.
Food safety: keep raw fish refrigerated, cook to at least 63°C and wash hands and boards after handling raw fish and egg.

title: Cheesy Corn Muffins
summary: Savoury cornbread muffins with cheddar and chives.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a 6-hole muffin tin.
Mix the polenta, flour, baking powder and salt.
Whisk the milk, egg and oil, then stir into the dry mix with the corn, cheddar and chives until just combined.
Divide between the holes and bake for 20 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 muffin.
Food safety: wash hands after handling raw egg.

title: Sweet Potato Wedges with Yoghurt Dip
summary: Crisp-edged baked sweet potato wedges with smoked paprika and a lemony yoghurt dip.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C fan (240°C conventional).
Cut the sweet potato into thick wedges and toss with the oil, paprika and salt.
Spread on two trays without crowding and roast for 35 minutes, turning once, until the edges are crisp and a knife slides in easily.
Stir the yoghurt, lemon juice and garlic together.
Serve the wedges hot with the dip.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: a quarter of the wedges with dip.

title: Spinach and Ricotta Filo Rolls
summary: Crisp filo cigars filled with spinach, ricotta and lemon.

steps.text: Wilt the spinach in a pan for 2 minutes, cool for 10 minutes, squeeze very dry and chop.
Mix with the ricotta, egg, lemon zest, nutmeg and salt.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Halve each filo sheet, brush with oil, spoon filling along one short edge and roll into a cigar, folding in the sides.
Place seam down on a lined tray, brush with the remaining oil and bake for 20 minutes until deep golden.
Rest for 5 minutes before eating.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 or 3 rolls.
Food safety: wash hands after handling raw egg.

title: Prawn Rice Paper Rolls with Peanut Dip
summary: Fresh rice paper rolls with cooked prawns, herbs and vermicelli, served with a peanut dipping sauce.

steps.text: Soak the vermicelli in boiling water for 5 minutes until tender, drain and rinse under cold water.
Dip a rice paper sheet in warm water for 10 seconds until just pliable and lay flat.
Arrange 2 prawn halves, a little vermicelli, carrot, cucumber and mint, then fold in the sides and roll up tightly.
Repeat with the remaining sheets until you have 12 tightly rolled rolls.
Whisk the peanut butter, hoisin, warm water and lime juice until smooth and serve for dipping.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 3 rolls with dip.
Food safety: use cooked prawns kept below 5°C, eat the rolls within 4 hours of making, and discard any left out for more than 2 hours.

title: Oat and Raisin Cookies
summary: Chewy oat cookies packed with raisins and cinnamon.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line two trays.
Beat the butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the egg.
Fold in the flour, oats, raisins, bicarbonate of soda and cinnamon.
Roll into 16 balls, place 5cm apart and flatten slightly.
Bake for 12 minutes until golden at the edges but soft in the middle. Cool for 10 minutes on the tray.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 cookies.
Food safety: wash hands after handling raw egg.

title: Tomato Basil Bruschetta Bites
summary: Crisp baguette slices topped with juicy tomatoes, basil and garlic.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional).
Brush the baguette slices with 2 tbsp oil and bake for 8 minutes until golden and crisp.
Mix the tomato, garlic, basil, vinegar, salt and remaining oil, and rest for 10 minutes.
Spoon onto the toasts just before serving.
Eat within 15 minutes so the bread stays crisp.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 4 bites.

title: Honey Soy Chicken Drumettes
summary: Sticky baked chicken wing drumettes in a honey, soy and ginger glaze.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional).
Mix the soy sauce, honey, ginger and garlic and toss with the chicken.
Spread on a lined tray and bake for 35 minutes, turning and basting twice, until sticky, deep golden and at least 75°C at the thickest part.
Scatter with the sesame seeds.
Rest for 5 minutes before eating.

notes: Snack. Per serving: about 5 drumettes.
Food safety: cook chicken to at least 75°C, wash hands and boards after handling raw chicken, and refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Lemon Yoghurt Loaf Slices
summary: A moist, tangy loaf with a thin lemon glaze, cut into thick slices for the lunchbox or afternoon tea.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a 22 x 12cm loaf tin with baking paper. Whisk the eggs, sugar and lemon zest for 2 minutes until pale.
Whisk in the yoghurt, olive oil and 2 tbsp of the lemon juice, then fold in the flour and baking powder until just combined.
Pour into the tin and bake for 50 minutes, until golden and a skewer in the centre comes out clean. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then lift out onto a rack.
Stir the remaining lemon juice into the icing sugar until smooth, then drizzle over the warm loaf. Let the glaze set for 15 minutes before cutting into 10 slices.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 slice. Keeps 4 days in an airtight container.
Food safety: wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg.

title: Chewy Oat and Sultana Cookies
summary: Soft-centred oat cookies with plump sultanas and brown sugar, ready from bowl to biscuit tin in half an hour.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line two trays with baking paper. Beat the butter and sugar for 3 minutes until fluffy, then beat in the egg and vanilla.
Stir in the flour, bicarbonate of soda, oats and sultanas until a thick dough forms.
Roll heaped tablespoons (about 40g each) into 18 balls, place 5cm apart and flatten slightly.
Bake for 12 minutes, swapping the trays halfway, until golden at the edges but still soft in the middle. Cool on the tray for 5 minutes, then move to a rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 cookies. Keeps 5 days in an airtight container.
Food safety: wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg.

title: Lemon Coconut Slice
summary: A shortbread base under a chewy lemon and coconut topping made with condensed milk, cut into small squares.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin with baking paper. Mix the flour, sugar and melted butter, press firmly into the tin and bake for 20 minutes until pale golden.
Stir the condensed milk, coconut, lemon zest, lemon juice and egg together until combined.
Spread over the hot base and bake for a further 20 minutes, until the top is golden and set.
Cool completely in the tin, then cut into 16 squares.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 squares. Keeps 5 days in an airtight container.
Food safety: wash your hands after handling raw egg and make sure the topping is baked until set.

title: Mixed Berry Oat Squares
summary: A buttery oat crumble pressed around a jammy mixed berry centre, cut into squares that travel well.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin with baking paper. Mix the oats, flour, brown sugar and baking powder, then stir in the melted butter until crumbly.
Press two-thirds of the mixture firmly into the tin and bake for 10 minutes, until the edges are just set.
Toss the berries with the caster sugar, cornflour and lemon juice, spread over the base and scatter the remaining crumble on top.
Bake for 25 minutes, until the top is golden and the berries are bubbling. Cool completely in the tin, then cut into 12 squares.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 square. Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

title: Cheddar and Chive Scones
summary: Tall, tender savoury scones with sharp cheese and fresh chives, best eaten warm with butter.

items.raw: 1 cup grated vegetarian hard cheese, cheddar style (100g)
1 cup milk (250ml), plus 1 tbsp for glazing

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray with baking paper. Rub the butter into the flour, salt and mustard powder with your fingertips until it looks like breadcrumbs.
Stir in 3/4 of the cheese and the chives, then add the milk and mix with a knife to a soft, slightly sticky dough.
Turn onto a floured bench and pat out to 3cm thick. Cut 12 rounds with a 6cm cutter and place them close together on the tray.
Brush with milk, top with the remaining cheese and bake for 18 minutes, until risen and deep golden. Cool for 5 minutes before serving.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 scone. Best on the day; freeze for up to 2 months and reheat at 160°C fan for 8 minutes.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Apple and Walnut Scones
summary: Scones studded with grated apple, walnuts and cinnamon, soft inside with a golden top.

items.raw: 3/4 cup milk (185ml), plus 1 tbsp for glazing

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray with baking paper. Rub the butter into the flour, sugar and cinnamon until it looks like breadcrumbs.
Squeeze the grated apple in your fist to remove extra juice, then stir it through with the walnuts.
Add the milk and mix with a knife to a soft dough. Pat out to 3cm thick on a floured bench and cut 12 rounds with a 6cm cutter.
