Place close together on the tray, brush with milk and bake for 18 minutes, until risen and golden. Cool for 5 minutes before serving.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 scone. Best on the day; freeze for up to 2 months.

title: Fruit Scones with Jam and Cream
summary: Classic sultana scones served with strawberry jam and softly whipped cream, a proper afternoon tea.

items.raw: 1 cup milk (250ml), plus 1 tbsp for glazing
100ml thickened cream, whipped to soft peaks

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray with baking paper. Rub the butter into the flour and sugar until it looks like breadcrumbs, then stir in the sultanas.
Add the milk and mix with a knife to a soft dough. Pat out to 3cm thick on a floured bench and cut 12 rounds with a 6cm cutter.
Place close together on the tray, brush with milk and bake for 18 minutes, until risen and golden. Cool for 5 minutes under a tea towel.
Split each scone and serve with a spoonful of jam and a dollop of cream.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 scone with jam and cream. Scones are best on the day; freeze them for up to 2 months.

title: Cinnamon Scone Scrolls
summary: No-yeast scone dough rolled up with cinnamon sugar and finished with a thin icing, ready in under an hour.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin with baking paper. Rub the cold butter into the flour until it looks like breadcrumbs, then stir in the 1 cup of milk to make a soft dough.
Roll the dough on a floured bench into a 25 x 40cm rectangle. Spread with the soft butter and scatter with the brown sugar and cinnamon.
Roll up from the long side, trim the ends and cut into 10 even pieces. Pack them cut side up in the tin.
Bake for 18 minutes, until golden and cooked through. Stir the icing sugar with the 1 tbsp of milk and drizzle over the warm scrolls.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 scroll. Best on the day; keeps 2 days airtight.

title: Custard Tarts
summary: Crisp shortcrust cases holding a barely-set nutmeg custard, baked in a muffin tin.

steps.text: Rub the butter into the flour and icing sugar until it looks like breadcrumbs. Mix in the egg yolk and enough cold water to form a dough, wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Roll the pastry to 3mm thick, cut 12 rounds with a 9cm cutter and press into a greased 12-hole muffin tin. Bake for 10 minutes until pale and dry.
Reduce the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional). Whisk the eggs, sugar, milk and vanilla together and pour into the cases, then dust with nutmeg.
Bake for 20 minutes, until the custard is just set with a slight wobble in the centre. Cool in the tin for 15 minutes and chill before serving.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 tart. Plus 30 minutes chilling the pastry. Keeps 2 days in the fridge.
Food safety: bake the custard until set, wash your hands after handling raw egg, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Apricot Jam Tarts
summary: Little buttery pastry cases filled with bubbling strawberry jam, a party plate favourite.

steps.text: Rub the butter into the flour and icing sugar until it looks like breadcrumbs. Mix in the egg yolk and cold water to form a dough, wrap and chill for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Roll the pastry to 3mm thick, cut 12 rounds with a 8cm cutter and press into a greased 12-hole tart or muffin tin.
Spoon 1 tbsp jam into each case, filling them only two-thirds full as the jam bubbles up.
Bake for 15 minutes, until the pastry is golden and the jam is bubbling. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, as the jam is very hot.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 tart. Plus 20 minutes chilling the pastry. Keeps 4 days airtight.
Food safety: wash your hands and the bench after handling the raw egg yolk.

title: Lemon Curd Tartlets
summary: Crisp pastry cases filled with a tangy, silky home-made lemon curd.

steps.text: Rub the 125g butter into the flour and icing sugar, mix in the egg yolk and water to a dough, wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Roll the pastry to 3mm, cut 12 rounds with a 8cm cutter, press into a 12-hole tin and bake for 12 minutes until golden. Cool.
Whisk the eggs, extra yolk, sugar, zest and juice in a small saucepan over low heat, stirring for 8 minutes until thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. Do not let it boil.
Off the heat, whisk in the 60g butter until smooth, then spoon the hot curd into the cases. Chill for 1 hour until set.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 tartlet. Plus 30 minutes chilling the pastry and 1 hour setting. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
Food safety: cook the curd until thick and hot, wash your hands after handling raw egg, and refrigerate within 2 hours.

title: Mixed Berry Almond Friands
summary: Light, moist almond cakes made with egg whites and berries in the middle.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and grease a 12-hole muffin tin. Whisk the egg whites lightly with a fork until just frothy.
Stir in the icing sugar, almond meal, flour and orange zest, then mix in the melted butter until smooth.
Divide among the holes, push 2 or 3 berries into each and bake for 20 minutes, until golden and springy to the touch.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then turn out onto a rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 friand. Keeps 3 days airtight.
Food safety: bake until golden and set; wash your hands and bowls after handling raw egg white.

title: Orange and Sesame Seed Muffins
summary: Bright, citrusy muffins with a crunch of sesame seeds, mixed in one bowl.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases. Mix the flour, sugar, sesame seeds and orange zest in a large bowl.
Whisk the eggs, milk, melted butter and orange juice together, tip into the dry mix and fold until just combined; a few lumps are fine.
Divide among the cases and bake for 20 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then move to a rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 muffin. Keeps 3 days airtight; freezes for 2 months.
Food safety: wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg.

title: Mixed Berry Coconut Muffins
summary: Tender muffins with tart mixed berries and desiccated coconut, with no mixer needed.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases. Mix the flour, coconut and sugar in a large bowl.
Whisk the eggs, milk and melted butter together, tip into the dry mix and fold until just combined.
Gently fold in the frozen berries, divide among the cases and bake for 22 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then move to a rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 muffin. Keeps 3 days airtight; freezes for 2 months.
Food safety: wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg.

title: Carrot Cake Squares with Cream Cheese Icing
summary: Spiced carrot and walnut cake topped with tangy icing, cut into party-size squares.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin with baking paper. Whisk the eggs, brown sugar and oil together, then stir in the carrot and walnuts.
Fold in the flour and cinnamon until just combined. Pour into the tin and bake for 35 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool completely in the tin. Beat the cream cheese, butter and icing sugar until smooth, spread over the cake and chill for 20 minutes.
Cut into 16 squares with a hot, dry knife.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 squares. Plus 20 minutes chilling. Keeps 4 days in the fridge.
Food safety: wash your hands after handling raw egg and keep the iced cake in the fridge.

title: Honey Oat Flapjacks
summary: Chewy, golden oat bars sweetened with honey and brown sugar, with just five ingredients.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin with baking paper. Melt the butter, sugar and honey in a saucepan over low heat for 3 minutes until smooth.
Stir in the oats and salt until every oat is coated.
Press firmly into the tin and bake for 25 minutes, until golden around the edges but still soft in the centre.
Cool completely in the tin before cutting into 12 bars; they firm up as they cool.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian, not vegan (honey). Per serving: 1 bar. Keeps 5 days airtight.

title: Fudgy Brownie Squares
summary: Dense chocolate squares with a crackly top and a fudgy middle.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin with baking paper. Melt the chocolate and butter together over low heat, stirring, then cool for 5 minutes.
Whisk the sugar and eggs into the chocolate mixture until glossy.
Fold in the flour and cocoa until just combined, then pour into the tin.
Bake for 25 minutes, until the top is set and cracked but the centre is still slightly soft. Cool completely in the tin and cut into 16 squares.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 squares. Keeps 4 days airtight.
Food safety: wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg.

title: Shortbread Fingers
summary: Pale, crumbly Scottish-style shortbread that melts in the mouth.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 140°C fan (160°C conventional) and line a 20 x 30cm tin with baking paper. Beat the butter and sugar for 3 minutes until pale.
Stir in the flour and cornflour to form a soft dough, then press evenly into the tin and prick all over with a fork.
Bake for 30 minutes, until pale golden at the edges; it should not colour much.
Cut into 24 fingers while hot, then cool completely in the tin.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 fingers. Keeps 2 weeks airtight.

title: Ginger Crunch Squares
summary: A crisp ginger base topped with a sticky, sweet ginger icing, a classic bakery slice.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin with baking paper. Beat the 125g butter and caster sugar until pale, then stir in the flour, baking powder and 1 tbsp ginger.
Press firmly into the tin and bake for 20 minutes, until golden.
While it bakes, melt the 80g butter and golden syrup in a saucepan, then stir in the icing sugar and remaining ginger until smooth.
Pour the icing over the hot base, cool completely and cut into 20 squares.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 squares. Keeps 5 days airtight.

title: Cinnamon Sugar Doughnut Muffins
summary: Soft muffins brushed with butter and rolled in cinnamon sugar, tasting like a baked doughnut.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and grease a 12-hole muffin tin. Whisk the egg, milk and the 80g melted butter together.
Stir in the flour and 1/2 cup sugar until just combined and divide among the holes.
Bake for 20 minutes, until golden and springy. Cool for 5 minutes.
Mix the coating sugar and cinnamon. Brush each warm muffin all over with the melted butter, then roll in the cinnamon sugar.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 muffin. Best on the day.
Food safety: wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg.

title: Soft-Baked Chocolate Chip Cookies
summary: Thick cookies with crisp edges, a soft centre and plenty of dark chocolate.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line two trays with baking paper. Beat the butter and both sugars for 3 minutes until fluffy, then beat in the egg, yolk and vanilla.
Stir in the flour and bicarbonate of soda, then fold through the chocolate chips.
Roll 24 balls (about 40g each), place 6cm apart on the trays and bake for 11 minutes, swapping trays halfway, until the edges are set and the centres look slightly underdone.
Rest on the tray for 5 minutes, then move to a rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 cookies. Keeps 5 days airtight.
Food safety: wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg.

title: Gingerbread Biscuits
summary: Spiced golden syrup biscuits that hold their shape for cutting and decorating.

steps.text: Beat the butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the golden syrup and egg. Stir in the flour, bicarbonate of soda, ginger and cinnamon to form a dough, wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line two trays with baking paper.
Roll the dough 4mm thick on a floured bench and cut out 30 shapes with a 7cm cutter, re-rolling the offcuts.
Bake for 10 minutes, until firm at the edges and lightly browned. Cool on the tray for 5 minutes, then on a rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 3 biscuits. Plus 30 minutes chilling. Keeps 2 weeks airtight.
Food safety: wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg.

title: Peanut Butter Oat Bars
summary: No-bake chewy bars of oats, peanut butter, honey and sultanas, set in the fridge.

steps.text: Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper. Warm the peanut butter and honey in a saucepan over low heat for 5 minutes, stirring until smooth and runny.
Off the heat, stir in the oats, sultanas and salt until evenly coated.
Press very firmly into the tin with the back of a spoon so the bars hold together.
Chill for 1 hour until firm, then cut into 12 bars.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian, not vegan (honey). Contains peanuts. Per serving: 1 bar. Plus 1 hour chilling. Keeps 5 days in the fridge.

title: Paneer Gulab Jamun
summary: Soft, golden paneer and semolina dumplings soaked in a rose and cardamom syrup, made without milk powder.

steps.text: Boil the sugar and water for 5 minutes until slightly syrupy, then stir in the cardamom and rose water and keep warm.
Knead the paneer, semolina, flour and milk together for 4 minutes until the dough is smooth and holds together without cracks. Roll into 12 smooth balls, each about 28g.
Heat the ghee in a wide frying pan over low heat. Fry the balls in batches, turning often, for 8 minutes until deep golden brown on all sides.
Drop the hot balls into the warm syrup and soak for 30 minutes, until they swell and feel soft.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 gulab jamun. Keep the heat low so the centres cook through. Keeps 3 days in the fridge in the syrup.

title: Nariyal Ladoo Coconut Balls
summary: Chewy coconut sweets with cardamom, made from just three ingredients in a single pan.

items.raw: 160g desiccated coconut, plus 2 tbsp extra for rolling

steps.text: Stir the coconut, condensed milk and cardamom in a non-stick frying pan over low heat for 8 minutes, until the mixture thickens and pulls away from the pan.
Cool the mixture for 10 minutes until you can handle it.
Roll level tablespoons into 12 balls, about 25g each, then roll in the extra coconut.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 ladoo. Keeps 5 days in the fridge.

title: Kaju Katli Cashew Diamonds
summary: Smooth, delicate cashew fudge rolled thin and cut into diamonds.

steps.text: Blitz the cashews in short pulses for 30 seconds until a fine powder, stopping before it turns oily. Sift to remove any large pieces.
Boil the sugar and water in a small non-stick pan for 4 minutes until it becomes a sticky syrup that forms a thread between your finger and thumb.
Stir in the cashew powder over low heat for 4 minutes until it forms a soft dough that leaves the sides of the pan. Stir in the ghee.
Knead briefly while warm, roll to 5mm between two sheets of baking paper and cool for 15 minutes. Cut into 20 diamonds.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains tree nuts. Per serving: 2 pieces. Keeps 1 week in the fridge.

title: Rasgulla Syrupy Cheese Balls
summary: Spongy fresh cheese balls simmered in light syrup, a Bengali mithai that is lighter than it looks.

steps.text: Bring the milk to the boil, then turn off the heat and stir in the lemon juice a spoon at a time until the curds separate and the whey turns clear.
Pour through a muslin-lined sieve, rinse the curds under cold water for 1 minute to remove the lemon taste, then squeeze out the water and hang for 20 minutes.
Knead the warm chhena on the bench for 8 minutes until it is smooth and no longer grainy. Roll into 12 smooth balls.
Boil the sugar and water in a wide pan, then drop in the balls and simmer with the lid on for 25 minutes until they double in size and sink when pressed.
Stir in the rose water and cool completely in the syrup, then chill.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 rasgulla. Plus 20 minutes draining. Keeps 4 days in the fridge in the syrup.

title: Sooji Halwa Squares
summary: Toasted semolina cooked with ghee, cashews and sultanas, set in a tray and cut into squares.

steps.text: Heat the ghee in a large pan over medium heat, fry the cashews for 1 minute until pale gold, then add the semolina and stir for 6 minutes until it smells nutty and turns light golden.
Boil the water with the sugar and cardamom until the sugar dissolves, then carefully pour into the semolina, stirring fast, as it will spit.
Add the sultanas and cook for 4 minutes, stirring, until thick and the mixture leaves the sides of the pan.
Press into a greased 18cm square tin, level the top and cool for 30 minutes before cutting into 12 squares.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 square. Keeps 4 days at room temperature, covered.

title: Mysore Pak Ghee Fudge
summary: A rich, melt-in-the-mouth gram flour and ghee sweet with a honeycombed texture.

steps.text: Mix the chickpea flour with 3 tbsp of the melted ghee into a smooth paste. Grease a 15cm square tin.
Boil the sugar and water in a deep pan for 5 minutes until it forms a one-thread syrup between finger and thumb.

Add the chickpea paste and stir for 2 minutes over medium heat, then add the remaining ghee a few spoons at a time, stirring all the while, for 12 minutes until the mixture bubbles, thickens and turns glossy.
Pour into the tin immediately, level and cool for 10 minutes, then cut into 12 pieces while still warm. Leave to set for 15 minutes.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 piece. Be careful: the sugar syrup is very hot. Keeps 1 week airtight.

title: Ricotta Kalakand Squares
summary: A soft, grainy milk-cake sweet made from ricotta, set in a tray and topped with pistachios.

steps.text: Stir the ricotta and sugar in a non-stick pan over medium-low heat for 20 minutes, until it thickens, loses most of its moisture and starts to pull away from the sides.
Stir in the cardamom, then press into a greased 15cm square tin and level the top.
Scatter with the pistachios, press them in lightly and cool for 30 minutes.
Chill for 1 hour until firm, then cut into 12 squares.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains tree nuts. Per serving: 1 square. Plus 1 hour chilling. Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

title: Walnut and Pistachio Baklava Fingers
summary: Crisp layers of filo with a spiced nut filling, cut into fingers and soaked in lemon honey syrup.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Mix the walnuts, pistachios and cinnamon. Grease a 20 x 30cm tin.

Lay 4 filo sheets in the tin, brushing each with butter. Spread over the nut mix, then top with the remaining sheets, brushing each with butter. Brush the top and cut into 24 fingers with a sharp knife.
Bake for 35 minutes, until deep golden and crisp.
While it bakes, simmer the sugar, water, honey and lemon juice for 8 minutes until slightly syrupy. Cool.
Pour the cool syrup over the hot baklava and leave for 2 hours before serving.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian, not vegan (honey and butter). Contains tree nuts and gluten. Per serving: 2 fingers. Plus 2 hours soaking. Keeps 1 week airtight.

title: Basbousa Semolina and Coconut Cake
summary: A tender semolina and coconut cake cut into diamonds and drenched in lemon and rose syrup.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and grease a 20cm square tin. Mix the semolina, coconut, 110g sugar and baking powder, then stir in the yoghurt and butter to a thick batter.
Spread into the tin, score into 12 diamonds and press an almond into each.
Bake for 30 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Meanwhile simmer the syrup sugar, water and lemon juice for 6 minutes until slightly syrupy, stir in the rose water and cool.
Pour the cool syrup over the hot cake and leave to soak for 20 minutes, then cut through the lines.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains tree nuts and gluten. Per serving: 1 diamond. Keeps 4 days covered.

title: Ma'amoul Walnut Cookies
summary: Buttery semolina shortbread stuffed with spiced walnuts and dusted with icing sugar.

steps.text: Mix the semolina, flour and butter, rub together for 3 minutes, then stir in the milk and rose water to a soft dough. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional) and line a tray. Mix the walnuts, sugar and cinnamon for the filling.
Divide the dough into 16 balls, flatten each in your palm, put 1 tsp filling in the centre and close the dough around it. Press gently into a ma'amoul mould or flatten slightly.
Bake for 20 minutes, until set and pale with only a hint of colour. Cool completely and dust with icing sugar.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains tree nuts and gluten. Per serving: 2 cookies. Plus 30 minutes resting. Keeps 2 weeks airtight.

title: Atayef Ricotta Pancakes
summary: Small folded pancakes stuffed with sweet rose ricotta, drizzled with syrup and pistachios.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, semolina, yeast, 1 tsp sugar and baking powder with the warm water until smooth. Rest for 20 minutes until bubbly.
Simmer the syrup sugar and water for 6 minutes until slightly thick, then cool.

Mix the ricotta, 1 tbsp sugar and rose water. Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat and pour in 3 tbsp batter per pancake, cooking one side only for 2 minutes until the top is full of bubbles and dry. Make 12.
Fold each pancake in half around 1 tbsp of the ricotta mix and pinch the edge closed.
Serve drizzled with the syrup and scattered with pistachios.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains tree nuts and gluten. Per serving: 2 pancakes. Plus 20 minutes resting. Best the day they are made.

title: Alfajores with Dulce de Leche
summary: Melt-in-the-mouth cornflour biscuits sandwiched with a golden milk caramel.

steps.text: Beat the 125g butter and icing sugar for 3 minutes until pale, then beat in the yolks and vanilla. Stir in the cornflour, plain flour and baking powder to a soft dough, wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Stir the condensed milk and 20g butter in a saucepan over low heat for 25 minutes until it turns thick and golden like fudge. Cool.
Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Roll the dough 5mm thick, cut 24 rounds with a 5cm cutter and bake on lined trays for 12 minutes, until set and pale; they should not brown.
Cool completely, then sandwich pairs with 1 tbsp of the caramel.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 alfajor. Plus 30 minutes chilling. Keeps 5 days airtight.
Food safety: wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg yolks.

title: Brigadeiros Chocolate Truffles
summary: Fudgy Brazilian chocolate balls rolled in coconut, made from condensed milk and cocoa.

steps.text: Stir the condensed milk, cocoa and butter in a non-stick pan over medium-low heat for 8 minutes, until the mixture is thick enough to drag a clear line across the base for 2 seconds.
Pour onto a greased plate and cool for 20 minutes, then chill for 1 hour until firm enough to roll.
With buttered hands, roll level teaspoons (about 15g) into 24 balls, then roll in the coconut.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 brigadeiros. Plus 1 hour chilling. Keeps 5 days in the fridge.

title: Cocadas Baked Coconut Mounds
summary: Chewy coconut macaroon-style mounds with a golden edge, sweetened with condensed milk.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a tray with baking paper. Mix the coconut, condensed milk, egg yolks and vanilla.
Scoop 12 mounds, about 2 tbsp each, onto the tray, pressing them together.
Bake for 20 minutes, until the tips and edges are golden brown.
Cool on the tray for 10 minutes before lifting.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 mound. Keeps 5 days airtight.
Food safety: bake until golden and set; wash your hands after handling raw egg yolks.

title: Tres Leches Squares
summary: A light sponge soaked in three milks and topped with cinnamon cream.

items.raw: 200ml thickened cream, whipped to soft peaks

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and grease a 20 x 30cm tin. Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks, then whisk in the sugar a spoon at a time for 3 minutes until glossy.
Fold in the yolks, then the flour, baking powder and 3 tbsp milk until just combined. Pour into the tin and bake for 25 minutes, until golden and springy.
Whisk the condensed milk, 250ml milk and 125ml cream. Prick the warm cake all over with a fork and pour the mix slowly over it.
Chill for 4 hours, then spread with the whipped cream, dust with cinnamon and cut into 12 squares.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 square. Plus 4 hours chilling. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
Food safety: bake the sponge until set, wash your hands after handling raw egg, and refrigerate within 2 hours.

title: Polvorones Pecan Snowball Cookies
summary: Crumbly buttery cookies full of ground pecans, rolled in icing sugar.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional) and line two trays. Beat the butter and 65g icing sugar for 3 minutes until pale, then beat in the vanilla.
Stir in the flour and pecans to a soft dough. Roll level tablespoons into 24 balls and place 3cm apart.
Bake for 18 minutes, until set and pale golden underneath. Cool on the tray for 5 minutes.
Roll the warm cookies in the remaining icing sugar, then roll again once cool.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains tree nuts and gluten. Per serving: 2 cookies. Keeps 2 weeks airtight.

title: Mitarashi Dango with Sweet Soy Glaze
summary: Chewy rice-flour dumplings on skewers, brushed with a glossy sweet soy glaze.

items.raw: 2 tsp cornflour mixed with 1 tbsp water

steps.text: Mix the rice flour, 1 tbsp sugar and hot water, then knead for 3 minutes until smooth and like earlobe-soft dough. Roll into 12 balls.
Boil the dango in a pot of water for 4 minutes until they float, then lift into iced water for 1 minute and drain.
Simmer the soy sauce, 40g sugar and 100ml water for 2 minutes, stir in the cornflour mix and cook for 1 minute until glossy and thick.
Thread 3 dango onto each of 4 skewers, grill or pan-sear for 3 minutes until lightly charred, then brush with the glaze.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 1 skewer of 3 dango. Best eaten the day they are made.

title: Dorayaki Pancake Sandwiches with Apricot Jam
summary: Honey-scented pancakes sandwiched with apricot jam and whipped cream.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs, sugar and honey for 4 minutes until pale and doubled in volume, then whisk in the water.
Sift in the flour and baking powder and fold until smooth. Rest the batter for 10 minutes.
Heat a non-stick pan over low heat and pour in 3 tbsp batter to make a 9cm pancake. Cook for 2 minutes until bubbles appear on the surface, flip and cook for 1 minute until golden. Make 12 pancakes.
Sandwich pairs of cooled pancakes with jam and whipped cream.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian, not vegan (egg and honey). Per serving: 1 sandwich. Best the same day.
Food safety: cook the pancakes through until golden and set; wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg.

title: Daigaku Imo Candied Sweet Potato
summary: Crisp-edged roasted sweet potato wedges tossed in a sticky sweet soy glaze and sesame seeds.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Toss the sweet potato with the oil and roast on a lined tray for 25 minutes, turning once, until golden outside and tender when pierced.
Simmer the sugar, soy sauce and water in a small pan for 3 minutes until syrupy and bubbling.
Toss the hot potato wedges in the glaze for 1 minute until glossy and sticky.
Sprinkle with the sesame seeds and cool for 5 minutes, as the glaze is very hot.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: a quarter of the wedges. Best eaten warm.

title: Bibingka Cheese and Coconut Cups
summary: Soft rice-flour cakes baked with coconut milk, topped with melted cheese and a sprinkle of coconut.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and grease a 12-hole muffin tin. Mix the rice flour, sugar and baking powder.
Whisk the eggs, coconut milk, milk and butter, then stir into the dry mix until smooth.
Divide among the holes, scatter with the cheese and coconut, and bake for 20 minutes, until puffed and golden.
Rest in the tin for 5 minutes before lifting out.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 cake. Best eaten warm on the day.
Food safety: bake until set; wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg.

title: Puto Steamed Rice Cakes with Cheese
summary: Fluffy, lightly sweet steamed rice-flour cakes with a salty cheese topping.

items.raw: 30g vegetarian hard cheese, cut into small cubes

steps.text: Mix the rice flour, sugar and baking powder, then whisk in the milk, egg and oil until smooth.
Grease 12 small moulds or a 12-hole silicone muffin tray and fill each two-thirds full. Put a cube of cheese on top of each.
Steam over simmering water, covered with a tea towel under the lid, for 15 minutes until risen and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool for 5 minutes before turning out.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 cakes. Best eaten the same day.
Food safety: steam until set; wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg.

title: Maja Blanca Coconut Corn Pudding
summary: A set coconut milk pudding studded with sweet corn, cut into squares and topped with toasted coconut.

steps.text: Whisk the coconut milk, milk, sugar and cornflour in a saucepan until smooth.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 12 minutes until very thick and glossy, then stir in the corn.
Pour into a lightly oiled 18cm square tin, smooth the top and cool for 20 minutes.
Chill for 3 hours until firm, scatter with the toasted coconut and cut into 8 squares.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 square. Plus 3 hours chilling. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Pizza Scrolls with Ham and Mozzarella
summary: No-yeast scone dough rolled up with tomato paste, ham and melted mozzarella, a lunchbox favourite.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray with baking paper. Rub the butter into the flour until it looks like breadcrumbs, then stir in the milk to make a soft dough.
Roll the dough on a floured bench into a 25 x 40cm rectangle. Spread with the tomato paste and scatter with the ham, three-quarters of the mozzarella and the oregano.
Roll up from the long side, trim the ends and cut into 12 even pieces. Place cut side up on the tray and top with the remaining cheese.
Bake for 18 minutes, until golden and the cheese is bubbling. Cool for 5 minutes before serving.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 scroll. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; freeze for up to 2 months.
Food safety: keep the ham refrigerated until you assemble the scrolls, bake until hot throughout, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Chickpea and Mushroom Party Rolls
summary: Flaky pastry rolls filled with a savoury chickpea, mushroom and smoked paprika mix.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray with baking paper. Fry the onion and mushrooms in the olive oil for 8 minutes until the liquid has evaporated and they turn golden, then stir in the paprika and soy sauce and cool.
Roughly mash the chickpeas with a fork, then mix with the cooled mushrooms and breadcrumbs.
Cut each pastry sheet in half to make 4 strips. Spoon the filling down the centre of each strip, brush one edge with soy milk and roll to enclose with the seam underneath.
Cut each roll into 4, place seam side down on the tray, brush with soy milk and bake for 25 minutes, until deep golden and puffed.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 rolls. Check the pastry label for dairy and egg if serving vegans. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat at 180°C fan for 8 minutes.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Pork and Apple Sausage Rolls
summary: Juicy pork and apple filling in golden puff pastry with a hint of wholegrain mustard.

items.raw: 1 egg yolk, mixed with 1 tbsp water, for glazing
items.prep: mixed with 1 tbsp water, for glazing

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray with baking paper. Mix the pork, apple, onion, breadcrumbs, egg and mustard with your hands until well combined.
Cut each pastry sheet in half. Shape the filling into 4 logs, lay one along each strip, brush the edge with glaze and roll to enclose with the seam underneath.
Cut each roll into 4, place seam side down on the tray and brush with glaze.
Bake for 30 minutes, until deep golden and the pork reaches at least 75°C in the centre.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 rolls. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: mince must reach at least 75°C in the centre. Wash your hands, board and bench after handling raw pork and egg, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Soft Pretzels with Mustard
summary: Chewy, deep-brown pretzels dipped in a bicarbonate bath, sprinkled with salt and served with mustard.

items.raw: 1 egg yolk, mixed with 1 tbsp water

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, then add the warm water and oil and knead for 8 minutes until smooth and elastic. Cover and prove for 1 hour until doubled.
Heat the oven to 220°C fan (240°C conventional) and line two trays. Divide the dough into 8, roll each into a 50cm rope and twist into a pretzel shape.
Bring the water and bicarbonate of soda to a gentle boil in a wide pan. Lower the pretzels in 2 at a time and simmer for 30 seconds each side until puffed, then lift out and drain.
Brush with the egg wash, sprinkle with coarse salt and bake for 14 minutes, until deep mahogany brown. Serve warm with mustard.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 pretzel with 1/2 tbsp mustard. Plus 1 hour proving. Best the day they are made.
Food safety: wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg yolk. The bicarbonate bath is alkaline; do not splash it into your eyes.

title: Spinach and Feta Filo Triangles
summary: Crisp buttery filo parcels filled with spinach, feta and dill.

items.raw: 250g frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a tray. Mix the spinach, feta, egg, dill and nutmeg.
Lay 1 sheet of filo on the bench, keeping the rest covered with a damp tea towel. Brush with butter, cut lengthwise into 2 strips, and place 1 tbsp filling at the end of each strip.
Fold the corner over the filling to form a triangle and keep folding along the strip to the end. Repeat with the remaining sheets to make 16 triangles.
Place seam side down on the tray, brush with butter and bake for 20 minutes, until deep golden and crisp.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 triangles. Keeps 2 days in the fridge; crisp up in a 160°C fan oven for 8 minutes.
Food safety: wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg.

title: Frankfurt Muffin Bites
summary: Cheesy savoury muffins with a chunk of frankfurt in each, great hot or cold for kids.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and grease a 12-hole muffin tin. Whisk the egg, milk and butter together.
Stir in the flour, cheese and chives until just combined, then divide among the holes.
Press half a frankfurt into the centre of each muffin.
Bake for 20 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool for 5 minutes.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 muffins. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; freeze for 2 months.
Food safety: keep the frankfurts refrigerated until use, bake until piping hot, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours. Wash your hands after handling raw egg.

title: Cheese and Corn Muffins
summary: Savoury muffins with sweet corn, sharp cheese and chives, mixed in one bowl.

items.raw: 100g grated vegetarian hard cheese, cheddar style

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases. Mix the flour, three-quarters of the cheese, the corn and chives.
Whisk the eggs, milk and butter together, tip into the dry mix and fold until just combined.
Divide among the cases, scatter with the remaining cheese and bake for 22 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes before lifting out.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 muffin. Keeps 3 days airtight; freezes for 2 months.
Food safety: wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg.

title: Pumpkin and Feta Muffins
summary: Moist savoury muffins with grated pumpkin, creamy feta and pumpkin seeds.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases. Mix the flour, pumpkin, feta and thyme.
Whisk the eggs, milk and oil together, tip into the dry mix and fold until just combined.
Divide among the cases, scatter with the pumpkin seeds and bake for 25 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes before lifting out.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 muffin. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; freezes for 2 months.
Food safety: wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg.

title: Cheddar Oat Crackers
summary: Crisp, nutty crackers with oats and sharp cheese, rolled thin and baked.

items.raw: 100g grated vegetarian hard cheese, cheddar style

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line two trays. Blitz the oats in a food processor for 20 seconds until coarse, then add the flour, cheese, butter and salt and pulse until crumbly.
Add the water and pulse until the dough just comes together.
Roll the dough 2mm thick between two sheets of baking paper and cut into 30 squares, about 4cm. Place on the trays.
Bake for 15 minutes, until golden at the edges and crisp. Cool on the tray, as they crisp further as they cool.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 5 crackers. Keeps 1 week airtight.

title: Smoky Roasted Paprika Chickpeas
summary: Crunchy oven-roasted chickpeas with smoked paprika and garlic, a high-fibre snack.

items.raw: 2 x 400g tins chickpeas, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Dry the chickpeas very well on a clean tea towel for 3 minutes, removing any loose skins.
Toss with the olive oil on a lined tray and roast for 20 minutes, until starting to colour.
Shake the tray, add the paprika, garlic powder and salt and toss to coat.
Roast for a further 10 minutes until deep golden and crunchy. Cool for 10 minutes, as they crisp up further.

notes: Snack. Vegan, gluten-free. Per serving: about 1/2 cup (120g). Best the day they are made; keeps 2 days uncovered, then loses crunch.

title: Super Seed Crackers
summary: Thin, crisp crackers made from sunflower, pumpkin and sesame seeds.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional) and line a large tray with baking paper. Whisk the cornflour with 50ml cold water, pour in the boiling water and stir for 1 minute until clear and thick.
Mix in the seeds, oats and salt and rest for 5 minutes until the gel is absorbed.
Spread very thinly, about 3mm, over the tray and score into 24 pieces.
Bake for 45 minutes, until dry, golden and crisp, turning the tray halfway. Cool on the tray, then snap apart.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 4 crackers. Keeps 2 weeks airtight. Use certified gluten-free oats if required.

title: Crispy Baked Apple Chips
summary: Paper-thin apple slices dried in a low oven until crisp, with a dusting of cinnamon.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 100°C fan (120°C conventional) and line two trays with baking paper. Slice the apples 2mm thick, ideally with a mandoline, and toss in the lemon juice.
Lay the slices in a single layer and dust with cinnamon.
Bake for 90 minutes, flipping once at 45 minutes, until dry at the edges and just starting to crisp.
Turn off the oven and leave in for 15 minutes more, until crisp. They crisp more as they cool.

notes: Snack. Vegan, gluten-free. Per serving: about a quarter of the batch. Keeps 5 days airtight.

title: Mango Fruit Leather
summary: Chewy sheets of baked mango puree with a squeeze of lemon, no added sugar beyond a touch of honey.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 80°C fan (100°C conventional) and line a tray with baking paper. Blend the mango, lemon juice and honey for 1 minute until completely smooth.
Spread the puree 3mm thick across the tray, leaving a 2cm border.
Bake for 3 hours, until no longer sticky in the centre when touched.
Cool on the tray, peel off with the paper and cut into 8 strips.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian, not vegan (honey). Per serving: 1 strip. Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge, rolled in baking paper.

title: Berry Yoghurt Bark
summary: Frozen Greek yoghurt spread thin with berries, honey and pistachios, snapped into shards.

steps.text: Line a tray with baking paper. Stir the yoghurt and honey together until smooth and spread 1cm thick over the paper.
Scatter with the berries and pistachios and press them in lightly.
Freeze for 3 hours, until completely solid.
Break into 12 pieces and serve straight from the freezer.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian, not vegan (honey and dairy). Contains tree nuts. Per serving: 2 pieces. Plus 3 hours freezing. Keeps 1 month in the freezer.

title: Sesame Kale Chips
summary: Light, crackly baked kale leaves with sesame oil and sesame seeds.

items.raw: 200g kale, stems removed and torn into bite-size pieces
items.prep: stems removed and torn into bite-size pieces

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional) and line two trays with baking paper. Wash the kale and dry it completely, as any water will make it soggy.
Toss with both oils and the salt, rubbing it in with your hands.
Spread in a single layer on the trays and sprinkle with the sesame seeds.
Bake for 15 minutes, turning the trays halfway, until crisp but still green; remove any that brown early.

notes: Snack. Vegan, gluten-free. Per serving: half the batch. Best eaten the same day.

title: Garden Summer Rolls with Peanut Soy Dip
summary: Fresh, chewy rice paper rolls packed with crunchy vegetables, vermicelli and herbs, with a quick peanut dipping sauce.

items.raw: 1 Lebanese cucumber (100g), cut into thin sticks

steps.text: Soak the vermicelli in boiling water for 5 minutes until soft, then drain and rinse under cold water.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice and warm water until smooth for the dip.
Dip 1 rice paper sheet in warm water for 10 seconds until just pliable, lay it flat and pile on some vermicelli, carrot, cucumber, mint and lettuce.
Fold in the sides, roll up tightly and place on a plate under a damp cloth. Repeat to make 12 rolls and serve with the dip.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Contains peanuts. Per serving: 3 rolls with dip. Best eaten within 2 hours.

title: Baked Kumara Fries with Lime Yoghurt Dip
summary: Crisp-edged sweet potato fries with smoked paprika and a cooling lime and chive dip.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line two trays with baking paper. Toss the sweet potato with the oil, paprika and salt, spread in a single layer with space between the sticks.
Bake for 35 minutes, turning once at 20 minutes, until the edges are crisp and golden and the centres are tender.
Mix the yoghurt, lime juice and chives for the dip.
Serve the fries hot with the dip.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian, gluten-free. Per serving: a quarter of the fries with dip. Best eaten straight away.

title: Peanut Choc Energy Balls
summary: No-bake oat balls with peanut butter, cocoa and honey, ready to roll in 15 minutes.

steps.text: Mix the oats, peanut butter, honey and cocoa in a bowl until a sticky dough forms, adding 1 tbsp water if it is crumbly.
Chill the mixture for 20 minutes until firm enough to roll.
Roll level tablespoons into 16 balls, about 25g each.
Roll in the coconut and store in the fridge.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian, not vegan (honey). Contains peanuts. Per serving: 2 balls. Plus 20 minutes chilling. Keeps 1 week in the fridge.

title: Pumpkin Seed and Honey Clusters
summary: Crunchy baked oat clusters with pepitas, honey and cinnamon, ideal over yoghurt or by the handful.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional) and line a tray with baking paper. Warm the honey and oil together for 1 minute until runny and stir in the cinnamon.
Mix with the oats and pumpkin seeds until well coated.
Press firmly into a flat layer on the tray and bake for 25 minutes, until golden brown, without stirring.
Cool completely, then break into clusters and mix in the sultanas.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian, not vegan (honey). Per serving: about 1/2 cup. Keeps 2 weeks airtight.

title: Cucumber Hummus Bites
summary: Cool cucumber rounds topped with creamy home-made hummus and a dusting of paprika.

steps.text: Blend the chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, olive oil and water for 2 minutes until smooth and creamy, adding a little more water if it is too thick.
Season with a pinch of salt.
Spoon or pipe about 1 tbsp of the hummus onto each cucumber round.
Dust with paprika and serve straight away.

notes: Snack. Vegan, gluten-free. Contains sesame. Per serving: 6 bites. Keeps 1 day in the fridge.

title: Mini Pizza Toasts
summary: Crisp sourdough squares with tomato, mozzarella and capsicum, grilled until bubbling.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray. Lay the bread slices on the tray and toast for 3 minutes until just firm.
Spread each slice with the tomato paste and top with the capsicum, oregano and mozzarella.
Bake for 7 minutes, until the cheese is melted and golden.
Cut each slice into quarters and serve warm.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 slice (4 pieces). Best eaten warm.

title: Apple and Peanut Butter Sandwiches
summary: Crisp apple rings sandwiched with peanut butter and sunflower seeds, no cooking needed.

steps.text: Slice the apples into 8 rounds, about 8mm thick, and brush with the lemon juice to stop them browning.
Spread peanut butter on 4 of the rounds until it reaches the edges.
Scatter with the sunflower seeds and top with the remaining rounds, pressing lightly.
Cut each sandwich in half and serve straight away.

notes: Snack. Vegan, gluten-free. Contains peanuts. Per serving: 1 sandwich. Eat within 2 hours.

title: Rainbow Fruit Skewers with Honey Yoghurt
summary: Colourful skewers of watermelon, pineapple, mango and orange with a honey yoghurt dip for kids' parties.

steps.text: Thread the fruit onto 8 short skewers until each is full, in rainbow order: watermelon, orange, mango, pineapple. Trim any sharp ends or use paddle-pop sticks for young children.
Stir the honey into the yoghurt.
Serve the skewers with the dip on the side.
Chill under cling film until serving and eat within 2 hours.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian, gluten-free. Per serving: 2 skewers with dip. Use blunt skewers for children under 5, and cut fruit small to avoid choking.

title: Ham and Cheese Pinwheels
summary: Flaky puff pastry rolled with ham, cheese and mustard, sliced into party pinwheels.

items.raw: 100g grated vegetarian hard cheese, cheddar style

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line two trays. Spread the pastry sheets with the mustard and scatter over the ham and cheese.
Roll each sheet up tightly from one side, wrap and chill for 15 minutes until firm.
Slice each roll into 12 rounds, place cut side up on the trays and brush with the egg.
Bake for 20 minutes, until puffed and golden brown. Cool for 5 minutes.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 3 pinwheels. Plus 15 minutes chilling. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat until hot.

Food safety: keep the ham refrigerated until you assemble, bake until hot throughout, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours. Wash your hands after handling raw egg. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Herb and Cheese Drop Biscuits
summary: Fluffy savoury biscuits made with buttermilk, cheese and fresh herbs, with no rolling or cutting.

items.raw: 100g grated vegetarian hard cheese, cheddar style

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray with baking paper. Rub the butter into the flour until it looks like breadcrumbs.
Stir in the cheese and herbs, then add the buttermilk and mix until a rough, sticky dough forms.
Drop 12 heaped spoonfuls (about 60g each) onto the tray.
Bake for 15 minutes, until risen and golden brown. Cool for 5 minutes and serve warm.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 biscuit. Best on the day; freezes for 2 months.

title: Egg and Chive Mini Frittatas
summary: Protein-packed mini frittatas with spinach and cheese, baked in a muffin tin.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and grease a 12-hole muffin tin. Whisk the eggs, milk and salt together.
Divide the spinach, cheese and chives among the holes and pour in the egg mix.
Bake for 15 minutes, until set in the centre with no liquid egg left and lightly golden.
Cool in the tin for 3 minutes, then lift out.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian, gluten-free. Per serving: 3 frittatas. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat until steaming hot.
Food safety: cook until the egg is fully set, wash your hands and the bench after handling raw egg, and refrigerate within 2 hours.

title: Pandesal Filipino Rolls
summary: Soft, lightly sweet Filipino bread rolls rolled in breadcrumbs, best eaten warm.

steps.text: Mix the flour, sugar, yeast and salt, then stir in the milk, egg and butter to form a dough. Knead for 8 minutes on a floured bench until smooth and elastic, then cover and leave until doubled.
Roll the dough into a log and cut into 12 even pieces. Roll each piece in the breadcrumbs and place cut side up on a lined tray, 3cm apart. Cover and rest until puffy.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Bake for 18 minutes, until golden and the bases sound hollow when tapped.
Cool on a rack for 10 minutes before serving warm.

notes: Snack. Allow about 1 hour 30 minutes of proving, not included in the times. Per serving: 1 roll. Keeps 2 days in a sealed bag; freeze for up to 2 months and reheat at 160°C fan for 6 minutes.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs, wash your hands after handling raw egg, and bake the rolls until cooked through. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Steamed Bao Buns with Hoisin Mushrooms
summary: Pillowy steamed buns folded around quick hoisin mushrooms and spring onion.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and baking powder, add the water and oil, and knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and leave until doubled.
Roll the dough into 8 balls, flatten each into an oval about 10cm long, brush lightly with oil and fold in half over a small square of baking paper. Rest until puffy.
Fry the mushrooms in a dry non-stick frying pan over high heat for 6 minutes until golden and the liquid has gone, then stir in the hoisin and soy sauce for 1 minute.
Steam the buns in a lined steamer over simmering water for 12 minutes, until puffed and springy to the touch. Fill with the mushrooms and spring onions.

notes: Snack. Allow about 1 hour 20 minutes of proving, not included in the times. Per serving: 1 filled bun. Unfilled buns keep 3 days in the fridge or freeze for 2 months; re-steam for 5 minutes. Check the hoisin label if you need it gluten free.

title: Cheesy Naan Bites
summary: Quick yoghurt naan stuffed with mozzarella and brushed with garlic butter, no yeast needed.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yoghurt and oil into a soft dough and knead for 2 minutes. Rest for 15 minutes, then divide into 8 balls.
Flatten each ball into a 10cm round, put a spoonful of mozzarella in the centre, pinch to seal and roll out to 12cm.
Cook each naan in a hot dry frying pan for 2 minutes per side, until puffed and spotted brown.
Stir the garlic into the melted butter, brush over the naan and scatter with coriander. Cut each into 3 wedges.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 naan. Best warm; keeps 2 days in the fridge, reheat in a dry pan for 1 minute per side.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Sesame Bagel Bites
summary: Mini bagels boiled in honey water then baked with a sesame crust.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast and salt, add the water and 1 tbsp of the honey and knead for 10 minutes into a firm, smooth dough. Cover and leave until doubled.
Divide into 12 pieces, roll each into a ball and poke a hole through the centre, stretching to 3cm wide. Rest on a floured tray until puffy.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Bring a wide pan of water with the remaining honey to a gentle boil and simmer the bagels in batches for 1 minute each side. Drain on a rack.
Brush with the egg white, dip the tops in the sesame seeds and bake on a lined tray for 20 minutes, until deep golden.

notes: Snack. Allow about 1 hour 15 minutes of proving, not included in the times. Per serving: 1 mini bagel. Keeps 2 days in a paper bag; freeze for 2 months and toast from frozen.
Food safety: wash your hands after handling raw egg white, and bake the bagels until fully cooked through.

title: Garlic Flatbread Wedges
summary: Soft yoghurt flatbreads brushed with garlic butter and parsley, cut into wedges for dipping.

steps.text: Mix the flour, baking powder, salt and yoghurt into a soft dough, knead for 1 minute and divide into 8 balls.
Roll each ball into a 15cm round. Cook in a hot dry frying pan for 90 seconds per side, until puffed with brown spots.
Mix the butter, garlic and parsley and brush over the hot flatbreads. Cut each into 4 wedges.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 flatbread (4 wedges). Keeps 2 days in a sealed bag; reheat in a dry pan.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Sourdough Discard Crackers
summary: Crisp rosemary and sesame crackers that use up spare sourdough starter.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line 2 trays with baking paper. Mix the starter, flour, oil, salt, sesame seeds and rosemary into a firm dough.
Roll the dough between 2 sheets of baking paper to 2mm thick, slide onto a tray, sprinkle with flaky salt and cut into 5cm squares with a knife or pizza cutter.
Bake for 20 minutes, until golden and crisp, turning the tray halfway. Cool on the tray.

notes: Snack. Per serving: about 6 crackers. Keeps 2 weeks in an airtight container. If they soften, re-crisp at 150°C fan for 5 minutes.

title: Soft Milk Bread Rolls
summary: Fluffy Japanese-style rolls made with a cooked flour paste that keeps them soft for days.

items.raw: 30g bread flour, extra, for the paste

steps.text: Whisk the extra flour with 100ml of the milk and 50ml water in a small pan over medium heat for 2 minutes, until it forms a thick paste. Cool for 10 minutes.
Mix the flour, sugar, yeast and salt, then add the paste, remaining milk, egg and butter. Knead for 12 minutes until smooth and stretchy. Cover and leave until doubled.
Divide into 12 balls and place in a lined 20 x 30cm tin. Cover and rest until puffy. Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional).
Brush with a little milk and bake for 20 minutes, until golden and the centre rolls sound hollow when tapped. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes.

notes: Snack. Allow about 1 hour 40 minutes of proving, not included in the times. Per serving: 1 roll. Keeps 3 days in a sealed bag; freeze for 2 months.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs, wash your hands after handling raw egg, and bake the rolls until cooked through.

title: Corn Kernel Cornbread Muffins
summary: Golden cornmeal muffins studded with sweet corn, good warm with butter.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C fan (210°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases.
Mix the flour, polenta, baking powder, sugar and salt in a bowl. Whisk the egg, milk and butter, pour into the dry mix with the corn and stir until just combined.
Divide among the cases and bake for 20 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 muffin. Keeps 3 days in an airtight container; freeze for 2 months.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs and bake the muffins until a skewer comes out clean.

title: Sticky Raisin Toffee Pudding
summary: A soft, moist raisin sponge soaked in hot toffee sauce, the sticky date idea without dates.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and grease and line a 20cm square tin. Soak the raisins in the boiling water with the bicarbonate of soda for 10 minutes.
Beat the butter and first measure of sugar for 3 minutes until pale, then beat in the eggs one at a time. Fold in the flour, then the raisins and their liquid. Pour into the tin.
Bake for 35 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Meanwhile simmer the sauce ingredients in a small pan for 4 minutes, stirring, until smooth and glossy.
Cut the pudding into 8 squares and serve warm with the sauce spooned over.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 square with sauce. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat in the microwave for 40 seconds.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs, bake until a skewer comes out clean, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Creamy Rice Pudding Cups
summary: Slow-simmered vanilla rice pudding with a cinnamon dusting, served warm or cold.

steps.text: Put the rice, milk and sugar in a heavy saucepan and bring to a gentle simmer, stirring, until the sugar dissolves.
Cook over low heat for 45 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until the rice is tender and the pudding is thick and creamy.
Stir in the vanilla, spoon into 8 small cups and dust with cinnamon.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 small cup. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; loosen with a splash of milk. Refrigerate within 2 hours of cooking.

title: Vegetarian Coconut Pudding Cups with Mango
summary: Cornflour-set vanilla coconut puddings topped with fresh mango, no gelatine.

steps.text: Whisk the cornflour with 100ml of the almond milk until smooth. Heat the coconut milk, remaining almond milk and sugar in a saucepan until steaming.
Whisk in the cornflour mix and cook over medium heat for 4 minutes, stirring, until thick and bubbling. Stir in the vanilla.
Pour into 6 cups and cool for 15 minutes, then chill until set. Toss the mango with the lime juice and spoon over to serve.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 cup. Keeps 3 days covered in the fridge.

title: Crema Caramel Flan
summary: A silky baked custard turned out over a pool of golden caramel.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional). Melt the caramel sugar in a small pan over medium heat, without stirring, for 6 minutes until amber. Pour into a 20cm round cake tin or flan dish and tilt to coat the base.
Whisk the eggs, yolks, remaining sugar and vanilla. Warm the milk until steaming, whisk it into the eggs, then strain over the caramel.
Set the tin in a roasting tray, pour in hot water to halfway up the sides and bake for 45 minutes, until the edge is set and the centre has a slight wobble.
Cool, chill, then run a knife around the edge and turn out onto a plate. Cut into 8 wedges.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 wedge. Keeps 3 days covered in the fridge.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs, bake until the custard is set, and refrigerate within 2 hours. Not for anyone who needs to avoid lightly set egg.

title: Halo-Halo-Style Fruit Ice Cups
summary: Crushed ice layered with mango, pineapple and milk, a no-cook take on the Filipino classic.

steps.text: Crush the ice in a blender or in a clean tea towel with a rolling pin until fine and snowy.
Layer the mango and pineapple into 6 tall glasses, then pile on the crushed ice.
Stir the evaporated and condensed milk, pour over the ice and top with corn flakes. Serve straight away with a long spoon and mix before eating.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 glass. Make just before serving; the ice melts fast. Use ice from clean water.

title: Baked Vanilla Custard Cups
summary: Gently baked egg custards with a nutmeg top, set in small cups.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional). Whisk the eggs, yolks, sugar and vanilla. Warm the milk and cream until steaming, then whisk into the eggs and strain.
Pour into 6 ovenproof cups, dust with nutmeg and stand in a deep tray. Pour in hot water to halfway up the cups.
Bake for 30 minutes, until the custards are set at the edge with a slight wobble in the centre. Cool, then chill.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 cup. Keeps 3 days covered in the fridge.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs, bake until set, and refrigerate within 2 hours.

title: Berry Swirl Yoghurt Pops
summary: Blended frozen berries and yoghurt, sweetened with a little honey.

steps.text: Blend the berries, yoghurt, honey and orange juice until smooth.
Pour into 8 ice block moulds, add sticks and freeze for at least 5 hours, until solid.
Run the moulds under warm water for 10 seconds to release.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 ice block. Keeps 2 months in the freezer. Not suitable for children under 1 because of the honey.

title: Pistachio Kulfi
summary: Dense, creamy Indian ice cream flavoured with pistachios and rosewater.

steps.text: Simmer the evaporated and condensed milk in a saucepan for 10 minutes over low heat, stirring, until slightly thickened. Cool completely.
Whip the cream to soft peaks, fold in the cooled milk, chopped pistachios and rosewater.
Spoon into 8 small moulds or cups, cover and freeze for at least 6 hours, until firm.
Dip the moulds briefly in warm water to release, and top with a whole pistachio.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 kulfi. Keeps 1 month in the freezer. Contains tree nuts. Refrigerate the cooled milk if you are not folding it in right away.

title: Watermelon Granita
summary: Icy, fluffy shards of watermelon and lime, scraped with a fork.

steps.text: Blend the watermelon, sugar and lime juice until smooth, then pour into a shallow metal tray.
Freeze until ice forms around the edges, then scrape with a fork. Repeat 3 or 4 more times, until the whole tray is a mass of fine, fluffy ice crystals.
Spoon into 8 chilled glasses and serve straight away.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 glass. Keeps 1 week in the freezer; rake with a fork before serving.

title: Honey Pistachio Yoghurt Shards
summary: Thin sheets of honey yoghurt frozen with berries and pistachios, snapped into shards.

steps.text: Line a 25 x 35cm tray with baking paper. Mix the yoghurt and honey and spread to 8mm thick.
Scatter with the berries and pistachios, pressing them in lightly. Freeze for at least 3 hours, until completely firm.
Break into 12 shards and serve straight from the freezer.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 shard. Keeps 1 month in an airtight container in the freezer. Not suitable for children under 1 because of the honey. Contains tree nuts.

title: Mango Nice Cream
summary: Frozen mango blended with yoghurt into a soft-serve texture, no ice-cream machine needed.

steps.text: Let the mango sit at room temperature for 5 minutes. Blend with the yoghurt, honey and lime juice, scraping down the sides, until smooth and thick.
Serve straight away in 4 bowls as soft-serve.
For a scoopable texture, spoon into a container and freeze until firm enough to scoop.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 bowl. Best the day it is made. Not suitable for children under 1 because of the honey.

title: Lemon Sorbet Cups
summary: A sharp, clean lemon sorbet churned by hand in the freezer.

steps.text: Heat the sugar and water in a small pan for 3 minutes, stirring, until the sugar dissolves. Cool completely, then stir in the lemon juice and zest.
Pour into a shallow container and freeze until slushy at the edges. Beat well with a fork, then repeat 3 or 4 more times, until smooth and scoopable.
Scoop into 8 small cups to serve.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 small cup. Keeps 1 month in the freezer; soften for 10 minutes before scooping.

title: Chocolate Fudge Ice Blocks
summary: Thick chocolate milk custard frozen into old-school ice blocks.

steps.text: Whisk the cocoa, sugar and cornflour in a saucepan, then whisk in a splash of the milk to make a paste. Add the remaining milk.
Heat over medium heat for 6 minutes, stirring, until the mixture bubbles and thickens. Stir in the vanilla and cool.
Pour into 8 moulds, add sticks and freeze for at least 5 hours until solid.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 ice block. Keeps 2 months in the freezer.

title: Pineapple Coconut Ice Blocks
summary: Blended pineapple and coconut milk with a squeeze of lime, a tropical ice block.

steps.text: Blend the pineapple, coconut milk, sugar and lime juice until smooth.
Pour into 8 moulds, add sticks and freeze for at least 5 hours, until solid.
Run the moulds under warm water for 10 seconds to release.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 ice block. Keeps 2 months in the freezer.

title: Sutlac Turkish Baked Rice Pudding
summary: Rice pudding simmered then baked until the top blisters golden-brown.

steps.text: Simmer the rice in 250ml water for 10 minutes until the water is absorbed. Add 700ml of the milk and the sugar and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring often, until thick.
Mix the cornflour with the remaining milk, stir it in and cook for 3 minutes until thickened. Stir in the vanilla.

Heat the grill to high. Divide among 6 ovenproof bowls and grill 10cm from the heat for 5 minutes, until the tops blister and brown. Alternatively bake at 220°C fan (240°C conventional) for 12 minutes.
Cool for 10 minutes and serve warm, or chill.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 bowl. Keeps 3 days in the fridge. Refrigerate within 2 hours of cooking.

title: Bread and Butter Pudding Squares
summary: Buttered bread layered with sultanas and baked in a soft vanilla custard.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and grease a 20cm square dish. Butter the bread, cut into triangles and layer in the dish with the sultanas.
Whisk the eggs, milk, sugar and vanilla and pour over the bread. Leave to soak for 10 minutes.
Bake for 40 minutes, until golden on top and the custard is just set in the centre. Cool for 10 minutes and cut into 8 squares.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 square. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat in the microwave for 40 seconds.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs, bake until the custard is set, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Baked Cheese Crisps
summary: Lacy, crunchy oven-baked cheese crisps with a pinch of smoked paprika.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C fan (210°C conventional) and line 2 trays with baking paper.
Mix the cheese, paprika and pepper, then drop heaped tablespoons 4cm apart on the trays and flatten slightly.
Bake for 8 minutes, until the edges are deep golden and the centres have stopped bubbling. Cool on the tray for 5 minutes to crisp.

notes: Snack. Per serving: about 4 crisps. Keeps 4 days in an airtight container. Check the label to confirm the cheese is made with vegetarian rennet.

title: Rye Seed Crispbread
summary: Thin, crunchy Scandinavian-style rye crispbread with sesame and sunflower seeds.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line 2 trays with baking paper. Mix the flours, seeds and salt, then stir in the oil and water to form a firm dough.
Divide into 2, roll each piece between 2 sheets of baking paper to 3mm thick and prick all over with a fork. Slide onto the trays and cut into 12 rectangles.
Bake for 25 minutes, swapping trays halfway, until crisp and golden at the edges. Cool on a rack; they crisp further as they cool.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 pieces of crispbread. Keeps 2 weeks in an airtight container.

title: Seeded Oat Crackers
summary: Nutty, sturdy crackers loaded with oats, pumpkin and sunflower seeds.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line 2 trays with baking paper. Mix the oats, flour, seeds and salt, then stir in the oil and water to a firm dough.
Roll out between 2 sheets of baking paper to 3mm thick, slide onto a tray and cut into 24 squares.
Bake for 25 minutes, until golden and crisp, turning the tray halfway. Cool on the tray.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 crackers. Keeps 2 weeks in an airtight container.

title: Rosemary Olive Crackers
summary: Thin olive oil crackers flecked with rosemary and chopped black olives.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line 2 trays with baking paper. Mix the flour, salt, rosemary and olives, then stir in the oil and water to a smooth dough.
Roll out between 2 sheets of baking paper to 2mm thick and cut into 24 rectangles with a knife.
Bake for 18 minutes, until golden and crisp. Cool on the tray.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 crackers. Keeps 10 days in an airtight container.

title: Scottish Oatcakes
summary: Plain, crumbly oatcakes baked until crisp, good with cheese or hummus.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line a tray with baking paper. Blitz the oats in a food processor until coarse.
Mix the oats, salt and butter, then stir in the hot water to make a firm dough. Roll out to 5mm thick on a floured bench and cut into 24 rounds.
Bake for 20 minutes, turning once, until firm and golden at the edges. Cool on a rack.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 oatcakes. Keeps 10 days in an airtight container. Use certified gluten-free oats if needed.

title: Lavash Sesame Crackers
summary: Paper-thin Middle Eastern flatbread crackers snapped into shards.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line 2 trays with baking paper. Mix the flour, salt, oil and water into a smooth dough and knead for 2 minutes.
Divide into 4, roll each piece as thinly as you can, brush with a little water and sprinkle with the sesame seeds.
Bake for 12 minutes, until golden and bubbled. Cool, then snap into 12 shards.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 large shard. Keeps 2 weeks in an airtight container.

title: Sesame Rice Flour Crackers
summary: Light gluten-free crackers made with rice and tapioca flour.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line 2 trays with baking paper. Mix the flours, sesame seeds and salt, then stir in the oil and boiling water until a dough forms.
Knead for 1 minute while warm, roll out between 2 sheets of baking paper to 2mm thick and cut into 24 squares.
Bake for 20 minutes, until pale golden and crisp. Cool on the tray.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 crackers. Keeps 10 days in an airtight container. Check the flour labels for gluten-free certification.

title: Nori Sesame Crisps
summary: Rice paper and nori baked into airy, salty crisps.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line 2 trays with baking paper. Mix the sesame oil and tamari.
Dip each rice paper sheet in water for 3 seconds, lay on the tray, brush with the tamari oil, top with a piece of nori and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Cut into 4 with scissors.
Bake in batches for 8 minutes, until crisp and lightly golden. Cool on the tray.

notes: Snack. Per serving: about 6 crisps. Keeps 1 week in an airtight container.

title: Homemade Almond Butter
summary: Smooth roasted almond butter made with nothing but almonds and a pinch of salt.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Roast the almonds on a tray for 12 minutes, until fragrant and a shade darker.
Cool for 10 minutes, then blend in a food processor for 10 to 15 minutes, scraping down the sides, until the almonds turn from crumbs to a thick paste and then pour smooth.
Blend in the salt and oil, then spoon into a clean jar.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 tbsp. Keeps 1 month in the fridge; oil separation is normal, so stir. Contains tree nuts.

title: Homemade Cashew Butter
summary: Mild, creamy cashew butter, lightly toasted for depth.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Toast the cashews on a tray for 10 minutes, until pale golden.
Cool for 10 minutes, then blend in a food processor for 10 to 12 minutes, scraping down often, until completely smooth and runny.
Blend in the salt and honey and spoon into a clean jar.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 tbsp. Keeps 1 month in the fridge. Contains tree nuts. Not suitable for children under 1 because of the honey.

title: Homemade Sunflower Seed Butter
summary: A nut-free spread with a toasty flavour, made from roasted sunflower seeds.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Roast the seeds on a tray for 10 minutes, until fragrant and lightly golden.
Cool for 10 minutes, then blend in a food processor for 10 minutes, scraping down often, until thick and smooth.
Blend in the salt and oil, adding another spoonful of oil if it is too stiff, then spoon into a clean jar.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 tbsp. Keeps 1 month in the fridge. A nut-free option for lunchboxes, though check school rules on seeds.

title: Tahini Honey Halva Bites
summary: No-bake sesame bites with pistachios, firm enough to slice.

steps.text: Line a small loaf tin with baking paper. Warm the honey in a small pan over low heat for 2 minutes until runny.
Stir the honey, vanilla and salt into the tahini until smooth, then fold in the pistachios.
Press into the tin and chill until firm. Lift out and cut into 12 squares.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 square. Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge. Contains sesame and tree nuts. Not suitable for children under 1 because of the honey.

title: Hazelnut Chocolate Spread
summary: Silky roasted hazelnut and dark chocolate spread with no palm oil.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Toast the hazelnuts on a tray for 10 minutes, then rub in a tea towel to remove most of the skins.
Blend the nuts in a food processor for 8 minutes, scraping down often, until a smooth runny paste forms.
Melt the chocolate in a bowl over barely simmering water for 4 minutes, until smooth. Blend it into the nut paste with the cocoa, icing sugar, oil and salt.
Spoon into a clean jar and cool.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 tbsp. Keeps 3 weeks in a cool cupboard or 2 months in the fridge. Contains tree nuts.

title: Crunchy Roasted Peanut Spread
summary: Chunky peanut spread made with roasted peanuts, a touch of honey and salt.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Warm the peanuts on a tray for 10 minutes, until fragrant.
Blend 100g of the peanuts for 30 seconds, until just chopped, and set aside for crunch.
Blend the remaining peanuts with the honey and salt for 8 to 10 minutes, scraping down often, until smooth and glossy. Stir in the chopped peanuts and spoon into a jar.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 tbsp. Keeps 1 month in the fridge. Contains peanuts. Not suitable for children under 1 because of the honey.

title: Eggless Spiced Apple Muffins
summary: Moist egg-free muffins with chunks of apple and a cinnamon sugar top.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases.
Mix the flour, brown sugar and half the cinnamon. Whisk the soy milk, oil, vinegar and vanilla, pour into the dry mix and stir until just combined, then fold in the apple.
Divide among the cases, sprinkle with the raw sugar mixed with the remaining cinnamon and bake for 22 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 muffin. Keeps 3 days in an airtight container; freeze for 2 months.

title: Gluten-Free Berry Muffins
summary: Tender gluten-free muffins dotted with frozen berries.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases.
Mix the flour, baking powder and sugar. Whisk the eggs, milk, oil and vanilla, pour into the dry mix and stir until just combined, then fold in the berries.
Divide among the cases and bake for 22 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 muffin. Keeps 2 days at room temperature or 5 days in the fridge; freeze for 2 months. Check the flour and baking powder labels for gluten-free certification.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs and bake until a skewer comes out clean.

title: Vegan Chocolate Cupcakes
summary: Light, cocoa-rich cupcakes made without eggs or dairy.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C fan (195°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases.
Sift the flour, cocoa, sugar and bicarbonate of soda. Whisk the soy milk, oil, vinegar and vanilla, then stir into the dry mix until just smooth.
Divide among the cases and bake for 20 minutes, until risen and a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely and dust with icing sugar.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 cupcake. Keeps 3 days in an airtight container; freeze for 2 months.

title: Gluten-Free Mozzarella and Chive Scones
summary: Savoury gluten-free scones with melty mozzarella and fresh chives.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray with baking paper. Rub the butter into the flour and baking powder until it looks like breadcrumbs, then stir in the mozzarella and chives.
Beat the egg with the milk, reserve a spoonful for glazing, and stir the rest into the dry mix to form a soft dough.
Pat out to 3cm thick, cut into 8 rounds, brush with the reserved egg mix and bake for 18 minutes, until risen and golden.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 scone. Best on the day; keeps 2 days in the fridge and reheats at 160°C fan for 6 minutes. Check labels for gluten-free certification.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs and bake the scones until cooked through. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Flourless Orange Almond Squares
summary: A moist cake made with whole boiled oranges and almond meal.

steps.text: Cover the oranges with water in a saucepan and simmer for 45 minutes, until very soft. Drain, cool, halve, remove any pips and blend the whole fruit, skin and all, to a puree.
Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a 20 x 30cm tin. Whisk the eggs and sugar for 3 minutes until thick, then fold in the orange puree, almond meal and baking powder.
Pour into the tin and bake for 45 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tin and cut into 12 squares.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 square. Keeps 4 days in the fridge; freeze for 2 months. Contains tree nuts and egg.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs, bake until a skewer comes out clean, and refrigerate within 2 hours.

title: Chewy Vegan Raisin Oat Rounds
summary: Chewy oat cookies with raisins and cinnamon, made without eggs or dairy.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line 2 trays with baking paper. Mix the oats, flour, raisins, sugar, cinnamon and bicarbonate of soda.
Stir in the oil and soy milk to form a firm dough, then roll into 12 balls and flatten to 1.5cm thick on the trays, 4cm apart.
Bake for 14 minutes, until golden at the edges but still soft in the centre. Cool on the tray for 5 minutes.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 cookie. Keeps 5 days in an airtight container; freeze for 2 months.

title: Gluten-Free Fudge Brownies
summary: Dense, fudgy brownies made with almond meal instead of flour.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin. Melt the chocolate and butter in a bowl over barely simmering water for 5 minutes, until smooth, then cool slightly.
Whisk the sugar, eggs and vanilla for 3 minutes until thick and pale, stir in the chocolate mix, then fold in the almond meal, cocoa and salt.
Pour into the tin and bake for 28 minutes, until the top is set and a skewer comes out with a few moist crumbs. Cool in the tin and cut into 12 squares.
