notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 square. Keeps 5 days in an airtight container; freeze for 2 months. Check the chocolate and cocoa labels for gluten. Contains tree nuts and egg.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs, bake until set and refrigerate within 2 hours in warm weather.

title: Vegan Carrot Cake Bites
summary: No-bake bliss balls with grated carrot, walnuts, sultanas and cinnamon.

steps.text: Blitz the oats and walnuts in a food processor for 30 seconds until coarsely ground.
Add the carrot, sultanas, maple syrup, 2 tbsp of the coconut and the cinnamon and blend for 1 minute, until the mixture sticks together when pinched.
Roll into 12 balls, then roll in the remaining coconut and chill until firm.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 bite. Keeps 5 days in the fridge or 2 months in the freezer. Contains tree nuts.

title: Gluten-Free Lemon Polenta Squares
summary: Moist lemon cake squares made with polenta and almond meal.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin. Beat the butter, sugar and lemon zest for 3 minutes until pale, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Fold in the polenta, almond meal, baking powder and lemon juice, then spread into the tin.
Bake for 30 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tin and cut into 12 squares.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 square. Keeps 4 days in an airtight container. Contains tree nuts and egg.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs, bake until a skewer comes out clean, and refrigerate within 2 hours in warm weather.

title: Lemon Cashew Coconut Balls
summary: Vegan no-bake balls with raw cashews, lemon zest and coconut.

steps.text: Blitz the cashews and 70g of the coconut in a food processor for 1 minute, until finely ground.
Add the maple syrup, lemon zest, juice and salt and blend for 1 minute, until the mixture clumps together when pinched.
Roll into 12 balls, then roll in the remaining coconut and chill until firm.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 ball. Keeps 1 week in the fridge or 2 months in the freezer. Contains tree nuts.

title: Pikelets with Apricot Jam
summary: Small fluffy griddle cakes, an old Australian morning-tea favourite, served with jam.

steps.text: Mix the flour and sugar in a bowl. Whisk the egg, milk and butter, then stir into the flour until just smooth, with no big lumps.
Heat a non-stick frying pan over medium heat and grease lightly. Drop in tablespoons of batter and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until bubbles form and burst on top.
Flip and cook for 1 minute more, until golden. Repeat to make 24 pikelets and serve with the apricot jam.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 pikelets with 1 tsp jam. Best warm; keeps 2 days in the fridge and freezes for 2 months.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs and cook the pikelets until the centres are no longer wet.

title: Honey Joys
summary: Crunchy corn flake clusters in a buttery honey coating, baked in patty cases.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional) and set 24 mini paper cases in a mini muffin tin.
Melt the butter, sugar and honey in a saucepan over low heat for 3 minutes, stirring, until the sugar dissolves. Pour over the corn flakes and fold gently until evenly coated.
Spoon into the cases and bake for 12 minutes, until set and golden. Cool in the tin.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 honey joys. Keeps 5 days in an airtight container. Not suitable for children under 1 because of the honey.

title: Chocolate Crackles
summary: No-bake rice bubble and cocoa treats set with coconut oil, a party classic.

steps.text: Mix the puffed rice, sifted icing sugar, cocoa and coconut in a large bowl.
Pour in the cooled coconut oil and stir until every piece is coated and the mix holds together.
Spoon into 24 paper cases and refrigerate until firm.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 crackles. Keeps 1 week in the fridge; they soften in warm weather.

title: Chocolate Oat Fingers
summary: A baked cocoa oat slice with a melted chocolate topping.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin. Mix the oats, flour, cocoa and sugar.
Stir in the butter and egg to a crumbly dough, press firmly into the tin and bake for 20 minutes, until golden at the edges.
Scatter the chocolate over the hot slice, leave for 3 minutes and spread smooth. Cool and cut into 12 bars.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 bar. Keeps 5 days in an airtight container.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs and bake until the slice is firm and golden.

title: Afghan Biscuits
summary: New Zealand-style chocolate cornflake biscuits topped with chocolate icing and a walnut.

items.raw: 1 tbsp cocoa powder, for the icing

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line 2 trays with baking paper. Beat the butter and sugar for 3 minutes until pale, then stir in the flour and cocoa, then gently fold in the corn flakes.
Roll into 12 balls, place 5cm apart on the trays and flatten gently with a fork. Bake for 15 minutes, until firm. Cool on the tray.
Stir the icing sugar, icing cocoa, icing butter and 1 tbsp hot water until smooth and spreadable. Ice each biscuit and top with a walnut half.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 biscuit. Keeps 5 days in an airtight container. Contains tree nuts.

title: Lamington Bites
summary: Bite-sized sponge cubes dipped in chocolate icing and rolled in coconut.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C fan (195°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin. Whisk the eggs and sugar for 6 minutes until thick and tripled in volume. Fold in the sifted flour, then the butter and milk.
Pour into the tin and bake for 20 minutes, until golden and springy to the touch. Cool completely, then cut into 12 cubes.
Whisk the icing sugar, cocoa, icing butter and icing milk in a bowl over a pan of simmering water until smooth. Dip the cubes in the icing, then roll in the coconut and set on a rack.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 lamington bite. Best within 3 days in an airtight container; freeze for 2 months.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs and bake until the sponge springs back and a skewer comes out clean.

title: Vanilla Slice Squares
summary: Crisp puff pastry layers around thick vanilla custard and a white icing top.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Place the pastry sheets on lined trays, prick with a fork, top each with another tray and bake for 25 minutes, until golden and crisp. Cool.
Whisk the yolks, sugar and cornflour with a splash of the milk. Heat the rest of the milk until steaming, whisk into the yolk mix and return to the pan.
Cook over low heat for 5 minutes, whisking constantly, until thick and bubbling. Off the heat, stir in the butter and vanilla and cool for 15 minutes.

Lay one pastry sheet in a lined 20cm square tin, spread with the custard, then top with the second sheet. Mix the icing sugar with 2 tbsp water, spread over the top, then chill until the custard is firm. Cut into 12 squares with a serrated knife.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 square. Best within 2 days, kept in the fridge.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs, cook the custard until thick and bubbling, and keep refrigerated.

title: Ginger Nut Biscuits
summary: Crunchy golden syrup and ginger biscuits for dunking.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line 2 trays with baking paper. Mix the flour, sugar, ginger and bicarbonate of soda.
Melt the butter and golden syrup in a small pan for 2 minutes, then stir into the dry mix to form a firm dough.
Roll into 24 balls, place 5cm apart on the trays and bake for 15 minutes, until deep golden. Cool on the tray, where they firm up and crisp.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 biscuits. Keeps 2 weeks in an airtight container.

title: Tray Baked Granola Clusters
summary: Big crunchy oat and almond clusters sweetened with maple syrup.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional) and line a large tray with baking paper.
Mix the oats, almonds, pumpkin seeds and coconut. Stir the maple syrup and coconut oil together, pour over and mix until every piece is glossy.
Spread out and press down firmly. Bake for 30 minutes, until deep golden, then cool completely without stirring so it sets in clusters. Break up and stir through the raisins.

notes: Snack. Per serving: about 1/2 cup (45g). Keeps 3 weeks in an airtight container. Contains tree nuts.

title: Cinnamon Glazed Almonds
summary: Crisp sugar-and-cinnamon coated almonds, baked low and slow.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 140°C fan (160°C conventional) and line a tray with baking paper. Whisk the egg white until frothy, 1 minute.
Mix the sugar, cinnamon and salt, then toss the almonds in the egg white and then in the sugar mix.
Spread on the tray and bake for 35 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes, until dry and fragrant. Cool completely to crisp.

notes: Snack. Per serving: a small handful (35g). Keeps 2 weeks in an airtight container. Contains tree nuts and egg.
Food safety: use a fresh, uncracked egg and wash your hands after handling it. The low oven fully dries the coating.

title: Apple Sultana Lunchbox Muffins
summary: Lightly sweet apple and sultana muffins that freeze well for school lunchboxes.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases.
Mix the flour, sugar and cinnamon. Whisk the egg, milk and oil, pour into the dry mix with the apple and sultanas and stir until just combined.
Divide among the cases and bake for 22 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 muffin. Keeps 3 days in an airtight container; freeze for 2 months.
Food safety: use a fresh, uncracked egg and bake until a skewer comes out clean.

title: Zucchini Mozzarella Muffins
summary: Savoury muffins with grated zucchini, melty mozzarella and chives.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases.
Whisk the eggs, milk and oil. Stir into the flour with the zucchini, mozzarella and chives until just combined.
Divide among the cases and bake for 22 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 muffin. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; freeze for 2 months and reheat at 160°C fan for 8 minutes.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs, bake until a skewer comes out clean and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Hummus Veggie Pinwheels
summary: Soft tortilla rolls spread with hummus and packed with carrot, cucumber and spinach.

steps.text: Spread each tortilla edge to edge with the hummus.
Cover with the spinach, carrot and cucumber, leaving a 2cm border at one end.
Roll up tightly from the other end, wrap in baking paper and chill until firm enough to slice cleanly, then cut each roll into 6 pinwheels.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 4 pinwheels. Keeps 1 day in the fridge in an airtight container, so make them the morning you serve them.

title: Spanakopita Bites
summary: Crisp filo triangles filled with spinach, feta and ricotta.

items.raw: 300g frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line 2 trays with baking paper. Mix the spinach, feta, ricotta, egg and nutmeg.

Cut the stacked filo into 3 strips each, lengthways, and keep covered with a damp tea towel. Brush a strip with oil, put 1 tbsp of filling at one end and fold over and over like a flag into a triangle. Repeat to make 12 triangles.
Place seam side down on the trays, brush with the remaining oil and bake for 25 minutes, until deep golden and crisp.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 triangle. Keeps 2 days in the fridge; reheat at 180°C fan for 8 minutes to crisp.
Food safety: use a fresh, uncracked egg, bake until golden and hot throughout, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Bacon and Cheese Pastry Cups
summary: Buttery pastry cases filled with bacon, mozzarella and a soft egg custard.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and grease a 12-hole muffin tin. Cut 12 rounds from the pastry and press into the holes.
Fry the bacon in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 5 minutes until crisp. Divide the bacon and mozzarella among the cases.
Whisk the eggs, cream, nutmeg and pepper, pour over and bake for 22 minutes, until puffed, golden and just set in the centre.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes before turning out.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 pastry cups. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat at 170°C fan for 10 minutes.

Food safety: cook the bacon until crisp and the filling until it reaches at least 70°C and the custard is set, use fresh, uncracked eggs and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Cheesy Ham Egg Cups
summary: Baked egg muffins with ham, capsicum, spring onion and mozzarella, high in protein.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and grease a 12-hole muffin tin well.
Divide the ham, capsicum, spring onions and mozzarella among the holes. Whisk the eggs, milk and pepper and pour over.
Bake for 18 minutes, until puffed and set in the centre. Cool in the tin for 3 minutes before lifting out.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 egg cups. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; freeze for 1 month and reheat in the microwave for 1 minute.

Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs, bake until the egg is firm and the centres reach at least 70°C, keep the ham refrigerated until use and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Pizza Muffins
summary: Savoury muffins with tomato paste, ham and mozzarella, a lunchbox favourite.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases.
Whisk the egg, milk, oil and tomato paste. Stir into the flour with the ham, three-quarters of the mozzarella and the oregano until just combined.
Divide among the cases, top with the remaining mozzarella and bake for 20 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 muffin. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; freeze for 2 months.
Food safety: use a fresh, uncracked egg, keep the ham refrigerated until use, bake until hot throughout and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Baked Pumpkin Chickpea Nuggets
summary: Crisp-edged nuggets of roasted pumpkin and chickpeas with breadcrumbs and cumin.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray with baking paper. Roast the pumpkin with 1 tbsp of the oil for 20 minutes, until soft and golden.
Mash the pumpkin and chickpeas roughly with a fork, then mix in the egg, half the breadcrumbs, cumin and salt. Shape into 24 nuggets and coat in the remaining breadcrumbs.
Brush with the remaining oil and bake on the tray for 25 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 3 nuggets. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; freeze for 2 months and reheat at 180°C fan for 12 minutes.
Food safety: use a fresh, uncracked egg and bake until hot throughout. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Pear Oat Bars
summary: Crumbly oat bars layered with softened cinnamon pear.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin. Simmer the pear, cinnamon and lemon juice in a pan with 2 tbsp water for 6 minutes until soft.
Mix the oats, flour, sugar and butter. Press two-thirds into the tin and bake for 10 minutes.
Spread the pear over the base, crumble over the remaining oat mix and bake for 20 minutes, until golden. Cool in the tin and cut into 12 bars.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 bar. Keeps 4 days in an airtight container; freeze for 2 months.

title: Marmalade Oat Biscuits
summary: Chewy oat biscuits with a bittersweet orange marmalade note.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line 2 trays with baking paper. Beat the butter and sugar for 3 minutes until pale, then beat in the egg and marmalade.
Stir in the flour, oats and bicarbonate of soda to form a firm dough. Roll into 24 balls and flatten slightly on the trays, 4cm apart.
Bake for 14 minutes, until golden at the edges. Cool on the tray for 5 minutes.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 biscuits. Keeps 5 days in an airtight container; freeze for 2 months.
Food safety: use a fresh, uncracked egg and bake until golden.

title: Chocolate Coconut Rough
summary: Dark chocolate clusters with coconut, raisins and almonds, no baking.

steps.text: Melt the chocolate in a bowl over barely simmering water for 5 minutes, stirring, until smooth.
Stir in the coconut, raisins and almonds until everything is coated.
Drop 12 heaped spoonfuls onto a lined tray and refrigerate until firm.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 cluster. Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge. Contains tree nuts.

title: Honey Rice Bubble Bars
summary: Chewy puffed rice bars set with butter, honey and brown sugar.

steps.text: Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper. Melt the butter, honey and sugar in a saucepan over low heat for 4 minutes, stirring, until smooth, then boil gently for 1 minute until bubbling.
Pour over the puffed rice and sultanas and fold until coated.
Press firmly into the tin, chill until firm and cut into 12 bars.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 bar. Keeps 5 days in an airtight container. Not suitable for children under 1 because of the honey.

title: Carrot Raisin Lunchbox Loaf
summary: A moist spiced loaf with carrot and raisins, sliced for lunchboxes.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line a 10 x 21cm loaf tin.
Whisk the eggs, sugar and oil until smooth, stir in the carrot and raisins, then fold in the flour and cinnamon.
Pour into the tin and bake for 45 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes and cut into 12 slices.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 slice. Keeps 4 days in an airtight container; freeze slices for 2 months.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs and bake until a skewer comes out clean.

title: Fudgy Kumara Brownies
summary: Rich chocolate brownies made fudgy with mashed sweet potato and almond meal.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin. Boil the sweet potato for 12 minutes until soft, then drain and mash until smooth.
Melt the chocolate and butter in a bowl over barely simmering water for 4 minutes until smooth, then stir in the sweet potato, cocoa and sugar. Beat in the eggs, then fold in the almond meal.
Spread into the tin and bake for 28 minutes, until set with a few moist crumbs on a skewer. Cool and cut into 12 squares.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 brownie. Keeps 4 days in the fridge; freeze for 2 months. Contains tree nuts and egg.
Food safety: use fresh, uncracked eggs, bake until set and refrigerate within 2 hours.

title: Rava Ladoo Semolina Sweets
summary: Soft toasted semolina and coconut balls with sultanas, a classic Diwali sweet.

steps.text: Toast the semolina in 1 tbsp ghee in a wide pan over medium heat for 8 minutes, stirring, until it smells nutty and turns pale gold.
Stir in the coconut, sugar, sultanas and cinnamon and cook for 2 minutes until the sugar starts to melt.
Take off the heat, add the remaining ghee, then sprinkle in the warm milk a spoonful at a time until the mix just holds when pressed.
While still warm, roll the mix into 12 balls, pressing firmly with your palms.
Cool the ladoo on a plate until firm to the touch.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 ladoo.
Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 5 days.

title: Coconut Barfi Squares
summary: Fudgy coconut squares set from condensed milk, a quick Diwali and Holi sweet.

steps.text: Line a 18cm square tin with baking paper.
Melt the butter in a non-stick pan over low heat, add the condensed milk and coconut and stir for 10 minutes until the mix thickens and pulls away from the sides.
Stir in the cinnamon, then press firmly into the tin with the back of a spoon.
Scatter over the pistachios and press them in lightly.
Cool completely, then cut into 16 squares.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 squares. Plus 1 hour setting.
Keeps in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 7 days.

title: Baked Gujiya Coconut Pastries
summary: Crisp baked half-moon pastries filled with sweet coconut, semolina and nuts for Holi and Diwali.

steps.text: Mix the flour, salt and 2 tbsp ghee, add the water and knead for 5 minutes until smooth. Cover and rest.
Toast the semolina in the remaining ghee for 4 minutes until fragrant, then stir in the coconut, sugar, sultanas and almonds and cool.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Roll the dough thinly and cut 12 rounds about 10cm wide.
Put 1 heaped tbsp of filling on each round, brush the edge with water, fold over and press with a fork to seal.
Bake on a lined tray for 20 minutes, turning once, until pale gold and crisp. Cool on a rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 pastries. Plus 20 minutes resting the dough.
Store in an airtight container for up to 5 days.

title: Baked Chakli Rice Flour Spirals
summary: Crunchy spiced rice and chickpea flour spirals, baked instead of deep-fried for Diwali snack boxes.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line two trays.
Mix the flours, butter, cumin, sesame and salt, then add the warm water a little at a time to make a soft smooth dough.
Fill a piping bag fitted with a star nozzle and pipe 12 spirals about 6cm wide onto the trays.
Bake for 25 minutes, swapping the trays halfway, until pale gold and crisp.
Cool on the trays for 10 minutes so they crisp up.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 3 chakli. Baked rather than deep-fried, which also avoids hot oil.
Store in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks.

title: Shankarpali Diamond Biscuits
summary: Lightly sweet, crisp baked diamonds of semolina dough, a Maharashtrian Diwali snack.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line two trays.
Stir the sugar into the warm milk until dissolved, then mix with the flour, semolina, ghee and salt into a stiff dough. Cover and rest.
Roll the dough 5mm thick on a floured bench and cut into 40 small diamonds with a knife.
Spread on the trays and bake for 20 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
Cool completely before storing.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 5 pieces. Plus 15 minutes resting the dough.
Store in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks.

title: Walnut Maamoul Eid Cookies
summary: Buttery semolina cookies with a cinnamon walnut filling, baked for Eid.

steps.text: Rub the butter into the semolina, flour and 2 tbsp sugar, add the milk and knead lightly. Cover and rest.
Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Mix the walnuts, extra sugar and cinnamon.
Roll the dough into 16 balls. Press a hole into each, add 1 tsp filling and pinch closed, then flatten slightly.
Press each cookie with a fork or a mould to pattern it and place on a lined tray.
Bake for 20 minutes until set and just pale gold on the base. Cool on the tray.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 cookies. Plus 30 minutes resting the dough.
Store in an airtight container for up to 1 week.

title: Pineapple Tarts Lunar New Year
summary: Melt-in-the-mouth buttery pastry cases with a sticky spiced pineapple jam, a Lunar New Year favourite.

steps.text: Simmer the pineapple, sugar, cinnamon stick and ground cloves in a small pan for 30 minutes, stirring often, until thick and jammy. Remove the spices and cool.
Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Rub the butter into the flour and icing sugar, then mix in 1 egg yolk and the water to make a soft dough.
Roll into 24 balls of dough, press each into a mini muffin tin hole to make a case, then fill with 1 tsp jam.
Make little dough strips from any trimmings, lay two across each tart, and brush with the second egg yolk.
Bake for 15 minutes until golden at the edges. Cool for 10 minutes in the tin.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 3 tarts. Plus 20 minutes chilling the dough.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg yolk; the tarts are baked until cooked through.
Store in an airtight container for up to 1 week.

title: Lunar New Year Almond Crisps
summary: Crisp-edged, crumbly almond cookies with a whole almond on top, traditional at Lunar New Year.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line two trays.
Beat the butter and sugar for 3 minutes until pale, then beat in 1 egg and the almond extract.
Stir in the flour, ground almonds and baking powder to a soft dough.
Roll into 20 balls, flatten slightly on the trays and press a whole almond into each.
Bake for 18 minutes until golden at the edges but still pale on top. Cool on the trays for 10 minutes.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 cookies.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Store in an airtight container for up to 1 week.

title: Iced Lebkuchen Spiced Honey Cookies
summary: Soft German honey and spice cookies with a thin lemon glaze for Christmas.

steps.text: Warm the honey, brown sugar and butter in a small pan over low heat until the butter melts, then cool for 10 minutes.
Mix the flour, almonds, spices and bicarbonate of soda, then stir in the honey mix and egg to a firm dough. Chill.
Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Roll the dough 6mm thick and cut 20 rounds with a 6cm cutter.
Bake on lined trays for 12 minutes until puffed and set. Cool on a rack.
Stir the icing sugar and lemon juice into a thin glaze and brush over the cooled cookies. Let it set for 20 minutes.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 cookies. Plus 1 hour chilling the dough.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Store in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks; they soften and deepen in flavour.

title: Rough Puff Christmas Mince Pies
summary: Flaky homemade rough puff pastry cases around a spiced apple and dried fruit filling, with star lids.

steps.text: Simmer the apple, sultanas, raisins, sugar, extra butter, orange juice, zest and spices for 10 minutes until thick and sticky, then cool.
Mix the flour and salt, stir in the cold butter cubes, then add the iced water to a rough dough. Roll to a rectangle, fold in thirds and repeat 3 times, chilling between folds.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Roll the pastry 3mm thick, cut 12 rounds to line a 12-hole tin and 12 stars for the lids.
Fill each case with 1 heaped tbsp filling, top with a star and brush with the milk.
Bake for 22 minutes until deep golden and puffed. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then move to a rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 pie. Plus about 45 minutes chilling between folds.
Store in an airtight container for up to 4 days, or freeze for 1 month and warm at 160°C fan before serving.

title: Calaveras Sugar Skull Cookies
summary: Vanilla cut-out cookies iced with bright decorations for Day of the Dead.

steps.text: Beat the butter and caster sugar for 3 minutes until pale, then beat in the egg and vanilla.
Stir in the flour to a soft dough, wrap and chill.
Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Roll the dough 5mm thick and cut 24 skull or round shapes.
Bake on lined trays for 12 minutes until the edges are just golden. Cool on a rack.
Mix the icing sugar and milk into a thick icing, and decorate the cooled cookies. Leave to set for 30 minutes.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 cookies. Plus 45 minutes chilling the dough.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Store in an airtight container for up to 5 days.

title: Baked Jam Doughnuts Hanukkah
summary: Soft cake-style doughnuts baked in a muffin tin, filled with apricot jam and rolled in cinnamon sugar.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and grease a 12-hole muffin tin.
Mix the flour, sugar, baking powder and nutmeg, then whisk the milk, egg and 50g butter and fold into the dry mix until just combined.
Divide among the holes and bake for 18 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool for 5 minutes.
Use a skewer to make a hole in the side of each, then pipe or spoon in about 2 tsp jam.
Brush each with the extra melted butter and roll in the extra sugar mixed with the cinnamon.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 doughnut.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Best the day they are made; keep up to 2 days in an airtight container.

title: Cinnamon Walnut Rugelach
summary: Flaky cream cheese pastry crescents rolled around cinnamon sugar, walnuts and apricot jam.

steps.text: Rub the butter into the flour, 2 tbsp sugar and salt, add the cream cheese and bring together into a dough. Divide in two, wrap and chill.
Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Roll each half into a 28cm circle and spread with jam.
Mix the extra sugar, cinnamon and walnuts and scatter over the jam. Cut each circle into 8 wedges.
Roll each wedge from the wide end to the point and place point-down on lined trays.
Bake for 22 minutes until golden. Cool on the tray for 10 minutes.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 rugelach. Plus 1 hour chilling the dough.
Store in an airtight container for up to 4 days.

title: Almond Mandelbrot Twice-Baked Slices
summary: Crunchy twice-baked almond and cinnamon slices, ideal for dunking in a hot drink.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line a tray.
Whisk the eggs, sugar, oil and vanilla, then fold in the flour, baking powder, cinnamon and almonds to a sticky dough.
Shape into two logs about 25cm long and bake for 25 minutes until firm and golden.
Cool for 10 minutes, then cut each log on the diagonal into 10 slices.
Lay the slices cut-side up and bake for 15 minutes at 150°C fan (170°C conventional), turning once, until dry and crisp.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 slices.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Store in an airtight container for up to 3 weeks.

title: Baked Chin Chin Nigerian Crunchies
summary: Nutmeg-scented crunchy little dough cubes, baked for a lighter version of the party snack.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line two trays.
Rub the butter into the flour, sugar, baking powder and nutmeg, then mix in the egg and milk to a firm dough.
Roll 5mm thick and cut into small 1.5cm cubes with a knife.
Spread over the trays in one layer and bake for 25 minutes, stirring halfway, until golden and crunchy.
Cool completely on the trays so they crisp up.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: about 1/2 cup.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Store in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks.

title: Coconut Mandazi Baked Triangles
summary: Soft, lightly sweet East African doughnut triangles made with coconut milk and baked rather than fried.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray.
Mix the flour, sugar, baking powder, cinnamon and salt, then stir in the coconut milk and egg to a soft dough.
Knead for 1 minute on a floured bench, roll 1cm thick and cut into 12 triangles.
Brush the tops with oil and place on the tray.
Bake for 18 minutes until puffed and golden. Serve warm.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 triangles.
Best the same day; reheat in a 160°C fan oven for 5 minutes.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Classic Victoria Sponge Squares
summary: Light butter sponge sandwiched with apricot jam and whipped cream, cut into tea-time squares.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line two 20cm square tins.
Beat the butter and sugar for 4 minutes until pale and fluffy, then beat in the eggs one at a time with a spoon of the flour.
Fold in the remaining flour, milk and vanilla and divide between the tins.
Bake for 25 minutes until golden and springy to the touch, then cool completely.
Whip the cream to soft peaks, spread jam on one sponge, top with the cream and the second sponge, and cut into 12 squares.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 square.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg; keep filled cake chilled and eat within 2 days.

title: Lemon Madeira Cake
summary: A close-crumbed, buttery lemon loaf cake, the classic with a cup of tea.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional). Grease and line a 900g loaf tin.
Beat the butter, sugar and lemon zest for 4 minutes until pale and creamy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time with a spoon of flour each, then fold in the remaining flour, milk and lemon juice.
Spoon into the tin and bake for 55 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 15 minutes, then on a rack. Cut into 10 slices.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 slice.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Store wrapped for up to 4 days.

title: Whole Orange Gluten-Free Tea Cake
summary: A moist cake made from whole simmered oranges and ground almonds.

steps.text: Simmer the whole oranges in water for 60 minutes until very soft, then cool, halve and remove any pips.
Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line a 20cm round tin.
Blend the oranges to a smooth purée, then beat in the eggs, sugar, almonds and baking powder.
Pour into the tin and bake for 45 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin, then cut into 12 slices.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian and gluten-free. Per serving: 1 slice.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days; it is better the next day.

title: Rosh Hashanah Honey Cake
summary: A tall spiced honey and orange loaf cake that stays moist for days.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line a 900g loaf tin.
Whisk the eggs, sugar, honey and oil until smooth.
Stir in the flour, baking powder and spices alternately with the orange juice until just combined.
Pour into the tin and bake for 50 minutes until deep golden and a skewer comes out clean, covering with foil if it browns too quickly.
Cool in the tin for 20 minutes, then on a rack. Cut into 10 slices.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 slice.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Wrap well and keep for up to 5 days; the flavour improves after a day.

title: Cheese and Chive Muffins
summary: Fluffy savoury muffins with melted cheese and fresh chives, great for lunchboxes.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin.
Mix the flour, baking powder, mustard powder, salt, 80g of the cheese and the chives.
Whisk the egg, milk and oil and stir into the dry mix until just combined.
Divide among the cases and top with the remaining cheese.
Bake for 22 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool for 5 minutes in the tin.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 muffin.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Keeps in an airtight container for 2 days or freezes for 1 month.

title: Corn and Zucchini Polenta Muffins
summary: Savoury muffins with sweetcorn, grated zucchini and a crumbly polenta texture.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin.
Mix the flour, polenta, baking powder, salt, zucchini, corn and cheese.
Whisk the eggs, milk and oil and fold through the dry mix until just combined.
Divide among the cases and bake for 25 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool for 5 minutes in the tin, then on a rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 muffin.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Keeps in an airtight container for 2 days or freezes for 1 month.

title: Spinach and Feta Muffins
summary: Moist savoury muffins with spinach, salty feta and a hint of nutmeg.

items.raw: 100g frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin.
Mix the flour, baking powder, nutmeg, salt, spinach and feta.
Whisk the eggs, milk and oil and stir into the dry mix until just combined.
Divide among the cases and bake for 22 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool for 5 minutes in the tin.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 muffin.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Keeps in an airtight container for 2 days or freezes for 1 month.

title: Pumpkin and Sage Savoury Loaf
summary: A moist savoury loaf of pumpkin, sage and cheese, lovely sliced and buttered.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Grease and line a 900g loaf tin.
Whisk the pumpkin, eggs, oil and milk until smooth.
Fold in the flour, baking powder, salt, sage and cheese until just combined.
Pour into the tin, scatter with the pumpkin seeds and bake for 45 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then on a rack. Cut into 10 slices.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 slice.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Keeps in the fridge for 3 days or freezes sliced for 1 month.

title: Peanut Butter Oat Protein Bites
summary: No-bake peanut butter, oat and coconut bites with chocolate chips, an easy after-school or gym-bag snack.

steps.text: Mix the oats, peanut butter, honey, coconut and milk in a bowl until a thick sticky dough forms.
Fold through the chocolate chips.
Roll into 16 balls with damp hands.
Place on a tray lined with baking paper and chill until firm.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 bites. Plus 30 minutes chilling.
Keep in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 7 days.

title: Dark Chocolate Topped Oat Squares
summary: Chewy no-bake oat bars bound with peanut butter and honey, topped with dark chocolate.

steps.text: Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Melt the butter, peanut butter and honey in a pan over low heat for 3 minutes, stirring until smooth.
Stir in the oats and cocoa until evenly coated, then press firmly into the tin.
Melt the chocolate in short bursts in the microwave, stirring, and spread over the top.
Chill until set, then cut into 12 bars.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 bar. Plus 1 hour setting.
Keep in the fridge for up to 7 days.

title: Apple and Walnut Crumble Cups
summary: Cinnamon apples under a buttery oat and walnut crumble, baked in individual cups.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional).
Toss the apple with the caster sugar, cinnamon and lemon juice and divide among six 200ml ovenproof cups.
Rub the butter into the flour, oats and brown sugar until it looks like coarse crumbs, then mix in the walnuts.
Scatter the crumble over the apples and place the cups on a tray.
Bake for 30 minutes until the top is golden and the apple is tender when pierced.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 cup.
Store covered in the fridge for up to 3 days and reheat at 160°C fan for 10 minutes.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Rustic Apple Cinnamon Galette
summary: A free-form buttery pastry tart folded around sliced cinnamon apple.

steps.text: Rub the butter into the flour, sugar and salt, add the iced water to bring it to a dough, then flatten, wrap and chill.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Toss the apple with the extra sugar, cinnamon and cornflour.
Roll the pastry to a 30cm round on baking paper and pile the apple in the middle, leaving a 5cm border.
Fold the border over the fruit, brush with the milk and scatter over the almonds.
Bake for 40 minutes until the pastry is deep golden and the juices bubble. Cool for 15 minutes before cutting into 8 wedges.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 wedge. Plus 30 minutes chilling the dough.
Best eaten the day it is made; keep leftovers covered for 2 days.

title: Pear and Almond Galette
summary: Free-form shortcrust tart with thin pear slices over a sweet almond layer.

steps.text: Rub the cold butter into the flour, sugar and salt, add the iced water to make a dough, then flatten, wrap and chill.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Mix the ground almonds, extra sugar and soft butter into a paste.
Roll the pastry to a 30cm round on baking paper, spread the paste over the middle leaving a 5cm border, then fan the pears on top.
Fold the border over the fruit and brush with the milk.
Bake for 40 minutes until deep golden. Cool for 15 minutes and cut into 8 wedges.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 wedge. Plus 30 minutes chilling the dough.
Store covered for up to 2 days.

title: Spiced Poached Pears
summary: Tender pears poached in a light cinnamon, ginger and lemon syrup, served warm or chilled.

steps.text: Combine the water, sugar, cinnamon, ginger, cloves and lemon peel in a saucepan and stir over medium heat until the sugar dissolves.
Add the pears, cover with a piece of baking paper and simmer gently for 20 minutes until a knife slides in easily.
Lift the pears out and boil the syrup for 5 minutes until reduced by about a third.
Serve each pear with a spoonful of syrup.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 1 pear with syrup.
Keeps in its syrup in the fridge for up to 4 days.

title: Pear and Ginger Crumble Pots
summary: Soft pears with ginger and orange under a golden oat crumble.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional).
Toss the pear and ginger with the caster sugar and orange juice and divide among six 200ml ovenproof pots.
Rub the butter into the flour, oats and brown sugar until crumbly and scatter over the fruit.
Bake on a tray for 30 minutes until the topping is golden and the fruit bubbles.
Cool for 5 minutes before eating.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 pot.
Store covered in the fridge for up to 3 days.

title: Apricot Jam Frangipane Tartlets
summary: Shortcrust cases with a spoonful of apricot jam under golden almond cream.

steps.text: Rub the cold butter into the flour and sugar, add the iced water to make a dough, then wrap and chill.
Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Roll the pastry 3mm thick, cut 12 rounds and press into a 12-hole tin.
Beat the soft butter and sugar until creamy, beat in the egg, then fold in the almonds and flour.
Put 1/2 tsp apricot jam in each case, divide the almond cream over the top and scatter with the flaked almonds.
Bake for 30 minutes until the filling is golden and set. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 tartlet. Plus 30 minutes chilling the dough.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Keeps in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

title: Choux Puffs with Vanilla Cream
summary: Crisp, hollow choux buns filled with softly whipped vanilla cream.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line two trays.
Bring the butter and water to a boil, tip in the flour all at once and beat for 2 minutes until it forms a smooth ball. Cool for 5 minutes.
Beat in the eggs one at a time until the paste is glossy and drops off the spoon, then pipe or spoon 12 mounds onto the trays.
Bake for 15 minutes, then reduce to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and bake for 15 minutes until deep golden and hollow-sounding. Pierce each with a skewer and cool on a rack.
Whip the cream with the icing sugar and vanilla, split the puffs and fill just before serving.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 puffs.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg; keep filled puffs in the fridge and eat within 1 day.

title: Cheese Gougères
summary: Light savoury choux puffs flavoured with mustard and nutty cheese, best warm.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line two trays.
Bring the butter and water to a boil, tip in the flour all at once and beat for 2 minutes until it forms a smooth ball. Cool for 5 minutes.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then stir in 60g of the cheese, the mustard and pepper.
Spoon 20 walnut-sized mounds onto the trays and sprinkle with the remaining cheese.
Bake for 15 minutes, then at 180°C fan (200°C conventional) for 15 minutes until puffed, deep golden and crisp.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 4 puffs.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Best warm the same day; re-crisp at 160°C fan for 5 minutes.

title: Mini Chocolate Eclairs
summary: Choux fingers filled with whipped cream and dipped in dark chocolate glaze.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line two trays.
Bring the butter and water to a boil, tip in the flour and beat for 2 minutes until smooth. Cool for 5 minutes, then beat in the eggs one at a time until glossy.
Pipe 12 fingers about 8cm long onto the trays and bake for 15 minutes, then at 180°C fan (200°C conventional) for 15 minutes until golden and hollow-sounding. Cool on a rack.
Whip the 200ml cream with the icing sugar to soft peaks and fill the split éclairs.
Melt the chocolate with the extra cream, stir until smooth and dip the tops in the glaze. Let it set for 15 minutes.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 eclairs.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg; keep filled éclairs in the fridge and eat within 1 day.

title: Smoked Paprika Cheese Straws
summary: Crisp, buttery cheese pastry straws with a little mustard and paprika.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line two trays.
Rub the butter into the flour, mustard and paprika, then mix in the cheese, egg yolk and water to a dough.
Roll out 5mm thick and cut into 30 straws about 10cm long.
Place on the trays and bake for 15 minutes until golden, turning the trays halfway.
Cool on the trays for 5 minutes, then move to a rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 5 straws.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Store in an airtight container for up to 5 days.

title: Cinnamon Apple Turnovers
summary: Flaky puff pastry parcels around cinnamon-spiced apple.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray.
Cook the apple, sugar, cinnamon, lemon juice and butter in a pan over medium heat for 8 minutes until soft but still holding shape, then cool.
Cut each pastry sheet into 4 squares, put a spoonful of apple on each and fold into triangles, pressing the edges with a fork.
Brush with the milk and cut a small slit in the top of each.
Bake for 25 minutes until puffed and deep golden. Cool for 10 minutes.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 turnover.
Best the day they are baked; reheat at 160°C fan for 5 minutes.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: No-Bake Lemon Cheesecake Jars
summary: Layers of buttery oat base and whipped lemon cream cheese filling, set in jars without gelatine.

steps.text: Toast the oats in a dry pan for 4 minutes until golden, then stir in the butter and honey until combined. Cool.
Beat the cream cheese, icing sugar and lemon zest until smooth.
In another bowl whip the cream to soft peaks, then fold it into the cream cheese with the lemon juice until thick.
Press the oat mix into the base of six jars, then spoon the filling over the top.
Chill until the filling is firm and set.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 jar. Plus 4 hours chilling.
Keep in the fridge and eat within 3 days.

title: Chocolate Peanut Crunch Slice
summary: Toasted oat and peanut slice set in glossy dark chocolate, no oven needed for the base.

steps.text: Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Toast the oats in a dry pan for 5 minutes until golden, then mix with the peanuts.
Melt the chocolate, butter and golden syrup gently in a pan for 4 minutes, stirring until smooth.
Stir in the oats and peanuts, then press into the tin.
Chill until firm, then cut into 12 pieces.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 piece. Plus 1 hour chilling.
Keep in the fridge for up to 10 days.

title: Baked Zeppole with Ricotta Cream
summary: Oven-baked choux rings for San Giuseppe, filled with sweet lemony ricotta.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line two trays.
Bring the butter and water to a boil, tip in the flour and beat for 2 minutes until smooth. Cool for 5 minutes, then beat in the eggs one at a time until glossy.
Pipe 12 rings about 6cm wide onto the trays and bake for 15 minutes, then at 180°C fan (200°C conventional) for 15 minutes until deep golden and hollow-sounding. Cool on a rack.
Beat the ricotta with the caster sugar and lemon zest until smooth.
Split the rings, fill with the ricotta cream and dust with the icing sugar.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 zeppole.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg; keep filled zeppole in the fridge and eat within 1 day.

title: Spinach Pakoras Shallow-Fried
summary: Crisp chickpea-flour and spinach fritters, shallow-fried in a little oil.

steps.text: Mix the besan, rice flour, cumin, turmeric, chilli and salt, then stir in enough water for a thick batter.
Fold in the spinach and onion.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat. Drop in tablespoons of batter and fry for 3 minutes per side until deep golden and cooked through, in batches.
Drain on paper towel to make 16 pakoras, then serve hot with chutney.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 4 pakoras.
Frying safety: shallow oil only, never leave the pan unattended, add batter away from you so it does not splash, and keep a lid nearby to smother a flare-up (never use water on oil).

title: Oven-Crisp Calamari Rings
summary: Golden crumbed squid rings baked on a hot tray with paprika and lemon, no deep-frying.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 210°C fan (230°C conventional) with a lined tray inside.
Pat the squid dry. Toss with the flour, dip in the egg, then press into the breadcrumbs mixed with the paprika and salt.
Brush the hot tray with the oil, spread the rings in a single layer and bake for 12 minutes, turning once, until golden and cooked through.
Serve straight away with lemon wedges.

notes: Snack. Per serving: about 10 rings.
Food safety: keep raw squid refrigerated until needed, cook until opaque and piping hot, wash hands, boards and tray after handling raw seafood and egg, and refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

title: Baked Peas Kachori
summary: Flaky spiced green pea parcels baked instead of fried.

steps.text: Mix the flour, 2 tbsp oil and salt, add the water and knead for 5 minutes until smooth. Cover and rest.
Heat the remaining oil, fry the cumin and ginger for 1 minute, add the peas roughly mashed, spices and besan and cook for 4 minutes until dry. Add the lemon juice and cool.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Divide the dough into 8 balls and roll each into a 9cm round.
Put a spoonful of filling in each, gather the edges, pinch closed and flatten gently.
Bake on a lined tray for 25 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 2 kachori. Plus 20 minutes resting the dough.
Store in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

title: Coconut Lime No-Bake Bites
summary: Zesty coconut and cashew bites rolled in coconut, no cooking required.

steps.text: Blend the cashews and 100g of the coconut in a food processor to fine crumbs.
Add the honey, lime zest, lime juice and coconut oil and blend until the mix clumps when pressed.
Roll into 16 balls, then roll in the remaining coconut and chill until firm.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 bites. Plus 30 minutes chilling.
Keep in the fridge for up to 7 days.

title: Chickpea Chocolate Brownie Bites
summary: Fudgy mini brownie bites made with chickpeas and peanut butter, baked in a muffin tin.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and grease a 12-hole mini muffin tin.
Blend the chickpeas, peanut butter, honey, cocoa, eggs and baking powder until completely smooth.
Stir in half the chocolate chips and spoon into the holes.
Top with the remaining chips and bake for 20 minutes until set and a skewer comes out nearly clean.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 bites.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Keep in the fridge for up to 4 days.

title: Apple Cinnamon Hand Pies
summary: Little shortcrust pies filled with cinnamon apple, easy to carry.

steps.text: Rub the butter into the flour and salt, add the iced water to make a dough, then wrap and chill.
Cook the apple, sugar, cinnamon and cornflour in a pan for 6 minutes until soft and thick, then cool.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Roll the pastry 3mm thick and cut 10 rounds with a 11cm cutter.
Put a spoonful of filling on each, fold over, press the edges with a fork and brush with the milk.
Bake on a lined tray for 25 minutes until golden. Cool for 10 minutes.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 pie. Plus 30 minutes chilling the dough.
Store in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

title: Spinach and Cheese Quiche Cups
summary: Mini shortcrust cases filled with a soft egg, cheese and spinach custard.

steps.text: Rub the butter into the flour, add the iced water to make a dough, then wrap and chill.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Roll the pastry 3mm thick, cut 12 rounds and press into a 12-hole tin.
Whisk the eggs, milk and salt, then stir in the cheese, spinach and spring onion.
Pour into the cases and bake for 25 minutes until the filling is puffed, set and golden.
Cool for 5 minutes in the tin.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 cups. Plus 30 minutes chilling the dough.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg; the filling must be fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.

title: Roasted Cinnamon Apples with Yoghurt
summary: Soft cinnamon-honey apples roasted until jammy, spooned over thick yoghurt with pistachios.

items.raw: 4 apples (about 600g), cored and cut into wedges

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional).
Place the apple wedges in a baking dish with the honey, cinnamon stick and orange juice.
Roast for 25 minutes until tender and the juices turn syrupy.
Divide the yoghurt among four bowls and spoon over the apple and juices.
Scatter with the pistachios.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 cup of apple with yoghurt.
Apples keep in the fridge for 3 days; add yoghurt when serving.

title: Suji Halwa Semolina Pudding Cups
summary: Warm, glossy semolina pudding toasted in ghee with sultanas and almonds, served at Diwali and pujas.

steps.text: Warm the milk and water together in a small pan until steaming.
Toast the semolina in the ghee in a wide pan over medium heat for 6 minutes, stirring, until golden and fragrant.
Pour in the hot liquid carefully (it will spit), then add the sugar, sultanas and cinnamon and stir for 4 minutes until thick and the mix leaves the sides of the pan.
Spoon into six small cups and press down lightly.
Top with the almonds and serve warm.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 cup.
Keep covered in the fridge for up to 3 days and reheat with a splash of milk.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Crunchy Peanut Brittle
summary: Glassy golden sugar brittle packed with roasted peanuts, a sweet gift for the holidays.

steps.text: Line a tray with baking paper and have all the ingredients measured and ready.
Heat the sugar and water in a heavy saucepan over medium heat without stirring for 10 minutes until it turns a light amber colour.
Take off the heat and quickly stir in the peanuts, butter, salt and bicarbonate of soda; it will foam.
Pour onto the tray and spread thin with an oiled spoon, then cool completely.
Snap into about 16 pieces.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 pieces.
Safety: molten sugar reaches over 150°C and causes severe burns. Keep children and pets away, use a heavy pan, never touch or taste it hot, and soak the pan in hot water to clean.
Store in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks.

title: Ghorayeba Eid Shortbread
summary: Pale, crumbly Middle Eastern shortbread that melts in the mouth, topped with a pistachio.

steps.text: Beat the butter and icing sugar for 5 minutes until very pale and fluffy.
Stir in the flour to a soft dough, wrap and chill.
Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional) and line two trays.
Roll into 16 balls, place on the trays and press a pistachio into each.
Bake for 15 minutes until set but still pale, with no colour. Cool on the trays.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 cookies. Plus 30 minutes chilling the dough.
Store in an airtight container for up to 1 week; they are fragile.

title: Firni Rice Milk Pudding Cups
summary: Silky ground rice and milk pudding set in cups with pistachios, served chilled at Eid.

steps.text: Whisk the rice flour with 1/2 cup of the cold milk until smooth.
Heat the remaining milk with the sugar in a saucepan until steaming, then whisk in the rice flour mix.
Stir constantly over medium heat for 10 minutes until the pudding thickens and coats the back of a spoon.
Pour into four cups, sprinkle with the cinnamon and pistachios and chill until set.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 cup. Plus 3 hours chilling.
Keep in the fridge and eat within 3 days.

title: Jam Thumbprint Christmas Cookies
summary: Buttery vanilla cookies with a pool of apricot jam, a simple holiday biscuit-tin favourite.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line two trays.
Beat the butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the yolk and vanilla.
Stir in the flour to a soft dough and roll into 24 balls.
Place on the trays, press a deep thumbprint into each and fill with 1/2 tsp jam.
Bake for 15 minutes until the edges are pale gold. Cool on the trays for 10 minutes.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 cookies.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg yolk.
Store in an airtight container for up to 1 week.

title: Chocolate Oat Crunch Easter Nests
summary: Crunchy toasted oat and chocolate nests, easy for kids to make at Easter.

steps.text: Line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases.
Toast the oats in a dry pan for 4 minutes until golden. Melt the chocolate, butter and golden syrup in a bowl over a pan of barely simmering water, stirring until smooth, about 5 minutes.
Fold in the toasted oats until coated.
Spoon into the cases, press a hollow in the middle of each with the back of a spoon and chill until set.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 nest. Plus 1 hour chilling.
Keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 5 days.

title: Orange Cinnamon Day of the Dead Muffins
summary: Soft orange and cinnamon muffins with a sugar crust, inspired by the flavours of pan de muerto.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin.
Mix the flour, baking powder, sugar, cinnamon and orange zest.
Whisk the eggs, milk, orange juice and butter and stir into the dry mix until just combined.
Divide among the cases and sprinkle with the extra sugar.
Bake for 22 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 muffin.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Keep in an airtight container for 2 days or freeze for 1 month.

title: French Yoghurt Loaf Cake
summary: A simple, moist everyday cake measured from one pot of yoghurt, with lemon zest.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line a 900g loaf tin.
Whisk the yoghurt, sugar, eggs, oil and lemon zest until smooth.
Fold in the flour and baking powder until just combined.
Pour into the tin and bake for 40 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then on a rack. Cut into 10 slices.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 slice.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Keeps wrapped for up to 4 days.

title: Glazed Fairy Cakes
summary: Light little butter cakes with a thin glacé icing, a party-table classic.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a 12-hole bun tin with paper cases.
Beat the butter and sugar for 4 minutes until pale, then beat in the eggs one at a time with a spoon of flour.
Fold in the remaining flour, milk and vanilla and divide among the cases.
Bake for 15 minutes until golden and springy. Cool on a rack.
Mix the icing sugar and water into a thin glaze and spoon over each cake. Leave to set for 20 minutes.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 cake.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Best within 2 days in an airtight container.

title: Coconut Jam Shortbread Squares
summary: A shortbread base with apricot jam and a chewy coconut topping.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line a 20cm square tin.
Beat the butter and icing sugar, stir in the flour to a dough and press into the tin. Bake for 15 minutes until pale gold.
Spread the jam over the warm base.
Whisk the eggs and caster sugar, stir in the coconut and spread over the jam.
Bake for 25 minutes until the top is golden and set. Cool completely and cut into 16 squares.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 squares.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Store in an airtight container for up to 4 days.

title: Greek Yoghurt Oat Muffins
summary: Moist apple and walnut muffins made with Greek yoghurt and oats for extra protein.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin.
Mix the oats, flour, baking powder and cinnamon.
Whisk the yoghurt, eggs, honey and oil, stir in the apple and combine with the dry mix until just mixed.
Fold through the walnuts, divide among the cases and bake for 22 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool for 5 minutes in the tin.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 muffin.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Keeps in the fridge for 3 days or freezes for 1 month.

title: Zucchini and Cheddar Savoury Loaf
summary: A moist loaf packed with grated zucchini, cheese and chives, lovely sliced and buttered.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Grease and line a 900g loaf tin.
Mix the flour, baking powder, salt, zucchini, cheese and chives.
Whisk the eggs, oil and milk and fold through until just combined.
Pour into the tin and bake for 45 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then on a rack. Cut into 10 slices.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 slice.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Keeps in the fridge for 3 days or freezes sliced for 1 month.

title: Olive and Rosemary Quick Loaf
summary: An easy yeast-free loaf with green olives, rosemary and a little cheese.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Grease and line a 900g loaf tin.
Mix the flour, baking powder, olives, rosemary and cheese.
Whisk the eggs, milk and olive oil and fold through until just combined.
Pour into the tin and bake for 40 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then on a rack. Cut into 10 slices.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 slice.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Keeps wrapped for 3 days or freezes sliced for 1 month.

title: Chilli Cornbread Muffins
summary: Golden cornmeal muffins with sweetcorn, cheese and fresh chilli.

items.raw: 1 red chilli, deseeded and finely chopped

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin.
Mix the polenta, flour, baking powder, salt, corn, cheese and chilli.
Whisk the eggs, milk and oil and stir through until just combined.
Divide among the cases and bake for 20 minutes until golden and firm.
Cool for 5 minutes in the tin.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 muffin.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Best the same day; keeps 2 days and freezes for 1 month.

title: Sundried Tomato and Basil Muffins
summary: Savoury muffins studded with sundried tomato, basil and cheese.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin.
Mix the flour, baking powder, salt, tomatoes, basil and cheese.
Whisk the eggs, milk and oil and fold through until just combined.
Divide among the cases and bake for 22 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool for 5 minutes in the tin.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 muffin.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Keeps in an airtight container for 2 days or freezes for 1 month.

title: Rough Puff Jam Pinwheels
summary: Flaky homemade rough puff swirled with apricot jam.

steps.text: Mix the flour and salt, stir in the cold butter cubes, then add the iced water to a rough dough. Roll to a rectangle, fold in thirds and repeat 3 times, chilling between folds.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray.
Roll the pastry to a 30 x 24cm rectangle, spread with the jam and roll up from the long side.
Cut into 12 slices, lay flat on the tray and brush with the milk.
Bake for 25 minutes until puffed and deep golden. Cool for 10 minutes.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 pinwheels. Plus about 45 minutes chilling between folds.
Best the day they are baked; keeps 2 days.

title: Mini Apple Strudel Rolls
summary: Flaky puff pastry rolls with a cinnamon, apple and sultana filling, sliced into bites.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray.
Mix the apple, sultanas, sugar and cinnamon.
Sprinkle each pastry sheet with the breadcrumbs, spread the apple mix along one edge and roll up tightly, sealing the edge with a little water.
Brush with the melted butter and cut each roll into 4 pieces.
Bake, cut-side up, for 25 minutes until puffed and deep golden. Cool for 10 minutes.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 piece.
Best the day they are baked; keeps 2 days.

title: Chocolate Orange Truffles
summary: Rich dark chocolate ganache truffles with orange zest, rolled in cocoa.

steps.text: Heat the cream in a small pan until just steaming, about 2 minutes.
Pour over the chocolate and orange zest, wait 1 minute, then stir until smooth.
Chill until firm enough to scoop.
Roll into 20 balls with cool hands, coat in the cocoa and chill until firm.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 truffles. Plus 2 hours chilling.
Keep in the fridge for up to 10 days.

title: Baked Ricotta Frittelle Bites
summary: Soft, lemony ricotta bites baked in a mini muffin tin instead of fried.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and grease a 24-hole mini muffin tin with the butter.
Beat the ricotta, eggs, sugar and lemon zest until smooth.
Stir in the flour and baking powder until just combined.
Spoon into the holes and bake for 18 minutes until puffed and golden.
Cool for 5 minutes and dust with the icing sugar.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 4 bites.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Best warm; keep covered in the fridge for 2 days.

title: Roasted Beetroot Hummus
summary: Earthy pink hummus with roasted beetroot and tahini, served with warm pita wedges.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Wrap the beetroot in foil and roast for 40 minutes, until a knife slides in easily. Cool, then rub off the skins and chop.
Blend the beetroot, chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, cumin and salt until smooth, adding the water a spoonful at a time until creamy.
Cut the pita into wedges and warm them in the oven for 5 minutes until crisp at the edges.
Spoon the hummus into a bowl, swirl with a little extra oil and serve with the pita.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: about 1/4 cup hummus and 1/3 of a pita. Keeps 4 days in the fridge. Wear gloves to avoid pink hands.

title: Spicy Harissa Hummus
summary: Creamy hummus lifted with harissa, served with crisp raw vegetable dippers.

steps.text: Blend the chickpeas, tahini, harissa, lemon juice, garlic, oil and salt until thick and smooth.
With the motor running, add the water a spoonful at a time until the hummus is silky.
Taste and add more lemon or salt if needed, then spoon into a bowl.
Serve with the carrot and cucumber sticks and a drizzle of oil.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: about 1/4 cup hummus with vegetable sticks. Keeps 4 days in the fridge. Harissa brands vary in heat, so start with 1 tbsp if unsure.

title: Edamame Hummus
summary: A bright green, high-protein dip made with edamame, tahini and lime.

steps.text: Boil the edamame for 4 minutes until tender, then drain and cool under cold running water.
Blend the edamame with the tahini, lime juice, garlic, oil, cumin and salt until chunky-smooth.
Add the water a spoonful at a time until creamy, then spoon into a bowl.
Serve with the capsicum strips and cucumber sticks.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: about 1/4 cup dip with vegetables. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; the colour dulls but the flavour holds.

title: Sweet Potato Hummus
summary: Mellow roasted sweet potato blended into hummus with smoked paprika, served with pita chips.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Toss the sweet potato with 1 tbsp of the oil and roast for 30 minutes, until soft and lightly browned.
Cut the pita into triangles and bake alongside for the last 6 minutes until crisp.
Blend the sweet potato with the chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, remaining oil, paprika and salt until smooth, adding 2 to 3 tbsp water if thick.
Serve the hummus topped with a pinch of paprika and the pita chips.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: about 1/4 cup hummus with 1/3 of a pita. Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

title: Roasted Red Pepper Hummus
summary: Sweet roasted capsicum hummus with garlic and lemon, served with toasted pita wedges.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C fan (240°C conventional). Roast the whole capsicums for 25 minutes, turning once, until the skins blister and blacken.
Cover the capsicums in a bowl for 10 minutes, then peel, deseed and roughly chop.
Blend the capsicum with the chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, oil, salt and paprika until smooth.
Cut the pita into wedges and toast under the grill until crisp, then serve with the hummus, drizzled with oil.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: about 1/4 cup hummus and 1/3 of a pita. Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

title: Mutabal Tahini Eggplant Dip
summary: Smoky roasted eggplant blended with tahini and Greek yoghurt, creamier than baba ganoush.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C fan (240°C conventional). Prick the eggplants, set on a tray and roast for 40 minutes, turning once, until collapsed and charred.
Split the eggplants and scoop the soft flesh into a sieve to drain for 5 minutes, discarding the skins.
Mash the flesh with the tahini, yoghurt, lemon juice, crushed garlic and salt until creamy but still textured.
Spoon into a bowl, drizzle with the oil, scatter with parsley and serve with warm pita wedges.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: about 1/3 cup dip with 1/3 of a pita. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Muhammara Walnut Dip
summary: Syrian roasted red capsicum and walnut dip with a sweet-tart finish, thick enough to scoop.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C fan (240°C conventional). Roast the capsicums for 25 minutes, turning once, until blackened in patches. Cover for 10 minutes, then peel and deseed.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 4 minutes until fragrant, then cool.
Blitz the capsicum, walnuts, breadcrumbs, lemon juice, honey, garlic, cumin, chilli and salt to a thick, slightly coarse paste, then stream in the oil.
Spoon into a bowl and serve with toasted pita wedges.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian (honey). Contains tree nuts and gluten. Per serving: about 3 tbsp dip and 1/4 of a pita. Keeps 5 days in the fridge.

title: Avocado Salsa Verde Dip
summary: Creamy avocado blended with a cooked green tomato salsa, served with baked tortilla chips.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Cut the tortillas into wedges, toss with the oil and a pinch of salt, and bake for 8 minutes until crisp.
Simmer the green tomatoes and jalapeno in a small pan with 1/4 cup water for 5 minutes until soft, then cool slightly.
Blend the cooked tomato mixture with the coriander, lime juice, onion and salt, then add the avocado and pulse until creamy.
Serve straight away with the warm chips.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: about 1/3 cup dip with 4 chips. Best eaten within 2 hours; press cling film onto the surface to stop browning.

title: Pea Guacamole
summary: A thrifty, vivid guacamole stretched with peas, with lime, coriander and chilli.

steps.text: Cover the peas with boiling water for 3 minutes, then drain and cool under cold water.
Blitz the peas to a rough paste, then mash in the avocado, lime juice, onion, coriander, chilli, cumin and salt until creamy but still chunky.
Toast the tortillas in a dry pan for 1 minute each side, cut into wedges and crisp for a further 2 minutes.
Serve the guacamole with the tortilla wedges.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: about 1/3 cup guacamole with 2/3 of a tortilla. Eat within a day; press cling film onto the surface.

title: Mango Guacamole
summary: Chunky guacamole with ripe mango, lime and a little heat, great with corn chips.

steps.text: Mash the avocados with a fork until creamy but still chunky.
Fold in the mango, onion, chilli, lime juice, coriander and salt.
Taste and add more lime or salt, then spoon into a bowl.
Serve straight away with the corn chips.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: about 1/3 cup guacamole with 13g of chips. Best eaten the same day.

title: Cucumber Raita
summary: Cooling yoghurt with cucumber, mint and roasted cumin, a classic partner for spiced snacks.

steps.text: Toast the cumin seeds in a dry pan for 1 minute until fragrant, then crush lightly.
Squeeze the grated cucumber in your hands to remove excess water.
Stir the cucumber, mint, salt and cumin through the yoghurt.
Spoon into a bowl, dust with the chilli powder and serve with chapati wedges.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: about 1/3 cup raita with 2/3 of a chapati. Keeps 2 days in the fridge.

title: Beetroot Raita
summary: Magenta yoghurt dip with grated cooked beetroot, curry leaves and mustard seeds.

steps.text: Simmer the beetroot in a small pan with 1/4 cup water for 15 minutes, until tender and the water has gone. Cool.
Heat the oil, add the mustard seeds and cook for 30 seconds until they pop, then stir in the curry powder.
Stir the beetroot, salt and the tempered spices through the yoghurt.
Serve with warm chapati wedges.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: about 1/3 cup raita with 2/3 of a chapati. Keeps 2 days in the fridge.

title: Mint and Coriander Yoghurt Dip
summary: Fresh green chutney folded through yoghurt for kebabs, pakoras and crisps.

steps.text: Blend the mint, coriander, chilli, lemon juice, sugar, cumin and salt with 2 tbsp water to a smooth green paste.
Fold the paste through the yoghurt until evenly green.
Taste and adjust the salt and lemon, then spoon into a bowl.
Serve with the carrot sticks.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: about 3 tbsp dip with vegetables. Keeps 2 days in the fridge.

title: Beetroot Tzatziki
summary: Pink-purple tzatziki with grated raw beetroot, garlic and dill, served with warm pita.

items.raw: 1 small raw beetroot (100g), peeled and grated

steps.text: Squeeze the grated cucumber in your hands to remove excess water.
Stir the cucumber, beetroot, garlic, oil, lemon juice, dill and salt through the yoghurt until evenly pink.
Warm the pita in a dry pan for 1 minute each side and cut into wedges.
Serve the tzatziki with the warm pita.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: about 1/3 cup tzatziki with 1/3 of a pita. Keeps 2 days in the fridge.

title: Rosemary Cannellini Dip with Sourdough Fingers
summary: A smooth cannellini dip with roasted garlic flavour, rosemary and lemon, served with toasted sourdough.

items.raw: 400g can cannellini beans, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Warm the garlic and rosemary in 1 tbsp of the oil in a small pan for 3 minutes, without letting the garlic brown.
Blend the beans, the warm garlic oil, lemon juice, salt and 3 tbsp water until completely smooth.
Toast the sourdough until golden, cut each slice into 4 fingers and arrange around a bowl.
Spoon in the dip and finish with the remaining oil.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: about 1/4 cup dip with 2/3 of a slice of toast. Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

title: Caprese Skewers
summary: Cherry tomato, basil and bocconcini on skewers with a balsamic drizzle for easy entertaining.

steps.text: Thread a tomato, a basil leaf and a bocconcini onto each of 24 short skewers or toothpicks.
Arrange the skewers on a platter.
Whisk the oil, balsamic, salt and pepper until combined and drizzle over the skewers just before serving.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian (fresh mozzarella uses non-animal rennet in most brands; check the label). Per serving: 4 skewers. Best eaten within 2 hours; keep chilled until serving.

title: Prawn and Chorizo Skewers
summary: Garlicky prawns and chorizo threaded and grilled, a quick tapas-style party bite.

items.raw: 18 large raw prawns (about 400g), peeled and deveined

steps.text: Toss the prawns with the oil, garlic, paprika, lemon juice and salt. Thread each skewer with 3 prawns, alternating with 3 pieces of chorizo.
Heat a grill or griddle pan to high and cook the skewers for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until the prawns are pink and opaque and the chorizo is sizzling.
Scatter with the parsley and serve hot with lemon wedges.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 skewer of 3 prawns and 3 pieces of chorizo.
Food safety: keep raw prawns refrigerated until cooking, cook until opaque and pink throughout, wash hands and boards after handling raw seafood, and eat within 2 hours or refrigerate leftovers.

title: Soy-Mirin Chicken Thigh Skewers
summary: Glazed chicken thigh skewers with a sweet soy tare, cooked in the oven.

items.raw: 500g chicken thigh fillets, cut into 3cm pieces

steps.text: Simmer the soy sauce, mirin, honey and ginger in a small pan for 4 minutes until slightly syrupy, then cool a little.
Thread the chicken and spring onion onto 12 skewers and brush with oil.
Heat the oven grill to high and grill the skewers on a lined tray for 12 minutes, turning and brushing with the glaze every 4 minutes, until the chicken reaches 75°C in the centre.
Brush with a final layer of glaze and serve hot.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 skewers.

Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C throughout, wash hands, boards and utensils after handling raw chicken, do not reuse the raw-chicken brush on cooked skewers, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Mini Beef Sliders
summary: Juicy beef patties on mini buns with cheese, pickles and a quick sauce.

steps.text: Mix the mince with the salt and pepper and shape into 8 small patties slightly wider than the buns.

Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat and cook the patties for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through with no pink inside. Lay half a cheese slice on each in the last minute.
Toast the buns cut side down in the pan for 1 minute.
Mix the tomato sauce and mayonnaise, spread on the buns, then add lettuce, patty and pickle.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 slider.
Food safety: cook beef mince to 75°C throughout until no pink remains, wash hands and surfaces after handling raw mince, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
