title: Crispy Baked Chicken Sliders
summary: Oven-crisped crumbed chicken pieces on mini buns with slaw.

items.raw: 500g chicken breast, sliced into 8 thin pieces

steps.text: Heat the oven to 210°C fan (230°C conventional). Mix the panko with the paprika, salt and oil.
Dip each chicken piece in the flour, the egg, then the panko mixture, pressing on firmly.
Bake on a lined tray for 20 minutes, turning once, until golden and the chicken reaches 75°C in the centre.
Toss the cabbage with 1 tbsp of the mayonnaise and the lemon juice. Spread the rest on the buns and fill with chicken and slaw.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 slider.
Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C throughout, wash hands and boards after handling raw chicken and egg, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Mushroom Walnut Sliders
summary: A savoury mushroom and walnut patty on mini buns with mustard and rocket.

steps.text: Cook the mushrooms in a dry frying pan over medium-high heat for 8 minutes until the liquid has gone, then add 1 tbsp of the oil, the onion and the garlic and cook for 5 minutes more.
Stir in the soy sauce, mustard, walnuts and oats, then cool slightly and shape into 8 small patties.
Fry the patties in the remaining oil for 3 minutes per side until crisp and golden.
Fill the toasted buns with the patties and rocket.

notes: Snack. Vegan (check the bun label). Contains tree nuts and gluten. Per serving: 1 slider. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Spinach and Ricotta Stuffed Mushrooms
summary: Button mushrooms filled with spinach, ricotta and lemon, baked until golden.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Twist the stalks out of the mushrooms and finely chop 4 of them.
Cook the chopped stalks and garlic in the oil for 2 minutes, add the spinach and cook for 2 minutes more until wilted, then squeeze dry and chop.
Mix with the ricotta, lemon zest, salt and pepper and fill the mushroom caps, then top with the breadcrumbs.
Bake for 20 minutes until the filling is golden and the mushrooms are tender.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 3 stuffed mushrooms. Best served warm. Keeps 2 days in the fridge.

title: Pork and Thyme Mushroom Caps
summary: Large mushrooms stuffed with seasoned pork sausage meat and herbs, baked until sizzling.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Remove the mushroom stalks and finely chop 3 of them.
Fry the onion, garlic and chopped stalks in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, then cool and mix with the sausage meat, breadcrumbs, thyme and pepper.
Fill the caps with the mixture, pressing firmly, and place on a lined tray.
Bake for 22 minutes, until the filling is browned and cooked through at 75°C.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 stuffed mushrooms.
Food safety: pork sausage meat must reach 75°C throughout with no pink remaining, wash hands and surfaces after handling raw pork, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Smoked Salmon Cucumber Rounds
summary: Thick cucumber rounds topped with dill cream cheese and smoked salmon, ready in minutes.

items.raw: 2 Lebanese cucumbers, cut into 12 thick rounds

steps.text: Mix the cream cheese with the lemon juice, half the dill and the pepper until smooth.
Pipe or spoon a small mound onto each cucumber round.
Fold a piece of smoked salmon on top of each, then finish with the remaining dill and a caper.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 3 rounds.
Food safety: smoked salmon is a ready-to-eat chilled food. Keep refrigerated, eat within 2 hours of serving, and pregnant women and people with weakened immunity should avoid it.

title: Classic Devilled Eggs
summary: Creamy mustard-and-paprika egg yolk filling piped into halved boiled eggs.

steps.text: Cover the eggs with cold water, bring to the boil, then simmer for 10 minutes. Cool in iced water, then peel.
Halve the eggs lengthways and pop the yolks into a bowl.
Mash the yolks with the mayonnaise, mustard, vinegar and salt until smooth, then spoon or pipe into the whites.
Dust with paprika and scatter with chives.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 egg halves.
Food safety: cook the eggs until the yolks are firm, keep chilled until serving, eat within 2 hours at room temperature and refrigerate leftovers for up to 2 days.

title: Marinated Artichoke Hearts
summary: Tender artichoke quarters tossed in lemon, garlic, oregano and olive oil, ready for a snack plate.

items.raw: 400g can artichoke hearts, drained and quartered

steps.text: Pat the artichokes dry on paper towel so the marinade clings.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, chilli and salt until combined.
Toss the artichokes through the marinade until evenly coated, then spoon into a jar or bowl and serve with toothpicks.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: about 4 quarters. Plus 30 minutes marinating at room temperature, or up to 5 days in the fridge; bring to room temperature before serving.

title: Garlic and Thyme Marinated Mushrooms
summary: Tapas-style button mushrooms softened in a sherry vinegar and thyme marinade.

steps.text: Warm 1 tbsp of the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat and cook the mushrooms for 6 minutes, until golden and no liquid remains.
Add the garlic and thyme and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Tip into a bowl and stir through the remaining oil, vinegar, salt and pepper until glossy.
Serve warm or at room temperature with toothpicks.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: about 1/2 cup. Plus 1 hour marinating. Keeps 5 days in the fridge.

title: Pickled Beetroot Eggs
summary: Hard-boiled eggs steeped in a sweet-sharp beetroot brine until pink, a pub-style snack.

steps.text: Cover the eggs with cold water, bring to the boil and simmer for 10 minutes. Cool in iced water and peel.
Simmer the vinegar, water, sugar, salt and peppercorns for 3 minutes until the sugar dissolves, then cool.
Pack the eggs and beetroot into a clean jar and pour over the brine until covered.
Seal and keep in the fridge until the eggs are pink through the outer white.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 egg with a few beetroot slices. Plus 2 days pickling.
Food safety: use only clean, sterilised jars, keep the jar in the fridge at all times, and eat within 5 days.

title: Korean Style Spicy Cucumber Pickle
summary: Salted cucumber chunks tossed in chilli flakes, garlic, sesame and a little sugar, ready in an hour.

steps.text: Toss the cucumber with the salt and leave in a colander until it releases water, then squeeze lightly and dry.
Mix the chilli flakes, garlic, soy sauce, vinegar and sugar into a paste.
Toss the cucumber, paste, spring onion and sesame seeds together until evenly coated.
Serve as a crunchy side snack.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: about 1 cup. Plus 20 minutes salting. Best within 2 days.

title: Giardiniera Italian Pickled Vegetables
summary: Crunchy carrot, cauliflower, celery and capsicum in a tangy herbed brine, finished with olive oil.

steps.text: Pack all the vegetables into a clean jar.
Simmer the vinegar, water, sugar, salt, oregano and garlic for 3 minutes until the sugar and salt dissolve, then pour over the vegetables until just covered.
Cool, then seal and refrigerate for 1 day until the vegetables taste pickled.
To serve, drain the vegetables and toss with the olive oil.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: about 1/2 cup. Plus 1 day pickling. Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge.

title: Marinated Feta Cubes
summary: Salty feta cubes in olive oil with lemon peel, thyme and chilli to spear or spread.

steps.text: Pack the feta into a clean jar.
Mix the oil, lemon zest, thyme, chilli and peppercorns and pour over the feta until fully covered.
Seal and refrigerate until the flavours develop, then serve with toothpicks.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian (check the feta label for non-animal rennet). Per serving: about 5 cubes with some oil. Plus 4 hours marinating. Keeps 1 week in the fridge.

title: Tamari Roasted Chickpeas
summary: Crunchy chickpeas roasted with tamari and smoked paprika for a high-fibre desk snack.

items.raw: 2 x 400g cans chickpeas, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Dry the chickpeas very well on a clean tea towel.
Toss with the oil, tamari, paprika and garlic powder.
Roast on a lined tray for 30 minutes, shaking twice, until crisp and deep golden.
Cool on the tray, where they crisp further.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: about 1/2 cup. Store in an open container; sealed jars soften them. Best within 3 days.

title: Vegan Sun-Dried Tomato and White Bean Spread
summary: A cheese-free spread of cannellini beans, sun-dried tomatoes and basil on toasted sourdough.

items.raw: 400g can cannellini beans, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Blend the beans, sun-dried tomatoes, garlic, oil, lemon juice, basil and salt until thick and nearly smooth.
Toast the sourdough until golden and cut each slice in half.
Spread the toast generously with the bean mixture until covered, then serve.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 1 half slice with spread. The spread alone keeps 4 days in the fridge.

title: Vegan Mushroom and Walnut Pate
summary: A rich, cheese-free pate of mushrooms, walnuts and white beans on toasted sourdough.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 4 minutes until soft, add the mushrooms, garlic and thyme and cook for 8 minutes until all the liquid has gone.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Blend the mushroom mixture, walnuts, beans and soy sauce until thick and spreadable.
Toast the sourdough until golden, cut each slice in half and serve with the pate.

notes: Snack. Vegan (check the bread label). Contains tree nuts and gluten. Per serving: 1 half slice with pate. Plus 2 hours chilling. Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

title: Vegan Potato and Carrot Nacho Dip
summary: A cheese-free orange dip made from potato, carrot and tahini, with a smoky kick, served with corn chips.

steps.text: Simmer the potato, carrot, onion and garlic in water for 18 minutes, until very soft, then reserve 1/2 cup of the cooking water and drain.
Blend the vegetables with the tahini, oil, lemon juice, paprika and salt, adding the reserved water until smooth and pourable.
Serve warm with the corn chips.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: about 1/3 cup dip with 16g of chips. Keeps 4 days in the fridge; thin with water when reheating.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Seed Cracker Dippers
summary: Crisp olive oil crackers packed with sunflower, pumpkin and sesame seeds, sturdy enough for any dip.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Mix the flour, seeds and salt, then stir in the oil and water to a firm dough.
Roll the dough very thinly between two sheets of baking paper and cut into 32 small rectangles.
Bake on a lined tray for 22 minutes, turning the tray halfway, until golden and crisp.
Cool on a wire rack, where they crisp further.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 4 crackers. Contains gluten and sesame. Keeps 7 days in an airtight container.

title: Vegan Stuffed Mini Capsicums
summary: Sweet mini capsicum halves filled with a lemony basil tofu cream, baked until the edges soften.

items.raw: 8 mini capsicums, halved lengthways and deseeded

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Roast the capsicum halves cut side up on a lined tray for 8 minutes until just soft.
Blend the tofu, oil, tahini, lemon juice, garlic and salt until creamy, then stir in the basil.
Spoon the filling into the capsicums and bake for 4 minutes more until warmed through.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

notes: Snack. Vegan, cheese-free. Per serving: 4 halves. Keeps 2 days in the fridge.

title: Sunflower Seed Chocolate Oat Balls
summary: Nut-free, school-safe oat balls rolled in coconut, sweetened with honey.

steps.text: Mix the oats, ground sunflower seeds, honey, chocolate chips and water until the mixture holds together when pressed.
Roll into 12 balls and coat each in the coconut.
Place on a tray and keep cold until firm.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Nut-free and school-safe (check the chocolate label for traces). Per serving: 2 balls. Plus 30 minutes chilling. Keeps 5 days in the fridge.

title: Nut-Free Oat and Seed Bars
summary: Chewy baked bars with oats, sultanas and seeds, free of nuts for lunchboxes.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin.
Warm the honey and oil together until runny, then mix with the oats, seeds, sultanas, cinnamon and egg.
Press firmly into the tin and bake for 25 minutes, until golden at the edges.
Cool completely in the tin before cutting into 12 bars.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Nut-free and school-safe (check labels for traces). Per serving: 1 bar. Keeps 5 days in an airtight container.
Food safety: the egg is fully cooked through in the bake; keep the bars refrigerated if your kitchen is warm.

title: Nut-Free Veggie Pizza Scrolls
summary: Soft yoghurt-dough scrolls with tomato paste, mozzarella and capsicum for lunchboxes.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C fan (210°C conventional). Mix the flour and yoghurt to a soft dough and knead briefly until smooth.
Roll into a 25 x 35cm rectangle, spread with the tomato paste and scatter with the mozzarella, capsicum and oregano.
Roll up from the long side, cut into 12 slices and place cut side up on a lined tray.
Bake for 20 minutes, until puffed and golden.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Nut-free and school-safe. Per serving: 2 scrolls. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; freeze for up to 2 months.

title: Nut-Free Apple Oat Muffins
summary: Moist wholemeal muffins with grated apple, oats and cinnamon.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line a 12-hole muffin tin.
Mix the oats, flour, baking powder, sugar and cinnamon, then stir in the apple, egg, milk and oil until just combined.
Divide among the cases and bake for 22 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then on a wire rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Nut-free and school-safe. Per serving: 1 muffin. Keeps 3 days in an airtight container; freeze for up to 2 months.

title: Chocolate Oat Breakfast Bars
summary: Soft baked oat bars with cocoa and chocolate chips for breakfast on the go.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin.
Mix the oats, cocoa and baking powder, then stir in the honey, milk, eggs and oil, followed by half the chocolate chips.
Spread into the tin, scatter with the remaining chips and bake for 25 minutes, until firm in the centre.
Cool in the tin, then cut into 12 bars.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 bar. Keeps 4 days in an airtight container; freeze for up to 2 months.

title: Mixed Berry Oat Breakfast Bars
summary: Yoghurt and honey oat bars studded with frozen berries.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin.
Mix the oats, baking powder and cinnamon, then stir in the yoghurt, eggs, honey and oil until combined, and fold in the frozen berries.
Spread into the tin and bake for 28 minutes, until golden and set in the centre.
Cool in the tin, then cut into 12 bars.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 bar. Keeps 4 days in the fridge; freeze for up to 2 months.

title: Tropical Coconut Oat Breakfast Bars
summary: Chewy oat bars with coconut, pineapple and honey for a quick breakfast.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin.
Mix the oats, coconut, baking powder and salt, then stir in the pineapple, eggs, honey and coconut oil until combined.
Press into the tin and bake for 25 minutes, until golden and firm.
Cool in the tin, then cut into 12 bars.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 bar. Keeps 4 days in an airtight container; freeze for up to 2 months.

title: Pumpkin Oat Breakfast Squares
summary: Spiced oat squares with mashed pumpkin and sultanas, soft and not too sweet.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line a 20cm square tin.
Mix the oats, baking powder and spices, then stir in the pumpkin, eggs, honey and oil, and fold in the sultanas.
Spread into the tin and bake for 28 minutes, until set and golden at the edges.
Cool in the tin, then cut into 12 squares.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 square. Keeps 4 days in the fridge; freeze for up to 2 months.

title: Chocolate Hazelnut Biscotti
summary: Twice-baked cocoa biscotti with whole hazelnuts and chocolate chips, made for dunking.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a tray. Mix the flour, cocoa, sugar and baking powder, then stir in the eggs and vanilla to a stiff dough and fold in the hazelnuts and chocolate chips.
Shape into two logs 25cm long and 6cm wide and bake for 30 minutes, until firm to the touch.
Cool for 10 minutes, then slice each log into 12 pieces on an angle with a serrated knife.
Lay the slices cut side down, lower the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional) and bake for 12 minutes more, until dry and crisp. Cool on a wire rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains tree nuts and gluten. Per serving: 2 biscotti. Keeps 3 weeks in an airtight container.
Food safety: the eggs are cooked through in the bake; do not taste the raw dough.

title: Pistachio and Sultana Biscotti
summary: Orange-scented biscotti with green pistachios and plump sultanas, baked twice until crisp.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a tray. Mix the flour, sugar and baking powder, then stir in the eggs, oil and zest to a stiff dough and fold in the pistachios and sultanas.
Shape into two logs 25cm long and 6cm wide and bake for 28 minutes, until golden and firm.
Cool for 10 minutes, then slice each log into 12 pieces on an angle.
Lay the slices cut side down and bake at 150°C fan (170°C conventional) for 12 minutes, until dry and lightly golden. Cool on a wire rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains tree nuts and gluten. Per serving: 2 biscotti. Keeps 3 weeks in an airtight container.
Food safety: the eggs are cooked through in the bake; do not taste the raw dough.

title: Orange and Fennel Seed Biscotti
summary: A nut-free biscotti with orange zest and toasted fennel seeds, lovely with tea or coffee.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a tray. Mix the flour, sugar, baking powder, orange zest and fennel seeds, then stir in the eggs and oil to a stiff dough.
Shape into two logs 25cm long and 5cm wide and bake for 26 minutes, until golden and firm.
Cool for 10 minutes, then slice each log into 12 pieces on an angle.
Lay the slices cut side down and bake at 150°C fan (170°C conventional) for 12 minutes, until dry and crisp. Cool on a wire rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Nut-free. Per serving: 2 biscotti. Keeps 3 weeks in an airtight container.
Food safety: the eggs are cooked through in the bake; do not taste the raw dough.

title: Scottish Shortbread Wedges
summary: Buttery, crumbly shortbread pressed into a round, pricked and baked slowly until pale gold.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional) and line a 23cm round tin. Beat the butter and sugar together until creamy.
Work in the flour and salt with your hands until a smooth dough forms, then press into the tin and prick all over with a fork.
Mark into 12 wedges and bake for 40 minutes, until pale golden at the edges.
Re-cut along the lines while hot and cool in the tin before removing.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 wedge. Keeps 2 weeks in an airtight container.

title: Lemon Shortbread Rounds
summary: Tender icing sugar shortbread rounds with lemon zest, crisp at the edges.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line two trays. Beat the butter, icing sugar and lemon zest together until pale and creamy.
Mix in the flour and lemon juice until a soft dough forms, then roll into 20 balls and flatten slightly.
Bake for 15 minutes, until barely coloured on top and golden underneath.
Cool on the trays for 5 minutes, then on a wire rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 rounds. Keeps 10 days in an airtight container.

title: Nankhatai Cardamom Biscuits
summary: Crumbly North Indian ghee biscuits with chickpea flour, semolina and cardamom, topped with pistachio.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a tray. Whisk the ghee and icing sugar for 3 minutes until pale and fluffy.
Mix in the flour, besan, semolina, cardamom and baking powder until a soft dough forms.
Roll into 16 balls, flatten slightly, press a little pistachio on top and bake for 18 minutes, until set and pale golden.
Cool on the tray, as they firm up when cold.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains tree nuts and gluten. Per serving: 2 biscuits. Keeps 2 weeks in an airtight container.

title: Italian Almond Amaretti
summary: Chewy gluten-free almond macaroons with crisp cracked tops.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line two trays. Whisk the egg whites until foamy, then stir in the almond meal, caster sugar and almond extract to a sticky dough.
Roll into 16 balls, roll each in the icing sugar and place on the trays.
Bake for 18 minutes, until lightly golden and cracked on top.
Cool on the trays, as they firm up when cold.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Gluten-free (check labels). Contains tree nuts and egg. Per serving: 2 amaretti. Keeps 1 week in an airtight container.
Food safety: the eggs are cooked through in the bake; do not taste the raw dough.

title: Sables Bretons Butter Biscuits
summary: Rich Breton butter biscuits made with egg yolks and salted butter, baked in rings for a tall, crumbly texture.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and grease 16 holes of a muffin or tartlet tin. Beat the butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the egg yolks one at a time.
Fold in the flour and baking powder until a soft dough forms, then press the dough 1.5cm thick into the greased holes.
Bake for 15 minutes, until deep golden at the edges.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then ease out and cool on a wire rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 biscuits. Keeps 1 week in an airtight container.
Food safety: the eggs are cooked through in the bake; do not taste the raw dough.

title: Speculoos Spiced Biscuits
summary: Thin caramel-spiced biscuits with cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg and cloves, crisp enough for coffee.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line two trays. Beat the butter, sugar and honey together until creamy, then mix in the milk.
Stir in the flour, spices and baking powder to a firm dough, then roll to 4mm thick between two sheets of baking paper.
Cut into 24 rectangles, place on the trays and bake for 12 minutes, until golden brown at the edges.
Cool on the trays, as they crisp up when cold.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 biscuits. Keeps 2 weeks in an airtight container.

title: Pepparkakor Swedish Ginger Thins
summary: Very thin, snappy Swedish ginger biscuits with cinnamon and cloves.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line two trays. Beat the butter, sugar and syrup together until creamy, then mix in the milk.
Stir in the flour, spices and bicarbonate of soda to a firm dough, then roll very thinly, about 2mm, between sheets of baking paper.
Cut out 40 shapes, place on the trays and bake for 7 minutes, until crisp and a shade darker at the edges.
Cool on the trays, as they crisp up when cold.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 4 thins. Keeps 3 weeks in an airtight container.

title: Spritz Butter Cookies
summary: Piped vanilla butter cookies in ridged ribbons, tender and crisp-edged.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line two trays. Beat the butter and sugar until pale and fluffy, then beat in the egg and vanilla.
Mix in the flour and salt to a soft dough and pipe 30 small ribbons or rosettes onto the trays with a star nozzle.
Bake for 12 minutes, until pale gold at the edges.
Cool on the trays for 5 minutes, then on a wire rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 3 cookies. Keeps 10 days in an airtight container.
Food safety: the eggs are cooked through in the bake; do not taste the raw dough.

title: Moroccan Ghriba Coconut Biscuits
summary: Soft, chewy coconut biscuits with a crackled top, lightly scented with lemon.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a tray. Mix the coconut, sugar, semolina, vanilla and lemon zest, then stir in the egg whites until the mixture clumps together.
Roll into 16 small balls and place on the tray.
Bake for 15 minutes, until lightly golden at the edges and cracked on top.
Cool on the tray, as they firm up when cold.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains gluten (semolina) and egg. Per serving: 2 biscuits. Keeps 1 week in an airtight container.
Food safety: the eggs are cooked through in the bake; do not taste the raw dough.

title: Un Kurabiyesi Turkish Flour Biscuits
summary: Melt-in-the-mouth Turkish butter biscuits with a dusting of icing sugar.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a tray. Beat the butter and icing sugar until pale and creamy, then beat in the egg yolk and vanilla.
Mix in the flour to a soft dough, then roll into 20 balls and press an indent in each with your thumb.
Bake for 20 minutes, until set and barely coloured.
Cool on the tray, as they are fragile while warm.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 biscuits. Keeps 10 days in an airtight container.
Food safety: the eggs are cooked through in the bake; do not taste the raw dough.

title: Nan-e Nokhodchi Persian Chickpea Flour Biscuits
summary: Delicate gluten-free Persian chickpea flour biscuits scented with cardamom and topped with pistachio.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional) and line two trays. Toast the besan in a dry pan over low heat for 5 minutes, until it smells nutty, then cool.
Mix the besan, icing sugar and cardamom, then stir in the melted butter to a soft dough.
Roll into 24 balls, flatten gently and top with pistachio.
Bake for 18 minutes, until set and barely coloured. Cool on the trays, as they are fragile while warm.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains tree nuts. Per serving: 2 biscuits. Keeps 10 days in an airtight container.

title: Swedish Dream Biscuits
summary: Drommar: pale, tender butter biscuits with vanilla that dissolve on the tongue.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional) and line two trays. Beat the butter and sugar until pale and fluffy, then beat in the vanilla.
Mix in the flour, baking powder and salt to a soft dough, then roll into 24 balls and place on the trays.
Bake for 18 minutes, until set and barely coloured.
Cool on the trays, as they are fragile while warm.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 biscuits. Keeps 10 days in an airtight container.

title: Vanillekipferl Almond Crescents
summary: Austrian crescent biscuits with almond meal and vanilla icing sugar.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line two trays. Rub the butter into the flour, almond meal and 70g of the icing sugar, then mix in the yolk and vanilla to a smooth dough.
Roll pieces into 30 small logs and curve each into a crescent.
Bake for 12 minutes, until pale gold at the edges.
Dust with the remaining icing sugar while still warm, then cool on a wire rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains tree nuts, gluten and egg. Per serving: 3 crescents. Keeps 2 weeks in an airtight container.
Food safety: the eggs are cooked through in the bake; do not taste the raw dough.

title: Baci di Dama Hazelnut Sandwich Biscuits
summary: Little hazelnut shortbread domes sandwiched with dark chocolate, the Italian lady's kisses.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional) and line two trays. Beat the butter and sugar until creamy, then mix in the ground hazelnuts and flour to a dough.
Roll into 40 small balls and bake for 18 minutes, until pale golden. Cool on the trays.
Spread a little melted chocolate on the flat side of 20 biscuits and sandwich with the rest.
Leave to set until the chocolate is firm.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains tree nuts and gluten. Per serving: 2 sandwiched biscuits. Keeps 2 weeks in an airtight container.

title: Mexican Wedding Cookies
summary: Walnut shortbread balls rolled in icing sugar, tender and crumbly.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line two trays. Beat the butter and 80g icing sugar until pale and fluffy, then beat in the vanilla.
Mix in the flour, salt and walnuts to a soft dough, then roll into 24 balls and place on the trays.
Bake for 15 minutes, until pale golden underneath.
Roll the warm biscuits in the remaining icing sugar and cool on a wire rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains tree nuts and gluten. Per serving: 2 cookies. Keeps 2 weeks in an airtight container.

title: Vanilla Birthday Sponge Squares
summary: Soft vanilla sponge squares with a thin buttercream layer, easy to cut and carry to a party.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Beat the 175g butter and the caster sugar for 4 minutes until pale and fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Fold in the flour and milk until just smooth, scrape into the tin and level the top.
Bake for 30 minutes until golden and a skewer in the centre comes out clean. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then lift out onto a rack to cool completely.
Beat the 80g butter with the icing sugar and 1 tbsp water until fluffy, spread over the cold cake and cut into 12 squares.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 square.
Storage: keeps 3 days in an airtight container in a cool spot; the iced cake freezes for 2 months.

title: Victoria Sponge Fingers
summary: Two light sponge layers sandwiched with jam and whipped cream, cut into tidy fingers.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Grease and line two 18cm square tins.
Beat the butter and caster sugar for 4 minutes until pale and fluffy, then beat in the eggs and vanilla one at a time.
Fold in the flour and baking powder, divide between the tins and level the tops.
Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until risen, golden and springy to a light press. Cool in the tins for 5 minutes, then turn out onto a rack.
Whip the cream with the icing sugar to soft peaks. Spread one sponge with the jam, then the cream, top with the second sponge and cut into 10 fingers.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 finger.
Storage: best the day it is filled; keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days.

title: Lemon Chiffon Cake Wedges
summary: A tall, airy cake made with oil and whipped egg whites, finished with a light lemon glaze.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Leave a 20cm tube tin ungreased so the cake can climb the sides.
Whisk the flour, 120g of the sugar, baking powder and salt in a bowl. Make a well and add the oil, water, egg yolks and lemon zest, then whisk to a smooth batter.
Whisk the egg whites to soft peaks, then add the remaining 80g sugar a spoonful at a time until stiff and glossy.
Fold a third of the whites into the batter to loosen it, then gently fold in the rest. Pour into the tin and bake for 45 minutes until deep golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Turn the tin upside down onto a bottle neck and cool completely. Run a knife around the edges, release, then drizzle with the icing sugar mixed with the lemon juice and cut into 12 wedges.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian.
Storage: keeps 3 days covered at room temperature.

title: Orange Chiffon Slices
summary: Cloud-soft orange chiffon baked in a loaf tin, sliced thickly for the lunchbox.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Line the base of a 23cm loaf tin with baking paper and leave the sides ungreased.
Whisk the flour, 100g of the sugar, baking powder and salt. Add the oil, orange juice, zest, vanilla and egg yolks and whisk until smooth.
Whisk the egg whites to soft peaks, add the remaining 70g sugar gradually and whisk to stiff, glossy peaks.
Fold a third of the whites into the batter, then fold in the rest gently so the air stays in.
Bake for 40 minutes until golden, springy and a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely in the tin before slicing into 12.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian.
Storage: keeps 3 days in an airtight container.

title: Classic Butter Loaf Cake Slices
summary: A dense, buttery loaf with a fine crumb, perfect with a cup of tea or sliced fruit.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional). Grease and line a 23cm loaf tin.
Beat the butter and sugar for 5 minutes until very pale and fluffy. Add the eggs one at a time, beating well, then the vanilla.
Fold in the flour, baking powder and salt alternately with the milk until just combined.
Scrape into the tin and bake for 60 minutes until deep golden, the top has cracked and a skewer comes out clean. Cover loosely with foil if it browns too quickly.
Cool in the tin for 15 minutes, then turn out and slice into 12 even slices.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 slice.
Storage: keeps 4 days wrapped; freezes well in slices for 2 months.

title: Glazed Pineapple Ring Cake Squares
summary: A buttery brown sugar and pineapple topping baked over a soft vanilla cake, turned out and cut into squares.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Stir the melted butter and brown sugar together, spread over the base of the tin and arrange the drained pineapple on top.
Beat the softened butter and caster sugar for 3 minutes until pale. Beat in the eggs and vanilla, then fold in the flour and pineapple juice.
Spoon the batter over the pineapple and level it. Bake for 40 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Rest for 5 minutes, then turn out onto a board while still warm, peel off the paper and cut into 12 squares.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 square.
Storage: best within 2 days; keep covered at room temperature.

title: Apple Upside-Down Cake
summary: Caramelised cinnamon apples under a tender sponge, flipped to show the glossy top.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Line a 20cm round cake tin with baking paper.
Melt the 50g butter with the brown sugar in a frying pan, add the apples and cinnamon and cook for 5 minutes until just soft and glossy. Spread over the base of the tin.
Beat the softened butter and caster sugar for 3 minutes until pale. Beat in the eggs, then fold in the flour and milk.
Spoon over the apples and level. Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Rest for 5 minutes, then turn out onto a plate and cut into 12 wedges.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 wedge.
Storage: keeps 2 days covered; reheat a wedge for 20 seconds in the microwave if wanted.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Pear Upside-Down Ginger Cake
summary: Spiced ginger sponge over caramelised pear slices, sticky and fragrant.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Line a 20cm round cake tin with baking paper.
Melt the 50g butter and the first 80g brown sugar in a frying pan, add the pears and cook for 4 minutes until glossy. Arrange in the tin.
Beat the softened butter, remaining 100g brown sugar and golden syrup for 3 minutes. Beat in the eggs, then fold in the flour, ginger, cinnamon and milk.
Spoon over the pears. Bake for 45 minutes until a skewer comes out clean and the top is deep golden.
Rest for 5 minutes, turn out onto a plate and cut into 12 wedges.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 wedge.
Storage: keeps 3 days covered at room temperature.

title: Chocolate Birthday Traybake
summary: A fudgy chocolate sheet cake with a glossy chocolate icing, made for sharing.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line a 20cm by 30cm tin.
Beat the butter and sugar for 4 minutes until pale. Beat in the eggs one at a time.
Sift in the flour, cocoa and baking powder, add the milk and fold until smooth. Spread into the tin.
Bake for 28 to 30 minutes until the cake springs back and a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tin.
Heat the cream until steaming, pour over the broken chocolate, stand for 2 minutes and stir until glossy. Cool for 10 minutes, spread over the cake and cut into 12.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 piece.
Storage: keeps 4 days in an airtight container.

title: Coconut Vanilla Celebration Cake
summary: A moist coconut milk sponge topped with vanilla icing and toasted coconut, light enough for a crowd.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line a 20cm square tin.
Beat the butter and caster sugar for 4 minutes until pale. Beat in the eggs and vanilla.
Fold in the flour, the first 30g coconut and the 200ml coconut milk until smooth, then spread into the tin.
Bake for 35 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely.
Toast the last 30g coconut in a dry pan for 2 minutes until pale gold. Mix the icing sugar with 2 tbsp coconut milk, spread over the cake, scatter with the coconut and cut into 12.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 piece.
Storage: keeps 3 days in an airtight container.

title: Madeira Cake Slices
summary: A classic lemony loaf with a firm, even crumb that slices cleanly.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional). Grease and line a 23cm loaf tin.
Beat the butter, caster sugar and lemon zest for 4 minutes until pale and fluffy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then fold in the flour, lemon juice and milk.
Spoon into the tin, level, and sprinkle with the 1 tbsp sugar. Bake for 50 to 55 minutes until golden with a split top and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, turn out and slice into 12.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian.
Storage: keeps 5 days wrapped in baking paper in a tin.

title: Almond Orange Syrup Cake
summary: A moist almond cake soaked in orange syrup, naturally wheat free if gluten-free baking powder is used.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line a 20cm round cake tin.
Whisk the eggs and caster sugar for 4 minutes until thick and pale.
Fold in the almond meal, baking powder, zest and oil, pour into the tin and bake for 40 to 45 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Simmer the orange juice and the 3 tbsp sugar for 5 minutes until slightly syrupy.
Prick the warm cake with a skewer, pour over the syrup, cool in the tin and cut into 12 wedges.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains nuts and eggs.
Storage: keeps 4 days covered; it improves on day two.

title: Marble Loaf Cake
summary: Vanilla and chocolate batters swirled together for a pretty striped slice.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line a 23cm loaf tin.
Beat the butter and sugar for 4 minutes until pale. Beat in the eggs, then fold in the flour, milk and vanilla.
Spoon half the batter into a second bowl. Mix the cocoa and hot water to a paste and stir into that half.
Drop alternate spoonfuls of the batters into the tin, then drag a skewer through once or twice to swirl.
Bake for 50 to 55 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, turn out and slice into 12.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian.
Storage: keeps 4 days in an airtight container.

title: Carrot Cake Traybake Squares
summary: Spiced carrot cake with walnuts and a light cream cheese frosting.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line a 20cm square tin.
Whisk the eggs, sugar and oil for 2 minutes. Fold in the carrot, then the flour, baking powder, cinnamon, nutmeg and walnuts.
Spread into the tin and bake for 35 minutes until firm, golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely.
Beat the cream cheese, butter and icing sugar until smooth. Spread over the cake and cut into 12 squares.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains nuts.
Storage: keep in the fridge for up to 4 days because of the frosting.

title: Spiced Pumpkin Loaf
summary: A tender spiced loaf made with roasted pumpkin purée, lovely with butter.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line a 23cm loaf tin.
Whisk the pumpkin, eggs, sugar and oil until smooth.
Fold in the flour, baking powder and spices, then the walnuts, until just combined.
Scrape into the tin and bake for 50 to 55 minutes until deep golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, turn out and slice into 12.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains nuts.
Storage: keeps 4 days wrapped; freezes well sliced.

title: Pineapple Coconut Layer Cake Wedges
summary: Two spiced pineapple and coconut layers with a cream cheese frosting, a hummingbird-style cake without banana.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line two 18cm round cake tins.
Whisk the eggs, caster sugar and oil for 2 minutes. Fold in the pineapple, flour, baking powder, cinnamon and coconut.
Divide between the tins and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely.
Beat the cream cheese, butter and icing sugar until smooth. Sandwich the layers with a third of the frosting and spread the rest on top, then cut into 12 wedges.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian.
Storage: keep in the fridge for up to 3 days; bring to room temperature to serve.

title: Honey Ginger Loaf Slices
summary: A sticky, gently spiced loaf sweetened with honey and golden syrup.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional). Grease and line a 23cm loaf tin.
Melt the butter, honey, golden syrup and sugar together over low heat, stirring until smooth. Cool for 5 minutes.
Whisk in the eggs and milk, then fold in the flour, ginger, baking powder and bicarbonate soda.
Pour into the tin and bake for 45 to 50 minutes until risen and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 15 minutes, turn out and slice into 12.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian.
Storage: keeps 5 days wrapped; the stickiness improves after a day.

title: Chocolate Beetroot Cake Squares
summary: A moist chocolate cake made with cooked beetroot, which adds sweetness and keeps it soft.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line a 20cm square tin.
Whisk the beetroot, eggs, sugar and oil until smooth.
Sift in the flour, cocoa and baking powder and fold until combined. Spread into the tin.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely in the tin.
Heat the cream until steaming, pour over the broken chocolate, stand for 2 minutes and stir until glossy. Spread over the cake, set for 20 minutes and cut into 12.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 square.
Storage: keeps 3 days in the fridge in an airtight container.

title: Cinnamon Sour Cream Crumb Cake Squares
summary: A tender sour cream cake topped with a thick cinnamon crumble.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line a 20cm square tin.
Mix the brown sugar, 60g flour, cinnamon and melted butter into big crumbs and set aside.
Beat the softened butter and caster sugar for 3 minutes. Beat in the eggs, sour cream and vanilla, then fold in the 240g flour, baking powder and bicarbonate soda.
Spread into the tin and scatter with the crumbs. Bake for 40 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 15 minutes, lift out and cut into 12 squares.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian.
Storage: keeps 3 days in an airtight container.

title: Orange Polenta Cake Wedges
summary: A rustic cake of polenta and almond meal with orange syrup.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line a 20cm round cake tin.
Beat the butter and caster sugar for 4 minutes until pale. Beat in the eggs one at a time with a spoonful of the almond meal to stop curdling.
Fold in the rest of the almond meal, polenta, baking powder and orange zest, then spread into the tin.
Bake for 40 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Simmer the orange juice and the 3 tbsp sugar for 4 minutes. Spoon over the warm cake, cool in the tin and cut into 12 wedges.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains nuts and eggs. Use gluten-free baking powder for a gluten-free cake.
Storage: keeps 4 days covered.

title: Flourless Chocolate Almond Cake Wedges
summary: A dense, fudgy flourless cake with melted chocolate and almond meal.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line a 20cm springform tin.
Melt the chocolate and butter together gently, stir and cool for 5 minutes.
Whisk the egg yolks with 60g of the sugar until pale, then stir in the chocolate mixture, almond meal and cocoa.
Whisk the egg whites to soft peaks, add the remaining 60g sugar and whisk until glossy. Fold a third into the chocolate mixture, then fold in the rest.
Bake for 28 to 30 minutes until the edges are set and the centre has a slight wobble. Cool in the tin, then cut into 12 wedges.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains nuts and eggs.
Storage: keeps 4 days in the fridge; serve at room temperature.

title: Sugar-Reduced Lemon Loaf
summary: A tangy lemon loaf using about half the sugar of a classic recipe, sweetened further by apple sauce.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Grease and line a 23cm loaf tin.
Whisk the eggs and sugar for 2 minutes, then whisk in the apple sauce, oil, yoghurt, zest and juice.
Fold in the flour and baking powder until just combined.
Pour into the tin and bake for 40 to 45 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, turn out and slice into 12.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. About 6g sugar a slice, against 15g in a classic loaf.
Storage: keeps 3 days in an airtight container.

title: Apple Pie Slab Squares
summary: A buttery pastry slab filled with cinnamon apples and topped with a crumb, cut into hand-held squares.

steps.text: Rub the flour, butter and icing sugar into fine crumbs, add the egg yolk and water and press into a dough. Wrap and chill until firm.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Line a 20cm by 30cm tin with baking paper.
Cook the apples, brown sugar, cinnamon, cornflour and lemon juice in a pan for 8 minutes until the apples are just tender, then cool.
Press two thirds of the dough into the tin, spread with the apples and crumble the remaining dough over the top.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until the top is golden and the filling bubbles at the edges. Cool in the tin, then cut into 12 squares.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Plus 30 minutes chilling the dough.
Storage: keeps 3 days in an airtight container; refrigerate in hot weather.

title: Lemon Meringue Tartlets
summary: Crisp sweet pastry cases with a tangy lemon curd and a toasted meringue peak.

steps.text: Rub the flour, butter and icing sugar into crumbs, mix in the 1 yolk and water to a dough, wrap and chill until firm.

Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Roll out the dough, cut 12 rounds and press into a 12-hole muffin tin. Prick, line with paper and baking beans, and blind bake for 12 minutes, then remove the paper and bake 5 minutes more until pale gold.
Whisk the 3 yolks, 100g sugar, zest, juice, butter and cornflour in a saucepan over medium heat for 5 minutes until thick, then divide between the cases.
Whisk the egg whites to soft peaks, add the 150g sugar a spoonful at a time and whisk until stiff and glossy. Pipe or spoon onto the tartlets.
Bake at 150°C fan (170°C conventional) for 8 minutes until the meringue peaks are golden. Cool in the tin.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Plus 30 minutes chilling the dough.
Storage: best the day they are made; keep in the fridge for up to 2 days.

title: Portuguese-Style Custard Tartlets
summary: Flaky puff pastry cups holding a vanilla custard with dark blistered tops.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C fan (240°C conventional). Roll the pastry sheet into a tight log, slice into 12 rounds and press each into a greased 12-hole muffin tin, thinning the base and pushing the pastry up the sides.
Whisk the cornflour with a little of the milk, then heat the rest of the milk, cream, sugar and lemon zest in a pan until steaming. Whisk in the cornflour mixture and stir for 3 minutes until thick.
Whisk a little hot custard into the yolks, then stir back into the pan with the vanilla. Remove the zest and cool for 5 minutes.
Spoon the custard into the pastry cases.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes until the pastry is golden and the custard tops are blistered and dark in patches. Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then on a rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 tartlet.
Storage: eat within 2 days; refresh in a hot oven for 4 minutes.

title: Treacle Tart Wedges
summary: Golden syrup and breadcrumb filling in a crisp sweet pastry, balanced with lemon.

steps.text: Rub the flour, butter and icing sugar into crumbs, mix in the yolk and water, wrap and chill until firm.

Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Roll out the dough to line a 23cm tart tin, prick the base, line with paper and baking beans and blind bake for 12 minutes, then remove the paper and beans.
Warm the golden syrup until runny, stir in the breadcrumbs, zest, juice and egg.
Pour into the pastry case and bake for 25 minutes until set at the edges and golden. Cool in the tin and cut into 12 wedges.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Plus 30 minutes chilling the dough.
Food safety: bake until the egg filling is fully set, with no liquid centre, and reaches 75°C in the middle.
Storage: keeps 4 days in an airtight container; serve with cream if wanted.

title: Bakewell Tart Slices
summary: Jam and almond frangipane in a sweet pastry case with flaked almonds on top.

steps.text: Rub the 200g flour, cold butter and icing sugar into crumbs, mix in the yolk and water, wrap and chill until firm.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Line a 23cm tart tin with the rolled dough, prick, line with paper and baking beans and blind bake for 12 minutes, then remove the paper.
Spread the jam over the base. Beat the softened butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs, almond meal and 25g flour.
Spoon the frangipane over the jam, level it and scatter with the sliced almonds.
Bake for 30 minutes until puffed, golden and firm in the middle. Cool in the tin and cut into 12 slices.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains nuts. Plus 30 minutes chilling the dough.
Storage: keeps 4 days in an airtight container.

title: Chocolate Ganache Tartlets
summary: Crisp cocoa pastry cases filled with a silky dark chocolate ganache.

steps.text: Rub the flour, cocoa, butter and icing sugar into crumbs, mix in the yolk and water, wrap and chill until firm.

Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Roll out and cut 12 rounds to line a 12-hole muffin tin. Prick, line with paper and baking beans and bake for 12 minutes, then remove the paper and bake 5 minutes more. Cool.
Heat the cream with the honey and salt until steaming and pour over the broken chocolate. Stand for 2 minutes, then stir until glossy.
Divide the ganache between the cases and chill until set.
Remove from the tin and serve at room temperature.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Plus 30 minutes chilling the dough and 1 hour setting the ganache.
Storage: keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Maple Walnut Tart Squares
summary: A gooey maple and walnut filling over a buttery shortbread-style base.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Rub the flour, cold butter and caster sugar into crumbs, mix in the yolk and press firmly into the tin. Bake for 15 minutes until pale gold.
Whisk the eggs, maple syrup, brown sugar, melted butter and vanilla until smooth, then stir in the walnuts.
Pour over the base and bake for 25 minutes until just set with a slight wobble in the middle.
Cool completely in the tin, then cut into 12 squares.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains nuts.
Food safety: bake until the egg filling is fully set, with no liquid centre, and reaches 75°C in the middle.
Storage: keeps 4 days in an airtight container.

title: Pear and Almond Frangipane Tartlets
summary: Small tarts with almond cream and poached pear slices, glazed with warm apricot jam.

steps.text: Rub the flour, cold butter and icing sugar into crumbs, mix in the yolk and water, wrap and chill until firm.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Roll out and cut 12 rounds to line a 12-hole muffin tin and prick the bases.
Beat the softened butter and caster sugar until pale, then beat in the egg and almond meal.
Spoon the almond cream into the cases and top each with 3 or 4 pear slices.
Bake for 28 to 30 minutes until the pastry and almond cream are golden. Warm the jam with 1 tbsp water, brush over the warm tartlets and cool in the tin.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains nuts. Plus 30 minutes chilling the dough.
Storage: best within 2 days; keep covered in a cool place.

title: Orange Almond Tart Slices
summary: A sweet pastry tart with a fragrant orange and almond filling.

steps.text: Rub the flour, cold butter and icing sugar into crumbs, mix in the yolk and water, wrap and chill until firm.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Line a 23cm tart tin with the rolled dough, prick, line with paper and baking beans and blind bake for 12 minutes, then remove the paper.
Whisk the eggs and sugar for 3 minutes until pale. Fold in the almond meal, zest, juice and rose water.
Pour into the pastry case, scatter with the sliced almonds and bake for 28 minutes until golden and set.
Cool in the tin and cut into 12 slices.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains nuts. Plus 30 minutes chilling the dough.
Storage: keeps 3 days in an airtight container.

title: Oat Apple Pie Bars
summary: An oat crumble base and topping around spiced apple filling, no pastry rolling needed.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Mix the oats, flour, sugar, first cinnamon, baking powder and melted butter into a crumbly dough.
Press two thirds into the tin and bake for 10 minutes.
Toss the apples with the lemon juice, cornflour and remaining cinnamon, spread over the base and scatter with the remaining crumble.
Bake for 30 minutes until golden and the apples are tender. Cool completely in the tin and cut into 12 bars.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 bar.
Storage: keeps 4 days in an airtight container.

title: Pumpkin Pie Squares
summary: Spiced pumpkin custard on a shortbread base, cut into neat squares.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Rub the flour, butter and icing sugar into crumbs, press into the tin and bake for 15 minutes until pale gold.
Whisk the pumpkin, eggs, sugar, cream and spices until smooth and pour over the base.
Bake for 35 minutes until set with a slight wobble in the centre and the edges are dry.
Cool in the tin, chill, then cut into 12 squares.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Plus 2 hours chilling before cutting.
Storage: keep in the fridge for up to 4 days.

title: Sweet Potato Pie Bars
summary: Creamy spiced sweet potato filling over an oat and pecan base.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Mix the oats, flour, pecans, melted butter and brown sugar and press into the tin. Bake for 12 minutes.
Whisk the sweet potato, eggs, milk, maple syrup and cinnamon until smooth and pour over the base.
Bake for 35 minutes until set with a slight wobble in the middle.
Cool, chill until firm, then cut into 12 bars.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains nuts. Plus 2 hours chilling before cutting.
Storage: keep in the fridge for up to 4 days.

title: Lime Pie Squares
summary: A tangy lime custard on a crisp oat base, light and refreshing.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Mix the oats, flour, melted butter and brown sugar and press into the tin. Bake for 12 minutes until golden.
Whisk the egg yolks, condensed milk, lime zest and juice until thick and pour over the warm base.
Bake for 12 minutes until just set with a slight wobble. Cool, then chill until firm.
Whip the cream with the icing sugar, spread over the top and cut into 12 squares.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Plus 3 hours chilling before cutting.
Food safety: bake until the egg filling is fully set, with no liquid centre, and reaches 75°C in the middle.
Storage: keep in the fridge for up to 3 days.

title: Caramel Pecan Tartlets
summary: Crisp pastry cases filled with a buttery caramel and toasted pecans.

steps.text: Rub the flour, cold butter and icing sugar into crumbs, mix in the yolk and water, wrap and chill until firm.

Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Roll out and cut 12 rounds to line a 12-hole muffin tin. Prick, line with paper and baking beans and bake for 12 minutes, then remove the paper and bake 5 minutes more.
Boil the sugar, butter, golden syrup and cream for 3 minutes, stirring, until thick and glossy. Stir in the pecans.
Spoon into the cases and bake for 8 minutes until bubbling. Cool in the tin until the caramel is firm.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains nuts. Plus 30 minutes chilling the dough.
Storage: keeps 4 days in an airtight container.

title: Jam Tart Bars
summary: A shortbread base and crumb topping around a layer of apricot jam, like a jam tart in bar form.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Rub the flour, baking powder, butter and sugar into crumbs, then mix in the egg, yolk and vanilla to a soft dough.
Press two thirds into the tin, spread with the jam and crumble the rest over, scattering with the coconut.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until golden. Cool completely in the tin and cut into 12 bars.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 bar.
Storage: keeps 5 days in an airtight container.

title: Apricot Coconut Slice
summary: A chewy oat and coconut slice layered with apricot jam.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Mix the flour, oats, 80g coconut, sugar and melted butter. Press two thirds into the tin.
Spread with the jam. Mix the egg into the remaining mixture, crumble it over the jam and scatter with the 30g coconut.
Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until golden. Cool in the tin and cut into 12 pieces.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 piece.
Storage: keeps 5 days in an airtight container.

title: Butterscotch Blondie Squares
summary: Chewy brown sugar blondies with a butterscotch flavour and chopped pecans.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Whisk the melted butter and sugar until smooth, then whisk in the eggs and vanilla.
Fold in the flour, baking powder, salt and pecans until just combined and spread into the tin.
Bake for 25 to 28 minutes until the top is crackled and golden, and the centre is just set. Cool in the tin and cut into 12 squares.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains nuts.
Food safety: bake until the egg filling is fully set, with no liquid centre, and reaches 75°C in the middle.
Storage: keeps 4 days in an airtight container.

title: Millionaire-Style Shortbread Squares
summary: Shortbread topped with a soft condensed milk caramel and dark chocolate.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Rub the flour, cold butter and caster sugar together until it clumps, press into the tin and bake for 20 minutes until pale gold.
Heat the 100g butter, brown sugar, condensed milk and golden syrup over medium heat for 8 minutes, stirring constantly, until thick and caramel coloured.
Pour over the shortbread and cool.
Melt the chocolate, spread over the caramel and chill until set, then cut into 12 squares with a hot knife.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Plus 1 hour setting.
Storage: keeps 5 days in the fridge in an airtight container.

title: Cream Cheese Brownie Swirls
summary: Fudgy chocolate brownies marbled with a tangy cream cheese swirl.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Melt the butter and chocolate together and cool slightly. Whisk in the 150g sugar and the eggs, then fold in the flour and cocoa.
Beat the cream cheese, 40g sugar and yolk until smooth.
Spread the brownie batter in the tin, dollop the cream cheese mixture on top and drag a knife through to swirl.
Bake for 32 to 35 minutes until the edges are set and the centre has a slight wobble. Cool in the tin and cut into 12 squares.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 square.
Storage: keep in the fridge for up to 4 days.

title: Sugar-Reduced Chocolate Brownies
summary: Rich brownies using about half the sugar of a classic recipe, with apple sauce for moisture.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Melt the chocolate and butter, stir smooth and cool slightly.
Whisk in the eggs, sugar, apple sauce and vanilla, then fold in the flour, cocoa and baking powder.
Spread into the tin and bake for 22 to 25 minutes until the top is set and a skewer comes out with a few moist crumbs.
Cool in the tin and cut into 12 squares.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. About 8g sugar a brownie, against 18g in a classic one.
Storage: keeps 4 days in an airtight container.

title: Black Bean Brownies
summary: Fudgy brownies blended with black beans for fibre and moisture, and no flour.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Blend the beans, eggs, oil, sugar, cocoa, vanilla and baking powder until completely smooth.
Stir in half the chocolate, spread into the tin and scatter with the rest.
Bake for 25 to 28 minutes until the top is set and a skewer comes out with a few moist crumbs.
Cool completely in the tin before cutting into 12 squares, as they firm up as they cool.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Gluten free if the baking powder is gluten free.
Storage: keep in the fridge for up to 5 days.

title: Chickpea Blondies
summary: Soft blondies made from blended chickpeas, with a nutty butterscotch flavour.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Blend the chickpeas, eggs, peanut butter, sugar, vanilla, baking powder and salt until completely smooth.
Stir in half the chocolate, spread into the tin and scatter with the rest.
Bake for 25 to 28 minutes until golden and set in the centre. Cool completely in the tin and cut into 12 squares.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains peanuts. Gluten free if the baking powder is gluten free.
Storage: keep in the fridge for up to 5 days.

title: Dutch Baby Wedges
summary: A puffed oven pancake baked in a hot pan, dusted with cinnamon sugar and cut into wedges.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 210°C fan (230°C conventional) with a 25cm ovenproof frying pan inside.
Blend the eggs, milk, flour, 1 tbsp sugar, salt and vanilla until smooth.
Add the butter to the hot pan until it melts and foams, swirl to coat, then pour in the batter.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until puffed and deep golden at the edges. Dust with the cinnamon and remaining sugar, then cut into 8 wedges and serve straight away.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 wedge. It deflates as it cools, which is normal.
Storage: best eaten warm.

title: Scottish Shortbread Rounds
summary: Buttery, crumbly shortbread with only three ingredients and a hint of salt.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional). Line two trays with baking paper.
Beat the butter and 100g sugar until pale, then work in the flour and salt to a soft dough.
Roll out to 1cm thick, cut 12 rounds with a 6cm cutter and place on the trays. Prick with a fork.
Bake for 20 minutes until pale gold and just firm. Sprinkle with the remaining sugar while hot and cool on the tray.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 round.
Storage: keeps 2 weeks in an airtight tin.

title: Clafoutis Squares
summary: A baked custard batter around soft apple, cut into squares and served warm or cold.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Grease a 20cm by 30cm baking dish.
Fry the apples in the butter for 5 minutes until just soft and arrange in the dish.
Whisk the eggs and sugar, then whisk in the flour, milk, cream and vanilla until smooth.
Pour over the apples and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until puffed, golden and set.
Dust with the icing sugar, cool for 10 minutes and cut into 12 squares.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 square.
Storage: best the day it is made; keep in the fridge for 2 days.

title: Cinnamon Sugar Scrolls with Cream Cheese Glaze
summary: Soft yeasted spirals filled with cinnamon sugar and finished with a tangy cream cheese glaze.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, caster sugar and salt, then stir in the warm milk, melted butter and egg to a soft dough. Knead for 8 minutes until smooth and elastic, then cover and prove until doubled.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Line a 23cm square tin or 12-hole tin with baking paper.
Roll the dough to a 30cm by 40cm rectangle. Spread with the softened butter and sprinkle with the brown sugar and cinnamon. Roll up from the long side and cut into 12 slices.
Place cut side up in the tin, cover and rest until puffy. Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until golden and the base sounds hollow when tapped.
Beat the cream cheese and icing sugar with 1 tbsp warm water until smooth. Spread over the warm scrolls.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Plus about 1 hour 30 minutes proving.
Storage: best the day they are baked; keep covered for 2 days and warm for 15 seconds before eating.

title: Orange Cardamom Knots
summary: Twisted buns with orange zest and cardamom, glazed with a sugar syrup.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, 70g sugar, salt and half the cardamom. Stir in the warm milk, melted butter, egg and zest, then knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and prove until doubled.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Line two trays with baking paper.
Roll the dough to a 30cm by 40cm rectangle. Spread with the softened butter and sprinkle with the 40g sugar and remaining cardamom. Fold into thirds and cut into 12 strips.
Twist each strip, tie into a loose knot and place on the trays. Cover and rest until puffy, then brush with the beaten egg.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes until deep golden. Dissolve the glaze sugar in 2 tbsp hot water, brush over the buns and cool on a rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Plus about 1 hour 30 minutes proving.
Storage: keeps 2 days; freezes for 2 months.

title: Chocolate Babka Buns
summary: Twisted chocolate swirl buns baked in a muffin tin, with a sugar syrup shine.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, caster sugar and salt. Stir in the warm milk, melted butter and eggs and knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and prove until doubled.
Mix the chocolate, softened butter, cocoa and icing sugar into a thick paste.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Grease a 12-hole muffin tin.

Roll the dough to a 30cm by 40cm rectangle, spread with the chocolate paste and roll up from the long side. Halve lengthways, twist the two strands together, cut into 12 pieces and press each into the tin.
Cover and rest until puffy. Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until deep golden. Brush with the sugar dissolved in 2 tbsp hot water and cool in the tin for 5 minutes.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Plus about 1 hour 30 minutes proving.
Storage: keeps 2 days; best slightly warm.

title: Mini Brioche Buns
summary: Rich, golden and buttery little buns, soft enough to eat plain or with jam.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, then add the eggs and warm milk and knead for 10 minutes until smooth and sticky.
Add the butter a piece at a time, kneading until the dough is glossy, smooth and pulls away from the bowl. Cover and prove until doubled.
Heat the oven to 190°C fan (210°C conventional). Divide the dough into 12 pieces, shape into balls and place on lined trays.
Cover and rest until puffy, brush with the beaten egg and bake for 14 to 15 minutes until deep golden and hollow when tapped on the base.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 bun. Plus about 2 hours proving.
Storage: keeps 2 days; freezes for 2 months.

title: Sweet Brioche Rolls with Honey Butter
summary: Soft brioche rolls brushed with honey butter while hot.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the eggs and warm milk and knead for 10 minutes until smooth.
Add the softened butter a piece at a time, kneading until the dough is glossy and elastic. Cover and prove until doubled.
Heat the oven to 190°C fan (210°C conventional). Divide into 12 pieces, shape into balls and place close together in a lined 23cm by 33cm tin.
Cover and rest until puffy, then bake for 16 to 18 minutes until deep golden and hollow when tapped.
Stir the melted butter and honey together and brush over the hot rolls.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Plus about 2 hours proving.
Storage: keeps 2 days in an airtight container.

title: Apple Cinnamon Pull-Apart Bread
summary: Sweet dough balls tossed in cinnamon sugar around cooked apple, baked in a loaf tin and torn apart.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, caster sugar and salt, add the warm milk, 50g butter and egg and knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and prove until doubled.
Cook the apples in the 1 tbsp butter for 5 minutes until just soft, then cool.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Line a 23cm loaf tin with baking paper.
Divide the dough into 24 pieces. Roll each in the 60g melted butter, then in the brown sugar and cinnamon mixed together. Layer in the tin with the apples scattered between.
Cover and rest until puffy, then bake for 28 to 30 minutes until deep golden. Cool for 10 minutes before pulling apart and serving in 12 portions.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Plus about 1 hour 30 minutes proving.
Storage: best warm on the day; keeps 2 days.

title: Sticky Honey Buns
summary: Soft buns baked in a honey and butter syrup so the bases come out glossy and sticky.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, caster sugar and salt, add the warm milk, melted butter and egg and knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and prove until doubled.
Melt the 80g butter, honey and brown sugar together, stirring for 3 minutes until smooth and bubbling, then pour into a lined 23cm by 33cm tin and scatter with the pecans.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Divide the dough into 12 pieces, shape into balls and place on the syrup. Cover and rest until puffy.
Bake for 25 to 28 minutes until deep golden. Cool for 5 minutes, then turn out onto a board with the syrup side up.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains nuts. Plus about 1 hour 30 minutes proving.
Storage: best the day they are baked; keep covered for 2 days.

title: Finnish Pulla Braid Slices
summary: A cardamom-scented braided loaf, sliced for coffee time.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt and cardamom, add the warm milk, melted butter and egg and knead for 10 minutes until smooth. Cover and prove until doubled.
Divide the dough into three, roll each into a 40cm rope and braid. Place on a lined tray, cover and rest until puffy.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional).
Brush with the beaten egg, scatter with the almonds and bake for 28 to 30 minutes until deep golden and hollow when tapped.
Cool on a rack and cut into 12 slices.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains nuts. Plus about 1 hour 30 minutes proving.
Storage: keeps 3 days wrapped; freezes well in slices.

title: Swedish Saffron Buns
summary: Golden saffron buns shaped as S curls, traditionally made for winter celebrations.

steps.text: Soak the saffron in the warm water. Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the milk, melted butter, egg and saffron water and knead for 8 minutes until smooth and golden. Cover and prove until doubled.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Line two trays with baking paper.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces, roll each into a 25cm rope and coil the ends in opposite directions into an S shape. Press a sultana into each coil.
Cover and rest until puffy, brush with the beaten egg and bake for 12 to 15 minutes until golden.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Plus about 1 hour 30 minutes proving.
Storage: keeps 2 days; freezes for 2 months.

title: Challah Rolls with Honey
summary: Plaited-style egg bread rolls with a honey glaze and no dairy.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the eggs, oil and warm water and knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Cover and prove until doubled.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces. Roll each into a rope, loop into a loose knot and place on lined trays.
Cover and rest until puffy. Heat the oven to 190°C fan (210°C conventional).
Brush with the beaten egg and bake for 18 to 20 minutes until deep golden and hollow when tapped.
Warm the honey with 1 tbsp water, brush over the hot rolls and cool on a rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Dairy free. Plus about 1 hour 30 minutes proving.
Storage: keeps 2 days; freezes for 2 months.

title: Glazed Yeast Doughnuts
summary: Light, airy ring doughnuts fried until golden and dipped in a vanilla glaze.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the warm milk, butter and egg and knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and prove until doubled.
Roll to 1.5cm thick, cut 12 rings with a 8cm and a 3cm cutter and rest on baking paper until puffy.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 175°C. Fry 3 doughnuts at a time for 1 minute each side until golden, turning once, and drain on paper towel.
Whisk the icing sugar, vanilla and 3 tbsp warm water into a glaze.
Dip the warm doughnuts in the glaze and set on a rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Plus about 1 hour 30 minutes proving. Never leave hot oil unattended and keep the lid of the pan nearby.
Storage: best the day they are made.

title: Apple Cider Doughnut Holes
summary: Fried cake doughnut bites with apple juice and cinnamon, tossed in sugar.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder, 1 tsp cinnamon, nutmeg and brown sugar. Whisk the egg, apple juice and butter, then stir in until a soft thick batter forms.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 175°C.
Drop heaped tablespoons of batter into the oil, 5 at a time, and fry for 2 to 3 minutes, turning, until deep golden and cooked through.
Drain on paper towel. Toss the warm holes in the caster sugar and remaining cinnamon.
Serve warm, 3 or 4 to a portion.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: about 3 holes. Never leave hot oil unattended.
Storage: best within a few hours of frying.

title: Apple Fritters
summary: Chunks of apple in a light batter, fried until crisp and rolled in cinnamon sugar.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder and 1 tbsp sugar. Whisk in the egg and milk to a thick batter, then fold in the apples.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 170°C.
Drop heaped tablespoons of batter into the oil, 4 at a time, and fry for 3 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and the apple is soft.
Drain on paper towel and roll in the remaining sugar mixed with the cinnamon.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 fritters. Never leave hot oil unattended.
Storage: best the day they are made.

title: Pineapple Fritters
summary: Rings of pineapple in a light batter, fried until crisp and dusted with sugar.

items.raw: 8 tinned pineapple rings, drained and patted dry

steps.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder and caster sugar. Whisk in the egg and milk until smooth.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 175°C.
Dip the pineapple rings in the batter, let the excess drip off and fry 3 at a time for 2 minutes, turning once, until deep golden.
Drain on paper towel, dust with the icing sugar and serve warm.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 fritter. Never leave hot oil unattended.
Storage: best eaten straight away.

title: Sweet Corn Fritters with Maple
summary: Sweet corn fritters pan-fried until crisp, served with maple syrup.

steps.text: Mix the corn, flour, baking powder, eggs, milk, spring onions and salt into a thick batter.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Cook 3 heaped tablespoons of batter at a time for 3 minutes each side until golden and cooked through, making 12 fritters.
Drain on paper towel and serve with the maple syrup.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 3 fritters.
Storage: keeps 1 day in the fridge; reheat in a hot oven for 5 minutes.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Lemon Ricotta Doughnut Puffs
summary: Light fried puffs made with ricotta and lemon zest, rolled in sugar.

steps.text: Beat the ricotta, eggs, 2 tbsp sugar and lemon zest until smooth, then stir in the flour and baking powder.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 170°C.
Drop heaped teaspoons of the mixture into the oil, 6 at a time, and fry for 3 minutes, turning, until deep golden and puffed.
Drain on paper towel and roll in the 40g sugar.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: about 4 puffs. Never leave hot oil unattended.
Storage: best eaten warm on the day.

title: Sufganiyot
summary: Round yeast doughnuts filled with apricot jam and dusted with icing sugar, made for Hanukkah.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the yolks, warm milk and butter and knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and prove until doubled.
Roll to 1.5cm thick, cut 12 rounds with a 7cm cutter and rest on baking paper until puffy.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 175°C. Fry 3 at a time for 1 minute each side until golden, then drain on paper towel.
Cool slightly, then use a piping bag to fill each with about 1 tbsp of jam through a small hole and dust with the icing sugar.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Plus about 1 hour 30 minutes proving. Never leave hot oil unattended.
Storage: best the day they are made.

title: Beignets
summary: Square pillowy yeast doughnuts, fried and buried in icing sugar.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the egg, warm milk and butter and knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and prove until doubled.
Roll to 8mm thick and cut into 24 squares about 5cm wide. Rest on baking paper until puffy.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 175°C. Fry 4 at a time for 1 minute each side until puffed and golden.
Drain on paper towel and dust generously with the icing sugar.
Serve straight away, 2 to a portion.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Plus about 1 hour 30 minutes proving. Never leave hot oil unattended.
Storage: best eaten within an hour of frying.

title: Zeppole
summary: Choux dough puffs fried until crisp and golden, dusted with icing sugar.

steps.text: Heat the butter, water, sugar and salt in a pan until the butter melts and the mixture boils. Tip in the flour all at once and stir for 2 minutes until it forms a smooth ball that leaves the pan.
Cool for 5 minutes, then beat in the eggs one at a time until glossy, and stir in the lemon zest.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 170°C. Using two spoons, drop tablespoons of the dough into the oil, 5 at a time, and fry for 5 minutes, turning, until deep golden and puffed.
Drain on paper towel and dust with the icing sugar.
Serve warm, 3 to a portion.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Never leave hot oil unattended.
Storage: best eaten warm on the day.

title: Fruit Loaf Slices
summary: A soft spiced yeast loaf studded with sultanas and raisins, best toasted with butter.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt and spices, add the warm milk, melted butter and egg and knead for 8 minutes until smooth.
