Knead in the sultanas and raisins, cover and prove until doubled.
Shape into a loaf and place in a lined 23cm loaf tin. Cover and rest until it rises just above the tin.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Bake for 32 to 35 minutes until deep golden and hollow when tapped on the base.
Cool on a rack and slice into 12.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Plus about 1 hour 30 minutes proving.
Storage: keeps 4 days wrapped; freezes well sliced.

title: Sweet Potato Dinner Rolls
summary: Soft, golden rolls made with mashed sweet potato for moisture and a mild natural sweetness.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the mashed sweet potato, warm milk, butter and egg and knead for 8 minutes until smooth and slightly tacky. Cover and prove until doubled.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces, shape into balls and place in a lined 23cm square tin. Cover and rest until puffy.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Brush with the milk and bake for 20 to 22 minutes until deep golden and hollow when tapped.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then on a rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Plus about 1 hour 30 minutes proving.
Storage: keeps 3 days in a sealed bag; freezes for 2 months.

title: Chocolate Cream Mousse Cups
summary: Silky dark chocolate mousse made with whipped cream and no raw egg.

steps.text: Melt the chocolate gently over a pan of barely simmering water, stir until smooth and cool for 10 minutes.
Whip 250ml of the cream with the sugar, vanilla and salt to soft peaks.
Stir a spoonful of the whipped cream into the chocolate to loosen it, then fold in the rest gently until no streaks remain.
Spoon into 6 small cups or glasses and chill until set.
Whip the remaining 50ml cream and top each cup with a spoonful and the grated chocolate.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Plus 2 hours chilling.
Storage: keeps 2 days covered in the fridge.

title: Vegan Chocolate Avocado Mousse Cups
summary: A rich, smooth mousse made from ripe avocado and coconut cream, with no dairy or eggs.

steps.text: Scoop the avocado into a blender with the cocoa, maple syrup, coconut cream, vanilla and salt.
Blend for 2 minutes, scraping down the sides, until completely smooth and glossy.
Taste and add a little more maple syrup if wanted.
Spoon into 6 small cups and chill until firm. Top with the grated chocolate.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Plus 1 hour chilling. Check the chocolate label says dairy-free.
Storage: keeps 2 days covered in the fridge; the surface may darken slightly.

title: Lemon Posset Cups
summary: Three-ingredient set cream cups with a tart lemon flavour.

steps.text: Heat the cream, sugar and lemon zest in a saucepan, stirring until the sugar dissolves, then boil gently for 3 minutes.
Remove from the heat and stir in the lemon juice. Strain into a jug.
Pour into 6 small glasses and cool for 15 minutes, then chill until set.
Serve topped with the berries.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Plus 4 hours chilling.
Storage: keeps 3 days covered in the fridge.

title: Cornflour Vanilla Panna Cotta Cups
summary: A soft-set vanilla cream dessert thickened with cornflour instead of gelatine, so it is vegetarian.

steps.text: Whisk the cornflour with 3 tbsp of the milk until smooth.
Heat the cream, remaining milk and sugar until steaming, whisk in the cornflour mixture and stir for 4 minutes until thick enough to coat a spoon.
Stir in the vanilla, pour into 6 glasses and cool for 15 minutes, then chill until set.
Warm the berries with the honey for 2 minutes and spoon over to serve.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Plus 4 hours chilling.
Storage: keeps 3 days covered in the fridge.

title: Coconut Panna Cotta Cups
summary: Vegan coconut milk puddings set with cornflour and served with pineapple.

steps.text: Whisk the cornflour with 4 tbsp of the oat milk until smooth.
Heat the coconut milk, remaining oat milk and sugar until steaming, whisk in the cornflour mixture and stir for 4 minutes until thick.
Stir in the vanilla, pour into 6 glasses, cool for 15 minutes and chill until set.
Toast the coconut in a dry pan for 2 minutes until pale gold. Top each cup with pineapple and coconut.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Plus 4 hours chilling.
Storage: keeps 3 days covered in the fridge.

title: Berry Trifle Cups
summary: Layers of sponge, fruit, custard and cream in small glasses.

steps.text: Toss the sponge with the apple juice and divide between 8 glasses. Warm the berries with the jam for 2 minutes and spoon over the sponge.

Whisk the yolks, sugar and cornflour. Heat the milk until steaming and whisk into the yolk mixture, then return to the pan and stir over low heat for 5 minutes until thick enough to coat a spoon and reaches 75°C.
Cool the custard for 15 minutes, spoon over the berries and chill until set.
Whip the cream to soft peaks and spoon on top.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Plus 3 hours chilling.
Storage: assemble up to a day ahead; keep in the fridge.

title: Marsala Trifle Cups
summary: Sponge soaked in a Marsala syrup with mascarpone cream and cocoa, a tiramisu-style cup.

steps.text: Warm the Marsala with the caster sugar and 2 tbsp water for 1 minute until dissolved, then cool.
Beat the mascarpone, cream, icing sugar and vanilla to soft peaks.
Divide half the sponge between 8 small glasses, sprinkle with half the Marsala syrup, and spoon over half the cream.
Repeat the layers, then chill until set.
Dust with the cocoa just before serving.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains alcohol (Marsala is cooked off only slightly). Plus 3 hours chilling.
Storage: keeps 2 days in the fridge.

title: Baked Vanilla Cheesecake Squares
summary: A creamy baked cheesecake on a crumbly oat and butter base.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Mix the oats, melted butter and brown sugar and press firmly into the tin. Bake for 10 minutes.
Beat the cream cheese and caster sugar until smooth, then beat in the eggs, sour cream, vanilla and lemon juice.
Pour over the base and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until set at the edges with a slight wobble in the middle.
Cool in the tin, chill, then cut into 12 squares.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Food safety: bake until the filling is fully set with no liquid centre, reaching 75°C in the middle.
Plus 4 hours chilling before cutting.
Storage: keep in the fridge for up to 4 days.

title: Mini Chocolate Cheesecakes
summary: Single-serve chocolate cheesecakes baked in a muffin tin.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional). Line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases.
Mix the oats, butter and brown sugar and press a spoonful into each case until firmly packed.
Beat the cream cheese and caster sugar until smooth, beat in the eggs, melted chocolate, cocoa and sour cream.
Divide between the cases and bake for 16 to 18 minutes until set at the edges with a slight wobble in the middle.
Cool in the tin, then chill.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Food safety: bake until the filling is fully set with no liquid centre, reaching 75°C in the middle.
Plus 3 hours chilling.
Storage: keep in the fridge for up to 4 days.

title: Pumpkin Cheesecake Bars
summary: Spiced pumpkin cheesecake on an oat and pecan base.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Mix the oats, pecans, butter and brown sugar, press into the tin and bake for 10 minutes.
Beat the cream cheese and caster sugar until smooth, then beat in the eggs, pumpkin, cinnamon and ginger.
Pour over the base and bake for 35 to 40 minutes until set at the edges with a slight wobble in the middle.
Cool in the tin, chill, then cut into 12 bars.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains nuts. Food safety: bake until the filling is fully set with no liquid centre, reaching 75°C in the middle.
Plus 4 hours chilling.
Storage: keep in the fridge for up to 4 days.

title: Mango Coconut Cheesecake Cups
summary: A no-bake cheesecake in glasses with mango and coconut, firmed with chilling rather than gelatine.

steps.text: Mix the oats, butter and honey and press into the base of 6 glasses.
Beat the cream cheese, coconut cream, icing sugar and vanilla until thick and smooth.
Spoon over the bases, smooth the tops and chill until firm.
Top with the mango, and scatter with the coconut just before serving.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Plus 4 hours chilling.
Storage: keeps 2 days covered in the fridge.

title: Mini Pavlova Nests
summary: Crisp-shelled, marshmallow-centred meringue nests with cream and berries.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 120°C fan (140°C conventional). Line two trays with baking paper.
Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks, then add the sugar a spoonful at a time and whisk for 8 minutes until thick, glossy and no longer gritty when rubbed between fingers.
Fold in the cornflour, vinegar and vanilla. Spoon 12 mounds onto the trays and make a well in the centre of each.
Bake for 70 to 75 minutes until dry and crisp on the outside. Turn off the oven and cool inside with the door ajar.
Whip the cream with the icing sugar, fill the nests and top with the berries just before serving.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Gluten-free if you use cornflour labelled gluten-free.
Storage: store unfilled nests in an airtight tin for 3 days; fill just before serving.

title: Chocolate Pots de Creme
summary: Baked chocolate custards in small pots, smooth and fudgy.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional). Place six 100ml ramekins in a deep baking dish.
Heat the cream and milk until steaming and pour over the broken chocolate. Stand for 2 minutes, then stir until smooth.
Whisk the yolks, sugar, vanilla and salt, then slowly whisk in the chocolate mixture.
Strain into a jug, pour into the ramekins and pour hot water into the dish to halfway up the sides.
Bake for 28 to 30 minutes until set at the edges with a slight wobble in the middle, then cool and chill.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Food safety: bake until the custard is set with no liquid centre, reaching 75°C in the middle.
Plus 3 hours chilling.
Storage: keeps 3 days covered in the fridge.

title: Poached Pear Cups
summary: Pears gently poached in spiced apple juice and served with yoghurt.

steps.text: Combine the apple juice, cinnamon, honey and lemon zest in a pan and bring to a gentle simmer until the honey dissolves.
Add the pears and poach for 20 to 25 minutes, turning once, until a knife slides in easily.
Lift out the pears and boil the liquid for 8 minutes until reduced to a syrup.
Slice each pear half and divide between 6 cups with the yoghurt, drizzle with syrup and scatter with the walnuts.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains nuts.
Storage: pears keep 3 days in their syrup in the fridge.

title: Self-Saucing Chocolate Pudding Cups
summary: Soft chocolate puddings that make their own sauce as they bake.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Grease eight 150ml ramekins.
Whisk the flour, 30g cocoa and caster sugar, then whisk in the milk, butter and egg until smooth.
Divide between the ramekins. Mix the brown sugar and remaining cocoa, sprinkle over the batter, then pour 2 tbsp of the boiling water over each until the sugar is covered.
Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until the tops are set and springy.
Stand for 3 minutes and serve with the sauce at the base.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 pudding.
Storage: best eaten straight from the oven.

title: Steamed Golden Syrup Puddings
summary: Small steamed sponge puddings with golden syrup running down the sides.

steps.text: Grease six 150ml pudding moulds and spoon 2 tsp golden syrup into the base of each.
Beat the butter and sugar for 3 minutes until pale. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then fold in the flour, milk and zest.
Divide between the moulds, cover each tightly with foil and place in a deep pan with boiling water to halfway up the sides.
Cover the pan and steam gently for 40 to 45 minutes until risen and a skewer comes out clean, topping up the water if needed.
Turn out and serve with the remaining syrup warmed.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 pudding.
Storage: best eaten warm; reheat for 30 seconds in the microwave.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Orange Cardamom Rice Pudding Cups
summary: Creamy rice pudding cooked on the hob scented with cardamom and orange, served warm or cold.

steps.text: Rinse the rice, then combine with the milk, coconut milk, sugar, cardamom and zest in a saucepan.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 30 to 35 minutes, stirring often, until the rice is very soft and the pudding is thick and creamy.
Remove the cardamom pods, spoon into 6 cups and scatter with the pistachios.
Serve warm or chill until cold.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Contains nuts.
Storage: keeps 3 days covered in the fridge; stir in a splash of milk when reheating.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Pineapple Buns
summary: Soft milky buns with a sweet, crackled cookie crust, the Hong Kong bakery classic (no pineapple inside).

steps.text: Mix the bread flour, caster sugar, yeast and salt, then add the warm milk, egg and 40g butter. Knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Cover and let it double.
For the topping, beat the 60g butter and icing sugar until pale, mix in the yolk, then fold in the plain flour to a soft dough. Roll into a log, wrap and chill.
Divide the risen dough into 8 balls, shape them smooth and set on a lined tray 5cm apart. Cover and prove until puffy and nearly doubled.
Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Slice the topping dough into 8 discs, flatten each to 8cm and drape over a bun. Score a light crisscross with a knife and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until the tops are deep golden and the buns sound hollow when tapped underneath. Cool on a rack for 10 minutes.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 bun. Plus about 2 hours proving and chilling.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake the buns until fully cooked through; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: best the day they are baked; keep covered for 2 days or freeze for 1 month and warm for 8 minutes at 150°C fan.

title: Melon Pan
summary: Fluffy sweet buns wrapped in a thin crisp cookie shell scored to look like a melon.

steps.text: Mix the bread flour, 45g sugar, yeast and salt, then add the warm milk, egg and 40g butter. Knead for 10 minutes until smooth, cover and let it double.
For the crust, beat the 60g butter and 60g sugar until pale, mix in the yolk and vanilla, then fold in the plain flour and baking powder. Chill, then divide into 8 balls.
Divide the risen dough into 8 balls. Flatten each crust ball to an 8cm disc between baking paper, press a bun into it and wrap so the dough is covered on the top and sides.
Dip the tops in the coating sugar, score a diamond pattern with a knife and set on a lined tray 5cm apart. Cover and prove until puffy.
Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Bake for 16 to 18 minutes until the crust is pale gold and cracked in places and the buns sound hollow underneath. Cool on a rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 bun. Plus about 1 hour 45 minutes proving and chilling.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake the buns until fully cooked through; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: best the day they are baked; keep covered for 2 days or freeze for 1 month.

title: Hotteok
summary: Chewy yeasted pancakes stuffed with a melting cinnamon, brown sugar and walnut filling.

steps.text: Stir the flour, caster sugar, yeast and salt together, add the warm milk and 1 tbsp oil and mix to a sticky dough. Cover and let it double.
Stir the brown sugar, cinnamon, walnuts and sesame seeds together in a bowl until evenly combined.
Using damp hands, divide the dough into 8 balls. Flatten each ball in your palm, put 2 tbsp of the filling in the middle and pinch the edges closed.

Heat a little oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat. Place a ball seam side down and press flat to 10cm with an oiled spatula. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes per side until deep golden and the sugar inside has melted.
Cool for 3 minutes before eating, as the filling is very hot.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 hotteok. Plus about 1 hour proving.
Contains tree nuts (walnuts) and sesame.
Storage: best eaten warm; keep covered for 1 day and reheat in a dry pan for 2 minutes per side.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Dorayaki
summary: Fluffy honey pancakes sandwiched around sweet red bean paste.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs, sugar and honey for 3 minutes until pale and thick. Sift in the flour and bicarbonate of soda, add the water and fold to a smooth batter.
Heat a non-stick frying pan over low heat and wipe with a little oil. Pour 2 tbsp of batter into a 7cm round and cook for 2 minutes until bubbles appear and the surface looks dry.
Flip and cook for 30 seconds until pale gold. Stack the pancakes under a clean tea towel to keep them soft and make 16 in total.
For the filling, mash the beans with the 70g sugar and simmer for 8 minutes, stirring, until thick and jammy. Cool.
Spread 1 tbsp of the bean paste on a pancake, top with a second and press gently.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 sandwich (2 pancakes). Plus 10 minutes resting the batter.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and cook each pancake until the centre is set and no longer wet; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keeps 2 days in an airtight container; the pancakes freeze well for 1 month.

title: Kuih Bahulu
summary: Tiny sponge cakes with a crisp edge and soft eggy middle, baked in a mini muffin tin.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Brush two 12-hole mini muffin tins well with oil and heat them in the oven for 5 minutes.
Whisk the eggs and sugar with an electric whisk for 8 minutes until pale, thick and tripled, with a ribbon trail.
Sift in the flour and baking powder, add the vanilla and melted butter and fold gently until just combined.
Spoon the batter into the hot tin holes until three-quarters full. Bake for 12 to 14 minutes until risen, golden and springy to the touch. Turn out onto a rack and repeat with any remaining batter.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 cakes (makes 24).
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake the cakes until fully set in the middle; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: best the day they are baked; keep airtight for 3 days.

title: Kuih Keria
summary: Sweet potato doughnuts fried until crisp and rolled in a sandy sugar coating.

items.raw: 500g orange sweet potato, peeled and cubed

steps.text: Boil the sweet potato for 15 minutes until very tender, drain well and mash until smooth. Mix with the flour and salt into a soft dough and shape into 24 rings, about 5cm wide, with a hole in the middle.
Heat the oil in a deep heavy pot to 170°C. Fry the rings in batches of 5 for 3 to 4 minutes, turning once, until golden brown and crisp. Drain on paper towel.
Boil the sugar and water for 3 minutes until it turns thick and begins to crystallise on the spoon. Take it off the heat, toss in the doughnuts and stir until coated in a dry sandy sugar.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 3 doughnuts. Plus 10 minutes cooling before shaping.
Deep-frying safety: use a deep, heavy pot no more than one-third full, never leave hot oil unattended, keep a lid nearby and never put water on an oil fire. Let the oil cool fully before moving it.
Storage: best the day they are made; keep airtight for 1 day.

title: Onde-Onde Sweet Potato Balls
summary: Chewy sweet potato balls with a palm sugar centre, rolled in salted coconut.

items.raw: 250g orange sweet potato, peeled and cubed

steps.text: Boil the sweet potato for 15 minutes until very tender, drain and mash smooth. Work in the rice flour, salt and water to a soft dough that does not stick to your hands.
Roll into 24 balls the size of a walnut. Press a hollow into each, put in a pinch of palm sugar and seal.
Bring a large pot of water to the boil. Cook the balls in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until they float, then 1 minute more. Lift out with a slotted spoon.
Toss the warm balls in the coconut mixed with the 1/4 tsp salt and serve right away.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 3 balls. Plus 10 minutes cooling.
Storage: best eaten warm on the day; the palm sugar centre will be hot when freshly cooked.

title: Bibingka Muffin Cups
summary: Soft rice flour cakes with coconut milk, baked golden and finished with butter, sugar and coconut.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and grease a 12-hole muffin tin.
Whisk the rice flour, baking powder and 100g sugar. Beat the eggs with the coconut milk and 60g melted butter, then mix into the dry ingredients to a smooth batter and stir in the mozzarella.
Fill the holes two-thirds full and bake for 20 minutes until the tops are set and the edges are golden.
Brush with the extra melted butter, sprinkle with the 1 tbsp sugar and coconut and grill for 2 minutes until the coconut turns golden. Cool for 5 minutes before turning out.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 cakes (makes 12).
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake until set in the middle with a clean skewer; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: best warm on the day; keep covered for 1 day.

title: Castella Cubes
summary: A honey-sweet Japanese sponge cake with a fine soft crumb, cut into neat cubes.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional). Grease a 15cm square tin and line it with baking paper.
Beat the eggs and sugar with an electric whisk for 10 minutes until pale, thick and the ribbon holds for 5 seconds. Warm the honey and milk together and fold in.
Sift in the flour in three batches and fold gently until just combined. Pour into the tin and tap it on the bench to remove large bubbles.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the top is deep golden and a skewer comes out clean. Turn out, peel off the paper and cool wrapped in baking paper. Cut into 16 cubes.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 cubes.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake until the centre is fully set; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep wrapped for 3 days; the flavour is best the day after baking.

title: Yakgwa
summary: Crisp-edged honey ginger cookies fried and soaked in a fragrant syrup.

steps.text: Rub the flour, sesame oil and salt together until sandy, add the hot water and bring to a firm dough without kneading. Roll to 1cm thick and cut into 20 diamonds.
Poke a few holes in each with a fork. Heat the oil in a deep heavy pot to 150°C and fry the cookies in batches for 6 to 8 minutes until deep golden, turning now and then. Drain on paper towel.
Simmer the honey, water, ginger and cinnamon for 5 minutes until slightly thickened. Soak the warm cookies in the syrup for 10 minutes, then lift onto a rack to drain.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 cookies. Plus 10 minutes soaking.
Contains sesame.
Deep-frying safety: use a deep, heavy pot no more than one-third full, never leave hot oil unattended, keep a lid nearby and never put water on an oil fire.
Storage: keeps 3 days in an airtight container.

title: Spiced Puff-Puff Dough Balls
summary: Soft, pillowy fried dough balls, lightly sweet and spiced with nutmeg.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt and nutmeg, then stir in the warm water to a thick, stretchy batter. Cover and let it rise until doubled and bubbly.
Heat the oil in a deep heavy pot to 175°C. Drop in walnut-sized scoops of batter with a wet spoon in batches of 6 to 8.
Fry for 4 to 5 minutes, turning, until deep golden and puffed. Drain on paper towel and serve warm.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 4 balls (makes about 32). Plus about 1 hour rising.

Deep-frying safety: use a deep heavy pot no more than one-third full, never leave hot oil unattended, keep a lid nearby and never put water on an oil fire. Let the oil cool completely before moving it.
Storage: best eaten the same day.

title: Syrup-Soaked Plaited Doughnuts
summary: Plaited fried dough dunked in ice-cold syrup to give a crackling shell and sticky centre.

steps.text: Make the syrup first: boil the 300g sugar, water, ginger and lemon juice for 8 minutes, then chill until ice cold.

Rub the butter into the flour, baking powder and 1 tbsp sugar. Mix the egg and milk, stir in and knead to a soft dough. Rest, then roll to 1cm thick and cut into 8 strips of 3 plaits each, pinching the ends together.
Heat the oil in a deep heavy pot to 175°C. Fry the plaits in batches for 3 to 4 minutes, turning once, until deep golden brown.
Lift each hot koeksister straight into the cold syrup for 1 minute, turn, then drain on a rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 koeksister. Plus 2 hours chilling the syrup and 30 minutes resting.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and fry until the dough is cooked through; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Deep-frying safety: use a deep heavy pot no more than one-third full, never leave hot oil unattended, keep a lid nearby and never put water on an oil fire.
Storage: keeps 3 days in an airtight container in the fridge.

title: Mandazi
summary: Lightly sweet, cardamom-scented coconut doughnut triangles, a staple of East African tea breaks.

steps.text: Mix the flour, sugar, baking powder and cardamom. Beat the egg with the coconut milk, stir in and knead briefly into a soft dough. Cover and rest.
Roll to 1cm thick, cut into 8 squares and cut each in half diagonally to make 16 triangles, then halve again if you like smaller pieces.
Heat the oil in a deep heavy pot to 175°C. Fry in batches for 2 to 3 minutes per side until puffed and golden brown. Drain on paper towel.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 3 pieces (makes 24). Plus 20 minutes resting.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and fry until the dough is cooked through and golden; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Deep-frying safety: use a deep heavy pot no more than one-third full, never leave hot oil unattended, keep a lid nearby and never put water on an oil fire.
Storage: best the day they are made; keep airtight for 2 days.

title: Vetkoek with Apricot Jam
summary: Golden fried bread balls, crisp outside and soft inside, filled with apricot jam.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the warm water and knead for 5 minutes into a soft sticky dough. Cover and let it double.
Divide into 8 balls and flatten slightly.
Heat the oil in a deep heavy pot to 170°C. Fry 3 at a time for 8 to 10 minutes, turning often, until deep golden and cooked through when you tear one open.
Drain, split each open and fill with 1 tsp jam.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 1 vetkoek. Plus about 1 hour rising.

Deep-frying safety: use a deep heavy pot no more than one-third full, never leave hot oil unattended, keep a lid nearby and never put water on an oil fire. Let the oil cool completely before moving it.
Storage: best fresh; keep covered for 1 day.

title: Melktert Cups
summary: Mini sweet pastry cups filled with a cinnamon milk custard, a South African favourite.

steps.text: Rub the 75g butter into the flour and icing sugar, add the yolk and water and bring to a dough. Wrap and chill, then roll and cut 12 rounds to fit a 12-hole muffin tin, pressing them in.

Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Simmer 300ml milk with the cinnamon stick for 5 minutes, then remove the stick. Whisk the cornflour, sugar, egg and remaining milk in a bowl, pour in the hot milk, return to the pan and stir for 3 minutes until thick. Stir in the 15g butter and vanilla.
Spoon the custard into the pastry cases and bake for 18 to 20 minutes until the pastry is golden and the custard just set.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, dust with cinnamon and lift out.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 cup. Plus about 30 minutes chilling the pastry.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs; cook the custard until thick and bake until just set. Keep refrigerated; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep refrigerated for 2 days and eat within that time.

title: Hertzoggies
summary: Jam-filled pastry cups with a golden coconut meringue topping.

steps.text: Rub the butter into the flour and icing sugar, add the yolk and water and bring to a dough. Chill, then roll and cut 12 rounds to fit a 12-hole muffin tin, pressing them in.
Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Spoon 1 tsp jam into each case.
Whisk the whites to soft peaks, add the sugar a spoonful at a time and beat for 4 minutes until stiff and glossy. Fold in the coconut and spoon over the jam.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the topping is golden and the pastry is cooked underneath. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 cup. Plus about 30 minutes chilling the pastry.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake the meringue until firm and dry; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep airtight for 4 days.

title: Soetkoekies
summary: Old-fashioned spiced sweet biscuits with ginger, cinnamon and nutmeg.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line two trays.
Beat the butter and sugar for 3 minutes until pale, then beat in the egg. Stir in the flour, spices, baking powder and milk to a soft dough.
Roll into 20 balls, set 4cm apart on the trays and flatten with a fork.
Bake for 13 to 15 minutes until golden at the edges but still soft in the middle. Cool on the trays for 5 minutes, then on a rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 biscuits.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake until set; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep airtight for 1 week.

title: Mahamri
summary: Soft cardamom and coconut fried bread triangles from the Swahili coast.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, cardamom and salt, add the coconut milk and warm water and knead for 5 minutes into a soft dough. Cover and let it double.
Roll to 1cm thick, cut into 6 squares, halve each diagonally and cut again to make 12 triangles.
Heat the oil in a deep heavy pot to 175°C. Fry in batches for 2 to 3 minutes per side until puffed and golden. Drain on paper towel.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 2 triangles. Plus about 1 hour rising.
Deep-frying safety: use a deep heavy pot no more than one-third full, never leave hot oil unattended, keep a lid nearby and never put water on an oil fire.
Storage: best the day they are made.

title: Luqaimat
summary: Crisp golden fried dumplings drizzled with honey, a Gulf Ramadan favourite.

steps.text: Mix the flour, cornflour, yeast, sugar and cardamom, add the warm water and beat for 2 minutes to a thick sticky batter. Cover and let it rise until bubbly.
Heat the oil in a deep heavy pot to 175°C. Drop in small spoonfuls of batter, using a wet spoon, in batches of 8.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until crisp and deep golden. Drain on paper towel and drizzle with honey.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 5 dumplings (makes about 40). Plus about 1 hour rising.
Deep-frying safety: use a deep heavy pot no more than one-third full, never leave hot oil unattended, keep a lid nearby and never put water on an oil fire.
Storage: best eaten within an hour of frying.

title: Qatayef with Ricotta and Pistachio
summary: Folded yeast pancakes filled with sweet ricotta, baked and brushed with lemon syrup.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, semolina, sugar, yeast, baking powder and warm water into a smooth thin batter. Cover and let it rest.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat. Pour in 2 tbsp batter for each 10cm pancake and cook one side only for 1 to 2 minutes until bubbles appear and the top is dry. Make 12 and cool on a tea towel.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional). Mix the ricotta and honey, spoon onto the cooked side of each pancake, fold over and pinch the edge closed.
Brush with melted butter and bake on a lined tray for 8 to 10 minutes until golden.
Boil the syrup sugar, water and lemon juice for 5 minutes and brush a little over the hot qatayef. Top with pistachios.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 qatayef. Plus 30 minutes resting the batter.
Contains tree nuts (pistachios).
Storage: best warm on the day; keep refrigerated for 1 day.

title: Barazek Sesame Pistachio Cookies
summary: Thin, crisp Syrian sesame cookies glazed in honey and covered with toasted seeds and pistachios.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line two trays.
Beat the butter and sugar until pale, beat in the egg, then stir in the flour, baking powder and milk to a soft dough. Roll into 16 balls.
Warm the honey, dip the top of each ball, then press into the mixed sesame seeds and pistachios. Flatten to 6cm discs, seed side up, on the trays.
Bake for 13 to 15 minutes until golden at the edges. Cool on the trays.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 cookies. Contains sesame and tree nuts (pistachios).
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake until set; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep airtight for 1 week.

title: Kuli-Kuli Spiced Peanut Sticks
summary: Crunchy baked peanut sticks with ginger, paprika and chilli, inspired by Nigerian kuli-kuli.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional) and line a tray.
Blitz the peanuts in a food processor for 1 to 2 minutes into a coarse, oily paste. Mix in the ginger, paprika, chilli, salt and water until it holds together.
Roll into 24 thin sticks, 7cm long, and set on the tray.
Bake for 22 to 25 minutes, turning once, until dry and deep golden. Cool completely so they crisp up.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 3 sticks. Contains peanuts.
Storage: keep airtight for 2 weeks.

title: Nigerian Buns
summary: Dense, nutmeg-scented fried dough balls, crisp outside and soft inside.

steps.text: Mix the flour, sugar, baking powder and nutmeg, rub in the butter, then add the beaten egg and milk and knead briefly into a soft dough. Rest, then roll into 16 balls.
Heat the oil in a deep heavy pot to 170°C. Fry in batches of 5 for 5 to 6 minutes, turning, until deep golden and a ball tears open cooked through.
Drain on paper towel and cool for 5 minutes before eating.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 buns. Plus 15 minutes resting.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and fry until cooked through; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Deep-frying safety: use a deep heavy pot no more than one-third full, never leave hot oil unattended, keep a lid nearby and never put water on an oil fire.
Storage: best the day they are made.

title: Tres Leches Cups
summary: Light vanilla sponge cubes soaked in three milks and topped with whipped cream and cinnamon.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Grease and line a 20cm square tin.
Beat the eggs and sugar with an electric whisk for 8 minutes until pale and thick. Fold in the flour and baking powder, then the 60ml milk and vanilla.
Pour into the tin and bake for 22 to 25 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool for 10 minutes.
Prick the sponge all over with a fork. Mix the condensed milk, evaporated milk and 150ml milk and pour slowly over the sponge until absorbed.
Cut the sponge into 2cm cubes and divide among 8 cups. Whip the cream to soft peaks, spoon on top and dust with cinnamon.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 cup. Plus about 2 hours chilling.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs, bake the sponge until fully set and keep the cups refrigerated; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep refrigerated and eat within 2 days.

title: Conchas
summary: Soft sweet bread rolls topped with a crisp shell-patterned sugar crust.

steps.text: Mix the bread flour, sugar, yeast and salt, add the warm milk, egg and 50g butter and knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Cover and let it double.
Beat the 60g butter and icing sugar until pale, mix in the vanilla and plain flour to a soft dough and divide into 8 balls.
Divide the risen dough into 8 balls and set on a lined tray 5cm apart. Flatten each topping ball to an 8cm disc between baking paper and press one onto each bun.
Score a shell pattern into each top with a knife. Cover and prove until puffy.
Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until the buns sound hollow underneath and the topping is pale gold. Cool on a rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 concha. Plus about 2 hours proving.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake until fully cooked through; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: best the day they are baked; keep covered for 2 days.

title: Cocadas
summary: Chewy baked coconut macaroon mounds with a golden crust.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line a tray.
Stir the coconut, sugar, egg whites, vanilla and salt in a pan over low heat for 3 minutes until the mixture is warm and sticks together.
Scoop 12 mounds with a damp spoon onto the tray, pressing them firmly.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes until the tips and edges are golden brown. Cool on the tray, as they firm up as they cool.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Gluten-free. Per serving: 1 cocada.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake until the mounds are set and golden; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep airtight for 5 days.

title: Colombian Cheese Fritters
summary: Crisp golden balls with a salty cheese centre, inspired by Colombian bunuelos.

steps.text: Mix the feta, cornflour, flour, sugar and baking powder, add the egg and milk and work to a soft dough. Roll into 24 balls the size of a walnut.
Heat the oil in a deep heavy pot to 160°C. Fry in batches of 6 for 5 to 6 minutes, turning, until deep golden and puffed. They should float and a ball should be cooked through when broken open.
Drain on paper towel and serve warm.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 3 fritters.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and fry until the dough is cooked through; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Deep-frying safety: use a deep heavy pot no more than one-third full, never leave hot oil unattended, keep a lid nearby and never put water on an oil fire.
Storage: best fresh; keep refrigerated for 1 day.

title: Marranitos
summary: Soft ginger and brown sugar cookies, a Mexican pan dulce favourite.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line two trays.
Beat the butter, sugar and golden syrup for 3 minutes until fluffy, then beat in the egg. Stir in the flour, spices, baking powder and bicarbonate of soda to a soft dough.
Roll to 1cm thick, cut into 20 shapes with a 6cm cutter and set 3cm apart on the trays.
Bake for 12 to 14 minutes until firm and lightly browned at the edges. Cool on the trays for 5 minutes.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 cookies. Plus 20 minutes chilling the dough.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake until set; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep airtight for 1 week.

title: Chilean Sopaipillas
summary: Golden pumpkin fritters served with a warm cinnamon brown sugar syrup.

steps.text: Mix the pumpkin, flour, baking powder, butter and salt into a soft dough, kneading for 2 minutes. Roll to 5mm thick and cut into 16 rounds with a 7cm cutter, pricking each with a fork.
Simmer the brown sugar, water and cinnamon stick for 8 minutes until slightly thick.
Heat the oil in a deep heavy pot to 175°C. Fry 3 at a time for 2 minutes per side until puffed and golden brown. Drain on paper towel and serve with the warm syrup.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 sopaipillas with syrup. Plus 15 minutes resting the dough.
Deep-frying safety: use a deep heavy pot no more than one-third full, never leave hot oil unattended, keep a lid nearby and never put water on an oil fire.
Storage: best fresh on the day.

title: Mexican Hot Chocolate Biscuits
summary: Tender cocoa shortbread biscuits warmed with cinnamon and a pinch of chilli.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C conventional) and line two trays.
Beat the butter and sugar for 3 minutes until pale, beat in the yolk, then mix in the flour, cocoa, cinnamon, chilli and salt to a firm dough.
Roll to 8mm thick, cut 20 biscuits with a 5cm cutter and set on the trays.
Bake for 11 to 12 minutes until firm at the edges. Cool on the trays for 10 minutes.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 biscuits. Plus 20 minutes chilling.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake until set; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep airtight for 1 week.

title: Quesadilla Salvadorena
summary: A rich, dense Salvadoran cheese cake with sesame seeds, cut into slices.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Grease and line a 20cm round tin.
Beat the butter and sugar for 3 minutes until pale, then beat in the eggs one at a time. Mix in the ricotta, then fold in the rice flour, baking powder and milk until just combined.
Pour into the tin, level the top and scatter with sesame seeds.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tin for 15 minutes, then cut into 12 slices.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Gluten-free if you use gluten-free baking powder. Per serving: 1 slice. Contains sesame.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake until the centre is fully set; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep covered in the fridge for 3 days; bring to room temperature before serving.

title: Calzones Rotos
summary: Chilean fried dough twists with a lemony crunch, dusted in icing sugar.

steps.text: Mix the flour, sugar and baking powder, add the egg, yolk, butter and lemon juice and knead for 3 minutes into a firm dough. Rest, then roll to 3mm thick and cut into 24 diamonds. Make a slit in the middle of each and pull one end through to twist.
Heat the oil in a deep heavy pot to 175°C. Fry in batches for 1 to 2 minutes per side until puffed and golden. Drain on paper towel.
Dust with icing sugar while warm.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 3 twists. Plus 20 minutes resting.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and fry until the dough is cooked through; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Deep-frying safety: use a deep heavy pot no more than one-third full, never leave hot oil unattended, keep a lid nearby and never put water on an oil fire.
Storage: best fresh; keep airtight for 2 days.

title: Pao de Mel Honey Spice Bites
summary: Mini Brazilian honey spice cakes dipped in dark chocolate.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Grease two 12-hole mini muffin tins.
Whisk the honey, sugar, milk, egg and butter, then fold in the flour, cocoa, baking powder and spices until just combined.
Fill the holes two-thirds full and bake for 12 to 14 minutes until risen and springy to the touch. Cool on a rack.
Melt the chocolate in short bursts in the microwave, stirring, then dip the tops of each cake and set on baking paper.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 bites (makes 24). Plus 15 minutes setting the chocolate.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake until set; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep airtight for 4 days.

title: Baked Gyoza Pockets
summary: Crisp-based tofu, mushroom and cabbage dumplings pan-fried then steamed until tender.

steps.text: Mix the flour, hot water and salt into a dough, knead for 5 minutes until smooth, then cover and rest.
Fry the cabbage, mushrooms, ginger and garlic with sesame oil in a dry pan for 5 minutes until the moisture has gone, then mix with the tofu, spring onion and soy. Cool.
Roll the dough thin, cut 24 rounds of 8cm and fill each with 1 tsp filling. Fold and pleat the edges to seal.

Heat the neutral oil in a lidded frying pan over medium heat and arrange the gyoza flat side down. Fry for 2 minutes until the bases are golden, add the water, cover and steam for 5 minutes until the wrappers are translucent and the water has gone.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 4 gyoza. Contains soy. Plus 30 minutes resting the dough.
Storage: keeps 2 days in the fridge; freeze uncooked for 1 month.

title: Chive and Egg Pockets
summary: Golden pan-fried dough pockets stuffed with egg, tofu and spring onion.

steps.text: Mix the flour and hot water into a dough, knead for 5 minutes until smooth, cover and rest.
Beat the eggs with the salt and scramble in a pan for 2 minutes until just set but still moist. Mix with the tofu, spring onions and soy and cool.
Roll the dough thin, cut 12 rounds of 10cm, fill each with 1 tbsp filling, fold in half and pleat the edge closed.
Heat the oil in a lidded frying pan over medium heat and fry the pockets for 3 minutes per side until golden brown and the egg is hot all the way through.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 pockets. Contains soy. Plus 30 minutes resting the dough.
Storage: keeps 1 day refrigerated; reheat until hot all the way through.

Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs, cook the filling until set and heat the pockets through before eating; check the thickest part reaches 75°C. Use fresh, uncracked eggs; for pregnant women, older people, young children and anyone with low immunity, cook the eggs until the yolks are firm.

title: Tuna Karipap Puffs
summary: Flaky baked puffs with a curried tuna and potato filling.

steps.text: Boil the potato for 8 minutes until tender, drain. Fry the onion in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, stir in the curry powder and tomato paste for 1 minute, then mix in the potato and tuna, flaking the fish. Cool.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line two trays.
Cut each pastry sheet into 4 squares, put 1 tbsp filling in the centre of each, fold into a triangle and press the edges with a fork.
Brush with yolk and bake for 20 to 25 minutes until puffed and deep golden. Cool for 5 minutes.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 puffs. Contains fish.
Food safety: use tinned fish within its date and keep the puffs refrigerated within 2 hours of baking; reheat until piping hot all the way through; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep refrigerated for 2 days; reheat in a 180°C fan oven for 8 minutes.

title: Okonomiyaki Muffin Bites
summary: Savoury cabbage and spring onion mini pancakes baked in a muffin tin.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and grease a 24-hole mini muffin tin with the oil.
Whisk the flour, water, eggs and soy into a smooth batter and stir in the cabbage and spring onion.
Spoon into the holes until full and bake for 15 to 18 minutes until risen and golden brown at the edges and set in the middle.
Mix the mayonnaise and tomato sauce, drizzle over the bites and serve warm.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 4 bites. Contains soy.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake until the centre is fully set with no runny egg; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keeps 2 days refrigerated; reheat until hot all the way through.

title: Spring Onion Layered Flatbread Wedges
summary: Flaky layered pan-fried flatbread with spring onion, cut into crisp wedges.

steps.text: Mix the flour, hot water and half the salt into a dough, knead for 5 minutes until smooth, cover and rest.
Divide into 3 balls and roll each into a thin round. Brush with the 3 tbsp oil, sprinkle with the spring onion and remaining salt, roll up into a log, coil into a snail and flatten gently.
Roll each coil out to 18cm, then heat the cooking oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Fry each pancake for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden brown and crisp at the edges with visible layers.
Cut into 6 wedges each and serve warm.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 3 wedges. Plus 30 minutes resting the dough.
Storage: best fresh; reheat in a dry pan.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Mini Pork Baozi
summary: Fluffy steamed buns with a ginger and spring onion pork filling.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and baking powder, add the water and oil and knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and let it double.
Mix the pork, spring onions, ginger, soy and sesame oil until sticky.
Divide the dough into 12 balls, flatten each to 9cm, put 1 tbsp filling in the centre and pleat the edges closed.
Rest the buns on baking paper squares in a steamer, then steam over boiling water for 12 minutes until the buns are puffed and the pork reaches 75°C in the thickest part.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 buns. Contains soy. Plus about 1 hour 30 minutes proving.
Food safety: cook the pork mince until 75°C in the centre of the filling, keep the buns refrigerated within 2 hours of cooking and reheat until piping hot all the way through.
Storage: keep refrigerated for 2 days or freeze for 1 month; steam from frozen for 15 minutes.

title: Pan de Coco Buns
summary: Soft sweet buns filled with a buttery brown sugar and coconut mixture.

steps.text: Mix the bread flour, caster sugar, yeast and salt, add the warm milk, egg and 40g butter and knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Cover and let it double.
Mix the coconut, brown sugar and 40g butter until evenly combined and crumbly.
Divide the dough into 8 balls, flatten each to 10cm, put 2 tbsp filling in the centre and pinch the edges closed. Set seam side down on a lined tray 5cm apart and prove until puffy.
Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until the buns are golden brown and sound hollow when tapped underneath. Cool on a rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 bun. Plus about 2 hours proving.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake until fully cooked through; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: best the day they are baked; keep covered for 2 days.

title: Sweet Potato Toddler Fingers
summary: Soft oat and cheese sweet potato fingers that little hands can hold, baked rather than fried.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray with baking paper. Boil the sweet potato for 12 minutes until very soft, drain and mash smooth.
Mix in the egg, oats, cheese, flour and cumin to a thick, sticky mixture.
With damp hands shape into 18 fingers about 6cm long and 1.5cm thick, set on the tray and brush with the oil.
Bake for 22 to 25 minutes, turning once, until golden and firm. Cool until just warm.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 3 fingers. Toddler snack.
Choking hazard: always sit toddlers down to eat and supervise them; serve soft and cooled, and break fingers into smaller pieces for babies under 12 months.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake until the fingers are firm all the way through; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep refrigerated for 2 days or freeze for 1 month.

title: Veggie Pancake Strips
summary: Soft zucchini and carrot pancakes cut into finger-sized strips.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, egg and milk into a smooth batter and stir in the zucchini and carrot.
Heat a little of the oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat. Pour in a sixth of the batter to make a 12cm pancake and cook for 2 minutes until bubbles appear and the underside is golden.
Flip and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until golden and set in the middle. Repeat to make 6 pancakes, then cut into strips.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 pancake in strips. Toddler snack.
Choking hazard: cut into thin strips for toddlers, seat them to eat and supervise them.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and cook until no wet batter remains; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep refrigerated for 2 days; reheat until warm.

title: Apple Oat Toddler Biscuits
summary: Soft biscuits sweetened only with apple, with no added sugar.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and line two trays.
Mix the oats, flour, cinnamon and baking powder, then stir in the apple, egg and melted butter to a soft dough.
Roll into 20 balls, set 3cm apart on the trays and flatten to 1cm thick.
Bake for 16 to 18 minutes until golden and firm. Cool on the tray.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 biscuits. Toddler snack.
Choking hazard: seat toddlers to eat and supervise them; break biscuits up for younger children.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake until firm; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep airtight for 3 days.

title: Cheesy Broccoli Bites
summary: Little baked egg and cheese bites with hidden broccoli.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and grease a 12-hole mini muffin tin.
Mix the broccoli, cheese, eggs and breadcrumbs.
Spoon into the holes, pressing down, and bake for 18 to 20 minutes until golden on top and set in the middle. Cool in the tin for 5 minutes.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 2 bites. Toddler snack.
Choking hazard: chop broccoli very finely, seat toddlers to eat and supervise them; cut bites in half for young toddlers.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake until the centre is firm with no runny egg; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep refrigerated for 2 days.

title: Pea and Mint Fritters
summary: Soft green fritters with a mild cheese flavour, cooked in a little oil.

steps.text: Mash the peas roughly. Stir in the flour, egg, milk, cheese and mint to a thick batter.

Heat a little oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat. Drop in tablespoons of batter, flatten slightly and cook for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden and set in the middle. Make 18 fritters.
Drain on paper towel and cool until just warm.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 3 fritters. Toddler snack.
Choking hazard: mash peas well, seat toddlers to eat and supervise them; halve fritters for young toddlers.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and cook until the middle is set; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep refrigerated for 2 days.

title: Soft Pikelet Fingers
summary: Fluffy pikelets cut into fingers, lightly buttered for small hands.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, egg, milk and sugar into a smooth batter.

Melt a little butter in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat. Drop in tablespoons of batter and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until bubbles appear, then flip and cook for 1 minute until golden. Make 16 and cool.
Cut each pikelet into 2 fingers to serve.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 pikelets. Toddler snack.
Choking hazard: seat toddlers to eat and supervise them; skip thick spreads and cut up for younger children.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and cook until no wet batter remains; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep airtight for 1 day or freeze for 1 month.

title: Carrot Toddler Muffins
summary: Mini muffins sweetened with carrot and apple, with no added sugar.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and grease two 12-hole mini muffin tins.
Mix the flour and cinnamon, stir in the carrot and apple, then add the egg, milk and oil and fold until just combined.
Fill 24 holes two-thirds full and bake for 13 to 15 minutes until risen and a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tin for 5 minutes.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 mini muffins. Toddler snack.
Choking hazard: seat toddlers to eat and supervise them; break muffins up for younger children.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake until the centre is set; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep airtight for 2 days or freeze for 1 month.

title: Mini Frittata Toddler Squares
summary: Soft baked egg squares with zucchini, peas and cheese, cut for finger food.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Brush a 20cm square tin with the oil and line it with baking paper.
Whisk the eggs and milk, then stir in the zucchini, peas and cheese.
Pour into the tin and bake for 18 to 20 minutes until set in the centre and lightly golden. Cool for 10 minutes and cut into 24 squares.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 3 squares. Toddler snack.
Choking hazard: mash the peas lightly, seat toddlers to eat and supervise them; halve squares for young toddlers.
Food safety: bake until the egg is firm all the way through with no runny egg, cool quickly and keep refrigerated for up to 2 days; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep refrigerated for 2 days.

title: Zucchini Cheese Toddler Fingers
summary: Soft baked zucchini and cheese fingers with a golden crust.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray.
Mix the zucchini, egg, breadcrumbs and cheese to a firm mixture.
Shape into 18 fingers 6cm long, set on the tray and brush with the oil.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, turning once, until golden and firm.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 3 fingers. Toddler snack.
Choking hazard: seat toddlers to eat and supervise them; break fingers into smaller pieces for younger children.
Food safety: use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs and bake until firm all the way through; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep refrigerated for 2 days.

title: Hiking Trail Mix Bars
summary: Chewy oat, nut and seed bars packed with slow energy for the track.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional). Line a 20cm square tin.
Mix the oats, nuts, sultanas and seeds. Warm the honey, peanut butter and coconut oil together and stir into the dry mix until well coated.
Press very firmly into the tin and bake for 22 to 25 minutes until golden at the edges and set.
Cool completely in the tin before cutting into 12 bars.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 bar. Contains peanuts and tree nuts. Plus 1 hour cooling.
Storage: wrap individually for hiking; keeps 2 weeks.

title: Honey Oat Energy Balls
summary: No-bake oat, peanut butter and honey balls for the daypack.

steps.text: Mix everything in a bowl until the mixture holds together when squeezed.
Roll into 16 balls the size of a walnut.
Chill in the fridge until firm to the touch.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 balls. Contains peanuts. Plus 30 minutes chilling.
Storage: keep refrigerated for 1 week; packed in a cool bag they hold for a day's hike.

title: Puffed Rice Sports Bars
summary: Crunchy honey and peanut butter bars that give a quick carbohydrate hit before or during exercise.

steps.text: Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Warm the honey and peanut butter in a pan over low heat for 2 minutes until runny and smooth.
Stir through the puffed rice, oats and seeds until evenly coated, then press very firmly into the tin.
Chill until firm, then cut into 12 bars.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 bar. Contains peanuts. Plus 1 hour chilling.
Storage: keep airtight for 1 week.

title: Savoury Rice and Cheese Recovery Slice
summary: A baked rice, egg and vegetable slice with protein and carbohydrate for after training.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Grease and line a 20cm square tin with the oil.
Beat the eggs, then mix in the rice, cheese, zucchini, carrot, corn and spring onions.
Press into the tin and bake for 28 to 30 minutes until golden and firm in the middle. Cool for 10 minutes and cut into 8 slices.

notes: Snack. Per serving: 1 slice.

Food safety: cool cooked rice within 1 hour and keep it refrigerated; use fresh, clean, uncracked eggs, bake until the middle is firm and reheat leftovers until piping hot; check the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Storage: keep refrigerated for 2 days.

title: Homemade Grissini
summary: Long thin crisp breadsticks made with olive oil and a little sesame.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast and salt, add the oil and warm water and knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and let it rise until doubled.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line two trays.
Roll the dough to a 20cm by 30cm rectangle and cut into 20 strips. Stretch each to 30cm, set on the trays and sprinkle with sesame.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp when snapped. Cool on a rack.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 2 grissini. Contains sesame. Plus about 1 hour rising.
Storage: keep airtight for 1 week.

title: Sesame Simit Sticks
summary: Crisp-chewy sesame-coated bread sticks inspired by Turkish simit.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast and salt, add the oil, honey and warm water and knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and let it rise until doubled.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line two trays.
Divide into 16 pieces, roll each into a 20cm stick and roll in the sesame seeds.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until golden and crisp on the outside. Cool on a rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 sticks. Contains sesame. Plus about 1 hour rising.
Storage: keep airtight for 3 days.

title: Olive Oil Cracker Crisps
summary: Thin crisp crackers with oregano and flaky salt.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line two trays.
Mix the flour, salt and oregano, then add the oil and water to a firm dough and knead for 2 minutes.
Roll as thin as possible, cut into 32 rectangles and prick with a fork.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until golden at the edges and crisp when cooled. Cool on a rack.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 4 crackers. Plus 15 minutes resting the dough.
Storage: keep airtight for 1 week.

title: Wholemeal Za'atar Crackers
summary: Crisp wholemeal crackers with thyme, sesame and sumac.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line two trays.
Mix the flours, salt, thyme, sesame and sumac, then add the oil and water to a firm dough.
Roll as thin as possible, cut into 32 squares and prick with a fork.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until crisp and golden at the edges. Cool on a rack.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 4 crackers. Contains sesame. Plus 15 minutes resting the dough.
Storage: keep airtight for 1 week.

title: Soft Bavarian Pretzel Sticks
summary: Chewy pretzel sticks with a deep brown skin, dipped in a bicarbonate bath before baking.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the warm water and butter and knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and let it rise until doubled.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line two trays. Divide the dough into 20 pieces and roll each into a 15cm stick.
Bring the water and bicarbonate of soda to the boil. Lower in a few sticks at a time for 20 seconds each until they puff slightly, lift out with a slotted spoon and drain.
Set on the trays, sprinkle with flaky salt and bake for 12 to 15 minutes until deep brown and firm.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 sticks. Plus about 1 hour rising.
Use care with the boiling bicarbonate bath: it can splash and should not be touched while hot.
Storage: best the day they are baked.

title: Garlic Bread Chips
summary: Thin crisp bread squares baked with olive oil, garlic and oregano.

items.raw: 8 slices day-old white bread, cut into 3cm squares

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150°C fan (170°C conventional) and line two trays.
Toss the bread squares with the oil, garlic powder, oregano and salt.
Spread in a single layer and bake for 12 to 15 minutes, turning once, until dry, golden and crisp. Cool on the trays.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: about 20 chips.
Storage: keep airtight for 1 week.

title: Paprika Pitta Chips
summary: Crisp pitta triangles with smoked paprika, ideal for dips.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line two trays.
Split each pitta into 2 rounds, brush with the oil and sprinkle with paprika and salt. Cut each round into 6 triangles.
Bake for 8 to 12 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp. Cool completely.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 1 pitta (12 pieces).
Storage: keep airtight for 1 week.

title: Parmesan Crisps
summary: Crisp lacy cheese rounds with black pepper, high in protein and low in carbohydrate.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray with baking paper.
Mix the cheese, pepper and rosemary and spoon 24 small mounds onto the tray, 3cm apart, flattening each slightly.
Bake for 5 to 6 minutes until lacy and golden brown at the edges. Cool on the tray to crisp.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Gluten-free. Per serving: 4 crisps.
Storage: keep airtight for 2 days.

title: Fennel Taralli
summary: Crunchy Puglian ring snacks with fennel seeds, boiled and then baked.

steps.text: Mix the flour, fennel and salt, add the oil and water and knead for 5 minutes into a smooth dough. Rest, then roll into 24 ropes of 10cm and join the ends to make rings.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line two trays. Boil the rings in batches in a pan of water for 1 to 2 minutes until they float, then drain on a tea towel.
Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until golden and crisp. Cool on a rack.

notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 3 taralli. Plus 30 minutes resting the dough.
Storage: keep airtight for 2 weeks.

title: Rosemary Polenta Crackers
summary: Crumbly buttery crackers with a corn crunch and rosemary.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line two trays.
Rub the butter into the polenta, flour, salt and rosemary, then add the water to a firm dough.
Roll to 3mm thick, cut 24 rectangles and prick with a fork.
Bake for 13 to 15 minutes until golden at the edges and firm. Cool on a rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 3 crackers.
Storage: keep airtight for 1 week.

title: Chilli Cheese Crackers
summary: Crisp buttery cheese crackers with a hint of chilli and smoked paprika.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line two trays.
Rub the butter into the flour, then mix in the cheese, chilli and paprika and add the water to a firm dough.
Roll to 3mm thick and cut 30 rounds with a 4cm cutter.
Bake for 12 to 14 minutes until golden and crisp at the edges. Cool on a rack.

notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 3 crackers. Plus 30 minutes chilling the dough.
Storage: keep airtight for 5 days.

title: Ricotta and Honey Toast with Roasted Figs and Pistachios
summary: Thick sourdough toast spread with whipped ricotta, drizzled with honey and topped with pistachios.

steps.text: Toast the sourdough until golden and crisp at the edges.
Whisk the ricotta with the lemon zest and salt until smooth and fluffy.
Brush the toast with the oil, then spread thickly with the ricotta.
Drizzle with the honey and scatter over the pistachios.

notes: Swap the honey for maple syrup if you prefer.

title: Congee-Style Oat Porridge with Soy Egg and Spring Onion
summary: Savoury oats cooked in stock, topped with a jammy egg, soy and crisp shallots.

steps.text: Bring the stock and ginger to a simmer in a saucepan until steaming.
Stir in the oats and cook for 8 minutes, until thick and creamy.
Meanwhile boil the eggs for 6.5 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks jammy, then cool in cold water and peel.
Spoon the porridge into bowls and halve the eggs on top.
Finish with the soy, sesame oil, spring onion and fried shallots.

notes: Food safety: boil the eggs until the whites are fully set. Cook the yolks through if serving anyone vulnerable.
Use vegetable stock for a vegetarian version.

title: Dosa-Style Chickpea Flour Pancakes with Coconut Chutney
summary: Crisp savoury pancakes from chickpea flour and spices, served with a fresh coconut chutney.

steps.text: Whisk the chickpea flour, water, cumin, turmeric and a pinch of salt into a smooth batter, then stir in the chilli, onion and coriander.
Blitz the coconut, yoghurt and 3 tbsp water until smooth for the chutney, then season with salt.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat with a little oil. Pour in a ladle of batter and spread thin.
Cook for 2 minutes, until the underside is golden, then flip and cook for 1 minute more until set.
Fry the mustard seeds in a teaspoon of oil until they pop and spoon over the chutney. Serve the pancakes hot.

notes: Vegan if you use a plant-based yoghurt.

title: Bubble and Squeak Cakes with Poached Egg and Brown Sauce
summary: Crisp patties of leftover potato and cabbage topped with a runny egg.

steps.text: Fry the onion and cabbage in half the butter until soft and lightly coloured.
Mix with the mashed potato, flour, worcestershire sauce and seasoning, then shape into 4 patties.
Melt the remaining butter in a frying pan and cook the patties for 4 minutes each side, until deep golden and crisp.
Poach the eggs in barely simmering water for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Serve each cake with a poached egg on top and a spoonful of tangy sauce.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set; cook the yolks through if serving anyone vulnerable.

title: Spinach and Feta Breakfast Burek Rolls
summary: Flaky filo rolls filled with spinach, feta and egg, baked until golden.

items.raw: 300g frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry

steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C. Soften the onion in the oil until translucent, then cool.
Mix the onion with the spinach, feta and one egg, plus pepper.
Layer two filo sheets, brush with butter, and spoon a line of filling along the long edge. Roll up tightly and coil into a spiral on a lined tray. Repeat with the rest.
Beat the second egg and brush over the rolls, then scatter over the seeds.
Bake for 25 minutes, until deep golden and crisp.

notes: Food safety: bake until the egg in the filling is fully set.
Plus 10 minutes cooling before serving.

title: Dill Creme Fraiche Rosti Towers
summary: Crisp grated potato rosti layered with smoked salmon, creme fraiche and dill.

steps.text: Squeeze the grated potato in a clean tea towel until dry, then toss with the flour and a good pinch of salt.
Heat the butter and oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Press the potato into four rounds.
Cook for 8 minutes each side, until deep golden and crisp.
Mix the creme fraiche with the dill and lemon zest.
Top each rosti with creme fraiche, salmon and capers.

notes: Food safety: smoked salmon is ready to eat but keep it chilled until serving; avoid in pregnancy.

title: Oat and Apple Breakfast Cookies
summary: Soft oat cookies sweetened with apple and a little maple syrup, easy to eat on the go.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C and line a tray.
Mix the apple, peanut butter, maple syrup and egg until combined, then stir in the oats, cinnamon, sultanas and baking powder.
Scoop 12 mounds onto the tray and flatten slightly.
Bake for 15 minutes, until golden at the edges and firm to touch.

notes: Dessert-style snack. Keeps 4 days in a sealed container.

title: Tomato and Basil Gazpacho with Sherry Vinegar
summary: A chilled soup of ripe tomatoes, cucumber and capsicum, blitzed until silky.

steps.text: Blitz the tomato, cucumber, capsicum, garlic, bread and basil until completely smooth.
With the blender running, add the oil and vinegar in a slow stream until the soup is glossy.
Season with salt, then pass through a sieve for a silkier texture if you like.
Chill for at least 2 hours until very cold, and drizzle with olive oil to serve.

notes: Plus 2 hours chilling.
Vegan.

title: White Bean and Rosemary Soup with Garlic Oil
summary: A creamy blended cannellini soup finished with a sizzling garlic and rosemary oil.

steps.text: Soften the onion and celery in half the oil until translucent.
Add the beans and stock, then simmer for 15 minutes, until the beans are very soft.
Blend until smooth, loosening with water if too thick, and add the lemon juice.
Warm the remaining oil with the garlic and rosemary until the garlic is just golden.
Ladle the soup into bowls and spoon over the garlic oil.

notes: Vegan and gluten free.
Food safety: Keep any leftover garlic, herb or chilli oil in the fridge and use it within 4 days.

title: Sweet Corn Chowder with Chilli and Lime
summary: A creamy but dairy-free corn soup lifted with fresh lime and a chilli oil finish.

steps.text: Soften the onion with the paprika in a saucepan until fragrant.
Add the potato, two-thirds of the corn and the stock. Simmer for 15 minutes, until the potato is tender.
Blend until smooth, then stir in the coconut milk and the rest of the corn.
Warm through for 3 minutes, then add the lime juice and salt.
Serve topped with the coriander and a drizzle of chilli oil.

notes: Vegan and gluten free.
Food safety: Keep any leftover garlic, herb or chilli oil in the fridge and use it within 4 days.

title: Greek Egg-Lemon Soup with Shredded Chicken
summary: A silky Greek soup thickened with egg and lemon over soft rice.

steps.text: Simmer the chicken, onion, bay leaf and stock gently for 15 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and white in the centre.
Lift out the chicken, shred it, and discard the onion and bay leaf.
Add the rice to the stock and simmer for 12 minutes, until tender.
Whisk the eggs and lemon juice, then slowly whisk in a ladle of hot stock. Stir the mixture back into the pot off the heat, until the soup turns pale and slightly thickened.
Return the chicken and stir in the dill.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C in the centre and avoid boiling the soup after adding the egg.

title: Pumpkin and Ginger Soup with Toasted Pepitas
summary: A smooth roasted pumpkin soup with warm ginger and crunchy pumpkin seeds.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C. Toss the pumpkin and onion in the oil and roast for 30 minutes, until soft and caramelised.
Cook the ginger in a saucepan for 1 minute, add the roast vegetables and stock, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Blend until smooth and stir through most of the coconut cream.
Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan until they pop.
Serve with a swirl of cream and the seeds.

notes: Vegan and gluten free.

title: Miso Mushroom Soup with Soba and Spinach
summary: A savoury miso broth with mushrooms, buckwheat noodles and wilted spinach.

steps.text: Simmer the stock and mushrooms for 6 minutes, until the mushrooms are tender.
Cook the soba in boiling water for 4 minutes, until tender, then drain and rinse.
Whisk the miso with a ladle of hot stock until smooth and stir back into the pot with the soy sauce. Do not boil.
Divide the noodles and spinach between bowls and ladle over the soup.
Finish with the spring onion and sesame oil.

notes: Check the soba label if you need it gluten free; many contain wheat.
Vegan.

title: Spicy Peanut and Sweet Potato Soup
summary: A West African inspired soup of sweet potato, tomato and peanut butter with ginger and chilli.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the oil until translucent, then stir in the garlic, ginger and chilli for 1 minute.
Add the sweet potato, tomatoes and stock. Simmer for 20 minutes, until the sweet potato is very soft.
Stir in the peanut butter and blend until smooth.
Season with salt and serve topped with coriander.

notes: Vegan and gluten free. Contains peanuts.

title: Hearty Lamb and Barley Broth
summary: A slow-simmered Scottish style soup with lamb, barley and root vegetables.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in a large pot until deeply coloured on all sides.
Add the onion, leek and thyme and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the stock, barley, bay leaf and vegetables. Simmer for 1 hour, until the lamb and barley are tender.
Skim off any fat, season, and serve in deep bowls.

notes: Food safety: lamb pieces should reach 70°C and be tender throughout.

title: Lemongrass Prawn Soup with Rice Noodles
summary: A light Vietnamese style broth with lemongrass, lime and prawns.

steps.text: Simmer the stock with the lemongrass and chilli for 10 minutes to infuse.
Soak the vermicelli in hot water until soft, then drain.
Add the tomato and prawns to the broth and cook for 3 minutes, until the prawns are pink and opaque.
Stir in the fish sauce and lime juice.
Place noodles in bowls, ladle over the soup and scatter with the mint.

notes: Food safety: cook prawns until pink and opaque all the way through.

title: Roasted Cauliflower and Cumin Soup
summary: A velvety cauliflower soup deepened by roasting and warm cumin.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 210°C. Toss the cauliflower with half the oil and half the cumin and roast for 25 minutes, until deep golden at the edges.
Soften the onion and garlic with the remaining cumin in a pot for 5 minutes.
Add the cauliflower and stock and simmer for 10 minutes.
Blend with the tahini until silky and add the lemon juice and salt.

notes: Vegan and gluten free.

title: Chilled Cucumber and Yoghurt Soup with Mint
summary: A cool, refreshing summer soup of cucumber, yoghurt and mint with a walnut crunch.

steps.text: Blitz the cucumber, yoghurt, garlic, mint, vinegar and water until smooth.
Season with salt and chill for 1 hour, until very cold.
Ladle into bowls and top with the walnuts and a drizzle of oil.

notes: Plus 1 hour chilling.
Vegetarian and gluten free.

title: Tomato and Fennel Seafood Soup
summary: A light tomato broth with white fish and mussels.

steps.text: Soften the onion with the fennel seeds in the oil until translucent, then add the garlic.
Add the tomatoes and stock and simmer for 15 minutes until the soup tastes rich.
Add the mussels and cover for 3 minutes, until the shells open. Discard any that stay closed.
Slip in the fish and simmer gently for 3 minutes, until it flakes and turns opaque.
Scatter with parsley and serve.

notes: Food safety: cook fish until opaque and flaking; discard mussels that do not open.

title: Spiced Red Lentil and Carrot Soup
summary: A vibrant Indian style soup of red lentils, carrot and warm spices.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the oil until translucent, then cook the garlic, ginger and curry powder for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the lentils, carrot and stock. Simmer for 20 minutes, until the lentils collapse.
Blend half the soup and stir it back in for a thick texture.
Add the lemon juice and serve with coriander.

notes: Vegan and gluten free.

title: Warm Roast Pumpkin and Quinoa Salad with Lemon Tahini
summary: Roast pumpkin on herby quinoa with a creamy lemon tahini dressing.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C. Roast the pumpkin and onion in the oil for 30 minutes, until caramelised.
Cook the quinoa in boiling water for 12 minutes, until the germ spirals out, then drain.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice and 3 tbsp water until pourable.
Toss quinoa, vegetables, spinach and parsley together and drizzle with the dressing and scatter over the seeds.

notes: Vegan and gluten free.

title: Mexican Street Corn and Bean Salad
summary: A bright Mexican salad of charred corn, beans, tomato and avocado.

steps.text: Char the corn in a hot dry pan for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until blackened in spots.
Cut the kernels off the cobs.
Whisk the lime juice, oil, cumin and salt.
Toss the corn with the beans, tomato, onion and coriander, then fold in the avocado and dressing.

notes: Vegan and gluten free.

title: Greek Horiatiki with Whipped Feta
summary: Classic chunky tomato, cucumber and olive salad on a base of whipped feta.

steps.text: Blend the feta and yoghurt with 1 tbsp of oil until smooth and whipped.
Toss the tomato, cucumber, onion and olives with the vinegar, remaining oil and oregano.
Spread the feta on a platter and pile the salad on top.

notes: Vegetarian and gluten free.

title: Sicilian Orange, Radish and Olive Salad
summary: A crisp Sicilian style salad of shaved radish, orange segments and olives.

steps.text: Shave the radish very thinly and soak in iced water for 10 minutes until curled and crisp, then drain.
Whisk the oil, vinegar, chilli flakes and a pinch of salt.
Toss the radish with the oranges, onion, olives and mint, and dress just before serving.

notes: Vegan and gluten free.
Plus 10 minutes soaking.

title: Som Tam Style Green Mango Salad
summary: A crunchy sweet, sour and salty salad of green mango, beans and peanuts.
