steps.text: Crush the garlic and chilli in a mortar and pestle until a coarse paste forms.
Add the sugar, fish sauce and lime juice and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Bruise the beans lightly in the dressing, then add the tomato and mango and toss.
Scatter with peanuts and serve at once.

notes: Use 1 chilli for a milder salad.
Contains peanuts.

title: Bulgur and Pomegranate Salad with Herbs
summary: A fresh Levantine style grain salad packed with parsley, mint and pomegranate seeds.

steps.text: Soak the bulgur in 300ml boiling water for 15 minutes, until tender, then fluff and cool.
Fold in the herbs, tomato, spring onion and pomegranate.
Dress with the oil, lemon juice and salt and let sit 10 minutes before serving.

notes: Vegan.
Plus 25 minutes soaking and resting.

title: Smashed Potato Salad with Mustard Dressing
summary: Boiled and smashed baby potatoes crisped in a hot pan with a punchy wholegrain mustard dressing.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes for 18 minutes, until a knife slides in easily, then drain.
Press each potato flat with a spoon and fry in 2 tbsp of the oil for 4 minutes each side, until crisp and golden.
Whisk the mustard, vinegar and remaining oil.
Toss with the hot potatoes, spring onion, capers and parsley.

notes: Vegan and gluten free.

title: Cheesy Cauliflower Mash with Chives
summary: A lighter creamy mash of cauliflower and potato.

steps.text: Boil the cauliflower and potato for 15 minutes, until very tender, then drain well.
Mash with the butter, milk and cheddar until smooth.
Season and stir through the chives.

notes: Vegetarian and gluten free.

title: Garlic Butter Green Beans with Almonds
summary: Blistered green beans tossed with garlic butter and crunchy almonds.

steps.text: Boil the beans for 3 minutes, until bright green and tender-crisp, then drain.
Melt the butter and cook the almonds and garlic until the garlic is golden.
Toss the beans in the butter with the lemon zest and salt.

notes: Vegetarian and gluten free.

title: Coconut Rice with Pandan and Toasted Coconut
summary: Fragrant coconut rice, light and creamy, topped with toasted coconut.

steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear.
Simmer with the coconut milk, water, sugar and salt, covered, for 15 minutes until all liquid is absorbed.
Rest for 5 minutes, then fluff.
Toast the desiccated coconut in a dry pan until golden and sprinkle on top.

notes: Vegan and gluten free.
Plus 5 minutes resting.

title: Honey Roasted Carrots with Za'atar and Labneh
summary: Sweet roasted carrots with fragrant za'atar on tangy labneh.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 210°C. Toss the carrots with the oil, honey, za'atar and salt.
Roast for 30 minutes, until tender and caramelised at the edges.
Mix the labneh with the lemon juice and spread on a plate.
Pile the carrots on top and scatter with mint.

notes: Vegetarian and gluten free.

title: Crispy Roast Potatoes with Rosemary and Sea Salt
summary: Fluffy inside, crisp outside roast potatoes scented with rosemary.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C and heat the oil in a roasting tin.
Boil the potatoes for 8 minutes, then drain and shake to roughen the edges.
Tip into the hot oil and turn to coat. Roast for 40 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and crisp.
Add the rosemary and garlic for the last 10 minutes and finish with salt.

notes: Vegan and gluten free.

title: Sesame Bok Choy with Garlic and Oyster Sauce
summary: Quick wok-fried bok choy glazed with garlic and oyster sauce.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Fry the garlic for 15 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the bok choy and 2 tbsp water and toss for 2 minutes, until the stems are just tender.
Stir in the oyster sauce and sesame oil, and finish with sesame seeds.

notes: Use a vegetarian mushroom oyster sauce if preferred.

title: Braised Red Cabbage with Apple and Caraway
summary: Sweet and sour slow-braised red cabbage with apple and warm caraway.

steps.text: Melt the butter and soften the onion with the caraway until translucent.
Add the cabbage, apple, vinegar, sugar, bay leaf and 100ml water.
Cover and braise over low heat for 40 minutes, until very tender and glossy.
Season with salt and a splash more vinegar to balance.

notes: Vegetarian and gluten free.

title: Garlicky Sauteed Spinach with Pine Nuts and Raisins
summary: A quick Spanish style side of spinach with golden raisins and toasted pine nuts.

steps.text: Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan until golden, then set aside.
Warm the oil and garlic with the chilli flakes until the garlic is pale gold.
Add the spinach in batches and toss until wilted, then stir in the raisins.
Season and top with the pine nuts.

notes: Vegan and gluten free.

title: Blistered Broccolini with Garlic and Sesame
summary: Blistered broccolini with chilli and a squeeze of lemon.

steps.text: Heat a heavy pan until very hot and add the oil.
Cook the broccolini for 5 minutes, turning, until charred in spots and tender.
Add the chilli and garlic for 1 minute until fragrant.
Finish with a squeeze of lemon, salt and the sesame seeds.

notes: Vegan and gluten free.

title: Peruvian Style Green Aji Sauce
summary: A creamy green sauce with jalapeno, coriander and lime for chicken, potatoes or eggs.

steps.text: Blitz everything in a blender until completely smooth.
Taste and add more lime juice or salt until the sauce is bright and balanced.
Season with salt and chill for 30 minutes before serving.

notes: Makes about 300 ml; keeps 5 days refrigerated.
Plus 30 minutes chilling.
Vegetarian and gluten free.

title: Smoky Roasted Capsicum and Walnut Dip
summary: A Turkish style dip of roasted capsicum, walnuts and pomegranate molasses.

steps.text: Blitz the walnuts, breadcrumbs and garlic until crumbly.
Add the capsicum, molasses, cumin and chilli and process until a thick, spoonable paste.
With the motor running, stream in the oil until creamy.
Season with salt and serve with warm bread.

notes: Vegan.

title: Quick Pickled Red Onions with Lime and Oregano
summary: Bright pink pickled onions that lift tacos, salads and grain bowls.

steps.text: Warm the vinegar, water, sugar, salt and oregano until the sugar dissolves.
Pack the onions in a jar, pour over the warm liquid and add the lime juice.
Cool, then refrigerate for at least 1 hour.

notes: Plus 1 hour pickling; keeps 2 weeks refrigerated.
Vegan and gluten free.

title: Tzatziki with Dill and Lemon
summary: A thick garlicky Greek yoghurt dip with cucumber and lemon.

steps.text: Stir the yoghurt, cucumber, garlic, dill and lemon juice together until combined.
Season with salt and chill for 30 minutes.
Drizzle with the oil to serve.

notes: Plus 30 minutes chilling.
Vegetarian and gluten free.

title: Fresh Pineapple and Chilli Salsa
summary: A tropical sweet and hot salsa for fish, pork and tacos.

steps.text: Mix everything in a bowl until combined.
Season with salt and rest for 10 minutes until the juices run.
Serve soon after mixing for the freshest crunch.

notes: Vegan and gluten free.
Plus 10 minutes resting.

title: Peanut Satay Sauce
summary: A rich, glossy satay sauce for skewers, noodles and vegetables.

steps.text: Warm the coconut milk with the garlic and sambal oelek in a saucepan for 2 minutes.
Whisk in the peanut butter, soy, sugar and lime juice.
Simmer for 5 minutes, until thick and glossy, adding water to loosen.

notes: Vegan. Use tamari to keep it gluten free.
Contains peanuts.

title: Salsa Verde with Capers and Anchovy
summary: A punchy Italian herb sauce for grilled meat, fish and vegetables.

steps.text: Finely chop the herbs, capers, anchovy and garlic together until almost a paste.
Stir in the mustard, vinegar and oil until loose and glossy.
Season with pepper and rest for 15 minutes.

notes: Plus 15 minutes resting; keeps 4 days refrigerated.
Gluten free.

title: Chimichurri with Oregano and Chilli
summary: An Argentinian herb sauce, tangy with vinegar and fiery with chilli.

steps.text: Finely chop the parsley, oregano, garlic and chilli.
Mix with the vinegar, oil and salt.
Rest for 20 minutes until the flavours blend.

notes: Plus 20 minutes resting.
Vegan and gluten free.

title: Homemade Tomato Chilli Jam
summary: A sticky, sweet and spicy jam for cheese, burgers and eggs.

steps.text: Blitz the tomato, chilli, garlic and ginger to a rough purée.
Simmer with the sugar, vinegar and fish sauce for 1 hour, stirring, until thick and glossy and it leaves a trail when a spoon is dragged across the base.
Pour into hot sterilised jars and seal.

notes: Makes about 6 small jars; plus cooling. Keeps 3 months unopened.
Gluten free.

title: Creamy Garlic Mushroom Sauce
summary: A rich sauce for steak, chicken or pasta.

steps.text: Fry the mushrooms in the butter until golden and the liquid evaporates.
Add the garlic and thyme for 1 minute, then pour in the wine and bubble until reduced by half.
Stir in the cream and mustard and simmer for 5 minutes, until thickened and season and serve hot.

notes: Vegetarian and gluten free.

title: Miso Ginger Dressing
summary: A creamy, tangy dressing for noodle bowls and salads.

steps.text: Whisk all the ingredients until smooth and emulsified.
Taste and adjust with more vinegar if needed.
Shake in a jar before using, as it will separate on standing.

notes: Keeps 1 week refrigerated.
Use maple syrup for a vegan version.

title: Roasted Tomato Harissa Sauce
summary: A deep, smoky red sauce for eggs, roast vegetables and grilled meats.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C. Roast the tomato, capsicum, onion and garlic with the oil for 35 minutes, until blistered and soft.
Peel the capsicum, then blend everything with the harissa and cumin until smooth.
Season and simmer for 5 minutes until thick enough to coat a spoon.

notes: Keeps 5 days refrigerated.
Vegan and gluten free.

title: Ginger and Spring Onion Oil
summary: Silky, fragrant oil for noodles, rice and steamed fish.

steps.text: Mix the spring onion, ginger and salt in a heatproof bowl.
Heat the oil until shimmering and almost smoking, then pour over the mixture until it sizzles.
Stir in the soy sauce once the sizzling stops.

notes: Keeps 2 weeks refrigerated.
Vegan.

title: Yoghurt Raita with Roasted Cumin and Mint
summary: A cooling Indian yoghurt side for curries and spicy rice.

steps.text: Toast the cumin in a dry pan until fragrant.
Stir the yoghurt, cucumber, mint, cumin and salt together.
Dust with cayenne to serve.

notes: Vegetarian and gluten free.

title: Fried Eggs over Spiced Sweet Potato and Beans
summary: A hearty one-pan breakfast of crisp sweet potato, beans and runny eggs.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a frying pan and cook the sweet potato for 12 minutes until tender and golden.
Add the onion and paprika and cook for 4 minutes until soft.
Stir in the beans to heat through.
Make two wells, crack in the eggs and cover for 4 minutes, until the whites are set.
Top with avocado and coriander.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set; cook the yolks through if serving anyone vulnerable.

title: Spiced Ful Medames with Tahini and Soft Egg
summary: Warm mashed broad beans with lemon, cumin and a soft-boiled egg.

steps.text: Warm the beans with the garlic, cumin and 100ml water for 8 minutes, until hot, then mash roughly with a fork.
Stir in the lemon juice, half the oil and salt.
Boil the eggs for 6 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks soft, then peel.
Spoon the beans into bowls, drizzle with tahini and the remaining oil, and add the tomato, parsley and an egg.
Serve with warm flatbread.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set; cook the yolks through if serving anyone vulnerable.

title: Brown Rice Breakfast Bowl with Miso Greens and Egg
summary: Leftover rice topped with miso-glazed greens and a jammy egg.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 7 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks jammy, then peel.
Warm the sesame oil and cook the kale for 4 minutes, until wilted and bright.
Whisk the miso and mirin with 2 tbsp water and stir through the kale until glossy.
Heat the rice until steaming, then divide between bowls and top with kale, egg, sesame and nori.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set; cook the yolks through if serving anyone vulnerable.

title: Savoury Mince on Toast with Poached Egg
summary: A comforting British breakfast of spiced beef mince on buttered toast.

steps.text: Brown the mince with the onion until no pink remains.
Stir in the carrot, tomato paste, stock and worcestershire sauce and simmer for 12 minutes, until thick and rich.
Poach the eggs for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Butter the toasted bread until the slices are glossy, then spoon over the mince and add an egg.

notes: Food safety: cook the mince until 75°C in the centre and no pink remains.
Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set; cook the yolks through if serving anyone vulnerable.

title: Cinnamon Rice Porridge with Poached Pear
summary: Creamy rice pudding style porridge with warm cinnamon and soft pear.

steps.text: Simmer the rice, milk and cinnamon stick, stirring, for 20 minutes, until the rice is tender and creamy.
Melt the butter and cook the pear for 5 minutes, until soft and golden.
Remove the cinnamon, stir in half the maple syrup, and spoon into bowls.
Top with pear, walnuts and the remaining syrup.

notes: Use oat milk for a dairy free version.

title: Pesto Scrambled Eggs on Sourdough
summary: Soft scrambled eggs ribboned with basil pesto and cherry tomatoes.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs and a pinch of salt.
Melt the butter and add the tomatoes for 2 minutes, until blistered.
Pour in the eggs and stir gently over low heat for 3 minutes, until just softly set.
Fold in the pesto and serve on toasted sourdough with rocket.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set; cook the yolks through if serving anyone vulnerable.

title: Mushroom Congee with Soy Cashews
summary: Plant-based rice porridge with seared mushrooms and crunchy soy cashews.

steps.text: Simmer the rice, stock and ginger for 45 minutes, stirring now and then, until the grains burst and the porridge is thick.
Sear the mushrooms in a dry pan until golden, then add the soy sauce until glossy.
Toast the cashews in a pan until golden.
Ladle the congee into bowls and top with mushrooms, cashews, spring onion and sesame oil.

notes: Vegan. Use tamari for gluten free.

title: Dutch Baby Pancake with Roasted Berries
summary: A puffed oven pancake served with warm roast berries and yoghurt.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C with a 24cm ovenproof frying pan inside.
Blend the eggs, flour, milk and sugar until smooth.
Melt the butter in the hot pan, pour in the batter and bake for 18 minutes, until puffed and golden.
Warm the berries with the honey for 3 minutes until they release their juices.
Serve the pancake with berries and yoghurt.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set; cook the yolks through if serving anyone vulnerable.

title: Turkish Egg and Yoghurt with Chilli Butter (Cilbir)
summary: Poached eggs on garlicky yoghurt with sizzling paprika butter.

steps.text: Mix the yoghurt and garlic with a pinch of salt and let it come to room temperature.
Poach the eggs in barely simmering water for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Melt the butter with the paprika and chilli until foaming and deep red.
Spoon the eggs onto the yoghurt, drizzle with the butter until it pools, and scatter with dill. Serve with toast.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set; cook the yolks through if serving anyone vulnerable.

title: Beetroot and Feta Rye Toast
summary: Earthy roast beetroot, creamy feta and walnuts on seeded rye.

steps.text: Toast the rye until crisp.
Mash the feta with the oil until spreadable.
Spread the feta on the toast, and layer with beetroot and rocket until generously piled.
Top with walnuts and a drizzle of honey.

notes: Vegetarian.

title: Spicy Tofu Scramble with Black Beans
summary: A smoky vegan scramble loaded with capsicum, beans and fresh herbs.

steps.text: Soften the onion and capsicum in the oil for 5 minutes, until tender.
Crumble in the tofu with the spices and cook for 5 minutes, until golden at the edges.
Stir through the beans and warm until hot.
Warm the tortillas and serve the scramble inside, topped with coriander.

notes: Vegan and gluten free.

title: Overnight Oats with Coconut and Mango
summary: Make-ahead oats in coconut milk topped with fresh mango.

steps.text: Stir the oats, coconut milk, yoghurt and honey together.
Chill overnight, until the oats are soft and creamy.
Spoon into bowls and top with mango, toasted coconut and lime zest.

notes: Plus overnight chilling.
Vegetarian.

title: Soba Noodle Breakfast Bowl with Soft Egg and Dashi
summary: Warm noodles in a light dashi broth with an egg and spring onion.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 6 minutes, until the whites are set, then peel.
Cook the soba in boiling water until tender, about 4 minutes, then drain.
Heat the dashi with the soy and mirin until steaming.
Divide the noodles into bowls, pour over the broth and top with egg, spring onion and nori.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set; cook the yolks through if serving anyone vulnerable.
Check the soba label for gluten if needed.

title: Garlic Mushroom Frittata with Thyme
summary: A thick baked frittata studded with browned mushrooms and thyme.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C. Fry the mushrooms in the oil until golden and the liquid cooks off.
Add the onion, garlic and thyme and soften for 4 minutes.
Whisk the eggs and cream with salt and pour over the vegetables in an ovenproof pan, adding the gruyere.
Bake for 18 minutes, until set in the centre and golden on top.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set; cook the yolks through if serving anyone vulnerable.

title: Baked Coconut Rice Pudding Breakfast with Cardamom
summary: A baked, creamy rice breakfast scented with cardamom.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C. Mix the rice, coconut milk, milk, sugar, cardamom and sultanas in a baking dish.
Bake, stirring once, for 50 minutes, until the rice is tender and the pudding is creamy.
Rest for 5 minutes and scatter with pistachios.

notes: Plus 5 minutes resting.
Vegetarian and gluten free.

title: Roast Tomato and Ricotta Breakfast Tart
summary: A buttery puff pastry tart filled with ricotta, tomatoes and basil.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C. Score a 2cm border on the pastry and prick the middle.
Mix the ricotta with the egg, thyme and salt and spread inside the border.
Top with tomatoes and oil and bake for 28 minutes, until puffed and golden and scatter with basil.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set; cook the yolks through if serving anyone vulnerable.

title: Berry Bircher with Grated Apple
summary: Soaked oats and grated apple with berries and a nutty finish.

steps.text: Combine the oats, apple, juice and yoghurt.
Chill overnight, until the oats have softened.
Top with berries and almonds.

notes: Plus overnight chilling.
Vegetarian.

title: Filipino Garlic Rice with Tomato and Fried Egg
summary: Fragrant garlic fried rice with a runny egg and fresh tomato.

steps.text: Fry the garlic in the oil until golden and crisp, then lift out half.
Add the rice and soy sauce and stir-fry for 4 minutes, until hot and lightly toasted.
Fry the eggs until the whites are set.
Serve the rice topped with the egg, tomato, spring onion and the crisp garlic.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set; cook the yolks through if serving anyone vulnerable.

title: Ginger Sweet Potato Pancakes with Maple Yoghurt
summary: Fluffy spiced pancakes made with mashed sweet potato.

steps.text: Whisk the sweet potato, eggs and milk until smooth, then stir in the flour, baking powder and spices.
Melt a little butter in a pan and cook ladles of batter for 3 minutes, until bubbles form, then flip for 2 minutes until golden.
Mix the yoghurt and syrup and serve over the stacks.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set; cook the yolks through if serving anyone vulnerable.

title: Breakfast Burrito with Chorizo, Beans and Avocado
summary: A hand-held burrito packed with spicy chorizo, eggs and avocado.

steps.text: Cook the chorizo until crisp and the fat runs.
Add the beans, then pour in the whisked eggs and stir for 3 minutes until just set.
Warm the tortillas, fill with the eggs, avocado, cheddar and salsa, and roll up.

notes: Food safety: cook the chorizo to 75°C and the eggs until fully set.

title: Rye Porridge with Cardamom Stewed Apples
summary: A hearty Nordic porridge with soft cinnamon apples.

steps.text: Simmer the oats, crumbs and milk for 12 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Cook the apples with the butter, sugar and cardamom for 8 minutes, until soft and syrupy.
Spoon the porridge into bowls and top with the apples.

notes: Vegetarian.

title: Mushroom and Spinach Savoury Breakfast Crepes
summary: Thin buckwheat style crepes filled with garlicky mushrooms and spinach.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, eggs and milk to a thin batter.
Cook the mushrooms and garlic in butter until golden, then wilt in the spinach.
Cook ladles of batter in a lightly oiled pan for 1 to 2 minutes each side, until the edges lift and set.
Fill each crepe with vegetables and gruyere and fold.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set; cook the yolks through if serving anyone vulnerable.

title: Raisin and Almond Breakfast Pudding
summary: Warm oat and almond pudding sweetened with raisins.

steps.text: Simmer the oats, milk and raisins for 10 minutes, until the oats are soft.
Stir in the cinnamon and honey.
Top with toasted almonds.

notes: Vegetarian; vegan with maple syrup.

title: Spinach and Paneer Breakfast Bhurji
summary: Soft scrambled paneer with spinach, tomato and chilli.

steps.text: Heat the ghee and fry the cumin seeds until they crackle.
Cook the onion and chilli for 5 minutes until soft, then add turmeric and tomato for 3 minutes.
Stir in the spinach until wilted, then the paneer to warm through and serve with warm roti.

notes: Vegetarian.

title: Smashed Avocado with Dukkah Eggs on Seeded Toast
summary: Smashed avocado topped with dukkah-crusted soft eggs.

steps.text: Toast the mixed seeds, cumin and sesame in a dry pan until fragrant, then crush coarsely with salt for a dukkah.
Mash the avocado with lemon juice and oil.
Boil the eggs for 6 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks soft, then peel.
Toast the bread until crisp, then spread with avocado and top with halved eggs and dukkah.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set; cook the yolks through if serving anyone vulnerable.

title: Hearty Lentil and Kale Soup with Smoked Paprika
summary: A thick soup of brown lentils, kale and paprika for a cold day.

steps.text: Soften the onion and carrots in the oil for 6 minutes, until tender.
Stir in the garlic and paprika for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the lentils and stock and simmer for 25 minutes, until the lentils are tender.
Add the kale for 3 minutes until wilted, then finish with the vinegar.

notes: Vegan and gluten free.

title: Roasted Tomato and Red Capsicum Soup
summary: A velvety soup of slow-roasted tomatoes and red capsicum.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C. Roast the tomato, capsicum, onion and garlic in the oil for 40 minutes, until blistered and caramelised.
Blend with the stock and vinegar until smooth.
Reheat gently and season. Serve with basil.

notes: Vegan and gluten free.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Chicken and Sweet Corn Egg Drop Soup
summary: A silky Chinese style soup with sweet corn and ribbons of egg.

steps.text: Simmer the stock with the ginger and corn for 5 minutes.
Add the chicken and cook for 5 minutes, until opaque and cooked through.
Stir the cornflour with 3 tbsp water and add, simmering until slightly thickened.
Stream in the eggs while stirring until ribbons form, then add soy and spring onion.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C and until white all the way through.

title: Smoky Black Bean Soup with Lime and Avocado
summary: A hearty Latin American soup topped with creamy avocado.

steps.text: Soften the onion in oil until translucent, then cook the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Add the beans and stock and simmer for 25 minutes, until the beans break down.
Blend half the soup and stir it back in.
Add the lime juice and serve with avocado and coriander.

notes: Vegan and gluten free.

title: Creamy Potato and Leek Soup with Crispy Bacon
summary: Smooth potato soup finished with crisp bacon pieces.

steps.text: Soften the leek and onion in the butter for 8 minutes, until very soft.
Add the potato and stock and simmer for 18 minutes, until the potato is tender.
Blend until smooth and stir in the cream.
Fry the bacon until crisp and scatter over with the chives.

notes: Food safety: cook the bacon until crisp and well done.

title: Tom Kha Style Mushroom and Coconut Soup
summary: A fragrant coconut soup with galangal, lemongrass and mushrooms.

steps.text: Simmer the stock, lemongrass, galangal and lime leaves for 10 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the coconut milk and mushrooms and simmer for 6 minutes until tender.
Season with soy sauce and lime juice and top with chilli.

notes: Vegan. Fish out the aromatics before eating.

title: Turkish Yoghurt Soup with Rice and Mint (Yayla)
summary: A tangy warm yoghurt soup with tender rice and mint butter.

steps.text: Simmer the rice in the stock for 15 minutes, until soft.
Whisk the yoghurt, yolk and flour in a bowl, then temper in a ladle of hot stock.
Stir the mixture back into the pot over low heat for 5 minutes, until slightly thickened. Do not boil.
Sizzle the butter with the mint and chilli until foaming, then drizzle over.

notes: Vegetarian if made with vegetable stock.

title: Pearl Barley and Mushroom Soup with Dill
summary: A warming Central European mushroom and barley soup.

steps.text: Sweat the onion and carrots in butter for 8 minutes, until soft.
Add the mushrooms and cook for 6 minutes until golden.
Add the barley and stock and simmer for 40 minutes, until the barley is tender.
Stir in the sour cream and dill.

notes: Vegetarian.

title: Silky Ramen-Style Chicken Broth with Greens
summary: A clean, savoury chicken broth with noodles, soy egg and greens.

steps.text: Cover the wings with water and bring to a gentle simmer, skimming the scum, then add onion, garlic and ginger and cook for 2 hours, until the broth is rich and golden.
Boil the eggs for 6.5 minutes, then peel and soak in the soy and mirin until tinted.
Strain the broth and season.
Cook the noodles until tender and wilt the bok choy in the broth.
Ladle over the noodles, halve the eggs onto the top and add spring onion.

notes: Food safety: simmer the chicken until cooked through at 75°C; cook the eggs until the whites are fully set; cook the yolks through if serving anyone vulnerable.
Plus 1 hour soaking the eggs.

title: Watermelon, Feta and Mint Salad with Lime
summary: A cooling summer salad of watermelon and salty feta.

steps.text: Toss the watermelon with the onion, lime juice and oil until coated.
Crumble the feta over and scatter with mint and pistachios.
Serve at once, while the watermelon is still cold.

notes: Vegetarian and gluten free.

title: Roasted Beetroot, Orange and Goat Cheese Salad
summary: Earthy beetroot with orange and creamy goat cheese on rocket.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C. Wrap the beetroot in foil and roast for 45 minutes, until a knife slides in easily.
Peel and wedge the beetroot.
Whisk the oil and vinegar and toss with the rocket.
Arrange with the beetroot, orange, cheese and walnuts.

notes: Vegetarian and gluten free.

title: Asian Pear and Cabbage Slaw with Gochujang Dressing
summary: A crunchy, sweet and spicy slaw with fresh pear and gochujang.

steps.text: Whisk the gochujang, vinegar and sesame oil until smooth.
Toss the cabbage, pear, carrot and spring onion with the dressing.
Serve topped with sesame seeds.

notes: Vegan.

title: Chicken Caesar Salad with Anchovy Crumbs
summary: Crisp cos with grilled chicken and a creamy anchovy dressing.

steps.text: Toast the breadcrumbs in oil until crisp and golden.
Pan-fry the chicken for 6 minutes each side, until golden and 75°C inside, then slice.
Mash the anchovy and garlic and whisk in mayonnaise, mustard and lemon juice.
Toss the lettuce with dressing, top with chicken and crumbs.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C in the thickest part.

title: Lentil, Cucumber and Herb Salad with Preserved Lemon
summary: A fresh lentil salad with herbs and bright preserved lemon.

steps.text: Simmer the lentils for 20 minutes, until tender but holding their shape, then drain and cool.
Whisk the oil and vinegar.
Toss the lentils with the cucumber, herbs, preserved lemon, onion and dressing.

notes: Vegan and gluten free.

title: Noodle Salad with Peanut Lime Dressing
summary: Cold rice noodles with crunchy veg and a zesty peanut lime dressing.

steps.text: Soak the vermicelli in boiling water for 4 minutes, until tender, then drain and rinse cold.
Whisk the peanut butter, lime juice, fish sauce, chilli sauce and 3 tbsp water until smooth.
Toss the noodles with julienned vegetables and herbs, drizzle with dressing and sprinkle with peanuts.

notes: Contains peanuts.

title: Grilled Pear, Halloumi and Rocket Salad
summary: Charred pears with salty halloumi on peppery rocket.

steps.text: Grill the pears cut side down in a hot pan for 3 minutes, until charred.
Fry the halloumi for 2 minutes each side, until golden.
Toss the rocket with oil and vinegar and top with peach, halloumi, honey and pistachios.

notes: Vegetarian and gluten free.

title: Mediterranean Chickpea and Roast Vegetable Salad
summary: Warm chickpeas with roasted zucchini, capsicum and lemon.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C. Roast the vegetables in 2 tbsp oil for 25 minutes, until tender and charred.
Add the chickpeas for the last 10 minutes.
Toss with lemon juice, oregano, parsley and the remaining oil.

notes: Vegan and gluten free.

title: Cucumber Yoghurt Salad with Toasted Cumin and Chilli
summary: A cooling Indian-style kachumber with creamy yoghurt.

steps.text: Toast the cumin seeds in a dry pan until fragrant.
Mix the vegetables, yoghurt, chilli and coriander.
Season and top with the cumin.

notes: Vegetarian and gluten free.

title: Warm Green Bean and Tomato Salad with Fried Shallots
summary: A West African inspired warm bean salad topped with crisp shallots.

steps.text: Boil the beans for 4 minutes, until just tender.
Fry the onion and tomato in oil for 4 minutes, until soft.
Toss with beans, lemon juice and salt and sprinkle with fried shallots.

notes: Vegan and gluten free.

title: Creamy Polenta with Roasted Garlic and Thyme
summary: Soft, buttery polenta scented with sweet roasted garlic.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C. Roast the garlic head drizzled with oil for 30 minutes, until soft and golden.
Bring the stock to a boil, then whisk in the polenta and cook over low heat, stirring, for 20 minutes, until thick and creamy.
Squeeze the garlic into the polenta with the butter, milk and thyme, and stir until smooth.

notes: Vegetarian and gluten free.

title: Orange and Fennel Seed Roasted Beetroot
summary: Sweet roast beetroot with orange juice and aromatic fennel seeds.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C. Toss the beetroot with the oil, fennel seeds, orange juice and salt in a roasting tin.
Cover and roast for 30 minutes, then uncover and roast 20 minutes more, until tender and glazed.
Splash with vinegar and scatter over parsley.

notes: Vegan and gluten free.

title: Maple Miso Glazed Pumpkin Wedges
summary: Roasted pumpkin with a sticky sweet and salty miso glaze.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 210°C. Roast the pumpkin in the oil for 20 minutes.
Whisk the miso and maple syrup with 1 tbsp water, brush over the pumpkin, and roast for 12 minutes more, until sticky and caramelised.
Finish with sesame seeds and spring onions.

notes: Vegan and gluten free (check miso).

title: Oregano Lemon Roast Potatoes, Athens Style
summary: Tender roast potatoes soaked with lemon, oregano and garlic.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C. Toss the potatoes with lemon juice, oil, garlic, oregano and salt in a tin and pour over the stock.
Roast for 60 minutes, turning twice, until golden and the liquid is absorbed.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving so the potatoes soak up the last of the lemony juices.

notes: Use vegetable stock to make it vegan.
Gluten free.

title: Cumin Cauliflower on Garlic Tahini Yoghurt
summary: Spiced cauliflower under a cooling tahini yoghurt.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C. Toss the cauliflower with the oil, cumin and salt.
Roast for 28 minutes, until deeply golden and tender.
Whisk the yoghurt, tahini and lemon juice until smooth, spread on a plate, and pile on the cauliflower and parsley.

notes: Vegetarian and gluten free.

title: Coconut Spinach Sambal
summary: Quick Malaysian style spinach in a fragrant coconut sambal.

steps.text: Fry the shallots, garlic and chilli in the oil until fragrant and golden.
Add the coconut and toast for 2 minutes until lightly browned.
Stir in the spinach until it wilts, and finish with the lime juice and salt.

notes: Vegan and gluten free.

title: Garlic Roasted Mushrooms with Parsley
summary: Meaty roast mushrooms with garlic and fresh parsley.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C. Toss the mushrooms with the oil, garlic, thyme and salt.
Roast for 25 minutes, until deeply browned and any liquid has evaporated.
Finish with parsley and lemon juice.

notes: Vegan and gluten free.

title: Japanese Cucumber and Wakame Sunomono
summary: A light vinegared cucumber and seaweed side.

steps.text: Soak the wakame in cold water for 10 minutes until soft, then squeeze dry.
Salt the cucumber for 10 minutes and squeeze out the water.
Whisk the vinegar, sugar and soy until the sugar dissolves and toss with the vegetables, topping with sesame seeds.

notes: Plus 10 minutes soaking.
Vegan.

title: Charred Spring Greens with Anchovy Butter
summary: Quick charred greens tossed with salty anchovy butter.

steps.text: Char the greens in a hot dry pan for 4 minutes, until blistered and tender.
Melt the butter with the anchovy, garlic and chilli until the anchovy dissolves.
Toss with the greens and finish with lemon zest.

notes: Gluten free.

title: Sweet Potato Wedges with Smoky Lime Mayo
summary: Crisp-edged baked wedges with a smoky mayo dip.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C. Toss the wedges with the oil, paprika, garlic powder and salt.
Roast for 35 minutes, turning once, until crisp at the edges and tender inside.
Stir the mayonnaise and lime juice together and serve for dipping.

notes: Vegetarian and gluten free.

title: Spiced Basmati Pilaf with Toasted Vermicelli
summary: A fluffy, buttery pilaf with golden noodles and spices.

steps.text: Toast the noodles in the butter until deep golden, then add the onion, cumin and cinnamon for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the rinsed rice, water and salt and bring to a boil until bubbling.
Cover and cook on low heat for 14 minutes, until the water is absorbed. Rest 5 minutes and fluff.

notes: Plus 5 minutes resting.
Vegetarian.

title: Herbed Couscous with Preserved Lemon and Almonds
summary: Fluffy couscous studded with preserved lemon and nuts.

steps.text: Pour the boiling stock over the couscous, cover and leave for 5 minutes until the liquid is absorbed.
Fluff with a fork and stir through the oil, preserved lemon, almonds and herbs.
Taste, and add a squeeze of lemon if it needs more brightness.

notes: Plus 5 minutes standing.
Use vegetable stock for vegan.

title: Kimchi Egg Stir-Fry with Grated Cauliflower
summary: A quick low-carb fried 'rice' with kimchi.

steps.text: Stir-fry the cauliflower in oil for 4 minutes, until dry and lightly golden.
Add the kimchi and soy and fry for 2 minutes.
Push to the side, scramble the eggs until set, and mix through with the sesame oil and spring onions.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until fully set.

title: Braised Fennel-Style Celery with Lemon and Thyme
summary: Tender braised celery in lemon butter.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a wide pan and add the celery and thyme.
Add the stock and lemon juice, cover and braise for 20 minutes, until tender.
Uncover and reduce until the liquid glazes the celery.

notes: Vegetarian and gluten free.

title: Fresh Tomato Lime Salsa with Jalapeno
summary: A fresh chopped tomato salsa with onion, chilli and lime.

steps.text: Combine everything in a bowl.
Rest for 15 minutes until the juices run and flavours blend.
Serve with corn chips, grilled fish or tacos.

notes: Plus 15 minutes resting.
Vegan and gluten free.

title: Tahini Garlic Sauce
summary: A nutty lemony sauce for falafel, grilled veg and wraps.

steps.text: Whisk the tahini, lemon juice and garlic; it will seize and thicken.
Whisk in the water slowly until smooth and pourable.
Season with salt and refrigerate, where it keeps for 5 days.

notes: Vegan and gluten free.

title: Mango and Lime Chutney
summary: A sweet, tangy chutney for curries, cheese and grilled meat.

steps.text: Combine everything in a pot and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring, until thick and glossy.
Cool completely, then spoon into a clean jar and refrigerate until needed.
Stir through a squeeze of lime juice before serving.

notes: Keeps 2 weeks refrigerated.
Vegan and gluten free.

title: Peri Peri Sauce
summary: A fiery Portuguese-African chilli and garlic sauce.

steps.text: Blend everything until smooth.
Simmer for 8 minutes until the sauce thickens and darkens slightly.
Cool, then pour into a jar and refrigerate.

notes: Keeps 2 weeks refrigerated.
Vegan and gluten free.

title: Blue Cheese Dressing
summary: A thick tangy dressing for salads and wings.

steps.text: Mash half the cheese with the sour cream, mayonnaise, buttermilk and lemon juice until mostly smooth.
Fold through the remaining cheese until chunky.
Chill for 30 minutes before serving so the flavour develops.

notes: Vegetarian only with vegetarian blue cheese.
Gluten free.

title: Chipotle Tomato Salsa
summary: A smoky red salsa with chipotle and roasted tomato.

steps.text: Char the tomatoes, onion and garlic under a hot grill until blackened in spots.
Blend with chipotle, lime and coriander until slightly chunky.
Season with salt and chill; serve with chips or eggs.

notes: Vegan and gluten free.

title: Soy Ginger Dipping Sauce
summary: A savoury dumpling dip with ginger and black vinegar.

steps.text: Stir everything until the sugar dissolves.
Let it sit for 5 minutes before serving.
Spoon into small bowls for dipping dumplings or noodles.

notes: Vegan.

title: Roasted Garlic Aioli
summary: A rich garlic mayonnaise made with soft roasted garlic.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C and roast the garlic with oil for 30 minutes, until soft.
Squeeze out the cloves, mash smooth, and mix with the mayonnaise and lemon juice.
Chill for 30 minutes, where the aioli keeps for 4 days.

notes: Vegetarian and gluten free.

title: Lemon Herb Yoghurt Dressing
summary: A zesty herb dressing for grain bowls and roast vegetables.

steps.text: Blitz everything until smooth and pale green.
Thin with water until pourable.
Season with salt and chill until ready to serve.

notes: Vegetarian and gluten free.

title: Pickled Ginger and Cucumber Relish
summary: A bright quick relish for rice bowls, fish and burgers.

steps.text: Toss the cucumber with the pickled ginger, vinegar and sugar until coated.
Fold in the spring onion and sesame seeds.
Rest for 10 minutes so the cucumber takes on the flavour.

notes: Vegan and gluten free.

title: Smoky Baba Ganoush Toast
summary: Charred eggplant dip spread on warm toast with pomegranate.

steps.text: Char the whole eggplants over a flame or under a grill for 25 minutes, turning, until blackened and collapsing.
Scoop out the flesh and mix with tahini, lemon, garlic and half the oil.
Toast the bread until golden, spread with the dip and top with pomegranate.

notes: Vegan.

title: Slow Cooker Style Lamb and White Bean Soup
summary: A rich lamb and cannellini soup simmered until tender.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in batches until golden, then set aside.
Soften the onion and carrots, stir in the garlic, tomato paste and thyme.
Return the lamb with the stock and simmer for 80 minutes, until the lamb is tender.
Add the beans for the last 15 minutes.

notes: Food safety: the lamb should reach 70°C and be tender.

title: Clear Chicken and Ginger Soup with Silken Tofu
summary: A gentle, comforting soup for when you feel under the weather.

steps.text: Simmer the stock, ginger and chicken for 15 minutes, until the chicken is white throughout.
Shred the chicken, return to the pot, and add the soy.
Add the tofu and spinach until the spinach wilts.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until 75°C and no pink remains.

title: Cabbage Roll Soup with Paprika
summary: All the flavour of stuffed cabbage in a soup bowl.

steps.text: Brown the mince with the onion until no pink remains.
Add the paprika, tomatoes, stock, bay leaf and rice and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the cabbage for 15 minutes until tender, and season.

notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C and rice must be piping hot.

title: Vegetable Barley Soup with Lemon Zest
summary: A fresh vegetable barley soup finished with lemon.

steps.text: Dice the vegetables and simmer with the barley and stock for 40 minutes, until the barley is tender.
Stir in the lemon zest and dill.
Season with salt and pepper and ladle into bowls.

notes: Vegan.

title: Smoked Haddock Style White Fish Chowder
summary: A creamy fish chowder with potato and corn.

steps.text: Soften the onion in butter, then add the potatoes and stock and simmer 12 minutes until tender.
Add the milk and corn and warm without boiling.
Slip in the fish and poach 5 minutes, until opaque and flaking and scatter with chives.

notes: Food safety: cook fish until opaque, flaking and 63°C.

title: Spiced Pumpkin and Chickpea Soup (Harira Style)
summary: A Moroccan inspired soup of pumpkin, tomato and chickpeas.

steps.text: Soften the onion with the spices in oil until fragrant.
Add the pumpkin, tomatoes, chickpeas and stock and simmer for 25 minutes, until the pumpkin is tender.
Finish with lemon juice and coriander.

notes: Vegan and gluten free.

title: Hot and Sweet Corn Fritter Breakfast Stack
summary: Crisp corn fritters with sweet chilli and fried eggs.

steps.text: Mix the corn, flour, eggs, spring onion and baking powder with salt into a thick batter.
Fry spoonfuls in oil for 3 minutes each side, until golden and set.
Fry the other eggs until the whites are set, then stack with the fritters and drizzle with chilli sauce.

notes: Food safety: cook eggs until the whites are fully set.

title: Salmon and Soft Egg Rye Breakfast Plate
summary: Smoked salmon with creamy eggs on dark rye.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs and scramble gently in the butter for 3 minutes, until just set.
Toast the rye until crisp.
Pile the eggs onto the toast until generous and top with salmon, creme fraiche and dill.

notes: Food safety: cook eggs until fully set; smoked salmon should stay chilled.

title: Savoury Kimchi Pancake for Breakfast
summary: A crisp chewy pancake studded with kimchi.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, water, egg and kimchi into a thick batter and fold in the spring onions.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Pour in the batter and fry for 4 minutes each side, until crisp and golden. Serve with soy sauce.

notes: Food safety: cook until the centre is set.

title: Fresh Ricotta and Lemon Hotcakes
summary: Light and tender ricotta pancakes with lemon.

steps.text: Mix the ricotta, eggs, lemon zest and sugar, then fold in the flour and baking powder.
Melt the butter in a frying pan over medium heat.
Cook spoonfuls for 3 minutes each side, until golden and puffed, and serve with maple syrup.

notes: Food safety: cook until the centre is set.

title: Roast Tomato Bruschetta Breakfast
summary: Garlic toast loaded with roast tomatoes and basil.

steps.text: Roast the tomatoes with oil at 200°C for 18 minutes, until burst and sticky.
Toast the sourdough until golden and rub with garlic.
Top with tomatoes, basil and vinegar.

notes: Vegan.

title: Bouillabaisse-Style Fish Soup with Rouille
summary: A saffron and fennel-seed fish soup with mussels and prawns, served with garlicky rouille on toasted baguette.

steps.text: Soften the onion and leek in the oil for 8 minutes until translucent, then add the garlic and fennel seeds and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the tomato paste, tomatoes, saffron and fish stock and simmer for 25 minutes until the broth is rich and slightly reduced.
Whisk the mayonnaise with the paprika, grated garlic and a spoonful of the hot broth to make the rouille.
Add the fish and mussels to the pot, cover and cook for 5 minutes until the fish turns opaque and the mussel shells have opened.
Add the prawns for 2 minutes until pink and opaque, then discard any mussels that stay shut.
Toast the baguette until crisp, ladle the soup into bowls and serve with the rouille on the toast.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, and the prawns until pink and opaque. Discard any mussel that does not open.
Rouille uses shop-bought mayonnaise so there is no raw egg to worry about.

title: Beef Pho from Scratch
summary: A clear spiced beef broth simmered for hours, poured over rice noodles, brisket, sprouts and fresh herbs.

steps.text: Cover the bones with cold water in a large pot, boil for 10 minutes, then drain and rinse the bones and pot to keep the broth clear.
Char the onions and ginger in a dry pan over high heat for 6 minutes until blackened in spots.
Return the bones to the pot with the brisket, charred aromatics, spices, rock sugar and 3 litres of fresh water, then bring to a bare simmer.
Simmer gently for 3 hours, skimming off the scum, until the brisket is tender when pierced with a knife.
Lift out the brisket, cool a little and slice thinly against the grain, then strain the broth and season with the fish sauce.
Soak the noodles in hot water until soft, then divide among bowls with the brisket.
Ladle over the boiling broth and top with sprouts, herbs, chilli and lime wedges.

notes: Food safety: simmer the brisket until tender, with an internal temperature of at least 75°C.
Keep the broth just below a boil for a clear result.

title: Chicken Consomme with Herb Royale
summary: A crystal-clear chicken consomme clarified with an egg-white raft, served with delicate herb custard cubes.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C and whisk the egg yolks with the milk, chives, nutmeg and half the salt, then pour into a small greased dish.
Bake the custard in a tray of hot water for 20 minutes until just set in the centre, then cool and cut into small cubes.
Mix the mince, egg whites, vegetables and tomato in a cold pot, then stir in the cold stock and bay leaf.
Heat gently, stirring now and then, until a raft forms on the surface at about 80°C, then stop stirring.
Simmer very gently for 45 minutes, making a small hole in the raft so the liquid bubbles through.
Ladle the clear broth through a muslin-lined sieve without disturbing the raft, and season with the remaining salt.
Warm the consomme, drop a few custard cubes into each bowl and serve hot.

notes: Food safety: the mince cooks in the raft; the consomme should simmer for the full 45 minutes so the chicken reaches at least 75°C. Cook the custard until set.
Strain gently for the clearest result.

title: Fermented Flatbread, Injera-Style
summary: A soft, tangy, spongy pancake fermented for two days, for scooping up stews and salads.

steps.text: Whisk the flours, yeast and 500ml of the water into a smooth batter, cover loosely and leave at room temperature for two days until bubbly and sour.
Stir the batter, add the salt and enough of the remaining water to make a thin pouring consistency like cream.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat and wipe with the oil on a paper towel.
Pour in a thin layer, swirling to cover the base, and cover with a lid for 2 minutes until the surface is full of holes and set.
Slide it out without flipping and cool on a clean cloth, cooking the remaining batter in the same way until all the pancakes are done.
Stack once cool and serve with stews, lentils and salads.

notes: Traditionally made with teff flour; this is a simple everyday version.
Fermenting time is not counted in the prep time.

title: Mtori Tanzanian Beef and Plantain Soup
summary: A creamy beef and plantain soup from Tanzania, thickened with the cooked plantain and finished with a little cream.

steps.text: Brown the beef in the oil for 5 minutes until coloured on all sides, then lift it out.
Cook the onion and garlic in the same pot for 5 minutes until soft, then add the tomatoes until they break down.
Return the beef with the water and salt, bring to the boil, then simmer for 40 minutes until the beef is tender.
Add the plantains and simmer for 15 minutes until completely soft.
Lift out a few pieces of beef, blend the soup until smooth and return the beef to the pot with the cream.
Heat through, season with the pepper and serve with the coriander.

notes: Food safety: simmer the beef until tender, with an internal temperature of at least 75°C before serving.
Choose green or very firm plantains for the traditional texture.

title: Sukuma Wiki with Tomato and Onion
summary: Kenyan braised greens with soft onion and tomato, the everyday side served with ugali.

steps.text: Fry the onion in the oil for 6 minutes until golden and soft, then add the garlic and coriander and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 4 minutes until pulpy.
Stir in the kale, water and salt, cover and cook for 6 minutes until the greens are tender but still bright.
Taste and adjust the salt before serving hot.

notes: Add a chopped chilli if you like heat.
Leftovers keep for 3 days in the fridge.

title: Ugali with Kachumbari Salad
summary: Stiff maize porridge to scoop with the fresh tomato, onion and chilli salad of Kenya and Tanzania.

steps.text: Bring the water and salt to the boil in a heavy pot, then whisk in a third of the polenta until smooth.
Add the rest gradually, beating with a wooden spoon, and cook on low heat for 12 minutes until the mass pulls away from the pot.
Mix the tomatoes, onion, chilli, coriander and lime juice in a bowl.
Shape the ugali into mounds with a wet spoon and serve with the kachumbari.

notes: Eat with your hands: pinch off a piece of ugali and use it to scoop up the salad.
Rest the salad for 10 minutes for the best flavour.

title: Maharagwe ya Nazi Coconut Beans
summary: Swahili-coast kidney beans simmered in coconut milk with tomato, garlic and turmeric.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 6 minutes until soft, then add the garlic, turmeric and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until jammy.
Stir in the beans and coconut milk and simmer for 12 minutes until thick and creamy.
Season with salt and scatter over the coriander.

notes: Serve with rice, chapati or ugali.
Mash a few beans against the pot to thicken it.

title: Mukimo Mashed Potato with Peas and Corn
summary: Kikuyu-style mash of potatoes, green peas and sweetcorn, a comforting side for stews.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes until a knife slides in easily.
Add the peas and corn for the last 4 minutes of cooking, then drain.
Fry the onion in the butter for 5 minutes until soft and golden.
Mash everything with the milk and onion until chunky and green-flecked.
Serve hot with a stew or grilled meat.

notes: Leave some lumps for the traditional texture.
Use oat milk and oil for a dairy-free version.

title: Pili Pili Hot Sauce
summary: A bright East African chilli, garlic and lime sauce that keeps well in the fridge.

steps.text: Simmer the chillies, garlic and water for 5 minutes until the chillies are soft.
Blend with the lime juice, oil, salt and paprika until smooth.
Cool completely and store in a clean jar.
Serve with grilled meats, eggs or beans.

notes: Keeps for 2 weeks in the fridge.
Wear gloves when chopping the chillies.

title: Jamaican Chicken Soup with Pumpkin and Dumplings
summary: A turmeric-gold chicken and root vegetable soup with chewy spinner dumplings and a little scotch bonnet heat.

steps.text: Simmer the chicken in the stock with the thyme, allspice, turmeric and whole scotch bonnet for 30 minutes until the meat is tender.
Lift out the chicken, shred the meat and discard the skin and bones.
Add the pumpkin and carrot to the broth and simmer for 12 minutes until soft.
Mix the flour, water and salt into a firm dough and roll small pieces into thin spinners between your palms.
Drop the spinners into the soup and cook for 8 minutes until firm and cooked through.
Return the chicken and add the spring onions, then remove the scotch bonnet before serving.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and the juices run clear.
Leave the scotch bonnet whole for flavour without the full heat.

title: Callaloo and Crab Soup
summary: A green Trinidadian soup of spinach, okra and coconut milk with sweet crab meat.

steps.text: Melt the butter and cook the onion and garlic for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the okra, thyme, whole scotch bonnet and stock and simmer for 10 minutes until the okra is tender.
Add the spinach until wilted, then blend the soup until smooth, keeping the scotch bonnet out.
Stir in the coconut milk and simmer for 8 minutes.
Fold in the crab and heat gently for 3 minutes until hot and opaque, then season with salt.

notes: Food safety: heat the crab until opaque and piping hot.
Remove the scotch bonnet before blending.

title: Haitian Pikliz Pickled Slaw
summary: A fiery crunchy cabbage and carrot pickle that cuts the richness of fried foods.

steps.text: Pack the cabbage, carrot, capsicum, scotch bonnet and spring onions into a clean jar with the cloves.
Pour over the vinegar, lime juice and salt, adding water to cover if needed.
Press down until the vegetables are submerged and seal.
Chill for at least 24 hours before serving.

notes: Keeps for 3 weeks in the fridge.
Wear gloves to slice the scotch bonnet.

title: Rice and Peas with Coconut and Thyme
summary: Jamaican Sunday side of rice cooked in coconut milk with kidney beans, thyme and allspice.

steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear.
Bring the coconut milk, water, beans, thyme, spring onions, allspice, garlic and whole scotch bonnet to a simmer until steaming, seasoning with the salt.
Stir in the rice, cover and cook on the lowest heat for 20 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.
Rest for 10 minutes covered, then remove the thyme and scotch bonnet and fluff with a fork.

notes: Food safety: cool leftover rice quickly and refrigerate within an hour, and reheat until steaming hot.
Keep the scotch bonnet whole to avoid blowing your head off.

title: Fried Sweet Plantain
summary: Ripe plantain slices fried until caramelised and golden, a staple side across the Caribbean.

items.raw: 3 plantains, peeled and sliced on an angle
items.prep: peeled and sliced on an angle

steps.text: Heat half the oil in a wide pan over medium heat.
Fry the plantain in batches for 3 minutes each side until deep golden with dark edges.
Drain on paper towel and sprinkle with salt.
Serve warm with lime wedges.

notes: Use very ripe plantains with black skins for the sweetest result.
Add the rest of the oil as you go.

title: Johnny Cakes with Scrambled Eggs and Tomato
summary: Golden fried cornmeal-flour dumplings from the islands, served with soft scrambled eggs and tomato.

steps.text: Rub the butter into the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt until crumbly.
Stir in the water to make a soft dough, divide into 8 pieces and flatten into discs.
Fry the discs in 2 tbsp oil for 3 minutes each side until golden and cooked in the middle.
Heat the remaining oil in another pan, add the tomatoes and spring onions for 2 minutes.
Pour in the whisked eggs and stir gently over low heat for 3 minutes until set and no liquid egg remains.
Serve the eggs with the warm johnny cakes.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until firm with no runny egg, and serve immediately.
Johnny cakes freeze well.

title: Jerk Marinade
summary: A sweet-hot paste of scotch bonnet, allspice and thyme for chicken, pork, fish or vegetables.

steps.text: Blitz the scotch bonnets, spring onions, garlic and ginger until a rough paste forms.
Add the allspice, thyme, soy sauce, lime juice, sugar, oil and pepper and blitz until nearly smooth.
Rub over your protein and marinate for at least 4 hours before cooking.
Store leftover marinade in a jar for up to 2 weeks.

notes: Food safety: cook marinated chicken to 75°C and pork to at least 70°C, and never reuse marinade that touched raw meat.
Works beautifully with tofu or cauliflower too.

title: Mango and Scotch Bonnet Hot Sauce
summary: A sweet, tangy and fiery Caribbean table sauce to dollop on grilled fish, rice and eggs.

steps.text: Simmer the mango, scotch bonnet, garlic, vinegar and turmeric for 12 minutes until the mango is very soft.
Blend with the lime juice, honey and salt until completely smooth.
Cool and bottle in a clean jar.
Keep in the fridge for up to 3 weeks.

notes: Use a whole scotch bonnet for more heat.
Shake before using.

title: Cornmeal Porridge with Coconut and Nutmeg
summary: Creamy Jamaican cornmeal porridge sweetened with condensed-style sugar, coconut milk and warming spice.

steps.text: Whisk the polenta with 250ml of the water until smooth.
Bring the remaining water, coconut milk, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt to a simmer until steaming.
Stir in the polenta mixture and cook over low heat for 15 minutes until thick and creamy.
Add the sugar and vanilla and stir until dissolved.

notes: Loosen with a splash of milk if it thickens as it cools.
Naturally dairy-free and gluten-free.

title: Soto Ayam Indonesian Chicken Soup
summary: A turmeric-gold chicken broth with lemongrass and galangal, vermicelli, egg and fresh sprouts.

steps.text: Blitz the garlic, shallots, turmeric and coriander with a splash of water to a paste and fry in the oil for 4 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chicken, water, lemongrass, lime leaves, galangal and salt and simmer for 35 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Boil the eggs for 8 minutes until firm, then peel and halve.
Lift out the chicken, shred it and soak the vermicelli in hot water until soft.
Strain the broth and divide the noodles, chicken, eggs and sprouts among bowls.
Ladle over the hot broth and top with spring onion and lime.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C and boil the eggs until the whites and yolks are firm.
Serve with sambal on the side.

title: Gado-Gado Vegetable Platter with Tofu
summary: Blanched vegetables, tofu and eggs under a warm sweet-spicy peanut dressing.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes for 12 minutes until tender, then lift out and cool.
Blanch the beans, cabbage and sprouts in the same water for 2 minutes until just tender, then refresh in cold water.
Boil the eggs for 9 minutes until the yolks are firm, then cool, peel and quarter.
Warm the peanut butter, water, kecap manis, lime juice, garlic and chilli in a pot until smooth and pourable.
Arrange the vegetables, tofu, cucumber and eggs on a platter.
Spoon over the sauce and finish with the fried shallots.

notes: Food safety: boil the eggs until the yolks are firm.
Swap the eggs for extra tofu to make it vegan.

title: Sambal Matah Lemongrass and Shallot Sambal
summary: A raw Balinese relish of shallots, lemongrass, chilli and lime, warmed with a splash of hot oil.

steps.text: Toast the shrimp paste in a dry pan for 1 minute until fragrant.
Mix the shallots, lemongrass, chillies and lime leaves in a bowl.
Heat the coconut oil until shimmering and pour over the mixture.
Stir in the lime juice, shrimp paste and salt and rest for 10 minutes before serving.

notes: Serve with grilled fish, chicken or rice.
Best eaten the day it is made.

title: Bubur Ayam Indonesian Chicken Rice Porridge
summary: A silky rice porridge with shredded chicken, fried shallots, spring onion and a soy egg.

steps.text: Simmer the rice with the stock, garlic and ginger, stirring occasionally, for 45 minutes until the grains collapse into a thick porridge.
Poach the chicken in the porridge for 15 minutes until cooked through, then lift out and shred.
Boil the eggs for 7 minutes until jammy, then peel and halve.
Season the porridge with salt and spoon into bowls.
Top with chicken, egg, kecap manis, spring onion and fried shallots.

notes: Add water if the porridge gets too thick.

Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C and the juices run clear. Use fresh, uncracked eggs; for pregnant women, older people, young children and anyone with low immunity, cook the eggs until the yolks are firm.

title: Sayur Lodeh Vegetable Coconut Soup
summary: A gentle Javanese soup of mixed vegetables in lemongrass-scented turmeric coconut broth.

steps.text: Blitz the shallots, garlic, turmeric and coriander with a splash of water to a paste.
Fry the paste in the oil for 4 minutes until fragrant.
Add the stock, coconut milk, lemongrass and pumpkin and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the carrot, beans and cabbage and simmer for 8 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and remove the lemongrass before serving.

notes: Serve with rice.
Add tofu or tempeh-style firm tofu for protein.

title: Bakso Indonesian Meatball Soup
summary: Springy beef meatballs in a peppery garlic broth with noodles and greens.

steps.text: Blitz the mince, tapioca starch, 2 garlic cloves, salt, pepper and egg to a sticky paste.
Bring the stock to a gentle simmer with the remaining garlic until steaming.
Roll the mixture into walnut-sized balls and drop into the stock.
Simmer for 15 minutes until the balls float and are cooked through.
Add the bok choy for 2 minutes until just tender and soak the vermicelli in hot water until soft.
Divide the noodles among bowls, ladle over the meatballs and broth, then top with shallots, spring onion and kecap manis.

notes: Food safety: cook the meatballs until they reach an internal temperature of 75°C and no pink remains.
Serve with sambal.

title: Acar Timun Pickled Cucumber Salad
summary: A sweet-sour cucumber, carrot and shallot pickle served alongside satay and fried rice.

steps.text: Heat the vinegar, sugar, water and salt until the sugar has dissolved, then cool.
Combine the cucumber, carrot, shallots and chillies in a bowl.
Pour over the cooled pickling liquid and stir.
Chill for 30 minutes, then top with the peanuts.

notes: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.
Peanuts are optional.

title: Nasi Uduk Coconut Rice
summary: Jakarta-style fragrant rice cooked in coconut milk with lemongrass, bay leaf and pandan-style lime leaves.

steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear.
Combine the rice, coconut milk, water, lemongrass, bay leaves, lime leaves and salt in a pot.
Bring to a simmer, cover and cook on the lowest heat for 18 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid absorbed.
Rest for 10 minutes covered and fluff, removing the aromatics, then top with fried shallots.

notes: Food safety: refrigerate any leftover rice within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with fried tofu and sambal.

title: Arroz Caldo Filipino Chicken and Ginger Rice Porridge
summary: A warming ginger and garlic rice porridge with chicken, boiled egg and crisp garlic.

steps.text: Fry the onion, ginger and half the garlic in the oil for 5 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the chicken, rice and stock and simmer for 40 minutes, stirring now and then, until the rice breaks down and the chicken is tender.
Lift out the chicken, shred the meat, discard the bones and skin, and stir the meat back through with the fish sauce.
Boil the eggs for 8 minutes until firm, then peel and halve.
Fry the remaining garlic in a little oil for 2 minutes until golden and crisp.
Top bowls with egg, crisp garlic, spring onion and a squeeze of lemon.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C and boil the eggs until the yolks are firm.
Add more stock for a looser porridge.

title: Sinigang na Hipon Sour Tamarind Prawn Soup
summary: The classic Filipino sour soup of tamarind, tomato and prawns with greens.

steps.text: Simmer the water, tamarind, tomatoes and onion for 10 minutes until the tomatoes soften.
Add the daikon and cook for 8 minutes until tender.
Add the green beans and chillies and simmer for 4 minutes.
Stir in the prawns for 3 minutes until pink and opaque.
Fold through the spinach until just wilted and season with the fish sauce.

notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until pink and opaque.
Adjust the tamarind to taste for more sourness.

title: Tinolang Manok Chicken, Ginger and Green Papaya Soup
summary: A clear, comforting Filipino soup of chicken, plenty of ginger and green papaya.

steps.text: Fry the ginger, onion and garlic in the oil for 4 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chicken and brown for 5 minutes.
Pour in the water and fish sauce, bring to the boil and simmer for 20 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Add the green papaya and cook for 8 minutes until just tender.
Stir in the spinach and chilli until wilted.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C and the juices run clear.
Use chayote or zucchini if papaya is hard to find.

title: Bulalo Filipino Beef Shank Soup
summary: A long-simmered beef shank soup with sweet corn, cabbage and bok choy in a clear, rich broth.

steps.text: Boil the beef shin in water for 10 minutes, then drain, rinse and wipe out the pot to keep the broth clear.
Return the beef to the pot with the water, onion and peppercorns and bring to a bare simmer until the surface just trembles.
Simmer for 2.5 hours, skimming off scum, until the meat is falling off the bone.
Add the fish sauce, corn and potatoes and cook for 20 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Add the cabbage and bok choy and cook for 4 minutes until just soft.
Season with salt and serve with rice.

notes: Food safety: simmer the beef until tender, with an internal temperature of at least 75°C.
Skim the fat for a lighter broth.

title: Ensaladang Mangga Green Mango Salad
summary: Crunchy green mango with tomato, red onion and a salty-sweet dressing.

steps.text: Mix the mangoes, tomatoes and onion in a bowl.
Whisk the fish sauce, lime juice and sugar until the sugar dissolves.
Toss through the salad until coated.
Top with chilli and coriander and serve.

notes: Use firm, unripe mango for the right crunch.
Serve with grilled fish or pork.

title: Ensaladang Talong Charred Eggplant Salad
summary: Smoky grilled eggplant with tomato, onion and a sharp vinegar dressing.

steps.text: Char the whole eggplants over a flame or under a hot grill for 15 minutes, turning often, until the skin is blackened and the flesh collapses.
Cool, peel and chop the flesh.
Whisk the vinegar, fish sauce, garlic and sugar in a bowl.
Toss with the eggplant, tomato, onion and chilli and serve.

notes: Serve with fried fish or rice.
Leave out the fish sauce and use soy for a vegetarian version.

title: Tortang Talong Eggplant Omelette
summary: A silky charred eggplant folded into an egg omelette, served with ketchup or vinegar.

steps.text: Char the whole eggplants under a hot grill for 12 minutes until blackened and soft.
Cool, peel and flatten the flesh with a fork, keeping the stems on.
Whisk the eggs with the salt and spring onion.
Heat the oil in a pan, dip the eggplants in the egg and fry for 3 minutes each side until set and golden.
Serve hot with tomato sauce.

notes: Food safety: cook the omelette until the egg is completely set.
Serve with garlic rice.

title: Sinangag Filipino Garlic Fried Rice
summary: The breakfast staple of crisp garlic and day-old rice, served with eggs and cured meats.

steps.text: Break up the cold rice with your fingers.
Fry the garlic in 1 tbsp oil over medium heat for 2 minutes until golden.
Add the rice and salt and stir-fry for 5 minutes until hot and lightly crisp.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil until the whites are set.
Serve the rice with the eggs and spring onion on top.

notes: Food safety: cool cooked rice quickly and refrigerate within an hour, and cook the fried rice until steaming hot all through.
Cook the eggs until the whites are fully set.

title: Atchara Pickled Green Papaya
summary: A sweet and tangy Filipino pickle of green papaya, carrot and capsicum for fried and grilled food.

steps.text: Mix the papaya, carrot, capsicum, onion and ginger with the salt and leave for 20 minutes, then squeeze out the liquid.
Heat the vinegar, sugar and pepper until the sugar has dissolved.
Pack the vegetables into clean jars and pour over the warm pickling liquid.
Cool, seal and chill for at least 2 days before serving.

notes: Keeps for a month in the fridge.
Pickling time is not counted.

title: Sawsawan Spiced Vinegar Dipping Sauce
summary: A garlicky chilli vinegar dip for fried fish, grilled meat and spring rolls.

steps.text: Combine all the ingredients in a small bowl.
Stir until the sugar dissolves.
Rest for 15 minutes so the flavours mellow before serving.

notes: Keeps for a week in the fridge.
Add a squeeze of calamansi or lime for extra zing.

title: Chakalaka South African Vegetable Relish
summary: A warming braai relish of capsicum, carrot, beans and curry spices.

steps.text: Fry the onion in the oil for 6 minutes until soft, then add the garlic, ginger, curry powder and paprika for 1 minute.
Stir in the capsicum and carrot and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and chilli and simmer for 10 minutes until thick.
Stir through the beans and heat for 4 minutes, then season with salt.

notes: Serve warm or cold with pap, grilled meat or bread.
Keeps for 5 days in the fridge.

title: Pap and Tomato Gravy
summary: Stiff maize porridge with a sweet-sharp tomato and onion gravy, a staple side.

steps.text: Bring the water and salt to the boil, whisk in the polenta and cook over low heat for 15 minutes, stirring, until thick and stiff.
Fry the onion in the oil for 6 minutes until soft, then add the garlic and curry powder.
Add the tomatoes, sugar and bay leaf and simmer for 12 minutes until saucy.
Shape the pap into mounds and ladle over the gravy.

notes: Serve with grilled sausage or chicken.
Remove the bay leaf before serving.

title: Cape Malay Butternut Soup
summary: A silky pumpkin soup spiced with cinnamon, ginger and curry, topped with toasted seeds.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the butter for 6 minutes until translucent.
Add the garlic, ginger, curry powder and cinnamon for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the pumpkin and stock, cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the pumpkin is completely soft.
Blend until smooth, stir in the cream and heat through.
Serve with toasted pumpkin seeds.

notes: Use coconut cream for a dairy-free version.
Toast the seeds in a dry pan until golden.

title: Mealie Bread with Cheddar
summary: A moist sweetcorn loaf studded with cheese, perfect warm with butter or alongside a braai.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C and grease a loaf tin.
Mix the polenta, flour, baking powder, salt and sugar.
Whisk the eggs, milk and butter, then stir into the dry mix with the corn and cheese.
Pour into the tin and bake for 45 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Rest in the tin for 10 minutes before slicing.

notes: Food safety: the egg is cooked once a skewer comes out clean and the centre reaches at least 75°C.
Serve with butter and chakalaka.

title: South African Peri-Peri Basting Sauce
summary: A smoky garlic and chilli sauce for basting chicken, prawns or halloumi.

steps.text: Blitz the chillies, capsicum, garlic, lemon juice, vinegar, paprika and oregano to a chunky sauce.
Heat the oil in a pan and cook the sauce for 8 minutes until darker and thicker.
Season with salt and cool.
Store in a jar in the fridge for up to 2 weeks.

notes: Food safety: use a clean spoon each time, and bring any marinade that touched raw chicken to the boil before using as a sauce, cooking the chicken to 75°C.
Swap in dried chilli for more smoke.

title: Savoury Vetkoek Buns Filled with Spiced Beef
summary: Crisp, airy fried bread buns split and filled with fragrant curried beef mince.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the warm water and knead for 5 minutes until the dough is soft, then rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Fry the onion in a little oil for 5 minutes until soft, add the mince and garlic and brown for 6 minutes.
Stir in the curry powder, tomatoes and chutney and simmer for 15 minutes until thick.
Heat the oil to 170°C and fry golf-ball sized pieces of dough for 5 minutes, turning, until deep golden and cooked in the middle.
Split the vetkoek and spoon in the mince.

notes: Food safety: cook the mince until it reaches 75°C with no pink remaining.
Resting time is not counted in the prep time.

title: Pampoenkoekies Pumpkin Fritters
summary: Cinnamon-sugar pumpkin fritters, a traditional South African side with roasts.

steps.text: Mix the pumpkin, flour, baking powder, egg, 1 tbsp sugar and salt into a thick batter.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat.
Spoon in tablespoons of batter and fry for 3 minutes each side until golden and cooked in the middle.
Drain and roll in the remaining sugar mixed with the cinnamon.

notes: Food safety: cook the fritters until golden and set in the middle.
Roast the pumpkin first for the best flavour.

title: Palusami Spinach in Coconut Cream
summary: Samoan-style parcels of greens baked in coconut cream with onion, a luscious side for roasts.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C and lightly grease a baking dish.
Mix the coconut cream with the onion, salt and lemon juice.
Layer the spinach in a baking dish and pour over the coconut mixture.
Cover with foil and bake for 25 minutes until the greens are soft and the cream has thickened.
Stir well until creamy and serve hot alongside roast meat or fish.

notes: Traditionally made with taro leaves.
Serve with roast pork, fish or sweet potato.

title: Hawaiian-Style Macaroni Salad
summary: A creamy plate-lunch macaroni salad with carrot, onion and a touch of sweetness.

steps.text: Cook the macaroni until completely soft, a minute longer than the packet, then drain and rinse.
Whisk the mayonnaise, vinegar, sugar, salt and pepper in a bowl.
Fold through the warm macaroni, carrot, onion and celery.
Chill for at least 1 hour before serving.

notes: Serve with rice and grilled meat as a plate lunch.
The pasta absorbs the dressing, so loosen with milk if needed.

title: Lomi Lomi Smoked Salmon Salad
summary: Hawaiian-style salad of salmon, tomato and sweet onion, fresh and bright with lime.

steps.text: Mix the salmon, tomatoes, onion and spring onions in a bowl.
Add the lime juice, oil, salt and chilli flakes and toss gently.
Chill until cold, about 15 minutes, so the flavours mingle.
Serve in small bowls with rice or crackers.

notes: Use fresh sashimi-grade salmon only if you are confident of its source; smoked salmon is the safer option.
Serve with rice or crackers.

title: Kumara Hash with Fried Egg and Spring Onion
summary: Crisp pan-fried sweet potato hash topped with a runny-yolk egg.

steps.text: Toss the sweet potato with the salt and paprika.
Fry in the coconut oil in a wide pan over medium heat for 12 minutes, turning, until crisp and golden.
Make two wells and crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 4 minutes until the whites are set.
Scatter with spring onion and coriander.

notes: Food safety: cook the egg whites until completely set; cook the yolk through for children, pregnant women and the elderly.
Add chilli for kick.

title: Fijian Fish and Coconut Soup
summary: A light, lime-bright broth of coconut milk, fresh fish and tomatoes.

steps.text: Cook the onion, garlic and ginger in a little coconut milk for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes, stock and remaining coconut milk and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the fish and chilli and simmer gently for 5 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Finish with the lime juice, salt and coriander.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, with an internal temperature of at least 63°C.
Do not boil hard or the fish will break up.

title: Lobster Bisque with Cognac Cream
summary: A velvety shellfish soup built on a roasted lobster shell stock, finished with brandy and cream.

steps.text: Cut the lobster tails in chunks, shell on, and sear in the butter for 4 minutes until the shells turn red, then lift out the meat once it is opaque and set aside.
Cook the onion, carrot, celery and garlic in the same pot for 8 minutes until golden.
Stir in the tomato paste for 2 minutes, add the brandy and let it bubble until nearly gone.
Add the stock, thyme, bay leaf and the lobster shells and simmer for 40 minutes.
Strain the stock, pressing hard on the shells, then whisk in the rice flour and simmer for 5 minutes until lightly thickened.
Stir in the cream, cayenne and salt and add the chopped lobster meat for 1 minute until heated through.

notes: Food safety: cook the lobster until the flesh is opaque and firm.
Do not boil after adding the cream or it may split.

title: Shoyu Ramen with Ajitama Marinated Eggs
summary: A soy-seasoned chicken and kombu broth with springy noodles, a marinated jammy egg and spring onion.

steps.text: Simmer the stock with the kombu and shiitake for 20 minutes, then lift out the kombu and strain.
Boil the eggs for 6.5 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks jammy, then cool in iced water and peel.
Marinate the eggs in 2 tbsp soy sauce and the mirin for at least 4 hours, turning now and then.
Sear the pork belly in the sesame oil for 8 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Season the broth with the remaining soy sauce and sake and keep hot.
Cook the noodles until just tender, drain and divide among bowls.
Ladle over the hot broth and top with pork, halved eggs, nori and spring onion.

notes: Marinating time is not counted in the prep time.

Food safety: cook the pork until it reaches an internal temperature of 70°C, and serve jammy eggs only to healthy adults. Use fresh, uncracked eggs; for pregnant women, older people, young children and anyone with low immunity, cook the eggs until the yolks are firm.

title: Laksa Lemak from Scratch
summary: A coconut curry noodle soup made with a fresh spice paste, prawns, tofu puffs and herbs.

steps.text: Blitz the shallots, garlic, galangal, lemongrass, chillies, turmeric and shrimp paste to a fine paste.
Fry the paste in the oil for 8 minutes until darker and the oil separates.
Add the stock and simmer for 10 minutes, then stir in the coconut milk and fish sauce.
Cook the noodles in boiling water until tender, drain and divide among bowls.
Add the prawns and tofu puffs to the broth for 3 minutes until the prawns are pink and opaque.
Ladle over the noodles and top with sprouts, mint and lime.

notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until pink and opaque.
Use vegetable stock and extra tofu to make it vegetarian, swapping the fish sauce for soy.

title: Pozole Rojo
summary: A hominy and pork stew in a smoky dried chilli broth, topped with cabbage, radish and lime.
