steps.text: Simmer the pork with the onion, 3 garlic cloves and the stock for 1 hour, skimming the surface.
Blend the soaked chillies with the remaining garlic, oregano, cumin and a ladle of broth until smooth, then strain.
Stir the chilli sauce into the pot with the corn and salt.
Simmer for 1 hour more until the pork is tender and falls apart.
Serve in bowls topped with the cabbage, radish, coriander and a squeeze of lime.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork until it reaches at least 75°C and is fork tender.
Hominy is traditional; sweetcorn is an easy swap.

title: Ham and Poached Egg Muffins with Lemon Butter Sauce
summary: Poached eggs and ham on toasted English muffins under a warm lemony hollandaise.

steps.text: Whisk the egg yolks and lemon juice in a heatproof bowl over a pot of barely simmering water for 4 minutes until pale and thick.
Slowly whisk in the melted butter until the sauce is glossy, then season with the cayenne and keep warm.
Bring a wide pan of water with the vinegar to a gentle simmer and poach the eggs for 3 minutes until the whites are set.
Toast the muffins until golden and top each half with ham.
Lift on the poached eggs and spoon over the hollandaise.

notes: Serve immediately; hollandaise does not reheat well.

Food safety: whisk the yolks over the heat until they reach about 70°C, and cook the poached eggs until the whites are fully set. This uses raw or lightly cooked egg: pregnant women, older people, young children and anyone with low immunity should skip it or use pasteurised eggs. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Sauce Bearnaise
summary: A classic tarragon, shallot and vinegar butter sauce for steak, asparagus and fish.

steps.text: Simmer the vinegar, wine, shallots, half the tarragon and the pepper for 6 minutes until reduced to about 2 tablespoons, then strain.
Melt the butter and keep warm.
Whisk the yolks with the reduction in a bowl over barely simmering water for 4 minutes until thick and pale.
Slowly whisk in the butter until glossy, then stir through the remaining tarragon and season with salt.

notes: Food safety: whisk the yolks over the heat until they reach about 70°C.
Serve warm; it splits if overheated, so whisk in a teaspoon of cold water to rescue it.

title: Crisp Fermented Dosa Rolled Around Turmeric Potato
summary: Crisp fermented rice and lentil crepes folded around a turmeric potato and onion masala.

steps.text: Soak the rice, lentils and fenugreek in water for 6 hours, then blend with enough water to a smooth batter and ferment covered overnight until bubbly.
Stir the salt into the batter.
Pop the mustard seeds in 1 tbsp oil for 30 seconds until they crackle, then add the curry leaves, chilli and onion and cook for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the turmeric and potatoes, mash lightly and cook for 5 minutes until fragrant, then add the coriander.
Heat a non-stick pan, pour a ladle of batter and spread thin, then drizzle with oil.
Cook for 3 minutes until crisp and golden underneath, then fill and fold.

notes: Soaking and fermenting time are not counted in the prep time.
Serve with coconut chutney or sambar.

title: Cheese Souffle with Vegetarian Hard Cheese
summary: A tall, golden souffle with a soft centre, made with vegetarian hard cheese.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C and butter four ramekins.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk until a smooth, thick sauce forms.
Take off the heat, beat in the yolks, vegetarian hard cheese, mustard, nutmeg, cayenne and salt.
Whisk the egg whites until stiff peaks form and fold in gently in two batches.
Spoon into the ramekins and bake for 20 minutes until risen and golden.
Serve straight away at the table.

notes: Food safety: bake until the souffle is set and the centre is at least 70°C, especially for anyone vulnerable.
Do not open the oven door early.

title: Pumpkin Seed Egusi-Style Soup
summary: A thick West African soup of ground seeds, tomato and greens, usually made with egusi melon seeds.

steps.text: Blend the tomatoes, capsicum and half the onion with the scotch bonnet until smooth.
Fry the remaining onion in the oil for 6 minutes until soft, then add the blended mix and cook for 12 minutes until the oil rises to the top.
Stir in the ground seeds and stock and simmer for 15 minutes until thick.
Add the chicken and simmer for 12 minutes until cooked through.
Stir through the spinach until wilted and season with salt.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C with no pink remaining.
Omit the chicken for a vegan soup.

title: Beurre Blanc
summary: A light white wine and shallot butter sauce for steamed or grilled fish.

steps.text: Simmer the shallots, wine and vinegar for 8 minutes until reduced to about 2 tablespoons and almost syrupy.
Lower the heat and whisk in the cold butter one cube at a time until the sauce is smooth and creamy.
Season with the lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Strain if you want a smooth sauce and serve at once.

notes: Keep the sauce warm, not hot, or it will split.
Serve with poached salmon or asparagus.

title: Caramelised Onion Soup with Gruyere Toasts
summary: Deeply caramelised onions in beef broth, topped with a toasted cheese crouton.

steps.text: Cook the onions in the butter, oil and sugar over medium-low heat for 45 minutes, stirring, until deep golden brown.
Add the garlic for 1 minute, then pour in the wine and let it reduce by half.
Add the stock and thyme and simmer for 20 minutes.
Heat the grill until very hot, ladle the soup into ovenproof bowls and float a slice of baguette on each.
Top with the gruyere and grill for 4 minutes until bubbling and golden.

notes: Use vegetable stock if you prefer, though the soup will taste lighter.
Gruyere is made with animal rennet, so this is not vegetarian.

title: Tomato Clam Chowder with Bacon and Thyme
summary: A tomato-based clam chowder with bacon, potato and celery, lighter than the New England style.

steps.text: Fry the bacon for 6 minutes until crisp, then add the onion, celery and carrot for 6 minutes until soft.
Stir in the tomatoes, stock, potatoes, thyme and bay leaf and simmer for 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Add the clams, cover and cook for 5 minutes until the shells have opened.
Discard any that stay shut and scatter with parsley.

notes: Food safety: cook the clams until their shells have opened and discard any that do not open.
Tinned clams work in a pinch, added at the end.

title: Cullen Skink Smoked Fish Soup
summary: A creamy Scottish soup of potato, onion and smoked white fish.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the butter for 5 minutes until translucent.
Add the potatoes, stock and bay leaf and simmer for 12 minutes until the potato is tender.
Pour in the milk, add the fish and simmer for 5 minutes until the fish turns opaque and flakes.
Lightly crush some potato to thicken, stir in the cream and pepper and scatter with chives.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, with an internal temperature of at least 63°C.
Use smoked haddock if you can find it.

title: Mulligatawny Soup with Chicken
summary: A fragrant curried lentil soup with chicken and apple, from the Anglo-Indian kitchen.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 6 minutes until soft, then add the garlic and curry powder for 1 minute.
Add the apple, lentils, chicken and stock and simmer for 25 minutes until the lentils are soft and the chicken is cooked through.
Lift out the chicken, shred it and blend the soup until smooth.
Return the chicken with the coconut milk and heat through, then add the lemon juice.
Serve topped with coriander.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C with no pink remaining.
Skip the chicken for a vegan soup.

title: Caldo Verde with Chorizo
summary: A Portuguese-style potato and kale soup with sliced chorizo and olive oil.

steps.text: Cook the onion and garlic in 1 tbsp oil for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the potatoes and stock and simmer for 18 minutes until completely tender.
Fry the chorizo in a pan for 4 minutes until crisp and cooked through.
Mash or blend the soup until almost smooth, add the kale and simmer for 5 minutes until tender.
Serve topped with the chorizo and a drizzle of oil.

notes: Food safety: cook the chorizo until it reaches 75°C and is crisp.
Cut the kale very finely for the right texture.

title: Lemon Egg Thickened Chicken and Rice Soup from Greece
summary: A silky Greek soup of chicken, rice and an egg and lemon liaison.

steps.text: Simmer the chicken in the stock for 15 minutes until cooked through, then lift out and shred.
Add the rice to the stock and cook for 12 minutes until tender.
Whisk the eggs with the lemon juice until frothy, then whisk in a ladle of hot stock slowly.
Pour the mixture back into the pot off the heat, stirring until the soup turns creamy and slightly thickened.
Return the chicken, season and top with dill.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C and do not boil the soup after adding the egg or it will curdle.
The egg cooks gently from the heat of the soup.

title: Lamb Harira
summary: A Moroccan soup of lamb, lentils, chickpeas, tomato and warm spices, traditionally served to break the Ramadan fast.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil for 6 minutes until coloured, then add the onion, celery and spices for 4 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in the tomatoes, tomato paste, lentils and water and simmer for 35 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and simmer for 15 minutes until the lamb is tender and the lentils are soft.
Finish with the lemon juice and coriander.

notes: Food safety: cook the lamb until tender, with an internal temperature of at least 70°C.
Serve with dates and lemon wedges.

title: Nigerian-Style Chicken Pepper Soup
summary: A fiery, aromatic clear soup scented with ground spices, ginger and scotch bonnet.

steps.text: Put the chicken, water, onion, ginger, garlic, scotch bonnet and spices in a pot.
Bring to the boil, then simmer for 30 minutes until the chicken is tender and cooked through.
Season with salt and add the basil for the last 2 minutes.
Serve hot in mugs or bowls.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C and the juices run clear.
Prick the scotch bonnet for more heat.

title: West African Groundnut Soup with Chicken
summary: A rich peanut and tomato soup with chicken, ginger and a little chilli.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil for 5 minutes, then lift out.
Cook the onion, garlic and ginger in the same pot for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes, cumin and scotch bonnet and cook for 8 minutes until pulpy.
Whisk in the peanut butter and stock, return the chicken and simmer for 20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Add the spinach until wilted and remove the scotch bonnet.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C.
Use pumpkin or sweet potato for a vegetarian version.

title: Ukrainian Borscht with Beef
summary: A deep red beetroot soup with beef, cabbage and potato, finished with sour cream and dill.

steps.text: Simmer the beef in the stock for 60 minutes until tender.
Fry the onion, carrot and beetroot in the oil for 10 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste and vinegar.
Add the potatoes to the pot and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the beetroot mix and cabbage and simmer for 15 minutes until all vegetables are tender.
Serve with the sour cream and dill.

notes: Food safety: simmer the beef until tender, with an internal temperature of at least 75°C.
The vinegar keeps the colour bright.

title: Root Vegetable Scotch Broth with Lamb Shoulder
summary: A hearty soup of lamb shoulder, pearl barley and root vegetables.

steps.text: Simmer the lamb with the barley and water, skimming off foam, for 40 minutes.
Add the onion, carrots, leek, swede and thyme and simmer for 35 minutes until the lamb is tender and the barley soft.
Add the cabbage and cook for 5 minutes until just tender.
Season with salt and serve with parsley.

notes: Food safety: cook the lamb until tender, with an internal temperature of at least 70°C.
Soup thickens overnight, so loosen with stock.

title: Canh Chua Vietnamese Sour Fish Soup
summary: A tamarind-sour fish soup with tomato, pineapple and bean sprouts.

steps.text: Simmer the stock with the tamarind, garlic, fish sauce and sugar for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, pineapple and celery and simmer for 5 minutes until just soft.
Add the fish and cook gently for 4 minutes until opaque and flaking.
Stir in the sprouts and chilli and top with coriander.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, with an internal temperature of at least 63°C.
Taste and balance the sour and sweet.

title: Tom Kha Gai Chicken Coconut Soup
summary: Galangal, lemongrass and lime leaf in a rich coconut broth with tender chicken.

steps.text: Simmer the stock, galangal, lemongrass and lime leaves for 10 minutes until fragrant.
Add the coconut milk, mushrooms and chicken and simmer gently for 8 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Season with the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar and chillies.
Top with coriander and serve without eating the whole aromatics.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C with no pink remaining.
Do not boil hard or the coconut milk may split.

title: Korean Knife-Cut Noodle Soup with Chicken and Zucchini
summary: Hand-cut style wheat noodles in a clean chicken broth with zucchini and potato.

steps.text: Simmer the stock, chicken and garlic for 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through, then lift out and shred.
Add the potato and simmer for 8 minutes until tender.
Add the noodles and zucchini and cook for 4 minutes until the noodles are tender.
Whisk the egg and stream it in, stirring until it sets in ribbons.
Season with soy and sesame oil and return the chicken.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C and the egg until fully set.
Top with kimchi if you like.

title: Tonjiru Japanese Pork and Vegetable Miso Soup
summary: A hearty miso soup stocked with pork, daikon, carrot and tofu.

steps.text: Fry the pork in the sesame oil for 4 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Add the dashi, daikon, carrot and potato and simmer for 12 minutes until tender.
Stir in the tofu and heat for 2 minutes.
Remove from the heat, whisk in the miso and serve with spring onion.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork until it reaches at least 70°C with no pink.
Do not boil the soup after adding miso.

title: Peppery Black Vinegar Soup with Pork, Tofu and Egg Ribbons
summary: A peppery vinegary soup of pork, mushrooms, tofu and ribbons of egg.

steps.text: Simmer the stock with the pork and mushrooms for 8 minutes until the pork is cooked through.
Add the tofu, vinegar, soy sauce and pepper.
Stir the cornflour with 3 tbsp water and add until the soup thickens slightly.
Stream in the whisked eggs, stirring gently until they form ribbons.
Finish with sesame oil and spring onions.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork mince until it reaches 75°C with no pink.
Cook the egg ribbons until fully set.

title: Hungarian Goulash Soup
summary: A paprika-rich beef and potato soup with caraway.

steps.text: Brown the beef in the oil for 6 minutes until coloured, then remove.
Cook the onions for 8 minutes until golden, then add the garlic, paprika, caraway and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Return the beef and add the stock, then simmer for 60 minutes until the beef is tender.
Add the potatoes and capsicum and simmer for 20 minutes until soft.
Season with the salt and rest for 5 minutes before serving.

notes: Food safety: simmer the beef until tender, with an internal temperature of at least 75°C.
Take the pan off the heat when adding paprika to avoid bitterness.

title: Nasi Lemak Breakfast Plate
summary: Coconut rice with sambal, a fried egg, crispy anchovies, peanuts and cucumber.

steps.text: Cook the rice with the coconut milk, water, lime leaves and salt covered on low heat for 18 minutes until the grains are tender.
Fry the anchovies and peanuts in half the oil for 3 minutes until crisp.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil until the whites are set.
Serve the rice with the eggs, anchovies, peanuts, cucumber and sambal.

notes: Food safety: cook the egg whites until fully set, and refrigerate leftover rice within an hour.
Pandan leaves can replace the lime leaves if you can find them.

title: Kelewele Spiced Fried Plantain
summary: Ghanaian ripe plantain cubes tossed in ginger, chilli and cloves, fried until caramelised.

steps.text: Toss the plantain with the ginger, chilli, cloves, salt and lime juice.
Heat the oil to 175°C in a deep pan.
Fry in batches for 3 minutes until deep golden and crisp at the edges.
Drain on paper towel and serve hot with peanuts.

notes: Take care with hot oil.
Serve with roasted peanuts.

title: Suya Spice Rub and Yaji Mix
summary: A peanutty chilli spice mix for grilled meat, vegetables and tofu.

steps.text: Blitz the peanuts in a food processor until fine and sandy.
Mix with the paprika, ginger, garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne, salt and cloves.
Toast in a dry pan for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Store in a jar for up to 2 months.

notes: Food safety: when using the rub on chicken, cook to 75°C; on beef, cook to at least 70°C.
Rub on meat or vegetables with a little oil.

title: Shito Ghanaian Black Pepper Sauce
summary: A dark, savoury chilli oil sauce of dried shrimp, onions and ginger.

steps.text: Heat the oil and fry the onions for 15 minutes until deep golden.
Blitz the ginger, garlic and chillies to a paste and add with the shrimp and tomato paste.
Cook, stirring, for 20 minutes until dark and the oil separates.
Add the chilli flakes, salt and fish sauce and cook for 3 minutes.
Cool, then store in a clean jar.

notes: Keeps for 2 months in the fridge.
Serve with rice, eggs and fried plantain.

title: Nigerian Akara Bean Puffs with Scotch Bonnet
summary: Crisp, fluffy fried bean fritters from Nigeria, eaten for breakfast with pap or bread.

steps.text: Blitz the beans with the onion, scotch bonnet, salt and water to a thick, fluffy batter.
Beat the batter with a spoon for 2 minutes until it holds a peak.
Heat the oil to 175°C in a pan.
Spoon in tablespoons of batter and fry for 4 minutes, turning, until deep golden and cooked in the middle.
Drain on paper towel and serve hot.

notes: Take care with hot oil.
Use dried beans soaked overnight and peeled for the traditional texture.

title: Nuoc Cham Vietnamese Dipping Sauce
summary: A sweet, sour, salty and spicy sauce for spring rolls, noodles and grilled meat.

steps.text: Stir the sugar into the warm water until dissolved.
Add the fish sauce and lime juice.
Stir in the garlic and chilli and let it rest for 10 minutes.
Taste and adjust the balance until sweet, sour and salty.

notes: Keeps for 1 week in the fridge.
Use soy sauce for a vegetarian version.

title: Do Chua Pickled Carrot and Daikon
summary: A crunchy sweet pickle for banh mi, noodle bowls and grilled meats.

steps.text: Dissolve the sugar and salt in the warm water and vinegar.
Pack the carrot and daikon into a clean jar.
Pour over the pickling liquid until covered.
Chill for 2 hours until tangy and crisp.

notes: Keeps for 3 weeks in the fridge.
Salt the daikon first for 10 minutes for extra crunch.

title: Goi Ga Vietnamese Chicken and Cabbage Salad
summary: Shredded chicken, cabbage, carrot and herbs in a lime and fish sauce dressing.

steps.text: Poach the chicken in simmering water for 12 minutes until cooked through, then cool and shred.
Whisk the fish sauce, lime juice and sugar.
Toss the chicken, cabbage, carrot, onion and herbs with the dressing.
Top with peanuts and fried shallots.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C and the juices run clear.
Dress just before serving.

title: Banh Mi Style Fried Eggs on Baguette
summary: Crisp baguette with fried eggs, pickles, chilli, coriander and a squirt of soy.

steps.text: Toast the baguette until crisp.
Fry the eggs in the oil until the whites are set and edges crisp.
Spread the baguette with the mayonnaise.
Fill with the eggs, cucumber, coriander, chilli and pickle.
Splash with the soy sauce and serve.

notes: Food safety: cook the egg whites until fully set, and cook the yolks through for children and pregnant women.
Use the Do Chua pickle if you have it.

title: Tofu Scramble with Spinach and Tomato
summary: A savoury vegan scramble spiced with turmeric and smoked paprika.

steps.text: Heat the oil and add the tofu, turmeric, paprika and salt.
Cook, stirring, for 6 minutes until the tofu is golden and dry.
Add the tomato and spinach until the spinach is wilted.
Scatter with spring onion and serve.

notes: Serve on toast for breakfast.
The nutritional yeast adds a cheesy flavour.

title: Chickpea Flour Omelette with Herbs
summary: A vegan, high-protein savoury pancake with spring onion, coriander and chilli.

steps.text: Whisk the chickpea flour, water, turmeric, cumin and salt to a smooth batter.
Stir in the spring onions, coriander and chilli.
Heat half the oil in a non-stick pan and pour in half the batter.
Cook for 3 minutes until set and golden underneath, flip and cook for 2 minutes.
Repeat with the remaining batter.

notes: Serve with tomato chutney or yoghurt.
Rest the batter for 10 minutes for a softer texture.

title: High-Protein Egg White Frittata Cups
summary: Muffin-sized baked frittatas with spinach, feta and capsicum, easy to batch for the week.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C and grease a 6-hole muffin tin.
Whisk the eggs, egg whites, salt and pepper.
Divide the spinach, capsicum, feta and spring onion among the holes.
Pour in the egg and bake for 18 minutes until puffed and set in the centre.

notes: Food safety: bake until the egg is completely set, with an internal temperature of at least 71°C.
Keeps for 4 days in the fridge or freezes well.

title: Lentil and Kale Salad with Lemon Tahini Dressing
summary: A hearty vegan, high-protein salad with warm lentils, kale, roasted pumpkin and a creamy dressing.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C and roast the pumpkin with 1 tbsp oil for 25 minutes until golden.
Simmer the lentils in plenty of water for 20 minutes until tender but still holding their shape, then drain.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, water and salt until creamy.
Toss the warm lentils with the kale, onion, pumpkin and remaining oil.
Drizzle with the dressing.

notes: Lightly massage the kale to soften it.
Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

title: Edamame and Quinoa Salad with Sesame Dressing
summary: A gluten-free, vegan high-protein salad with edamame, quinoa, cucumber and a tamari dressing.

steps.text: Rinse the quinoa and simmer in 400ml water for 15 minutes until the grains are tender with a visible curl.
Cook the edamame in boiling water for 4 minutes until bright green, then drain.
Whisk the tamari, vinegar, sesame oil and ginger.
Toss the quinoa, edamame, cucumber, carrot and spring onions with the dressing.
Scatter with the sesame seeds and serve.

notes: Serve cold or at room temperature.
Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

title: Caribbean Doubles with Curried Chickpeas
summary: Trinidad street-food breakfast of soft fried flatbreads topped with spiced chickpeas and tamarind sauce.

steps.text: Mix the flour, baking powder, turmeric, salt, yeast and water to a soft dough, knead for 5 minutes and rest for 1 hour until doubled.
Fry the onion and garlic for 5 minutes until soft, then add the curry powder, chickpeas and a splash of water.
Simmer for 15 minutes until thick and the chickpeas are very soft, mashing some.
Stir the tamarind and finely chopped scotch bonnet into a spoon of hot water for the sauce.
Flatten small balls of dough into thin rounds and fry in hot oil at 175°C for 30 seconds each side until puffed and pale gold.
Top two bara with the chickpeas and a drizzle of tamarind sauce.

notes: Rest time is not counted in the prep time.
Take care with hot oil.

title: Cuban-Style Black Bean Soup
summary: A smoky black bean soup with garlic, cumin and a splash of vinegar, topped with raw onion.

steps.text: Soften the onion and capsicum in the oil for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, cumin and oregano for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the beans, stock and bay leaf and simmer for 25 minutes until thick.
Mash some beans, stir in the vinegar and top with the red onion.

notes: Serve with rice.
Naturally vegan and gluten-free.

title: Supu ya Samaki Swahili Coconut Fish Soup
summary: A light, tangy fish and tomato soup from the Swahili coast with coconut milk, lime and coriander.

steps.text: Cook the onion and garlic in a splash of coconut milk for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the turmeric, cumin and tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until pulpy.
Pour in the stock and remaining coconut milk and simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the fish and simmer gently for 4 minutes until opaque and flaking.
Finish with the lime juice, coriander and salt.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, with an internal temperature of at least 63°C.
Serve with chapati or rice.

title: Timatim Ethiopian Tomato Salad
summary: Juicy tomatoes with onion, green chilli and a sharp lemon dressing.

steps.text: Combine the tomatoes, onion and chilli in a bowl.
Whisk the lemon juice, oil, garlic and salt.
Toss the dressing through the salad.
Rest for 5 minutes until the juices mingle, then serve.

notes: Serve with injera or flatbread.
Use ripe summer tomatoes for the best flavour.

title: Chapati Kenyan Layered Flatbread
summary: Soft, layered flatbreads rolled and fried until flaky, for dipping in stews.

steps.text: Mix the flour, salt and sugar, add the water and 1 tbsp oil and knead for 8 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Rest for 20 minutes, then divide into 6 balls.
Roll each ball thin, brush with oil, roll into a rope and coil into a spiral.
Roll out each spiral to 3mm thick.
Cook in a dry pan for 2 minutes each side, brushing with oil, until golden with brown spots.

notes: Resting time is not counted in the prep time.
Eat warm or wrap in a cloth to keep soft.

title: Githeri Kenyan Beans and Corn
summary: A rustic dish of beans and maize stewed with tomato and onion.

steps.text: Fry the onion in the oil for 6 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the garlic, coriander and tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until pulpy.
Stir in the beans, corn, water and salt and simmer for 15 minutes until thick.
Serve topped with coriander.

notes: Add kale or cabbage if you want more greens.
Naturally vegan.

title: Zanzibar Spiced Pilau Rice
summary: Fragrant rice cooked with cumin, cardamom, cinnamon and cloves.

steps.text: Fry the onion in the oil for 10 minutes until deep brown.
Add the cumin, cardamom, cinnamon and cloves for 1 minute, then the garlic and ginger.
Add the rinsed rice and stir for 2 minutes.
Pour in the stock and salt, cover and cook on low heat for 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.
Rest for 10 minutes, then fluff.

notes: Food safety: cool leftover rice quickly and refrigerate within an hour, reheating until steaming hot.
Add cooked beef for a meat pilau.

title: Pancit Molo Filipino Wonton Soup
summary: Pork and prawn dumplings in a clear garlic chicken broth.

steps.text: Mix the pork, prawns, spring onion, soy sauce and pepper.
Spoon a teaspoon onto each wrapper, wet the edges and fold into parcels.
Fry the garlic in the oil for 2 minutes until golden, then add the stock and fish sauce and bring to a simmer.
Drop in the dumplings and cook for 6 minutes until they float and the filling is cooked through.
Top with the fried shallots and serve hot.

notes: Food safety: cook the dumplings until the pork reaches 75°C and the prawns are pink and opaque.
Freeze uncooked dumplings for later.

title: Champorado Chocolate Rice Porridge
summary: Filipino breakfast porridge of glutinous rice and cocoa, drizzled with milk.

steps.text: Simmer the rice in the water for 25 minutes, stirring, until soft and thick.
Stir in the cocoa, sugar and salt until dissolved.
Cook for 5 minutes until glossy.
Serve with the milk poured over.

notes: Add more water for a looser porridge.
Traditionally served with salty dried fish.

title: Perkedel Jagung Indonesian Corn Fritters
summary: Crisp corn fritters with spring onion and a hint of coriander.

steps.text: Mash half the corn with the garlic, then mix with the remaining corn, flour, egg, spring onions, coriander and salt.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat.
Spoon in the batter and fry for 3 minutes each side until golden and cooked in the middle.
Drain and serve with sambal.

notes: Food safety: cook the fritters until golden and fully set in the middle.
Serve with sweet chilli sauce.

title: Loco Moco Hawaiian Breakfast Plate
summary: Rice topped with a beef patty, fried egg and rich onion gravy.

steps.text: Cook the rice in boiling water for 12 minutes until tender, then drain and keep warm.
Mix the mince with the salt and pepper, shape into two patties and fry for 4 minutes each side until browned and cooked through.
Fry the onion in the butter for 6 minutes until golden, stir in the flour, then add the stock and soy and simmer until thick.
Fry the eggs until the whites are set.
Serve the patties on rice with the eggs and gravy.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef patties until they reach 75°C with no pink.
Cook the egg whites until set.

title: Tonkotsu-Style Pork Rib Broth Ramen
summary: A milky, collagen-rich pork rib broth simmered for hours, served with noodles, soft egg and sesame.

steps.text: Boil the pork ribs in water for 10 minutes, then drain and rinse the ribs and pot.

Return the ribs to the pot with the fresh water, onion, garlic, ginger and spring onion and boil hard for 3 hours, topping up with hot water, until the broth turns cloudy and the meat falls off the bone.
Strain the broth and season with the soy sauce, mirin and sesame oil.
Boil the eggs for 6.5 minutes until jammy, then cool in iced water and peel.
Cook the noodles until just tender and divide among bowls.
Ladle over the hot broth and top with pulled rib meat, halved eggs and sesame seeds.

notes: Boil hard, not gently, to get the milky broth.

Food safety: cook the pork until it reaches at least 75°C and is falling off the bone, and serve jammy eggs only to healthy adults. Use fresh, uncracked eggs; for pregnant women, older people, young children and anyone with low immunity, cook the eggs until the yolks are firm.

title: Coq au Vin Blanc Style Chicken Soup
summary: A white-wine chicken soup with mushrooms, pearl onions and bacon, finished with cream and thyme.

steps.text: Brown the chicken skin side down in the butter for 8 minutes until deep golden, then lift out.
Fry the bacon, onions and mushrooms in the same pot for 8 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic, then the wine and let it reduce by half.
Return the chicken and add the stock, thyme and bay leaf and simmer for 40 minutes until the meat is falling from the bone.
Shred the meat, discard the skin and bones, stir in the cream and return the chicken.
Serve in warm bowls with the chopped parsley on top.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C and the juices run clear.
Serve with crusty bread.

title: Cioppino San Francisco Seafood Stew
summary: A tomato and wine seafood stew with clams, prawns and white fish, finished with parsley.

steps.text: Soften the onion and celery in the oil for 8 minutes until translucent, then add the garlic and chilli.
Pour in the wine and reduce by half, then add the tomatoes, stock and bay leaf and simmer for 25 minutes until rich.
Add the fish and clams, cover and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the mussels and prawns and cook for 3 minutes until the shells open and the prawns are pink and opaque.
Discard any shellfish that stay shut and finish with parsley.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, the prawns until pink and opaque, and discard any shells that do not open.
Serve with sourdough.

title: Duck and Mushroom Consomme Dumpling Soup
summary: A clear spiced duck broth with delicate duck and mushroom dumplings.

steps.text: Simmer the duck legs with the water, star anise, ginger and spring onions for 90 minutes, skimming, until the meat is tender.
Lift out the duck, shred the meat and strain the broth.
Fry the mushrooms in the sesame oil for 6 minutes until golden, then mix with half the duck, shaoxing wine and half the soy.
Fold spoonfuls into wonton wrappers, sealing the edges with water.
Season the broth with the remaining soy and pepper and bring to a simmer until steaming.
Cook the dumplings for 4 minutes until they float and the filling is hot.
Serve with sliced spring onion.

notes: Food safety: cook the duck until it reaches 75°C and is fork tender.
Save the remaining duck for another meal.

title: Cassava Leaf Style Greens in Peanut Sauce
summary: Silky greens stewed in a peanut and tomato sauce, a Sierra Leone-inspired side.

steps.text: Fry the onion and garlic in the oil for 6 minutes until golden.
Add the tomatoes and scotch bonnet and cook for 8 minutes until reduced.
Whisk in the peanut butter and water until smooth.
Add the kale and simmer for 20 minutes until completely tender and the oil rises.
Season with salt and remove the scotch bonnet.

notes: Serve over rice or with plantain.
Naturally vegan and gluten-free.

title: Ghanaian Light Soup with Chicken and Eggplant
summary: A thin, peppery tomato soup with chicken, eggplant and ginger.

steps.text: Blend the onion, tomatoes, ginger and scotch bonnet until smooth.
Pour into a pot with the chicken, water and salt.
Bring to the boil, then simmer for 25 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Add the eggplant and simmer for 10 minutes until soft.
Season with the pepper and serve hot with rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C and the juices run clear.
Serve with rice balls or fufu.

title: Rawon-Inspired Black Beef Soup
summary: An East Javanese beef soup with a dark spice paste, lemongrass and lime leaves.

steps.text: Blitz the shallots, garlic, macadamias, coriander, turmeric and galangal to a paste.
Fry the paste in the oil for 8 minutes until fragrant and darker.
Add the beef, water, lemongrass, lime leaves, dark soy and salt.
Simmer for 2 hours until the beef is very tender.
Serve topped with bean sprouts and spring onion.

notes: Food safety: simmer the beef until tender, with an internal temperature of at least 75°C.
Serve with rice and sambal.

title: Rice Flour Crepes with Cream Cheese and Warm Berries
summary: Delicate crepes made with rice flour, filled with berries and cream cheese.

steps.text: Whisk the rice flour, cornflour, eggs, milk, melted butter and salt until smooth, then rest for 15 minutes.
Heat a non-stick pan and add a thin layer of batter.
Cook for 1 minute each side until pale gold and set, making 8 crepes.
Warm the berries with the honey for 3 minutes until juicy.
Spread the crepes with cream cheese, fill with berries and fold.

notes: Food safety: cook the crepes until the egg is fully set.
Rest time is not counted in the prep time.

title: Smoky Kumara and Black Bean Pan Hash
summary: A vegan, gluten-free hash of diced sweet potato, black beans, capsicum and lime.

steps.text: Fry the sweet potato in the oil for 12 minutes, stirring, until golden and tender.
Add the onion and capsicum for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the spices and beans and cook for 4 minutes until hot.
Finish with the lime juice and coriander and top with avocado.

notes: Add fried eggs for extra protein.
Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

title: Moroccan Spiced Chickpea Breakfast Bowl
summary: A vegan, high-protein bowl of warm spiced chickpeas, tomato and herbs with tahini.

steps.text: Heat the oil and fry the chickpeas for 6 minutes until crisp at the edges.
Add the ras el hanout, garlic and tomatoes for 4 minutes until jammy.
Stir through the spinach until wilted.
Whisk the tahini with the lemon juice and a splash of water until pourable.
Spoon into bowls and drizzle with tahini.

notes: Serve with flatbread.
Naturally vegan and dairy-free.

title: Soaked Oats with Grated Apple, Maple and Crunchy Walnuts
summary: Creamy no-cook oats soaked in oat milk with grated apple, cinnamon and walnuts.

steps.text: Stir the oats, oat milk, apple, cinnamon and maple syrup together.
Cover and chill overnight until thick and creamy.
Loosen with the soy milk if needed.
Top with the walnuts and serve cold.

notes: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.
Warm gently if you prefer it hot, until steaming.

title: Greek Yoghurt Bowl with Honey, Pistachios and Pomegranate
summary: A high-protein Greek yoghurt bowl with honey, pistachios and pomegranate.

steps.text: Spoon the yoghurt into bowls.
Drizzle generously with the honey.
Top with the pistachios, pomegranate, cardamom and sesame seeds until the bowl is full of texture.

notes: High in protein and quick to assemble.
Use a dairy-free yoghurt if needed.

title: Smoky Lentil and Sweet Potato Soup
summary: A thick vegan soup of red lentils, sweet potato and smoked paprika, high in fibre.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the oil for 6 minutes until translucent.
Add the garlic, paprika and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, sweet potato and stock and simmer for 25 minutes until the lentils collapse and the sweet potato is soft.
Blend half the soup for a thick texture and add the lemon juice.

notes: Naturally vegan, gluten-free and dairy-free.
Freezes well.

title: Ginger Miso Mushroom Soup
summary: A vegan umami-rich broth of shiitake, ginger and miso with silken tofu.

steps.text: Simmer the stock with the ginger and mushrooms for 12 minutes until the mushrooms are tender.
Add the tofu and soy sauce and heat for 3 minutes.
Remove from the heat, whisk in the miso and sesame oil.
Serve hot with the sliced spring onion on top.

notes: Do not boil after adding the miso.
Naturally vegan; check the miso for gluten.

title: Cold Cucumber Dill Soup Thickened with Greek Yoghurt
summary: A refreshing cold soup of cucumber, yoghurt, dill and mint, high in protein.

steps.text: Blend the cucumber, yoghurt, garlic, dill and mint until smooth.
Thin with the water and stir in the oil, lemon juice and salt.
Chill for at least 1 hour until very cold.
Serve with a drizzle of oil.

notes: Serve in chilled bowls.
Keeps for 2 days in the fridge.

title: Gluten-Free Corn Fritters with Avocado
summary: Crisp fritters made with corn, chickpea flour and herbs, served with avocado and lime.

steps.text: Mix the corn, chickpea flour, egg, milk, spring onions, cumin and salt into a thick batter.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat.
Spoon in the batter and fry for 3 minutes each side until golden and cooked in the middle.
Serve with the avocado and lime.

notes: Food safety: cook the fritters until set in the middle.
Naturally gluten-free.

title: Dairy-Free Spinach and Pea Soup with Coconut
summary: A vivid green vegan soup with peas, spinach and a splash of coconut cream.

steps.text: Soften the onion and garlic in the oil for 6 minutes until translucent.
Add the stock and peas and simmer for 8 minutes until tender.
Add the spinach until wilted, then blend until smooth.
Stir in the coconut cream and lemon juice and heat gently.
Serve hot or cold with the torn mint on top.

notes: Naturally vegan and gluten-free.
Serve cold in summer.

title: Smoky Tofu Rice Paper Salad Rolls
summary: Fresh rolls of smoky tofu, vermicelli, herbs and crunchy vegetables with peanut dipping sauce.

steps.text: Fry the tofu with the soy sauce and paprika in the oil for 6 minutes until golden.
Soak the vermicelli in hot water until soft, then drain.
Soften one rice paper sheet in warm water for 10 seconds until pliable.
Fill with tofu, noodles, vegetables and herbs, then roll tightly.
Whisk the peanut butter, sweet chilli, lime juice and a splash of warm water until pourable.
Serve the rolls with the sauce.

notes: Keep rolls under a damp cloth until serving.
Naturally vegan; check the sweet chilli sauce for fish.

title: Chargrilled Corn and Black Bean Salad
summary: A smoky vegan salad of grilled corn, black beans, tomato and avocado with lime.

steps.text: Char the corn on a hot grill for 10 minutes, turning, until blackened in spots.
Cut off the kernels with a sharp knife and discard the cobs.
Mix the kernels with the beans, tomatoes, onion and coriander.
Whisk the lime juice, oil, cumin and salt and toss through.
Fold in the avocado gently.

notes: Naturally gluten-free and dairy-free.
Serve with corn chips.

title: Za'atar Roasted Cauliflower and Chickpea Salad
summary: A vegan, gluten-free salad of roast cauliflower, crisp chickpeas, parsley and a lemony tahini.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C and line a large baking tray.
Toss the cauliflower and chickpeas with the oil and zaatar.
Roast for 30 minutes until the cauliflower is golden and the chickpeas are crisp.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice and water until smooth.
Toss the roasted vegetables with the parsley and onion and drizzle with the dressing.

notes: Naturally dairy-free.
Serve warm or cold.

title: Maple Pumpkin and Pepita Quinoa Bowl
summary: A vegan, gluten-free salad with roast pumpkin, quinoa, pepitas and a maple dressing.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C and roast the pumpkin with 1 tbsp oil for 30 minutes until golden.
Simmer the quinoa in 400ml water for 15 minutes until tender with a visible curl.
Whisk the remaining oil, maple syrup, vinegar and mustard.
Toss the warm quinoa with the pumpkin, spinach, onion and dressing.
Top with the pumpkin seeds.

notes: Naturally dairy-free.
Check the mustard for gluten if serving coeliacs.

title: Pineapple Mango Slaw with Lime and Chilli
summary: A bright, crunchy slaw of cabbage, pineapple and mango with a lime and chilli dressing.

steps.text: Mix the cabbage, mango, pineapple, carrot, chilli and coriander.
Whisk the lime juice, oil, honey and salt.
Toss through the slaw until coated.
Rest for 10 minutes until the cabbage softens slightly.

notes: Serve with jerk chicken or fish.
Use maple syrup for vegan.

title: Cape Malay Carrot Salad with Raisins
summary: A sweet and spiced grated carrot salad with raisins, lemon and cinnamon.

steps.text: Mix the carrot and raisins in a bowl.
Whisk the lemon juice, oil, cinnamon, sugar and salt.
Toss through the carrots and rest for 15 minutes until the flavours mingle.
Top with the torn mint and serve at room temperature.

notes: Serve with curries and braai meats.
Vegan and gluten-free.

title: Urap Sayur Indonesian Vegetable Salad with Coconut
summary: Blanched vegetables dressed with a spiced coconut mix.

steps.text: Blanch the beans for 3 minutes, then add the cabbage and sprouts for 1 minute until just tender, and drain.
Crush the garlic, chillies, palm sugar and salt to a paste.
Mix with the coconut and lime leaves.
Toss the vegetables with the coconut mix and lime juice.

notes: Vegan and gluten-free.
Serve with rice and tempeh-style fried tofu.

title: Pacific Coconut Rice Breakfast Bowl
summary: Warm coconut rice porridge topped with pineapple, toasted coconut and lime.

steps.text: Simmer the rice with the coconut milk, water, sugar and salt, stirring often, for 25 minutes until creamy.
Toast the coconut in a dry pan for 2 minutes until golden.
Spoon the porridge into bowls.
Top with pineapple, coconut and lime zest.

notes: Vegan and gluten-free.
Refrigerate leftover rice within an hour.

title: Samoan Style Oka Cooked Fish Salad with Coconut
summary: Poached white fish with cucumber, tomato, onion and coconut cream dressing.

steps.text: Poach the fish in simmering water for 5 minutes until opaque and flaking, then cool and flake.
Mix the cucumber, tomatoes and onion.
Whisk the coconut cream, lime juice, chilli and salt.
Fold the fish and dressing through the vegetables.
Chill for 10 minutes before serving.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, with an internal temperature of at least 63°C.
The traditional version uses raw fish; this cooked version is safer.

title: Fiji-Style Rourou Greens with Coconut Milk
summary: Silky stewed greens in coconut milk with onion, garlic and chilli.

steps.text: Cook the onion, garlic and chilli in the oil for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the spinach until wilted, then pour in the coconut milk.
Simmer for 10 minutes until creamy and thickened.
Season with the salt and simmer until glossy, then serve hot with roast fish or meat.

notes: Traditionally made with taro leaves.
Vegan and gluten-free.

title: Trinidadian Pelau Style Chicken and Pigeon Pea Rice
summary: One-pot caramelised chicken and rice with beans, coconut and thyme.

steps.text: Caramelise the sugar in the oil for 2 minutes until dark amber, then add the chicken and brown for 6 minutes.
Add the onion, carrot and garlic for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the rice, beans, coconut milk, stock, thyme and whole scotch bonnet.
Cover and cook on low heat for 22 minutes until the rice is tender and the chicken is cooked through.
Rest for 10 minutes and fluff.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C, and refrigerate leftover rice within an hour.
Leave the scotch bonnet whole.

title: Jamaican Red Pea Soup with Beef
summary: Beef and kidney bean soup with root vegetables and spinners, thick with thyme and allspice.

steps.text: Simmer the beef with the water, thyme, allspice and scotch bonnet for 75 minutes until nearly tender.
Add the beans, sweet potato and carrot and simmer for 20 minutes.
Mix the flour with a pinch of salt and enough water to make a firm dough, then roll into thin spinners.
Stir in the coconut milk and drop in the spinners.
Cook for 10 minutes until the spinners are firm and the beef is falling apart.
Add the spring onions and remove the scotch bonnet.

notes: Food safety: simmer the beef until tender, with an internal temperature of at least 75°C.
Leave the scotch bonnet whole.

title: Pepperpot Style Beef and Callaloo Stew Soup
summary: A dark, aromatic beef soup with spinach, okra, thyme and cinnamon.

steps.text: Simmer the beef with the water, onion, garlic, cinnamon, thyme and scotch bonnet for 75 minutes until tender.
Add the soy sauce, sugar and okra and simmer for 12 minutes.
Add the spinach until wilted.
Season with salt and remove the scotch bonnet.

notes: Food safety: simmer the beef until tender, with an internal temperature of at least 75°C.
Serve with rice or dumplings.

title: Bacon and Egg Mealie Meal Breakfast Bake
summary: A baked polenta breakfast bake with bacon, tomato and eggs.

steps.text: Cook the polenta in the salted water for 12 minutes, stirring, until thick, then spread into a baking dish.
Heat the oven to 200°C and grease a baking dish.
Fry the bacon for 6 minutes until crisp and scatter over the polenta with the tomatoes.
Make six wells, crack in the eggs and top with the cheddar.
Bake for 15 minutes until the whites are set.
Scatter with the chives and serve in squares.

notes: Food safety: bake until the egg whites are completely set and the bacon is cooked through.
Cook yolks firm for vulnerable eaters.

title: Boerewors-Style Sausage Hash with Tomato Relish
summary: Crisp potato and spiced sausage hash with chakalaka-style tomato.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes for 8 minutes until just tender, then drain.
Fry the sausage in the oil for 6 minutes until browned.
Add the potatoes, onion and capsicum and fry for 10 minutes until crisp.
Stir in the spices and tomato paste for 2 minutes.
Make four wells and cook the eggs for 4 minutes until the whites are set.

notes: Food safety: cook the sausage until it reaches 75°C with no pink, and the egg whites until set.
Serve with chutney.

title: Pho Ga Vietnamese Chicken Noodle Soup
summary: A clear ginger and onion chicken broth with rice noodles, shredded chicken and herbs.

steps.text: Char the onion and ginger in a dry pan for 5 minutes until blackened.
Simmer the chicken with the water, charred aromatics and spices for 40 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Lift out the chicken, shred the meat and strain the broth, seasoning with fish sauce.
Soak the noodles in hot water until soft and divide among bowls.
Top with chicken, ladle over the hot broth and finish with the herbs, sprouts, spring onion and lime.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C and the juices run clear.
Skim off fat for a cleaner broth.

title: Spicy Peanut Sauce for Grilled Skewers
summary: A smooth, sweet-spicy peanut sauce for satay, gado-gado and salad rolls.

steps.text: Warm the coconut milk and peanut butter in a pot, stirring, until smooth.
Add the kecap manis, lime juice, garlic, ginger, chilli and sugar.
Simmer for 5 minutes until thick and glossy.
Loosen with water if needed.

notes: Keeps for 5 days in the fridge.
Reheat gently until warm.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Mango Avocado Salsa with Lime
summary: A fresh, vegan salsa of mango, avocado, red onion and lime.

steps.text: Mix the mango, avocado, onion, jalapeno and coriander gently.
Add the lime juice and salt until just combined.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve.

notes: Serve with grilled fish or corn chips.
Vegan and gluten-free.

title: Sweet Tamarind and Ginger Chutney
summary: A sweet-sour tamarind and ginger chutney for samosas, chaat and snacks.

steps.text: Simmer the tamarind, water and sugar for 10 minutes.
Add the ginger, cumin, chilli and salt.
Simmer for 8 minutes until thick and syrupy.
Cool the chutney, then strain into a clean jar.

notes: Keeps for 3 weeks in the fridge.
Vegan and gluten-free.

title: Parsley and Oregano Chimichurri
summary: A bright Argentine herb sauce of parsley, garlic and red wine vinegar for grilled meat and vegetables.

steps.text: Mix the parsley, garlic, oregano, chilli and salt.
Stir in the vinegar and oil until combined.
Rest for 30 minutes until the flavours blend.
Spoon over steak or roast vegetables once the flavours have rested until fragrant.

notes: Keeps for 5 days in the fridge.
Vegan and gluten-free.

title: Roasted Garlic and White Bean Dip
summary: A creamy vegan dip of roast garlic, cannellini beans and lemon.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C and roast the garlic bulb with a drizzle of oil for 40 minutes until soft and golden.
Squeeze the garlic into a blender with the beans, remaining oil, lemon juice, cumin and salt.
Blend for 2 minutes until completely smooth, scraping down the sides.
Spoon into a bowl and top with the paprika.

notes: Vegan, gluten-free and dairy-free.
Serve with vegetable sticks.

title: Jollof Style Tomato Rice with Peppers
summary: Smoky tomato and pepper rice from West Africa, cooked until the grains are fluffy and fragrant.

steps.text: Blend the tomatoes, capsicums and scotch bonnet to a smooth purée.
Fry the onion in the oil for 6 minutes until soft, add the tomato paste for 3 minutes, then the purée and cook for 15 minutes until reduced and dark.
Stir in the thyme, curry powder, bay leaf and stock and bring to a simmer until steaming.
Add the rinsed rice, cover tightly and cook on low heat for 22 minutes until the rice is tender.
Rest for 10 minutes and fluff.

notes: Food safety: cool leftover rice quickly and refrigerate within an hour, reheating until steaming hot.
Vegan and gluten-free.

title: Roti Canai with Dhal Dipping Curry
summary: Flaky, layered Malaysian flatbreads stretched thin, folded and pan-fried, served with a spiced lentil curry.

steps.text: Mix flour, salt, sugar, egg and water into a soft dough and knead for 8 minutes.
Divide into 8 balls, coat each in oil and rest in a covered tray for 2 hours.
Simmer onion, garlic, curry powder, tomato and lentils in the water for 20 minutes until thick and soft.
Stretch each ball on an oiled bench until paper thin, then fold into a square.
Fry in a hot pan with ghee for 3 minutes each side until golden.
Clap the roti between your hands to fluff the layers and serve with the dhal.

notes: Food safety: the egg in the dough is fully cooked by frying.
The long oiled rest is what lets the dough stretch without tearing.

title: Coconut Rice Breakfast with Sambal Eggs and Anchovies
summary: Coconut rice with crisp anchovies, peanuts, cucumber and eggs braised in a sweet chilli sambal.

steps.text: Rinse the rice and cook with the coconut milk, water and lemongrass for 18 minutes, then rest covered.
Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, cool and peel.
Fry the onion and garlic in oil for 6 minutes, add the chilli paste and cook 4 minutes until the oil separates.
Stir in the tamarind and sugar with a splash of water, add the eggs and coat for 3 minutes.
Fry the anchovies in a little oil for 2 minutes until crisp.
Serve the rice with sambal eggs, anchovies, peanuts and cucumber.

notes: Food safety: boil the eggs for at least 8 minutes so they are set through.
Anchovies make this pescatarian, not vegetarian.

title: Sambal Belacan
summary: A fiery fresh chilli and toasted shrimp paste condiment pounded with lime, served with rice and grilled fish.

steps.text: Toast the shrimp paste in a dry pan for 2 minutes until crumbly and fragrant.
Crush the chillies coarsely in a mortar until broken down.
Add the shrimp paste, sugar and salt and grind until a rough paste forms.
Stir in the lime juice and oil and serve at once.

notes: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 3 days.
Toasting the paste mellows its smell and deepens the flavour.

title: Kangkung Belacan
summary: Water spinach stir-fried with chilli, garlic and toasted shrimp paste, a classic Malaysian side.

steps.text: Cut the water spinach into 8cm lengths, keeping stems and leaves apart.
Grind the garlic, chillies and shrimp paste until a rough paste forms.
Fry the paste in hot oil for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the stems and toss for 2 minutes, then the leaves, oyster sauce and sugar.
Toss for 1 minute until just wilted and serve hot.

notes: Wash the greens very well as the hollow stems hold grit.
Work on a high heat so the greens stay bright.

title: Acar Awak
summary: A Nyonya-style pickle of crunchy vegetables in a turmeric, chilli and peanut dressing.

items.raw: 1 cucumber, deseeded and cut in batons

steps.text: Salt the cabbage, carrot, cucumber and beans and leave them for 20 minutes, then squeeze dry.
Blend the chillies, shallots, garlic and turmeric to a paste.
Fry the paste in oil for 5 minutes until fragrant.
Add the vinegar and sugar and simmer for 3 minutes, then cool.
Toss the vegetables with the dressing and half the peanuts.
Top with the remaining peanuts and rest for an hour before serving.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for up to 5 days.
Squeezing the vegetables dry keeps the pickle crunchy.

title: Bak Kut Teh Pork Rib Soup
summary: A peppery Klang-style pork rib soup with garlic, white pepper and soy, simmered until the meat falls away.

steps.text: Blanch the ribs in boiling water for 5 minutes and rinse.
Return to a clean pot with water, garlic, peppercorns, star anise and cinnamon.
Simmer gently for 90 minutes, skimming the surface, until the meat pulls from the bone.
Add the soy sauces, sugar and mushrooms and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the tofu for 5 minutes and serve with rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork until it reaches at least 75°C and is tender.
Serve with chopped chilli in soy sauce.

title: Curry Laksa Noodle Soup
summary: A rich coconut curry soup with rice noodles, prawns, tofu puffs and a fragrant homemade spice paste.

steps.text: Soak the dried chillies in hot water for 15 minutes, then blend with shallots, garlic, lemongrass, ginger, turmeric and shrimp paste.
Fry the paste in the oil for 10 minutes until the oil separates.
Add the stock and simmer for 10 minutes, then stir in the coconut milk and fish sauce.
Cook the vermicelli until tender, then drain and divide among bowls.
Poach the prawns and tofu puffs in the soup for 3 minutes.
Ladle over the noodles and top with sprouts, mint and lime.

notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until pink and opaque all through.
Freeze leftover paste in portions.

title: Kaya Toast with Soft Eggs
summary: Crisp toasted bread with sweet coconut and butter, with runny eggs seasoned with soy and white pepper.

steps.text: Toast the bread until crisp and golden.
Spread two slices with the sweet coconut and top with slices of cold butter.
Close the sandwiches and cut them into fingers.
Lower the eggs into boiling water for 6 minutes.
Crack into a bowl and season with soy sauce and white pepper.
Eat the toast dipped in the eggs until the plate is clean.

notes: Food safety: soft eggs are not recommended for pregnant women, older adults or small children.
Toast the coconut lightly until golden for extra flavour.

title: Rojak Buah Fruit Salad
summary: Crunchy tropical fruit and vegetables tossed in a sticky, sweet and tangy tamarind and chilli dressing with peanuts.

steps.text: Whisk tamarind, palm sugar, chilli paste and lime juice until the sugar dissolves.
Place the fruit and vegetables in a large bowl.
Pour over the dressing and toss well.
Scatter with peanuts and sesame seeds and serve straight away.

notes: Serve immediately or the fruit will turn watery.
Add more chilli for a hotter dressing.

title: Kuih Dadar Coconut Pancakes
summary: Thin crepes wrapped around gula melaka coconut filling.

steps.text: Blend the flour, egg, coconut milk, water, pandan juice and salt until smooth and rest for 20 minutes.
Melt the palm sugar with the water, add the coconut and cook for 6 minutes until sticky.
Cook thin crepes in a lightly oiled non-stick pan for 1 minute per side.
Spoon filling down the centre of each crepe.
Roll up each crepe around the filling and serve warm.

notes: Food safety: the egg is fully cooked in the crepe.
The batter should be thin like cream.

title: Crispy Anchovy and Peanut Sambal Crunch
summary: Crunchy fried anchovies and peanuts tossed in sweet chilli sambal.

steps.text: Fry the peanuts in oil for 4 minutes until golden and lift out.
Fry the anchovies in the same oil for 3 minutes until crisp and lift out.
Fry the onion for 3 minutes, add the chilli paste and cook 2 minutes.
Stir in the tamarind and sugar until sticky.
Fold through the anchovies and peanuts and cool before serving.

notes: Keeps for a week in a sealed jar.
Rinse and dry the anchovies well before frying.

title: Caesar Salad with Homemade Dressing
summary: Crisp cos, garlic croutons and a from-scratch anchovy and lemon dressing, topped with shaved parmesan.

steps.text: Tear the bread, toss with 3 tbsp oil and bake at 190C for 12 minutes until crisp.
Mash the garlic and anchovies to a paste.
Whisk in the yolk, mustard, lemon juice and worcestershire.
Drizzle in the oil, whisking until thick and glossy.
Toss the cos leaves with the dressing and croutons.
Top with shaved parmesan.

notes: Food safety: the dressing uses raw egg yolk, so avoid it for pregnant women, older adults and small children.
Use pasteurised egg yolk if you prefer.

title: Béchamel Mother Sauce
summary: The silky white sauce at the base of lasagne, gratins and cheese sauces, with a smooth roux and a hint of nutmeg.

items.raw: 1 small onion, peeled and studded with 2 cloves

steps.text: Warm the milk with the onion and bay leaf for 10 minutes and strain.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook for 2 minutes without browning.
Add the hot milk a little at a time, whisking smooth after each addition.
Simmer for 8 minutes, stirring, until thick enough to coat a spoon.
Season with nutmeg and salt.

notes: Press cling film on the surface to stop a skin forming.
Add more milk if it thickens on standing.

title: Veloute Mother Sauce
summary: A light golden roux sauce built on chicken stock, the base for supremes, mushroom and tarragon sauces.

steps.text: Melt the butter and stir in the flour.
Cook for 3 minutes until pale blond.
Pour in the warm stock gradually, whisking smooth.
Add the bay leaf and peppercorns and simmer gently for 20 minutes, skimming.
Strain, season and finish with lemon juice.

notes: Use a good stock, as the sauce will taste only of it.
Swap in fish or veal stock for other classic versions.

title: Espagnole Brown Sauce
summary: A deep brown sauce from dark roux, roasted bones and aromatics, the foundation for a demi-glace.

steps.text: Brown the vegetables in half the butter for 10 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook until brick red.
Make a dark roux with the remaining butter and flour, cooking for 8 minutes until nutty brown.
Whisk in the warm stock slowly.
Add the vegetables, bay leaf and thyme and simmer for 75 minutes, skimming.
Strain through a fine sieve until smooth, then season to taste.

notes: Keeps 4 days in the fridge or freezes well.
Reduce by half with red wine for a demi-glace style sauce.

title: Mayonnaise from Scratch
summary: Rich homemade mayonnaise whisked by hand from egg yolk, mustard, lemon and oil.

steps.text: Whisk the yolks, mustard and lemon juice in a bowl until pale and combined.
Add the oil one drop at a time, whisking constantly.
Once it thickens, pour in the oil in a thin stream.
Whisk in the vinegar and salt.
Store covered in the fridge and use once chilled until thick.

notes: Food safety: this contains raw egg yolk, so avoid for pregnant women, older adults and small children, and use within 3 days.
Use pasteurised yolks for safety.

title: Chicken Stock, Slow-Simmered
summary: A clear, gelatinous chicken stock from roasted bones, the base for soups and sauces.

steps.text: Roast the carcasses at 220C for 30 minutes until golden.
Put them in a pot with the vegetables, herbs and peppercorns.
Cover with the cold water and bring to a gentle simmer until the first scum rises.
Simmer for 4 hours, skimming the surface.
Strain through a fine sieve and chill.
Lift off the fat once set and reheat the stock to steaming before using.

notes: Food safety: simmer until the chicken reaches 75°C throughout, cool quickly, store in the fridge for 4 days or freeze up to 3 months, and always reheat to steaming.
Never boil hard or the stock turns cloudy.

title: Dashi from Kombu and Bonito
summary: The foundational Japanese broth of kelp and smoked bonito flakes, clean and savoury.

steps.text: Soak the kombu in the water for 30 minutes.
Heat gently until just below a simmer, then remove the kombu.
Add the bonito flakes and turn off the heat.
Steep for 2 minutes until the flakes sink, then strain.

notes: Do not boil the kombu or the stock turns bitter and slimy.
Use within 3 days.

title: Kimchi, Napa Cabbage
summary: Fermented napa cabbage with chilli, garlic and ginger, pungent and tangy after a few days.

steps.text: Salt the cabbage between the leaves and stand for 2 hours, turning once.
Rinse three times and drain well.
Cook the rice flour with the water until a thick paste forms, then cool.
Blend the garlic, ginger, fish sauce and sugar with the gochugaru and flour paste.
Mix in the carrot, daikon and spring onion.
Rub the paste between the cabbage leaves and pack tightly into a jar.
Ferment at room temperature for 2 days until bubbly and sour, then refrigerate.

notes: Wear gloves to avoid chilli burns.
Keep the cabbage submerged and open the jar to release gas daily.

title: Sauerkraut
summary: Raw fermented cabbage salted to make its own brine, tart and crunchy.

steps.text: Shred the cabbage finely and mix with the salt.
Massage for 10 minutes until it releases plenty of liquid.
Mix in the caraway and fennel.
Pack tightly into a jar so the liquid covers the cabbage.
Weigh it down and ferment at room temperature for 7 to 10 days.
Refrigerate once sour enough, until the cabbage tastes tangy.

notes: Skim any scum. Discard if it smells rotten or has pink or fuzzy mould.
Use non-iodised salt.

title: Preserved Lemons
summary: Whole lemons cured in salt and their own juice, essential for tagines and dressings.

steps.text: Quarter the lemons almost through, keeping the base attached.
Pack the cut sides with salt.
Layer in a sterilised jar with bay and coriander.
Press down and cover with the juice of 3 lemons.
Seal and shake daily for 4 weeks until the rinds are soft.

notes: Rinse the lemons before using and use the skin only.
Keeps in the fridge for a year.

title: Pommes Anna
summary: Thin overlapping potato slices pressed in butter and baked until golden, crisp outside and tender within.

steps.text: Slice the potatoes very finely and keep them dry.
Brush a frying pan with butter and arrange a circle of slices overlapping like fish scales.
Season each layer, brush with butter and add thyme.
Repeat until all are used, pressing firmly.
Cover with foil and bake at 200C for 30 minutes.
Remove the foil and bake 25 minutes until crisp and golden.
Rest, loosen the edge and turn out.

notes: Do not rinse the starch off the slices as it helps them bind.
Use a mandoline for even slices.

title: Duchess Potatoes
summary: Piped mashed potato rosettes baked until golden and crisp at the edges.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes until tender and drain well.
Steam dry in the pot for 3 minutes and mash until smooth.
Beat in the butter, yolks, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Pipe rosettes onto a lined tray.
Brush with the beaten egg and bake at 220C for 25 minutes until golden.

notes: Food safety: bake until the egg is fully cooked and golden.
A dry mash is the secret to piping neatly.

title: Yorkshire Puddings
summary: Tall, crisp, airy puddings baked in smoking-hot fat, perfect with roast beef and gravy.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, eggs, milk and salt until a smooth batter forms.
Rest the batter for 30 minutes until it thickens slightly.
Heat the oven to 230C and add a spoonful of dripping to each cup of a muffin tin.
Heat the tin until smoking, about 10 minutes.
Pour in the batter and bake for 22 minutes without opening the door.

notes: Food safety: bake until the eggs are fully set.
Keep the fat very hot or the puddings will not rise.

title: Gratin Dauphinois
summary: Thinly sliced potatoes baked in garlicky cream and milk until bubbling and tender.

steps.text: Rub a baking dish with the garlic and butter.
Slice the potatoes thinly and layer in the dish.
Heat the cream, milk, nutmeg and salt until just steaming.
Pour the hot cream mixture over the potatoes until just covered.
Bake at 170C for 70 minutes until golden and tender.

notes: This version uses no cheese.
Cover with foil if it browns too fast.

title: Romesco Sauce
summary: A smoky red pepper and almond sauce, a Catalan classic for grilled vegetables and fish.

steps.text: Roast the capsicums, tomatoes and garlic at 220C for 25 minutes.
Peel the charred skins from the capsicum until the flesh is clean.
Toast the almonds until golden.
Blend the almonds, toast and garlic until a coarse paste forms.
Add the vegetables, vinegar and paprika and blend.
Stream in the oil and season.

notes: It thickens as it rests.
Keeps 5 days in the fridge.

title: Salsa Macha
summary: A Veracruz oil-based salsa of dried chilli, nuts and garlic, nutty, smoky and addictive.

steps.text: Warm the oil with the garlic until golden and lift out the garlic.
Fry the chillies for 30 seconds until they darken slightly, then lift out.
Fry the peanuts and sesame in the oil until golden.
Blend half the mixture coarsely.
Stir all together with vinegar, sugar and salt.

notes: Keep submerged in oil in the fridge for up to 3 weeks.
Do not let the chillies burn or the sauce turns bitter.

title: Mole Poblano
summary: A deep chilli, chocolate and spice sauce with sesame and nuts, long and slow in the making.

steps.text: Toast and deseed the chillies and soak in hot water for 20 minutes.
Fry the onion, garlic, tomato, nuts, seeds, raisins, tortilla and spices in the lard until brown.
Blend with the chillies and some soaking water.
Fry the paste in a pot for 10 minutes, stirring.
Add the stock and chocolate and simmer for an hour until glossy and thick.
Season with salt and sugar to balance.

notes: Serve over turkey or chicken.
Freezes well in portions.

title: Harissa from Scratch
summary: Fiery Tunisian chilli paste with roasted capsicum, caraway, cumin and garlic.

steps.text: Soak the chillies in hot water for 20 minutes and drain.
Toast the spices in a dry pan until fragrant.
Blend the chillies, capsicum, garlic and spices to a paste.
Stir in the lemon juice and oil and season.

notes: Cover with a film of oil and keep for 3 weeks in the fridge.
Wear gloves.

title: XO Sauce
summary: Luxurious Cantonese seafood condiment of dried scallop, shrimp, ham and chilli slowly cooked in oil.

steps.text: Soak the scallops and shrimp in hot water until soft and shred the scallops.
Chop the ham, shallots, garlic and chillies finely.
Warm the oil and fry the shallots and garlic gently for 15 minutes until golden.
Add the ham, shrimp, scallops and chillies and cook for 20 minutes.
Add the oyster sauce, sugar and wine and simmer 5 minutes until glossy.

notes: Food safety: the dried seafood is rehydrated and cooked in hot oil for 20 minutes until opaque and cooked through, so keep it refrigerated under oil and use within a month.
Great with noodles, eggs and steamed fish.

title: Dairy-Free Ranch Dressing
summary: Creamy herbed cashew ranch with chives, dill and garlic, no dairy needed.

steps.text: Soak the cashews in boiling water for 20 minutes and drain.
Blend with the water, lemon, garlic, vinegar and onion powder until very smooth.
Stir in the chives and dill.
Chill for 30 minutes until the dressing thickens slightly.

notes: Thins out in the fridge, so add water if too thick.
Keeps 5 days.

title: Gribiche Sauce
summary: A cold French sauce of hard-boiled eggs, mustard, capers and herbs for asparagus and cold fish.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes and cool.
Mash the yolks with mustard and vinegar.
Whisk in the oil in a thin stream until glossy and thick.
Chop the whites and fold in with capers, cornichons and herbs.
Season with salt and serve until the bowl is empty.

notes: Food safety: boil the eggs for 10 minutes until firm throughout.
Use within 2 days.

title: Brioche Cinnamon Rolls
summary: Soft, buttery brioche dough rolled with cinnamon sugar and iced with cream cheese frosting.

steps.text: Mix flour, yeast, sugar and salt with milk and eggs.
Knead in the butter until silky, about 10 minutes.
Prove for 90 minutes until doubled.
Roll to a rectangle, spread with softened butter and cinnamon sugar.
Roll up and cut into 8 pieces.
Prove 45 minutes in a pan.
Bake at 180C for 28 minutes.
Beat cream cheese with icing sugar and spread over warm rolls.

notes: Food safety: bake until the rolls are cooked through.
Warm milk should be no hotter than 40C.

title: Homemade Bagels
summary: Chewy, shiny bagels shaped by hand, boiled in honey water, then baked.

steps.text: Mix flour, salt, yeast, honey and water and knead for 10 minutes.
Prove for 1 hour until doubled in size.
Divide into 8 and shape into rings.
Rest the rings for 20 minutes until slightly puffy.
Boil in the honey water for 1 minute each side.
Top with sesame and bake at 220C for 20 minutes.

notes: Boiling gives the shiny, chewy crust.
Slice and freeze for easy breakfasts.

title: Sourdough Crumpets
summary: Tangy, hole-riddled crumpets cooked in rings in a pan, ideal for butter to soak into.

steps.text: Whisk the discard, flour, milk, salt and sugar into a batter.
Rest the batter for 1 hour until bubbles appear on top.
Dissolve the bicarb in the water and stir through.
Heat greased rings in a pan on low heat.
Fill the rings 1cm deep and cook for 8 minutes until set and dotted with holes.
Flip and cook for 1 minute until pale gold on top.

notes: Eat with melted butter.
Reheat in the toaster.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Japanese Soufflé Pancakes
summary: Tall, wobbly meringue-lightened pancakes cooked slowly under a lid.

steps.text: Whisk the yolks, milk and vanilla and fold in flour and baking powder.
Whisk the whites with the sugar to stiff peaks.
Fold the meringue into the batter in thirds until no streaks remain.
Pile mounds into a low-heat buttered pan.
Cover and cook for 6 minutes, flip and cook for 5 more.
Serve the stacks straight away with maple syrup.

notes: Food safety: cook gently until the centres are set.
Keep the heat low.

title: Tofu Scramble with Greens
summary: A dairy-free, high-protein scramble of turmeric tofu, spinach and tomatoes on toast.

steps.text: Crumble the tofu into a bowl.
Warm the oil and cook the tofu with turmeric and cumin for 5 minutes.
Stir in the yeast, spinach and tomato until wilted.
Toast the bread until golden and crisp.
Pile the scramble on top.

notes: Press the tofu first for a firmer texture.
Add black salt for an eggy flavour.

title: Egg White and Spinach Frittata
summary: A lean, high-protein baked frittata with egg whites, whole eggs and greens.

steps.text: Soften the capsicum and spring onion in the oil.
Add the spinach until wilted.
Whisk the egg whites and eggs.
Pour over the vegetables.
Cook for 3 minutes, then bake at 180C for 12 minutes.

notes: Food safety: cook until the eggs are set through.
Great cold for the work week.

title: High-Protein Peanut Butter Oats
summary: Creamy oats cooked with soy milk, peanut butter and sesame, finished with banana.

steps.text: Simmer the oats and milk for 4 minutes.
Whisk in the protein powder until no lumps remain.
Stir through the peanut butter and sesame until smooth.
Top with sliced apple and serve warm.

notes: Add more milk if too thick.
Dairy-free and vegan.

title: Tuna and White Bean Salad
summary: Protein-rich tuna, creamy cannellini beans and red onion in a lemon and parsley dressing.

steps.text: Drain the tuna and beans.
Slice the onion very thinly and soak it in water for 5 minutes.
Mix with parsley and tomato.
Dress with lemon juice and oil until everything is glossy.
Season with salt and serve until the bowl is empty.

notes: Food safety: keep refrigerated and eat within 2 days.
Rinse the beans.

title: Edamame and Soba Salad
summary: Chewy soba, edamame, cucumber and carrot in a ginger sesame dressing.

steps.text: Boil the soba for 5 minutes and rinse under cold water.
Cook the edamame for 3 minutes.
Whisk the soy, oil, vinegar and ginger.
Toss with the noodles and vegetables until coated.
Top with sesame seeds and serve cold.

notes: Use 100% buckwheat soba for gluten free.
Vegan.

title: Malaysian Chicken Curry Mee Soup
summary: A coconut chicken noodle soup with a mild curry paste, tofu puffs and bean sprouts.

steps.text: Blend the shallots, garlic and ginger with the curry powder into a paste.
Fry the paste in the oil for 6 minutes until the oil separates and it smells toasty.
Add the chicken and stir until it is sealed on all sides.
Pour in the stock and simmer for 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the coconut milk and tofu puffs and heat for 5 minutes until hot.
Boil the noodles until tender, divide among bowls, then ladle over the soup and top with sprouts and lime.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C and no pink remains.
Add sambal on the side for extra heat.

title: Sambal Tumis Prawns
summary: Prawns cooked in a sweet, sticky tamarind chilli sambal, served over steamed rice.

steps.text: Cook the rice according to the packet until fluffy, then keep warm.
Fry the onions in the oil for 6 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the garlic and chilli paste and fry for 4 minutes until the oil rises to the top.
Stir in the tamarind, sugar and tomatoes and simmer for 5 minutes until jammy.
Add the prawns and cook for 3 minutes until pink and opaque.
Serve spooned over the rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until opaque and pink all the way through.
Balance the sweet, sour and heat with extra sugar or tamarind.

title: Telur Dadar Malaysian Omelette
summary: A thin, crisp-edged omelette with onion, chilli and spring onion, folded over and served with rice or toast.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs with the fish sauce and white pepper until well combined.
Stir in the onion, chilli and spring onion.
Heat the oil in a frying pan until shimmering.
Pour in the egg and cook for 3 minutes until the base is golden and crisp at the edge.
Flip and cook for 1 minute until the egg is fully set, then fold and serve.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until firm with no liquid egg remaining.
Serve with sambal and plain rice.

title: Corn Chowder with Smoked Paprika
summary: A creamy summer corn chowder with potato, smoked paprika and bacon.

steps.text: Fry the bacon in the butter for 6 minutes until crisp, then lift out.
Soften the onion in the same pot for 5 minutes until translucent.
Add the paprika, potato, corn and stock and simmer for 15 minutes until the potato is tender.
Blend a third of the soup until smooth and stir back in.
Add the milk and heat gently, then top with bacon and spring onion.

notes: Food safety: cook the bacon until crisp and fully cooked.
Do not boil after adding milk.

title: Spring Pea and Mint Soup
summary: A vivid green spring soup of peas, mint and lettuce, served with a swirl of cream.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the butter for 5 minutes until translucent.
Add the stock and bring to a simmer until the surface bubbles lightly.
Add the peas and lettuce and cook for 5 minutes until just tender but still green.
Add the mint and blend until completely smooth.
Season and serve with a swirl of cream.

notes: Do not overcook or the green turns dull.
Serve hot or chilled.

title: Wombok and Ginger Chicken Broth
summary: A clear chicken broth with wombok, ginger and egg noodles, light and restoring.

steps.text: Simmer the stock with ginger and garlic for 10 minutes.
Add the chicken and poach for 6 minutes until cooked through at 75°C.
Add the noodles and cook for 3 minutes until tender.
Stir in the wombok until just wilted.
Season with soy sauce and sesame oil.

notes: Food safety: poach the chicken until it reaches 75°C with no pink.
Add chilli oil at the table.

title: Ribollita Tuscan Bread Soup
summary: A thick Tuscan soup of cannellini beans, cavolo nero and day-old bread, better the next day.

steps.text: Fry the onion, carrot, celery and garlic in half the oil for 10 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes, stock and half the beans and simmer for 20 minutes.
Mash the remaining beans and stir in.
Add the cavolo nero and cook for 10 minutes until tender.
Tear the bread into the soup and stir until it thickens.
Serve with remaining oil.

notes: Vegan.
Reheat the next day until thick.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Cold Soba Salad with Sesame Dressing
summary: Chilled soba, cucumber and edamame in a soy and sesame dressing, a light summer meal.

steps.text: Boil the soba for 5 minutes until tender, then rinse under cold water.
Cook the edamame for 3 minutes until bright green.
Whisk the soy sauce, tahini, vinegar and honey until smooth.
Toss the noodles, vegetables and dressing until coated.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds.

notes: Check the soba is 100% buckwheat for gluten-free.
Serve cold.

title: Waldorf Salad with Walnuts
summary: Crisp apple, celery and grapes in a light yoghurt dressing with toasted walnuts.

steps.text: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan until golden and fragrant.
Slice the apples and celery and toss with lemon juice.
Mix the yoghurt and mayonnaise.
Fold the apples, celery, grapes and walnuts through the dressing until coated.
Spoon into lettuce cups and serve straight away.

notes: Contains egg in the mayonnaise.
Squeeze lemon on the apple to stop browning.

title: Chicken Larb Lettuce Cups
summary: Minced chicken tossed with lime, fish sauce, mint and toasted rice powder in crisp lettuce cups.

steps.text: Cook the chicken mince in the oil for 8 minutes, breaking it up, until it reaches 75°C and no pink remains.
Cool the cooked chicken for 2 minutes until just warm.
