Return the chicken and season with salt.
Serve with cream, capers and avocado.

notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C and show no pink.
Contains dairy.

title: Turkish Ezogelin Red Lentil and Bulgur Soup
summary: Warming red lentil, bulgur and rice soup with mint and chilli butter.

steps.text: Fry the onion in half the oil for 6 minutes until soft.
Stir in both pastes for 2 minutes until darker.
Add the lentils, rice, bulgur, water and salt and simmer for 25 minutes until everything is soft.
Heat the remaining oil with mint and chilli for 1 minute until it sizzles, and pour over each bowl with lemon.

notes: Vegan.
Contains gluten from the bulgur.

title: Ukrainian Borshch with Beef and Dill
summary: Beetroot and cabbage soup with beef, finished with sour cream and dill.

steps.text: Simmer the brisket in the water for 1 hour 30 minutes, until tender, then shred and keep the stock.
Grate the beetroot and carrot and fry with the onion in the oil for 10 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and vinegar, then add to the stock with the potato and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the cabbage and beef and simmer for 8 minutes until the cabbage is tender.
Serve with sour cream and dill.

notes: Food safety: beef must reach 75°C throughout; chill leftovers within 2 hours.
Contains dairy.

title: Kerala Fish Moilee Coconut Soup
summary: Mild coconut curry soup with firm white fish, ginger and curry spices.

steps.text: Fry the mustard seeds, onion, ginger and chilli in the oil for 6 minutes until soft.
Add turmeric, tomato and coconut milk and simmer for 8 minutes until slightly thickened.
Slip in the fish and cook for 5 minutes until opaque and flaking.
Finish with the lime juice and serve hot, until just warmed through.

notes: Food safety: cook fish until opaque and flaking; refrigerate within 2 hours.
Contains fish.

title: Greek Fasolada White Bean Soup
summary: Greece's humble national soup of white beans, tomato, carrot and olive oil.

steps.text: Cover the beans with water, boil for 10 minutes, then drain.
Cook the onion, carrot and celery in half the oil for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the beans, tomatoes, bay and water and simmer for 50 minutes, until the beans are completely tender.
Season with salt and stir in parsley and the remaining oil.

notes: Vegan.
Soak the beans overnight if you have time, which is not counted in prep time.

title: Shakshuka Verde with Spinach and Feta
summary: Green version of shakshuka with spinach, leek and herbs, eggs baked on top.

steps.text: Soften the sliced leeks in the oil for 6 minutes until tender.
Add garlic, cumin and spinach and cook for 4 minutes until wilted.
Stir in the parsley, make 6 wells and crack in the eggs.
Cover and cook for 6 minutes until the whites are set.
Crumble over the feta and serve straight from the pan.

notes: Food safety: cook until the whites are fully set; firmer yolks for vulnerable eaters.
Contains egg and dairy.

title: Bircher Muesli with Apple and Hazelnuts Dairy Free
summary: Soaked oats with grated apple, oat milk and toasted hazelnuts.

steps.text: Stir the oats and oat milk together in a bowl.
Grate in the apples and mix with the lemon juice, maple and cinnamon.
Cover and chill overnight until creamy.
Toast the hazelnuts for 3 minutes until golden and scatter over the bowls.

notes: Vegan.
Contains tree nuts and gluten.
Soak at least 6 hours, which is not counted in prep time.

title: High Protein Cottage Cheese Pancakes
summary: Soft cottage cheese and oat pancakes, about 25 g protein per serve.

steps.text: Blend the cottage cheese, eggs, oats, baking powder and vanilla until smooth.
Cook scoops in a lightly oiled pan for 3 minutes until set and golden underneath.
Flip and cook for 2 minutes until the centre is firm and cooked through.
Serve with sliced apple and honey.

notes: Food safety: cook until the middle is no longer wet.
Contains egg, dairy and gluten.

title: Quinoa Tabbouleh Style Super Green Salad
summary: Herby quinoa with cucumber, edamame and a lemon dressing, high in plant protein.

steps.text: Rinse the quinoa and simmer in 400ml water for 15 minutes, until tender and the tails pop.
Boil the edamame for 4 minutes until bright green.
Chop the herbs and cucumber finely.
Toss everything with the lemon, oil and salt.

notes: Vegan and gluten-free.
Contains soy.

title: Spiced Lentil and Roasted Carrot Salad with Tahini
summary: Earthy lentils with cumin carrots, rocket and a lemon tahini dressing.

steps.text: Simmer the lentils in water for 22 minutes until tender but holding shape, then drain.
Roast the carrots with the oil, cumin and salt at 220C for 30 minutes, until charred and tender.
Whisk the tahini with lemon and 3 tbsp water until pourable.
Toss the lentils with the carrots, rocket and sliced onion and drizzle over the tahini.

notes: Vegan.
Contains sesame.

title: Patatas Bravas with Smoky Tomato Sauce
summary: Crisp roast potatoes with spicy smoked paprika tomato sauce and garlic mayo.

steps.text: Roast the potato cubes with 3 tbsp oil and salt at 220C for 40 minutes, turning once, until crisp and golden.
Fry the garlic, paprika and chilli in the remaining oil for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and vinegar and simmer for 12 minutes until thick.
Spoon over the potatoes and dollop with mayonnaise.

notes: Contains egg from the mayonnaise.

title: Greek Style Silverbeet with Garlic and Lemon
summary: Garlicky wilted greens finished with olive oil and lemon.

steps.text: Separate the stalks and leaves and slice the stalks thinly.
Cook the stalks in the oil for 4 minutes until soft.
Add garlic and cook 1 minute until fragrant, then add the leaves for 4 minutes until wilted.
Season with salt and lemon juice.

notes: Vegan.

title: Chimichurri Verde Argentine Herb Sauce
summary: Garlic, parsley and vinegar sauce for grilled steak.

steps.text: Chop the parsley and garlic finely.
Stir through the oregano, chilli, vinegar and salt.
Whisk in the oil and rest 15 minutes until the flavours blend.

notes: Vegan.
Rich in oil, so a spoonful goes a long way.

title: Hollandaise Style Yoghurt Lemon Sauce for Eggs
summary: Lighter creamy lemon sauce for poached eggs and asparagus.

steps.text: Whisk the yolks and lemon in a bowl over simmering water for 4 minutes until thick and pale.
Whisk in the melted butter slowly until glossy.
Fold in the yoghurt and warm for 1 minute without boiling.

notes: Contains egg and dairy.
Food safety: heat the yolks until they thicken; serve at once and do not reheat. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Czech Kulajda Dill and Potato Soup
summary: Creamy South Bohemian soup of potato, dill and a gently poached egg, sharpened with vinegar.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a large pot and soften the onion and mushrooms for 6 minutes, until the mushroom liquid has cooked off.
Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then add the stock and potato and simmer for 15 minutes, until the potato is completely tender.
Stir in the cream and most of the dill and simmer gently for 3 minutes, then season with salt and white pepper.
Bring a wide pan of water with the vinegar to a bare simmer and poach the eggs for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Ladle the soup into bowls, top each with a poached egg and the remaining dill.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set, and cook the yolks through for anyone pregnant, elderly or unwell.

title: Polish Zurek Sour Rye Soup
summary: Tangy soup of soured rye flour, potato and smoked sausage, served with halved boiled eggs.

steps.text: Mix the rye flour with the warm water, garlic and bay leaf in a jar and leave covered at room temperature for 3 days, until sour and bubbly.
Brown the sausage in a large pot for 4 minutes, until it releases its fat, then add the carrot, potato and stock.
Simmer for 15 minutes, until the potato is tender, then strain in the soured rye starter and stir.
Simmer for 8 minutes, stirring, until the soup thickens slightly, then add the marjoram, horseradish, salt and pepper.
Boil the eggs for 9 minutes until firm, peel and halve them, and serve them in the bowls of soup.

notes: Food safety: heat the sausage until steaming hot and above 75°C in the centre, and boil the eggs until the yolks are firm.
The soured starter is made with cooked-through simmering, so always boil the soup for 8 minutes before serving.

title: Hungarian Halaszle Fisherman's Soup
summary: Fiery paprika-red river fish soup in the style of the Danube, built on onion and tomato.

items.raw: 600g firm white fish fillets, cut in chunks

steps.text: Soften the onions in the oil for 10 minutes, until deep golden and sweet, then stir in both paprikas off the heat.
Add the tomatoes, capsicum and stock and simmer for 15 minutes, until the vegetables are soft and the broth is dark red.
Slide in the fish chunks and simmer gently for 5 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Season with salt, scatter with parsley and serve with lemon slices.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, and keep chilled until it goes into the pot.
Do not stir hard once the fish is added or it will break up.

title: Polish Mizeria Cucumber Salad
summary: Thin cucumber slices in a cool sour cream and dill dressing, a summer staple beside grilled meat.

steps.text: Toss the cucumber with a good pinch of salt and let it sit in a colander for 10 minutes, then squeeze out the liquid.
Stir the sour cream with the vinegar, sugar, dill and spring onion until smooth.
Fold the cucumber through the dressing, season with pepper and serve very cold.

notes: Serve within an hour of dressing or the cucumber will release more water and thin the sauce.

title: Romanian Ciorba de Perisoare Meatball Sour Soup
summary: Sour vegetable soup studded with herby pork and rice meatballs, finished with sour cream.

steps.text: Mix the pork, rice, egg, half the parsley, salt and pepper and roll into 24 small meatballs.
Simmer the onion, carrots, celery and capsicum in the stock for 12 minutes, until almost tender, then stir in the tomato paste.
Drop in the meatballs and simmer for 15 minutes, until the rice in them is tender and the centres reach 75°C.
Stir in the lemon juice, then temper the sour cream with a ladle of hot broth and stir it back in.
Serve in deep bowls scattered with the remaining parsley.

notes: Food safety: cook the meatballs until they reach 75°C in the centre and no pink remains.
Do not boil once the sour cream is added or it may split.

title: Serbian Ajvar Roasted Pepper Relish
summary: Smoky roasted pepper and aubergine spread that keeps for weeks in the fridge.

steps.text: Roast the capsicums and aubergine on a tray at 220°C for 45 minutes, turning once, until the skins are blistered and the flesh collapsed.
Rest them covered for 15 minutes, then peel off the skins and discard the seeds and stalks.
Chop the flesh finely and cook it in a wide pan with the garlic and half the oil for 15 minutes, stirring, until thick and jammy.
Stir in the vinegar, salt and sugar and the remaining oil, and cook 2 minutes more.
Cool and spoon into a clean jar, then chill.

notes: Store in a clean jar with a film of oil in the fridge for up to 2 weeks.

title: Czech Bramborak Garlic Potato Pancakes
summary: Crisp grated potato pancakes with marjoram and plenty of garlic.

steps.text: Squeeze the grated potato in a clean tea towel to remove the liquid, then mix with the garlic, egg, flour, marjoram and salt.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat and spoon in flat pancakes the size of a saucer.
Cook for 4 minutes each side, until deep golden and crisp at the edges.
Drain on paper and serve hot.

notes: Food safety: cook the egg-bound batter until the pancakes are golden and set all the way through.

title: Russian Syrniki Quark Pancakes
summary: Small golden fried cheese pancakes, soft inside, served with sour cream.

steps.text: Mash the ricotta with the egg, sugar, vanilla and salt, then fold in the flour to a soft, tacky dough.
Shape into 12 small thick discs with floured hands.
Fry in the oil over medium-low heat for 3 minutes each side, until deep golden and just firm.
Serve warm with a spoonful of sour cream.

notes: Food safety: cook until the centres are hot and set, as the mixture contains raw egg.

title: Russian Okroshka Cold Buttermilk Soup
summary: Chilled summer soup of buttermilk, cucumber, radish, egg and dill.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes until the yolks are firm, cool in cold water, peel and chop.
Combine the cucumber, radish, potato, ham, eggs, dill and spring onions in a large bowl.
Whisk the buttermilk with the cold water and a pinch of salt and pour over, then chill for 30 minutes before serving.

notes: Food safety: boil the eggs until the yolks are firm, and keep the soup refrigerated, eating within a day.

title: Russian Olivier Salad
summary: Diced potato, egg, pickles and peas bound with a tangy dressing, the classic party salad.

steps.text: Boil the potato and carrots in salted water for 18 minutes, until a knife slides in easily, then cool and dice.
Boil the eggs for 9 minutes until firm, then cool, peel and dice them.
Blanch the peas in boiling water for 2 minutes, drain and cool.
Fold everything together with the mayonnaise and sour cream, season and chill for 30 minutes before serving.

notes: Food safety: use fully cooked chicken, heated to 75°C before cooling, and keep the salad chilled, eating within 2 days.

title: Georgian Pkhali Spinach Walnut Balls
summary: Cold spinach and walnut paste with garlic and herbs, shaped into little balls and topped with pomegranate.

steps.text: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 2 minutes until wilted and bright green, then cool, squeeze dry and chop very finely.
Blend the walnuts, garlic, coriander leaves, vinegar and ground coriander to a coarse paste.
Mix the paste with the spinach, onion and salt until it holds together when squeezed.
Roll into 18 balls, top with pomegranate seeds and chill until firm, about 30 minutes.

notes: Chill in a covered container for up to 2 days.

title: Czech Cesnecka Garlic Soup
summary: Clear garlic and caraway soup with crisp bread croutons and a poached egg.

steps.text: Toss the bread in the olive oil and bake at 200°C for 10 minutes, until crisp and golden.
Soften the garlic in the butter for 2 minutes without browning, then add the stock, caraway, marjoram and potato.
Simmer for 15 minutes, until the potato is tender, then season.
Poach the eggs in barely simmering water with the vinegar for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Ladle into bowls and top with croutons and an egg.

notes: Food safety: poach the eggs until the whites are set, and cook fully for anyone vulnerable.

title: Polish Zupa Ogorkowa Pickle Soup
summary: Comforting potato soup soured with grated dill pickles and their brine.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the butter for 6 minutes, then add the carrots, parsnip, potato and stock.
Simmer for 18 minutes until all the vegetables are tender.
Add the grated pickles and brine and simmer for 5 minutes more.
Temper the sour cream with a ladle of hot soup, stir it in off the heat, then add the dill and season.

notes: Do not boil after adding the sour cream.

title: Russian Shchi Cabbage Soup
summary: Long-simmered beef and cabbage soup with a sour finish and dill.

items.raw: 400g beef chuck, cut in small cubes

steps.text: Simmer the beef with the water, stock and bay leaves for 35 minutes, skimming, until the meat is tender.
Add the onion, carrot and potato and simmer for 10 minutes, until nearly soft.
Add the cabbage and tomato paste and cook 10 minutes more, until the cabbage has softened.
Season with the vinegar, salt and pepper and serve with dill and a spoonful of sour cream.

notes: Food safety: simmer the beef until tender and steaming hot throughout, at least 75°C in the centre of the pieces.

title: Lithuanian Saltibarsciai Cold Beet Soup
summary: Vivid pink chilled beetroot soup with buttermilk, cucumber and boiled egg.

steps.text: Boil the beetroot in water for 30 minutes until a knife slides in easily, then cool and coarsely grate.
Boil the eggs for 9 minutes until firm, cool, peel and halve.
Whisk the buttermilk with the water and mix with the beetroot, cucumber, spring onion and dill, then season with salt and chill for 1 hour.
Serve cold with the eggs and the hot potato alongside.

notes: Food safety: boil the eggs until the yolks are firm, and keep the soup refrigerated, eating within a day.

title: Austrian Frittatensuppe Pancake Soup
summary: Clear beef broth with ribbons of thin herb pancake and chives.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, milk, eggs, a pinch of salt and nutmeg into a smooth thin batter.
Melt a little butter in a non-stick pan and cook thin pancakes for 2 minutes each side, until set and lightly golden.
Roll the pancakes up, slice them into thin ribbons and add the chives.
Heat the stock until steaming and ladle over the ribbons to serve.

notes: Food safety: cook the pancakes until fully set and golden, as they contain raw egg.

title: German Warmer Kartoffelsalat Bacon Potato Salad
summary: Warm waxy potatoes in a tangy bacon and onion dressing, the south German way.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes whole for 20 minutes, until a knife slides in easily, then peel while warm and slice.
Fry the bacon until crisp for 6 minutes, then add the onion and cook 4 minutes, until soft.
Add the stock, vinegar, mustard and sugar and simmer 2 minutes, then pour over the warm potato with the oil.
Toss gently, season and scatter with chives.

notes: Food safety: cook the bacon until crisp and hot throughout, and refrigerate leftovers promptly.

title: Slovenian Jota Bean and Sauerkraut Soup
summary: Hearty soup of beans, sauerkraut and potato with smoked meat from the Karst region.

steps.text: Cook the bacon and onion in the oil for 8 minutes, until the fat renders and the onion softens, then add the garlic and paprika.
Add the potato, sauerkraut, water and bay leaf and simmer for 25 minutes, until the potato is soft.
Stir the flour into a ladle of the soup, then add it back with the beans and simmer 8 minutes, until slightly thickened.
Season to taste with salt and pepper and serve hot with bread.

notes: Food safety: cook the bacon until crisp at the edges and steaming hot.

title: Swedish Raggmunk Potato Pancakes
summary: Thin crisp potato pancakes served with crisp bacon and a spoonful of lingonberry-style preserve.

steps.text: Whisk the milk, eggs, flour and salt to a batter and stir in the grated potato.
Fry the bacon in a wide pan for 5 minutes until crisp, and keep warm.
Heat the butter in the pan and spoon in thin pancakes, then cook 3 minutes each side, until golden and crisp.
Serve with the bacon and cranberry sauce.

notes: Food safety: cook the bacon until crisp and the pancakes until set throughout.

title: Swedish Ärtsoppa Yellow Pea Soup
summary: Thick yellow split pea soup with ham and mustard, a Thursday tradition.

items.raw: 300g ham hock, or diced cooked ham

steps.text: Put the peas, water, onion, carrot and ham in a large pot and bring to a boil, skimming until the foam stops rising.
Simmer gently for 60 minutes, until the peas are completely soft and the soup thick.
Take out the ham, shred the meat and return it, then add the herbs, salt and pepper.
Serve with a spoonful of mustard.

notes: Food safety: heat the ham until steaming hot throughout.

title: Finnish Lohikeitto Salmon Soup
summary: Creamy salmon and potato soup with dill and allspice.

steps.text: Soften the leek in the butter for 5 minutes, then add the carrot, potato, stock and allspice.
Simmer for 15 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Pour in the cream and add the salmon, then simmer gently for 4 minutes, until the salmon turns opaque.
Season, stir through the dill and serve.

notes: Food safety: cook the salmon until opaque throughout and keep it refrigerated until needed.

title: Swedish Hovmästarsås Mustard and Dill Sauce
summary: Sweet-sharp mustard and dill sauce for cured salmon, boiled potato and gravlax.

steps.text: Whisk the mustard, sugar, vinegar and a pinch of salt until the sugar has dissolved.
Slowly whisk in the oil in a thin stream until the sauce is thick and glossy.
Stir through the dill, season and chill for 30 minutes.

notes: Keep chilled in a jar for up to 5 days.

title: Finnish Rosolli Beetroot Salad
summary: Ruby diced beetroot, apple, potato and pickles in a creamy dressing.

steps.text: Boil the beetroots, potato and carrots for 25 minutes, until a knife slides in easily, then cool, peel and dice.
Whip the cream until soft peaks form, then stir in the vinegar, sugar, salt and pepper.
Toss the vegetables, apple, pickles and onion with the dressing and chill for 1 hour before serving.

notes: Serve cold, and keep refrigerated for up to 2 days.

title: Norwegian Eggerøre Soft Scrambled Eggs
summary: Very softly scrambled eggs on rye with chives and smoked salmon.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs, milk and seasoning in a bowl.
Melt the butter in a small pan over low heat and add the eggs, stirring slowly for 3 minutes until just set but still creamy.
Pile onto toasted rye, top with the smoked salmon and chives.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until just set with no liquid egg remaining, and keep the smoked salmon refrigerated until serving. Use fresh, uncracked eggs; for pregnant women, older people, young children and anyone with low immunity, cook the eggs until the yolks are firm.

title: Swedish Skagenröra Prawn and Dill Toast Topping
summary: Cold prawns folded through mayonnaise, dill and lemon over buttered toast.

steps.text: Mix the prawns, mayonnaise, sour cream, lemon juice, dill and onion until lightly bound.
Season with salt and white pepper, then chill for 15 minutes.
Toast the bread for 3 minutes until golden, butter it while hot and pile the prawn mixture on top.

notes: Food safety: use prawns that are cooked and kept refrigerated, and eat within 24 hours.

title: Danish Remoulade Sauce
summary: Curry-spiced pickle mayonnaise for fish fillets, roast pork and hot dogs.

steps.text: Stir the mayonnaise with the curry powder, mustard and lemon juice until smooth.
Fold through the pickles, capers and parsley.
Season, then chill for at least 20 minutes so the flavours settle.

notes: Keep chilled in a jar for up to 5 days.

title: Jamaican Escovitch Pickled Vegetable Sauce
summary: Hot, tangy pickled carrot, onion and chilli to spoon over fried fish or chicken.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a pan and fry the carrot, onion, capsicum and chilli for 3 minutes, until just starting to soften but still crisp.
Add the vinegar, allspice, sugar and salt and simmer for 5 minutes, until the vegetables are tender but bright.
Cool to room temperature, then spoon over hot fried fish or chicken.

notes: Keeps in a clean jar in the fridge for up to 2 weeks.

title: Trinidadian Corn Soup
summary: Sweet corn soup with split peas, pumpkin and small dumplings, sold by street vendors at night.

items.raw: 4 corn cobs, kernels cut off and cobs halved
items.prep: kernels cut off and cobs halved

steps.text: Simmer the split peas and corn cobs in the water with the onion and garlic for 25 minutes, until the peas are soft.
Add the pumpkin, carrot and whole chilli and simmer 12 minutes, until tender.
Rub the butter into the flour with a pinch of salt, add water to a stiff dough and roll into small dumplings.
Add the dumplings and corn kernels and simmer for 10 minutes, until the dumplings float and are cooked through.
Remove the cobs and chilli, stir through the coriander, then season and serve.

notes: Remove the corn cobs before serving.

title: Haitian Soup Joumou Pumpkin Soup
summary: Freedom soup of pumpkin, beef and vegetables eaten on New Year's Day.

steps.text: Simmer the beef in the water with the onion, garlic, thyme and cloves for 40 minutes, until tender.
Add the pumpkin, potato, carrot and celery and simmer for 15 minutes, until all are soft.
Lift out about half the pumpkin and mash or blend it smooth, then return it to thicken the soup.
Add the cabbage and rigatoni and simmer for 10 minutes, until the pasta is tender.
Stir in the parsley and lime juice, season and serve hot.

notes: Food safety: simmer the beef until tender and steaming hot throughout, at least 75°C in the centre of the pieces.

title: Puerto Rican Sofrito
summary: Fresh green herb and capsicum base used to start rice, beans and braises.

steps.text: Pulse the capsicum, onion, garlic and spring onion in a food processor until finely chopped but not a puree.
Add the coriander, parsley, oil, vinegar and salt and pulse until a coarse green paste forms.
Spoon into a jar or ice cube trays, and freeze in tablespoon portions.

notes: Freezes for up to 3 months in portions.

title: Dominican Mangú Mashed Plantain Breakfast
summary: Boiled green plantain mashed with butter and topped with quick pickled onion and fried eggs.

items.raw: 4 green plantains, peeled and cut in chunks

steps.text: Boil the plantain in salted water for 20 minutes, until a knife slides in easily, saving a cup of the water.
Soak the onion in the vinegar with a pinch of salt for 15 minutes while the plantain cooks.
Mash the plantain with the butter and a splash of the cooking water to a smooth, thick puree.
Fry the eggs in the oil for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Pile the mangú on plates and top with the pickled onion and eggs.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set, and the yolks too for anyone vulnerable.

title: Bajan Macaroni Pie
summary: Baked macaroni in a cheesy custard with mustard, a fixture of the Sunday lunch table.

steps.text: Boil the macaroni in salted water for 8 minutes, until just tender, then drain and toss with the butter.
Soften the onion in a little water for 4 minutes, until translucent.
Whisk the eggs with the evaporated milk, mustard, tomato sauce, pepper and most of the cheese.
Fold the pasta and onion through the custard and tip into a baking dish, then top with the remaining cheese.
Bake at 180°C for 30 minutes, until set in the centre and golden on top.

notes: Food safety: bake until the custard is fully set, as it contains raw egg.

title: Nigerian Moi Moi Steamed Bean Pudding
summary: Soft steamed pudding of black-eyed beans with capsicum, onion and chilli, often with a boiled egg inside.

items.raw: 300g dried black-eyed beans, soaked overnight and skinned

steps.text: Blend the beans with the capsicum, onion and chilli, adding the water, until completely smooth.
Stir in the oil, salt and crumbled stock cube, then fold the sliced eggs through gently.
Pour into 6 ramekins or foil cups, cover each tightly with foil.
Steam over simmering water for 40 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean and the tops are firm.
Rest for 5 minutes before turning out.

notes: Food safety: use hard-boiled eggs with firm yolks, and eat within a day or reheat until steaming hot.

title: Nigerian Efo Riro Spinach Stew
summary: Rich spinach stew in a pepper and tomato base with chicken and chilli, finished with a little stock.

items.raw: 400g chicken thigh fillet, cut in chunks

steps.text: Blend the capsicums, tomatoes, half the onion and chillies to a smooth sauce, then boil it for 15 minutes until reduced and thick.
Simmer the chicken in the stock for 15 minutes, until cooked through and no pink remains.
Fry the remaining onion in the oil for 5 minutes, then add the reduced sauce and cook 10 minutes, until the oil rises to the surface.
Add the chicken with a little stock and the spinach and cook 5 minutes, until the leaves are soft but still green.
Season with the salt and serve with rice or boiled yam.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C in the thickest part and the juices run clear.

title: Ghanaian Waakye Rice and Beans
summary: Rice and beans cooked together until russet, served with fried eggs, spaghetti and a spicy sauce.

steps.text: Boil the beans in the water with the soda and onion for 30 minutes, until just tender and the water turns reddish.
Stir in the rice and salt and cook, covered, for 20 minutes until the rice is tender and the water absorbed.
Blend the passata, chillies and garlic and simmer 8 minutes, until thickened into a sauce.
Fry the eggs in the oil for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Serve the waakye with the sauce and an egg on each plate.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set, and the yolks too for anyone vulnerable.

title: Senegalese Salade Avocat Avocado and Prawn Salad
summary: Creamy avocado, tomato, cucumber and prawns in a mustard vinaigrette.

steps.text: Whisk the lime juice, oil, mustard, salt and pepper into a smooth vinaigrette.
Gently toss the avocado, prawns, tomato, cucumber and onion with the dressing until just coated.
Scatter with parsley and serve right away.

notes: Food safety: use prawns that are cooked and kept refrigerated, and eat the salad within a few hours.

title: Persian Ash Reshteh Herb Noodle Soup
summary: Thick soup of beans, lentils, herbs and noodles topped with fried onion, mint oil and yoghurt.

steps.text: Fry the onions in 2 tbsp oil for 20 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden and crisp, and set a third aside for the topping.
Add the turmeric, lentils and water to the rest of the onions and simmer for 20 minutes, until the lentils are soft.
Add the chickpeas, kidney beans, spinach and herbs, boil hard for 10 minutes then simmer 5 minutes more, until the greens are cooked down.
Add the linguine and simmer for 8 minutes, until the noodles are tender, then season well.
Warm the mint in the remaining oil for 1 minute and serve over the soup with the reserved onion and yoghurt.

notes: Add a splash of hot water if the soup thickens too much on standing.

title: Persian Mast-o-Khiar Yoghurt and Cucumber
summary: Cooling yoghurt with cucumber, mint and walnuts, eaten as a salad or dip.

steps.text: Stir the yoghurt, garlic, most of the mint, salt and pepper until smooth.
Fold through the cucumber and sultanas, then chill for 20 minutes.
Serve topped with the walnuts and a pinch of mint.

notes: Best the day it is made, as the cucumber releases water.

title: Persian Salad Shirazi
summary: Finely diced cucumber, tomato and onion with lime and dried mint.

steps.text: Dice the cucumber, tomato and onion to the same small size, around 5mm, until they are like a fine relish.
Toss with the lime juice, olive oil, mint, salt and pepper.
Rest 5 minutes, then taste and adjust the lime and salt.

notes: Dress just before serving so the vegetables stay crisp.

title: Persian Halim Chicken and Barley Porridge
summary: Slow-cooked porridge of shredded chicken and barley, topped with cinnamon sugar and melted butter.

steps.text: Simmer the chicken with the onion, turmeric and half the water for 25 minutes, until cooked through and tender, then shred the meat.
Simmer the barley in the remaining water for 90 minutes, stirring now and then, until completely soft and thick.
Add the shredded chicken and cook 40 minutes more, beating with a wooden spoon until the porridge is smooth and stretchy.
Season with the salt and pepper and divide among bowls.
Top with melted butter and a dusting of cinnamon and sugar.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C in the centre before shredding.
Add water if the porridge becomes too stiff while cooking.

title: Persian Mirza Ghasemi Smoky Aubergine and Egg
summary: Charred aubergine mashed with garlic, tomato and egg, a breakfast from northern Iran.

steps.text: Char the whole aubergines over a flame or under a hot grill for 20 minutes, turning, until blackened and collapsed.
Peel off the skin and mash the flesh roughly.
Fry the garlic and turmeric in the oil for 1 minute, then add the tomato and cook 6 minutes, until it breaks down.
Stir in the aubergine and cook 5 minutes, until thick and the oil separates.
Make three wells, crack in the eggs and stir until the eggs are fully set, about 3 minutes, then season.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until firm and fully set.

title: Israeli Sabich Aubergine and Egg Pita
summary: Fried aubergine, hard-boiled egg, salad and tahini in warm pita, a breakfast sandwich from Tel Aviv.

steps.text: Brush the aubergine with oil and roast at 220°C for 25 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and soft.
Boil the eggs for 9 minutes until the yolks are firm, then cool, peel and slice.
Whisk the tahini with the lemon juice, garlic, salt and enough water to make a pourable sauce.
Warm the pita until soft and pliable, about 1 minute.
Fill with aubergine, egg, tomato, cucumber and pickles, then drizzle with tahini and scatter with parsley.

notes: Food safety: boil the eggs until the yolks are firm, and eat the sandwich the same day.

title: Peruvian Salsa Criolla Onion Relish
summary: Sharp, crisp red onion relish with lime and chilli for grilled meat, fish and sandwiches.

steps.text: Soak the sliced onion in cold salted water for 10 minutes, until the sharp edge has softened, then drain well.
Toss the onion with the lime, chilli, coriander, tomato, oil and salt.
Rest 5 minutes and serve.

notes: Make just before serving; it softens after an hour.

title: Peruvian Chupe de Camarones Prawn Chowder
summary: Rich prawn and corn chowder with potato, rice, egg and a little cheese, from Arequipa.

steps.text: Soften the onion and garlic in the oil for 8 minutes, until golden, then stir in the tomato paste and paprika for 2 minutes.
Add the stock, potato, rice and corn and simmer for 20 minutes, until the rice and potato are tender.
Add the peas and evaporated milk and simmer 5 minutes, until hot and slightly thickened.
Add the prawns and cook 3 minutes, until pink and curled.
Poach the eggs in the soup for 3 minutes, until the whites are set, then top with ricotta and coriander.

notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until pink and opaque and the eggs until the whites are set.

title: Colombian Changua Milk and Egg Soup
summary: Bogotá's gentle breakfast soup of milk, spring onion and a poached egg with torn bread.

steps.text: Bring the milk, water and spring onion to a gentle simmer for 5 minutes, until the onion is soft and the milk steaming.
Season with salt and pepper, then crack in the eggs and poach for 3 minutes, until the whites are just set.
Ladle into bowls over the torn bread and sprinkle with coriander.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set, and the yolks too for anyone vulnerable.

title: Venezuelan Perico Scrambled Eggs
summary: Eggs scrambled with tomato, onion and capsicum, eaten with arepas or toast.

steps.text: Soften the onion and capsicum in the oil for 3 minutes, until translucent.
Add the tomato and cook 2 minutes, until it just starts to soften.
Pour in the beaten eggs and stir gently for 3 minutes until just set, then season and add spring onion.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until set with no runny egg left.

title: Brazilian Farofa Toasted Cassava Flour
summary: Buttery toasted flour with onion and bacon, scattered over rice, beans and grilled meat.

steps.text: Fry the bacon in the butter for 5 minutes, until crisp, then add the onion for 3 minutes, until soft.
Push to one side, scramble in the eggs and cook 2 minutes, until just set.
Add the flour and stir for 3 minutes, until golden and toasty, then fold through the parsley.
Season to taste with salt and pepper, then serve warm.

notes: Food safety: cook the bacon until crisp and the eggs until set with no runny egg.

title: Chilean Pebre Fresh Salsa
summary: Fresh tomato, onion, coriander and chilli salsa with vinegar, served with bread and grilled meat.

steps.text: Soak the onion in cold water for 5 minutes, until the sharpness mellows, then drain well.
Mix with the tomato, coriander, chilli and garlic.
Stir in the vinegar, oil and salt and rest 10 minutes before serving.

notes: Best eaten the day it is made.

title: Tahitian Poisson Cru Coconut Fish Salad
summary: Fresh tuna cured briefly in lime juice, then dressed with coconut milk, cucumber and tomato.

steps.text: Toss the tuna with the lime juice and a pinch of salt and leave in the fridge for 10 minutes, until the outside turns opaque and firm.
Drain off most of the lime juice.
Fold through the cucumber, tomato, onion, carrot and chilli.
Stir in the coconut milk and coriander and serve immediately, very cold.

notes: Food safety: use only very fresh sashimi-grade fish kept below 4°C. The lime only firms the outside, so the fish stays raw inside. Avoid for pregnant, elderly, young or immunocompromised people. Eat the same day.

title: Salvadoran Curtido Cabbage Slaw
summary: Lightly fermented-style cabbage, carrot and oregano slaw served with pupusas and grilled meat.

steps.text: Pour boiling water over the cabbage in a bowl, stand 1 minute, until just wilted, then drain and cool.
Mix with the carrot, onion and chilli in a large jar.
Dissolve the sugar and salt in the vinegar and hot water, then add the oregano and pour over the vegetables.
Cover and refrigerate for 24 hours before serving, until the cabbage is tangy and crunchy.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for up to 2 weeks.

title: Mexican Sopa Azteca Tortilla Soup
summary: Smoky tomato and chilli broth with crisp tortilla strips, avocado, lime and shredded chicken.

steps.text: Fry the tortilla strips in 2 tbsp oil for 2 minutes, until crisp and golden, and drain on paper.
Blend the tomato, half the onion, garlic and chillies, then fry in the remaining oil for 8 minutes, until darker and thick.
Add the stock and the chicken and simmer gently for 15 minutes, until the chicken reaches 75°C in the centre.
Shred the chicken, return it to the soup and season with salt.
Serve topped with tortilla strips, avocado, ricotta, coriander and a wedge of lime.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C in the centre and the juices run clear.

title: Mexican Salsa Macha Peanut and Chilli Oil
summary: Dark, nutty chilli oil with peanuts, garlic and sesame, spooned onto eggs, tacos and noodles.

steps.text: Warm the oil in a small pot over low heat, then add the garlic and cook 3 minutes, until pale gold.
Add the peanuts and sesame and cook 2 minutes, until fragrant and lightly golden.
Take off the heat, stir in the chilli flakes, vinegar, sugar and salt and let it settle until the sizzling stops.
Pulse briefly for a chunky texture, then cool and jar.

notes: Keeps in a clean jar in the fridge for up to 3 weeks.

title: Swedish Gubbröra Egg and Anchovy Spread
summary: Chopped egg, onion and anchovy with dill and sour cream, piled on rye crispbread at Midsummer.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes until the yolks are firm, then cool in cold water, peel and chop.
Fold the eggs with the anchovies, onion, sour cream, mayonnaise and herbs.
Season with pepper and chill for 15 minutes, then pile onto the rye bread.

notes: Food safety: boil the eggs until the yolks are firm, keep chilled and eat within 24 hours.

title: Icelandic Kjötsúpa Lamb and Root Vegetable Soup
summary: Plain, hearty lamb soup with swede, potato, carrot and rice, the Icelandic Sunday soup.

steps.text: Cover the lamb with the water, bring to a boil and skim until no foam rises.
Simmer for 60 minutes with the onion and bay leaves, until the meat is very tender and falling from the bone.
Add the rice, swede, potato, carrot and thyme and simmer 20 minutes, until the vegetables are soft.
Remove the bones, shred the meat and add the cabbage, then simmer 5 minutes, until wilted, and season.

notes: Food safety: cook the lamb until very tender and at least 75°C in the centre.

title: Danish Hønsesalat Chicken and Asparagus Salad
summary: Creamy chicken salad with asparagus and pineapple for open sandwiches.

steps.text: Boil the asparagus for 3 minutes, until bright green and just tender, then cool and cut in short lengths.
Stir the mayonnaise, sour cream and curry powder until smooth.
Fold in the chicken, asparagus, pineapple, celery and chives, then season.
Chill for 20 minutes and serve on rye bread or with lettuce.

notes: Food safety: use chicken cooked to 75°C and cooled quickly, keep the salad chilled and eat within 2 days.

title: Bulgarian Shopska Salad
summary: Tomato, cucumber and pepper salad under a thick drift of grated white cheese.

steps.text: Toss the tomato, cucumber, capsicum and onion with the oil, vinegar and salt.
Rest 5 minutes, until the vegetables begin to release their juice.
Pile on a platter and cover thickly with the grated feta and parsley.

notes: Serve immediately so the cheese stays fluffy.

title: Bulgarian Kyopolou Smoked Aubergine Dip
summary: Charred aubergine and pepper dip with garlic, parsley and oil.

steps.text: Char the aubergines and capsicums over a flame or under a hot grill for 25 minutes, turning, until blackened and collapsed.
Rest covered 10 minutes, then peel and drain away the juices.
Chop the flesh finely and mix with the garlic, oil, vinegar and salt.
Fold in the parsley and tomato, then chill for 30 minutes.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days.

title: Romanian Zacusca Vegetable Spread
summary: Slow-cooked aubergine, pepper and tomato spread, jarred in autumn for bread.

steps.text: Char the aubergines and capsicums under a hot grill for 25 minutes, turning, until blackened and soft, then peel and chop fine.
Fry the onion in the oil for 10 minutes, until golden, then add the tomatoes and bay leaves.
Add the aubergine and capsicum and simmer on low heat for 80 minutes, stirring often, until very thick and the oil separates.
Stir in the garlic, sugar and salt for the last 10 minutes of cooking.
Pack into clean jars and cool before chilling.

notes: Keeps in the fridge in sealed clean jars for up to 3 weeks.

title: Ukrainian Deruny Potato Pancakes
summary: Lacy grated potato and onion pancakes served with sour cream.

steps.text: Grate the potato and onion and squeeze very dry in a clean towel, then stir in the egg, flour, salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and spoon in the batter in flat rounds.
Fry for 4 minutes each side, until deep golden and crisp, then drain on paper.
Serve hot with sour cream.

notes: Food safety: cook the pancakes until golden and set throughout.

title: Czech Bramboracka Potato and Mushroom Soup
summary: Rustic soup of potato, root vegetables and dried mushroom with marjoram and caraway.

steps.text: Melt the butter and soften the onion and mushrooms for 8 minutes, until golden and the liquid cooks off.
Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then add the stock, potato, carrot, celery, caraway and marjoram.
Simmer for 20 minutes, until the potato is very tender, then crush a few pieces with a spoon to thicken.
Stir in the garlic, season and serve hot.

notes: Add a little water if the soup becomes too thick.

title: Slovak Kapustnica Sauerkraut Soup
summary: Smoked sausage and sauerkraut soup with paprika and a little cream, the Christmas Eve soup.

steps.text: Fry the bacon and sausage in the oil for 6 minutes, until browned, then add the onion for 4 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the garlic and paprika, then add the sauerkraut, mushrooms, water and bay leaves.
Simmer for 40 minutes, then add the potato and cook 15 minutes, until the potato is tender.
Stir in the cream, season with pepper and serve hot.

notes: Food safety: heat the sausage until steaming hot and above 75°C throughout.

title: Jamaican Festival Sweet Fried Dumplings
summary: Sweet cornmeal dumplings fried until crisp outside and tender within.

steps.text: Mix the flour, cornmeal, sugar, baking powder and salt, then stir in the vanilla and milk to a soft dough.
Knead for 2 minutes, until smooth, then roll into 8 finger-length shapes.
Heat the oil to 170°C and fry the dumplings in batches for 5 minutes, turning, until deep golden.
Drain on paper and serve warm.

notes: Keep the oil at a steady 170°C so the centres cook through.

title: Guyanese Cook-up Rice
summary: One-pot coconut rice with black-eyed beans, chicken and thyme.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil for 6 minutes, until golden on all sides, then add the onion and garlic for 3 minutes.
Add the coconut milk, water, beans, thyme, chilli and salt and bring to a simmer until the chicken is just cooked.
Stir in the rice, cover and cook on low heat for 20 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid absorbed.
Rest 10 minutes, stir through the spring onions and remove the chilli and thyme.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C in the centre and no pink remains.

title: Nigerian Ofada Ata Rodo Pepper Sauce
summary: Deep, fiery pepper sauce of roasted capsicum and chilli fried in oil with onion and seasoning.

steps.text: Roast the capsicums and chillies at 220°C for 25 minutes, until blackened and collapsed, then blend with half the onion and the garlic to a coarse puree.
Heat the oil until shimmering, then fry the remaining sliced onion for 8 minutes, until golden.
Add the puree and cook on medium heat for 20 minutes, stirring, until the sauce is thick and the oil rises to the surface.
Season with the cumin, stock cube and salt and serve with rice.

notes: Keeps in a jar in the fridge for up to 1 week.

title: Nigerian Dodo Fried Plantain
summary: Ripe plantain fried until caramelised at the edges, a favourite side with eggs or stew.

steps.text: Toss the plantain slices with the salt and chilli flakes.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat to about 170°C.
Fry in batches for 3 minutes each side, until deep golden and caramelised at the edges.
Drain on paper and serve hot.

notes: Choose plantains with black-spotted skins for the sweetest dodo.

title: Ghanaian Kontomire Spinach Stew
summary: Spinach stewed with onion, tomato and chilli in oil, served with boiled yam or rice and eggs.

steps.text: Blend the tomato, half the onion, the chillies, garlic and ginger to a smooth sauce.
Fry the remaining onion in the oil for 5 minutes, until golden, then add the sauce and cook 15 minutes, until thick and the oil separates.
Add the spinach and stock cube and simmer for 8 minutes, until the leaves are soft but still green.
Boil the eggs for 9 minutes until firm, peel and halve them.
Season and serve the stew with the eggs.

notes: Food safety: boil the eggs until the yolks are firm.

title: Georgian Ajapsandali Vegetable Stew
summary: Summer stew of aubergine, tomato, pepper and potato with plenty of coriander and basil.

steps.text: Salt the aubergine and rest 10 minutes, then pat dry and brown in oil for 8 minutes, until golden.
Soften the onion in the same pan for 5 minutes, then add the potato and capsicum and cook 10 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, aubergine, garlic and chilli and simmer 20 minutes, until the vegetables are tender and the sauce thick.
Stir in the herbs and season, serving warm or at room temperature.

notes: Resting the salted aubergine is not included in the prep time.

title: Polish Naleśniki Ricotta Crepes
summary: Thin crepes rolled around a sweet ricotta filling and browned in butter.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, eggs, milk and sugar into a smooth thin batter.
Cook thin crepes in a buttered pan for 1 to 2 minutes each side, until golden.
Mix the ricotta with the vanilla and lemon zest.
Fill and roll up the crepes, then brown them in the remaining butter for 2 minutes, until golden.
Dust with icing sugar and serve warm.

notes: Food safety: cook the crepes until fully set and golden since the batter contains raw egg.

title: Estonian Mulgikapsad Sauerkraut and Barley Stew
summary: Slow-braised sauerkraut with pork and pearl barley, a winter dish from Mulgi.

steps.text: Brown the pork in the oil for 8 minutes, until golden, then add the onion and carrot for 4 minutes.
Add the sauerkraut, barley, caraway, tomato paste and water.
Cover and simmer for 70 minutes, until the pork is tender and the barley is soft.
Season and serve with boiled potatoes.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork until tender and at least 75°C in the centre of the pieces.

title: Brazilian Vinagrete Tomato and Onion Salsa
summary: Chopped tomato, onion and capsicum in a vinegar dressing for churrasco and feijoada.

steps.text: Combine the tomato, onion, capsicum and parsley in a bowl.
Add the vinegar, oil, salt and pepper and stir until the vegetables are glossy.
Rest 15 minutes until the juices have mingled, then serve.

notes: Best eaten within a few hours.

title: Japanese Chawanmushi Savoury Egg Custard
summary: Silky steamed egg custard in dashi with prawn and shiitake, set gently so it wobbles like soft tofu.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs gently with the dashi, soy sauce, mirin and a pinch of salt, then strain through a sieve into a jug so the custard is smooth.
Divide the prawns and shiitake between four heatproof cups and pour the egg mixture over, skimming off any bubbles.
Cover each cup with foil and set in a steamer over barely simmering water.
Steam on low for 15 to 18 minutes, until the custard just sets with a gentle wobble and a skewer comes out clear.
Scatter with spring onion and serve hot with a spoon.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until fully set with no liquid egg, and the prawns until pink and opaque. Keep the steamer at a gentle simmer so the custard stays smooth. Eat the same day and do not reheat. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Japanese Okayu Egg and Spring Onion Rice Porridge
summary: Soft, gentle rice porridge simmered in dashi with a softly set egg, a comforting Japanese morning bowl.

steps.text: Put the rice, water and dashi powder in a saucepan and bring to the boil until bubbling, then reduce to a low simmer.
Cover with the lid slightly ajar and cook for 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the rice is very soft and creamy.
Season with a pinch of salt and the soy sauce.
Beat the eggs and swirl them in, then cook for 2 minutes, until the egg is fully set in soft ribbons.
Ladle into bowls and top with spring onion, sesame oil and pickled ginger.

notes: Food safety: cook the egg until fully set, with no runny egg left. Eat the same day.

title: Japanese Salmon Ochazuke Dashi Rice
summary: Hot dashi poured over rice and flaked grilled salmon, a light and soothing Japanese supper.

items.raw: 2 salmon fillets, skin on, about 120g each
1 sheet nori, cut in thin strips

steps.text: Season the salmon with a pinch of salt and grill for 8 to 10 minutes, turning once, until the flesh flakes easily and is opaque all the way through.
Flake the salmon into large pieces and discard the skin.
Divide the warm rice between two bowls and top with the salmon, nori, sesame seeds and spring onion.
Stir the soy sauce into the hot dashi and pour it over the rice until it is just covered.
Serve straight away with a little wasabi on the side.

notes: Food safety: cook the salmon until opaque all the way through, then eat it promptly. Cool any leftover rice and refrigerate it within 1 hour, then use within 24 hours.

title: Japanese Kenchinjiru Root Vegetable and Tofu Soup
summary: A temple-style vegan soup of daikon, carrot, sweet potato and crumbled tofu simmered in dashi and sesame oil.

steps.text: Heat the sesame oil in a large saucepan over medium heat and fry the tofu for 3 minutes, until lightly golden.
Add the daikon, carrot, sweet potato and shiitake and stir for 2 minutes, until glossy.
Pour in the dashi and bring to the boil, then simmer for 15 minutes, until all the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the soy sauce and mirin and taste for seasoning.
Ladle into bowls and top with spring onion.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days; reheat until steaming hot.

title: Japanese Goma-ae Sesame Spinach
summary: Blanched spinach in a sweet, nutty ground sesame dressing, a classic cold Japanese side.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of water to the boil and blanch the spinach for 40 seconds, until bright green and just wilted.
Drain and cool under cold water, then squeeze out the water firmly with your hands.
Grind the sesame seeds in a mortar until mostly crushed and oily.
Mix in the soy sauce, sugar, mirin and vinegar until the dressing is smooth.
Toss the spinach through the dressing and serve in small mounds.

notes: Best eaten the day it is made. Chill for 20 minutes for a cooler side.

title: Japanese Hiyayakko Chilled Tofu with Ginger and Bonito
summary: Cold silken tofu with grated ginger, spring onion, bonito flakes and soy, a no-cook summer starter.

steps.text: Drain the tofu gently on paper towel for 5 minutes, then cut it into two large blocks.
Place each block on a plate and top with the ginger, spring onion and bonito flakes.
Drizzle with the soy sauce and scatter with sesame seeds and herb.
Chill until very cold, then serve straight away.

notes: Keep the tofu in the fridge until the moment of serving.

title: Japanese Ohitashi Greens in Dashi
summary: Blanched greens soaked in cool soy dashi, a refreshing make-ahead side with bonito flakes.

steps.text: Blanch the bok choy in boiling water for 1 minute, until bright green and just tender at the stems.
Plunge into iced water, then drain well and squeeze lightly.
Mix the dashi, soy sauce and mirin in a shallow dish.
Add the greens and soak in the fridge for 30 minutes, turning once.
Lift out, cut into short lengths and serve topped with bonito flakes and sesame seeds.

notes: Keeps in its liquid in the fridge for 2 days.

title: Chinese Cong You Bing Spring Onion Egg Pancake
summary: Flaky, crisp-edged spring onion pancakes folded around a soft fried egg, a Taiwanese street breakfast.

steps.text: Mix the flour, boiling water and a pinch of salt into a shaggy dough, then knead for 3 minutes, until smooth, and rest under a bowl for 20 minutes.
Divide into 4 balls and roll each very thin, brush with sesame oil and scatter with spring onion and salt.
Roll up like a cigar, coil into a snail and flatten with your palm, then roll out to about 3mm thick.
Fry each pancake in a little vegetable oil for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden and blistered with crisp edges.
Fry the eggs in the same pan until the whites are set and the yolks are cooked to your liking.
Place an egg on each pancake, drizzle with soy, sugar and chilli sauce, fold and serve warm.

notes: Food safety: cook eggs until the whites are completely set. Pregnant, elderly and young people should have the yolk cooked firm.

title: Chinese Marbled Soy Eggs
summary: Hard-boiled eggs cracked and simmered in star anise, wine and soy until the shells show a marbled pattern.

steps.text: Boil the eggs in water for 9 minutes, until the yolks are fully set, then cool in cold water.
Tap the shells all over with a spoon so they crackle but stay on.
Simmer the wine, soy sauce, star anise, cinnamon, sugar, orange peel and water for 10 minutes, until fragrant and dark.
Add the eggs and simmer on very low heat for 40 minutes, until the colour has soaked in.
Turn off the heat and steep for at least 2 hours, or overnight in the fridge, then peel to reveal the marbling.

notes: Food safety: boil the eggs until the yolks are fully set. Keep refrigerated in the liquid and eat within 4 days.

title: Chinese Dry-Fried Green Beans with Pork
summary: Blistered green beans wok-tossed with pork mince, garlic and preserved vegetable, a Sichuan favourite.

steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat and fry the beans for 5 to 6 minutes, tossing, until blistered and wrinkled but still crisp.
Remove the beans and add the remaining oil to the wok.
Stir-fry the pork mince for 4 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and cooked through to 75°C.
Add the garlic, ginger and chillies and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Return the beans with the soy sauce, wine and sugar and toss for 1 minute, until glossy.
Finish with the sesame oil and serve hot.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork mince until it reaches 75°C in the centre and no pink remains. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and use in 2 days.

title: Chinese Doufu Nao Savoury Silken Tofu Pudding
summary: Warm, spoonable silken tofu in a soy, chilli oil and pickle broth, a northern Chinese breakfast.

items.raw: 1 tsp cornflour mixed with 1 tbsp water

steps.text: Heat the stock, soy sauce and vinegar in a small saucepan until simmering.
Stir in the cornflour mixture and cook for 1 minute, until the broth is lightly thickened.
Slide the tofu in large spoonfuls into the broth and warm gently for 3 minutes, until just steaming.
Ladle into two bowls and top with peanuts, spring onion, chilli oil and sesame oil.

notes: Serve at once; the tofu breaks up if boiled hard.
Food safety: Keep any leftover garlic, herb or chilli oil in the fridge and use it within 4 days.

title: Korean Kongnamul Guk Bean Sprout Soup
summary: A clear, clean soup of soybean sprouts and garlic, the classic Korean morning-after bowl.

steps.text: Bring the water and kombu to the boil until bubbling in a lidded pot, then remove the kombu.
Add the sprouts and garlic, cover and cook for 10 minutes, until the sprouts are tender and no longer raw-tasting.
Stir in the soy sauce and fish sauce and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add the spring onions and chilli flakes and drizzle with sesame oil before serving hot.

notes: Keep the lid on while cooking to avoid a grassy taste. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Korean Miyeok Guk Seaweed and Beef Soup
summary: Birthday soup of silky wakame simmered with beef, sesame oil and garlic.

steps.text: Soak the wakame in cold water for 15 minutes, until soft, then drain and cut into short lengths.
Heat the sesame oil in a pot and fry the beef for 4 minutes, until browned all over.
Add the seaweed and garlic and stir for 2 minutes, until fragrant.
Pour in the water and soy sauce, bring to the boil and simmer for 25 minutes, until the beef is tender.
Stir in the fish sauce and serve with the spring onion.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef to at least 71°C in the thickest piece and until tender, with no pink. Cool leftovers quickly and use within 3 days.

title: Korean Ssamjang Dipping Sauce
summary: Thick savoury dip of fermented soybean paste, gochujang, garlic and sesame for lettuce wraps.

steps.text: Mix the doenjang, gochujang, sesame oil and honey in a bowl until smooth.
Stir through the garlic, spring onion and sesame seeds.
Rest 10 minutes in the fridge so the flavours meld, then serve with lettuce leaves, rice and grilled meats.

notes: Keeps in a jar in the fridge for 2 weeks.

title: Korean Gamja Jorim Braised Soy Potatoes
summary: Baby potatoes simmered in a glossy sweet-salty soy glaze until sticky, a staple banchan.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pan and fry the potatoes for 4 minutes, until lightly golden on the cut sides.
Add the soy sauce, sugar, water and garlic and bring to the boil until bubbling.
Simmer uncovered for 15 to 18 minutes, until the potatoes are tender when pierced and the sauce is sticky.
Stir in the honey and sesame oil and cook 1 minute more until glossy.
Scatter with sesame seeds and serve warm or at room temperature.

notes: Keeps 4 days in the fridge. Good in lunchboxes.

title: Korean Dubu Jorim Soy-Chilli Tofu Slabs
summary: Pan-fried tofu slabs simmered in a garlicky soy and chilli flake sauce, a savoury banchan.

steps.text: Pat the tofu dry and fry in the oil for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until deep golden.
Mix the soy sauce, chilli flakes, sesame oil, garlic, sugar and water.
Pour over the tofu and simmer gently for 6 minutes, spooning the sauce over, until it thickens and clings.
Scatter with spring onion and serve with rice.

notes: Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Korean Oi Muchim Spicy Cucumber Salad
summary: Crunchy salted cucumber tossed with chilli flakes, garlic, vinegar and sesame, a fast no-cook side.

steps.text: Toss the cucumber with the salt and leave in a colander for 10 minutes, then squeeze out the water.
Mix the chilli flakes, garlic, vinegar, sesame oil and sugar into a paste.
Toss the cucumber with the paste, spring onion and sesame seeds.
Toss and chill until cold, then serve within 30 minutes while the cucumber is still crisp.

notes: Best eaten the day it is made.

title: Vietnamese Xoi Lac Peanut Sticky Rice
summary: Steamed glutinous rice with roasted peanuts, coconut and fried shallots, a Hanoi street breakfast.

steps.text: Drain the soaked rice well and toss with a pinch of salt and the sugar.
Spread on a steamer lined with baking paper and steam for 25 to 30 minutes, until the grains are translucent and tender.
Warm the coconut milk gently and fold half through the hot rice.
Pile into bowls and top with peanuts, shallots, sesame and a drizzle of the remaining coconut milk.

notes: Soak the rice at least 6 hours or overnight; this soaking time is not included in prep. Contains peanuts.

title: Vietnamese Chao Ga Chicken Congee
summary: Silky rice porridge with poached chicken, ginger and spring onion, the Vietnamese cure-all.

steps.text: Bring the stock, rice and ginger to a gentle boil and simmer, stirring often, for 30 minutes, until the rice breaks down and thickens.
Add the chicken and cook for 12 minutes, until it reaches 75°C in the centre.
Lift the chicken out and shred, then return it to the pot with the fish sauce.
Simmer 3 minutes more and loosen with hot water if too thick.
Serve topped with spring onion, coriander, fried shallots and pepper.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C with no pink. Cool leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days, reheating until steaming hot.

title: Vietnamese Canh Bi Do Pumpkin and Prawn Soup
summary: Sweet pumpkin and prawn soup scented with spring onion and a touch of fish sauce.

steps.text: Heat the oil and fry the garlic for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the pumpkin and stock and simmer for 12 minutes, until the pumpkin is soft.
Lightly mash a third of the pumpkin against the pot to thicken the soup.
Add the prawns and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until pink and curled.
Season with fish sauce and pepper and top with spring onion and coriander.

notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until pink and opaque. Eat the same day, or cool quickly and keep for 1 day.

title: Vietnamese Nuoc Mam Pha Sweet Fish Sauce Dressing
summary: The bright sweet, sour, salty and spicy table sauce for rice paper rolls, grilled meat and noodles.

steps.text: Stir the sugar into the warm water until fully dissolved.
Add the fish sauce and lime juice and taste, adjusting for sweet and sour.
Stir in the garlic, chilli and carrot and rest for 10 minutes before serving.

notes: Keeps 5 days in the fridge. High in salt, so use sparingly.

title: Thai Nam Prik Num Roasted Green Chilli Dip
summary: Smoky roasted green chilli, shallot and garlic dip from northern Thailand, served with raw and steamed vegetables.

steps.text: Grill the chillies, shallots and garlic under a hot grill for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until blistered, blackened in spots and soft.
Peel everything, discarding the burnt skins from the chillies and the stems.
Crush the garlic and shallot in a mortar until smooth, then add the chillies and crush to a rough paste.
Stir in the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar and oil until well mixed.
Serve with cucumber, cabbage wedges, green beans and sticky rice.

notes: Keeps 4 days in the fridge. Chillies are hot, so wear gloves when peeling.

title: Thai Kai Jeow Fluffy Thai Omelette with Rice
summary: Deep-fried-style puffy omelette seasoned with fish sauce and lime, served over jasmine rice with chilli sauce.

steps.text: Beat the eggs with the fish sauce, lime juice and cornflour until frothy.
Heat the oil in a wok until shimmering, then pour in the egg from a height.
Cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until puffed and golden underneath, then fold in half and cook 30 seconds more until set through.
Drain on paper towel and serve over the warm rice.
Top with spring onion and chilli sauce.

notes: Food safety: cook the omelette until fully set with no liquid egg. Eat the same day.

title: Indian Upma Semolina Vegetable Breakfast
summary: South Indian savoury semolina porridge with mustard seed, cashews and vegetables, ready in 25 minutes.

steps.text: Dry-roast the semolina in a dry pan over medium heat for 4 minutes, until fragrant and lightly golden, then set aside.
Heat the oil, add the mustard seeds and cashews and fry for 1 minute, until the seeds pop and the nuts turn golden.
Add the onion, chilli, ginger and carrot and cook for 5 minutes, until softened.
Pour in the hot water and salt and bring to the boil until bubbling.
Stir in the semolina gradually and cook, stirring, for 2 to 3 minutes, until thick and fluffy.
Finish with peas, lemon juice and serve hot.

notes: Contains gluten and cashews.

title: Indian Mint and Coriander Chutney
summary: Fresh green chutney of mint, coriander, chilli and lime for samosas, kebabs and sandwiches.

steps.text: Roughly chop the coriander including the soft stems, and wash the mint.
Blend everything with the water until a smooth green sauce forms.
Taste and adjust the salt and lime juice until bright and sharp.
Spoon into a jar and chill; use within 4 days.

notes: Keeps 4 days in the fridge; freeze in ice cube trays for up to 2 months.

title: Turkish Mercimek Corbasi Red Lentil Soup
summary: Silky red lentil soup with carrot, onion and paprika butter, the everyday Turkish restaurant starter.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion and carrot for 6 minutes, until softened.
Stir in the tomato paste, cumin and paprika for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the lentils, potato and stock, bring to the boil and simmer for 20 minutes, until the lentils and potato are very soft.
Blend with a stick blender until smooth, adding hot water if too thick, and season with salt.
Serve hot with lemon wedges.

notes: Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes well.

title: Turkish Coban Salatasi Shepherd's Salad
summary: Finely diced tomato, cucumber, pepper and onion with parsley, lemon and olive oil, served with grilled meats.

steps.text: Combine the tomato, cucumber, capsicum, onion and parsley in a bowl.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice and sumac with a pinch of salt.
Toss through the salad just before serving, until everything is lightly coated and glossy.

notes: Dress at the last minute so the vegetables stay crisp.

title: Turkish Cacik Cucumber and Mint Yoghurt
summary: Thick yoghurt with grated cucumber, garlic and dried mint, served as a dip or a cooling soup.

steps.text: Squeeze the grated cucumber in a clean cloth until quite dry.
Mix with the yoghurt, garlic, mint, lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Chill for 20 minutes until cold and drizzle with olive oil to serve.

notes: Keeps 2 days in the fridge; stir before serving.

title: Turkish Muhammara Red Pepper and Walnut Dip
summary: Roasted red capsicum, walnut and pomegranate molasses dip with a gentle chilli and cumin kick.

steps.text: Roast the capsicums under a hot grill for 10 minutes, turning, until the skins are blackened and blistered.
Cover in a bowl for 10 minutes, then peel and deseed.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 3 minutes, until fragrant.
Blend the capsicum, walnuts, breadcrumbs, molasses, oil, garlic, cumin, chilli, lemon and salt to a coarse paste.
Taste and serve with warm flatbread.

notes: Keeps 5 days in the fridge. Contains walnuts and gluten.

title: Turkish Kuru Fasulye White Bean Stew
summary: Creamy white beans in a tomato and capsicum paste sauce, Turkey's national comfort dish, served with rice.

steps.text: Heat the oil and cook the onion for 7 minutes, until golden and soft.
Add the garlic, tomato paste, capsicum paste and paprika and stir for 2 minutes, until the oil separates.
Add the beans, stock and sugar and simmer gently for 30 minutes, until the sauce is thick and the beans are creamy.
Season with salt, scatter with mint and parsley and serve with rice.

notes: Better the next day. Keeps 4 days.

title: Turkish Yayla Corbasi Warm Yoghurt Soup with Sizzled Paprika Butter
summary: Silky yoghurt and rice soup finished with sizzled mint butter, mellow, tangy and warming.

steps.text: Simmer the rice in the stock for 18 minutes, until completely tender.
Whisk the yoghurt, egg yolk and flour until smooth, then whisk in a ladle of hot stock.
Pour the yoghurt mixture back into the pot, whisking constantly, and heat gently for 5 minutes until it thickens and is just steaming, without boiling.
Melt the butter, then add the mint and paprika for 30 seconds until sizzling and fragrant.
Season the soup with salt and swirl the mint butter over to serve.

notes: Food safety: heat the soup until steaming hot throughout so the egg yolk is cooked. Do not boil hard or the yoghurt will split.

title: Middle Eastern Mutabal Smoked Eggplant and Tahini Dip
summary: Charred eggplant blended with tahini, garlic and lemon, smoky and creamy, a mezze staple.

steps.text: Pierce the eggplants and roast at 220°C for 30 to 35 minutes, turning once, until the skins are charred and the flesh collapses.
Scoop the flesh into a colander and drain for 10 minutes.
Mash with the tahini, lemon, garlic, yoghurt, cumin and salt until creamy but with some texture.
Spoon into a bowl, drizzle with olive oil and scatter with pomegranate.

notes: Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

title: Middle Eastern Shorbat Adas Spiced Lentil Soup
summary: Golden lentil and cumin soup brightened with lemon, the Levantine winter staple.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 6 minutes, until soft and golden.
Add the garlic, cumin and turmeric for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the lentils, carrot and stock, bring to the boil and simmer for 25 minutes, until the lentils are soft.
Blend roughly, leaving some texture, and stir in lemon juice and salt.
Serve with coriander on top.

notes: Keeps 4 days; freezes well.

title: Middle Eastern Hummus Masabacha Warm Chickpeas
summary: Warm whole chickpeas folded through lemony tahini with olive oil and chilli, a Levantine breakfast.

steps.text: Warm the chickpeas gently in a pan with a splash of water for 5 minutes, until steaming hot.
Whisk the tahini, lemon, garlic, salt and 3 tbsp water into a loose sauce.
Fold half the sauce through the chickpeas.
Spoon into bowls and top with the remaining sauce, olive oil, cumin, chilli and parsley.

notes: Serve with warm pita. Contains sesame.

title: Greek Skordalia Garlic Potato Dip
summary: Pungent garlic and olive oil potato dip served with fried fish, roasted beetroot or crisp vegetables.

items.raw: 500g floury potatoes, peeled and cut up

steps.text: Boil the potatoes for 15 to 18 minutes, until completely soft, then drain well.
Mash or rice them while hot until smooth.
Beat in the garlic, almonds and vinegar, then slowly beat in the oil until thick and glossy.
Season with salt and serve at room temperature.

notes: Keeps 3 days in the fridge. Contains almonds.

title: Greek Melitzanosalata Smoky Eggplant Dip
summary: Charred eggplant dip with garlic, parsley and red wine vinegar.

steps.text: Roast the eggplants at 220°C for 35 to 40 minutes, turning once, until the skins are black and the flesh is very soft.
Scoop the flesh into a sieve and drain for 10 minutes.
Chop finely and mix with the garlic, oil, vinegar, lemon juice and parsley.
Season with salt and chill until cold.

notes: Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

title: Greek Tirokafteri Whipped Feta and Chilli Dip
summary: Tangy whipped feta with roasted red pepper and chilli, a fiery Greek meze.

items.item: roasted red capsicum from a jar
items.raw: 1 roasted red capsicum from a jar, drained

steps.text: Roughly crumble the feta into a food processor.
Add the yoghurt, capsicum, chilli, olive oil and lemon juice and blend until smooth and creamy.
Taste and add more chilli if you like, then spoon into a bowl and sprinkle with oregano.

notes: Keeps 5 days in the fridge.

title: Greek Revithia Chickpea Soup
summary: Slow-simmered chickpeas with onion, rosemary and lemon, a Sifnos Sunday tradition.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 7 minutes, until golden.
Add the garlic, bay leaf, rosemary, chickpeas and stock.
Simmer gently for 30 minutes, until the chickpeas are very soft and the broth is slightly creamy.
Remove the herbs, stir in the lemon juice and season with salt.
Serve hot with crusty bread.

notes: Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

title: Italian Panzanella Tuscan Bread and Tomato Salad
summary: Juicy tomatoes and crisp sourdough cubes tossed with basil, red onion and a punchy vinaigrette.

steps.text: Toss the bread with 2 tbsp olive oil and bake at 200°C for 8 to 10 minutes, until golden and crisp at the edges.
Combine the tomato, onion, cucumber and capers in a large bowl.
Whisk the remaining oil, vinegar and salt, pour over and toss.
Add the bread and basil and rest for 10 minutes until the bread is just soaked but still chewy.

notes: Best eaten within 1 hour.

title: Italian Stracciatella Roman Egg Drop Soup
summary: Rags of egg, parmesan and semolina set in a hot chicken broth, a quick Roman classic.

steps.text: Bring the stock to a gentle boil until bubbling.
Beat the eggs with the parmesan, semolina, parsley, nutmeg and 2 tbsp cold stock.
Pour into the pot in a thin stream while stirring slowly, and cook for 2 minutes, until the egg sets in thin ragged ribbons.
Season with salt and serve straight away.

notes: Food safety: cook the egg until fully set, with no liquid egg. Parmesan is not vegetarian.

title: Italian Pappa al Pomodoro Tuscan Tomato Bread Soup
summary: Thick Tuscan soup of ripe tomatoes, stale bread, garlic and basil, finished with green olive oil.

steps.text: Warm 2 tbsp oil with the garlic and chilli for 2 minutes, until fragrant but not browned.
Add the tomatoes, crushing them, and the stock and simmer for 15 minutes, until thickened.
Stir in the bread and cook for 8 minutes, until it breaks down into a thick porridge-like soup.
Tear in the basil, season with salt and finish with the remaining oil.

notes: Thickens as it stands; loosen with hot water.

title: Italian Frittata di Zucchine
summary: Thick zucchini and cheese frittata, set under the grill and served warm or cold.

steps.text: Squeeze the zucchini dry and sauté in the oil with the garlic in an ovenproof pan for 5 minutes, until softened.
Beat the eggs with the cheese, basil and salt and pour over.
Cook on low heat for 5 minutes until the edges set, then grill for 3 to 4 minutes until the top is golden and the centre is set with no liquid egg.
Rest 5 minutes and cut into wedges.

notes: Food safety: cook until the egg is fully set with no liquid. Refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.

title: Moroccan Zaalouk Smoky Eggplant and Tomato Salad
summary: Slow-cooked eggplant and tomato with garlic, cumin and paprika, served warm or cold with bread.

steps.text: Salt the eggplant for 10 minutes, rinse and pat dry.
Cook the tomatoes, garlic and spices in the oil for 10 minutes, until jammy.
Add the eggplant and 100ml water, cover and simmer for 20 minutes, until completely soft.
Mash roughly with a fork and cook uncovered for 5 minutes until thick, then add lemon juice and coriander.

notes: Keeps 5 days in the fridge.

title: Ethiopian Misir Wot Red Lentil Stew
summary: Spiced red lentils simmered with onion, garlic, ginger and a berbere-style paprika blend.

steps.text: Cook the onions dry in a heavy pot for 8 minutes, until soft and starting to colour.
Add the oil, garlic and ginger, then the spices and tomato paste, and stir for 3 minutes until a thick paste forms.
Add the lentils and water, bring to the boil and simmer for 20 minutes, until the lentils are tender and the stew is thick.
Season with salt and serve with injera or rice.

notes: Keeps 4 days and freezes well.

title: Ethiopian Shiro Wot Chickpea Flour Stew
summary: Smooth, spiced chickpea flour stew with onion and garlic, an everyday fasting dish.

steps.text: Cook the onions in a dry pot for 8 minutes, until soft.
Add the oil, garlic, ginger and spices and stir for 2 minutes, until fragrant.
Whisk the chickpea flour into the water until no lumps remain and pour into the pot.
Simmer, stirring often, for 15 minutes, until thick, smooth and glossy.
Stir in the lemon juice and salt and serve with injera.

notes: Thickens as it cools; loosen with water. Keeps 4 days.

title: Ethiopian Gomen Braised Silverbeet and Garlic
summary: Garlicky, ginger-scented braised greens, a staple beside stews and injera.

steps.text: Blanch the silverbeet in boiling water for 2 minutes, until wilted, then drain and squeeze.
Cook the onion in the oil for 6 minutes, until soft.
Add the garlic, ginger, chilli and turmeric for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the greens and the water and simmer for 10 minutes, until tender and the liquid has reduced.
Season with salt and taste, adding a squeeze of lemon if you like.

notes: Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Mexican Chilaquiles Rojos
summary: Crisp tortilla wedges in roasted tomato and chilli salsa, topped with fried eggs and fresh ricotta.

steps.text: Fry the tortillas in 4 tbsp oil in batches for 2 to 3 minutes, until crisp, and drain on paper towel.
Grill the tomatoes, chillies and garlic for 8 minutes, until charred, then blend with the onion and stock to a smooth salsa.
Simmer the salsa in a wide pan for 5 minutes, until slightly thickened, and season with salt.
Fold in the chips for 1 minute, until just coated but still with some bite.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil until the whites are set and place on top, then scatter with ricotta, red onion and coriander.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set; pregnant, elderly and young people should have the yolks cooked firm.

title: Mexican Pico de Gallo Fresh Tomato Salsa
summary: Chunky tomato, onion, coriander and lime salsa, best eaten fresh with chips, tacos and grilled meat.

steps.text: Mix the tomato, onion, jalapeno and coriander in a bowl.
Stir through the lime juice and salt.
Rest for 10 minutes until the juices run, then taste and adjust.

notes: Best the same day; keeps 2 days in the fridge.

title: Colombian Hogao Tomato and Onion Sofrito
summary: Slow-cooked tomato, spring onion and garlic base that flavours Colombian rice, beans and arepas.

steps.text: Warm the oil in a pan and cook the brown onion and spring onions for 6 minutes, until soft.
Add the garlic, tomatoes, cumin and sugar and simmer for 12 minutes, until jammy and thick.
Stir in the coriander and salt and serve warm over rice, eggs or arepas.

notes: Keeps 5 days in the fridge or freeze in portions.

title: Achari Baingan Pickled Eggplant
summary: Eggplant fried until golden then tossed in a mustard, chilli and vinegar pickle masala, a tangy side for dal and rice.

steps.text: Heat half the oil in a wide frying pan and fry the eggplant in two batches for 6 minutes each, until golden and soft, then set aside.
Add the remaining oil and the mustard seeds, and cook for 30 seconds until they pop.
Stir in the garlic, turmeric, chilli and cumin for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Return the eggplant with the vinegar, sugar and salt and toss for 2 minutes, until glossy.
Cool and spoon into a clean jar.

notes: Keeps 1 week in the fridge in a clean, sterilised jar with the oil sealing the top; use a clean spoon each time and discard if it smells off or shows mould.

title: Indian Nimbu Achar Lime Pickle
summary: Lime wedges softened in salt and spices, a sharp, salty pickle to serve in small amounts with curries.

steps.text: Toss the limes with the salt and turmeric in a clean bowl and pack into a sterilised jar.
Press down, cover and leave on a sunny bench for 3 days, shaking each day, until the peel softens and the juice rises.
Heat the oil in a small pan and cook the mustard seeds for 30 seconds until they pop.
Stir in the chilli, cumin and sugar for 20 seconds, then pour over the limes and mix well.
Seal and rest 1 week before eating, then store in the fridge.
