notes: Fermenting and resting time is not included in prep. Use a sterilised jar, keep the limes under the brine and discard the jar if mould forms or it smells unpleasant. Keeps 2 months in the fridge. Serve in small amounts because it is very salty.

title: Gajar Achar Carrot and Chilli Pickle
summary: A crunchy fridge pickle of carrot and green chilli in mustard oil style brine, ready in two days.

items.raw: 2 tbsp brown mustard seeds, lightly crushed

steps.text: Heat the water, salt, vinegar and sugar until the salt dissolves, then cool completely.
Pack the carrot and chilli into a sterilised jar.
Mix the mustard seeds, turmeric and oil and stir through the carrot.
Pour in the cooled brine until the vegetables are covered.
Seal and leave at room temperature for 2 days, then refrigerate.

notes: Keeps 3 weeks in the fridge. Keep the vegetables submerged under the brine, use a clean spoon, and discard if cloudy with a bad smell, slime or mould.

title: Kerala Style Green Mango Pickle
summary: Firm green mango in a fiery chilli and mustard oil, the classic salty pickle that lifts plain rice and yoghurt.

items.raw: 3 green mangoes, cut in 2cm pieces with skin

steps.text: Toss the mango with the salt and turmeric, cover and stand for 12 hours, then drain the liquid.
Heat the oil in a pan and cook the mustard seeds for 30 seconds until they pop.
Add the garlic for 1 minute, then the chilli and cumin for 20 seconds.
Cool the oil completely, then mix with the mango.
Pack into a sterilised jar with the oil covering the top.

notes: Standing time is not included in prep. Cool the oil fully before mixing so the mango stays crisp. Keeps 1 month in the fridge; use a dry spoon, keep the mango under the oil and discard if mould appears.

title: Coconut Chutney South Indian Style
summary: Fresh coconut ground with green chilli, ginger and roasted chickpeas, served with dosa and idli.

items.raw: 200g desiccated coconut, soaked in warm water and drained
items.prep: soaked in warm water and drained

steps.text: Blend the coconut, chickpeas, green chilli, ginger, salt and water to a coarse paste, adding a little more water if needed.
Spoon the chutney into a serving bowl and smooth the top.
Heat the oil in a small pan and cook the mustard seeds and dried chilli for 30 seconds, until the seeds pop.
Pour the hot tempering over the chutney.
Serve within a few hours.

notes: Best the day it is made; keeps 2 days in the fridge in a covered container.

title: Tomato Kuthu Chutney Spicy Roast Tomato Chutney
summary: Tomatoes and chilli cooked down until jammy and ground with garlic, a quick chutney for flatbread and eggs.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a frying pan and cook the chilli and mustard seeds for 30 seconds, until the seeds pop.
Add the onion and garlic and cook for 4 minutes, until soft.
Add the tomatoes, salt and sugar and cook for 12 minutes, until pulpy and thick.
Blend to a coarse, jammy paste in a small blender.
Serve warm or at room temperature with flatbread.

notes: Keeps 5 days in the fridge in a clean container and freezes well.

title: Kashmiri Walnut Chutney Doon Chetin
summary: Walnut and yoghurt chutney with mint and a little chilli, a cooling Kashmiri dip for kebabs and bread.

steps.text: Blend the walnuts, mint, chilli, garlic and cumin to a coarse paste, until the walnuts are finely chopped.
Stir in the yoghurt, lemon juice and salt.
Taste and adjust the salt and lemon.
Chill for 30 minutes before serving so the flavours settle.

notes: Contains tree nuts and dairy. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Kkakdugi Cubed Radish Kimchi
summary: Crunchy cubes of daikon coated in gochugaru and garlic, the kimchi that goes with soups and rice.

items.raw: 2 tbsp cooked rice, blended with 60ml water

steps.text: Toss the radish with the salt and sugar and stand for 30 minutes, until it releases liquid.
Drain, keeping 3 tablespoons of the liquid.
Mix the gochugaru, fish sauce, garlic, ginger and rice paste, then stir through the radish with the spring onion and the saved liquid.
Pack tightly into a clean jar with the juices covering the radish.
Leave at room temperature for 1 to 2 days until sour and bubbling, then refrigerate.

notes: Salting and fermenting time is not included in prep. Keep the radish under the liquid and burp the jar daily. Discard if there is fuzzy mould or a rotten smell. Keeps 1 month in the fridge.

title: Oi Sobagi Stuffed Cucumber Kimchi
summary: Short cucumbers split and stuffed with a spicy chive paste, fresh and snappy within a day.

items.raw: 1 bunch garlic chives, cut in 2cm lengths

steps.text: Cut each cucumber in 4 lengthways, stopping 2cm from the end, and rub with the salt.
Stand for 20 minutes, then rinse and drain until the surface is no longer slippery.
Mix the carrot, chives, gochugaru, fish sauce, garlic, sugar and sesame seeds.
Stuff the paste into the cucumber cuts.
Pack into a clean container and leave at room temperature for 4 hours, then refrigerate.

notes: Resting time is not included in prep. Best eaten within 4 days and kept cold. Discard if slimy or smelling off. Contains fish sauce.

title: Korean Nabak Kimchi Water Kimchi
summary: A mild, cool, tangy brined kimchi of cabbage and radish in a lightly salted broth, drunk as well as eaten.

steps.text: Salt the cabbage and radish for 30 minutes, then drain.
Combine the water, a little extra salt and the sugar in a bowl until dissolved.
Put the vegetables, pear, garlic, ginger, spring onion and chilli in a clean jar.
Pour in the brine to cover.
Leave at room temperature for 1 day, until lightly sour, then refrigerate.

notes: Resting time is not included in prep. Keep everything submerged, use clean utensils and discard if cloudy with a rotten smell or mould. Keeps 10 days in the fridge.

title: Japanese Asazuke Quick Cabbage and Cucumber Pickle
summary: A light salt pickle of cabbage, cucumber and carrot with kombu and yuzu style lemon, ready in an hour.

steps.text: Rub the salt through the cabbage, cucumber and carrot in a bowl for 1 minute, until it begins to release liquid.
Add the kombu, lemon juice and ginger.
Press under a weighted plate for 15 minutes.
Squeeze out the excess liquid.
Serve cold in small bowls as a side.

notes: Pressing time is not included in prep. Keeps 3 days in the fridge in a covered container; discard if it smells off.

title: Gari Homemade Pickled Sushi Ginger
summary: Wafer slices of young ginger pickled in sweet rice vinegar, the pink palate cleanser for sushi.

steps.text: Peel the ginger and slice it paper thin with a mandoline or peeler.
Toss with the salt and stand for 20 minutes, then blanch in boiling water for 1 minute and drain.
Heat the vinegar and sugar until the sugar dissolves.
Pack the ginger and beetroot into a clean jar and pour over the hot vinegar.
Cool, seal and refrigerate for 2 days before using.

notes: Standing and pickling time is not included in prep. Keeps 2 months in the fridge in a clean jar with the ginger under the vinegar.

title: Takuan Style Pickled Daikon
summary: Sweet and sour yellow daikon pickle, a bright crunchy side for rice bowls.

items.raw: 500g daikon radish, peeled and cut in 5mm rounds

steps.text: Toss the radish with the salt and stand for 15 minutes, then squeeze out the liquid.
Heat the vinegar, water, sugar and turmeric until the sugar dissolves, then cool.
Put the radish and kombu in a clean jar.
Pour in the brine and press the radish under the surface.
Refrigerate for 1 day before serving.

notes: Standing and pickling time is not included in prep. Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge; keep submerged and discard if cloudy or smelling off.

title: Japanese Goma Dare Sesame Dressing
summary: Creamy sesame dressing with soy, rice vinegar and mirin for cold noodles, blanched greens and tofu.

steps.text: Whisk the tahini, vinegar, mirin and soy sauce in a bowl until smooth.
Whisk in the sesame oil, sugar and ginger.
Stir in the water a spoonful at a time, until it pours like thin cream.
Taste and add a little more vinegar if it needs lift.
Serve at room temperature.

notes: Contains sesame and soy. Keeps 1 week in a jar in the fridge; shake before using.

title: Vietnamese Dua Mon Pickled Mustard Greens
summary: Sour, lightly fermented mustard greens that sit beside rice, caramelised pork and canh soups.

steps.text: Wilt the greens in the sun or a low oven for 1 hour, until limp, then pack into a clean jar with the garlic and chilli.
Dissolve the salt and sugar in the water.
Pour over the greens, keeping them under the brine.
Leave in a warm spot for 3 days, tasting daily, until pleasantly sour.
Refrigerate the jar once the greens taste sour.

notes: Wilting and fermenting time is not included in prep. Keep greens submerged, burp the jar daily and discard if there is fuzzy mould or a rotten smell. Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge.

title: Homemade Sauerkraut
summary: Salted shredded cabbage fermented for a week into tangy, crunchy sauerkraut with caraway.

steps.text: Rub the salt through the cabbage for 8 minutes, until a lot of liquid comes out.
Mix in the caraway and apple.
Pack firmly into a clean jar, pressing so the liquid covers the cabbage, leaving 4cm of space.
Weigh the cabbage down with a clean small jar or zip bag of brine.
Leave at room temperature for 5 to 7 days, tasting from day 4, then refrigerate.

notes: Fermenting time is not included in prep. Keep the cabbage under the brine at all times, use clean utensils and burp daily. Discard if there is pink or fuzzy mould or a foul smell; a sour, clean smell and cloudy brine are normal. Keeps 3 months in the fridge.

title: Polish Ogorki Kiszone Sour Pickled Cucumbers
summary: Small cucumbers fermented in dill and garlic brine, the salty sour pickles of Polish tables.

steps.text: Dissolve the salt in the water to make a brine.
Pack the cucumbers upright in a clean jar with the dill, garlic, peppercorns, bay leaves and mustard seeds.
Pour in the brine to cover, weighing the cucumbers down.
Leave at room temperature for 4 to 6 days, tasting each day, until sour.
Refrigerate the jar once the cucumbers taste sour.

notes: Fermenting time is not included in prep. Keep submerged, skim any white film, and discard if there is fuzzy mould, slimy cucumbers or a foul smell. Keeps 1 month in the fridge.

title: Russian Pickled Beetroot with Garlic
summary: Roasted-style boiled beetroot in a garlic and vinegar marinade, a sharp side for dark bread.

steps.text: Boil the beetroot for 40 minutes, until a knife slides in, then cool, peel and slice.
Simmer the vinegar, water, sugar, salt, bay leaves and coriander for 3 minutes.
Pack the beetroot and garlic into a clean jar.
Pour over the hot brine to cover.
Cool and refrigerate for 1 day before serving.

notes: Pickling time is not included in prep. Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge with the beetroot under the brine; discard if cloudy or mouldy.

title: Swedish Pressgurka Pressed Pickled Cucumber
summary: Thin cucumber slices in sweet vinegar with parsley, served with meatballs and salmon.

steps.text: Toss the cucumber with the salt and stand for 20 minutes, then squeeze out the liquid.
Stir the vinegar, water and sugar until the sugar dissolves.
Mix in the cucumber, parsley and pepper.
Chill for 2 hours so the flavours settle.
Serve cold with meatballs or fish.

notes: Standing and chilling time is not included in prep. Keeps 5 days in the fridge in a covered container.

title: Danish Rugbrod Seeded Rye Bread
summary: A dense, sour, seed-packed rye loaf for open sandwiches, with no kneading.

steps.text: Mix the yeast, honey, yoghurt and water in a bowl.
Add the flours, seeds and salt and stir to a thick, wet dough.
Scrape into a lined loaf tin, smooth and rest for 2 hours, until puffy.
Bake at 200C for 70 minutes, until it sounds hollow when tapped underneath.
Cool fully on a wire rack before slicing thinly.

notes: Resting time is not included in prep. Keeps 5 days wrapped and freezes in slices.

title: Lebanese Pickled Turnips with Beetroot Left
summary: Bright pink pickled root vegetable sticks in a salty brine, the tangy partner to falafel and shawarma.

items.raw: 600g daikon radish, peeled and cut in sticks
1 small raw beetroot, peeled and cut in wedges

steps.text: Dissolve the salt in the water, then stir in the vinegar.
Pack the radish, beetroot and garlic into a clean jar.
Pour in the brine to cover.
Seal and leave at room temperature for 5 days, until pink and sour.
Refrigerate the jar once the brine turns pink.

notes: Fermenting time is not included in prep. Keep the vegetables submerged and discard if there is fuzzy mould or a foul smell. Keeps 1 month in the fridge.

title: Roomali Roti Handkerchief Flatbread
summary: Paper-thin, soft flatbreads stretched wide and cooked on an upturned pan, folded like a handkerchief.

items.raw: 2 tbsp plain flour, extra for dusting

steps.text: Mix the flours, salt, oil and water to a soft dough and knead for 8 minutes, until smooth and stretchy.
Cover and rest for 30 minutes, then divide into 8 balls.
Roll each ball as thin as you can and stretch gently over your knuckles until it is almost see-through.
Heat a wok or heavy pan upturned over high heat until very hot.
Cook each roti for 30 seconds each side, until pale with light brown freckles, then fold in quarters.

notes: Resting time is not included in prep. Keep the cooked rotis wrapped in a clean cloth so they stay soft. Best eaten the same day.

title: Palak Thepla Spinach Flatbread
summary: Soft Gujarati flatbreads flecked with spinach and spice, a travel-friendly breakfast with yoghurt or pickle.

steps.text: Mix the flour, spinach, yoghurt, 1 tablespoon of oil, spices and salt in a bowl.
Add the water and knead for 5 minutes into a soft, slightly sticky dough.
Rest for 15 minutes, then divide into 8 balls and roll each into a thin 14cm round.
Cook on a hot dry frying pan for 1 minute, until blistered, then flip and brush with oil.
Cook until golden brown spots appear on both sides, about 1 minute more.

notes: Resting time is not included in prep. Keeps 2 days wrapped; reheat in a dry pan.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Bhatura Puffed Fried Bread
summary: Puffed, tender fried breads, served with chana masala for a classic north Indian brunch.

steps.text: Mix the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt, then rub in 2 tablespoons of oil.
Add the yoghurt and enough water to make a soft dough, then knead for 5 minutes until smooth.
Cover and rest for 1 hour, then divide into 6 balls and roll each into a 15cm oval.
Heat the frying oil to 180C and slide in one bread at a time.
Press gently so it puffs, then fry about 40 seconds each side, until golden, and drain on paper towel.

notes: Resting time is not included in prep. Fry in a deep, stable pot, keep children away and never leave hot oil unattended. Serve straight away while puffed.

title: Afghan Bolani Leek and Potato Flatbread
summary: Thin pan-fried flatbread stuffed with spiced potato and leek, served with yoghurt and mint.

steps.text: Mix the flour, salt and water to a firm dough, knead for 5 minutes and rest for 30 minutes.
Cook the leek in 1 tablespoon of oil for 5 minutes, until soft, then mix with the potato, coriander, chilli and salt.
Divide the dough into 6 balls, roll thin and spread the filling over half of each round.
Fold over to a half moon and press the edges closed.
Cook in a frying pan with a little oil for 3 minutes each side, until golden and crisp, then serve with yoghurt.

notes: Resting time is not included in prep. Best eaten fresh.

title: Piadina Romagnola Flatbread
summary: A soft, thin Italian flatbread cooked on a hot pan and folded around cheese and greens.

steps.text: Mix the flour, salt and baking powder, then stir in the oil and enough milk to form a soft dough.
Knead for 3 minutes, rest for 30 minutes and divide into 6 balls.
Roll each into a thin 20cm round and prick all over with a fork.
Cook in a hot dry pan for 2 minutes each side, until golden with brown spots.
Fill with rocket, mozzarella and tomato and fold in half to serve.

notes: Resting time is not included in prep. Contains dairy and gluten.

title: Focaccia Barese with Potato and Tomato
summary: A soft, olive-oily Pugliese focaccia topped with cherry tomatoes and olives, made with mashed potato for tenderness.

steps.text: Mix the yeast, sugar and water and stand for 5 minutes until foamy.
Combine with the flour, potato, salt and 1 tablespoon of oil and knead for 8 minutes, until smooth.
Cover and rise for 1 hour, then press into an oiled 25 by 35cm tin.
Dimple the dough with your fingers, scatter with the tomato, olives and oregano, drizzle with the remaining oil and rise for 30 minutes.
Bake at 220C for 30 minutes, until deep golden.

notes: Rising time is not included in prep. Keeps 2 days; refresh in a hot oven.

title: Norwegian Lefse Potato Flatbread
summary: Tender potato flatbreads rolled thin and griddled, spread with butter and sugar or served with smoked salmon.

steps.text: Mash the potato until completely smooth with the butter, cream and salt, then cool completely.
Work in the flour to form a soft dough and divide into 8 pieces.
Roll each very thin on a floured surface into a 20cm round.
Cook on a dry hot pan for 1 minute each side, until pale with light brown spots.
Cool under a damp cloth, spread with butter and sugar and fold.

notes: Keeps 3 days in the fridge wrapped in a damp cloth, and freezes well.

title: Chinese Shaobing Sesame Flatbread
summary: Flaky, layered sesame breads baked until crisp, a northern Chinese breakfast beside soy milk.

steps.text: Mix the flour, salt, sugar, yeast and water and knead for 8 minutes until smooth, then rise for 1 hour.
Mix 2 tablespoons of oil with the extra flour to make a paste.
Roll the dough thin, spread with the paste, roll up like a log and cut into 8 pieces.
Flatten each into a 8cm disc, brush with water and press into the sesame seeds.
Bake at 220C for 18 minutes, until puffed and golden.

notes: Rising time is not included in prep. Best eaten warm.

title: Indonesian Roti Cane Griddled Bread
summary: Stretchy, flaky griddled breads served with curry sauce or sweetened condensed milk.

steps.text: Mix the flour, salt, egg, water and 1 tablespoon of oil to a soft dough, knead for 5 minutes and rest for 1 hour.
Divide into 6 balls and soak in the remaining oil for 20 minutes.
Stretch each ball by hand over an oiled surface until paper thin.
Fold into a square and fry on a hot oiled pan for 3 minutes each side, until golden and crisp.
Drizzle with condensed milk or serve with curry.

notes: Resting time is not included in prep. Food safety: cook until the egg in the dough is fully set; the bread should be golden throughout.

title: Gazpacho Verde Green Cucumber and Herb Gazpacho
summary: A cold green soup of cucumber, capsicum, herbs and a little bread, brighter and fresher than the red version.

steps.text: Blend all the ingredients until completely smooth.
Strain if you prefer a finer soup.
Taste and adjust the salt and vinegar.
Chill for 2 hours until very cold.
Serve in glasses or bowls with a drizzle of oil.

notes: Chilling time is not included in prep. Keeps 2 days in the fridge; stir before serving.

title: Salmorejo Cordobes Thick Chilled Tomato Soup
summary: A thick, creamy tomato and bread soup from Cordoba, finished with chopped egg and olive oil.

steps.text: Blend the tomatoes, bread and garlic until a thick puree forms.
Add the oil in a slow stream with the blender running until pale and creamy.
Blend in the vinegar and salt.
Chill for 2 hours until cold.
Serve topped with the chopped egg and a drizzle of oil.

notes: Chilling time is not included in prep. Food safety: boil the eggs for 10 minutes until the yolks are firm and keep the soup cold; eat within 2 days.

title: Chlodnik Polish Cold Beetroot and Buttermilk Soup
summary: A hot pink chilled soup of beetroot, buttermilk, cucumber and dill, served with a halved boiled egg.

steps.text: Simmer the beetroot in the water for 15 minutes, until tender, then cool completely.
Stir in the buttermilk, lemon juice and salt.
Fold through the cucumber, radish, dill and spring onion.
Chill for 2 hours until very cold.
Serve topped with halves of boiled egg.

notes: Chilling time is not included in prep. Food safety: boil the eggs for 10 minutes until the yolks are firm and keep the soup cold; eat within 2 days.

title: Korean Oi Naengguk Chilled Cucumber Soup
summary: A sour, savoury cold soup of cucumber in vinegar broth, refreshing beside spicy food and hot rice.

items.raw: 3 Lebanese cucumbers, cut in thin strips

steps.text: Stir the water, vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, salt and garlic until the sugar dissolves.
Add the cucumber and spring onion.
Chill for 30 minutes until very cold.
Taste and adjust with extra vinegar or sugar.
Serve in bowls with the sesame oil and seeds.

notes: Chilling time is not included in prep. Add a few ice cubes to serve. Keep cold and eat within a day.

title: Hiyashi Chuka Cold Ramen Salad
summary: Cold noodles under rows of egg, cucumber, tomato and ham with a sweet-sour soy dressing, a Japanese summer lunch.

items.raw: 2 Lebanese cucumbers, cut in thin strips
100g sliced cooked ham, cut in strips

steps.text: Whisk the eggs and cook in a thin layer in the oiled pan for 1 minute each side, until fully set, then cut in strips.
Boil the noodles for 3 minutes, drain, rinse under cold water until cold and drain well.
Stir the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, sesame oil and water until the sugar dissolves.
Divide the noodles between 4 plates.
Arrange the egg, cucumber, tomato and ham on top and pour over the dressing.

notes: Food safety: cook the egg until completely set and keep the ham refrigerated until serving. Eat within a few hours of making.

title: Chilled Avocado and Lime Soup
summary: A silky no-cook soup of avocado, cucumber and lime, finished with coriander and chilli.

steps.text: Blend the avocado, cucumber, stock, yoghurt, lime juice, coriander and chilli until completely smooth.
Season with the salt and blend again briefly.
Chill for 1 hour until very cold.
Taste and add more lime if needed.
Serve in chilled bowls with extra coriander.

notes: Chilling time is not included in prep. Avocado browns quickly, so serve within a day.

title: Chilled Watermelon, Lime and Mint Soup
summary: A lightly sweet chilled watermelon soup with lime, mint and a little chilli.

steps.text: Blend the rockmelon, lime juice, half the mint, yoghurt and honey until completely smooth.
Season with the salt and blend again briefly.
Chill for 1 hour until very cold.
Taste and adjust the lime.
Serve garnished with the remaining mint and the chilli.

notes: Chilling time is not included in prep. Serve within a day.

title: Chilled Sweet Corn Soup with Lime
summary: A sweet, creamy cold corn soup with a little heat, served with lime and coriander.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the corn, chilli and stock and simmer for 10 minutes, until the corn is tender.
Blend until completely smooth and strain for a silky texture.
Stir in the lime juice and salt, then chill for 2 hours until cold.
Serve topped with chopped coriander.

notes: Chilling time is not included in prep. Keeps 2 days in the fridge.

title: Vichyssoise Classic Chilled Leek and Potato Soup
summary: Velvety cold leek and potato soup with cream, the French summer classic with chives.

steps.text: Melt the butter and cook the leek for 8 minutes, until soft but not coloured.
Add the potato and stock and simmer for 15 minutes, until the potato is very soft.
Blend until completely smooth and stir in the cream and salt.
Chill for 3 hours until cold.
Serve cold, scattered with chives.

notes: Chilling time is not included in prep. Contains dairy. Keeps 2 days in the fridge.

title: Chilled Tomato and Watermelon Soup
summary: Ripe tomato and sweet watermelon blended with basil and a splash of vinegar, perfect for hot days.

steps.text: Blend the tomato, watermelon, half the basil, garlic and vinegar until smooth.
Blend in the oil and salt.
Strain for a smooth texture if you prefer.
Chill for 2 hours until icy cold.
Serve with torn basil and a drizzle of oil.

notes: Chilling time is not included in prep. Serve within a day.

title: Warm Bulgur Salad with Roasted Vegetables
summary: Chewy farro with roasted zucchini, capsicum and red onion, finished with balsamic and parsley while still warm.

steps.text: Cook the bulgur in boiling water for 12 minutes, until tender but chewy, then drain.
Roast the zucchini, capsicum and onion with 1 tablespoon of oil at 220C for 25 minutes, until golden at the edges.
Whisk the remaining oil, balsamic and salt.
Toss the warm bulgur with the roast vegetables and dressing until evenly coated.
Top with parsley and the vegetarian hard cheese.

notes: Vegetarian hard cheese is used so it suits vegetarians. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Warm Chickpea and Spinach Salad with Cumin
summary: Chickpeas sizzled with cumin and garlic, tossed through spinach with lemon and yoghurt.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a frying pan and cook the garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the chickpeas and cumin and cook for 6 minutes, until golden and lightly crisp.
Remove from the heat and stir through the spinach until just wilted.
Add the lemon juice and salt.
Serve warm with the yoghurt spooned over.

notes: Keeps 2 days in the fridge, but is best eaten warm.

title: Warm Barley and Mushroom Salad
summary: Nutty pearl barley with golden mushrooms, thyme and mustard dressing, a warm salad for cool days.

steps.text: Boil the barley for 30 minutes, until tender with a little chew, then drain.
Fry the mushrooms in 1 tablespoon of oil over high heat for 6 minutes, until golden.
Add the garlic and thyme leaves for 1 minute.
Whisk the remaining oil, mustard, vinegar and salt.
Toss the warm barley, mushrooms, dressing and parsley together.

notes: Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Warm Cannellini and Kale Salad
summary: White beans and cavolo nero wilted in garlicky oil with lemon, a Tuscan-style warm salad.

items.raw: 2 cans cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
1 bunch cavolo nero, stems removed and leaves shredded

steps.text: Heat the oil and cook the garlic and chilli for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the cavolo nero and cook for 5 minutes, until wilted and tender.
Add the beans and warm through for 3 minutes.
Stir in the lemon juice and salt.
Serve warm with crusty bread.

notes: Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Warm Israeli Couscous Salad with Herbs and Almonds
summary: Pearl couscous toasted and tossed with herbs, lemon, currants and almonds.

steps.text: Toast the couscous in 1 tablespoon of oil for 3 minutes, until golden.
Add the boiling water, cover and cook for 8 minutes, until the water is absorbed.
Fluff with a fork and cool for 5 minutes.
Stir in the oil, lemon juice, herbs, currants, almonds and salt.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

notes: Contains gluten and tree nuts. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Shakshuka with Preserved Lemon and Olives
summary: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato and capsicum sauce brightened with preserved lemon and green olives.

steps.text: Cook the onion and capsicum in the oil for 8 minutes, until soft.
Add the garlic, cumin and paprika for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the tomatoes, preserved lemon and olives and simmer for 10 minutes, until thick.
Make 4 wells and crack in the eggs, then cover and cook for 6 minutes, until the whites are set.
Scatter with coriander and serve from the pan.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set and the yolks are as firm as you are comfortable with; cook the yolks through for anyone vulnerable.

title: Huevos Divorciados Divorced Eggs
summary: Two fried eggs on corn tortillas, one under red salsa and one under green, with beans between.

steps.text: Warm the beans in a small pan for 4 minutes, until hot.
Fry the tortillas in the oil for 30 seconds each side, until lightly crisp.
Fry the eggs in a little oil for 3 minutes, until the whites are set and the edges crisp.
Warm both salsas separately for 2 minutes, until steaming.
Top each tortilla with an egg, spoon red salsa on one side and green on the other, then add beans, feta and coriander.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set; cook the yolks through for anyone vulnerable.

title: Oeufs Cocotte with Spinach and Cream
summary: Eggs baked in ramekins over creamed spinach until the whites are just set.

steps.text: Wilt the spinach with the butter and garlic in a pan for 2 minutes, until soft, then squeeze out any liquid and chop.
Stir in half the cream, nutmeg and salt.
Divide among four buttered ramekins and crack an egg into each.
Spoon over the remaining cream and bake at 180C for 12 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks wobble slightly.
Serve with toast soldiers while the eggs are still warm and just set.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set; bake a few minutes longer for firm yolks if serving anyone vulnerable.

title: Persian Nargesi Spinach and Egg Pan
summary: Spinach cooked with garlic and turmeric, topped with eggs that set into the greens.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 6 minutes, until soft and golden.
Add the garlic and turmeric for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the spinach in batches and cook for 5 minutes, until wilted, then stir in the salt and lemon juice.
Make 4 wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 5 minutes, until the whites are set.
Serve with warm flatbread.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set; cook the yolks through for anyone vulnerable.

title: Indian Egg Bhurji Masala Scramble
summary: Spiced scrambled eggs with onion, tomato and green chilli, the Mumbai street breakfast.

steps.text: Heat the oil and cook the onion and chilli for 4 minutes, until soft.
Add the tomato, turmeric and cumin and cook for 3 minutes, until pulpy.
Beat the eggs with the salt, pour in and stir gently for 2 minutes, until just set.
Scatter with coriander and check the eggs are fully set with no liquid left.
Serve with buttered toast until the plates are clean, while hot.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until fully set with no liquid egg remaining; serve straight away.

title: Korean Gyeran Mari Rolled Omelette
summary: A neat rolled omelette with carrot and spring onion, cut in rounds as a banchan or lunchbox side.

steps.text: Beat the eggs with the salt, spring onion and carrot.
Heat a thin film of oil in a small non-stick pan over low heat.
Pour in a thin layer and cook for 1 minute, until just set but still glossy, then roll to one end.
Oil the pan again, pour in more egg, lift the roll to let it flow under and cook until set, then roll again.
Repeat until the egg is used, rest for 2 minutes and slice.

notes: Food safety: cook the egg until fully set with no liquid egg remaining. Keeps 2 days in the fridge. Use fresh, uncracked eggs; for pregnant women, older people, young children and anyone with low immunity, cook the eggs until the yolks are firm.

title: Khai Palo Thai Five Spice Egg Stew
summary: Boiled eggs braised in a sweet, five-spice soy broth until deeply brown, served with rice.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes until the yolks are firm, then cool in cold water and peel.
Simmer the water, soy sauce, sugar, cinnamon, star anise, garlic and pepper for 10 minutes, until slightly syrupy.
Add the eggs and simmer for 10 minutes, turning, until deeply brown and glossy.
Serve with coriander and steamed rice.

notes: Food safety: boil the eggs for 10 minutes until the yolks are firm. Keeps 3 days in the fridge in the braising liquid.

title: Greek Strapatsada Tomato and Feta Scramble
summary: Soft eggs folded into stewed tomato and feta, a classic island breakfast.

steps.text: Cook the garlic in the oil for 30 seconds, until fragrant, then add the tomato.
Simmer for 8 minutes, until thick and jammy.
Beat the eggs and pour in, stirring gently for 2 minutes, until just set.
Crumble in the feta and oregano.
Serve straight away with thick toast, while the eggs are still hot.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until fully set with no liquid egg remaining.

title: Uova in Purgatorio Eggs in Spicy Tomato
summary: Eggs poached in fiery tomato and garlic sauce, mopped up with crusty bread.

steps.text: Cook the garlic and chilli in the oil for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, oregano and salt and simmer for 12 minutes, until thick.
Make 4 wells and crack in the eggs.
Cover and cook for 5 minutes, until the whites are set.
Scatter with basil and serve with bread.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set; cook the yolks through for anyone vulnerable.

title: Hungarian Lecso with Eggs
summary: Sweet capsicum, tomato and onion stewed with paprika, with eggs stirred in for a rustic one-pan meal.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 8 minutes, until soft.
Add the capsicum and paprika and cook for 8 minutes more, until soft.
Add the tomatoes and salt and simmer for 6 minutes, until saucy.
Crack the eggs in, cover and cook for 4 minutes, until the whites are set.
Serve straight from the pan with warm rye bread.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set; cook the yolks through for anyone vulnerable.

title: Chimichurri Rojo Red Chimichurri
summary: A red capsicum and paprika chimichurri, smoky and herby for grilled vegetables and steak.

items.item: roasted red capsicum from a jar
items.raw: 1 roasted red capsicum from a jar, chopped

steps.text: Chop the parsley and garlic finely.
Mix with the capsicum, oil, vinegar, paprika, oregano, chilli and salt.
Stand for 20 minutes so the flavours develop.
Taste and add more vinegar or salt if needed.
Spoon over grilled meat or vegetables until generously coated.

notes: Keeps 5 days in the fridge in a clean jar.

title: Imli Tamarind and Date Chutney
summary: Sweet-sour tamarind and date chutney with ginger and cumin, the chaat table's essential drizzle.

steps.text: Simmer the tamarind, dates and water for 15 minutes, until very soft.
Blend until smooth and sieve to remove fibres.
Return to the pan with the sugar, spices and salt and simmer for 5 minutes, until thick and glossy.
Cool completely before serving or storing in a jar.

notes: Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge in a clean jar and freezes well.

title: Sweet Mango Chutney
summary: Slow-cooked green mango chutney with ginger, chilli and vinegar to serve with curries and cheese.

items.raw: 3 firm green mangoes, peeled and diced

steps.text: Simmer the vinegar and sugar for 5 minutes until the sugar dissolves.
Add the mango, onion, ginger, chilli, cinnamon, sultanas and salt.
Cook for 35 minutes, stirring often, until thick and jammy.
Cool for 10 minutes, remove the cinnamon and pack into sterilised jars.
Seal the jars and refrigerate once cooled.

notes: Keeps 1 month in the fridge in sterilised jars; discard if mouldy.

title: Raita Crunch Yoghurt with Crunchy Chickpeas
summary: Cool spiced yoghurt with crunchy roasted chickpeas, served with biryani and kebabs.

steps.text: Whisk the yoghurt, water, cumin, chilli and salt until smooth.
Stir in the chopped mint and taste for salt.
Fold in the chickpeas just before serving so they stay crisp.
Taste and adjust the salt.
Serve chilled in a bowl alongside rice.

notes: Contains dairy. Make just before serving, as the chickpeas soften quickly.

title: Syrian Muhammara Walnut and Capsicum Dip
summary: A smoky dip of roasted capsicum and walnuts with pomegranate molasses and chilli.

items.item: roasted red capsicums from a jar
items.raw: 2 roasted red capsicums from a jar

steps.text: Blend the capsicum, walnuts, breadcrumbs, molasses, garlic, cumin and chilli until almost smooth.
With the blender running, add the oil in a slow stream.
Season with the salt and blend briefly.
Taste and add more molasses or chilli if needed.
Serve with warm flatbread or vegetable sticks.

notes: Contains tree nuts and gluten. Keeps 5 days in the fridge.

title: Green Zhug Herb and Chilli Sauce
summary: A blistering green sauce of coriander, parsley, chilli and cardamom, spooned over falafel and eggs.

steps.text: Blend the herbs, chillies, garlic and spices to a rough paste.
Blend in the oil and lemon juice until combined.
Season with the salt and blend briefly.
Taste and add more lemon if needed.
Spoon into a clean jar and press down.

notes: Keeps 1 week in the fridge with a film of oil on top.

title: Harissa Paste
summary: A deep red Tunisian chilli paste with roasted capsicum, caraway and garlic to stir into stews and marinades.

items.raw: 10 dried red chillies, soaked and drained

items.item: roasted red capsicums from a jar
items.raw: 2 roasted red capsicums from a jar

steps.text: Toast the caraway, cumin and coriander in a dry pan for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Blend the chillies, capsicum, garlic and spices to a thick paste.
Blend in the lemon juice, salt and 2 tablespoons of oil.
Spoon into a jar and cover with the remaining oil.
Refrigerate the jar with the oil on top.

notes: Wear gloves for the chillies. Keeps 1 month in the fridge under a film of oil.

title: Moroccan Chermoula Herb Marinade
summary: A garlicky coriander, parsley and cumin sauce, spooned over roast vegetables and grilled fish.

steps.text: Blend the coriander, parsley and garlic to a coarse paste.
Blend in the spices, oil and lemon juice until combined.
Season with the salt and blend briefly.
Taste and adjust the lemon.
Store in a clean jar with a film of oil.

notes: Keeps 5 days in the fridge. Use for marinating only before cooking; do not reuse marinade that touched raw meat or fish.

title: Sambal Matah Balinese Raw Shallot Sambal
summary: A fresh raw sambal of sliced shallot, chilli and lemongrass, dressed with hot oil and lime.

items.raw: 2 lemongrass stalks, white part finely sliced

steps.text: Mix the shallot, chilli, lemongrass and lime leaves in a bowl.
Heat the coconut oil until shimmering and pour over the mixture so it sizzles.
Stir in the lime juice and salt.
Taste and adjust the lime and salt.
Serve within an hour with grilled fish or rice.

notes: Serve the same day. Handle hot oil carefully.

title: Thai Nam Jim Jaew Roasted Chilli Dipping Sauce
summary: Smoky, tangy dipping sauce with toasted rice powder, lime and fish sauce for grilled meats and vegetables.

steps.text: Toast the rice in a dry pan for 4 minutes, until deep golden, then crush to a coarse powder.
Stir the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar and chilli flakes until the sugar dissolves.
Add the rice powder, shallots and herbs.
Taste and balance with more lime or sugar.
Serve in small bowls beside grilled food.

notes: Best on the day it is made. Contains fish sauce.

title: Japanese Ponzu Citrus Soy Sauce
summary: A tangy citrus soy sauce for dumplings, grilled fish and cold noodles.

steps.text: Combine the soy sauce, lemon juice, lime juice, mirin, vinegar, sugar and kombu in a jar.
Shake until the sugar dissolves.
Rest in the fridge overnight.
Remove the kombu and discard it.
Serve in small dishes for dipping.

notes: Resting time is not included in prep. Keeps 1 month in the fridge.

title: Mushroom XO Style Umami Sauce
summary: A savoury, chilli-spiked mushroom and garlic condiment with a deep umami taste, great on noodles and rice.

steps.text: Fry the mushrooms in the oil over medium heat for 10 minutes, until deep golden and dry.
Add the shallot, garlic, chilli and ginger and cook for 5 minutes, until fragrant and golden.
Stir in the soy sauce, oyster sauce and sugar and cook for 4 minutes, until glossy.
Cool and pack into a clean jar.
Refrigerate with the oil on top.

notes: Contains oyster sauce. Keeps 3 weeks in the fridge under the oil.

title: Filipino Tapsilog Beef and Garlic Rice
summary: Thin soy and calamansi-style marinated beef with garlic fried rice and a fried egg, the classic silog plate.

steps.text: Mix the beef with the soy sauce, lemon juice, sugar, pepper and half the garlic, then leave to marinate for 30 minutes.
Fry the remaining garlic in 1 tbsp oil for 1 minute until golden, add the rice and toss for 4 minutes until hot and lightly toasted.
Fry the beef in a hot pan in two batches for 3 minutes each, until browned and cooked through at 71°C.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil for 3 minutes until the whites are set.
Serve the rice with the beef, an egg and sliced tomato on each plate.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef slices right through and the egg whites until fully set; cook the yolks through for anyone vulnerable. Cool leftover rice within an hour and refrigerate it, eating it within a day.

title: Filipino Longsilog Sausage and Egg Breakfast
summary: Sweet garlicky pork sausages with garlic rice, a fried egg and a quick vinegar dip.

steps.text: Cook the sausages in a pan with a splash of water over medium heat for 12 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through at 75°C.
Fry the garlic in half the oil for 1 minute until golden, add the rice and stir-fry for 4 minutes until hot.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil for 3 minutes until the whites are set.
Mix the vinegar, onion and pepper for the dipping sauce.
Plate the rice with the sausages and eggs and serve with the dip.

notes: Food safety: cook the sausages until 75°C in the centre and the egg whites fully set; cook the yolks through for anyone vulnerable. Cool leftover rice and refrigerate it within an hour.

title: Filipino Ginataang Kalabasa Pumpkin in Coconut Milk
summary: Pumpkin and green beans simmered in coconut milk with garlic and ginger, creamy and lightly savoury.

steps.text: Cook the onion, garlic and ginger in the oil for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the pumpkin and coconut milk and simmer for 12 minutes until the pumpkin is tender.
Add the beans and fish sauce and cook for 4 minutes until the beans are bright and just tender.
Season with the pepper and serve with rice.

notes: Swap the fish sauce for soy sauce to keep it plant-based.

title: South African Bobotie Breakfast Muffins
summary: Curried beef mince baked in muffin tins under a savoury egg custard, a handheld take on bobotie.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C and grease a 6-hole muffin tin.
Cook the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add the mince, curry powder and turmeric and cook for 8 minutes until browned.
Stir in the jam, lemon juice, sultanas and soaked bread, then press the mix into the muffin holes.
Whisk the eggs with the milk and pour over each muffin, then top with a bay leaf.
Bake for 20 minutes until the custard is set and golden, with the mince at 75°C.

notes: Food safety: cook the mince until 75°C all the way through and the egg custard until fully set. Chill leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until steaming hot.

title: South African Potjie Style Butternut Soup
summary: Butternut, carrot and apricot simmered in one pot with mild curry spice and blended smooth.

steps.text: Cook the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, then stir in the curry powder for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the pumpkin, carrot, apricots and stock and simmer for 22 minutes until all the vegetables are very soft.
Blend until smooth, then stir in the coconut milk and lemon juice.
Reheat gently for 2 minutes and serve hot.

notes: Freezes well for up to 3 months.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: South African Boerewors Breakfast Roll
summary: Coiled spiced beef and pork sausage in a soft roll with fried onion and tomato relish.

steps.text: Cook the sausage in a pan over medium heat for 15 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through at 75°C.
Fry the onion in the oil in a second pan for 8 minutes until soft and golden.
Split the rolls and spread with chutney.
Fill with the sausage cut in pieces, the onion, tomato and rocket.

notes: Food safety: cook the sausage until 75°C in the centre with no pink inside.

title: Ethiopian Firfir Spiced Torn Flatbread
summary: Torn flatbread soaked in a warm berbere-spiced tomato sauce, a classic Ethiopian morning dish.

items.raw: 4 flatbreads (or large wraps), torn into pieces

steps.text: Cook the onion in a dry pan for 4 minutes, add the oil, garlic and ginger and cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in the chilli powder and paprika and tomatoes and simmer for 8 minutes until thick and glossy.
Add the water and salt and simmer for 3 minutes, until the sauce is loose and glossy.
Fold in the torn bread and toss for 2 minutes until it has soaked up the sauce.

notes: Serve with a fried egg on top if you like.

title: Ethiopian Azifa Green Lentil Salad
summary: Cold lentils dressed with mustard, lemon and chilli, a zesty fasting-day salad.

steps.text: Simmer the lentils in plenty of water for 20 minutes until tender but holding their shape, then drain and cool.
Whisk the lemon juice, mustard, oil, ginger and salt.
Toss the lentils with the onion, chilli, parsley and dressing.
Chill for 15 minutes before serving.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days.

title: Peruvian Huancaina Sauce for Potatoes
summary: Creamy yellow chilli and cheese sauce that is spooned over boiled potatoes and egg.

steps.text: Soak the bread in the milk for 5 minutes.
Blend the feta, bread and milk, chillies, garlic, oil and lime juice until smooth and creamy.
Arrange the potato slices on a platter and pour the sauce over.
Top with the halved eggs and olives.

notes: Food safety: boil the eggs for at least 10 minutes until fully set. Keep the sauce in the fridge and use within 2 days.

title: Peruvian Quinoa and Avocado Salad
summary: Fluffy quinoa with avocado, corn, tomato and lime, a fresh Lima-style lunch salad.

steps.text: Simmer the quinoa in 400ml water for 14 minutes until the water is absorbed, then cool.
Whisk the lime juice, oil, cumin and salt.
Toss the quinoa with the avocado, corn, tomato, onion and coriander.
Pour over the dressing and fold gently.

notes: Add a handful of toasted pepitas for crunch.

title: Peruvian Tacu Tacu Rice and Bean Cakes
summary: Day-old rice and canned beans fried together into crisp golden cakes with garlic and chilli.

steps.text: Fry the onion, garlic and chilli in 1 tbsp oil for 5 minutes until soft.
Roughly mash the beans, then mix with the rice, cumin, salt and the onion mix.
Shape into 4 thick patties.
Fry in the remaining oil for 4 minutes each side until crisp and golden.
Scatter with parsley and serve hot.

notes: Top with a fried egg or avocado.

title: Peruvian Crema de Zapallo Pumpkin Soup
summary: Smooth pumpkin soup with garlic and a touch of cumin, finished with a swirl of cream.

steps.text: Cook the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the cumin, pumpkin and stock and simmer for 18 minutes until very soft.
Blend until completely smooth.
Stir in the cream, reheat gently for 2 minutes and scatter with coriander.

notes: Use coconut milk in place of cream for a dairy-free soup.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Argentinian Salsa Golf Seafood Sauce
summary: Sweet pink mayonnaise and ketchup sauce served with prawns, ham and palm hearts on every Buenos Aires menu.

steps.text: Stir the mayonnaise, tomato sauce, Worcestershire sauce, lemon juice and paprika until smooth and pale pink.
Taste and add the pinch of salt as needed.
Chill for 10 minutes before serving.
Serve with cooked prawns, boiled egg or crisp chips.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for 4 days.

title: Argentinian Ensalada Rusa Potato Salad
summary: Diced potato, carrot and peas bound with mayonnaise and egg, a staple of Argentinian tables.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes and carrots in salted water for 12 minutes until just tender, adding the peas for the last 2 minutes.
Boil the eggs for 10 minutes until firm, then peel and chop.
Drain the vegetables well and cool completely.
Fold in the mayonnaise, lemon juice, eggs and parsley.
Chill for 15 minutes before serving so the flavours settle.

notes: Food safety: boil the eggs until fully set and keep the salad cold, eating within 2 days.

title: Argentinian Tortilla de Papas Potato Omelette
summary: A thick golden omelette of sliced potato and onion, flipped and served warm or cold.

steps.text: Cook the potato and onion in the oil over low heat for 15 minutes, turning, until very soft but not browned.
Beat the eggs with the salt, then fold in the warm potato mix.
Pour back into the pan and cook for 6 minutes over low heat until the base is set.
Flip using a plate and cook for 3 minutes more until the egg is fully set.
Rest for 5 minutes and slice.

notes: Food safety: cook the omelette until the egg is fully set in the centre.

title: Indian Aloo Tikki Chaat
summary: Crisp spiced potato patties topped with yoghurt, tamarind and mint chutneys.

steps.text: Mix the potato, cornflour, cumin, garam masala, chilli and half the coriander and season, then shape into 8 patties.
Fry in the oil for 4 minutes each side until crisp and golden.
Whisk the yoghurt until smooth.
Plate the patties and top with yoghurt, tamarind sauce, mint chutney, onion and the remaining coriander.

notes: Serve straight away so the patties stay crisp.

title: Italian Insalata di Riso Summer Rice Salad
summary: Chilled rice with tuna, olives, tomatoes and capers, a picnic favourite across Italy.

items.raw: 2 cans tuna in oil (185g each), drained

steps.text: Cook the rice in boiling salted water for 12 minutes until tender, then drain, rinse and cool.
Boil the eggs for 10 minutes until firm, cool, peel and quarter.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice and salt.
Toss the rice with the tuna, tomatoes, olives, capers, parsley and dressing, then top with the eggs.

notes: Food safety: keep the salad chilled and eat within 2 days. Boil the eggs until fully set.

title: Italian Fagioli all Uccelletto Tuscan Tomato Beans
summary: Cannellini beans simmered with sage, garlic and tomato, an easy Tuscan side or light meal.

steps.text: Warm the oil with the garlic and sage for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, chilli, salt and pepper and simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the beans and simmer for 12 minutes until the sauce clings and thickens.
Serve the beans spooned over the toasted bread.

notes: Finish with a little extra virgin olive oil.

title: Italian Salsa Verde Piemontese Parsley Sauce
summary: Punchy parsley, caper and anchovy sauce served with boiled meats and eggs.

steps.text: Soak the bread crumbs in the vinegar for 5 minutes.
Finely chop the parsley, capers, anchovies and garlic together.
Mix in the bread, egg yolk and oil until it forms a loose, rich sauce.
Rest for 10 minutes so the flavours meld.

notes: Food safety: boil the egg for at least 10 minutes until fully set. Keep chilled and use within 3 days.

title: Italian Bagna Cauda Warm Anchovy and Garlic Dip
summary: Warm olive oil and butter dip with garlic and anchovy, served with raw and roasted vegetables.

steps.text: Cook the garlic gently in the oil and butter for 8 minutes without browning.
Add the anchovies and stir for 4 minutes until they melt into the oil.
Pour into a small pot over a candle or low heat to keep warm.
Serve with the vegetables and bread for dipping.

notes: Keep the heat low so the garlic stays sweet and does not turn bitter.

title: Italian Pesto alla Trapanese Almond and Tomato Pesto
summary: Sicilian pesto of raw tomato, almonds, garlic and basil tossed through pasta.

steps.text: Boil the pasta in salted water for 10 minutes until al dente.
Blend the tomatoes, almonds, garlic, basil, oil, cheese and salt into a rough sauce.
Drain the pasta, keeping 60ml of the water.
Toss with the sauce, loosening with the water until glossy.

notes: Use vegetarian hard cheese to keep this vegetarian.

title: Egyptian Ful Medames Breakfast Beans
summary: Mashed warm broad-style beans with garlic, cumin and lemon, a daily Cairo breakfast.

steps.text: Warm the beans in a pot with 100ml water for 8 minutes, until hot.
Mash roughly with the garlic, cumin and salt.
Stir in the lemon juice and half the oil.
Spoon into bowls and top with tomato, parsley and the remaining oil, then serve with warm pita.

notes: Add a boiled egg on top for extra protein.

title: Moroccan Msemen Layered Pan-fried Pancakes
summary: Folded square pancakes of semolina dough, crisp outside and soft within, eaten with honey.

steps.text: Knead the flour, semolina, salt, sugar and water for 8 minutes until smooth, then rest for 15 minutes.
Divide into 6 balls and brush with oil.
Stretch each ball thin on an oiled bench, fold into a square and press flat.
Cook in a hot pan for 3 minutes each side until golden and flaky.
Serve with melted butter and honey.

notes: Brush each pancake with butter while hot for extra flakiness.

title: Hazelnut Dukkah Egyptian Spice and Nut Blend
summary: A dry crumbly mix of toasted hazelnuts, sesame, coriander and cumin for dipping bread in olive oil.

steps.text: Toast the hazelnuts in a dry pan for 5 minutes, then rub off the skins.
Toast the sesame, coriander and cumin seeds in the pan for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Crush everything together coarsely with the pepper and salt.
Dip bread in olive oil, then into the dukkah.

notes: Store in a jar for up to 3 weeks.

title: English Bubble and Squeak Fried Leftover Veg Cakes
summary: Mashed potato and cabbage fried until crisp, topped with a poached egg and bacon.

steps.text: Mix the potato, cabbage, onion and pepper and shape into 4 patties.
Fry the patties in the oil for 5 minutes each side until deeply golden and crisp.
Grill or fry the bacon for 5 minutes until crisp.
Poach the eggs in barely simmering water for 3 minutes until the whites are set.
Top each cake with bacon and an egg.

notes: Food safety: cook the bacon until crisp and the egg whites fully set; cook the yolks through for anyone vulnerable.

title: Portuguese Molho de Piri Piri Chilli and Lemon Sauce
summary: A bright, hot sauce of chilli, garlic, lemon and olive oil for brushing over grilled food.

steps.text: Warm the oil with the chillies and garlic over low heat for 4 minutes until fragrant.
Cool slightly, then blend with the lemon juice, vinegar, paprika, salt and oregano.
Pour into a clean jar and seal while still slightly warm.
Rest for an hour before using.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for 2 weeks.

title: Scottish Cranachan Oat Porridge with Apple and Honey
summary: Creamy oats finished with cream, honey and raspberries in the style of the Scottish dessert.

steps.text: Simmer the oats with the milk and salt for 8 minutes, stirring, until thick and creamy.
Spoon the porridge into two warm bowls.
Top with the apple, honey and a swirl of cream.
Scatter over the toasted oats.

notes: Stir through a spoon of yoghurt for extra tang.

title: French Vinaigrette a la Moutarde Dijon Mustard Dressing
summary: The everyday French dressing of mustard, red wine vinegar and olive oil, emulsified until glossy.

steps.text: Whisk the mustard, vinegar, shallot, salt, pepper and honey in a bowl until combined.
Pour in the oil in a thin stream, whisking until thick and glossy.
Taste and adjust the salt or vinegar to your liking.
Toss with the salad leaves just before serving.

notes: Keeps in a jar in the fridge for 2 weeks; shake well before using.

title: Japanese Wafu Onion Dressing for Grilled Meat and Salads
summary: Grated onion, soy and rice vinegar dressing that is savoury, sweet and sharp, spooned over salad or steak.

steps.text: Simmer the mirin for 1 minute to cook off the alcohol, then cool.
Mix the onion, soy sauce, vinegar, oils, sugar and ginger in a jar.
Add the cooled mirin and shake for 20 seconds until blended.
Leave for 10 minutes so the onion mellows before using.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for 5 days.

title: Thai Nam Prik Pao Roasted Chilli Jam
summary: Sweet, smoky chilli jam of dried chilli, garlic and shallot, stirred into soups, noodles and fried eggs.

steps.text: Toast the chillies in a dry pan for 2 minutes until fragrant and darker, then soak in hot water for 10 minutes.
Fry the garlic and shallots in half the oil for 6 minutes until golden, then cool.
Blend the chillies, garlic and shallots to a coarse paste.
Fry the paste in the remaining oil for 8 minutes, add the sugar, tamarind, fish sauce and water and simmer for 6 minutes until dark and jammy.
Cool and spoon into a clean jar.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for 3 weeks.

title: Thai Panang Curry Paste
summary: Rich dry red curry paste with roasted peanuts and coriander seed, the base of panang curry.

items.raw: 8 dried red chillies, deseeded and soaked

steps.text: Toast the coriander and cumin seeds in a dry pan for 2 minutes until fragrant, then grind finely.
Drain the chillies and chop with the lemongrass.
Crush or blend everything together with the peanuts, salt, zest and oil to a smooth thick paste.
Scrape the paste into a clean jar and press it down.

notes: Use 3 tbsp per can of coconut milk with chicken or tofu; keeps in the fridge for 2 weeks.

title: Thai Yellow Curry Paste
summary: Mild golden curry paste of turmeric, lemongrass and dried chilli with warm spices.

items.raw: 6 dried red chillies, deseeded and soaked

steps.text: Drain the chillies and chop them with the lemongrass.
Blend with the shallots, garlic, ginger, turmeric, coriander, cumin, salt and oil to a smooth paste, scraping the bowl often.
Fry a teaspoon of paste in a pan for 30 seconds until fragrant, to check the balance.
Spoon into a jar and cover with a film of oil.

notes: Use 3 tbsp per can of coconut milk with chicken, potato and onion; keeps in the fridge for 2 weeks.

title: Malaysian Rendang Spice Paste
summary: Fragrant blended paste of galangal, lemongrass and chilli that flavours beef, chicken or jackfruit rendang.

items.raw: 8 dried red chillies, deseeded and soaked

steps.text: Drain the chillies and chop with the shallots, garlic, ginger, galangal and lemongrass.
Blend with the turmeric and 1 tbsp oil to a smooth paste.
Fry the paste in the remaining oil over medium heat for 8 minutes until the oil separates and the aroma is deep.
Stir in the salt and cool.

notes: Use 5 tbsp per 1 kg of meat; freezes for 3 months in ice cube trays.

title: Indian Tandoori Chicken Marinade and Oven Chicken
summary: Yoghurt, lemon and spice marinade that gives chicken thighs the smoky red look of the tandoor.

steps.text: Mix the yoghurt, lemon juice, ginger, garlic, spices, salt and oil, then coat the chicken and marinate in the fridge for at least 2 hours.
Heat the oven to 230°C and line a tray.
Arrange the chicken on a rack on the tray and roast for 30 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges and 75°C inside.
Rest for 5 minutes, then slice and serve with lemon and onion.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until 75°C in the thickest part. Discard the used marinade and wash hands and board after raw chicken.

title: Goan Vindaloo Curry Paste
summary: Hot, tangy Goan paste of dried chilli, vinegar and warm spices for pork, beef or potatoes.

items.raw: 10 dried red chillies, deseeded and soaked

steps.text: Toast the cumin, peppercorns, cloves and cinnamon in a dry pan for 2 minutes until fragrant, then grind fine.
Blend the drained chillies, garlic, ginger, ground spices, turmeric, vinegar, sugar and salt to a smooth paste.
Fry the paste in the oil for 4 minutes until the oil separates and it darkens.
Cool completely and spoon into a clean jar.

notes: Use 4 tbsp per 600g of meat or vegetables; keeps in the fridge for 3 weeks.

title: Cuban Mojo Criollo Garlic and Citrus Marinade
summary: Garlicky sour orange style marinade and sauce, hot oil poured over raw garlic and citrus.

steps.text: Mix the garlic, orange juice, lime juice, cumin, oregano and salt in a heatproof bowl.
Heat the oil in a small pan for 2 minutes until shimmering and pour over the garlic mixture, stirring as it sizzles.
Cool for 10 minutes and add the coriander.
Use as a marinade for pork or chicken, or as a sauce over yuca and rice.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for 4 days.

title: Korean Bulgogi Beef and Lettuce Wraps
summary: Thinly sliced beef in a sweet soy and pear marinade, grilled quickly and wrapped in lettuce.

steps.text: Mix the soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, garlic, pear and spring onions, add the beef and marinate in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a pan over high heat until smoking.
Cook the beef in two batches for 3 minutes each, until browned and the centre reaches 71°C.
Serve in lettuce leaves with rice and chilli paste.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef until 71°C in the centre, and discard any raw marinade left in the bowl.

title: Spanish Alioli Garlic Emulsion
summary: Traditional garlic and olive oil sauce, pounded smooth and whisked in the old way with an egg yolk for stability.

steps.text: Crush the garlic and salt to a smooth paste in a bowl.
Whisk in the egg yolk until pale.
Add the oil drop by drop at first, then in a thin stream, whisking until thick and glossy.
Stir in the lemon juice and taste for salt.

notes: Food safety: raw egg yolk is not recommended for pregnant women, young children, older people or anyone vulnerable; use pasteurised egg. Keep chilled and eat within 2 days.

title: Georgian Adjika Fresh Chilli and Walnut Paste
summary: Sharp, herby red chilli paste with garlic, walnuts and coriander, stirred into soups and grilled meat.

steps.text: Chop the chillies, garlic and fresh coriander roughly, until evenly small.
Blend with the walnuts, ground coriander, paprika, salt and vinegar to a coarse paste.
Taste and adjust the salt and vinegar.
Rest for 30 minutes before using.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for 10 days.

title: Georgian Satsebeli Plum Tomato Sauce
summary: Sweet and sour cooked tomato sauce with garlic and coriander, a table sauce for grilled meats and potatoes.

steps.text: Simmer the tomatoes with the sugar and salt for 20 minutes until reduced and thick.
Stir in the garlic, chilli, vinegar and oil and cook for 4 minutes.
Add the coriander and cool.
Spoon the sauce into a clean jar and cool.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for 5 days.

title: Armenian Aubergine and Walnut Spread
summary: Roasted aubergine mashed with walnuts, garlic and parsley, served as a dip or spread.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C and roast the whole aubergines for 35 minutes until collapsed and soft.
Scoop out the flesh and drain in a sieve for 5 minutes.
Blend the flesh with the walnuts, garlic, lemon juice, oil and salt to a rough paste.
Fold in the parsley and serve with warm pita.

notes: Pierce the aubergine skin before roasting so steam can escape.

title: Swiss Rosti Golden Potato Cake
summary: Grated potato pressed and fried in butter until golden and crisp outside, soft within.

items.raw: 700g waxy potatoes, boiled for 8 minutes and cooled

steps.text: Peel and coarsely grate the cooled potatoes and toss with the salt and pepper.
Heat half the butter and the oil in a pan and press in the potato in an even cake.
Cook over medium heat for 10 minutes until golden, then flip using a plate and add the rest of the butter.
Cook for 10 minutes more, then fry the eggs and serve on top.

notes: Food safety: fry the eggs until the whites are fully set; cook the yolks through for anyone vulnerable.

title: German Bratkartoffeln Pan-Fried Potatoes with Onion
summary: Sliced cooked potatoes fried in butter with onion until deeply golden and crisp edged.

steps.text: Slice the cooled potatoes about 5 mm thick.
Heat the oil and half the butter in a large pan and fry the potatoes in a single layer for 12 minutes, turning only once, until golden.
Add the onion and remaining butter and cook for 8 minutes until the onion is soft and caramelised.
Season and scatter with parsley.

notes: Leave the potatoes undisturbed so they crisp rather than steam.

title: Swedish Hasselbackspotatis Fanned Roast Potatoes
summary: Whole potatoes sliced into fans and roasted with butter and breadcrumbs until crisp on top.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C and slice each potato crosswise nearly through, every 3 mm.
Brush with the butter and oil, season with the salt and roast for 35 minutes.
Sprinkle with the breadcrumbs, cheese and thyme.
Roast for 15 minutes more until golden and a knife slides in easily.

notes: Rest the potatoes on wooden spoons while slicing to stop the knife cutting through.

title: Belgian Liege Waffles with Brown Sugar
summary: Yeasted waffle dough with butter and caramelising sugar for a chewy golden waffle.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, then stir in the milk and eggs to a sticky dough.
Beat in the soft butter and vanilla, then cover and prove for 1 hour until doubled.
Fold in the brown sugar until just marbled, then divide into 6 balls.
Cook each ball in a hot waffle iron for 4 minutes until deeply golden.

notes: Food safety: cook the waffles until the egg is cooked through and the centre is hot.

title: Dutch Poffertjes Mini Pancakes with Butter and Icing Sugar
summary: Small puffy yeasted pancakes, served hot with melting butter and icing sugar.

steps.text: Whisk the flours, yeast, milk, egg, salt and sugar into a smooth batter and rest for 30 minutes.
Heat a pan with a little butter and drop small spoonfuls of batter in, cooking for 1 minute until bubbles show.
Flip with a fork and cook for 1 minute more until puffed and golden.
Serve piled high with butter and icing sugar.

notes: Food safety: cook the pancakes until the egg is fully set.

title: Finnish Ohukaiset Thin Pancakes with Berries
summary: Thin lacy pancakes made with a milky batter and served with jam or fruit.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, milk, eggs, salt and sugar into a thin smooth batter and rest for 10 minutes.
Melt a little butter in a hot pan and pour in a thin ladle of batter, swirling to cover.
Cook for 1 minute each side until golden and lacy.
Fold and serve with jam and yoghurt.

notes: Food safety: cook until the egg is fully set.

title: Hungarian Palacsinta Crepes with Apricot Jam
summary: Thin Hungarian crepes, rolled around apricot jam and dusted with icing sugar.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, milk, soda water, eggs, salt and sugar into a thin batter and rest for 15 minutes.
Brush a pan with oil and pour in a thin layer of batter, cooking for 1 minute each side until golden.
Spread each crepe with jam and roll up.
Dust the rolled crepes generously with icing sugar.

notes: Food safety: cook the crepes until the egg is fully set.

title: Indonesian Martabak Manis Thick Sweet Pancake
summary: A thick, honeycombed pancake filled with chocolate sprinkles, peanuts and condensed milk.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder, eggs, milk, sugar and bicarb into a smooth batter and rest for 20 minutes.
Pour into a greased lidded pan over medium heat and cook for 10 minutes until bubbles form and the top is nearly set.
Scatter with peanuts and chocolate chips, drizzle with condensed milk, fold in half and brush with butter.
Cut in squares and serve warm.

notes: Food safety: cook the batter until the top is no longer wet and the egg is fully set.

title: Korean Hobak Juk Sweet Pumpkin Porridge
summary: Smooth rice and pumpkin porridge, mellow and slightly sweet, served warm.

steps.text: Boil the pumpkin in the water for 20 minutes until completely soft.
Blend until smooth, then return to the pot.
Whisk in the rice flour mixed with 3 tbsp cold water and simmer for 8 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Season with the sugar and salt and top with the pine nuts.

notes: Stir constantly as it thickens to avoid lumps.

title: Korean Dakjuk Chicken and Rice Porridge
summary: Comforting rice porridge cooked in a ginger and chicken broth with shredded chicken.

steps.text: Simmer the chicken in the water with the garlic and ginger for 15 minutes until cooked through at 75°C, then lift out and shred.
Add the rice and carrot to the broth and simmer for 25 minutes, stirring often, until soft and creamy.
Stir in the shredded chicken, sesame oil and salt.
Serve with spring onions.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until 75°C in the thickest part and chill leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Scottish Skirlie Toasted Oatmeal and Onion Side
summary: Toasted oats fried with onion in butter, a nutty traditional side or stuffing.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a pan and cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the oats and toast over medium heat for 6 minutes, stirring, until golden and fragrant.
Season with salt, pepper and the parsley.
Serve warm with roast meat or soup once the oats are crisp.

notes: Serve under a poached egg for a quick breakfast.

title: Persian Tahdig Crispy Saffron Rice
summary: Fluffy rice with a golden crust of saffron and yoghurt baked in the base of the pot.

steps.text: Soak the rice in warm water with the salt for 1 hour, then drain and boil for 6 minutes until al dente.
Bloom the saffron in the hot water, then mix half with the yoghurt and 3 tbsp rice.
Heat the oil and 2 tbsp butter in a non-stick pot, spread the yoghurt rice over the base and pile the rest on top.
Cover with a towel-wrapped lid and steam on low for 40 minutes until a golden crust forms.
Drizzle with the remaining butter and saffron water, then invert onto a plate.

notes: Dip the pot base in cold water for 1 minute before inverting so the crust releases.

title: Mexican Arroz Rojo Tomato Rice
summary: Fluffy long-grain rice toasted in oil and cooked in a blended tomato, onion and garlic broth.

steps.text: Blend the tomato, onion and garlic with a splash of the stock until smooth.
Fry the rice in the oil for 4 minutes until pale golden.
Add the tomato mix and cook for 3 minutes, then add the stock, carrot, peas and salt.
Cover and simmer on low for 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed, then rest for 5 minutes.

notes: Use vegetable stock to keep it plant-based.

title: Cuban Moros y Cristianos Black Beans and Rice
summary: Black beans cooked with rice, green capsicum, garlic and cumin in one pot.

steps.text: Cook the onion, capsicum and garlic in the oil for 6 minutes until soft, then add the cumin and oregano for 1 minute.
Add the rice, beans with liquid, bay leaf, water and salt.
Bring to a boil, cover and cook on low for 22 minutes until the rice is tender.
Stir in the vinegar and remove the bay leaf.

notes: Serve with sliced avocado and lime.

title: Turkish Bulgur Pilav with Vermicelli and Tomato
summary: Nutty bulgur cooked with toasted vermicelli, tomato paste and butter.

steps.text: Melt the butter and cook the vermicelli for 2 minutes until golden, then add the onion for 4 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute, add the bulgur and toast for 2 minutes.
Add the stock, salt and pepper and simmer covered on low for 12 minutes until absorbed.
Rest for 5 minutes and fluff with a fork.

notes: Swap the butter for olive oil to keep it dairy-free.

title: Greek Dakos Cretan Barley Rusk Salad
summary: Crunchy rusks softened by grated tomato and topped with feta, olives and oregano.

items.raw: 4 barley rusks (or thick dried bread slices)

steps.text: Wet the rusks with a splash of water for 20 seconds until slightly softened but still chewy.
Top with the grated tomato.
Crumble over the feta and scatter with olives, capers and oregano.
Drizzle with the olive oil.

notes: Eat straight after assembling so the rusks keep some crunch.

title: Mexican Esquites Charred Corn Cup
summary: Charred corn tossed with mayonnaise, lime, chilli and cotija style cheese, served in a cup.

steps.text: Char the corn kernels in the oil in a hot pan for 8 minutes, stirring, until deeply golden.
Mix with the mayonnaise, lime juice and chilli powder while still warm.
Spoon into cups and top with the feta and coriander.
Serve warm in cups with extra lime wedges.

notes: Serve with extra lime wedges.

title: Chicken Caesar Grain Bowl
summary: Grilled chicken, brown rice and cos lettuce tossed in a lemony caesar dressing with croutons.

steps.text: Cook the rice in plenty of boiling water for 25 minutes until tender, then drain and cool.
Cook the chicken in the oil for 6 minutes each side, until golden and 75°C in the centre, then rest and slice.
Toast the bread cubes in a dry pan for 4 minutes until crisp.
Whisk the mayonnaise, lemon juice, garlic and anchovies, then toss with the rice and lettuce.
Top with the chicken, croutons and cheese.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until 75°C in the thickest part with no pink inside.

title: Roast Beetroot Salad with Goats Cheese and Walnuts
summary: Sweet roast beetroot with peppery rocket, creamy goats cheese and toasted walnuts in a mustard vinaigrette.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C, wrap the beetroot in foil with 1 tbsp oil and roast for 45 minutes until a knife slides in.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 4 minutes until fragrant.
Peel and wedge the beetroot once cool enough to handle.
Whisk the remaining oil, balsamic, mustard and salt, then toss with the beetroot and rocket.
Top with crumbled goats cheese and walnuts.

notes: Wear gloves when peeling the beetroot to avoid staining.

title: Italian Chickpea and Tuna Salad with Red Onion
summary: Quick tinned chickpea and tuna salad with parsley, red onion and lemon.

items.raw: 2 cans tuna in oil (185g each), drained

steps.text: Soak the onion slices in cold water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice and salt.
Toss the chickpeas, tuna, onion, parsley and tomatoes with the dressing.
Rest for 10 minutes until the flavours meld.

notes: Food safety: keep the salad chilled and eat within 2 days.

title: Spanish Ensalada de Garbanzos with Roasted Capsicum
summary: Chickpeas with roasted capsicum, tomato, cucumber and sherry vinegar dressing.

steps.text: Whisk the oil, vinegar and paprika.
Toss the chickpeas with the capsicum, tomatoes, cucumber and onion.
Pour over the dressing and fold in the parsley.
Chill for 15 minutes until the flavours soften.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days.

title: Spanish Pipirrana Andalusian Summer Salad
summary: Finely diced tomato, cucumber and capsicum in a sherry vinegar dressing, often served with seafood.

steps.text: Combine the tomatoes, cucumber, capsicum, onion and parsley in a bowl.
Whisk the oil, vinegar and salt and pour over.
Toss and rest for 10 minutes until juicy.
Serve cold with bread to mop up the juices.

notes: Peel the cucumber if the skin is thick.

title: Spanish Sopa de Ajo Castilian Garlic Soup
summary: Garlic and paprika soup with stale bread and a poached egg dropped in at the end.

steps.text: Fry the garlic in the oil for 2 minutes until golden, then add the bread for 3 minutes until crisp.
Stir in the paprika for 20 seconds, then pour in the stock.
Simmer for 15 minutes until the bread is soft and thick.
Crack in the eggs and poach for 4 minutes until the whites are set.

notes: Food safety: cook until the egg whites are fully set; cook the yolks through for anyone vulnerable.

title: Spanish Salmorejo Cordoba Tomato and Bread Soup
summary: Thick chilled tomato and bread soup, finished with olive oil, egg and ham.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes until firm, then cool and chop.
Blend the tomatoes, bread, garlic, vinegar and salt until completely smooth.
Blend in the oil slowly until the soup is thick and pale orange.
Chill for 1 hour, then top with egg and ham.

notes: Food safety: boil the eggs until fully set; keep the soup cold and eat within 2 days.

title: Portuguese Sopa de Feijao Bean and Cabbage Soup
summary: Hearty bean, carrot and cabbage soup with garlic and olive oil, finished with a splash of vinegar.

steps.text: Cook the onion, carrots and garlic in the oil for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the beans, stock and bay leaf and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the cabbage and simmer for 6 minutes until tender.
Stir in the vinegar and salt and remove the bay leaf.

notes: Mash a ladle of beans against the pot to thicken the soup.

title: French Soupe a l'Oignon Gratinee Onion Soup with Cheese Toast
summary: Deeply caramelised onions in beef stock topped with toasted bread and melted cheese.

steps.text: Cook the onions in the butter and oil over low heat for 40 minutes, stirring often, until deep brown and jammy.
Stir in the flour for 1 minute, pour in the wine and let it bubble for 3 minutes.
Add the stock and thyme and simmer for 15 minutes.
Top the baguette with the cheese and grill for 3 minutes until melted and bubbling.
Ladle the soup into bowls and float a toast on top while the cheese is still bubbling.

notes: Cook the onions slowly; rushing them leaves a bitter taste.

title: French Soupe au Pistou Vegetable Soup with Basil Paste
summary: Summer vegetable and white bean soup stirred with a garlicky basil pistou.

steps.text: Simmer the onion, potatoes, carrots and water for 15 minutes.
Add the green beans, zucchini and white beans and cook for 10 minutes more.
Add the pasta and cook for 8 minutes until al dente.
Crush the basil, garlic, oil and cheese to a green paste.
Stir the pistou into the soup off the heat and serve.

notes: Do not boil the soup after adding the pistou or the basil turns dark.

title: French Salade de Lentilles du Puy with Mustard Vinaigrette
summary: Green lentils tossed warm with shallot, carrot, parsley and mustard vinaigrette.

steps.text: Simmer the lentils with the bay leaf in plenty of water for 22 minutes until tender but whole.
Drain and discard the bay leaf.
Whisk the oil, vinegar, mustard and salt.
Toss the warm lentils with the carrot, shallot, parsley and dressing.

notes: Better the next day once the lentils absorb the dressing.

title: French Crepes Bretonnes Buckwheat Galettes with Ham and Egg
summary: Savoury buckwheat crepes folded around ham, cheese and a baked egg.

steps.text: Whisk the buckwheat flour, salt, 1 egg and water to a thin batter and rest for 15 minutes.
Cook thin crepes in buttered pan for 2 minutes each side until crisp at the edges.
Add ham, cheese and an egg to the centre of each crepe and cook for 4 minutes until the white is set.
Fold the edges in to make a square and serve.

notes: Food safety: cook until the egg whites are fully set; cook the yolks through for anyone vulnerable.

title: Swiss Birchermuesli Overnight Apple Oats
summary: Rolled oats soaked in milk and yoghurt with grated apple, honey and nuts.

steps.text: Mix the oats, milk, yoghurt and lemon juice in a bowl.
Cover and soak in the fridge overnight until creamy.
Stir through the grated apple, honey and raisins.
Top with the chopped hazelnuts and serve.

notes: Keeps for 2 days in the fridge.

title: German Kaiserschmarrn Torn Pancake with Apple Compote
summary: A fluffy thick pancake torn into pieces and caramelised, served with fruit.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, milk, yolks, sugar and salt into a smooth batter, then fold in whipped egg whites.
Melt half the butter in a large pan, pour in the batter, scatter with raisins and cook for 5 minutes until golden underneath.
Flip, tear into pieces with two forks and fry for 4 minutes with the remaining butter until caramelised.
Simmer the apples with a splash of water for 5 minutes until soft and serve with the pancake dusted with icing sugar.

notes: Food safety: cook the batter until the egg is fully set.

title: Slovak Halusky with Cabbage and Bacon
summary: Soft grated potato dumplings tossed with fried cabbage and crisp bacon.

steps.text: Finely grate the potatoes and mix with the flour, egg and salt to a sticky dough.
Drop small pieces into boiling salted water and cook for 3 minutes until they float.
Fry the bacon for 5 minutes until crisp, then cook the onion and cabbage in the fat and oil for 8 minutes until soft and golden.
Toss the dumplings through and serve hot.

notes: Food safety: cook the bacon until crisp and the dumpling dough until firm all the way through.

title: Finnish Karjalanpiirakka Karelian Rice Pies
