summary: Thin rye shells filled with creamy rice porridge, baked and brushed with butter, topped with egg butter.

steps.text: Simmer the rice with the milk and 200ml water for 25 minutes, stirring, until a thick porridge.
Knead the flours, salt and 120ml water to a dough, divide into 8, and roll each thin.
Spoon porridge into the centre of each, pinch the edges and bake at 250°C for 12 minutes until the crust is golden.
Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, chop and mix with the soft butter.
Brush the pies with melted butter and top with egg butter.

notes: Food safety: boil the eggs until fully set.

title: Chinese Wonton Soup in Clear Chicken Broth
summary: Silky pork and prawn wontons in a clear ginger broth with bok choy.

steps.text: Mix the pork, prawns, soy sauce, sesame oil and grated ginger.
Place a teaspoon of filling in each wrapper and fold into a parcel.
Simmer the stock and sliced ginger for 5 minutes.
Add the wontons and cook for 4 minutes until they float and the filling reaches 75°C.
Add the bok choy for 1 minute and serve with spring onions.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork and prawn filling until 75°C and the prawns are opaque; chill leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Chinese Black Vinegar Dumpling Dipping Sauce
summary: Sharp, salty dipping sauce of Chinkiang vinegar, soy and fresh ginger.

steps.text: Stir the vinegar, soy sauce and sugar until the sugar dissolves.
Add the sesame oil, ginger, garlic and chilli oil.
Rest for 5 minutes so the garlic mellows.
Serve in small dishes for dumplings.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for 5 days.

title: Chinese Sesame Noodle Salad with Cucumber
summary: Cold wheat noodles in a creamy sesame and soy dressing with crisp cucumber and carrot.

steps.text: Boil the noodles for 5 minutes until tender, then rinse in cold water and drain.
Whisk the tahini, soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, sugar and garlic with 3 tbsp warm water until smooth.
Toss the noodles with the dressing, cucumber and carrot.
Scatter with sesame seeds.

notes: Serve with chilli oil for extra heat.

title: Japanese Potato Salad with Cucumber and Ham
summary: Creamy mashed potato salad with cucumber, carrot and ham in a Japanese-style mayonnaise.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes and carrot for 15 minutes until soft, adding the eggs for the last 10 minutes.
Salt the cucumber and squeeze out the liquid after 10 minutes.
Drain the potatoes, mash roughly, and cool.
Mix with the mayonnaise, vinegar, sugar, ham, cucumber and chopped eggs.

notes: Food safety: boil the eggs until fully set and keep the salad chilled, eating within 2 days.

title: Japanese Tonkatsu Sauce Sweet Fruity Cutlet Sauce
summary: Thick, sweet and tangy sauce for crumbed cutlets and cabbage.

steps.text: Whisk the tomato sauce, Worcestershire sauce, soy sauce, sugar, apple juice and mustard in a small pot.
Simmer for 3 minutes until slightly thickened and glossy.
Cool and pour into a jar.
Serve with fried pork cutlets or shredded cabbage.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for 2 weeks.

title: Korean Tteokguk New Year Rice Cake Soup
summary: Beef broth with sliced rice cakes and egg ribbons, eaten on Lunar New Year.

steps.text: Fry the beef in the sesame oil for 4 minutes, add the garlic and 1 tbsp soy sauce, then pour in the water.
Simmer for 20 minutes until the beef is tender.
Add the rice cakes and cook for 6 minutes until soft and floating.
Stream in the eggs and stir for 1 minute until set in ribbons.
Season with the remaining soy sauce and top with spring onions and nori.

notes: Food safety: simmer the beef until 71°C throughout and the egg is fully set.

title: Indonesian Sambal Kecap Sweet Soy Chilli Sauce
summary: Sweet soy sauce with fresh chilli, shallot and lime, a table sauce for satay and grilled food.

steps.text: Fry the shallots, garlic and chillies in the oil for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Remove from the heat and stir in the sweet soy sauce and lime juice.
Rest for 5 minutes so the flavours blend.
Serve in a bowl with satay, grilled meat or eggs.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for 1 week.

title: Thai Jok Pork and Ginger Rice Porridge
summary: Silky rice porridge with pork meatballs, ginger and a soft egg, a Bangkok breakfast.

steps.text: Simmer the rice in the stock for 25 minutes, stirring, until broken and creamy.
Mix the pork with the soy sauce and pepper and roll into small balls.
Drop the meatballs into the porridge and simmer for 6 minutes until cooked through at 75°C.
Crack in the eggs and stir through for 2 minutes until set.
Top with ginger, spring onions and coriander.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork until 75°C and the eggs until fully set.

title: Sri Lankan Pol Sambol Coconut Relish
summary: Spicy dry coconut, chilli and lime relish eaten with hoppers and rice.

steps.text: Soak the coconut in the warm water for 5 minutes until just moist.
Mix with the shallots, chillies, chilli flakes and salt.
Add the lime juice and crush with clean fingers for 2 minutes until the colour is even.
Serve with breads or rice.

notes: Best eaten the day it is made.

title: Sri Lankan Kiribath Coconut Milk Rice Cake
summary: Creamy coconut milk rice pressed into diamonds, served with sambol.

steps.text: Simmer the rice with the water and salt for 15 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Stir in the coconut milk and cook for 10 minutes more, stirring, until thick and sticky.
Press into a greased dish, 3 cm thick, and cool for 10 minutes.
Cut into diamonds and serve with a spicy sambol.

notes: Serve with the pol sambol for a classic breakfast.

title: Nepali Aloo Achar Spiced Potato Salad with Sesame
summary: Warm boiled potato with toasted sesame, lemon, chilli and mustard oil style dressing.

steps.text: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan for 2 minutes until golden, then grind coarsely.
Heat the oil and fry the cumin for 30 seconds until sizzling, then add the turmeric and chilli.
Pour over the potato with the sesame, lemon juice and salt.
Toss and scatter with coriander.

notes: Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Mango Lassi Smoothie Bowl with Cardamom Granola
summary: Thick mango and yoghurt smoothie bowl topped with crunchy cardamom granola and toasted coconut flakes.

steps.text: Blend the mango, yoghurt, milk and half the cardamom for 1 minute, until thick and smooth, scraping down twice.
Spoon into two chilled bowls and smooth the tops.
Toast the coconut and oats in a dry pan for 3 minutes, until golden and fragrant.
Toss with the remaining cardamom and scatter over the bowls.
Drizzle with the honey and eat straight away.

notes: Add a splash more milk if your blender struggles.
Use dairy-free yoghurt for a no-dairy bowl.

title: Green Mango and Spinach Smoothie Bowl
summary: A bright green bowl of mango, cucumber and spinach blended thick and topped with seeds and fresh apple.

steps.text: Blend the mango, spinach, cucumber, yoghurt and apple juice for 1 minute, until completely smooth and thick.
Pour into two bowls and smooth the tops.
Arrange the sliced apple on top.
Scatter over the pumpkin and sunflower seeds and finish with the honey.

notes: Use fully frozen mango for the thickest texture.

title: Peanut Butter Jar Oats with Honey and Grated Apple
summary: Creamy jar oats soaked overnight in milk with peanut butter, grated apple and a drizzle of honey.

steps.text: Stir the oats, milk, yoghurt, grated apple and cinnamon together in a bowl until combined.
Divide between two jars and cover.
Chill overnight or for at least 6 hours, until the oats are soft and the mixture has thickened.
Warm the peanut butter and honey for 15 seconds, then swirl over the top.
Finish with sliced apple.

notes: Keeps 3 days in the fridge without the apple on top.

title: Apple Pie Overnight Oats with Walnuts
summary: Soaked oats with grated apple, cinnamon and maple, topped with toasted walnuts for a cold apple pie breakfast.

steps.text: Mix the oats, milk, maple syrup, cinnamon, nutmeg and half the grated apple in a bowl.
Spoon into two jars, cover and chill overnight, until thick and creamy.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 3 minutes, until fragrant.
Top with the yoghurt, the remaining apple and the walnuts just before eating.

notes: Squeeze a little lemon over the grated apple to stop it browning.

title: Carrot Cake Overnight Oats
summary: Grated carrot, sultanas and warm spice soaked into oats, finished with a tangy ricotta topping.

steps.text: Stir the oats, milk, carrot, sultanas, cinnamon, ginger and 1 tbsp maple syrup together.
Divide into two jars, cover and chill overnight, until the oats are soft and plump.
Beat the ricotta with the remaining maple syrup until smooth.
Dollop onto the oats and scatter with the pecans.

notes: Walnuts work as well as pecans.

title: Bircher Muesli with Pear and Hazelnuts
summary: Classic Swiss soaked muesli with grated pear, apple and yoghurt, finished with toasted hazelnuts.

steps.text: Mix the oats and apple juice in a large bowl and leave for 10 minutes.
Stir through the yoghurt, grated apple, grated pear, lemon juice and cinnamon.
Cover and chill for at least 4 hours or overnight, until creamy.
Toast the hazelnuts in a dry pan for 3 minutes.
Serve topped with the sliced pear, hazelnuts and honey.

notes: Loosen with a splash of milk if it firms up overnight.

title: Cheese and Spinach Borek Rolls
summary: Crisp filo rolls filled with feta and spinach, brushed with yoghurt butter and baked until deeply golden.

items.raw: 300g frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C. Cook the onion in the oil for 6 minutes, until soft, then cool and mix with the spinach, feta, 1 egg and the pepper.
Lay a filo sheet down, brush with butter, spoon a line of filling along one long edge and roll tightly into a log.
Coil the log loosely into a round tin and repeat with the rest, brushing the filo with butter as you go.
Whisk the second egg with the yoghurt and pour over the top, then scatter with sesame seeds.
Bake for 30 minutes, until deep golden and crisp, then rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

notes: Food safety: bake until the egg filling is fully set and hot through.
Keep unused filo covered with a damp tea towel so it does not dry out.

title: Welsh Bara Brith Fruit Loaf
summary: A sticky Welsh fruit loaf with sultanas and currants soaked in orange juice, sliced and spread with butter.

steps.text: Soak the sultanas, currants, sugar and orange juice in a bowl for at least 6 hours or overnight, until plump.
Heat the oven to 160°C and line a 900g loaf tin.
Stir the egg, flour, spices and zest into the fruit until just combined.
Scrape into the tin and level the top.
Bake for 60 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 15 minutes, then turn out and slice thickly.

notes: Food safety: bake until the centre is fully cooked and the skewer is clean, as the batter contains raw egg.
Keeps 5 days wrapped, and is excellent buttered.

title: Irish Soda Bread with Caraway
summary: A no-yeast Irish loaf with a craggy crust and soft crumb, flavoured with caraway and best eaten warm.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C and flour a tray.
Mix the flours, bicarbonate of soda, salt and caraway in a large bowl.
Add the buttermilk and honey and stir quickly with a fork until a shaggy dough forms, without overworking it.
Shape into a round on the tray and cut a deep cross in the top.
Bake for 15 minutes, then lower the oven to 200°C and bake for 25 minutes, until golden and hollow-sounding underneath.
Cool for 15 minutes before slicing.

notes: Best the day it is baked; toast leftovers.

title: Irish Boxty Potato Pancakes
summary: Pan-fried Irish potato pancakes made from raw grated and mashed potato, crisp outside and soft within.

steps.text: Squeeze the grated potato in a clean tea towel until very dry.
Mix the grated potato, mashed potato, flour, egg, buttermilk, bicarbonate of soda, salt and spring onion into a thick batter.
Melt a little butter in a frying pan over medium heat.
Fry spoonfuls for 4 minutes each side, until golden and cooked through, adding butter as needed.
Serve hot with more butter or alongside bacon and eggs.

notes: Food safety: cook until the pancakes are golden and set through the middle, as they contain raw egg.

title: Apple and Walnut Breakfast Bread
summary: Moist apple loaf with walnuts and cinnamon and a crackly sugar top, sliced thick and toasted with butter.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C and line a 900g loaf tin.
Squeeze the grated apple lightly, then whisk it with the milk, eggs, butter and sugar until combined.
Fold in the flour, bicarbonate of soda, cinnamon, salt and half the walnuts until just mixed.
Pour into the tin and top with the remaining walnuts.
Bake for 55 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn out and cool before slicing.

notes: Food safety: bake until a skewer comes out clean, as the batter contains raw egg.
Slices freeze well.

title: Zucchini and Lemon Breakfast Loaf
summary: A tender loaf with grated zucchini and lemon, lightly sweet and perfect with ricotta or butter.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C and line a 900g loaf tin.
Squeeze the zucchini in a tea towel to remove the extra water.
Whisk the eggs, oil, sugar, lemon zest and juice and yoghurt.
Fold in the flour, baking powder, salt and zucchini until just combined.
Scrape into the tin, sprinkle with the pepitas and bake for 55 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes before slicing.

notes: Food safety: bake until a skewer comes out clean, as the batter contains raw egg.
Swap the pepitas for sunflower seeds if you like.

title: Pumpkin Spice Breakfast Loaf
summary: A soft pumpkin loaf with cinnamon, ginger and nutmeg, lovely toasted and spread with butter.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170°C and line a 900g loaf tin.
Whisk the pumpkin, eggs, oil and sugar until smooth.
Fold in the flour, baking powder, spices and salt until just combined.
Pour into the tin and scatter with the pepitas.
Bake for 55 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn out to cool.

notes: Food safety: bake until a skewer comes out clean, as the batter contains raw egg.
Use canned pumpkin puree or roast and mash your own.

title: Swedish Cardamom Buns Kardemummabullar
summary: Soft enriched buns rolled with butter, sugar and cardamom, twisted into knots and sprinkled with pearl sugar.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, cardamom and salt, then add the warm milk, egg and softened butter.
Knead for 10 minutes, until smooth and elastic, then cover and prove for 1 hour, until doubled.
Roll the dough to a 40 x 30 cm rectangle, until about 5 mm thick, and spread with the filling butter, brown sugar and cardamom.
Fold into thirds, cut into 12 strips, twist each into a knot and place on lined trays.
Prove for 30 minutes, then brush with beaten egg and sprinkle with sugar crystals.
Bake at 220°C for 12 minutes, until deep golden.

notes: Food safety: the egg wash is baked hard at 220°C; cook until the buns are golden all over.
Freeze cooled buns for up to 2 months.

title: Finnish Pulla Cardamom Braid
summary: A glossy braided Finnish coffee bread, scented with cardamom and sprinkled with almonds and sugar.

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, cardamom and salt with the warm milk and 2 eggs.
Knead in the butter, then knead for 10 minutes, until smooth and elastic.
Cover and prove for 1 hour, until doubled.
Divide into three ropes, plait them, place on a lined tray and prove for 30 minutes.
Brush with beaten egg and top with the almonds and sugar crystals.
Bake at 190°C for 30 minutes, until deep golden and hollow-sounding underneath.

notes: Food safety: bake until golden and cooked through, as the egg wash and dough contain raw egg.
Delicious toasted with butter the next day.

title: Cambodian Kuy Teav Pork and Rice Noodle Soup
summary: A clear pork broth with rice noodles, minced pork and fresh herbs, the Phnom Penh breakfast soup.

steps.text: Simmer the ribs, water and onion for 35 minutes, skimming, until the broth is clear and the meat is tender.
Season the broth with the fish sauce and sugar.
Soak the noodles in hot water for 8 minutes until soft, then drain.
Fry the garlic and mince in a dry pan for 5 minutes, until cooked through at 75°C and lightly browned.
Divide the noodles, mince and bean sprouts between bowls and ladle over the hot broth with a few ribs.
Top with shallots, coriander, spring onion and a squeeze of lime.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork mince until 75°C in the centre with no pink inside, and keep the broth at a rolling simmer.
Add chilli and garlic vinegar at the table.

title: Japanese Shoyu Ramen Soup
summary: Clear soy broth with springy noodles, soft eggs, sliced chicken and spring onion.

steps.text: Simmer the chicken, water, ginger, garlic and onion for 35 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through at 75°C and the broth is savoury.
Lift out the chicken, shred the meat and strain the broth back into the pot.
Stir the soy sauce and mirin into the broth and keep it hot.
Boil the eggs for 6.5 minutes, cool in cold water, peel and halve.
Cook the noodles in boiling water for 3 minutes, until tender, and drain.
Divide the noodles between bowls, ladle over the broth and top with chicken, egg, nori, spring onion and sesame oil.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until 75°C in the thickest part, and boil the eggs until the whites are fully set; cook the yolks through if serving anyone vulnerable.
Reheat leftover broth to a rolling boil.

title: Japanese Kitsune Udon with Sweet Tofu Pockets
summary: Thick udon in a clean dashi and soy broth topped with sweet simmered tofu pockets and spring onion.

steps.text: Simmer the tofu pockets in 150ml of the dashi with 1 tbsp soy sauce, the sugar and 1 tbsp mirin for 8 minutes, until the liquid reduces and they are glossy.
Bring the remaining dashi, soy sauce and mirin to a gentle boil in a pot, until steaming and fragrant.
Cook the udon in boiling water for 3 minutes, until tender, then drain.
Divide the udon between bowls and pour over the hot broth.
Top with the tofu pockets, spring onion and white pepper.

notes: Pour the pocket syrup over for extra sweetness.
Check the dashi for fish if you need a vegetarian dish.

title: Indonesian Soto Mie Noodle Soup
summary: A turmeric and lemongrass chicken broth with egg noodles, bean sprouts and boiled egg.

steps.text: Blend the garlic, shallots, turmeric and coriander to a paste with a splash of water.
Fry the paste in the oil for 4 minutes, until fragrant, then add the chicken, lemongrass and water.
Simmer for 25 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through at 75°C, then shred the meat and season with the soy sauce.
Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, cool, peel and halve.
Cook the noodles in boiling water for 3 minutes and drain.
Divide the noodles, chicken, sprouts and egg between bowls, ladle over the broth and finish with fried shallots and lime.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until 75°C in the thickest part, and boil the eggs until the yolks are fully set.
Serve with sambal.

title: Sri Lankan Parippu Red Lentil Soup
summary: A comforting red lentil and coconut milk dhal-style soup scented with turmeric, curry spices and lime.

steps.text: Cook the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the spices and stir for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the lentils, tomato and water and simmer for 20 minutes, until the lentils collapse.
Stir in the coconut milk and heat for 5 minutes.
Season with the salt and lime juice, thin with water if needed and serve with rice.

notes: Keeps 4 days and freezes well.
Top with fried curry onions for extra crunch.

title: Egyptian Shorbet Ads Yellow Lentil Soup
summary: A silky Egyptian lentil soup with cumin and lemon, served with fried bread and extra lemon.

steps.text: Cook the onion, carrot and garlic in 1 tbsp oil for 6 minutes, until softened.
Stir in the cumin and turmeric for 1 minute.
Add the lentils and stock and simmer for 25 minutes, until completely soft.
Blend with a stick blender until smooth, then season with the lemon juice and salt.
Fry the bread cubes in the remaining oil for 4 minutes, until crisp and golden.
Serve the soup with the croutons and extra lemon.

notes: Add a splash of water if the soup thickens on standing.

title: Tunisian Lablabi Chickpea and Bread Soup
summary: A garlicky cumin chickpea broth ladled over torn bread and finished with harissa, olive oil and lemon.

steps.text: Drain the chickpeas, add to a pot with the water and simmer for 40 minutes, until soft.
Crush 4 garlic cloves with the cumin and salt into a paste and stir into the pot.
Simmer for 5 minutes more, then stir in the lemon juice.
Place the torn bread in four bowls.
Ladle over the chickpeas and broth.
Top with the harissa, capers, remaining finely sliced garlic and a generous pour of olive oil.

notes: Canned chickpeas work in a hurry: use 3 tins and simmer for 15 minutes.

title: Brazilian Black Bean Soup with Orange and Chorizo
summary: A smoky black bean soup with chorizo and a splash of orange juice, served with rice and a squeeze of lime.

steps.text: Fry the chorizo in the oil for 5 minutes, until crisp and the fat runs.
Add the onion and garlic and cook for 5 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the paprika, then add the drained beans, bay leaf and water.
Simmer for 50 minutes, until the beans are completely tender.
Mash a quarter of the beans against the side of the pot to thicken, then add the orange juice.
Season, simmer for 5 minutes, and serve with the coriander and lime.

notes: Food safety: cook the chorizo until 75°C in the centre and piping hot; boil dried beans for at least 10 minutes in fresh water before simmering.
Skip the chorizo for a vegan soup.

title: Sichuan Mala Chilli Oil
summary: A fragrant red oil with Sichuan pepper, chilli flakes and aromatics for dumplings, noodles and eggs.

steps.text: Toast the Sichuan peppercorns in a dry pan for 1 minute and crush coarsely.
Put the chilli flakes, crushed pepper, sesame seeds and salt in a heatproof bowl.
Heat the oil with the star anise, cinnamon, garlic and ginger over low heat for 8 minutes, until just bubbling around the aromatics.
Strain the hot oil over the chilli mixture and it will sizzle, then stir in the soy sauce.
Cool completely and store in a clean jar.

notes: Keeps 1 month in a cool dark cupboard.
Stir the oil before use so the chilli sinks to the bottom.
Food safety: Keep any leftover garlic, herb or chilli oil in the fridge and use it within 4 days.

title: Mushroom Gravy with Thyme
summary: A rich vegetarian gravy of browned mushrooms, onion and thyme, ready for roasts, mash and pies.

steps.text: Cook the mushrooms in the butter in a wide pan for 8 minutes, until deeply browned and the liquid has gone.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the flour and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the stock and soy sauce.
Add the thyme and bay leaf and simmer for 10 minutes, until glossy and slightly thickened.
Remove the herbs, season with the pepper and serve hot.

notes: Blend half for a smoother gravy.
Use cornflour instead of flour for a gluten-free gravy.

title: Fermented Red Jalapeno Hot Sauce
summary: A tangy, lightly funky hot sauce made from salt-brined red jalapenos fermented for a week and blended with vinegar.

steps.text: Dissolve the salt in the water to make a brine.
Pack the jalapenos, garlic and carrot into a clean jar and pour over the brine, keeping everything submerged under a weight.
Cover loosely and ferment at room temperature for 7 days, until bubbly and pleasantly sour, releasing the gas daily.
Drain, keeping the brine, and blend the solids with the vinegar, honey and 100ml of the brine for 2 minutes, until smooth.
Simmer the sauce for 5 minutes, then cool and bottle.

notes: Keeps 3 months in the fridge.
Wear gloves when chopping chillies.

title: Fermented Habanero and Carrot Hot Sauce
summary: A fruity, fiery Caribbean-style hot sauce built on fermented habaneros, carrot and lime.

steps.text: Dissolve the salt in the water.
Pack the chillies, carrots, onion and garlic into a jar, cover with the brine and weigh down.
Ferment at room temperature for 7 days, until bubbly and sour, opening the lid daily to release the gas.
Drain and blend the solids with the lime juice, vinegar, sugar and 100ml of the brine for 2 minutes, until silky.
Simmer for 5 minutes, then cool and bottle.

notes: Very hot: use 100g habanero for a medium sauce.
Keeps 3 months in the fridge.

title: Louisiana-Style Vinegar Hot Sauce
summary: A thin, sharp, pourable hot sauce of red chilli, garlic and vinegar for eggs, wings, beans and fried food.

steps.text: Simmer the chillies, garlic, water and half the vinegar for 15 minutes, until the chillies are very soft.
Blend with the salt, sugar and remaining vinegar for 2 minutes, until completely smooth.
Strain through a sieve, pressing well, then bottle.
Rest for 3 days in the fridge before using, until the flavours mellow.

notes: Keeps 3 months in the fridge.
Wear gloves and open a window while simmering the chillies.

title: Kuwaiti Daqoos Tomato and Chilli Sauce
summary: A tangy Gulf tomato sauce with garlic, cumin, coriander and chilli, served with grilled meat, rice and flatbread.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a pan and cook the garlic and chillies for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, cumin, coriander and salt and simmer for 15 minutes, until the sauce is thick and the oil separates.
Stir in the vinegar and lemon juice and cook for 2 minutes.
Cool slightly, then stir through the chopped coriander.

notes: Serve warm or cold; it keeps 5 days in the fridge.

title: Brown Butter and Sage Pan Sauce
summary: Nutty brown butter with crisp sage and lemon, spooned over pasta, gnocchi, roast pumpkin or fish.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a light-coloured pan over medium heat.
Cook for 4 minutes, until the milk solids turn golden brown and smell nutty.
Add the sage and garlic and cook for 1 minute, until the sage is crisp and the garlic pale gold.
Remove from the heat and add the lemon juice, which will spit, then season with the salt and pepper.

notes: Use immediately while it is hot and frothy.

title: Red Wine and Shallot Pan Sauce
summary: A glossy steak sauce of shallots reduced with red wine, stock and thyme, enriched with cold butter.

steps.text: Cook the shallots in the first measure of butter for 5 minutes, until soft and golden.
Add the wine and thyme and boil for 8 minutes, until reduced by two thirds.
Add the stock and boil for 8 minutes, until syrupy enough to coat a spoon.
Remove the thyme, whisk in the vinegar and the cold butter a cube at a time, until glossy.
Season with the pepper and serve straight away.

notes: Do not boil once the butter is in, or the sauce splits.

title: Onion Gravy with Thyme
summary: Slowly browned onions simmered in rich stock with thyme and a splash of balsamic, ideal for sausages and mash.

steps.text: Cook the onions in the butter and oil over medium-low heat for 25 minutes, stirring often, until deeply golden and sweet.
Stir in the flour for 1 minute.
Gradually add the stock, stirring, then add the vinegar, worcestershire sauce and thyme.
Simmer for 10 minutes, until glossy and thickened enough to coat a spoon.
Remove the thyme, season with the pepper and serve hot.

notes: Use vegetable stock and omit the worcestershire sauce for a vegetarian gravy.

title: Peppercorn Cream Pan Sauce
summary: A classic steak-house sauce of cracked peppercorns, brandy, stock and cream.

steps.text: Cook the shallots and peppercorns in the butter for 3 minutes, until soft.
Carefully add the brandy and let it bubble for 1 minute, until almost evaporated.
Add the stock and boil for 5 minutes, until reduced by half.
Stir in the cream and mustard and simmer for 3 minutes, until it coats the back of a spoon.
Season with the salt and taste, adding more pepper if you like.

notes: Keep the heat low once the cream is in, or it will split.

title: Mustard and Tarragon Cream Sauce
summary: A tangy, herby cream sauce with Dijon, white wine and tarragon for chicken, fish and vegetables.

steps.text: Cook the shallots in the butter for 3 minutes, until soft.
Add the wine and boil for 4 minutes, until reduced by two thirds.
Add the stock and cream and simmer for 5 minutes, until thick enough to coat a spoon.
Whisk in the mustard, tarragon, lemon juice and salt and warm through without boiling.

notes: Swap the tarragon for dill for fish.

title: Carolina Mustard BBQ Sauce
summary: A thin, tangy South Carolina sauce of yellow mustard, cider vinegar and brown sugar for pulled pork and sausages.

steps.text: Whisk everything together in a saucepan.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 15 minutes, stirring often, until slightly thickened and glossy.
Cool completely, then pour into a clean jar and store in the fridge.

notes: Keeps 3 weeks in the fridge.
Add a dash of hot sauce for more heat.

title: Honey Roasted Carrots with Hazelnut Spice Crunch
summary: Sweet roasted carrots glazed with honey and dusted with a crunchy nut and spice dukkah, served over yoghurt.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C and line a large tray with baking paper.
Toss the carrots with the oil, honey and salt on a lined tray.
Roast for 30 minutes, turning once, until tender and caramelised at the edges.
Toast the hazelnuts and sesame in a dry pan for 3 minutes, until golden, then stir through the cumin and coriander.
Stir the lemon juice into the yoghurt and spread on a platter.
Pile the carrots on top and scatter with the toasted nut mix and mint.

notes: Use maple syrup instead of honey for a vegan side with dairy-free yoghurt.

title: Roast Broccoli with Garlic and Chilli
summary: Charred broccoli florets roasted hot with garlic and chilli flakes, finished with lemon and toasted almonds.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 230°C and line a large tray with baking paper.
Toss the broccoli with the oil, garlic, chilli flakes and salt on a large tray.
Roast for 18 minutes, turning once, until the tips are charred and the stems tender.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 3 minutes, until golden.
Finish with the lemon zest, juice and almonds.

notes: Swap the almonds for toasted breadcrumbs.

title: Maple Roast Pumpkin Wedges with Sage
summary: Sweet roasted pumpkin wedges glazed with maple, brown butter and crisp sage.

items.raw: 1 kg pumpkin, cut into wedges with skin on
items.prep: cut into wedges with skin on

steps.text: Heat the oven to 210°C and line a large tray with baking paper.
Toss the pumpkin with the oil, 2 tbsp maple syrup and the salt on a lined tray.
Roast for 35 minutes, turning once, until caramelised and tender.
Melt the butter in a pan until foaming, add the sage and cook for 1 minute, until crisp.
Pour over the pumpkin with the remaining maple syrup, pecans and pepper.

notes: Leave the skin on, it is edible and holds the wedges together.

title: Crispy Smashed Potatoes with Rosemary
summary: Boiled baby potatoes smashed flat and roasted until the edges are shatteringly crisp, with rosemary and garlic.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in well-salted water for 20 minutes, until a knife slides in easily, then drain well.
Heat the oven to 230°C and heat the oil on a large tray.
Space the potatoes on the tray and smash each flat with a glass.
Scatter over the rosemary, garlic and salt.
Roast for 30 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and crisp.

notes: Dry the boiled potatoes well so they crisp.

title: Roasted Beetroot with Yoghurt and Dill
summary: Earthy roast beetroot wedges on garlicky yoghurt with dill, walnuts and a little lemon.

items.raw: 800g beetroot, scrubbed and cut into wedges

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C and line a large tray with baking paper.
Toss the beetroot with the oil and salt on a lined tray and cover loosely with foil.
Roast for 40 minutes, then uncover and roast for 10 minutes, until tender and slightly caramelised.
Mix the yoghurt, garlic and half the lemon juice and spread on a plate.
Pile the beetroot on top and finish with the dill, walnuts and remaining lemon.

notes: Wear gloves to avoid staining your hands.

title: Oven-Roasted Cherry Tomatoes with Thyme
summary: Slowly roasted cherry tomatoes concentrated with thyme and garlic, to spoon over toast, pasta or grilled meat.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C and line a large tray with baking paper.
Toss the tomatoes with the oil, garlic, thyme, sugar, salt and pepper in a baking dish.
Roast for 35 minutes, until the skins burst and the tomatoes are jammy and slightly caramelised.
Squash the garlic into the juices and serve warm.

notes: Keeps 5 days covered in the fridge.

title: Chinese-Style Sesame Cabbage Slaw
summary: Crunchy shredded cabbage and carrot in a nutty sesame, soy and rice vinegar dressing.

steps.text: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan for 2 minutes, until golden.
Whisk the soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, honey and ginger together.
Toss the cabbage, carrots, spring onions and coriander with the dressing.
Scatter over the sesame seeds and serve straight away.

notes: Add roasted peanuts or crispy noodles for extra crunch.

title: Apple and Celery Slaw with Mustard Dressing
summary: A crisp, tangy slaw of matchstick apple, celery and red cabbage in a mustard and yoghurt dressing.

steps.text: Whisk the yoghurt, mayonnaise, mustard, vinegar, honey and salt together.
Toss the apples, celery and cabbage in the dressing until evenly coated.
Scatter with the walnuts and eat within 30 minutes, while crisp.

notes: Squeeze lemon over the apple to stop browning.

title: Pearl Couscous Salad with Roasted Vegetables
summary: Chewy pearl couscous tossed with roasted capsicum, zucchini and red onion, with a lemon and herb dressing.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C and line a large tray with baking paper.
Toss the vegetables with 1 tbsp oil, the cumin and salt on a tray and roast for 25 minutes, until tender and charred at the edges.
Boil the couscous in salted water for 8 minutes, until tender but chewy, then drain.
Toss the warm couscous with the remaining oil, lemon juice, herbs and vegetables.
Crumble the feta over the top and serve warm or at room temperature.

notes: Leave out the feta for a vegan salad.

title: Barley and Roast Pumpkin Salad
summary: Nutty pearl barley with roast pumpkin, spinach and pepitas in a maple and mustard dressing.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C and line a large tray with baking paper.
Toss the pumpkin with 1 tbsp oil and the salt on a tray and roast for 30 minutes, until golden and tender.
Simmer the barley in plenty of water for 30 minutes, until tender, then drain.
Whisk the remaining oil, mustard, maple syrup and vinegar.
Toss the warm barley, pumpkin, onion and dressing, then fold through the spinach and pepitas.

notes: Good warm or cold the next day.

title: Wild Rice, Orange and Pecan Salad
summary: Chewy wild rice mix with orange segments, pecans and herbs in a citrus vinaigrette.

steps.text: Simmer the rice in plenty of salted water for 35 minutes, until the grains split, then drain well.
Toast the pecans in a dry pan for 3 minutes, until fragrant.
Whisk the reserved orange juice, oil, vinegar, mustard and salt.
Toss the warm rice with the dressing, then fold in the orange segments, pecans, parsley and spring onion.

notes: Serve at room temperature.

title: Pacific Sweet Potato Wedges with Coconut Lime Dip
summary: Oven-roasted sweet potato wedges served with a cool coconut yoghurt, lime and chilli dip.

items.raw: 1 kg sweet potatoes, cut into wedges

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C and line a large tray with baking paper.
Toss the sweet potato with the oil, salt and paprika on a large tray.
Roast for 30 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender inside.
Mix the coconut yoghurt with the lime zest, juice, chilli and half the coriander.
Serve the wedges with the dip and the remaining coriander.

notes: Use ordinary oil if you dislike the coconut flavour.

title: Pacific Coconut Pumpkin and Cabbage Soup
summary: A gentle coconut milk soup of pumpkin, cabbage and ginger with lime, inspired by island home cooking.

steps.text: Cook the onion, garlic and ginger in the oil for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the pumpkin, stock and coconut milk and simmer for 15 minutes, until the pumpkin is tender.
Add the cabbage and simmer for 5 minutes, until just wilted.
Season with the lime juice and salt.
Scatter with the coriander.

notes: Mash some of the pumpkin for a thicker soup.

title: Iraqi Shorbat Rizz Rice and Lemon Soup
summary: A comforting rice, lentil and lemon soup with turmeric, cumin and a drizzle of olive oil.

steps.text: Cook the onion and garlic in half the oil for 5 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the turmeric and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the rice, lentils and stock and simmer for 22 minutes, until both are very soft and the soup thick.
Stir in the lemon juice and salt.
Serve with the parsley and a drizzle of oil.

notes: Thin with a splash of water when reheating.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Burmese Mohinga Fish and Lemongrass Noodle Soup
summary: Burma's breakfast soup of thick fish and lemongrass broth over rice noodles with boiled egg and lime.

steps.text: Simmer the fish, water, lemongrass and ginger for 8 minutes, until the fish flakes, then lift out the fish and flake the meat, discarding bones and skin.
Fry the onion, garlic and turmeric in the oil for 6 minutes, until golden and fragrant.
Toast the chickpea flour in a dry pan for 2 minutes, then whisk it into the broth with the fried onion mix.
Simmer the broth for 20 minutes, until thickened enough to coat a spoon, then season with the fish sauce.
Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, cool, peel and halve, and soak the noodles in hot water for 8 minutes, until soft.
Serve the noodles in bowls with the fish, egg, broth, shallots, coriander and lime.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, and boil the eggs until the yolks are fully set.
Add chilli flakes at the table.

title: Thai Khao Soi Style Coconut Chicken Noodle Soup
summary: Northern Thai coconut curry noodle soup with chicken, crispy noodles, pickled mustard greens and lime.

steps.text: Fry the curry paste, turmeric and curry powder in 1 tbsp oil for 2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the chicken and cook for 4 minutes, until lightly browned.
Pour in the coconut milk and stock and simmer for 20 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through at 75°C and the broth is rich.
Season with the fish sauce and sugar.
Fry the 50g noodles in the remaining oil for 1 minute, until puffed and golden, and drain on paper towel.
Boil the remaining noodles for 3 minutes, until tender, drain and divide between bowls.
Ladle over the soup and top with the crispy noodles, spring onion, pickles and lime.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until 75°C in the thickest part with no pink inside.
Use tofu and vegetable stock for a vegetarian bowl.

title: Chinese Egg Drop Soup with Sweetcorn
summary: Silky ribbons of egg in a gingery chicken broth with sweetcorn, white pepper and spring onion.

steps.text: Simmer the stock and ginger for 5 minutes, until fragrant, then remove the ginger.
Add the sweetcorn and soy sauce and simmer for 3 minutes, until tender.
Mix the cornflour and water, stir into the soup and cook for 1 minute, until slightly thickened.
Stir the soup in one direction and pour in the eggs in a thin stream, so they form ribbons.
Switch off the heat, then add the sesame oil, spring onion and white pepper.

notes: Food safety: make sure the egg is fully set in the simmering broth before serving.
Use vegetable stock for a vegetarian version.

title: Japanese Zosui Egg and Rice Soup
summary: A gentle dashi and soy rice porridge with soft-set egg, ginger and spring onion, ideal for slow mornings.

steps.text: Rinse the cooked rice under hot water to remove the starch, then drain.
Bring the dashi, soy sauce, mirin and salt to a simmer in a saucepan, until steaming.
Add the rice and simmer for 8 minutes, until the grains are soft and the broth slightly thick.
Pour in the egg in a thin circle, cover for 1 minute off the heat, until just set.
Top with ginger, spring onion and nori.

notes: Food safety: cook the egg until it is fully set before serving.
Check the dashi for fish if you need a vegetarian bowl.

title: Italian Pasta e Ceci Chickpea and Rosemary Soup
summary: Rustic Roman chickpea and small pasta soup with rosemary, garlic and a drizzle of good olive oil.

steps.text: Cook the onion, carrot, celery and garlic in 2 tbsp oil for 8 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and rosemary for 1 minute.
Add the chickpeas and stock and simmer for 12 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Mash a third of the chickpeas against the pot to thicken.
Add the pasta and simmer for 8 minutes, until al dente, adding water if too thick.
Season and serve with the remaining oil.

notes: Remove the rosemary stalks before serving.
Add a splash of water on reheating, as the pasta absorbs liquid.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Tuscan White Bean and Kale Soup
summary: A thick brothy soup of white beans, kale, garlic and tomato, with a slice of toasted bread underneath.

items.raw: 1 bunch kale, stems removed and leaves sliced

steps.text: Cook the onion, carrots and garlic in 2 tbsp oil for 8 minutes, until soft.
Add the tomatoes, oregano, beans and stock and simmer for 15 minutes.
Mash a quarter of the beans against the pot to thicken the broth.
Add the kale and simmer for 8 minutes, until tender but still green.
Toast the bread until golden and crisp, then place in bowls.
Ladle the soup over, season with the salt and finish with the remaining oil.

notes: Keeps 4 days and tastes better the next day.

title: Spanish Fabada Style White Bean Soup with Chorizo
summary: A hearty white bean and chorizo soup coloured with smoked paprika, cooked low until creamy.

steps.text: Fry the chorizo in the oil for 5 minutes, until it releases its fat and crisps slightly.
Add the onion and garlic and cook for 6 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the paprika, then add the drained beans, bay leaf, saffron and water.
Simmer gently for 50 minutes, until the beans are completely tender and creamy.
Season with the salt, remove the bay leaf and serve.

notes: Food safety: cook the chorizo until 75°C in the centre and piping hot; boil dried beans vigorously for 10 minutes in fresh water before simmering to destroy toxins.
Skip the chorizo for a vegan soup and add extra paprika.

title: Greek Fakes Lentil Soup with Vinegar and Oregano
summary: Everyday Greek brown lentil soup, simmered with bay and garlic and finished with red wine vinegar and olive oil.

steps.text: Cook the onion, carrot and garlic in 2 tbsp oil for 6 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and oregano for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, bay leaves and water and simmer for 30 minutes, until the lentils are tender and the soup thick.
Season with the salt and stir in the vinegar.
Serve with the remaining oil poured over.

notes: Serve with feta and olives for a fuller meal.

title: Ukrainian Green Borscht with Spinach and Egg
summary: A sharp, lemony green borscht of potato, spinach and dill, topped with a boiled egg and a spoon of sour cream.

steps.text: Cook the onion and carrot in the butter for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the stock and potatoes and simmer for 15 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, cool, peel and halve.
Stir the spinach into the soup for 2 minutes, until just wilted, then add the dill, lemon juice and salt.
Serve topped with the eggs and sour cream.

notes: Food safety: boil the eggs until the yolks are fully set.
Use vegetable stock for a vegetarian soup.

title: Spiced Chickpea Flour Stew with Paprika and Ginger
summary: A smooth, spiced chickpea flour stew with onion, garlic and paprika, served with injera or rice.

steps.text: Cook the onion in a dry pot for 5 minutes, until softened, then add the oil, garlic and ginger and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, paprika, cumin and cardamom for 1 minute.
Whisk the chickpea flour into the water until smooth, then pour it into the pot.
Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring often, until thick and smooth.
Season with the salt and lemon juice.

notes: Whisk constantly as you add the flour to prevent lumps.
Serve with bread or rice.

title: South African Split Pea and Ham Soup
summary: A thick winter soup of green split peas, a smoky ham hock and root vegetables, served with buttered bread.

steps.text: Place the ham hock, split peas, onion, carrots, celery, garlic, bay leaves and water in a large pot.
Bring to the boil, skim the surface, then simmer for 75 minutes, until the peas have collapsed and the ham is very tender.
Lift out the hock and shred the meat, discarding skin and bones.
Add the potatoes and simmer for 12 minutes, until tender.
Return the meat to the pot, season with the pepper and thin with water if needed.

notes: Food safety: cool leftovers within 2 hours and keep for up to 3 days.
The hock is salty, so taste before adding salt.

title: Mexican Caldo de Pollo
summary: A homely Mexican chicken soup with corn, carrots, potatoes and zucchini, served with coriander, onion and lime.

steps.text: Simmer the chicken, water, halved onion, garlic and salt for 30 minutes, skimming, until the chicken is cooked through at 75°C.
Lift out the chicken and shred the meat, discarding skin and bones.
Add the carrots, potatoes and corn to the broth and simmer for 12 minutes, until almost tender.
Add the zucchini and simmer for 5 minutes, until just soft.
Return the chicken to the pot and serve with coriander, chopped onion and lime.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until 75°C in the thickest part with no pink inside; chill leftovers within 2 hours.
Add a chopped chilli for heat.

title: Chilean Cazuela de Pollo with Pumpkin and Corn
summary: A whole-meal Chilean chicken soup with a big piece of pumpkin, potato, corn and rice, finished with coriander.

steps.text: Simmer the chicken, onion, garlic, paprika and water for 20 minutes, skimming.
Add the pumpkin, potatoes and corn and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the rice and capsicum and simmer for 12 minutes, until the rice is tender and the chicken is cooked through at 75°C.
Season with the salt and serve with the coriander.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until 75°C at the bone and the juices run clear.
Use a pumpkin with firm flesh so it holds its shape.

title: Argentinian Locro Style Pumpkin and Bean Stew
summary: A thick, hearty stew of white beans, pumpkin, corn and chorizo that warms the Andes in winter.

steps.text: Boil the drained beans in fresh water for 10 minutes, then drain.
Fry the bacon and chorizo in the oil for 6 minutes, until the fat runs and they are lightly browned.
Add the onion and garlic and cook for 5 minutes, then stir in the paprika.
Add the beans and water and simmer for 40 minutes, until the beans are nearly tender.
Add the pumpkin and corn and simmer for 15 minutes, until the pumpkin starts to break down and the stew is thick.
Season with the salt and serve with the spring onion.

notes: Food safety: cook the chorizo until 75°C in the centre and piping hot; boil dried beans for at least 10 minutes before simmering.
Mash some of the pumpkin to thicken.

title: Ecuadorian Locro de Papa Potato and Cheese Soup
summary: A creamy Andean potato soup with milk and soft cheese, served with avocado and a crunchy side of corn.

steps.text: Cook the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the cumin and turmeric for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes and water and simmer for 20 minutes, until very soft.
Mash roughly with a potato masher, then add the milk and warm through for 3 minutes.
Season with the salt and serve topped with the queso fresco, avocado and spring onion.

notes: Mash fully for a smooth soup.
Use feta if you cannot find queso fresco.

title: Canadian Split Pea Soup with Smoked Ham
summary: A thick Quebec-style yellow split pea soup with smoky ham, carrot, celery and thyme.

steps.text: Place the peas, ham, onion, carrots, celery, garlic, thyme, bay leaves and water in a large pot.
Bring to the boil, skim the surface, then simmer for 70 minutes, stirring often, until the peas have collapsed and the soup is thick.
Remove the thyme and bay leaves.
Season with the pepper, adding water if too thick.

notes: Food safety: cool leftovers within 2 hours and keep up to 3 days.
Taste before adding salt, as the ham is salty.

title: New England Corn Chowder
summary: A creamy chowder of sweetcorn, potato and bacon, thickened with milk and finished with chives.

steps.text: Cook the bacon in a pot for 6 minutes, until crisp, then lift out half and keep for topping.
Cook the onion and celery in the bacon fat for 6 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then gradually add the stock.
Add the potatoes and simmer for 15 minutes, until tender.
Add the corn, milk and cream and simmer for 5 minutes, until thick.
Season with the pepper and serve with the reserved bacon and chives.

notes: Food safety: cook the bacon until crisp and piping hot.
Blend a third of the soup for a thicker chowder.

title: Hawaiian Saimin Noodle Soup
summary: Hawai'i's comfort noodle soup: wheat noodles in a clear dashi and pork broth with ham, egg and spring onion.

steps.text: Simmer the stock, dashi, soy sauce, sugar and ginger for 10 minutes, until fragrant.
Boil the eggs for 7 minutes, cool, peel and halve.
Cook the noodles in boiling water for 3 minutes, until tender, and drain.
Divide the noodles between bowls and top with ham and fish cake.
Strain the hot broth over and finish with the egg and spring onion.

notes: Food safety: boil the eggs until the whites are set and cook the yolks through if serving anyone vulnerable.
Use sliced chicken or tofu in place of ham.

title: Yemeni Shafut Yoghurt and Bread Salad
summary: A cool Yemeni dish of flatbread soaked in herby yoghurt with tomato, cucumber and chilli.

steps.text: Whisk the yoghurt with the garlic, chilli, half the herbs and the salt until smooth.
Lay half the torn bread in a large dish.
Spoon over half the yoghurt, then repeat with the remaining bread and yoghurt, and rest for 10 minutes, until the bread softens.
Scatter over the cucumber, tomato, onion and remaining herbs and finish with the oil.

notes: Serve straight away or the bread will turn mushy.

title: Saudi Jareesh Style Cracked Wheat Porridge
summary: A creamy Gulf cracked wheat and yoghurt porridge finished with sizzling cumin and onion butter.

steps.text: Simmer the cracked wheat in the water for 30 minutes, stirring often, until very soft and thick.
Add the milk and yoghurt and cook for 10 minutes, stirring, until creamy.
Beat the porridge with a wooden spoon for 2 minutes, until smooth.
Fry the onion in the butter for 8 minutes, until deeply golden, then add the cumin.
Season the porridge with the salt and pepper and spoon into bowls with the cumin butter on top.

notes: Beat vigorously with a wooden spoon for a creamier texture.

title: Lebanese Fattet Hummus Chickpea and Bread Bowl
summary: Crisp pita pieces layered with warm chickpeas, garlicky yoghurt and sizzling pine nut butter.

steps.text: Bake the pita with the oil at 200°C for 8 minutes, until golden and crisp.
Warm the chickpeas in a small pan with a splash of water and the cumin for 5 minutes, until hot.
Whisk the yoghurt, tahini, garlic, lemon juice and salt until smooth.
Melt the butter and toast the pine nuts for 3 minutes, until golden.
Layer the pita, chickpeas and yoghurt in bowls, then pour over the pine nut butter and scatter with the parsley.

notes: Serve straight away so the pita stays a little crisp.

title: Fijian Rourou Spinach in Coconut Cream
summary: Wilted greens simmered gently in coconut cream with onion, ginger and chilli, a classic Fijian side.

steps.text: Cook the onion, garlic and ginger in the oil for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the chilli and coconut cream and simmer for 4 minutes, until slightly reduced.
Add the spinach in handfuls and cook for 4 minutes, until wilted and tender.
Season with the lime juice and salt and serve with rice or root vegetables.

notes: Use frozen spinach, well squeezed, if fresh is unavailable.

title: Tahitian Cucumber and Tomato Coconut Salad
summary: A cooling salad of cucumber, tomato and red onion dressed in lime-spiked coconut cream.

steps.text: Salt the cucumber and onion for 5 minutes and drain off the liquid.
Whisk the coconut cream, lime juice, chilli and salt.
Toss the cucumber, tomato and onion with the dressing until well coated.
Scatter with coriander and serve chilled.

notes: Best eaten within an hour while crisp.

title: Vietnamese Sup Bap Sweetcorn and Egg Soup
summary: A silky chicken and sweetcorn soup with egg ribbons, popular as a Vietnamese street-side snack.

steps.text: Simmer the stock and half the sweetcorn for 8 minutes, until sweet and tender.
Blend the remaining sweetcorn with a little stock until smooth and stir into the pot.
Add the chicken and fish sauce and simmer for 3 minutes.
Mix the cornflour and water, stir in, and cook for 1 minute, until slightly thickened.
Pour in the egg in a thin stream while stirring, so it forms ribbons, then add the pepper.
Serve with spring onion and coriander.

notes: Food safety: make sure the chicken is piping hot at 75°C and the egg fully set before serving.
Skip the chicken for a vegetarian soup.

title: Korean Sujebi Hand-Torn Dough Soup
summary: Chewy hand-torn wheat dough flakes in an anchovy and kelp broth with zucchini, potato and spring onion.

steps.text: Knead the flour, water and oil into a smooth dough for 5 minutes, then rest for 30 minutes under a damp cloth.
Simmer the dashi, potato, onion and garlic for 10 minutes, until the potato is almost tender.
Stretch pieces of dough thin between your fingers and drop into the pot until all used.
Simmer for 8 minutes, until the dough floats and is chewy.
Add the zucchini, soy sauce and salt and cook for 3 minutes, then add the spring onion.

notes: Dough should be stretched very thin so it cooks quickly.
Check the dashi for fish if you need a vegetarian soup.

title: Indian Masala Omelette Roll with Green Chilli
summary: A fluffy omelette packed with onion, tomato, green chilli and coriander, rolled up for a quick Indian breakfast.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs with the onion, tomato, chilli, coriander, turmeric and salt.
Melt half the butter in a nonstick pan over medium heat.
Pour in half the mixture and cook for 3 minutes, until the underside is golden and the top is almost set.
Roll up and slide onto a plate, then repeat with the rest.

notes: Food safety: cook the omelette until the egg is fully set with no runny egg.
Serve with buttered toast or paratha.

title: Greek Spanakopita Breakfast Scramble
summary: Soft scrambled eggs with wilted spinach, feta and dill, finished with lemon and served on toast.

steps.text: Wilt the spinach and spring onion in the oil for 2 minutes, until soft, then press out the water.
Beat the eggs and pour into the pan.
Stir gently for 3 minutes, until just set and creamy.
Fold in the feta, dill and lemon juice.
Toast the sourdough until golden and pile the eggs on top.

notes: Food safety: cook until the egg is fully set if serving anyone vulnerable.

title: Italian Frittata with Zucchini and Ricotta
summary: A light baked frittata of zucchini, spring onion and mint, studded with ricotta.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C and grease a 20cm ovenproof dish.
Squeeze the zucchini dry and cook with the spring onion in the oil for 4 minutes, until soft.
Whisk the eggs with the mint, salt and pepper and pour over.
Dot the ricotta over and bake for 14 minutes, until puffed and just set in the centre.
Rest for 3 minutes, then slice.

notes: Great cold in lunchboxes.
Food safety: bake until the centre is set and no longer liquid. Wash fresh produce well, refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat them within 3 days.

title: German Bauernfruhstuck Farmer's Breakfast
summary: Crispy fried potatoes with bacon, onion and eggs, a hearty German breakfast cooked in one pan.

steps.text: Fry the bacon in the butter for 5 minutes, until crisp.
Add the potatoes and fry for 10 minutes, turning rarely, until golden and crunchy.
Add the onion and cook for 4 minutes, until soft.
Beat the eggs and pour over, then cook for 4 minutes, stirring gently, until set.
Scatter with chives and pepper.

notes: Food safety: cook the bacon until crisp and piping hot, and the eggs until fully set.
Cook the potatoes ahead for crisp results.

title: Ricotta Hotcakes with Lemon and Warm Apple Compote
summary: Light, tender ricotta hotcakes served with warm blueberry compote and a squeeze of lemon.

steps.text: Whisk the ricotta, egg yolks, milk and lemon zest together.
Fold in the flour, baking powder and sugar.
Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks and gently fold them in.
Melt a little butter in a pan and cook 1/4 cup scoops for 2 minutes each side, until puffed and golden.
Simmer the apple, honey and lemon juice in a small pan for 6 minutes, until soft and syrupy, and spoon over.

notes: Food safety: cook the hotcakes until the batter is set in the middle.
Add a pinch of cinnamon to the compote.

title: Scandinavian Smorrebrod Smoked Salmon and Dill Rye
summary: Open rye sandwiches with dill cream cheese, smoked salmon, cucumber and capers.

steps.text: Beat the cream cheese with the dill and lemon juice until smooth.
Spread thickly over the rye slices.
Layer on the cucumber and fold the smoked salmon on top.
Scatter with the capers, onion and pepper and serve straight away.

notes: Food safety: keep smoked salmon chilled and avoid it in pregnancy or when serving anyone vulnerable.
Add boiled egg slices for more protein.

title: Vietnamese Banh Mi Omelette Baguette
summary: Egg omelette in a crisp baguette with pickled carrot, cucumber, coriander and chilli mayonnaise.

steps.text: Toss the carrot with the vinegar and sugar and leave for 10 minutes, until lightly pickled.
Whisk the eggs with the fish sauce.
Cook in the butter in a pan for 3 minutes, until set, then fold and halve.
Mix the mayonnaise and sriracha and spread inside the warmed baguettes.
Fill with the omelette, pickled carrot, cucumber and coriander.

notes: Food safety: cook the egg until fully set with no runny egg.
Add pate for a classic version.

title: Korean Gyeran Ppang Egg Bread
summary: Fluffy Korean street-food muffins baked with a whole egg in the middle, sweet and savoury at once.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C and grease a 4-hole muffin tin.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt, then add the milk, butter and 1 egg to make a thick batter.
Fill the holes half full, then crack an egg into the middle of each.
Bake for 18 minutes, until the batter is golden and the egg whites are set.
Sprinkle with parsley and eat warm.

notes: Food safety: bake until the whites are fully set, and until the yolk is set if serving anyone vulnerable.

title: Chinese Jianbing Crepe with Egg and Crackers
summary: A Tianjin street crepe with egg, hoisin and chilli sauce wrapped around crispy wonton wrappers.

steps.text: Whisk the flours and water into a thin batter.
Heat a nonstick pan with a little oil and pour in half the batter, swirling thin.
Cook for 1 minute, then crack an egg on top, spread it and scatter with sesame and spring onion.
Cook for 2 minutes, until the egg is set, then flip.
Spread with the hoisin and chilli sauces, add the coriander and fried wonton wrapper, and fold up.

notes: Food safety: cook the egg until fully set.
Repeat for the second crepe.

title: Ghanaian Hausa Koko Millet Porridge
summary: A peppery, ginger-spiced millet porridge sweetened with sugar and served with milk.

steps.text: Whisk the millet flour with 200ml cold water into a paste.
Bring the remaining water, ginger, cloves and pepper to a rolling boil, until fragrant.
Whisk in the paste and simmer for 12 minutes, stirring, until thick and smooth.
Stir in the sugar and salt and serve with the milk.

notes: Add groundnut paste for extra richness.
Strain through a sieve for a very smooth porridge.

title: South African Mealie Pap with Tomato Relish
summary: Soft white maize porridge served with a warm tomato and onion relish, a South African staple.

steps.text: Bring the water and salt to a rolling boil, then slowly whisk in the cornmeal until no lumps remain.
Cover and cook on low heat for 20 minutes, stirring often, until thick and cooked.
Cook the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, then add the tomatoes, curry powder, sugar and chilli and cook for 8 minutes, until pulpy.
Stir the butter into the pap and serve with the warm relish.

notes: Add more water for a runny porridge.

title: Caribbean Cornmeal Porridge with Nutmeg and Cinnamon
summary: Smooth Jamaican-style cornmeal porridge flavoured with cinnamon, nutmeg and vanilla and sweetened with condensed milk.

steps.text: Whisk the cornmeal with 250ml cold water into a paste.
Bring the remaining water and cinnamon to a rolling boil, until the water smells spiced.
Whisk in the paste and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring, until thick and smooth.
Remove the cinnamon, add the nutmeg, vanilla, salt, milk and condensed milk and warm for 2 minutes.

notes: Stir often to avoid lumps.
Add extra condensed milk to taste.

title: Caribbean Cornmeal Johnnycakes
summary: Golden pan-fried cornmeal and flour cakes with a crisp edge and soft centre, great with butter and fried fish or eggs.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, cornmeal, sugar, baking powder and salt together.
Rub in the butter until it resembles crumbs, then add the milk to make a soft dough.
Knead briefly, then shape into 8 flat discs.
Fry in the oil over medium heat for 4 minutes each side, until golden and cooked through.

notes: Serve warm.
Store cooled cakes in a sealed container for 2 days.

title: Ethiopian Genfo Barley Porridge with Spiced Butter
summary: A thick barley flour porridge with a well of spiced butter and berbere-style paprika sauce in the centre.

steps.text: Bring the water and salt to a rolling boil, until bubbling hard.
Whisk in the flour and cook for 12 minutes, stirring hard with a wooden spoon, until the porridge is thick and smooth.
Melt the butter with the paprika, cardamom, ginger and chilli for 2 minutes, until sizzling.
Shape the porridge into bowls, make a well and fill with the spiced butter.
Serve with the yoghurt alongside and eat while hot.

notes: Eat by scooping the porridge into the butter.
Use oat flour if barley flour is hard to find.

title: Peruvian Quinoa Breakfast Porridge with Cinnamon
summary: Warm quinoa cooked in milk with cinnamon, cloves and apple, sweetened with honey.

steps.text: Simmer the quinoa, milk, cinnamon, cloves and salt for 18 minutes, stirring often, until the grains are tender and the porridge thick.
Add the apple and honey and cook for 2 minutes.
Remove the cinnamon and cloves.
Serve with the toasted almonds scattered over the top.

notes: Use almond milk for a no-dairy bowl.

title: French Gougeres Cheese Puffs
summary: Light choux pastry puffs flavoured with vegetarian hard cheese, mustard and nutmeg, best eaten warm.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C and line two trays with baking paper.
Bring the water, milk, butter and salt to the boil, then tip in the flour and stir for 2 minutes, until a smooth ball forms.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the cheese, mustard and nutmeg, until glossy.
Pipe or spoon walnut-sized mounds onto the trays.
Bake for 25 minutes, until puffed and deep golden.

notes: Food safety: bake until deep golden and cooked through, as the dough contains raw egg.
Do not open the oven in the first 15 minutes, or they collapse.

title: Korean Doenjang Jjigae with Zucchini and Tofu
summary: A salty, earthy fermented soybean paste stew with zucchini, potato, tofu and chilli, served bubbling with rice.

steps.text: Bring the water to a simmer and whisk in the doenjang and gochugaru until the paste dissolves.
Add the potato and onion and simmer for 8 minutes, until the potato is nearly tender.
Add the zucchini, tofu and garlic and simmer for 5 minutes, until the zucchini is soft.
Top with the spring onion and chilli and serve with the rice.

notes: Doenjang is salty, so taste before adding any extra salt.
Add a handful of sliced mushrooms if you like.

title: Korean Seolleongtang Ox Bone Soup
summary: A milky, mild beef bone broth with sliced brisket and noodles, seasoned at the table with salt, pepper and spring onion.

steps.text: Cover the bones and brisket with cold water, boil for 10 minutes, then drain and rinse the bones and meat.
Return them to the pot with the 3 litres water, onion, garlic and ginger and simmer gently for 2.5 hours, until the broth turns milky and the brisket is tender.
Lift out the brisket and slice it thinly, then strain the broth and discard the bones.
Soak the glass noodles in hot water for 8 minutes, until soft, then drain.
Divide the noodles, rice and brisket between bowls, ladle over the hot broth and top with the spring onion.
Season at the table with the salt and pepper.

notes: Food safety: simmer the beef until very tender and at least 70°C throughout, and keep the broth hot until serving.
Chill leftover broth quickly and use within 3 days.

title: Korean Galbitang Short Rib Soup
summary: A clear, savoury soup of tender beef short ribs, daikon and glass noodles, lightly sweet and deeply comforting.

steps.text: Boil the ribs in water for 8 minutes, then drain and rinse them.
Return the ribs to the pot with 2 litres fresh water and simmer for 1 hour, skimming now and then.
Add the daikon, carrot, garlic, soy sauce, sesame oil and sugar and simmer for 40 minutes, until the ribs are tender.
Soak the noodles in hot water for 8 minutes, then add them to the soup for the final 3 minutes.
Beat the egg, pour a thin stream into the hot soup and stir once to make ribbons.
Top with the spring onion and pepper.

notes: Food safety: cook the ribs until very tender and at least 70°C throughout, and make sure the egg ribbons cook through in the simmering soup.
Skim off the fat once the soup has chilled.

title: Korean Dwaeji Gukbap Pork and Rice Soup
summary: A milky Busan pork and rice soup with garlic and spring onion, seasoned at the table with chilli.

steps.text: Cover the pork with water, boil for 5 minutes, then drain and rinse the pork.
Return it to the pot with 2 litres fresh water, onion, ginger, garlic and doenjang and simmer for 1 hour, until the pork is very tender.
Lift out the pork, slice it thinly and strain the broth.
Reheat the broth with the soy sauce and fish sauce until steaming hot.
Divide the rice and pork between bowls, ladle over the broth and top with spring onion, gochugaru and pepper.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork until very tender and at least 70°C throughout.
Chill leftover soup within 2 hours and use within 3 days.

title: Korean Dakgomtang Chicken Soup
summary: A clean, milky whole-chicken soup with garlic, ginger and spring onion, seasoned with salt and pepper at the table.

items.raw: 4 spring onions, 2 left whole and 2 sliced

steps.text: Put the chicken, water, onion, garlic, ginger and the whole spring onions in a large pot.
Bring to the boil, then simmer gently for 50 minutes, skimming the surface, until the chicken is cooked through and falling from the bone.
Lift out the chicken, shred the meat and discard the skin and bones.
Strain the broth, return it to the pot and add the noodles, simmering for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the chicken back and serve over the rice with sliced spring onion.
Season with the salt and pepper.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C at the thickest part of the thigh and keep the soup hot until serving.
Chill leftovers within 2 hours and use within 3 days.

title: Korean Manduguk Dumpling Soup
summary: Plump pork and kimchi dumplings in a light soy and garlic broth with egg ribbons and seaweed.

steps.text: Mix the pork, kimchi, tofu, half the spring onion and half the garlic into a filling.
Place a teaspoon of filling on each wrapper, wet the edges, fold into a parcel and press to seal.
Bring the stock, soy sauce and remaining garlic to a simmer until bubbling.
Add the dumplings and simmer for 6 minutes, until they float and the pork is cooked through.
Beat the eggs and pour them in a thin stream into the soup, stirring once until ribbons set.
Add the sesame oil and pepper, then ladle into bowls and top with the seaweed and remaining spring onion.

notes: Food safety: cook the dumplings until the pork reaches 75°C and no pink remains, and cook the egg until fully set.
Freeze uncooked dumplings on a tray, then bag them.

title: Korean Saengseon Guk White Fish and Daikon Soup
summary: A restorative morning soup of white fish simmered with daikon, sesame oil and egg, light and clean tasting.

items.raw: 400g firm white fish fillets, cut into chunks

steps.text: Stir-fry the daikon in the sesame oil for 3 minutes, until it turns translucent.
Add the water and garlic and simmer for 10 minutes, until the daikon is soft.
Season with the soy sauce and fish sauce.
Add the fish and simmer for 4 minutes, until opaque and flaking.
Beat the eggs and stir them into the soup in a thin stream until set.
Top with the spring onion and pepper.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, and the egg until fully set.
Use any firm white fish.

title: Korean Mandu Dipping Sauce with Vinegar and Gochugaru
summary: A bright, sharp dumpling sauce of soy, rice vinegar, chilli flakes and sesame seeds.

steps.text: Stir the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar and sesame oil until the sugar dissolves.
Add the gochugaru, spring onion, sesame seeds and garlic.
Rest for 5 minutes, then serve with dumplings.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for 5 days.
Serves 2 as a dip.

title: Japanese Oden Simmered Winter Hot Pot
summary: A gentle pot of daikon, boiled eggs, konnyaku and fish cakes simmered in a light dashi, served with hot mustard.

items.raw: 1 daikon, about 400g, cut into thick rounds

steps.text: Hard-boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool and peel them.
Simmer the dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar in a wide pot until the sugar dissolves.
Add the daikon and potatoes and simmer for 25 minutes, until nearly tender.
Add the mushrooms, fish cakes, tofu and eggs and simmer gently for 20 minutes, until everything has taken on the flavour.
Serve in bowls with a little broth and a dab of mustard.

notes: Food safety: boil the eggs until the yolks are fully set and keep the pot hot until serving.
Oden is even better the next day.

title: Japanese Tara Chiri Cod Hot Pot
summary: A light kombu broth hot pot of cod, tofu, napa cabbage and mushrooms, dipped in soy and lemon at the table.

steps.text: Put the water and kombu in a wide pot and heat gently to just below a simmer until small bubbles form, then remove the kombu.
Add the carrot, cabbage stalks and mushrooms and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the cod, tofu, leek and cabbage leaves and simmer for 6 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flaking.
Serve straight from the pot with the soy and lemon dipping sauce and spring onion for dipping.
Finish with the leftover broth and rice if you like.

notes: Food safety: cook the cod until opaque throughout and flaking.
Do not leave the pot sitting warm for hours.

title: Japanese Asari Clam Miso Soup
summary: Sweet little clams opening in a savoury miso broth, finished with spring onion.

items.raw: 800g small clams, purged in salted water

steps.text: Scrub the clams and rinse them well.
Warm the water and kombu in a pot, then discard the kombu just before it boils.
Add the clams and sake and cook over medium heat for 4 minutes, until they open.
Remove from the heat and whisk in the miso, discarding any clams that stay shut.
Top with the spring onion and serve.

notes: Food safety: cook until the clams open and the flesh is opaque, and discard any clams that are open before cooking or that do not open after cooking.
Do not boil the miso, which dulls the flavour.

title: Japanese Gyoza Dipping Sauce with Rayu
summary: A classic gyoza sauce of soy, rice vinegar and chilli oil with a little sesame and ginger.

steps.text: Whisk the soy sauce, vinegar, chilli oil and sesame oil in a small bowl until combined.
Stir in the ginger and spring onion.
Serve alongside pan-fried gyoza.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for 1 week.
Add more rayu for extra heat.

title: Japanese Kimchi Nabe
summary: A fiery kimchi hot pot with pork, tofu, mushrooms and leeks, finished with rice or noodles in the leftover broth.

steps.text: Bring the stock, kimchi, kimchi juice and gochujang to a simmer in a wide pot until bubbling.
Add the pork and cabbage and simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the tofu, mushrooms and soy sauce and simmer for 5 minutes, until the pork is cooked through.
Top with the spring onion and serve with the rice.
Add noodles to the remaining broth to finish.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork until no pink remains and it reaches 70°C.
The kimchi brings plenty of salt, so taste before adding more.

title: Japanese Tamago Tofu Clear Soup
summary: Silky chilled egg tofu cubes set in a delicate hot dashi with mushroom and spring onion.

items.raw: 300ml dashi stock, for the egg tofu

steps.text: Whisk the eggs gently with the 300ml dashi, the 1 tsp mirin and the salt, avoiding bubbles, then strain into a small lined tin.
Cover with foil and steam over simmering water for 18 minutes, until just set, then chill for at least 1 hour.
Simmer the 800ml dashi with the soy sauce, 1 tbsp mirin and mushrooms for 5 minutes.
Cut the egg tofu into cubes and place in bowls.
Ladle the hot soup over and top with spring onion and peel.

notes: Food safety: steam the egg tofu until fully set and keep it chilled until serving.
Serve within 2 days.

title: Thai Tom Yum Goong Prawn Soup
summary: A hot and sour prawn soup with lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaf, mushrooms and a good squeeze of lime.

steps.text: Simmer the stock, lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves and chillies for 8 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and tomatoes and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add the prawns and cook for 3 minutes, until pink and curled.
Stir in the fish sauce, lime juice and chilli jam, then taste and adjust.
Scatter over the coriander and serve at once.

notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until pink and opaque throughout.
Do not eat the lemongrass, galangal or lime leaves.

title: Thai Gaeng Jued Woonsen Glass Noodle Soup
summary: A mild, clear Thai soup of glass noodles, minced pork, tofu and cabbage, gently seasoned with garlic and white pepper.

steps.text: Soak the noodles in hot water for 8 minutes, then drain and cut into shorter lengths.
Bring the stock and garlic to a simmer until bubbling.
Roll the pork into small balls and drop them in, simmering for 5 minutes.
Add the carrot, tofu and cabbage and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the noodles, fish sauce and pepper and simmer for 2 minutes.
Top with the spring onion and coriander.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork balls until they reach 75°C and no pink remains.
Add a splash of soy sauce for more depth.

title: Thai Gaeng Liang Pumpkin and Prawn Soup
summary: A peppery, herbal Thai soup of pumpkin, sweet corn and prawns thickened with a spoon of shrimp paste and shallots.

steps.text: Grind or blend the curry paste, shrimp paste and shallots into a rough paste.
Bring the water to the boil until bubbling and stir in the paste until dissolved.
Add the pumpkin and corn and simmer for 10 minutes, until the pumpkin is tender.
Add the prawns and cook for 3 minutes, until pink.
Stir in the fish sauce, pepper and basil.

notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until pink and opaque throughout.
Add chilli for more heat.

title: Thai Tom Saap Isaan Pork Rib Soup
summary: A sour, spicy Isaan soup of tender pork ribs with lemongrass, galangal, chilli and lime.

items.raw: 800g pork spare ribs, cut into short pieces

steps.text: Boil the ribs in water for 5 minutes, then drain and rinse them.
Return them to the pot with 1.5 litres fresh water, lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves, dried chillies and shallots.
Simmer gently for 1 hour, until the pork is tender.
Season with the fish sauce and lime juice.
Top with the herbs and spring onion.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork until very tender, at least 70°C throughout.
Skim the surface while simmering for a cleaner broth.

title: Thai Gaeng Hed Mushroom Jungle Soup
summary: A clear, fiery northern Thai soup of mixed mushrooms, long beans, lemongrass and Thai basil without coconut milk.

items.raw: 150g long beans, cut into short lengths

steps.text: Simmer the stock, curry paste, lemongrass and lime leaves for 5 minutes.
Add the eggplant and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and beans and simmer for 5 minutes, until tender.
Season with the soy sauce and sugar.
Stir in the basil before serving.

notes: Add chilli slices for extra heat.
Serve with jasmine rice.

title: Lao Or Lam Stew
summary: A herbal Lao pork stew of eggplant, mushrooms and long beans thickened with toasted sticky rice.

steps.text: Simmer the pork, water, lemongrass, shallots and dried chillies for 30 minutes, until the pork is almost tender.
Add the eggplant, mushrooms and beans and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the rice powder and simmer for 5 minutes, until the stew thickens.
Season with the fish sauce and stir in the dill and basil.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork until tender and at least 70°C throughout.
Make the rice powder by toasting sticky rice in a dry pan until golden, then grinding it.

title: Lao Jeow Mak Len Roasted Tomato Dip
summary: A smoky Lao tomato dip of charred tomatoes, chilli, garlic and shallot, pounded into a rustic relish for sticky rice.

steps.text: Roast the tomatoes, garlic, shallots and chillies under a hot grill or in a dry pan for 12 minutes, turning, until blackened in patches.
Peel the garlic and shallots.
Grind the chillies, garlic and shallots into a paste, then add the tomatoes and crush roughly.
Stir in the fish sauce, lime juice, spring onion and coriander.

notes: Serve with sticky rice and raw vegetables.
Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

title: Lao Khao Piak Sen Chicken Noodle Soup
summary: A comforting Lao noodle soup of chewy rice noodles in clear chicken broth with garlic oil and herbs.

steps.text: Simmer the stock, chicken and ginger for 20 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through, then lift out and shred.
Fry the garlic in the oil for 2 minutes, until golden.
Cook the noodles in the stock for 5 minutes, until tender.
Season with the fish sauce.
Serve the noodles and broth with the chicken, garlic oil, spring onion, coriander, chilli and lime.

notes: Rice noodles are best eaten straight away.
Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C throughout and keep the soup hot until serving. Keep any leftover garlic, herb or chilli oil in the fridge and use it within 4 days.

title: Lao Tam Mak Hoong Papaya Salad
summary: Shredded green papaya pounded with chilli, garlic, fermented fish sauce and lime for a funky, fiery Lao salad.

items.raw: 100g long beans, cut into short lengths

steps.text: Crush the garlic and chillies to a rough paste in a mortar.
Add the long beans and bruise lightly.
Add the papaya, tomato, fish sauce, lime juice and palm sugar and toss, crushing gently, until the papaya softens.
Taste and adjust for sour, salty and hot.
Scatter over the peanuts and serve at once.

notes: Serve immediately with sticky rice.
Padaek is very pungent, so use fish sauce if you want it milder.

title: Lao Jeow Bong Chilli Paste
