summary: A sweet-savoury Lao chilli paste of dried chillies, galangal, shallot and garlic, slowly cooked in oil.

steps.text: Soak the chillies in hot water for 10 minutes, then drain.
Dry-fry the shallots, garlic and galangal for 6 minutes, until golden.
Blend the chillies with the shallots, garlic and galangal into a coarse paste.
Fry the paste in the oil for 8 minutes over low heat, until darkened and fragrant.
Stir in the tamarind, sugar, fish sauce and sesame seeds.

notes: Keeps in a clean jar in the fridge for 2 weeks.
Eat with sticky rice and grilled vegetables.

title: Indian Rava Idli with Cashews
summary: Soft steamed semolina cakes with cashews, mustard seed and curry leaf, ready without any fermenting.

steps.text: Heat the oil and fry the mustard seeds, curry leaves, cashews, chilli and ginger for 2 minutes, until the cashews turn golden.
Stir in the semolina and toast for 3 minutes, until fragrant, then cool.
Mix in the yoghurt, water and salt to a thick batter and rest for 10 minutes.
Stir in the bicarbonate of soda and spoon into greased idli moulds.
Steam for 12 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.

notes: Serve hot with coconut chutney and sambar.
Makes about 12 idli.

title: Indian Rava Dosa Crisp Semolina Crepes
summary: Lacy, crisp restaurant-style crepes of semolina, rice flour and plain flour with cumin, pepper and cashews.

steps.text: Whisk the semolina, rice flour, plain flour, yoghurt, water and salt into a very thin batter and rest for 15 minutes.
Stir in the cumin, pepper, chilli, cashews, onion and curry leaves.
Heat a flat pan until very hot and pour the batter from a height in a lacy pattern to cover the pan.
Drizzle with oil and cook for 3 minutes, until the underside is crisp and golden, then fold and serve.

notes: Stir the batter before each dosa as the semolina settles.
Makes about 8 rava dosa.

title: Indian Spinach and Chickpea Flour Pancakes
summary: Quick savoury chickpea-flour pancakes with spinach, onion, green chilli and spices.

steps.text: Whisk the chickpea flour, water, turmeric, cumin, chilli powder and salt into a smooth batter.
Stir in the spinach, onion, chilli and coriander.
Pour a ladleful onto a hot oiled pan and spread into a thin round.
Cook for 2 minutes, until the underside is golden, then flip and cook for 2 minutes, until set and speckled brown.

notes: Serve with mint chutney or yoghurt.
Makes about 8 chilla.

title: Indian Instant Rava Uttapam with Onion and Tomato
summary: Thick, soft semolina and yoghurt pancakes with onion, tomato, chilli and coriander, with no fermenting.

steps.text: Mix the semolina, yoghurt, water and salt and rest for 15 minutes, until thick.
Stir in the bicarbonate of soda.
Pour a ladleful onto a hot oiled pan, spreading into a 12cm round, then scatter over the onion, tomato, chilli and coriander.
Drizzle oil around the edge and cook for 3 minutes, until the underside is golden.
Flip and cook for 2 minutes, until the topping is tender and the centre is cooked through.

notes: Makes about 6 uttapam.
Serve with coconut chutney.

title: Indian Kanda Poha Maharashtrian Flattened Rice
summary: A fluffy, turmeric-yellow breakfast of flattened rice, onion, peanut and curry leaf with lemon and coriander.

steps.text: Rinse the poha in a sieve until just soft, then drain and sprinkle with the salt, sugar and turmeric.
Heat the oil, fry the mustard seeds and peanuts for 2 minutes, until the seeds pop and the peanuts are golden.
Add the curry leaves, chillies, onion and potato and cook for 6 minutes, until the potato is tender.
Fold in the poha and cook for 3 minutes, until heated through.
Finish with the lemon juice and coriander.

notes: Serve with sev and a wedge of lemon.
Do not over-rinse the poha or it turns mushy.

title: Indian Egg Bhurji with Green Chilli
summary: Spiced scrambled eggs with onion, tomato, green chilli and turmeric, scooped up with toast or paratha.

steps.text: Heat the oil and fry the cumin for 30 seconds, until it sizzles.
Add the onion and chilli and cook for 4 minutes, until soft and golden.
Add the tomato, turmeric and garam masala and cook for 3 minutes, until pulpy.
Whisk the eggs with the salt, pour in and stir gently for 3 minutes, until just set.
Scatter over the coriander and serve at once.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until fully set with no runny egg.
Serve with buttered toast or paratha.

title: Indian Lemon Rice with Peanuts
summary: A bright South Indian rice dish tempered with mustard seed, peanut and curry leaf and finished with lemon.

steps.text: Cook the rice, drain and spread out to cool for 10 minutes, until the grains are dry and separate.
Heat the oil and fry the mustard seeds and peanuts for 2 minutes, until the seeds pop and the peanuts are golden.
Add the dried chillies, curry leaves, green chilli and turmeric and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Fold in the rice and salt and heat for 3 minutes, until hot.
Finish with the lemon juice and coriander.

notes: Serve with yoghurt and papad.
Cooked rice should be cooled quickly and not left out for long.

title: Indian Masoor Sambar with Pumpkin and Beans
summary: A tangy South Indian lentil and vegetable stew with tamarind, pumpkin and green beans.

steps.text: Cook the lentils with the water and turmeric for 20 minutes, until completely soft, then mash.
Add the tamarind, beans, pumpkin, tomato, onion, coriander, cumin and chilli powder and simmer for 15 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Heat the oil and fry the mustard seeds, curry leaves and chillies for 1 minute, until the seeds pop.
Pour the tempering into the sambar and stir in the salt.

notes: Serve with idli, dosa or rice.
Thin with hot water if it thickens as it stands.

title: Indian Tomato Rasam
summary: A thin, peppery, sour South Indian soup of tomato, tamarind and garlic with cumin and mustard tempering.

steps.text: Simmer the tomato, tamarind, water, turmeric and salt for 10 minutes, until the tomato is soft.
Mash and add the garlic, 1 tsp cumin and the pepper, then simmer for 5 minutes.
Heat the ghee and fry the mustard seeds, remaining cumin, curry leaves and chillies for 1 minute, until the seeds pop.
Pour the tempering into the rasam and top with the coriander.

notes: Serve in small cups as a soup or over rice.
Do not boil hard after adding the tempering.

title: Indian Gujarati Kadhi
summary: A silky, lightly sweet and sour yoghurt soup thickened with chickpea flour and tempered with cumin and curry leaf.

steps.text: Whisk the yoghurt, chickpea flour and water until smooth.
Pour into a pot with the ginger, chillies, sugar, salt and turmeric and simmer over low heat for 15 minutes, stirring, until it thickens slightly.
Heat the ghee and fry the cumin, mustard seeds, curry leaves and dried chillies for 1 minute, until the seeds pop.
Pour the tempering over the kadhi.

notes: Stir constantly at first so the yoghurt does not split.
Serve with steamed rice and khichdi.

title: Indian Dhokla Steamed Chickpea Cake
summary: A light, springy, tangy Gujarati steamed cake of chickpea flour, with a mustard and sesame tempering.

steps.text: Whisk the chickpea flour, yoghurt and water into a smooth batter, then stir in the ginger, chilli, turmeric, salt and sugar and rest for 10 minutes.
Pour into a greased 20cm tin and stir in the fruit salt just before steaming.
Steam for 18 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Heat the oil and fry the mustard seeds, curry leaves and sesame for 1 minute, until the seeds pop.
Pour over the dhokla, cut into squares and top with coriander.

notes: Serve warm with green chutney.
Steam as soon as the fruit salt goes in.

title: Indian Thepla Fenugreek Flatbread
summary: Soft Gujarati flatbreads of wholemeal flour, fresh fenugreek and yoghurt that keep well for travelling.

steps.text: Mix the flour, fenugreek, yoghurt, spices, sugar, salt and 1 tbsp oil.
Add the water bit by bit and knead for 5 minutes into a soft dough, then rest it for 15 minutes.
Divide into 10 balls and roll each into a thin round.
Cook each on a hot pan for 1 minute per side, brushing with the rest of the oil, until brown spots appear.

notes: Serve with pickle and yoghurt.
Keep in a covered container for up to 2 days.

title: Indian Aloo Paratha Breakfast
summary: Wholemeal flatbreads stuffed with spiced mashed potato and pan-fried in ghee until golden.

steps.text: Knead the flour, water and a pinch of salt into a soft dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Mix the potato, chilli, cumin, garam masala, chilli powder, coriander and the rest of the salt.
Roll a ball of dough into a small round, add 2 tbsp filling, seal like a purse and roll out gently.
Cook on a hot pan for 2 minutes per side with a little ghee, until golden with brown spots.

notes: Serve with yoghurt, butter and pickle.
Makes 6 parathas.

title: Indian Semiya Upma Vermicelli Breakfast
summary: A quick South Indian breakfast of toasted vermicelli with mustard seed, onion, peas and curry leaf.

items.raw: 250g rice vermicelli, broken into short lengths

steps.text: Dry-roast the vermicelli in a pan for 4 minutes, until lightly golden, then set aside.
Heat the oil and fry the mustard seeds, curry leaves and cashews for 2 minutes, until the seeds pop.
Add the onion, chilli and carrot and cook for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the water, peas and salt, bring to the boil until bubbling, then stir in the vermicelli.
Cover and cook for 4 minutes, until the vermicelli is tender and the water is absorbed.
Finish with the lemon juice.

notes: Serve with coconut chutney.
Do not over-stir or the vermicelli turns sticky.

title: Indian Bisi Bele Bath
summary: Karnataka's spiced rice and lentil one-pot with vegetables, tamarind and a ghee tempering.

steps.text: Cook the rice, dal, turmeric and water for 20 minutes, until both are very soft and mushy.
Add the beans, carrot, peas, tamarind, spice powder and salt and simmer for 12 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Heat the ghee and fry the mustard seeds, curry leaves, chillies and cashews for 2 minutes, until the cashews are golden.
Stir the tempering into the rice and loosen with hot water to a porridge-like consistency.

notes: Serve with boondi, papad and yoghurt.
Thin with hot water if it thickens.

title: Indian Tomato Onion Chutney
summary: A tangy, spicy South Indian chutney of slow-cooked tomato and onion with tamarind and chilli, ideal with dosa.

steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil and fry the mustard seeds and curry leaves for 1 minute, until the seeds pop, then set aside.
Fry the onion, chillies and garlic in the rest of the oil for 6 minutes, until golden.
Add the tomato, tamarind and salt and cook for 8 minutes, until pulpy and the oil separates.
Blend to a coarse chutney and stir in the tempering.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for 4 days.
Serve with idli, dosa or uttapam.

title: Sri Lankan Appam Hoppers
summary: Lacy, bowl-shaped fermented rice and coconut pancakes with a soft centre and crisp edge.

steps.text: Mix the yeast, sugar and 100ml warm water and leave for 10 minutes, until frothy.
Mix with the rice flour, coconut milk, remaining water and salt to a thin batter and rest for 4 hours, until bubbly.
Heat a small hopper pan, grease with a little oil and pour in a ladleful of batter, then swirl to coat the sides.
Cover and cook for 3 minutes over medium heat, until the edges are crisp and the centre is set.

notes: Makes about 8 hoppers.
Serve with pol sambol or a curry.

title: Sri Lankan String Hoppers
summary: Steamed nests of fine rice-flour noodles, served with coconut sambol and dhal.

steps.text: Mix the rice flour and salt, then add the boiling water bit by bit and knead into a soft, smooth dough.
Brush a string hopper press or large piping bag with oil and fill it with dough.
Press out spirals onto oiled trays or mats.
Steam for 8 minutes, until firm and cooked through.

notes: Serve with dhal, coconut sambol and fish curry.
Makes about 20 string hoppers.

title: Sri Lankan Lunu Miris Chilli and Onion Sambol
summary: A fiery red onion, chilli and lime pounded paste, traditionally eaten with hoppers and roti.

steps.text: Crush the chilli flakes, salt and sugar with a little onion in a mortar to a paste.
Add the rest of the onion and the lime juice and crush lightly.
Crush until the mixture is moist and well combined, then adjust the salt and lime.

notes: Eat the same day.
Serve with hoppers or roti.

title: Sri Lankan Kiri Bath Milk Rice
summary: Creamy coconut milk rice cut into diamonds, a festive Sri Lankan breakfast served with lunu miris.

steps.text: Rinse the rice and cook with the water and salt for 15 minutes, until the water is absorbed.
Stir in the coconut milk and cook gently for 10 minutes, until the mixture is thick and creamy.
Press into a greased tray and smooth the top.
Cool for 15 minutes, then cut into diamonds.

notes: Serve with lunu miris or katta sambol.
Eat the same day.

title: Sri Lankan Pittu Steamed Rice and Coconut
summary: Cylinders of steamed rice flour and fresh coconut, crumbly and soft, served with coconut milk and sambol.

items.raw: 100g desiccated coconut, soaked in 3 tbsp warm water

steps.text: Dry-roast the rice flour in a pan for 5 minutes, until fragrant and no longer raw-smelling, then cool.
Mix with the salt and water, rubbing between your fingers until it forms damp crumbs that hold when squeezed.
Layer the crumbs with coconut in a pittu steamer or tall tin.
Steam for 10 minutes, until steam rises through the top layer.

notes: Serve with coconut milk gravy and pol sambol.
Do not add too much water or the pittu turns gummy.

title: Sri Lankan Mallung Greens with Coconut
summary: Finely shredded greens quickly stir-fried with fresh coconut, onion, turmeric and green chilli.

steps.text: Heat the oil and fry the onion, chillies and curry leaves for 3 minutes, until soft and golden.
Add the turmeric and silverbeet and cook for 3 minutes, until wilted.
Stir in the coconut and salt and cook for 2 minutes, until tender.
Finish with the lime juice.

notes: Serve with rice and curry.
Swap in kale or spinach.

title: Mexican Huevos a la Mexicana
summary: Scrambled eggs with tomato, onion, jalapeno and coriander in the colours of the Mexican flag.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs with the salt.
Fry the onion and jalapeno in the oil for 3 minutes, until soft.
Add the tomato and cook for 3 minutes, until the juices reduce.
Pour in the eggs and stir gently for 3 minutes, until just set.
Top with the coriander and serve with warm tortillas.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until fully set with no runny egg.
Serve with refried beans.

title: Mexican Molletes
summary: Open bolillo rolls spread with refried beans, topped with melted cheese and fresh pico de gallo.

items.raw: 250g tinned black beans, drained and mashed

steps.text: Toast the roll halves under the grill for 2 minutes, until lightly golden.
Spread each with the mashed beans and top with the cheese.
Grill for 4 minutes, until the cheese melts and bubbles.
Mix the tomato, onion, jalapeno, coriander, lime juice and salt and spoon over the molletes.

notes: Serve straight away.
Add sliced avocado if you like.

title: Mexican Sopa de Fideo Toasted Noodle Soup
summary: Thin noodles toasted golden, then simmered in a smoky tomato and garlic broth until soft and comforting.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pot and fry the broken noodles for 4 minutes, stirring, until deep golden.
Blend the tomatoes, garlic, onion and chipotle until smooth.
Pour the sauce over the noodles and cook for 3 minutes, until it darkens and thickens.
Add the stock, oregano and salt, bring to the boil, then simmer for 8 minutes, until the noodles are tender.
Ladle into bowls and top with avocado and a squeeze of lime.

notes: The noodles keep absorbing broth, so add a splash of water when reheating.
Toast the noodles evenly, as pale pieces taste floury.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Mexican Caldo de Pollo Chicken and Vegetable Soup
summary: A clear, golden home-style chicken soup with corn, carrot, zucchini and potato, served with rice, coriander and lime.

steps.text: Put the chicken, water, onion, garlic and salt in a large pot and bring to a gentle boil, until the surface just trembles.
Simmer for 20 minutes, skimming any foam, until the chicken is almost cooked through.
Add the carrots, potatoes, corn and oregano and simmer for 12 minutes.
Add the zucchini and cook for 8 minutes, until all the vegetables are tender and the chicken is cooked to 75C in the thickest part.
Serve with a scoop of rice, coriander and lime.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until the juices run clear and the centre reaches 75°C. Wash hands and boards after handling raw chicken, and chill leftovers within 2 hours.
Remove the chicken skin before serving for a lighter soup.

title: Mexican Guajillo Tortilla Breakfast with Fried Egg
summary: Crisp tortilla triangles tossed in a smoky red chilli sauce, topped with a runny egg, crema, onion and queso fresco.

steps.text: Soak the guajillo chillies in hot water for 10 minutes, then drain and blend with the tomatoes, garlic, onion, water and salt until smooth.
Fry the tortilla wedges in 3 tbsp oil in batches for 3 minutes, until crisp and golden, and drain on paper.
Simmer the sauce in the same pan for 5 minutes, until slightly thick.
Fold in the tortilla wedges for 1 minute, so they soften at the edges but keep some crunch.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil until the whites are set, then top the chilaquiles with eggs, sour cream, cheese, onion and coriander.

notes: Food safety: eggs are cooked until the whites are fully set; cook the yolks through for pregnant women, older people and young children.
Serve at once, as the chips soften quickly.

title: Mexican Chilaquiles Verdes with Shredded Chicken
summary: Crisp tortilla chips in a tangy green tomato and chilli sauce with shredded chicken and soft cheese.

steps.text: Simmer the chicken in the stock for 15 minutes, until cooked through with no pink inside, then shred it and keep the stock.
Boil the green tomatoes, chillies and garlic in water for 8 minutes, until soft, then blend with the onion, coriander and salt.
Fry the tortilla wedges in oil in batches for 3 minutes, until crisp, and drain.
Simmer the green sauce with 100ml of the chicken stock for 5 minutes in a wide pan.
Fold in the chips and chicken for 1 minute, then serve topped with cheese, sour cream and avocado.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken until it reaches 75°C and the juices run clear, wash hands and boards after handling it, and chill leftovers within 2 hours.
Keep extra stock to loosen the sauce if it thickens too much.

title: Mexican Lime Chicken Soup with Fried Tortilla Strips
summary: A Yucatecan-style soup of shredded chicken in a fragrant lime broth, finished with crisp tortilla strips and avocado.

steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pot and cook the onion, garlic and capsicum for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the tomatoes, oregano and cumin and cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in the stock, add the chicken and salt, and simmer for 18 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
Lift out the chicken, shred it, and return it to the pot with the lime juice and lime slices.
Fry the tortilla strips in the remaining oil for 2 minutes until crisp, and serve the soup topped with strips, avocado and coriander.

notes: Food safety: simmer chicken until the centre reaches 75°C and no pink remains; chill leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until steaming hot.
Add the lime juice at the end so the broth stays fresh and not bitter.

title: Mexican Crema de Poblano Creamy Roast Chilli Soup
summary: Charred poblano chillies blended with potato, corn and cream into a velvety, mildly spicy soup.

steps.text: Char the poblanos over a gas flame or under a hot grill for 10 minutes, turning, until blackened, then cover for 10 minutes to steam, peel and remove the seeds.
Melt the butter in a pot and cook the onion and garlic for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the potato, stock and salt and simmer for 12 minutes, until the potato is tender.
Blend with the poblanos and half the corn until silky, then stir in the cream and heat gently.
Serve with the remaining corn, a dollop of sour cream and coriander.

notes: Do not rinse the charred chillies under water, as it washes away the smoky flavour.
The soup thickens as it cools, so loosen with stock.

title: German Kartoffelsalat Swabian Warm Potato Salad
summary: Warm waxy potatoes dressed in a tangy broth, vinegar and mustard dressing with onion, in the south German style.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes whole in salted water for 18 minutes, until a knife slides in easily, then drain and peel while hot.
Slice the warm potatoes into thin rounds in a large bowl.
Whisk the hot stock with the vinegar, mustard, oil, salt and pepper, and stir in the onion.
Pour over the potatoes and fold gently, then rest for 10 minutes so they soak up the dressing.
Fold in the chives and pickles just before serving.

notes: Dress the potatoes while warm, as cooled ones will not absorb the dressing.
It is lovely at room temperature and keeps for 2 days in the fridge.

title: Greek Patatosalata Lemon and Oregano Potato Salad
summary: Tender potatoes with spring onion, parsley, capers and olives, dressed with olive oil, lemon and dried oregano.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 12 minutes, until just tender, then drain well.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice, oregano, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Toss the warm potatoes in the dressing so they absorb it.
Fold in the spring onions, parsley, capers and olives.
Rest for 10 minutes, then taste and add more lemon if needed.

notes: Serve with grilled fish or as part of a meze table.
Keep for up to 2 days in the fridge and bring to room temperature before serving.

title: French Salade de Pommes de Terre Dijon Potato Salad
summary: Warm new potatoes tossed in white wine, Dijon vinaigrette with shallot, tarragon and cornichons.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes, until tender, then drain and halve while still warm.
Sprinkle the wine over the hot potatoes and leave for 5 minutes to soak in.
Whisk the vinegar, mustard, oil, salt and pepper into a vinaigrette.
Toss the potatoes with the vinaigrette, shallots and cornichons.
Fold through the herbs before serving.

notes: Dress the potatoes warm for the best flavour.
Serve with roast chicken or a poached egg for lunch.

title: Portuguese Salada de Batata Potato, Egg and Olive Salad
summary: Chunky boiled potatoes with hard-boiled egg, onion, parsley and olives in a garlicky olive oil and vinegar dressing.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 12 minutes, until tender, and drain.
Boil the eggs in a separate pan for 9 minutes until hard-set, cool in cold water, peel and quarter.
Whisk the oil, vinegar, garlic and salt together.
Toss the warm potatoes with the dressing and onion.
Fold in the parsley, olives and eggs gently so the yolks stay intact.

notes: Food safety: boil the eggs for at least 9 minutes until the yolk is fully set, and keep the salad chilled; eat within 2 days.
Soak the sliced onion in cold water for 5 minutes for a milder bite.

title: Peruvian Ensalada Rusa Potato and Beetroot Salad
summary: A creamy, ruby-pink Peruvian-style potato salad with beetroot, carrot, peas and mayonnaise.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes and carrots in salted water for 10 minutes, add the peas for 2 minutes, then drain and cool.
Boil the eggs for 9 minutes until hard-set, cool, peel and chop.
Mix the mayonnaise, yoghurt, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Fold the cooled potatoes, carrots, peas and eggs into the dressing.
Gently add the beetroot last so the colour does not bleed too much, then top with parsley.

notes: Food safety: boil the eggs until the yolks are fully set, keep the salad refrigerated, and eat within 2 days.
Cool the potatoes completely before adding the mayonnaise.

title: Chinese Shredded Ginger Soy Vinegar Dip
summary: A sharp, savoury dip of Chinkiang black vinegar, soy and fresh ginger threads for any dumpling.

steps.text: Stir the sugar into the vinegar and soy sauce until it dissolves.
Add the ginger, garlic, sesame oil and chilli oil.
Rest for 5 minutes, then serve in small dishes alongside the dumplings.

notes: Rest is optional, but the ginger mellows the vinegar.
Keeps for 3 days in a jar in the fridge.

title: Nepali Jhol Achar Sesame and Tomato Dumpling Sauce
summary: The thin, tangy sesame and roast tomato sauce served with momo, spiced with pepper, cumin and coriander.

steps.text: Roast the tomatoes and chillies under a hot grill for 10 minutes, turning, until blistered and soft.
Toast the sesame seeds and peanuts in a dry pan for 3 minutes, until golden.
Blend the tomatoes, chillies, sesame, peanuts, garlic, ginger, cumin and pepper with the water into a loose sauce.
Heat the oil in a small pan and cook the sauce for 3 minutes, then stir in the lemon juice, salt and coriander.
Serve warm or cool with dumplings.

notes: Thin with water until it pours like a light soup, as the sauce is meant to be runny.
Keeps for 4 days in the fridge.

title: Ethiopian Spiced Butter Bean Breakfast Mash
summary: Mashed butter beans simmered with garlic, cumin and chilli, finished with olive oil, tomato and green chilli.

steps.text: Warm 1 tbsp oil in a pot and cook the garlic and chilli flakes for 1 minute.
Add the beans, cumin, salt and 100ml water and simmer for 8 minutes, until hot and soft.
Mash roughly with a fork, leaving some beans whole.
Stir in the lemon juice and spoon into bowls.
Top with tomato, onion, green chilli and the remaining oil, and serve with bread.

notes: Serve with a hard-boiled egg on the side if you like.
Drain and rinse the beans to cut the tinned flavour.

title: Ethiopian Chechebsa Spiced Flatbread Scramble
summary: Torn flatbread fried in spiced clarified butter until crisp at the edges, served with honey or yoghurt.

steps.text: Melt the ghee in a wide pan over medium heat and stir in the paprika, cayenne, cardamom, ginger and salt for 1 minute.
Add the torn flatbread and toss to coat evenly.
Fry for 8 minutes, stirring, until the pieces are crisp at the edges and chewy in the middle.
Serve warm with yoghurt and a drizzle of honey for dipping.

notes: Use less cayenne for a milder version.
Eat straight away while it is still crisp.

title: Ethiopian Enkulal Firfir Spiced Egg Scramble
summary: Soft eggs scrambled with tomato, onion, green chilli and spiced butter, a classic Ethiopian morning plate.

steps.text: Melt the ghee in a pan and cook the onion and chilli for 4 minutes, until soft.
Add the tomato and turmeric and cook for 2 minutes.
Beat the eggs with the salt, pour into the pan and stir gently for 2 to 3 minutes until just set.
Scatter with coriander and serve with the bread.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until firm with no liquid egg left, particularly for pregnant women, older people and young children.
Add a pinch of cayenne for more heat.

title: Ethiopian Kinche Spiced Cracked Wheat Porridge
summary: Cracked wheat simmered until tender then finished with spiced butter, a savoury or sweet Ethiopian breakfast.

steps.text: Bring the water and salt to the boil, until bubbling, and stir in the bulgur.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft and thick.
Melt the ghee with the cardamom, cumin and pepper in a small pan for 1 minute.
Spoon the porridge into bowls, pour over the spiced ghee and top with yoghurt.

notes: Add a spoon of honey for a sweet version.
Add more water if the porridge thickens as it stands.

title: Argentinian Salsa Criolla Onion, Tomato and Pepper Relish
summary: A fresh relish of red onion, tomato and capsicum in vinegar and oil, served with grilled meats and choripan.

steps.text: Mix the onion, tomato, capsicum, garlic and parsley in a bowl.
Whisk the vinegar, oil, oregano and salt, and pour over.
Stir and rest for 20 minutes, until the onion softens and the juices pool.

notes: Spoon over grilled meat or bread.
Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

title: Peruvian Salsa Huancaina Creamy Yellow Chilli Cheese Sauce
summary: A silky, mildly spicy sauce of aji amarillo and fresh cheese, served over boiled potatoes and egg.

steps.text: Blend the aji amarillo, queso fresco, crackers, evaporated milk, oil, garlic and salt until smooth and thick.
Taste and add salt or a splash of milk to loosen.
Arrange the sliced potatoes on a plate and spoon over the sauce.
Garnish with halved hard-boiled eggs and olives.

notes: Food safety: boil the eggs for at least 9 minutes until fully set, and keep the sauce chilled; eat within 2 days.
The sauce also suits pasta or grilled chicken.

title: Peruvian Aji Verde Green Chilli and Coriander Sauce
summary: The bright green sauce served with roast chicken, made with jalapeno, coriander, lime and mayonnaise.

steps.text: Blend all the ingredients until smooth and pale green.
Taste and add more lime or salt as needed.
Chill for 20 minutes before serving.

notes: Serve with roast chicken, grilled vegetables or chips.
Keeps for 4 days in the fridge.

title: Italian Pearl Barley Salad with Roast Tomatoes and Rocket
summary: Nutty pearl barley tossed with sweet roast cherry tomatoes, rocket, olives and a lemon dressing.

steps.text: Roast the tomatoes with 1 tbsp oil and a pinch of salt at 200C for 20 minutes, until collapsing.
Boil the barley in salted water for 25 minutes, until chewy, and drain.
Whisk the remaining oil, lemon juice, garlic, salt and pepper.
Toss the warm barley with the dressing.
Fold in the tomatoes, rocket, olives and basil.

notes: Add crumbled feta for a salty finish.
Keeps for 2 days in the fridge, without the rocket.

title: Italian Insalata di Orzo with Lemon, Peas and Mint
summary: Pasta shaped like rice tossed with peas, lemon, mint and olive oil for a light summer lunch.

steps.text: Boil the orzo in salted water for 8 minutes, adding the peas for the last 2 minutes, then drain and rinse briefly.
Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan for 3 minutes, until golden.
Whisk the oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Toss the warm orzo and peas with the dressing.
Fold in the mint, parsley, spring onions and pine nuts.

notes: Serve cool or at room temperature.
Add flaked tuna or cooked chicken for a main meal.

title: Lebanese Sumac Bulgur Salad with Walnuts
summary: Nutty bulgur with pomegranate seeds, parsley, mint and walnuts in a sumac and lemon dressing.

steps.text: Simmer the bulgur in salted water for 12 minutes, until tender but chewy, then drain.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice, sumac and salt.
Toss the warm bulgur with the dressing and leave to cool for 10 minutes.
Fold in the herbs, onion, walnuts and pomegranate seeds.

notes: Serve with grilled lamb or chicken, or as part of a mezze spread.
Add the pomegranate just before serving to keep it fresh.

title: Mustard Seed Honey Vinaigrette
summary: A glossy, sweet-sharp salad dressing of wholegrain mustard, honey and cider vinegar that keeps for a week.

steps.text: Whisk the mustard, honey, vinegar, salt and pepper in a bowl until smooth.
Pour the oil in a thin stream, whisking until the dressing is thick and glossy.
Stir in the shallot and taste, adding more honey or vinegar until balanced.

notes: Shake in a jar to emulsify again before using.
Keeps for 7 days in the fridge.

title: Miso Sesame Dressing
summary: A creamy, savoury-sweet dressing of white miso, toasted sesame and rice vinegar for cabbage, greens and noodles.

steps.text: Whisk the miso, tahini, rice vinegar, soy sauce, mirin, sesame oil and ginger in a bowl.
Add the water a spoon at a time, whisking until the dressing is smooth and pourable.
Stir in the sesame seeds and taste.

notes: Thin with more water for noodles or leave thicker as a dip.
Keeps for 5 days in a jar in the fridge.

title: Green Goddess Dressing
summary: A thick herb dressing of yoghurt, avocado, parsley, chives and lemon that turns any salad into a feast.

steps.text: Blend the avocado, yoghurt, mayonnaise, herbs, garlic, lemon juice, vinegar and salt until smooth.
Add the water and blend again until the dressing is creamy and pourable.
Taste and add more lemon or salt.

notes: Pour over cos lettuce, boiled eggs or roast vegetables.
Keeps for 2 days in a jar in the fridge.

title: Japanese Style Ginger Carrot Dressing
summary: The orange, zingy dressing from the sushi bar, blended from carrot, fresh ginger and rice vinegar.

steps.text: Blend the carrots, onion, vinegar, soy sauce, ginger, honey, oils and water until smooth.
Taste, adding more vinegar or honey until bright and balanced.
Pour into a jar and chill.

notes: Spoon over iceberg lettuce or cabbage.
Keeps for 5 days in the fridge.

title: Buttermilk Ranch Dressing
summary: A cool and creamy herb dressing for crunchy salads, wings and raw vegetable platters.

steps.text: Whisk the buttermilk, sour cream and mayonnaise in a bowl until smooth.
Stir in the garlic, herbs, onion powder, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Taste, then chill for 30 minutes so the flavour deepens.

notes: Thin with a little more buttermilk for a pourable dressing.
Keeps for 4 days in the fridge.

title: Thai Sweet Chilli Lime Dressing
summary: A sticky, tangy dressing of sweet chilli, lime and fish sauce for noodle salads and grilled meats.

steps.text: Warm the lime juice, sugar and fish sauce in a small pan for 2 minutes, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Remove from the heat and stir in the sweet chilli sauce, vinegar, garlic and chilli.
Cool, then whisk in the oil.

notes: Toss through cucumber and herb salads or noodles.
Keeps for 7 days in the fridge.

title: Vietnamese Sweet Lime Fish Sauce Dressing
summary: The balanced sweet, sour, salty and spicy sauce for spring rolls, vermicelli bowls and grilled pork.

items.raw: 2 red bird's eye chillies, finely chopped

steps.text: Stir the sugar into the warm water until it dissolves.
Add the fish sauce and lime juice and stir.
Taste and adjust, adding more lime for sour or sugar for sweet, then add the garlic, chilli and carrot.
Leave to infuse for 10 minutes before serving.

notes: Taste it on a piece of cucumber to check the balance.
Keeps for 5 days in a jar in the fridge.

title: Greek Lemon and Oregano Vinaigrette
summary: The dressing for a horiatiki salad and grilled fish, with lemon, dried oregano and plenty of extra virgin olive oil.

steps.text: Whisk the lemon juice, mustard, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper in a bowl.
Whisk in the oil in a thin stream until thick and emulsified.
Taste and adjust the lemon.

notes: Also good over roast potatoes and grilled chicken.
Keeps for 5 days in the fridge.

title: Italian Balsamic Shallot Vinaigrette
summary: A rounded, slightly sweet vinaigrette of aged balsamic, sharp shallot and Dijon for bitter leaves.

steps.text: Combine the shallot, vinegar, mustard, honey, salt and pepper in a bowl and stir.
Slowly whisk in the oil until thick and glossy.
Taste, then use straight away or store.

notes: Leave the shallot in the vinegar for 5 minutes first to soften its bite.
Keeps for 7 days in the fridge.

title: Mexican Quick Pickled Red Onions
summary: Pink, tangy onion rings in a lime and vinegar brine that lift tacos, eggs and rice bowls in half an hour.

steps.text: Pack the onions into a clean jar.
Simmer the vinegar, water, sugar, salt, oregano and garlic for 2 minutes, until the sugar and salt dissolve.
Pour the hot brine over the onions with the lime juice and press down until submerged.
Cool for 30 minutes, then chill.

notes: Ready to eat in 30 minutes, best after a day.
Keeps for 2 weeks in the fridge.

title: Japanese Asazuke Quick Pickled Cucumber
summary: Lightly salted cucumber with ginger and seasoning, crisp and fresh in under an hour.

steps.text: Rub the cucumber slices with the salt in a bowl and leave for 15 minutes, until they release water.
Squeeze out the liquid with your hands.
Toss with the vinegar, soy sauce, ginger and chilli.
Chill for 20 minutes and sprinkle with sesame seeds to serve.

notes: Serve with steamed rice and miso soup.
Eat within 2 days for the best crunch.

title: Vietnamese Pickled Daikon and Carrot Sticks for Banh Mi
summary: Sweet, sour and crunchy matchsticks for banh mi, noodle bowls and rice plates.

steps.text: Toss the carrot and daikon with the salt and 1 tbsp sugar, and leave for 10 minutes, until slightly softened.
Rinse the vegetables well and squeeze them dry.
Stir the remaining sugar into the warm water and vinegar until dissolved.
Pack the vegetables into a jar and pour over the brine until covered.
Chill for 1 hour before using.

notes: Keeps for 2 weeks in the fridge.
The jar smells strong at first, but the smell fades.

title: Indian Quick Pickled Carrot and Green Chilli
summary: Tangy carrot batons with mustard seed and turmeric, for curries and rice.

steps.text: Heat the oil and fry the mustard seeds for 30 seconds, until they pop.
Add the turmeric, chilli flakes, vinegar, sugar and salt and bring to a simmer for 2 minutes until the sugar dissolves.
Pour the hot brine over the carrots and chillies in a jar and press to submerge.
Cool, then chill for at least 2 hours.

notes: Keeps for 2 weeks in the fridge.
Add a few lime wedges for extra tang.

title: Middle Eastern Quick Pickled Radish and Beetroot
summary: Bright pink wedges of radish and beetroot for falafel, shawarma and mezze.

items.raw: 1 raw beetroot, cut in thin wedges

steps.text: Pack the radish and beetroot into a clean jar with the garlic and bay leaf.
Simmer the water, vinegar and salt for 3 minutes, until the salt dissolves.
Pour the hot brine over the vegetables, leaving them fully covered.
Cool, then chill for 2 days, until pink all through.

notes: Keeps for 3 weeks in the fridge.
Wear gloves to avoid pink hands.

title: Korean Quick Pickled Radish Slices
summary: Crisp and sweet pickled radish slices that cut through fried chicken and rich barbecue meat.

steps.text: Pack the radish rounds into a jar.
Heat the vinegar, sugar, water, salt and peppercorns for 2 minutes, until the sugar dissolves.
Pour the hot brine over the radish and cool.
Chill for 2 hours before serving.

notes: Add a few drops of yellow food colouring if you like it bright.
Keeps for 2 weeks in the fridge.

title: Quick Pickled Jalapenos
summary: Crunchy, fiery rings to pile on nachos, burgers and tacos.

steps.text: Pack the jalapeno rings into a jar with the garlic and cumin seeds.
Simmer the vinegar, water, sugar and salt for 2 minutes, until dissolved.
Pour the hot brine over the chillies until covered.
Cool, then chill for 1 day.

notes: Wear gloves when slicing the chillies.
Keeps for 1 month in the fridge.

title: Quick Pickled Celery and Orange
summary: Crisp celery slices and orange peel in a sweet vinegar brine, lovely with fish, ham and salads.

steps.text: Pack the celery into a jar with the orange zest.
Warm the orange juice, vinegar, water, sugar, salt and fennel seeds for 2 minutes, until dissolved.
Pour the warm brine over the celery until covered.
Cool, then chill for 1 hour.

notes: Eat within 5 days.
Spoon onto grilled fish or ham sandwiches.

title: Swedish Dill Pickled Cucumber Slices
summary: Paper-thin cucumber slices in a sweet vinegar brine with dill, a Swedish table staple for meatballs and salmon.

steps.text: Whisk the vinegar, sugar, water, salt and pepper until the sugar dissolves.
Layer the cucumber and dill in a bowl.
Pour over the brine and press down until submerged.
Chill for 1 hour and drain before serving.

notes: Slice thinly with a mandoline.
Keeps for 4 days in the fridge.

title: Mexican Eggs Under Red and Green Salsa with Beans
summary: Two fried eggs "divorced" by a line of refried beans, one under red salsa and one under green salsa.

items.raw: 200g tinned black beans, mashed and warmed

steps.text: Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 30 seconds each, until soft and flecked, and keep warm.
Fry the eggs in the oil for 3 minutes until the whites are set and the edges crisp.
Place 2 tortillas on each plate and top each with an egg.
Spoon red salsa over one egg and green over the other, with a line of warm beans between.
Scatter with cheese, onion and coriander.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set and the yolks thickened, especially for pregnant women, older people and young children.
Use your favourite jarred salsas to save time.

title: Mexican Sopa de Frijol Black Bean Soup
summary: A smoky, thick black bean soup with cumin and chipotle, topped with sour cream, coriander and lime.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a pot and cook the onion for 6 minutes, until soft and golden.
Add the garlic, cumin and paprika and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the beans, chipotle, stock, tomatoes and salt and simmer for 20 minutes, until thick.
Blend half the soup until smooth and stir back in.
Serve with sour cream, coriander and lime.

notes: Blend more for a smoother soup.
Keeps for 4 days in the fridge and freezes well.

title: Mexican Albondigas Soup Meatball Vegetable Soup
summary: Tender beef and rice meatballs poached in a tomato broth with carrot, zucchini and potato.

steps.text: Mix the beef, rice, egg, oregano, cumin, 1 tsp salt, half the garlic and the mint, and roll into 24 small balls.
Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion and remaining garlic for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the tomatoes, stock, carrots, potato and remaining salt and bring to a simmer, until bubbling gently.
Drop in the meatballs and simmer for 20 minutes, until the meatballs are cooked through and the potato is tender.
Add the zucchini for the last 5 minutes and serve with coriander.

notes: Food safety: cook the meatballs until the centre reaches 75°C with no pink inside, wash hands after handling raw mince, and chill leftovers within 2 hours.
Do not stir for the first 5 minutes, so the meatballs set.

title: Australian Corn Fritters with Avocado and Tomato
summary: Golden corn fritters with smashed avocado, tomato and a squeeze of lime, a cafe brunch classic.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder, eggs, milk, salt and paprika into a thick batter.
Fold in the corn, spring onions and coriander.
Heat the oil in a frying pan and fry spoonfuls of the batter for 3 minutes each side, until golden and cooked through.
Mash the avocados with the lime juice and a pinch of salt.
Serve the fritters with avocado and tomato slices.

notes: Food safety: make sure the fritters are cooked through, as raw egg batter is unsafe; keep egg dishes chilled and eat within 2 days.
Keep warm in a 100C oven while frying the rest.

title: Scottish Creamy Leek, Potato and Fish Soup
summary: A creamy soup of poached cod, potato and leek with a pinch of smoked paprika.

steps.text: Poach the cod in the milk with the bay leaf for 8 minutes, until it flakes easily, then lift out, flake and discard the skin and bones.
Melt the butter in a pot and cook the leek and onion for 6 minutes, until soft.
Add the potatoes and fish stock and simmer for 12 minutes, until the potato is tender.
Pour in the poaching milk and mash roughly with a fork to thicken.
Return the fish with the cream and 1/2 tsp smoked paprika and heat for 3 minutes without boiling, then add pepper and parsley.

notes: Food safety: cook fish until it flakes easily and is opaque all through, chill leftovers within 2 hours, and eat within 2 days.
Add a pinch of salt at the end if needed.

title: American Corn Chowder Potato and Sweet Corn
summary: A thick, creamy chowder of sweet corn, potato and capsicum with a hint of smoked paprika.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a pot and cook the onion, celery and capsicum for 6 minutes, until soft.
Add the potatoes, half the corn, the stock, paprika and salt and simmer for 15 minutes, until the potato is tender.
Blend half the soup until smooth and return it to the pot.
Add the milk, cream and remaining corn and heat for 5 minutes, until hot.
Season with pepper and serve with chives.

notes: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge; reheat gently.
Use evaporated milk for a lighter chowder.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Creamy Caesar Dressing
summary: A thick, garlicky Caesar dressing with anchovy, lemon and parmesan, ready in five minutes.

steps.text: Mash the anchovies and garlic together into a paste in a bowl.
Whisk in the mayonnaise, lemon juice, mustard and worcestershire sauce until smooth.
Stir in the parmesan, then loosen with the water and season with pepper.
Chill for at least 15 minutes before tossing through cos lettuce.

notes: Keeps for 4 days in the fridge.
Also good as a dip for crisp raw vegetables.

title: Blue Cheese Dip for Wings
summary: A cool, tangy blue cheese dip to cut through spicy chicken wings and celery sticks.

steps.text: Mash half the blue cheese with the sour cream and mayonnaise until mostly smooth.
Stir in the buttermilk, lemon juice, garlic and chives.
Fold through the remaining blue cheese so there are chunks, then season with pepper.
Chill for 20 minutes to let the flavours settle.

notes: Thin with a little extra buttermilk for a dressing.
Keeps for 4 days in the fridge.

title: Thousand Island Dressing
summary: A pink, creamy dressing with pickles and tomato sauce for burgers, slaw and salad.

steps.text: Combine the mayonnaise and tomato sauce in a bowl until evenly pink.
Stir in the pickles, onion, worcestershire sauce, lemon juice and paprika.
Loosen with the water to a spoonable consistency and chill before serving.

notes: Keeps for 5 days in the fridge.
Spoon over a wedge of iceberg lettuce.

title: Honey Mustard Dipping Sauce
summary: Sweet, sharp and four ingredients, a favourite with chicken tenders and sausage rolls.

steps.text: Whisk the mustard, honey and mayonnaise together until smooth.
Add the lemon juice and salt, then taste and adjust the sweetness.
Serve in a small bowl for dipping.

notes: Keeps for a week in the fridge.
Brush it over chicken thighs in the last 10 minutes of roasting for a sticky glaze.

title: Chipotle Lime Crema
summary: Smoky, cooling sour cream sauce for tacos, grilled corn and burrito bowls.

items.raw: 1 chipotle chilli in adobo, finely chopped

steps.text: Whisk the sour cream and mayonnaise together until smooth.
Stir in the chipotle, adobo sauce, lime juice, garlic and coriander.
Season with salt and chill for 15 minutes before drizzling.

notes: Thin with a splash of water to drizzle from a squeeze bottle.
Keeps for 5 days in the fridge.

title: Tartare Sauce
summary: Classic fish and chip shop sauce with capers, gherkins and fresh parsley.

steps.text: Mix the mayonnaise with the gherkins, capers, parsley and shallot.
Stir in the lemon juice and pepper, then taste for balance.
Chill for 20 minutes, until the flavours have melded, before serving with crumbed fish.

notes: Keeps for 5 days in the fridge.
Use a little of the gherkin brine for extra tang.

title: Louisiana Style Remoulade
summary: A Louisiana style remoulade with mustard, horseradish and paprika for crab cakes and prawns.

steps.text: Stir the mayonnaise, mustard, horseradish and paprika together in a bowl.
Add the celery, parsley, lemon juice, hot sauce and garlic.
Mix well and chill until cold and the flavours have developed, about 30 minutes.

notes: Serve with crab cakes, boiled prawns or fried green tomatoes.
Keeps for 5 days in the fridge.

title: Comeback Sauce
summary: A Mississippi style dipping sauce, tangy and a little spicy, for chips, burgers and salads.

steps.text: Whisk the mayonnaise, chilli sauce and ketchup together.
Add the worcestershire sauce, garlic, paprika, hot sauce and lemon juice.
Chill until cold and the garlic has mellowed, about an hour.

notes: Keeps for a week in the fridge.
Excellent on fried chicken sandwiches.

title: Smoky Barbecue Sauce
summary: A thick, smoky-sweet sauce simmered from pantry staples for ribs, chicken and burgers.

steps.text: Combine everything in a saucepan and bring to a gentle simmer, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Cook for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring often, until thick enough to coat a spoon.
Taste and add a splash of vinegar or a pinch more sugar if needed.
Cool and store in a clean jar.

notes: Keeps for 2 weeks in the fridge.
Brush on in the last few minutes of grilling so the sugar doesn't burn.

title: Smoked Salmon and Dill Brunch Tart
summary: A crisp pastry case filled with a soft egg custard, smoked salmon and fresh dill.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C and line a 23 cm tart tin with the pastry, trimming the edge.
Prick the base, line with baking paper and rice, and bake for 10 minutes. Remove the paper and rice.
Whisk the eggs, cream, milk, dill, spring onions and pepper together.
Scatter the salmon in the case, pour in the custard and bake for 25 minutes until just set with a slight wobble.
Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

notes: Food safety: bake until the centre is set and reaches 75°C, and keep leftovers in the fridge for up to 2 days.
Serve with a rocket salad.

title: Baked Eggs in Tomato and Chorizo Pan
summary: Eggs baked in a spiced tomato and chorizo base, served straight from the pan with bread.

steps.text: Fry the chorizo in the oil in a large ovenproof pan for 3 minutes until the oil runs red.
Add the onion, garlic and capsicum and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the paprika and tomatoes, then simmer for 10 minutes until thick.
Make four wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook over low heat for 6 to 8 minutes until the whites are set.
Scatter with parsley and serve with the bread.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set, especially for pregnant women, older people and young children, and make sure the chorizo is cooked through to 75°C.
Use a lid or foil if your pan has none.

title: Ricotta Hotcakes with Berry Compote
summary: Light, tender hotcakes made with ricotta, served with warm berries and a spoonful of yoghurt.

steps.text: Simmer the berries and honey in a small saucepan for 5 minutes until syrupy, then keep warm.
Mix the ricotta, egg yolks and milk, then stir in the flour, baking powder and sugar.
Whisk the egg whites to soft peaks and fold gently into the batter.
Melt a little butter in a non-stick pan and cook spoonfuls for 2 minutes each side until golden.
Stack the hotcakes, spoon over the berries and add the yoghurt.

notes: Food safety: cook the hotcakes until set through the middle, especially for pregnant women, older people and young children.
Keep cooked hotcakes warm in a low oven.

title: Lemon Dutch Baby with Fresh Fruit
summary: A puffed oven pancake with crisp edges and a custardy middle, finished with lemon and berries.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C and place a 25 cm ovenproof frypan inside to heat for 5 minutes.
Blend the eggs, milk, flour, sugar and vanilla until smooth.
Add the butter to the hot pan, swirl to melt, then pour in the batter.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until deeply puffed and golden.
Squeeze over the lemon juice, top with the fruit and dust with icing sugar.

notes: Food safety: bake until the centre is fully set and no longer liquid, especially for pregnant women, older people and young children.
It sinks as it cools, so serve immediately.

title: Sheet Pan Breakfast Hash
summary: Crisp potatoes, capsicum and bacon roasted on one tray with eggs baked in at the end.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C and toss the potatoes, capsicum, onion, bacon, oil, paprika and pepper on a large tray.
Roast for 30 minutes, turning once, until the potatoes are crisp.
Make four hollows, crack an egg into each and bake for 6 to 8 minutes until the whites are set.
Scatter with chives and serve from the tray.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set and the bacon is cooked through to 75°C.
Use sweet potato for a change.

title: Brunch Frittata with Zucchini and Feta
summary: A thick, golden frittata studded with zucchini, fetta and mint, finished under the grill.

steps.text: Squeeze the grated zucchini in a clean cloth to remove the water.
Cook the onion in the oil in a 24 cm ovenproof frypan for 4 minutes, then add the zucchini and cook 3 minutes more.
Whisk the eggs, milk, mint and pepper, then pour into the pan and scatter the fetta on top.
Cook gently for 6 minutes until the edges set, then grill for 4 minutes until the top is golden and the centre is set.

notes: Food safety: cook the frittata until the centre is fully set, especially for pregnant women, older people and young children.
Delicious cold in a lunchbox.

title: Egg and Bacon Breakfast Pie
summary: A classic Aussie bacon and egg pie with a flaky pastry lid, cut into wedges for brunch.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C and line a 23 cm pie dish with the shortcrust pastry.
Scatter the bacon, cheddar and parsley over the base, then crack the six eggs on top and prick the yolks lightly.
Season with pepper and cover with the puff pastry, sealing the edges.
Brush with the beaten egg and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until deep golden.
Rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

notes: Food safety: bake until the eggs are fully set and the bacon is cooked through to 75°C.
Serve with tomato relish.

title: Avocado and Poached Egg on Seeded Toast
summary: The cafe favourite at home, with lemony smashed avocado, a soft egg and a sprinkle of seeds.

steps.text: Toast the sourdough until golden and brush with the olive oil.
Mash the avocado with the lemon juice and salt, keeping it chunky.
Poach the eggs in barely simmering water for 3 to 4 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks still soft.
Pile the avocado onto the sourdough, then add the eggs, seeds and coriander.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set, especially for pregnant women, older people and young children.
A splash of white vinegar in the water helps the whites hold together.

title: Corn Fritter Stack with Bacon and Avocado
summary: Golden sweetcorn fritters stacked with crisp bacon, avocado and a drizzle of sweet chilli.

steps.text: Mix the corn, flour, eggs, milk, spring onions and coriander into a thick batter.
Fry the bacon until crisp and set aside.
Heat the oil in a pan and cook spoonfuls of batter for 2 to 3 minutes each side until golden and cooked through.
Stack the fritters with bacon and avocado and drizzle with the sweet chilli.

notes: Food safety: cook the fritters until the centres are firm and hot, and the bacon through to 75°C.
Freeze leftover fritters between baking paper.

title: Chilli and Spring Onion Soft Scramble
summary: Soft, creamy eggs cooked with fresh chilli and spring onion, piled on buttery toast.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs, milk and salt together.
Melt half the butter in a non-stick pan and soften the chilli and spring onion for 1 minute.
Pour in the eggs and stir gently over low heat for 2 to 3 minutes until just set but still creamy.
Toast the sourdough until golden, butter it, then top with the eggs and coriander.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until fully set and no longer runny, especially for pregnant women, older people and young children.
Leave the chilli seeds out for a milder dish.

title: Whipped Ricotta Bruschetta
summary: Grilled sourdough with whipped ricotta, ripe tomatoes, basil and a drizzle of olive oil.

steps.text: Grill the sourdough until charred at the edges, then rub with the cut garlic.
Mix the tomatoes with half the oil, the vinegar and salt.
Grill until the edges are charred, then spread the ricotta on the toast and spoon over the tomatoes.
Finish with basil and the remaining oil.

notes: Add a poached egg on top for extra protein.
Best made just before eating so the toast stays crisp.

title: Nostalgic Beef Mince Gravy on Toast
summary: A retro favourite, tender beef mince in a rich gravy spooned over thick buttered toast.

steps.text: Brown the mince in the oil in a large pan for 6 minutes, breaking up any lumps.
Add the onion and carrot and cook for 4 minutes.
Stir in the flour, tomato paste and worcestershire sauce, then pour in the stock.
Simmer for 12 minutes until thick, adding the peas for the last 3 minutes.
Toast the bread until golden, butter it and spoon the mince over.

notes: Food safety: cook the mince until no pink remains and it reaches 75°C throughout.
Leftovers reheat well and freeze for 3 months.

title: Mushroom and Thyme Brunch Toast
summary: Garlicky mixed mushrooms with thyme and a swipe of cream cheese on crisp toast.

steps.text: Heat the butter and oil in a large pan and cook the mushrooms in a single layer over high heat for 6 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic and thyme and cook for 1 minute.
Finish with the lemon juice and parsley.
Toast the sourdough until golden, spread with cream cheese and pile on the mushrooms.

notes: Do not crowd the pan, or the mushrooms will steam instead of browning.
Top with a soft egg for a heartier brunch.

title: Strata with Ham and Cheddar
summary: A savoury bread and egg bake with ham and cheddar that you can build ahead and bake at brunch.

steps.text: Grease a 20 x 30 cm baking dish and layer in the bread, ham, cheddar and spring onions.
Whisk the eggs, milk, mustard and pepper, then pour over the bread and press down.
Stand for 20 minutes so the bread soaks up the custard.
Bake at 180°C for 40 to 45 minutes until puffed, golden and set in the middle.

notes: Food safety: bake until the centre is fully set and reaches 75°C, especially for pregnant women, older people and young children.
Assemble the night before and keep covered in the fridge.

title: Egg in a Hole Toast
summary: A fried egg cooked in the middle of a slice of buttered toast, simple and fun for kids.

steps.text: Cut a round hole from the centre of each slice of bread with a cutter or glass.
Melt the butter in a frypan and toast the bread and the cut-out rounds for 1 minute on one side.
Flip the bread, crack an egg into each hole and season with salt.
Cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the whites are set, then top with chives.

notes: Food safety: cook until the whites are fully set and the yolk thickened, especially for young children, pregnant women and older people.
Dip the toasted rounds in the yolk.

title: Manhattan Tomato Chowder with Clams
summary: A tomato-based chowder with potato, celery and tender clams, lighter than the creamy kind.

steps.text: Cook the bacon in the oil in a large pot for 4 minutes until it renders and crisps.
Add the onion, celery, carrot and garlic and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the potatoes, tomatoes, stock and thyme, then simmer for 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Add the clams and heat through for 3 minutes. Scatter with parsley.

notes: Food safety: cook the bacon through, heat the clams until steaming hot and opaque at 75°C, and keep leftovers in the fridge for up to 2 days.
Serve with crackers.

title: Creamy White Fish Chowder with Thyme
summary: A chunky chowder of white fish, potato and sweetcorn in a gently thickened milk base.

items.raw: 500 g firm white fish fillets, cubed

steps.text: Melt the butter in a large pot and cook the onion and celery for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then add the stock, milk, potatoes and thyme.
Simmer for 12 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Add the corn and fish and poach gently for 5 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Stir in the cream and parsley.

notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque throughout and the chowder steaming at 75°C, and eat leftovers within 2 days.
Do not boil hard once the fish is in or it will break up.

title: Prawn Bisque
summary: A silky, deeply flavoured bisque made from prawn shells, tomato paste and a splash of cream.

steps.text: Peel the prawns and keep the shells. Refrigerate the prawn meat.
Fry the shells in the butter for 5 minutes until bright orange and fragrant.
Add the onion, carrot and celery and cook for 5 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste and paprika.
Add the rice and stock and simmer for 25 minutes until the rice is very soft.
Blend well and strain through a sieve, pressing out all the liquid.
Return to the pot, add the prawns and cook for 3 minutes until pink and curled. Stir in the cream and lemon juice.

notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until opaque and firm, and bring the bisque to 75°C before serving. Keep leftovers refrigerated and eat within 2 days.
The rice thickens the soup so no flour is needed.

title: Crab and Sweetcorn Bisque
summary: A smooth corn bisque finished with sweet crab meat and a swirl of cream.

steps.text: Melt the butter and cook the onion and garlic for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the corn, stock and paprika and simmer for 12 minutes until the corn is tender.
Blend with the milk until very smooth, then return to the pot.
Stir in the cream and crab and warm gently for 3 minutes until steaming. Add the lemon juice.
Ladle into bowls and serve with chives on top.

notes: Food safety: use fresh, refrigerated crab meat, heat until the crab is opaque and the bisque a steaming 75°C. Eat leftovers within 2 days.
Strain for a restaurant style finish.

title: Mushroom Bisque
summary: An earthy, velvety soup of browned mushrooms, thyme and cream, with no flour needed.

steps.text: Cook the mushrooms in the butter in a large pot over high heat for 8 minutes until deeply golden.
Add the onion, garlic and thyme and cook for 4 minutes until soft.
Stir in the potato, stock and soy sauce, then simmer for 15 minutes until the potato is tender.
Blend until smooth, stir in the cream and reheat until steaming. Scatter with parsley.

notes: Reserve a few fried mushroom slices to garnish.
Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Roasted Butternut Bisque
summary: Roasted pumpkin blended with apple and a touch of cream for a sweet, silky soup.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C and toss the pumpkin, apple and onion with the oil and cumin on a tray.
Roast for 35 minutes until soft and caramelised at the edges.
Blend with the stock until smooth and warm in a pot until steaming.
Stir in the cream and nutmeg, then scatter with pepitas.

notes: Skip the cream and use coconut milk for a dairy free version.
Freezes well for 3 months.

title: Salmon and Leek Chowder
summary: Fresh salmon, sweet leek and potato in a creamy, dill-scented chowder.

items.raw: 400 g salmon fillet, skinned and cubed

steps.text: Melt the butter and cook the leeks for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the potatoes, stock and milk and simmer for 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Crush a few potatoes against the side of the pot to thicken the soup.
Add the salmon and poach gently for 4 minutes until opaque and just cooked through.
Stir in the cream, dill, lemon juice and pepper.

notes: Food safety: cook the salmon until opaque throughout and the chowder steaming at 75°C. Eat leftovers within 2 days.
Do not boil once the salmon is in.

title: Potato and Bacon Chowder
summary: A thick, hearty potato soup loaded with smoky bacon, chives and a little cheddar.

steps.text: Cook the bacon in a large pot for 6 minutes until crisp, then lift half out for garnish.
Cook the onion and celery in the bacon fat for 5 minutes until soft, then stir in the flour.
Add the stock, milk and potatoes and simmer for 15 minutes until the potatoes are very tender.
Mash some of the potatoes roughly, stir in the cheddar and pepper until melted.
Serve with the crisp bacon and chives.

notes: Food safety: cook the bacon through and bring the chowder to a steaming 75°C. Keep leftovers refrigerated and eat within 2 days.
Use a little less cheddar for a lighter bowl.

title: Roasted Tomato and Basil Bisque
summary: Slow roasted tomatoes and garlic blended into a rich, creamy soup with fresh basil.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C and roast the tomatoes, onion and garlic with the oil for 35 minutes until collapsed and caramelised.
Squeeze the garlic from the skins and tip everything into a pot with the stock and sugar.
Simmer for 5 minutes, then blend with the basil until smooth.
Stir in the cream and pepper and reheat until steaming.

notes: Serve with a grilled cheese sandwich.
Keeps for 4 days in the fridge or freezes for 3 months.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Vietnamese Cold Vermicelli Bowl with Lemongrass Beef
summary: Cool rice vermicelli with fresh herbs, pickled carrot and sizzling lemongrass beef.

steps.text: Mix the beef with the lemongrass, garlic, 1 tbsp fish sauce and half the sugar.
Cook the vermicelli in boiling water for 4 minutes until tender, then rinse under cold water and drain.
Whisk the lime juice, remaining fish sauce, sugar and water into a dressing.
Sear the beef in the oil over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Divide the noodles, vegetables, herbs and beef between bowls and finish with peanuts and dressing.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef until browned with no pink inside, and cook the beef to at least 71°C, and keep any raw marinated meat refrigerated until cooking.
Use grilled tofu for a vegetarian bowl.

title: Korean Bibim Guksu Spicy Cold Noodles
summary: Chewy wheat noodles tossed in a sweet, spicy gochujang sauce with crunchy vegetables and egg.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 8 minutes until the yolks are set, then cool in iced water and halve.
Cook the noodles in boiling water for 3 minutes until tender, then rinse well under cold water.
Whisk the gochujang, soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, sesame oil and garlic into a sauce.
Toss the noodles with the sauce, then top with cucumber, kimchi, egg and sesame seeds.

notes: Food safety: boil the eggs until the yolks are fully set, especially for pregnant women, older people and young children.
Add more gochujang for extra heat.

title: Thai Glass Noodle Salad with Prawns
summary: Slippery glass noodles with prawns, lime, chilli and fresh herbs in a bright Thai dressing.

steps.text: Soak the noodles in hot water for 5 minutes until soft and translucent, then drain and cut.
Poach the prawns in simmering water for 2 to 3 minutes until pink and opaque, then drain.
Whisk the lime juice, fish sauce, sugar, chilli and garlic until the sugar dissolves.
Toss the noodles, prawns, carrot, onion and herbs with the dressing and top with peanuts.

notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until pink, firm and opaque throughout, and keep the salad chilled until serving.
Serve straight away so the noodles stay slippery.

title: Chilled Buckwheat Noodles with Ginger Soy Edamame
summary: Nutty buckwheat noodles with edamame, cucumber and a sharp ginger soy dressing.

steps.text: Cook the soba in boiling water for 4 to 5 minutes until just tender, adding the edamame for the last 2 minutes.
Drain and rinse under cold water until the noodles are cold.
Whisk the soy sauce, vinegar, ginger, sesame oil and honey together.
Toss with the noodles, cucumber and spring onions, then scatter with sesame seeds.

notes: Rinsing removes the surface starch so the noodles do not clump.
Keeps for 2 days in the fridge.

title: Somen Noodle Salad with Tomato and Shiso
summary: Fine chilled somen with juicy tomato, cucumber and a light citrus soy dressing.

steps.text: Cook the noodles in boiling water for 2 minutes until tender, then rinse in iced water and drain well.
Whisk the soy sauce, vinegar, lemon juice and sesame oil.
Toss the noodles with the tomato, cucumber and mint, then pour over the dressing and top with sesame seeds.

notes: Mint stands in for shiso if you cannot find it.
Serve very cold on a hot day.

title: Cold Dan Dan Noodle Salad
summary: Sesame and chilli noodles dressed in a nutty Sichuan style sauce with cucumber and peanuts.

steps.text: Cook the noodles in boiling water for 4 minutes until tender, then rinse under cold water and drain.
Whisk the tahini, soy sauce, vinegar, chilli oil, sugar, garlic and warm water until smooth and pourable.
Toss the noodles with the sauce, then top with cucumber, spring onions and peanuts.

notes: Add more chilli oil for heat.
Sauce can be made 3 days ahead.

title: Cold Sesame Tofu Noodle Bowl
summary: Cold noodles with silken tofu, cucumber and a soy sesame dressing for a no-cook lunch.

steps.text: Cook the noodles in boiling water for 3 to 4 minutes until tender, then rinse cold and drain.
Whisk the soy sauce, sesame oil, vinegar and sugar together.
Toss the noodles with the dressing, cucumber and carrot.
Top with the tofu, spring onions and sesame seeds.

notes: Handle the silken tofu gently so it stays in cubes.
Use extra firm tofu if you prefer more bite.

title: Rice Noodle Bowl with Peanut Lime Tofu
summary: Cool rice noodles, crunchy raw vegetables and crisp tofu in a peanut lime sauce.

steps.text: Cook the noodles in boiling water for 4 minutes until tender, then rinse cold and drain.
Pan-fry the tofu in the oil for 8 minutes until golden on all sides.
Whisk the peanut butter, lime juice, soy sauce, sugar and water until smooth.
Toss the noodles with the sauce and vegetables, then top with tofu, coriander and peanuts.

notes: Thin the sauce with extra water if it is too thick.
Keeps well for a packed lunch.

title: Apple Oat Pancakes for Kids
summary: Soft, naturally sweet pancakes made from apple and oats with no added sugar.

steps.text: Blend the apples, oats, eggs, milk, baking powder and cinnamon until smooth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Melt a little butter in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Cook small spoonfuls for 2 minutes each side until golden and cooked through.
Stack on plates and serve with a spoonful of yoghurt.

notes: Freeze cooked pancakes and reheat in the toaster.
Food safety: cook until the centre is set and no longer wet, especially for young children, pregnant women and older people. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Peanut Butter and Apple Toast Fingers
summary: Wholemeal toast spread with smooth peanut butter and thin apple slices, cut into fingers for small hands.

steps.text: Toast the bread until golden.
Spread with the peanut butter and top with the apple slices.
Dust with cinnamon and cut into fingers.

notes: Use a nut-free spread such as sunflower seed butter for school and childcare settings.
Cut into small pieces for toddlers.

title: Rainbow Fruit and Yoghurt Pots
summary: Layers of mango, berries and orange over creamy yoghurt, no sweetener needed.

steps.text: Spoon a layer of yoghurt into four small cups or jars.
Add layers of mango, berries and orange.
Repeat the layers until the cups are full and top with the toasted oats just before serving.

notes: Keep the toasted oats separate until serving so it stays crisp.
Make the pots the night before for a quick breakfast.

title: Cheesy Scrambled Egg Fingers
summary: Soft scrambled egg with a little grated cheddar, spooned over toast fingers.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs and milk together.
Melt the butter in a small pan over low heat, pour in the eggs and stir gently for 2 to 3 minutes until set but still soft.
Fold through the cheddar until it melts.
Toast the bread until golden, cut into fingers and top with the egg.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until fully set and no longer runny, especially for young children, pregnant women and older people.
Leave out salt for babies and toddlers.

title: Apple Oat Breakfast Muffins
summary: Wholegrain muffins sweetened only with apple and a little honey, ideal for school mornings.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C and line a 12 hole muffin tin.
Mix the oats, flour and cinnamon, then stir in the apples.
Whisk the eggs, milk, honey and oil, then fold into the dry mix until just combined.
Spoon into the tin and bake for 20 to 22 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.

notes: Food safety: bake until a skewer comes out clean so the egg is fully cooked.
Freeze for up to 3 months.

title: Wholemeal Pikelets with Ricotta
summary: Small, fluffy wholemeal pikelets served with ricotta and sliced pear, lightly sweetened.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, honey, egg and milk into a thick, lump-free batter.
Melt a little butter in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Drop in tablespoons of batter and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until bubbles appear, then flip and cook 1 minute until golden.
Serve with ricotta, pear and a dusting of cinnamon.

notes: Food safety: cook the pikelets until set through, especially for young children, pregnant women and older people.
Cold pikelets are good in lunchboxes.

title: Baked Apple Cinnamon Oatmeal
summary: A tray of oats baked with apple, cinnamon and milk, cut into squares for the week.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C and grease a 20 cm baking dish.
Mix the oats, apples, cinnamon, baking powder and half the walnuts in the dish.
Whisk the milk, egg, honey and butter, then pour over the oats.
Scatter with the remaining walnuts and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until set and golden.

notes: Keeps for 4 days in the fridge and reheats in the microwave.
Food safety: bake until the middle is fully set, especially for pregnant women, older people and young children. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Tropical Mango Oat Pots with Lime
summary: Creamy overnight oats soaked in coconut milk and layered with fresh mango, no added sugar.

steps.text: Stir the oats, coconut milk, yoghurt and vanilla together in a bowl.
Cover and chill for at least 4 hours or overnight until the oats are soft and thick.
Toss the mango with the lime juice.
Layer the oat mixture and mango in jars and top with coconut.

notes: Stir well before layering.
Keeps for 4 days in the fridge.

title: Cottage Cheese Bowl with Cucumber and Seeds
summary: A savoury, high-protein bowl of cottage cheese, crisp cucumber, cherry tomatoes and mixed seeds.

steps.text: Spoon the cottage cheese into two bowls.
Toss the cucumber and tomatoes with the oil and lemon juice until well coated.
Pile the vegetables over the cheese and finish with the seeds, dill and pepper.

notes: Serve with wholegrain crispbread.
Low in sugar and quick for busy mornings.

title: Quick Berry Jam on Toast
summary: A quick jam from frozen berries with no added sugar, spread over wholegrain toast.

steps.text: Simmer the berries in a small saucepan for 12 to 15 minutes until broken down and syrupy.
Mash roughly and stir in the lemon juice.
Cool for 10 minutes until thickened.
Toast the bread until golden, spread with ricotta and top with the jam.

notes: Store extra jam in a jar in the fridge for up to 10 days.
The berries give natural sweetness, so no sugar is needed.

title: Almond Meal Breakfast Pancakes
summary: Low-carb pancakes made with almond meal and eggs, with a squeeze of lemon and yoghurt.

steps.text: Whisk the almond meal, eggs, milk, baking powder and vanilla into a thick batter.
Melt a little butter in a non-stick pan over medium-low heat.
Cook small spoonfuls for 2 to 3 minutes each side until golden and firm in the middle.
Serve with yoghurt and a squeeze of lemon.

notes: Food safety: cook until the pancakes are firm and set through, especially for pregnant women, older people and young children.
Keep the pancakes small because they are delicate to flip.

title: Spinach and Mushroom Egg Muffin Cups
summary: Baked egg cups with spinach, mushroom and feta, made in a muffin tin for easy grab-and-go breakfasts.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C and grease a 12 hole muffin tin.
Cook the mushrooms in the oil for 4 minutes until golden, add the spinach and cook for 1 minute until wilted.
Whisk the eggs, milk and pepper, then divide the vegetables, feta and spring onion across the tin.
Pour in the egg mixture and bake for 18 to 20 minutes until puffed and set.

notes: Food safety: bake until the centre is fully set, especially for pregnant women, older people and young children.
Keeps for 4 days in the fridge and freezes well.

title: Greek Yoghurt Bowl with Walnuts and Cinnamon
summary: Thick Greek yoghurt with toasted walnuts, apple and cinnamon, a quick bowl with no added sugar.

steps.text: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2 to 3 minutes until fragrant and lightly golden.
Spoon the yoghurt into bowls and top with apple and walnuts.
Dust with cinnamon and drizzle with the honey.

notes: Use unsweetened yoghurt to keep the sugar low.
Add a spoon of chia seeds for fibre.

title: Oat and Seed Porridge with Poached Pear
summary: A creamy, nutty porridge of oats and seeds topped with soft cinnamon pear.

steps.text: Simmer the pear with the cinnamon and water for 8 to 10 minutes until tender.
Cook the oats, sunflower seeds and milk in a saucepan over medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring until creamy.
Spoon into bowls and top with the pear and pepitas.

notes: Use any plant milk for a dairy free bowl.
Poach extra pear and keep it in the fridge for 3 days.

title: Rosemary Roast Potatoes for Christmas
summary: Crisp-edged, fluffy roast potatoes with garlic and rosemary, parboiled and roughed up for maximum crunch.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C and heat the oil in a roasting tray for 10 minutes.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 10 minutes until the edges are soft, then drain and shake to rough up the surfaces.
Tip the potatoes into the hot oil, turn to coat and roast for 30 minutes.
Turn them, add the garlic and rosemary and roast for 20 to 25 minutes more until deep golden and crisp.

notes: Roughing up the surface gives a crunchy crust.
Use a hot tray so the potatoes sizzle on contact.

title: Maple Roasted Carrots and Sweet Potato
summary: Sweet roasted root vegetables glazed with maple syrup, mustard and thyme.

items.raw: 500 g sweet potato, cut into batons

steps.text: Heat the oven to 210°C and toss the vegetables with the oil, salt and thyme on a large tray.
Roast for 25 minutes, turning once.
Mix the maple syrup and mustard, drizzle over and roast for 10 to 15 minutes more until caramelised and tender.

notes: Do not crowd the tray or they will steam.
Good on a roast dinner or cooked ahead and reheated.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Green Beans with Bacon and Almonds
summary: Garlicky green beans with crisp bacon and toasted almonds, a festive side that suits any roast.

steps.text: Cook the bacon in the oil in a large pan for 5 minutes until crisp and lift out.
Add the butter and beans and cook for 8 minutes until blistered and tender.
Add the almonds and cook for 3 minutes until golden, tossing often.
Return the bacon, add the vinegar and pepper and cook until the beans are glazed.

notes: Food safety: cook the bacon through to 75°C before serving.
Trim the beans the same length so they cook evenly.

title: Orange and Berry Sauce for the Christmas Table
summary: A tart, jewel-red sauce simmered with orange juice and berries, great with turkey and ham.

steps.text: Combine the berries, orange zest and juice, sugar, cinnamon and water in a saucepan.
Simmer for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the berries burst and the sauce thickens.
Remove the cinnamon stick and cool, as the sauce firms up as it cools.

notes: Keeps for 2 weeks in a clean jar in the fridge.
Stir through a spoon of horseradish for ham.

title: Longevity Noodles with Mushrooms for Lunar New Year
summary: Long, uncut noodles tossed with mushrooms and garlic chives for luck and long life.

items.raw: 1 bunch garlic chives, cut into 5 cm lengths

steps.text: Cook the noodles in boiling water until just tender, then drain and rinse. Do not cut the noodles, for long life.
Stir-fry the mushrooms in the vegetable oil over high heat for 5 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Toss in the noodles, soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar and chives and stir-fry for 2 minutes until hot.
Finish with the sesame oil.

notes: Leave the noodles long as they stand for long life.
