Use vegetarian mushroom sauce in place of the oyster sauce if you prefer.

title: Garlic Stir Fried Greens for Lunar New Year
summary: Bright, glossy choy sum stir-fried with plenty of garlic and a splash of Shaoxing wine.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and fry the garlic for 15 seconds until fragrant.
Add the bok choy and toss for 2 minutes.
Splash in the wine, soy sauce and sugar and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until the stems are tender but still crisp.
Finish with the sesame oil.

notes: Cook in two batches if your wok is small.
Greens stand for prosperity at the Lunar New Year table.

title: Jeera Aloo Cumin Potatoes for Diwali
summary: Golden potatoes tossed with toasted cumin seeds, turmeric and fresh coriander.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes for 8 minutes until just tender, then drain.
Heat the oil, add the cumin seeds and fry for 30 seconds until they sizzle.
Add the turmeric, ground coriander and chilli, then the potatoes and salt.
Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp at the edges.
Finish with the lemon juice and coriander.

notes: Skip the chilli for a milder dish.
Serve warm with puri or flatbread.

title: Paneer and Pea Pulao for Diwali
summary: Fragrant basmati rice cooked with golden paneer, peas and whole spices.

steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and soak it for 15 minutes.
Fry the paneer in 1 tbsp ghee for 4 minutes until golden, then set aside.
Heat the remaining ghee, add the whole spices and cumin and fry for 30 seconds, then cook the onion for 6 minutes until golden.
Add the rice, water, salt and peas, bring to the boil, cover and cook on low for 12 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Fold in the paneer, rest for 5 minutes and scatter with coriander.

notes: Soaking the rice is not counted in the preparation time.
Serve with raita.

title: Eid Saffron Rice with Almonds and Sultanas
summary: Buttery rice scented with saffron and cardamom, scattered with toasted almonds and sultanas.

steps.text: Soak the saffron in 2 tbsp of hot water.
Toast the almonds in the butter for 2 minutes until golden, then lift out.
Add the rice and cardamom and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the water and salt, bring to the boil, cover and cook on low for 15 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Drizzle over the saffron, rest for 5 minutes, fluff and fold in the sultanas and almonds.

notes: Rinse the rice first for separate grains.
A pinch of saffron goes a long way.

title: Sheer Khurma Eid Vermicelli Pudding
summary: A creamy, cardamom-scented milk pudding with fine vermicelli, pistachios and sultanas.

steps.text: Toast the vermicelli in the ghee over medium heat for 3 minutes until golden brown.
Pour in the milk, add the cardamom and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring often, until the vermicelli is tender and the milk reduced.
Stir in the sugar and sultanas and cook for 3 minutes more until slightly thickened.
Serve warm or chilled, topped with the nuts.

notes: The pudding thickens as it cools, so loosen with milk.
Serve warm on Eid morning.

title: Classic Sage and Onion Stuffing
summary: A moist bread stuffing with onion, celery and plenty of sage, baked until crisp on top.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C and grease a baking dish.
Cook the onions and celery in the butter for 8 minutes until soft.
Mix with the bread, sage, parsley and pepper in a large bowl.
Beat the egg with the stock and stir through until the bread is moist.
Spoon into a greased dish and bake for 35 minutes until golden and crisp on top.

notes: Food safety: bake until hot throughout at 75°C and the egg is cooked, particularly if cooked inside poultry.
Make the day before and bake just before serving.

title: Green Bean Casserole from Scratch
summary: Green beans in a creamy mushroom sauce topped with crisp fried onions, no tins needed.

steps.text: Blanch the beans in boiling water for 3 minutes until bright green, then drain.
Cook the mushrooms in the butter for 8 minutes until golden, add the garlic, then stir in the flour for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the milk and stock and simmer for 5 minutes until thick.
Toss the beans in the sauce and tip into a baking dish.
Fry the onion in the oil for 8 minutes until golden, mix with the panko, scatter over the beans and bake at 190°C for 15 minutes until bubbling and golden.

notes: Assemble ahead and bake just before serving.
Use gluten-free crumbs if needed.

title: Sweet Potato Mash with Pecan Crumble
summary: Smooth, buttery sweet potato mash topped with a crunchy pecan and oat crumble.

steps.text: Boil the sweet potato for 15 minutes until very soft, then drain well.
Mash with half the butter, the milk, cinnamon and salt until smooth, then spread in a baking dish.
Rub the remaining butter into the pecans, oats and sugar and scatter on top.
Bake at 190°C for 20 minutes until the crumble is golden and crisp.

notes: Make the mash a day ahead and add the crumble before baking.
Swap the pecans for walnuts.

title: Pan Juice Gravy for the Holiday Roast
summary: A rich, glossy gravy made from the roasting tray juices, stock and a splash of wine.

items.raw: 1/4 cup pan drippings from the roast

steps.text: Pour the fat and juices from the roasting tray into a saucepan, leaving the dark sediment behind.
Stir in the flour and cook for 2 minutes until golden brown.
Whisk in the wine, then the stock, worcestershire sauce and thyme.
Simmer for 8 to 10 minutes until glossy and thick enough to coat a spoon, then season with pepper.

notes: Food safety: bring the gravy to a rolling boil and serve steaming hot, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Strain for a smooth finish.

title: Creamed Corn from Scratch
summary: Sweet corn simmered in cream and a little butter until thick, spooned alongside holiday roasts.

steps.text: Melt the butter and soften the shallot for 3 minutes.
Add the corn and flour and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the cream and milk and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes until thick and creamy.
Crush a third of the corn with a spoon and season with nutmeg and pepper.

notes: Frozen corn works well, as long as it is thawed first.
Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

title: Tomato and Cheese Scrolls
summary: Soft, golden scrolls with a tomato swirl and melted cheese, perfect for weekend brunch.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C and line a tray with baking paper.
Mix the flour and sugar, then stir in the milk and butter to form a soft dough, adding flour if sticky.
Roll out on a floured bench to a 30 x 40 cm rectangle.
Spread with the tomato paste and scatter with cheddar, then roll up from the long side and cut into 8 slices.
Place cut-side up on the tray and bake for 22 to 25 minutes until golden and cooked through.

notes: Add a pinch of dried oregano to the paste.
Reheat in the oven to crisp up the next day.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Barbecue Coleslaw with Cider Dressing
summary: A crunchy, creamy-tangy slaw of cabbage, carrot and apple, built to sit beside pulled pork and ribs.

steps.text: Toss both cabbages, the carrots and the apple in a large bowl.
Whisk the mayonnaise, vinegar, honey, mustard, celery seeds and pepper until smooth.
Pour the dressing over and toss until everything is evenly coated.
Chill for 30 minutes until the cabbage softens slightly, then toss again.

notes: Best eaten within 2 days.
Squeeze the lime or lemon over just before serving if you like extra tang.

title: Grilled Corn with Chilli Lime Butter
summary: Charred corn cobs brushed with a chilli, lime and coriander butter, grilled until the kernels blister.

steps.text: Mash the butter with the chilli, lime zest, coriander and salt.
Heat a barbecue or grill to medium-high and cook the corn for 12 to 15 minutes, turning, until charred in spots and tender.
Brush generously with the butter and squeeze over the lime juice.

notes: Wrap in foil and grill for 20 minutes if you prefer softer corn.
Keep leftover butter in the fridge for 1 week.

title: Slow Baked Beans for the Barbecue
summary: Smoky, sweet baked beans in a thick tomato sauce, simmered low until glossy, with bacon for depth.

items.raw: 2 x 400 g cans cannellini beans, drained

steps.text: Cook the bacon in a heavy pot for 5 minutes until crisp.
Add the onion and garlic and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the beans, tomato sauce, sugar, vinegar, worcestershire sauce, paprika, mustard and water.
Simmer very gently with the lid ajar for 45 minutes until thick and glossy, stirring occasionally.

notes: Food safety: cook the bacon through to 75°C and bring the beans to a steaming heat before serving.
Even better the next day.

title: Creamy Picnic Macaroni Salad with Celery
summary: Classic cold macaroni in a tangy creamy dressing with celery, carrot and boiled egg.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes until the yolks are fully set, cool in cold water, peel and chop.
Cook the macaroni in salted boiling water for 10 minutes until tender, then rinse under cold water and drain.
Whisk the mayonnaise, sour cream, vinegar, mustard and pepper.
Fold the pasta, vegetables, egg and parsley through the dressing.
Chill for 1 hour until cold.

notes: Food safety: boil the eggs until the yolks are fully set and keep the salad chilled below 5°C until serving, especially in hot weather.
Loosen with a splash of milk if the pasta absorbs the dressing.

title: Charred Zucchini Salad with Mint and Feta
summary: Smoky grilled zucchini ribbons with mint, lemon and creamy feta, fast on the barbecue.

steps.text: Brush the zucchini with half the oil and grill on a hot barbecue for 2 to 3 minutes each side until charred and tender.
Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes until golden.
Arrange the zucchini on a platter and dress with the remaining oil, lemon juice and zest.
Scatter with the feta, mint, pine nuts and chilli flakes.

notes: Cut the zucchini thickly so it does not collapse on the grill.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Grilled Pineapple with Lime and Chilli
summary: Sweet, caramelised pineapple rings brushed with lime, chilli and a little honey, served warm.

items.raw: 1 pineapple, peeled and cut into rings

steps.text: Whisk the lime juice, honey, chilli flakes and oil together.
Brush the pineapple rings and grill on a hot barbecue for 3 to 4 minutes each side until caramelised with dark grill marks.
Brush again with the dressing and scatter with mint.

notes: Excellent beside grilled chicken, pork or fish.
Serve with vanilla yoghurt for dessert.

title: Beef and Barley Soup
summary: A thick, comforting soup of beef chuck, pearl barley and root vegetables simmered until the meat falls apart.

steps.text: Brown the beef in the oil in batches in a large pot for 6 minutes and set aside.
Cook the onion, carrots and celery in the same pot for 6 minutes, then add the garlic and tomato paste.
Return the beef, add the barley, stock, thyme and bay leaf and bring to the boil and stir until the barley is submerged.
Simmer gently for 75 to 90 minutes until the beef is tender and the barley is soft.
Remove the bay leaf and thyme and serve with parsley.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef until tender and the soup reaches a steaming 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.
The soup thickens overnight, so add a splash of stock when reheating.

title: Lemony Chicken and Rice Soup with Dill
summary: A bright, comforting soup of chicken, rice and carrot finished with lemon juice and plenty of dill.

steps.text: Cook the onion, carrots and celery in the oil for 6 minutes until soft, adding the garlic for the last minute.
Add the stock and chicken and simmer gently for 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Lift out the chicken, shred it and return it to the pot with the rice.
Simmer for 12 minutes until the rice is tender.
Whisk the eggs and lemon juice, slowly whisk in a ladle of hot soup, then stir it all back into the pot off the heat until the soup turns creamy. Add the dill.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until no pink remains and it reaches 75°C, and do not boil the soup after adding the eggs. Eat leftovers within 2 days.
Warm gently when reheating so the eggs do not scramble.

title: Chilean Cazuela Chicken and Pumpkin Stew
summary: A soupy Chilean chicken stew with pumpkin, potato, corn and rice, served in a deep bowl with coriander.

steps.text: Brown the drumsticks in the oil in a large pot for 8 minutes and set aside.
Cook the onion, garlic and capsicum for 5 minutes, then stir in the paprika.
Return the chicken, add the stock, potatoes and corn and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the pumpkin and rice and simmer for 15 minutes until the rice and vegetables are tender.
Scatter with coriander and serve.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until the juices run clear and the thickest part reaches 75°C, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
A drumstick in each bowl is the traditional way to serve.

title: Venezuelan Sancocho Chicken and Root Vegetable Soup
summary: A hearty South American soup of chicken, potato, sweet potato and corn with lime and coriander.

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil in a large pot for 8 minutes and set aside.
Cook the onion and garlic for 5 minutes, then stir in the cumin.
Return the chicken, add the water and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the potatoes, sweet potato and corn and simmer for 20 minutes until the chicken is cooked and the vegetables are tender.
Stir through the coriander and serve with the lime wedges.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C and the juices run clear, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Serve with white rice and avocado.

title: Winter Lamb Shoulder and Pearl Barley Soup
summary: A thick, old-fashioned lamb and vegetable broth with barley, swede and leek.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil in a large pot for 6 minutes.
Add the water and barley, bring to the boil and skim until the scum is gone from the surface.
Simmer for 45 minutes, then add the onion, leek, carrots, swede and thyme.
Simmer for 30 to 40 minutes until the lamb is tender and the barley soft, then stir in the parsley.

notes: Food safety: cook the lamb until tender and at least 75°C throughout, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Better the day after, thinned with a little water.

title: Cock-a-Leekie Soup
summary: A Scottish chicken and leek soup with a little rice and dried fruit, simple and soothing.

steps.text: Simmer the chicken, stock and bay leaf in a large pot for 20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Lift out the chicken, shred it and return it to the pot.
Add the leeks, carrot and rice and simmer for 15 minutes until the rice is tender.
Add the sultanas for the last 5 minutes. Season with pepper and finish with parsley.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until no pink remains and it reaches 75°C, and eat leftovers within 2 days.
Dried fruit is traditional and add gentle sweetness.

title: Split Pea and Ham Hock Soup
summary: A thick, smoky winter soup of green split peas simmered with ham hock until silky.

steps.text: Cook the onion, carrots and celery in the oil for 6 minutes, adding the garlic for the last minute.
Add the ham hock, split peas, water and bay leaf and bring to the boil, skimming until the foam stops.
Simmer gently for 80 to 90 minutes until the peas break down and the meat is falling off the bone.
Lift out the hock, shred the meat, discard the skin and bone and stir the meat back in.
Season with pepper, tasting for salt as the hock is already salty.

notes: Food safety: simmer until the meat is tender and the soup reaches a steaming 75°C. Eat leftovers within 3 days.
The soup thickens as it stands, so thin with a little water.

title: Sweet Potato and Black Bean Chilli Soup
summary: A smoky, thick vegetarian soup of sweet potato and black beans with chipotle and lime.

items.raw: 2 x 400 g cans black beans, drained

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, adding the garlic, cumin and paprika for the last minute.
Add the sweet potato, beans, tomatoes, stock and chipotle.
Simmer for 25 minutes until the sweet potato is very tender.
Mash roughly with a potato masher to thicken, then stir in the lime juice and coriander.

notes: Top with avocado and sour cream.
Freezes well for 3 months.

title: Tofu and Mushroom Hot Pot Broth
summary: A light, savoury broth for the table, with tofu, mushrooms, cabbage and noodles cooked at the table.

steps.text: Bring the stock, ginger, spring onions, soy sauce and wine to a gentle simmer in a wide pot for 10 minutes.
Add the tofu and mushrooms and simmer for 5 minutes until the mushrooms are tender.
Add the cabbage and noodles and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the noodles are soft and the cabbage wilted.
Drizzle with the sesame oil and serve straight from the pot.

notes: Add thinly sliced beef or fish balls for non-vegetarian hot pot, cooking them until no pink remains.
Dip cooked pieces in soy sauce and chilli.

title: Sichuan Style Hot Pot Soup
summary: A numbing, spicy broth with chilli bean paste and Sichuan pepper, loaded with vegetables and tofu.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a pot and fry the chilli bean paste, peppercorns, ginger and garlic for 2 minutes until the oil turns red and fragrant.
Pour in the stock and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the carrot and tofu and cook for 5 minutes until tender.
Add the mushrooms and bok choy and cook for 2 minutes until just wilted.
Scatter with spring onions.

notes: Reduce the chilli bean paste for less heat.
Fish out the peppercorns before eating if you prefer.

title: Tomato Egg Drop Soup
summary: A quick Chinese style soup of ripe tomato and ribbons of egg in a gingery broth.

steps.text: Fry the tomatoes and ginger in the oil for 4 minutes until soft and pulpy.
Add the stock, soy sauce and sugar and simmer for 5 minutes.
Mix the cornflour with the water, stir into the soup and cook for 1 minute until slightly thickened.
Slowly pour in the eggs in a thin stream, stirring gently until they form ribbons and are set.
Finish with spring onions and sesame oil.

notes: Food safety: cook the egg until fully set and the soup steaming at 75°C, especially for pregnant women, older people and young children.
Ripe tomatoes give the best flavour.

title: Barbecue Potato Salad with Bacon and Chives
summary: A warm-to-cold potato salad with crisp bacon, a creamy mustard dressing and lots of chives.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 12 to 15 minutes until just tender, then drain and cool for 10 minutes.
Boil the eggs for 9 minutes until the yolks are fully set, then peel and chop. Fry the bacon for 6 minutes until crisp.
Whisk the mayonnaise, sour cream, mustard, vinegar and pepper.
Fold the potatoes, bacon, eggs, celery and half the chives through the dressing.
Chill for 30 minutes until cold and top with the remaining chives.

notes: Food safety: boil the eggs until the yolks are set, cook the bacon through to 75°C and keep the salad chilled below 5°C until serving.
Dress the potatoes while still slightly warm for more flavour.

title: Grilled Halloumi and Watermelon Salad
summary: Salty golden halloumi, juicy watermelon, mint and rocket with a lime dressing, ideal for summer barbecues.

steps.text: Grill the halloumi on a hot barbecue for 2 to 3 minutes each side until golden with dark grill marks.
Toss the watermelon, rocket and mint on a platter.
Whisk the lime juice, oil and pepper, then drizzle over.
Top with the warm halloumi and pepitas.

notes: Halloumi is salty, so no extra salt is needed.
Serve straight away while the cheese is warm.

title: Smoky Eggplant Dip from the Barbecue
summary: Eggplants charred whole on the grill, then mashed with tahini, garlic and lemon for a smoky dip.

steps.text: Grill the whole eggplants over a hot barbecue for 25 to 30 minutes, turning, until the skins blacken and the flesh collapses.
Cool slightly, then scoop out the soft flesh and drain in a sieve for 10 minutes.
Mash the flesh with the tahini, garlic, lemon juice and salt until creamy.
Transfer to a bowl, drizzle with the oil and top with parsley and paprika.

notes: Keeps for 4 days in the fridge.
Serve with warm flatbread.

title: Barbecued Pear Salad with Ricotta and Walnuts
summary: Caramelised pears with peppery rocket, creamy ricotta and a balsamic drizzle.

steps.text: Brush the pears with half the oil and grill cut-side down for 3 to 4 minutes until caramelised with grill marks.
Slice the pears and arrange over the rocket.
Dot with the ricotta and scatter with the walnuts.
Whisk the remaining oil, vinegar, honey and pepper and drizzle over.

notes: Use firm-ripe pears that hold their shape on the grill.
Peaches also work in summer.

title: Barbecue Broccolini with Garlic, Lemon and Almonds
summary: Blistered broccolini tossed with garlic, lemon and chilli flakes, a quick grilled side.

steps.text: Blanch the broccolini in boiling water for 1 minute, then drain and dry well.
Toss with half the oil and grill on a hot barbecue for 3 to 4 minutes until charred and tender.
Warm the garlic in the remaining oil for 1 minute until fragrant.
Toss the broccolini with the garlic oil, lemon juice and zest, chilli flakes, almonds and salt.

notes: Do not let the garlic brown or it turns bitter.
Good with grilled fish or steak.

title: Grilled Capsicum and White Bean Salad
summary: Charred capsicum with creamy cannellini beans, red onion, parsley and a sharp red wine dressing.

items.raw: 2 x 400 g cans cannellini beans, drained

steps.text: Grill the capsicums skin-side up on a hot barbecue for 10 to 12 minutes until blackened, then cover and rest for 10 minutes.
Peel off the skins and slice the flesh.
Whisk the oil, vinegar, garlic and salt.
Toss the capsicum, beans, onion and parsley with the dressing.

notes: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge and improves overnight.
Serve with grilled sausages or lamb.

title: Barbecue Baked Potatoes with Sour Cream and Chives
summary: Foil-wrapped potatoes cooked in the coals until fluffy, split and loaded with sour cream and chives.

steps.text: Prick the potatoes, rub with the oil and salt, and wrap each tightly in foil.
Cook on a covered barbecue or in the coals for 50 to 60 minutes, turning once, until a skewer slides in easily.
Split each potato and fluff the flesh with a fork.
Add butter, sour cream, cheddar and chives.

notes: Cook on indirect heat so the skins do not burn.
Try adding crisp bacon pieces for a loaded version.

title: Garlic Bread Foil Parcels
summary: Crusty bread slathered with garlic parsley butter, wrapped in foil and heated on the barbecue.

steps.text: Mash the butter with the garlic, parsley and salt.
Slice the baguette on the diagonal without cutting right through and spread the butter between the slices.
Wrap tightly in foil and heat on the barbecue for 10 to 12 minutes, turning once, until hot and the butter has melted through.
Open the foil for the last 2 minutes to crisp the crust.

notes: Add grated cheddar between the slices for cheesy garlic bread.
Garlic butter freezes well for 2 months.

title: Sticky Barbecue Sweet Potato Wedges
summary: Crisp-edged sweet potato wedges glazed with a smoky, sweet barbecue sauce at the end.

items.raw: 800 g sweet potato, cut into wedges

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C and toss the wedges with the oil, paprika and salt on a tray.
Roast for 25 minutes, turning once, until the edges are crisp.
Mix the barbecue sauce and honey, brush over the wedges and roast for 8 to 10 minutes until sticky and caramelised, then scatter with chives.

notes: Do not crowd the tray, or the wedges steam.
Serve with sour cream and chives.

title: Honey Soy Grilled Mushrooms
summary: Meaty field mushrooms basted with honey, soy and garlic and grilled until deeply browned.

steps.text: Whisk the soy sauce, honey, oil, garlic and ginger together.
Brush the mushrooms with the glaze and grill, gill-side up, for 5 minutes.
Flip, brush again and grill for 5 to 6 minutes until deeply browned and tender.
Scatter with sesame seeds and spring onions.

notes: Wipe the mushrooms rather than washing them.
Serve with steak or in a burger bun.

title: Zucchini and Corn Fritters for the Barbecue
summary: Golden pan fritters of grated zucchini and corn, cooked on the barbecue flat plate.

steps.text: Squeeze the zucchini in a clean cloth to remove the water.
Mix the zucchini, corn, flour, eggs, milk, cheddar and chives into a thick batter.
Heat the oil on a barbecue flat plate or pan and cook spoonfuls for 3 minutes each side until golden and cooked through.

notes: Food safety: cook the fritters until the centres are firm and no longer wet, especially for pregnant women, older people and young children.
Serve with sweet chilli sauce and yoghurt.

title: Chimichurri Corn Salad
summary: Sweet grilled corn kernels tossed with a punchy parsley chimichurri, tomato and red onion.

steps.text: Grill the corn for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until charred in spots, then cut the kernels from the cobs.
Blend the parsley, garlic, oil, vinegar, chilli flakes and salt into a loose chimichurri.
Toss the corn, tomatoes and onion with the chimichurri.

notes: Serve warm or at room temperature.
Keeps for 2 days in the fridge.

title: Lemon Garlic Aioli
summary: A quick garlic mayonnaise with plenty of lemon, perfect with chips, seafood and grilled vegetables.

steps.text: Stir the garlic into the mayonnaise with the lemon zest, juice and mustard.
Whisk in the olive oil until smooth and glossy.
Rest for 15 minutes so the garlic mellows, then taste for salt.

notes: Keeps for 5 days in the fridge.
Use a microplane to crush the garlic so it blends smoothly.

title: Sriracha Mayo
summary: A creamy, medium-hot dipping sauce with lime and a hint of honey, made in two minutes.

steps.text: Whisk the mayonnaise, sriracha, lime juice, honey and garlic until smooth.
Taste and add more sriracha for extra heat.
Chill until cold before serving.

notes: Spread it on burgers or sushi bowls.
Keeps for 1 week in the fridge.

title: Gochujang Mayo Dip
summary: A sweet, spicy and savoury Korean-inspired dip for fries, dumplings and fried chicken.

steps.text: Measure the mayonnaise, gochujang, vinegar, sesame oil and honey into a bowl.
Whisk until completely smooth, then stir in the sesame seeds.
Chill the dip until cold and thick before serving.

notes: Thin with a splash of water for a drizzle.
Keeps for 5 days in the fridge.

title: Minted Yoghurt Sauce
summary: A cooling mint and cucumber yoghurt sauce for grilled lamb, kebabs and spicy curries.

steps.text: Squeeze the grated cucumber to remove the extra water.
Stir the yoghurt, cucumber, mint, garlic, lemon juice, cumin and salt together.
Chill for 15 minutes until cold and the flavours have blended.

notes: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.
Use as a dip with warm flatbread.

title: Horseradish Cream
summary: A sharp, creamy sauce for roast beef, smoked salmon and ham, made with just five ingredients.

steps.text: Stir the sour cream, horseradish, mustard and lemon juice together in a bowl.
Fold in the chives and chill until cold.
Taste and add more horseradish for a stronger bite.

notes: Keeps for 4 days in the fridge.
Add a pinch of sugar if the horseradish is very sharp.

title: Pearl Barley Salad with Roasted Carrots and Feta
summary: Chewy barley, caramelised carrots, feta and parsley in a lemon dressing, good warm or cold.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C and toss the carrots with the oil and cumin on a tray.
Roast for 25 minutes, turning once, until the edges are browned and the carrots are tender.
Simmer the barley in plenty of salted water for 30 minutes until tender but still chewy, then drain well.
Toss the warm barley with the lemon juice, extra oil, salt and parsley, then fold through the carrots and feta.

notes: Swap the barley for farro-style grains only if your pantry has them; wheat berries also work.
Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Quinoa, Chickpea and Cucumber Salad with Lemon Tahini
summary: A vegan protein salad of fluffy quinoa, chickpeas and crunchy cucumber with a creamy lemon tahini dressing.

steps.text: Simmer the quinoa in 2 cups of water for 12 minutes until the water is absorbed, then rest covered for 5 minutes and fluff with a fork.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, water and salt until smooth and pourable.
Toss the cooled quinoa with the chickpeas, cucumber, tomatoes and parsley.
Drizzle with the dressing and toss until everything is coated.

notes: Add a handful of toasted pumpkin seeds for crunch.
Keeps 3 days in the fridge; add the dressing just before serving.

title: Brown Rice, Edamame and Carrot Salad with Sesame Ginger Dressing
summary: Nutty brown rice with edamame, shredded carrot and spring onion in a gingery sesame dressing.

steps.text: Simmer the rice in 2 1/2 cups of water, covered, for 30 minutes until tender, then rinse under cold water and drain.
Boil the edamame for 3 minutes until bright green and tender, then drain.
Whisk the soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, ginger and honey together.
Toss the rice with the edamame, carrot, spring onion and dressing, then scatter over the sesame seeds.

notes: Use tamari for a gluten-free version.
Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Lentil and Roasted Carrot Salad with Parsley and Pumpkin Seeds
summary: Earthy green lentils with sweet roasted carrot, herbs and toasted seeds.

steps.text: Roast the carrots with the oil at 200°C for 25 minutes until golden and tender.
Simmer the lentils in plenty of water for 22 minutes until tender but not mushy, then drain.
Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan for 3 minutes until they pop.
Whisk the vinegar, extra oil, mustard and salt, then toss everything together with the parsley.

notes: Vegan and gluten-free as written.
Good with a spoonful of yoghurt on top.

title: Quinoa Tabbouleh with Mint and Tomato
summary: A gluten-free take on tabbouleh using fluffy quinoa, loads of herbs and ripe tomato.

steps.text: Simmer the quinoa in 1 1/2 cups of water for 12 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Rest covered for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork and spread out until cool.
Mix the cooled millet with the tomato, parsley, mint and spring onion.
Dress with the lemon juice, oil and salt and toss until glossy.

notes: Drain the diced tomato briefly so the salad does not turn watery.
Best eaten the day it is made.

title: Chicken, Quinoa and Avocado Power Bowl Salad
summary: A high-protein salad of shredded chicken, quinoa, avocado and lime-dressed greens.

steps.text: Poach the chicken in simmering salted water for 15 minutes until cooked through with no pink and the juices run clear, then shred.
Simmer the quinoa in 2 cups of water for 12 minutes until the water is absorbed, then fluff and cool slightly.
Whisk the lime juice, oil, cumin and salt.
Toss the quinoa, spinach, corn and capsicum with the dressing, then top with the chicken and avocado.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken until it reaches 75°C in the thickest part; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Slice the avocado just before serving.

title: Lentil and Grilled Halloumi Salad with Roasted Capsicum
summary: Savoury lentils, squeaky halloumi and smoky capsicum in a lemony dressing.

steps.text: Simmer the lentils in plenty of water for 22 minutes until tender but not mushy, then drain.
Grill the capsicum skin-side up under a hot grill for 10 minutes until blistered, then slice.
Fry the halloumi in a dry non-stick pan for 2 minutes each side until golden.
Whisk the lemon juice, oil, cumin, garlic and salt, toss with the lentils, capsicum and rocket, then top with the halloumi.

notes: Halloumi is made with rennet-free options in some brands; check the label if you need it vegetarian.
Serve warm.

title: Soft-Boiled Egg, Edamame and Brown Rice Salad Jars
summary: Make-ahead lunch jars layered with brown rice, edamame, cucumber and a jammy egg.

steps.text: Simmer the rice in 2 1/2 cups of water, covered, for 30 minutes until tender, then cool.
Boil the eggs for 7 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks jammy, then cool in cold water and peel.
Boil the edamame for 3 minutes until tender, then drain.
Whisk the soy sauce, vinegar and sesame oil into the base of each jar, then layer the rice, edamame, cucumber and carrot, and top with the halved egg and sesame seeds.

notes: Food safety: use fresh eggs, keep the jars chilled and eat within 2 days; pregnant women, older people and young children should have the eggs boiled hard.
Shake or tip the jar into a bowl to serve.

title: Smoked Salmon, Chickpea and Dill Yoghurt Salad
summary: Flaked smoked salmon over crisp chickpeas, cucumber and a cool dill yoghurt dressing.

steps.text: Stir the yoghurt, dill, lemon juice and salt together until smooth.
Toss the chickpeas, cucumber, onion and leaves together in a large bowl.
Divide between plates, top with the smoked salmon and spoon over the dill yoghurt until generously coated.

notes: Food safety: smoked salmon is a ready-to-eat chilled fish; pregnant women, older people and those with weakened immunity should avoid it and use hot-cooked salmon instead.
Keep chilled until serving.

title: Crisp Tofu and Soba Salad with Peanut Lime Dressing
summary: Golden tofu cubes and cold soba with crunchy veg in a lime peanut dressing.

steps.text: Pat the tofu dry and fry in the oil over medium-high heat for 8 minutes, turning, until golden on all sides.
Boil the soba for 5 minutes until just tender, then rinse under cold water and drain.
Whisk the peanut butter, lime juice, soy sauce, maple syrup and warm water until smooth.
Toss the noodles, carrot, cabbage and spring onion with the dressing and top with the tofu.

notes: Use 100 percent buckwheat soba and tamari for a gluten-free version.
Add chilli flakes for heat.

title: Cottage Cheese, Tomato and Basil Protein Salad Bowl
summary: A no-cook high-protein bowl of cottage cheese with juicy tomato, cucumber, basil and olives.

steps.text: Spoon the cottage cheese into two bowls, chilled until you are ready to serve.
Pile the tomato, cucumber and olives over the top.
Drizzle with the oil and vinegar, scatter over the basil and pepper, and serve straight away.

notes: Add a boiled egg for extra protein.
Use dairy-free cottage cheese substitutes only if they are labelled to suit.

title: Beef and Black Bean Taco Salad
summary: Spiced beef mince and black beans over crisp lettuce with corn, tomato and a lime yoghurt dressing.

steps.text: Brown the mince in the oil over high heat for 6 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains.
Stir in the spice mix and beans and cook for 3 minutes until hot and sticky.
Stir the yoghurt and lime juice together.
Pile the lettuce, corn, tomato and avocado onto plates, top with the beef mixture, cheddar and the lime yoghurt.

notes: Food safety: cook mince until it reaches 75°C throughout with no pink; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Crush a few corn chips over the top if you like.

title: Shaved Cabbage, Apple and Walnut Autumn Salad
summary: Crunchy shaved cabbage with crisp apple, toasted walnuts and a mustardy cider dressing.

items.raw: 2 crisp red apples, sliced into matchsticks

steps.text: Whisk the vinegar, oil, mustard, honey and salt together until emulsified.
Toss the cabbage and apple with the dressing straight away, until coated, so the apple does not brown.
Fold through the walnuts and parsley and serve.

notes: Rest 10 minutes for a softer slaw.
Use maple syrup for a vegan version.

title: Sauteed Asparagus with Garlic and Lemon Zest
summary: Spring asparagus tossed quickly in garlic butter and finished with lemon zest.

items.raw: 2 bunches asparagus, woody ends snapped off

steps.text: Melt the butter in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.
Add the asparagus and cook for 4 minutes, turning, until bright green and just tender.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant, then toss through the lemon zest, salt and pepper.

notes: Thick spears may need 1 extra minute.
Use olive oil for a dairy-free side.

title: Charred Broccolini with Chilli Garlic Oil
summary: Blistered broccolini glugged with warm garlic and chilli oil.

steps.text: Blanch the broccolini in boiling water for 1 minute until bright green, then drain and pat dry.
Char in a hot dry frying pan for 4 minutes, turning, until blistered in spots.
Warm the oil with the garlic and chilli over low heat for 2 minutes until the garlic is pale gold.
Pour the oil over the broccolini and finish with the lemon juice and salt.

notes: Watch the garlic closely; it turns bitter if it browns.
Good with grilled fish.
Food safety: Keep any leftover garlic, herb or chilli oil in the fridge and use it within 4 days.

title: Zucchini Ribbons with Ricotta, Mint and Lemon
summary: Raw zucchini ribbons tossed with creamy ricotta, fresh mint and lemon.

steps.text: Shave the zucchini into long ribbons with a vegetable peeler.
Toss the ribbons with the lemon juice, oil and salt in a bowl.
Spoon the ricotta over the top and scatter with the mint, lemon zest and pine nuts until evenly covered.

notes: Serve straight away; the zucchini weeps if left.
Toast pine nuts until golden for the best flavour.

title: Buttered New Potatoes with Dill and Peas
summary: Waxy new potatoes tossed with butter, sweet peas and fresh dill.

steps.text: Cover the potatoes with cold salted water and simmer for 15 minutes until a knife slides in easily.
Add the peas for the last 2 minutes of cooking until bright green and hot.
Drain well and return to the pot, then toss with the butter, dill, lemon juice and salt until glossy.

notes: Mint works well in place of dill.
Use olive oil to keep it dairy-free.

title: Roasted Radishes with Brown Butter and Chives
summary: Halved radishes roasted until sweet and mellow, finished with nutty brown butter.

steps.text: Toss the radishes with the oil and salt on a tray and roast at 220°C for 15 minutes until tender and golden at the edges.
Melt the butter in a small pan over medium heat for 3 minutes, swirling, until it smells nutty and turns light brown.
Pour the brown butter over the radishes with the lemon juice and toss until coated, then scatter with chives.

notes: Roasting takes away the peppery bite.
Leave a little stalk on for looks.

title: Creamed Spinach with Nutmeg
summary: Silky wilted spinach in a light béchamel with a grating of nutmeg.

steps.text: Squeeze the thawed spinach hard in a clean cloth to remove the water.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute until bubbling.
Whisk in the milk a little at a time and simmer for 4 minutes, stirring, until thick and smooth.
Stir in the spinach, nutmeg, salt and pepper and cook for 3 minutes until hot.

notes: Add a splash of cream for a richer finish.
Reheats well.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Vegan Cashew Basil Pesto
summary: A dairy-free pesto using cashews and nutritional yeast for a cheesy depth.

steps.text: Pulse the cashews, garlic and nutritional yeast in a food processor until coarsely ground.
Add the basil, lemon juice and salt and pulse until finely chopped.
With the motor running, drizzle in the oil until the pesto is thick and green, then taste for salt.

notes: Keeps 5 days in the fridge under a layer of oil, or freezes for 3 months.
Toss through 400 g of cooked pasta.

title: Classic Basil Pesto with Vegetarian Hard Cheese
summary: Bright Genoese-style pesto made with pine nuts and a vegetarian hard cheese.

steps.text: Crush or pulse the garlic, pine nuts and salt in a food processor until a coarse paste forms.
Add the basil and pulse until finely chopped.
Stir in the cheese, then drizzle in the oil until the pesto is thick and glossy.

notes: Parmesan is not vegetarian because it uses animal rennet; use a vegetarian hard cheese.
Keeps 5 days in the fridge under a layer of oil.

title: Mexican Salsa Verde with Coriander and Green Chilli
summary: Tangy cooked green salsa with green chilli, lime and coriander.

steps.text: Simmer the green tomatoes, chillies, onion and garlic in 1/2 cup of water for 10 minutes until very soft.
Blend with the coriander, lime juice, salt and oil until smooth but still a little textured.
Cool and taste, adding more lime or salt as needed.

notes: Seed the chillies for a milder sauce.
Keeps 5 days in the fridge.

title: Peppery Rocket and Walnut Pesto
summary: A punchy rocket pesto with toasted walnuts and lemon, great on pasta or toast.

steps.text: Pulse the walnuts and garlic in a food processor until coarsely ground.
Add the rocket, cheese, lemon juice and salt and pulse until a rough paste forms.
Drizzle in the oil with the motor running until thick and spoonable.

notes: Use a vegetarian hard cheese; parmesan is not vegetarian.
Keeps 5 days in the fridge.

title: Tahini and Parsley Green Sauce
summary: A creamy, tangy green sauce of parsley, tahini and lemon for falafel, fish and roast vegetables.

steps.text: Blitz the parsley, garlic and lemon juice in a food processor until finely chopped.
Add the tahini and salt, then pour in the water with the motor running until the sauce is smooth and pourable.
Taste and add more lemon or salt until balanced.

notes: Thickens in the fridge; loosen with a splash of water.
Keeps 5 days.

title: Thai Green Chilli, Lime and Coriander Dipping Sauce
summary: A sharp, fragrant sauce of green chilli, lime, garlic and coriander for grilled meat and fish.

steps.text: Crush the chillies, garlic and sugar in a mortar until a rough paste forms.
Stir in the lime juice, fish sauce and water until the sugar dissolves.
Fold through the coriander and taste for a balance of sour, salty and sweet.

notes: Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
Use soy sauce in place of fish sauce for a vegetarian version.

title: Vegan Oat Porridge with Stewed Apple and Cinnamon
summary: Creamy oats cooked in soy milk with soft cinnamon apple, entirely plant-based.

steps.text: Simmer the apples with 2 tbsp of water and half the cinnamon for 6 minutes until soft.
Cook the oats with the soy milk and salt over medium heat for 6 minutes, stirring, until thick and creamy.
Spoon into bowls, top with the apple, maple syrup and walnuts.

notes: Use certified gluten-free oats for coeliacs.
Stewed apple keeps 4 days.

title: Gluten-Free Buckwheat Pancakes with Cinnamon Apple
summary: Light buckwheat flour pancakes with a sharp spoonful of cinnamon apple.

items.raw: 1 tbsp butter, extra, for the pan

steps.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder, egg, milk and melted butter into a smooth batter and rest 5 minutes.
Simmer the apples with the honey, a pinch of cinnamon and 2 tbsp of water for 5 minutes until soft and syrupy.
Cook ladlefuls of batter in a buttered pan over medium heat for 2 minutes a side until golden and cooked through.
Stack the pancakes and spoon over the apple.

notes: Food safety: cook the pancakes until the centres are set and no longer wet, especially for pregnant women, older people and young children.
Check the buckwheat flour label if cooking for coeliacs.

title: Vegan Chickpea Flour Pancakes with Spinach and Tomato
summary: Savoury besan pancakes cooked with spinach and cherry tomatoes, no egg or dairy.

steps.text: Whisk the chickpea flour, water, turmeric, cumin and salt into a smooth batter and stir in the spinach.
Heat half the oil in a non-stick pan and pour in half the batter, scattering with tomatoes.
Cook for 3 minutes until the base is golden and the top is set, then flip and cook 2 minutes more until firm.
Repeat with the remaining oil and batter.

notes: Let the batter sit 10 minutes for a softer texture.
Serve with coconut yoghurt.

title: Tofu Scramble with Turmeric, Kale and Cherry Tomatoes
summary: Savoury crumbled tofu scramble with kale and cherry tomatoes, vegan and high in protein.

steps.text: Crumble the tofu into a bowl with your hands.
Heat the oil in a frying pan, add the tofu, turmeric and cumin and cook for 5 minutes until the edges colour and most of the water has gone.
Stir in the kale, tomatoes and soy sauce and cook for 3 minutes until the kale wilts.
Finish with the nutritional yeast and pepper.

notes: Serve on toast with avocado. For gluten-free, use tamari instead of soy sauce and gluten-free toast.
Use tamari for gluten-free.

title: Gluten-Free Quinoa Breakfast Bowl with Cinnamon Pears
summary: Warm quinoa simmered in milk with spiced pears and toasted seeds.

steps.text: Simmer the quinoa with the milk and water for 15 minutes until soft and the liquid is mostly absorbed.
Cook the pears in a small pan with the cinnamon and 2 tbsp of water for 5 minutes until tender.
Spoon the quinoa into bowls, top with the pears, maple syrup and pumpkin seeds.

notes: Use oat or soy milk to make it vegan.
Quinoa keeps 4 days cooked for quick bowls.

title: Vegan Coconut Jasmine Rice Porridge with Lime and Mango
summary: Creamy coconut milk rice pudding, topped with fresh mango.

steps.text: Simmer the rice with the coconut milk, water and salt, stirring often, for 28 minutes until the rice is very soft and the pudding is thick.
Stir through the maple syrup.
Serve warm in bowls topped with the mango and toasted coconut.

notes: Stir often at the end to prevent sticking.
Thin with a splash of water if it thickens on standing.

title: Gluten-Free Polenta Porridge with Maple and Walnuts
summary: Soft, creamy cornmeal porridge sweetened with maple and topped with crunchy walnuts.

steps.text: Bring the water, milk and salt to a gentle simmer until steaming.
Whisk in the polenta in a thin stream and cook for 12 minutes, stirring often, until thick and no longer gritty.
Serve in bowls topped with maple syrup, walnuts and cinnamon.

notes: Use soy milk for dairy-free.
Leftovers set firm; slice and pan-fry.

title: Vegan Savoury Oats with Mushrooms and Soy
summary: Savoury rolled oats cooked in stock with fried mushrooms and spring onion.

steps.text: Fry the mushrooms in the oil over high heat for 5 minutes until golden and the liquid has gone.
Simmer the oats in the stock for 6 minutes, stirring, until thick and creamy.
Stir in the soy sauce, then top with the mushrooms, spring onion and sesame oil.

notes: Add a soft egg for non-vegan protein.
Use tamari and gluten-free oats for coeliacs.

title: Smoky Sweet Potato, Capsicum and Bean Hash, Vegan
summary: Crisp sweet potato cubes, black beans and capsicum with smoky paprika.

steps.text: Fry the sweet potato in the oil over medium heat for 15 minutes, turning, until tender and browned.
Add the capsicum, paprika, cumin and salt and cook for 5 minutes until softened.
Stir in the beans and cook for 3 minutes until hot.
Top with spring onion and avocado.

notes: Cover the pan for the first 5 minutes to soften the sweet potato faster.
Add a squeeze of lime.

title: Japanese Breakfast Rice Bowl with Soft Egg and Nori
summary: Warm rice topped with a soft-boiled egg, nori and soy for a quick Japanese-style breakfast.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 6 1/2 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks soft, then cool in cold water and peel.
Divide the warm rice between bowls and drizzle with the sesame oil.
Top with the halved eggs, nori, spring onion, soy sauce and sesame seeds.

notes: Food safety: soft yolks carry a small salmonella risk; pregnant women, older people and young children should boil eggs until firm.
Cool leftover rice and refrigerate within 1 hour; reheat until steaming hot and eat within 1 day.

title: Mexican Breakfast Bowl with Black Beans, Eggs and Salsa
summary: Black beans, rice and fried eggs topped with fresh salsa and avocado.

steps.text: Warm the beans and rice together in a small pan for 3 minutes until hot.
Mix the tomato, onion, coriander, lime juice and salt for a quick salsa.
Fry the eggs in the oil over medium heat for 3 minutes until the whites are set and opaque.
Spoon the rice and beans into bowls and top with the eggs, salsa and avocado.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set; pregnant women, older people and young children should have yolks firm.
Add hot sauce to taste.

title: Turkish Menemen Breakfast Bowl with Yoghurt
summary: Soft scrambled eggs cooked in a pepper and tomato sauce, served over cool garlic yoghurt.

steps.text: Fry the capsicum in the oil for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes and chilli and simmer for 6 minutes until thick and jammy.
Crack the eggs in and stir gently for 3 minutes until just set but still creamy and cooked through.
Spoon the yoghurt mixed with garlic and salt into bowls, top with the eggs and parsley.

notes: Food safety: cook eggs until fully set, especially for pregnant women, older people and young children.
Serve with crusty bread.

title: Savoury Masala Oats Bowl with Peas and Carrot
summary: Spiced savoury oats cooked with onion, peas and carrot, a quick Indian-style breakfast.

steps.text: Fry the cumin seeds in the oil for 30 seconds until they sizzle, then add the onion and cook 4 minutes until soft.
Add the carrot, garam masala and turmeric and cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in the oats, water, peas and salt and simmer for 6 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Serve topped with coriander.

notes: Add a squeeze of lemon to brighten.
Use gluten-free oats for coeliacs.

title: Middle Eastern Shakshuka Grain Bowl
summary: Warm barley or rice topped with eggs poached in a spiced tomato sauce.

steps.text: Fry the onion and capsicum in the oil for 6 minutes until soft.
Stir in the cumin, paprika, tomatoes and salt and simmer for 8 minutes until thick.
Make two wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 5 minutes until the whites are set.
Spoon the barley into bowls, top with the eggs and sauce, and scatter with parsley.

notes: Food safety: cook eggs until the whites are firm and the yolks are not runny for pregnant women, older people and young children.
Add feta if you like.

title: Vietnamese Egg and Pork Rice Breakfast Bowl
summary: Rice topped with a fried egg, savoury caramelised pork mince and fresh cucumber.

steps.text: Fry the pork mince with the garlic for 6 minutes, breaking it up, until browned with no pink left.
Stir in the fish sauce and sugar and cook for 2 minutes until sticky.
Fry the eggs in the oil for 3 minutes until the whites are crisp at the edges and set.
Serve the rice topped with the pork, eggs, cucumber and spring onion.

notes: Food safety: cook pork mince to 75°C throughout with no pink; cook eggs until whites are set, firm yolks for pregnant women, older people and young children.
Add chilli sauce.

title: Hangover Bacon, Egg and Cheese Brekkie Rolls
summary: Soft rolls stuffed with crisp bacon and a fried egg, a classic hangover fix.

steps.text: Fry the bacon in the oil for 5 minutes, turning, until crisp.
Fry the eggs in the same pan for 3 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks are cooked as you like.
Butter the rolls, fill with the bacon, eggs and cheddar until the cheese melts, and add the tomato sauce.

notes: Food safety: cook eggs until the whites and yolks are fully set for pregnant women, older people and young children; cook bacon until no pink remains.
Add a slice of cheese for extra comfort.

title: Hangover Fry-Up Tray Bake
summary: Sausages, bacon, tomatoes, mushrooms and eggs baked on one tray for an easy fry-up.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C and arrange the sausages and bacon on a large tray with the tomatoes and mushrooms, drizzled with oil.
Bake for 18 minutes, turning the sausages once, until golden and sausages are cooked through with no pink.
Make four gaps, crack in the eggs, and bake 6 minutes more until the whites are set.
Toast the bread until golden and serve with the tray bake and pepper.

notes: Food safety: cook sausages to 75°C throughout with no pink; cook eggs until fully set for pregnant women, older people and young children.
Add baked beans in a small ovenproof dish.

title: Hangover Cheesy Baked Beans on Toast with Fried Egg
summary: Hot baked beans melted with cheddar on buttered toast, topped with a fried egg.

steps.text: Warm the beans with the Worcestershire sauce in a saucepan for 4 minutes until bubbling, then stir through the cheddar until melted.
Fry the eggs in the oil for 3 minutes until the whites are set.
Butter the toast, spoon over the beans until generously covered and top with the eggs.

notes: Food safety: cook eggs until fully set for pregnant women, older people and young children.
Worcestershire sauce contains anchovy, so it is not vegetarian.

title: Hangover Ginger and Spring Onion Rice Congee
summary: A soothing rice porridge with fresh ginger, soy and a soft egg, easy on the stomach.

steps.text: Simmer the rice with the water and ginger, stirring now and then, for 30 minutes until the grains break down into a thick porridge.
Crack the eggs into the simmering congee and cook for 3 minutes until the whites are set.
Season with the soy sauce and pepper and serve topped with spring onion and sesame oil.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until firm for pregnant women, older people and young children.
Add shredded chicken to make it more filling.

title: Hangover Egg Drop Miso Soup with Rice
summary: Warm miso broth with ribbons of egg, tofu and a scoop of rice.

steps.text: Bring the water and dashi to a gentle simmer until steaming.
Dissolve the miso paste in a ladleful of the hot dashi, then stir it back into the pot without boiling.
Pour in the egg in a thin stream, stirring gently, and cook 1 minute until it forms ribbons and is set.
Add the tofu, heat for 1 minute until warm, and ladle over the rice with spring onion.

notes: Food safety: eggs are cooked fully set in the hot broth.
Dashi granules contain fish; use a kombu stock for vegetarian.

title: Hangover Spicy Egg Breakfast Burrito
summary: Scrambled eggs, beans, cheese and hot sauce wrapped in a warm tortilla.

steps.text: Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 20 seconds each until pliable.
Melt the butter and scramble the eggs over medium heat for 3 minutes, stirring, until just set and cooked through.
Fill the tortillas with the eggs, beans, cheese, tomato and hot sauce.
Roll up tightly and toast in the pan for 1 minute a side until golden.

notes: Food safety: cook eggs until fully set for pregnant women, older people and young children.
Wrap in foil to take out.

title: Hangover Hash Brown Stack with Egg and Bacon
summary: Crisp potato hash brown topped with bacon, a poached egg and chives.

steps.text: Squeeze the grated potato dry in a cloth and mix with the salt.
Fry two large mounds in the oil for 6 minutes a side, pressing flat, until crisp and golden.
Cook the bacon in a pan for 5 minutes until crisp.
Poach the eggs in barely simmering water with the vinegar for 3 minutes until the whites are set, then stack on the hash browns with the bacon and chives.

notes: Food safety: cook bacon until no pink remains and eggs until whites are fully set for pregnant women, older people and young children.
Add hollandaise if you are brave.

title: Clear Chicken Stock from Roasted Bones
summary: A golden, clear chicken stock built from roasted bones, aromatics and a long, gentle simmer.

steps.text: Roast the chicken bones at 220°C for 35 minutes until deep golden.
Tip the bones into a large pot with the onion, carrot, celery, garlic, bay and peppercorns, and cover with the cold water.
Bring to a bare simmer over medium heat, skimming the scum, then reduce the heat so only a few bubbles break the surface.
Simmer uncovered for 3 hours, topping up with water if needed, until rich and golden.
Strain through a fine sieve, cool quickly and chill; lift the set fat off the top. Check the meat on the wings has reached at least 75°C.

notes: Food safety: the stock must simmer well above 75°C, cool within 2 hours and keep in the fridge for 3 days or freeze for 3 months; reheat until boiling hot.
Never salt the stock; season whatever you make with it.

title: Roasted Vegetable Stock with Leek and Mushroom
summary: A deeply savoury vegetable stock from roasted onion, leek, mushroom and herbs.

steps.text: Roast the onions, leeks, carrots, mushrooms and garlic with the oil at 220°C for 30 minutes until browned at the edges.
Tip into a large pot with the parsley, bay, peppercorns and water.
Bring to the boil, then simmer gently for 1 hour until the stock tastes rich and savoury.
Strain through a fine sieve and cool.

notes: Keeps 4 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen.
Skip the cabbage family; it turns the stock bitter.

title: Rich Brown Beef Stock from Roasted Bones
summary: A deep, glossy brown stock from well-roasted beef bones and vegetables, the base for gravies and French onion soup.

steps.text: Roast the bones at 230°C for 45 minutes, turning once, until deep brown.
Smear the vegetables with the tomato paste and roast them alongside for the last 25 minutes until caramelised.
Tip everything into a large pot with the bay and peppercorns and cover with the cold water.
Bring to a bare simmer, skim well, then cook gently uncovered for 5 hours until the stock is rich and brown.
Strain through a fine sieve, cool quickly and lift off the fat once chilled.

notes: Do not boil hard or the stock turns cloudy.
Food safety: cool within 2 hours, keep in the fridge up to 4 days or freeze for 3 months, and reheat until boiling hot. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Clear Fish Stock from Snapper Frames
summary: A light, sweet fish stock simmered only 25 minutes so it stays clean and clear.

items.raw: 1 kg white fish frames, gills removed

steps.text: Rinse the fish frames well under cold water until the water runs clear.
Place everything in a pot, bring to a bare simmer and skim until the surface is clear.
Simmer gently for 25 minutes, no longer, until the fish flesh turns opaque and flakes and the stock is fragrant.
Strain through a fine sieve and cool quickly.

notes: Food safety: cool within 1 hour, keep in the fridge up to 2 days or freeze for 3 months.
Boiling or simmering past 30 minutes makes it bitter.

title: Ham Hock and Bay Bone Broth
summary: A smoky, collagen-rich broth from ham hock with bay, onion and peppercorns.

steps.text: Place the ham hock and vegetables in a large pot with the bay, peppercorns and vinegar and cover with cold water.
Bring to a bare simmer and skim, then cook gently for 3 hours until the meat falls from the bone.
Lift out the hock, pull off the meat and keep it for soup.
Strain the broth through a fine sieve and cool.

notes: Taste before salting; ham hock stock is salty.
Food safety: cool within 2 hours, keep in the fridge up to 4 days, and reheat until boiling hot. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Roasted Carrot and Ginger Bisque
summary: Smooth, sweet carrot soup roasted until caramelised, with fresh ginger and a swirl of cream.

steps.text: Roast the carrots and onion with the oil at 200°C for 25 minutes until golden and soft.
Simmer with the ginger and stock for 10 minutes until completely tender.
Blend until silky smooth, stir in the cream and salt, and reheat gently until steaming.
Ladle into bowls and sprinkle with chives.

notes: Use coconut cream for dairy-free.
Freezes well without the cream for 3 months.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Roasted Pumpkin and Coconut Bisque
summary: Velvety pumpkin soup roasted with garlic and finished with coconut cream and lime.

steps.text: Roast the pumpkin, onion and garlic with the oil at 200°C for 30 minutes until soft and browned.
Simmer with the stock for 5 minutes until hot.
Blend until smooth, stir in the coconut cream, lime juice and salt, and reheat until steaming.
Serve with a pinch of chilli.

notes: Naturally vegan and gluten-free if the stock is.
Freezes well for 3 months.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Thick Cream of Mushroom Soup
summary: Earthy, creamy mushroom soup with browned mushrooms, thyme and a splash of cream.

steps.text: Fry the mushrooms in the butter over high heat for 8 minutes until golden and the liquid has gone.
Add the onion, garlic and thyme and cook for 4 minutes until soft.
Stir in the flour, then add the stock gradually and simmer for 10 minutes until thickened.
Blend half the soup until smooth, return to the pot and stir in the cream and salt until hot.

notes: Use vegetable stock for vegetarian.
Do not boil after adding the cream.

title: Sweet Corn Bisque with Chilli Oil
summary: Silky corn soup blended with potato and finished with a drizzle of chilli oil.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes until translucent.
Add the corn, potato and stock and simmer for 15 minutes until the potato is very tender.
Blend until completely smooth and press through a sieve for extra silkiness.
Stir in the milk and salt, reheat until steaming and drizzle with chilli oil.

notes: Fresh sweetcorn off 4 cobs works well in summer.
Freezes for 2 months.
Food safety: Keep any leftover garlic, herb or chilli oil in the fridge and use it within 4 days. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Cauliflower and Cheddar Bisque
summary: Creamy roasted cauliflower soup enriched with mature cheddar and a hint of mustard.

steps.text: Roast the cauliflower and onion with the oil at 200°C for 25 minutes until golden and tender.
Simmer with the stock and milk for 8 minutes until hot.
Blend until smooth, then stir in the cheddar and mustard until melted.
Season with the salt and reheat gently until steaming.

notes: Cheddar made with animal rennet is not suitable for vegetarians; choose a vegetarian cheddar.
Freezes for 2 months.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Kids' Chicken Noodle Soup for the Thermos
summary: A mild chicken soup with tiny noodles and soft vegetables, ideal for a school lunchbox thermos.

steps.text: Simmer the chicken in the stock for 12 minutes until cooked through with no pink, then lift out and shred.
Add the carrot, celery and pasta to the stock and simmer for 8 minutes until the pasta is tender.
Return the chicken with the peas and cook for 2 minutes until hot, then stir in the parsley.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C throughout; keep the soup above 60°C in the thermos by pre-heating it with boiling water, and eat within 4 hours.
Use low-salt stock for little ones.

title: Kids' Creamy Tomato Soup with Cheese Toast Dippers
summary: Smooth mild tomato soup with strips of cheesy toast for dunking.

steps.text: Soften the onion and carrot in the oil for 6 minutes until tender.
Add the tomatoes and stock and simmer for 15 minutes until thick.
Blend until smooth and stir in the milk.
Top the bread with cheddar, grill for 3 minutes until bubbling, then cut into strips for dipping.

notes: Add a pinch of sugar if the tomatoes are sharp.
Freezes for 3 months.

title: Kids' Mild Veggie Minestrone for the Lunchbox
summary: A gentle vegetable and small pasta soup with no spice, perfect for a thermos.

steps.text: Soften the carrot, zucchini and celery in the oil for 5 minutes until tender.
Add the tomatoes and stock and simmer for 10 minutes until the vegetables are soft.
Stir in the pasta and beans and simmer for 8 minutes until the pasta is tender, then add the parsley.

notes: Pre-heat the thermos with boiling water before filling.
Sprinkle a little vegetarian hard cheese over the top if you like.

title: Quick Pickled Red Onions with Orange and Chilli
summary: Bright pink onions in an orange and cider vinegar brine, ready in 15 minutes for brunch plates.

steps.text: Pack the onions into a clean jar.
Warm the vinegar, orange juice, sugar, salt and chilli in a small pan for 2 minutes until the sugar dissolves.
Pour over the onions, press down until covered, and cool before using.

notes: Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge.
Ready to eat after 20 minutes.

title: Quick Pickled Carrot and Radish Ribbons
summary: Crisp, tangy carrot and radish ribbons that perk up avocado toast and eggs.

steps.text: Pack the carrot and radish into a clean jar.
Heat the vinegar, water, sugar and salt for 2 minutes until the sugar dissolves.
Pour over the vegetables and cool until room temperature before covering.

notes: Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge.
Great on rice bowls.

title: Gluten-Free Cornbread Stuffing Muffins
summary: Cornmeal and sage stuffing baked into muffins with crisp tops, a gluten-free side for Thanksgiving.

steps.text: Dry the bread cubes at 150°C for 15 minutes until crisp.
Soften the onion and celery in the butter for 6 minutes until tender, then stir in the sage.
Toss the bread with the vegetables, stock, egg and salt until just moist.
Spoon into a greased muffin tin and bake at 190°C for 25 minutes until golden and set.

notes: Food safety: cook until the centre reaches 75°C because the mixture contains raw egg.
Use vegetable stock for vegetarian.

title: Maple Sweet Potatoes with Toasted Pecans
summary: Roasted sweet potato chunks glazed with maple syrup and sprinkled with pecans.

items.raw: 1 kg sweet potatoes, cut into chunks

steps.text: Toss the sweet potatoes with the oil, cinnamon and salt and roast at 200°C for 30 minutes until tender and browned.
Drizzle with the maple syrup and roast for 8 minutes more until glossy and caramelised.
Scatter with the pecans and serve hot.

notes: Vegan and gluten-free.
Use walnuts if you prefer.

title: Sage Cornbread Dressing
summary: Savoury baked cornbread dressing with onion, celery and plenty of fresh sage.

steps.text: Soften the onion and celery in the butter for 8 minutes until tender, then stir in the sage.
Toss with the cornbread, stock, eggs and salt until well moistened.
Spoon into a greased dish and bake at 190°C for 35 minutes until golden on top and set.

notes: Food safety: bake until the centre reaches 75°C because of the raw egg.
Use vegetable stock for vegetarian.

title: Korean Spring Onion and Sesame Pesto
summary: A punchy no-cook paste of spring onion, toasted sesame and soy, spooned over rice, eggs or noodles.

steps.text: Blitz the spring onions, sesame seeds and garlic in a food processor until a coarse paste forms.
Add the soy sauce, sesame oil, vinegar and vegetable oil and pulse until combined but still textured.
Spoon into a jar and serve over rice, noodles or fried eggs.

notes: Keeps 5 days in the fridge.
Use tamari for gluten-free.

title: Korean Soy Spring Onion Dressing
summary: A thin, savoury-sweet dressing for cold noodles, tofu and steamed greens.

steps.text: Whisk the soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil and honey together until the honey dissolves.
Stir in the spring onions, garlic and sesame seeds.
Spoon over noodles, tofu or greens just before serving.

notes: Keeps 1 week in the fridge.
Use tamari for gluten-free.

title: Cold Beetroot Soup Hlodnik
summary: A bright pink Lithuanian-style chilled soup of beetroot, yoghurt, cucumber and dill, served with a hot potato.

steps.text: Simmer the grated beetroot in 1 cup water for 15 minutes until tender, then cool completely in the fridge.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 20 minutes until a knife slides in easily.
Stir the beetroot and its liquid into the yoghurt with the lemon juice and salt until the soup turns bright pink.
Fold in the cucumber, radishes, dill and spring onions and chill until very cold.
Ladle into bowls, top with egg quarters and serve a hot potato alongside.

notes: Food safety: chill the soup within 2 hours of cooking, keep it at 5°C or below and eat within 2 days.
Use thick plant yoghurt thinned with water for dairy-free.

title: Tomato and Watermelon Gazpacho
summary: A cold, no-cook soup of ripe tomato, sweet watermelon and cucumber with a little sherry vinegar.

steps.text: Blend the tomatoes, watermelon, cucumber, capsicum and garlic until completely smooth.
Blend in the olive oil, vinegar and salt until the soup is silky.
Chill for at least 1 hour, taste and adjust the seasoning.
Pour into bowls and scatter with torn mint.

notes: Best made the day before.
Keeps 2 days in the fridge.

title: Maple Glazed Roasted Carrots with Thyme
summary: Whole carrots roasted until caramelised, brushed with maple and thyme.

steps.text: Toss the carrots with the oil and salt on a large tray until evenly coated.
Roast at 220°C for 25 minutes until tender and browned at the edges.
Stir the maple syrup and butter into the hot tray with the thyme and roast for 8 minutes until the carrots turn glossy and sticky, then serve hot.

notes: Use olive oil instead of butter for vegan.

title: Honey Roasted Sweet Potato Wedges
summary: Crisp-edged sweet potato wedges roasted with paprika and a final honey drizzle.

items.raw: 900 g sweet potato, cut into wedges

steps.text: Toss the wedges with the oil, paprika and salt on a large tray in a single layer.
Roast at 220°C for 30 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and tender inside.
Drizzle with the honey and lemon juice and roast for 5 minutes until sticky.
Scatter with parsley and serve.

notes: Use maple syrup for vegan.

title: Creamed Leeks with Nutmeg
summary: Soft leeks in a light cream sauce, a quiet side for roast chicken or fish.

items.raw: 4 leeks, white and pale green parts, sliced
items.prep: white and pale green parts, sliced

steps.text: Melt the butter with the oil in a wide pan and cook the leeks over medium heat for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the stock, cover and cook for 5 minutes until the leeks are tender.
Stir in the cream, nutmeg and salt and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes until lightly thickened.
Scatter with chives and serve.

notes: Wash the sliced leeks well in a bowl of cold water to remove grit.

title: Barley Salad with Sultanas and Pecans
summary: Chewy pearl barley with dried sultanas, toasted pecans, celery and an apple cider dressing.

steps.text: Simmer the barley in plenty of water for 30 minutes until tender, then drain and cool for 10 minutes.
Whisk the oil, vinegar, mustard and salt together.
Toss the barley with the dressing, sultanas, pecans, celery, spring onions and parsley until evenly coated, then serve warm or cold.

notes: Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
Not suitable for gluten-free.

title: Brown Rice Salad with Mango and Cashews
summary: Nutty brown rice tossed with ripe mango, cucumber, mint and toasted cashews in a lime dressing.

steps.text: Simmer the rice in plenty of water for 28 minutes until tender, then drain and spread out to cool.
Whisk the lime juice, oil and soy sauce together.
Toss the cooled rice with the mango, cucumber, cashews, mint, spring onions and dressing until combined.

notes: Food safety: cool the cooked rice and refrigerate within 1 hour, and eat within 1 day.
Use tamari for gluten-free.

title: Quinoa Salad with Roasted Corn and Black Beans
summary: Fluffy quinoa with charred corn, black beans, tomato and coriander in a cumin-lime dressing.

steps.text: Simmer the quinoa in 2 cups water for 15 minutes until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender, then fluff and cool.
Char the corn cobs in a hot dry pan for 10 minutes, turning, until browned in spots, then slice off the kernels.
Whisk the lime juice, oil, cumin and salt together.
Toss the quinoa with the corn, beans, tomatoes, coriander, spring onions and dressing until combined.

notes: Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
Food safety: cool and refrigerate the cooked quinoa within 1 hour.

title: Pearl Couscous Salad with Preserved Lemon
summary: Toasted pearl couscous with preserved lemon, chickpeas, olives and herbs.

steps.text: Toast the couscous in a dry pan for 3 minutes until lightly golden.
Boil in salted water for 8 minutes until tender, then drain and cool for 10 minutes.
Toss with the chickpeas, preserved lemon, olives, parsley, mint, oil and lemon juice until combined.

notes: Rinse the preserved lemon rind before chopping to cut the salt.
Not suitable for gluten-free.

title: Black Rice Salad with Edamame and Ginger
summary: Chewy black rice with edamame, carrot and spring onion in a ginger-soy dressing.

steps.text: Simmer the black rice in plenty of water for 35 minutes until tender, adding the edamame for the last 4 minutes, then drain and cool.
Whisk the soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil and ginger together.
Toss the rice and edamame with the carrot, spring onions and dressing until combined.
Scatter with sesame seeds.

notes: Food safety: cool and refrigerate the cooked rice within 1 hour, and eat within 1 day.
Use tamari for gluten-free.

title: Polish Krupnik Barley Soup
summary: A thick, homely soup of pearl barley, root vegetables and chicken stock with dill.

steps.text: Cook the onion, carrots and celery in the butter in a large pot for 8 minutes until softened.
Add the barley, stock and bay leaves and simmer for 25 minutes until the barley is nearly tender.
Add the potatoes and simmer for 15 minutes until soft.
Stir in the salt and dill, remove the bay leaves and ladle into bowls with a spoonful of sour cream.

notes: Thickens on standing, so loosen with water when reheating.
Use vegetable stock for vegetarian.
Not suitable for gluten-free.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Russian Solyanka Sour Meat Soup
summary: A tangy, smoky soup of sausage, ham, pickles and olives, finished with lemon and dill.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil in a large pot for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the sausage and ham and cook for 5 minutes until lightly browned, then stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute.
Pour in the stock and diced pickles and simmer for 25 minutes until the flavours are well blended.
Stir in the olives and capers and simmer for 5 minutes until hot.
Serve with lemon slices, dill and a spoonful of sour cream.

notes: Food safety: cool leftovers within 2 hours, refrigerate and reheat until steaming hot at 75°C or above.
Salty, so skip extra salt.

title: Serbian Sopska Salad
summary: Chopped tomato, cucumber and roasted capsicum under a snow of grated white cheese.

steps.text: Toss the tomatoes, cucumbers, capsicum and onion with the oil, vinegar and salt until glossy.
Pile onto a platter and cover generously with grated feta.
Scatter with parsley and serve at once.

notes: Traditionally made with sirene, a white brined cheese; feta is a close match.

title: Bosnian Begova Chicken and Okra Soup
summary: A creamy chicken and okra soup thickened with a butter and flour roux and finished with lemon.

steps.text: Simmer the chicken, carrots and onion in the water for 30 minutes until the chicken is cooked through, then lift out the chicken and shred it.
Add the okra to the broth and simmer for 10 minutes until tender.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 2 minutes until pale, then whisk in 1 cup of the hot broth until smooth and stir the mixture back into the pot.
Whisk the egg yolks, cream and lemon juice in a bowl, whisk in a ladle of hot soup, then stir it into the pot off the heat until the soup turns glossy.
Return the chicken, season with the salt and serve.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until the juices run clear and it reaches 75°C, and do not boil after adding the yolks; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Not suitable for gluten-free.

title: Croatian Manestra Bean and Corn Soup
summary: A rustic Istrian soup of borlotti beans, corn and potato simmered with a little smoked bacon.

steps.text: Cook the bacon in the oil in a large pot for 5 minutes until it turns golden, then add the onion and garlic and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste, then add the beans, corn, potatoes, water and salt.
Simmer for 25 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the soup thickens.
Mash a few beans against the side of the pot, scatter with parsley and serve.

notes: Leave out the bacon for vegetarian and use smoked paprika instead.
Food safety: refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Hungarian Gulyasleves Beef Soup
summary: The soup cousin of goulash: beef, potato and carrot in a paprika broth.

steps.text: Brown the beef in the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat for 8 minutes until coloured, then lift out.
Cook the onions in the same pot for 8 minutes until soft, then stir in the garlic, paprika, tomato paste and caraway for 1 minute.
Return the beef, add the water and salt and simmer gently for 1 hour until the beef is tender.
Add the carrots, potatoes and capsicum and simmer for 20 minutes until the vegetables are soft.

notes: Food safety: cool leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until steaming hot at 75°C or above.
Keep the heat low when adding paprika so it does not turn bitter.

title: Latvian Sauerkraut Salad with Caraway
summary: A crunchy sauerkraut and carrot salad with onion and caraway, a classic with roast pork and potatoes.

steps.text: Squeeze the sauerkraut with your hands to remove excess brine.
Toss with the carrots, onion, oil, caraway seeds and honey until evenly coated.
Scatter with parsley and serve cold.

notes: Rinse the sauerkraut briefly if you want it milder.
Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

title: Georgian Green Bean Salad with Walnuts
summary: Steamed green beans in a garlicky walnut and coriander dressing, a classic Georgian starter.

steps.text: Steam the beans for 6 minutes until just tender and bright green, then cool under cold water and drain.
Blitz the walnuts, garlic, coriander leaves, vinegar, ground coriander, salt and water to a thick paste.
Toss the beans in the paste until coated and scatter with pomegranate seeds.

notes: Best served at room temperature.
Keeps 2 days in the fridge.

title: Georgian Ajika Chilli Paste
summary: A fiery red chilli and garlic paste with walnuts and dried herbs, used by the spoonful.

steps.text: Blitz the chillies, garlic and walnuts until a coarse paste forms.
Add the coriander, fenugreek, vinegar, oil and salt and blitz until combined.
Pack into a jar and rest in the fridge before serving with grilled meat, bread or beans.

notes: Wear gloves when handling the chillies.
Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge.

title: Bulgarian Kyopolou Eggplant Spread
summary: Smoky charred eggplant blended with roasted capsicum, garlic and walnuts.

steps.text: Roast the eggplants and capsicums at 230°C for 40 minutes, turning, until the skins blacken and the flesh collapses.
Peel the vegetables and drain the eggplant flesh for 5 minutes.
Mash the flesh with the garlic, walnuts, oil, vinegar and salt until chunky.
Spoon into a bowl and top with parsley.

notes: Serve with bread or grilled meat.
Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

title: Hungarian Cucumber Salad with Paprika
summary: Paper-thin cucumber in a sweet-sour dressing with garlic, sour cream and a dusting of paprika.

steps.text: Toss the cucumber slices with the salt and drain in a colander for 10 minutes, then squeeze out the water.
Whisk the vinegar, sugar, garlic and sour cream together until smooth.
Toss through the cucumber and dust with paprika.

notes: Serve straight away so the cucumber stays crisp.

title: Russian Vinegret Beetroot Salad
summary: A ruby salad of diced beetroot, potato, carrot and pickles in sunflower oil.

steps.text: Boil the beetroot, potatoes and carrots in their skins for 35 minutes until a knife slides in easily, then cool and peel.
Dice everything into 1 cm cubes.
Toss with the pickles, sauerkraut, onion, oil and salt, stirring the beetroot in last so the colour does not bleed.
Chill and scatter with dill.

notes: Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Nigerian Egusi Soup with Spinach
summary: A rich West African soup of ground pumpkin seeds, spinach and chicken simmered in a tomato and chilli base.

steps.text: Blend the tomatoes, onion and chilli to a smooth puree.
Cook the puree in the oil in a large pot for 10 minutes until it thickens and the oil separates.
Stir the ground pumpkin seeds with 1/2 cup stock to a paste, drop spoonfuls into the pot and cook for 5 minutes until they form soft curds.
