Add the chicken, remaining stock and salt and simmer for 20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Fold in the spinach and cook for 3 minutes until wilted.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C and keep leftovers refrigerated within 2 hours, reheating until steaming hot.
Serve with rice, fufu or boiled yam.

title: Ghanaian Groundnut Peanut Soup
summary: A velvety peanut and tomato soup with chicken and a slow chilli warmth, served with rice balls.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil in a large pot for 6 minutes until soft, then add the ginger, chilli and tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until broken down.
Add the chicken, water and salt and simmer for 20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Whisk the peanut butter with a ladle of hot broth until smooth and stir it back into the pot.
Simmer gently for 10 minutes until the soup thickens and a slick of oil rises to the top.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Use natural peanut butter with no added sugar.
Contains peanuts.

title: Nigerian Ofada Style Pepper Stew
summary: A smoky, deep red stew of roasted capsicum and chilli, cooked down in oil with onion and spices.

steps.text: Char the capsicums under a hot grill for 15 minutes until blistered and blackened, then peel and deseed.
Blend with the chillies and 1 onion to a coarse puree.
Cook the remaining diced onion in the oil in a pot for 5 minutes until soft, then add the tomato paste and curry powder for 1 minute.
Add the puree and cook for 20 minutes, stirring, until the sauce darkens and the oil separates.
Add the beef, stock and salt and simmer for 20 minutes until the beef is tender.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef until tender and at least 75°C and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Traditionally eaten with rice and boiled egg.

title: West African Party Jollof Rice
summary: Long-grain rice cooked in a smoky tomato and capsicum sauce until every grain is red and fluffy.

steps.text: Blend the tomatoes, capsicum, half the onion and the chilli, then simmer the puree for 15 minutes until reduced by half.
Cook the remaining onion in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, then stir in the tomato paste, curry powder and thyme for 2 minutes.
Add the reduced puree, stock, salt and rinsed rice, stir once, cover tightly and cook on low heat for 25 minutes until the rice is tender.
Rest for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.

notes: Food safety: cool and refrigerate leftover rice within 1 hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Use vegetable stock for vegetarian.

title: Fried Plantain with Pepper Sauce
summary: Ripe plantain slices fried until caramelised, served with a quick tomato and chilli sauce.

steps.text: Cook the onion in 1 tbsp oil for 4 minutes until soft, then add the tomatoes, chilli and salt and simmer for 10 minutes until thick.
Heat the 1/3 cup oil in a frying pan over medium heat and fry the plantain for 3 minutes each side until deep golden.
Drain on paper towel and serve with the sauce.

notes: Use plantains that are mostly yellow with black spots for the sweetest result.

title: Jamaican Steamed Cabbage with Carrot
summary: Quick-steamed cabbage with thyme, garlic and a touch of chilli, a staple Jamaican side.

steps.text: Cook the onion, garlic and chilli in the oil in a large pan for 3 minutes until soft.
Add the cabbage, carrot, thyme, salt and water, cover and steam for 6 minutes until the cabbage is tender but still bright.
Uncover and toss for 2 minutes until the liquid evaporates.

notes: Serve with rice and peas or jerk chicken.

title: Trinidadian Callaloo Style Spinach Side
summary: Silky wilted spinach with coconut milk, okra and thyme, in the style of Trinidad's Sunday callaloo.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a pot and cook the onion and garlic for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the spinach, okra, coconut milk, water, thyme, chilli and salt and simmer for 15 minutes until the okra is tender.
Remove the chilli and blend with a stick blender until smooth.

notes: Use oil instead of butter for vegan.

title: Puerto Rican Tostones with Garlic Mojo
summary: Twice-fried green plantain discs with a hot garlic and lime dipping oil.

steps.text: Peel the plantains and cut into 3 cm chunks.
Fry in the vegetable oil over medium heat for 3 minutes each side until pale gold, then lift out and press flat with a plate.
Return to the oil and fry for 2 minutes each side until crisp and deep golden, then drain and sprinkle with salt.
Warm the olive oil with the garlic for 2 minutes until fragrant, then stir in the lime juice and coriander and serve for dipping.

notes: Serve while hot and crisp.

title: Bajan Cou-Cou Cornmeal and Okra
summary: A smooth, golden cornmeal and okra pudding from Barbados, stirred until it pulls away from the pot.

steps.text: Boil the okra in the water with the salt for 8 minutes until tender, then lift out and set aside, keeping the water.
Mix the cornmeal with 1/2 cup cold water, whisk into the hot okra water and cook over low heat, stirring constantly, for 10 minutes until very thick.
Fold in the okra and beat in the butter until the mixture pulls away from the pot.
Shape into a smooth dome with a wet spoon and serve.

notes: Traditionally served with flying fish or a spicy stew.
Use oil instead of butter for vegan.

title: Dominican Habichuelas Guisadas Stewed Beans
summary: Butter beans simmered with pumpkin, sofrito and oregano into a thick, savoury stew.

steps.text: Cook the onion, capsicum and garlic in the oil for 6 minutes until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and oregano for 1 minute, then add the beans, pumpkin, water and salt.
Simmer for 25 minutes, mashing some of the pumpkin into the sauce, until the beans are creamy and thick.
Stir in the coriander and serve over rice.

notes: Keeps 4 days in the fridge and tastes better the next day.

title: Pork Dumplings in Ginger Broth
summary: Plump pork and chive dumplings floating in a light ginger broth with bok choy.

steps.text: Mix the pork, chives, soy sauce, sesame oil and half the ginger until sticky.
Place a teaspoon of filling in each wrapper, wet the edge, fold and press closed.
Simmer the stock with the remaining ginger and vinegar for 5 minutes until fragrant.
Drop in the dumplings and cook for 5 minutes until they float and the pork is cooked through, adding the bok choy for the last 2 minutes until tender.
Ladle into bowls and scatter with spring onions.

notes: Food safety: cook the dumplings until the filling reaches 75°C and eat within 1 day if stored.
Not suitable for gluten-free.

title: Pelmeni in Chicken Broth
summary: Small Russian meat dumplings served in a clear dill-scented chicken broth.

steps.text: Knead the flour, egg, water and a pinch of salt for 5 minutes until a smooth dough forms, then cover and rest.
Mix the beef, onion, salt and pepper, roll the dough thin and cut 5 cm rounds.
Place a small ball of filling in each round, fold and press the edges, then pinch the corners together.
Simmer the stock, drop in the pelmeni and cook for 7 minutes until they float and the beef is cooked through.
Serve with dill and sour cream.

notes: Food safety: cook until the filling reaches 75°C. Freeze uncooked pelmeni on a tray, then bag.
Not suitable for gluten-free.

title: Tibetan Momo Thukpa Soup
summary: Beef momo dumplings in a warming ginger, tomato and vegetable broth.

steps.text: Mix the beef, spring onion, half the ginger, half the garlic and soy sauce until sticky.
Place a teaspoon of filling in each wrapper, wet the edge and pleat closed.
Simmer the stock with the tomatoes, carrot, cumin and remaining ginger and garlic for 10 minutes until the carrot is tender.
Add the cabbage and momos and cook for 6 minutes until the momos float and the beef is cooked through.
Serve scattered with coriander.

notes: Food safety: cook the momos until the filling reaches 75°C; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Not suitable for gluten-free.

title: Warm Lentil Salad with Goats Cheese
summary: Peppery rocket and warm green lentils with roasted red onion and crumbled goat's cheese.

steps.text: Roast the onion wedges with 1 tbsp of the oil at 200°C for 25 minutes until soft and charred at the edges.
Simmer the lentils in plenty of water for 20 minutes until tender but still holding their shape, then drain.
Whisk the remaining oil, vinegar, mustard and salt and toss through the warm lentils.
Fold in the onions and rocket and crumble the goat's cheese over the top.

notes: Serve warm for the best flavour.

title: Warm Kale and Roasted Pumpkin Salad
summary: Tender kale, caramelised pumpkin, toasted pepitas and a maple mustard dressing.

steps.text: Roast the pumpkin with 1 tbsp of the oil at 220°C for 25 minutes until golden and soft.
Whisk the remaining oil, maple syrup, vinegar, mustard and salt together.
Massage the kale with half the dressing for 2 minutes until it softens and darkens.
Toss with the warm pumpkin and toasted pepitas, then crumble over the feta and drizzle with the remaining dressing.

notes: Leave out the feta for vegan.

title: Warm Mushroom and Spinach Salad with Thyme
summary: Golden pan-fried mushrooms tossed through baby spinach with a warm garlic and balsamic dressing.

steps.text: Cook the mushrooms in 2 tbsp oil in a hot pan for 6 minutes until golden and their liquid has evaporated.
Add the garlic, thyme and salt and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the balsamic vinegar and remaining oil and stir for 30 seconds until sizzling.
Pour over the spinach, toss until just wilted and top with walnuts.

notes: Do not crowd the pan or the mushrooms will steam instead of browning.

title: Warm Cabbage and Apple Salad with Bacon
summary: Sweet-sour sauteed cabbage and crisp apple with smoky bacon and a hot cider dressing.

steps.text: Cook the bacon in a large pan for 5 minutes until crisp, then add the onion and cook for 3 minutes until soft.
Add the cabbage and cook for 5 minutes until just wilted but still crunchy.
Stir in the vinegar, honey and mustard until the dressing bubbles, then toss through the apples and parsley.

notes: Food safety: cook the bacon until crisp and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Leave out the bacon and use smoked paprika for vegetarian.

title: Egg and Tomato Congee with Ginger
summary: Silky rice porridge with soft-set egg, sweet tomato and ginger, a comforting savoury breakfast.

steps.text: Simmer the rice with the water and ginger for 35 minutes, stirring now and then, until the grains break down into a thick porridge.
Stir in the tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes until soft.
Slowly pour in the beaten eggs in a thin stream, stirring gently, and cook for 1 minute until set in ribbons.
Season with the soy sauce and salt, and serve topped with sesame oil and spring onions.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until fully set and eat the congee hot, with leftover rice porridge refrigerated within 1 hour of cooking.
Use tamari for gluten-free.

title: Savoury Oat Porridge with Mushrooms and Parmesan
summary: Creamy stove-top oats cooked in stock and topped with golden mushrooms, spinach and a soft egg.

steps.text: Simmer the oats with the stock and water for 7 minutes, stirring, until thick and creamy.
Cook the mushrooms in the oil in a hot pan for 6 minutes until golden, adding the spinach for the last minute until wilted.
Poach the eggs in barely simmering water for 3 minutes until the whites are set.
Spoon the oats into bowls and top with the mushrooms, eggs, cheese and pepper.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set; avoid runny yolks for pregnant, elderly or immune-compromised eaters.
Not suitable for gluten-free unless certified oats.

title: Chinese Soy Braised Eggs Breakfast Plate
summary: Marbled eggs simmered in soy and star anise, served with cucumber and warm rice.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 8 minutes until firm, then cool in cold water and tap all over with a spoon to crack the shells.
Simmer the vinegar, soy sauce, star anise, cinnamon, sugar and water for 5 minutes until fragrant, then add the eggs.
Simmer the eggs gently for 15 minutes until the whites are deeply coloured, then leave in the liquid to cool.
Peel and halve the eggs and serve with cucumber and warm rice.

notes: Food safety: boil the eggs until the yolks are firm; keep refrigerated in their liquid and eat within 3 days.
Food safety: cool and refrigerate the cooked rice within 1 hour.
Use tamari for gluten-free.

title: Thai Khai Jiao Fluffy Omelette over Rice
summary: A crisp-edged, puffy omelette flavoured with fish sauce, served over steamed rice with chilli sauce.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs with the fish sauce and lime juice until frothy.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat until it shimmers.
Pour in the eggs and cook for 1 minute until puffed and golden underneath, then flip and cook for 30 seconds until just set.
Lift onto the rice and top with spring onions and sweet chilli sauce.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until fully set and refrigerate cooked rice within 1 hour.
Drain the omelette well on paper towel to remove excess oil.

title: Japanese Tamagoyaki Breakfast Plate
summary: A layered sweet-savoury rolled omelette with rice, pickled cucumber and miso soup.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs with the mirin, soy sauce and sugar until just combined.
Oil a small non-stick pan over medium heat and pour in a thin layer of egg, cooking for 1 minute until almost set.
Roll the egg to one side, oil the pan again, add another layer and roll, repeating until all the egg is used and the omelette is firm.
Slice into thick rounds and serve with rice, cucumber dressed with the vinegar and shredded nori.

notes: Food safety: cook the omelette until firm and refrigerate leftover rice within 1 hour.
Use tamari for gluten-free.

title: Lebanese Eggs with Sumac and Labneh
summary: Fried eggs sprinkled with sumac and served on labneh with warm flatbread, tomatoes and mint.

steps.text: Spread the labneh over two plates.
Fry the eggs in the oil for 3 minutes until the whites are set and the edges are crisp.
Slide onto the labneh, sprinkle with sumac and salt and serve with the tomatoes, mint and warm flatbread.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set.
Use thick plain yoghurt if you cannot find labneh.

title: Spanish Huevos Rotos with Potatoes
summary: Crisp fried potatoes topped with runny eggs, broken at the table into a pile of golden yolk.

steps.text: Fry the potato slices in the oil in a wide pan for 15 minutes, turning, until golden and tender, then lift out and season with the salt.
Fry the eggs in the same oil for 3 minutes until the whites are set and the edges are lacy.
Pile the potatoes on plates, top with the eggs and jamon, dust with paprika and parsley, and break the yolks at the table.

notes: Food safety: eggs are best cooked until the whites are set, and avoid runny yolks for vulnerable eaters.
Leave out the jamon for vegetarian.

title: Swiss Rosti with Fried Egg
summary: Crisp golden grated potato cake topped with a fried egg and chives.

items.raw: 500 g waxy potatoes, boiled and cooled

steps.text: Coarsely grate the cooled potatoes and toss with the salt.
Heat the butter and half the oil in a non-stick pan, pack in the potato and press into a cake.
Cook over medium heat for 10 minutes until golden underneath, then slide onto a plate, add the remaining oil and flip back to cook for 8 minutes until crisp.
Fry the eggs in a separate pan for 3 minutes until the whites are set and place on top with the chives.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set.
Cooking the potatoes the day before gives the best crisp.

title: Irish Boxty with Poached Egg
summary: Griddled potato pancakes with a poached egg and a spoonful of sour cream.

steps.text: Grate the raw potatoes and squeeze out the liquid in a clean tea towel until dry.
Mix with the mashed potato, flour, baking powder, salt and milk until a thick batter forms.
Cook spoonfuls in the butter in a pan over medium heat for 4 minutes each side until golden and cooked through.
Poach the eggs for 3 minutes until the whites are set and serve on the boxty with sour cream and chives.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set; avoid runny yolks for vulnerable eaters.
Not suitable for gluten-free.

title: Scottish Porridge with Berries and Honey
summary: Creamy oats simmered in milk and water, with a warm berry compote and a drizzle of honey.

steps.text: Simmer the oats with the milk, water and salt for 8 minutes, stirring, until thick and creamy.
Warm the berries in a small pan for 3 minutes until they release their juices.
Spoon the porridge into bowls and top with the berries, honey and almonds.

notes: Use plant milk for dairy-free.
Not suitable for gluten-free unless certified oats.

title: Orange and Ricotta Breakfast Toast
summary: Crisp toast with creamy ricotta, orange segments, honey and basil.

steps.text: Toast the sourdough until golden and crisp.
Spread each slice thickly with ricotta.
Arrange the orange segments on top, drizzle with honey and finish with basil and pepper.

notes: Add a squeeze of lemon if the berries are not very sweet.

title: Grilled Mango Yoghurt Breakfast Bowl
summary: Caramelised mango cheeks over thick yoghurt with toasted coconut and lime.

steps.text: Grill the mango cheeks cut side down in a hot dry pan for 3 minutes until charred and caramelised.
Toast the coconut in a dry pan for 2 minutes until golden.
Spoon the yoghurt into bowls, top with the mango, coconut, honey and pistachios, and squeeze over the lime.

notes: Use coconut yoghurt for dairy-free.

title: Pineapple and Coconut Yoghurt Parfait
summary: Layers of coconut yoghurt, roasted pineapple and crunchy oats, ready in minutes.

steps.text: Toast the oats and coconut with the maple syrup and cinnamon in a dry pan for 5 minutes, stirring, until golden and crunchy.
Sear the pineapple in a hot pan for 4 minutes until lightly caramelised.
Layer the yoghurt, pineapple and crunchy oats into two glasses.

notes: Make the crunchy oats ahead and keep in a jar for 1 week.

title: Spiced Pear and Walnut Porridge
summary: Cinnamon oats cooked with grated pear and finished with toasted walnuts and a drizzle of maple.

items.raw: 2 pears, one grated and one sliced

steps.text: Simmer the oats with the milk, grated pear, cinnamon and ginger for 8 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Spoon into bowls and top with the sliced pear, walnuts and maple syrup.

notes: Use plant milk for dairy-free.
Not suitable for gluten-free unless certified oats.

title: Costa Rican Gallo Pinto with Fried Egg
summary: Rice and black beans stir-fried with onion, capsicum and a splash of Worcestershire-style sauce, topped with an egg.

steps.text: Cook the onion and capsicum in the oil for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the beans and Worcestershire sauce and cook for 3 minutes until hot.
Stir in the rice and coriander and cook for 4 minutes until heated through and lightly crisp.
Fry the eggs for 3 minutes until the whites are set and serve on top.

notes: Food safety: use rice cooled and refrigerated within 1 hour, and reheat until steaming hot; cook the eggs until the whites are fully set.
Worcestershire sauce contains anchovies.

title: Nigerian Akara Bean Fritters
summary: Light, crisp black-eyed pea fritters fried until golden, a Lagos breakfast served with pap or bread.

steps.text: Blend the peas, onion, chilli, salt and water to a thick, fluffy paste.
Beat the batter by hand for 2 minutes until it turns light and airy.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 180°C and drop in tablespoons of batter, frying for 4 minutes until deep golden and cooked through.
Drain on paper towel and serve hot.

notes: Keep the batter thick so the fritters hold together.
Serve with a tomato and chilli sauce.

title: Russian Syrniki Cottage Cheese Pancakes
summary: Golden pan-fried cottage cheese pancakes served with sour cream and berry jam.

steps.text: Mash the cottage cheese with the egg, sugar, vanilla and salt, then stir in the flour until a soft dough forms.
Shape into 8 small discs, dusting your hands with flour.
Cook in the butter over medium heat for 3 minutes each side until golden and cooked through.
Serve with sour cream and honey.

notes: Food safety: cook until the centre is hot and set, as the mix contains raw egg.
Not suitable for gluten-free.

title: Swedish Pytt i Panna Breakfast Hash
summary: Crisp diced potato, sausage and onion fried together and topped with a fried egg and pickled beetroot.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes for 6 minutes until just tender, then drain and dry.
Fry the potatoes in the butter in a large pan for 10 minutes until golden and crisp, then add the onion and sausage and cook for 6 minutes until browned.
Season with the salt and divide among plates.
Fry the eggs for 3 minutes until the whites are set and serve on top with the beetroot and parsley.

notes: Food safety: reheat the sausage until steaming hot at 75°C or above and cook the eggs until the whites are fully set.
Use pre-cooked sausage.

title: Ukrainian Kapusniak Cabbage and Pork Soup
summary: A hearty soup of cabbage, potatoes, smoked pork and dill.

steps.text: Simmer the pork ribs in the water with the bay leaves for 30 minutes until the meat is tender, then lift out and shred.
Cook the onion and carrot in the oil with the tomato paste for 6 minutes until soft and stir into the broth.
Add the potatoes and cabbage and simmer for 15 minutes until tender.
Return the shredded pork, add the salt and serve with dill.

notes: Food safety: reheat the pork until steaming hot at 75°C or above and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Leave out the pork and use smoked paprika for vegetarian.

title: Romanian Ciorba Radauteana Chicken Sour Soup
summary: A creamy chicken and vegetable soup soured with vinegar and finished with sour cream and garlic.

steps.text: Simmer the chicken, carrots, onion, celery and capsicum in the water for 30 minutes until the chicken is cooked through, then lift out the chicken and shred it.
Whisk the egg yolks, sour cream and vinegar in a bowl and whisk in a ladle of hot soup until smooth.
Stir the mixture into the pot off the heat with the shredded chicken and salt until the soup turns creamy.
Serve with garlic and parsley.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C and do not boil after adding the yolks; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Garlic is traditionally stirred in at the table.

title: Bulgarian Bob Chorba White Bean Soup
summary: A smoky white bean and vegetable soup finished with paprika and dried mint.

steps.text: Cook the onion, carrots and capsicum in the oil for 8 minutes until soft.
Stir in the paprika for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes, beans, stock and salt.
Simmer for 20 minutes until the vegetables are tender and the soup thickens.
Stir in the dried mint and serve.

notes: Mash some of the beans for a creamier soup.
Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

title: Serbian Pasulj Smoky Bean Soup
summary: A thick, smoky soup of white beans, paprika and smoked sausage, a Serbian family staple.

steps.text: Cook the sausage and onion in the oil for 8 minutes until browned and soft.
Stir in the garlic and paprika, then add the carrot, beans, bay leaves, water and salt.
Simmer for 25 minutes until the soup is thick and the carrot is tender.

notes: Food safety: reheat leftover sausage dishes until steaming hot at 75°C or above.
Leave out the sausage for vegetarian.

title: Armenian Spas Yoghurt and Barley Soup
summary: A warm, tangy yoghurt soup with chewy barley and dried mint.

steps.text: Simmer the barley in the water for 25 minutes until tender.
Whisk the yoghurt, egg and flour in a bowl until smooth, then whisk in a ladle of the hot barley liquid.
Stir the mixture into the pot and simmer gently, stirring constantly, for 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
Cook the onion in the butter with the mint for 4 minutes until golden and spoon over the soup.

notes: Food safety: cook the soup until steaming hot and the egg is fully set; do not boil hard or the yoghurt will split.
Not suitable for gluten-free.

title: Polish Barszcz Clear Beetroot Soup
summary: A ruby-red clear beetroot broth with garlic and marjoram, traditionally served in a cup.

steps.text: Simmer the beetroot, carrot, onion and stock for 40 minutes until the vegetables are very tender.
Strain through a fine sieve into a clean pot, pressing lightly.
Stir in the garlic, marjoram, lemon juice, sugar and salt and warm gently, without boiling, so the colour stays bright.

notes: Serve with small mushroom dumplings or bread.
Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

title: Romanian Eggplant Salad Salata de Vinete
summary: Smoky charred eggplant beaten with oil and onion into a creamy white-pink spread.

steps.text: Roast the eggplants at 230°C for 45 minutes, turning, until the skins blacken and the flesh collapses.
Peel and drain the flesh in a colander for 15 minutes, then chop finely with a wooden knife.
Beat the flesh with the oil in a bowl, a little at a time, until pale and creamy.
Stir in the onion, lemon juice and salt and serve with tomatoes and parsley.

notes: Use a wooden or plastic knife to keep the colour pale.
Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Polish Surowka Carrot and Apple Salad
summary: Crunchy grated carrot and apple dressed with lemon, a touch of sugar and sour cream.

steps.text: Toss the carrots and apples with the lemon juice straight away to stop browning.
Stir in the sugar, sour cream and salt until evenly coated.
Chill briefly and scatter with parsley.

notes: Serve within a few hours for the best crunch.

title: Hungarian Tomato and Pepper Salad
summary: Ripe tomato and sweet pepper in a simple vinegar and oil dressing with onion, a summer staple.

steps.text: Arrange the tomatoes and capsicums on a platter with the onion.
Whisk the oil, vinegar, sugar and salt together until the sugar dissolves.
Pour over the salad and scatter with parsley.

notes: Best made with summer tomatoes.

title: Korean Chojang Chilli Vinegar Dip
summary: A bright, sweet-sour chilli and vinegar dip for dumplings, pancakes and grilled meat.

steps.text: Whisk the gochujang, vinegar, honey and water together until smooth.
Stir in the sesame oil and seeds.
Spoon into a small dish and serve with dumplings or pancakes.

notes: Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge.
Check the gochujang label for gluten.

title: Korean Yangnyeom Soy Garlic Sauce
summary: A sticky soy, garlic and honey glaze for fried chicken, tofu and roasted vegetables.

steps.text: Simmer the soy sauce, honey, garlic, vinegar and ginger in a small pan for 4 minutes until syrupy.
Remove from the heat and stir in the sesame oil.
Use to coat hot chicken, tofu or vegetables until glossy.

notes: Keeps 1 week in the fridge.
Use tamari for gluten-free.

title: Cold Cucumber and Buttermilk Soup with Chives
summary: A cooling no-cook soup of cucumber and buttermilk with lemon and chives, ready in ten minutes.

steps.text: Blend the cucumbers, buttermilk, lemon juice, garlic and salt until completely smooth.
Chill for at least 1 hour, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
Pour into bowls, drizzle with the oil and scatter with chives.

notes: Use thick plant yoghurt thinned with water for dairy-free.
Keeps 2 days in the fridge.

title: Chilled Zucchini and Basil Soup
summary: A pale green soup of gently cooked zucchini and fresh basil, served cold with a swirl of olive oil.

steps.text: Cook the onion and garlic in 1 tbsp of the oil for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the zucchini and stock and simmer for 8 minutes until completely tender.
Blend with the basil, lemon juice and salt until smooth, then chill until very cold.
Pour into bowls and drizzle with the remaining oil.

notes: Cool the soup quickly and keep in the fridge for up to 3 days.
Vegan and gluten-free.

title: Cold Carrot and Orange Soup
summary: A sunny chilled soup of carrot, orange juice and ginger with a spoon of yoghurt.

steps.text: Cook the onion and ginger in the oil for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the carrots and stock and simmer for 18 minutes until completely tender.
Blend with the orange juice and salt until smooth and chill until very cold.
Serve topped with yoghurt and coriander.

notes: Leave out the yoghurt for vegan.
Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Chilled Roasted Capsicum Soup
summary: Sweet roasted red capsicum blended with tomato and a little cream, served cold with basil.

steps.text: Roast the capsicums, tomatoes and garlic at 220°C for 30 minutes until the skins blister and blacken.
Peel the capsicums and tomatoes and remove the seeds.
Blend with the oil, stock, vinegar and salt until completely smooth.
Stir in the cream, chill until very cold and top with basil.

notes: Use coconut cream for dairy-free.
Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Corn Cob Stock
summary: A sweet, light stock made from the cobs left after cutting off the kernels.

steps.text: Break the cobs in half and place in a large pot with the onion, carrot, celery, parsley, bay leaf and water.
Bring to a boil, then simmer gently for 40 minutes until the stock tastes sweet and golden.
Strain, season with the salt and cool.

notes: Use for chowders, risotto and soups.
Freezes well for 3 months.

title: Mushroom and Thyme Stock
summary: A dark, savoury vegetarian stock built on mushrooms, onion and thyme.

steps.text: Brown the mushrooms and onion in the oil in a large pot for 10 minutes until deeply golden.
Add the carrot, garlic, water, thyme, bay leaves and soy sauce.
Simmer gently for 40 minutes until the stock turns dark and fragrant.
Strain through a fine sieve.

notes: Freezes well for 3 months.
Use tamari for gluten-free.

title: Roasted Garlic and Herb Vegetable Broth
summary: A golden, aromatic broth of roasted garlic, leek and herbs, good for sipping or soups.

steps.text: Cut the tops off the garlic heads, drizzle with the oil and roast at 200°C for 30 minutes until soft and golden.
Place the roasted garlic, leeks, carrots, celery, water, bay leaf, thyme and parsley in a large pot.
Simmer gently for 30 minutes until the broth is fragrant, then strain and season with the salt.

notes: Squeeze the leftover roasted garlic into mash or bread.

title: Garlic Roasted Cabbage Wedges
summary: Cabbage wedges roasted until crisp at the edges and sweet inside, finished with lemon.

steps.text: Brush the wedges with the oil and place on a tray with the garlic.
Roast at 220°C for 25 minutes, turning once, until the edges are crisp and charred and the centres are tender.
Season with the salt, chilli and lemon juice and serve.

notes: Keep the core in so the wedges hold together.

title: Honey Mustard Roasted Onions
summary: Whole small onions roasted until jammy with a honey and wholegrain mustard glaze.

steps.text: Toss the onion halves with the oil, salt and thyme in a roasting tray, cut side down.
Roast at 200°C for 30 minutes until soft and golden.
Stir the honey, mustard and vinegar together, spoon over the onions and roast for 10 minutes until glossy and sticky.

notes: Good with roast meat or a cheese board.

title: Herb Roasted Baby Potatoes with Lemon
summary: Crisp-skinned baby potatoes roasted with rosemary, garlic and a squeeze of lemon.

steps.text: Toss the potatoes with the oil, garlic, rosemary and salt on a large tray.
Roast at 220°C for 35 minutes, turning once, until crisp and golden and a knife slides in easily.
Toss with the lemon zest, juice and parsley and serve hot.

notes: Vegan and gluten-free.

title: Buttered Corn with Chives
summary: Sweet corn kernels tossed in butter with chives, pepper and a squeeze of lime.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a frying pan over medium-high heat.
Cook the corn kernels for 6 minutes, stirring, until tender and lightly golden.
Stir in the chives, lime juice, salt and pepper and serve hot.

notes: Use olive oil instead of butter for vegan.

title: Orzo Salad with Lemon and Peas
summary: Tender orzo tossed with peas, mint, feta and a lemon dressing, good warm or cold.

steps.text: Boil the orzo in salted water for 9 minutes until al dente, adding the peas for the last 2 minutes until bright green.
Drain and toss with the oil, lemon zest, juice and salt while still warm.
Fold in the feta, mint and spring onions.

notes: Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
Not suitable for gluten-free.

title: Barley and Roasted Capsicum Salad
summary: Chewy barley with smoky roasted capsicum, rocket and a sherry vinegar dressing.

steps.text: Roast the capsicums at 220°C for 30 minutes until blistered and soft, then peel, deseed and slice.
Simmer the barley in plenty of water for 30 minutes until tender, then drain and cool.
Whisk the oil, vinegar, garlic and salt and toss through the barley with the capsicums, rocket and almonds until coated.

notes: Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
Not suitable for gluten-free.

title: Chickpea and Cucumber Grain Salad
summary: Brown rice, chickpeas and crisp cucumber with parsley and a lemon tahini dressing.

steps.text: Simmer the rice in plenty of water for 28 minutes until tender, then drain and cool.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice, water, garlic and salt until smooth.
Toss the rice with the chickpeas, cucumbers, parsley and dressing until coated.

notes: Food safety: cool and refrigerate the cooked rice within 1 hour and eat within 1 day.
Contains sesame.

title: Swedish Cardamom Oat Porridge
summary: Creamy milk oats scented with cardamom, finished with butter and honey.

steps.text: Bring the oats, milk, salt and cardamom to a gentle simmer in a saucepan, stirring often until bubbling.
Cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring, until thick and creamy.
Stir through the butter, spoon into bowls and drizzle with honey.

notes: Use oat milk for a dairy-free version.
Oats can contain traces of gluten.

title: Finnish Oven Pancake Pannukakku
summary: A puffed, custardy oven pancake baked in butter, cut into wedges.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C and put the butter in a 25 cm baking dish until melted.
Whisk the eggs, milk, flour, sugar and salt until smooth.
Pour the batter into the hot dish and bake for 20 to 25 minutes until puffed and golden.
Cut into wedges and serve straight away.

notes: Food safety: bake until the centre is fully set with no wet egg.
Not suitable for gluten-free.

title: Estonian Rye Bread with Egg and Chive Butter
summary: Dense rye bread spread with soft chive butter and topped with sliced boiled egg.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes until the yolks are firm, then cool, peel and slice.
Mash the butter with the chives and salt until combined.
Spread the chive butter over the rye bread and top with the egg.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the yolks are firm and keep leftovers chilled for up to 2 days.
Not suitable for gluten-free.

title: Norwegian Creamed Cabbage
summary: Soft cabbage in a light white sauce with nutmeg, a traditional side for sausages and meatballs.

steps.text: Simmer the cabbage in salted water for 8 minutes until tender, then drain well.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Whisk in the milk and simmer for 4 minutes until thickened, then season with nutmeg and salt.
Fold the cabbage through the sauce and heat for 2 minutes until hot.

notes: Use a dairy-free spread and oat milk to make it dairy-free.
Not suitable for gluten-free.

title: Estonian Rosolje Beetroot and Potato Salad
summary: A ruby salad of beetroot, potato, apple, pickles and egg in a sour cream dressing.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes for 20 minutes until tender, then cool and dice.
Boil the eggs for 10 minutes until the yolks are firm, then cool, peel and chop.
Mix the sour cream, mustard and salt together.
Fold the potato, beetroot, apple, pickles and egg through the dressing.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the yolks are firm and keep the salad chilled, eating within 2 days.
Beetroot will tint everything pink.

title: Portuguese Chickpea and Spinach Soup
summary: A hearty cumin and paprika chickpea soup finished with wilted spinach.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic, cumin and paprika for 1 minute.
Add the chickpeas and stock and simmer for 15 minutes until the flavours meld.
Stir in the spinach for 2 minutes until wilted, then add the vinegar.

notes: Mash a few chickpeas against the pot to thicken the soup.
Check the stock label for gluten.

title: Spanish Garlic Soup with Poached Egg
summary: Castilian sopa de ajo: golden garlic, paprika and bread in broth with a poached egg.

steps.text: Fry the garlic in the oil for 1 minute until golden, then add the bread and cook for 3 minutes until crisp.
Stir in the paprika, then the stock, and simmer for 10 minutes until the bread softens.
Crack the eggs into the soup and poach for 3 minutes until the whites are fully set.
Ladle into bowls with one egg each.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set.
Not suitable for gluten-free.

title: Galician Bean and Greens Broth
summary: A rustic broth of white beans, potato, cabbage and smoky bacon.

steps.text: Cook the bacon in the oil for 5 minutes until browned, then add the onion for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the potato, paprika and stock and simmer for 15 minutes until the potato is tender.
Add the beans and cabbage and cook for 8 minutes until the cabbage is soft.

notes: Food safety: cook the bacon until browned and the soup until steaming, at least 75°C, and eat within 3 days.
Check the stock label for gluten.

title: Salmorejo Cordoban Tomato Soup
summary: A thick, chilled Andalusian tomato and bread soup topped with egg.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes until the yolks are firm, then cool, peel and chop.
Blend the tomatoes, bread, garlic, vinegar and salt until smooth.
With the blender running, pour in the oil until the soup is thick and creamy.
Chill, then serve topped with the chopped egg.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the yolks are firm and keep the soup chilled, eating within 2 days.
Not suitable for gluten-free.

title: Spanish Russian Potato Salad Ensaladilla Rusa
summary: Potato, carrot, peas, tuna and egg bound with mayonnaise, a staple tapas plate.

steps.text: Boil the potato and carrot for 12 minutes until just tender, adding the peas for the last 2 minutes, then drain and cool.
Boil the eggs for 10 minutes until the yolks are firm, then cool, peel and chop.
Fold the vegetables, tuna, egg, mayonnaise, vinegar and salt together until coated.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the yolks are firm and keep the salad chilled, eating within 2 days.
Contains fish and egg.

title: Catalan Tomato Bread Pa amb Tomaquet
summary: Toasted bread rubbed with garlic and ripe tomato, finished with olive oil.

steps.text: Toast the bread under a hot grill for 2 minutes each side until golden.
Rub each slice with the garlic, then with the cut tomato until the flesh soaks in.
Drizzle with the oil and sprinkle with the salt.

notes: Use very ripe tomatoes for the best flavour.
Not suitable for gluten-free.

title: Uzbek Achichuk Tomato and Onion Salad
summary: Paper-thin tomato and red onion with chilli and coriander, served with plov and kebabs.

steps.text: Arrange the tomato and onion in overlapping layers on a plate.
Scatter over the chilli and coriander.
Sprinkle with the vinegar and salt and toss gently until coated, just before serving.

notes: Soak the sliced onion in cold water for a milder bite.
Naturally vegan and gluten-free.

title: Georgian Cucumber and Walnut Salad
summary: Crisp cucumber with ground walnuts, garlic and coriander in a light vinegar dressing.

steps.text: Mix the walnuts, garlic, vinegar, oil and salt into a rough paste.
Toss the cucumber and coriander with the paste until coated.
Serve straight away so the cucumber stays crisp.

notes: Contains tree nuts.
Naturally vegan and gluten-free.

title: Armenian Herb and Radish Salad
summary: A bright pile of parsley, mint, radish and tomato with lemon and olive oil.

steps.text: Combine the parsley, mint, radish, tomato and spring onions in a bowl.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice, sumac and salt together.
Toss the dressing through the salad until every leaf is glossy, just before serving.

notes: Naturally vegan and gluten-free.

title: Azerbaijani Grilled Eggplant and Tomato Salad
summary: Smoky roasted eggplant with tomato, capsicum, garlic and coriander.

steps.text: Roast the whole eggplants at 220°C for 40 minutes until collapsed and charred, then peel and chop the flesh.
Mix the eggplant with the tomato, capsicum, onion, garlic and coriander.
Dress with the oil, vinegar and salt.

notes: Drain the eggplant flesh well so the salad is not watery.
Naturally vegan and gluten-free.

title: Uzbek Spiced Carrot Salad
summary: Shredded carrot with garlic, coriander seed and chilli under hot oil.

steps.text: Mix the carrot, garlic, coriander, chilli flakes, sugar, vinegar and salt in a heatproof bowl.
Heat the oil for 2 minutes until shimmering, then pour it over the carrot.
Stir well and serve warm or chilled.

notes: Keeps 4 days in the fridge.
Naturally vegan and gluten-free.

title: Uzbek Lagman Noodle Soup
summary: Beef, capsicum and noodles in a tomato-rich broth, a Central Asian one-pot.

items.raw: 300 g beef rump, cut in thin strips

steps.text: Brown the beef in the oil for 4 minutes until coloured, then add the onion, carrot and capsicum for 5 minutes until softened.
Stir in the garlic, tomato paste and cumin for 1 minute, then add the stock.
Simmer for 15 minutes until the beef is tender.
Add the noodles and cook for 5 minutes until tender, then scatter with coriander.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef until no pink remains and the soup reaches 75°C; eat leftovers within 2 days.
Not suitable for gluten-free.

title: Peruvian Choclo con Queso
summary: Sweet corn on the cob served with salty feta, as sold on Andean street corners.

steps.text: Boil the corn in water for 12 minutes until the kernels are tender.
Drain and let the cobs steam dry for 1 minute.
Serve each cob with a slab of feta.

notes: Traditional queso fresco can replace the feta.
Naturally gluten-free.

title: Ecuadorian Llapingachos Cheesy Potato Patties
summary: Mashed potato patties stuffed with melting cheese and pan-fried until golden.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes for 15 minutes until soft, drain and mash with the salt.
Cook the onion in the butter for 5 minutes until soft and mix into the potato.
Shape into 8 balls, press a pinch of mozzarella into each and flatten into patties.
Fry in the oil for 4 minutes each side until golden and crisp.

notes: Serve with a fried egg or peanut sauce.
Naturally gluten-free.

title: Bolivian Quinoa Vegetable Soup
summary: A warming Andean soup of quinoa, potato, carrot and cumin.

steps.text: Cook the onion and carrot in the oil for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the potato, quinoa, cumin and stock and simmer for 20 minutes until the quinoa is tender and the potato soft.
Stir through the coriander and serve.

notes: Rinse the quinoa well to remove any bitterness.
Naturally vegan; check the stock for gluten.

title: Hawaiian Lomi Lomi Tomato Salad
summary: Juicy tomato massaged with sweet onion, spring onion and lemon, a luau side.

steps.text: Combine the tomato, onion and spring onions in a bowl.
Add the lemon juice, sesame oil and salt.
Massage gently with your fingers until the tomato releases its juices.

notes: Traditionally served with salmon or pork.
Naturally vegan and gluten-free.

title: Finnish Creamy Mushroom Salad
summary: Blanched button mushrooms in a cream and vinegar dressing with onion and chives.

steps.text: Blanch the mushrooms in boiling water for 3 minutes until just tender, then drain and cool.
Whisk the cream, vinegar and salt together until slightly thickened.
Fold through the mushrooms, onion and chives until coated.

notes: Serve on rye bread or beside roast meats.
Keeps 2 days in the fridge.

title: Hawaiian Pineapple Coleslaw
summary: Crunchy cabbage and carrot with sweet pineapple in a tangy creamy dressing.

steps.text: Combine the cabbage, carrot, pineapple and spring onions in a bowl.
Whisk the mayonnaise and vinegar together.
Toss through the slaw until evenly coated.

notes: Contains egg.
Naturally gluten-free.

title: Latvian Cabbage and Potato Soup
summary: A simple, homely soup of cabbage, potato and carrot finished with sour cream and dill.

steps.text: Cook the onion and carrot in the oil for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the cabbage, potato, stock and bay leaf and simmer for 20 minutes until the potato is tender.
Ladle into bowls and top with the sour cream and dill.

notes: Remove the bay leaf before serving.
Check the stock label for gluten.

title: Lemon Caper Butter Sauce for Fish
summary: A quick pan sauce of browned butter, capers, lemon and parsley for grilled or pan-fried fish.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a small pan over medium heat and cook for 2 minutes until foaming and lightly golden.
Add the garlic and capers for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Take off the heat, stir in the lemon juice and parsley and spoon over the fish.

notes: Use the sauce straight away while it is warm.
Rinse the capers if you want less salt.

title: Garlic and Parsley Compound Butter for Steak
summary: Soft butter blended with garlic, parsley and lemon zest, melted over hot grilled steak.

steps.text: Mash the butter with the garlic, parsley, lemon zest and salt in a bowl until smooth.
Roll into a log in baking paper and chill until firm.
Slice a round onto each hot steak just before serving.

notes: Freeze the log for up to 2 months.
Naturally gluten-free.

title: Mango Salsa for Grilled Fish
summary: Sweet mango, red onion, chilli and lime with fresh coriander, cool against smoky fish.

steps.text: Combine the mango, onion, chilli and coriander in a bowl.
Stir in the lime juice and salt until evenly mixed.
Spoon over grilled fish or chicken.

notes: Use firm, ripe mangoes so the pieces hold their shape.
Naturally vegan and gluten-free.

title: Tamarind Barbecue Glaze for Ribs and Chicken
summary: A sticky, tangy glaze of tamarind, brown sugar, soy and smoked paprika for brushing on the grill.

steps.text: Warm the oil in a small pan and cook the garlic and paprika for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the remaining ingredients and simmer for 8 minutes, stirring, until thick and glossy.
Brush over meat in the last 10 minutes of grilling.

notes: Food safety: use fresh glaze for brushing during cooking only and boil any glaze that touched raw meat for 2 minutes before serving.
Not suitable for gluten-free unless you use tamari.

title: Miso Glaze for Grilled Fish
summary: Sweet white miso, mirin and honey, brushed on salmon or eggplant before grilling.

steps.text: Whisk the miso, mirin, honey and vinegar in a small pan.
Warm over low heat for 2 minutes, stirring, until smooth and glossy.
Stir in the sesame oil and brush onto fish or vegetables before grilling.

notes: Watch closely under the grill, as the sugars catch quickly.
Check the miso label for gluten.

title: Lemon and Garlic Gremolata
summary: Chopped parsley, lemon zest and raw garlic in olive oil, a sharp finish for grilled meat and fish.

steps.text: Finely chop the parsley and garlic together until almost a paste.
Mix in the lemon zest and salt.
Stir in the oil and spoon over grilled meat or fish.

notes: Make it just before serving for the brightest colour.
Naturally vegan and gluten-free.

title: Chinese Black Vinegar and Chilli Dressing
summary: A dark, tangy dressing with soy, garlic and chilli oil for cold noodles and cucumber.

steps.text: Whisk the vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, chilli oil and sugar together until the sugar dissolves.
Stir in the grated garlic until evenly mixed.
Spoon over salads or noodles and toss until coated.

notes: Not suitable for gluten-free unless you use tamari.
Keeps 1 week in the fridge.

title: Vietnamese Lemongrass and Lime Dressing
summary: Fish sauce, lime and fragrant lemongrass for herb salads and rice noodle bowls.

steps.text: Stir the fish sauce, lime juice and sugar together until the sugar dissolves.
Add the lemongrass, chilli, garlic and oil and mix well.
Spoon over noodles, grilled meat or salad.

notes: Contains fish.
Keeps 5 days in the fridge.

title: Tahini Soy Dressing for Cold Noodles
summary: A nutty, creamy sesame dressing with soy and rice vinegar for cabbage and cold noodle salads.

steps.text: Whisk the tahini, soy sauce, vinegar, sugar and mayonnaise together until smooth.
Loosen with the water until pourable.
Toss through noodles or cabbage until coated.

notes: Contains sesame, soy and egg.
Not suitable for gluten-free unless you use tamari.

title: Thai Tamarind and Lime Dressing
summary: Sweet, sour and salty tamarind dressing for green mango and papaya salads.

steps.text: Whisk the tamarind, fish sauce, sugar and lime juice together until the sugar dissolves.
Stir in the chilli and oil.
Toss through salad until coated.

notes: Contains fish.
Keeps 5 days in the fridge.

title: Crispy Fried Shallots
summary: Golden, crunchy shallots to scatter over rice, noodles, soups and salads.

steps.text: Pat the shallots dry and put them in a cold pan with the oil.
Heat over medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring, until the shallots are deep golden.
Lift out with a slotted spoon onto paper towel and sprinkle with salt, where they crisp as they cool.

notes: Take them out slightly pale, as they keep darkening off the heat.
Store in an airtight jar for 1 week and keep the flavoured oil for cooking.

title: Hazelnut Dukkah
summary: Egyptian nut and spice mix of hazelnuts, sesame, coriander and cumin for dipping bread and oil.

steps.text: Toast the hazelnuts in a dry pan for 4 minutes until golden, then rub off the skins.
Toast the sesame, coriander and cumin seeds for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Crush or pulse everything with the salt and pepper until coarsely crushed.

notes: Contains tree nuts and sesame.
Keeps 3 weeks in a jar.

title: Furikake-Style Seed and Seaweed Sprinkle
summary: A toasted sesame, nori and salt seasoning for rice, eggs and avocado.

steps.text: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan for 3 minutes until golden.
Crumble the nori into fine flakes.
Mix with the sugar and salt and tip into a jar.

notes: Contains sesame.
Keeps 1 month in an airtight jar.

title: Crispy Garlic Chips
summary: Paper-thin garlic fried until golden, for soups, stir-fries and noodles.

steps.text: Put the garlic in a cold pan with the oil and heat over medium heat.
Stir for 3 minutes until the garlic is pale gold, then lift out onto paper towel.
Season with the salt and leave to crisp.

notes: Take it off before it browns, as it turns bitter quickly.
Keeps 3 days in a sealed jar.

title: Toasted Coconut Topping
summary: Golden coconut flakes with lime zest and a pinch of salt for curries, porridge and salads.

steps.text: Toast the coconut in a dry pan over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until golden.
Tip into a bowl straight away so it stops cooking.
Mix with the lime zest and salt.

notes: Watch closely, as coconut burns quickly.
Naturally vegan and gluten-free.

title: Za'atar Breadcrumbs
summary: Crisp olive-oil crumbs with za'atar for scattering over soups, roast vegetables and pasta.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a pan and fry the breadcrumbs for 4 minutes, stirring, until golden and crisp.
Take the pan off the heat and let the crumbs cool for 1 minute.
Stir through the za'atar and salt while still warm.

notes: Not suitable for gluten-free.
Keeps 3 days in an airtight tin.

title: Homemade Gomasio Sesame Salt
summary: Japanese toasted sesame and salt condiment for rice, vegetables and eggs.

steps.text: Toast the white and black sesame seeds in a dry pan for 3 to 4 minutes until golden and popping.
Tip into a mortar with the salt.
Crush lightly until about half the seeds are broken.

notes: Contains sesame.
Keeps 1 month in a jar.

title: Crispy Spiced Chickpea Topping
summary: Oven-roasted smoked paprika chickpeas that crunch over soups and salads.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C and line a tray with baking paper.
Toss the chickpeas with the oil, paprika and salt on a tray.
Roast for 25 minutes, shaking once, until crisp and golden.

notes: Eat the same day for the best crunch.
Naturally vegan and gluten-free.

title: Pangrattato Garlic Breadcrumbs
summary: Italian toasted breadcrumbs with garlic, chilli and parsley for pasta and vegetables.

steps.text: Heat the oil and fry the breadcrumbs for 4 minutes, stirring, until golden.
Add the garlic and chilli for 1 minute until fragrant.
Take off the heat and stir through the parsley.

notes: Not suitable for gluten-free.
Keeps 3 days in an airtight tin.

title: Peanut and Chilli Crunch Oil
summary: A crunchy chilli oil with peanuts, garlic and sesame for dumplings, noodles and eggs.

steps.text: Warm the oil and garlic in a small pan over low heat for 4 minutes until pale gold.
Add the peanuts and sesame seeds and cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Stir the chilli flakes, soy sauce and sugar into a heatproof bowl and pour over the hot oil until it sizzles.

notes: Contains peanuts and sesame.
Not suitable for gluten-free unless you use tamari.
Food safety: Keep any leftover garlic, herb or chilli oil in the fridge and use it within 4 days.

title: Apple and Lime Breakfast Smoothie with Mint
summary: A fresh yoghurt smoothie of apple, lime and mint with a little honey.

steps.text: Add everything to a blender.
Blend on high for 1 minute until smooth and frothy.
Pour into two tall glasses and drink straight away while cold.

notes: Use a dairy-free yoghurt and milk to make it vegan.
Naturally gluten-free.

title: Avocado and Spinach Breakfast Smoothie
summary: A creamy green smoothie with avocado, apple, spinach and yoghurt.

steps.text: Add the avocado, spinach, apple, milk, yoghurt and honey to a blender.
Blend for 1 minute until completely smooth.
Pour into two tall glasses and drink straight away while cold.

notes: Drink straight away, as it darkens on standing.
Naturally gluten-free.

title: Mango and Ginger Breakfast Smoothie
summary: Mango, yoghurt and orange juice with a warm kick of fresh ginger.

steps.text: Add everything to a blender.
Blend for 1 minute until smooth.
Pour into two tall glasses and drink straight away while cold.

notes: Use frozen mango for a thicker smoothie.
Naturally gluten-free.

title: Pear and Ginger Oat Breakfast Smoothie
summary: A filling smoothie of pear, rolled oats, milk and ginger with a touch of cinnamon.

steps.text: Add everything to a blender.
Blend for 1 to 2 minutes until the oats are fully broken down and the smoothie is smooth.
Pour into two tall glasses and drink straight away while cold.

notes: Oats can contain traces of gluten.
Use oat milk for a dairy-free version.

title: Pineapple and Coconut Breakfast Smoothie
summary: Pineapple, coconut milk and yoghurt blended into a creamy, sunny drink.

steps.text: Add everything to a blender.
Blend for 1 minute until smooth and creamy.
Pour into two tall glasses and drink straight away while cold.

notes: Shake the coconut milk can before opening.
Naturally gluten-free.

title: Orange and Carrot Breakfast Smoothie
summary: Carrot, orange and yoghurt with ginger and turmeric for a bright morning glass.

steps.text: Add everything to a blender.
Blend on high for 1 to 2 minutes until the carrot is fully broken down and the smoothie is smooth.
Pour into two tall glasses and drink straight away while cold.

notes: Strain through a sieve for a silky texture.
Naturally gluten-free.

title: Swedish Pickled Beetroot Salad
summary: Sliced beetroot in a sweet, sharp brine with red onion, a staple of the Swedish smorgasbord.

steps.text: Warm the vinegar, sugar, water, salt and bay leaf in a pan for 4 minutes, stirring, until the sugar dissolves.
Layer the beetroot and onion in a jar or bowl.
Pour over the warm brine and leave to cool before serving.

notes: Best after a few hours in the fridge.
Keeps 1 week chilled.

title: Lithuanian Grated Beetroot Salad with Sour Cream
summary: Grated cooked beetroot with garlic, dill and sour cream, bright and tangy.

steps.text: Mix the sour cream, garlic, lemon juice and salt together in a bowl.
Fold the grated beetroot through the dressing until evenly coated and pink.
Scatter with the dill and serve chilled.

notes: Naturally gluten-free.
Keeps 2 days in the fridge.

title: Danish Cauliflower Soup
summary: A smooth, buttery cauliflower and potato soup with a splash of milk.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the butter for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the cauliflower, potato and stock and simmer for 15 minutes until the vegetables are very tender.
Blend until smooth, then stir in the milk and nutmeg and warm for 2 minutes until hot.

notes: Use oil and oat milk for a dairy-free soup.
Check the stock label for gluten.

title: Nigerian Maize Pap Porridge
summary: A smooth, lightly sweet cornmeal porridge made with milk, a common family breakfast.

steps.text: Whisk the cornmeal with 1/2 cup of the cold water until no lumps remain.
Bring the rest of the water to the boil, then whisk in the cornmeal paste until smooth.
Cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring, until thick and glossy, then stir in the milk and sugar.

notes: Add more water for a thinner pap.
Naturally gluten-free.

title: Kenyan Uji Maize and Lemon Porridge
summary: A thin, tangy maize flour porridge with lemon and sugar, a warming Kenyan breakfast drink.

steps.text: Whisk the maize flour with 1/2 cup of the cold water until smooth.
Bring the remaining water to the boil, pour in the paste and whisk until smooth.
Simmer for 8 minutes, stirring, until thickened and cooked through, then stir in the sugar, lemon juice and salt.

notes: Serve hot in mugs.
Naturally vegan and gluten-free.

title: Antiguan Greens and Pumpkin Soup
summary: Spinach, pumpkin and sweet potato simmered with thyme and a little coconut milk.

steps.text: Cook the onion and garlic in the oil for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the pumpkin, sweet potato, thyme and stock and simmer for 18 minutes until tender.
Add the spinach and coconut milk and cook for 3 minutes until the spinach is wilted, then blend roughly.

notes: Add a whole chilli while simmering for gentle heat.
Check the stock label for gluten.

title: Thai Suki Dipping Sauce
summary: A sweet, sour and garlicky chilli dip with sesame, the classic partner to Thai hot pot.

steps.text: Whisk the sriracha, fish sauce, lime juice, sugar and peanut butter together until smooth.
Stir in the garlic, sesame seeds and coriander.
Spoon into small dipping bowls.

notes: Contains fish, peanuts and sesame.
Keeps 5 days in the fridge.

title: Taiwanese-Style Sesame Satay Hot Pot Dip
summary: A rich peanut, garlic and chilli oil dip for dunking hot pot meats and vegetables.

steps.text: Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, vinegar, sugar and hot water together until smooth.
Stir in the sesame oil, chilli oil and garlic.
Scatter with the spring onions and serve in small bowls.

notes: Contains peanuts.
Not suitable for gluten-free unless you use tamari.
Food safety: Keep any leftover garlic, herb or chilli oil in the fridge and use it within 4 days.

title: Pacific Pineapple and Cucumber Salad
summary: Sweet pineapple, cool cucumber, chilli and lime topped with toasted coconut.

steps.text: Combine the pineapple, cucumber, chilli and mint in a bowl.
Pour over the lime juice and toss until coated.
Scatter with the coconut just before serving.

notes: Naturally vegan and gluten-free.
Serve with grilled fish or chicken.

title: Hawaiian Sweet Potato Salad
summary: Tender sweet potato in a creamy rice vinegar dressing with spring onion, like a luau potato salad.

steps.text: Boil the sweet potato for 12 to 15 minutes until just tender, then drain and cool.
Mix the mayonnaise, vinegar, mustard and salt together.
Fold the sweet potato and spring onions through the dressing until coated.

notes: Contains egg.
Keeps 2 days in the fridge.

title: Samoan Coconut Cabbage Salad
summary: Crisp cabbage with tomato, onion and a lime and coconut cream dressing.

steps.text: Combine the cabbage, tomato and onion in a bowl.
Whisk the coconut cream, lime juice and salt together.
Toss the dressing through the salad until the cabbage is coated.

notes: Serve straight away for the best crunch.
Naturally vegan and gluten-free.

title: Tajik Radish and Onion Salad
summary: Sharp radish and red onion in a light dill and vinegar dressing, a crisp table salad for plov.

steps.text: Combine the radish, onion and dill in a bowl.
Whisk the oil, vinegar and salt together.
Pour over the salad and toss until lightly coated.

notes: Soak the onion in cold water for a milder bite.
Naturally vegan and gluten-free.

title: Peruvian Ocopa Peanut and Herb Sauce
summary: A creamy peanut, coriander and chilli sauce for boiled potatoes and grilled meats.

steps.text: Cook the onion and garlic in the oil for 4 minutes until soft.
Blend with the peanuts, feta, milk, coriander and chilli until smooth.
Spoon over boiled potatoes or grilled meat.

notes: Contains peanuts and dairy.
Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Bolivian Llajwa Tomato and Chilli Salsa
summary: A fresh Andean salsa of tomato, chilli and coriander, served beside grilled meat and potatoes.

steps.text: Blend the tomato, chillies, coriander and garlic until finely chopped.
Stir in the oil and salt until combined.
Serve cool in a small bowl.

notes: Remove the chilli seeds for a milder salsa.
Naturally vegan and gluten-free.

title: Alentejo Bread and Coriander Soup with Poached Egg
summary: A Portuguese peasant soup of garlic, coriander and bread softened in olive oil broth.

steps.text: Crush the garlic, coriander and salt to a paste.
Stir in the oil and boiling water and simmer for 5 minutes until fragrant.
Poach the eggs in the broth for 3 minutes until the whites are fully set.
Place the bread in bowls and ladle over the broth and eggs.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set.
Not suitable for gluten-free.

title: Portuguese Tomato Rice Soup
summary: A light tomato soup with rice, garlic and parsley, simple Portuguese comfort.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, rice, stock and bay leaf and simmer for 15 minutes until the rice is tender.
Stir through the parsley.

notes: Food safety: cool leftovers and refrigerate within 1 hour, then reheat until steaming hot.
Remove the bay leaf before serving.

title: Spanish Garlic Migas Breakfast Fry-Up
summary: Crisp garlicky breadcrumbs fried with smoked paprika and chorizo, topped with a fried egg.

steps.text: Fry the chorizo in the oil for 3 minutes until crisp and the fat has run.
Add the bread and garlic and cook for 6 minutes, tossing, until golden and crisp.
Stir in the paprika, push the migas aside and fry the eggs for 3 minutes until the whites are set.

notes: Food safety: cook the chorizo until it reaches 75°C and the egg whites are fully set.
Not suitable for gluten-free.

title: Basque Piperade with Eggs
summary: Soft capsicum, tomato and onion stew with eggs scrambled through.

steps.text: Cook the onion and capsicum in the oil for 10 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, paprika and tomato and simmer for 10 minutes until jammy.
Crack in the eggs and stir gently for 3 minutes until just set.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until fully set.
Naturally gluten-free.

title: Dill Yoghurt Sauce for Grilled Salmon
summary: Cool, garlicky Greek yoghurt with dill, lemon and a touch of mustard.

steps.text: Stir the yoghurt, dill, lemon juice, garlic, mustard and salt together until smooth.
Taste and add more lemon if needed.
Spoon beside grilled salmon and finish with a little extra dill.

notes: Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
Naturally gluten-free.

title: Pineapple Teriyaki Sauce
summary: A glossy pineapple, soy and ginger sauce for grilled chicken, pork and tofu.

steps.text: Simmer the pineapple juice, soy sauce, sugar, garlic and ginger for 5 minutes until reduced a little.
Mix the cornflour with the water and stir in.
Cook for 2 minutes, stirring, until glossy and thick.

notes: Food safety: if you used it to marinate raw meat, boil the sauce for 2 minutes before serving.
Not suitable for gluten-free unless you use tamari.

title: Charred Spring Onion Salsa for Grilled Meat
summary: Smoky charred spring onions chopped with olive oil, capers and parsley.

steps.text: Grill the spring onions on a hot barbecue or pan for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until charred and tender.
Chop roughly and mix with the oil, vinegar, capers, parsley and chilli flakes.
Spoon over grilled steak, lamb or chicken.

notes: Make it while the onions are warm so they soak up the dressing.
Naturally vegan and gluten-free.

title: Lithuanian Bulviniai Blynai Potato Pancakes
summary: Crisp-edged grated potato pancakes with onion, fried golden and eaten with sour cream.

steps.text: Squeeze the grated potato in a clean tea towel to remove the liquid.
Mix with the onion, egg, flour and salt.
Fry spoonfuls in the oil for 4 minutes each side until deep golden and cooked through.

notes: Food safety: cook the pancakes until the centre is hot and the egg fully set.
Not suitable for gluten-free.

title: Kyrgyz Beef and Cabbage Soup
summary: A plain, filling beef broth with potato, carrot, cabbage and dill.

steps.text: Brown the beef in the oil for 5 minutes until coloured, then add the onion and carrot for 4 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and stock and simmer for 35 minutes until the beef is tender.
Add the potato and cabbage and cook for 15 minutes until soft, then stir through the dill.

notes: Food safety: cook the beef until tender and the soup reaches 75°C; eat leftovers within 3 days.
Check the stock label for gluten.

title: Ecuadorian Tuna and Onion Soup
summary: A lime-sharp tuna, potato and tomato soup finished with red onion and coriander.

steps.text: Cook the onion and capsicum in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, then stir in the tomato and cumin.
Add the potato and stock and simmer for 15 minutes until the potato is tender.
Stir in the tuna and cook for 3 minutes until heated through, then add the lime juice and coriander.

notes: Food safety: keep the tuna chilled until use and eat leftovers within 2 days, reheating until steaming hot.
Contains fish.

title: Norwegian Sour Cream Porridge Rommegrot
summary: A rich, silky porridge simmered from sour cream, flour and milk, served with cinnamon and sugar.

steps.text: Simmer the sour cream in a heavy saucepan for 5 minutes until it thins and the fat starts to separate.
Sift in the flour, whisking, and cook for 3 minutes until smooth and thick.
Add the milk gradually, whisking, and simmer for 8 minutes until thick and glossy.
Stir in the butter and serve topped with the sugar and cinnamon.

notes: Traditionally the separated butter is skimmed off and drizzled on top.
Not suitable for gluten-free.

title: Estonian Cucumber and Sour Cream Salad
summary: Cool cucumber slices dressed with sour cream, dill and a splash of vinegar.

steps.text: Whisk the sour cream, dill, vinegar, sugar and salt together until smooth.
Fold the cucumber through the dressing until coated.
Serve straight away with potatoes or grilled fish.

notes: Naturally gluten-free.
Salt draws water from the cucumber, so dress it just before serving.

title: Portuguese Chickpea and Egg Salad
summary: Chickpeas, boiled egg and red onion in olive oil and parsley, a classic Portuguese petisco.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes until the yolks are firm, then cool, peel and chop.
Combine the chickpeas, onion and parsley in a bowl.
Whisk the oil, vinegar and salt, toss through the salad and fold in the egg.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the yolks are firm and keep the salad chilled, eating within 2 days.
Naturally gluten-free.

title: Spanish Orange and Red Onion Salad
summary: Juicy orange rounds with red onion, black olives and olive oil, a bright Andalusian winter salad.

steps.text: Arrange the orange slices on a platter and scatter over the onion and olives.
Whisk the oil and vinegar together.
Drizzle over the salad until the slices glisten, then finish with the parsley.

notes: Naturally vegan and gluten-free.
Soak the onion in cold water first for a milder bite.

title: Spanish Garlic Mushrooms Champinones al Ajillo
summary: Mushrooms sizzled in olive oil with lots of garlic, chilli and lemon, a tapas bar favourite.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pan and cook the mushrooms for 6 minutes until golden and their liquid has gone.
Add the garlic and chilli and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Take off the heat and stir through the lemon juice, parsley and salt.

notes: Serve with crusty bread to mop up the oil.
Naturally vegan and gluten-free.

title: Galician Paprika Potatoes
summary: Boiled potatoes tossed in olive oil, sweet smoked paprika and coarse salt.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 to 20 minutes until tender, then drain and let them steam dry for 2 minutes.
Toss with the oil, paprika and salt until evenly coated.
Serve warm straight from the bowl, with extra paprika on the side if you like.

notes: Naturally vegan and gluten-free.
Use a mix of sweet and hot paprika for extra warmth.

title: Peruvian Corn, Tomato and Feta Salad
summary: Sweet corn kernels, tomato and salty feta with lime and coriander, like the Andean solterito.

steps.text: Boil the corn for 10 to 12 minutes until tender, then cool and cut the kernels from the cobs.
Combine the kernels, tomato, onion and feta in a bowl.
Dress with the oil and lime juice and scatter with the coriander.

notes: Naturally gluten-free.
Serve with grilled meat or fish.

title: Ecuadorian Peanut Sauce for Potatoes
summary: A warm, creamy peanut and onion sauce for boiled potatoes, eggs and grilled meat.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic and cumin for 1 minute.
Whisk in the peanut butter, milk and salt and simmer for 4 minutes, stirring, until thick and smooth.
Spoon over potatoes or grilled meat.

notes: Contains peanuts and dairy.
Thin with extra milk if it thickens on standing.

title: Smoky Paprika Aioli for Grilled Fish
summary: Garlicky mayonnaise with smoked paprika and lemon, a spoonful for grilled fish and prawns.

steps.text: Mix the mayonnaise, garlic, paprika and lemon juice together in a bowl.
Stir until smooth, then taste and adjust the lemon and paprika.
Spoon beside grilled fish or prawns.

notes: Contains egg.
Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

title: Green Chilli and Coriander Chutney for Grilled Meat
summary: A fiery, fresh herb chutney with yoghurt and lime for kebabs and tandoori-style meats.

steps.text: Blend the coriander, mint, chillies, garlic, lemon juice, oil and salt until smooth.
Stir through the yoghurt until evenly green.
Spoon beside grilled meat.

notes: Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
Naturally gluten-free.

title: Hoisin Barbecue Glaze
summary: A sticky hoisin, honey and soy glaze with five spice for ribs, chicken and pork belly.

steps.text: Combine all the ingredients in a small pan.
Simmer for 4 minutes, stirring, until thick and glossy.
Brush over meat during the last 10 minutes of grilling.

notes: Food safety: do not reuse glaze that touched raw meat unless you boil it for 2 minutes first.
Not suitable for gluten-free unless you use tamari.

title: Ginger Soy Dressing for Steamed Greens
summary: A quick dressing of soy, ginger, sesame oil and garlic to spoon over bok choy and broccoli.

steps.text: Whisk the soy sauce, vinegar, ginger, honey and garlic together until combined.
Whisk in the sesame oil and vegetable oil until glossy.
Spoon over steamed greens.

notes: Not suitable for gluten-free unless you use tamari.
Keeps 1 week in the fridge.

title: Seeded Crunch Topping
summary: Toasted sunflower, pumpkin and sesame seeds with honey, for porridge, yoghurt and salads.

steps.text: Toast the sunflower, pumpkin and sesame seeds in a dry pan for 4 minutes until golden.
Add the honey and salt and stir for 2 minutes until the seeds clump and the honey turns sticky.
Spread on baking paper and cool until crisp, then break into pieces.

notes: Contains sesame.
Keeps 2 weeks in a jar.

title: Egyptian Eggah Herb Omelette
summary: A thick, sliceable omelette packed with parsley, dill and spring onion.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs with the flour, cumin and salt, then stir in the parsley, dill and spring onions.
Heat the oil in a 24 cm non-stick frying pan and pour in the mixture.
Cook over low heat for 10 minutes until the base is golden and the top is nearly set, then grill for 3 minutes until set.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until fully set with no runny egg.
Not suitable for gluten-free.

title: Malawian Peanut Butter Maize Porridge
summary: Thick maize porridge enriched with peanut butter and a spoon of sugar.

steps.text: Whisk the maize flour with 1/2 cup of the cold water until smooth.
Bring the remaining water to the boil and whisk in the paste until smooth.
Simmer for 8 minutes, stirring, until thick, then stir in the peanut butter and sugar.

notes: Contains peanuts.
Naturally gluten-free.

title: Tongan Cucumber and Coconut Lime Salad
summary: Crisp cucumber and tomato in a creamy lime and coconut dressing with chilli.

steps.text: Combine the cucumber, tomato and chilli in a bowl.
Whisk the coconut cream, lime juice and salt together.
Toss the dressing through the salad until coated.

notes: Serve straight away to keep the cucumber crisp.
Naturally vegan and gluten-free.

title: Coriander and Lime Dressing for Fish Tacos
summary: A zesty blended dressing of coriander, lime, garlic and olive oil for fish, slaw and tacos.

steps.text: Blend the coriander, lime juice, oil, garlic, honey, cumin and salt until smooth.
Taste and add more lime if needed.
Drizzle over fish, slaw or tacos.

notes: Keeps 4 days in the fridge.
Naturally gluten-free.

title: Irish Brown Bread with Smoked Salmon and Cucumber
summary: Wholemeal brown bread layered with cream cheese, smoked salmon, cucumber and lemon.

steps.text: Spread the cream cheese over the brown bread until it reaches the edges.
Top with the cucumber and smoked salmon.
Finish with the lemon juice and dill, then cut into triangles.

notes: Food safety: smoked salmon is eaten uncooked, so keep it chilled and avoid it in pregnancy.
Not suitable for gluten-free.

title: Savoury Mushroom and Barley Breakfast Porridge
summary: Pearl barley simmered in mushroom stock, soy and spring onion, a warming savoury start.

steps.text: Cook the onion and mushrooms in the oil for 6 minutes until golden.
Add the barley, stock and soy sauce and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the barley is tender and the porridge is thick.
Ladle into bowls and top with the spring onions.

notes: Not suitable for gluten-free.
Add a poached egg for extra protein.

title: Carrot and Cumin Soup with Yoghurt
summary: A sweet, earthy carrot soup spiced with cumin and swirled with yoghurt.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, then stir in the cumin for 1 minute.
Add the carrots and stock and simmer for 20 minutes until very tender.
Blend until smooth and serve with a swirl of yoghurt.

notes: Check the stock label for gluten.
Use a dairy-free yoghurt to make it vegan.

title: Lemon Tahini Dressing
summary: A creamy sesame dressing sharpened with lemon and garlic for grain bowls and roast vegetables.

steps.text: Whisk the tahini and lemon juice together until thick, which will look curdled at first.
Whisk in the garlic, salt and water until smooth and pourable.
Drizzle over salads or vegetables from the oven.

notes: Contains sesame.
Keeps 5 days in the fridge.

title: Danish Brown-Butter Carrots with Parsley
summary: Carrot batons glazed in nutty brown butter, honey and lemon.

steps.text: Put the carrots, water and salt in a wide frying pan, cover and simmer for 8 minutes until the carrots are just tender.
Uncover and boil off the remaining water until the pan is nearly dry.
Add the butter and cook for 2 minutes, stirring, until the butter foams and smells nutty.
Stir in the honey and lemon juice and toss for 1 minute until the carrots are glossy, then scatter with parsley.

notes: Pairs well with roast chicken, fish or pork.
Keeps in the fridge for 3 days.

title: Swedish Honey-Roasted Swede Wedges
summary: Sweet, sticky roast swede with thyme, a classic Nordic winter side.

items.raw: 700g swede, peeled and cut into wedges

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200C and line a tray with baking paper.
Toss the swede with the oil, thyme, salt and pepper and spread in a single layer.
Roast for 30 minutes, turning once, until tender and browned at the edges.
Drizzle with the honey and roast for 8 minutes more until sticky and caramelised.

notes: Swede can be tough to cut, so slice a flat side first for a stable base.

title: Danish Sweet-Sour Red Cabbage with Apple
summary: Slow-braised red cabbage with apple, cinnamon and vinegar, served warm or cold.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the cabbage, apple, cinnamon, sugar, salt and water and stir well.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 35 minutes, stirring now and then, until the cabbage is very tender.
Stir in the vinegar and cook uncovered for 5 minutes until the liquid is syrupy.

notes: Flavour improves overnight; reheat gently.
Freezes well for up to 3 months.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Garlic Walnut Paste with Coriander for Roast Vegetables
summary: A garlicky walnut sauce with coriander and vinegar for roast vegetables, chicken or fish.

steps.text: Blend the walnuts, garlic, coriander leaves, ground coriander, chilli and salt until a coarse paste forms.
Add the vinegar and water a little at a time and blend until a thick, spoonable sauce forms.
Taste and add a pinch more salt if needed.

notes: Keeps in a clean jar in the fridge for 4 days; thin with water if it thickens.
Serve about 2 tablespoons per person.

title: Warm Green Beans in Garlic Walnut Paste
summary: Tender green beans in a garlicky walnut and coriander dressing, served warm or at room temperature.

steps.text: Boil the beans in salted water for 5 minutes until tender but still bright green, then drain.
Blend the walnuts, garlic, vinegar, oil, ground coriander, salt and water until a thick, rough paste forms.
Toss the warm beans with the walnut paste until evenly coated.
Scatter with coriander leaves and serve.

notes: Also good as a cold lunchbox side.

title: Latvian Grated Carrot Salad with Sour Cream and Sultanas
summary: A sweet and creamy carrot salad with dill, common on Baltic tables.

steps.text: Mix the sour cream, lemon juice, dill and salt in a large bowl until smooth.
Fold through the grated carrot and sultanas until evenly coated.
Taste, adjust the lemon and serve cold.

notes: Best eaten within 2 days; the carrot softens as it sits.

title: Creamy Chilled Avocado Soup with Coriander
summary: A no-cook blended soup, creamy and bright, for warm days.

steps.text: Blend the avocado, cucumber, stock, yoghurt, lime juice, spring onion and salt until completely smooth.
Taste and add more lime or salt if needed.
Ladle into bowls and top with coriander.

notes: The colour browns in the air, so serve the same day.
Use cold stock for a properly chilled soup.

title: Guyanese Split Pea Soup with Flour Spinners
summary: A hearty yellow split pea soup with thyme, cumin and little rolled flour dumplings.
