steps.text: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion, garlic and carrot for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the cumin and thyme for 30 seconds until fragrant, then add the split peas, the 2 litres of water and 1 tsp salt.
Simmer for 45 minutes, stirring now and then, until the peas have broken down into a thick soup.
Mix the flour, 1/4 tsp salt and 1/3 cup water into a firm dough, roll into thin finger-length spinners and drop them into the soup.
Simmer for 10 minutes until the spinners are cooked through and the soup is thick.

notes: Add a splash of water when reheating; the soup thickens as it cools.
Freezes well without the spinners.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Bajan Sweet Potato Soup with Ginger and Coconut
summary: A velvety orange soup with fresh ginger, coconut milk and a squeeze of lime.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion, garlic and ginger for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the sweet potato and stock, cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the sweet potato is very soft.
Blend with a stick blender until smooth, stir in the coconut milk and heat for 3 minutes until just steaming.
Finish with the lime juice and season to taste.

notes: Freezes well for up to 3 months without the coconut milk; add it when reheating.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Swedish Dill and Mustard Potato Salad
summary: Warm waxy potatoes in a tangy mustard and olive oil dressing with red onion and dill, no mayo.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 18 minutes until a knife slips in easily, then drain.
Whisk the oil, mustard, vinegar, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Add the warm potatoes and onion and toss gently until coated.
Fold through the dill and serve warm or at room temperature.

notes: Travels well in a lunchbox; it does not need keeping cold for a few hours but is best chilled for longer transport.

title: Turmeric Silverbeet with Ginger, Ethiopian Style
summary: Silverbeet gently braised with garlic, ginger and turmeric in the style of gomen.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pan and cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the garlic, ginger and turmeric and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the silverbeet stems, water and salt, cover and cook for 5 minutes until the stems soften.
Add the leaves and cook uncovered for 6 minutes, stirring, until tender and the liquid has cooked off.

notes: Serve with flatbread, lentils or rice.
Silverbeet is naturally salty, so taste before adding more salt.

title: Ugandan Rolex Egg and Chapati Rolls
summary: Street-style breakfast rolls of folded omelette, cabbage and tomato in warm flatbread.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs with the salt and stir through the onion and tomato.
Heat half the oil in a frying pan and cook half the egg mixture for 3 minutes, flipping once, until fully set; repeat with the rest.
Warm the flatbreads in a dry pan for 30 seconds each side until soft.
Lay an omelette on each flatbread, top with cabbage and roll up tightly.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until fully set with no runny egg, especially for children, older adults or anyone pregnant.
Eat the same day.

title: Trinidadian Curried Channa Breakfast with Flatbread
summary: Spiced curried chickpeas with tomato, scooped up with toasted flatbread.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a pot and cook the onion and garlic for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the curry powder for 1 minute until fragrant, then add the tomato and cook for 3 minutes until it breaks down.
Add the chickpeas, water and salt and simmer for 10 minutes, mashing a few chickpeas, until thick.
Toast the flatbreads in a dry pan until warm and lightly browned, then serve with the channa and coriander.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for 4 days and tastes better the next day.

title: Toasted Sesame and Rice Vinegar Slaw Dressing
summary: A quick Asian-style dressing for crunchy cabbage and carrot slaw.

steps.text: Whisk the sesame oil, rice vinegar, soy sauce, honey, ginger and garlic in a bowl until the honey dissolves.
Stir in the sesame seeds and taste, adding a little more vinegar if you like it sharper.
Toss through shredded cabbage, carrot and spring onion just before serving.

notes: Makes enough for about 600g of shredded vegetables.
Keeps in a jar in the fridge for 5 days; shake before using.

title: Coconut Lime Dressing for Red Cabbage Slaw
summary: A creamy, tangy dressing with lime, chilli and coriander for slaws and grilled fish.

steps.text: Whisk the coconut cream, lime juice, honey, oil and salt in a bowl until smooth.
Stir in the chilli and coriander and taste, adding more lime or honey to balance.
Toss through shredded red cabbage and carrot just before serving.

notes: Coconut cream firms in the fridge; stir or warm briefly to loosen.
Keeps for 3 days.

title: Cocoa Oat Smoothie with Peanut Butter
summary: A filling chocolatey breakfast smoothie with rolled oats and peanut butter.

steps.text: Put the oats, milk, peanut butter, cocoa, honey and ice in a blender.
Blend on high for 1 minute until completely smooth with no oat flecks.
Pour into two glasses and drink straight away.

notes: Contains peanuts and milk; swap in oat milk and sunflower seed butter if needed.
For a thicker smoothie use less ice.

title: Gentle Rice and Chicken Soup with Ginger
summary: A mild soup of poached chicken, soft rice, carrot and ginger, plain and warm.

steps.text: Bring the stock, water, ginger, carrots and celery to a simmer in a large pot for 5 minutes until the carrots start to soften.
Add the chicken and rice and simmer gently for 20 minutes until the rice is very soft and the chicken is cooked through.
Lift out the chicken, shred it with two forks and return it to the pot.
Season with the salt and top with spring onions.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until there is no pink and the juices run clear, with an internal temperature of 75°C.
Food safety: cooked rice should be cooled and refrigerated within 1 hour, and reheated until steaming hot.
Keeps for 2 days in the fridge.

title: Pumpkin and Chicken Soup with Thyme
summary: A mild, comforting soup of poached chicken and soft pumpkin with thyme and white pepper.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the pumpkin, stock, water, thyme and bay leaf and bring to a simmer for 5 minutes until steaming.
Add the chicken and simmer for 20 minutes until the pumpkin is very soft and the chicken is cooked through.
Lift out the chicken and shred it, discard the bay leaf, then lightly mash the pumpkin into the broth until thick.
Return the chicken to the pot, season with salt and white pepper and heat for 2 minutes until hot.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until there is no pink and the juices run clear, with an internal temperature of 75°C.
Freezes well for up to 3 months.

title: Budget Cabbage, Potato and White Bean Soup
summary: A cheap, filling pantry soup that feeds six for very little.

items.raw: 400g can cannellini beans, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion and carrots for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the potatoes, cabbage, water, stock powder and thyme and simmer for 20 minutes until the potato is tender.
Add the beans and simmer for 5 minutes until heated through.
Mash a few potato cubes against the side of the pot to thicken the soup and season to taste.

notes: Costs roughly a dollar a serve using supermarket basics.
Freezes well for up to 3 months.

title: Freezer-Batch Tomato and Red Capsicum Soup
summary: A big batch of smoky roasted-style tomato and capsicum soup that freezes in single portions.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onions and capsicum for 10 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, paprika and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and stock and simmer for 20 minutes until the capsicum is very soft.
Blend with a stick blender until smooth and season with the salt.

notes: Cool completely before freezing in portions for up to 3 months; reheat until steaming hot.
Leave a gap at the top of each container as the soup expands.

title: High-Fibre Oat Bran and Apple Breakfast Bowl
summary: Creamy oat bran porridge topped with grated apple, sunflower seeds and walnuts.

steps.text: Stir the oat bran, milk and cinnamon in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Cook for 4 minutes, stirring, until thick and creamy.
Spoon into bowls and top with the apple, sunflower seeds and walnuts.

notes: Use any milk you like; the fibre is mostly from the oat bran, apple and sunflower seeds.
Add a splash more milk for a looser porridge.

title: High-Fibre Black Bean and Corn Breakfast Tostadas
summary: Crisp corn tortillas with black beans, sweet corn, avocado and a fried egg.

items.raw: 400g can black beans, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200C, brush the tortillas with the olive oil and bake on trays for 8 minutes until crisp and lightly golden.
Warm the beans, corn, cumin and salt in a saucepan for 5 minutes, mashing some beans, until hot.
Fry the eggs in the vegetable oil for 3 minutes until the whites are fully set.
Pile the bean mixture on the tostadas, top with avocado and a fried egg, then finish with lime juice and coriander.

notes: Make the bean mixture ahead and reheat until steaming.
Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites and yolks are firm if serving children, older adults or anyone pregnant. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Lunchbox Chickpea, Corn and Herb Jar Salad
summary: A layered jar salad that stays crisp until lunch, with the dressing kept at the bottom.

steps.text: Whisk the oil, lemon juice, mustard and salt and divide between four jars.
Layer in the chickpeas, corn, cucumber, capsicum and spring onions, then top with the parsley and feta.
Seal and keep refrigerated until lunchtime, then shake into a bowl.

notes: Pack with an ice brick; keep chilled and eat within 4 hours out of the fridge.
Assembled jars last 2 days in the fridge.

title: Kids' Cheesy Cauliflower Bites
summary: Soft baked cauliflower and cheese nuggets, mild enough for little ones and good cold in a lunchbox.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200C and line a tray with baking paper.
Steam the cauliflower for 8 minutes until very tender, then chop finely and squeeze out excess water.
Mix with the egg, cheddar and breadcrumbs until a thick mixture forms, then shape into 16 small bites.
Brush with the oil and bake for 18 minutes, turning once, until golden and firm.

notes: Food safety: bake until the egg is cooked through and the bites are hot in the centre.
Freeze uncooked bites on a tray, then bag for up to 2 months; bake from frozen for a few minutes longer.

title: Maple Carrot and Spinach Salad (Low-FODMAP Friendly)
summary: Roasted maple carrots over baby spinach with pumpkin seeds and lemon, no onion or garlic.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 210C and line a tray with baking paper.
Toss the carrots with 1 tbsp of the oil, 1 tbsp of the maple syrup and the salt and roast for 25 minutes until tender and caramelised.
Whisk the remaining oil, maple syrup and the lemon juice in a large bowl.
Add the spinach and warm carrots and toss until the leaves just wilt, then scatter with the pumpkin seeds.

notes: Low-FODMAP friendly: the ingredients are generally considered low in FODMAPs at these serve sizes, but individual tolerance varies, so check against your own plan.
Serve warm or cold.

title: Holiday Brunch Baked Egg Cups with Spinach and Ham
summary: Make-ahead muffin-tin egg cups with ham, spinach and cheddar, ideal for a crowd.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180C and brush a 12-hole muffin tin with the butter.
Whisk the eggs, milk and pepper, then divide the ham, spinach and cheddar between the holes.
Pour in the egg mixture and bake for 20 minutes until puffed, golden and set in the centre.

notes: Food safety: bake until the eggs are fully set with no runny egg; reheat leftovers until steaming hot.
Keeps in the fridge for 3 days or freezes for 2 months.

title: Orange Cinnamon French Toast Bake for Holiday Brunch
summary: A custardy baked French toast with orange and cinnamon, prepared the night before.

steps.text: Grease a large baking dish with the butter and spread the bread cubes in it.
Whisk the eggs, milk, sugar, orange zest and juice, cinnamon and vanilla until smooth and pour over the bread, pressing it down to soak.
Heat the oven to 180C and bake for 40 minutes until puffed, golden and the centre is set.
Serve warm with extra orange segments or yoghurt.

notes: Assemble the night before and keep covered in the fridge, then bake in the morning.
Food safety: bake until the custard is fully set and reaches 71C in the centre. Wash fresh produce well, refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat them within 3 days.

title: Asparagus and Pea Frittata Squares
summary: Fluffy baked frittata studded with spring asparagus and sweet peas, cut into squares for brunch.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180C and line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Warm the oil in a frying pan and cook the asparagus for 3 minutes, until just tender, then stir through the peas.
Whisk the eggs with the mint, seasoning and grated cheese, then pour into the tin and scatter over the vegetables and spoonfuls of ricotta.
Bake for 22 minutes, until puffed, golden and set in the centre.
Rest for 5 minutes, then cut into 6 squares.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until fully set in the centre; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Lemon Roasted Asparagus with Toasted Almonds
summary: Blistered asparagus finished with lemon zest and crunchy almonds, a fast spring side.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220C and line a large tray with baking paper.
Toss the asparagus with half the oil and seasoning on a tray and roast for 10 minutes, until tender with charred tips.
Toast the almonds in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 3 minutes, until golden.
Stir the garlic into the remaining oil, then toss through the hot asparagus with the lemon zest and juice.
Scatter with almonds and serve warm.

notes: Serve with grilled fish or chicken.

title: Fresh Pea and Mint Soup with Lemon
summary: A bright green spring soup of sweet peas, mint and a squeeze of lemon.

steps.text: Warm the oil in a saucepan and cook the onion for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the potato and stock, bring to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes, until the potato is tender.
Add the peas and cook for 3 minutes, until bright green.
Blend with the mint until smooth, then stir through the lemon juice and season.
Reheat gently until steaming and serve.

notes: Swirl through a spoonful of yoghurt for extra creaminess.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Split Pea and Ham Soup for the Freezer
summary: A thick, comforting soup that freezes well in single portions.

steps.text: Warm the oil in a large pot and cook the onion, carrot and celery for 6 minutes, until soft.
Add the garlic, split peas, ham hock, bay leaves and water, stirring until it comes to the boil.
Simmer gently for 70 minutes, stirring now and then, until the peas collapse and the ham falls from the bone.
Lift out the hock, shred the meat and return it to the pot, discarding skin and bone.
Season with pepper and add a splash of water if too thick.

notes: Food safety: cool quickly, refrigerate within 2 hours and freeze in portions; reheat until steaming hot all the way through.
Freezes for up to 3 months. Taste before salting as the ham is salty.

title: Radish and Cucumber Spring Salad with Dill Yoghurt
summary: Crisp radish and cucumber ribbons tossed in a cooling dill yoghurt dressing.

steps.text: Whisk the yoghurt, dill, lemon juice, honey, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Add the cucumber, radish and spring onion and toss until evenly coated.
Chill for 10 minutes, until cold and crisp.

notes: Serve with rye bread or smoked fish.

title: Asparagus and New Potato Salad with Chive Vinaigrette
summary: Warm baby potatoes and asparagus in a sharp wholegrain mustard dressing.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 12 minutes, until just tender.
Add the asparagus for the final 3 minutes, until bright green and tender, then drain well.
Whisk the oil, mustard, vinegar, honey and seasoning, and toss through the warm vegetables.
Scatter with chives and serve warm or at room temperature.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

title: Pea and Feta Smash on Sourdough
summary: Smashed minty peas and salty feta piled onto crisp sourdough.

steps.text: Cook the peas in boiling water for 3 minutes, until tender, then drain.
Mash roughly with the oil, mint, lemon zest and pepper.
Toast the sourdough until golden and crisp.
Pile the pea smash onto the hot toast until generously covered, then top with feta.

notes: Add a poached egg for extra protein.

title: Spring Vegetable Broth with Orzo
summary: A light broth of asparagus, peas and baby zucchini with tiny orzo pasta.

steps.text: Warm the oil in a large saucepan and cook the leek for 5 minutes, until soft, adding the garlic for the last minute.
Add the stock and water and heat until it boils steadily.
Stir in the orzo and simmer for 8 minutes, until nearly tender.
Add the asparagus, peas and zucchini and simmer for 3 minutes, until just cooked.
Stir through the lemon zest and parsley and season.

notes: Add a squeeze of lemon at the table.

title: Low-FODMAP Friendly Chicken and Rice Soup
summary: A gentle, ginger-scented chicken soup made without onion or garlic, using garlic-infused oil.

steps.text: Warm the garlic-infused oil in a pot and cook the carrot, celery and ginger for 5 minutes, until softening.
Add the stock and chicken and simmer for 15 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through with no pink.
Lift out the chicken, shred it and return it to the pot with the rice.
Simmer for 12 minutes, until the rice is tender, then stir through the spinach until wilted.
Season and scatter with chives.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken until it reaches 75°C in the thickest part; refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour of cooking rice and eat within 1 day.
Check stock labels, as many contain onion and garlic.

title: Low-FODMAP Friendly Quinoa Salad with Cucumber and Olives
summary: Fluffy quinoa with cucumber, tomato, olives and feta in a lemon dressing, free of onion and garlic.

steps.text: Simmer the quinoa in 400ml water for 15 minutes, until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender.
Spread on a tray to cool for 10 minutes.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice and seasoning, then toss through the quinoa with the cucumber, tomato, olives and parsley, then top with the feta.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

title: Low-FODMAP Friendly Carrot and Ginger Soup
summary: Sweet carrot and zingy ginger blended into a velvety soup with no onion or garlic.

steps.text: Warm the oil in a saucepan and cook the ginger and cumin for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the carrot, potato and stock and simmer for 22 minutes, until the vegetables are very soft.
Blend until smooth and season to taste.
Reheat until steaming and scatter with chives.

notes: Freezes well for up to 3 months.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Low-FODMAP Friendly Tomato and Basil Soup
summary: A smooth tomato soup built on garlic-infused oil and fresh basil.

steps.text: Warm the oil in a saucepan and cook the carrot for 5 minutes, until softening.
Add the tomatoes, stock and sugar and simmer for 20 minutes, until the carrot is tender.
Blend with the basil until smooth.
Season and reheat until steaming.

notes: Serve with gluten-free toast if needed.
Food safety: Keep any leftover garlic, herb or chilli oil in the fridge and use it within 4 days. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Low-FODMAP Friendly Spinach and Egg Breakfast Muffins
summary: Savoury egg muffins with spinach, tomato and chives that travel well.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180C and oil a 6-hole muffin tin.
Whisk the eggs with the seasoning, then stir through the spinach, tomato, cheese and chives.
Divide among the holes and bake for 18 minutes, until risen and set in the centre.
Cool for 3 minutes before turning out.

notes: Food safety: cook until the eggs are fully set; refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 2 days, reheating until steaming. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Low-FODMAP Friendly Greek Salad
summary: Cucumber, tomato, olives and feta with a simple lemon and oregano dressing.

steps.text: Combine the cucumber, tomato, capsicum and olives in a bowl.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice, oregano and seasoning and toss through the salad until coated.
Top with the feta and a pinch of oregano.

notes: Leave out the capsicum if it does not agree with you.

title: Cauliflower and Potato Smash for Fussy Eaters
summary: Creamy cauliflower mashed with a little cheese, a gentle side for fussy eaters.

steps.text: Boil the cauliflower and potato in salted water for 15 minutes, until very tender.
Drain well and return to the pot.
Add the butter, milk and cheese and mash until smooth and creamy.
Season to taste and serve hot.

notes: Serve with sausages or crumbed fish.

title: Kids' Hidden Veg Tomato Sauce
summary: A smooth tomato sauce with carrot, zucchini and pumpkin blended in unnoticed.

steps.text: Warm the oil in a large pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the carrot, zucchini and pumpkin and cook for 5 minutes, stirring until softening.
Add the tomatoes, water and oregano and simmer for 20 minutes, until the pumpkin is completely soft.
Blend until smooth and season lightly.

notes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Toss through pasta or spread on pizza bases.

title: Kids' Honey Glazed Carrot Sticks
summary: Sweet roasted carrot sticks that are easy for little hands.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200C and line a large tray with baking paper.
Toss the carrots with the oil, cinnamon and a pinch of salt on a tray.
Roast for 18 minutes, until tender with golden edges.
Drizzle with the honey and roast for 2 minutes, until glossy.

notes: Not suitable for babies under 12 months because of the honey.

title: Kids' Broccoli Trees with Cheesy Dip
summary: Steamed broccoli florets with a warm cheddar dip.

steps.text: Steam the broccoli for 6 minutes, until bright green and just tender.
Melt the butter in a small saucepan, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Whisk in the milk gradually and stir for 4 minutes, until thickened.
Remove from the heat, stir in the cheese until melted and season with pepper.
Serve the broccoli with the dip for dunking.

notes: Let it cool a little before serving to small children.

title: Kids' Corn and Zucchini Fritters
summary: Golden little fritters packed with sweetcorn and grated zucchini.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs, milk and flour into a smooth batter, then fold in the zucchini, corn, chives and seasoning.
Heat half the oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
Cook spoonfuls of batter for 2 minutes each side, until golden and cooked through, working in batches with the remaining oil.
Drain on paper and serve warm.

notes: Food safety: cook until the batter is set and no longer wet in the centre.
Cooked fritters freeze well for 2 months.

title: Kids' Rainbow Veggie Rice
summary: Fluffy rice with colourful diced vegetables and a little soy sauce.

steps.text: Rinse the rice and place in a pot with the water and carrot.
Bring to the boil, cover and cook on low for 12 minutes, until the water is absorbed.
Stir the capsicum, peas, corn, sesame oil and soy sauce through the hot rice, cover and rest off the heat for 5 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Fluff with a fork and serve.

notes: Food safety: cool leftover rice quickly and refrigerate within 1 hour; reheat until steaming hot.

title: Kids' Mini Pea and Ham Pancakes
summary: Savoury drop pancakes with peas and diced ham for lunchboxes.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder, egg and milk into a smooth batter, then fold in the peas, ham and pepper.
Heat a little oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat.
Cook spoonfuls of batter for 2 minutes each side, until golden and cooked through.
Keep warm while cooking the rest.

notes: Food safety: cook until the batter is set; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Kids' Cucumber Boats with Hummus
summary: Cucumber halves filled with hummus and cherry tomatoes.

items.raw: 2 Lebanese cucumbers, halved lengthways and scooped

steps.text: Scoop out the cucumber seeds with a teaspoon to make boats.
Spoon in the hummus until each boat is generously filled.
Top with tomato, a drizzle of oil and sesame seeds.

notes: Cut into short pieces for younger children.

title: Alphabet Pasta Chicken Soup for Kids
summary: A mild chicken soup with soft vegetables and tiny pasta letters.

steps.text: Warm the oil in a large pot and cook the onion, carrot and celery for 6 minutes, until soft.
Add the chicken and stock and simmer for 15 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through with no pink.
Lift out the chicken and shred it.
Add the pasta and peas and cook for 6 minutes, until the pasta is tender, then return the chicken.
Season with pepper and serve.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken until it reaches 75°C in the thickest part; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until steaming.

title: Homemade Baked Beans on Toast Fingers
summary: Smoky tomato butter beans spooned over toast fingers.

items.raw: 2 x 400g tins butter beans, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Warm the oil in a saucepan and cook the onion for 5 minutes, until soft, adding the garlic for the final minute.
Stir in the paprika, tomato paste, crushed tomatoes, maple syrup and worcestershire sauce.
Add the beans and simmer for 12 minutes, until the sauce is thick.
Toast the bread until golden and cut into fingers.
Spoon the beans over the toast until generously covered.

notes: Canned beans are already cooked, so no soaking is needed.

title: Mason Jar Chickpea and Cucumber Salad
summary: Layered jar salads that travel well, with the dressing at the bottom to keep everything crisp.

items.raw: 2 x 400g tins chickpeas, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Whisk the oil, lemon juice, cumin and seasoning in a small bowl.
Divide the dressing among four 500ml jars, then layer in the chickpeas, cucumber, capsicum and tomatoes until each jar is two thirds full.
Add the feta and finish with the spinach, packing it in until the jar is full.
Seal and keep chilled, then shake into a bowl to serve.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days. Keep jars cold in an insulated bag when travelling.

title: Train Journey Tuna and Cannellini Lunch Box
summary: A no-heat tuna and cannellini salad that packs into a container for the journey.

items.raw: 400g tin cannellini beans, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Combine the beans, tuna, celery, tomatoes and parsley in a container.
Add the lemon juice, oil and seasoning and fold gently until the beans are coated.
Seal and keep chilled until ready to eat.

notes: Food safety: keep below 5°C in a cooler bag and eat within 4 hours, or keep refrigerated and eat within 1 day.

title: Road Trip Pasta Salad with Pesto and Cherry Tomatoes
summary: A basil pesto pasta salad that holds up well at room temperature.

steps.text: Cook the penne in salted boiling water for 11 minutes, until al dente, then drain and rinse under cold water until cool.
Toss the pasta with the pesto and oil until evenly coated.
Fold through the tomatoes, bocconcini and rocket.
Season and pack into containers.

notes: Food safety: keep chilled in a cooler bag and eat within 2 hours of leaving the fridge.

title: Picnic Potato Salad with Herbs and Mustard
summary: A mayo-free potato salad with a mustard vinaigrette, safe for a day outside.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes, until just tender, then drain.
Whisk the oil, vinegar, mustard and seasoning in a large bowl.
Toss the warm potatoes through the dressing with the onion until coated.
Cool for 20 minutes, then fold through the herbs.

notes: Without mayonnaise this travels better, but still keep it in a cooler bag and eat within 4 hours.

title: Airport Friendly Couscous Salad with Dried Apricots
summary: A dry, light couscous salad with apricots, almonds and mint that packs flat.

steps.text: Place the couscous in a heatproof bowl, pour over the boiling water, cover and stand for 5 minutes, until the water is absorbed.
Fluff with a fork and add the oil, lemon juice, cumin and salt.
Fold through the apricots, almonds, mint and cucumber until evenly mixed.
Pack into a container once cool.

notes: Keep a spare lemon wedge in the bag to brighten it up before eating.

title: Travel Tabbouleh in a Jar
summary: Parsley-heavy tabbouleh with fine bulgur layered in a jar for easy carrying.

steps.text: Soak the bulgur in the lemon juice and 100ml water for 15 minutes, until tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Whisk the oil, salt and pepper into the bulgur.
Layer the tomato, spring onion, bulgur, mint and parsley in jars, with the parsley on top.
Seal and chill, then shake to mix before eating.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for 1 day. The bulgur soaks, so prep time includes only chopping.

title: Camping Corn and Chickpea Salad
summary: Charred corn and chickpeas with lime and coriander, no refrigeration needed until opened.

steps.text: Grill the corn over a hot flame or barbecue for 8 minutes, turning until charred in places and tender.
Cut the kernels from the cobs.
Toss the corn with the chickpeas, capsicum, oil, lime juice, paprika and seasoning until coated.
Fold through the avocado and coriander just before serving.

notes: Eat the same day. Add the avocado at the last minute to avoid browning.

title: Christmas Morning Smoked Salmon Toast Platter
summary: A festive platter of toasted sourdough, cream cheese, smoked salmon, capers and dill for a relaxed morning.

steps.text: Toast the sourdough until golden, then cool slightly.
Spread each half with cream cheese.
Arrange the smoked salmon, cucumber, onion, capers and dill on a platter.
Serve with lemon and black pepper so everyone can build their own.

notes: Food safety: keep smoked salmon below 5°C until serving, and avoid it during pregnancy or for anyone with a weakened immune system.

title: Easter Brunch Spinach and Ricotta Tart
summary: A free-form tart of puff pastry, creamy ricotta, spinach and egg for a holiday table.

items.raw: 150g baby spinach, wilted and squeezed dry

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200C and line two trays with baking paper.
Wilt the spinach in a hot pan with the oil for 2 minutes, until soft, then squeeze out all the liquid and chop.
Mix the ricotta, spinach, 2 eggs, cheese, zest, nutmeg and seasoning until smooth.
Place a pastry sheet on each tray, spread with the filling leaving a 2cm border and fold the edges over.
Brush the pastry with the remaining beaten egg and bake for 30 minutes, until deep golden and the filling is set.

notes: Food safety: bake until the egg filling is fully set; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Mother's Day Baked Eggs in Tomato Cups
summary: Large tomatoes hollowed and baked with an egg, herbs and a little cream.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 190C and line a small tray with baking paper.
Slice the tops off the tomatoes, scoop out the centres and season the insides.
Place the tomatoes on the tray and bake for 8 minutes, until just softening.
Spoon a little cream into each, crack in an egg, and top with cheese and pepper.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are still soft.
Scatter with chives and serve with sourdough for dipping.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set; cook the yolks through if serving anyone vulnerable.

title: New Year's Day Ham and Potato Hash
summary: Crisp potato and leftover ham fried with onion and topped with a fried egg.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes for 6 minutes, until just tender, then drain and dry well.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan and fry the potatoes for 10 minutes, turning until golden and crisp.
Add the onion, capsicum, ham and paprika and cook for 6 minutes, until the vegetables are soft and the ham is hot.
Make four wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 3 minutes, until the whites are set, then scatter with parsley.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set; reheat leftover ham until steaming hot and eat refrigerated ham within 3 days.

title: Boxing Day Ham and Cheese Breakfast Strata
summary: A make-ahead bake of bread, leftover ham, cheddar and egg custard.

steps.text: Butter a 22cm by 30cm baking dish and heat the oven to 180C.
Layer half the bread, ham and cheese in the dish, then repeat with the remainder.
Whisk the eggs, milk, mustard and pepper and pour over, pressing the bread down until it is soaked.
Bake for 45 minutes, until puffed, golden and set in the centre.
Rest for 5 minutes, scatter with chives and cut into squares.

notes: Food safety: bake until the centre reaches 75°C; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
Can be assembled the night before and refrigerated.

title: Holiday Walnut and Apple Oat Bake
summary: A tray of baked oats with apple, cinnamon and walnuts that feeds a full house.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180C and grease a 22cm square baking dish.
Mix the oats, apple, walnuts, cinnamon and baking powder in a bowl.
Whisk the milk, eggs, maple syrup, vanilla and butter, then stir into the oats.
Pour into the dish and bake for 35 minutes, until golden and set in the centre.
Rest for 5 minutes and cut into squares.

notes: Food safety: bake until the egg is fully set; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until steaming. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Christmas Brunch Potato Galette with Dill Sour Cream and Salmon
summary: Crisp grated potato rosti topped with sour cream, smoked trout and dill.

steps.text: Squeeze the grated potato and onion in a clean tea towel until very dry, then mix with the flour and seasoning.
Heat half the oil in a large non-stick frying pan and press in half the mixture, cooking for 8 minutes until deep golden underneath.
Flip and cook for 2 minutes, until crisp and tender in the middle, then repeat with the rest.
Top the wedges with sour cream, salmon, dill and a squeeze of lemon.

notes: Food safety: keep smoked salmon refrigerated until serving; avoid in pregnancy or if immunocompromised.

title: Budget Lentil and Carrot Soup
summary: A cheap, filling soup of red lentils, carrots and cumin.

steps.text: Warm the oil in a pot and cook the onion and carrot for 6 minutes, until softening, adding the garlic and cumin for the final minute.
Add the lentils and stock and bring to a simmer, skimming until the foam clears.
Simmer for 22 minutes, until the lentils are completely soft.
Blend lightly if you like a thicker texture, then stir through the lemon juice and season.

notes: Costs about a dollar a serve. Freezes for 3 months.

title: Freezer Batch Minestrone
summary: A big pot of minestrone to portion and freeze, with pasta added on reheating.

items.raw: 150g small pasta, cooked, to add when serving

steps.text: Warm the oil in a large pot and cook the onion, carrot and celery for 8 minutes, until soft, adding the garlic for the last minute.
Stir in the tomato paste and oregano and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, beans and stock and simmer for 20 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Add the zucchini and green beans and simmer for 8 minutes, until just tender.
Cool, then portion into freezer containers.

notes: Freeze without pasta. To serve, reheat until steaming and add a handful of cooked small pasta.
Cool within 2 hours and freeze for up to 3 months.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Freezer Pumpkin and Red Lentil Soup
summary: Sweet pumpkin and lentils blended into a velvety soup that freezes beautifully.

steps.text: Warm the oil in a large pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes, until soft, then add the garlic and spices for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the pumpkin, lentils and stock and simmer for 28 minutes, until everything is very soft.
Blend until smooth and season.
Cool before portioning into containers.

notes: Freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat until steaming.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Penny-Wise Caraway Cabbage Soup
summary: Humble cabbage, potato and caraway soup that costs very little.

steps.text: Warm the oil in a pot and cook the onion and caraway for 5 minutes, until soft and fragrant.
Add the potato, carrot, cabbage and stock and heat until bubbling.
Simmer for 22 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Stir in the vinegar and season to taste.

notes: Mash a few potatoes against the side of the pot for a thicker soup.

title: Freezer Chicken and Vegetable Soup Base
summary: A shredded chicken and vegetable base to freeze, then add noodles or rice when serving.

steps.text: Warm the oil in a large pot and cook the onion, carrot and celery for 7 minutes, until soft, adding the garlic for the final minute.
Add the chicken, stock and bay leaves and simmer for 25 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through with no pink.
Lift out the chicken, shred it and return it to the pot with the peas.
Simmer for 3 minutes, until the peas are tender, then cool and portion.

notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C in the thickest part; cool and freeze within 2 hours; reheat until steaming hot.
Freezes for up to 3 months. Add cooked noodles or rice after reheating.

title: Budget Bean and Bacon Soup
summary: A smoky bean soup that uses a little bacon for a lot of flavour.

items.raw: 2 x 400g tins butter beans, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Fry the bacon in a pot for 5 minutes, until crisp, then add the onion, carrot and celery and cook for 6 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the garlic, tomato paste and thyme for 1 minute.
Add the beans and stock and simmer for 20 minutes, until thick and the vegetables are tender.
Mash some of the beans against the side of the pot and season with pepper.

notes: Food safety: cook the bacon until it is crisp and cooked through; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until steaming. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Freezer Sweet Potato and Coconut Soup
summary: Sweet potato, coconut milk and a little curry paste, blended and frozen in portions.

steps.text: Warm the oil in a pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes, until soft, then stir in the paste for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the sweet potato and stock and simmer for 20 minutes, until very soft.
Blend with the coconut milk until smooth.
Season with lime juice and salt, then cool before freezing.

notes: Freezes for 3 months. Reheat gently until steaming.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Budget Egg Drop Soup with Spinach
summary: Silky egg ribbons in a ginger broth, ready in ten minutes from the pantry.

items.raw: 2 tsp cornflour mixed with 2 tbsp water

steps.text: Bring the stock, ginger and soy sauce to a simmer in a saucepan, until small bubbles break the surface.
Stir in the cornflour mixture and cook for 1 minute, until slightly thickened.
Pour in the eggs slowly in a thin stream while stirring until ribbons form and are fully set.
Add the spinach until just wilted, then finish with sesame oil, spring onion and pepper.

notes: Food safety: cook until the eggs are fully set throughout the soup.

title: Hearty Freezer Soup of Beef and Pearl Barley
summary: A thick beef and barley soup that suits batch cooking and freezing.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the beef in batches for 6 minutes, until well coloured, then set aside.
Cook the onion, carrot and celery for 6 minutes, until soft, adding the garlic for the final minute.
Return the beef with the tomato paste, barley, stock and bay leaves.
Simmer gently for 80 minutes, until the beef is tender and the barley is soft.
Season and cool before portioning.

notes: Food safety: cook beef until tender and steaming hot throughout; cool and freeze within 2 hours; reheat to 75°C.
Freezes for 3 months. The barley thickens on standing, so add water when reheating.

title: Pantry Crushed Tomato and Rice Supper Soup
summary: Tinned tomatoes and a handful of rice make a cheap, comforting supper.

steps.text: Warm the oil in a pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes, until soft, adding the garlic for the final minute.
Add the tomatoes, stock and basil and heat until bubbling.
Stir in the rice and simmer for 15 minutes, until the rice is tender.
Season to taste and serve hot.

notes: Food safety: cool leftover rice and soup quickly and refrigerate within 1 hour; reheat until steaming hot.

title: Silky Freezer Leek Soup with Chives
summary: A silky classic made without cream, perfect for freezing.

items.raw: 3 leeks, white and pale green parts sliced
items.prep: white and pale green parts sliced

steps.text: Melt the butter in a large pot and cook the leeks for 10 minutes, until very soft but not coloured.
Add the potatoes and stock and simmer for 18 minutes, until the potatoes fall apart when pressed.
Blend until smooth, then stir in the milk and season.
Cool before freezing, and scatter with chives when serving.

notes: Freeze for up to 3 months, and reheat gently until steaming.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Heirloom Tomato Salad with Basil Oil
summary: Thick slices of ripe mixed tomatoes with a vivid basil oil and flaky salt.

steps.text: Blend the basil, oil, garlic and a pinch of salt until smooth and bright green.
Arrange the tomatoes on a platter and season with salt and pepper.
Drizzle with the vinegar and basil oil until well coated, then stand for 5 minutes.

notes: Use tomatoes at room temperature for the best flavour.

title: Tomato and Watermelon Salad with Mint
summary: Juicy tomato and watermelon cubes with mint, red onion and salty feta.

steps.text: Combine the tomato, watermelon and onion in a large bowl.
Whisk the oil, lime juice and pepper and pour over.
Toss gently until just coated, then scatter with feta and mint.

notes: Serve straight away, as the watermelon releases juice if it stands.

title: Roast Cherry Tomato Pasta Sauce
summary: Cherry tomatoes roasted until jammy with garlic, then crushed into a sauce.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200C and line a large tray with baking paper.
Toss the tomatoes and garlic with the oil, sugar, salt and pepper on the tray.
Roast for 30 minutes, until the tomatoes burst and the edges caramelise.
Squeeze the garlic from its skins and crush everything with a fork until chunky, then fold through the basil.

notes: Spoon over cooked pasta or serve on toast. Freezes for 3 months.

title: Ripe Tomato and Chilli Table Salsa
summary: A chunky fresh salsa with lime, coriander and a little chilli for corn chips or tacos.

steps.text: Combine the tomato, onion, chilli and coriander in a bowl.
Stir through the lime juice, oil and salt until evenly mixed.
Rest for 10 minutes so the flavours mingle, then drain off any excess liquid.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

title: Panzanella with Ripe Tomato and Cucumber
summary: Torn crusty bread soaks up tomato juice and a sharp vinaigrette.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200C. Toss the bread with 2 tbsp oil and bake for 10 minutes, until crisp and golden.
Salt the tomatoes in a large bowl and stand for 10 minutes to draw out their juices.
Add the vinegar, remaining oil, cucumber and onion and toss until combined.
Fold through the warm bread and basil, then rest for 10 minutes, until the bread softens slightly at the edges.

notes: Best eaten within 2 hours of mixing.

title: Burst Tomato and Ricotta Toast
summary: Blistered cherry tomatoes spooned over whipped ricotta on crisp toast.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a frying pan over high heat and cook the tomatoes for 5 minutes, until they blister and burst.
Stir the ricotta with the lemon zest and a pinch of salt.
Toast the sourdough until golden and crisp.
Spread the ricotta over the sourdough until thickly covered, then spoon over the tomatoes and finish with balsamic, basil and pepper.

notes: Add a fried egg on top for a bigger brunch.

title: Slow Roasted Tomato Sauce for Freezing
summary: Halved tomatoes roasted slowly with garlic and thyme, then puréed into a sweet, deep sauce.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160C and line two large trays with baking paper.
Place the tomatoes cut-side up on two trays with the onion and garlic, drizzle with oil and season.
Roast for 90 minutes, until the tomatoes are soft, collapsed and caramelised at the edges.
Discard the thyme stalks and blend until smooth.
Cool completely, then portion into containers.

notes: Freezes for up to 4 months. Taste and add sugar if the tomatoes were tart.

title: Summer Tomato and Corn Chowder
summary: Sweet corn and ripe tomatoes in a lightly creamy chowder.

steps.text: Warm the oil in a large pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the potato, corn, tomato and stock and simmer for 20 minutes, until the potato is tender.
Blend about a third of the soup, then stir it back in with the milk and heat until steaming.
Season and scatter with basil.

notes: Do not boil after adding the milk.

title: Grilled Pear and Rocket Salad with Goat's Cheese
summary: Charred pear halves with peppery rocket, creamy goat's cheese and toasted almonds.

steps.text: Brush the pears with the oil and grill cut-side down in a hot pan for 4 minutes, until charred and softening.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 2 minutes, until golden.
Whisk the vinegar, extra oil and pepper, and toss with the rocket.
Slice the pears onto the rocket and finish with goat's cheese and almonds.

notes: Use firm, just-ripe pears so they hold their shape.

title: Honeyed Yoghurt Cups with Mango and Toasted Almonds
summary: Fresh mango with thick yoghurt, toasted almonds and a drizzle of honey.

steps.text: Stir the vanilla through the yoghurt until smooth.
Divide among two bowls and top with the mango slices.
Scatter over the almonds and finish with honey and cinnamon.

notes: Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 3 minutes until golden for extra flavour.

title: Mango, Cucumber and Rocket Salad with Lime Dressing
summary: Fresh mango with cucumber, rocket and a zesty lime dressing.

steps.text: Whisk the oil, lime juice, honey and seasoning in a large bowl.
Add the cucumber and rocket and toss until lightly coated.
Fold in the mango and scatter with walnuts.

notes: Slice the mango cheeks off the stone and cube the flesh.

title: Spiced Pear Chutney
summary: A tangy, spiced pear chutney that keeps for weeks in the fridge.

steps.text: Combine all of the ingredients in a saucepan over medium heat.
Cook for 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the pears soften and the chutney is thick and glossy.
Spoon into a clean jar while hot.
Cool and refrigerate once sealed.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for 3 weeks. Serve with cheese, curries or cold meats.

title: Crisp Pear and Chilli Salsa for Barbecued Fish
summary: A sweet, tangy salsa of pear, lime and chilli to spoon over barbecued fish.

steps.text: Combine the pear, capsicum, onion, chilli and coriander in a bowl.
Add the lime juice, oil and salt and stir until evenly mixed.
Rest for 10 minutes, until the juices pool and the flavours come together.

notes: Best on the day it is made. Delicious with grilled barramundi or prawns.

title: Roast Pumpkin and Sage Salad with Pepitas
summary: Caramelised pumpkin with crisp sage, pepitas and a tangy dressing over rocket.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 210C and line a large tray with baking paper.
Toss the pumpkin with 2 tbsp oil and seasoning and roast for 25 minutes, until golden and tender.
Add the sage and pepitas to the tray for the last 4 minutes, until crisp.
Whisk the vinegar, mustard, honey and remaining oil and toss through the rocket.
Top with the pumpkin, sage and pepitas.

notes: Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Spiced Pumpkin Soup with Coconut Cream
summary: Pumpkin with curry spices, blended smooth and finished with coconut cream.

steps.text: Warm the oil in a pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes, until soft, then add the garlic, ginger and curry powder for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the pumpkin and stock and simmer for 25 minutes, until the pumpkin is very tender.
Blend until smooth and stir through most of the coconut cream.
Season and serve with a swirl of coconut cream and coriander.

notes: Freezes well without the coconut cream swirl.

title: Pumpkin Spice Overnight Oats
summary: Creamy oats with pumpkin purée, cinnamon and maple, prepared the night before.

steps.text: Stir the oats, milk, pumpkin, yoghurt, maple syrup and spices in a bowl until smooth.
Divide into two jars and cover.
Refrigerate overnight, until thick and creamy, then top with pecans.

notes: Soaking time is not counted in the prep time. Keeps for 2 days in the fridge.

title: Creamy Mushroom and Thyme Soup
summary: Earthy mushrooms and thyme blended with a splash of cream.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a large pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the mushrooms and cook for 10 minutes, until deeply golden and their liquid has evaporated, adding the garlic and thyme for the last minute.
Pour in the stock and simmer for 10 minutes, until the flavours meld.
Blend until smooth, stir in the cream and season.

notes: Do not boil after adding the cream. Keep a few cooked slices aside for garnish if you like.

title: Garlic Field Mushrooms Piled on Sourdough Slices
summary: Golden mushrooms with garlic, thyme and a splash of lemon piled onto thick toast.

steps.text: Melt half the butter in a large frying pan over high heat and cook the mushrooms in two batches for 5 minutes, until golden and any liquid has evaporated.
Return all the mushrooms, add the remaining butter, garlic and thyme and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the lemon juice and season.
Toast the sourdough until golden and spoon the mushrooms over, finishing with parsley.

notes: Do not overcrowd the pan, or the mushrooms will steam instead of brown.

title: Barley-Thickened Winter Mushroom Soup
summary: A hearty soup of mushrooms, pearl barley and dill.

steps.text: Warm the oil in a pot and cook the onion and carrot for 6 minutes, until soft.
Add the mushrooms and cook for 8 minutes, until browned, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the barley, stock and bay leaves and simmer for 35 minutes, until the barley is tender.
Stir through the dill and lemon juice and season.

notes: Barley thickens on standing, so add water when reheating.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Roast Pumpkin Hummus
summary: Hummus with roasted pumpkin for a sweet, earthy dip.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200C and roast the pumpkin with 1 tbsp oil for 30 minutes, until very tender and caramelised.
Blend the pumpkin with the chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin and salt until smooth.
Add the remaining oil and 2 tbsp cold water until silky.
Spoon into a bowl and drizzle with oil.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for 4 days.

title: Marinated Mushroom Salad
summary: Lightly cooked mushrooms in a lemon and herb dressing, served at room temperature.

steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a frying pan and cook the mushrooms for 5 minutes, until golden and just tender.
Toss with the remaining oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, parsley and seasoning while warm.
Cool to room temperature, until the mushrooms soak up the dressing.
Serve over the rocket, tossing until just coated.

notes: Marinating time is not counted. Keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

title: Mushroom and Spinach Breakfast Hash
summary: Crisp potatoes tossed with mushrooms, spinach and a poached egg.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes for 6 minutes, until just tender, then drain and dry well.
Heat the oil in a large pan and fry the potatoes for 8 minutes, until golden and crisp.
Add the onion and mushrooms and cook for 5 minutes, until browned, then fold in the paprika and spinach until wilted.
Poach the eggs in gently simmering water for 3 minutes, until the whites are set, and place on top.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set; cook the yolks through for anyone vulnerable.

title: Pumpkin Wedges with Tahini Yoghurt
summary: Roasted pumpkin with a cooling tahini yoghurt and a sprinkle of za'atar.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 210C and line a large tray with baking paper.
Toss the pumpkin with the oil, cumin and salt and roast for 35 minutes, until tender and charred at the edges.
Stir the yoghurt, tahini, lemon juice and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Spread the yoghurt on a platter, top with pumpkin, then sprinkle with za'atar and parsley.

notes: Add a little water if the yoghurt is too thick.

title: Onion and Mushroom Gravy for Roasts
summary: A rich vegetarian gravy of browned mushrooms and soy, good with roasts, mash or pies.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a saucepan and cook the onion for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the mushrooms and cook for 8 minutes, until deep brown and dry.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then whisk in the stock gradually.
Add the soy sauce and thyme and simmer for 8 minutes, until glossy and thick enough to coat a spoon.

notes: Strain for a smoother gravy if you like.

title: Curried Pumpkin and Chickpea Soup in Coconut Broth
summary: A soupy, mildly spiced bowl of pumpkin and chickpeas in a coconut broth.

steps.text: Warm the oil in a large pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes, until soft, then add the garlic, ginger and curry powder for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the pumpkin, chickpeas, coconut milk and stock and simmer for 25 minutes, until the pumpkin is tender.
Stir through the spinach until wilted and finish with lime juice and salt.

notes: Mash some of the pumpkin into the broth for a thicker texture.

title: Sicilian Orange, Olive and Red Onion Salad
summary: Juicy orange slices with salty olives, red onion and olive oil, a bright winter side.

items.raw: 4 oranges, peeled and sliced into rounds
1 small red onion, very thinly sliced

steps.text: Arrange the orange rounds on a platter, overlapping slightly.
Scatter over the onion and olives until evenly spread.
Drizzle with the oil and season with chilli, salt and pepper, then finish with parsley.

notes: Soak the onion slices in cold water for 5 minutes for a milder bite.

title: Orange and Avocado Salad with Honey Lime Dressing
summary: Orange segments and creamy avocado over baby leaves with a sweet-sharp dressing.

steps.text: Whisk the oil, lime juice, honey and a pinch of salt in a bowl.
Arrange the spinach, orange, avocado and onion on a platter.
Spoon over the dressing until lightly coated and scatter with pepitas.

notes: Serve straight away so the avocado stays green.

title: Orange and Mint Winter Citrus Salad
summary: Orange and lemon segments with mint, honey and a pinch of cinnamon for a fresh start to the day.

steps.text: Combine the orange and lemon segments in a bowl with any juices.
Drizzle with the honey and toss until lightly coated.
Scatter with mint, cinnamon and pistachios.

notes: Serve chilled with plain yoghurt if you like.

title: Golden Cauliflower Soup with Toasted Cumin Seeds
summary: Caramelised cauliflower blended with potato and cumin into a nutty, velvety soup.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 210C and line a large tray with baking paper.
Toss the cauliflower with 2 tbsp oil, the cumin and salt and roast for 25 minutes, until deeply golden at the edges.
Warm the remaining oil in a pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes, until soft, adding the garlic for the last minute.
Add the potato, stock and roasted cauliflower and simmer for 15 minutes, until the potato is soft.
Blend until smooth, stir in the milk and season.

notes: Keep a few roasted florets aside to garnish.

title: Broccoli and Cheddar Soup
summary: A creamy broccoli soup with melted cheddar, a cold-weather favourite.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes, until soft, adding the garlic for the final minute.
Add the broccoli, potato and stock and simmer for 15 minutes, until the vegetables are very tender.
Blend until smooth, then stir in the milk and cheese until melted.
Season with pepper and serve hot.

notes: Do not boil after adding the cheese or the soup may split.

title: Rosemary Cannellini and Kale Soup with Carrot
summary: Tuscan-style soup of kale, cannellini beans, tomato and rosemary.

items.raw: 400g tin cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
150g kale, stems removed and leaves torn

steps.text: Warm the oil in a pot and cook the onion and carrot for 6 minutes, until soft, adding the garlic and rosemary for the last minute.
Add the tomatoes, beans and stock and simmer for 15 minutes, until the flavours blend.
Stir in the kale and simmer for 5 minutes, until tender.
Season and serve with a drizzle of oil.

notes: Mash some of the beans against the pot for a thicker soup.

title: Savoy Cabbage Slaw with Orange and Sesame
summary: A crunchy winter slaw tossed in an orange and mustard dressing.

steps.text: Whisk the orange juice, oil, vinegar, mustard, honey, sesame seeds and seasoning in a large bowl.
Add the cabbage, carrot and orange.
Toss for 1 minute until everything is coated, then stand for 10 minutes until the cabbage softens slightly.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

title: Spice-Rubbed Whole Cauliflower with Lemon Tahini and Pomegranate
summary: A blistered whole cauliflower with spice rub, lemony tahini and pomegranate.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200C and line a tray with baking paper.
Rub the cauliflower with the oil, cumin, paprika and salt and place on the tray.
Roast for 50 minutes, until deep golden and a knife slides easily into the centre.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice, garlic and water until smooth and pourable.
Spoon the tahini over the cauliflower and finish with pomegranate and parsley.

notes: Add more water to the tahini if it thickens.

title: Glazed Broccoli Tips with Mustard and Honey
summary: Broccoli roasted until the tips crisp, glazed with honey mustard.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220C and line a large tray with baking paper.
Toss the broccoli with 2 tbsp oil, salt and pepper and roast for 15 minutes, until charred at the tips.
Whisk the mustard, honey, lemon juice and remaining oil.
Toss the hot broccoli with the glaze until glossy.

notes: Not suitable for babies under 12 months because of the honey.

title: Slow Red Cabbage with Grated Apple and Orange Juice
summary: Sweet and sour red cabbage slowly braised with apple and a hint of orange.

steps.text: Warm the oil in a large pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the cabbage, apple, vinegar, sugar, orange juice, cinnamon and water and stir to combine.
Cover and braise on low for 45 minutes, stirring now and then, until the cabbage is very tender and glossy.
Season and serve warm, tasting until the sweet and sour balance is right.

notes: Tastes better the next day and keeps for 4 days.

title: Kale Caesar Style Salad with Crunchy Chickpeas
summary: Massaged kale with a creamy lemon dressing and crisp roasted chickpeas.

items.raw: 300g kale, stems removed and leaves finely shredded
items.prep: stems removed and leaves finely shredded

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200C and line a tray with baking paper.
Toss the chickpeas with the oil and paprika and roast for 20 minutes, until crisp and golden.
Whisk the yoghurt, lemon juice, mustard, garlic and cheese into a dressing.
Massage the kale with the dressing for 2 minutes, until it softens and darkens.
Top with the chickpeas and pepper.

notes: Dry the chickpeas well before roasting so they crisp.

title: Quick Lemon Pickle for Rice and Curries
summary: A tangy, mildly spiced lemon pickle you can make in a saucepan in minutes.

items.raw: 4 lemons, diced with skin on and seeds removed
items.prep: diced with skin on and seeds removed

steps.text: Heat the oil in a saucepan and fry the mustard seeds for 1 minute until they pop.
Add the lemon, turmeric, chilli, sugar, salt and water.
Simmer for 8 minutes, until the lemon is tender and the liquid is syrupy.
Cool and spoon into a clean jar.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for 2 weeks. Strong, so serve in small spoonfuls.

title: Ginger Carrot Soup Brightened with Orange Zest
summary: Sweet carrot, fresh ginger and orange juice for a sunny winter soup.

steps.text: Warm the oil in a pot and cook the onion and ginger for 5 minutes, until soft and fragrant.
Add the carrots and stock and simmer for 20 minutes, until the carrots are very soft.
Blend until smooth and stir in the orange juice and zest.
Season and reheat until steaming.

notes: Freezes for 3 months.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Roast Cauliflower and Cheese Gratin
summary: Cauliflower baked in a mustardy cheese sauce with a crumb topping.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200C and grease a baking dish.
Steam the cauliflower for 6 minutes, until just tender, then arrange in the dish.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk gradually and stir for 5 minutes, until thickened.
Stir in the mustard and half the cheese until melted and season.
Pour over the cauliflower, top with crumbs and remaining cheese and bake for 25 minutes, until bubbling and golden.

notes: Make ahead and bake just before serving.

title: Roast Cabbage Wedges with Caraway
summary: Cabbage wedges roasted until the edges char and the centres turn sweet.

items.raw: 1 small green cabbage, cut into 8 wedges

steps.text: Heat the oven to 210C and line a large tray with baking paper.
Brush the wedges with the oil and sprinkle with caraway, salt and pepper.
Roast for 30 minutes, turning once, until the edges are charred and the centres are tender.
Drizzle with the vinegar and serve.

notes: Add a spoonful of mustard on the side.

title: Orange and Yoghurt Breakfast Bowl with Pomegranate
summary: Thick yoghurt with orange segments, pomegranate and pistachios.

steps.text: Divide the yoghurt among two bowls, stirring until smooth.
Top with the orange segments, pomegranate seeds and pistachios.
Drizzle with honey and finish with cinnamon.

notes: Not suitable for babies under 12 months because of the honey.

title: Orange Vinaigrette for Winter Salads
summary: A glossy orange and Dijon dressing that lifts bitter leaves and roast vegetables.

steps.text: Combine the orange juice, vinegar, mustard and honey in a jar.
Add the oil, seal and shake until thick and emulsified.
Season to taste, shaking until the dressing is well blended.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for 5 days.

title: Garlicky Tahini Drizzle with Fresh Lemon
summary: A smooth, tangy sauce for roasted vegetables, falafel and grain bowls.

steps.text: Whisk the tahini, lemon juice, garlic and salt in a bowl; it will seize and thicken.
Add the water a splash at a time, whisking until smooth and pourable.
Finish with the oil and whisk until the sauce is glossy.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for 5 days; stir in more water if it thickens.

title: Raw Broccoli Stem Slaw
summary: Shaved broccoli stems and carrot in a creamy yoghurt dressing that makes use of the whole broccoli.

steps.text: Whisk the yoghurt, vinegar, honey, mustard and seasoning in a large bowl.
Add the broccoli, carrot, sultanas and sunflower seeds.
Toss until coated and chill for 10 minutes until the flavours blend.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days. Not suitable for babies under 12 months because of the honey.

title: Kale and Potato Soup with Smoked Paprika
summary: Spanish-style kale and potato soup with a smoky kick.

items.raw: 200g kale, stems removed and leaves shredded

steps.text: Warm the oil in a pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes, until soft, adding the garlic and paprika for the last minute.
Add the potatoes and stock and simmer for 15 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Mash a few potatoes against the pot for body, then add the kale and simmer for 5 minutes, until tender.
Stir in the vinegar and season.

notes: Drizzle with olive oil to serve.

title: Beetroot Wedge Salad with Walnuts and Orange
summary: Earthy roast beetroot with orange segments, walnuts and goat's cheese.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200C and wrap the beetroot in foil.
Roast for 50 minutes, until a knife slides easily into the centre, then cool, peel and cut into wedges.
Whisk the oil, orange juice, vinegar and seasoning.
Toss the beetroot, rocket and orange with the dressing and top with walnuts and goat's cheese.

notes: Wear gloves to peel the beetroot to avoid staining.

title: Coriander and Lime Dressing
summary: A fresh, zesty dressing for noodle salads, slaws and grilled fish.

items.raw: 1 bunch coriander, leaves and stems chopped

steps.text: Blend the coriander, lime juice, oil, fish sauce, honey, chilli and garlic until smooth.
Taste and adjust with more lime or honey until balanced.
Transfer to a jar and chill.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Not suitable for babies under 12 months because of the honey.

title: Winter Greens Frittata with Lemon
summary: Kale, silverbeet and herbs baked into a thick frittata with a squeeze of lemon.

items.raw: 150g kale, stems removed and leaves chopped

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180C and warm the oil in an ovenproof frying pan.
Cook the leek for 5 minutes, until soft, then add the kale and silverbeet and cook for 4 minutes, until wilted.
Whisk the eggs, cheese, zest and seasoning and pour over the greens.
Cook for 3 minutes, until the edges set, then bake for 15 minutes, until puffed and cooked through in the centre.
Rest for 5 minutes and cut into wedges.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until fully set; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

title: Cauliflower and Potato Curry Soup
summary: Comforting cauliflower and potato soup with gentle curry spices and coconut milk.

steps.text: Warm the oil in a pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes, until soft, adding the garlic and curry powder for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the cauliflower, potato and stock and simmer for 22 minutes, until completely tender.
Blend until smooth and stir through the coconut milk.
Finish with lemon juice and salt.

notes: Do not boil after adding the coconut milk.

title: Nam Jim Seafood Chilli Lime Sauce
summary: A sharp, garlicky green chilli and lime sauce that wakes up steamed fish and prawns.

steps.text: Blend the chillies, garlic and coriander with the lime juice, fish sauce, sugar and water until a loose, slightly chunky sauce forms.
Taste and add sugar if too sharp or lime if too flat.
Spoon over hot steamed fish or prawns just before serving.

notes: Wear gloves when cutting the chillies, or wash your hands well afterwards.
Use within 3 days; the colour fades as it sits.

title: Balkan Ajvar Roasted Capsicum Spread
summary: A smoky roasted capsicum and eggplant relish eaten on bread or with grilled meat.

steps.text: Roast the whole capsicums and eggplant at 220°C for 45 minutes, turning once, until blackened and collapsing.
Cover the vegetables in a bowl for 10 minutes, then peel off the skins and remove the seeds and stalks.
Blend the flesh with the garlic, vinegar, salt and sugar, then cook in a saucepan with the oil over low heat for 10 minutes until thick.

notes: Stir often so it does not catch on the base.
Keeps for 1 week in the fridge.

title: Canarian Mojo Rojo Red Sauce
summary: A garlicky red pepper sauce from the Canary Islands, served with potatoes and grilled meat.

steps.text: Soak the chillies in hot water for 10 minutes until soft, then drain and discard the stalks.
Blend the chillies, paprika, garlic, cumin and salt to a paste.
Add the vinegar and water, then blend while slowly pouring in the oil until thick and glossy.

notes: Classic with salt-crusted baby potatoes.
Keeps for 1 week in the fridge.

title: Portuguese Piri Piri Sauce
summary: A hot lemon and garlic chilli sauce for basting chicken or dipping chips.

steps.text: Blend the chillies, garlic, paprika, oregano and salt with the lemon juice and vinegar until fairly smooth.
Pour into a saucepan with the oil and simmer over low heat for 8 minutes, stirring, until slightly thickened and the raw edge is gone.
Cool, taste and adjust the salt and acid.

notes: Brush on at the end of cooking so the sugars do not burn.
Keeps in the fridge for 2 weeks.

title: Argentine Red Chimichurri
summary: A red version of chimichurri with capsicum and chilli, built for grilled steak.

items.raw: 1 roasted red capsicum, from a jar, drained

steps.text: Finely chop the parsley and garlic by hand or in short pulses.
Blend or chop the capsicum into small pieces and stir it in with the oregano, chilli flakes and salt.
Stir in the oil and vinegar until combined, then leave for 15 minutes so the flavours soften.

notes: Keep it chunky, not puréed.
Use within 5 days.

title: Peruvian-Style Yellow Chilli Cream Sauce
summary: A creamy, mild yellow chilli sauce in the style of Peruvian huancaina, for potatoes and eggs.

steps.text: Blend the capsicum, chilli, feta, milk, crackers, turmeric and lime juice until smooth.
Pour in the oil slowly while blending until the sauce is thick and creamy.
Taste and adjust with lime or a pinch of salt, then chill before serving.

notes: Feta is salty, so check before adding any extra salt.
Use within 3 days.

title: Sweet Tomato Chutney for Snacks
summary: A sticky tomato chutney with cumin and ginger for dosa, fritters and cheese toasties.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat, add the cumin seeds and cook for 30 seconds until they sizzle.
Add the onion and cook for 6 minutes until soft, then stir in the ginger, garlic, chilli and turmeric for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, sugar, vinegar and salt, then simmer for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and jammy.

notes: Cool before spooning into a clean jar.
Keeps in the fridge for 2 weeks.

title: Homemade Japanese Ponzu Sauce
summary: A citrus-soy sauce for dumplings, grilled fish and cold noodles.

steps.text: Combine the lemon juice, lime juice, soy sauce, mirin, vinegar and sugar in a jar.
Add the water and shake until the sugar dissolves.
Taste and add a little more citrus or soy as you prefer.

notes: Leave overnight in the fridge for a rounder flavour if you have time.
Keeps for 2 weeks.

title: Sichuan Chilli Oil Dipping Sauce
summary: A numbing, fragrant chilli oil for dumplings, noodles and cold dishes.

steps.text: Put the chilli flakes, sesame seeds, sugar and salt in a heatproof bowl.
Heat the oil with the peppercorns, garlic and star anise over low heat for 6 minutes until the garlic is just golden, then strain the hot oil over the chilli flakes, discarding the solids.
Let it sizzle, cool for 10 minutes, then stir in the soy sauce.

notes: Do not let the oil smoke or the chilli will taste bitter.
Keeps for 3 weeks in the fridge.

title: Lebanese Garlic Yoghurt Sauce
summary: A creamy garlic and lemon yoghurt sauce for shawarma, kebabs and roast vegetables.

steps.text: Crush the garlic with the salt into a paste.
Mix with the yoghurt and lemon juice until smooth.
Stir through the oil and mint and leave for 10 minutes before serving.

notes: Use less garlic for a gentler sauce.
Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

title: Quick Tomato Sambal
summary: A cooked tomato and chilli sambal that comes together in minutes for rice and fried eggs.

steps.text: Blend the chillies, shallots and garlic into a coarse paste.
Fry the paste in the oil over medium heat for 5 minutes until fragrant and the oil separates.
Add the tomatoes, sugar and salt and cook for 6 minutes until pulpy and thick, then stir in the lime juice.

notes: Add more chilli for heat, or deseed some for a milder sauce.
Keeps for 5 days in the fridge.

title: Hot Honey Chilli Drizzle
summary: A sweet, hot chilli honey for pizza, fried chicken, cheese boards and roast vegetables.

steps.text: Warm the honey with the chilli flakes in a small saucepan over low heat for 5 minutes until runny and gently simmering.
Remove from the heat and stir in the vinegar and salt.
Cool for 20 minutes, then pour into a clean jar.

notes: Strain out the flakes for a smoother drizzle.
Keep at room temperature for a month.

title: Korean Spinach Namul
summary: Blanched spinach seasoned with garlic, sesame oil and soy, the quickest banchan on the table.

steps.text: Blanch the spinach in a large pot of boiling water for 30 seconds until just wilted, then plunge into cold water.
Squeeze out as much water as you can and loosen the clumps with your fingers.
Toss with the garlic, soy sauce, sesame oil, spring onion and sesame seeds until evenly coated.

notes: Squeezing well stops the dish becoming watery.
Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

title: Korean Soybean Sprout Namul
summary: Crunchy sprouts dressed with sesame oil and garlic, served at room temperature.

steps.text: Rinse the sprouts and put them in a saucepan with the water and salt.
Cover and cook over medium heat for 6 minutes until tender but still crunchy, then drain well.
Toss with the garlic, sesame oil, soy sauce, spring onion and sesame seeds.

notes: Keep the lid on while cooking to remove the raw bean smell.
Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

title: Korean Gochugaru Cucumber Ribbons with Sesame and Rice Vinegar
summary: Cool, crunchy cucumber in a spicy-sweet dressing, a refreshing partner to barbecued meat.

steps.text: Shave the cucumbers into ribbons with a vegetable peeler and toss with the salt.
Leave for 5 minutes, then squeeze out the excess liquid.
Toss with the vinegar, sugar, chilli, garlic, sesame oil and seeds until coated.

notes: Serve within an hour for the best crunch.
Reduce the chilli for a milder side.

title: Korean Zucchini Stir-Fry Hobak Bokkeum
summary: Soft golden zucchini half-moons with garlic and sesame, gently salted.

steps.text: Heat the vegetable oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat and add the zucchini and salt.
Stir-fry for 5 minutes until golden at the edges and tender.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant, then finish with the sesame oil, spring onion and seeds.

notes: Do not crowd the pan or the zucchini will steam.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Korean Radish Salad Musaengchae
summary: A crunchy, tangy radish salad in a chilli-vinegar dressing, perfect with fatty meat.

items.raw: 400g daikon radish, cut into fine matchsticks

steps.text: Toss the radish with the salt and leave for 10 minutes, then drain and squeeze lightly.
Mix the chilli flakes, vinegar, sugar, garlic and fish sauce into a dressing.
Toss the radish with the dressing, spring onion and sesame seeds until well coated.

notes: Best eaten within 2 days.
Add a little more sugar if the radish is sharp.

title: Korean Mushroom Bokkeum
summary: Browned mixed mushrooms with garlic and soy, a savoury side that takes 10 minutes.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide frying pan over high heat and cook the mushrooms in a single layer for 6 minutes without stirring too often, until well browned.
Add the garlic, soy sauce and sugar and cook for 1 minute until sticky.
Finish with the sesame oil, spring onion and seeds.

notes: Cook in two batches if your pan is small.
Keeps for 3 days.

title: Korean Carrot Stir-Fry Namul
summary: Thin carrot strips tossed with garlic and sesame, a sweet and colourful plate filler.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and add the carrots with the salt.
Stir-fry for 5 minutes until just tender but still bright.
Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then turn off the heat and finish with the sesame oil and seeds.

notes: Serve warm or cold.
Keeps for 4 days in the fridge.

title: Korean Eggplant Namul Gaji Muchim
summary: Steamed eggplant strips pulled apart and dressed in a garlicky soy and sesame sauce.

steps.text: Steam the eggplant halves for 12 minutes until completely soft, then cool for 5 minutes.
Tear into long strips and gently squeeze out excess moisture.
Toss with the garlic, soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar, spring onion and seeds.

notes: Use a pot with a steamer basket or a bamboo steamer.
Keeps for 2 days in the fridge.

title: Korean Fresh Cabbage Kimchi Geotjeori
summary: Unfermented fresh kimchi with a chilli, garlic and fish sauce dressing, ready to eat straight away.

steps.text: Cut the cabbage into bite-sized pieces and toss with the salt, then leave for 15 minutes and squeeze out the liquid.
Mix the chilli flakes, garlic, fish sauce, sugar and ginger into a paste.
Toss the cabbage with the paste, spring onions and sesame seeds until every piece is coated.

notes: Eat within 3 days; it is a fresh salad, not a fermented kimchi.
Wear gloves when mixing the chilli paste.

title: Gyeran Mari Layered Korean Egg Roll with Carrot and Spring Onion
summary: A tender rolled omelette studded with finely chopped vegetables, sliced into rounds.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs with the salt and soy sauce, then stir in the carrot and spring onions.
Heat a little oil in a small non-stick frying pan over low heat and pour in a thin layer of egg, cooking until the surface is just set.
Roll the omelette to one end, add more egg to the empty space, cook until set, and roll again, repeating until all the egg is used.
Slide onto a board, rest for 2 minutes and slice into rounds.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until firm throughout, with no runny egg, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Use low heat so the outside does not brown.

title: Japanese Spinach Ohitashi
summary: Blanched spinach steeped in a light soy and mirin sauce, served chilled.

steps.text: Heat the soy sauce, mirin, water and sugar in a small saucepan until just simmering, then cool completely.
Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 40 seconds until just tender, cool in iced water and squeeze dry.
Cut into 4cm lengths, arrange in a bowl, pour over the cooled sauce and scatter with sesame seeds.

notes: The spinach will keep absorbing flavour for a day.
Serve cold in small bowls.

title: Japanese Green Bean Goma-ae
summary: Crisp green beans tossed in a nutty, sweet sesame dressing.

steps.text: Boil the beans in salted water for 3 minutes until bright green and just tender, then drain and refresh in cold water.
Grind the sesame seeds in a mortar or spice grinder until mostly crushed.
Mix with the soy sauce, sugar and mirin, then toss with the beans until coated.

notes: Do not grind the sesame to a paste, a little texture is lovely.
Serve cold or at room temperature.

title: Japanese Carrot Kinpira
summary: Sweet and savoury sautéed carrot and capsicum matchsticks with sesame.

steps.text: Heat the sesame oil in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the carrot for 4 minutes until it begins to soften.
Add the capsicum and cook for 2 minutes more.
Stir in the soy sauce, mirin, sugar and chilli and toss until the liquid is nearly gone and the vegetables glossy, then top with sesame seeds.

notes: Serve warm or cold in a bento.
Keeps for 4 days.

title: Sunomono Thin Cucumber Slices in Sweet Rice Vinegar Dressing
summary: Salted cucumber in a light sweet vinegar dressing, served cold between rich dishes.

steps.text: Toss the cucumber with the salt and leave for 10 minutes, then squeeze out the water.
Stir the vinegar, sugar and soy sauce together until the sugar dissolves.
Toss the cucumber with the dressing and ginger, then pile into small bowls with sesame seeds on top.

notes: Serve chilled.
Best eaten within 2 hours.

title: Shiozuke Salted Cabbage with Yuzu-Style Lemon and Chilli
