summary: A crisp, lightly salted cabbage pickle with lemon zest and chilli.

steps.text: Massage the cabbage with the salt in a bowl for 2 minutes until it begins to release liquid.
Add the lemon zest, juice, chilli and sugar and press down firmly.
Leave for 20 minutes, then squeeze out the liquid and serve.

notes: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge in a sealed jar.
Squeezing out the brine keeps it crunchy.

title: Asazuke Overnight Ginger Cucumber Salted Pickle
summary: Thick cucumber slices lightly pickled in salt, ginger and brine for a crunchy side.

items.raw: 3 Lebanese cucumbers, cut into thick slices

steps.text: Put the cucumber, salt, ginger, sugar, vinegar and chilli in a zip-lock bag.
Massage the bag for 1 minute until the cucumber starts to release liquid.
Press out the air, seal and chill until the cucumbers taste lightly pickled, at least 2 hours.

notes: Drain before serving.
Keeps for 2 days.

title: Creamy Japanese Potato Salad with Cucumber and Carrot Crunch
summary: A silky, mashed potato salad with Japanese-style mayonnaise, cucumber and ham.

items.raw: 600g potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks

steps.text: Boil the potatoes and carrot in salted water for 15 to 18 minutes until the potatoes are completely tender.
Drain and let the steam escape for 5 minutes, then roughly mash with the vinegar, sugar and salt.
Salt the cucumber slices, squeeze out the liquid and fold into the cooled potato with the mayonnaise, ham and pepper.

notes: Cool the potatoes fully before adding mayonnaise.
Keep chilled and eat within 2 days.

title: Hiyayakko Silken Tofu Block with Ginger Soy Topping
summary: Chilled silken tofu with ginger, spring onion and soy, light and quick.

steps.text: Drain the tofu gently and keep it chilled until cold, then cut into four blocks.
Mix the soy sauce, mirin and sesame oil in a small bowl.
Place the tofu on plates, top with ginger, spring onion and sesame seeds, and spoon over the sauce.

notes: Keep the tofu chilled until the last minute.
Serve straight away.

title: Nasu Dengaku Grilled Eggplant Halves under Sweet White Miso Glaze
summary: Silky grilled eggplant halves under a caramelised sweet miso glaze.

steps.text: Score the cut side of the eggplants, brush with the oil and roast at 200°C for 25 minutes until soft and golden.
Stir the miso, mirin and sugar together and spread on the eggplants.
Grill for 3 to 4 minutes until the glaze is bubbling and caramelised at the edges, then scatter with the sesame seeds.

notes: Watch the glaze closely because miso burns easily.
Serve hot.

title: Japanese Simmered Pumpkin Nimono
summary: Soft pumpkin chunks simmered in sweet soy until glazed, a gentle home-style side.

steps.text: Arrange the pumpkin skin-side down in a wide saucepan and add the water, soy sauce, mirin and sugar.
Cover and simmer over medium-low heat for 15 minutes until the pumpkin is tender when pierced.
Uncover and cook for 3 minutes more until the liquid is reduced to a glaze.

notes: Do not stir, to keep the pieces intact.
Serve warm or cold.

title: Broccoli Florets in Creamy Toasted Sesame Tahini Dressing Goma-Dare
summary: Bright green broccoli in a nutty, creamy sesame dressing with a touch of sweetness.

steps.text: Steam or boil the broccoli for 3 to 4 minutes until bright green and just tender.
Whisk the tahini, soy sauce, vinegar, sugar and water until smooth and pourable.
Arrange the broccoli on a plate, spoon over the dressing and finish with sesame seeds.

notes: Add more water if the dressing is too thick.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Japanese Cabbage Sesame Salad
summary: A crunchy shredded cabbage salad with a toasted sesame and rice vinegar dressing.

steps.text: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry frying pan for 2 minutes until golden, then cool.
Whisk the vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil and sugar together.
Toss the cabbage and carrot with the dressing and sesame seeds just before serving.

notes: Dress it just before eating to keep the crunch.
Keeps shredded cabbage fresh in the fridge for 2 days.

title: Gamja Jorim Glossy Korean Baby Potatoes in Soy and Honey
summary: Small potatoes simmered in a sweet soy glaze until sticky and glossy.

steps.text: Fry the potatoes in the oil over medium heat for 4 minutes until lightly golden.
Add the soy sauce, honey, sugar and water, then simmer for 18 minutes, turning occasionally, until the potatoes are tender and the sauce reduces to a glaze.
Stir in the sesame oil and sprinkle with the seeds.

notes: Add a small splash of water if the sauce reduces too fast.
Serve warm or cold.

title: Marie Rose Prawn Cocktail Sauce
summary: The pink, tangy sauce for a Christmas prawn cocktail, thick enough to coat cold prawns.

steps.text: Whisk the mayonnaise with the tomato sauce, lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce and hot sauce until smooth.
Stir in the cream until the sauce is light and pink, then season with salt and pepper.
Taste and add more lemon if it needs sharpness.

notes: Serve over cold cooked prawns on shredded lettuce.
Keeps in the fridge for 3 days.

title: Summer Christmas Potato Salad with Dill and Egg
summary: A creamy herby potato salad with soft chopped eggs for the Boxing Day cold table.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes until tender when pierced, then drain and cool.
Boil the eggs for 10 minutes until hard-set, cool in cold water, peel and chop.
Mix the mayonnaise, sour cream, vinegar, dill, spring onions, capers, salt and pepper, then fold through the potato and eggs gently.

notes: Food safety: keep the salad chilled and do not leave it out for more than 2 hours, or 1 hour in hot weather.
Make it a day ahead for the best flavour.

title: Maple Mustard Roasted Broccoli Trees with Crunchy Pecan Crumble
summary: Roasted broccoli glazed with maple and mustard, finished with a crunchy pecan topping.

steps.text: Toss the broccoli with the oil, salt and pepper and spread on a baking tray.
Roast at 220°C for 18 minutes until browned at the edges and tender.
Stir through the maple, mustard and pecans and roast for 5 minutes more until glossy, then serve hot.

notes: Do not crowd the tray or the broccoli will steam.
Best served straight from the oven.

title: Honey Thyme Glazed Carrots and Sweet Potato Wedges for the Festive Table
summary: Roasted root vegetables with a sticky honey and thyme glaze for the Christmas roast.

steps.text: Toss the carrots and sweet potato with the oil and salt on a large tray.
Roast at 200°C for 30 minutes, turning once, until golden at the edges.
Drizzle with the honey and thyme and roast for 8 minutes more until sticky, then finish with the lemon juice.

notes: Cut the vegetables to similar thickness so they cook evenly.
Serve straight away.

title: Traditional English Bread Sauce
summary: Creamy, nutmeg-scented bread sauce that goes with roast poultry at Christmas.

steps.text: Heat the milk with the onion, bay leaves and nutmeg in a saucepan until barely simmering, then turn off the heat and infuse for 15 minutes.
Remove the onion and bay leaves and stir in the breadcrumbs.
Cook over low heat for 5 minutes, stirring, until thick, then add the butter, cream, salt and pepper.

notes: Loosen with a splash of milk if it thickens as it stands.
Keeps for 3 days; reheat gently with extra milk.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Apple and Orange Christmas Relish
summary: A chunky spiced apple and orange relish, a fruity alternative to cranberry sauce.

steps.text: Put the apples, orange zest and juice, sugar, vinegar and spices in a saucepan.
Simmer gently over medium-low heat for 20 minutes, stirring, until the apple is soft and the liquid is thick and syrupy.
Cool and spoon into a jar.

notes: Serve warm or cold with ham and turkey.
Keeps in the fridge for 2 weeks.

title: Slow Caramelised Red Onion Pan Gravy for Sunday Roasts
summary: A deep onion gravy built from slowly browned red onions, flour and stock.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a heavy saucepan over medium-low heat and cook the onions with the sugar for 25 minutes, stirring often, until deeply golden.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then pour in the stock gradually, stirring.
Add the vinegar, thyme and soy sauce and simmer for 10 minutes until thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.

notes: Add pan juices from the roast for extra flavour.
Reheats well; add water if too thick.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Chinese Stir-Fried Lettuce with Garlic
summary: A quick, crunchy lettuce stir-fry with garlic and oyster sauce, popular at Lunar New Year.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wok over very high heat and add the garlic for 15 seconds until fragrant.
Add the lettuce and toss for 1 minute until just wilted but still crisp.
Stir in the oyster sauce, soy sauce and sugar, toss for a few seconds and finish with the sesame oil.

notes: Work fast because lettuce wilts quickly.
Serve straight away.

title: Lunar New Year Buddhist Vegetable Jai
summary: A braised vegetarian feast of mushrooms, tofu, cabbage and carrot in a savoury soy sauce.

steps.text: Soak the mushrooms in hot water for 20 minutes until soft, then slice, keeping 200ml of the soaking water.
Fry the tofu in the oil over medium-high heat for 5 minutes until golden, then add the garlic, ginger, cabbage and carrots and stir-fry for 4 minutes.

Add the mushrooms, soaking water, soy sauce, oyster sauce and sugar, simmer for 8 minutes until the vegetables are tender, then stir in the cornflour mixed with 2 tbsp water and the snow peas and cook until thickened.
Finish with the sesame oil.

notes: Soaking is not part of the prep time.
Serve with steamed rice.

title: Sweet and Sour Cucumber Pickle for Banquets
summary: A crisp, bright pickle that cuts through rich banquet dishes.

items.raw: 3 Lebanese cucumbers, chopped into bite-sized pieces

steps.text: Toss the cucumbers with the salt and leave for 10 minutes, then drain.
Stir the vinegar and sugar until dissolved and pour over the cucumbers.
Add the garlic, chilli and sesame oil and toss until evenly coated.

notes: Best the same day while still crisp.
Serve cold.

title: Hot Sizzled Ginger Spring Onion Oil for Steamed Chicken and Fish
summary: A fragrant, salty ginger and spring onion oil poured hot over steamed chicken or fish.

steps.text: Mix the spring onions, ginger and salt in a heatproof bowl.
Heat the oil in a small saucepan for 2 minutes until shimmering and just starting to smoke.
Pour the hot oil over the spring onion mixture so it sizzles, then stir in the soy sauce.

notes: Pour carefully, the oil is very hot.
Use within 2 days.

title: Kachumber Fine-Chopped Cucumber Tomato Red Onion Salad with Roasted Cumin
summary: A crisp, juicy Indian salad with lemon and roasted cumin, served alongside curries.

steps.text: Combine the cucumber, tomato, onion and chilli in a bowl.
Season with the lemon juice, cumin and salt.
Toss in the coriander and leave for 3 minutes until the juices mingle, then serve.

notes: Add the salt last so the salad does not turn watery.
Serve within 30 minutes.

title: Street Style Sweet Potato Chaat with Mint Yoghurt and Lime
summary: Roasted sweet potato cubes with spiced yoghurt, lime and crisp onions, a Diwali party snack.

steps.text: Toss the sweet potatoes with the oil, garam masala and half the salt and roast at 210°C for 25 minutes until crisp at the edges.
Whisk the yoghurt with the mint, lime juice, sugar and remaining salt.
Pile the hot potatoes onto a plate and top with the yoghurt, onion and coriander.

notes: Serve straight away so the potato stays crisp.
Add a pinch of chilli powder for extra heat.

title: Dry Gobi Masala Cauliflower
summary: Spiced dry-fried cauliflower with ginger, tomato and cumin, ideal for Diwali spreads.

items.raw: 1 small cauliflower, cut into small florets

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat, add the cumin seeds for 30 seconds until sizzling, then cook the onion for 6 minutes until golden.
Stir in the ginger, garlic and spices, then add the tomato and cook for 3 minutes until pulpy.
Add the cauliflower and salt, cover and cook for 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until tender with golden spots, then top with the coriander.

notes: Add a splash of water if it starts to catch.
Serve hot.

title: Thanksgiving Sage Apple and Celery Bread Dressing Baked Crisp on Top
summary: A buttery oven-baked bread dressing with sage, apple and celery, crisp on top and soft inside.

steps.text: Dry the bread cubes in a 160°C oven for 10 minutes until firm.
Melt the butter in a frying pan and cook the onion, celery and apple for 8 minutes until soft, then stir in the sage.
Mix everything with the stock, egg, salt and pepper, tip into a baking dish and bake at 190°C for 30 minutes until golden and the egg is set.

notes: Food safety: cook the dressing until it reaches at least 74°C in the centre, especially if it was stuffed in poultry.
Use stale bread for best texture.

title: Roasted Garlic Mashed Potatoes
summary: Silky mashed potatoes with sweet roasted garlic and plenty of butter.

steps.text: Cut the top off the garlic head, drizzle with the oil, wrap in foil and roast at 200°C for 40 minutes until soft and golden.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 18 minutes until completely tender, then drain and steam dry.
Squeeze the garlic into the potatoes, add the butter and milk and mash until smooth.

notes: Warm the milk so the potatoes stay hot.
Reheat with a splash of milk.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Homemade Mushroom Cream Green Bean Bake with Crispy Fried Onion Crown
summary: Green beans in a creamy mushroom sauce topped with crisp golden onions, made without tinned soup.

steps.text: Boil the beans for 3 minutes until bright green, then drain.

Cook the mushrooms in the butter over medium-high heat for 6 minutes until browned, stir in the garlic and flour for 1 minute, then add the milk, cream, salt and pepper and simmer for 3 minutes until thick.
Fold in the beans, tip into a dish, top with the onion tossed in the oil and bake at 200°C for 20 minutes until bubbling and the onions are crisp.

notes: Cover the dish loosely if the onions brown too fast.
Reheats well.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Orange Maple Sweet Potato Wedges Roasted with Cinnamon for Thanksgiving
summary: Sweet potato wedges roasted with orange, cinnamon and maple until caramelised.

steps.text: Toss the sweet potatoes with the oil, cinnamon and salt on a large tray.
Roast at 210°C for 30 minutes until tender and browned at the edges.
Pour over the maple and orange juice and roast for 8 minutes more until sticky, then scatter with pecans and orange zest.

notes: Turn the wedges once for even browning.
Serve hot.

title: Passover Apple and Walnut Charoset
summary: A sweet apple and walnut paste with cinnamon, symbolic on the Passover table.

steps.text: Mix the apples with the lemon juice to stop them browning.
Stir in the walnuts, honey and cinnamon.
Add the orange juice gradually until the mixture holds together like a chunky paste.

notes: Serve with matzo crackers.
Best eaten the day it is made.

title: Beetroot Salad with Horseradish Dressing
summary: Roasted beetroot with a creamy horseradish and lemon dressing.

steps.text: Wrap the beetroot in foil with the oil and roast at 200°C for 45 minutes until a knife slides in easily.
Cool, peel and cut into wedges.
Mix the sour cream, horseradish, lemon juice, dill and salt, then spoon over the beetroot.

notes: Wear gloves when peeling to avoid pink fingers.
Keeps for 3 days.

title: Passover Potato Kugel
summary: A crisp-edged baked potato pudding with onion and egg, a Passover and Shabbat favourite.

steps.text: Grate the potatoes and onion and squeeze out as much liquid as possible.
Mix with the eggs, 2 tbsp oil, potato starch, salt and pepper.
Heat the remaining oil in a baking dish in a 200°C oven for 5 minutes, add the potato mixture and bake for 50 minutes until deep golden and crisp at the edges.

notes: Food safety: bake until the egg is fully set in the centre and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Serve straight from the oven.

title: Carrot Tzimmes
summary: A sweet, slow-baked carrot dish with orange and cinnamon.

steps.text: Toss the carrots with the oil, honey, cinnamon, ginger and salt in a baking dish.
Add the orange juice, zest and water and cover tightly with foil.
Bake at 180°C for 35 minutes, then uncover and bake for 10 minutes more until tender and glazed.

notes: Serve with roast chicken or brisket.
Keeps for 3 days.

title: Pea and Potato Salad with Mint for Easter
summary: A fresh, minty potato salad with sweet green peas, perfect with Easter lamb.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 12 minutes until tender, adding the peas for the last 2 minutes, then drain and cool slightly.
Whisk the oil, vinegar, mustard and salt together.
Toss the warm potatoes and peas with the dressing, mint and spring onions.

notes: Dress while warm to soak in the flavour.
Serve warm or cold.

title: Lemony Roast Chicken Leftovers Soup with Egg Noodles and Parsley
summary: A comforting soup that turns the last of the roast chicken into a quick weeknight meal.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion, carrots and celery over medium heat for 6 minutes until softened, adding the garlic for the last minute.
Pour in the stock, bring to a simmer and cook for 8 minutes until the carrots are tender.
Add the noodles and chicken and simmer for 5 minutes until the noodles are cooked and the chicken is steaming hot at 75°C, then stir in the lemon juice, parsley and salt.

notes: Food safety: use roast chicken within 3 days of cooking, keep it chilled, and reheat until steaming hot at 75°C all the way through.
Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

title: Leftover Roast Chicken Congee
summary: A silky rice porridge made with leftover roast chicken, ginger and spring onion.

steps.text: Put the rice, stock and ginger in a large pot and bring to a gentle boil, stirring until the rice begins to bubble.
Reduce to a low simmer and cook for 40 minutes, stirring now and then, until the rice breaks down into a thick, creamy porridge.
Stir in the chicken and cook for 5 minutes until steaming hot at 75°C, then season with the soy sauce, sesame oil and pepper and top with the spring onions.

notes: Food safety: cool leftover congee and refrigerate within 1 hour, because cooked rice can grow harmful bacteria, and reheat until steaming hot at 75°C.
Add water if it thickens too much on standing.

title: Leftover Roast Lamb Scotch Broth
summary: A hearty barley broth that makes the most of Sunday's roast lamb and any bone.

steps.text: Soften the onion, carrots, swede and leeks in the oil in a large pot over medium heat for 8 minutes.
Add the barley, stock and bay leaves and simmer for 40 minutes until the barley and vegetables are tender.
Stir in the lamb and cook for 5 minutes until steaming hot at 75°C, then season and finish with the parsley.

notes: Food safety: use roast lamb within 3 days and reheat until steaming hot at 75°C.
The soup thickens overnight; thin with a little water.

title: Next Day Roast Beef Pearl Barley Soup with Carrot and Turnip
summary: A rich, beefy soup with barley, built on leftover roast beef and its pan juices.

steps.text: Cook the onion, carrots, turnip and celery in the oil in a large pot for 8 minutes until softened, then add the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the barley, stock and thyme and simmer for 40 minutes until the barley is tender.
Stir in the beef and Worcestershire sauce and simmer for 5 minutes until steaming hot at 75°C, then season with salt.

notes: Food safety: eat roast beef within 3 days of cooking and reheat until steaming hot at 75°C.
Freezes for 2 months.

title: Next Day Roast Pork Shreds in Caraway Cabbage Broth
summary: A warming Eastern European soup with shredded pork, cabbage and caraway.

steps.text: Cook the onion and carrots in the oil over medium heat for 6 minutes until soft, then add the caraway for 1 minute.
Add the cabbage, stock and potatoes and simmer for 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Stir in the pork and simmer for 5 minutes until steaming hot at 75°C, then add the vinegar, salt and dill.

notes: Food safety: use roast pork within 3 days and reheat until steaming hot at 75°C.
Serve with rye bread.

title: Leftover Chicken and Rice Soup with Carrot and Celery
summary: Shredded leftover roast chicken simmered with rice, carrot and celery in a savoury broth.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil over medium heat for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the stock, bay leaves, rice, carrots and celery and simmer for 18 minutes until the rice and vegetables are tender.
Add the chicken and simmer for 5 minutes until steaming hot at 75°C, then season with salt and parsley.

notes: Food safety: use roast chicken within 3 days of cooking, and refrigerate the soup within 1 hour of cooking because it contains cooked rice.
Use the carcass to make stock separately if you like.

title: Leftover Roast Vegetable Soup
summary: Blitz the tray of roasted vegetables from yesterday into a velvety soup.

items.raw: 600g leftover roasted vegetables (pumpkin, carrot, potato, onion)

steps.text: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the garlic and spices for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the vegetables and stock and simmer for 12 minutes until completely heated through and soft.
Blend until smooth, stir in the cream and salt, and top with parsley.

notes: Add a squeeze of lemon for brightness.
Use leftovers within 3 days; freezes for 2 months.

title: Roast Chicken Tortilla Soup
summary: A smoky tomato and lime soup with shredded roast chicken and crisp tortilla strips.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil over medium heat for 6 minutes until soft, then add the garlic, cumin and paprika for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and stock and simmer for 15 minutes until slightly thickened.

Add the chicken and simmer for 5 minutes until steaming hot at 75°C, while baking the tortilla strips at 200°C for 8 minutes until crisp, then serve topped with strips, avocado, lime juice and coriander.

notes: Food safety: use roast chicken within 3 days and reheat until steaming hot at 75°C.
Add chilli if you like heat.

title: Christmas Ham Bone Soup with Split Peas and Smoked Paprika
summary: A thick, smoky split pea soup made with the leftover Christmas ham bone.

items.item: leftover ham bone with some meat
items.raw: 1 leftover ham bone with some meat

steps.text: Soften the onion, carrots and celery in the oil in a large pot for 6 minutes, stirring in the paprika for the last minute.
Add the ham bone, water, split peas and bay leaves and simmer gently for 90 minutes until the peas have collapsed into a thick soup.
Lift out the bone, shred the meat back into the soup, season with pepper and simmer for 5 minutes until steaming hot at 75°C.

notes: Food safety: use the ham bone within 3 days and reheat the soup until steaming hot at 75°C.
The ham is already salty, so taste before adding any salt.

title: Silky Roast Pumpkin Soup Finished with Coconut Cream and Lime Zest
summary: Leftover roasted pumpkin blitzed with coconut cream, ginger and lime for a velvety soup.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil over medium heat for 5 minutes until soft, then add the ginger and garlic for 1 minute.
Add the pumpkin and stock and simmer for 10 minutes until completely hot.
Blend until smooth, stir in the coconut cream, lime juice and salt and top with lime zest.

notes: Cool leftovers quickly and refrigerate within 2 hours.
Freezes for 2 months.

title: Shredded Roast Lamb Moroccan Harira with Lentils Chickpeas and Tomato
summary: A warming spiced soup of lentils, chickpeas and tomato with the last of the roast lamb.

steps.text: Cook the onion and celery in the oil for 6 minutes until soft, then add the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, lentils, chickpeas and stock and simmer for 25 minutes until the lentils are soft.
Stir in the lamb and simmer for 5 minutes until steaming hot at 75°C, then add the lemon juice, coriander and salt.

notes: Food safety: use roast lamb within 3 days and reheat until steaming hot at 75°C.
Serve with lemon wedges.

title: Roast Chicken Laksa-Style Soup
summary: A coconut curry noodle soup that revives leftover roast chicken in 20 minutes.

steps.text: Fry the laksa paste in the oil for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the coconut milk and stock and simmer for 8 minutes, then add the chicken and cook for 5 minutes until steaming hot at 75°C.
Soak the noodles in boiling water for 4 minutes until tender, drain into bowls and ladle over the soup, then top with sprouts, lime juice, fish sauce and coriander.

notes: Food safety: use roast chicken within 3 days and reheat until steaming hot at 75°C.
Add chilli oil for extra heat.

title: Greek Avgolemono Soup with Leftover Roast Chicken
summary: A silky Greek-style lemon soup with rice, chicken and egg-thickened broth.

steps.text: Simmer the stock and rice in a pot for 15 minutes until the rice is tender.
Whisk the eggs with the lemon juice, then slowly whisk in 1 cup of hot stock to temper them.
Return the mixture to the pot off the heat with the chicken, stirring gently for 3 minutes until hot at 75°C and slightly thickened, then season and add the dill.

notes: Food safety: keep the soup below a boil once the egg is added, and make sure the soup reaches 75°C so the egg is cooked through.
Use roast chicken within 3 days of cooking.

title: Oven Tray Baked Eggs and Sausages for a Crowd
summary: A hands-off breakfast tray of sausages, tomatoes and baked eggs for a full table.

steps.text: Toss the sausages, tomatoes and mushrooms with the oil on a large tray and roast at 200°C for 15 minutes until the sausages are browned.
Make 8 small wells in the vegetables and crack an egg into each.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes until the whites are set and the sausages reach 75°C in the centre, then season and add parsley.

notes: Food safety: cook the sausages until they reach 75°C in the centre and the eggs until the whites are fully set.
Serve with toast.

title: Baked French Toast Casserole for Eight
summary: A custardy cinnamon French toast bake that feeds a crowd from one dish.

steps.text: Spread the bread cubes in a buttered baking dish and drizzle with the melted butter.
Whisk the eggs, milk, cream, sugar, vanilla, cinnamon and salt, then pour evenly over the bread and press down.
Bake at 180°C for 40 minutes until puffed, golden and the custard is set in the centre.

notes: Food safety: bake until the egg custard is fully set and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Serve with fruit and maple syrup.

title: Big Pot Oat Porridge for Eight
summary: A creamy porridge cooked on the stove for a crowd, ready for any toppings.

steps.text: Put the oats, milk, water and salt in a large saucepan.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Stir in the honey and cinnamon and add a splash of milk if too thick.

notes: Set out bowls of fruit, nuts and seeds for toppings.
Stir regularly to prevent catching.

title: Breakfast Burrito Tray Bake
summary: Oven-baked burritos filled with eggs, beans and cheese, made in bulk for a brunch table.

steps.text: Cook the onion and capsicum in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, then add the beaten eggs, cumin and salt and stir for 3 minutes until just set.
Stir in the beans, spoon the filling onto the tortillas with the cheese and roll tightly.
Bake seam-side down at 200°C for 12 minutes until golden and hot throughout.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until firm and bake until steaming hot, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Freeze wrapped burritos for up to 1 month.

title: Brunch Frittata Squares
summary: A tray-baked frittata of spinach, capsicum and feta, cut into squares for sharing.

steps.text: Cook the onion and capsicum in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, then wilt in the spinach for 1 minute.
Whisk the eggs, cream, salt and pepper and stir in the vegetables and feta.
Pour into a lined 20x30cm tray and bake at 180°C for 22 minutes until set and lightly golden.

notes: Food safety: bake until the egg is completely set and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Make-Ahead Egg and Bacon Muffins
summary: Savoury egg muffins with bacon and cheese that reheat in a minute.

steps.text: Fry the bacon in the oil for 6 minutes until crisp, then drain.
Whisk the eggs with the salt and pepper and stir in the bacon, cheese and spring onions.
Pour into a greased 12-hole muffin tray and bake at 180°C for 18 minutes until puffed and set in the centre.

notes: Food safety: bake until the eggs are fully set and refrigerate within 2 hours; reheat until steaming hot.
Freezes for 1 month.

title: Oven Baked Pancake Tray for a Crowd
summary: A single-tray pancake that puffs and browns in the oven, so nobody is flipping at the stove.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt in a bowl.
Whisk the eggs, milk, butter and vanilla, pour into the dry ingredients and stir until just combined.
Pour into a lined 25x35cm tray and bake at 200°C for 20 minutes until puffed and golden, then cut into squares.

notes: Serve with berries and maple syrup.
Food safety: bake until set in the centre. Wash fresh produce well, refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat them within 3 days.

title: Baked Shakshuka for Six
summary: A big dish of spiced tomato and capsicum sauce with baked eggs.

steps.text: Soften the onion and capsicum in the oil in an ovenproof pan for 6 minutes, then add the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and salt and simmer for 12 minutes until thick.
Make 6 wells, crack in the eggs, scatter with feta and bake at 190°C for 10 minutes until the whites are set, then add parsley.

notes: Food safety: cook until the egg whites are fully set.
Serve with warm flatbread.

title: Oven Hash Browns Tray with Capsicum Onion and Sausage Crumble for Twelve
summary: A big oven-baked hash with crisp potato, capsicum, onion and browned sausage.

items.raw: 4 pork sausages, meat squeezed from casings

steps.text: Toss the potatoes, capsicums, onions, oil, paprika, salt and pepper on two large trays and roast at 220°C for 20 minutes.
Add the sausage meat in small pieces and roast for 20 minutes more, stirring once, until the potatoes are crisp and the sausage is cooked through at 75°C.
Season and serve straight from the tray.

notes: Food safety: make sure the sausage is cooked until no pink remains and it reaches 75°C.
Use two trays so the potatoes crisp up.

title: Sweet Potato Black Bean Oven Tray Topped with Baked Eggs and Avocado
summary: Roasted sweet potato and black beans with baked eggs, avocado and lime.

steps.text: Toss the sweet potatoes with the oil, spices and salt on a tray and roast at 210°C for 20 minutes until tender.
Add the beans, make 6 wells, crack an egg into each and bake for 10 to 12 minutes until the whites are set.
Top with avocado, lime juice and coriander.

notes: Food safety: cook until the egg whites are fully set.
Add chilli sauce if you like.

title: Cheddar and Mushroom Breakfast Strata
summary: A savoury bread and egg bake with mushrooms and cheddar, ideal for brunch.

steps.text: Cook the mushrooms and onion in the oil over medium-high heat for 8 minutes until browned.
Layer the bread, mushrooms and half the cheese in a baking dish.
Whisk the eggs, milk, mustard, salt and pepper, pour over, top with the remaining cheese and bake at 180°C for 40 minutes until puffed, golden and set in the centre.

notes: Food safety: bake until the egg is fully set and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Assemble the night before and keep chilled.

title: Apple Cinnamon Oat Breakfast Bake for a Crowd
summary: A soft, gently sweet oat bake with apple, cinnamon and walnuts.

steps.text: Mix the oats, baking powder, cinnamon and salt in a bowl.
Whisk the apples with the eggs, milk and maple syrup and stir into the oats with half the walnuts.
Pour into a baking dish, scatter with the remaining walnuts and bake at 180°C for 30 minutes until golden and set.

notes: Serve with yoghurt and fruit; reheats well.
Food safety: bake until the egg is set in the centre. Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Apple Bircher Muesli Big Bowl with Toasted Seeds for Brunch Guests
summary: A fresh, chilled apple muesli with yoghurt and toasted seeds.

steps.text: Toast the pumpkin and sunflower seeds in a dry pan for 3 minutes until golden, then cool.
Mix the oats, apple juice, apples, yoghurt, honey and cinnamon.
Cover, chill until the oats have softened, then serve topped with seeds.

notes: Soaking time is not included in the prep time.
Keeps for 3 days.

title: Charred Barbecue Corn Cobs with Smoky Paprika Lime Butter
summary: Sweet corn charred on the barbecue and brushed with smoky paprika and lime butter.

steps.text: Mash the butter with the paprika, lime juice, zest and salt until smooth.
Grill the corn on a hot barbecue for 12 to 15 minutes, turning often, until tender and charred in spots.
Brush with the butter while hot and scatter with coriander.

notes: Keep the corn moving so it chars without burning.
The butter keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

title: Campfire Foil Packet Potatoes with Herbs
summary: Baby potatoes steamed in foil with garlic and herbs, nestled in the coals.

steps.text: Toss the potatoes with the oil, garlic, herbs, salt and pepper and divide between four large foil sheets.
Seal into tight parcels and place on hot coals or a barbecue.
Cook for 35 to 40 minutes, turning once, until the potatoes are completely tender when pierced.

notes: Open carefully, the steam is very hot.
No campfire needed, they work in a 200°C oven too.

title: Camp Vinegar Coleslaw
summary: A crisp, mayo-free coleslaw that holds up in the heat on camping trips and picnics.

steps.text: Whisk the vinegar, oil, sugar, mustard, salt and celery seeds in a large bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Add the cabbage, carrots and onion and toss well.
Leave for 15 minutes until the cabbage softens slightly, tossing once.

notes: Keeps well in a cooler for hours because there is no mayonnaise.
Keeps for 4 days in the fridge.

title: Barbecue Zucchini with Mint Dressing
summary: Grilled zucchini planks with a bright lemon, garlic and mint dressing.

steps.text: Brush the zucchini with 1 tbsp of the oil and grill on a hot barbecue for 3 to 4 minutes per side until tender and charred.
Whisk the remaining oil with the garlic, lemon juice, mint, salt and chilli.
Arrange the zucchini on a platter and spoon over the dressing.

notes: Grill in batches without crowding.
Best served warm.

title: Smoky Campfire Baked Beans
summary: Beans in a smoky tomato sauce simmered over the fire in one pot.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a pot over the fire or stove and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic and paprika for 1 minute.
Add the beans, tomatoes, sugar, vinegar, tomato paste and salt.
Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce is thick and the beans are glossy.

notes: Stir often so it does not catch on the base.
Reheats well; keeps for 4 days.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Campfire Foil Pack Vegetables
summary: Mixed vegetables seasoned and steamed in foil parcels, ideal for camping.

steps.text: Toss the vegetables with the oil, garlic, oregano and salt.
Divide between four large foil sheets and seal into tight parcels.
Cook on hot coals or a barbecue for 25 to 30 minutes, turning once, until the vegetables are tender.

notes: Open carefully because of hot steam.
Add a squeeze of lemon at the end.

title: Barbecue Capsicum and Onion Skewers
summary: Colourful skewers of capsicum and red onion, glazed with garlic and smoked paprika oil.

steps.text: Thread the capsicum and onion onto skewers.
Mix the oil, garlic, paprika, lemon juice and salt and brush over the skewers.
Grill on a hot barbecue for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until charred and tender.

notes: Soak wooden skewers in water for 30 minutes first.
Serve with grilled meat or hummus.

title: Grilled Pineapple Spears with Chilli Lime Salt and Mint for the Barbecue
summary: Caramelised pineapple spears with a hit of chilli lime salt, great beside grilled pork.

items.raw: 1 pineapple, peeled and cut into spears

steps.text: Mix the chilli, lime zest and salt together.
Brush the pineapple with the oil and grill on a hot barbecue for 3 to 4 minutes per side until charred and caramelised.
Squeeze over the lime juice, dust with the chilli salt and scatter with mint.

notes: Grill cut-side down for the best char marks.
Serve warm.

title: Wholegrain Mustard Potato Salad with Crisp Bacon Bits and Gherkin
summary: A tangy potato salad with crisp bacon, gherkins and mustard dressing for barbecues.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes until tender, then drain and cool slightly.
Fry the bacon for 6 minutes until crisp and drain on paper.
Mix the mayonnaise, sour cream, mustard, vinegar, gherkins, spring onions and salt, then fold through the potatoes and top with the bacon.

notes: Food safety: keep the salad chilled and do not leave it out for more than 2 hours, or 1 hour in hot weather.
Keeps for 2 days.

title: Classic Macaroni Salad for Picnics
summary: A creamy elbow macaroni salad with celery, capsicum and a tangy dressing.

steps.text: Boil the macaroni for 9 to 10 minutes until tender, then drain and rinse under cold water.
Whisk the mayonnaise, sour cream, vinegar, mustard, salt and pepper.
Fold the macaroni, celery, capsicum and onion into the dressing until coated.

notes: Food safety: keep chilled in a cooler and discard after 2 hours out of the fridge.
Loosen with a splash of milk if it thickens.

title: Camp Cucumber and Yoghurt Salad
summary: A cooling cucumber and mint salad that needs no cooking, ideal beside spicy barbecue food.

steps.text: Mix the yoghurt, garlic, lemon juice, oil and salt in a bowl.
Fold through the cucumber and mint and leave for 5 minutes until the flavours blend.
Taste and adjust the lemon and salt, then keep chilled.

notes: Keep it in a cooler until serving.
Best within 4 hours.

title: Camp Tuna Pasta Salad
summary: A filling tinned tuna and pasta salad with tomatoes, olives and lemon, easy to pack.

items.raw: 2 x 185g tins tuna in olive oil, drained

steps.text: Boil the pasta for 10 minutes until al dente, drain and rinse under cold water.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice and salt.
Toss the pasta with the tuna, tomatoes, olives, onion, parsley and dressing until coated.

notes: Food safety: keep chilled and eat within 2 hours of leaving the cooler.
Keeps for 2 days in the fridge.

title: Barbecue Eggplant with Garlic Yoghurt
summary: Smoky grilled eggplant slices with a garlic yoghurt sauce and parsley.

steps.text: Brush the eggplant with the oil and salt and grill on a hot barbecue for 5 to 7 minutes per side until soft and deeply charred.
Mix the yoghurt, garlic and lemon juice.
Spoon the yoghurt over the eggplant and scatter with parsley and chilli.

notes: Salting first for 10 minutes reduces bitterness, rinse and pat dry before oiling.
Serve warm.

title: Foil Wrapped Herb Garlic Baguette Baked on Campfire Coals
summary: A crusty baguette stuffed with garlic and herb butter, warmed in foil on the coals.

steps.text: Mix the butter, garlic, parsley, oregano and salt until smooth.
Slice the baguette almost through at 3cm intervals and spread the butter between the slices.
Wrap tightly in foil and heat on hot coals or a 200°C oven for 12 to 15 minutes, turning once, until hot and the butter has melted.

notes: Open the foil for the last 3 minutes for a crisper crust.
Serve straight away.

title: Chickpea and Tuna Protein Salad
summary: A high protein lunch salad of chickpeas, tinned tuna and crunchy vegetables with a lemon dressing.

items.raw: 185g tin tuna in olive oil, drained

steps.text: Combine the chickpeas, tuna, cucumber, tomatoes and onion in a bowl.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice and salt.
Toss the dressing and parsley through the salad until evenly coated.

notes: Food safety: keep refrigerated and eat within 2 days.
Add chilli flakes for a kick.

title: High Protein Shredded Chicken Quinoa Bowl with Cucumber Mint and Lemon Tahini
summary: Quinoa, shredded chicken and crisp vegetables with a creamy lemon tahini dressing.

steps.text: Simmer the quinoa in 400ml water for 15 minutes until tender and the water is absorbed, then fluff and cool.
Poach the chicken in simmering water for 12 to 14 minutes until cooked through at 75°C, then shred.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice, water, oil and salt, then toss with the quinoa, chicken, cucumber, tomatoes and mint.

notes: Food safety: make sure the chicken reaches 75°C in the thickest part and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Keeps for 2 days.

title: Lentil and Feta Protein Salad
summary: Earthy green lentils with feta, cucumber and herbs in a red wine vinaigrette.

steps.text: Simmer the lentils in plenty of water for 18 to 20 minutes until tender but holding their shape, then drain and cool.
Whisk the oil, vinegar and salt.
Toss the lentils with the cucumber, tomatoes, onion, parsley and dressing, then top with the feta.

notes: Cook the lentils gently so they do not turn mushy.
Keeps for 3 days.

title: Protein Packed Edamame Baked Tofu Cubes and Cabbage with Ginger Sesame Dressing
summary: Crisp baked tofu with edamame and cabbage in a ginger and sesame dressing.

steps.text: Toss the tofu with 1 tbsp soy sauce, the cornflour and vegetable oil and bake at 220°C for 25 minutes, turning once, until crisp and golden.
Boil the edamame for 4 minutes until tender, then drain and cool.
Whisk the remaining soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, ginger and honey, then toss with the cabbage, carrot, edamame and tofu and top with sesame seeds.

notes: Press the tofu in paper towel first for crisper cubes.
Keeps for 2 days.

title: Egg and Lentil Salad with Mustard Dressing
summary: Hard-boiled eggs over green lentils, rocket and a sharp mustard dressing.

steps.text: Simmer the lentils for 20 minutes until tender, then drain and cool.
Boil the eggs for 10 minutes until hard-set, cool in cold water and peel.
Whisk the oil, vinegar, mustard and salt, toss with the lentils, rocket and tomatoes and top with halved eggs.

notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until firm, keep the salad chilled and eat within 2 days.
Add capers for extra bite.

title: Flaked Salmon Cannellini Bean Lunch Salad with Dill Lemon and Rocket
summary: Flaked tinned salmon with creamy white beans, rocket and a dill and lemon dressing.

steps.text: Flake the salmon into a bowl, removing any large bones.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice, dill and salt.
Toss the beans, onion, rocket and salmon with the dressing until just combined.

notes: Food safety: tinned salmon is already cooked and opaque, and it flakes easily; discard it if it smells off; keep the salad refrigerated and eat within 2 days.
Serve with crusty bread.

title: Seared Beef Salad with Cucumber, Mint and Lime Chilli Dressing
summary: Seared beef strips with cucumber, herbs and a lime and fish sauce dressing.

steps.text: Season the beef and sear in the oil in a hot pan for 3 to 4 minutes per side until medium, then rest for 5 minutes and slice thinly.
Stir the lime juice, fish sauce, sugar and chillies until the sugar dissolves.
Toss the cucumber, onion and herbs with the beef and dressing.

notes: Food safety: whole cuts like steak can be eaten medium, but cook until at least 63°C in the centre; mince should always be well done.
Serve straight away.

title: Chicken Taco Salad Bowl with Black Beans
summary: A crunchy taco salad with spiced chicken, beans, corn and a lime yoghurt dressing.

steps.text: Toss the chicken with the oil, cumin, paprika and half the salt and cook in a hot pan for 7 minutes until golden and cooked through at 75°C.
Whisk the yoghurt with the lime juice and remaining salt.
Assemble the lettuce, beans, corn, tomatoes, avocado and chicken in bowls and drizzle with the dressing.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C in the thickest part and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Add crushed corn chips for crunch.

title: Greek Chicken and Chickpea Salad
summary: Lemony grilled chicken with chickpeas, cucumber, tomato, olives and feta.

steps.text: Rub the chicken with 1 tbsp of the oil, the lemon juice and oregano and cook in a hot pan for 6 to 7 minutes per side until cooked through at 75°C, then rest and slice.
Whisk the remaining oil and the vinegar.
Toss the chickpeas, cucumber, tomatoes, olives and onion with the dressing and top with the chicken and feta.

notes: Food safety: cook the chicken until it reaches 75°C in the thickest part and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Serve with pita bread.

title: Prawn and Quinoa Salad with Lime
summary: Garlic prawns over quinoa with avocado, cucumber and a lime dressing.

steps.text: Simmer the quinoa in 300ml water for 15 minutes until tender, then fluff and cool.
Cook the prawns with the garlic in 1 tbsp of the oil for 3 to 4 minutes until pink and opaque throughout.
Whisk the remaining oil, lime juice and salt, then toss with the quinoa, avocado, cucumber, tomatoes, coriander and prawns.

notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until pink and opaque, keep the salad chilled and eat within 1 day.
Add chilli if you like heat.

title: Turkish Kahvalti Plate with Olives and Cucumber
summary: A relaxed Turkish breakfast spread of soft-boiled eggs, feta, olives, tomato, cucumber and warm bread.

steps.text: Lower the eggs into a pan of boiling water and simmer for 7 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks are jammy, then cool in cold water and peel.
Arrange the feta, olives, tomato and cucumber on a large platter, drizzle the feta with the olive oil and scatter with oregano and parsley.
Toast the bread until golden, then serve with the eggs and honey so everyone can build their own plate.

notes: Slice the feta thickly so it holds its shape on the plate.

Food safety: cook eggs until the whites are fully set and keep leftovers in the fridge for no more than 2 days. Use fresh, uncracked eggs; for pregnant women, older people, young children and anyone with low immunity, cook the eggs until the yolks are firm.

title: Turkish Sigara Boregi Cheese Rolls
summary: Thin filo cigars filled with feta and parsley, baked until golden and crisp.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C. Mix the feta, parsley, pepper and half the egg until evenly combined.
Cut each filo sheet in half, brush lightly with butter, then spoon a line of filling along the short edge and roll up tightly like a cigar, tucking in the sides.
Place seam side down on a lined tray, brush with the remaining egg and bake for 18 to 20 minutes until deep golden and crisp.

notes: Keep unused filo under a damp tea towel so it does not dry out.
Food safety: bake until golden and piping hot throughout, and keep leftovers refrigerated for up to 2 days.

title: Turkish Kuymak Cornmeal and Cheese Pan
summary: A stretchy, molten cornmeal and cheese breakfast from the Black Sea coast, eaten with bread.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a small heavy pan, add the cornmeal and stir over medium heat for 3 minutes until it smells nutty and darkens slightly.
Pour in the water and milk, whisking constantly, and cook for 5 minutes until thick and smooth.
Stir in the mozzarella and salt over low heat for 2 to 3 minutes until the cheese melts into long strands, then serve straight from the pan.

notes: Whisk as you pour in the liquid to avoid lumps.
Serve with torn bread for dipping.

title: Turkish Zucchini Mucver Fritters with Dill
summary: Grated zucchini fritters with feta and dill, pan-cooked until golden and served with garlic yoghurt.

steps.text: Salt-free squeeze: wrap the grated zucchini in a clean tea towel and wring out as much liquid as possible.
Mix the zucchini with the feta, eggs, flour, dill, spring onions and pepper until a thick batter forms.
Heat the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat, drop in spoonfuls of batter and cook for 3 to 4 minutes each side until deep golden and cooked through.
Stir the garlic into the yoghurt and serve alongside.

notes: Squeezing the zucchini well keeps the fritters crisp.
Food safety: cook until the centres are firm and set, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Georgian Lobiani Butter Bean Bread
summary: A flaky Georgian flatbread filled with spiced mashed butter beans and onion.

steps.text: Mix the flour, baking powder, salt, yoghurt, water and 1 tbsp oil into a soft dough and knead for 3 minutes until smooth, then cover.
Fry the onion in the remaining oil for 5 minutes until soft, add the garlic and spices for 1 minute, then mash in the beans and fresh coriander until a thick paste forms.
Divide the dough into 3, roll each into a circle, spread the filling over half, fold the other half over and press out to a thin circle about 20cm wide.
Cook each flatbread in a dry hot pan for 3 to 4 minutes each side until golden and speckled.

notes: Press gently so the filling does not break through the dough.
Best eaten warm; reheat in a dry pan.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Georgian Chikhirtma Chicken and Egg Soup
summary: A silky Georgian soup of chicken broth thickened with beaten egg, lemon and fresh herbs.

steps.text: Simmer the chicken, onion, carrot, salt and water for 25 minutes until the chicken reaches 75°C and is cooked through, then lift out and shred.
Melt the butter in a small pan, stir in the flour for 1 minute, whisk in 200ml hot broth until smooth, and return it to the pot, simmering for 5 minutes until lightly thickened.
Beat the eggs with the lemon juice, then slowly whisk in a ladle of hot broth, and pour back into the pot off the boil, stirring for 2 minutes until the soup turns silky and pale.
Return the chicken, add the herbs and pepper and ladle into bowls.

notes: Keep the pot off a hard boil once the egg goes in so it does not scramble.
Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C, and the egg-thickened soup should be heated until steaming hot before serving.

title: Georgian Baked Eggs in Walnut Tomato Sauce
summary: Eggs baked in a tomato sauce enriched with ground walnuts, garlic and warm spices.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the oil in an ovenproof pan for 5 minutes until golden, then add the garlic and spices for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, walnuts and salt and simmer for 10 minutes until thick and jammy.
Make four wells, crack in the eggs, cover and bake at 190°C for 8 to 10 minutes until the whites are set.
Scatter with coriander and serve with bread.

notes: Ground walnuts thicken the sauce and add a gentle richness.
Food safety: bake until the whites are fully set and the yolks are no longer runny if serving to anyone vulnerable.

title: Ethiopian-Style Firfir with Spiced Tomato Sauce
summary: Torn flatbread soaked in a spicy berbere tomato sauce, a classic Ethiopian breakfast.

steps.text: Fry the onion in the oil in a wide pan for 6 minutes until soft and golden, then stir in the garlic, ginger, paprika and chilli for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomato paste, tomatoes, water and salt and simmer for 10 minutes until reduced to a thick sauce.
Fold in the torn flatbread and cook for 2 minutes until it has soaked up the sauce, then top with parsley.

notes: Day-old flatbread works best as it absorbs the sauce without going mushy.
Add more chilli for extra heat.

title: Ethiopian-Style Spiced Butter Bean Ful
summary: Creamy butter beans warmed with cumin, tomato and green chilli and topped with a squeeze of lemon.

steps.text: Fry the onion in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic, cumin and turmeric for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomato and cook for 3 minutes until it breaks down, then tip in the beans and water and simmer for 6 minutes until creamy.
Mash roughly with a fork until creamy but still chunky, then stir in the chilli, lemon juice and parsley and serve with the toast.

notes: Mash only part of the beans so the dish keeps some texture.
Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Ethiopian Atkilt Wat Cabbage Carrot and Potato
summary: A mild turmeric-scented stew of cabbage, carrot and potato, served with flatbread or rice.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil in a large pot for 6 minutes until soft, then add the garlic, ginger and spices for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the potatoes, carrots and water, cover and simmer for 10 minutes until the potato is just starting to soften.
Stir in the cabbage and salt, cover and cook for 12 minutes more until all the vegetables are tender.
Finish with the lemon juice.

notes: The vegetables should be tender but not falling apart.
Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

title: Filipino Longsilog Sausage Garlic Rice and Egg
summary: Sweet pork sausages with garlic fried rice and a fried egg, a Filipino breakfast favourite.

steps.text: Cook the sausages in a pan over medium heat for 12 to 14 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through to 75°C inside.
Fry the garlic in the oil in a large pan for 1 minute until golden, add the rice and salt and stir-fry for 4 minutes until hot and lightly crisp.
Fry the eggs in the same pan for 3 minutes until the whites are set.
Serve the rice with the sausages, eggs, tomato and a small dish of vinegar with spring onion.

notes: Day-old rice fries better than fresh.
Food safety: pork sausages must reach 75°C. Cool leftover rice and refrigerate it within 1 hour, and use it within 1 day.

title: Malaysian Telur Belado Egg Sambal
summary: Boiled eggs coated in a sweet and tangy chilli sambal, great over rice.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes until firm, cool in cold water, peel and set aside.
Fry the onion, garlic and chillies in the oil for 6 minutes until soft and fragrant, then add the tomato paste, tomato, tamarind, sugar, salt and water.
Simmer for 8 minutes until the sambal is thick and glossy, then stir in the eggs for 2 minutes until coated and hot.

notes: Use fewer chillies for a milder sambal.
Food safety: boil eggs until fully firm, and keep leftovers refrigerated for up to 2 days.

title: Indonesian Vegetable Salad with Spiced Peanut Dressing
summary: A bowl of blanched vegetables, potato, egg and tofu with a rich peanut dressing.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes for 12 minutes until tender, lift out, then boil the eggs in the same water for 9 minutes until firm, cool and halve.
Blanch the green beans, cabbage and bean sprouts for 2 minutes in boiling water until just tender, then drain and cool.
Whisk the peanut butter, garlic, soy, lime, sugar, chilli and warm water until smooth and pourable.
Arrange the vegetables, potato, tofu, egg and cucumber on plates and spoon over the sauce.

notes: Thin the sauce with more warm water if it thickens as it stands.
Food safety: boil the eggs until firm and eat the salad within 1 day.

title: Indonesian Sayur Asem Tamarind Vegetable Soup
summary: A light sweet and sour vegetable soup with sweetcorn, green beans and tamarind.

steps.text: Fry the onion and garlic in the oil for 4 minutes until soft and fragrant.
Add the water, tamarind, sugar and salt and bring to a simmer, then add the corn and pumpkin and cook for 10 minutes until nearly tender.
Add the beans, cabbage and tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until the beans are tender and the soup is tangy.

notes: Taste and balance the sweet and sour with more sugar or tamarind.
Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: South Indian Instant Rava Dosa with Potato Masala
summary: Thin crisp semolina crepes, ready without fermenting, filled with a turmeric potato masala.

steps.text: Whisk the semolina, flours, cumin, salt, yoghurt and water into a thin batter and let it stand while you make the filling.

Heat half the oil in a pan, pop the mustard seeds, then cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft, add the turmeric, chilli and potato and stir for 4 minutes until coated and hot, then add the coriander.
Heat a wide non-stick pan, ladle in the batter from the edge inwards in a lacy pattern and drizzle with a little oil, cooking for 2 to 3 minutes until crisp and golden.
Fill with the potato masala and fold.

notes: The batter is thin, so stir it before each ladle.
Eat dosa straight away while crisp.

title: South Indian Ven Pongal with Black Pepper and Cashews
summary: Soft, creamy rice and lentil porridge tempered with pepper, cumin, ginger and cashews.

steps.text: Rinse the rice and lentils, then simmer them with the water and salt, stirring now and then, for 25 minutes until completely soft and creamy.
Heat the ghee in a small pan, fry the cashews for 1 minute until golden, then add the cumin, pepper, ginger  for 1 minute until sizzling.
Stir the tempering into the pongal and loosen with hot water if needed.

notes: Serve with coconut chutney or sambar.
The pongal thickens as it cools; add water when reheating.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: South Indian Onion Semolina Uttapam
summary: Thick savoury semolina pancakes studded with onion, tomato and green chilli.

steps.text: Stir the semolina, yoghurt, water and salt into a thick batter, then fold in the baking powder just before cooking.
Heat a non-stick pan with a little oil, pour on a ladle of batter and spread to about 12cm.
Scatter with onion, tomato, chilli and coriander, press lightly and cook for 3 minutes until the base is golden, then flip and cook for 2 minutes until the topping is tender and the centre is set.

notes: Keep the heat at medium so the centres cook through.
Serve with coconut chutney or tomato chutney.

title: South Indian Rasam with Black Pepper and Tomato
summary: A thin, peppery tomato and tamarind soup that is sharp, warming and easy to sip.

steps.text: Heat the oil, pop the mustard and cumin seeds for 30 seconds, then add the chillies and garlic for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 4 minutes until soft, then stir in the tamarind, pepper, turmeric, salt and water.
Simmer gently for 12 minutes until the flavours are well blended, then stir in the coriander.

notes: Do not boil hard or the aroma will fade.
Serve as a soup or spooned over rice.

title: South Indian Vegetable Sambar
summary: A tangy lentil and vegetable stew with tamarind and sambar spices, served with rice or idli.

steps.text: Simmer the lentils with the water and turmeric for 20 minutes until completely soft, then mash lightly.
Heat the oil, pop the mustard seeds, then fry onion and curry powder for 4 minutes until soft and fragrant.
Add the carrot, pumpkin, beans, tomatoes, tamarind and salt with the lentils and simmer for 15 minutes until the vegetables are tender.

notes: Thin with water for a soupier sambar.
Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes well.

title: South Indian Tomato Rice with Curry Leaves
summary: Fragrant rice cooked with tomato, onion and whole spices, a favourite lunchbox dish.

steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear. Heat the oil, pop the mustard and cumin seeds, then add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, tomatoes, chilli and turmeric and cook for 5 minutes until the tomatoes collapse into a thick paste.
Add the rice, water and salt, bring to the boil, cover and cook on low for 12 minutes until the water is absorbed and the rice is tender, then rest for 5 minutes and fluff with coriander.

notes: Cover tightly so the steam cooks the rice evenly.
Keeps 2 days in the fridge; reheat until steaming hot.

title: Mexican Huevos Rancheros with Black Beans
summary: Fried eggs on crisp tortillas with warm black beans and a chilli tomato salsa.

steps.text: Simmer the onion, garlic, chilli, tomatoes and salt in a small pan for 10 minutes until thick, then blend roughly for a salsa.
Warm the beans with the cumin and a splash of water for 5 minutes until hot and mashable, then mash part of them.
Fry the tortillas in the oil for 1 minute each side until crisp, then fry the eggs for 3 minutes until the whites are set.
Layer the tortillas with beans, eggs and salsa and top with coriander.

notes: Cook the eggs until firm if serving to young children.
Food safety: cook eggs until the whites are set and the yolks thickening; keep leftover salsa refrigerated for up to 3 days.

title: Mexican Molletes Bean and Cheese Toasts
summary: Split bread rolls spread with refried-style black beans, topped with cheese and grilled until bubbling.

steps.text: Mash the beans in a small pan with the garlic, cumin, oil and a splash of water and warm for 4 minutes until thick and spreadable.
Spread the beans over the cut sides of the rolls, top with mozzarella and grill for 4 to 5 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and golden.
Mix the tomato, onion, coriander and lime juice into a quick salsa and spoon over the toasts.

notes: Keep the grill at medium so the bread toasts without burning.
Use a bolillo-style roll if you can find one.

title: Honduran-Style Baleadas with Beans and Cheese
summary: Soft folded flour tortillas filled with creamy beans, cheese and a drizzle of cream.

steps.text: Mix the flour, baking powder, salt, water and 2 tbsp oil into a soft dough and knead for 2 minutes, then cover and rest.
Mash the beans in a small pan with the garlic and a splash of water, warming for 5 minutes until thick and creamy.
Roll the dough into 4 circles and cook in a dry pan for 1 to 2 minutes each side until puffed and spotted, then fry the eggs in the remaining oil for 3 minutes until the whites are set.
Spread each tortilla with beans, feta and cream, add an egg and fold.

notes: Keep the cooked tortillas wrapped in a cloth so they stay soft.
Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set.

title: Panamanian-Style Sancocho Chicken and Corn Soup
summary: A comforting chicken soup with corn, sweet potato and coriander, finished with lime.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, add the garlic and cumin for 1 minute, then add the chicken, water and salt.
Simmer for 20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through to 75°C, then lift out, shred and return to the pot.
Add the corn, sweet potato, carrots and celery and simmer for 15 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the coriander and serve with lime wedges.

notes: Stew keeps 3 days in the fridge.
Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C before shredding, and the soup should be reheated until steaming hot.

title: Polish Naleśniki Sweet Cheese Crepes
summary: Thin crepes rolled around sweet ricotta filling and pan-warmed in butter until golden.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, eggs, milk, salt and melted butter into a thin lump-free batter.
Cook thin crepes in a lightly buttered non-stick pan, about 1 minute each side until pale golden, and stack them.
Mix the ricotta, sugar, vanilla, zest and grated apple, spoon along each crepe, roll up and warm in the butter for 2 minutes each side until golden and hot through.

notes: The batter should be the consistency of single cream.
Food safety: cook until the crepes are golden and the filling is hot.

title: Russian Blini with Smoked Salmon and Sour Cream
summary: Small yeast-free pancakes topped with smoked salmon, sour cream and dill.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder, salt, sugar, egg, milk and melted butter into a smooth batter.
Cook spoonfuls in a lightly oiled non-stick pan for 2 minutes each side until puffed and golden.
Top the warm blini with sour cream, smoked salmon and dill and serve with lemon.

notes: Make the blini small so they are easy to eat by hand.
Food safety: smoked salmon should be kept at or below 4°C and not left out for more than 2 hours; avoid in pregnancy.

title: Freezer Breakfast Burritos with Black Beans and Cheese
summary: Scrambled egg, black beans and cheese rolled in tortillas, wrapped and frozen for quick reheating.

steps.text: Fry the onion and capsicum in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, then add the beans and cumin and cook for 2 minutes until warmed through.
Whisk the eggs with the salt, pour into the pan and stir gently for 3 minutes until just set and no liquid egg remains.
Cool the filling for 15 minutes, stir in the cheese, divide among the tortillas, fold in the sides and roll up tightly.
Wrap each burrito in baking paper and freeze for up to 2 months.
To reheat, microwave one from frozen for 2 minutes then turn and heat for 1 to 2 minutes more until steaming hot throughout.

notes: Cool the filling before wrapping or the tortillas go soggy.
Food safety: cook eggs until fully set, cool burritos within 2 hours before freezing and reheat until steaming hot (at least 75°C).

title: Make-Ahead Egg and Spinach Muffin Cups
summary: Baked egg cups with spinach and cheese that keep all week in the fridge.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C and brush a 12-hole muffin tin lightly with the oil.
Whisk the eggs, milk, salt and pepper, then stir in the spinach, onion and cheese.
Pour into the tin holes about three-quarters full and bake for 20 to 22 minutes until puffed and set in the centre.

notes: Cool completely before storing in an airtight box.
Food safety: bake until the centres are firm, refrigerate within 2 hours, eat within 4 days and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Cold-Soaked Oats with Grated Apple, Walnuts and Honey
summary: Creamy cold oats softened in milk and yoghurt with grated apple and a hint of cinnamon.

steps.text: Stir the oats, milk, yoghurt, apple, cinnamon, and honey together in a jar or bowl until combined.
Cover and chill in the fridge overnight until the oats are soft and the mixture is thick.
Stir, loosen with a splash of milk if needed and top with the walnuts.

notes: Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
Use any grated firm fruit in place of the apple.

title: Baked Apple and Walnut Oatmeal Squares
summary: Chewy baked oat squares with apple and cinnamon, cut up for the week ahead.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C and line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Mix the oats, baking powder, cinnamon, salt and half the apple and walnuts in a bowl.
Whisk the eggs, milk, maple syrup, vanilla and butter, pour over the oats and stir, then tip into the tin and top with the remaining apple and walnuts.
Bake for 30 minutes until golden and the centre is firm.

notes: Cut into squares once cool for neat edges.
Food safety: bake until set in the centre, refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 4 days.

title: Mango Coconut Soaked Oat Jars
summary: Coconut-milk soaked oats layered with fresh mango, set in jars overnight.

steps.text: Stir the oats, milk, coconut milk, honey and vanilla together.
Cover and chill for at least 4 hours or overnight until the oats are soft and the mixture is thick.
Mix the mango with the lime juice, then spoon the pudding and mango into jars in layers and finish with the coconut.

notes: Stir once more before layering for a creamy texture.
Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Freezer Wholemeal Pancakes
summary: Fluffy wholemeal pancakes cooked in batches and frozen between sheets of baking paper.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, sugar and salt, then add the eggs, milk, butter and vanilla and stir until just combined with a few small lumps.
Heat a non-stick pan with a little oil over medium heat, pour in about 1/4 cup batter per pancake and cook for 2 minutes until bubbles appear and the edges set.
Flip and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Cool, stack between baking paper and freeze for up to 2 months; reheat in the toaster until hot.

notes: Do not overmix the batter or the pancakes turn tough.
Food safety: cook until no wet batter remains, cool within 2 hours before freezing and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Savoury Corn and Cheddar Breakfast Muffins
summary: Tender cornmeal muffins with sweetcorn, cheddar and chives for a grab-and-go breakfast.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C and line a 6-hole muffin tin.
Stir the flour, cornmeal, baking powder and salt in a bowl, whisk the eggs, milk and oil together and fold into the dry mix until just combined, then fold in the corn, cheese and chives.
Spoon into the cases and bake for 20 to 22 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.

notes: Best warm, split and spread with butter.
Food safety: bake until a skewer comes out clean, and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Cottage Cheese Egg Bake with Chives
summary: A high-protein baked egg and cottage cheese dish, sliced like a frittata.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C and grease a 20cm baking dish with the oil.
Whisk the eggs with the cottage cheese, zucchini, chives, salt and pepper until combined.
Pour into the dish, scatter with the cheddar and bake for 28 to 30 minutes until puffed, golden and set in the centre.

notes: Squeeze the grated zucchini in a cloth first so the bake stays firm.
Food safety: bake until the centre is firm and fully set, then refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: High-Protein Greek Yoghurt Bowl with Nuts and Honey
summary: Thick Greek yoghurt with toasted nuts, seeds and honey for a quick protein-rich start.

steps.text: Toast the almonds and pumpkin seeds in a dry pan over medium heat for 3 minutes until golden and fragrant, then cool briefly.
Dice the apple and spoon the yoghurt into a bowl.
Top with the apple and toasted nuts, drizzle with the honey and dust with cinnamon.

notes: Add a handful of rolled oats for extra fibre.
Swap in any fruit that is in season.

title: Lentil and Egg Breakfast Hash
summary: Crisp potato and lentil hash topped with fried eggs, smoky paprika and fresh parsley.

steps.text: Cook the potato in a wide pan with the oil for 10 minutes, turning, until golden and tender.
Add the onion and paprika and cook for 3 minutes until soft, then stir in the lentils and salt and cook for 3 minutes until hot and crisp in places.
Make two wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the whites are set, then top with the parsley.

notes: Use pre-cooked potato to save time.
Food safety: cook until the egg whites are fully set.

title: Edamame and Avocado Toast with Lime
summary: Smashed edamame and avocado piled on seeded toast with chilli and lime.

steps.text: Simmer the edamame in boiling water for 3 minutes until tender, then drain.
Mash the edamame roughly with the avocado, lime juice and salt, leaving some texture.
Toast the bread until crisp and golden, spread with the mixture and finish with chilli, sesame and spring onion.

notes: Add a poached egg for extra protein.
Eat soon after making as avocado browns.

title: Lentil Salad with Roast Carrots and Tahini
summary: Warm roast carrots on lentils with a lemony tahini dressing and parsley.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C, toss the carrots with the oil, cumin and a pinch of salt and roast for 25 minutes until tender and caramelised.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, water and salt until smooth and pourable.
Toss the lentils with the red onion and parsley, top with the warm carrots and drizzle with the dressing.

notes: Serve warm or at room temperature.
Keeps 3 days in the fridge without the parsley.

title: Chickpea Tabbouleh with Mint and Lemon
summary: Herb-heavy tabbouleh bulked up with chickpeas and a little fine bulgur.

steps.text: Soak the bulgur in 100ml boiling water for 10 minutes until tender, then drain well.
Toss the herbs, tomatoes, cucumber, spring onions and chickpeas together.
Mix in the bulgur, lemon juice, olive oil and salt and toss again until everything is glossy.

notes: Chop the herbs finely with a sharp knife so they stay fresh.
Keeps 2 days in the fridge.

title: Bulgur and Tomato Kisir with Pomegranate Molasses
summary: A Turkish bulgur salad with tomato paste, parsley and tangy pomegranate molasses.

steps.text: Pour the boiling water over the bulgur and tomato paste, stir, cover and let stand for 15 minutes until the grains are tender and the water is absorbed.
Mix in the molasses, oil, lemon juice, chilli and salt.
Fold in the spring onions, herbs and tomatoes and serve in lettuce leaves.

notes: Pomegranate molasses can be replaced with an extra splash of lemon juice.
Keeps 2 days in the fridge.

title: Warm Kale Salad with Roast Sweet Potato and Pepitas
summary: Roast sweet potato on massaged kale with toasted pepitas and a maple mustard dressing.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C, toss the sweet potato with 1 tbsp oil, paprika and a pinch of salt and roast for 25 minutes until tender and caramelised at the edges.
Whisk the remaining oil, lemon juice, mustard, maple and salt together, then massage into the kale for 2 minutes until softened.
Toss the kale with the warm sweet potato, scatter with the pepitas and feta and serve.

notes: Massaging the kale takes away the bitterness.
Keeps 2 days in the fridge.

title: Roast Cauliflower Salad with Tahini and Raisins
summary: Spiced roast cauliflower with sweet raisins, almonds and herbs in a garlicky tahini drizzle.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 230°C, toss the cauliflower with the oil, cumin, coriander and half the salt and roast for 25 minutes until deep golden at the edges and tender.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, water and remaining salt until smooth.
Toss the warm cauliflower with the raisins, almonds and parsley and drizzle with the dressing.

notes: Roast on a single layer so the florets brown rather than steam.
Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Roast Carrot Salad with Harissa Yoghurt and Pistachios
summary: Sweet roast carrots on cooling harissa yoghurt with mint and crushed pistachios.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C, toss the carrots with the oil, cumin and a pinch of salt and roast for 30 minutes until tender and charred at the edges.
Mix the yoghurt with the harissa, lemon juice and remaining salt.
Spread the yoghurt on a platter, top with the warm carrots, drizzle with the honey and scatter with pistachios and mint.

notes: Use less harissa for a milder yoghurt.
Keeps 2 days in the fridge.

title: Spring Pea and Edamame Salad with Mint and Feta
summary: A bright, fresh salad of peas, edamame and cucumber with mint, lemon and feta.

steps.text: Simmer the peas and edamame in boiling water for 3 minutes until tender and bright green, then drain and cool in cold water.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice, honey and salt together.
Toss the peas, edamame, cucumber and spring onions with the dressing, then fold in the mint and feta.

notes: Dress just before serving to keep the colour bright.
Keeps 1 day in the fridge.

title: Winter Red Cabbage and Pear Slaw
summary: Crunchy red cabbage with pear, walnuts and a light cider mustard dressing.

steps.text: Whisk the oil, vinegar, mustard, honey and salt until emulsified.
Toss the cabbage, pears, carrot and parsley with the dressing.
Fold through the walnuts and let stand for 10 minutes before serving so the cabbage softens slightly.

notes: Add the pear just before serving so it stays crisp and pale.
Keeps 2 days in the fridge without the walnuts.

title: Green Beans Almondine with Lemon
summary: Crisp-tender green beans tossed with butter, toasted almonds and lemon zest.

steps.text: Boil the beans in salted water for 4 minutes until bright green and just tender, then drain.
Melt the butter in a pan and cook the almonds for 2 minutes until golden, then add the garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Toss the beans in the pan with the lemon zest, juice and salt until glossy and hot.

notes: Do not let the almonds burn once they start to colour.
Serve with fish or roast chicken.

title: Indian Aloo Jeera Cumin Potatoes
summary: Quick pan-cooked potatoes with cumin seeds, turmeric and coriander.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes for 8 minutes until just tender and drain well.
Heat the oil in a wide pan, add the cumin seeds for 30 seconds until sizzling, then add the turmeric, chilli and ground coriander.
Add the potatoes and salt and cook for 8 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp at the edges.
Finish with lemon juice and fresh coriander.

notes: Drain the potatoes very well so they fry rather than steam.
Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Indian Jeera Rice with Whole Spices
summary: Fluffy basmati scented with cumin seeds, bay leaf and cardamom.

steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then drain.
Heat the ghee in a pot and fry the cumin, bay leaf and cardamom for 1 minute until sizzling and fragrant.
Add the rice, salt and water, bring to the boil, cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes until all the water is absorbed.
Rest, covered, for 5 minutes and fluff with a fork.

notes: Do not lift the lid while the rice cooks.
Food safety: cool leftover rice within 1 hour and refrigerate; eat within 1 day and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Hasselback Potatoes with Garlic and Thyme
summary: Fan-cut potatoes roasted until crisp at the edges and soft in the middle, with garlic and thyme.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C. Cut thin slits across each potato about 3mm apart, stopping before the base, using two chopsticks as guides.
Brush with the oil, tuck garlic slices into some slits and sprinkle with thyme, salt and pepper.
Roast for 50 to 55 minutes, basting once, until the edges are crisp and golden and the centres are soft when pierced.

notes: Chopsticks either side of the potato stop the knife cutting all the way through.
Serve straight away while crisp.

title: Sweet Potato Wedges with Smoked Paprika and Lime
summary: Crisp roast sweet potato wedges with smoked paprika, finished with lime and a cooling yoghurt dip.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C and toss the wedges with the oil, paprika, garlic powder and salt.
Roast on a lined tray, turning once, for 30 to 35 minutes until crisp at the edges and tender inside.
Stir the lime juice and coriander into the yoghurt and serve alongside.

notes: Leave space between the wedges so they crisp.
Eat the same day for best crunch.

title: Peruvian Papa a la Huancaina with Boiled Egg
summary: Sliced potatoes under a creamy cheese and chilli sauce, a Peruvian classic.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes for 18 to 20 minutes until tender, and boil the eggs for 9 minutes until firm, then cool both.
Blend the feta, evaporated milk, lime juice, chilli, bread, oil and salt until smooth and creamy.
Peel and slice the potatoes, arrange on lettuce, spoon over the sauce and top with halved eggs and olives.

notes: The sauce thickens as it chills; thin with a splash of milk.
Food safety: boil eggs until firm and eat within 1 day if keeping.

title: Pumpkin and Sweet Potato Congee
summary: Silky rice porridge simmered with pumpkin and sweet potato, topped with spring onion and sesame.

steps.text: Rinse the rice, then simmer it in the water with the ginger and salt for 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the grains burst and the porridge is thick.
Add the pumpkin and sweet potato and simmer for 12 to 15 minutes until completely tender and starting to fall apart.
Stir well, loosen with hot water if needed and top with soy, sesame oil, spring onion and sesame seeds.

notes: Stir often near the end so the base does not catch.
Congee thickens as it cools; add water when reheating until steaming hot.

title: Mushroom and Spring Onion Congee
summary: Savoury rice porridge with browned mushrooms, ginger and a drizzle of sesame oil.

steps.text: Rinse the rice, then simmer it in the water with the ginger and salt for 35 minutes, stirring now and then, until creamy and thick.
Fry the mushrooms in the oil in a hot pan for 6 minutes until golden, add the garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant and splash in the soy.
