Stir the mushrooms into the congee, then serve topped with spring onion, sesame oil and white pepper.

notes: Cook the mushrooms in batches so they brown rather than steam.
Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat until steaming hot.

title: Chilled Carrot and Ginger Soup
summary: A smooth, bright carrot soup with fresh ginger and orange, served cold with yoghurt.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, add the ginger and cumin for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the carrots and stock, cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the carrots are very tender.
Blend until completely smooth, stir in the orange juice and salt, then chill for at least 3 hours.
Serve topped with yoghurt and chives.

notes: Thin with cold water if the soup thickens as it chills.
Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Chilled Buttermilk and Herb Soup
summary: A cooling no-cook soup of buttermilk, cucumber and fresh herbs.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes until firm, then cool in cold water and peel.
Whisk the buttermilk, yoghurt, cucumber, garlic, herbs, lemon juice, salt and pepper together.
Chill for 1 hour until cold, then ladle into bowls and top with radish and egg.

notes: Taste before serving and add salt if needed as chilling dulls flavour.
Food safety: boil eggs until firm and keep the soup refrigerated, eating within 2 days.

title: Beef Pho Broth with Rice Noodles
summary: Aromatic star anise and ginger beef broth poured over rice noodles and thin sliced beef.

steps.text: Char the onion and ginger in a dry pan for 5 minutes until blackened in spots.
Simmer the stock with the onion, ginger, star anise, cinnamon, cloves, fish sauce and sugar for 30 minutes until deeply fragrant, then strain.
Cook the noodles in boiling water for 4 minutes until tender, drain and divide among bowls.
Top with the raw beef, ladle over the boiling broth until the beef changes colour and is cooked through, then add sprouts, herbs, lime and chilli.

notes: The broth must be bubbling hot when it hits the beef.
Food safety: thin beef must be cooked in the boiling broth to at least 63°C (no pink remains); keep leftover broth refrigerated and use within 3 days.

title: Clear Chicken Broth with Vegetables
summary: A simple, clear chicken soup with shredded chicken, carrot, celery and thyme.

steps.text: Place the chicken, water, onion, bay leaf, thyme and salt in a pot and bring to a gentle simmer, skimming off any foam until the surface is clear.
Simmer gently for 25 minutes until the chicken reaches 75°C and is cooked through, then lift out, shred and discard the onion, bay leaf and thyme.
Add the carrots and celery to the broth and simmer for 15 minutes until tender.
Return the chicken, add the pepper and parsley and serve hot.

notes: Keep the broth at a gentle bubble so it stays clear.
Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C; cool leftovers within 2 hours and use within 3 days.

title: Mushroom Ginger Broth with Rice Noodles and Greens
summary: A light, savoury mushroom and ginger broth with soft tofu, noodles and bok choy.

steps.text: Simmer the stock with the mushrooms, ginger, soy and vinegar for 10 minutes until the mushrooms are tender.
Cook the noodles in boiling water for 4 minutes until soft, then drain and divide between bowls.
Add the bok choy and tofu to the broth and cook for 2 minutes until the bok choy is tender and the tofu is hot.
Ladle over the noodles and finish with spring onion and sesame oil.

notes: Add the tofu gently so it stays in cubes.
Keeps 2 days in the fridge without the noodles.

title: Silverbeet and Chickpea Soup with Lemon
summary: A wholesome chickpea soup with silverbeet and lemon, with a little garlic and cumin.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the oil for 6 minutes until golden, then add the garlic and cumin for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the chickpeas and stock and simmer for 12 minutes until the chickpeas are soft, mashing a few against the pot.
Stir in the silverbeet and cook for 4 minutes until wilted and tender, then add the lemon juice, salt and pepper.

notes: Mash some chickpeas to thicken the soup naturally.
Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes well.

title: Cream of Celery Soup with Thyme
summary: A smooth, gently flavoured celery soup with potato, thyme and a swirl of cream.

steps.text: Cook the onion and celery in the butter for 10 minutes until soft without colour.
Add the potato, stock and thyme and simmer for 20 minutes until the potato is falling apart.
Remove the thyme, blend until smooth, then stir in the cream, salt and pepper and heat gently until hot.

notes: Strain the soup for a very smooth finish.
Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Leek and Pearl Barley Broth
summary: A rustic broth of leek, carrot and pearl barley with parsley.

steps.text: Soften the leeks, carrots and celery in the oil for 8 minutes until the leek is soft.
Add the barley, stock and bay leaves and simmer for 35 to 40 minutes until the barley is plump and tender.
Remove the bay leaves, season and stir in the parsley.

notes: The barley absorbs liquid, so add water when reheating.
Keeps 4 days in the fridge.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Hearty Minestrone with Cannellini Beans
summary: A thick vegetable minestrone with beans, small pasta and basil.

steps.text: Cook the onion, carrot, celery and garlic in the oil for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes and stock and simmer for 10 minutes, then stir in the zucchini, cannellini beans, green beans and pasta.
Simmer for 10 to 12 minutes until the pasta is tender, then season and finish with basil.

notes: Add extra stock if the pasta soaks up too much liquid.
Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Chilled Beetroot Soup with Yoghurt and Dill
summary: A vivid pink chilled beetroot soup with yoghurt, cucumber and dill.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add the beetroot and stock and simmer for 25 minutes until the beetroot is very tender.
Blend until smooth, stir in the vinegar, sugar and salt and chill for 3 hours.
Whisk in half the yoghurt, ladle into bowls and top with cucumber, dill and the remaining yoghurt.

notes: Wear gloves or an apron as beetroot stains.
Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Pumpkin Laksa with Rice Noodles and Tofu
summary: A creamy coconut laksa with sweet pumpkin, tofu puffs and rice noodles.

steps.text: Fry the laksa paste in the oil for 2 minutes until fragrant, then add the pumpkin, stock and coconut milk.
Simmer for 15 minutes until the pumpkin is tender, then add the tofu and heat for 3 minutes until hot.
Soak the vermicelli in boiling water for 5 minutes until soft, drain and divide into bowls.
Season the soup with lime juice and soy, ladle over the noodles and top with sprouts and coriander.

notes: Use less paste for a milder soup.
Keeps 2 days in the fridge without the noodles.

title: Zucchini Lemon Orzo Soup
summary: A light, lemony orzo soup with zucchini and dill.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, add the garlic and zucchini for 3 minutes until lightly coloured.
Add the stock and bring to the boil, stir in the orzo and simmer for 9 minutes until the pasta is tender.
Stir in the lemon juice, zest, dill and salt and serve topped with feta.

notes: Orzo keeps absorbing liquid, so thin leftovers with stock.
Keeps 2 days in the fridge.

title: Japanese Takikomi Gohan Mixed Vegetable Rice
summary: Rice cooked with mushrooms, carrot and edamame in a light soy broth.

steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then place in a pot with the water, soy, vinegar and ginger.
Scatter the mushrooms and carrot over the top without stirring, cover, bring to the boil and cook on low for 15 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Add the edamame, cover and rest off the heat for 10 minutes until the rice is tender, then fold through the sesame oil and seeds.

notes: Do not stir while cooking so the rice steams evenly.
Food safety: cool leftover rice within 1 hour and refrigerate; use within 1 day.

title: Israeli Couscous with Roast Vegetables and Lemon
summary: Pearl couscous tossed with roast zucchini, capsicum and red onion in a lemon herb dressing.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C, toss the vegetables with 1 tbsp oil and roast for 25 minutes until tender and charred at the edges.
Cook the couscous in the boiling water for 8 minutes until tender, drain any excess and cool slightly.
Toss with the roast vegetables, remaining oil, lemon juice, salt, parsley and toasted pine nuts until evenly coated.

notes: Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes until golden.
Eat warm or at room temperature.

title: Lebanese Batata Harra Spiced Potatoes
summary: Crispy cubed potatoes tossed with garlic, chilli and coriander.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes for 8 minutes until just tender, drain well and let the steam rise.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and fry the potatoes for 12 to 15 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp.
Add the garlic, chilli, ground coriander and salt for 1 minute until fragrant, then toss with fresh coriander and lemon juice.

notes: Let the potatoes steam-dry before frying for extra crispness.
Eat the same day.

title: Quinoa Breakfast Bowl with Poached Egg and Spinach
summary: Warm quinoa with wilted spinach, a poached egg and a squeeze of lemon.

steps.text: Rinse the quinoa, then simmer in the water for 15 minutes until tender and the germ has spiralled out, then drain well.
Wilt the spinach in the oil for 1 minute until soft and stir through the quinoa with the salt and lemon.
Poach the eggs in barely simmering water with the vinegar for 3 minutes until the whites are set, then drain.
Top the bowls with avocado, eggs and chilli flakes.

notes: Rinse quinoa well to remove any bitterness.

Food safety: poach eggs until the whites are fully set. Use fresh, uncracked eggs; for pregnant women, older people, young children and anyone with low immunity, cook the eggs until the yolks are firm.

title: Egg White Omelette with Mushrooms and Herbs
summary: A light, high-protein omelette with mushrooms, spinach and herbs.

steps.text: Fry the mushrooms in the oil for 5 minutes until golden, add the spinach for 30 seconds until wilted, then tip out.
Whisk the egg whites with the salt, pepper and herbs, pour into the same pan and cook gently for 2 to 3 minutes until nearly set.
Spoon the mushrooms over half, fold and cook for 1 minute until the egg is fully set.

notes: Use a non-stick pan so the whites slide out easily.
Food safety: cook until the egg is firm throughout.

title: Autumn Apple and Celery Salad with Walnuts
summary: A crisp, juicy salad of apple, celery and walnuts in a light mustard dressing.

steps.text: Whisk the oil, lemon juice, mustard, honey and salt together.
Toss the apple and celery with the dressing right away until every slice is coated, so the apple stays pale.
Fold in the walnuts, parsley and rocket and serve immediately.

notes: Slice the apple just before assembling.
Best eaten the same day.

title: Charred Cabbage Wedges with Miso Butter
summary: Cabbage wedges roasted until charred and tender, glazed with garlicky miso butter.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 230°C, brush the cabbage with the oil and roast cut side down for 20 to 25 minutes until charred at the edges and tender in the centre.
Mash the butter with the miso, garlic and honey.
Dot the hot wedges with the miso butter until it melts, then scatter with sesame and spring onion.

notes: Do not move the wedges while roasting so they char.
Miso butter keeps 1 week in the fridge.

title: Braised Leeks with Mustard Vinaigrette
summary: Tender braised leeks dressed warm in a sharp mustard vinaigrette with parsley.

steps.text: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes until firm, cool, peel and chop.
Simmer the leeks in the stock, covered, for 15 to 20 minutes until completely tender, then drain well.
Whisk the oil, mustard, vinegar, honey and salt, pour over the warm leeks and top with parsley and egg.

notes: Wash the leeks thoroughly between the layers.
Food safety: boil eggs until firm and eat within 2 days.

title: Vietnamese Cucumber Pickle Salad
summary: Crunchy cucumber with sweet and sour rice vinegar, chilli and herbs.

steps.text: Stir the vinegar, sugar and salt together until the sugar dissolves.
Toss the cucumber and carrot with the dressing and chilli and leave for 10 minutes to lightly pickle.
Top with mint and peanuts and serve cold.

notes: Salting the cucumber first makes it crunchier.
Keeps 2 days in the fridge.

title: Ricotta Pancakes with Orange Zest and Honey
summary: Light, soft pancakes made with ricotta and orange zest, served with honey and yoghurt.

steps.text: Whisk the ricotta, egg yolks, milk, flour, baking powder, sugar, zest and salt into a thick batter.
Whisk the egg whites to soft peaks and fold gently through the batter until just combined.
Melt a little butter in a non-stick pan, spoon in the batter and cook for 2 to 3 minutes each side over medium heat until golden and cooked through.
Serve warm with honey and yoghurt.

notes: Keep the heat moderate so the middle cooks before the outside browns.
Food safety: cook until no wet batter remains in the centre.

title: Savoury Oat Pancakes with Cottage Cheese and Chives
summary: High-protein oat pancakes with cottage cheese, chives and a hint of black pepper.

steps.text: Blend the oats, cottage cheese, eggs, baking powder, salt and pepper until fairly smooth, then stir in the chives.
Heat the oil in a non-stick pan and spoon in the batter, cooking for 3 minutes until set at the edges and golden underneath.
Flip and cook for 2 minutes until golden and cooked through, then serve with sliced tomato.

notes: Let the batter stand for 5 minutes so the oats soften.
Food safety: cook until the pancakes are firm in the centre.

title: Greek Yoghurt Pancakes with Maple Pears
summary: Tender Greek yoghurt pancakes served with warm maple-spiced pears.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder, salt and sugar, then add the yoghurt, eggs and milk and stir into a thick batter.
Warm the butter, pears, maple and cinnamon in a small pan for 6 minutes until the pears are tender and glazed.
Cook spoonfuls of batter in a lightly oiled pan for 2 minutes each side until golden and cooked through.
Serve the pancakes with the pears and syrup.

notes: Do not overmix, or the pancakes turn chewy.
Food safety: cook until the batter is set through.

title: Armenian Eggs with Tomato and Basil
summary: Soft scrambled eggs in a juicy tomato and basil base, eaten with warm bread.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes until golden, then add the tomatoes, paprika and salt and cook for 7 minutes until jammy.
Break the eggs into the pan and stir gently for 2 to 3 minutes until just set.
Fold through the basil, toast the bread until golden and serve together.

notes: Cook the tomatoes until the liquid has mostly evaporated.
Food safety: cook until the eggs are fully set with no liquid egg.

title: Iranian Nargesi Spinach Eggs
summary: Garlicky wilted spinach with eggs baked on top, a favourite Persian breakfast.

steps.text: Cook the onion in the oil for 6 minutes until golden, then add the garlic and turmeric for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the spinach in handfuls and cook for 3 minutes until wilted and most liquid has evaporated, then season.
Make four wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 4 to 5 minutes until the whites are set, then finish with lemon juice.

notes: Press the spinach well so it does not flood the eggs.
Food safety: cook until the whites are fully set.

title: Syrian-Style Foul with Chickpeas Cumin and Lemon
summary: Warm mashed chickpeas with garlic, lemon, cumin and olive oil, scooped up with bread.

steps.text: Warm the chickpeas with the water, garlic, cumin and salt for 8 minutes until hot and very soft.
Mash roughly with a fork until creamy but still chunky, then stir in the lemon juice and half the oil.
Top with tomato, parsley and the remaining oil and serve with warmed pita.

notes: Add a splash more water if the mash is too thick.
Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Zucchini and Cheddar Breakfast Fritters with Poached Egg
summary: Crisp zucchini and cheddar fritters topped with a soft poached egg and chives.

steps.text: Squeeze the grated zucchini in a clean cloth until quite dry, then mix with the cheddar, spring onions, flour, egg, salt and pepper.
Cook spoonfuls in the oil in a non-stick pan for 3 minutes each side until deep golden and cooked through.
Poach the two eggs in barely simmering water with the vinegar for 3 minutes until the whites are set, then top the fritters.

notes: Squeezing the zucchini is the secret to crisp fritters.
Food safety: cook the fritters through and poach the eggs until the whites are fully set.

title: Bengali Khichuri Rice and Lentil Comfort Bowl
summary: A soft, golden rice and lentil dish with vegetables and gentle spices, ideal on a cold night.

steps.text: Rinse the rice and lentils together until the water runs clear.
Heat the ghee, fry the cumin and ginger for 1 minute until fragrant, then add the turmeric, rice, lentils and vegetables and stir for 1 minute.
Add the water and salt, bring to the boil, cover and simmer for 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the rice and lentils are soft and porridge-like.
Stir in the lemon juice before serving.

notes: Add more water for a looser, soupier khichuri.
Food safety: cool leftover rice within 1 hour and refrigerate; eat within 1 day.

title: Pakistani Daal Chawal with Tadka
summary: Yellow lentils simmered soft and finished with a sizzling garlic and cumin tadka, served with rice.

steps.text: Simmer the lentils, water, turmeric, tomato and salt for 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until completely soft.
Cook the rice in boiling water for 11 minutes until tender, then drain.
Heat the ghee, fry the cumin and garlic for 2 minutes until golden, add the chilli and pour over the lentils.
Serve the lentils over the rice with coriander.

notes: Do not let the garlic go dark or it turns bitter.
Food safety: cool leftover rice within 1 hour and refrigerate.

title: Afghan Shorwa Lamb and Chickpea Soup
summary: A tomato-based lamb and chickpea soup with potato and dried coriander, served with bread.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil for 6 minutes until coloured, then add the onion for 4 minutes until soft, followed by the garlic, spices and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the water and salt, cover and simmer for 40 minutes until the lamb is tender.
Add the potatoes and chickpeas and simmer for 15 minutes until the potatoes are soft.
Stir in the lemon juice and fresh coriander.

notes: Skim the surface for a clear broth.
Food safety: lamb pieces must be cooked until tender and reach at least 63°C inside; cool within 2 hours.

title: Uzbek Mastava Rice and Beef Soup
summary: A hearty soup of rice, beef mince and vegetables in a tomato broth, finished with dill.

steps.text: Brown the beef in the oil for 5 minutes until no pink remains, add the onion, carrots and capsicum for 5 minutes until soft, then stir in the tomato paste.
Add the water, rice, potatoes, salt and pepper, bring to the boil and simmer for 25 minutes until the rice and potatoes are tender.
Stir in the dill and serve hot.

notes: The rice thickens the soup as it stands.
Food safety: beef mince must reach 75°C and no pink remains; cool within 2 hours.

title: Mongolian-Style Tsuivan Noodle Stir Fry with Beef
summary: Chewy noodles stir-fried with beef, cabbage and carrot in a savoury soy sauce.

steps.text: Cook the noodles in boiling water for 5 minutes until tender, then drain.
Stir-fry the beef in half the oil over high heat for 3 minutes until browned and no pink remains, then remove.
Stir-fry the onion, carrots and cabbage in the remaining oil for 6 minutes until tender-crisp, add the garlic for 30 seconds, then return the beef.
Toss in the noodles, soy sauce, sugar and pepper for 3 minutes until heated through and coated.

notes: Thin slices cook quickly, so do not overcook the beef.
Food safety: beef must be cooked until no pink remains and reach at least 63°C inside.

title: Libyan Shorba Lamb Orzo Soup
summary: A spiced tomato lamb soup with chickpeas and orzo, finished with lemon and mint.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil for 5 minutes until coloured, add the onion for 4 minutes until soft, then stir in the garlic, spices and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the water, salt and chickpeas, cover and simmer for 35 minutes until the lamb is tender.
Stir in the orzo and simmer for 9 minutes until tender, then add the lemon juice and mint.

notes: Add extra water as the orzo absorbs liquid.
Food safety: lamb must be cooked until tender and reach at least 63°C inside; cool within 2 hours.

title: Chilean-Style Cazuela Chicken Pumpkin and Corn Soup
summary: A clear chicken soup with a big piece of pumpkin, potato, corn and rice, finished with coriander.

steps.text: Simmer the chicken, onion, garlic, salt and water for 15 minutes until the chicken is about half cooked.
Add the potatoes, pumpkin and corn and simmer for 15 minutes, then stir in the rice and beans.
Simmer for 15 to 18 minutes more until the rice is tender, the vegetables are soft and the chicken reaches 75°C.
Serve each bowl with a piece of chicken and sprinkle with coriander.

notes: Keep the vegetables in large pieces so they hold their shape.
Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C; cool leftovers within 2 hours and use within 3 days.

title: Nepali Jhol Dal Thin Lentil Soup with Cumin
summary: A thin, tangy yellow lentil soup finished with a sizzling garlic and cumin tarka.

steps.text: Simmer the lentils, water, turmeric, tomato and salt for 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until completely soft and smooth.
Heat the oil, fry the cumin, garlic and chilli for 1 to 2 minutes until golden and fragrant.
Pour the tarka into the lentils with the coriander and lemon juice and stir well.

notes: Whisk the lentils for a smoother soup.
Serve with rice.

title: Zimbabwean-Style Sadza with Silverbeet and Tomato
summary: Soft white cornmeal porridge served with silverbeet cooked with tomato and onion.

steps.text: Whisk the cornmeal into 700ml of the water, then bring the remaining water to the boil, whisk it in with half the salt and cook for 15 minutes, stirring, until thick and pulling from the sides.
Cook the onion in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, add the garlic and tomatoes for 5 minutes until thick, then add the silverbeet and remaining salt.
Cook the greens for 6 minutes until tender and shape the sadza into balls to serve with the greens.

notes: Stir hard with a wooden spoon to keep the sadza smooth.
Eat hot as it firms up when cold.

title: Azerbaijani Dovga Yoghurt and Herb Soup with Chickpeas
summary: A warm, tangy Azerbaijani-style soup of yoghurt, rice, chickpeas and plenty of fresh herbs.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large saucepan and cook the onion over medium heat for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the rice and stock, bring to a simmer and cook for 12 minutes until the rice is tender, then add the chickpeas.

Whisk the yoghurt, egg and flour in a bowl, then whisk in a ladle of hot soup. Stir this back into the pan over low heat for 5 minutes until slightly thickened and steaming; do not let it boil hard or it may split.
Stir in the spinach, dill, coriander, mint and salt and cook for 2 minutes until the greens are just wilted.

notes: Whisking the yoghurt with flour and egg first helps it stay smooth in the hot pot.
Food safety: heat the soup until steaming hot throughout so the egg is cooked.

title: Madagascan Romazava Greens and Beef Broth
summary: A brothy Madagascan-style stew of tender beef, ginger, tomato and silky greens, served with rice.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the beef in two batches over high heat for 5 minutes until coloured all over.
Add the onion, garlic and ginger and cook for 3 minutes until fragrant, then stir in the tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes until they break down.
Add the water, salt and pepper, cover and simmer gently for 45 minutes until the beef is tender.
Stir in the bok choy and spinach and cook for 4 minutes until the greens are soft. Serve in bowls with steamed rice.

notes: Brown the beef well for a deeper broth.
Food safety: cook the beef until tender and at least 75°C inside, and the broth is steaming hot; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Colombian Lentil and Pumpkin Soup with Coriander and Lime
summary: A hearty lentil soup with pumpkin, tomato and cumin, finished with coriander and lime.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion and carrot over medium heat for 6 minutes until soft.
Stir in the garlic and cumin for 1 minute until fragrant, then add the lentils, pumpkin, tomatoes and stock.
Bring to a simmer and cook for 25 minutes until the lentils and pumpkin are tender.
Season with the salt and lime juice, scatter with coriander and serve hot.

notes: Mash a few spoonfuls against the side of the pot for a thicker soup.
Rinse the lentils well before cooking.

title: Pakistani Haleem-Style Lentil and Beef Porridge
summary: A thick, spiced porridge of beef, lentils and barley, cooked slowly and topped with ginger, lemon and coriander.

steps.text: Melt the ghee in a heavy pot and cook the onion over medium heat for 10 minutes until deep golden.
Add the beef, garlic, ginger, garam masala and turmeric and cook for 5 minutes until the beef is browned.
Add the lentils, barley, water and salt, cover and simmer gently, stirring now and then, for 75 minutes until the beef is falling apart and the porridge is thick.
Beat the mixture with a wooden spoon for 2 minutes until the meat breaks into strands, then serve with lemon and coriander.

notes: Add a splash of hot water if it thickens too much.
Food safety: cook the beef until very tender and at least 75°C inside, and the porridge is steaming hot; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until piping hot.

title: Hungarian Tarhonya-Style Browned Orzo with Onion and Paprika
summary: Orzo toasted until nutty, then simmered with onion and sweet paprika as a Hungarian-style side.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a deep frying pan and cook the onion over medium heat for 6 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the orzo and stir for 4 minutes until lightly browned and nutty, then stir in the paprika for 30 seconds.
Pour in the hot stock and salt, cover and simmer on low for 10 minutes until the orzo is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Fluff with a fork, scatter with parsley and serve.

notes: Take care not to burn the paprika; it turns bitter if scorched.
Delicious beside roast chicken or grilled sausages.

title: Yemeni Maraq Lamb Soup with Fresh Herbs
summary: A clear, gently spiced Yemeni-style lamb soup with potato, tomato and a handful of fresh herbs.

steps.text: Place the lamb, onion, garlic, cumin, turmeric, pepper and water in a large pot and bring to a simmer, skimming the surface until clear.
Cover and cook gently for 45 minutes until the lamb is tender.
Add the potatoes, tomatoes and salt and simmer for 20 minutes until the potato is soft.
Scatter with coriander and serve with lemon wedges.

notes: Skim well for a clean-tasting broth.
Food safety: cook the lamb until very tender and at least 75°C inside, and the soup is steaming hot; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Israeli Hamin-Style Barley and Bean Stew
summary: A slow-simmered stew of barley, beans, potato and sweet paprika, rich enough to serve as a main.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a heavy pot and cook the onion for 8 minutes over medium heat until golden.
Add the garlic, paprika and cumin and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the barley, beans, potato, carrot, stock, honey and salt, cover and simmer on low for 90 minutes until the barley is soft and the stew is thick.
Stir in the parsley and serve hot.

notes: Stir now and then so the barley does not catch on the base.
It tastes even better the next day.

title: Sri Lankan Brinjal Moju Pickled Eggplant
summary: Fried eggplant folded through a sweet-and-sour onion pickle, served as a side with rice and curries.

steps.text: Heat half the oil in a large frying pan and fry the eggplant in two batches for 8 minutes until golden and soft, then set aside.
Add the remaining oil, onion, garlic and ginger and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the mustard, turmeric and chilli, then add the vinegar, sugar and salt and simmer for 3 minutes until syrupy.
Fold the eggplant through until coated and cook for 2 minutes until heated through. Cool and serve.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for up to 5 days and improves with time.
Dry the eggplant well before frying to keep the oil from spitting.

title: Indian Upma with Vegetables and Mustard Seeds
summary: Savoury semolina porridge cooked with vegetables, mustard seeds and lemon, a quick south Indian breakfast.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a deep pan over medium heat and add the mustard seeds until they pop.
Add the onion, ginger and carrot and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the semolina and stir for 3 minutes until lightly toasted, then pour in the hot water and salt, add the peas and stir constantly for 3 minutes until thick and the semolina is cooked.
Stir through the lemon juice and coriander and serve at once.

notes: Add the water slowly while stirring to avoid lumps.
Top with roasted peanuts for crunch.

title: Indian Vegetable Dalia Cracked Wheat Porridge
summary: A warming porridge of cracked wheat simmered with vegetables, cumin and turmeric.

steps.text: Melt the ghee in a saucepan and add the cumin seeds until they sizzle.
Add the onion and carrot and cook for 5 minutes until softened, then stir in the turmeric and bulgur for 2 minutes.
Pour in the water and salt, cover and simmer on low for 15 minutes until the bulgur is tender and the water is absorbed.
Fluff with a fork, stir through the peas and coriander for 2 minutes until the peas are hot, and serve with yoghurt.

notes: A spoon of lemon pickle on top is a classic addition.
Leftovers reheat well with a splash of water.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Pakistani Breakfast Chickpea Curry with Flatbread
summary: A spiced tomato chickpea curry, eaten with warm flatbread, from the Pakistani breakfast table.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a pan and cook the onion for 6 minutes over medium heat until golden.
Add the garlic, ginger and spices and stir for 1 minute until fragrant, then add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until thick.
Stir in the chickpeas, water and salt and simmer for 10 minutes until saucy.
Scatter with coriander and serve with warm flatbread.

notes: Mash a few chickpeas to thicken the sauce.
Warm the flatbreads in a dry pan for a minute each side.

title: Maldivian Mas Huni Tuna and Coconut Breakfast
summary: Canned tuna tossed with coconut, onion, lime and chilli, a fast Maldivian-style breakfast eaten with flatbread.

items.raw: 2 x 95g cans tuna in springwater, drained (190g)

steps.text: Mix the tuna, coconut, onion, chilli, lime juice and salt in a bowl, breaking the tuna into flakes with a fork.
Warm the flatbreads in a dry pan for 1 minute each side until soft and lightly blistered.
Spoon the tuna mixture onto the flatbreads and serve straight away.

notes: Soak the desiccated coconut in a splash of warm water for 5 minutes for a softer texture.
Food safety: use tuna from a sealed, in-date can and eat within 2 days of opening if refrigerated.

title: Iraqi Eggs with Tomato and Sumac
summary: Eggs gently cooked in a garlicky tomato base with sumac and parsley, served with bread.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a frying pan and cook the onion for 5 minutes over medium heat until soft.
Add the garlic, tomatoes, sumac, cumin and salt and simmer for 6 minutes until the tomatoes collapse into a sauce.
Make four wells in the sauce, crack in the eggs, cover and cook gently for 4 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks are as firm as you like.
Scatter with parsley and serve with bread.

notes: Keep the heat low so the eggs cook evenly.
Food safety: cook eggs until the whites are fully set and the yolks thickened; avoid runny eggs for young children, pregnant women and older adults.

title: Egyptian Ta'ameya-Style Chickpea Falafel with Dill
summary: Baked herb-packed chickpea patties with dill, coriander and sesame, served with tahini and salad.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200C and line a tray with baking paper.
Blitz the chickpeas, onion, garlic, herbs, spices, flour, baking powder and salt in a food processor until a rough, sticky mixture forms.
Shape into 12 patties, press into the sesame seeds, place on the tray and brush with oil.
Bake for 25 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp. Whisk the tahini with the lemon juice and a little water and drizzle over to serve.

notes: Pat the chickpeas dry well so the patties hold together.
Serve with tomato, cucumber and flatbread.

title: Somali Canjeero Pancake with Honey and Sesame Oil
summary: Thin, spongy Somali-style pancakes drizzled with honey and a little sesame oil.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, semolina, yeast, sugar, salt and warm water into a smooth thin batter and rest it for 20 minutes until bubbly.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat and lightly oil it.
Pour in a ladle of batter and cook for 2 minutes until the top is covered in holes and dry, without turning.
Repeat with the rest of the batter, drizzle with honey and sesame oil and serve warm.

notes: Cook on one side only so the top stays spongy.
Stack the pancakes under a clean tea towel to keep them soft.

title: Tanzanian Chapati Rolls with Beans
summary: Soft pan-cooked chapati rolled around a spiced tomato bean filling.

steps.text: Mix the flour, salt, 1 tbsp oil and the water into a soft dough, knead for 5 minutes until smooth, then divide into 4 balls.
Heat the remaining oil in a pan and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic and curry powder for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and beans and simmer for 8 minutes until thick, then stir in the coriander.
Roll each ball thin and cook in a dry hot pan for 2 minutes per side until golden spotted and cooked through. Spoon in the beans and roll up.

notes: Rest the dough for 15 minutes for softer chapati.
Serve with a little chilli sauce.

title: Senegalese Lakh Yoghurt and Couscous Pudding
summary: Couscous folded through creamy vanilla yoghurt, a cool Senegalese-style breakfast pudding.

steps.text: Place the couscous and butter in a bowl, pour over the boiling water, cover and stand for 5 minutes until the water is absorbed, then fluff with a fork.
Cool for 10 minutes, then fold in the yoghurt, sugar, vanilla, nutmeg and sultanas until creamy.
Chill for 30 minutes and serve cold in bowls.

notes: Add a little milk if you prefer a looser pudding.
Top with chopped nuts for crunch.

title: Guyanese Roti with Chana
summary: Soft pan-cooked roti with a mild curried chickpea filling.

steps.text: Mix the flour, baking powder, salt, oil and warm water into a soft dough, knead for 5 minutes until smooth, then rest for 20 minutes and divide into 4 balls.
Cook the onion in a little oil for 5 minutes until soft, add the garlic and curry powder for 1 minute until fragrant, then add the chickpeas, potato and water.
Simmer for 15 minutes until the potato is tender and the curry is thick, then mash lightly and stir in the coriander.
Roll each ball thin and cook in a dry pan for 2 minutes each side until puffed and flecked. Serve the chana with the roti.

notes: Brush the hot roti with a little oil for softness.
Keep the cooked roti wrapped in a tea towel.

title: Bajan Cou Cou with Steamed Greens
summary: A smooth cornmeal and okra mash, served with lightly steamed greens.

steps.text: Simmer the okra in the water and salt for 8 minutes until tender, then lift out and set aside, keeping the water.
Mix the cornmeal with 250ml cold water, stir into the hot okra water and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes, beating with a wooden spoon, until thick and smooth.
Fold the okra and butter through until combined and shape into a mound.
Sauté the garlic in the oil for 1 minute, add the silverbeet and 2 tablespoons water and steam for 4 minutes until wilted, then serve with the cou cou and lime.

notes: Beat constantly to avoid lumps.
Traditionally served with fish or stew.

title: Colombian Arepa de Huevo
summary: Corn arepas split open and filled with a soft-cooked egg, baked in the oven for easy cooking.

steps.text: Mix the cornmeal, water and salt into a dough, rest for 5 minutes, then shape into 4 thick discs.
Brown the discs in a pan with the oil for 3 minutes each side until golden, then bake at 180C for 15 minutes until they sound hollow.
Cut a pocket in the side of each arepa, add a quarter of the cheese and crack in an egg, then bake for 8 minutes until the egg white is fully set.
Scatter with chives and serve warm.

notes: Keep the pocket small so the egg stays inside.
Food safety: bake until the egg white is completely set and the yolk is thickened; avoid runny eggs for young children, pregnant women and older adults.

title: Argentine Revuelto Gramajo Egg and Potato Scramble
summary: A comforting scramble of crisp potato, ham, onion and eggs.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a frying pan and fry the potato over medium heat for 12 minutes, stirring, until golden and tender.
Add the onion and ham and cook for 4 minutes until the onion is soft.
Pour in the eggs, salt and pepper and stir gently over low heat for 3 minutes until the egg is just set and no liquid egg remains.
Scatter with parsley and serve.

notes: Parboil the potato first if you want it crisper.
Food safety: cook eggs until set with no liquid egg remaining; avoid undercooked eggs for young children, pregnant women and older adults.

title: Mexican Champurrado-Style Corn Porridge
summary: A thick, warm corn porridge with cocoa and cinnamon.

steps.text: Whisk the cornmeal with the water in a saucepan until smooth.
Add the milk, sugar, cocoa, cinnamon stick, vanilla and salt and cook over medium heat for 12 minutes, whisking, until thick and smooth.
Remove the cinnamon stick and ladle into mugs or bowls.

notes: Whisk constantly to prevent lumps.
Use a little extra milk if the porridge thickens as it stands.

title: Swedish Oven Pancake Ugnspannkaka with Apple and Cinnamon
summary: A big, golden oven pancake baked with sliced apple and cinnamon.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220C and melt the butter in a 26cm ovenproof dish in the oven for 3 minutes.
Whisk the eggs, milk, flour, sugar and salt into a smooth batter.
Scatter the apple over the dish, pour over the batter, sprinkle with cinnamon and bake for 30 minutes until puffed, golden and cooked through in the centre.
Serve hot, cut in wedges.

notes: Do not open the oven in the first 20 minutes so it rises well.
Food safety: bake until the centre is fully set with no wet batter. Wash fresh produce well, refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat them within 3 days.

title: Green Shakshuka with Zucchini and Herbs
summary: Eggs poached in a green sauce of zucchini, spinach, herbs and a little chilli.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a deep frying pan and cook the onion for 5 minutes over medium heat until soft, then add the garlic, zucchini, chilli, cumin and salt and cook for 5 minutes until the zucchini is soft.
Add the spinach and stock and cook for 3 minutes until the spinach is wilted, then stir in the parsley.
Make four wells in the mixture, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 5 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks are as firm as you like.
Scatter with feta and serve with bread.

notes: Squeeze the grated zucchini dry so the sauce is not watery.
Food safety: cook eggs until the whites are fully set; avoid runny eggs for young children, pregnant women and older adults.

title: Shakshuka with Roasted Capsicum and Olives
summary: Eggs baked in a smoky roasted capsicum and tomato sauce with olives.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a deep frying pan and cook the onion for 6 minutes over medium heat until soft.
Add the garlic, capsicum, tomatoes, paprika, cumin and salt and simmer for 10 minutes until thick, then stir in the olives.
Make six wells in the sauce, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 6 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks as firm as you like.
Scatter with parsley and serve with bread.

notes: Use jarred roasted capsicum for speed.
Food safety: cook eggs until the whites are fully set; avoid runny eggs for young children, pregnant women and older adults.

title: Carrot and Raisin Slaw with Yoghurt Dressing
summary: A crunchy carrot and cabbage slaw with sweet raisins and a lemony yoghurt dressing.

steps.text: Toss the carrot, cabbage, raisins and parsley in a large bowl until combined.
Whisk the yoghurt, mayonnaise, lemon juice, honey and salt in a small bowl until smooth.
Pour the dressing over the slaw and toss until coated, then chill for 15 minutes before serving.

notes: Add toasted sunflower seeds for crunch.
Best eaten within 2 days.

title: Albanian Baked Lamb and Rice with Yoghurt Crust
summary: Tender lamb and rice baked under a golden egg and yoghurt crust, inspired by Albanian tave kosi.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180C. Heat the oil in a frying pan and brown the lamb over high heat for 6 minutes until coloured, then add the onion, garlic and oregano for 3 minutes until soft.
Tip the lamb mixture into a baking dish with the rice, water and salt, cover with foil and bake for 40 minutes until the lamb and rice are tender.
Whisk the yoghurt, eggs and flour until smooth, pour over the dish and dust with paprika.
Bake uncovered for 20 minutes until the top is set and golden.

notes: Let the dish stand for 5 minutes before serving so the crust firms up.
Food safety: cook the lamb until very tender and at least 75°C inside, and the egg topping until fully set; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Bulgarian Cheese and Egg Filo Squares
summary: Crisp filo layered with eggs, yoghurt and feta, baked and cut into squares in the style of banitsa.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180C and grease a 20cm square dish.
Whisk the eggs, yoghurt, feta, pepper and baking soda in a bowl until combined.
Brush each filo sheet with butter, scrunch it loosely and layer in the dish, spooning some of the filling between layers until all is used.
Bake for 35 minutes until deep golden and the filling is set in the centre. Rest for 10 minutes and cut into squares.

notes: Keep unused filo covered with a damp tea towel so it does not dry out.
Food safety: bake until the egg filling is fully set with no wet centre.

title: Eritrean Chickpea and Egg Breakfast Scramble
summary: Chickpeas and eggs scrambled with onion, tomato and mild spices, scooped up with bread.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a frying pan and cook the onion and chilli for 5 minutes over medium heat until soft.
Add the tomato, cumin and turmeric and cook for 3 minutes until the tomato breaks down, then stir in the chickpeas for 2 minutes until hot.
Pour in the eggs and salt and stir gently over low heat for 3 minutes until set with no liquid egg remaining.
Scatter with coriander and serve with bread.

notes: Mash a few of the chickpeas for a creamier scramble.
Food safety: cook eggs until fully set; avoid undercooked eggs for young children, pregnant women and older adults.

title: Beetroot and Apple Slaw with Horseradish Yoghurt
summary: A vivid raw beetroot and apple slaw dressed with a sharp horseradish yoghurt.

steps.text: Toss the beetroot, apple, cabbage and dill in a large bowl.
Whisk the yoghurt, horseradish, lemon juice, honey and salt in a small bowl until smooth.
Pour the dressing over the slaw and toss until coated, then chill for 10 minutes before serving.

notes: Wear gloves when grating the beetroot to avoid staining your hands.
Add the dressing just before serving to keep the colour bright.

title: Shredded Kale Salad with Shaved Cheese and Lemon
summary: Finely shredded kale massaged with lemon and olive oil, topped with shaved parmesan and toasted breadcrumbs.

items.raw: 300g kale, stems removed and thinly shredded

steps.text: Toast the breadcrumbs in 1 tsp oil in a dry pan for 3 minutes until golden and crisp.
Place the kale in a large bowl with the oil, lemon juice, garlic and salt and massage for 2 minutes until the leaves soften and darken.
Top with the cheese and breadcrumbs and serve.

notes: Let it sit for 10 minutes for a more tender salad.
Slice the kale as thinly as you can.

title: Indian Cabbage Thoran with Coconut
summary: A dry south Indian stir-fry of finely shredded cabbage with mustard seeds and coconut.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and add the mustard seeds until they pop.
Add the onion and chilli and cook for 4 minutes until soft, then stir in the turmeric.
Add the cabbage and salt and stir-fry for 5 minutes until just tender and still bright.
Stir through the coconut and coriander for 1 minute until warm, and serve.

notes: Do not add water; the cabbage releases enough as it cooks.
Great beside rice and dal.

title: Indian Palak Dal Spinach Lentils
summary: Red lentils simmered with spinach, garlic and cumin for a quick, comforting dal.

steps.text: Rinse the lentils and simmer with the water and turmeric for 20 minutes until soft and creamy.
Heat the ghee in a small pan and fry the cumin seeds, garlic, onion and ginger for 6 minutes until golden.
Stir the spinach into the lentils for 2 minutes until wilted, then add the salt and lemon juice.
Pour the spiced onion mix over the top and serve with rice.

notes: Skim off any foam from the lentils as they start to simmer.
Add a little water if the dal thickens too much.

title: Persian Herbed Rice with Dill and Peas
summary: Fragrant basmati rice cooked with plenty of dill, parsley and peas, with a golden crust if you like.

steps.text: Rinse the rice, then boil in a large pot of salted water for 7 minutes until just tender, adding the peas for the last 2 minutes, and drain.
Mix the dill and parsley through the rice.
Heat the oil, butter and turmeric in the pot, spoon in the rice, cover with a tea towel and lid and cook on low for 20 minutes until steamed through and the base is crisp.
Fluff and serve, breaking up the crust.

notes: Wrap the lid in a tea towel to catch steam and keep the rice fluffy.
Delicious alongside grilled chicken or lamb.

title: Spanish Rice with Peas and Paprika
summary: A simple one-pan rice with smoked paprika, tomato and peas, a Spanish-style side.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pan and cook the onion for 5 minutes over medium heat until soft.
Add the garlic, paprika and rice and stir for 2 minutes until coated, then add the tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes until thick.
Pour in the stock and salt, bring to a simmer, cover and cook on low for 12 minutes until the rice is tender, adding the peas for the last 3 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes, fluff and serve with lemon.

notes: Do not stir after adding the stock for fluffier rice.
Add a pinch of saffron if you have it.

title: Roasted Broccoli with Cheese and Lemon Crumbs
summary: Crisp-edged roasted broccoli finished with parmesan and a lemony toasted crumb.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220C. Toss the broccoli with 2 tbsp oil and the salt on a tray.
Roast for 15 minutes until charred at the edges and tender.
Mix the crumbs, cheese, zest, garlic and remaining oil, scatter over the broccoli and roast for 5 minutes until golden.
Squeeze over the lemon juice and serve hot.

notes: Dry the broccoli well before roasting for better browning.
Add a pinch of chilli flakes for heat.

title: Grilled Capsicum with Garlic and Parsley Oil
summary: Charred red capsicum strips dressed in garlic, parsley and good olive oil.

steps.text: Grill or roast the capsicums at 230C for 20 minutes, turning, until the skin is blistered and black.
Place in a covered bowl for 10 minutes, then peel, deseed and slice into strips.
Toss with the oil, garlic, parsley, vinegar and salt and serve at room temperature.

notes: Keep the juices that collect in the bowl for the dressing.
Good with crusty bread and cheese.

title: Charred Spring Onions with Almond Dressing
summary: Sweet charred spring onions served on a nutty almond and garlic dressing.

steps.text: Toss the spring onions with 2 tbsp oil and grill on a hot pan for 8 minutes, turning, until charred and tender.
Blitz the almonds, garlic, vinegar, remaining oil, soaked bread and salt in a blender with 3 tbsp water until a coarse sauce forms.
Spread the sauce on a platter, lay the spring onions on top and serve warm.

notes: Use a smoky paprika pinch to echo the char.
Trim the roots, but leave the white ends intact so the onions hold together.

title: Hash Brown Cakes with Spring Onion and Cheddar
summary: Crisp grated potato cakes with spring onion and cheddar, perfect beside eggs.

steps.text: Squeeze the grated potato in a clean tea towel until very dry.
Mix with the spring onion, cheddar, egg, flour, salt and pepper, then shape into 8 patties.
Fry in the oil over medium heat for 5 minutes each side until deep golden and cooked through.
Drain on paper towel and serve hot.

notes: Squeezing out the moisture is the secret to crisp edges.
Food safety: cook until the potato is tender and the egg is cooked through.

title: Creamy Polenta with Cheese and Black Pepper
summary: Creamy polenta stirred with butter, parmesan and plenty of black pepper.

steps.text: Bring the water and salt to a simmer in a heavy saucepan and pour in the polenta in a thin stream, whisking until smooth.
Cook on low heat for 20 minutes, stirring often, until thick and the grains are tender.
Stir in the butter, cheese and pepper until melted and creamy, and serve at once.

notes: Add a splash of hot water if it stiffens before serving.
Serve under braised meats or roasted vegetables.

title: Pumpkin and Sage Rice Cakes
summary: Golden pan-fried cakes made from pumpkin and sage risotto, crisp outside and soft inside.

steps.text: Mix the rice, pumpkin, sage, cheese, eggs, flour and salt in a bowl until it holds together.
Shape into 8 patties and chill for 15 minutes.
Fry in the oil over medium heat for 4 minutes each side until golden and heated through.
Drain on paper towel and serve hot with a green salad and lemon wedges.

notes: Chilling the patties helps them hold their shape.
Food safety: fry until golden and hot throughout, and cool and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Cheese and Herb Scones for Soup
summary: Savoury scones with cheddar and chives, ideal for dunking into soup.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220C and line a tray. Rub the butter into the flour and salt until like breadcrumbs.
Stir in the cheddar and chives, then add the milk and mix gently with a knife until a soft dough forms.
Pat out to 3cm thick, cut into 8 rounds, place on the tray and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 18 minutes until risen, golden and cooked through.

notes: Do not overwork the dough or the scones will be tough.
Food safety: bake until golden and cooked through in the middle.

title: Herbed Cornbread with Jalapeno
summary: A moist cornbread with jalapeno and fresh herbs, baked in a tin.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200C and grease a 20cm square tin.
Mix the cornmeal, flour, baking powder and salt in a bowl.
Whisk the eggs, milk, butter and honey, pour into the dry mix with the jalapeno and chives and stir until just combined.
Pour into the tin and bake for 25 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.

notes: Serve warm with butter or alongside chilli and soup.
Food safety: bake until a skewer comes out clean. Wash fresh produce well, refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat them within 3 days.

title: Asparagus Soup with Lemon Cream
summary: A silky green asparagus soup finished with a swirl of lemon cream.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes over medium heat until soft, then add the potato, asparagus, stock and salt.
Simmer for 15 minutes until the potato and asparagus are very tender.
Blend until smooth, then stir in half the cream and half the lemon juice and reheat until steaming.
Whip the remaining cream with the zest and pepper, spoon over the soup and serve.

notes: Save a few tips to garnish.
Do not boil after adding the cream.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

title: Seafood Chowder with Dill
summary: A creamy chowder of white fish, prawns and potato with sweet corn and fresh dill.

items.raw: 300g white fish fillet, cut in chunks

steps.text: Melt the butter in a large pot and cook the onion and celery for 5 minutes over medium heat until soft.
Add the potato and stock and simmer for 12 minutes until the potato is tender.
Add the milk, corn and fish and simmer gently for 4 minutes, then add the prawns and cook for 3 minutes until the fish flakes and the prawns are pink and opaque.
Stir in the dill and salt and serve hot.

notes: Keep the heat low once the milk goes in so it does not curdle.
Food safety: cook fish and prawns until opaque and 63°C inside; eat leftovers within 1 day and reheat until piping hot.

title: Silverbeet and Ricotta Egg Muffins
summary: Make-ahead egg muffins packed with silverbeet, ricotta and a little parmesan.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180C and grease a 6-hole muffin tin with the oil.
Wilt the silverbeet in a hot pan for 2 minutes until soft, cool slightly and squeeze dry.
Whisk the eggs, ricotta, silverbeet, spring onion, cheese, salt and pepper and divide among the holes.
Bake for 25 minutes until puffed, golden and set in the centre.

notes: Keep refrigerated and reheat until hot for weekday breakfasts.
Food safety: bake until the centres are fully set; refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 3 days, reheating until piping hot.

title: Carrot Cake Porridge with Walnuts
summary: Creamy rolled oats cooked with grated carrot, cinnamon and sultanas, topped with walnuts.

steps.text: Combine the oats, milk, carrot, cinnamon and nutmeg in a saucepan.
Cook over medium heat, stirring, for 8 minutes until thick and creamy.
Stir in the sultanas and maple syrup, then spoon into bowls and top with the walnuts and yoghurt.

notes: Add a splash of milk if you like it looser.
Swap the walnuts for pecans or almonds.

title: Corn and Capsicum Breakfast Tacos with Scrambled Egg
summary: Soft tortillas filled with fluffy scrambled egg, charred corn and capsicum.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a pan and cook the capsicum and corn over high heat for 4 minutes until charred and tender.
Pour in the eggs and salt and stir over low heat for 3 minutes until the egg is just set.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 30 seconds each side.
Fill the tortillas with the egg mixture, top with avocado and coriander and serve with lime.

notes: Keep the egg soft but fully set.
Food safety: cook eggs until set with no liquid egg remaining; avoid undercooked eggs for young children, pregnant women and older adults.

title: Tofu and Mushroom Hot Pot with Rice Noodles
summary: A fragrant ginger broth simmered with vegetables, tofu and rice noodles.

steps.text: Bring the stock, ginger and soy sauce to a simmer in a large pot and cook for 8 minutes until fragrant.
Add the mushrooms and tofu and simmer for 4 minutes until tender.
Add the rice noodles and cook for 4 minutes until tender, then add the bok choy for 2 minutes until wilted.
Stir in the sesame oil, scatter with spring onion and serve in bowls.

notes: Soak the noodles first if they are very thick.
Add chilli oil at the table if you like heat.

title: Pork and Apple Soup with Sage
summary: A gentle pork shoulder soup with apple, sage, carrot and potato.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the pork in two batches over high heat for 5 minutes until coloured.
Add the onion and carrot and cook for 5 minutes until soft, then add the sage, stock, salt and pepper and simmer gently for 35 minutes until the pork is tender.
Add the potato and apple and simmer for 15 minutes until the potato is cooked and the apple is soft.
Taste, adjust the seasoning and serve hot.

notes: Choose a tart apple so it holds some shape.
Food safety: cook the pork until tender and at least 75°C inside; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until steaming.

title: Ham and Corn Fritters with Chive Yoghurt
summary: Golden pan-fried fritters with ham and sweet corn, served with a cool chive yoghurt.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder, eggs, milk and salt into a thick batter, then fold in the corn, ham and spring onion.
Heat a little oil in a frying pan over medium heat and spoon in the batter in 1/4 cup mounds.
Cook for 3 minutes each side until golden and cooked through, keeping the cooked fritters warm.
Stir the chives into the yoghurt and serve with the fritters.

notes: Do not overcrowd the pan or the fritters will steam.
Food safety: cook until golden and the centres are fully set with no wet batter; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Coconut Porridge with Roasted Pineapple
summary: Creamy oats cooked in coconut milk, topped with caramelised roasted pineapple and toasted coconut.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200C. Place the pineapple on a tray, drizzle with honey and roast for 15 minutes until golden and caramelised.
Cook the oats, coconut milk, water and salt in a saucepan over medium heat, stirring, for 8 minutes until thick and creamy.
Toast the coconut in a dry pan for 2 minutes until golden.
Spoon the porridge into bowls and top with pineapple and toasted coconut.

notes: Use canned pineapple rings in juice if fresh is not available; drain well.
Stir in a little extra water if the porridge is too thick.

title: Apple and Oat Yoghurt Parfait
summary: Layers of yoghurt, stewed cinnamon apple and crunchy toasted oats.

steps.text: Simmer the apples, water and cinnamon in a saucepan for 6 minutes until soft, then stir in the honey and cool.
Toast the oats in the butter in a dry pan for 4 minutes until golden and crisp.
Layer the yoghurt, apple and oats in two glasses and top with walnuts.

notes: Make the apple the night before for quick mornings.
Add a pinch of nutmeg if you like.

title: Sticky Soy Roasted Pumpkin Wedges
summary: Roasted pumpkin glazed in soy, honey and ginger until sticky and caramelised.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220C. Toss the pumpkin with the oil and roast for 20 minutes until starting to brown.
Mix the soy, honey, ginger and garlic, brush over the pumpkin and roast for 12 minutes until sticky and tender.
Scatter with sesame seeds and spring onion and serve.

notes: Line the tray with baking paper to avoid sticking.
Keep the skin on for easier handling.

title: Spiced Cabbage and Potato Side
summary: A dry-spiced cabbage and potato stir-fry with mustard seeds and turmeric.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pan and fry the mustard and cumin seeds for 30 seconds until they pop.
Add the onion and cook for 4 minutes until soft, then add the potato, turmeric, ground coriander and salt and cook for 8 minutes, stirring, until the potato starts to soften.
Add the cabbage and water, cover and cook for 8 minutes until both are tender.
Scatter with coriander and serve.

notes: Cut the potato small so it cooks at the same pace as the cabbage.
Add a squeeze of lemon at the end.

title: Turmeric Rice with Peas and Cashews
summary: Fluffy turmeric rice with peas and toasted cashews, a bright side for curries.

steps.text: Melt the ghee in a saucepan and fry the cumin seeds for 30 seconds until they sizzle, then add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the rice and turmeric for 1 minute, add the water and salt, cover and cook on low for 12 minutes until the water is absorbed, adding the peas for the last 3 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes, fluff with a fork and stir through the cashews.

notes: Rinse the rice first for separate grains.
Do not lift the lid while it cooks.

title: Smoky Baked Bean Side with Bacon
summary: Slow-simmered white beans in a smoky tomato sauce with bacon and a little brown sugar.

steps.text: Cook the bacon and oil in a saucepan over medium heat for 5 minutes until crisp, then add the onion and garlic and cook for 4 minutes until soft.
Stir in the paprika, tomatoes, sugar and vinegar and simmer for 8 minutes until slightly thick.
Add the beans and salt and simmer gently for 15 minutes until the sauce clings to the beans.
Stir once more until glossy and heated through, then serve hot with grilled meats or on toast.

notes: It thickens as it cools; add a splash of water to loosen.
Food safety: cook the bacon until crisp and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Tangy Pickled Carrots
summary: Crisp carrot batons in a sweet and tangy vinegar brine, ready to eat the next day.

steps.text: Pack the carrots into clean jars.
Heat the vinegar, water, sugar, salt, mustard seeds, garlic and peppercorns in a saucepan for 4 minutes until the sugar dissolves and the brine is steaming.
Pour the hot brine over the carrots, cool and refrigerate.

notes: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 weeks.
Only part of the brine is eaten, so the sodium is an estimate.

title: Mince and Vegetable Soup with Macaroni
summary: A family-style soup with beef mince, vegetables and macaroni.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the mince over high heat for 6 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains.
Add the onion, carrot, celery and garlic and cook for 5 minutes until soft, then add the tomatoes, stock and oregano and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the macaroni and simmer for 8 minutes until tender, adding the peas for the last 3 minutes.
Season with salt and serve hot.

notes: The pasta will absorb liquid on standing, so add water when reheating.
Food safety: cook the mince until no pink remains and at least 75°C; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Smoky Sausage and Capsicum Soup
summary: Sausage, capsicum and tomato simmered with smoked paprika and white beans.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a pot and brown the sausage over medium heat for 6 minutes until golden and cooked.
Add the onion and capsicum and cook for 6 minutes until soft, then stir in the garlic and paprika for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, stock, beans and salt and simmer for 15 minutes until the capsicum is tender and the soup is slightly thick.
Scatter with parsley and serve.

notes: Mash a few beans to thicken the soup.
Food safety: cook sausages until no pink remains and at least 75°C inside; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Italian Sausage and Tortellini Soup
summary: Italian sausage, spinach and cheese tortellini in a tomato broth.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a pot and cook the sausage meat over medium-high heat for 7 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and cooked through.
Add the onion and garlic and cook for 4 minutes until soft, then pour in the tomatoes, stock, oregano and pepper and simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the tortellini and cook for 4 minutes until it floats and is tender, then stir in the spinach for 1 minute until wilted.
Ladle into warm bowls and serve hot with crusty bread.

notes: Choose fresh tortellini from the chilled aisle.
Food safety: cook the sausage until no pink remains and at least 75°C inside; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Eggy Bread with Maple Bacon
summary: Egg-dipped bread fried until golden, served with maple-glazed crispy bacon.

steps.text: Fry the bacon in a dry pan over medium heat for 5 minutes until crisp, then brush with maple syrup and cook for 1 minute until glossy and set aside.
Whisk the eggs, milk and cinnamon in a shallow dish.
Dip the bread into the egg mix until soaked, then fry in the butter for 3 minutes each side until golden and cooked through.
Serve the eggy bread topped with the bacon.

notes: Use slightly stale bread for the best texture.
Food safety: cook the egg-soaked bread until golden and no wet egg remains; avoid undercooked eggs for young children, pregnant women and older adults.

title: Spinach and Cheese Breakfast Quesadilla
summary: Crisp tortilla folded around scrambled egg, wilted spinach and melted cheese.

steps.text: Wilt the spinach in a hot pan with the oil for 2 minutes until soft, then pour in the eggs and salt and stir for 2 minutes until just set.
Sprinkle half of each tortilla with the cheese, top with the egg and spinach and the tomato, and fold over.
Toast in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 minutes each side until golden and the cheese has melted.
Cut into wedges and serve.

notes: Press down lightly with a spatula for even browning.
Food safety: cook eggs until set with no liquid egg remaining; avoid undercooked eggs for young children, pregnant women and older adults.

title: Broccoli Salad with Bacon and Sunflower Seeds
summary: Raw broccoli florets with crispy bacon, sunflower seeds and a tangy yoghurt dressing.

steps.text: Fry the bacon in a dry pan over medium heat for 6 minutes until crisp, then drain on paper towel.
Toss the broccoli, onion, sunflower seeds and sultanas in a large bowl.
Whisk the yoghurt, mayonnaise, vinegar, honey and salt, pour over the salad and toss to coat.
Top with the bacon and serve cold.

notes: Chop the florets small so every bite has some dressing.
Food safety: cook the bacon until crisp and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

title: Herbed Cauliflower Rice Salad
summary: Finely chopped cauliflower tossed with herbs, tomato and lemon in a tabbouleh style.

steps.text: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pan and cook the cauliflower for 4 minutes over medium heat until just tender, then cool.
Toss with the tomato, cucumber, parsley, mint and spring onion.
Dress with the lemon juice, remaining oil and salt and toss until combined.
Chill for 10 minutes before serving.

notes: Squeeze the cauliflower in a tea towel after cooking to avoid a watery salad.
Serve with grilled meats or falafel.

title: Cheesy Garlic Mushrooms Side
summary: Pan-roasted mushrooms in garlic butter with melted mozzarella and parsley.

steps.text: Heat the oil and half the butter in a wide pan and cook the mushrooms over high heat for 8 minutes until golden and any liquid has gone.
Add the remaining butter, garlic, salt and pepper and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Scatter with the mozzarella, cover and cook for 2 minutes until melted, then top with parsley and serve.

notes: Do not crowd the pan or the mushrooms will steam instead of browning.
Serve on toast for a quick lunch.

title: Cabbage Steaks with Garlic Butter
summary: Thick cabbage slices roasted until caramelised and brushed with garlic butter.

items.raw: 1 small green cabbage (about 800g), cut in 4 thick slices

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220C. Brush the cabbage with the oil, season with salt and arrange on a tray.
Roast for 25 minutes, turning once, until the edges are charred and the centres are tender.
Melt the butter with the garlic for 1 minute until fragrant and bubbling, then stir in the lemon juice.
Drizzle the garlic butter over the cabbage and scatter with parsley.

notes: Keep the core in each slice so the layers stay together.
Add chilli flakes for a little heat.

title: Thai Jungle Curry with Pork and Green Beans
summary: A hot, brothy red curry with no coconut milk, full of beans, eggplant, lime leaves and Thai basil.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wok or large saucepan over medium heat. Add the curry paste and galangal and stir for 2 minutes, until the paste darkens a shade and smells fragrant.
Add the pork and stir-fry for 2 minutes, until every slice is coated in paste and no longer looks raw on the outside.
Pour in the stock, add the eggplant and lime leaves and bring to a simmer. Cook for 8 minutes, until the eggplant is just tender.
Add the beans and simmer for 4 minutes more, until they are bright green and tender-crisp and the pork is cooked through with no pink in the middle.
Season with the fish sauce and palm sugar, then taste: it should be hot, salty and herby rather than sweet. Stir in the basil until it just wilts and serve with jasmine rice.

notes: Food safety: cook the pork until it reaches 70°C in the centre. Thin slices get there in a few minutes of simmering.
Jungle curry has no coconut milk, so it is thinner and hotter than a red curry. Use 2 tbsp paste for a milder pot.
Most red curry paste contains shrimp paste. Check the label if you're cooking for someone who avoids shellfish.

title: Vegan Lemon and Olive Oil Loaf Cake
summary: A tender, lemony loaf made with olive oil and soy milk, finished with a sharp lemon glaze.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Grease a 22 x 11cm loaf tin and line the base and long sides with baking paper.
Rub the lemon zest into the caster sugar with your fingertips in a large bowl until it smells strongly of lemon. Whisk in the flour, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda and salt.
In a jug, whisk the soy milk, olive oil, lemon juice and vinegar. The milk will thicken and curdle a little, which is what you want.
Pour the wet mix into the dry and fold with a spatula until no dry flour shows. Stop there: a few lumps are fine, and overmixing makes a tough loaf.

Scrape into the tin and bake for 45 to 50 minutes, until risen and golden and a skewer pushed into the middle comes out clean. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then lift onto a rack and cool completely.
Stir the icing sugar with the lemon juice until smooth and thick enough to coat a spoon. Spoon over the cold loaf and leave it to set for 15 minutes before slicing.

notes: Soy milk works best because its protein thickens with the vinegar. Other unsweetened plant milks work but give a slightly flatter loaf.
Keeps in an airtight tin for 3 days. It is moist enough not to need butter.

title: Rigatoni with Cavolo Nero, White Beans and Chilli Crumbs
summary: A 30-minute vegan pasta: garlicky greens and creamy beans, with crisp chilli breadcrumbs on top.

items.raw: 1 bunch cavolo nero (about 250g), stems removed, leaves shredded
400g tin cannellini beans, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Bring a large pot of water to the boil and salt it well. Cook the rigatoni for 2 minutes less than the packet says, until it is still firm in the centre.

While the pasta cooks, warm 2 tbsp of the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Fry the breadcrumbs with half the chilli flakes and a pinch of the salt for 4 minutes, stirring, until golden and crisp. Tip into a bowl and wipe out the pan.
Add the rest of the oil to the pan with the garlic and the remaining chilli. Cook gently for 2 minutes, until the garlic is pale gold and fragrant; don't let it brown.
Add the cavolo nero and beans with a ladle of pasta water. Cover and cook for 4 minutes, until the leaves have wilted and turned dark and silky.

Scoop out a mugful of pasta water, then drain the rigatoni and add it to the pan with the lemon zest, lemon juice, pepper and the rest of the salt. Toss over the heat for 2 minutes, adding splashes of pasta water, until the sauce turns glossy and clings to the pasta.
Taste for salt and lemon, then serve straight away with the chilli crumbs scattered over.

notes: Kale or silverbeet work in place of cavolo nero; add silverbeet stems with the garlic.
Keep the crumbs separate until serving or they go soft.

title: Red-Braised Beef with Daikon
summary: Beef chuck slow-braised in soy, Shaoxing wine, star anise and rock sugar until it falls apart.

items.raw: 600g daikon, peeled and cut into 3cm chunks

steps.text: Put the beef in a large heavy pot, cover with cold water and bring to the boil. Boil for 3 minutes, until grey scum rises, then drain and rinse the beef and the pot. This keeps the sauce clear.
Heat the oil in the clean pot over medium-high heat. Fry the spring onion, ginger and garlic for 1 minute until fragrant, then add the beef and stir for 3 minutes, until browned in places.
Add the star anise and cinnamon, pour in the Shaoxing wine and let it bubble for 30 seconds. Stir in both soy sauces, the rock sugar and the water, which should just cover the beef.
Bring to the boil, then cover, turn the heat to low and simmer gently for 1 hour 45 minutes, stirring now and then, until the beef is nearly tender.
Add the daikon, pushing it under the liquid, and simmer uncovered for 40 minutes, until the beef is fork-tender and the daikon is translucent and soft.
Lift out the spices. If the sauce is thin, boil it hard for 5 to 10 minutes until it is glossy and coats a spoon. Serve with rice.

notes: Food safety: braised beef passes a safe 70°C long before it turns tender, so the cue to watch for is a fork sliding in easily. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until steaming hot all the way through (75°C).
It tastes even better the next day and keeps in the fridge for 3 days.
For a gluten-free version, use tamari for both soy sauces and dry sherry for the Shaoxing wine, and check the labels.

title: Besan Chilla with Spinach and Tomato
summary: Savoury chickpea flour pancakes flecked with spinach, tomato, chilli and coriander. Ready in 30 minutes.

steps.text: Whisk the chickpea flour, turmeric, cumin seeds, ajwain and salt in a bowl. Slowly whisk in the water until you have a smooth batter about as thick as pouring cream. Leave it to stand for 10 minutes so the flour hydrates.
Stir the spinach, tomato, onion, chilli, coriander and ginger into the batter. If it has thickened, loosen it with a splash of water.
Heat a non-stick frying pan over medium heat and brush it with a little oil. Pour in a ladle of batter and quickly spread it with the back of the ladle into a 15cm round.

Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until the top looks dry and the underside is golden with crisp edges. Drizzle a few drops of oil around the edge, flip and cook for 2 minutes more, until both sides are golden and the middle is cooked through.
Keep each chilla warm in a low oven while you cook the rest, brushing the pan with oil each time. Serve hot with lemon wedges.

notes: Chickpea flour has no gluten but is sometimes milled alongside wheat. Buy one labelled gluten-free if you're cooking for someone with coeliac disease.
Many versions add asafoetida (hing). Most hing powder is cut with wheat flour, so it is left out here.
